title: Circle the Pictures
text: Look at the pictures. Circle fact if the picture shows someone who is real. Circle fiction if the picture shows someone who is not real.

title: Thanksgiving Traditions
text: The Pilgrims came to America in 1620. They wanted to be free to worship in their own way. They wanted to start a new community. It took 66 days for the Pilgrims to sail from England to America.

title: Wampanoag Indian Customs
text:
When the Pilgrims came to America, they started new customs.

A custom is how people do certain things. The Wampanoag Indians showed the Pilgrims how to plant corn. They taught the Pilgrims their custom of putting a small fish in each hill of corn. That would help the corn to grow tall.

title: Thanksgiving
text: The Pilgrims and Wampanoag Indians had a big feast to celebrate the fall harvest. This feast became known as Thanksgiving.

title: Traditions and Customs
text: A tradition is a custom or belief that is passed down from one generation to another. Today, it is a tradition to celebrate Thanksgiving in November. We eat a special meal with our families. Why is it important that traditions be passed down?

title: Thanksgiving Customs
text: Customs and traditions are important to families and communities. What is a Thanksgiving custom your family follows? What is a Thanksgiving tradition in your community? Why is it important?

title: Draw a Picture
text: Draw a picture of your family’s Thanksgiving custom. Why is it important to your family?

title: Fun and Games
text: Write a green X on the map to show where the Pilgrims’ journey began. Write a red X on the map to show where the Pilgrims’ journey ended. Draw a line to show their journey.

title: American Stories: William Bradford
text: When the Pilgrims came to America, they wrote rules for everyone in the colony to follow. The rules were called the Mayflower Compact. William Bradford knew that it was very important to have rules. The Pilgrims elected him the governor of their colony more than 30 times! Would you like to be a governor someday?

title: Maps
text: Maps are drawings of places. Some maps help people find their way around.

title: Boundaries of States
text: Some maps show boundaries between states or countries. A boundary is a line that shows where one place ends and another place begins.

title: Map Keys
text: Most maps have a key to help you read them. A map key tells you what the symbols on the map stand for. An airplane () shows where an airport is located.

title: Cardinal Directions
text:
North, south, east and west are cardinal directions. Do you see something that looks like a star below the map? That is a compass rose. It tells directions, or which way to go to get to your location.

Put your finger on Birmingham, Alabama, on the map. Which way would you go to get from Birmingham to the other cities on the map?

title: Practice Map
text: Look at your classroom. Point to the north wall. Which direction would you walk to get from your classroom to the cafeteria? Your teacher will give you another practice map.

title: Land on Earth
text: Maps and globes can show what the land on Earth looks like. This map shows landforms. Landforms are the shapes of the land. Landforms are things like mountains, valleys, deserts and beaches. Look at the map. How many landforms do you see?

title: Bodies of Water
text: Maps and globes can show bodies of water on Earth. Bodies of water can be large like oceans, lakes and rivers. Bodies of water can be small like ponds and creeks. Look at the map. How many bodies of water do you see?

title: American Stories: Vitus Bering
text: Vitus Bering was an explorer from Denmark. Can you imagine traveling 6,000 miles across land and then sailing over very cold seas? That’s what Vitus Bering did! He found a new waterway between Russia and Alaska. The waterway was named the Bering Strait after this brave explorer.

title: Earth
text:
Earth is our planet. Landforms and bodies of water are on Earth.

A globe is a model of the Earth. Do you see the United States on the globe? Can you see Texas? Use your classroom globe to find your community.

title: What on Earth?
text: Look at the map of the United States. Do you see your city or town? Maps cannot show every city and town. Maps usually show larger cities. Do you live close to any of the cities on the map? Have you been to any of the cities on the map?

title: The Plains
text: The middle part of the United States is sometimes called the Plains. The land there is mostly flat.

title: The Mountains
text: In the West, the Rocky Mountains can be seen from miles away.

title: Bodies of Water
text: In most parts of the world, there are oceans, rivers, lakes and streams.

title: The Desert
text: But in deserts, like the Sahara Desert of Africa, there is almost no water at all.

title: Natural Resources
text: Natural resources are found across our state and our country. A natural resource is a thing found in nature that humans can use. Water, trees and oil are natural resources. What natural resources are found in your community?

title: Who Is in Charge?
text: Who is in charge of making rules and laws? Some adults have the authority to make rules and laws. Authority is the right and power to do something.

title: Making and Enforcing Laws
text: Your parents and other citizens elect (vote for) leaders to make laws. Other people, like police officers, have the authority to make sure people obey the laws. This helps citizens feel secure.

title: Rules at School
text: At school, teachers and principals make the rules. They have the authority to make sure students obey the rules. The rules help keep your school safe and orderly.

title: Rules at Home
text: Your parents have the authority to make rules for your home. They make decisions that keep you safe and healthy. Many parents make rules about picking up toys. Can you name another rule that keeps you safe and healthy at home?

title: School Property
text: Rules and laws help keep order. Students must take care of school property like books and computers. Students must respect others and keep their hands and feet to themselves. What are some other rules at your school?

title: Safety
text: Some rules and laws help keep us safe and secure. In Texas, it is a law that you must wear a seat belt when you ride in a car. How does wearing a seat belt keep you safe? What other rules in your community keep you safe?

title: Rules and Consequences
text:
A conflict happens when people are not getting along. Parents and teachers make rules that help us solve conflicts. One rule is to listen to what the other person has to say. Even adults need help solving some conflicts. A judge helps adults understand the laws.

If you break the rules or laws, there are consequences. What happens if you break the rules at school?

title: Fun and Games

title: Rules and Laws
text: We have rules at school. We have laws in our communities, state and country. Rules help keep order in schools. Laws help keep order in our communities, state and country.

title: Draw a Picture
text: Draw a picture of someone who has the authority to make sure people obey the rules or laws. Write a word that describes the person on the line.

title: I Am Responsible
text: There are many ways to be responsible. You can keep your promises. You can admit when you do something wrong, even if there are consequences. At school, you can listen to your teacher and follow directions. At home, you can listen to your parents and do your chores. Are you responsible?

title: Be a Friend
text: What if a new student comes to your class? What can you do to make them feel welcome? Smile and say hello. You can ask the new student to sit with you at lunch or play with you and your friends at recess.

title: Be Kind and Respectful
text: If you are responsible, you are kind to other people and to animals. You show respect to everyone. Being kind and respectful shows that you care about others.

title: Be a Responsible Owner
text: Do you have a pet? Being responsible means you take care of your pets. You make sure they have food and water. You do your best to keep them safe and healthy.

title: Playground Decisions
text: How do you make decisions during outdoor play? What if everyone wants to play on the slide? You can take a vote with your friends to see who goes first. Voting is a fair way to decide.

title: Making Decisions
text: There are other ways to make a decision. Responsible people think about the decision before they decide. They gather information and think about their choices. Next, they predict what might happen. They make a decision and try it out. Last, they think about what happened. Was it a good decision or a bad decision?

title: Solving Problems
text: What should you do if you and a friend are not getting along? Talk about the problem. Use quiet voices when you talk. Listen to each other. If you still are not getting along, take a break. Then try again later.

title: Fun and Games
text: Jack says it is his turn to use the computer. Jill says it is her turn. How can Jack and Jill solve the problem? Read each sentence below. Circle the sentences that tell what Jack and Jill should do. Write an X on the sentences that tell something they should not do.

What is one thing you should do before you make a decision? Write your answer on the lines.

title: Celebrate America
text: A symbol is something that stands for something else. The Statue of Liberty and the Liberty Bell are symbols of freedom. Americans believe in freedom for everyone.

title: Liberty Bell
text: You can see the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia. It is more than 200 years old. Liberty is another word for freedom.

title: Statue of Liberty
text: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of France more than 100 years ago. It is in New York City.

title: The Bald Eagle
text: The bald eagle is strong, brave and free. It stands for America, because our country is strong, brave and free, too.

title: Uncle Sam
text: Uncle Sam stands for our government. He wears red, white and blue clothes. Uncle Sam often asks Americans to help their country. How can you help make America a great place to live?

title: Special Celebrations
text:
On Constitution Day we celebrate American freedom. We are free to speak and free to think. Constitution Day is September 17. How does your school celebrate Constitution Day?

What special celebrations are held in your community?

title: San Jacinto Day
text:
April 21 is San Jacinto Day. On this day we remember an important battle Texans fought against Mexico. Today, people celebrate San Jacinto Day by going to a festival and watching reenactments of the battle.

The San Jacinto Monument is in La Porte, Texas.

title: Celebrating Differences
text: People in America speak many different languages. We celebrate many cultures, even though we are not all alike. We are individuals. Our differences help make America a great place to live!

title: Veterans Day
text: Veterans Day is celebrated on November 11. On this holiday we honor the people who served our country. We celebrate by watching parades and ceremonies that honor veterans.

title: Fill in the Blanks
text:

1. Texans remember an important battle with Mexico on _______________ Day.

2. On _______________ Day we celebrate American freedom.

3. On November 11 we celebrate _______________ Day.

title: Fact or Opinion?
text:
A fact is something you can prove is true. (Fact: There are 50 states in the United States of America.) An opinion is something you believe is true, even though others may not agree. (Opinion: Grape is the best flavor for bubble gum.)

Listen as your teacher reads these sentences. Circle fact if the sentence is a fact. Circle opinion if the sentence is an opinion.

factopinion

2. The bald eagle is the best symbol of America.

factopinion

title: American Monuments
text: The Washington Monument honors George Washington. It is in Washington, D.C.

title: American Monuments Part II
text: Monuments can be many things. They can be statues, buildings, or works of art. Many monuments honor the people who have helped make America a strong and free country.

title: Memorials Help Us Remember
text: A memorial helps us remember important people. All of these memorials are in Washington, D.C.

title: The Jefferson Memorial
text: The Jefferson Memorial honors Thomas Jefferson. A large statue of Thomas Jefferson is inside the building.

title: The Lincoln Memorial
text: The Lincoln Memorial honors Abraham Lincoln. You can see the Lincoln Memorial on the back of some pennies and a five-dollar bill.

title: The Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial
text: The Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial honors our 32nd president. He could not stand or walk without help, and he used a wheelchair for many years. Roosevelt was president for twelve years, longer than any other president. His dog, Fala, slept in his room every night.

title: The Empire State Building
text:
The Empire State Building is in New York City. It is more than 1,400 feet tall.

For many years, the Empire State Building was the tallest building in the world.

title: The Alamo
text: In 1836, a battle took place at the Alamo. Texans fought Mexican troops. About 200 Texan soldiers died. This battle became a symbol of Texas’ wish for independence. The Alamo is located in San Antonio.

title: Asking for Help
text: Most people like to be independent. That means they like to do things on their own. But everyone needs help sometimes. It is OK to ask for help when you need it.

title: Find San Antonio
text: Write an X on the map where San Antonio, Texas, is located. Have you ever seen the Alamo?

title: American Stories: Salem Poor
text: Salem Poor was a patriot. He was born enslaved, but he bought his own freedom. He fought in the American Revolution against the British to help America become free, too. Salem was a brave soldier. He got a reward for being brave during the war.

title: Presidents and Patriots
text: A president is the leader of a country. Patriots are people who love their country. Our country has one president. Our country has many patriots.

title: Presidents and Patriots Part II
text: George Washington was the first president of the United States. He led an army that fought and won against the British. This war led to our country’s independence. Many people think he was one of our greatest presidents.

title: John Adams
text: John Adams was our second president. He was born in Massachusetts. John Adams was the first president who lived in the White House.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text: Thomas Jefferson was our third president. He was born in Virginia. He was an author, an inventor and an architect (a person who designs buildings).

title: Presidents Day
text: In America, we celebrate Presidents Day on the third Monday in February. On that day, we honor George Washington and Abraham Lincoln because they helped make America a great place to live.

title: Betsy Ross
text: Betsy Ross lived in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Many people believe she made the first American flag. The story says that George Washington asked her to make a flag with thirteen stripes and thirteen stars. The stars and stripes stood for the thirteen United States.

title: Crispus Attucks
text: Americans fought a war with Britain to become a free country. That war is called the American Revolution. Crispus Attucks was an African American patriot from Boston, Massachusetts. He was one of the first patriots to die in the American Revolution.

title: Sam Houston
text:
Sam Houston led an army that won a battle for Texas’ independence. The city of Houston is named for him.

How are George Washington and Sam Houston similar? How are they different?

title: Yankee Doodle
text: British soldiers first sang “Yankee Doodle” to make fun of Americans. Before long, Americans were singing new words to the song. The new words were about George Washington and the brave American soldiers. “Yankee Doodle” is one of our country’s favorite patriotic songs.

title: Sequoyah
text: Sequoyah was a Cherokee Indian from North Carolina. He invented a written alphabet for the Cherokee language. Soon thousands of Cherokee learned to write using Sequoyah’s alphabet.

title: Fill in the Blanks
text:
1. Many people believe Betsy _____________ made the first American flag.

2. John _____________ was the first president who lived in the White House.

3. George Washington was the _____________ president of the United States.

title: Matching
text: Where were these presidents and patriots from? Draw a line from each person’s name to the state that it matches. You will use some of the states more than once.

title: Fun and Games
text: Look at this map of the first states. Find the four states that were home to the people we studied this week. Color the state where more than one person lived blue. Color the state where Betsy Ross lived red. Color the state where Sequoyah lived green.

title: Rights and Responsibilities
text: Americans believe that everyone has the right to be treated equally. We have the responsibility to treat others the way we want to be treated. Americans have the right to worship in their own way. We have the responsibility to respect others’ beliefs.

title: Voting
text: American citizens are responsible for voting for our country’s leaders. When people vote, they have a choice to make. It is important to vote so that everyone has a say in the way our country works.

title: Taking Care of Our Things
text: Americans have the right to own things like land, houses and cars. We have the responsibility to take care of our things. We have the responsibility not to hurt or take away things that belong to other people.

title: The President
text: The president is the leader of our country. Being the president is a big responsibility. Many people help the president decide what is best for America. The president lives in the White House. Who is our president? Draw our president’s face in the picture above.

title: The U.S. Constitution
text: A constitution lists the basic laws of a country or a state. The U.S. Constitution protects the rights of all Americans.

title: Governors
text: The governor is the leader of a state. Governors work in the state capitol. Who is the governor of Texas?

title: Obeying Laws
text: The U.S. Constitution says one of the president’s jobs is to make sure people obey the laws of our country. The Texas Constitution says that one of the governor’s jobs is to make sure people obey the laws of the state.

title: Mayors
text: The mayor is the leader of a city. Mayors work in the city hall. They are responsible for the police, fire and transportation departments of a city. Who is the mayor of your city?

title: Communities
text: A community is a place where people live. In every community, people need food, shelter and clothing.

title: Communities II
text: People who live in different communities have different kinds of food, shelter and clothing.

title: Heat
text: In some communities, it is usually hot. People wear clothes that help keep them cool.

title: Cold
text: In other communities, it is usually cold. People wear clothes that help keep them warm.

title: Air Conditioner
text: Some homes have fans or an air conditioner for hot weather.

title: Heater
text: Some homes have a furnace or fireplace for cold weather.

title: Weather
text: In some communities, there is plenty of sunshine and rain. Many different kinds of food will grow. In other communities, it is very dry or very rainy. Only a few different kinds of food will grow.

title: Texas
text: People who live in Texas often wear shorts and sandals. Farmers in Texas can grow lots of fruits and vegetables. Grapefruit, watermelon, onions and corn grow in Texas.

title: Alaska
text: People who live in Alaska often wear heavy coats and snow boots. People who live in Alaska get most of their fruits and vegetables from other places.

title: Needs
text: All people need food, shelter and clothing. People meet these needs in different ways. Some families grow their own food. Some families make their own clothes.

title: Needs II
text: People also work to earn money. Many families use money to buy food and clothing. They pay for their homes with the money that they earned. How does your family get the things you need?

title: Changes in Communities
text: Before people lived on Earth, only plants and animals were here.

title: Building Villages
text: More than 3,000 years ago, people began to change things. They cut down trees and other plants so they could grow food and build villages.

title: Population Growth
text: Over time, the number of people on Earth kept getting larger. They needed more food, so they cleared more land for farms. They cleared land to raise cows, horses and sheep.

title: Roads
text: The first roads were just dirt paths made by people and animals walking from place to place. Later, people built better roads to get from one place to another. After cars were invented, people needed more and more roads.

title: Technology
text: Technology helped to change the way people lived. Machines helped workers build better homes and larger buildings. Soon more families moved to these areas. Some small towns grew into the large cities we see now. How does your family use technology today?

title: Consequences of Change
text: All of the changes people make in their communities have consequences.

title: Traffic Jams and Pollution
text: There are traffic jams on many roads. Pollution is making the air and water in many places very dirty. How can we help keep the Earth clean and safe?

title: How to Protect Natural Resources
text: Natural resources are things found in nature, such as air and water. People need clean air and clean water every day. There are many things we can do to protect our natural resources.

title: Protecting Natural Resources
text: We can take buses, ride bicycles or walk instead of driving cars. We can turn off the lights and television when we leave a room. We can take shorter showers. We can recycle.

title: Goods and Services
text: People in every community have needs and wants. Some of the things they need and want are called goods. Goods are things made for people to buy, like skateboards and helmets. Can you think of some other goods?

title: Goods and Services II
text: A service is work or a duty that someone does for another person. When parents aren’t home, they can hire a babysitter. Taking care of children is a service that babysitters do. Can you think of some other services?

title: Consumers
text: Consumers are people who pay for goods or services. They can buy many goods and services in their own communities. Some things they need and want come from other communities. What goods can you purchase in your community?

title: Producers
text: Producers are people who make goods or provide services for consumers. They sell some goods and services in their own communities. Some producers send goods to other communities, too. What services are offered in your community?

title: Schools
text: Goods and services are found in schools. Paper and pencils are goods. So is Studies Weekly! Principals, teachers and cafeteria workers are providing you with a service. Teachers help you learn. Cafeteria workers serve you lunch. Can you name the goods and services in the picture?

title: Choices
text: Sometimes you have to give up one thing to get something else. You need to make a choice. What you give up is called an opportunity cost. Pretend you want an apple and a banana, but you only have enough money for one. If you buy the apple, the banana is the opportunity cost.

title: Needs and Wants
text: Needs and wants have benefits, too. Benefits are the good things that happen. If you plant a garden, you can get beautiful flowers or delicious fruits and vegetables.

title: Citrus Trees
text: Citrus trees grow fruits like oranges, lemons, limes and grapefruits. Florida, California and Texas grow most of the citrus trees in the United States. What is your favorite citrus fruit?

title: Earning
text: People use money to buy things they need and want. Money is a capital resource. Most people earn money by working.

title: Jobs People Do
text: People have many different kinds of jobs. Jobs help families because workers earn money to buy things they need and want. The money workers earn is called income.

title: Jobs People Do II
text: Many workers pay taxes. Some taxes help pay for community services like trash collection, the police department and the fire department.

title: Dentists
text: Dentists take care of people’s teeth. They fill cavities, repair broken teeth and teach people how to take care of their teeth and gums. To be a dentist, you have to spend four or more years in college.

title: Musicians
text: Musicians sing or play musical instruments. To be a musician, you must have a special talent. Musicians often take many years of music lessons and study music in college.

title: Server
text: In order to do a job well, you have to perform the tasks and take care of customers. Servers serve food in restaurants. They have to listen carefully and be polite to the customers. How do servers know they’ve done their job well?

title: Human Resources
text: People who work are human resources. They help other people get the things they need and want.

title: Letter Carriers
text: Letter carriers work hard to deliver letters and packages to people. Some letter carriers walk many blocks in all kinds of weather. Others drive cars or vans.

title: Children
text: A long time ago, many children in America had to work to help their families. Some worked on farms. Some worked in factories. Factories are places where goods are made.

title: Pilots
text: Airline pilots fly airplanes. They have to know how to get the plane off the ground, guide it in the air and land it safely. To get a pilot’s license, you must go to a special school and pass difficult tests.

title: Turkey
text: In Turkey, many children start working on the family farm when they are very young. It is a custom for older kids to learn how to weave Turkish carpets. Selling these goods helps bring money to the family.

title: Money and Trade
text: Long ago, people traded with each other at a market to get things they needed and wanted. People in one community might have more rice than they needed. They could trade it for something they didn’t have, like cloth.

title: Money and Trade II
text: Money was invented about 4,000 years ago. People used shells, stones, beads and even whales’ teeth as money. Some people used coins made of silver or gold.

title: Trade
text: People traded goods and services. People often traded with weavers (people who make cloth). They might give the weaver a tea kettle or some vegetables. Trading goods and services is called bartering.

title: Traveling
text: Did people only trade with those who lived close to them? No. People often traveled hundreds of miles to trade. Some travelers rode on animals like camels or donkeys, and some sailed in canoes or ships.

title: Around the World
text: Today, people all around the world still depend on others to get things they need and want. The United States sends corn, computers and other goods to many different countries. People in Texas buy goods like cars, clothes and furniture that come from other countries.

title: Brazil
text: Brazil grows more coffee than any other country in the world. Brazil sends coffee to people around the world. Every year, they send 28 million bags of coffee to other places.

title: Saved
text: Many years ago, people saved money and other valuable things by burying them. Today, some people save coins in a jar or a piggy bank. Many people take their money to a bank to keep it safe.

title: Rainy Day
text: Have you ever heard anyone say, “Save for a rainy day”? That means people should save some money in case of an emergency.

title: Mexico

title: Spend or Save
text: People spend money for goods like food and services like haircuts. When you spend money on goods or services, you are a buyer. A person who gives you goods or services for your money is a seller. People who make the goods or provide the services are called producers.

title: Spend or Save Part II
text: What if a good or service costs more money than you have? You can save your money until you have enough.

title: Spending
text: Most people do not have enough money to buy everything they want and need. They have to make responsible choices about how to use their money. Most people spend money to pay bills and buy things their families need. They save some money, too.

title: Saving
text: Saving money is very important. People save money to buy things in the future. Many families save money to buy a car or a house. Some families save money to go on a vacation. The more something costs, the more you have to work to save enough money to buy it. It is not always easy to save money.

title: Need
text: One way to be responsible with money is to buy the things you need before you buy the things you want. Before you spend money, ask yourself, “Do I need this or do I want this?” It’s OK to spend money on something you want, as long as you don’t have to give up something you need.

title: Saving Up
text: If you want to save money to buy something, you need to know how much it costs. You need to know how much money you already have. Then you can start saving.

title: Opportunity Cost
text: When you decide to start saving, you will probably have to give up something else. If you save to buy a bicycle, you might have to give up buying a treat each week with your allowance. Do you remember what we call something we give up to get something else? If you said it’s an opportunity cost, you are right!

title: Share
text: Many people also share some of their money to help others. Sharing money is called donating.

title: Helping
text: Your money can help build houses for people with no homes or help take care of dogs and cats in shelters. Can you think of other ways your money can help?

title: Welcome to Second Grade
text: Welcome back to another fun year at school. This year Studies Weekly will help you learn more about your community, your state, your country and your world.

title: Important Words and Their Meanings
text:
A republic is a country where the people choose leaders to represent them in the government.

The word indivisible means that our country cannot be divided or separated.

Liberty means freedom. Justice means fairness for all people.

title: The Pledge of Allegiance
text: I pledge allegiance to the flag of the United States of America, and to the republic for which it stands, one nation under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.

title: Honesty
text: Being honest is very important. Sometimes it is hard to tell the truth, especially if you did something you shouldn’t have done. If you always tell the truth, people will know that you are trying hard to be a good citizen. What are some other ways you can be a good citizen?

title: Pledge to the Texas Flag

title: The Bald Eagle
text: The bald eagle is a symbol of the United States of America. Did you know that Benjamin Franklin thought the turkey should be our national symbol? He said that eagles are found in many countries, but wild turkeys are only found in America. Other people thought the bald eagle was the best choice because it was a strong and brave bird. The bald eagle represents strength and bravery in the United States of America!

title: American Stories
text: Hi! This year Studies Weekly will tell you the story of our amazing country—the United States of America. You will learn about some American heroes and how they helped America become a great country. We hope you enjoy reading our “American Stories!”

title: American Stories: George Washington
text: You probably know that George Washington was our first president. When he was young, he had a different job. He measured land and drew maps. George measured carefully, so his maps would be correct. He knew people needed maps to help them find their way around our new country. When you do your work at school, do you think and work carefully? If you do, then you are like George Washington!

title: Good Citizens
text:
Who is responsible for making a community a good place to live? Everyone who lives in the community must work together.

Good citizens believe in justice for everyone. Fairness is another word for justice.

title: U.S. Constitution
text: The U.S. Constitution lists the basic laws of our country.

title: James Madison
text: James Madison helped write the United States Constitution. The Constitution protects our right to privacy. Things that are private are not for others to see or to know.

title: Tell an Adult
text: Sometimes you cannot keep things private. If you know a secret that could hurt someone, you have a responsibility to tell an adult. You can tell your parents, a teacher or any adult you trust.

title: Equal Rights
text:
The Constitution says that everyone has the right to be treated equally.

No matter what we look like or where we come from, we should all have the same opportunities.

title: Respect and Kindness
text: Good citizens treat others with respect and kindness. How do you feel when someone is kind to you? Talk to a friend about how to show respect and kindness.

title: Children in India
text: In India, like in the United States, children have many responsibilities. Many children help in the kitchen to make chapati. Chapati is a round flat bread that is served at many meals. Children learn responsibilities by helping family and friends.

title: Airplanes

title: Explorers
text: More than 500 years ago, Christopher Columbus tried to sail across the Atlantic Ocean and around the world to the East Indies. He wanted to bring back spices and other things to sell. Instead, he landed at a place he called the New World—Central America.

title: Marco Polo
text: Marco Polo was only 17 years old when he left Italy with his father and uncle to explore China in the year 1271. Their journey was very difficult and very dangerous. Marco kept a journal of their travels.

title: Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca
text: Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca was an explorer from Spain. In 1528, he sailed from Florida on a raft and landed near Galveston Island. He named the place Isla de Malhado, which means Island of Misfortune.

title: Lewis and Clark Expedition
text: An expedition is a journey. The Lewis and Clark Expedition happened more than 200 years ago. Meriwether Lewis and William Clark led a group called the Corps of Discovery. They traveled more than 8,000 miles from St. Louis, Missouri, to the Pacific Ocean and back. One of their guides was a young Shoshone Indian woman named Sacagawea.

title: Ferdinand Magellan
text: The first journey around the world by sea happened in 1519-1522. Ferdinand Magellan led the expedition, but he died before the journey was over. Only one of his five ships made it all the way around the world and back to Spain.

title: North American Indian Nations
text: American Indians were the first people who lived in North America. There are more than 500 American Indian nations in North America. People in many American Indian nations demonstrate their traditions at powwows. At modern powwows, people sing, dance, and tell stories. They showcase arts and crafts made by American Indians.

title: Cheyenne
text: The Cheyenne live in the Great Plains region of the United States. Long ago, the Cheyenne hunted buffalo for food. In the winter, they wore buffalo skins to keep warm.

title: Hopi
text: The Hopi live in the Southwestern region of the United States. The Hopi believe that everyone should love all people, plants and animals.

title: Iroquois
text: Many Iroquois live in the state of New York. For many years, they grew corn, beans and squash. They called them “The Three Sisters.”

title: Seminole
text: The Seminole have lived in Florida for nearly 300 years. Long ago, many Seminole lived in homes called chickees. A chickee is an open building with a roof made of cabbage palm leaves.

title: Tlingit
text: The Tlingit live in Alaska. Tlingit often carve totem poles. A totem is an animal spirit that belongs to a group of Tlingit.

title: Pictures as Records
text: For many years, American Indians had no written language. Some American Indians drew pictures on animal skins or on rocks to keep track of important things that happened.

title: American Indian Sign Language
text: Many American Indians once communicated with sign language. These pictures show two of the signs they used a long time ago.

title: Changes for American Indians
text: The first people who lived in North America were American Indians. They lived here for thousands of years. Then other people started coming to America. Many people came from countries in Europe. Europe is a continent.

title: Different Ways of Living
text:
People who move to a new country are called immigrants. The Pilgrims came to America in 1620. The American Indians were already living there. Some of them lived in large shelters that held many families. Other American Indian families lived in smaller shelters.

The Pilgrims and the American Indians had different ways of living. It was not always easy to share the land. Sometimes they fought.

As more and more people came to America, things changed for the American Indians. Their land was taken away from them. They were forced to leave their homes. They got sick from germs brought by the immigrants. Many American Indians died.

title: Communities
text:
Over time, more immigrants came to America. Settlements grew larger and became crowded. Different types of communities started to form.

Urban is a word we use to describe a city. Urban communities have many tall buildings that are close together. When urban communities become crowded, some people choose to move away. A suburban community is a group of neighborhoods near a big city. There is more space for homes and businesses in suburban communities. Where do you live if you want even more space? A rural community is a place where there are not many people or buildings. There are small towns, farms and open land.

title: Changes in America
text: The Pilgrims were not the only people who left England and came to America. More and more people came. Soon there were 13 colonies. The people cleared more land by cutting down trees and large plants. This gave them room to plant more crops and build more houses.

title: Life in the Colonies
text: Life in the colonies was very hard at first, but it got easier. The people learned how to plant different kinds of food. They built better homes. Some people opened shops. The shops sold clothes, tools, food and other things people needed. In 1635, the first public school opened in America.

title: Population
text: As time passed, the population of America got much larger. (Population is the number of people living in a certain place.) More land had to be cleared to grow enough food to feed all the people. People settled in places that had rich natural resources. A natural resource is any material from the Earth that people can use. We use natural resources for food, clothing and shelter.

title: Buildings
text: People needed more and more buildings—homes, stores and places to meet. They built factories to make things they needed. They built roads leading to every town and city. People invented new technology to build taller buildings. People also found ways to grow more food and to make clothing quickly.

title: Consequences
text: All of those changes had consequences. Some animals lost their habitats, and some became extinct (gone forever). Cars and factories polluted the air. Homes and factories polluted the water.

title: Protecting Resources
text: Soon people began to worry about the Earth. Many people decided to do something to save the natural resources in the world. They knew it was important to protect natural resources like air, water and trees.

title: What Can We Do?
text: What can we do to help conserve the Earth’s natural resources? Conserve means to save or use carefully. Here are some ideas.

title: Water
text: Water is a natural resource. Don’t let the water run while you are brushing your teeth. Take short showers instead of baths. If there is a leaky faucet at your house, ask your parents to fix it. Volunteer to help clean up a beach or river bank near your home.

title: Trees
text: Trees are natural resources. Paper is made from trees. Recycle paper or reuse it. Use cloth napkins instead of paper. Ask your parents to buy paper that has been recycled.

title: Electricity
text: We use natural resources to make electricity that runs machines in our homes. Turn off things that use electricity—lights, TVs and computers—when you leave a room. Before you open the refrigerator door, decide what you want. Ask your parents to adjust the thermostat in your house to save energy.

title: Texas Crops
text: When people save water, it can be used in other places. Crops in Texas need a lot of water. Irrigation systems were built to bring water from one place to another. This helps crops to grow. More people can eat the food we grow in Texas.

title: American Celebrations
text:
Our country has celebrations. Our state has celebrations. Our community has celebrations. Thanksgiving is celebrated by our whole nation. In 1620, the Pilgrims sailed from England to America on the Mayflower. The next year, the Pilgrims held a special feast. The Wampanoag Indians joined the celebration of the successful harvest.

Today, most people celebrate Thanksgiving in November with friends and family. Thanksgiving is a day that we remember all of the good things in our lives. How does your community celebrate Thanksgiving?

title: Independence Day
text: Independence Day is a national holiday. On July 4, Americans celebrate our freedom from Great Britain. We remember and honor the patriots who helped build the United States of America. Today, it is a custom for communities to celebrate this holiday with flags, parades and fireworks. What are some Independence Day customs in your community?

title: Memorial Day
text: Memorial Day is the last Monday in May. It is a day to remember the men and women who died while serving our country. On this national holiday, you will probably see American flags in many places. Does your community have a Memorial Day parade?

title: Juneteenth
text:
Juneteenth is a special celebration in Texas. On June 19, 1865, enslaved people in Texas learned that they were free. It is a custom for many communities to celebrate Juneteenth with picnics and parades. What other special celebrations does your community have?

These people organized a Juneteenth celebration in 1900.

title: Veterans
text: People who have served in the armed forces are called veterans. Our nation remembers and appreciates the men and women who have served our country. This holiday is called Veterans Day. It is celebrated on November 11. Veterans are honored guests at many parades and ceremonies.

title: Fact or Opinion
text:
A fact is something you can prove is true. (Fact: There are 50 states in the United States of America.) An opinion is something you believe is true, even though others may not agree. (Opinion: Grape is the best flavor for bubble gum.)

title: American Stories: William Bradford
text: When the Pilgrims came to America, they wrote rules for everyone in the colony to follow. The rules were called the Mayflower Compact. William Bradford knew that it was very important to have rules. The Pilgrims elected him the governor of their colony more than 30 times! Would you like to be a governor someday?

title: Maps
text: Maps tell people where places are located and how to get there. But some maps do much more. Maps can tell us about the Earth—the height of the mountains and the depth of the oceans. Maps can tell us about people—where they live and how they change their communities.

title: Parts of a Map
text: A map key explains the symbols on a map. Legend is another name for a map key. Many maps have coordinates. Coordinates are numbers or letters (or both) along the margins of a map. Coordinates help you find places on a map.

title: Map Symbols
text: These are map symbols. A picnic table shows where a picnic area is located. A tent stands for a campground. Capital cities are marked with a star in a circle. The symbol that has a number in it is the sign for a U.S. Highway.

title: Relative Location
text: One way to describe where a place is located is by saying it is close to a familiar place. For example, you might say that the library is across the street from the park. When you describe the location of a place this way, you are giving the relative location.

title: Distance and Scale
text: Distance is how far it is from one place to another. You can tell the distance on a map by looking at the scale. A scale uses inches to stand for miles. On this scale, one inch equals one mile.

title: Cardinal and Intermediate Directions
text: Look at this compass rose. You have probably heard of north, south, east and west. There are other directions in between these directions. For example, northeast is between north and east. Southwest is between south and west.

title: Types of Maps
text: There are many different types of maps. The map’s title tells you what it shows. A physical map shows things like mountains and bodies of water. A political map shows boundaries. Boundaries are dividing lines between places. A theme map shows special things like the regions of a place or how many people live there.

title: People, Seasons and Weather
text: Seasons and weather affect where people live and what they do. Weather is what is happening in the air right now. Different times of the year have different weather patterns. These are called seasons. Most places have four seasons: winter, spring, summer and fall. Describe the seasons where you live in Texas.

title: Different Climates
text: People sometimes choose to settle in an area because of the seasons and the weather. If people like cold weather, they might settle in a place that has a longer winter season. If people like warm weather, they might settle in a place that has a longer summer season. Different areas on Earth have different climates. Climate is another word for the seasonal patterns that are usually the same year after year. What kind of climate would you like to live in?

title: Outdoor Activities
text: People plan many activities based on the seasons and weather. During a season, the weather can affect what we do. Have you ever played outside on a warm day in the winter? Have you ever cancelled swimming because it rained? Activities like farming and construction also depend on the seasons and weather. Many crops grow best during the spring and summer. They get plenty of rain and sun. Other crops do well in a drier climate. Construction workers cannot build homes during heavy rain. Think about your favorite outdoor activity. Can you do this activity outside any day of the year?

title: Natural Hazard
text:
A natural hazard is a dangerous event in nature. Some examples of natural hazards are tornadoes, wildfires and earthquakes. People have to think about the hazards of an area when they choose a place to settle. Natural hazards also affect our activities. What activities could you not do during a tornado or a wildfire? What hazards might farmers need to prepare for?

Think about your community. Why do you think people settled here?

title: Climate Map of Texas
text:
Look at the climate map of Texas. Read the climate definitions below. Then answer the questions.

Cold-Dry: This climate region is typically the coldest in the state. It experiences crisp to cold winters, with extreme temperature ranges daily. Summers are usually warm to hot and dry. However, they are not as hot as the summers in hot deserts.

Hot-Dry: This climate region is typically the hottest in the state. It experiences hot to scorching summers, with lots of sunshine and little precipitation. Winters are usually warm to cool. It is mostly dry all year.

Mixed-Humid: This climate region is the most varied in the state. It experiences warm to hot to sweltering summers. Winters are usually cold to mild and wet. Rainfall and dry seasons differ from year to year.

title: Presidents and Patriots
text: Patriots are people who love their country. They are good citizens. You can be a patriot no matter how young or old you are. Are you a patriot?

title: Thomas Jefferson
text: Thomas Jefferson was born in Virginia. He was the third president of our country. He wrote the Declaration of Independence. The Declaration of Independence said that America was a free country. Thomas Jefferson died on the Fourth of July, fifty years after he wrote the Declaration of Independence.

title: James Madison
text: James Madison was another president born in Virginia. He was known as the “Father of the Constitution,” because many of the ideas in the Constitution came from him. The Constitution is the law of the United States. James Madison believed that citizens have both rights and responsibilities.

title: John Hancock
text: John Hancock was born in 1737. He was a governor and a member of the Massachusetts Congress. He was also one of the signers of the Declaration of Independence. His name is the largest on the document. John Hancock died in 1793. He is known as one of America’s greatest Patriots.

title: Irma Rangel
text: Irma Rangel was born in Texas. She was the first Mexican American woman elected to the Texas House of Representatives! Irma Rangel knew that school was important. She wanted all children in Texas to get the chance to go to college.

title: Slavery
text: For over 300 years, some Americans owned enslaved people. Enslaved people were brought from Africa on crowded ships. They were chained together so they could not escape. Many got sick and died on the journey. People who owned plantations (large farms) bought enslaved people to work in the fields and in their homes. Enslaved people were not paid for the work they did. They had no rights and no freedom. All enslaved people were declared free after the Civil War ended.

title: Harriet Tubman
text: Some enslaved people escaped to states where slavery was not allowed. Harriet Tubman escaped when she was about 30 years old. Harriet was born in slavery in Maryland. After she escaped, she went back to the South many times to help other enslaved people escape. Thanks to Harriet, almost 300 enslaved people were freed.

title: Escaping Slavery
text: Thousands of people escaped slavery to freedom on the Underground Railroad. The Underground Railroad was not a real railroad. The “stations” on the Underground Railroad were houses or barns or churches where slaves stayed as they traveled north. The “conductors” were people who believed slavery was wrong. They risked their lives to help people escape slavery.

title: Thurgood Marshall
text: Thurgood Marshall was born in Maryland. His grandfather had been a slave. Thurgood went to school to become a lawyer. He became the first African American justice (judge) on the Supreme Court. Thurgood Marshall worked to make sure that African Americans had the same rights as white Americans.

title: Good Citizenship
text: How did these people show good citizenship? What people and events have influenced your community?

title: President of the United States
text: Would you like to be the president of the United States someday? You have to be at least 35 years old. You must have been born an American citizen. And you must have lived in the United States for at least 14 years.

title: The Statue of Liberty
text: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of France. It is one of our most famous monuments. It took 10 years to make the statue. Americans celebrated the 100th birthday of the Statue of Liberty on July 4, 1986.

title: The Liberty Bell
text:
The Liberty Bell is a symbol of independence and freedom.

It is more than 250 years old. It cracked many years ago. The last time the bell rang was on George Washington’s birthday in 1846. You can see the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

title: Minutemen
text: During the American Revolution, some soldiers were called minutemen. They had to be ready to fight for freedom on just a minute’s notice. There are statues of minutemen in Lexington, and Concord, Massachusetts.

title: Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness
text: Americans believe that everyone has rights that cannot be taken away. The Declaration of Independence says people have the right to “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.” That means we have the right to live, to be free and to try to be happy. Many American symbols remind us that these rights are very important and should be protected.

title: Symbols of American Courage
text: Some of our American symbols are people who stood up for their beliefs. These people are symbols of American courage.

title: César Chávez
text: César Chávez was born of Mexican heritage. He and his family were migrant workers (people who move from place to place working on farms). They had almost no money and no home of their own. Chávez believed that migrant workers should have the same rights as others. When Chávez grew up, he helped migrant workers get better pay and better homes.

title: President Theodore Roosevelt
text: President Theodore Roosevelt believed that creating parks would be a good way to celebrate America. In the early 1900s, Roosevelt created five national parks. Roosevelt wanted to protect the land, plants and animals in these parks. Have you visited a national park?

title: A Symbol of Freedom
text: When immigrants came by ship to America, they could see the Statue of Liberty from the ship. The statue is a symbol of freedom for all people.

title: Chief Joseph
text: Chief Joseph was an American Indian who belonged to the Nez Perce Nation. He believed that American Indians should have the same rights as other Americans. He did not want the government to make the people of the Nez Perce Nation move to a new place. Chief Joseph gave many speeches asking for freedom and equal rights for American Indians.

title: American Cultures
text: Long ago, only American Indians lived in America. Then settlers came from Spain, France and England. Next, enslaved people were brought from Africa. Today, many different people from many different places live here. There are many different cultures in America.

title: Culture
text: Culture is all the beliefs and traditions of a group of people. It is food, clothing, art, beliefs, language and much more.

title: Food
text:
Long ago, American Indians ate what they could hunt or grow. They fished and hunted animals like rabbits, turkeys and deer. They grew corn and beans. We still eat some of these foods today.

Slave ships from Africa brought foods like rice, okra and yams to America. Peanuts came from Africa, too. Asian families brought stir-fried foods and egg rolls to America. Hispanic families brought arroz con pollo (rice with chicken) and empanadas to America.

title: Languages
text: Most people in America speak English. Many people in Texas speak both English and Spanish. In different parts of the country you may hear Chinese, French, Igbo and many other languages. Different cultures make America a great place to live!

title: Holidays
text: Many people celebrate winter holidays. Compare the following winter holidays. Most families in America celebrate Christmas with gifts and Christmas trees. Jewish families celebrate Hanukkah by lighting a candle each night for eight nights. Hindu families light lamps and set off fireworks to celebrate Diwali.

title: Las Posadas
text: Many Hispanic Americans celebrate Las Posadas in December. They remember Mary and Joseph’s journey before Jesus was born. They celebrate Christmas on December 25.

title: Kwanzaa
text: Many African Americans celebrate Kwanzaa in the winter. Families light a candle each day for seven days. It is a time to remember their African culture.

title: Dong Zhi
text: Many Asian Americans celebrate Dong Zhi on the first day of winter. They eat food like long noodles, soup and rice dumplings.

title: Government
text: The United States Constitution explains how our government works. It gives the government many powers, like the power to protect our rights and keep us safe. It also says those powers have limits. For example, the government cannot force people to worship a certain way. Do you know the name of this government building? What happens there?

title: The President
text: The president is the leader of our country. The governor is the leader of a state. The mayor is the leader of your city or town. Senators and representatives make laws.

title: Why Do People Form Governments?
text: Why do people form governments? Governments provide many services for citizens. The government helps pay for roads and parks. It helps pay for schools and libraries in communities. It helps pay for firefighters and police officers to protect citizens. Do you know any other services the government provides?

title: Governments Make Laws
text: Governments make laws, decide if the laws are fair and make sure people obey the laws. Laws help keep us safe. Laws help make sure everyone is treated fairly. If we didn’t have laws, many things would not run smoothly. There would be no consequences for people who steal things or hurt people. Governments help solve conflicts.

title: U.S. Citizens
text: Most people who live in our country are U.S. citizens. Some people who live in our country are immigrants. Many immigrants hope to become U.S. citizens someday.

title: How Do People Become Citizens?
text: How do people become citizens? If you are born in the United States, you are a U.S. citizen. If your parents are citizens, you are a citizen no matter where you were born.

title: Naturalization
text: Immigrants can become citizens by naturalization. Naturalization is all of the things immigrants must do to become citizens. They have to fill out many forms. They have to pass a test about U.S. history and government. They must promise to obey the laws and be loyal to the United States.

title: What is a Government?
text: What is a government? A government is a group of people who lead a country, state or city.

title: Rights and Responsibilities
text: One of our most important rights is the right to free speech. Free speech is the right to express your thoughts and opinions. Free speech does not mean we can say anything we want to. We have the responsibility to tell the truth. We have the responsibility to use our words to make things better and not to hurt others.

title: Mayor
text: The mayor is the leader of a city. The people who live in a city vote for the person they want to be the mayor. Mayors must do their best to make the city clean and safe for everyone. Most mayors have lots of people who help them every day.

title: The Right to Vote
text: American citizens who are at least 18 years old have the right to vote. They elect the leaders of their city, state and country. Voting is an important responsibility, too. In some countries, citizens do not have the right to vote.

title: City Commissioners
text: City commissioners are people who help the mayor make decisions. The citizens vote for the people they want to be city commissioners. Many people have jobs that help make our cities great places to live. Police officers and firefighters help keep the city safe. Waste collectors help keep the city clean.

title: Appointed Officials
text: Another way to work as a city official is to be appointed. Appointed officials are chosen by a leader to perform a certain job. You can give your opinion to both elected and appointed leaders. It is their responsibility to listen to the concerns of citizens.

title: Community Service
text: Everyone has the right to live in a safe, clean community. But it takes hard work to make a community a good place to live. We all have a responsibility to do everything we can to keep our community clean and safe. Good citizens participate in community service. You can volunteer to pick up trash at the park. You can recycle bottles, cans and newspapers. You can follow the rules that help keep you safe, like wearing a bicycle helmet. What other ways can you think of?

title: Child Labor
text: Long ago, many children worked in factories. Factories are places where things are made. They had the responsibility to work every day except Sunday. They could not go to school. Many children worked in mills where cloth was made, and many boys worked in mines.

title: George Washington Carver

title: Benjamin Banneker

title: Margaret Knight
text: Margaret (Mattie) Knight was only 12 when she started inventing things. In 1868, she invented a machine to make paper grocery bags.

title: Robert Fulton
text: Robert Fulton improved the steamboat. This technology helped transportation. Steamboats moved goods and people quickly around the country.

title: Carlos Finlay
text: Carlos Finlay was a Cuban doctor who helped prove that mosquitos carry yellow fever. Doctors were able to control the spread of this disease.

title: Thomas Edison
text:
Did you know Thomas Edison created more than 1,000 inventions?

He invented the light bulb, the film projector and the phonograph. A phonograph is a machine that records sounds and plays them back.

title: Ruth Wakefield
text: Some inventions were discovered accidentally. One day, Ruth Wakefield wanted to make chocolate cookies, but she didn’t have the right kind of chocolate. She chopped up a chocolate candy bar and stirred it into the cookie dough. The bits of chocolate didn’t melt, and the chocolate chip cookie was born!

title: Scarcity
text:
Scarcity is not having enough of something like food or water. Millions of people around the world do not have enough food to eat or clean water to drink.

Many families do not have enough money to buy everything they need. They have to make difficult choices about how to spend their money.

title: Resources and Choices
text:
A resource is anything that people can use. There are many types of resources. It is important for people and communities to use resources wisely, so that they will be there for us to use in the future.

Trees are natural resources. How are trees used to meet our needs? People build houses with wood from trees. How else are trees used?

title: Money
text: Money is a capital resource. People use money to buy things they need and want. They can also save money for the future or donate money to people in need.

title: Using Capital Resources
text: When we use capital resources, we have to make choices. Most people don’t have enough money to buy everything they want. They have to choose the things that are most important to them.

title: Spend or Save?
text: Imagine you had $5.00 to spend. Would you spend it all? Would you save it to buy something more expensive? What are some other ways you could use your money?

title: Using Natural Resources
text: We also have to make choices when we use natural resources. Cutting down too many trees could destroy some animals’ homes. But people need wood to build homes, furniture and other things. We have to work together to make the best choices.

title: Costs and Benefits
text:
The choices people make have costs and benefits. The cost can be money, time or loss of natural resources. The benefits are the good things that happen, like when families have everything they need and some things they want.

If your family decides to eat at a restaurant, it might cost more money than you would spend on a meal at home. But you would probably have fun, and the people who work at the restaurant would do all the cooking and cleaning up.

title: Oil
text: Oil is an important natural resource. A lot of oil is used to make fuel for cars, trains, boats and planes. Oil is also used to make other things like paint, tires, ink and plastic. Texas produces more oil than any other state in the United States.

title: Wasting Natural Resources
text: Some choices have costs but no benefits. If you let the water run while you brush your teeth, you are wasting one of our most important natural resources—water. It also costs your parents money when they pay the water bill.

title: Replenishing Natural Resources
text: Can people replenish (replace) natural resources? We can replenish some of them, but it may take a very long time. It takes 20 years or more for many trees to grow, but new fruits and vegetables can be grown year after year. Things that become extinct can never be replaced.

title: Goods and Services
text: Goods are things that are made for people to buy and use. The people who make goods are called producers. The people who buy goods are called consumers.

title: Income
text: People in the U.S. make choices about earning money. We are also free to choose where we live and work. The money workers earn is called income. Income helps families buy things they need and want. Money can buy goods or services.

title: Doctors and Nurses
text: Many people work to help keep people healthy. Doctors, nurses and paramedics take care of people who are sick or hurt. It takes at least 11 years of college and special training to become a doctor.

title: Photographers
text: Photographers are creative and talented people who take pictures. Some photographers help us learn about things that are happening in our world. Some photographers help us remember special occasions like weddings and holidays.

title: Taxes
text: Most workers pay taxes. Taxes help pay for community services, roads, parks and many other things. The laws of our state and our country say taxes must be paid. Good citizens obey the law and pay their taxes.

title: Librarians
text: Librarians choose books for libraries. They help people pick out books they will enjoy reading. Librarians also help people find information about many things. Librarians go to college for at least four years.

title: Responsibilities at Work
text:
People who work have many responsibilities.

They have to come to work every day, unless they are sick or have a day off. They have to be on time every day. It is important for workers to do their best, no matter what job they do.

title: Farmers
text: Farmers are producers. They grow food for people to eat. Farmers are also consumers. They need tractors and other machines to plant and harvest crops. Part of a farmer’s income is used to purchase these goods.

title: Growing and Selling Produce
text: In the U.S., thousands of people work on farms. Some are growers, and others pick produce (fruits and vegetables). Truck drivers take the produce to stores. Salespeople help customers buy produce for their families.

title: Sending and Receiving Goods

title: Supply and Demand

That’s called “supply.” It also depends on how many people want or need that resource. That’s called “demand.” When the supply is low and the demand is high, the price goes up. When the supply is high and the demand is low, the price goes down.

title: Credit Cards
text: Many people use credit cards. Credit cards let you buy something now and pay for it later. You will often have to pay interest, too. Banks give credit cards to people who agree to pay for the things they buy.

title: Where in the World Are You?
text:
Where are you in the world right now? You are probably in your classroom at your school. Your school is in a neighborhood in a city. Your city is in a state. The state is in a country. And your country is on a continent. Seven continents cover Earth. Whew! Now where, exactly, did you say you were?

People need to be able to describe where they are located. Sometimes you need to describe about where you are. Sometimes you need to describe exactly where you are. Because of this, people have found ways to describe their position on Earth. More than 4,000 years ago, people began using maps to show what the world looked like. Maps are information tools. We can use maps to find and study certain places.

Maps are models of Earth and its features. People who make maps are called cartographers. These map makers use points, lines, symbols and color to explain details on the maps. Maps are always drawn on a flat surface. Earth isn’t flat, though. Sometimes this makes a map hard to understand. That’s why globes were invented.

Long ago, people did not understand the shape or size of Earth very well. Explorers began to gather good information about Earth’s features. Map makers began to show the world as a sphere. These special maps are called globes. Globes are great tools. On a globe, the places on Earth are in their correct positions. Globes show the correct shape of continents and bodies of water. Early explorers liked to use globes because they were easier to understand than maps.

Today people use both maps and globes. There are many different kinds of each. They can be used to find out all kinds of information about the world. Maps can help you learn about places and the people who live there.

Knowing how to read maps is important. In this issue, you’ll find out how to use maps and globes to learn more about the world and people. And the next time someone asks where you are, you’ll have a great answer!

title: Mapping the News
text:
Have you ever heard or read a news report about a certain place and wondered where it is? Mapping the news can help. This is a fun way to learn geography and keep up with things that are going on in the world at the same time. Here’s how it works: Your teacher will put a world map on a bulletin board in your classroom or in the hall. Once a week, students can bring in news articles to share with the class. (Ask your parents to help you with that part, especially if you get your news articles from the internet. Also, do some research before you get to class to get a general idea of where the place is located.) In class, talk about each article and the place where the event happened. Find that place on the world map, and mark it with a push pin or a sticker.

For example, let’s say your friend brings an article about a mountain climber who reaches the top of Mount Everest on the border between Tibet and Nepal. She found out that those two countries are in south Asia. That will help you find Mount Everest more quickly.

Try mapping the news for several weeks. Then get into groups and make up a game that involves the places you mapped. Playing the game will help you remember what you learned. Have fun mapping the news!

title: Using Maps and Globes
text:
Maps

There are many different types of maps. Not all maps look alike. They look different because they are used for different reasons. Cartographers often start with two basic types of maps. Then they add other information. Many maps start as either a physical map or a political map.

Physical maps show what the land looks like. These maps show the borders of places. Borders are the outside edges of a place. Physical maps also show bodies of water and use different colors to show how the land looks.

Another type of map is the political map. This type of map shows countries and states and their capitals. Borders are clearly marked. Political maps also show major cities in the states and countries. Many political maps use different colors to show different places.

Even though there are different types of maps for many different purposes, most maps have a few things in common. Maps have a title, a map key, a compass rose and a scale. Many maps also include a grid.

Title

Maps have titles, just like books. The title of a map tells you the subject of the map. You can use the title of the map to help you decide if the map will give you the information you need. What type of information will you find in this map?

Map Key

The map key is an important part of the map. On most maps, the key is in a smaller box somewhere near the edge of the map. The key explains what symbols on the map stand for. Symbols are drawings or pictures on a map that stand for real things. Symbols can be colors, patterns, lines or special marks. They can stand for one thing on one map, but mean something else on another map. It is important for you to study the map key before you begin using any map. Look at the map key. Find the symbol for the national capital. Where is that symbol on the map?

Compass Rose

The compass rose is a small drawing on the map that will help you find directions. It usually shows the four main, or cardinal, directions - north, south, east and west. A compass rose can also help you find the directions that are between the cardinal directions. These directions are called the intermediate directions. They are northwest, southwest, northeast and southeast. Find the compass rose on the map to the left. What direction would you travel from the state capital of Texas to the national capital?

Map Scale

The map scale helps you compare distances on a map with real distances in the world. You can use a map scale to help you find how far it really is between places on a map. Look at the map scale on the map to the left. How many miles are shown by one unit of scale on the map?

Grid

To make it easier for you to find specific places on a map, cartographers sometimes add lines that cross each other in a pattern. This pattern of crossing lines is called a grid. The lines form boxes on the map. Each box is named by a letter and a number. Find the row and column for the area of Texas that contains your city. What box name (letter and number) best describes where you live?

Globes

Globes are models of Earth. You use a globe in much the same way you would use a map to find places on Earth. Globes show the North and South poles. The globe also shows the imaginary line that circles the Earth at its center. This line is called the equator. Texas is in the country of the United States. If your classroom has a globe, find our country on it.

title: Latitude and Longitude
text:
The Earth is a sphere. The top and bottom of the Earth are the North and South poles. On a map or globe, a grid line known as the equator is drawn exactly halfway between the poles. Grid lines are found on many maps. Any location on Earth can be described using these grid lines.

The equator is the starting point for measuring with lines of latitude. These lines are always drawn east to west around the Earth. They are always the same distance apart, and they never meet. Lines above the equator are labeled N for north latitude. Lines below the equator are labeled S for south latitude. The equator itself is labeled 0˚ or zero degrees. Each latitude line is labeled with a degree number. The larger the number, the farther north or south from the equator the line is.

There are also lines that run north and south on a map. These lines are called lines of longitude. Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole. Longitude lines meet at the poles. These lines get further apart at the equator. The line of longitude labeled 0˚ is called the prime meridian. Lines to the west of this line are labeled W for west longitude. Lines to the east of the prime meridian are labeled E for east longitude. These lines are numbered by degrees in the same way the lines of latitude are numbered.

You can use these grid lines to describe an exact location on a map. Find a location to describe. What lines intersect, or cross, closest to the location? Use the names of these lines to describe the location.

title: Christopher Columbus
text:
Christopher Columbus was an explorer from Italy who lived in the past. He explored the world more than 500 years ago. As a boy, Christopher was curious about the world. He asked many questions. He wanted to know what the world looked like. He studied maps. He likely thought the Earth is smaller than it actually is.

Christopher studied hard. He learned different languages. He learned how to sail a boat. He used the sun and stars to find his way. He studied many different maps and globes of the world. Christopher wanted to sail around the world. He wanted to trade goods.

Christopher asked the king and queen of Spain for help. After a long time, they gave him money and ships for his trip. During his journey Columbus confirmed that the world was a sphere. He also found land that people in Europe didn't even know existed. This land was North America.

Other explorers followed Columbus. Times began to change. People began communities on the new lands. They started trading goods.

title: What are hemispheres?
text:
Earth is a sphere. Hemi- is a prefix. It means half. So a hemisphere of the Earth is half of the Earth. Half of the Earth is above the equator. This is the northern hemisphere. Most of the Earth’s land and people are here. Half of the Earth is below the equator. This is the southern hemisphere. You can also divide the Earth in half along the prime meridian. The United States is in the western hemisphere. China and Russia are in the eastern hemisphere.

Earth is tilted. Because of this, seasons are opposite in the northern and southern hemispheres. While you’re celebrating winter in December, boys and girls who live in the sout!hern hemisphere are just beginning their summer vacation

title: Time Flies
text:
Have you ever heard the saying "time flies"? It means time is passing very quickly. We can measure time. Clocks measure seconds, minutes and hours. Calendars measure days, weeks, months and years.

Anything that has already happened is in the past. Anything that is happening now is the present. And anything that will happen - a minute from now or a thousand years from now - is the future.

Things that happened a very, very long time ago happened in ancient times. Things that happened more recently happened in modern times. An ancient event could have happened thousands of years ago. A modern event could have happened last week or hundreds of years ago. Sometimes people need to know more about when an event happened. Then we can use words like year, decade or century. In what year were you born?

Any way you say it, time always flies when you're having fun!
