title: Changes to Land Bring Changes for People
text:
Did you know that only one out of four parts of the Earth is land? It's hard to believe, but most of the Earth is covered by water! People live on the part that is land. Unless you live near a large body of water, it's easy to forget how much water is on our planet.

Not all the land looks the same. Land has many different shapes and sizes. This is because landforms cover the Earth. Landforms are natural features of the Earth's surface. Some landforms are large like mountains. Some landforms are small like hills. Bodies of water like oceans, lakes and rivers are landforms, too.

The way people live depends on the landforms near them. People build communities on or near landforms. The communities must sometimes adapt to the land. That means the people have to change the way they live. This is important for the community to survive.

The shape of the land can affect the climate of a community. Climate is the weather pattern of a place that happens over time. For example, communities near large bodies of water are usually cooler than other areas. People who live in desert areas have to find ways to keep cool in the desert heat. Landforms can also affect how much rain falls in a community.

People in communities grow some plants for food. They grow plants like trees for wood to build homes. The kinds of plants that grow in an area depend on the landforms there. Some plants grow best on flat areas of land known as prairies. Some plants grow well in the mountains. People have to know which plants grow best where they live. They must plant these kinds of plants so that the community will have food and shelter.

People need transportation to and from places. Cars, trains, boats and airplanes are types of transportation people can use. Some people use animals to get from place to place. Some people walk to get where they are going. Communities need transportation that works well with the landforms near them. If one type of transportation does not work well, the people must find another way to move about.

It is important for people to know how landforms change over time. People must also understand how communities change because of landforms. This issue of Texas Community Studies Weekly is packed with information. You'll learn why people choose to live in different places and how to use maps to find your place on the Earth.

title: Landforms of Texas
text:
Landforms are natural shapes that make up the Earth's surface. There are many types of landforms. They come in different shapes and sizes. Landforms are on the Earth's outer layer. This layer is called the crust. Most landforms take many years to form. Many of them were formed even hundreds of centuries ago.

What makes landforms? Most landforms were formed long ago by heat, pressure and movement in and on the Earth. Earthquakes and volcanoes can help create new landforms. These forces can also change the landforms already on the Earth. Earthquakes move and separate the Earth's crust. Volcanoes spill lava, which builds up to make new landforms.

Ice, water and wind can all change the Earth's surface. These things break down the materials of the Earth's crust. This weathering is a natural process that is always taking place. Weathering changes the land by loosening the Earth's surface. Sometimes these loosened surfaces move away. This is called erosion. Sometimes the parts that have moved away build up again in other places. Hills and mountains are made. Valleys are formed. Rivers can even seem smaller or disappear because of erosion.

Even though nature is usually responsible for changing landforms, people help too. Humans live on the land. Sometimes the land must be cleared, farmed or mined. Then people are also changing the way the land looks. People also try to find ways to protect landforms from the forces of nature.

Below are landforms you should be able to identify and describe.

1. Mountain - Mountains are the highest type of landform on Earth. They often rise up hundreds of meters above the Earth's surface. The highest mountain in the United States is Denali (formerly Mount McKinley) in Alaska. The highest mountain in Texas is Guadalupe Peak near El Paso.

2. Hill - Hills are landforms that rise slightly above the land around them. Hills are smaller than mountains.

3. Cliff - A cliff is high, steep land that is the face of a rock.

4. Mesa - A mesa is a mountain with a flat top. The sides of a mesa are usually very tall and steep.

5. Cave - A cave is a hole in the ground or in the side of a hill or mountain. Many animals make their homes in caves. Carlsbad Caverns in New Mexico are large room-size caves underground.

6. Delta - A delta is an area of land at the point where a river reaches an ocean. Deltas are areas where earth builds up into new land.

7. Canyon - A canyon is a deep, narrow valley with very tall steep sides. Canyons are usually landforms made by water movement. A large canyon in the United States is the Grand Canyon in Arizona.

8. Island - An island is land that is surrounded by water. The state of Hawaii is actually made up of islands.

9. Lake - A lake is a body of water with land on all sides. Lakes can be natural or made by people. Really large lakes are often called seas.

10. River - Rivers are large flowing bodies of water that move across the land. They can join up with other rivers or flow into the ocean or a sea.

11. Ocean - An ocean is a large body of salt water. There are five major oceans on Earth: Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean and Arctic Ocean.

12. Plain - A plain is a flat piece of land. The Great Plains Region of the United States covers most of the central part of the United States.

13. Valley - A valley is the low land between hills and mountains. Napa Valley is a large valley with communities in California.

title: Forever Changing
text:
The state of Texas is always changing. From someone building a house down the street to the opening of a new shopping center, our state is a growing place. As you ride in the car, you may have noticed trucks carrying lumber (wood). Where did all that wood come from? Why did someone cut down all those trees? We need wood to build homes and businesses. But cutting down trees changes the look of the land and often takes away many animals' homes.

Many people today are thinking of ways to improve the state of Texas while still protecting the Earth and its beauty. Many builders use earth-friendly materials and build on less land. Lumber companies plant new trees to replace the ones they cut down.

Do you recycle? Recycling is one way you can help improve the state of Texas. Did you know that landfills can recycle too? Some landfills in Texas now use gases from trash to produce heat, natural gas and electric power. So, the next time you throw away a piece of trash, remember - your trash might be someone else's energy! We need to balance getting the things we need with protecting the environment. That's a big job, but this is Texas. We can do it!

title: Land Affects Life
text:
People often can choose where they want to live. Sometimes they make their choices because of the land and what it has to offer. Some people choose to live on or near mountains. Here they are able to enjoy the fresh cool air, wildlife and a peaceful feeling. Other people choose to live near beaches, where it is warm and sunny. They enjoy fun water activities. People might even choose their community because it is good for their health. Dry desert air makes it easier for some people to breathe. Some people move closer to hospitals to get the medical treatment they need.

Even people’s houses are different because of the land. In desert areas, many houses are made of adobe. This is a mixture of clay and straw that helps the homes stay cool. People who live near oceans, rivers and wetlands often build houses on stilts high off the ground. This helps protect the home and people from floods. Houses in mountain areas usually have many windows so people can enjoy the sights and sounds of nature. Wherever you choose to live, there are homes that will fit your needs and fit with the area.

People often choose where they are going to live because of their jobs. Farmers want to live in an area where the soil is good and there is plenty of rain. Most farmers choose to live on a plain with flat fields. Many fishers want to live along the coast, where it is easiest to get to work. Some scientists choose to live near wetlands so that they can study the plants and animals that live there.

One great thing about Texas is that there are plenty of interesting places to live, work and play.

title: Scientists Believe Volcanoes Caused a ‘Little Ice Age’
text:
An ice age usually lasts thousands of years. But between 1300 and 1900 C.E., the northern hemisphere experienced a cooling called the “Little Ice Age.” The cooling was so intense that glaciers moved south, causing northern European towns to be destroyed. It was so cold that the Thames River in London and canals in the Netherlands froze! A scientist at the University of Colorado, using plant fossils from this period, may have discovered why this happened.

The plants died suddenly between 1275 and 1300 C.E. That’s exactly when many volcanoes erupted. Fifty years later, volcanoes erupted again. Billions of tiny particles from the eruptions were in the atmosphere, reflecting the sun’s heat away from the Earth. Fossils (remains of dead plants and animals) formed under the ice.

The growing ice cap sparked a feedback loop. A feedback loop causes something to happen over and over. First, the tiny particles stopped a lot of the sun’s heat from reaching land. This cooling caused the ice cap to grow. The ice reflected more of the sun’s heat back into the atmosphere. This caused more cooling. Finally, the glaciers became so large that they stopped the warmer ocean currents from melting the ice cap. Over centuries the glaciers grew to cover northern Europe.

Volcanic eruptions started the cooling, but it took the feedback loop to keep the “Little Ice Age” going for centuries!

title: Celebrate Your Freedom
text:
Each year on Sept. 17, citizens in the United States can celebrate the freedoms we have in our country. This day is known as Constitution Day and Citizenship Day. It is a time to think about our country and its past. It is also a time to celebrate the rights, or privileges, Americans have.

Long ago the country of England ruled America. England made all of the rules for people in America to follow. Americans didn’t get to help make decisions about these rules. The people wanted to have the chance to make their own laws.

Declaration of Independence, 1776

In 1776, a group of colonists decided to let England know they wanted the freedom to rule themselves in America. One of the men, a lawyer named Thomas Jefferson, wrote a special document for the people. In this paper, Jefferson wrote some very important information. The document was the Declaration of Independence. It stated that Americans believed people should be free and equal. It stated that Americans should have the right to make their own laws. The Declaration also stated that a good government should care for its people.

Once the Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776, the Americans had to fight for the rights in the document. For nearly eight years, the American Revolutionary War was fought in our country against the English. There were many battles, and many soldiers lost their lives. The Americans finally won. England agreed to let them govern, or rule, themselves.

The Constitution, 1789

Next, Americans had to develop a plan for the new government. The details of their plan were written in another important document, the Constitution of the United States. The Constitution was written at a special meeting called the Constitutional Convention. Fifty-five men attended the meeting. They were smart men from many different cities. They discussed the type of government the United States should have. They talked about how much power the government would have. They agreed that the people would be able to make decisions about the government. In the end, 39 of the men signed the document.

Two of the men who signed were George Washington and James Madison. Each later became president of the United States. Benjamin Franklin, who was 81 years old, was also there. Because of his health and age, he had to be carried around in his chair.

The U.S. government was designed to protect the freedoms of the people. The Constitution stated that the government would pass laws only if the people approved of those laws. The approval would come in the form of voting.

People vote to let the government know what to do. People in our country give the governments of the city, county, state and nation their approval by voting. The Constitution promises that Americans will have the right to vote.

Many people from other countries have studied the Constitution. Some of those countries set up their own government to be like ours.

The Bill of Rights, 1791

After the Constitution was written, there was still work to be done. Some of the leaders felt people needed to have their rights, or freedoms, written down even more clearly. They added the Bill of Rights to the Constitution.

The Bill of Rights was a list of 10 important freedoms Americans have. Some of the freedoms explained in the document include:

Freedom of religion - Americans can choose if and how they worship.

Freedom of speech - Americans have the right to speak many things, even if other people don’t agree with what they say.

Freedom of the press - Americans have the freedom to write and report about many things, even if their ideas are different from other people’s ideas.

Freedom to gather - Americans may get into groups to share their ideas.

Right to bear arms - Americans may own weapons to protect themselves.

The United States of America is a good place to live today because of all these important documents and the Founding Fathers — the men who helped write them.

title: People in Local Government
text:
People in Local Government

When the Founding Fathers planned the government of the United States, they gave the people many rights. This also means people have many responsibilities. People must work together to take care of their communities.

There are jobs to be done within your community. Your local government is in charge of many of the jobs. A local government is the government of a community. Some people keep you safe. Other people take care of the streets. Someone must make sure trash is carried away. Schools must educate students. The local government takes care of these and many more responsibilities.

Mayor

The head of a city is called the mayor. A mayor is chosen by the people of the community. The people elect the mayor by voting. Being a mayor is an important job.

Compare a mayor’s job to the principal’s job at your school. The principal makes sure that all students follow all the rules at your school. The mayor of a community makes sure all citizens obey the laws of the community.

The principal makes sure that teachers, secretaries, custodians and students in the school do their jobs. A mayor makes sure that all the community workers in every department do their jobs. The principal makes certain you receive your education, get hot lunches and have a safe, clean classroom. The mayor makes sure the fire department and police officers keep your community safe. The mayor also makes sure there is clean water in the community.

The principal listens to students, teachers and parents who have concerns or problems. The mayor listens to citizens with problems. The mayor must try to find ways to solve problems in the community.

City Council

The principal of a school has help running the school. The school board makes some decisions for the school. A mayor has help running a city too. The city council makes decisions and laws for the community. The city council is a group of leaders elected by the people of the community. They have meetings with the mayor to discuss the city’s needs and problems. If citizens in the community have a concern, they may meet with the city council to discuss it.

The city council also works with the mayor to find ways to pay for all the things a city needs. They meet with leaders of all the city’s departments. These leaders let the mayor and council know what needs to be done. Together they all make decisions that are best for the people of a community.

People in State Government

Each Texas community has leaders who help run the community. Texas also has leaders who help run the state. State government leaders make decisions for all the people of the state, not just one community. The government of a state is located in the state capital. Austin is the state capital of Texas. The state government leaders work in Austin.

Governor

The people of a state choose a person to lead the state government. This person is the governor. The governor serves in this position for four years. The governor helps make laws for the state and leads the military forces for the state. Deciding how the state makes and spends money is part of the governor’s job. The governor helps find people who serve in special jobs that help the state. Being a governor is a very important job.

Legislature

Just as the mayor gets help from the city council, a governor works with the state’s legislature. The legislature is a group of people elected by citizens to help make laws for the state. In Texas, the legislature has two parts, the Senate and the House of Representatives.

Responsibilities of Each Citizen

Every member of a community has rights. These rights are given to us by the U.S. Constitution. But all of us also have responsibilities as citizens of a community. Responsibilities are those things we must do to help our community.

The most important responsibility of a U.S. citizen is to vote. The country was set up so that every person’s vote has the same importance. When citizens vote, they are letting the government know what they think. They can help choose the people who will represent them in the government.

All citizens are expected to obey the laws and pay taxes to the government. It is also good for people to get involved in projects that help the community. Many citizens volunteer to help keep their communities clean or agree to work on project ideas for the community.

The responsibilities of U.S. citizens are a small price to pay for the rights and freedoms we enjoy.

title: Pierre L’Enfant — Changing a Community for All Time
text:
Who was responsible for planning how our national capital, Washington, D.C., would look? That man was Pierre L’Enfant, an engineer and designer from France. After going to art school, L’Enfant came to America to help our country win the war against England. He fought as part of General George Washington’s army.

After the war, Washington asked L’Enfant to design a city that would be the center of the nation’s government. Washington had picked the perfect spot along the Potomac River. Washington, D.C., would be near several states, but it would not be part of any of them. The nation’s capital would belong to the people of the United States of America.

L’Enfant planned the city after a lot of careful thought. He had a big vision for the city. Even though it was not a large community at that time, he knew it would be a very important city. He planned the streets very carefully. They were wide and easy to identify. He planned big parks for everyone to enjoy.

Unfortunately, L’Enfant didn’t get along with everyone on the project. He decided to leave. He did not get paid for the work he had done for a long time. Even though government leaders were very happy with his plans, they were not happy he had quit his job.

For many years, Pierre L’Enfant did not receive credit for the important work he had done planning the city of Washington, D.C. He died a very poor man in 1825. In 1909, L’Enfant was reburied in Arlington National Cemetery, near the city he designed. A monument in his honor was placed overlooking the Potomac River. From L’Enfant’s burial spot, visitors can admire the whole city.

title: What are taxes?
text:
Taxes are an amount of money that must be paid to the government. The money collected from taxes is used to run the government. People who work for the government must be paid. Taxes help pay for services like libraries, trash pickup and police and fire departments. Schools use tax money to buy books and supplies, keep the buildings in good repair and pay the teachers and staff.

There are many types of taxes. All people who earn money at a job must pay income tax. When we purchase items at a store, we pay sales tax. When citizens own a home or business, they must pay a property tax.

While it is never fun to pay a tax, it is the responsibility of all good citizens to do so.

title: How Do Good Citizens Solve Problems?
text:
Have you ever had a problem you needed to solve? Maybe you need to get a school project done with a group of classmates, or perhaps you and a friend can't decide what game to play together. Good citizens can use this process to help find solutions, or answers, to problems.

Identify the problem - What exactly needs to be done or solved?

Gather information - Get all the facts. Everyone should listen to each other's ideas.

Think about all the options - What are all the possible ways to solve the problems?

Consider each option - What are the good things and bad things about every possible solution?

Choose a solution - Once everyone agrees, go ahead and solve the problem.

Think about the results - Did the plan work? Will you use the same plan next time? What could you do differently next time?

Using a problem-solving process like this can help people solve problems without getting angry or frustrated. Give it a try!

title: The Founding of a Nation
text:
If you were going to start your own country, how would you do it? Would you decide that one person should make decisions for everyone? That is sometimes called a dictatorship. Or would you like to have a country like the United States, where the people vote for their leaders and everyone follows rules called laws?

When you found, or start, a country, you need rules or laws. The rules and laws are the foundation of the country. A foundation is something very strong to build on. The foundation of a house is often made of iron, steel and concrete. People build walls of brick, wood or plaster on top of the foundation to keep them safe. Without that foundation, a house would not last very long!

The United States has a foundation, just like a house. But our foundation is made of words instead of concrete and metal. It is called the Constitution. A constitution is not just a set of laws or rules. That would be good, but not very powerful. The thing that makes a constitution powerful is that every member of the country agrees to live by it. Writing a constitution can be a long and difficult process because people don’t always agree. Sometimes citizens have to compromise. To compromise means that everyone gets some of the things they want, but most people don’t get everything they want.

The Constitution of the United States was written over a long period of time at an event called a convention. (A convention is a series of meetings.) The Constitutional Convention was held in Philadelphia, from May through September of 1787. Fifty-five representatives from 12 of the new 13 states were there, even the man who would later be our first president, George Washington. When they were finished, they had written most of the laws that we still follow in our country today. The delegates (representatives) signed the document and laid the foundation for our great nation!

More than 200 years later, there are not just 13 states; there are 50. Before they could join the union of states, the people of those states had to agree to live by the laws of our Constitution. That is what makes our foundation strong!

title: Texas State Fair - Food, Farms and Fun!
text: Are you looking for a sample of the best that Texas has to offer? Maybe you’re hungry for a fried peanut butter and banana sandwich! Do you have a pet, recipe, plant or craft you want to show everyone? Well, look no further than the Texas State Fair! Every fall, the people of Texas hold a HUGE party on the grounds of the Dallas Fair Park. Farmers and ranchers bring their best produce and animals to show, hoping that they will be awarded a blue ribbon. The most delicious food you can imagine will make your mouth water as cooks compete for prizes. There are rides, games, concerts and so much to see that the fair lasts for 24 days. That’s more than three weeks! The fair is held in the fall of each year.

title: The Foundation of a Nation: Our Founding Fathers
text:
Building a new country is a lot of hard work! Thousands of citizens risked their lives fighting for American independence from England, and many more worked to support the soldiers in their fight. A small group of men are known as the Founding Fathers of the United States because they actually wrote or signed the Declaration of Independence or worked with representatives to write the Constitution. Later in their lives, they continued to make a difference!

Four of our Founding Fathers went on to become Presidents of the United States. Do the names George Washington, John Adams, Thomas Jefferson and James Madison sound familiar? Benjamin Franklin was never a president. But he was one of the most famous of our Founding Fathers because he made so many contributions to our daily lives. You can read more about him in the biography section of this magazine. Another Founding Father, Alexander Hamilton, was the first Secretary of the Treasury. He was an expert at managing money and helped our country grow. Can you find a picture of him on a piece of money? (Hint: Look on a $10 bill.) John Jay was a Founding Father who also became the very first Chief Justice of the United States. He felt very strongly about equal rights for all men. He worked hard to make slavery illegal in his state of New York. These men did their very best to create the right kind of government to make sure that citizens had the rights they deserved and to ensure the safety of us all. Let’s take a closer look at the government they built and helped to grow.

The United States has a system or structure of government that is very special. There are three separate sections called branches. These branches work together to make sure that everyone in the United States has an opportunity to be independent and free. Because the branches have to work together, no one person or group can ever have too much control or power. This is especially true because so many of our leaders have to be elected.

One branch is called the Legislative Branch. Legislation means law, and in our country, the laws are made by Congress. Members of Congress belong to two different groups. Representatives are elected by citizens of every state and are members of the House of Representatives. Senators belong to the group called the Senate. Members of Congress write, discuss and vote on the laws of the land.

Another branch of our government is called the Executive Branch. The leader of our country is the president, who works with Congress to approve the laws and to make sure that they are carried out for the citizens. The president is the head of our armed forces and is sometimes called the Commander in Chief. He also represents the United States in other parts of the world.

The third branch is called the Judicial Branch and is in charge of the court system in our country. The judges and courts interpret the Constitution and make sure that the laws are constitutional (agree with the Constitution). If they think that a law does not agree with the Constitution, they can send it back to Congress for review!

Checks and Balances

We have three government branches, and each one is just as powerful as the other. That means no branch can have too much power. This is the balance of power referred to in the article.

1. The legislative branch makes our laws.

2. The executive branch (president) enforces laws.

3. The judicial branch interprets and applies the law.

The balance of power is also known as checks and balances. As shown below, each branch has checks on the other two.

title: Founding Father: Ben Franklin 1706-1790
text:
Benjamin Franklin was born in 1706. That was over 300 years ago, but he is still one of the most famous Americans in history. The people of Philadelphia are especially fond of him, since that was his home for much of his life. Ben was a leader in our country’s struggle to be a free, independent country. He represented Pennsylvania at the Continental Congress and he signed the Declaration of Independence. After the United States was formed, he represented our country in France and England. He helped form friendships after a time of war and gave advice to our leaders at home.

Ben Franklin was also a writer, a scientist and an inventor. He liked to study the mysteries of life because he loved to investigate and try to solve them. He was always looking for a way to make life better for those around him. For example, Ben experimented with electricity and found ways to capture the energy of an electrical storm in a lightning rod. That made people safer in their homes. He also organized the first fire-fighting company in Philadelphia, started the first public library and published a newspaper called The Philadelphia Gazette. But that’s not all. In those days, it took two weeks for a letter to travel just 100 miles, but not after Franklin was in charge. He became the very first postmaster of Philadelphia, and he soon cut that time in half! Today we can send an email in seconds and a letter overnight. Do you think he would be surprised?

While he was helping make life easier for others, Ben Franklin was also taking care of himself. He believed in regular exercise for good health and was a strong swimmer his whole life! He read as many books as he could and practiced being a writer by studying the writing of others. Franklin lived 84 years and never stopped learning!

title: Truthfulness, Justice and Equality
text:
Have you ever wondered what it means to be a good citizen? In a country like the United States, where the people elect their leaders, good citizenship is a way of showing that you care about your country and your fellow citizens. One important way to show that you care about your country is to understand truthfulness, justice and equality. Your parents and teachers have probably talked to you about these wonderful qualities, but let’s review them.

Truthfulness means just what it sounds like. If you are a truthful person, it means that you are filled with truth! You are honest, you tell the truth all the time, and people can trust what you say and do. Good citizens trust each other to be honest and to tell the truth.

Justice is another important quality of good citizenship, because it means that you understand the difference between right and wrong behavior. In a country where citizens understand justice, there are consequences for inappropriate or unlawful behavior and rewards for appropriate behavior. Without justice, our country would be a messy, unsafe and unhappy place to live.

Equality is another important characteristic of good citizenship. Our Constitution guarantees that we are all equal under the law. It does not matter in which state we are born, or if we are boys or girls, or rich or poor. Citizens of the United States all have equal rights.

title: Who Pays For That?
text:
Have you ever stopped to wonder about who pays for things in our lives? Your family probably has a budget, a plan for how much money they can spend on things each month. For example, when your parents go to the store, they probably have a good idea about how much they can afford to spend on different things. They may have enough money in the budget for popcorn at the movies, but not popcorn and a box of candy for everyone. Some families might be able to afford a movie night once a month, while others might go to the movies more or less often. Your family pays for most of the things you need from their own bank account. But they also give money to the government each year, and the government uses that money to pay for many other services that we all use. The money we give the government is called a tax, and our elected officials use taxes to pay for things like the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines and Coast Guard. The government pays the salaries of people who keep us safe and also those who protect the environment. Have you ever been to Big Bend National Park in Big Bend, Texas? That park and many others just like it all over the United States are paid for by the taxes we send to the government. The government also pays for scientific research, like the spacecraft and satellites that explore outer space. Whether you are an astronaut for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration or a mail carrier for the U.S. Postal Service, the government pays your salary.

The government is in charge of more than two dozen different organizations or groups that are paid for with taxes from the citizens. The total budget for each year is measured in trillions of dollars!

title: Money Makes the World Go ’Round!
text:
If you’re like most kids, you’ve asked your parents to buy you things. Maybe you felt you needed an allowance. Perhaps you wanted a new tech toy or a cool pair of jeans. Maybe you just wanted to stop at a fast food restaurant on the way home from school. To buy things, you must use money. People in communities must work to earn money. They use the money to buy things they want and need.

People in communities need to earn money to pay for goods like food, clothes and a place to live. Goods are items people make or grow. Money is also used to pay for services people need. Services are things that can be done for people. Haircuts and lawn mowing are two examples of services some people pay for with money.

People can earn, or make, money by working at a business. There are many types of businesses. People can work for a business owned by someone else. People who work for someone else are called employees.

Many people operate their own businesses. Sometimes they work by themselves. Other times they pay people to work for them. If they hire workers, they are called employers.

Money received for work done is called income. The income people receive for their work is different for each job. There are some jobs that are hard to fill and some that require many years of education. The income for these jobs is usually higher than for some other jobs.

Besides earning and spending income, people can save some of their money. People can save money in banks. Saving money is a good idea. People save money for their children’s education. They take vacations with money they saved. Sometimes unexpected emergencies occur. Saving money helps people make sure they can take care of themselves no matter what happens.

Just like its citizens, communities must earn money to spend and save. In this issue, you will learn about ways communities and citizens use their money.

title: Help a Rat and Learn to Run the Country This Year!
text:
Hey, kids! I’m Revere the Rat, but you can call me Rev. I’m your online Studies Weekly friend, and I need your help. You can help me get great stuff by earning points while you learn. Just scan the code or go to www.studiesweekly.com and click on my picture.

Has your family ever bought something that came with an owner’s manual? Cars, TVs and other things have an owner’s manual, a book on how to use them. Your social studies class is the “owner’s manual” for the United States of America. You’ll learn about history, government by the people, geography and much more, so you can do a good job of running our country someday.

In America, rats can’t vote, so “you the people” govern (run) the country. Someday you will be in charge of this country, and you’ll choose leaders and representatives by voting. Then you can tell the representatives you help elect how you think the country should be run. In fact, Studies Weekly kids are so smart that many of you will someday be mayors, senators, governors — maybe even the president!

For now, you have two jobs: Learn about the country and how it works, and earn points for me so I can get that great stuff I told you about. It’s easy. Just scan or click, and you’re on your way!

title: Communities Care for their Citizens
text:
There are thousands of communities throughout the state of Texas. These communities come in all different sizes. There are many different people who live in them. One thing communities all have in common is that they try to find ways to take care of the safety and well being of their citizens. After all, that's why people form communities - they need security, laws and material well being. All communities want the people who live there to be safe, happy, productive and successful. Communities provide many services to their citizens. These services make the citizens' lives better.

Public Safety

All people want to live in a safe place. Communities provide services to keep citizens from harm. The police department helps fight crime. Police officers work to keep criminals off the community's streets. They patrol neighborhoods to make sure everyone is following the rules. They make sure drivers are obeying traffic laws. Most police departments work in schools to teach students how to stay away from drugs and crime. Citizens in a community can count on the police department to help them in any emergency.

The fire department responds to many emergencies. Members of a fire department are trained to fight fires. They can also help with medical problems. Just like the police department, firefighters risk their own lives to keep the citizens safe.

Paramedics usually work within the fire department. These specially trained men and women respond when people have a health emergency. They can offer first aid and treatment and take people to a hospital by ambulance.

Education

Communities provide citizens with ways to improve their education. Almost all communities have schools for children of all ages. Colleges and universities offer education for adults.

Libraries provide places for everyone to read, research, study and learn. Most community libraries also have computers for people to use. Citizens can check out books and other materials to take home to read and enjoy.

Some communities provide training programs for citizens to learn new skills. With the skills they learn, these people can work at jobs within the community. This helps the community, too.

Health

Many communities provide health care for citizens. Hospitals care for sick people. Many hospitals also have classes to help citizens learn how to take better care of their health. Ambulances get people who are very ill or who have been injured to the hospital quickly.

Some communities have public health services. These services help people who cannot afford medical care to get the help they need. Public health services also keep track of illnesses in the community and help teach citizens how to stay healthy.

Utilities

Clean water and trash pick-up are important to everyone. Communities provide both of these services. Utility departments in communities make sure that water is available at all times. Trash is picked up regularly.

Utility departments also make sure that roads and alleys are kept clean and safe. Street signs and lights are kept in working condition. When weather conditions cause wind or water damage, the utility department of a community helps clean up.

Transportation

Communities help citizens get from place to place safely. Roads have to be kept in good condition. Sometimes roads need to be repaired. Snow and ice must be removed from them after a storm. Communities have workers who help people get where they need to go.

Many communities provide transportation for citizens. Buses and shuttles provide a way for people to get from place to place at a very reasonable cost. Larger communities may have above ground and underground (subway) train service as well.

Where Does Money Come From?

People work to earn money. But where do communities get the money they need to provide the services citizens want? All communities receive money by asking their citizens to pay taxes. A tax is an amount of money paid to a government to be used for the good of its citizens.

Local, state and national governments ask their citizens to pay taxes to help pay for goods and services people in the community need. People pay many kinds of taxes. Some of the most common taxes are income taxes, property taxes and sales taxes.

Income Taxes

People and businesses earn income. A portion of all income is paid to the government as income tax. There are many different ways governments decide how much income tax people must pay. Paying income taxes is an important responsibility. It is against the law for a citizen to avoid paying taxes on an income.

Property Taxes

U.S. citizens have the right to buy and own property and land. Communities have a right to tax the value, or worth, of any property owned by its citizens. The amount of property tax charged in each community is different. The people and government leaders help decide a fair tax amount.

Sales Taxes

Communities have the right to charge a tax for certain goods and services purchased there. Sales tax is an additional amount people must pay when they buy something.

Citizens work hard for their income. Most people do not enjoy paying taxes. Good citizens know, however, that these taxes are necessary to the community. Without tax money, communities would not be able to provide the services people need.

Benjamin Franklin once said, "In this world, nothing is certain except death and taxes." You can be sure that as long as there are people living in communities there will be taxes to pay.

title: A Need for Communities
text:
Most of us live in a community. People form communities for many different reasons. One reason is that we can’t get everything we need and want on our own. We need each other! For example, when you go to the grocery store, where does all the food you buy come from? You depend on many people within your community for your food. A nearby farmer probably grows the oranges for the juice you drink. Truck drivers take it to stores. Cashiers work in the checkout lane so your family can buy the juice.

We also depend on our community to keep us safe. Each community has laws to help protect the people who live there. The police department makes sure people obey the laws. Without laws and the police, your community would not be protected. Police officers also teach students in the community how to stay safe. Have you thanked your local police department lately?

Long ago, the Pilgrims sailed to a new continent to find a place where they could worship freely. They formed a community in their new home. Living in a community allowed them to worship the way they wanted to. Today people in American communities are still free to practice their beliefs, even if they don’t have the same beliefs as you do. Respecting everyone’s beliefs is part of what makes America — and Texas — a great place to live.

title: What is a savings account?
text: A savings account is money that is kept in a bank or savings and loan company until you need it. Money can be placed, or deposited, in the account and taken out at any time. The money in a savings account is usually extra money you don't think you will need right away. While your money is in the savings account, the bank pays you interest. The bank pays you for keeping your money in the account, because you are actually lending the bank your money. The bank may use the money until you decide to withdraw (take out) money from the account.

title: Earning, Spending and Saving
text:
Below are different pictures that show people using money. Study the pictures carefully. Decide whether the people in the pictures are earning, saving or spending money.

• Circle pictures that show people earning money.

• Draw a box around pictures that show people saving money.

• Draw a line below pictures that show people spending money.

title: Where Does Money Go?
text:
Did you ever have a dollar to spend but couldn’t decide how to spend it? It is sometimes hard to decide how to spend money that you’ve worked hard to earn. But people do have to spend money. People must buy food, clothing and shelter. Most families also spend some money on health care, transportation and entertainment.

In the U.S., about $0.30 of every dollar made pays for housing. Food takes about $0.15. Americans spend about $0.05 of each dollar on clothes. Transportation costs $0.10, and paying off debts takes about $0.10 of each dollar. The rest of the dollar is spent on things like insurance, utilities and entertainment.

One thing is certain about spending. It’s a lot easier to spend money than it is to make it!

title: Community Heroes - Explorers
text:
American Indian Communities

American Indians were the first people who started communities in what is now the United States. The American Indians of each community spoke the same language. They lived in the same kind of homes. They cooked and ate their foods in the same way. They used things they found in nature for food, clothing and shelter. They lived off the land for thousands of years before explorers and settlers came from Europe.

European Communities

Christopher Columbus sailed to North America in 1492. That was more than 500 years ago. People from Europe began coming to North America. They wanted to build communities. They also hoped to find gold and other valuable things. Life in the new communities was hard. The people had to work very hard. Many people became sick and died. Some communities did not last very long. Others got help from the American Indians. The communities began to grow. More and more people came to America to build communities.

English Colonies

Most of the early communities were on the East Coast. Many were English colonies. The people in these colonies had to obey the king of England. Many of them didn't like England's taxes and laws. They wanted to be able to make their own rules and laws. The colonies fought a long war with England and became the United States of America.

More New Communities

After the war against England, the United States kept growing. People began finding new paths leading west. They explored the frontier. This was the wilderness area beyond the edge of the communities. We often call the first people to settle in an area pioneers. In 1803, the United States bought land from France. The land was called the Louisiana Territory. It was west of the Mississippi River. Many pioneers moved west to start new communities in the Louisiana Territory.

title: Blazing a Westward Trail
text:
New Leader, New Ideas

On March 4, 1801, Thomas Jefferson became the third president of the United States. Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence and helped America win freedom from England. Now Jefferson wanted to explore the land to the west.

In 1801, the United States didn't look like it does today. It was much smaller. The Mississippi River was the border on the west. Jefferson wondered what the land was like further west. Were the native people living there friendly? Did strange, giant animals live there? Would explorers find gold and other riches on the land? Jefferson really wanted to know.

Louisiana Purchase

People had already explored the Mississippi River. Farmers used the river to ship animals and goods. The river ended in New Orleans, which was owned by France. Jefferson asked France to sell New Orleans and all the land around it. In 1803, France did just that. They sold even more land than Jefferson asked for. This sale is called the Louisiana Purchase. The United States paid $15 million for the land, and it doubled the size of our country.

Explorers Wanted

President Jefferson needed someone to explore the land and look for a river route to the Pacific Ocean. He knew a man who would be perfect for the job. Meriwether Lewis worked for the Army. Lewis was smart and had experience exploring land. Jefferson sent for him and told him about the plans. Lewis said yes and started getting ready for the long journey.

Lewis spent hours talking with Jefferson about the plans. Then he went to the University of Pennsylvania to study animals, plants, rocks, minerals and medicine. He learned how to use the stars to find his way at night. He even helped build a boat for the journey. He chose another explorer to help him. William Clark, a childhood friend of Lewis, would go on the journey too.

Heading West

Lewis and Clark chose about 30 men to travel to the Pacific Ocean with them. They called their group the Corps of Discovery. All of the men had skills to help the explorers on their trip. There were soldiers, carpenters, blacksmiths and boatmen. Some of the men understood different American Indian languages. They took food, tools, medicine and weapons. They also brought along beads, ribbons, mirrors and kettles to use as gifts for American Indian groups they met.

In May 1804, Lewis and Clark and their men headed west from St. Charles, Missouri. They had no maps to help guide them. They followed the Missouri River. Lewis and Clark wrote in their journals every day. They made maps of the land as they traveled. They wrote about and drew pictures of 122 plants and animals that no one back east had ever seen. The group saw buffalo and grizzly bears for the first time.

Home at Last

The Corps of Discovery traveled for two years, four months and 10 days. They made it all the way to the Pacific Ocean before heading home. The journey covered almost 8,000 miles. Lewis and Clark shared their journals and maps. Other people could now head west and start new communities.

title: Daniel Boone
text:
Daniel Boone was a famous explorer who lived about 200 years ago. He helped settle land in what is now Kentucky. Even though he is famous now, his life started out just like most boys of that time.

Daniel's family was large. He had 10 brothers and sisters. His parents, Sarah and Squire Boone, worked very hard as pioneers in Pennsylvania. Daniel liked to spend his time outside. He loved to hunt in the woods. He could hunt with just a sharp stick. When he was 12, he learned to hunt with a rifle. Daniel learned to read and write, but he liked the woods better than school. When Daniel's family moved to North Carolina a few years later, he earned a living hunting and selling furs. Later, Daniel married and had 10 children. He hunted and farmed to take care of his family.

One day Daniel went on a long hunting trip. He saw Kentucky for the first time. He explored the land with some of his friends. They followed American Indian trails. In 1773, Daniel decided to bring his family to Kentucky to live. On the way, the family was attacked by a group of American Indians. One of Daniel's sons was killed. A very sad Boone family went back to North Carolina.

Daniel went to work helping to build a road to Kentucky. It became known as the Wilderness Road. The road made it possible for people to move to and settle in Kentucky.

Daniel helped build one of the first communities in Kentucky, too. Many people came to live in Boonesborough. Over time, the Kentucky wilderness got too crowded for Daniel and his family. They moved further west to the Missouri frontier.

Daniel Boone was a man who loved and respected the wilderness. His work creating roads and building communities helped the United States grow. Daniel Boone is a true American hero.

title: Clarity of Expression: Henry Hudson
text:
Henry Hudson was an English sea captain and explorer who started off as a failure. He sailed on two voyages for England to find a northeast water route to the rich spice trade in Asia. But both times the icy northern seas blocked his way. He had to return home defeated.

Sounds like the end of his career, right? It wasn’t. Hudson next convinced the Dutch East India Company to hire him for exactly the same expedition. In 1609, Hudson and his crew sailed west across the Atlantic. He reached the New World, landing on the island we know today as Manhattan. He sailed inland up a wide river and explored the surrounding valley.

It wasn't a passage to Asia. But Hudson's explorations allowed the Dutch to claim the land and build a fur trading post there in 1614, before the Pilgrims arrived. A Dutch settlement called New Netherland soon followed.

Unfortunately, Hudson's last voyage ended in mutiny. He refused his crew's demands to return home, so the sailors took over the ship, setting Hudson adrift in a small boat. His fate is unknown, but his legacy is Hudson Bay, Hudson River, Hudson Valley and the Dutch settlement that became New York City.

Henry Hudson must have had excellent clarity of expression. He had to be able to explain clearly to the Dutch that his experience and determination made him the best man for the job, even though he was an Englishman and not a Dutchman.

Think about a time that you wanted to convince your parents or teachers to let you try something new. Did you beg and plead? Or did you give them a clear explanation of your reasons? Which way do you think works better?

title: What is bartering?
text: Have you ever traded the tuna sandwich in your lunch for a PBJ? That's called bartering. Bartering is trading one good or service for another without using money. In early communities, many people had little or no money. They traded things they had for things they needed. For example, a family with several cows might trade one cow to a family who had plenty of corn. The first family got corn to eat. The second family got a new cow and had milk to drink. Both families got something they needed without paying money for it. Everyone was happy.

title: Sacagawea
text:
Lewis and Clark might never have been able to explore the West if it hadn't been for a Shoshone woman. Sacagawea was kidnapped when she was just a little girl. She was sold to a fur trader, and she later became his wife. Lewis and Clark met Sacagawea and her husband when they camped for the winter in North Dakota. She had a baby boy at camp and brought him along for the rest of the journey.

Sacagawea knew the land around her very well. She understood the languages of the American Indians in the area. Sacagawea spoke with American Indians about bartering for horses and supplies the group needed. Sacagawea was a brave young woman. She helped blaze a trail for many people who moved to the West in the 1800s.

title: Understanding Timelines
text:
You have read about many events that took place in the past. Sometimes all the dates can be confusing. A timeline can help you. A timeline tells the order in which events happened. The events are written from left to right on the timeline. An event on the left happened before an event on the right.

Directions: Use the information in the chart to fill in the timeline below with key dates from the Lewis and Clark Journey.

title: Let's Write
text: Lewis and Clark kept journals on their trip. Pretend you are one of the explorers. Create a journal entry. Write about a day you discovered a new animal. Describe the animal and how it acts. Explain where you found the animal. Write about why your discovery is important to people who follow your trails. Draw a picture of the animal to go with your writing.

title: Every Little Bit Helps
text:
The sun was beating down on Gaby's head. Drops of sweat trickled down her forehead. It was the hottest day of the summer so far. Most of her friends were spending the day at the swimming pool. Her best friend, Emanuel, had called that morning. He wanted her to go to the movies with him in the afternoon. Gaby had to tell him no, but she didn't mind. She had important things to do. Gaby was helping her parents build a house.

The house wasn’t for Gaby’s family. The house was for a family who didn’t have a safe place to live. In fact, Gaby didn’t really know the family who would live there. She had seen the young mother and three children who would one day call the house a home. Yesterday evening, they were there with Gaby’s family, painting yellow trim around the windows.

For the last week, Gaby's parents had helped at the house each evening after work. They had hammered, sawed, drilled and painted. Gaby's parents were not getting paid for their work. They were volunteering their time to help someone else. Gaby's mom said it made her feel good to know she was helping someone in the community.

Gaby was too young to work with tools, but she was really good at bringing lemonade to the volunteers when they needed a break. She liked pulling around the wagon and pouring the ice cold drinks. Everyone always said a big thank you. Helping people made her feel good, too.

Soon the house would be finished. The mother and her children would have a beautiful, safe home. Gaby and her parents would have the happy memory that they were able to give such a wonderful gift to someone. All the volunteers were glad they could help make their community a great place to live.

title: Building Homes, Changing Lives
text:
Since 1976, Habitat for Humanity International has helped build more than 600,000 homes for people who did not have a place to live. Millard and Linda Fuller started the group. No one who works on the homes gets paid. People volunteer, or donate their time, to help others.

Many different people work on the homes. They come from different backgrounds. They speak different languages. They belong to different religions. But they all have one thing in common. They want to help other people.

More than one million people now live in homes they helped build with Habitat for Humanity. The group has built homes in nearly 100 different countries around the world. They are very busy. A new Habitat for Humanity home is completed somewhere in the world every 24 minutes!

There are lots of different ways people can help Habitat for Humanity. Of course, many people volunteer to help build the houses. But other people donate money or building materials, like wood or paint. Some people travel all over the world to build homes. There are probably people in your own community right now who are working with Habitat for Humanity to help people change their lives.

title: Good Citizens
text:
Being a good citizen in your community involves many things. It means caring about where you live. It means believing that all people in the community should be treated fairly. Being a good citizen also means telling the truth. What else makes a good citizen?

The Common Good

What do you do at school when you see litter on the playground? Do you pick it up and put it in the trash can? If so, then you are acting for the common good. That means you are doing things that are good for everyone. Picking up trash keeps the playground clean. That makes it a nicer place for everyone in the school to enjoy. There are many other things you can do for the common good of your school and community. Good citizens find many ways to make the community a better place to live.

Obey Laws

Why are there rules in your school? Rules help to make sure everyone is safe and has a chance to learn. Communities have rules, too. These rules are called laws. Everyone in a community must obey the laws. They help keep people safe, just like the rules in your school. When people do not obey laws, there are consequences. Wearing a seat belt in the car is one law citizens must obey. People driving cars must obey traffic laws. They cannot drive too fast, and they must stop at stop signs and red lights. There are special laws for bicycles. These laws help keep drivers, bicycle riders and pedestrians (people who are walking) safe. A person who doesn’t obey these laws may get a ticket and a fine. A fine is money you pay as a punishment for breaking a law.

Vote

Citizens who care about their communities must vote. Voting gives people a chance to choose their leaders and make their voices heard. It is a right and a responsibility. Voters have the responsibility to learn about issues they are voting for. If you don't have all the facts, you may find out later that you voted for something you didn't want. In some countries, people are not allowed to vote. Americans are lucky to have a voice in our government!

Keeping Promises

Most elected leaders must take an oath of office before they start their jobs. An oath of office is a promise leaders make to do the best job they can and uphold the laws. Elected leaders who do not keep their word may be removed from office.

Serving on a Jury

One important job American citizens have is to serve on a jury. A jury is a group of people who makes decisions about court cases. If you are chosen to be on a jury, you and the other jury members are responsible for making decisions that are fair and equal. To serve on a jury, you must be at least 18 years old and be able to read and write.

Volunteer

Good citizens who want to give something back to the community can volunteer, or donate their time, to help others. Many people volunteer because they want to help others in need. There are many ways you can volunteer in your community. Food banks collect canned goods or deliver food to people in need. Other programs teach people to read. Some volunteers even build homes for people. The list of volunteer jobs is very long. If you want to give back to your community, talk to your parents about where you could volunteer. Someone will really appreciate your help!

title: The President of the United States
text:
Every four years in America, an exciting event takes place. The people vote for a leader. The President of the United States has the important job of making decisions for our country. Of course, not everyone always agrees with those decisions. But the president tries to do what’s best for the common good of all people.

What does it take to become president of the United States? Do you have to be rich? Do you need a college degree? Believe it or not, the Constitution lists only three requirements for being the president. You must be at least 35 years old. You must have been born in the United States. And you must have lived in the United States for at least 14 years. In 1951, the people voted to change one thing about being president. Now, a person may only be elected president two times.

Many U.S. presidents were once lawyers, but many had other jobs, too. George Washington was a farmer and a general in the Army. Lyndon Johnson was once a teacher. Ronald Reagan was an actor. George W. Bush worked in the oil business and owned a professional baseball team.

The office of President of the United States has been held by some pretty ordinary citizens who wanted to make the country a better place to live. That seems to be the most important requirement of all.

Presidential Facts

Oldest person ever elected: Donald J. Trump, age 78

Youngest person ever elected: John F. Kennedy, age 43

President who served the longest time in office: Franklin D. Roosevelt, 12 years (1933-1945)

President who served the shortest time in office: William Henry Harrison, 31 days (March 4 - April 4, 1841)

Only person to serve two terms not in a row: Grover Cleveland, 1885-1889 and 1893-1897

First president to live in the White House: John Adams

Want to know more about our presidents? The library has lots of books you’ll enjoy, or you can ask your parents or teacher for permission to search the internet.

title: Harriet the Brave
text:
In 1820, a little girl was born in Maryland. Her name was Araminta, but everyone called her Minty. Minty and her family were enslaved. They had no rights or freedoms. Minty didn’t think this was fair.

Minty and her family lived and worked on a plantation, a large farm. They had to work very hard. Even though Minty was only seven years old, she had to cook, clean, make cloth, pick cotton and trap animals. She wasn’t allowed to go to school. When she made a mistake, she was punished very severely.

After Minty got married, she changed her name to Harriet. Harriet was her mother’s name, too. One time she saw one of the other enslaved people trying to run away. The man was caught, but this gave her the idea that someday she could run away, too.

Harriet heard people talk about the Underground Railroad. This wasn’t a real railroad with trains and tracks. It was a name for a group of people who worked together to help enslaved people get to states where they would be free. The people who worked on the Underground Railroad knew slavery was wrong.

Harriet’s husband, John Tubman, didn’t want her to run away. She had to leave secretly. She stayed with people along the Underground Railroad. Finally, she reached Pennsylvania and freedom!

Harriet was happy to be free. She wanted to help others be free, too. Harriet went back to get her family. Then, she went back 18 more times to help people escape from slavery. For the rest of her life, Harriet Tubman continued to help people. She started schools for people who used to be enslaved. She helped them find homes, food and jobs. Harriet Tubman was a brave woman and a real American hero.

title: What is a nonprofit group?
text: Many groups work for the common good of the people in their communities and in the world. A nonprofit group helps others without making a profit. A profit is money left over after a business pays all of its expenses. Nonprofit groups use money donated by caring people to help others who are in need. In the United States, they do not have to pay taxes, like most businesses do. There are more than one million nonprofit groups in our country. These groups include the YMCA, the American Red Cross and the Salvation Army. Many churches, schools and hospitals are nonprofit groups, too. Can you name some nonprofit groups in your community?

title: The American Red Cross
text:
In 1881, a nurse named Clara Barton started a group that helps people when terrible things like fires and natural disasters happen. She called the group the American Red Cross. It is a nonprofit group.

The Red Cross helps during natural disasters all over the world. Hurricanes, floods, earthquakes and tornadoes can destroy homes. People can be injured. The Red Cross provides shelter, food and medical care to people who are hurt or have lost their homes.

The American Red Cross also helps people get ready for emergencies before they happen. Red Cross workers give lessons in first aid and water safety. You may know someone who has given blood to help save lives. Red Cross workers volunteer in many areas in the community. Even kids can volunteer for the American Red Cross.

title: Cause and Effect
text:
Some events are connected. One event makes another event happen. The first event is called a cause. What happens next is called the effect. Read the story below:

Tyler rides his bike to school each day. One morning, he notices the bike has a flat tire. Tyler hurries to the bus stop and rides the bus to school.

In this situation, the cause is the flat tire on Tyler’s bike. The effect is that Tyler has to ride the bus to school.

Directions
Use the information and ideas from the articles in this week’s paper to fill in the cause-and-effect chart below. Write your ideas in complete sentences. The first one has been done for you.

title: Let's Write
text: Pretend you are Harriet Tubman. Write a letter to the editor of a Pennsylvania newspaper from Harriet’s point of view. Tell why you think slavery is not fair. Talk about how people can join the Underground Railroad. Write your ideas in complete sentences. Be sure to use capital letters and punctuation marks correctly. Check your spelling and grammar carefully in your final draft.

title: Looking Back: Geography, Communities and Government
text:
Modeling Earth

Maps are flat models of Earth and its features. Globes are models too, but they are spheres. People use different types of maps and globes to find all kinds of information about the world.

Physical maps show what the land looks like. These maps show borders of places and bodies of water. Different colors on these maps show how the land looks. Political maps show countries, states, capitals and large cities. Borders are clearly marked, and different colors are used to show different places.

There are different maps for different purposes. However, most maps have things in common. Maps have a title, key, compass rose and a scale. Some maps also have a grid.

The title of a map tells you the subject of the map. The title helps you know if the map will give you the information you need. A key explains what the symbols on the map mean. The key is usually in a separate box on the map. The compass rose is a drawing on the map that shows cardinal directions (north, south, east and west) and intermediate directions (northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest). A map scale helps you compare distances on the map with real-world distances. Many maps have lines that cross in a grid pattern. These lines make it easier to find exact locations on the map.

Being able to understand your location in the world and your distance from other places is an important skill. Learning how to use a map will also help you get to a certain place easier.

Our Changing Land

Three-fourths of the Earth is covered by water. The rest of the land is in many different shapes and sizes. Landforms are natural shapes, such as mountains, hills, oceans, lakes and rivers, that make up the land’s surface, or crust. Heat, pressure and movement in and on Earth formed most landforms thousands of years ago. Other forces change the way the Earth’s surface looks. Earthquakes and volcanoes can create new landforms. Earthquakes move and separate the Earth’s crust. Volcanoes shoot out lava, which builds up and makes new land. Ice, water and wind can break down and carry land away.

Nature usually changes landforms, but people also affect Earth. People build communities on or near landforms. They often clear land for homes or for farming. People also mine land for resources such as coal and oil. Communities even build transportation systems that work well with the landforms in the area.

The shape of the land affects the climate of a community. Communities near bodies of water stay cooler than those in deserts. Plants grown in a community for food and shelter depend on the landforms there. Some plants grow well on flat grasslands. Others do best in the high elevation of mountains. Communities change because of landforms, and people must learn ways to protect the Earth.

Freedom’s Rewards

Americans are free and have equal rights. We have the freedom to vote in elections. Here we vote to approve or disapprove of laws and the people who lead our government. Each year on Constitution Day (September 17), we celebrate the freedoms we have in our country. It is the perfect time to think about three very important historical documents.

Our nation’s leaders wrote the Declaration of Independence in 1776. It explains the rights people in our country think are important. It says people should be able to make their own laws. It also says the government should take care of its people. The U.S. Constitution is a written plan for government. It explains just how the government should be organized. It also tells how people of the United States can approve of all laws the government passed. This document promises that Americans will have the right to vote.

Many of America’s leaders wanted the people’s freedoms written down even more clearly. So, they added the Bill of Rights to the Constitution. This list of 10 freedoms Americans have is very important. It includes the freedoms of religion, speech and the press. Americans also have the freedom to gather together and the right to own weapons.

These three important documents help make the United States a good place to call home.

title: Money Matters
text:
Earn, Spend, Save, Donate

Third graders don't have jobs yet. However, most of you understand how important money is. People need money to buy things they want and need. You use money to buy goods. Goods are things made or grown, like clothes and food. Money can also pay for services, or things done for people. A doctor's visit and a car wash are examples of services.

Most adults earn an income (money received for doing a job) by working as employees. They work for other people who are called employers. Entrepreneurs own their own businesses and work for themselves. People who earn an income often make a budget. This means they plan how they are going to spend the money they make. It is also a good idea to save some money. People save for education, vacations, retirement or emergencies. Many people include donations as a part of their budget. Donations include money that is given away to help others. This money supports charities such as the American Red Cross. Earned, spent, saved or donated ... money is important for many people.

It Costs Communities to Care

Just like families, communities also need money. They must provide services the citizens want and need. All communities want the people who live there to be safe, productive and successful. Where do communities get the money they need? They pay for services with money collected from citizens. This money is called taxes.

Local, state and national governments ask their citizens to pay taxes. There are many kinds of taxes. The most common are income taxes, property taxes and sales taxes. Income taxes are a portion of all earned income that is paid to the government. A citizen who does not pay income tax is breaking the law. U.S. citizens have the right to buy and own property and land. Communities may tax the value, or worth, of this property. The amount of property tax charged in each community is different. Leaders try to decide on a fair tax amount. Communities also have the right to charge a tax for certain goods and services. This is called sales tax. People work hard for their income. Most people do not enjoy paying taxes. Good citizens know, though, that it is their responsibility to pay taxes.

Community Services

Local, state and national governments use tax income to provide services for their citizens. People form communities to have safety, security and laws. The services that are provided to people help them live better lives.

Feeling safe is very important for most people. Communities provide services to make sure the public's safety is protected. Police departments fight crime. Police officers help keep criminals out of the community. They make sure all citizens are following the laws. They visit schools to help students understand the dangers of drugs and crime. Fire departments respond to many emergencies. Firefighters battle fires and help with medical problems. Paramedics in the fire department help citizens who have health emergencies. They are trained to give first aid and help sick or injured people get to a hospital quickly. Men and women who work in public safety often put their own lives at risk to keep citizens safe.

Tax money also pays for education and health care in communities. These are two areas that are important to people. Citizens can attend public schools, colleges and universities. They can go to community libraries to read, research, study and learn. People can check out books and other materials to take home to enjoy. People who receive a good education usually get better jobs. Hospitals care for sick people in the community. Tax dollars pay for public health services that teach citizens how to stay healthy.

Communities also provide utility and transportation services to its citizens. Clean water is available to people 24 hours a day. Trash collectors pick up trash. These services are necessary to keep the people in the community safe and healthy. Utility departments keep the roads and alleys clean and repaired. They work on street signs and lights. They help people when bad weather causes wind or water damage. Communities also provide busses for people to use to get from place to place cheaply. Larger cities might even have a train service above ground or a subway service underground.

title: Local and State Leaders
text:
People have a responsibility to make their communities and states safe and successful. They vote, pay taxes and follow laws. There are jobs that also must be done. In Texas, many of these jobs are taken care of by the local and state governments. A mayor leads a local government. A governor leads each state. These leaders help make sure people follow laws. Mayors and governors also work to make sure government money is spent well.

Mayors work with city councils to make laws, solve community problems and find ways to pay for things a city needs. The people elect city council members. The people also elect the members of the state legislature. The legislature helps make the laws of the state.

title: Historical Heroes
text:
The United States was able to grow with the help of many important people. These men and women are historical heroes.

People from Europe followed explorer Christopher Columbus to North America after his voyage in 1492. They built communities and searched for gold and other riches. The work was hard, and not all of the communities survived.

Our Founding Fathers were from England. They wanted to establish communities where they could make their own laws and rules. These men fought many battles to form the United States of America.

One pioneer explorer who helped the country grow was Daniel Boone. He helped settle land that is now Kentucky. He worked to build roads and many new communities.

title: What makes a person a 'good citizen'?
text:
Good citizens care about where they live. They believe all people should be treated fairly. Being a good citizen also means that you tell the truth. There are many other characteristics of a good citizen.

People who find ways to make their communities better for everyone are good citizens. People who want to be elected leaders fit this category. They must keep their promises and follow the laws that keep people safe.

All Americans are being good citizens when they vote or serve on a jury. People can also volunteer their time or money to help others. Being a good citizen begins when you are young. You can start right now at home, school and in your community.

title: Past and Present Good Citizens
text:
Good citizens help others. Police officers, firefighters, paramedics and those in the military have qualities we respect every day.

Many people in history were good citizens. During the Civil War, Clara Barton made sure that soldiers had food, water, clothing and medical care. Her work led to the creation of the American Red Cross.

You will learn about Helen Keller. She could not see or hear, but she tried to make other people's lives better. She helped form community libraries.

Another example is Ruby Bridges. She was the first African American child to attend an all-white school in the south in the 1950s. Ruby was respectful and kind even when other people were not treating her nicely.

Who can you look up to as good citizens in your school or community?
