title: Education Then and Now
text:
This story is historical fiction. The characters are made up, but what they do is what real school children did in 1923 and do today.

Deaver Creek Schoolhouse - 1923

“Did you remember to feed the chickens? And don’t forget the stick of wood!” I heard Mama call from the kitchen as I headed out the door. Quickly, I ran to the firewood stack and picked up a piece of wood. My teacher, Miss Bebb, expected students to bring a stick of wood each morning. Without wood to burn in the big stove, the classroom would sure be cold.

The walk to school today would not be an easy one. Flakes of snow drifted gently down. It was pretty enough now, but it would be cold and slushy this afternoon. I put my hands in my pockets. The sweet potato Mama baked for my lunch was still warm.

I couldn’t wait to get to school today. Every Friday after recess, all 30 of us kids would have a spelling bee. I really wanted to win, but I knew I might not be a match for Agnes. She was one of the older girls. She often helped the first and second graders with reading lessons in their primers. Miss Bebb even said Agnes would take the teacher’s test next month. Then she could be a teacher, too.

As I entered the one-room building, I noticed my desk partner, Sarah, was already at work. Sarah was a first grader. She was practicing her letters and numbers on a little chalk tablet in her lap. Since I was already a third grader, I had to help if she needed it. Today she was doing fine, so I started answering the history questions Miss Bebb put on the board.

I wrote answers on my tablet for Albert Jenkins, a sixth grader, to check. Then it was time to stand in front of the class and recite my multiplication facts. I had been studying hard since last week, when Miss Bebb frowned at me for stumbling over my four facts. Today I got them all right. Miss Bebb said as a reward I could take the erasers outside and beat the chalk dust out of them. Today was a great day at school.

Deaver Creek Elementary School - Today

“Hurry up, or you’ll miss the bus!” Mom called as she packed her briefcase. “Don’t forget to take your flash drive. Mr. Ramsey is going to have each student save a history research project on it,” she added.

I grabbed my backpack and my lunch card and hurried out the door.

The bus ride to school seemed fast. Maybe it was because I was excited. Today was the day of the Science Fair. I was sure my project would win. I had spent hours on the internet in the media center researching how plants grow. Then I grew my own plants in the science lab. Mrs. Dalton, the science specialist, said my idea was very original. She even asked what computer program I used to make the graph on my project board!

In the classroom, I joined the rest of my group, and we practiced our multiplication facts using flash cards and a very cool website. Then we read our social studies magazine and finished a project about endangered animals in Texas. Mr. Ramsey worked with our group to make a cause-and-effect chart.

During PE, Coach Carrasco said we were going to start a new fitness unit. Each student would get a special dance pad. Then a computer would show dance moves on the big-screen monitor. We could all dance along. It was a fun way to exercise.

After that, our class went to the computer lab. We used the internet to talk to a family sailing around the world. The webcast was very interesting. We each got to use the computer microphone to ask a question about the family’s travels. I couldn’t believe I was talking to someone so far away. Finally, it was time to go to the Science Fair. Even if I didn’t win the top prize, this was still a great day at school.

title: History of Education
text:
Have you ever wondered what schools were like long ago? Step into our time machine, and let's go back about 2,400 years to see what education was like at the time...

Ancient Schools

In the ancient communities of Greece and Rome, many men enjoyed being teachers and sharing their ideas. They gave speeches to people in the community. In some communities, the sons of wealthy families went to school in the temple. Some families hired their own teachers. Many boys learned a trade. They could then make a living using their new skills. Back then, girls were usually not allowed to go to school. They learned how to take care of a home and family instead.

American Indians who lived in North America in ancient times taught their children by telling stories. Storytelling was an important way to answer children’s questions about the world around them. They used stories to teach children how to behave. Boys also learned to hunt, and girls learned to gather or grow food.

Now let's travel to the 1600s when our country was just beginning...

Early American Schools

The Pilgrims came to America from England in 1620. They believed children should be educated. But different children got different kinds of educations. There were schools for children of wealthy families. These children often studied history, math and Latin. Some schools were only for girls. They learned to read, write and take care of a home. Some schools were not what we would think of as schools at all. Many young people went to work with adults who taught them a skill. They learned trades like candle making, blacksmithing and leather tanning. For many poor or enslaved children, there was no school at all.

First Public School

The first public school in America opened on April 23, 1635, in Boston, Massachusetts. The city used some of its money to pay for the school. Reverend John Cotton started the Boston school. He wanted the city to have a school like the ones in England. Philemon Pormort was the first teacher. Classes were held in the teacher’s house for many years. He taught them many subjects, even Greek and Latin. Today, students can still attend Boston Latin School. They can study in the same rooms where many famous people went to school. Samuel Adams, Benjamin Franklin and John Hancock were all students there.

Back to the time machine! This time, set the dial for 1852. Why then? Keep reading ...

More Schools

Over time, people in communities began to realize how important schools were. Many cities and towns began building schools. In 1852, Massachusetts was the first state to pass a law that required children to attend school. Other states passed laws like that, too. There were still many different types of schools, but more and more children were getting an education.

One more trip in our Studies Weekly time machine will bring us home...

Schools Today

Today, every child in America has to go to school. It is the law. Students and parents have many choices. Most schools offer exciting ways for students to learn. Of course, you study reading, writing and math. But many students can also study different languages, music, art, dance and computer science. There are all kinds of clubs and activities to join. Students may play on sports teams. Schools help students learn to be good citizens of the community. Some families teach their children at home. They have to work very hard and pass the same tests as students who go to a school building to learn.

title: Is Education a Right?
text:
The Constitution of the United States lists the rights of each citizen. But does the Constitution promise us the right to an education? A few weeks ago, you learned about the Bill of Rights. They are the first 10 amendments to the Constitution. The right to an education is not listed in those rights. But the 10th Amendment gives states a lot of power.

The 10th Amendment says that each state is responsible for any power the Constitution does not give to the national government. That includes education. Each state is responsible for its own schools.

In most states, this means that public schools are paid for with taxes. Schools need money for buildings, supplies and equipment. They also need money to pay the people who work in the schools.

In Texas, each school gets money from the state. Each school gets a different amount of money. That's because the money each school gets depends on how many students come to school each day. This is just one of the reasons it is important not to miss school. Even though the state gives the schools money, they do not make all the decisions about how the school should be run.

Each public school is part of a district. A school board leads each district. Citizens vote for the people on the school board. People who live and work in the community may be on the board. People who want to be on the school board care about the children of the community. They help make decisions about how to make sure all students get a good education.

People in communities work together so you and your friends have good teachers and everything you need to learn. All children in the United States have a right to an education. You cannot be kept away from school because of your race, your religion or your physical differences. But you also have a responsibility to do your best in school. Someday, you may be a leader in your community. And the children in your community will be counting on you.

title: An Amazing Student and An Amazing Teacher
text:
Can you imagine a student who grew up to write books, give speeches all over the world, and meet 12 U.S. presidents? Now, imagine that the student could not hear or see. That student was a real person. She was an amazing woman named Helen Keller.

Keller was born in Alabama in 1880. Before she was two years old, she became very sick. The illness left her deaf and blind. Learning was very hard for her. She couldn’t communicate with people. She did not understand basic rules or lessons. Her parents knew they needed help.

The family heard about the Perkins School for the Blind. They wrote to the school and asked them to send a teacher for Keller. The school sent their best teacher, Anne Sullivan.

Anne Sullivan was born in 1866 in Massachusetts. Her family was poor. When Sullivan got an eye infection, they could not take care of her. After Sullivan’s mother died, she was sent to a home for poor and sick people. She had operations on her eyes, but her vision was still very bad. When she was almost 15, she went to the Perkins School for the Blind. There, Sullivan finally had a successful operation on her eyes. After that, she could see a little bit better.

Sullivan quickly made up for lost time. She studied hard. She read all the books she could get her hands on. She did so well that she graduated as the top student in her class. When the school needed a teacher for a young girl in Alabama, they sent Sullivan. The teachers knew Sullivan would work hard to help Helen Keller.

Sullivan had to work hard with Keller. Keller could not hear or see what people were saying. She didn't understand the rules at places like the dinner table. She was frustrated that she could not communicate. Sometimes she cried and would hit or kick her parents, who couldn't understand her behavior. Sullivan asked the Keller family if she and Keller could move out to the gardening shed. She knew she would have to spend a lot of time teaching Keller.

Over time, Sullivan taught Keller to read, write, and speak. She often made the outdoors their classroom. She taught Keller how to use her hands to make letters to “sign” words. Sullivan taught Keller to read using Braille. Braille uses sets of raised dots on paper that stand for letters. Later, Keller learned how to speak by holding her hands on her teacher’s face and neck to feel the vibrations made by Sullivan’s voice. Keller also learned to use her senses of smell and touch. She was very curious about nature. She asked her teacher many questions. Sullivan went with Keller to schools for the deaf and blind. These schools helped Keller get ready for college.

Sullivan was a devoted teacher, and she went with Keller to Radcliff College. She helped her learn Latin, German, and French. Sullivan even read the textbooks to Keller by signing them into her hand. Anne Sullivan was Helen Keller’s friend and teacher throughout her whole life.

In 1904, Keller became the first deaf and blind person ever to receive a college degree. Keller was a good citizen. She wrote books and gave speeches about things she felt were important. She believed people should help each other. She talked about how all people should be treated equally. She spoke out for the rights of poor people. She spent a great deal of time working to make sure blind and deaf people were taken care of. Helen Keller was an amazing student who grew up to be a remarkable woman.

title: Living in the Information Age
text:
How many ways can you get a message to a friend? You can deliver the message in person. You can write a letter and send it through the post office mail. If your family still has a landline, you can pick up the phone and call your friend. You can even use a computer to talk to your friend with a webcam and a microphone. Maybe you'd rather use a cell phone to call or send a text message. Today there are many ways to get information from person to person very easily. That's why some people call the time we are living in now the Information Age.

Communication has always been important. In ancient times people used hand signs and drawings. They probably used sounds, too. Spoken language came next. Later, people figured out ways to write down what they wanted to say. People in ancient China used messengers and horses as an early postal system. In ancient Greece, people often sent messages using homing pigeons. The ancient Romans built roads for messengers to travel on when they carried messages. And the printing press changed everything! More people in more communities learned to read, because books were easier to get. Then came newspapers and magazines.

It seems that the more information people got, the more they wanted. Inventors kept finding new ways to help people get information about the world around them. Today people get information from radios, televisions, telephones and computers. We can do research on the internet and read e-books. Who knows what new inventions will be helping people communicate a hundred years from now?

New ideas are changing the way people communicate. That means communities are changing, too. Have you noticed how the words communicate and communities start with the same seven letters? In this issue, you will learn more about how communities and communication are connected. Technology is changing fast, so start reading!

title: Was Bell a Thief?
text:
The telephone is one of the most important inventions of all time. Alexander Graham Bell gets most of the credit for the invention. He was a leader in the communications field. His work in the deaf community helped many people. He helped open schools for people who could not hear. Is it possible that someone who helped so many people actually stole part of the design for his telephone from someone else? We may never know for sure.

Elisha Gray was also an inventor. He was working on a telephone at the same time as Bell. An author named Seth Shulman said he believes Bell was able to see Gray's telephone design without his permission. He thinks Bell used part of that design to build his own telephone. Other authors and historians think Shulman is wrong. They say he doesn't have enough proof to say Bell stole part of the design. There won't be a trial to see if Bell committed a crime, though. The famous inventor died in 1922.

People who study history don't always agree about who invented things. Sometimes several inventors are working on the same idea. When that happens, they might come up with different versions of the same invention. Sometimes people invent things but never get a patent for their ideas. (A patent gives you the right to make and sell an invention.) That means more than one person can get credit for inventing the same thing. How confusing!

title: Communities Help People Communicate
text:
Communicating is sharing information. All people need to communicate. People must share a common language to be able to share information with each other. Language can be spoken. It can be written in words or symbols.

Throughout history, people have needed to communicate with each other. Communities had to find ways to help people meet this need. The ways people communicate with each other are constantly changing.

Below is a timeline of how communication has changed over the past centuries. As you study the timeline, think about how each invention changed communities and the people who lived there.

The Printing Press - 1455

Before 1455, most books were written by hand. Johannes Gutenberg lived in Germany. He invented the first printing press with movable type. His invention made printing books easier. Soon, people all over the world were able to read all kinds of information.

The Electric Telegraph - 1831

Joseph Henry invented a way to send electronic signals over wire in 1831. He got some of his ideas from earlier scientists who studied electricity and magnets. Henry's invention changed communication forever.

The Daguerreotype Photograph - 1837

In 1837 Louis Daguerre, a French artist and inventor, developed a special photograph. The daguerreotype was a sheet of copper coated with silver. The sheet was placed in a camera. The image was imprinted on the sheet. You had to sit perfectly still for several minutes to have your picture taken.

The Telegraph - 1844

Samuel Morse continued to work with Joseph Henry’s ideas. In 1844, he sent the first telegraph message using Morse code. Morse code used dots and dashes to stand for letters.

The Pony Express - 1860

Young men riding horses delivered mail on the Pony Express. The Pony Express ran through eight western states. Riders could carry mail about 100 miles per day. It took about 10 days for a letter to get from Missouri to California.

The Telephone - 1876

Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone in 1876. Telephones send sound over wire. People all over the world could speak to each other, even if they were far away. Today, phones are everywhere — even in our pockets!

The Radio - 1901

Inventors like Guglielmo Marconi and Nikola Tesla studied electronic radio waves more than 100 years ago. Soon they were able to send sounds around the world. For the first time, people could get news and information as it was happening.

The Television - 1927

Several inventors helped develop television, including John Baird and Herbert Ives. In 1927, Philo T. Farnsworth invented the first all-electronic TV. By 1949, many American homes had a television.

The Computer - 1940s

Many inventors worked on inventing a computer, too. In 1945, Army engineers built the first electronic computer that could solve many computing problems. In 1976, Apple built the first successful personal computer.

The Internet - 1973

The government used early forms of the internet for almost 20 years before it became available to the public in the early 1990s. Today, people use the internet to get information on almost any subject very quickly.

The Cell Phone - 1973

Martin Cooper got a patent on the world's first cell phone in 1973. He worked for the Motorola Company then. Cell phones made it easier for people all over the world to stay in contact with one another.

What ways of communicating do you think are still to come? Are there new inventions that have been developed since you've been in school? How many inventions were developed since your parents were in school? Imagine all the possibilities!

title: Bill Gates
text:
The first computers were used in the United States in the 1940s. In the 1950s and 60s, businesses, universities and the government were the biggest computer users. Today millions of people can use computers in their homes, at schools or in libraries.

One of the most famous people in computer history is William (Bill) H. Gates. He is the leader of Microsoft. Microsoft is a computer software company. Gates is now one of the richest men in America.

Bill was born in Seattle, Washington. His father was an attorney, and his mother was a teacher. Bill did very well in school. He especially liked his math and science classes. When Bill was in junior high school he began learning about computers. He learned how to program them. He was hired to write software programs for a computer company before he was even old enough to drive.

Bill went to Harvard University. While he was there he invented a new programming language for computers. He also began to think about how computers could change the world. Bill knew that computers were not just useful for businesses. He believed someday everyone would have home computers. In 1975, he and a friend started Microsoft. The company has grown to be one of the most successful businesses in the world.

Today, Bill Gates has other important things on his mind. He still works at Microsoft but not as much as he used to. Now he spends more time thinking about ways to make the world a better place. He and his ex-wife started the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. They have set aside almost $50 billion to improve health and learning for people all over the world.

title: Making a Flow Chart
text:
Directions

Have you ever made chocolate chip cookies? If so, you know you have to follow the steps in the recipe in order. A recipe is kind of like a flow chart. A flow chart shows how to do or make something. The steps are listed in order from first to last, starting with the box on the left. Arrows show you which step to do next.

Read this story about cell phones. Then fill in the flow chart by writing each step in one of the empty boxes. Be sure to put the steps in the right order.

How Cell Phones Work

People all over the world use cell phones. Cell phones let people talk to others from just about anywhere on the planet. Cell phones do not work exactly like regular phones. They are kind of like a very special radio. What actually happens when you speak into a cell phone? First, a cell phone uses a small computer chip to turn your voice into a computer code. Next, your voice is changed into another code, so only the person you are talking to can hear your voice. Then your voice code is changed into special signals that can travel through the air. Finally, these signals are sent to the cell phone you called. Inside your friend’s phone, the signals are changed back into human voice sounds. Technology is amazing!

title: Are We There Yet?
text:
Have you ever been on a trip and asked the question, "Are we there yet?" Probably so. People always seem eager to get from one place to another. It's been that way since ancient times. Transportation has always been important to people and communities.

Long ago people had to walk to get from place to place. They soon learned to use animals to help them. Then people learned more about the world. They invented ways to help them go farther, faster. After the invention of the wheel, people began to use wagons and carts. Transportation became much easier. It was easier to move goods, too. People learned to build small boats and larger ships to travel on the water. It was now easier for people to get to far away places that were near waterways. This meant that most of the world's early communities were built near oceans and rivers.

For many centuries, human transportation really did not change much. In the 15th and 16th centuries, people from Europe sailed in ships and discovered the land that is now the Americas. Before long, many other people sailed across the ocean in ships to settle the new land. These early communities all were located near the waterways where they landed. They used animals and wagons to move from place to place on land. They began making paths and roads for people to travel. Most people lived their whole lives in the same community.

America grew quickly. More and more people came to settle the land on the East Coast. Then people wanted to find out what adventures awaited them in the West. In only a few decades, the world changed forever as people invented new methods of transportation.

In this issue you will learn more about the ways communities have met people's needs for transportation over time. You will learn about different methods of transportation and about people who have helped change the way we get from place to place. You will find out if we are there yet!

title: Gooey Green Slime—The Fuel of the Future
text:
Every form of transportation needs energy to operate. Often, this energy comes in the form of fuel. Automobiles, trains, planes and ships all run on fuel. For decades, gasoline, oil and coal have been the main fuels used to power transportation vehicles. But scientists predict these fossil fuels will be gone within a few centuries. People must find new fuels. Scientists are hard at work to solve the problem. They think they may have found an amazing new fuel source. Believe it or not, it is green algae.

Algae are simple organisms that are usually found in or near water. You've probably seen algae growing on rocks in ponds and puddles. Scientists think they have found a way to use algae to make a fuel that could power every transportation vehicle in the United States.

The new fuel, called a biodiesel fuel, would never run out. Algae don't need much space to grow. Fuel made from algae would not pollute the Earth. In fact, animal wastes could be used to help grow the algae. Who knows, maybe in the future you will fill up your car with a gallon of slimy green goo instead of gasoline!

title: History of Transportation
text:
Communities on the Move

Transportation did not change much for many decades after the first Europeans came to North America. Those first settlers used carts with wheels, animals and boats. Early inventors in Europe had also designed very simple hot air balloons and submarines. Leonardo da Vinci designed plans for a human flying machine. After America became an independent country, transportation seemed to get better almost every day.

1769 - First Self-Propelled Road Vehicle

Many men had tried to design a machine on wheels that would run on its own power. In 1769, a Frenchman named Nicolas Joseph Cugnot succeeded. His military tractor had a steam engine to provide power. The machine had three wheels and ran at two and a half miles per hour. Cugnot later invented a similar machine that carried passengers. Unfortunately, in 1771, Cugnot’s machine may have been involved in the first vehicle accident. It crashed into a stone wall when the driver lost control.

1787 - Steamboat

For many centuries, people traveled by water. Early boats and ships used the wind for power. But in 1787, John Fitch invented a boat powered by steam. He even built one that could carry people. Fitch was proud of his steamboat. Twenty years later, Robert Fulton improved Fitch’s design. Fulton’s steamboats could travel down the river at an amazing five miles per hour. Soon steamboats were moving crops, supplies and people to communities along the river. Many new communities began along the Mississippi and other rivers, thanks to steamboats.

1790 - Modern Bicycles

Several wooden bicycle machines had been invented before 1790. The rider pushed with his feet to move the machine. French carriage maker Ernest Michaux invented the modern bicycle in 1790. His design included the pedals and cranks similar to those found on today's bikes.

1814 - First Steam Engine for Locomotives

Twenty-year-old George Stephenson built the first steam engine for a locomotive completely by hand in 1814. It was the first steam-powered locomotive engine to run on a railroad track. The machine did very well. It pulled 30 tons of coal uphill at four miles per hour. Stephenson later built the first public railways in his home country, England.

1885 - First Modern Automobile

Karl Benz of Germany invented a gas-powered car in 1885. The car was known as the Benz Three-Wheeler. Soon Benz was producing cars for people to buy. His gas-powered engine made it possible for people to have their own powerful transportation machines.

1903 - First Airplane

Orville and Wilbur Wright invented the first airplane. The brothers' first inspiration came from watching birds fly. They tried many designs. Some worked better than others. They continued working on their designs. Finally, in 1903, their airplane flew for 12 seconds. Today, thousands of planes are in the sky over Earth every day.

1908 - Automobile Assembly Line

Henry Ford designed motorcars and built them one at a time. He wanted ordinary people to be able to buy an automobile. He wanted to make cars that did not cost a lot of money. He thought the best way to do this was to change the way they were made. Ford set up an assembly line to make it faster and easier to build his Model T. His idea changed the way automobiles — and many other things — were made. Soon, many more families in America were able to afford a car.

1940 - Modern Helicopter

In the 1400s, Leonardo da Vinci designed a helicopter. Throughout the years, many other men designed a flying machine with rotating blades. In 1940, a man from Russia named Igor Sikorsky invented a helicopter that was successful at staying in the air. His work helped other people invent different types of helicopters. Military units from many countries use helicopters today. They can fly in any direction. Some can even take off from and land on water.

1969 - Man Goes to the Moon

The United States worked for many years to send a manned spaceship to the moon. Scientists and astronauts studied the moon and how to get there from here. Many people worked for years on the project. Finally, on July 20, 1969, the Apollo 11 lunar module landed on the moon. Astronaut Neil Armstrong was the first person ever to walk on the moon.

1981 - Space Shuttle Launched

Scientists wanted to study other parts of outer space, too. They wanted to know if people could live in outer space. They developed a special kind of spaceship called a shuttle. The space shuttle lifted off like a rocket but landed like an airplane. Scientists on space shuttles performed many experiments. They tried to find out what it would be like to live in space. They helped us learn more about our solar system.

title: Henry Ford: Automotive Industry Leader
text:
Today, almost every family in America owns a car. We can all thank Henry Ford for that. He helped change the ways cars were made. His ideas helped make it easier for people to afford cars.

Henry Ford was born and raised in Michigan. He did well in school and became an engineer. He liked to work on engines and machines. He liked to build motorcars. Henry dreamed of being able to make cars for other people.

Henry started his own car company in Detroit, Michigan. Two or three men worked together and made a few cars a day to be sold. People liked the Ford Model T cars, but they still cost more than most people made in a year. Ford needed to be able to make more than a few cars a day. That way he could lower the price for each car.

Ford opened up a new factory. He thought about ways he could make more cars there. He came up with a plan. Ford used an assembly line to put the cars together. In the past, two or three people built each car. Now all the company’s workers would help each other. In the assembly line, each worker and machine stayed in one place. The car being built moved past them. Each worker added a part or worked on the car until it was done.

Cars could be made more quickly and would cost less. Before, it took 14 hours to build one car. Now it only took 93 minutes. The cost of each car was cut in half. More people could own the Ford Model T.

For the rest of his life, Henry Ford worked to find better ways to make cars. Many of his ideas are still used in the manufacturing industry today.

title: What is manufacturing?
text:
Manufacturing is the business of making products, or goods, to sell. There are many types of manufacturing companies. Cars, computers, toys and soft drinks are some examples of manufactured products.

People usually work in factories to manufacture the goods. Thanks to Henry Ford, many people work together to make products on an assembly line. The people depend on each other to do their job well so the product is made correctly.

The goods you buy in the store are made in a factory then shipped by boat, truck, train or plane to the store where you buy them. Sometimes it takes a combination of two or more of those transportation methods to get the products to a store. Manufacturing is an important part of business in America.

title: Railroads Link the Nation
text:
America was founded in 1776. One hundred years later, railroads stretched all the way across the country. Railroads crossed plains, prairies, mountains and valleys. Trains linked communities together.

Railroads made it possible for people to move around the country. People could travel from coast to coast in only one week. The same trip would have taken months by horse and wagon. Traveling by train was safer than the long, dangerous wagon journeys of the past. The railroad gave people many new opportunities.

Railroads helped American business grow quickly. Trains carried materials to factories for manufacturing. The goods were loaded on other trains and shipped to cities across the country. Ranchers used the railroad to ship cattle to market. Fresh produce could be shipped from farms directly to people in cities. Today, railroads are still an important part of American business and industry.

title: Interpreting Transportation Maps
text:
People in big cities can travel by automobile, airplane and train. Materials and manufactured goods can be shipped from place to place in trucks, planes and trains, too.

People who are traveling or shipping goods need to know how to get from one place to another. This information can be found on transportation maps. These special maps show different routes that can be taken from place to place. A transportation map may show roads, railways and airports.

Look at this transportation map of Texas. Think about the best way to use information from the map.
• Map Title — Use the map title to help you know exactly what information can be found on the map.
• Map Key — Study the symbols shown on the key. Find the symbols on the map to help you know the types of transportation available in an area.
• Use the information on the map to help you determine exactly what kinds of transportation are available between two places.

Use the map to help you answer the following questions.

1. What is the title of the map?_______

2. What kind of information do you think you will find on the map?______

3. Explain three symbols in the map key, and circle one example of each of them on the map._______

4. Can you create a transportation map that shows the neighborhood where you live? You can draw your map on a separate piece of paper. Be sure to put in a title, map key and compass rose. Think about the kinds of transportation people in your neighborhood use the most. You may want to show the location of bicycle racks, parking lots and benches for tired walkers to sit on.

title: Keeping Communities Safe and Healthy
text:
Think about your usual day. You get up, get dressed and head to school. In your classroom, you work hard, but you also have fun learning. Your classroom is a clean and happy place to spend the day. You take a lunch break around noon. Some kids bring a meal from home. Others eat a hot, healthy meal in the school cafeteria. Afternoon is recess time. You get to run and play. If you get hot and thirsty, there is always cool water from the fountains to drink. If someone falls and scrapes a knee on the playground, the school nurse is always there to help. It’s a good feeling to know there are people who care about your health and safety. You don’t have to spend a lot of time worrying about those things. You know there are adults in your community who are always watching out for you.

But it has not always been this way for people in the United States. About a century ago, many cities in America grew very quickly. Railroads made it easier for people to move around, so lots of people filled the communities at once. Some cities grew so big and so fast that they became crowded, unsafe places to live.

Many people worked at jobs that were dangerous. The factory buildings were unsafe and unhealthy. Even children worked long hours. When they got home at night, many people were in a bad situation. Their homes were filthy and cold. The water they drank was often dirty and unsafe. People bought food that was sometimes rotten. Many people got sick. Diseases spread very quickly from one person to another.

Community leaders knew that something had to be done to make the cities clean, safe and healthy. People who lived in the communities began to work together to make changes. They came up with plans to make drinking water safer. They passed laws about how food should be handled and sold. Scientists studied how diseases are spread. They helped find ways to keep people from getting sick. Life in communities improved.

In this issue you will learn about how communities work together to improve the safety and health of citizens. You will also learn about some amazing men and women whose work and ideas changed the ways people live. You will understand how life in communities has changed over time.

title: Improving Health in Communities
text:
In 1900 the average life expectancy was less than 50 years. This meant that most people could expect to live only to about the age of 50. Today most people in the United States will live to be nearly 80 years old. Why do people today have a better chance of living longer?

You know certain habits can lead to a healthier life. People exercise to stay healthy. People know they should eat nutritious food and not overeat. People also know that smoking and using drugs are unhealthy habits. Even wearing a seat belt each time you get into a car will improve your chances of living longer. Many of the ideas that improved health and safety in communities changed the world. These scientific ideas are helping people live longer, healthier lives.

Pasteurization - Louis Pasteur

Louis Pasteur lived in France in the 1860s. He was a scientist who studied chemistry. One of Pasteur's jobs as a chemist was to try and find out why wine and milk sometimes went sour. Pasteur performed many experiments. He found that tiny living things called germs were making the foods spoil.

Pasteur set out to find a way to kill the germs. He used heat. The foods stayed fresh and safe longer. Today the heating process is called pasteurization. The process is still used to keep foods safe.

Penicillin - Sir Alexander Fleming

Alexander Fleming was a medical researcher who was born in Scotland. He moved to England to go to medical school. Fleming studied germs. He wanted to know why people got sick. He wanted to know how he could help people stay healthy. Dr. Fleming's amazing discovery was an accident.

Dr. Fleming left a dish of germs out in his lab while he was on vacation. He also left a window in the lab open. A certain kind of mold blew in through the window. Mold is a living thing found in air, water and soil. When he returned to work, Fleming noticed the mold growing in the bacteria dish. He realized the mold was killing the bacteria that caused diseases. By luck, a wonderful new medicine had been found. It was called penicillin.

Dr. Fleming's penicillin could be used to cure diseases that were caused by bacteria. When people are sick today they are often treated with penicillin or another medicine similar to it.

Vaccines - Jonas Salk

Jonas Salk was born in 1914 and lived in New York City. Salk studied medicine. He studied viruses. Viruses are small living things that attack the human body. Viruses cause many diseases. One disease caused by a virus is polio. Polio makes people very sick. It can make people unable to move or walk. In the 1940s and 1950s, there were many people in the United States who were infected by the polio virus. Jonas Salk wanted to find a way to keep other people from getting the disease.

He found a way to make a vaccine for the polio virus. A vaccine is a liquid made from dead or weak germs of a disease. The vaccine is given to people. They do not get sick from the vaccine. The vaccine helps protect the body from disease.

Salk’s vaccine was given to many people. It kept them from getting polio. Today, there are few cases of polio in the United States. Salk’s work continues to protect communities today.

title: Jane Addams
text:
Chicago, Illinois, was much like other large U.S. cities of the late 19th century. By 1889 it had grown into a very large and crowded community. Many people there lived in bad conditions. They worked long hours at dangerous jobs. The water in the community was dirty and unsafe to drink. Much of the food that people could buy often made them sick. Many people were ill with diseases that spread quickly to other people. One woman in the city wanted to change those terrible living conditions.

Jane Addams grew up in a happy family. She lived in a beautiful home. She traveled all over the world. Jane wanted to help people. She thought about ways she could make the world better. She started in Chicago. Jane and a friend began Hull House.

People who lived in the worst conditions in the city could come to Hull House. Many of them were immigrants who had moved to the United States from other countries. Jane believed there was hope for everyone. She helped all kinds of people. She wanted to give them a chance to learn new skills. She helped them find better jobs and homes. At Hull House, people could receive medical care and healthy meals. Children were taken care of while their parents went to work.

But Jane’s work for the people of Chicago didn’t stop there. She tried to stop drug abuse. She helped pass laws that would make food safer to eat. She even worked as a garbage inspector so she could make sure neighborhoods were kept clean.

People admired Jane and her work. They listened to her ideas about peace and freedom in the world. She helped take supplies to women and children around the world during times of war. In 1931, Jane was the first woman ever given a very special award. It was called the Nobel Peace Prize. It was given to her to honor her work to improve the lives of people everywhere.

title: Hospitals Through Time
text:
Where can people in a community go for help when they are very sick? To hospitals, of course. Hospitals care for people who are sick or injured. Hospitals also offer many services to help keep the community healthy. There are many types of hospitals in America today. Some hospitals are only for children or for women. Other hospitals treat patients with certain types of illnesses or injuries. People in communities depend on hospitals and the people who work in them. But the hospitals we have in today’s communities are very different from early hospitals.

In ancient times, medicine and religion were closely related. Sick people went to temples to pray for healing. There was not much else they could do. For thousands of years, churches in communities tended to the ill and injured. Priests, monks and nuns also served as doctors and nurses. In ancient Rome, church hospitals were also a place for the poor and homeless to seek shelter and food.

The first free hospitals opened in Asia nearly 3,000 years ago. The people who took care of these early patients used what they knew about science to treat illnesses and injuries. Governments also began running hospitals as places where injured soldiers could receive care.

Modern hospitals began in Europe in the 18th century. These hospitals were no longer places of worship. Homeless people could not stay in hospitals just for food and shelter. In these clean buildings, doctors and surgeons worked to make the sick well again.

In the United States today, there are thousands of hospitals. Most communities have a hospital in town or nearby. Some communities pay for hospitals with taxes collected from citizens. Some hospitals are owned and paid for by private businesses or people. Hospitals use modern science and technology to keep citizens healthy.

title: Why are doctors called "-ologists"?
text: The suffix “-ology” is used to describe a field of study. An “-ologist” is a person who studies in that field. In medicine, doctors have specialties. That means most of them treat only one part of the body or one health condition. For example, “cardio” means heart. When we add the suffix “–ologist,” we get cardiologist. The word means a person who studies the heart. A cardiologist treats diseases that affect the heart. By breaking apart the word that is the doctor’s title we can see what their medical specialty happens to be.

title: Hector P. Garcia
text: Hector P. Garcia was an important person during the fight for Hispanic civil rights. When Hector was a child, he and his family lived in Mexico. They later fled to Texas to escape the fighting taking place there. As Hector grew up, his parents pushed him to do well in school. He earned a degree from the University of Texas and became a doctor. He graduated from college in 1940 and joined the U.S. Army. He earned six Battle Stars and the Bronze Star for his hard work and courage in World War II. When he came home from the war, he was shocked at the unfair treatment the Hispanic veterans (soldiers who fought in war) faced. Hector formed the American G.I. Forum in 1948. The organization was created to protect the civil rights of Hispanics, women and other minorities (smaller groups). The official motto of the American G.I. Forum is "Education is Our Freedom and Freedom Should be Everybody's Business."

title: Main Idea and Details
text: A main idea is given to you in the box below. Read this issue, and look for the names of people whose work in communities supports the main idea. Write their names in the circles connected to the main idea box. Explain what each person did to help improve communities. Be sure you only give details that support the main idea.

title: Let's Write
text: Which scientist — Pasteur, Salk or Fleming — do you think had the greatest impact on the health of communities? Choose one scientist and write a paragraph about his accomplishments. Explain how his work improved life for people. Support your ideas by giving specific reasons for your choice. Write in complete sentences. Edit your final draft for correct capitals, punctuation, spelling and grammar.

title: Stand Up for Healthy School Lunches
text:
Curly fries. Chicken wings. Fried mozzarella cheese sticks. These high-fat, high-calorie items are not healthy. Why do schools offer unhealthy foods in their school cafeteria? It's simple: because kids buy them. Many school districts today hire companies to provide food for the schools. It's a business, and a business makes money when people buy the product.

The School Lunch Initiative (SLI) is a program designed to connect school subjects with food. Students are involved in activities that include growing, preparing, serving and enjoying food. SLI provides students with healthy meals made from local ingredients.

At Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School in Berkeley, California, each student participates in the Edible Schoolyard. Classes taught in the one-acre garden teach about plant life cycles, community values and the pleasures of work. Kitchen classes allow kids to prepare and eat delicious and nutritious meals from foods they grew in the garden.

People are standing up for healthy choices in school cafeterias!

title: Who Can Be a Hero?
text:
"Hero" is a very powerful word. It can make you think of courage, strength, honor, sacrifice and intelligence. What does a hero look like? Heroes come in many shapes and sizes. Some are men. Some are women. Some are children. Heroes come from all races. Heroes may be rich or poor. Heroes can look like someone famous. They can look like your next-door neighbor. So how can you tell if someone is a hero?

Heroes are those special people who work to help others. Sometimes they offer a helping hand. Sometimes they say a kind word. Some heroes give us inspiring ideas. Other heroes quietly stay in the background and donate money to people in need. All heroes help others without thinking about themselves first. Heroes help people in the community even though they may never know them by name.

As you study history, you will learn about many individual heroes. Many people have changed their own communities and the entire world with their efforts. Many heroes made choices that were not easy to make. Most took risks. You will learn that many heroes had to overcome obstacles. Obstacles are the things that get in the way of reaching a goal. You might be surprised to learn what some heroes sacrificed, or gave up, to help others.

Why do people do the things that make them heroes? It's easy, really. Heroes believe in the community. They want to accomplish what others say can't be done. They want to make life better for all people. This is what leads people on journeys to find new inventions and ideas. The bottom line is that heroes want to make a difference in the world.

In this issue you will learn about people you might not have thought of as heroes before. These are people whose ideas and inventions have changed communities and the entire world. You will study how these heroes have changed things for all of us. You will see that heroes can be fathers, mothers, students, teachers, scientists, inventors, politicians, adventurers and anything in between. Above all, you will see heroes are thinkers and doers. They share a sense of purpose and represent the very best spirit of people everywhere.

title: Sally Ride Leaves a Legacy
text:
America lost a hero in 2012 when astronaut Sally Ride died. She was born in 1951 in California. She played tennis and loved science and English literature classes. Ride studied physics, the science of matter and energy. Her journey to space began when she applied to a NASA program for astronauts. She was one of the 35 people chosen from over 8,000 applications! Ride worked hard in the training program and helped design the robotic arm on the space shuttle. Her 1983 mission on the space shuttle Challenger launched her into space and into the history books. Sally Ride was the first American woman to fly in space!

Sally Ride was also an educator. Ride saw that as girls got older, they lost interest in science and math classes. She wrote children's books and started a company that provides exciting science materials to schools. Ride was proud to be a role model for girls who wanted to be astronauts and scientists.

When Ride began her space career, most of the other astronauts and engineers were men. When asked about being one of the few women in this profession, she said, "I never ran into a teacher or a counselor who told me that science was for boys." Thanks to Sally Ride, both boys and girls know that they can reach for the stars!

title: Inventors Change the World
text:
Our communities change every day. Our world changes every day. As a matter of fact, most communities have changed a lot over the last 200 years. Why have they changed?

Communities change when people solve problems or find ways to make tasks easier. These changes can happen over time. Many of these changes happen because someone has a dream about making the world a better place. People with those kinds of dreams want to improve the community and people's lives.

New technology is followed by new inventions. This changes life in communities. The people behind these inventions are responsible for changing the way people live. These people make communities better.

Not every inventor was successful the first time. Sometimes people thought the new ideas were foolish. Sometimes people just didn't see the need to have a new way of doing something they had always done.

Read about one inventor whose ideas changed the world. It took many years for people to see how important his ideas were, but he never gave up. He knew his ideas could help people.

Cyrus McCormick

Cyrus McCormick grew up in Virginia. His parents were farmers. Farming was a difficult job in the 1880s. There weren't many machines that made the work easier. Cyrus' father was always trying to invent a machine that would help him gather his crops faster. He didn't succeed. Cyrus decided to continue his father's work.

Young Cyrus liked to invent things. He was always watching and learning from his father’s inventions. In 1831, using his father’s unfinished model, Cyrus went to work to design a machine that could cut and bundle grain in the harvest field. In less than two months, Cyrus had invented a reaping machine that was pulled by horses. Crops could now be harvested 10 times faster than before.

However, farmers were not very interested in the reaper. At first they were afraid of the strange machine. One of them said the new reaper looked like "a cross between a wheelbarrow, a chariot and a flying machine." McCormick asked the farmers to come and watch him harvest his crops. They watched him and then went home and used their old hand tools to cut the crops. They thought McCormick's reaper was just a very entertaining machine. They did not like change.

Cyrus didn't give up. He continued showing his machine to people. He even kept working on his design. He made his original design work even better. He kept inventing new farm equipment. Slowly, farmers began to realize how useful McCormick's reaper was. In 1843, McCormick sold 29 reapers. By 1850 he was selling 5,000 reapers each year. His company, International Harvester Company, still sells reapers today.

Cyrus McCormick is known as the Father of Modern Agriculture. He changed the way farmers raise and harvest crops. Farmers could now produce larger crops than they ever thought possible. The reaper made the work of farming much easier.

McCormick’s invention also changed communities in other ways. After the invention of the reaper, fewer farmers were needed to feed people. Each farmer could produce more food than before. Since communities need fewer farmers, more and more people could work in other businesses. Instead of farming, people could study the arts, science and engineering. In 1800, about 90 percent of all people farmed. Today in the United States, only about two percent of people make their living as farmers. Cyrus might never have dreamed his amazing machine would help change the world!

title: George Washington Carver: Scientific Hero
text:
Not all discoveries in farming and agriculture have to do with machines. Some of them are ideas. One man came up with hundreds and hundreds of ideas that changed the way people farmed and used farm products. This man was George Washington Carver.

George’s parents were enslaved when he was born in Missouri in 1864. Susan and Moses Carver adopted him after his own parents died. George was a sickly boy, but he found plenty of time to play outdoors. He especially liked to study plants. He grew his own garden. He liked to talk to the plants. George also experimented and made medicines from the garden plants.

George worked his way through school. It wasn’t easy. Some schools did not want him to attend because he was African American. Finally, George graduated from Iowa Agricultural College. He stayed and became a teacher at the college for a short time. He continued to study plants.

George soon changed jobs. At the Tuskegee Institute, George discovered ways for farmers to grow healthier plants. But George’s most famous work was probably with peanuts. Before this time, peanuts were mainly used to feed livestock. Carver went to work to find new uses for them. Over time, Carver developed 325 different uses for the peanut. This included peanut milk and cheese, printing ink, face cream, shampoo and soap.

Carver found new uses for other plants too. People began to realize that his ideas were changing the world. Many other scientists, inventors and leaders wanted to work with him. George helped raise a lot of money so other groups could study plants, too.

George Washington Carver is a hero. He worked hard his whole life to find ways to make life for other people better. This amazing scientist also loved the arts. He played piano and accordion, and one of his paintings won Honorable Mention at the Chicago World’s Fair in 1893.

title: Benjamin Banneker
text:
Benjamin Banneker was born on Nov. 9, 1731, in Baltimore County, Maryland. Both his mother and father had been enslaved but were then freed. Benjamin went to a small country school for only a short time. He loved to study history, read and practice math. For most of his life, he worked as a tobacco farmer. When he was 22, he built a working clock using only wood — no metal at all. The clock was destroyed in a fire 40 years later.

As he got older, his love for astronomy (the study of the universe) grew. Banneker was able to predict a solar eclipse in 1788. (A solar eclipse is the time when the moon passes between the Sun and the Earth.) Two years later, he published his first of six almanacs. These almanacs were full of information such as tide tables, when the sun would rise and set, eclipses and astronomy facts.

In 1791, Banneker sent a letter and a copy of his almanac to Thomas Jefferson. In his letter, he wrote about how terrible slavery was. He asked Jefferson to imagine what it was like to be a slave. At the time, many people didn’t believe that African Americans deserved the same rights as white people. Even though many disagreed with Banneker, he was strong and stood up for what he believed. Benjamin Banneker died in 1806, one month before his 75th birthday.

title: Maria Mitchell
text:
Maria Mitchell was born on August 1, 1818. Her family valued education and science. Back then, most girls were not encouraged to set high goals and achieve them. Maria's father, William Mitchell, was an astronomer (a scientist who studies the universe) and teacher. He shared his knowledge of science and math with Maria. Soon she loved astronomy just as her father did. She often helped her father with his telescope and observations. She enjoyed standing on the roof looking into the night sky with her telescope.

As she grew older, Maria loved to learn new things. She became her community’s first librarian and shared her knowledge with others. She continued to study the night sky and began to get more telescopes. On October 1, 1847, she noticed a blurry object moving across the sky. It was a comet! She wrote down its location so she knew where to look for it the next night. The next evening, she saw it again. The King of Denmark gave Maria a medal as a reward for her discovery. News of Maria’s discovery spread

News of Maria's discovery spread very quickly. She became a well-known astronomer who went on to make many more discoveries. Some of these include sunspots, stars and the moons of Jupiter and Saturn. In 1865, Maria began teaching at Vassar College. She was the first female astronomy professor in the United States. Maria Mitchell died in 1889. A ship, an observatory and a crater on the moon have been named after her. She will be remembered for her determination to learn and discover new things.

title: Using Information in a Table
text:
This week you read about a very famous scientist named George Washington Carver. He is responsible for many amazing scientific discoveries. His work changed the world.

However, Carver had trouble even finding schools that would accept him as a student. Long ago some schools did not allow African Americans to attend. That has changed now. Everyone in our country has the right to an education.

African Americans have made many great scientific discoveries and inventions. Use the table below to learn about some of these ideas and the people who thought of them. Then answer the questions below the table.

1. What invention listed on the table was created first? ________

2. Which inventor has more than one patented invention on the list? ________

3. In what year did G.A Morgan receive a patent for the traffic signal? _______

4. How many years passed between the patent for the helicopter and the patent for a rocket catapult? _______

5. Which discovery of George Washington Carver is included in this table? _______

6. In 1973, A. Prather received a patent for a man-powered glider aircraft. Add this information to the table.

title: Looking Back: Communities and Communication
text:
Back to School

Since ancient times, communities have educated their young people. In Greece and Rome, the sons of rich families went to school in the temple. Many boys learned a trade to make money. Girls did not go to school. They learned how to take care of the home and family. American Indians taught their children through stories. The stories helped explain the world around them. They also taught them lessons about how to behave. American Indian boys learned to hunt, and the girls learned to gather or grow food.

When the pilgrims came to North America in the 17th century, they believed their children should be educated, too. Wealthy children studied history, math and Latin. There were separate schools for girls. They learned to read, write and care for their homes. Other schools were places where children worked with adults to learn a trade. Candle making, blacksmithing and leather tanning were popular. Poor and slave children had no school at all.

The very first public school in America opened in 1635 in Boston, MA. Rev. John Cotton wanted the city to have a school like the ones in England. The Boston Latin School is still open today. Massachusetts was the first state to pass a law saying children must go to school. Other states followed. Today, every child in America must attend school.

Over time, people in communities realized schools were important for success. There are many different kinds of schools to help children learn to be good citizens in their communities.

Communication in the Information Age

There are many ways for people to communicate with one another. We are living in the Information Age. However, communication has always been important. Ancient people used hand signs and drawings. Spoken language then developed, as sounds became words. Most every culture developed its own language. Then, people figured out ways to write. Messages were carried back and forth between people. Eventually the printing press was invented. Books, newspapers and magazines were produced. More and more people learned to read and write to share ideas.

Over time there have been many communication innovations, or improvements. Many of these inventions happened in the 19th century. The telegraph and the photograph were two of the first remarkable advances in communication. In the late 1800s, young men riding horses on the Pony Express delivered mail to people living in Western communities. Communication improvements came quickly in the 19th century. The telephone, radio, television, computer and Internet are all important communication devices developed during this century. Most people now have non-stop access to the world through personal computers and smartphones. People in communities can easily share information with one another. It is also fun to dream about new ways to communicate that will be developed in the future!

Communities Need Transportation

In the past, people had to walk to get from place to place. Eventually animals were trained to help transport, or move, people and goods. After the wheel was invented, transportation was easier. Over time, people wanted to travel further away from their homes. They learned how to build and use boats and ships to travel on water. Humans could then travel and explore faraway places. They formed new communities in these places. The world began to grow and change as new forms of transportation were invented.

Throughout history, people have tried to invent better and faster forms of transportation. There were many new transportation inventions in the 1700s. The steamboat, the modern bicycle and the first type of vehicle were all invented. In the 19th century, the first steam engine for locomotives made it possible for trains to pull larger and heavier loads. The first modern automobile was also invented. Now people could have their very own powerful transportation machine. American automobile leader Henry Ford soon found ways to design and build cars so that every family could afford one. The 20th century and beyond has been a time when automobile improvements soared. Airplanes and helicopters have led to rockets and space shuttles that take transportation right into outer space! Today, transportation is still improving. Can you imagine what forms will be available to communities in the future?

title: Creating Successful Communities
text:
Why People Live in Communities

There are many different reasons people form communities. People have lived in community groups since the beginning of time. Sometimes people form communities because there is a need for security, law and order. It is safer for people to live and work together. Early American Indians often lived and traveled in bands for just this reason. Some communities are formed in order to give members religious freedom. Many of the first American communities were established for this reason. Remember the Pilgrims who settled Plymouth Rock in 1620? They left England to have a chance at a better life that included the right to worship as they wanted.

Many new communities began simply because people were looking for better lives for themselves and their families. They were willing to work hard in order to have all the things they needed and wanted. There are many different kinds of communities. However, they all seem to have the same types of needs. In this issue, we will review all of the ways people meet their needs in communities.

Communities Need Rules

People want to feel safe. In order for communities to be safe places for all people, there must be rules. Rules keep things in order. Rules help people find solutions to disagreements and problems. Rules help keep people within the community safe and healthy. There are different types of rules, including those to follow at home, at school and in the community.

Who makes all of these rules? Leaders can make rules. At home your parents make rules. At school the leaders are your teachers and principals. In a community government, leaders might include the mayor or city council. People vote for these leaders, so you could say that people help make some of their own rules. It is the responsibility of each citizen to follow the rules of the community.

There are consequences for breaking the laws of the community. Sometimes people who are accused of breaking laws have a trial. The U.S. Constitution promises that these people may have a jury. Citizens serve on the jury and decide if the person is guilty of breaking the rules. Juries often decide the punishment for breaking the law, too.

Communities Work ... then Play

People in communities have jobs to do. They work, go to school and take care of their families. These people also need time to play and relax. We call this recreation. Recreation is any activity that people choose to do for fun. These activities take place during free time away from work and school. There are many recreational choices. Some people like to read or watch television and movies. Visits to art museums, music concerts and live theaters are considered recreational activities, too. Other people like active recreation. These activities include jogging and bike riding. Most people enjoy recreational activities with their family and friends. Humans need play time to be happy. These activities also help keep people healthy. Most communities try to provide many recreational opportunities for their citizens.

Community and state governments use tax money to pay for recreation. Most local governments include a special recreation department.

The Recreation and Parks Department takes care of a community's parks, swimming pools and sports gyms/fields. Sometimes this department also provides educational programs for citizens. These programs help people learn about new ways to play and exercise.

Early communities quickly realized parks were important to people. Today, parkland is often the center of a community. Larger communities sometimes have several parks citizens can enjoy every day of the week. Parks are places where families might exercise, play games, rest and enjoy nature. Many parks even have equipment and activities that people with disabilities can enjoy. Wheelchair parks are becoming more and more common in many communities.

In addition to parks, most communities offer other recreational activities. Safe swimming and water parks are usually favorites with families and children. Special sports centers are also popular recreational facilities. Golf courses and tennis courts are used often in many communities. Sometimes there are even professional players who help the citizens learn to play the games. Community recreation centers also provide classes in martial arts, dance, boxing and gymnastics. Some of these centers offer child care for students whose parents work. There are many recreation choices for people in most communities. There simply is no excuse for NOT having a little fun!

title: Bill Gates: Trades and Technology
text:
William (Bill) H. Gates is one of the most famous (and richest) people in the world. He is the leader of a successful computer software company called Microsoft. Gates grew up in Seattle, WA. He did well in school and became interested in computers long before most people had even heard of them.

Gates invented a new programming language for computers while he was a student at Harvard University. He believed computers were going to change the world. Gates had many ideas about how computers could be used. He thought computers could be useful to businesses and people at home. He was right! Today, Gates uses his money to change the world by improving healthcare and education for all people.

title: Helen Keller: Amazing Scholar
text: There are many outstanding students in American history. One woman stands out, though. She was left deaf and blind after a terrible illness as a young child. Helen Keller did not let her disabilities keep her from reaching her goals. She learned to communicate with people. At first she communicated using sign language, but she later learned to talk. She learned to read using a special kind of writing called Braille. Helen graduated from college. She wrote books and gave speeches about things she felt were important. She wanted all people to be treated equally. She spoke for the rights of poor people. Helen Keller was a model scholar and a true example of a good citizen.

title: Citizenship
text:
You can be a good citizen in many different ways. Here are a few people whose work has changed the world for all of us.

Jonas Salk discovered a vaccine to prevent the severe disease called polio.

Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization, which is a process that helps keep foods safe to eat.

Cyrus McCormick invented the automatic reaping machine, making farmers' work much easier.

Maria Mitchell made many important discoveries about space as the first woman astronomer.

Benjamin Banneker was a mathematician and astronomer who wrote almanacs and spoke out for equal treatment of people of all races.

Hector P. Garcia formed the American G.I. Forum to protect the rights of women, Hispanics and other minorities.

title: Heroes Don't Always Wear Capes
text:
Communities provide important services to citizens that help keep people safe. Brave men and women provide these services. These heroes put needs of others above their own. They help and protect people. They put their own lives in danger while helping others. Military troops, police officers, firefighters and paramedics are all first responders. They are ready to assist people at any time.

A famous example of heroism is the WWII story of the Four Chaplains. The four military pastors were on board a ship named the Dorchester in 1943 when a German torpedo hit it. The Four Chaplains all died helping other people onboard the ship. This proved that heroes are often everyday people.

Discuss the community’s needs for government, education, communication, transportation, safety and recreation. Give at least one detail for each need. Explain what you will do as mayor to make sure needs are met in your community. Give your speech to the class. Use a computer program to design and print a campaign poster for yourself. What will your slogan be?

text:

2. What invention is most responsible for improving communication in communities around the world?

3. What is the relationship between transportation and trade of goods between communities?
