title: Looking Back: Economy and Culture
text:
Trade Brings Countries Together

Have you shopped with your parents lately? Did you buy avocados from South America or maybe special chocolate from Europe? How do goods that are manufactured, or made, in other countries end up in American stores? The answer is trade. The United States buys goods and services from people in many different parts of the world. We sell products to them, too.

International trade is between two different countries. Goods are exported, or sold and sent, from the U.S. to other countries. Goods are also imported, or brought in, to the U.S. from other countries. The U.S. trades many goods with our neighbors, Mexico and Canada. The three countries even have a special agreement to make it easier for their citizens to do business with each other.

There is also trade between the states in our own country. This is called domestic trade. Each state grows or manufactures goods that other states do not produce. These goods are shipped out every day to be sold in stores around the nation. This explains why people in Washington can enjoy Texas beef, and Texans enjoy salmon from Alaska.

People all over the world are connected to each other. Trade and technology allow countries and people to depend upon each other. Events such as hurricanes, earthquakes or wars may affect the cost and supply of scarce (very small in amount) goods that are traded around the world.

Writers Share Culture

A community's heritage is its history, traditions, beliefs and customs. These must be passed from older relatives to children. Reading, telling and listening to stories are ways that people share their heritage and culture with each other.

Writers share their culture with people. Speeches, stories and poems often tell about values and traditions that people share. There are many Americans who are well-known for sharing their culture through words.

Phillis Wheatley lived much of her life as an enslaved person. Unlike most enslaved people, she learned how to read and write. Her poems and letters helped people better understand the lives and culture of enslaved people.

Laura Ingalls Wilder wrote many stories about her family's adventures. They were settlers in the early years of America. These stories make it possible for us to imagine what life was like for pioneers.

Martin Luther King Jr. wrote and gave speeches about how African Americans were treated. People listened to him and made changes in the way they treated people from different cultures.

Tomie dePaola is a modern-day writer and illustrator. People around the world enjoy his books about his culture and other cultures.

Maya Angelou wrote many poems and stories about her own family and life as an African American. She used words to help the world better understand her heritage and culture.

History's Heroes

When you are asked to name your hero, who comes to mind first? A parent? A favorite teacher? There are many people we look up to. Heroes are people who do amazing things for others. Most communities have many heroes. These are the people who help shape the culture of the community. Heroes are often leaders, very smart and brave. We can learn a lot from studying the lives of these men and women.

Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States, and many people respected him. Lincoln studied hard in school. He worked to become a good lawyer and government leader. Most of all, President Lincoln worked to help the people of the United States get along with one another. He believed all people deserved to be free. When he signed a document called the Emancipation Proclamation, enslaved people were freed. Lincoln is often at the top of most people’s list of heroes.

Many people also think of Davy Crockett as another hero from the past. Crockett did not attend much school, but he was still very smart. He was also a good leader. The people of Tennessee elected him to their state government. They trusted him so much that he became a U.S. Congressman. Crockett heard people in Texas were fighting with Mexico. He immediately went to help. Crockett died a hero at the Alamo helping people claim their freedom.

title: Celebrate Cultural Differences
text:
What is There to Celebrate?

Texans and all Americans come from many different backgrounds. The cultures of these people make our state and country special. It is fun to learn how different groups of people live. Luckily, most people enjoy sharing their culture with others. They feel proud to share how their culture is special. You have probably eaten food or listened and danced to music that was from a culture different from your own. Maybe you have even gone to a special celebration held by an ethnic or cultural group. In most communities, there are many different celebrations to attend during the year. At these festivals, you can learn more about your own culture or about the cultures of your friends.

Mexican American Celebrations

Texas was once a part of Mexico. In 1845, Texas became a free republic and later a state in the U.S. Still, you can see and experience the Mexican culture today throughout Texas. People can experience the Mexican way of life through special cultural celebrations. Many people celebrate Cinco de Mayo on May 5th each year. It is when people of Mexican heritage remember the 1862 Battle of Puebla in Mexico. Today, many U.S. cities hold Cinco de Mayo celebrations. People honor their Mexican heritage and often go to parades and parties. They eat traditional Mexican foods such as menudo and tortillas. Children often play games to break open a piñata filled with candy and surprises.

Dia de los Muertos is another traditional Mexican celebration. For centuries, people have celebrated this Day of the Dead during every first week of November. It is a day to honor loved ones who have died. The day is filled with special cemetery picnics where many share food and memories of loved ones. Families clean the gravesites and leave special flowers. It is not a scary or sad time. It is a happy time for families to spend with loved ones and remember their heritage.

African American Celebrations

African Americans in Texas celebrate a very special day every year on June 19th. This marks the day in 1865 when enslaved people heard that the Civil War had ended. The war had been over for two months. On this day, though, they learned they were free citizens. In 1980, Juneteenth became a Texas state holiday. Many people hold parades, picnics and barbecues throughout the states. In large cities there are usually concerts, art shows and celebrations of African American culture. It is a special day for many citizens. People from different cultures come together on this day to celebrate the freedoms given to all Americans.

German Celebrations

German Americans make up a large part of the country's population. Many people enjoy the special celebrations held by this group of Americans. One of the most popular festivals held each year is Oktoberfest. In Germany, the festival began as a celebration of the king's marriage. Today, it is a party to honor German culture. People usually celebrate Oktoberfest in the last weeks of September and early October every year. During the festivals, people like to listen to German music. Many people polka dance or waltz. Most would agree that the tasty German food is special, too. Everyone who celebrates enjoys sausages, strudels and sweet pastries.

Irish Celebrations

Many immigrants from Ireland came to America for a better life. They worked hard to own land and homes. Today, Irish Americans enjoy celebrating their heritage and sharing their culture with others. Every St. Patrick's Day in March, many communities around the country have Irish festivals. Irish dancers, music, crafts and food make the day fun. There are usually special games for children to play. Those who go enjoy eating Irish foods, such as corned beef and a potato-and-cabbage dish called colcannon. Many people at Irish festivals wear the color green. This is the traditional color of Ireland. Watch out! If you're not wearing green, you might get a pinch.

Americans often share and respect the many cultures that make up the heritage of our country. People remember the customs they brought with them from their homelands. They also develop new customs as they begin their lives in their new homes. Learning about all the cultures at community celebrations is both fun and educational.

title: Selling for Success
text:
Entrepreneurs are people who start their own businesses. There are many entrepreneurs in America.

Mary Kay Ash started a women’s skin care and makeup business. Many women have worked for Ash, selling her products at home parties. People knew Mrs. Ash as a kind, dedicated and hardworking businesswoman.

You might not know his name, but you have probably eaten his cookies! Wallace Amos worked for years to develop the perfect chocolate chip cookie. The Famous Amos brand was sold to the Keebler Company, and Amos’ delicious cookies are still in stores.

Sam Walton probably never guessed in 1962 that the business he named Wal-Mart would grow to be the world's largest retail company. You've probably shopped at Walton's store many times yourself!

title: Culture Through Art
text:
Artists are important to a community. They entertain people, but they also help us understand our culture better. They create statues, photographs and paintings. Their artwork expresses the traditions of different people. These artists help us learn about how different cultures live, work and think. People see the artists' creations, and they are inspired. They can think about different cultures as they study and admire the work.

One important artist is Kadir Nelson. His illustrations and writings focus on African American culture and history. Carmen Lomas Garza has created art that honors the roots of her Texas Latino community. Gordon Parks was an artist who used photography to share his culture. Artists challenge people to study themselves through art.

title: Futuristic Field Trips
text:
Most students look forward to going on class field trips. Adventures to museums, plays or educational exhibits can be so much fun. Until recently, teachers had to load their students into buses to take such exciting trips. Those trips cost a lot of money. Today, though, technology makes it possible for teachers to take their students on free virtual field trips every day if they choose.

Classrooms are often supplied with computers, digital cameras and sound equipment. Students use the internet to connect with people and places all over the world. They can see famous paintings, sculptures and exhibits. The best part is that students can learn about other people. They can see different cultures right from the desks in their own classroom.

title: Can You Make a Change?
text:
Good citizens care about their communities. They want people to be safe and happy living there. Sometimes people think their community could be better. Even young people like you can share ideas that could improve the lives of everyone. Maybe you have a way to keep people from littering. Perhaps you have a plan to keep children safer at the park. What can you do to convince others in the community to make a change?

There are many ways for citizens to share their ideas with others. Sometimes a letter to the editor of a community newspaper can spark others to make a change. You can even share your ideas at a community government meeting. Ask a parent or teacher to help you put your plan into action. Who knows ... you might have an idea that could make your community better than ever!

title: Main Idea and Details
text: Read the article “Celebrate Cultural Differences.” Identify the main idea of each subsection. List two or three details that support the main idea.

title: Let's Write
text: Pretend you are a dollar bill. Write a story about how you were earned. Describe three times you were spent. How did you feel when you were being saved? Who did you help when you were donated? Use a computer program to write your story. As you write, be sure to use correct capitalization, grammar, punctuation and spelling. Be sure you write in complete sentences. Add electronic illustrations. Read your story out loud to your classmates.

title: Think and Review
text:
1. What was the main idea of “Trade Brings Countries Together”?

2. What reasons can you give for sharing written ideas?

3. If your school gave a “Hero of the Year” award, what are three qualities the winner should always have?

4. How does your family celebrate your heritage? Be specific.

5. What is the theme of the article “Selling for Success”?

6. In your opinion, have computers made the world a better place or just a faster place? Use specific examples to support your answer.

7. Brainstorm a list of three changes that would make your community a better place. Explain one way you could get your ideas heard by other people.

title: Where In The World Are We? – Part One
text:
Asking where we are may seem like a silly question. We live in Texas. Isn’t that the answer? It is part of the answer, but there is more, and it is very interesting. Texas hasn’t always looked like it does now. The land has changed. The kinds of plants and animals living in Texas have changed. Even the weather has changed. Many of these changes took place over millions of years. Texas has changed a lot since people first lived here 12,000 years ago. Let’s take a look at some of the changes Texas has seen.

Did you know that some Texans live on land that was once the floor of an ancient sea? Thirty million years ago, the body of water we call the Gulf of Mexico covered most of the southern and southeastern parts of Texas. The rest of the state was dry most of the time. When it wasn’t dry, shallow seas covered it.

Texans who live near Burnet or Llano live on land geologists believe is some of the oldest land on Earth. Geologists are people who study the Earth. They call this area the Llano Uplift. While the rest of Texas was still under water, the land around Burnet and Llano was pushed up out of an ancient ocean.

Some Texans live on land where dinosaurs once roamed. About 113 million years ago, dinosaurs lived in the area around Glen Rose. The land we now know as Texas was closer to the equator and was much warmer. The land looked more like a jungle than what we see today. Petrified palm wood found in Texas is evidence of this. In fact, palm wood is the state stone.

In spite of what you may have seen in the movies, humans were not on Earth when the dinosaurs roamed Texas. Even though people were not around to see them, we know the dinosaurs were here by the fossils and footprints people have found. Some of the footprints are preserved in stone at Dinosaur Valley State Park near Glen Rose.

You might think we have to go back millions of years for Texas to look different from the way it looks today. Actually, you only have to go back about 12,000 years. That is when the Earth was near the end of the last great Ice Age. An Ice Age happens when the Earth’s temperature cools for a long period of time.

Strange animals made Texas their home during the last Ice Age. Some were carnivores (meat-eating animals), and some were herbivores (plant-eating animals). The giant Columbian Mammoth looked like a huge elephant. Saber-tooth cats, camels and long-horned bison roamed the land. People did live in Texas during this time. They hunted some of these animals. At Lake Lubbock Landmark, you can see where these early Texans hunted, killed and butchered Columbian Mammoths.

You’ve learned that you live in a state that has seen many changes. Now that we know a little about Texas’ past, let’s take a closer look at the Texas you know today.

title: Mapping the News
text:
Have you ever heard or read a news report about a certain place and wondered where it is? Mapping the news can help. This is a fun way to learn geography and keep up with things that are going on in the world at the same time. Here’s how it works: Your teacher will put a world map on a bulletin board in your classroom or in the hall. Once a week, students can bring in news articles to share with the class. (Ask your parents to help you with that part, especially if you get your news articles from the internet. Also, do some research before you get to class to get a general idea of where the place is located.) In class, talk about each article and the place where the event happened. Find that place on the world map, and mark it with a push pin or a sticker.

For example, let’s say your friend brings an article about a mountain climber who reaches the top of Mount Everest on the border between Tibet and Nepal. She found out that those two countries are in south Asia. That will help you find Mount Everest more quickly. Try mapping the news for several weeks. Then get into groups and make up a game that involves the places you mapped. Playing the game will help you remember what you learned. Have fun mapping the news!

title: Settling Texas: Deciding Where to Live and Grow
text:
We'll begin our study of Texas this year by trying to imagine how Texas used to be millions of years ago.

How did early Texans decide where to live? They usually picked a place where they could meet their basic needs. You remember that basic needs are food, clothing and shelter. When people first settled in Texas, they wanted to live close to water. This was the most important thing they needed to survive.

Many of the plants and animals needed for food also lived near the water. Materials from these plants and animals were also used to make clothes and build homes. That is why many settlements in Texas were on rivers or along the coasts. We call settlements that are close together clusters.

Living near a river gave early people an easy way to travel. American Indians and settlers used rivers, large creeks and the coast as a liquid highway. Living close to a waterway also made it easier for them to trade goods with other settlements.

Later in Texas history, some settlers found other ways to meet their needs for water. They dug shallow wells. These wells meant they did not have to live close to a river. When people learned how to drill deep into the Earth to reach water, they moved farther away from rivers.

As railroads were built, people also settled near railroads. Railroads made it easier to receive and ship goods.

Wherever people settled, they formed communities. Communities provided safety on the frontier. Living in a community helped people meet their needs for friendship and help in times of trouble.

Texas did not have large cities in the beginning. Most people lived in small communities and worked as farmers, ranchers, hunters or fishermen. Since there were very few stores, they made most of the things they needed. Families made their own clothes, their own furniture and even their own homes. Sometimes, they bought or traded goods to get the things they could not make.

Over time, more and more people moved to Texas. Some small towns became cities like Houston, San Antonio and El Paso. The discovery of electricity and inventions like the light bulb were first available in these cities. This made the cities popular places to live. Other new inventions created jobs, and most of these jobs were in cities. Families left their farms and ranches and moved to the cities for these new jobs. They also wanted to enjoy the modern conveniences cities offered. A convenience is something that makes life easier.

When Texas cities grew even larger, many people wanted to leave the crowded cities and go back to smaller communities. By then, most areas outside of the cities had electricity. These small communities also had good roads that made driving to the cities easier. People discovered it was possible to live in less crowded areas and still drive to their jobs in the cities.

Something else helped Texas grow. Texas is a good place for people to find jobs. It is also a place where people find their basic needs at a reasonable price. This is because Texas practices free enterprise. Free enterprise means that the government does not control how people operate their businesses. And that means businesses have to compete for customers. To get new customers, businesses will work harder to give the best service and the best products. When businesses compete, prices are lower and quality is higher. That is good news for consumers in Texas!

As you can see, Texas has the resources people need to survive. It also has a long history of practicing free enterprise. These are two important reasons why people choose to make Texas home.

Finding A Big State In A Big World

Finding Texas is like observing an object in a science activity. You begin by looking at the object with the naked eye. Let's begin by looking at the top half of the Earth. This half is the Northern Hemisphere. The bottom half is the Southern Hemisphere. The line that divides these hemispheres is the equator. Texas is in the Northern Hemisphere. This means that Texas is north of the equator.

Next, picture the Earth sliced in two equal halves from top to bottom. The halves are called the Eastern and Western hemispheres. North America is in the Western Hemisphere. Since Texas is part of North America, it is in the Western Hemisphere.

Imagine taking a closer look at the Earth using a hand lens. This time, we will look for the continent of North America. When you have found North America, you are close to finding Texas.

Now imagine looking for Texas through a microscope. With the low power lens, we will find the southern half of North America. Most of this land is the United States of America. Texas is one of its 50 states. With so many states, how do we find Texas?

The United States is divided into geographic regions. A geographic region is an area of land with similar land features and climate. It can also have similar plants and animals. Texas is found in the southwestern part of the United States.

Using a stronger lens on our imaginary microscope, we see that Texas borders the country of Mexico. Another important Texas border is the Gulf of Mexico. Oklahoma borders Texas to the north. New Mexico borders us to the west and Louisiana borders us to the east. Arkansas borders a small piece of northeast Texas.

Looking at Texas in these different ways helps us to understand our state's place in the world. As we end our search, we now know how to find Texas on any map or globe.

title: Texas: Its Low and High Points
text:
The Coastal Plains and Mountains and Basins regions of Texas are at opposite ends of the state. Together, they show some of the ways land in Texas can be very different.

The Coastal Plains region stretches along the Gulf of Mexico. As you can see on the map, it also includes the eastern part of Texas. The land in the Coastal Plains region is mostly flat near the Gulf of Mexico. Some of this land is swampy, but it becomes hilly as you travel inland. Rainfall in the Coastal Plains can be very different. Beaumont receives about 58 inches a year. Brownsville gets about 27.5 inches a year.

The main industries of the Coastal Plains are ranching, farming and fishing. People in this region may also work in petroleum, poultry or timber industries.

The Mountains and Basins region is in far west Texas. Mexico borders it to the west. New Mexico borders it to the north. This area is also known as the Chihuahuan Desert or the Big Bend region. Some places in this area receive only eight inches of rain a year. Others receive as much as 20 inches. The Mountains and Basins region has the only mountains in the state. Guadalupe Mountain is the highest point in Texas. It is 8,749 feet high. The low land between mountains is called a basin. Many desert plants like cacti, yuccas and agaves grow here. While most of this region is dry and hot, the tops of some mountains have cool forests with many pine trees. Cougars and black bears live in these forests.

The main industries of the Mountains and Basins region are sheep, goat and cattle ranching. Tourism is also an important industry. People come to this region to enjoy outdoor activities like camping and hiking. When it comes to the regions of Texas, there are no low points. Every place is highly interesting.

title: Texas Ingenuity: The Galveston Seawall and Beyond
text:
Perhaps you have visited Galveston, a great vacation spot in the Coastal Plains region, and seen the Seawall that stretches ten miles down the beach. It’s hard to believe that Galveston was nearly wiped out by the deadliest natural disaster in U.S. history, the Great Storm of 1900.

In 1890, Galveston was the largest city in Texas because of its busy port. But on September 8, 1900, a hurricane swamped Galveston. More than 6,000 people were caught off guard and drowned in the 15-foot waves.

However, Texans have always been known for their ingenuity (finding inventive ways to solve problems). The city leaders built a seawall 17 feet high and three miles long. They also had sand dredged from the ocean floor and raised the level of the entire city by moving the buildings on top of the sand. Their efforts were so successful that when a similar hurricane struck in 1915, only eight people from Galveston died.

The Seawall helped Galveston weather many storms, but on September 13, 2008, waves from Hurricane Ike washed over Galveston Island from the bay side, flooding the city again. President George W. Bush declared an emergency in Texas, which helped thousands of people leave before the hurricane struck.

Hurricane Ike caused much property damage and concern about future storms. Once again, Texans are stepping up to the challenge. Dr. Bill Merrell of Texas A&M University at Galveston has designed a proposal called the Ike Dike. His plan includes floodgates and sand-covered dunes with hardened cores to protect cities like Galveston and Houston. Alicia Cahill, Galveston’s Public Information Officer, says, “The Seawall did its job, but Ike triggered a significant evaluation of coastal protective measures.” Some people are concerned about the cost of this project and what it might do to the environment, so Texans are studying the best ways to deal with future hurricane threats. That’s Texas ingenuity!

title: Mapping Your School
text: Create a map of your school below. Draw as many places as you can, and write the names of each place. Label the places that most or all of the students in your school need to be able to find (like the library and the office). You don’t have to label all of the classrooms, but be sure to label yours!

title: Let's Write
text: Write a letter to a group of people in Europe who pretend to be Texas cowboys on the weekends. Tell them about the Texas you know. Describe how the land looks and what the weather is like. Name the animals and plants you see. Finally, tell them what your life in Texas is really like. Try to write a paragraph for each of these four areas.

title: The Midwest Region
text:
The states in the Midwest Region are different from the rest of the nation. They are relatively flat. They feature fertile soil, big rivers, and thousands of lakes. They also get a lot of tornadoes.

Three of the largest rivers in the U.S. criss-cross the Midwest. The Missouri River, the Mississippi River, and the Ohio River help drain the lands. Parts of the region get heavy rainfall in the spring and summer. These rivers carry that water away. Both the Missouri and the Ohio are tributaries of the Mississippi. That means they flow into the Mississippi, which eventually flows south into the Gulf of Mexico.

The Great Lakes are an important physical feature of the Midwest. The term "great" is no exaggeration. They are so big that at their widest points, you cannot see the other side. Lakes Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, and Superior hold more than 80 percent of the freshwater in the United States. These five lakes provide drinking water for 48 million Americans and Canadians. They have a big impact on the economy of the Midwest, too. More than $50 billion is spent on recreation at all the lakes each year. Fishing and boating are two of the biggest activities. It is estimated that more than one million jobs are somehow connected to these massive lakes.

There is a lot of fertile soil in the area. Where does it come from? The rivers provide it. Regular flooding deposits nutrients into the soil. Unfortunately, it also creates headaches for people who live along the rivers. People have tried to control flooding, but it seems to happen every year.

The Midwest is not entirely flat. South Dakota’s Black Hills feature the rugged Badlands National Park. Rolling hills can be found in many states. Some of these are the remains of glaciers. As glaciers inched forward thousands of years ago, they left their mark on much of the Midwest.

Flat land can make for good farming. It also seems to get a lot of wind. Many states have fields of wind turbines that produce electricity as they spin. Other types of wind common to the Midwest are not so helpful. Tornadoes are a dangerous menace across the Midwest. While they have been known to strike in nearly every state, they seem to occur frequently in this region, especially during the months of May and June.

Tornadoes have the most violent winds on Earth. Although they are much smaller than hurricanes, wind speeds in a tornado are often higher than in a hurricane. Tornado winds can go over 300 miles per hour. That’s enough to completely level buildings, uproot trees, and toss cars around like toys. While hurricanes move slowly over a large area, tornadoes move quickly. Some are very wide, while others are narrow. They don’t follow a specific path, so they are very unpredictable. When a tornado strikes neighborhoods, it can completely destroy some houses while leaving others untouched.

Tornadoes form in the lower half of the Midwest because that’s where moist air from the Gulf of Mexico and cooler air from Canada collide. The Midwest deals with more tornadoes than most areas of the United States. Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas, for example, are a few states with frequent tornadoes. The Midwest state with the fewest tornadoes is also the northernmost state. Michigan gets about 14 a year.

title: Atlantic Coastal Plain
text:
If you leave the beaches of the Southeast and head west, the land stays flat for miles. You will not see any hills or mountains in this area. This area that borders the Atlantic Ocean to the west is called a plain. A plain is a landform that is a large area of flat land. Plains near oceans are called coastal plains. The Atlantic Coastal Plain begins at the eastern edge of the Piedmont and ends at the beach. The Atlantic Coastal Plain is considered all of the flat land between the Atlantic Ocean and the Piedmont Plateau. The Atlantic Coast Plain stretches for hundreds of miles, bordering the beaches of the Southeast Region.

An easy way to picture this is to imagine a ramp. The Appalachian Mountains would be the highest point, at the top of the ramp. Next would be the Piedmont, with its rolling hills and plateaus. At the bottom of the ramp, you would find the flat land of the Atlantic Coastal Plains. The Atlantic Coastal Plains were formed over millions of years. Rocks and dirt from the mountains were slowly moved east by weather, rivers, and erosion. The rocks and dirt settle at the Atlantic Ocean, forming the flat landscape we see today. The Atlantic Coastal Plains stretch over 2,000 miles, from Cape Cod, Massachusetts, all the way down to the southern tip of Florida!

title: Ecosystems of the Northeast
text:
The Northeast Region of the United States has many different ecosystems. An ecosystem is a group of living and nonliving things that depend on each other. The living things are plants, trees, animals, and insects. The nonliving things are soil, water, air, and even sunlight. An ecosystem can be as large as a huge lake or as small as a single drop of water. They can also be as large as a forest or as small as a single log on the ground. The forests of the Northeast are the largest ecosystems found there. Nearly half the land in the Northeast Region is covered in different types of trees! From the western border, on the Great Lakes, to the beaches of the Atlantic Ocean, all the states in the Northeast are covered with forests. There are also freshwater ecosystems like wetlands, lakes, ponds, streams, and rivers. Many beaches make up the main type of marine ecosystems of the Northeast. Let's take a look at each and find out where they are located and what animals and plants they have.

Forests

What do you think of when you hear the word "forest"? Trees, of course! Different types of trees make up most of what can be found in the forest ecosystem. There are also many animals in the Northeast Region's forest ecosystem. Can you name any animals you would find in the forest in the Northeast Region? There are bears, deer, squirrels, raccoons, chipmunks, and mountain lions. That's only naming a few! There are even moose in Maine! There are also many types of birds, insects, reptiles, and amphibians found in the forest of the Northeast Region.

Wetlands

A wetland is an area that has shallow water either year-round or for just part of the year. Wetlands can be bogs, swamps, or marshes. They can be found in flat lands that are often around water features like lakes, rivers, and the ocean. They are often flooded by rains or ocean tides. They keep part of the water in their soil. Trees don't do very well in the wetlands because there is too much water. Plants, shrubs, and grasses will get more sunlight without the trees covering them and will grow well. Since these areas are so wet, many mammals do not live there, besides beavers and deer. Instead of mammals, many different types of amphibians and reptiles can be found in wetlands. Snakes, turtles, salamanders, and newts thrive in wetlands. Many plant species that thrive in water also can be found here. These plants actually help the wetlands to stay wet by stopping the water from draining away.

Lakes, ponds, rivers, and streams are all freshwater ecosystems. They are found all over the Northeast Region. Many different types of fish are found here. There are also many types of plants that grow in freshwater. Lily pads, grasses, shrubs, and bushes all grow in freshwater.

Beaches

A beach is a marine ecosystem. A marine ecosystem has saltwater instead of freshwater. Beaches are all along the coast of the Northeast region. Crabs, starfish, lobsters, clams, sharks, and even dolphins are all part of the marine ecosystem. Many types of birds are also found here, including pelicans and sandpipers. A common plant found here is kelp. No matter which ecosystem you may visit in the Northeast, you are sure to find many different and exciting plants, animals, birds, and fish.

title: Rainforests of the West
text:
It takes a lot of rain in a region to create a rainforest: about 75 inches a year! One-third of the world's rainforests are in the country of Brazil. Those are tropical rainforests. But did you know that we have temperate rainforests right here in America? Several of them are in the west. The largest rainforest in the United States is in Alaska! Did you ever imagine that a rainforest could also have glacial fjords? The Tongass National Forest does. It runs for 500 miles along the coast of Alaska and borders Canada. Tongass landscape is rich with wildlife. Plants and animals are supported by thousands of streams and trees.

Chugach National Forest in Alaska has a large population of bald eagles. Hamakua Coast is a rainforest on Hawaii's Big Island. Mount Hood Wilderness is in Oregon, and Hoh Rainforest is in Washington State. Finally, the Redwood National Park, which is also a rainforest, is in northern California.

title: Taking a Peek at the Peaks
text:
Mountains, forests, and deserts are what most people picture when they think of the western region of the United States. The West features huge, snow-capped mountains. Three mountain ranges in this region form a huge oval shape. These ranges are the Cascades, the Rockies, and the Sierra Nevada. The largest of these mountain ranges is the Rocky Mountains. The Rockies range is over 3,000 miles long. It stretches through the eastern part of this region, through Canada, then all the way up to the north of Alaska. The mountains cover the states of Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico in the western region. The states that the Rockies go through are called the "mountain states." The Rockies are over 300 miles wide at their widest point. The Rockies are so large that they are split into over 100 smaller ranges, called sub-ranges. Pikes Peak, in Colorado, is the second-most-visited peak in the world, after Mount Fuji, in Japan. Although Pikes Peak is one of the most famous peaks in America, it is not the highest. Mount Denali in Alaska is the tallest peak in the U.S. The Rockies have so many tall mountain peaks that to list them, people often just group all the peaks together in a list called "the fourteeners." These are all peaks that are above 14,000 feet.

The Cascade Mountain Range runs north to south along the Pacific Coast of the United States. The range is located east of the Pacific Coast. The Cascades pass through the states of California, Oregon, and Washington and north into Canada. The Cascades are over 700 miles long. The Cascades are part of a series of volcanoes forming the eastern edge of the Pacific Ring of Fire. The Pacific Ring of Fire is a group of volcanoes around the edge of the Pacific Ocean. Most of the volcanoes are dormant. However, some of these have erupted in the recent past. Mount Saint Helens erupted in 1980 and 1981. Mount Rainier, the highest point in Washington and in all of the Cascade Range, is "actively dormant." Mount Shasta, a dormant volcano on the southern end of the Cascades, is in California. Mount Hood, also a dormant volcano, is the highest peak in Oregon.

The Sierra Nevada Range picks up right where the Cascades drop off in northern California. This range is often simply called the Sierras. A small part of the Sierras is in Nevada. "Sierra Nevada" means "snow-capped mountain range" in Spanish. The Sierra Nevada Range is over 400 miles long. Mount Whitney in the Sierras stands 14,505 feet high and is the highest mountain in the lower 48 states. The Sierras also include Yosemite, Death Valley, and Sequoia National Parks, which are some of the most unique parks in the country. The famous Lake Tahoe is also part of the Sierras.

title: Southwest Deserts
text:
Two of the largest deserts in the United States are very different. One desert is tall and bushy.The other is low and sandy. The Sonoran and the Chihuahuan Deserts cover huge areas of land in the Southwest Region of the United States.

The Chihuahuan Desert is the largest desert in North America. It covers three of the four states in the Southwest Region. Half of this desert lies in Mexico, while the other half is in the United States. Unlike many other deserts around the world, this desert gets rain in the summer season. It is also cold in the winter. Also unlike many other deserts, this desert has many shrubs and bushes, not just sand. This desert is called a rain shadow desert. A rain shadow is a dry part of land that is protected from rain and wind because it is next to a mountain. The Rio Grande runs straight through the middle of this desert. The Rio Grande helps many of the shrubs in this desert stay alive in the dry months. Not only is this desert a rain shadow desert, but it is also considered a shrub desert. Most deserts are low, but this desert is at a higher elevation.

The Sonoran Desert is a huge desert that lies mostly in Mexico but extends into southern Arizona and southern California. The cacti that you might imagine, with their arms pointing up, live here. They are native to this place and nowhere else in the world. It is the hottest desert in all of North America. It is also the driest desert in the United States.

title: The Great Plains
text:
Given their name, you may wonder what makes the Great Plains so great. "The Great Plains" is the name given to a huge area of flat land stretching from southern Canada to Texas. The Great Plains run right through the middle of the United States. They almost cut our great country into two perfect halves, but not quite. That's an area of land of nearly half a million square miles!

A plain is any large area of flat land. The plains are also sometimes referred to as prairies. The Great Plains cover part of southern Canada and 10 states in the United States. In the Midwest Region of the United States, the Great Plains cover only four states: North and South Dakota, Kansas, and Nebraska. The Great Plains start at the Rocky Mountains in the west and continue to the Mississippi River in the east.

The Great Plains formed mostly because the ground was so flat between the Rocky Mountains in the west and the Appalachian Mountains in the east. Low amounts of rain and scorching sunlight make it hard for trees to grow. Tall and short grass varieties grow well in the Great Plains. The grasses on these plains die every year when the region experiences harsh winters. The dead grasses help to make the soil richer each year for new grasses to grow back in the spring.

The flat land and rich soil mean that the Great Plains have always been an excellent spot for farming. These tall and short grass species make the Great Plains an excellent home for many different types of wildlife. Bison, pronghorn, foxes, prairie dogs, bobcats, ferrets, and gophers are just some of the animals that call the Great Plains home. There are also 200 species of birds that live in the Great Plains. Many of these birds are small and colored to fit in well with the grass for camouflage. Blackbirds, buntings, meadowlarks, and sparrows are just some examples of these small birds that live in the Great Plains.

title: Natural Resources of the Northeast
text:
The year was 1776, and the Declaration of Independence had just been signed. The United States was trying to figure out how to run as an independent country. The 13 Colonies had been settled in what is now the Northeast region of the United States. The states that make up the Northeast region of the United States are Maryland, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Vermont, and Maine. Many of these states were part of the original 13 Colonies and the first places in which European settlers lived in the United States. This region is where our country’s economy began and has remained an important part of the U.S. economy ever since.

The 13 Colonies were established in the northeast because of the rich resources available there. Many of these resources are still available today and make it a desirable place for many businesses to grow. Some of our country's largest industries are from the Northeast. The Northeast is known for its large forest, found in the Appalachian Mountains, as well as its many fisheries because of its proximity to the Atlantic Ocean. The Northeast region also has very fertile soil, which is ideal for farming. Many businesses have opened up in the Northeast because of these natural resources. The increase in businesses led to an increase in jobs in this region.

Because of the abundance of natural resources in the Northeast region, many people have made the region their home. They had lumber to make their homes, fertile soil to grow their food and many rivers that made transporting goods between the states much easier. The Northeast Region of the United States also witnessed much of our country's rich history. This draws many visitors each year to learn about the beginnings of our country and to explore the beautiful landscape of the area. Cities like Philadelphia, New York City and Boston have many historical sites.

In addition to the many historical sites in the Northeast, visitors can also see some of the most well-known landmarks in our country. The Appalachian Mountains, with their many different hiking trails, stretch from Alabama all the way through Maine. Many visitors hike these trails, with some visitors hiking all 2,000 miles! All of these visitors help to boost the economy in the Northeastern states.

title: Natural Wonders
text:
There are some great things about living in the Southwest. Among them are wide-open spaces, where you can see everything for miles, from flat prairies to soaring mountains.

The Gulf of Mexico

Much of our weather in the region is influenced by the Gulf of Mexico. The warm Gulf water keeps the snow away from the southern parts of the region. The Gulf water also adds humidity, or moisture, to the air. Summer can be a bit sticky. Being located near the Gulf gives our region easy access to seafood. In addition to shrimp, crabs, and oysters, many types of fish are caught in Gulf waters. Ports along the Gulf in Texas provide easy shipping access for resources and products. Oil and gas wells dot the countryside and Gulf, pulling up oil from miles below the surface.

Natural Wonders

One of the Southwest’s most popular attractions is the Grand Canyon in Arizona. This colorful canyon runs nearly 300 miles and is almost 20 miles across at its widest point. Its average depth is almost 6,000 feet! People even ride down steep trails on mules. Float trips can be taken on the Colorado River. The natural wonders continue in New Mexico. Carlsbad Caverns National Park gives visitors a look at a cave system that stretches for miles. The caves are home to more than 300,000 bats during the spring and summer. New Mexico is also home to Shiprock, a natural rock formation located on the Navajo Nation. It helped guide settlers as they moved west. Shiprock soars more than 1,600 feet above the ground. It is considered a sacred site for the Navajo.

Climate Change

The Southwest is already a dry region. Climate change is what people are calling the changes in weather patterns that are happening all over the world. With the temperature increase on Earth, what could happen to our region? Some scientists believe it could get hotter and drier. That’s bad news for our agriculture industry. Farmers will have to think about what is grown and where it is grown. People will also have to think about new sources of water for everyday things.

title: Vacation Land
text:
If you were to ask someone the first thing they think of when they think of the Southeast region of the United States, they would probably answer, "The beaches!" Some of the best beaches in the entire country can be found in the southeast. Although this region includes 12 states, only eight of them have beaches. Can you name the states that do not have beaches? Look at the map of the states in the Southeast region that are not on the coast. They are called landlocked states. For most of the year, the beaches of the Southeast have warmer weather than the beaches of the Northeast. This helps the water in the Atlantic Ocean warm up quicker. Swimming season starts early on these beaches. Many people from the Northeast region head south to vacation and to experience summer temperatures and the beach earlier in the year. Let's look at some of the most visited beaches throughout the Southeast region.

Virginia Beach is on Virginia's southern coast. Virginia Beach is 35 miles long. It is close to many major cities along the east coast. The main beach sees millions of tourists from all over the world each year. The beach is lined with a boardwalk that has many places to eat and shop. There are also many other beaches in the area where you can go to get away from the crowds of the main beach.

The Outer Banks beaches of North Carolina are on a long string of islands off the coast. They are 200 miles long and cover most of the coastline of North Carolina. These beaches have some extreme weather since they are out in the ocean. There are five lighthouses on the islands to warn ships when they come too close to land.

Myrtle Beach, in South Carolina, has just over 60 miles of beaches. This 60-mile stretch of beaches is known as the "Grand Strand." Myrtle Beach sees over 14 million visitors a year, making it one of the most popular beaches in all of the Southeast Region.

Tybee Island is a small island on the mouth of the Savannah River in Georgia. The island is the most eastern part of Georgia. Tybee Island has beautiful beaches on the eastern side facing the Atlantic Ocean.

Key West, off the southern tip of Florida, may be the most well-known beach in all of America. Key West is the westernmost island in a string of islands to the south of Florida. It sits between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. The island is only four miles long and one mile wide and is surrounded on all sides by some of the most beautiful beaches in the world.

The next two beaches are on the Gulf Coast, not the Atlantic coast. The Gulf Coast has calmer waters, whiter sand and warmer waters than the Atlantic. Ship Island, in Mississippi, is an island 12 miles off the Gulf Coast. There are no roads out to the island, so the only way to get there is by boat. The island was split into two separate islands, west and east, by a hurricane in 1969. Some of the quietest and most beautiful beaches in Mississippi can be found on West Ship Island for travelers willing to take the boat ride.

Grand Isle is a tiny island off the coast of Louisiana in the Gulf of Mexico. The island has seven miles of quiet, beautiful beaches. Grand Isle has a road that you can drive from the mainland to get to the beach.

title: Natural Wonders in the U.S. and Texas
text:
There are many natural wonders. Let's explore some of the wonders that are in different regions of the U.S. and see if similar wonders can be found in Texas!

Rivers

Missouri

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. It covers much of the Great Plains, or Midwest Region. The Missouri River is slightly longer than the Mississippi River. The Missouri stretches from Montana to the Mississippi River, at Saint Louis, Missouri.

In Texas

Rivers that flow in Texas are not the longest in the country or in the Southwest Region, but the Río Grande is close, since it does cover over 1,880 miles. It stretches from the Mountains and Basins region in the west into the Great Plains and Coastal Plains regions towards the east.

Mountains

Appalachians

The Appalachian Mountains in North America cover a lot of land in the Northeast and some of the Southeast Region of the United States. This mountain range is the largest of the eastern half of the country, but the Rockies are the largest in the U.S. The Appalachians are famous for having lots of hiking trails.

In Texas

Most of Texas is flatland, such as the North Central and Great Plains regions. But the Mountain and Basins region in the west does have some mountains. The tallest mountain in the state is part of the Guadalupe Mountains and is called Guadalupe Peak. The Guadalupe Mountains range is many times smaller than the Appalachians in the eastern regions of the U.S.

Deserts

Mojave

The Mojave Desert is in the West and parts of the Southwest Regions. The Southwest is the main region Texas is in. The Mojave Desert is in California, Nevada, Utah, and Arizona. It is considered to have reached the hottest temperature in the world. This took place in a spot within the desert called Death Valley.

In Texas

The Chihuahuan Desert in the Mountain and Great Basins region can get hot, but the hottest temperature recorded in Texas is still pretty far from reaching temperatures in the Mojave Desert. Lower temperatures and more rain means the Chihuahuan Desert supports plant and animal life better than the Mojave.

title: A World of Natural Wonders
text:
Have you ever wondered how the geography of Texas compares with the United States and the rest of the world? Let's take a look at some features from regions of the U.S. and the world and how they compare with regions in Texas.

Rivers

Amazon and Nile

The longest rivers in the world are the Amazon and the Nile.

The Amazon River is the longest river in South America. The Amazon winds its way along the northern part of South America from Peru and drains into the Atlantic at a point found in northern Brazil.

Have you ever wanted to visit the Nile River? It is found along the northeastern side of the African continent. It flows northward for just over 4,000 miles, from Uganda and Ethiopia, and empties into the Mediterranean Sea. The Nile is the longest river in Africa.

Río Grande and Red River

Unlike the Amazon in South America or the Nile in Africa, the rivers that flow in Texas are not the longest in their region (North America). However, the Río Grande does cover over 1,880 miles, stretching from the Mountains and Basins region into the Great Plains and Coastal Plains regions. The river forms part of the border between Texas and Mexico.

The Red River is the second-longest in Texas and flows in the Great Plains, North Central Plains, and Coastal Plains regions, close to Oklahoma. The river has helped to keep much of the plains watered.

Mountains and Ranges

Alps and Himalayas

The Alps are the tallest mountain range in Europe. They are one of the most popular sites for skiing in the world.

The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia. The world’s tallest mountain, Mount Everest, is part of this range. Over the years, many people have attempted to scale Mount Everest to reach its summit, but it's dangerous because of its high altitude and because the peaks are always covered with snow.

Guadalupe Mountains

Most of Texas has many flatlands, but the Mountains and Basins region in the west does have some mountains. The tallest mountain in the state is part of the Guadalupe Mountains and is called Guadalupe Peak. The Guadalupe Mountain range is many times smaller than the Alps in Europe and Himalayas in Asia.

Deserts

Gobi and Sahara

The Gobi Desert is located in the northern part of Asia, in Mongolia and China. It is actually a fairly cold desert.

The Sahara, which covers most of North Africa, is the largest hot desert on Earth. Despite the extreme heat and lack of water, people and animals have still been able to live in the Sahara thanks to a few oases and the northern highlands.

Chihuahuan Desert

The Chihuahuan Desert takes up parts of western Texas in the Great Basin and Mountains region. It is also in New Mexico, Arizona, and Mexico. This region has differences and similarities with the Sahara and the Gobi. The Chihuahuan Desert is smaller than both deserts. It can be really hot or really cold. It rains more there than in the Gobi and the Sahara deserts.

Bodies of Water

Mediterranean Sea

The Mediterranean Sea is a sea almost entirely surrounded by continental land. To its north is Europe, south is Africa, and to its east is Asia. Some of the earliest human civilizations formed around the Mediterranean.

Gulf of Mexico

Texas has just one body of water, off the coast of the Coastal Plains region to the southeast. It's called the Gulf of Mexico. It's located between North and South America. Like the Mediterranean Sea, the Gulf of Mexico is almost totally surrounded by land. One difference is that the Mediterranean Sea is wide, while the Gulf of Mexico has a nearly round shape.

Landforms

Great Barrier Reef

Found along the northeast coast of Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on our planet. A coral reef is made up of living organisms that have symbiotic (mutually beneficial) relationships with the algae found in the ocean water around it. The Great Barrier Reef is home to many species of fish and other marine life.

East Flower Garden Bank and West Flower Garden Bank

Off the coast of the Coastal Plains region, many coral reefs call the Gulf of Mexico home. The East Flower Garden Bank and West Flower Garden Bank are some of the best. They are smaller than other reefs, but like the Great Barrier Reef, these reefs have many different types of sea life living in them.

Niagara Falls

These falls can be found along the border between the U.S. and Canada. Niagara Falls is actually a series of three waterfalls, which are called Horseshoe Falls, American Falls, and Bridal Veil Falls.

Capote Falls

Texas does have waterfalls in many regions throughout the state, but they are much smaller than Niagara Falls. The tallest is Capote Falls, located in the Mountains and Basins region.

title: A World of Difference in One State
text:
If you've never traveled around Texas, you might not know how much it changes from one place to another. There is a world of difference in Texas when you look at its land, climate, plants and animals. In most states, people have to leave their state to see mountains, deserts, pine forests, beaches or prairie grasslands that stretch for miles. Texas has all of these and more. As you will see, Texas is where many major regions of the United States and Mexico come together in one big place.

Beaches and Ocean Waters

Since Texas is on the Gulf of Mexico, it has beaches like some of the other coastal states. States on the East Coast have beaches along the Atlantic Ocean. States on the West Coast have beaches along the Pacific Ocean.

Giant Pine Trees

Texas has tall pine forests like Arkansas and Louisiana. The trees in the Piney Woods of Texas are so tall that you have to look straight up to see the sky. This area has something no other place has. Deep in the Piney Woods is an area known as the Big Thicket. Biologists think there is no other place like it on Earth. Biologists are people who study living things. They think the Big Thicket is unusual because of the wide variety of plants that grow there.

Miles and Miles of Grassland

Texas also has grasslands like the states in the Great Plains. The panhandle of Texas is the southern edge of the Great Plains. This part of Texas looks like Oklahoma, Kansas, Nebraska and the Dakotas. There are very few trees in this area, and the land can be flat or hilly. This area also has a large canyon. Palo Duro Canyon is not as large as the Grand Canyon, but it is so interesting that people travel there for their vacations.

Deserts and Mountains

The desert in West Texas is similar to the deserts of New Mexico and Arizona. The only mountains in Texas are found in West Texas. The tallest mountain in Texas is Guadalupe Peak. It is 8,749 feet high! The tops of some of the mountains in Texas are covered with alpine forests.

Choose Your Weather

The weather in Texas can also be different, depending on where you are in the state. People living in East Texas and along the coast average about one inch of rain every week. In the West Texas desert, the rainfall can average less than one inch a month.

In the winter, people living in North Texas and the panhandle may see bitterly cold weather with snow and ice. Their weather is like the weather in many northern states. On that same day, people living near Brownsville may have weather so warm they can wear summer clothes and even go to the beach. Just like in Florida and southern California, the warm weather during the winter makes it possible for them to grow tall palm trees and fruit trees like orange and grapefruit.

Texas is for the Birds - All Kinds of Birds

Birds are a good example of how varied animal life in Texas can be. Since the weather in Brownsville is warm most of the year, it is not unusual for people to see parrots in their backyard trees. That is because the subtropical region of Mexico reaches into south Texas. Farther up the coast, the rare whooping crane makes its winter home. Speaking of winter homes, some bald eagles wait out the cold along the Colorado River near Burnet.

Products from Texas are Everywhere!

Texas oil - it's more important than you think. When you think of how oil is used, you probably think about cars and trucks. Get ready for a surprise! Oil is used to make things you never thought of.

Oil is used in making clothes. Some of the clothes you are wearing probably came from oil. Scientists have learned to make fibers from oil. These fibers can also be used to make items like towels and sheets.

Oil is also used in food. It is used to make preservatives. Preservatives are added to food to keep it fresh longer. Don't forget to add toothpaste to this list of things you put in your mouth that are made from oil.

Oil is used to make dishwashing liquids, contact lenses, shampoo and toys. Be sure to tell your mom that it's also used in making her lipstick. You will really make her happy when you tell her it's used in her perfume.

We've only listed a few of the many things that are made from oil. That black stuff beneath the ground is important to people around the world. Imagine what life would be like without oil.

They Do All of That With Cottonseeds?

Cottonseeds are used in daily life more than most people know. Businesses in Lubbock take cottonseeds and make them into many different products. Get ready for more surprises.

The mattress you sleep on may be stuffed with material made from cottonseeds. Cottonseeds are also used to make paper and plastics. Fertilizer, fish bait and feed for livestock also contain cottonseed products. The oil from the seeds is used in many snack foods. Think about that the next time you are enjoying a snack.

Now you know some of the amazing ways Texas oil and cotton are used to improve our lives.

title: I Didn’t Know That About Texas!
text:
Most Texans can tell you where to find the nearest shopping mall or discount store. Very few people know about the ancient forces that made Texas what it is today. Let's take a look at some of these forces.

Texas Blew Its Top?

It sure did. Texas once had volcanoes. They are extinct now, but you can still see what is left of them. When you drive on Highway 90 between Marfa and Alpine, you are driving where a giant volcano erupted 35 million years ago. There were also volcanoes in central Texas. One of these volcanoes was near Austin. If you visit McKinney Falls State Park, you can see Pilot Knob. Pilot Knob is all that is left of an ancient volcano.

An Underground Mountain Range?

It's true. Texas once had a giant mountain range in the middle of the state. What is left of that mountain range is buried along a line that stretches from Del Rio to San Antonio. It then stretches north to Austin and Waco. Three hundred million years ago, these mountains were giants. Geologists call them the Ouachita Mountains. It took about 200 million years for the Ouachita Mountains in Texas to erode, or wear away. They are still above ground in Oklahoma and Arkansas.

Is Texas on Shaky Ground?

They do not happen very often, but Texas does have earthquakes. These earthquakes occur along fault lines. A fault line is a crack in the Earth’s surface where two plates meet. Sometimes these plates move, causing an earthquake. At the Meadows Center, near San Marcos, you can see the effects of the Balcones Fault. A glass-bottom boat takes you into a clear lake. You can see hundreds of springs below the water.

Did you know all of this about Texas? With a state so large, there is a lot to learn.

title: The Great and Central Plains Regions
text:
The Great Plains Region

The Great Plains sweep down the middle of North America into the Texas Panhandle. We also call the upper part of the Great Plains region in Texas the High Plains. It is part of the Great Plains of the United States.

Geologists think soil eroded, or washed down, from the Rocky Mountains millions of years ago and formed the Great Plains region. This land is mostly flat with very few trees. It gets about 12-33 inches of rain each year.

Some very interesting land features are found in the Great Plains region. Palo Duro Canyon is southeast of Amarillo. The Alibates Flint Quarry is northeast of Amarillo. It was here that American Indians found the flint they needed to make tools.

Important industries are in the Great Plains region. Farmers near Lubbock grow cotton. The Midland and Odessa area leads the state in the production of oil and natural gas. Ranching is also a part of the Great Plains economy in Texas.

The Central Plains Region

The North Central Plains region is full of variety. Some places are nearly flat with very few trees. Other areas have beautiful hills with scenic views and many trees. Rainfall varies from about 20 inches per year in the southern part of the region to about 30 inches per year in the northern part.

The famous Texas Hill Country is in the North Central Plains region. Every spring, tourists flock to the Hill Country to see the wildflowers in bloom, especially the bluebonnet. The bluebonnet is the state flower. People also come to this area to hunt white tail deer. About half the white tail deer in Texas are found in Hill Country. Both tourism and hunting are important to the economy of the North Central Plains. Other industries include raising sheep for wool near San Angelo. San Saba is famous for its pecan groves. The pecan is the state tree. Fort Worth is the center for the ranching industry.

The Great Plains and North Central Plains regions are examples of how both older and modern industries are still important to the Texas economy.
