title: Fact or Fiction: You Decide
text:
Have you ever had engine oil on your hands or clothes? If so, you know it is messy stuff and hard to clean up. Scientists have discovered bacteria that eat oil. You’ve got it — that gooey oil is the diet of a little critter. When oil is accidentally spilled in the ocean, bacteria can help clean it up.

Now it’s time for you to decide. Is this fact or fiction?

title: How Texas Oil Changed the Life of a Pioneer Girl
text:
Florence Childress lived a life we will never know. Her home was a dugout in the side of a hill in the little railroad town of Taiban, New Mexico. The walls, floor and ceiling were all made of dirt. Her family raised chickens for money, but they were still poor. They did not own a car and walked everywhere they went.

Florence described life in her dugout. "Rats, mice and bugs crawled inside our dugout to get out of the hot sun. Snakes looking for food came right behind them. We were always finding snakes in our dugout.

"Our dugout had no electricity or running water. Even when my mother tucked us into bed at night, there were problems. Dirt was always falling from the ceiling. While we slept, it fell on our heads. When we woke up, it was in our hair and mouths. We had to shake the dirt off our sheets every morning. Of course, we had to worry about snakes crawling into bed with us."

When Florence's father heard that oil had been discovered at Spindletop, he decided to move his family there. Her father went to work for the Gulf Oil Company.

Florence's home must have seemed like a palace compared to the dugout in Taiban. The Gulf Oil Company built a community of homes for its workers and their families to live in. They were small and plain. "The houses were shanties," Florence said, "but they were better than a dugout."

Even with her father's new job, her family had very little money. "My parents could not afford to buy new shoes when I outgrew the old ones," Florence said. "Going barefoot in the busy streets around Spindletop was too dangerous, so I wore the old ones. To get my feet into the old shoes, I had to bend my toes over one another. After years of doing this, I couldn't straighten them out anymore."

With so little money, Florence didn't have many toys. "I planted flowers for fun. One of our neighbors had a beautiful flower garden in her front yard. She pulled up flowers she didn't want and threw them into the street. I picked them up and planted them in our yard." Growing flowers was a hobby she enjoyed for the rest of her life.

Florence also told about a time when she was bored. "I asked my sister, Alma, to lie down on the bed one afternoon. I took a pair of scissors and cut off her eyebrows and eyelashes."

While living at Spindletop, Florence's brother died and her father was killed in an oilfield accident. "Those were very sad times, but our family wasn't alone. Life back then was harder and more dangerous. Work in the oil fields was very dangerous, and doctors didn't know as much as they do today. There were many families who lost a loved one to accidents and illness."

Pioneers like Florence's family worked very hard and had very little. Their struggles, however, brought about great changes in the world that made life better.

One hundred years later, people around the world still know where to find Texas on a map. They need products Texans make. Oil products and technologies from Texas are used all around the world. Later in this issue, we will look at some of the ways oil and other Texas products are making life better for people today.

title: Texas Oil Changes the World
text:
In 1901, people around the world knew where Texas was. For many years, Texas was famous because people loved stories about the Wild West. When oil was discovered at Spindletop in 1901, Texas became important for another reason. Texas oil was about to change the world.

Oil made transportation faster and easier. Plenty of oil in Texas helped the automobile replace the horse and buggy. It played an important part in the invention of the airplane. To make all of this happen, Texans left their pioneer way of life to bring Texas and the world into a new age.

This brought more people to Texas. With more people came more jobs but more challenges to maintain clean air and water. To protect natural habitats, Texans built wind farms, established sanctuaries for endangered animals and took steps to improve water and air quality.

You are growing up in a world that has already been changed by oil. Life before Texas oil might be hard for you to imagine. To help us understand this important change, let's look at the life of one girl who left a pioneer way of life because of Texas oil.

title: Using a Map
text:
Map Features

Maps are wonderful tools. They often show details about areas on the Earth.

Maps contain several features, including the compass rose, the legend, and the scale. Those are all map elements that have important information. The compass rose shows us the directions north, south, east, and west. The legend shows us what the symbols and colors mean on the map. The scale helps us figure out how far it is from one place to another.

Relative Location

The relative location tells us where a place is compared to, or relative to, something else. If your friend tells you that his house is "down the street and across from the supermarket," he's using relative location. People often use stores, buildings, or other features to give relative locations.

Absolute Location

The absolute location of a place is its exact location. Absolute location is more helpful when you are trying to find a place you are not familiar with. Absolute location in a city could be an address, like 2536 W State Street. People often use lines of latitude and longitude to find an absolute location.

Longitude

Lines of longitude refer to imaginary lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole.

Latitude

Lines of latitude refer to imaginary lines that run from east to west around the Earth.

title: Grid Maps and More
text:
What way should we go? Have you ever asked your parents or friends for directions? People are very helpful when giving directions. Another great resource to help us go in the right direction is a map. Maps are pictures of specific areas that show the major landmarks of the area. They also show how places are related to each other by distance and direction. There are many types of maps. People have even mapped things like the ocean, the mountains, and even the stars. One of the most common types of maps is the general-purpose map. This type of map shows landmarks, such as cities, roads, large rivers, and lakes. If your family has ever gone on a vacation, this is the type of map your mom or dad uses. It would help guide your family to your final destination. This type of map is also what you would find on a phone app.

Another common type of map is a topographical map. This is what we would use when going on a hike in a forest or on a mountain. A topographical map shows details about the land. It tells how high and steep hills are. It shows where rivers and other important natural features are in the landscape. You would want to have this type of map if you are ever going on a long hike in an area that you are not very familiar with.

One important part of using any map is understanding directions and how they are related to places on the map. The most common way we can do this is by using cardinal directions. North, south, east, and west are the cardinal directions. In between each of those are the intermediate directions: northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest. When we look at a map of the state of Louisiana, we can see that cites are located all across the state. On the map, we can see that Baton Rouge is in the southeast corner of the state. Shreveport is in the northwest corner of the state. Now, see if you can use intermediate directions to identify what portion of the state New Orleans is in. Can you describe what direction Natchitoches is from New Orleans? Try another one: what direction is Lake Charles from the city of Monroe? Practice using intermediate directions in your daily life to describe directions to the store, a park, or even a friend’s house.

Another way maps can be laid out is by using a simple grid system. A grid divides the map into a number of equal-sized squares, creating rows and columns across the map. These rows and columns each have numbers and letters. The user of the map can locate places on the map by finding the number and letter of its location. On the grid map shown, what is the letter and number of the post office?

Maps are important tools we use to help find our way from one location to another. Now that you have learned about maps and directions, practice looking at maps and finding fun and new places you would like to go someday!

title: Can You Read a Map?
text:
Globes and Maps

You have seen both round globes and flat maps of the world. What is the difference between the two? Both a round globe and a flat map of the world show the same cities, countries, oceans, and landforms, but they are useful in different ways.

A globe is a round map of the world. A globe shows the Earth in its round form, just as it is in real life, only smaller. By using a globe, you can see how the Earth rotates, or turns, and where each country is in relation to other countries.

A flat map shows the same cities, countries, oceans, and landforms as a globe, but it allows us to see the entire world all at once, rather than in sections, as with a globe. You can only see one side of a globe at a time, but when the globe is flattened out into a map, you can see everything at one time.

Parts of a Map

Maps include more than just countries, cities, oceans, and landforms. Maps also include many special tools that help you to find what you are looking for. Each map has a title at the top. The title of a map tells what location, or place, the map shows. Some maps will be titled "Map of the World," "United States of America," "Landforms of the United States," or "Map of Texas."

Compass Rose

All maps have a compass rose, or a drawing showing the directions on the map. The compass rose always shows the cardinal directions. Cardinal directions are north, south, east, and west. North is always at the top of the compass rose, east is on the right, south is at the bottom, and west is on the left.

The compass rose also shows something called the intermediate directions. Intermediate directions are the directions directly between the cardinal directions. The intermediate directions are northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest. By looking at the compass rose, you can find out exactly where each item on the map is located.

Legend

The legend of the map is a key that lists all of the symbols on a map. These symbols stand for things such as the streets, rivers, monuments, parks, buildings, capital cities, and schools. The legend of the map helps you to know what each symbol on the map means.

Scale

Another tool used on a map is a scale. A map's scale shows the distance represented on the map. One inch on the map will be equal to an actual distance in miles. For example, an inch on the map may be equal to 1,000 real miles.

Political Maps

Some maps show the boundaries between countries, states, or provinces. These maps often show the major cities found within those areas. They also mark the separation between the governments of the world. Since these maps focus on the political parts of the world, they are called political maps. For example, the political map of North America shows the boundaries between countries like Canada, the United States, and Mexico. Each country is usually indicated by a different color. This makes it easy to see where one country ends and another begins, just like on this map.

Physical Maps

Mapmakers create other maps to show the physical features (characteristics of a place) of an area. This includes landforms or major bodies of water. We call these physical maps. For instance, the physical map of the United States shows the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans. It also shows the islands of Hawaii, the Rocky Mountains, the five Great Lakes, and the Mississippi River. Many times, physical maps will also include varying colors to indicate elevations of the land and landforms. On the map, the highest points on the mountains are a darker green than the lower lying area of the Great Plains. This allows us to easily see the changes in elevation.

People use maps for a variety of reasons. Most often, people use maps to plan a route, find their way, or locate a specific place, landmark, or landform. In your study of history, geography, and social studies, you will be using maps to help you find out where things are and how they relate to each other.

title: Geographic Tools
text:
Globes and Maps

You have seen both round globes and flat maps of the world. What is the difference between the two? Both a round globe and a flat map of the world show the same cities, countries, oceans, and landforms, but they are useful in different ways.

A globe is a round map of the world. A globe shows the Earth in its round form, just as it is in real life, only smaller. By using a globe, you can see how the Earth rotates, or turns, and where each country is in relation to other countries.

A flat map shows the same cities, countries, oceans, and landforms as a globe, but it allows us to see the entire world all at once. You can only see one side of a globe at a time, but when the globe is flattened out into a map, you can see everything all at one time.

Parts of a Map

Maps include more than just countries, cities, oceans, and landforms. Maps also include many special tools that help you to find what you are looking for. Each map has a title at the top. The title of a map tells what location, or place, the map shows. Some maps that you may be using this year will be titled Map of the World, United States of America, Landforms of the United States, or Map of Texas.

Compass Rose

All maps have a compass rose, or a drawing showing the directions on the map. The compass rose always shows the cardinal directions, which are north, south, east, and west. North is always at the top of the compass rose, east is on the right, south is at the bottom, and west is on the left.

The compass rose also shows something called the intermediate directions. Intermediate directions are the directions directly between the cardinal directions. The intermediate directions are northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest. By looking at the compass rose, you can find out exactly where each item on the map is located.

Legend

The legend of the map is a key that lists all of the symbols on a map. These symbols stand for things such as the streets, rivers, monuments, parks, buildings, capital cities, and schools. The legend of the map helps you to know what each symbol on the map means.

Scale

Another tool used on a map is a scale. A map's scale shows the distance represented on the map. One inch on the map will be equal to an actual distance in miles. For example, an inch on the map may be equal to 1,000 real miles.

Grid System

Some maps use a grid system, or a system of numbered and lettered lines, to help you find places more easily. On a map that uses a grid system, there will be letters, such as A, B, C, etc., running across the top of the map and numbers, such as 1, 2, 3, etc., running down the side of the map. If you know that a certain city is located at point 2A on the map, you can find it easily using the grid system of the map.

In our study of history, geography, and social studies this year, we will be using maps to help us find out where things are and how they relate to each other.

title: American Liberty
text:
During the past few weeks we have talked a lot about democracy and freedom. You have many rights just because you are an American citizen. How many can you think of?

The rights we have did not come easily. Wars have been fought and people have died so that we could have these freedoms. Freedom is something that is very important to Americans.

However, freedom doesn't mean lack of responsibility. It is illegal to yell "Fire!" in a crowded room if there is no fire. Can you imagine the trouble that would cause? People might get hurt trying to get out. When other people can be hurt by your actions, your freedom usually ends there.

In the United States we have a free press. That means reporters can investigate things that people in the government are doing. They can disagree with the president and tell citizens if they think people in the government are doing things that are illegal. A free press means that the government can't keep reporters from saying what they think. The government can disagree with what is said, but the reporters still have the right to say it. Often a free press keeps an eye on the government.

War is not the only price we pay for our freedom. It is up to each and every citizen to do their part as well. One of the most important responsibilities citizens have is to vote. Voting is our opportunity to have a voice in the way the country works. If we don't vote, we've lost our say.

If you don't like something that is going on, you can write or e-mail your senator or representative. If a lot of people agree with you, you can ask them to sign a paper saying they want things to change. This is called a petition. Isn't it great to know that every person in our country can express their concerns to our elected officials? After all, they were elected to represent us. If we don't like what is going on, it is our responsibility to speak up.

title: Help a Rat and Learn to Run the Country This Year!
text:
Hey, kids! I'm Revere the Rat, but you can call me Rev. I'm your online Studies Weekly friend and I need your help. You can help me get great stuff by earning points while you learn.

Has your family ever bought something that came with an owner's manual? Cars, TVs and other things have an owner's manual, a book on how to use them. Your social studies class is the "owner's manual" for the United States of America. You'll learn about history, geography, government by the people, and much more, so you can do a good job of running our country someday.

In America rats can't vote, so "you the people" govern (run) the country. Someday you will be in charge of this country, and you'll choose leaders and representatives by voting. Then you can tell the representatives you help elect how you think the country should be run. In fact, Studies Weekly kids are so smart, that many of you will someday be mayors, senators, governors - maybe even the president!

For now, you have two jobs: Learn about the country and how it works and earn points for me so I can get that great stuff I told you about. It's easy. Just scan or click and you're on your way!

title: The Price of Freedom
text:
Living free seems so easy. You might even wonder why anyone would have to pay for it. Here is the reason. When you live in a country without freedom, it's very hard to become free. Governments who control the lives of their citizens do not want to give up that power. Since they don't want to give up their power, people who want freedom have to fight. The fight for freedom often means death.

Many Americans do not know how dangerous it was to break away from Great Britain in the late 1700s. Great Britain was the most powerful country in the world. The American colonies were weak. The 56 men who signed the Declaration of Independence knew they would be hunted down and possibly killed for declaring freedom from Great Britain. Their desire for freedom was strong, however. They were willing to take that chance.

The Housecat Versus the Lion

What chance did the United States have of winning a war against Great Britain in 1776? Here is a helpful way to think about how dangerous it was to go to war against the most powerful country in the world.

Imagine your high school football team has decided to challenge last year's Super Bowl champions to a game. Do you think your school would have a chance of winning? Of course they wouldn't. It would be like a housecat challenging a lion.

Even if your school had the best high school team in Texas, they would be lucky to score any points against the Super Bowl champs. Your players would also be very lucky if they weren't seriously hurt. Professional football players know how to hit hard.

The same thing was true when the United States wanted independence from Great Britain. The American army lost battle after battle. At one point, General George Washington believed they had no chance, but they kept fighting. The desire for freedom combined with great courage made the impossible happen. The housecat won. The United States beat the mighty army of Great Britain.

One Story of Sacrifice

Courage was important in gaining our freedom. Abraham Clark was a man with great courage. He was one of the men who signed the Declaration of Independence. Clark's two sons joined the fight against Great Britain. During the war, they were captured and sent to the Jersey, a British prison ship. Living conditions there were horrible. More than 11,000 American prisoners died from disease or starvation on this ship.

Clark's young sons were treated more cruelly than the other prisoners because their father had signed the Declaration of Independence. When the war was almost over, the British made Abraham Clark an offer. They told him they would free his sons if he would turn against the United States. They also wanted Clark to say he supported the king of England. This was a painful decision for Abraham Clark. He said, "No."

Few people would have blamed Clark for saving his sons. The war was almost over. However, Clark knew freedom was precious. He knew it could not be won without sacrifice. Sacrifice means giving up something very important to get something of greater value.

There are many other stories about sacrifices made by the colonists. Without these sacrifices, we would not be free today.

Freedom is a hard-bought thing.

– Paul Robeson (1898-1976)

title: Design for the U.S. Government
text:
The writers of the Constitution wanted a government that could not grow large enough to take away the freedom of its citizens. The framers were people who constructed, or put together, the Constitution. They divided the power of the government among three branches. Each branch of government watches the other two to make sure they don't get too powerful. Here are the three branches of government.

Executive Branch

The president of the United States is elected by the nation. He is the leader of the country. The president's job is to uphold the Constitution. The president also enforces the laws and serves as the commander in chief of the nation's military.

Legislative Branch

Congress is called the legislative branch. Their job is to pass laws. They also approve spending and taxes. Congress is made up of the House of Representatives and the Senate. Representatives and senators are elected by the communities and states they represent.

Judicial Branch

The judicial branch is made up of the Supreme Court and the federal courts. The job of this branch is to explain the laws. Federal judges are not elected. They are appointed by the president.

Design for Texas Government

The Texas Constitution of 1876 is like the U. S. Constitution with three branches of government.

Executive Branch

The governor of Texas prepares the budget and enforces state laws. The governor is elected by the people of Texas.

Legislative Branch

Texas has a House of Representatives and a Senate. The people who serve in the legislative branch are elected by their communities. They pass laws, approve spending and vote on taxes.

Judicial Branch

Judges in Texas are elected by the people. Like U.S. judges, their job is to explain the laws.

title: More Than Pieces of Paper
text:
The Declaration of Independence was the beginning of our freedom. The Constitution guarantees our freedom. Learning what these documents mean will help you know how precious our freedom is. Texas also has these documents. Later this year you will learn more about them.

The Declaration of Independence

July 4th is a holiday because it is the day when the United States declared its independence from Great Britain in 1776. The American colonies wanted freedom from Great Britain. They were especially upset about the taxes the British government made them pay. A tax is money collected by a government from its citizens. Anyone who refuses to pay a tax can be punished. After the United States separated from Great Britain, it needed its own government. Representatives from the colonies met to create a new government. A representative is a person who speaks for other people.

The United States Constitution

The representatives wanted freedom to last. They wanted to make sure the new government could never take freedom away from its citizens. When they wrote the Constitution, they limited the size and power of the government. The representatives did this by separating the powers of government into three branches.

A Model for People Who Want Freedom

People around the world have used our Constitution as a model to create a government that protects the freedom of its citizens. Texas is a good example. In 1836, Texas won its freedom from Mexico. Texans used the U.S. Constitution as a model.

American Indians and the Constitution

Did you know that the idea for the U.S. Constitution came from the Iroquois Nation? Long before the British had colonies in America, the Iroquois made a constitution to end fighting among the tribes. They called it the Great Law of Peace.

title: What is the Bill of Rights?
text: The writers of the Constitution included a way to make changes or additions, called amendments, to the Constitution. Some basic rights, such as freedom of speech and freedom of religion, were not spelled out in the Constitution, and many people believed they should be added. Congress sent a list of these rights to the states, and the first 10 amendments became part of the Constitution. These amendments are known as the Bill of Rights. They also include such familiar rights as the freedom to bear arms and to have a trial by jury. Important amendments since then include the 13th Amendment, which made slavery illegal, and the 19th Amendment, which gave women the right to vote. The Bill of Rights and the amendment process guarantee that the Constitution will continue to reflect the will of the American people.

title: Don’t Forget to Vote!
text:
It's your right and your responsibility

On Election Day, you've probably seen lots of stickers and signs saying "I voted" or "Don't forget to vote." Why is this so important? It's one of the most important freedoms guaranteed to citizens. If you are 18 years old, a citizen of the United States and live in Texas, you can vote in all local, state and federal elections.

But it's also part of your duty as a citizen to learn about the people running for office so you can be sure that the best people for the job get elected.

All elected leaders promise to have an open door to citizens, including kids, even though kids can't vote yet. If you have an opinion about an issue or an idea for a new law, write a letter and make your voice heard.

To contact leaders of your town, state and country, go to:

www.statelocalgov.net/ (state and local)

www.usa.gov/Contact/ (U.S. Congress)

www.whitehouse.gov/contact (the president)

title: Reason and Logic: Young George Washington, Surveyor and Mapmaker
text:
Most people know about George Washington. He was born in Virginia. He was a general during the American Revolution and our first president. But his earliest jobs, surveyor and cartographer (mapmaker), taught him skills and values he would use for the rest of his life. Using reason and logic to solve problems helped Washington become one of our country's most important leaders.

When Washington grew up, there were few roads or boundaries in much of the land. A surveyor's job was to measure and map the land. He had to make exact measurements for boundaries and physical features. This was a very big responsibility. People needed accurate maps and surveys for traveling and buying land.

At age 17, Washington traveled across the Blue Ridge Mountains to map and survey part of the frontier. He was the surveyor for the whole county, and that was an important job. When he led the Continental Army, it was even more important to have reliable maps. He established the job of Geographer and Surveyor General and appointed a man named Robert Erskine to this position. He gave Washington some information that was very helpful in making reasonable and logical battle plans and decisions.

You can use these same skills to make important decisions. Be sure you have the facts and information you need instead of acting on opinions and emotions. In what areas of your life are reason and logic very important?
