title: Oil ‘Blows’ Texas into the 20th Century
text:
The railroads forever changed the lives of Texans in the late 1800s. The way people lived and worked was never the same again. More people had come to live in Texas. Many of them were looking for ways to find their fortunes. Some of these people had a feeling there was something very special about the Texas land. That something turned out to be oil. What would it have been like to be at the very spot oil was first discovered in Texas? Read 10-year-old Nate's diary entry below to find out.

January 10, 1901

They did it! They finally drilled oil at Spindletop! Daddy said Mr. Higgins and Mr. Lucas weren't crazy like people said. There really was oil there. I saw it myself. Mr. Higgins and Mr. Lucas have been telling people for years that there was oil here under all the salt. The drilling was hard work for Daddy and the other men. There were lots of days when I didn't think he would go back again.

What a lucky day for us all. It was my last day of winter vacation from school. Daddy told me I could go with him to the drilling site at the top of Spindletop Hill. The men were excited about drilling today. Mr. Lucas had told them their hard work would soon pay off.

I was sitting off to the side watching the men work. Daddy told me I couldn't get too close. Sometimes the oil drilling made the ground underneath the men cave in. It was too dangerous for me. But I watched the men working hard. They were repairing some of the drilling equipment. Mr. Lucas yelled out for the men to start drilling down the hole again.

Suddenly, I heard a lot of noise and confusion. Someone yelled, "Look at the mud bubbling up!" Without warning, that big drill pipe burst up out of the ground! Luckily, no one was hurt. The drillers all stood around looking confused. Then they started cleaning up the mess. They wanted to get the drill back into the ground as quickly as possible.

I could hear the men grumbling. Some of them seemed frustrated. I know I could tell by the look on Daddy's face that he was not too happy either. Some of the equipment looked damaged again. This only made things worse. I started wondering if maybe people were right. Maybe it was impossible to dig through the thick sand to find oil. Maybe Mr. Higgins and Mr. Lucas were wasting time. But I had to believe my daddy. I know he believed they would find oil soon. I just wished something would go right.

Suddenly I jumped up as I heard a loud noise. It sounded like a gun had been shot off. The men ran back as mud and rocks burst out of the hole. The black earth flew high into the sky and rained back down on all the men. Within seconds, spewing and sizzling sounds could be heard as natural gas started up out of the ground. Then, without warning, it was raining thick black oil on us all! The river of oil rocketed into the sky. It seemed to go higher and higher. Oil gushed higher than the wooden derrick that help the men lift heavy pipes and drilling tools. Daddy told Mama over dinner tonight that it shot about 150 feet into the air.

The men were all covered with the green-black slime. Oil ran down their faces and into their eyes. They weren't upset, though. Everyone was cheering, yelling and clapping. They had done it. Mr. Higgins and Mr. Lucas were right. There was oil right here in Texas!

title: The Texas Black Gold Rush
text:
Growth and Change in Texas

The railroads chugged into Texas in the late 1800s. They brought a new way of life to people there. Suddenly there were many new opportunities. Most people in Texas still lived in rural, or country, areas. Life in the countryside had not changed much yet. People were still using horse-drawn wagons for transportation. Most people didn't have electricity. But they could now move to more urban areas. In cities like Dallas and Austin, there were other new inventions that made life easier. Most people had things like telephones, automobiles and electricity. People began finding jobs in new businesses or industries. Some Texans thought there was the chance for an exciting new industry. They thought there might be oil in Texas.

First to Find Oil

Oil has been around in Texas for a long time. American Indians in Texas knew about the oil because they saw the black substance coming up through the ground. They thought the oil might be a magical medicine. They often rubbed it on wounds. Some American Indians even drank the black liquid. They hoped it would help cure stomach pain.

Early Spanish explorers found sticky black tar on the beaches. In 1543, some of the explorers recorded that they used the tar to help make their boots waterproof. These early people did not know how valuable oil really was.

Oil in the United States

Historians who study the oil industry in the United States say the first modern oil well was drilled in Pennsylvania. Colonel Edwin L. Drake drilled a well in 1859 near the town of Titusville. In those days they didn't need oil for the things we do, like automobiles. But they did use the oil to make different kinds of medicines. So the oil was worth a lot of money, just like it is today. This first oil sold for around $40 a barrel. This was a lot of money in those days. By the early 1900s, more new inventions used oil. So lots of people started trying to find more oil underneath the ground. They knew if they found oil, they could become very rich.

Oil for Texas

In the early days, people in Texas found oil by digging near places where oil and gas were coming out of the ground. Sometimes people digging water wells accidentally found oil. But these were not very large finds. Usually these sites would only have a few barrels of the black liquid. But they still attracted scientists and businessmen to Texas. Geologists (scientists who study the structure of the earth) started studying places in Texas that were most likely to have oil. Everyone knew it would only be a matter of time before someone found oil, also known as petroleum or "black gold."

Spindletop Gushes

Patillo Higgins lived near Beaumont in south Texas. He was a businessman and Sunday school teacher. Sometimes he went with his church group to have picnics on top of a hill near his home. At each picnic, a strange smell caught his attention. Higgins thought it smelled like gas and wondered if there might be oil under Spindletop Hill. He decided to drill holes in the ground to see if he could find oil. Higgins got other businessmen to help him, and they made big plans for an oil and gas company. They drilled several holes but didn't find oil. After a while, many of Higgins' business partners wanted out of the deal.

Patillo's only hope was to find a new partner. He convinced a man named Anthony F. Lucas to help him keep drilling. For almost three months, a team of men worked and drilled through the sand and salt under the hill. On Jan. 10, 1901, the team of oil drillers struck big. Tired but excited workers watched as oil spewed out of the ground. The gusher, or blast of oil, shot high into the air. The oil went higher and higher into the air. The workers were covered with mud and oil. They had to work for nine days before they could control the oil blast.

The Oil Boom Begins

News of the oil discovery at Spindletop spread quickly. Railroads and other industries needed oil and gas products. The demand, or need, for these products was very high. Word spread that there might be lots of oil, or black gold, near Beaumont. Suddenly thousands of people were coming to try to get rich. Within a few months, Beaumont grew from a population of 9,000 to more than 50,000.

The people who came to Beaumont hoped to strike it rich in the oil business. They wanted to drill oil wells. Some wanted to sell land or equipment. Others came to find good jobs. There were many jobs available in the new oil industry. Some people worked drilling or laying pipelines to carry the oil. Some people worked in oil refineries. Oil refineries are factories where oil is cleaned, processed and turned into products that other industries could use.

The Start of Big Things to Come

The amazing find at Spindletop was just the beginning of the oil boom in Texas. Soon many other communities were growing and prospering, or doing well. Oil was going to change the state of Texas for good.

title: Captain Anthony F. Lucas: Oil Pioneer
text:
When Captain Anthony F. Lucas came to America in the late 1800s, he had no idea he would become one of the most famous men in Texas history. Captain Lucas, born in Croatia, served in the Austrian navy. He attended college in Austria and studied engineering. Lucas was especially interested in geology. He was working as a salt miner in Louisiana when he heard a very interesting story about Texas.

Lucas heard people talk about a salt dome in south Texas that might have oil under it. He thought it was interesting and decided to work with Patillo Higgins at Spindletop Hill in Beaumont, Texas. At first, Lucas and his men did not have success. But they were smart. They tried to find new ways to drill into the sandy earth. They did not give up. In the end, Spindletop did have oil. Lucas was forever remembered as a leader in the oil industry in Texas.

title: Supply and Demand
text:
Suppose you had been saving your allowance to buy the latest game system and discovered that every store in town was sold out. Or what if your favorite game system was one price, but another brand was on sale for 25% off? What choices would you need to make?

Supply - the amount of something that is available, and demand - the amount of something that people actually want or need, are important economic terms to understand. The new supply of oil in Texas matched the demand for oil by railroads and industries. This balance can make a healthy economy.

A big demand for a certain game system could cause stores to be sold out. And if a store has a large supply of a different game system, you just might have the opportunity to catch them on sale. That's economics!

title: Oil and Gas — A Global Industry
text:
After they found oil at Spindletop, the face of Texas was changed forever. People started drilling oil wells all over the state. By 1928, Texas produced more oil than any other state. All this oil meant plenty of jobs and money for Texans. Oil was a very big business.

Many oil companies opened in all areas of the state. Many people moved to Texas, and the state's population grew. New oil wells were drilled each day in the years after they found oil at Spindletop. Refineries along the Gulf Coast opened to process the oil. These refineries would then ship the oil to the rest of the world.

Today, the oil industry is still an important part of the way the state makes money. Texas' economy still depends on oil production and distribution. The oil industry is not booming like it was at the beginning of the 20th century, but there are still many people who make a living in the Texas oil fields.

title: Patillo Higgins: A Man With a Dream
text:
Patillo Higgins had a dream. He wanted to be rich and successful. But he had a lot of work ahead of him. As a young boy, Higgins often found himself in trouble. He had run-ins with the local sheriff and challenged authority. But Higgins quickly changed his ways. He studied geology, drafting, and engineering all on his own. He worked in the timber, real estate, and brick-making industries.

In 1901, Higgins believed he could find oil under Spindletop Hill in Beaumont, Texas. Higgins and other investors started drilling. At first, they did not find oil, but Higgins did not give up. With the help of Captain Anthony F. Lucas, he finally succeeded. Patillo Higgins struck oil and landed himself in history as the man responsible for the beginning of the oil boom in Texas.

title: Frame of Reference
text:
As you study history, have you been able to see the frame of references that help people make decisions? This means you can put yourself in someone else’s shoes and see why he or she made certain decisions. Sometimes this means you have to think about the different beliefs people have. You might also think about what motivated, or pushed, each person to make that decision.

Patillo Higgins wanted to find oil at Spindletop. After several unsuccessful tries, some of his business partners gave up and got out of the oil business. Patillo kept drilling. Think about the reasons Patillo Higgins and his business partners made the decisions they did. Analyze their actions. What factors influenced their thinking?

Show that you understand why Patillo Higgins and the other businessmen made their choices. On the lines below write three statements that each would have made about the Spindletop business.

Now choose to be Mr. Higgins or one of his business partners. Share one of the points of your frame of reference aloud with the class. Do other people agree or disagree with your ideas? Discuss your ideas.

title: Making a Living in Texas Today
text:
If you were to judge from what you see on the media, you might think all Texans are either cowboys or people who became rich through the oil business. Actually, Texas has such a varied economy that if it were a nation, it would be number 10 in the world in making products. Texas is also first in the U.S. for exports, which means sending goods and services all over the world.

Texans can be found working in large cities and out in the country. Texas is known worldwide for its use of and transportation of natural resources. It's true some Texans can be miners and rich oil businesspeople. However, they can also be found in construction, heavy and civil engineering, space research and technology, and information technology.

If we divide Texas into regions, we can see some of the many kinds of its industries. Central Texas is known for its businesses. In fact, 49 Fortune 500 companies are headquartered in Texas. East Texas prides itself on its manufacturing, transportation, and food processing firms. Petroleum and chemical industries, technology and information firms, engineering, and biomedical innovators are located along the Gulf Coast. In fact, Houston is the hub for the world's operations in outer space. North Texas boasts major employers in business and information technology. South Texas is a leader in transportation. Finally, West Texas is known for agriculture, energy, manufacturing, healthcare, and aviation.

You can see that Texans can have lots of different kinds of jobs. Texans can be astronauts or doctors or business leaders or, yes, even cowgirls and cowboys.

title: From Boom to Bust
text:
The beginning of the 20th century brought Texas a promise of great times. Railroads crisscrossed the state. Towns were growing at a fast rate. People were making a good living in the ranching and farming industries. What was most exciting was the oil discovery at Spindletop in 1901. There was a job for everyone who wanted one. But the good times didn't last forever. By 1929, the United States - Texas included - had fallen on hard times. The Great Depression was hovering over everyone. People lost jobs; stores went out of business; families lost their homes. In the story below, you will read about Nancy and her brother Jimmy. They are worried because their father has lost his job. Will their family become victims of the Great Depression too?

March 1939 blew in with a gust of dusty wind. Nancy and Jimmy stood staring out the window as tumbleweeds sailed by. Mom and Dad stood outside on the porch, talking to Mr. Cosby from the bank. Dad's forehead was creased with a worried look. Mom kept wiping tears from her eyes with the corner of her apron. Nancy didn't know exactly what was going on, but it couldn't be good.

Things hadn't been the same since the grocery store closed down. Nancy's dad lost his job. Her mom said they might have to move in with Grandmother if they couldn't make any money. Nancy was scared. Their family had always been careful with money. But now the banker was telling her parents they might have to move. He had a "For Sale" sign in his hands.

Nancy had heard her parents say the depression was to blame for everyone's troubles. Businesses were slowing down. Many families were having the same problems. Just like most of the kids at school, Nancy hadn't had a new pair of shoes in more than a year. Many nights there was only a pot of beans on the table for supper. But now what would they do? Nancy didn't want to leave her home. There had to be a way for her family to survive. Would this Great Depression last forever?

title: A Census Full of Treasure
text:
On April 2, 2012, the government released the 1940 census. A census is a count of all the people in the United States, and it is done every 10 years. It also gives other information about citizens' jobs, income, birthplace and education level. The government only releases a census' records to the public after 72 years have passed. The 1940 census was the first one done after the Great Depression. It shows how important events caused people to move around and where immigrants went. You can find interesting facts about family members and famous people. For example, the future President Ronald Reagan paid $135 in rent in 1940!

The 1940 census was the last time census takers went door-to-door to personally interview people and write down the information. For the 1950 census the government started using census questionnaires sent through the mail.

The release of the 1940 census data is different from past years. This information was made digital and released through the Internet. There are more than 3.8 million pages of data in this census. Genealogists, or people who study family backgrounds, use this information to trace family history. Researchers, like historians, often use the census as a primary source of information.

So, was this release a success? Well, so many people tried to get the information on its first day of release that the server crashed! If you would like to learn more about your family history you can go to the 1940 census site at: 1940census.archives.gov

.

title: A Changing Texas, A Changing World
text:
Trouble Brews in Europe

The 20th century began with a bang when we discovered oil in Texas in 1901. There were plenty of jobs for everyone. But soon enough, Texans were living through very difficult times. It all started across the ocean in Europe.

In 1914, war broke out. Great Britain, France, Italy and Russia were known as the Allied Powers. They joined together against the Central Powers. This included Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire. In 1917, the United States joined the Allied Powers. About 200,000 Texans became soldiers during World War I.

New Jobs for Texans

There were many new jobs for Texans during the war. Airplane pilots trained at Texas Air Force bases. Women, who had not worked before, took over the factory jobs that were left when the men went to war. The war was being fought in Europe, but back in Texas everyone was working to help the Allied Powers win. In 1918, the Allied Powers did win and the war was over. Life would change in Europe now. It had already begun to change in Texas.

The Roaring Twenties

The 1920s were an exciting time of change for Texas and the world. This is when some women won the right to vote. In 1924, a woman was elected to be the Texas governor. Miriam "Ma" Ferguson's husband was the governor of Texas. But he was accused of breaking the law and was removed from office. The people voted to have Mrs. Ferguson take his place. It was exciting that a woman was given the position. There were other exciting changes too.

At the end of World War I, factories were no longer needed to make supplies for the war. Now they could make products people wanted and needed to buy. Factories hired new workers. The 1920s were "roaring" with business. People felt good about things. Industries were at a peak. People had good jobs. They had extra money to spend. Many people spent their extra money on a new exciting invention - the automobile.

Incredible Automobiles

Henry Ford opened the Ford Motor Company in Michigan in 1903. His company used a new manufacturing idea called the assembly line. This helped his company be able to make a new car in only 93 minutes. This was good news. By 1928, more than 250,000 cars and trucks were on the road in Texas.

Cars need gasoline to run. Texas had lots of oil. Gasoline companies built refineries in Texas to manufacture, or make, the gasoline. Once again, there were lots of available jobs in Texas. This gave the oil industry another boost.

Cars also needed good roads to travel on. Companies started building roads and highways to link Texas cities together. People started many new businesses for anything they needed. Times were good. People made and spent their money on homes and some of the new inventions of the century.

Industrial Revolution

Scientists and inventors were hard at work during this time period. Every day it seemed there was a new tool or machine that made life easier for people. Refrigerators, vacuum cleaners, radios and an early television were all created during this time. Factories used new technologies to improve mass production. Workers used new machines to make products quickly. They each had a different job to do instead of making one product all alone. This was called division of labor. This process improved speed and performance of workers. Texas businesses made lots of money selling their products to Americans and people in foreign countries.

It All Came Crashing Down

During the decade of the 1920s, businesses of all kinds boomed. Americans felt good about the future. People bought stocks in companies. These stocks were shares of ownership. When a company is doing well, their stocks increase in value. People can make a profit, or money, by buying and selling stocks. Unfortunately stocks can lose value too.

This is what happened in late 1929. In October the value of many companies' stocks fell. People worried and many of them tried to sell their stocks. This caused the value of stocks to fall even more. Soon companies didn't have enough money to stay open. Lots of people lost their jobs. People who had borrowed money to buy stocks could not pay the bank back. Banks who did not get repaid had to close. Some people lost all the money they had. To make matters worse, the nation experienced a severe drought during this time. The earth became very dry and there were lots of dust storms in Texas. The Great Plains area became known as the Dust Bowl. Crops were ruined and life was miserable for most people. The Great Depression had settled on Texas as well as the United States.

A New Deal to End the Depression

In 1933, President Franklin D. Roosevelt created a program to help the United States get out of the Great Depression. He called the plan the New Deal. The government gave many people jobs. Workers built dams and repaired roads and bridges. Some workers improved parks and government buildings. Businesses loaned money from the government so they could open again. Not everyone thought the New Deal was good. Some people did not like the power it gave the government. But people were feeling better. Unfortunately, it took a terrible crisis to get the United States in good shape again.

World War II

On Dec. 7, 1941, the United States entered World War II. Japan dropped bombs on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. Many men signed up to serve in the military. Suddenly Texas industry was busier than ever. Texas provided most of the gasoline needed for ships, tanks and planes during the war. Many new jobs were created when factories opened to make supplies for the war in Europe and the Pacific. Once again many people came to Texas to work. Women and people from Mexico made up a large part of the work force.

The Great Depression is Over

When the war ended in 1945, the United States was in good shape again. The Great Depression was over. People had jobs and money to spend. Texas was stronger than ever. It was a leading industry state. The good times seemed to be back.

title: Building a Workforce of Women
text:
When the United States entered World War II, changes had to be made fast. The country needed the factories to help produce goods for the war. Automobile and appliance factories were quickly turned into airplane and weapon factories. New factories were even built to produce more materials.

There was a major problem, though. The men all went off to war. Suddenly there were no workers to run the factories. At this time, most women did not work outside their homes. They spent their days taking care of their homes and children. But that was about to change.

Suddenly, housewives and young women were needed in the factories. In Texas and the rest of the United States, the government was calling on women to become "Rosie the Riveter." This image of a woman rolling up her sleeves and working in a factory was everywhere. "Rosie" was a strong woman. She was capable of doing anything she set her mind to. Advertisements to convince women to work were on billboards and in magazines. And they succeeded. The government changed the opinions of most people. Women came to believe that taking a job was not a choice. It was their duty as U.S. citizens.

Across Texas and the nation, women worked in factories to make equipment, weapons and supplies for the soldiers. After the war, the men came home. Most of the women went back to their homes and children. However, historians believe this time period was the beginning of the workforce of women we see in the United States today.

title: Texas Heroes of World War II
text:
1. Cleto Rodriguez

Cleto Rodriguez was one of only 14 men from Texas to earn the Medal of Honor. The Medal of Honor is given to members of the Armed Forces who risk their lives "above and beyond the call of duty" while fighting U.S. enemies. Only 464 men earned the Medal of Honor during World War II.

Cleto was born in San Marcos, Texas, in 1923. His parents died when he was nine years old, and he went to live with relatives in San Antonio. There he worked hard at a hotel and as a newsboy while going to school. Rodriguez entered the Army in 1944. During World War II, he was sent to the Philippine Islands in the Pacific Ocean. One day, Cleto and his partner fought off 82 enemy soldiers all by themselves. This made it possible for the United States to defeat the Japanese army in the Philippines. Cleto spent most of his life as a soldier. He is remembered as a brave Texan and soldier.

2. Audie Murphy

Audie Leon Murphy joined the Army when he was just 18 years old. By the time he was 20, he was the most decorated soldier in World War II. This means he earned more awards than any other soldier. Among his 33 awards, Audie received the Medal of Honor, our nation's highest military award. Even France and Belgium gave him awards for his bravery. During the war, Audie was wounded three times. He fought in nine major battles and came home a hero.

Audie was born in 1924 to a very poor Texas family. They made their living sharecropping near Dallas.

After his career in the military, Audie Murphy became a movie star in Hollywood. He made 44 movies during his lifetime. Most of them were westerns. Audie also wrote a book about his life as a soldier. It was made into a very popular movie during the 1950s.

Audie Murphy died in a plane crash in 1971. He is buried at Arlington National Cemetery in Washington, D.C. Audie's birthday, June 20, is officially Audie Murphy Day each year in Texas.

title: Main Idea Timeline
text: Study this timeline. After reading the lesson in this issue, complete the timeline. Think about the main idea of each event on the timeline: How did the event change lives in Texas? Write a sentence or two explaining the main idea for each event.

title: Let's Write
text: Work with a small group of your classmates. Write a script for a play about life during the Great Depression. Everyone in the group should have a part to write. Pretend you are a family. What is life like for you all? What are you worried about? How do you think your family will survive during this time? After you have written your play perform it for the rest of the class.

title: Post WWII Patterns of Settlement in Texas
text:
Texas is the second largest state in the United States. It’s twice as big as Japan and Germany and 10% bigger than France. Over 28 million people live in Texas and more are coming every year. You could say that Texas is a migration magnet. But why do people want to live here?

People move for all sorts of reasons. They want to find a better job or a warmer climate. They want to live closer to family or friends. They want to explore a different country. The first settlers in Texas were farmers. They came for the rich soil of the Coastal Plains. The soil was perfect for farming and raising cattle. The Coastal Plains stretch inland from the Gulf of Mexico and make up two fifths of Texas. Corpus Christi, Waco, and Laredo are three of the large cities on the Coastal Plains.

Later, settlers came to work in the oil fields that dot the state. The Permian Basin in West Texas is one of the biggest oil and gas fields in the world. El Paso, Lubbock, and Abilene are cities in West Texas.

Before World War II, most Texans lived on farms or in small towns. Back then, more people lived in New York City than in the whole state of Texas. Only about half had graduated from high school. Few families had a car and even fewer had a telephone or even a radio. Most women worked at home or on the farm. When the U.S. entered World War II in 1941, Texans left their small towns and farms. They moved to the cities to work. They took jobs building weapons and war supplies for U.S. soldiers fighting in Europe. Women of all ages and ethnicities worked in the factories.

When the war ended, the factory workers didn’t go home. They wanted to stay in the cities because they could find more resources there. Texans left their farms for better lives in large cities on the Coastal Plains like Houston, Dallas, San Antonio, and Austin. Big cities had jobs, shops, hospitals, opportunities of all kinds. Most small towns didn’t have those things. Year after year, people from nearby states like Louisiana, Oklahoma, and Arkansas moved to Texas to live and work in the big cities. People from other countries came to Texas to make it their home. Half of the people living in Texas today were born outside of the state. Nearly 3.5 million people were born in Mexico, Central America, and India.

Today, Texas is more urban than rural. That means it has more people in cities than in small towns. More than 80% of the entire population lives in urban (city) centers. Six of the twenty-five largest cities in the U.S. are in Texas, including Houston, San Antonio, Dallas, and Austin.

title: Specialization and Economic Growth in Texas
text:
The economy of Texas is home to many large industries. The three biggest are energy, technology, and agriculture. Each of these industries is successful because of division of labor, specialization, and mass production.

With division of labor, the production process is broken into many steps. Each step is performed by a different worker. Dividing tasks up makes production more consistent. Being more consistent allows for mass production. Mass production is the manufacture of large quantities of products. In the technology industry of Texas, large companies benefit from division of labor and mass production to produce many goods. Texas Instruments and Dell Computers are two examples.

With division of labor comes specialization. This is when a person focuses on doing just one or two tasks. A company or industry can also specialize. Instead of growing several different crops on one farm, an entire farm may grow just one crop.

Texas geography plays a role in this type of specialization. Cotton, fruit, and vegetables are grown in the coastal plains. Cattle and sheep are raised in the high plains. Oil production is linked to geography as well, with most refineries in the gulf region.

title: Texas Immigration and Economic Growth
text:
In 1744, Texas was still a new colony. There were only 1,500 settlers living in the state, plus a few thousand American Indians. Today, more than 28 million people live in Texas. Lots of these people moved, or immigrated, to Texas from other places.

The very first people to immigrate to Texas were Spanish and French explorers. The Spanish founded the first settlements in Texas, including San Antonio in 1718. These settlements didn’t have many people. The settlements struggled because they were far away from other Spanish colonies.

By 1820, Spain wanted people to move to Texas to settle it and boost the economy. To get people from Spain to come to Texas, Spain made land in Texas 30 times cheaper than U.S. land. People poured into Texas from all over. Each immigrant brought new skills and new money into Texas. The economy exploded. Soon, Texas became big enough to become its own country for a little while. Texas then joined the U.S., and even more people moved there.

Then, in the early 1900s, people started finding oil in Texas. Many cars and machines use oil, so it is really valuable. It’s also rare in most places. But in some places in Texas, oil poured out of the ground. People flocked into Texas to make money from this “liquid gold.” Before the oil boom, most people in Texas were farmers. The oil boom changed Texas completely. The economy exploded again as people made tons of money from oil. Even people who didn’t work with oil started making more money selling things to the oil producers. People came from all over to get a piece of this opportunity.

Today, Texas has more people than any state except California. In 2018, more than 185,000 people moved to Texas. The population just keeps growing.

title: Texas Blasts Off Into the Future
text:
The first half of the 1900s brought a lot of change to Texas. By the end of World War II in 1945, Texas looked nothing like it did only 50 years earlier. Soldiers came home from the war. The Great Depression was no longer weighing everyone down. There were lots of jobs and opportunities.

The oil industry was still going strong. As a matter of fact, oil-related businesses continued to be strong throughout the century. More companies opened new factories too. Texas was a good place to start businesses. People were moving from rural farms and ranches to urban areas. These people found new jobs in new businesses. The areas around cities grew as businesses grew.

Some of these new industries changed the world even more. In Houston, NASA worked to send ships and people into outer space. In 1969, a man actually walked on the moon. From then on, the space industry was big business in Texas too.

Later, computer and technology companies saw Texas as a perfect place to start businesses. Today, many Texans work in these technology-based industries. This is one field in Texas that will probably continue to grow.

After World War II, there were other big changes in the United States and Texas. African Americans and Hispanics gained more rights. Texas passed laws to give all people equal opportunities, or chances. Texas was home to many of the people who most often spoke up for equal rights.

In the last half of the 20th century, many people thought the opportunities in Texas were exciting. People started building homes in many new communities. People came to Texas to start businesses and raise families.

Yes, in the last part of the 20th century, Texas blasted off towards a bright and shining future.

title: Sally Ride Leaves a Legacy
text:
America lost a hero in 2012 when astronaut Sally Ride died. She was born in 1951 in California. She played tennis and loved science and English literature classes. Ride studied physics, which is the science of matter and energy. Her journey to space began when she applied to a NASA program for astronauts. She was one of the 35 people chosen from over 8,000 applications! Ride worked hard in the training program and helped design the robotic arm on the space shuttle. Her 1983 mission on the space shuttle Challenger launched her into space and into the history books. Sally Ride was the first American woman to fly in space!

Ride flew into space again on a mission in 1984. She worked on the investigations into the space shuttle tragedies of 1986 and 2003. Sally Ride was also an educator. Ride saw that as girls got older, they lost interest in science and math classes. She wrote children's books and started a company that provides exciting science materials to schools. Ride was proud to be a role model for girls who wanted to be astronauts and scientists.

When Ride began her space career, most of the other astronauts and engineers were men. When asked about being one of the few women in this profession, she said, "I never ran into a teacher or a counselor who told me that science was for boys." Thanks to Sally Ride, both boys and girls know that they can reach for the stars!

title: Notable Texans of the 20th Century
text:
In the second half of the 20th century, Texas moved forward in many areas. Read about some famous Texans who spent much of their lives working to help Texas improve. Their efforts made Texas and the world a better place.

Lyndon Baines Johnson

"We must open the doors of opportunity. But we must also equip our people to walk through those doors." - Lyndon B. Johnson

Franklin D. Roosevelt started his New Deal plan in 1933. He hoped to pull the nation out of a depression. One of his plans was the National Youth Administration. The NYA helped young people find jobs. The man in charge of the program was a young Texan named Lyndon B. Johnson.

Lyndon was born in 1908 in central Texas. He was the oldest of five children. Lyndon's family worked hard, but they often struggled for money. As a young boy Lyndon told his friends he would one day have a better life. He told them he would become president of the United States. Lyndon worked odd jobs after high school until he decided to become a teacher. Johnson worked with very poor children at his first teaching job. Most of them were from Mexican American families. Johnson said the children left a great impression on him and helped him want to help people.

Lyndon soon found a job working with a congressman from Texas in Washington, D.C. Johnson learned a lot, and lots of people liked him. He was later elected as a congressman for Texas. He served in the Navy during World War II and was then elected to the U.S. Congress. Johnson was very young but very skilled as a political leader.

In 1960, Johnson was elected as the vice president of the United States. In 1963, when President John Kennedy was assassinated, or killed, Johnson became president of the United States.

As president, Johnson wanted the people of the United States to work towards a great society. In 1964, the U.S. Congress passed the Civil Rights Act that Johnson supported. This law said all people in the United States must have equal rights and be treated the same. Since then, there have been many changes that make sure people of every race, religion and gender are treated fairly. Johnson also helped create programs to help poor and elderly people. He also led the country's space exploration programs.

Barbara Jordan

"What the people want is very simple. They want an America as good as its promise." - Barbara Jordan

Barbara Jordan was a little girl with big dreams. Her father was a minister, and her mother was a domestic worker. Barbara was born in Houston. She went to schools there and did very well. Barbara was an excellent debate student. She wanted to go on to college and become a lawyer. This was difficult though. In the 1950s, there was only one law school in Texas that would admit African American students. But Barbara was determined to meet her goals. She decided to attend Texas Southern University and Boston University School of Law. After law school, Barbara taught political history at a college in Alabama. She then decided to open a law office back in her home state of Texas. She was only the third African American woman in the state to have a law license.

As a lawyer, Barbara saw things about the state that should be changed. She wanted every person to have the same rights. At that time people of different races were often separated. Barbara did not want African Americans or Hispanics to be told they couldn't go into restaurants or theaters. She didn't want people of different races to have to go to different schools. This type of segregation is now illegal in our country.

In 1966, Barbara Jordan became the first African American state senator since 1883. She was the first African American woman to have the job. In 1972, she was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives. She quickly became known as a very smart and hard-working woman. She was especially known for her powerful speeches. She often spoke out for people's rights. She continued working throughout her life. Although she spent the last few years of her life in a wheelchair, Barbara Jordan never slowed down. She kept moving towards making Texas better for everyone.

Henry Barbosa Gonzalez

"Congressman Henry B. Gonzalez's 37 years of public service embodied the ultimate example of service and integrity to the nation." - Charles Garcia

Charles Garcia was First Recipient of the Henry B. Gonzalez Public Service and Integrity Award. Henry Barbosa Gonzalez was born in 1916 in San Antonio, Texas. His parents had escaped Mexico during the 1911 Mexican Revolution. Henry was an excellent student in San Antonio. He studied at the University of Texas, San Antonio College and St. Mary's University of Law. After graduating with a law degree, Henry worked as a probation officer. He then worked with the Army and Navy during World War II. He spoke four languages and worked as a translator.

After the war, he served on the San Antonio City Council. He worked to make sure people in his city were all treated fairly. Soon Henry became a member of the Texas state senate. In 1961, he became the first Mexican American from Texas to be elected to the U.S. Congress. He was known as a very smart and well-spoken man. He fought for people's rights to education, housing and good paying jobs. He often said he fought for the rights of the common man.

Gonzalez died in 2000. People throughout Texas and especially San Antonio still refer to Henry Barbosa Gonzalez as "Our Beloved Henry B."

title: Texas Technology — Industry for the Future
text:
Most Texas businesses want to compete in the global, or worldwide, industry market. This means they want to do business with people and companies around the world. To do this, businesses know they must use technology. Technology is the use of scientific knowledge, tools and skills to help people meet their needs. Today most everyone depends on technology each day. Some Texas companies are providing high-tech goods and services to other Texans.

These products include computers and software that help people communicate and do business with one another. Technology helps save money and time. Some of the largest computer technology companies in the world have offices in Texas.

What types of companies depend on this high technology? Well, think about the businesses you or your parents visit each day. Banks, restaurants, gas stations and hospitals all rely on technology. Even your school uses technology.

Economists have predicted that the technology industry in Texas is only just beginning. They say that within 10 years, technology will be a $3 trillion industry. With that kind of money at stake, it's no wonder Texas is always looking for ways to attract and keep technology-based businesses.

title: Texas Leads the Space Race
text:
On July 20, 1969, a round of cheers went up at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas. Neil Armstrong, an astronaut who studied and explored space, landed his spaceship on the moon. The people in the Mission Control Center felt proud of themselves. They had done what no one had ever been able to do. They helped put a man on the moon.

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is located in Texas. NASA runs the space program for the U.S. government. They train astronauts and study the sun, planets and comets. They are also responsible for building and testing spaceships and shuttles. They help teach people about space.

The Johnson Space Center is a part of the aerospace industry in Texas. This industry builds and operates spacecraft, missiles, aircraft and equipment. It brings lots of jobs to Texas. There are many people who work hard to keep the United States at the top of this industry. Scientists design and test ideas and equipment.

The aerospace industry adds money to the Texas economy too. In 2007, there were more than 400 aerospace businesses in Texas. They employed almost 50,000 Texans. This year these businesses added $269 million to the Texas economy. The companies also export products to other countries like Mexico and Canada. In 2007, they sent out more than $11 billion of goods. This means more money and growth for Texas.

The U.S. government has plans to send more spaceships into outer space soon. They also plan to design and test new kinds of military planes and helicopters. So hang on as the Texas aerospace industry blasts off.

title: Charting Oil Prices
text:
Study the line graph, then answer the questions that follow.

1. In what year did crude oil sell for the least amount?

2. How much did a barrel of crude oil sell for in 1980?

3. What happened to oil prices between 1970-1980?

4. In what year did crude oil prices drop below the 1970 price? How much lower was the price in that year than 1970?

6. Research question: Do some research to find out the price of oil per barrel today. How does that price compare with prices in other years? Why do you think the prices change?

title: An American Dream Come True
text:
...that I will support and defend the Constitution and laws of the United States of America against all enemies, foreign and domestic; that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the same;..."

Claudia Richards felt goosebumps on her arm. The day she had waited for was here. She raised her right hand and repeated the oath of citizenship with about 100 other people. In just a few minutes, Claudia would finally be a citizen, or member, of the United States.

Growing up in Bogotá, Colombia, Claudia had the dream to study music. She learned to play the guitar and piano, but she wanted the chance to be a music teacher. There were very few schools in Colombia where she could study. Claudia was sad that she might not be able to fulfill her dreams. But Claudia and her parents had an idea. They decided Claudia would go to America to study. There were many opportunities in the United States. Soon her dream of being a teacher might come true.

Being in the United States was very hard for Claudia at first. She had to work to improve her English. For months, Claudia carried a dictionary everywhere she went. Life in America was so different than in Colombia. Claudia was amazed at snow, canned food and pizza. She ate lots of pizza!

Claudia studied hard in college. She earned two degrees. At last, Claudia's dream of becoming a music teacher had come true. She also met and married her husband who was an American citizen. Soon Claudia was excited to add three daughters to her family.

After college, Claudia started teaching school. She loved her job, and the children loved her. But Claudia felt something was missing in her life. Through the lessons she planned and songs they sang, Claudia was teaching her students how to be good citizens. Claudia wanted to be a citizen too. She wanted to be able to vote in elections. She believed she owed the United States her loyalty. After all, America had given her an education, a job and a beautiful family.

There was a lot of paperwork to fill out. Claudia had to meet and talk to many people during the citizenship process. She even had to take a test on U.S. history and government. Finally, the day arrived. Claudia received a letter telling her she could become a citizen of the United States of America.

Claudia was very excited to become a citizen. "It is a great experience to appreciate the beauty and the resources that this country has to offer to its citizens. Here in the United States, all of my dreams really did come true," Claudia said.

title: Come Join the Party!
text:
Each June, San Antonio puts on the biggest cultural celebration in all of Texas. The Texas Folklife Festival has been around since 1972 and just keeps getting bigger and better.

The Texas Folklife Festival brings more than 40 different cultures from across the state together for three days of food, crafts, music and dancing. The money raised at the festival goes back to the different cultural groups who participate in the event. Some use the money for scholarships and others use it to teach their young people more about their native cultures.

At the festival, you can taste Polish pierogi (dumplings), Japanese yakitorit (chicken kabobs), Lebanese kibbee (ground lamb or pork) burgers, Filipino pancit (stir fried noodles) or dozens of other traditional foods. You can even try your hand at making pickles, compete in a watermelon seed spitting contest or learn to clog. You can also enjoy music and dances from all over the world and shop for crafts from many different countries and cultures.

The festival is held on the grounds of the Institute of Texan Cultures on the UTSA HemisFair Park Campus during the second weekend in June. The Texas Folklife Festival is one of the biggest and best parties in Texas!

title: One State, Many Cultures
text:
Texas is a one-of-a-kind state. It has many different landform regions. There are many industries that make it possible for people to make a living doing just about anything they like. Plus Texas, is the second-largest state. But the people are what really make Texas such a great place to live.

About 24 million people call Texas home today. These people come from many different backgrounds and ethnic groups. Ethnic groups are made up of people who share a common language and customs. These common practices make each group special. Your family probably has customs you all share. The types of foods you eat and the ways you celebrate holidays are both customs.

There are people from almost every country in the world who now call Texas home. People with African and Hispanic heritages, or shared histories, make up a big part of the Texas population. But there are also many people whose heritage comes from Europe and Asia. People with shared heritages have many things in common. They most often share a language, religion and way of life.

It is interesting to study the ethnic groups who have settled in Texas. They have many things in common. They are different in many ways too. Let's learn a little more about groups of people who came to live in Texas and stayed here.

African American Texans

African Americans are some of Texas' oldest residents. Estevanico was the first African to spend time in Texas. He explored Texas for Spain with Cabeza de Vaca. Other Africans came into Texas with the early Spanish explorers and settled the Texas land.

However, most African Americans came to Texas as enslaved people. After the Civil War, they were freed, but most of them stayed in Texas. Many of them moved from rural farms to cities, where they hoped to find work. This was not an easy choice. For many years there were laws that made it difficult for these people to enjoy their freedom and life in Texas. But they did not give up.

Over time, African Americans became involved in the government. They helped make new laws that would protect the rights of the people. They worked hard to improve their communities. Many industries in modern Texas improved because of the efforts of African American citizens. As of 2000, African Americans made up about 12 percent of the Texas population. African Americans have contributed a lot to make Texas the great state it is today.

Hispanic Texans

More than one-third of the people living in Texas today have a Hispanic ethnic background. Many of these people have relatives who came to live in Texas from Mexico. But this group also includes people with ties to South America, Puerto Rico, Cuba and Spain.

By 1850, there were more than 14,000 people in Texas with a Hispanic heritage. Many of these people migrated, or moved, from Mexico to Texas to find work and escape the violence of war in their homeland. Many found work in the ranching, farming and oil industries during the past two centuries. Thanks to their efforts, Texas grew and succeeded in all these industries.

After World War II, many Hispanic Texans left rural areas and headed to cities. They wanted the opportunity to work in different industries. These Hispanics continued to work hard and stick together. That culture is seen even today in the Hispanic population of Texas. Many Hispanic Texans share a strong sense of family and religion. They have proved their dedication to the state and look ahead to a bright future for themselves.

German Texans

People with a German descent make up the largest European ethnic group in Texas today. Germans started immigrating to Texas in the 1830s. They have always stuck together in their communities. Most of them settled in what is called the "German Belt" in south-central Texas. They lived in both urban and rural areas.

The Germans who settled Texas came from all backgrounds. Some had been poor farmers. Some were teachers with university educations. Others were craftsmen and artists. They had different religions. There were Germans who were Catholic, Jewish or Protestant. They even spoke different forms of their language.

The German immigrants did share some things in common. They were known for the rock houses they built. They were also known for their special foods such as sausage and beer. They danced German polka dances and celebrated German holidays such as Easter Fires. Today there are still strong German communities in the Hill Country region.

Asian Texans

In 2000, people with an Asian heritage owned almost five percent of all Texas businesses. But immigration into Texas has not been easy for this group.

Many Chinese people came to Texas to work on the railoads in the 1800s. Later the United States limited the number of Asians who could come into the country. In fact, until 1956, there were many laws to keep people of this ethnic group in their own countries.

Between 1975 and 2000, the number of Asian immigrants into Texas doubled, and that number is still growing. They come from many different Asian countries and cultures. Many of these people choose to live in some of the state's largest cities. Within their culture groups, these immigrants share common foods, music and religion.

title: Texans Honor Cultures with Celebrations
text:
There are many people from different cultures who live in Texas today. They want to keep their traditions and customs alive. One way they do this is by having celebrations just like they did back in their home country. These joyful occasions mark a special event. Parents usually pass on traditions to their children.

In the African American culture, there are celebrations to mark the end of slavery. In Texas, June 19 is celebrated as Juneteenth each year. Special celebrations throughout the month of February honor the memory and accomplishments of African Americans in history.

Hispanic Texans often celebrate birthdays by breaking open a piñata filled with candy. On a girl's 15th birthday, they have a special birthday party called a quinceanera. It is marked with a party and a religious service. At Christmas time, many Catholics celebrate the birth of Jesus with a Las Posadas festival.

Jewish Texans might find themselves having a special party called a bat mitzvah for girls or a bar mitzvah for boys. These celebrations are religious ceremonies to mark becoming an adult.

New year celebrations are held in many cultures. Al-Hijra marks the beginning of the Muslim new year. It is held the first month of each Islamic calendar. Asian families celebrate their new year in February.

Sharing these celebrations keeps the people in the cultures close. It also gives other Texans a chance to learn more about new cultures and traditions.

title: Hispanic Culture Seen in Texas Life Today
text:
If you live in Texas, chances are you've seen a rodeo. You have probably eaten chili or tacos and had a barbecue. And you'd be excited if a friend asked you to go with her to a fiesta. All of these events and foods have been passed to Texas culture today. And they all have a Hispanic background.

Some of the earliest settlers to Texas were from Spain and Mexico. They came to Texas for many reasons. Some came for work opportunities. Some wanted to own land. Others wanted to find gold and riches. Others simply wanted freedom. Many of these people brought their strong heritage and customs with them.

Many places in Texas have Hispanic names. (Think about San Antonio, Laredo and the Rio Grande and Brazos rivers.) Many Texans speak Spanish. Some businesses in Texas today make sure they have employees who can speak both English and Spanish.

Many of these early Hispanic Texans were cowboys, or vaqueros. They worked on ranches. Texas cowboys soon adapted the clothing, equipment and traditions of these cowboys. Ranchers in Texas today still use many of the techniques that were passed from the vaqueros.

Much of the food in Texas has a Tex-Mex style. This type of cooking is a blend of Mexican, Spanish and American Indian ways of cooking. Many families in Texas enjoy the spicy foods of Hispanic heritage.

If you listen and look around in Texas, you will also see the influence of the Hispanic culture. Some homes, churches and businesses have the same style of the early Spanish missions. Music in Texas is a unique blend of Mexican rhythms combined with the music of other cultures.

All of these things can remind us of our state's rich history. We can remember the culture and heritage of our ancestors. We can remember the things in the past that help make us the great state we are today.

title: Critical Analysis and Rumination: President Truman and The Atomic Bomb Decision
text:
rumination (noun): the act of giving serious thought and consideration to something

Adolf Hitler was defeated in May 1945 after years of war in Europe, and American troops would be coming home - wouldn't they? Victory in Europe meant that some U.S. soldiers would be returning home. Others would go to the Pacific to face Japanese armies. Scientists in the U.S. had made a weapon that could certainly end the war with Japan, but it was so powerful that tens of thousands of people would be killed, including civilians (citizens not in the military). President Harry Truman had a decision to make that would greatly affect the world. What would the commander in chief do?

In the years leading up to President Truman's decision, the Japanese had been a brutal enemy. They had killed thousands of Americans at sea and on Pacific islands, including the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor in Hawaii. The president wondered how many more lives would be lost if we tried to end the war without the atomic bomb. What would happen if another country improved the weapon and used the bomb before we did? Would they use it on us?

President Truman tried several times without success to work out surrender with Japan. He then ordered atomic bombs to be dropped on the cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945. Within a week of the second attack, Japan did surrender, which put an end to World War II. Historians estimate that between 150,000 and 240,000 Japanese were killed from effects of the two bombings. They also estimate that thousands of American lives were saved. Do you think President Truman made the right decision?

title: Texas Population
text:
Directions: Study the bar graph showing the percentage of the ethnic group populations in Texas in 2000.

Convert, or change, the data from the graph into a two-column table. Use the headings “Ethnic Group” and “Percentage of Population.” Be sure to include a title for your table.

title: Texas, Our Texas
text:
"I must say as to what I have seen of Texas, it is the garden spot of the world, the best land and the best prospects for health I ever saw, and I do believe it is a fortune to any man to come here." - Davy Crockett

Ask anyone to point to Texas on a map and, chances are, they will have no problem doing so. It is very easy to recognize the shape of Texas. But, just because you recognize Texas doesn't mean you really understand what it's like to live in Texas. For that, you must be a Texan.

We Texans take pride in our state. We like to let other people know how we feel about living on this beautiful, open land. We like to share stories that explain the spirit of the people who call Texas home.

What makes Texas so special, you ask? Perhaps it is the size. Texas is the second largest state. (Only Alaska is bigger.) Maybe Texas is special because the land is so diverse. The land looks amazing, but it is different in every part of our state. Is Texas special because of its wealth? After all, Texas leads the nation in oil and cattle production, and Texas exports more goods than any other state. Maybe Texas is special because Texas has great weather. Most cities have sunshine almost every day. Plus, there are great schools and universities in the Lone Star State. And we haven't even mentioned the people of the state. They are friendly and willing to help a neighbor at any time. The list goes on and on. The truth is that it's not just one thing that makes Texas a great place to live. These little things all add up to help make one amazing state.

In this issue, you will review all the changes Texas has gone through. You will be able to revisit all of the incredible events that have made Texas what it is today - the very best place in the world to live. Just ask a Texan!

title: A Big Bowl of Red
text:
When the state legislature decided to choose an official state dish in 1977, chili was the natural choice. Our traditional Texas chili got its start in the early 1900s at the market area of San Antonio. Here the cattle herders, missionaries and railroad men all met together to do their business. "Chili Queens" from the nearby mission would make big pots of traditional stew made from beef, chili peppers and onions and bring the chili to the market. They set up tables and sold the stew by the bowlful to their eager customers.

Texans take their chili very seriously and many believe a bowl should be hot, spicy and contain no beans. There is even a song called, "If You Know Beans About Chili, You Know That Chili Has No Beans."

Here is a copy of a basic, early recipe for our state dish:

Chili con Carne

Cut up as much meat as you think you will need (any kind will do, but beef is probably best) in pieces about the size of a pecan. Put it in a pot, along with some suet (enough so the meat won't stick to the sides of the pot) and cook it with about the same amount of wild onions, garlic, oregano and chilies as you have meat. Put in some salt. Stir it from time to time and cook it until the meat is as tender as you think it's going to get.

title: Six Flags Over Texas
text:
Texans often speak with pride about the "Six Flags Over Texas." They are not talking about the amusement park built in 1961. Instead, they are talking about the flags of the six nations that have governed Texas. The flags of Spain, France, Mexico, Texas, the Confederacy and the United States have each flown over Texas at one time in history.

Let's take a look at the history of Texas when each flag flew over our state.

Spain - 1500s

Christopher Columbus made an accidental discovery in 1492. He found the land known as North America. Spanish explorers were sent to find out more about the land. They quickly learned that the Americas were full of riches. This included what we know as Texas today. There was gold, silver and lots of good land. Spain's rulers quickly came up with a plan to explore the land.

Spain had three goals. First, they wanted to collect the riches that could be found on the new land. Second, they wanted to teach the American Indians about the Roman Catholic Church. Third, they wanted to conquer the land and make it their own.

Spanish explorers were very excited when they found Texas. Even though they didn't find gold and riches, they had found plenty of good land. Spain's flag was the first to fly over Texas. Spanish explorers such as Cabeza de Vaca, Alonso de Pineda, Francisco Coronado and Juan de Oñate all explored and mapped the Texas land.

France - 1685

Spain claimed much of North America for almost 100 years. But then another country from Europe started exploring the lands hoping to find their own riches. In 1685, Robert de LaSalle came to Texas from France. He had already claimed land near the Mississippi River for Louis XIV, the king of France. He named the land Louisiana in the king's honor. The king wanted to send LaSalle back to start a colony. The new settlement meant France would have control of the land.

But LaSalle could not find the Mississippi River again. Instead, he landed at Matagorda Bay on the Texas coast. There he and his men claimed the land for France. The French flag became the second flag to fly over Texas.

The French colony did not last very long. LaSalle was killed by his own men. But the French colony did make Spain take notice. Now Spain really wanted to make sure other explorers stayed off the Texas land.

Mexico - 1800s

The explorers from Spain had a firm control of Texas. They established missions and communities to help them hold onto the land. Small towns sprang up near the missions. The Spanish flag flew high over the land. But then change came again.

Spain was also in control of Mexico at this time. In the early 1800s, the Mexican citizens began to speak out against Spain's control. The people of Mexico wanted a government that would be fair to all people. They wanted Spain out of their country. The Mexican people fought a war to get the Spanish rulers out. In 1821, Mexico won the war. Spanish rulers had to return to their country. They also had to give up much of the North American land that was once theirs. This included Texas.

Mexico's flag now flew over Texas. Mexico wanted to hold onto the new land. They continued doing what Spain had done. They gave out grants of land to businessmen. These men would then use these land gifts to start colonies. Mexico thought it would be good to have lots of people and settlements on the Texas land. They thought it might help keep Spain and other countries from trying to take over again. One large land grant was given to a man from Missouri. His name was Stephen F. Austin. He would come to be known as the Father of Texas.

Republic of Texas - 1836 to 1845

Texas settlers were upset with Mexico's laws and unfair treatment. So they declared their independence from Mexico. For nine years, Texas was its own nation. The flag of the Republic of Texas flew during this time.

This was a difficult time for Texas. Many people died in battles against Mexico. The battles of Gonzales, Goliad, the Alamo and San Jacinto cost many Texans their lives. The new nation didn't have a lot of money. And they were always worried about being attacked. Many thought the best thing would be to become part of the United States of America.

Confederate States of America - 1861 to 1865

Texas became a state in 1845. But when the United States was torn apart during the Civil War, Texas seceded, or withdrew, with 10 other states to form the Confederate States of America.

The Confederate flag flew over Texas until the end of the Civil War in 1865. At that time, Texas was readmitted to the United States of America.

United States of America - 1845 to 1861 and 1865 to Present

Texans have proudly flown the flag of the United States of America since the end of the Civil War. While Texans are certainly proud of our state, we are equally proud of our nation. There are many people in Texas who have bravely fought to keep the freedoms that we have. The flag is a symbol of these freedoms.

title: Angels of the Alamo: Adina De Zavala and Clara Driscoll
text:
From an early age, Adina De Zavala was passionate about Texas history. Perhaps this was because her grandfather was Lorenzo de Zavala, the first vice-president of the Republic of Texas. (Did you notice that Adina used a capital "D" in her name but her grandfather did not? Adina's father changed from de Zavala to De Zavala.) Adina grew up to become a teacher in San Antonio. There she began her lifelong efforts to preserve historic Texas sites for the education of future generations.

Adina was concerned about the Mission San Antonio de Valero, also known as the Alamo. The State of Texas owned the chapel, but another building in the mission complex was being sold to a hotel chain. This was the long barracks, or convento, where much of the bloodiest fighting during the battle of the Alamo took place.

Adina joined with another Texan who loved history, the wealthy Clara Driscoll, to raise money to save the Alamo grounds. When they could not get the funds they needed, Clara Driscoll used her own money to buy the property and turn it over to the State of Texas in 1903. The Alamo was saved.

Adina De Zavala continued the fight to preserve Texas landmarks. She formed the De Zavala chapter of the Daughters of the Republic of Texas, or DRT, a conservationist group. She led the campaign, which put historic markers on almost 40 sites in Texas, which might have been forgotten, including the Spanish Governor's Palace in San Antonio and the Mission San Francisco de los Tejas in East Texas.

Clara Driscoll spent the rest of her life writing books, stories and an opera about Texas. When she died, she left most of her family's fortune to build a children's hospital in Corpus Christi.

Adina De Zavala and Clara Driscoll: Angels of the Alamo and much more. These remarkable women will long be remembered for their part in preserving Texas history for the ages.

title: How did Texas get its name?
text:
Texas gets its name from the Caddo Indian word "teysha" which means "hello friend." Early Spanish explorers called the friendly tribes they met "teyshas." This later became the name Texas.

Texas has several nicknames including the Lone Star State, the Friendship State and the Jumbo State.

In 1961, the New Yorker magazine called Texas "The Super-American State." That fits too, don't you think?

Early people of Texas were called Texians, but now the word has changed to Texans. No matter what we're called, Texans are proud to be a part of this terrific state.

title: Good Citizenship - Texas Style
text:
The people of Texas are known for their friendliness. They are also known for showing good character. There are several ways you can show that you are a good Texas citizen.

Respect - Treat people the way you want to be treated.

Fairness - Follow rules and listen to other people's ideas.

Responsibility - Do what you are supposed to do; do not rely on other people to make sure you do what needs to be done.

Courage - Be brave; do the right thing even if it is hard to do.

Honesty - Always tell the truth; if you say you will do something, follow through.

Care - Think about other people and try to be concerned about others.

Contribute - Help others; be part of a group that makes a difference in the world.

Think about what makes a good citizen. Design and create a "Good Citizen of Texas" award for a classmate you think has been a good citizen all year. Present your award in front of the class and explain why you chose that person for the award.
