Then he won international championships at Wimbledon in England and at the Australian Open Tennis Tournament in Australia. He paved the way for African Americans in a sport that was usually for white players.

Ashe had a great career playing tennis for a long time. But he had a heart attack in 1979 and had to retire from playing. Instead, he coached other young tennis players. He also became a powerful voice for the rights of African Americans. He spoke against racial discrimination. He marched and protested in New York City and Washington, D.C. As a well-liked athlete, Ashe brought attention to racial equality all over the world.

Even though he did some great things, Ashe also faced some hard times. In 1983, he had surgery on his heart. After the surgery, he needed some donated blood. Unfortunately, the blood the doctors put into his body was infected with the HIV virus. Five years later Ashe became ill, and doctors realized he had the virus. Ashe died in 1993. He was only 50 years old.

After his death, Ashe’s body lay in state, or was honored, at the governor’s mansion in Richmond. Anyone could come to show respect for this great man. Ashe was the first person to receive this praise since Stonewall Jackson died during the Civil War. Virginia was very proud of this great athlete from Richmond.

Arthur Ashe was more than a sports hero. He used his fame to help make positive changes. He was respectable and worked for worldwide civil rights. He is a fine example of an athlete who used his talent to make the world better.

title: Successful In Business
text:
Maggie L. Walker (1867 - 1934)

Maggie Lena Walker was a powerful businesswoman. She started her own business even when it was hard for women or African Americans to do well in business.

Maggie was born into a poor family right after the Civil War. Her mother was a former slave. As a child, Maggie helped her family earn money by washing the neighbors' laundry. When she was 14, she joined a charity group called the Order of St. Luke. The Order of St. Luke helped African Americans in many ways. She was a member of this group until she died.

In 1903, Maggie started the St. Luke Penny Bank. She told African Americans in Richmond to save their money and start businesses. She was the first woman president of a bank in the United States. In 1904, she and her husband moved to a new house in downtown Richmond. Their house had an elevator and 28 rooms. Maggie had come so far from her poor background.

Today, the Maggie Walker House is a national historic site, and you can visit it for a tour. Maggie worked hard and helped people who were less fortunate. She is a great example of business success in 20th century Virginia.

title: Fighting For Civil Rights
text:
Oliver W. Hill Sr. (1907 - 2007)

Oliver White Hill was a lawyer who fought for the civil rights of African Americans. He was born in Richmond and went to school in Washington, DC.

Oliver thought "separate but equal" schools were unfair and wrong. He worked to force Virginia counties to desegregate, or bring together, their schools. He also helped in the Brown vs. Board of Education case. This was a very important case that changed history in the United States. The outcome of this case said that segregated schools were unconstitutional.

Oliver practiced law for about 60 years. In 1999, President Clinton gave him the Presidential Medal of Freedom. This is the highest award a civilian, or a regular citizen, can earn.

Oliver passed away when he was 100 years old. He was a remarkable man who worked for equal rights for African Americans.

title: Famous Person Book
text:
Materials

12-inch by 18-inch piece of construction paper

6-inch by 6-inch piece of construction paper

Scissors

Glue

Crayons and markers

Instructions

Fold the piece of 12- by 18–inch paper into eight equal sections as shown in the picture.

(You don’t have to label your sections as they are labeled here. We’ve done that to help you know which pieces to cut and fold.) Cut out sections E and H. Save these pieces for later.

Fold sections A and D into the center to make a vest or jacket. Glue pieces E and H on the back for arms, as shown in the picture.

Cut a head from the 6 by 6–inch piece of construction paper. Glue it to the top of sections B and C. To make pants for your famous person, cut a small triangle between sections F and G as shown. (Or you can cut the lower corners off these sections to create a skirt.)

Draw your famous person’s face on the head. You can add hair and clothing. Add hands and shoes cut from paper scraps.

Open the flaps of the jacket and, on the inside, write something about your famous person. If you’d like, you can write a longer story or essay about your famous person on folded pieces of paper and then staple the pages into your famous person book.

Extra Activity: You can make your book about a family member or friend and give it to him or her as a gift.

title: Let's Write
text: In this issue you have learned about lots a great people in Virginia’s history. Write a fan letter to one of these outstanding Virginians. In your letter, be sure to introduce yourself. Explain why you admire this person and why you are his or her fan. Give at least two reasons. You can also ask any questions that you still have about this person. Be sure to use proper letter format.

title: Celebrating Virginia's Regions
text:
This is the final issue of Virginia Studies Weekly this year. That sure went by fast! We hope you have enjoyed our paper. You may have even learned something to boot! You learned about the American Indians who first lived here, the European explorers who settled here and present-day Virginia. Together we have learned so much. You read about many famous leaders, events and places in Virginia's rich history. By now you know that we are so lucky to live in Virginia. There are so many different regions, products and industries. There are natural resources and beautiful sights to see. Our state has grown and become more successful in the 20th and 21st centuries. Virginia really is a great place to be.

This week we will learn about industries and products. An industry is a group of businesses connected to a certain product. A product is one item or service that is sold. We'll take a look at the different regions of Virginia and what types of products and industries are in each one. We'll also discover what parts of our economy have helped Virginia prosper, or do well.

title: The Price of Growth
text:
Transportation has always been important to Virginia. Remember that early towns and cities grew along the rivers. Boats traveled to the fall line, where they unloaded goods to sell in other markets. Later, Virginia built trails and roads in the valleys and through the gaps in the mountains.

Today, Virginians still need to get around. But as you know, we do not use just rivers and trails for our transportation. Modern transportation uses cars, trucks and airplanes to tie us together. People use transportation to get to their jobs. Markets use transportations to get and sell products. Without those important transportation links, cities and towns cannot grow.

When the government decides to build a new road, there may be a few problems. Roads are expensive. Sometimes building them can destroy land and trees. Once the road is built, people will want homes and shops near it. Then they will use more land by the road. Soon there will be lots of crowds and traffic.

This process is called "sprawl." Sprawl is the uncontrolled growth into nearby countryside. You can see it in many parts of Virginia. You may even live in an area where there is sprawl. People disagree on how to deal best with this growth. Some people want to keep building more roads so there will be fewer traffic delays. Other people believe there should be more mass transportation - like buses, subways and commuter trains. Another idea is to build communities with sidewalks and bike trails. This would encourage more people to walk or ride bicycles instead of driving cars.

Virginia is a great place to live. People will continue to move here. The problem of how to handle growth will not go away. It is up to us to help reduce the number of cars on the road by carpooling, walking or biking whenever possible. Maybe by working together Virginians can solve these problems.

title: Regional Products and Industries
text:
Let's look at a map of Virginia's five regions. Each region has unique features and natural resources (things that exist or are formed in nature). Each region has different products and industries.

Coastal Plain (Tidewater)

Think of this region and you might think of Virginia Beach, Colonial Williamsburg or Busch Gardens. Those are all great places to take a vacation. That is why tourism is one of the most important industries in this region. Tourism is the industry that provides lodging (hotels and motels), transportation and other services to tourists. When tourists visit, they spend money at restaurants, parks, hotels and shops. The Coastal Plain region depends on this tourist income.

You might also think of Newport News shipbuilding, and you would be right. Shipbuilding is a major industry in this region. Another industry comes from the military. In this region, there are 14 military bases - like Oceana Naval Air Station in Virginia Beach.

Seafood is a major product of the Coastal Plain region. If you look at the map, it is not hard to see why. Blue crabs, scallops, oysters and fish are all harvested along this region's coastland and rivers.

Piedmont

Farming used to be the most important industry in this region. But now other industries are growing. This region now has technology companies that make and sell computers, software and office machines. Many Virginians in this region work for textile factories. The government is also a major industry in this region. Richmond, the state's capital, and Northern Virginia, where lots of federal workers live and work, are both in this region.

The Piedmont region also makes a lot of tobacco and information technology products.

Blue Ridge Mountain

This region has beautiful green hills, soaring mountains and blue skies. There are lots of places in this region to fish, ski, camp or boat on mountain lakes. So it is no surprise that its leading industry is recreation. People from all over like coming to the Blue Ridge Mountains to hike and enjoy the natural features.

This region is most famous for one product - its apples. The soil and climate here is great for growing apples. At harvest time, these apples are shipped all over the world.

Valley and Ridge

Farms dot the hillsides of this beautiful region. So you won't be surprised that farming is this region's most important industry. The biggest products from this region are apples and poultry. Some of the chicken you eat is probably raised in the Valley and Ridge region.

Appalachian Plateau

Only a small part of this plateau is in southwest Virginia. Ever since coal was discovered in the mountains, coal mining has been the leading industry in the region. And the leading product? Coal, of course!

title: Virginia Grows and Prospers
text:
In the past 100 years, Virginia has continued to grow. As more people choose to live in this state, the population has grown. Virginia has also grown in prosperity. Prosperity is a successful financial condition. There are four factors that helped: transportation, technology, tourism and federal workers.

Transportation

Virginia's transportation system now has many parts - highways, roads, railroads and airlines. These parts all work together. Virginia's modern system moves materials to factories and finished products to markets. Virginia exports many products, including tobacco, poultry, coal and large ships.

Technology

You know how important computers are these days. Computer technology is tied to better communication. Just think about it. You used to send a letter with an envelope and a stamp. Now you can now send an e-mail or a text message. When you needed to make a phone call, you used to have to find a telephone booth. Now you can use a cell phone. In Virginia, several areas have become technology centers. The computer industry has grown in Northern Virginia and Tidewater. This has helped bring more jobs and more people into Virginia.

Tourism

Virginia has lots of attractions for tourists. Caverns, mountains, beaches, historical sites and theme parks are just a few examples. Tourism helps a lot with Virginia's financial success.

Federal workers

Because many federal workers live or work in Virginia, the federal government really helps shape Virginia's economy. Just think of all the people you know who work in the military or for the government. All of those jobs, homes and offices bring more wealth to Virginia.

Each of these things helped Virginia become what it is today. Virginia's population and prosperity has grown because of its modern transportation systems, technology, tourism and federal workers.

title: State Parks in Virginia
text:
If you love outdoor fun, Virginia has just the place for you. Some of the best places for outdoor activities are in a Virginia state park. State parks are natural and protected areas. This means no one can build or develop on the land. State parks are open for visitors to use and enjoy.

Virginia state parks began in 1936 during the Great Depression. To help families, President Franklin D. Roosevelt started the Civilian Conservation Corps, or the CCC. This was a program for unmarried men, ages 18 to 25. The men could volunteer to work for the CCC and get paid $30 per month. They had to send $25 home to help their families, but they got to keep the other $5.

How is the CCC connected to Virginia’s state parks? Well, the men in the CCC worked on building projects. They built bridges, roads and shelters. They restored buildings and cleared trails for hiking. They built cabins and dug wells. They built six state parks in Virginia. These parks opened in 1936.

The park system has continued to grow over the years. The parks are responsible for two things—protecting wildlife and natural areas and making those areas available for visitors to enjoy. Look at the map. Which state park is closest to you? How many have you visited?

title: World Community Studies Weekly!
text:
What is a community? A community is a group of people who live in the same area. In Studies Weekly this year, you will learn about communities around the world. You will also study the many ways that people make a difference in their communities, their countries and the world.

We're going to start by learning about maps. Maps can help us learn something about a country or community. Reading maps is fun. When you learn about symbols and keys on a map, it's like learning a secret code. You'll discover keys and symbols inside this paper. First, let's answer a couple of questions: What is a map? How do maps help us?

Have you ever built a model of an airplane or seen a model of a car? Models are often small versions of something big, but they can also be big versions of something small. If you've ever put together a model of an insect, you know what we mean. The models are like the real objects, sometimes down to the smallest detail. A map is just like that. It would be impossible to make a map that was the size of a country or even the world. So map makers try to make the map just like the part of the world they are showing, only smaller.

There are many kinds of maps. Some maps show you what the Earth looks like. They show things like mountains, rivers and valleys. Other maps have a theme. Those maps tell you things like how many people live in a certain place or how much rain falls there. Other maps show us where states, countries and cities are located. We'll learn a lot more about all of these maps in later issues. Now it's time to travel through the rest of this week's paper. You won't need a map to find your way - just read and turn the pages!

title: Learning All About Maps
text:
Let's learn about maps and globes and how to use them to find places, measure distances and get important information.

Map Symbols and Keys Unlock the Code

Map symbols help us read a map. A symbol on a map stands for something real. A fast way to find something on a map is to look for the symbol. What if you don't know what a symbol stands for? Then you need to look for the key. (On some maps, it is called a legend.) The key is a box of symbols and words that tell what the symbols mean. (Look on Page 4 to see an example.) Look on a road map and find the key. Can you see a symbol for an airport? The scale of a map shows the map is proportionate. It usually looks something like this:

The scale above shows that one inch on the map equals one real mile.

Maps Show Directions

Looking at the directions on a map can tell you which way to go. The four main directions are north, south, east and west. These are called cardinal directions. On most maps, north is at the top, south is at the bottom, east is on the right, and west is on the left. But you don't always travel in one of those four directions. Sometimes, you need the intermediate directions - northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest. The intermediate directions lie in between the two cardinal directions that are in their names. For example, northeast would be between north and east. A compass rose shows us the cardinal and intermediate directions on a map. Larger points mark the cardinal directions, and smaller points mark the intermediate directions.

Score Yourself On the map to the right, find and label all of the things listed below. For each right answer, give yourself five points, plus a pat on the back for a really great job. We hope you will continue to practice your map skills by looking at many maps. Locate the key, find the symbols, and see if you can locate the items you need. You can find maps in an atlas at your school or local library. Check with your teacher to see if you labeled all the things correctly.

1. Write the cardinal and intermediate directions in the compass rose (N, S, E, W, NE, SE, NW, SW).

2. Draw symbols for the map key.

3. Using the symbols on your key, draw the following on the map:

A. A house between Red Street and Green Street

B. A school between Green Street and Yellow Street

C. A gas station west of White Avenue and south of Yellow Street

D. A lake between Blue Lane and White Avenue

E. An airport east of Blue Lane and north of Red Street

F. A hospital west of White Avenue and north of Red Street

title: Tools of the Trade - The Compass
text:
The compass is every explorer's best friend. It is a tool that often looks like a pocket watch. It has a magnetic needle that can turn easily. The cardinal directions - north, east, south and west - are labeled on the face of the compass. It always points north because there are magnetic fields around the Earth. The needle lines up with those fields to guide the traveler. It takes some practice to know how to use a compass, so be sure to learn before your next camping trip!

Who invented the compass? The Chinese invented the first compass to use a magnetic needle. They were using their compass to explore the oceans as early as 2,000 years ago.

What are some other ways to tell your directions? You can look for landmarks with which you are familiar. For example, you might remember that the tallest building in your town is north of you. Another way is to use the sun as your guide. Because the sun rises in the east, north is to the left of the sunrise. Finally, you can use the North Star, or Polaris. It is in line with the Earth's axis, so it always appears to remain in the north.

title: Rain Forests
text:
What is an ecosystem anyway? Well, it’s a community (group) of plants and animals that all work together as a unit in a specific place. During the year we’re going to look at a number of different ecosystems. This week we are looking at rain forests.

A rain forest is a thick evergreen forest that gets 50 to 260 inches of rain a year. Tropical rain forests are located in areas around the equator. Rain forests only cover six percent of the Earth’s surface, but they are home to more than half of all of the Earth’s plants and animals. Rain forests make much of the Earth’s oxygen. Many of the plants found there are used to make new medicines that fight diseases. Some of the food you eat comes from the rain forest, too. Things like cashews, bananas, cocoa (chocolate), cinnamon and vanilla all come from the rain forest.

The soil in a rain forest is very old and very thin. In fact it is only three to four inches thick. Once it is damaged it takes a very long time to recover. Unfortunately, much of the rain forest has been destroyed for lumber. People need wood for buildings and furniture. Lumber companies cut down rain forest trees to get wood. Every second we are losing 1 1⁄2 acres of trees! There are many organizations that are trying to stop this. Some are working to replant some of the trees. They are also helping people learn how important rain forests are to all of us. To find out more about rain forests go to: rain-tree.com/facts.htm.

title: My Neighborhood
text:
You can use grid lines to find the location of things on a map. Here’s how: Put your finger on the playground. Move your finger along the closest line that leads to the letters at the bottom. What letter do you see? Put your finger on the playground again. Move your finger along the closest line that leads to the numbers on the side. Your answer should look like this: playground A-6

Use the grid lines to find the location of these things on the map:

1. fire station ____________

2. hospital ______________

3. school _______________

4. lake _________________

5. house _______________

Next, draw one thing you want on the map. Write its location here.

text: You are so lucky! You just found a very old map in a chest in your grandmother’s attic. Draw a picture of the map and all that it shows you. Is it a treasure map? Be sure to include a title, compass rose, symbols and a key (legend).

title: The Amazing World of Maps
text:
This week we are continuing our study of map skills. Inside, you will learn about the way geographers describe the locations of different places. First, let's talk about the different kinds of maps that you can use to find any place on Earth.

Flat Maps

Some maps are better at showing how the land really looks than other maps are. A Mercator map is a map that uses lines like a checkerboard. All the lines are straight and even. It's pretty good for finding places, but it doesn't show how the land really looks.

An interrupted projection map looks like the land was peeled off the globe. The lines are curved, not straight, just like they are on the globe. Because of this, you can see how one piece of land compares in size to another piece of land much better. Compare Antarctica on the Mercator map and the interrupted projection map. Which one do you think is more correct? Look at a globe to find out!

Alphanumeric Map

An Alphanumeric map is a map with a grid on it to help you find places on the map. These maps have an index that lists all the places on the map and the grid lines where the place can be found. You might find a city called Happy Town at B-4. Follow the line across the bottom of the map to B, then follow the line marked B up until you come to 4. That is where Happy Town would be.

The letters and numbers are called coordinates. Look at the map and see if you can find the coordinates that are closest to your city.

Globes

When you want something realistic, the map of choice would be the globe. The globe is a very accurate way to represent our Earth. One disadvantage is that you can only see half of the globe at a time. Another disadvantage is that it's hard to fold a globe into your backpack for a geography project.

Theme Maps

Anytime you want to show something special about an area of land you can use a theme map. Theme maps might show the population, how much rain falls, what kinds of crops are grown, the different animals you might find —pretty much anything you want to show about a particular place.

title: Reason and Logic: Young George Washington, Surveyor and Mapmaker
text:
Most people know about George Washington. He was born in Virginia. He was a general during the American Revolution and our first president. But his earliest jobs, surveyor and cartographer (mapmaker), taught him skills and values he would use for the rest of his life. Using reason and logic to solve problems helped Washington become one of our country's most important leaders.

When Washington grew up, there were few roads or boundaries in much of the land. A surveyor's job was to measure and map the land. He had to make exact measurements for boundaries and physical features. This was a very big responsibility. People needed accurate maps and surveys for traveling and buying land.

At age 17, Washington traveled across the Blue Ridge Mountains to map and survey part of the frontier. He was the surveyor for the whole county, and that was an important job. When he led the Continental Army, it was even more important to have reliable maps. He established the job of Geographer and Surveyor General and appointed a man named Robert Erskine to this position. He gave Washington some information that was very helpful in making reasonable and logical battle plans and decisions.

You can use these same skills to make important decisions. Be sure you have the facts and information you need instead of acting on opinions and emotions. In what areas of your life are reason and logic very important?

title: Which End is Up?
text:
Hemispheres

Can you find the North and South poles on the globe? Halfway between those poles is an imaginary line around the Earth called the equator. We call the top half the Northern Hemisphere and the bottom half the Southern Hemisphere. The world can also be divided into Western and Eastern hemispheres. This is done by grouping continents. The Eastern Hemisphere is made up of Europe, Asia, Australia, Africa and half of Antarctica. The Western Hemisphere is made up of North America, South America and half of Antarctica.

Latitude and Longitude

Many maps have lines running east to west (side to side). These lines are called lines of latitude or parallels. These lines mark distances in degrees. If you can count by tens, you can name the lines of latitude. The equator is zero. The lines of latitude north of the equator are all named north latitude. They go all the way up to the North Pole, which is 90 N latitude. All of the lines south of the equator are named south latitude. They go all the way down to the South Pole, which is 90 S latitude. These lines are also called parallels because the distance between a line of latitude and another (either north or south) always stays the same... all the way around the Earth.

On some maps, you will see lines that are running north to south (up and down). These imaginary lines are called meridians or lines of longitude. These lines are different from the parallels because they are not the same distance apart, but they get closer and closer until they come together at the poles. Look on a globe and find the poles. See how the lines of longitude come together? The middle line, or the line that is zero, is called the prime meridian. Everything west of the prime meridian to 180 is named west longitude, and everything east of the prime meridian to 180 is named east longitude. Lines of longitude are also used for measuring distances and for establishing time zones. Their most important function is, together with the lines of latitude, to pinpoint locations on Earth.

International Date Line

Have you ever heard of the International Date Line? It's an imaginary line on the other side of the Earth from the Prime Meridian, and it's not a straight line! The International Date Line marks the place where the beginning of one day and the end of another day meet. In other words, on one side of the line it's Monday, and on the other side it's Tuesday. If that sounds confusing, imagine what it would be like to live in a country right on the International Date Line! What if it was Monday at your house and Tuesday at your friend's house just a few miles away? That was the problem in the country of Kiribati, so the people who live there decided to move the line in 1995. Now the line goes around Kiribati, and the days are the same all over the country. Look on a map or globe to see the way the International Date Line zigzags from the North Pole to the South Pole.

title: Global Positioning System
text:
What would you do if you went on a hike and got lost? You would be able to find out where you were if you had a Global Positioning System, or GPS.

The early Global Positioning Systems were very large and could only locate your position within 50 feet. Later, Charles Counselman, a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, made them about the size of a backpack. He also improved the technology so that you could determine your location to within just a centimeter! Today's GPS receivers are small enough to fit in your pocket. Many cars come with a GPS and a computer program that gives you directions to wherever you are going. In 2002 a GPS helped save nine coal miners who were trapped underground for more than three days.

title: Relative and Absolute Locations
text:
Imagine you have a pen pal in Africa. One day, you get a letter, and your pen pal asks you where your city or town is located. What would you say? If you live in Titusville, you might say that it's on the Atlantic Ocean near the Kennedy Space Center.

When you describe the location of a place by naming some nearby landmarks, you are giving the relative location of that place. But geographers and explorers often need more specific information about a place. They need to know the absolute location, or the latitude and longitude. The absolute location of Titusville is 29 degrees north latitude and 81 degrees west longitude.

Let's say that your pen pal lives in Nairobi, Kenya. She might tell you its relative location by saying that Nairobi is in the southern part of the country about 200 kilometers (about 125 miles) from the northern border of Tanzania. Nairobi's absolute location is 1 degree south latitude and 37 degrees east longitude. The latitude tells you that your pen pal lives very close to the equator. Most of the time, you will only need to know the relative location of a place, but who knows? You may be an explorer someday, and absolute location will be necessary.

title: Meet the Continents
text:
The Earth is divided into continents, or bodies of land. Earth is usually said to have seven continents. They are Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia, Africa, South America and Europe. The continents of Europe and Asia are different from the others. They are not separated by water like the other continents. Because there are differences in the look of the people, their customs and dress, they are usually considered separate continents. However, some geographers (experts on Earth's characteristics) and scientists feel Europe and Asia should be one continent, and they call it Eurasia. They count only six continents, with Eurasia being the largest.

North America is where you will find our own United States. It also includes Canada, Mexico, Central America, Greenland and the islands of the Caribbean. North America boasts the most varied climate of all the continents. Everything from desert to the ice-covered polar regions is found in North America. The narrowest part of North America, Panama, is only 30 miles wide.

South America is the fourth-largest continent. There are 12 independent countries in South America. The world's largest tropical rain forest covers one-third of the continent. South America is also the home to the driest desert in the world (except for Antarctica). The Atacam Desert has areas where it has not rained for hundreds of years.

Antarctica is the fifth-largest continent. Antarctica's center is the South Pole. It is so cold, only a handful of scientists and midges live there. (Midges are small, gnat-like insects.) The land of Antarctica is covered by a huge icecap. The highest mountain tips are the only lands that can be seen above the ice. Antarctica is the only continent without a country. It is probably the quietest continent, too!

Europe is the sixth-largest continent. It is the home of 35 countries. Vatican City, the world's smallest country, is in Europe. Although Europe is the second-smallest continent, it has more people than any other continent except Asia.

Asia is the largest continent in size. It is bigger than North America, Europe and Australia all put together. More people live in Asia than in all of the rest of our world. Asia also includes thousands of islands, including Cyprus, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan and Japan.

Australia is the smallest and flattest continent. It is certainly home to more kangaroos than any other continent - 45 different species, to be sure. Four great deserts cover the center of Australia. These deserts have many giant sand dunes. Some dunes are more than 200 meters high.

Africa is the second largest continent. Six hundred seventy million people live in Africa, and more than half are younger than age 15. The largest desert (Sahara), the longest river (Nile) and a large tropical forest are all found in Africa. Africa is home to 53 countries, and more than 1,600 languages are spoken there.

title: The Poles
text:
As you probably know, the North and South poles are at the top and bottom of the globe. At the poles, the sun never rises during part of the winter, and never sets during part of the summer. The South Pole region is called Antarctica, and it is a continent. There is actually land under all that ice and snow! It is the colder of the two poles. In fact, it is so cold that it can't snow very often, but it is very windy. It usually doesn't get above freezing even in the summertime. Penguins live there, but not polar bears. In fact, people don't even live there. The only people you would find at the South Pole are scientists.

The North Pole region is called the Arctic. It is not a continent because there is no land under it, only the frozen water of the Arctic Ocean. The ice is about six to 10 feet thick and floats on top of the ocean. In the winter the Arctic region is about the size of the United States, but in the summer, half of it melts into the ocean. There are many more animals living in the Arctic than in the Antarctic. Here you will find killer whales, seals, walruses and polar bears, just to name a few. Brrrr! The poles are a beautiful, exciting and very chilly part of our Earth.

title: Astrolabe
text:
Sea travelers figured out how to find out where they were by using the North Star as a guide. The North Star is always to the north. So by looking at where the North Star was above the horizon, they could determine their latitude. The latitude tells you how far north or south of the equator you are. People used to use their arms and fingers and "shoot" at the star to measure how far up the North Star is.

Eventually, people invented tools to help find out where they were. The astrolabe is a tool sailors often used to figure out latitude. People also used it to tell the time, day or night.

title: The Desert
text:
The desert is an amazing physical feature of our planet. You might think it is just sand and a cactus or two, but that's not true. It's definitely not a boring place. One thing deserts have in common is that they are all arid (very dry). More than one third of Earth's surface is covered by deserts. Deserts get less than 10 inches of rain a year, so desert plants enjoy a short but beautiful life cycle.

The temperature changes a lot between day and night in a desert. During the day it can reach 110 degrees but drop all the way to 50 degrees at night. Speaking of hot places, did you know that the hottest temperature on Earth was recorded in Death Valley, California, in 1913? On that date the temperature in Death Valley was 134 degrees Fahrenheit. Whew!

One of the most interesting things about a desert is the animals that live there. They really know how to adapt. Bighorn sheep can survive for more than 10 days without a drink. Some people say that the kangaroo rat is the desert's best survivor, because it only eats dry seeds, and no one has ever seen it drink water! In Africa, the lungfish buries itself in mud for months waiting for rain. Are you surprised to learn that fish can live in a desert?

There are interesting plants in the desert, too. Some bloom at night when it is cooler. One of these plants is the Saguaro Cactus, the state flower of Arizona. This cactus only grows about an inch a year, but it can grow to 50 feet tall and live to be more than 200 years old. Because it grows so slowly and can store a lot of water, it flowers every year. As a Saguaro Cactus ages, it develops holes that some animals use as homes. A desert may be hot and dry, but it is never, ever boring.

title: Mapping the News
text:
Have you ever heard or read a news report about a certain place and wondered where it is? Mapping the news can help. This is a fun way to learn geography and keep up with things that are going on in the world at the same time.

Here’s how it works: Your teacher will put a world map on a bulletin board in your classroom or in the hall. Once a week, students can bring in news articles to share with the class. (Ask your parents to help you with that part, especially if you get your news articles from the Internet. Also, do some research before you get to class to get a general idea of where the place is located.) In class, talk about each article and the place where the event happened. Find that place on the world map and mark it with a push pin or a sticker. For example, let’s say your friend brings an article about a mountain climber who reaches the top of Mount Everest on the border between Tibet and Nepal. She found out that those two countries are in south Asia. That will help you find Mount Everest more quickly.

Try mapping the news for several weeks. Then get into groups and make up a game that involves the places you mapped. Playing the game will help you remember what you learned. Have fun mapping the news!

title: What Is Time?
text:
Time is what keeps everything from happening at once. That's how one British clockmaker defines time. For ages, people have tried to define time, measure it and divide it. Today, we have a good way to mark the passage of time with calendars and clocks.

How do we talk about events of the past? Things that happened in the past are known as history. Historical events are usually described in the order in which they happened. Another way of saying that is in chronological order. When we put events in order, it links them together as if they were events on a chain. It is a way of linking the past with the present.

A timeline is a handy way to show events and happenings in chronological order. A timeline can cover any length of time from a day to many millions of years. For example, you could make a timeline of what you will do tomorrow starting at 6 a.m. and ending at 9 p.m. Or you could make a timeline of prehistoric life. That could cover millions of years. Inside, you will find a timeline of things that happened during ancient times.

To make a timeline, you first have to do some research. You can find information in many places - encyclopedias, almanacs, newspapers, and magazines. You can ask an adult to help you use the Internet to find the information you need.

Sources of information can be either primary or secondary. Primary sources are sources that are in their original form. Diaries, letters and autobiographies (books written by people about their own lives) are usually considered primary sources. Secondary sources often contain information from primary sources, but they are usually written some time after an event occurred. Encyclopedias, textbooks and almanacs are secondary sources.

title: The Crypt of Civilization
text:
Mark this date on your calendar: May 28, 8113. Oh, wait. You don't have a calendar for 8113 yet, do you? On that date, an amazing time capsule at Oglethorpe University in Georgia will be opened. What's inside? Hundreds of things from clothes to toys to tools to books, even a set of dentures!

In the 1930s, Dr. Thorwell Jacobs realized that we really didn't know much about very early civilizations of the world. He wanted people in the future to know a lot more about us. So, he collected as many items as possible and sealed them in a large crypt (an underground storage space). He put in 200 famous books and hundreds of photographs. He included a movie script from "Gone With the Wind" and recordings of dozens of famous people's voices.

The crypt is 20 feet long, 10 feet wide and 10 feet high. Its floor is two feet thick and it is under a stone roof that is seven feet thick. On May 28, 1940, the door was sealed shut in a very big ceremony. So, if you aren't busy in 6,000 years, be sure to head to Oglethorpe University for the opening of the time capsule.

title: Timelines of History
text:
The timeline shows some ancient events in chronological order. What happened first? What happened next? How many years passed between the events? (Hint: You can figure out how much time has passed by using a calculator to subtract the years.)

Is History True?

How can you be sure that the information you include in your timeline is true? If you are looking for information about something that happened a very long time ago, it might be hard to be sure that your information is correct.

Sometimes, our memories can play tricks on us, and things can become mixed up. Let's say that you went to five birthday parties when you were in first grade. Can you remember now what kind of cake you ate at each party? Did you have chocolate cake with white icing or white cake with chocolate icing? It's easy to forget details about things that happened. Not all of history is about happy times. Wars, slavery and discrimination (treating people differently because of their race or religion) happened, too. People don't always want to admit that humans have done things that they shouldn't have. Many years ago, people who wrote history books left out certain events or didn't tell the whole story. Today's history books are more honest, because writers know that people want the truth.

title: The Slabbing Saw
text:
Even though we aren't sure exactly how the ancient Egyptians built their pyramids, we do know that they used special tools. In order to cut the stone used in these amazing buildings, the Egyptians had to use a large, sharp cutting tool. One of the important tools used by the Egyptians to cut rock was a slabbing saw. A slabbing saw was a rectangle-shaped saw with a straight, wooden handle and a jagged blade made of copper or bronze.

Ancient Egyptians used slabbing saws to cut both wood and rock. The saw was meant to be pulled, not pushed, through the wood or rock, and most of these saws were about six feet long. Without these large saws, the pyramid builders wouldn't have been able to cut the rock into the proper sizes and shapes.

How do we know that the pyramid builders used these types of saws? Archaeologists have discovered saw marks on many of the rocks used to build the pyramids. They have also found pictures of these slabbing saws in Egyptian art.

Today, stonecutters use powerful saws with strong, long-lasting, jeweled blades to cut though tough rock, but in ancient times, the slabbing saw was the best tool available for the job.

title: Mountains
text:
So, what is a mountain anyway? It's a landform that is at least 600 meters taller than the land around it. It has sloping sides and ridges and peaks that can be sharp or rounded. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean. Mountain streams are the source for more than 80 percent of all the fresh water found on Earth.

It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They can be formed by volcanoes, erosion and even the movement of the Earth's crust. Did you know that the Earth's crust is like a big puzzle? The pieces of the "puzzle" keep moving because they are floating on the hot magma that is the middle layer of the Earth. When these pieces (called plates) bang into each other, they sometimes keep pushing and pushing until one of the pieces moves upward. That's how the Himalayan Mountains in Asia were formed. And the Himalayas are still being formed. Did you know that the highest mountain on the Earth's surface, Mount Everest, gets higher by a few inches each year because two plates are pushing against each other?

Over time erosion wears down even the tallest mountains until they are gentle hills. Mountains start as sharp rocks jutting into the air, but after millions of years of erosion, they form cracks where grass, trees and other plants grow. They become ecosystems that make great places for plants and animals, including humans, to live. In fact, old mountain ranges are home to almost 10 percent of all the people on Earth.

Fast Fact

The tallest known mountain in the solar system is Olympus Mons, located on Mars. It's a volcano that is 373 miles across (about the size of Arizona) and 18 miles tall. That's three times taller than Mount Everest!

title: Debate, Dissent and Civility: Lady Deborah Moody, a Dangerous Woman?
text:
In 1643 Governor John Winthrop of Massachusetts Bay Colony wrote in his journal that Lady Deborah Moody was "a wise and anciently religious woman." But Winthrop's deputy-governor called her "a dangerous woman" and told the governor that Lady Moody shouldn't be allowed to remain in the colony. Why did he think she was dangerous? Lady Moody's religious views didn't agree with the English church, so she moved to the American colonies after her husband died. She bought a large farm in Massachusetts. She was the first woman to own land in colonial America.

The Massachusetts Bay Colony was a Puritan community, and Lady Moody's opinions didn't agree with their ideas, either. For example, she and a group called the Anabaptists believed that adults, not babies, should be baptized. To avoid conflict, she moved again.

Lady Moody led a group of people who shared her beliefs to New Amsterdam. Under her planning and leadership, the town of Gravesend (today in Brooklyn, New York) got a government grant from the Dutch in 1645. It allowed freedom of worship and self-government, which was very unusual then. Lady Moody held meetings in her home to settle disagreements and welcomed Quaker missionaries who came to Gravesend.

Was Deborah Moody a dangerous woman? To people who expected her to "leave her opinions behind her" as the deputy-governor said, she was. Lady Moody became the only woman to settle a colony in the New World. As Governor Winthrop's journal also stated, "The Lady Moody ... appears to have been a lady of great worth."

A school in Brooklyn is named for Lady Deborah Moody. If you could name a school for someone like Deborah Moody, whom would you choose? Why?

title: Earth's Population
text:
Population density is a term for the number of people who live in a certain amount of space, such as one square mile. In urban areas (areas in and around cities), the population density is often very high. In rural areas (areas outside cities), the population density is often much lower.

Many factors affect how many people live in a certain area. Sudden weather disasters - like hurricanes, floods and droughts - can cause large changes in population density. Earthquakes and volcanoes have been known to destroy entire towns. Other factors - like diseases and the amount of available food - can also cause the population density to go up or down.

The continent of Antarctica has a population density of zero, because people cannot survive there for very long. The world's deserts have very low population densities because of the extreme temperatures and the lack of water. Cities like Tokyo, New York City, Los Angeles, and Beijing have high population densities. China is the most populated country per square mile in the world.

All living things, including humans, must adapt to their environment to survive. How do you think people have survived on Earth for thousands of years? Look inside to learn some ways that ancient people (people who lived long ago) adapted to and changed their environment to meet their needs.

title: Fighting Crowds, Finding Resources
text:
When a city gets crowded with too many people, there aren't enough resources for everyone to be comfortable. That is happening in many of the world's largest cities today. New York City needs more than 2,500 new classrooms to help with overcrowding. In Barcelona, Spain, thousands of immigrants from Asia and Africa have come to the city in the past few years. In some areas of the city, each person only has about 30 square feet of living space. That's about the size of your bathroom!

Tucson, Arizona, is a beautiful city in Pima County where lots of people want to live, but overcrowding is starting to be a problem. More than a million people live there, and that's putting a strain on the city's resources. Pollution is one of the biggest problems. Many people are concerned about pollution in the desert, the water and the air. They are very concerned about the Sonora Desert. Animals and plants are becoming endangered due to the many houses and businesses being built in the desert.

Making sure cities all over the world continue to be great places to live is a big job. It will take lots of people working hard to find ways to keep Earth's water, air and land free of pollution.

title: Ancient Civilizations
text:
What is a Civilization?

A civilization is a group of people with a unique and special culture. When we say culture, we mean food, clothing, beliefs, customs, housing and sports. Think about Italian food or wigwams used by American Indians. They are special things about that culture, or group of people. Let’s take a look at some ancient (very old) cultures from all around the world.

1. Paleo Indians

As the last great ice age came to an end more than 11,500 years ago, the first Americans arrived from the north looking for an ice-free place to live. These people ate small animals and plants from the land. Over time, these ancient people of our country began to settle in communities. They even started trading with other groups of people in their own region for the things they needed, but did not have.

2. Ancient Maya

Besides growing crops for food, the ancient Maya planted cotton to weave into light cloth and sisal to make heavier cloth and ropes. They built reservoirs to store water so that they could survive the dry months. As they hunted for game in the forests, they learned to avoid dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles and jaguars.

3. The Ancient Indus Valley

The ancient people of India had to adapt to cycles of floods and droughts. They built stone walls to keep the floodwaters from destroying their cities. They planted crops in the fall when the summer floods were over and used irrigation systems when the weather was too dry. The irrigation systems in the ancient Indus Valley were usually dams and canals that carried water to the crops.

4. Ancient Yellow River (China) Civilization

These ancient people developed medicine from plants to fight disease and help themselves live longer. They were the first to raise silkworms, which allowed them to make clothing instead of wearing animal skins and leaves. Over time, the ancient people in this part of the world learned to make clay pottery, as well as bronze tools and weapons.

5. Ancient Sumerians

The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers was home to the ancient Sumerian people. Because the soil was so rich and the climate so warm, the people were able to grow plenty of food. The rivers provided all the water they needed and gave them a way to trade with other people. Ancient Sumerians were the first to use boats with sails.

title: Rivers
text:
A river is a large, naturally flowing body of water. Where does all that water come from? We're glad you asked! Water from high in the mountains and from all the creeks and streams on Earth flows into rivers. Every river ends up flowing into an ocean.

How do rivers affect people? All through history people have wanted to live near rivers because they needed the water. People used the water for drinking, watering crops and transportation. Many ancient civilizations were found near rivers. Even modern cities are sometimes built near rivers. This pattern of population can be seen all over the world.

People depend on rivers. The Nile River in Egypt is a good example. It provides drinking water and transportation. No crops would grow without the flooding of the Nile River. Egypt is mostly desert, so without the water and silt that flooding brings to the soil, there just wouldn't be any crops. However, pollution has put the Nile at risk. In fact the river is so polluted that new laws are being made to help protect it.

Pollution is a big problem for rivers everywhere. Some people and companies thought it was OK to dump all of their garbage and waste in the rivers. This killed lots of fish and made the water undrinkable. Many countries have passed laws to help "sick" rivers get well again.

title: Roman Aqueducts
text:
Whenever large groups live together, they need a good water supply. Hundreds of years ago, most people lived in small villages where they were responsible for getting their own water from wells or streams. In Ancient Rome, however, the people knew that a large city needed a better way to get water. They used a system of aqueducts, or huge ditches, to carry water from where it was available to where the people used it.

These large aqueducts were made to slope downhill so that gravity would carry the water from a lake or river down to the city. The water was often carried in pipes made from lead or terra cotta (baked clay), and the people living in the city could get water anytime they needed it. Many of these Roman aqueducts were built as early as 312 B.C. (more than 2,300 years ago) and are still being used today.

The invention of the aqueduct made it possible for people to live in large groups and still get the water they needed each day.

title: Rights and Responsibilities
text:
As citizens of the United States, we all have rights and responsibilities. The U.S. Constitution lists the basic laws and ideas our country follows. The Bill of Rights is the part of the Constitution that says all Americans have the right to free speech, own property, choose a religion and go to school, among others.

Along with these rights come certain responsibilities. A responsibility is something that it is your duty to do. This means that although you have the right to free speech, you also have the responsibility to be honest and try not to hurt others by what you say.

In every community, citizens must take their responsibilities seriously. It is our responsibility to obey the law. When you go to a public park, you have the right to play on the playground, eat at the picnic tables and enjoy the natural beauty of the park. You have the responsibility to keep your pet on a leash and put your litter in the trash can.

Citizens have the right to help decide how things will be done in their community. They also have the responsibility to vote in elections. Voting lets people help choose who will run the local, state and national governments.

Another responsibility that citizens have is serving on a jury. A jury is a group of people, usually 12 men and women, who listen to all the evidence during a trial. The jury then decides whether the person accused of the crime is guilty or not guilty. That is called a verdict.

title: Responsible Helping Hands
text:
In 2000, the leaders of 189 nations agreed to work together to help poorer nations make the lives of their people better. The leaders of these nations believe it is the responsibility of strong countries to help people in need. They want to cut down on poverty, provide a better education for all children and improve the health of people. This will help millions of people in the poorest nations so they don’t have to live on less than a dollar a day anymore.

There’s more good news, too. Today, 34 million more children attend school, 550 million children have been given measles vaccinations and millions of women in poor countries are able to make a living and support their children. Many of the countries in need are also working to end poverty in their countries. They are taking some of the responsibility for their people, too. People and nations can make a difference. Responsibility is the key.

title: Good Citizens
text:
That's Not Fair!

What if only the second graders were allowed to play on the playground? Would it be fair if only the fourth graders got dessert with lunch? How would you feel about being a third grader if those were the rules at your school?

Justice is another word for "fairness." If you believe in justice, you stand up for what is right and fair. Being fair means believing that everyone should have the same opportunities. It also means taking turns, listening to each other and following the rules.

Equality

Equality means that everyone is equal. It doesn't mean that everyone is the same. People come in all shapes, sizes and colors. They come from different backgrounds and worship in different ways.

No matter what we look like, where we live, or what background we come from, we should all have the same opportunities.

Truth

You may have heard someone say, "Honesty is the best policy." That means that it is best always to tell the truth.

It's not always easy to be honest, especially after you did something you weren't supposed to do. But, if you always tell the truth, people will respect you for your honesty.

Responsibility

Responsibility means keeping your promises and doing what is right. Being responsible makes people know that they can trust you and depend on you, and that's something you can be proud of.

You have responsibilities at home. Doing chores is an important part of being a family. What are some of your responsibilities at home? You have responsibilities at school, too. You have to do your homework and turn it in on time. What other responsibilities do you have at school?

Believing in important things like justice, truth, equality, and responsibility will make your community a better place for everyone!

The Golden Rule

You may have heard of the Golden Rule. This rule is shared by every major world religion and society. There are several different ways to say it, but it just means that you should treat others the way you want to be treated.

In Christianity is says, “All things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye so to them...” Matthew 7:1

In Confusianism it says, “Do not do to others what you would not like yourself.” Analects 12:2

In Buddhism it says, “Hurt not others in ways that you yourself would find hurtful.” Udana-Varga 5,1

In Hinduism it says, “This is the sum of duty; do naught onto others what you would not have them do unto you.” Mahabharata 5,1517

In Islam it says, “No one of you is a believer until he desires for his brother that which he desires for himself.” Sunnah

In Judaism it says, “What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellowman.” Talmud, Shabbat 3id

The Golden Rule has been part of all societies for as long as anyone knows. Living by the Golden Rule is part of being a good citizen no matter where you live.

title: The Printing Press
text:
Before the printing press, the only way to make more than one copy of anything written was to do it by hand. This was a very long and difficult task, and it often took years for one person to copy a large book.

Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg, a German printer, invented the first printing press with moveable type. He made a mold, or pattern, of each letter of the alphabet and would set the type, or arrange the letters, to spell out what he wanted to print. He then used a large press with a screw that could be tightened or loosened to push the ink-covered type up against a piece of paper, making a copy of the page.

Gutenberg's printing press made it possible to print many copies of written works quickly and easily, bringing important information to citizens of communities all over the world.

title: Taking Care of the Earth
text:
A driver throws an empty cup out a car window. A kid walking home from the store throws a candy wrapper on the ground. A local company dumps its garbage in a nearby river. Is there anything wrong with that? The Earth belongs to the people who live on it, so we can do what we want with it, right? Wrong.

What would happen if everybody in the world threw all their garbage anyplace they wanted to? It would be a pretty nasty planet, wouldn't it? And does the planet belong to only people? Don't animals and plants live here too? Since humans have the most control over what happens on Earth, we also have the most responsibility to take care of it.

American Indians have a saying, "Walk gently on the Earth, and leave nothing but your footsteps." This means that we should leave the Earth as we found it, clean and natural. We have a right to use the Earth to help us live, but we don't have the right to mess it up for other living things that share it. Chief Seattle once said, "All things share the same breath - the beast, the tree, the man - the air shares its spirit with all the life it supports."

It's also important to think about the living things that will be on the Earth in the future. They need a clean, safe planet to call home, so we need to protect it. If you want to know 20 simple things you can do to protect our planet, go to: members.aol.com/Ramola15/help.html

title: Citizens in Ancient Democracies
text:
In ancient Greece, citizens played a part in government. Often, they attended a meeting called the Assembly to vote on laws and talk about changes. They took turns leading the Council of 500, a group of citizens that made up laws to be voted on by the Assembly. Citizens could also serve as judges or be on a jury in court.

One problem was that most people were not allowed to be citizens. Only free men who were born in Athens had that privilege. Women, slaves and metics (foreigners living in Athens) were not citizens and had no say in the government.

In ancient Rome, citizens participated in government by voting and taking part in assemblies. Like the women and slaves in ancient Greece, Roman women and slaves had no say in the government. Only free men were citizens.

What makes a person a good citizen? That’s what you’ll read about in this week’s lesson, so check it out. But don’t miss this week’s current event article!

title: Benefits of Government
text:
One of the most important jobs of a government is to make laws and enforce them. Enforcing laws means making sure that people obey them.

If there were no rules, or laws, in our society, what would life be like? People could do anything they wanted, even if it hurt someone else. Stronger people would have all the power.

When people live together in a community, life is more pleasant and comfortable if everyone follows the same rules. Laws also make communities safer and protect everyone's rights. Having a government means many benefits for the citizens. In addition to laws, governments provide important services. Our federal (national) government builds national highways and keeps them in good repair. It also helps pay for public schools, local roads and programs that help people in need.

State governments provide services like state police departments and driver's licenses. Local governments make sure that trash is picked up and sometimes offer recycling programs. They also provide local police, rescue, ambulance and fire departments to help keep citizens and their property safe.

Government protects the rights of citizens, too. In the United States, citizens have the right to free speech, the right to own property, the right to own guns, the right to go to school and other rights. Along with these rights come responsibilities. A responsibility is something that is your duty to do. This means that although you have the right to speak your mind, you also have the responsibility to be honest and avoid hurting others when you speak.

Read this week's lesson to learn about some of the different forms of government.

title: Government Through the Ages
text:
Forms of Government

The very first forms of government were usually just rules made by families or tribes. Long ago, the population of the Earth was so small that government was not really needed.

As people learned to grow their own food, that changed. Farming meant that communities needed someone to be in charge of irrigation, or getting water from nearby rivers to the fields.

Wars also caused communities to need government. They needed armies to defend their communities, and armies cost money. Communities began to collect taxes to pay for food, uniforms and supplies for their armies. Government got bigger and stronger.

Monarchy

A monarchy is a type of government led by one person, usually a king or queen, who makes all the decisions for a country. The king or queen is sometimes called the supreme ruler, because he or she has so much power. Monarchies were one of the earliest forms of government.

When the supreme ruler died, his or her oldest son became king. If there were no living sons in the royal family, the oldest daughter was crowned queen.

Today many countries are still ruled by kings or queens, but the monarchs usually do not have very much power. Their job is mostly to represent the country, not to run it. England, Monaco and Norway are monarchies.

City-States

The ancient Greeks had different ideas about citizenship. Instead of monarchies, they created city-states. City states were independent cities that controlled all of the areas around them. The city was the center of government, economy and culture.

Republic

A republic is a government in which people elect leaders to speak for them. It would be way too hard to get every person to go to every meeting and vote on everything. People would never get anything else done! The first republic was in ancient Rome.

Democracy

A democracy is a form of government in which people have the power to vote. It can be messy! People argue a lot and have to work hard to find ways to agree on things. But that is why a democracy is strong. When people talk and even argue, it makes them look at all sides of an issue. In a direct democracy, everyone can vote on everything. In most democracies, there are too many people for that to work. Most democracies are representative democracies. The citizens elect people to represent them. That's the kind of democracy we have in the United States. There are lots of democracies in the world today. Spain, France, Canada and the United States are just a few.

Dictatorship

A dictatorship is a government in which one person makes all the decisions and has complete power. Many dictators seize power without being elected and use force to keep control. Kim Jong-il in North Korea and Fidel Castro in Cuba were dictators for a long time in their countries. Zimbabwe and the Sudan are also ruled by dictators. The citizens of a dictatorship have almost no rights.

title: American Symbols
text: Many symbols represent the United States. The Statue of Liberty in New York City is a symbol of freedom all over the world. If you have ever been in Washington, D.C., you have probably seen a LOT of symbols! First of all there is the U.S. Capitol. That's where the members of the Senate and House of Representatives make laws. The Lincoln Memorial is also there. The statue of Abraham Lincoln reminds all of us that freedom does not come easily. Of course, you will see our flag all over Washington, D.C. Our flag is our most famous national symbol, and it is known all over the world.

title: The ATM
text:
A few years ago the only way to take money out of the bank was to walk into a bank and fill out a form. This wasn't always easy, because most banks closed at 3 p.m. But things are different now thanks to technology! We have Automatic Teller Machines (ATMs) almost everywhere that work like little banks. Thanks to ATMs we can take our money out anytime we want. We just put our ATM card in the machine and punch in the amount of money we need. Of course, the machines are only giving us our own money. If there is no more money in your account, the ATM can't give you any cash.

An ATM card is a card the bank gives you that allows you to take money out of your bank account even if the bank is closed. When you put in your card, you also have to type in a number, sort of like a password. If you lose your card, that number helps protect your money from thieves. Without the right password, the card will not work. Most ATM cards are also debit cards. You can use them to buy things almost anywhere. The money comes right out of your bank account, and you don't have to pay interest the way you do if you use a credit card.

title: The Urban Environment
text:
An urban environment is any big city and all the living things that call the city home - everything from squirrels in the park to people in houses to ants on the sidewalk. An urban environment also includes plants like trees, bushes and flowers. However, most urban environments have fewer plants than many ecosystems. Many of the plants have been removed to make room for more and more buildings.

Many people live in every urban environment. That means it needs to have rules and laws. So, it needs a government. In the United States and other democracies the people elect leaders. People also pay taxes to keep the city working. Taxes pay for things like firefighters, police officers, trash pickup, libraries and parks. The leaders in an urban environment make lots of decisions, like which areas will be for people to live in, which areas will be for schools and which will be shopping areas. Making an urban environment work for so many people takes a lot of, well, work!
