title: The Americas
text:
North America

North America is a pretty big continent. Look at the map on this page. It includes all of Canada, Greenland, the United States, Mexico and even all of the little countries between Mexico and the continent of South America. Wow!

Have you ever wondered where the name America came from? It was named after a man called Amerigo Vespucci from Italy. He did a lot of exploring in the southern part of the new world. When a map maker got around to making a map of the new world, he just went ahead and named the area Amerigo had explored South America. Then it made sense to call the land to the north, North America!

Was Columbus really the first person to come to the new world? Not at all! When Columbus first stepped foot in the New World there was a whole land full of American Indians. But where did they come from? Well, somewhere between 15,000 and 30,000 years ago there was actually a land bridge between Alaska and Asia. The Bering Strait is what is left of the land bridge today. The Stone Age people who came over the bridge lived by hunting and finding food. These people were the ancestors of our American Indians.

Columbus came to the New World from Spain in 1492. Many explorers followed Columbus, such as John Cabot who sailed to the coast of New England. Ponce de Leon sailed to Florida, and Cortes even took over Mexico. In 1524 France and England began to explore and settle areas in the New World.

South America

South America is made up of 12 countries. Some of those countries are Brazil, Chile, Peru and Argentina. Millions of people live in South America today. But where did these people come from? Actually, some of the same people who crossed the land bridge many thousands of years ago just kept moving south. As they moved, some would stay in their new home. Others would move on. People who wanted to stay in one place learned how to grow corn, which they called maize. They also learned how to grow beans and other crops. Over time, populations began to grow and new ideas and customs were started. That is how the great empires of the Maya, Aztec and Inca began!

title: Making the World a Kinder Place
text:
We sometimes wonder why bad things happen to innocent people. Although we may never understand it, we can do our best to keep things like this from happening in the future. When we do this, we are doing our part to make the world a kinder place, without anger and violence. One way to do this is by making a plan to replace bullying and violence with kindness. The Cool to Be Kind (C2BK) program was developed to help students create programs in their classes and schools that are based on pro-kindness - doing nice things for others. Students look for ways to "pay it forward" each day. Paying it forward means that when someone thanks you for doing something nice, you ask that person to pay it forward by doing something nice for someone else. By paying it forward, kindness continues to spread across the world and people start thinking kinder thoughts and ways that they can help other people. What are some ways you could practice paying it forward? How about doing yard work for an elderly neighbor for free? Or inviting a new student to eat lunch with you and your friends? What about giving up your seat on the bus to someone who looks tired, or helping someone pick up something they have dropped? Thinking kind thoughts and acting on them with acts of kindness is a simple change that you can do to change the world.

Teachers: Go to www.pifexperience.org to find out more about starting a C2BK program at your school!

title: Ancient Civilizations of the Western Hemisphere
text:
Mesoamerica and the Mayan People

Mesoamerica includes all of the area in Central America and Mexico. This is where a group called the Maya lived 1,000 to 2,000 years ago. The Maya was a very early culture that figured out how to do a lot of great things. They started a way of writing with pictures that they used to write about their history. Most of the time, they would write in stone or wood. They also were good at mathematics and started a very good calendar. They also built huge pyramids all through their lands that you can still see today. In order to be a king of a Mayan group, he had to catch an enemy in a war. Then, during the celebration to make him a king, that enemy was killed. Even though the Maya started many wonderful things, they were pretty violent. Blood and war was very important to them and may have caused their culture to come to an end. Some people think their culture may have ended because they messed up their environment. These people think they cut and burned so many trees and plants that it didn't rain as much as it should. That caused crops to fail and people to starve. What really did end the Mayan civilization? People are still trying to find out that question. We are just beginning to learn a lot about the Maya. What will we learn next?

Aztec Lived in Mexico, Too

The Aztec people were one of the strongest groups of people in the Americas before the Spanish came. There is an old story that says the Aztec began their first city where they saw an eagle with a snake in its claws. These symbols are on the Mexican flag and money today. Who were the Aztec anyway? They were at their best during the time that Columbus discovered America. They traded with people all over their area and beyond, became great farmers and had a love of education. However, they did kill people in ceremonies. In fact, when the Spanish came to their area, they were very upset about the number of people that were killed in all the ceremonies!

There was a huge problem for the Aztec when the Spanish came. They brought many sicknesses that the Aztec people were not used to. A sickness called smallpox spread all through the Aztec world and killed many, many people. In fact, the Aztec became so weak that the Spanish were able to conquer them. The Aztec was a group of people who are very important to Mexico, even today.

The Inca of Peru

The Inca was another civilization that did some pretty important things. They lived in a big area that covered the Andes Mountains all the way to Peru. In the middle of their land, high in the mountains, was their capital. It was filled with gold and gems. When the Spanish found out they had gold, silver and gems they waged war with the Inca and took over their lands. The areas in which the Inca lived are some of the highest mountain areas where people have ever lived. People still live in these areas today.

The Powhatan of Virginia

The person you might know about from the Powhatan tribe is Pocahantas. She was the Indian that saved Captain John Smith's life when she was about 11 years old. She was a daughter of a chief. There were lots and lots of Powhatan when the Europeans came to the New World. In fact, there were thousands of them! They were woodland Indians and used the materials around them to make their houses.

The Anasazi Lived in New Mexico and Arizona

The ancestors of the Pueblo Indians were the Anasazi. One of the things the Anasazi are best known for are houses called pueblos. These pueblo buildings were like apartments made of stone and mud bricks called adobe. The word Anasazi is a Navajo word that means "the ancient ones."

The Inuit Began in Alaska

The Inuit lived (and still do) in the cold areas of Alaska, Canada and Greenland. In fact, they were the original Alaskans. They hunted seals, whales and other animals. Their homes were made of driftwood (trees and logs washed down the river to the sea) and dirt. They also built igloos made of ice when they were hunting.

title: Ancient Calendars
text:
The Earth goes around the sun every 365 and slightly less than one-fourth day. In fact it's 11 minutes and 14 seconds less. For thousands of years people have tried to keep track of time with a calendar that uses the rotation of the Earth around the sun as a guide. The problem is that pesky "slightly less than one-fourth" day! If you don't keep track of it right, you could end up with spring starting when the calendar says July! That's a problem. Here is how some people in history have tried to keep track of time.

Aztec and Mayan Calendar

The Aztec and Mayan calendars are based on two cycles. The first cycle was used by the priests for devotion. It had 260 days. These days were broken into 20 periods of 13 days each. The second cycle was 365 days. The two together made a 52 year "century" called a "Calendar Round". The actual calendar used by the Aztec was carved about 1479. It weighs almost 25 tons, is 12 feet across and three feet thick! How would you like to hang THAT on your wall?

The Julian Calendar

The Julian calendar is made up of 365 days with one leap year day every four years. It is also divided into 12 months. It was started by Julius Caesar in 46 B.C. The problem with the Julian calendar was that it didn't take the "slightly less" than one-fourth day into account. So it was " slightly off" every year. By 1582 people realized the Julian calendar was 10 days off of the actual time of year! It was time for a better calendar! The Gregorian calendar was the answer.

The Gregorian Calendar

The Gregorian calendar is the calendar we use today. It's a lot like the Julian calendar except it takes that "slightly less" than one-fourth day into account. It's a little complicated, but by skipping leap year three times in a 400 year cycle, it works out just right!

title: The Eastern Hemisphere
text:
Asia

Asia has a LOT of people! In fact, it has 3/5 of the world’s people. You can see how much that is by taking a candy bar and cutting it into five equal pieces. Now take three of the pieces and hold them in your hand. Those three pieces stand for the people who live in Asia. The other two pieces stand for the people who live in all of the rest of the world! When you look at the map you can see Asia and Europe are one large area. If you are talking about Europe and Asia as one land mass, it is called Eurasia.

Asia is a huge place, as you can see on the map. Some of the countries in Asia are China, India and Japan. The lowest place on Earth is in Asia. It is at the shore of a place called the Dead Sea. It also has the highest place on Earth, which is the top of Mount Everest.

Europe

Only one other continent is smaller than Europe, but big ideas came out of that continent! All of the ideas about art and government from Greece and Rome came from the European continent. The explorers that discovered the New World all came from Europe as well. In fact, many of our very oldest civilizations started in this area. Some of the countries in Europe are Ireland, France and England.

Africa

Africa is a place where you can find everything from big modern cities, to wild and wonderful habitats where elephants and lions live. You might think of Africa as a rainbow: it has a little bit of everything. It has mountains, rivers, forests, deserts and grassy plains. There are small villages that have not changed for hundreds of years and cities with new tall buildings. Some of the countries in Africa are Egypt, Kenya and Sudan.

Australia

The whole continent of Australia is one country. It is the smallest continent, but one of the biggest countries. Sydney is the biggest city in Australia. Australia is one of the flattest places on Earth. In fact, the huge flat land in the center of the country is called the outback. Australia has some very unusual animals!

title: Pharaoh’s Statue Discovered While Searching for Cleopatra
text:
Have you ever wondered what you'd find if you dug a deep hole in your backyard? Unfortunately, what you'd most likely find are some pretty ordinary bugs, rocks, worms and maybe a pipe or two.

But if you decided to dig in an ancient place like Africa, the incredible things you might dig up would surprise you. Recently, Egyptian scientists discovered an interesting find in an ancient limestone temple a headless granite statue of an ancient Egyptian pharaoh.

While searching for the burial place of the Egyptian queen Cleopatra, the scientists discovered this well preserved sculpture about 30 miles west of the city of Alexandria. They said it may be one of the most beautiful examples of carvings from this period, called the Ptolemaic period, which was more than 2,000 years ago.

The statue is 53 inches tall, and the shoulders are 22 inches wide. That is just a little taller than most third graders. Although the scientists have been searching every inch of the temple, they have yet to find the statue's head, which would make it even taller. They think the head might have been destroyed several hundred years ago.

Because Ptolemy IV built the temple, the scientists said the statue may be a representation of him. Ptolemy IV was the fourth Egyptian pharaoh during the Ptolemaic period. Behind the temple, scientists also discovered a burial ground called a necropolis. The mummies in the necropolis were buried with their faces turned toward the temple, which may be a sign that a royal person was buried in the temple.

title: Where Are the Ancient Civilizations Today?
text:
Asia

The people who lived in the ancient civilization of Asia lived mostly in what is now China and India. Most people worked in farming. These people used stone and bronze tools, built temples and palaces and sailed ships. They had a special way of writing called “cuneiform,” and they made a pretty good calendar. Iraq and Iran are in Asia. In fact, Iran, which used to be called Persia, has a lot of oil and gas on their land. The Iranians sell oil to make money for their country. This area of the world has had a lot of problems in the last few years.

China has 1/5 of the world’s people. Remember that candy bar? If you hold one of those five pieces, that would stand for the people in China. People in China can read and write in the same language. However, when it is spoken in different areas of the country, people from one area cannot always understand people from another area. People from China have had some big and important ideas like fireworks, the printing press and gun powder. India has over 1 billion people! That is a 1 with 9 zeros! India has been a very poor country. However, during the last few years it has become very important to many businesses and is slowly adding important jobs.

Africa

One of the earliest civilizations in the world was Egypt. They made up a kind of writing called hieroglyphics, which is the oldest kind of writing in the world. They discovered how to make mummies and pyramids. They even made up a number system based on 10s like our decimal system, and made up a very good calendar much like the one we use today.

Australia

The first people who lived in Australia were called Aboriginals. They came to Australia more than 50,000 years ago. They were hunters and gatherers who lived in small family groups. Australia was not really noticed until the 1600s when the English came and made it an English colony. In 1901 Australia became a country of its own.

Europe

Europe’s past is really interesting! You have already learned about the things Greece and Rome have given to us, like government, architecture and philosophy. Today tourists and shipping are the main ways Greek people make money. European countries have decided to get together in something called the European Union. That means they use the same money and trade easily with each other. Before they got together, each country had its own different kind of money, so it was harder to trade with each other.

title: The Loom
text:
Looms were developed in ancient times when civilizations had finally developed. People had time and resources to spend on better-quality items like cloth. The cloth created on looms allowed people to wear clothing rather than crude animal hides or plant fibers. And fine linens were a status symbol of the wealthy.

The oldest known depiction of the loom dates from 5000 B.C. It is on a pottery dish found at Badari, Egypt.

The early loom was horizontal and made from wood. The yarns were lifted with two little sticks. Vertical looms with heavier wooden frames came into use later. The weaver sat in front of the loom on a little stool in order to weave cloth.

Early weavers produced linen. By 3000 B.C., Egyptian linen was fine and delicate.

In modern times, looms became high powered machines that could produce quality cloth quickly and without as much work from people.

title: How do we know what ancient civilizations were like?
text:
We know what ancient civilizations were like because of two different areas of science. They are called anthropology and archaeology. The word anthropology comes from a Greek word that means "man."

Did you notice the "ology" at the end of the word? That comes from another Greek word that means "the study of."

So, anthropology means the study of man. Anthropology is the study of all people, called humanity, and the cultures that people have made. People who study anthropology are called anthropologists. The word archaeology also comes from Greek words that mean "ancient speech and activity."

Archaeology is actually a special part of anthropology that studies people, their behavior and how their culture grew. They do this through studying buildings, things people made, tools, pottery and even the remains of food. This usually involves a lot of digging.

Archaeologists and anthropologists spend a lot of time trying to figure out what things are that they find buried in the ground. Their job is to figure out when they were made or formed and who made it.

You have to go to school for a long time and spend years learning about old civilizations. So, if you like learning about people from long ago, archaeology may be the job for you!

title: Achievements of Ancient Civilizations
text:
The story of man begins a long, long time ago, in a time we will call prehistoric time. "Prehistoric" is the word used to describe the time before people began writing. Imagine a people who hunted and gathered plants for their daily food. At night, they huddled around fires to keep warm. These people made their own tools out of sticks and stones.

They made clothing from animal skins sewn together with needles fashioned from bones. The most important task for these prehistoric people would have been the daily hunt for food. They hunted animals and gathered plants to eat. As the animals moved from place to place, the people had to follow.

Today, most people don't need to move around to hunt and survive. People have learned how to farm, and they produce goods that can be sold. Cities and countries have grown because people settle in one place, and people can communicate by writing. These changes--settling in one place, growing food, making and selling goods and communicating by writing--are ways that show when a group of people has become a civilization. Civilizations began to form when the prehistoric people learned to grow large amounts of food. With plenty of food, they no longer needed to move around, so they settled in one place. As more people joined them, cities and towns grew, and civilizations were born. As towns and cities grew, not all people farmed.

Some were soldiers; some made tools, clothing or jewelry. Still others became musicians, teachers or scholars. Each civilization developed a culture of its own. "Culture" is a word used to describe the arts, beliefs and customs of a group of people in a certain time. Culture is something that is passed from one generation to another.

Certain civilizations made remarkable achievements that eventually changed the lives of people around the world. Turn the page to learn more about some of the ancient (very old) civilizations and their amazing achievements.

title: Stone Tools Help Archaeologists Learn About Early People
text:
How do we learn about ancient peoples in the Americas? There is no time machine we can use to go back and see how they lived. Instead, we learn about how people lived in the past through clues left in the present. Sometimes ancient peoples left clues about how they saw the world in stories passed down to their descendants. They also left behind creations we still use. For example, corn only exists because of ancient American people who bred grasses into a new crop. We can also learn about ancient people through objects they made. Scientists called archeologists search for ancient objects, buildings, or even garbage heaps to learn about how people lived in the past.

Unfortunately, many of the clues disappear over time. Weather often wears away wood tools and buildings. Food decomposes. Clothing usually falls apart. Because stone wears away more slowly, stone clues are easier to find.

Studying stone tools has helped archeologists create theories about ancient Americans. Stone tools over 15,000 years old have been found in North and South America. These tools show people have lived on both continents since before the first cities in the world began. While there are still many questions about how they lived, the careful craftsmanship on their tools shows that ancient Americans used their ingenuity to survive. These early peoples prepared the way for hundreds of nations that developed later all across the Americas.

title: Ancient Achievements
text:
Our culture today has been made better because of the inventions of ancient people. The ancient Greeks gave us our kind of government, called democracy, where citizens choose who will lead them. Citizens also get the chance to make many decisions about how things will work in their government. They do this by voting.

Even writing started with ancient people. The first writing was called cuneiform. It was used more than 5,000 years ago by people in a place called Mesopotamia. People in the South Pacific learned how to find their way across the Pacific Ocean by looking at patterns of stars at night and watching the sun during the day! Do you like hot chocolate? If you do, say a big "Thank you" to the ancient Aztecs in Mexico who made something like it in ancient times. Look at the map to find where these ancient civilizations lived that are talked about in this lesson.

Mayan Astronomy

Astronomy is the study of the universe. What is the universe? It is the planets, stars and everything in outer space. The ancient Maya lived in what is now Mexico and really knew a lot about astronomy. They were able to tell where stars and planets in the sky were going to be on a certain date and when there would be an eclipse of the sun and moon. The Maya thought the planet Venus was the most important object in the sky, even more important than the sun!

Egyptian Mummification

The ancient Egyptians thought that when people died, they still needed their bodies. They started a way to keep the human body from rotting after it died called mummification. It cost so much money that only people who were rich or powerful could afford it.

Mummification took about two months. The brain and other organs (not the heart) were removed. Then things were used to dry the body and the organs that were taken out of the body. Once the body was mummified, it was covered with a burial mask and put inside a beautiful coffin called a sarcophagus. It was then carried to the tomb. Since the Egyptians thought the person who was mummified would need his body in the afterlife, they thought he would need things to be comfortable too. So they put clothing, jewelry, food and even weapons for the dead person to use in his afterlife.

Four Achievements of the Ancient Chinese

People in China made the first paper! They made it from silk so it cost a lot of money to buy. Later they found ways to make it so it would not cost so much. They learned how to make it from tree bark and wheat. Because it didn't cost so much, more and more people could use it around the world.

Once there was paper to use, the Chinese learned how to print things instead of writing everything by hand. They carved words or pictures on a block of wood, smeared the block with ink and then pressed the ink-covered block onto paper. They did this one page at a time. The first books were printed in China about 868 A.D. That was about 600 years before the printing press was invented in Germany.

The Chinese also invented gunpowder. At first they only used it to make fireworks. But later they found out that it could be used to change the way they hunted for food. By using guns instead of bows and arrows they could get much more food. In time, people all over the world started using gunpowder.

The compass is a great tool for helping people find their way around. The ancient Chinese invented the compass in about 1086 B.C.

Hindu Arabic Numbering System

The numbers we use every day started in India 2,000 years ago. Soon they were used by people all over the Arab world. This number system came to Europe 1,000 years ago. At first, the Europeans didn't understand how the new number system worked. Zero was the problem. They just didn't understand it! Finally in 1202 A.D. a mathematician named Leonardo Fibonacci from Italy wrote a book that helped Europeans understand it better. Today this number system is used in almost every country of the world.

title: The Abacus
text:
The word "technology" can be defined as using science to solve problems. Many ancient civilizations solved some of their problems using science.

About 2,500 years ago, a counting tool called an abacus was invented. It was especially helpful to merchants (people who sold goods), who needed a way to figure out the price of a customer's purchases. No one knows who invented the abacus, but it was used by many ancient cultures. The oldest known abacus was found on the island of Salamis, off the coast of Greece. It is made of marble and is more than 2,000 years old.

The type of abacus that you may have seen first came into use in China about 800 years ago. It is still used by many store owners in China, and Asian children learn how to use it in school. Blind children in many countries are taught to use an abacus because they cannot see to write on paper. Some people say you can solve math problems faster with an abacus than with pencil and paper.

title: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
text:
In ancient Greece, historians made a list of the greatest creations people had ever made. They called them the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Only one of them is still around, but stories of the other six are still told today.

The one that still survives is The Great Pyramid of Cheops near Cairo, Egypt. This pyramid was built about 5,000 years ago. It was the tallest structure on Earth for more than 4,300 years!

Nebuchadnezzar built amazing gardens called the Hanging Gardens of Babylon. They were located near Baghdad in what is now Iraq.

Several huge statues were ancient wonders. The Statue of Zeus at Olympia is said to have been made of gold and ivory and was 40 feet tall. Pictures of it can be found on ancient coins. The Colossus at Rhodes and the Lighthouse of Alexandria were both destroyed in earthquakes.

The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus (in what is now Turkey) had columns 60 feet high. It was destroyed by people who invaded the country.

Finally, the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus was built by a queen in memory of her dead husband. Some bits of the building are located in a museum in England. Do some research to learn more about these amazing wonders!

title: Communication in Ancient Times
text:
Today, there are many ways to communicate with people all over the world. We have e-mail and cell phones so we can talk to each other. Newspapers and books let people share their ideas with others. How did people communicate thousands of years ago, before all of those things were invented?

The timeline below shows some developments that helped people communicate. These developments changed people's lives in many ways. Once they learned to write, people could share ideas and information, keep track of the money they spent and record the important things that happened in their lives. Writing also allowed people to preserve (save) stories that people had been telling for generations. Because of writing, we can learn about the past.

Read This Week's Lesson to learn more about communication in ancient times.

title: Can Facebook Save Dying Languages?
text:
Can you say a few words in Siletz Dee-ni? No? How about saying "hello" in Aka? If you can't, you're not alone! These two languages and 3,500 more could become extinct by the end of this century. Almost 80 percent of the world's population now speaks only one percent of the world's 7,000 languages. This has happened because of globalization. Globalization means that countries are more connected through trade, money and workers. When countries work together, people must be able to communicate with each other. That means many people have to learn another language. English is the main language used throughout the world for business and the Internet.

Why is this a problem? When the last person who is able to speak a particular language dies, some of the knowledge that is found within that language dies with them. A language contains the history of its people, how they used their environment and their beliefs and ideas. Technology may just save many of these languages from extinction! With YouTube, Facebook and other forms of social media, languages that are spoken by even 5 or ten people can be taught to others around the world.

National Geographic has been working on the Enduring Voices Project. Its goals are to record native speakers of endangered languages into talking dictionaries and help communities learn ways to save their languages from extinction. What language do you want to help save?

title: Sharing Public Space: Vitus Bering and Russian Colonies in Alaska
text:
Imagine traveling 6,000 miles over land with supplies for an expedition, and THEN sailing through frigid seas to look for a new world. This was the job given to Vitus Bering, a Danish navigator who sailed for the Russian navy. Peter the Great, czar (ruler) of Russia, asked Bering to explore the eastern coast of Russia. He was wondering if land connected Asia and North America.

Bering's first trip began in 1725. After spending three years getting his supplies to eastern Russia, Bering sailed along the coastline. He didn't see any land to the east, and he didn't realize he was sailing in the narrow passage between Russia and Alaska. This waterway is now called the Bering Strait.

Bering led another expedition in 1741. This time his ship landed on Kayak Island, off the coast of Alaska. They explored some of the Aleutian Islands and met the native people there, the Aleut. He was the first European to arrive in present-day Alaska.

Bering died before returning to Russia, but his voyages paved the way for Russian settlements in North America. Many fur traders came to the area. In 1799 the Russian government established a fur-trading operation in Alaska. Furs from foxes, sea otters and seals were very valuable.

Unfortunately, the Russians took advantage of the native people just as some Europeans had done in settling New England. The Russians took over their lands and forced them to hunt for furs. They also brought new diseases, which killed many natives.

Today, the Aleut people continue to live along the western coast of North America, and their population has grown. What might have been different if the Russians and the Aleut had shared public space fairly? Where in your community is there a debate over public land? How should such debates be handled?

title: Communication in Ancient Times
text:
1. Cave Paintings

The first people communicated with each other by painting pictures in caves. They would use charcoal, dirt or even dyes from vegetables. They used sticks or their fingers to make the drawings. As time went by, the pictures became symbols. Later on the symbols became letters, and then words were started.

2. Sumerian Cuneiform (3100 B.C.)

A group of people called the Sumerians lived in what we now call Iraq. They lived near the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. They made a way of writing called cuneiform. It used pictures for sounds or ideas. Cuneiform means “wedge shaped.” It was given that name because the Sumerians used a stick with a triangular tip to press the pictures into wet clay tablets. When the clay dried, the writing was permanent (unless you dropped the tablet).

3. Egyptian Hieroglyphs (3000 B.C.)

The Egyptians knew about cuneiform, but decided to make up their own kind of writing. This kind of writing is called hieroglyphs. Egyptians didn’t usually include vowels when they used hieroglyphs. In our writing we always have a vowel in every word, but not the Egyptians! Their writing was also done right to left. We write left to right today.

4. Indus Valley (2750 B.C.)

The people who lived in the Indus Valley (India) used a way of writing that was kind of like the Sumerians. The problem is that no one has been able to understand it yet. Not very much of their writing is around today. Archaeologists have found clay pots with markings on them and a few other examples of this early writing.

5. Shang Dynasty (2000 B.C.)

The people of the Shang Dynasty lived in China near the Yellow River. We know they used picture writing, too, because of the oracle bones that have been found there. Oracle bones were bones with writing carved on them. They were used to tell fortunes. They also carved picture writing on bones and tortoise shells to keep track of their money and possessions.

title: The Telephone
text: Alexander Graham Bell was the first person to patent a device that could transmit speech electrically, the telephone. Bell wanted to improve the telegraph, and as a result, he invented the telephone. The telegraph could only receive and send one message at a time. Bell's knowledge of sound and understanding of music allowed him to think about the possibility of transmitting multiple messages over the same wire at the same time. And so they developed the multiple telegraph. Bell and his assistant, Thomas Watson, a young electrician, also began to explore the idea of a device that would transmit speech electrically. Bell and Watson had proven in 1875 that different tones would vary the strength of an electric current in a wire. Alexander discovered he could hear sound over a wire. Bell's next success marked the end of the multiple telegraph and the beginning of the telephone. Today, telephones are in nearly every household in most parts of the world.

title: Change Affects Everyone
text:
Change happens all the time and everywhere. It affects everyone and can't be stopped or avoided.

Weather changes, things change in governments, families change as children grow older, and technology changes almost daily.Change may make our lives better or worse, but it will continue to happen. It has been said that nothing is constant except change!

Sometimes moving from one kind of communication to another can be hard. When people first use the computer, they can get very upset because they make lots of mistakes. Learning how to use cell phones can be hard too.

Every new invention means people have to learn how to use it. That isn't always easy. Even learning how to use a new DVD player may take a long time with the instruction book! All people need to learn how to live with change. Nothing stays the same for long! Name three things that have changed in your life.

title: Paper Making
text:
Materials

Old paper, newspaper, old holiday cards, advertisements, napkins, junkmail, etc.

Wooden picture frame, glass and backing removed

Window or door screening

Pan big enough to sink wooden frame into

Two or three pieces of felt, newspapers, paper towels

Iron or clothes pins to dry

Blender

Stapler

Liquid starch

Rolling pin

Procedure

Tear paper into small pieces

Staple the screening to the bottom of the picture frame. Make it tight.

Place the paper pieces in a blender, fill the blender 1/4 full of paper, then fill the blender to ¾ full with water. Blend at medium speed for 30 seconds. You may need up to three blender’s worth of pulp for one sheet of paper.

Fill the large pan ½ full of water. Sink the picture frame with the screening stapled to the bottom into the water.

Pour the paper pulp into the picture frame. The pulp will float in the water. Now you can add glitter, flower pieces or other decorative small items. Mix them into the pulp mixture. Add a few drops of liquid starch to the mixture. This will allow ink to be used on your paper.

Lift the frame with the pulp out of the pan. Allow it to drip most of the water from the frame.

Turn the frame upside down onto a piece of felt that is put on top of layers of newspaper or layers of paper towels. If the pulp sticks to the screening, just give it a few taps to loosen it. Now it’s time to get the extra water out of your new paper.

Put another piece of felt on top of your new paper. Put some newspaper on top of this felt, then roll with a rolling pin. Push down as you roll.

Take the top layer of paper and felt off of your new paper, gently pull your paper up by the two top edges. Either iron to dry your paper on another dry piece of felt, or hang it to dry with clothespins. Enjoy!

title: Writing Hieroglyph Numbers
text:
In our number system numbers are counted in groups of 10. Every time you add a zero to the right of a number, it means it has been increased 10 times. For example, if you take 50 and put one more zero on it to make 500, it means that you have 10 groups of 50. In our number system, where a number is located tells you how much it is worth.

For example: 125,236 really represents 100,000 plus 20,000 plus 5,000 plus 200 plus 30 plus 6

That means a 3 could be worth 3, 30, 300, or 3,000 depending on where it is in the number.

In Egyptian number writing, it is the symbol alone that tells you how much it is worth. It doesn’t matter where the symbol is located, it always has the same value. To write a number, the Egyptian would just make the symbol as many times as was needed. For example 55 would be written as:

Write the following numbers in Egyptian Hieroglyphics:

78

47

291

658

7,534

65,331

496,132

You will notice that it takes a LOT more space to write in Egyptian Hieroglyphics than in our number system!

title: How Did They Get From Here to There?
text:
New ways of transporting goods and people changed the lives of ancient people in many ways. It gave them different ways to get food and made their work easier. It also allowed them to trade (to exchange something you have for something you need) with other people. Transportation made it possible for them to travel from one place to another more quickly, both on land and through the water. Read the lesson below to learn how transportation made these changes happen.

The first people on Earth were nomads, people who survived by wandering from place to place, hunting animals and gathering plants for food. They only had one way to get from here to there on foot. They walked everywhere, following the animals they hunted from season to season. Because nomads didn't have many possessions, it was pretty easy to carry the few things they had.

Early Farmers

Over time, people began to learn how to plant crops so they wouldn't have to search for all of their food. Once they knew how to grow their own plants, they didn't wander as much. They settled in one place, usually near water.

They began to build rafts so they could fish in the middle of wide rivers instead of fishing only from the banks. This made it so they could hunt on both land and water. Early farmers had more food choices than the nomads.

Many of the early farmers began to domesticate (tame) animals like camels, horses and oxen to help them move themselves and their crops from one place to another. This made it easier to get food from the fields to the settlements. It also saved them many steps!

Read this week's lesson to learn more about ancient transportation.

title: Paddling Across the Atlantic
text:
Do you dream of becoming a big sports star or exploring Mars someday? When Gabor Rakonczay was a kid in Hungary, he dreamed of being alone in a ship on the ocean. It may seem unusual, but Gabor has made his dream come true!

On Dec. 21st 2011, 30-year-old Gabor set out from Portugal in his 24-foot canoe. His destination was the Caribbean island of Antigua, 3,500 miles away. No one had ever crossed the Atlantic alone in a canoe!

After 26 days at sea his canoe capsized (turned over). His communications equipment was ruined. For seven weeks he was totally alone with no way to let his wife know where he was. He didn't use a satellite tracking system because at the last minute the price went up and he couldn't afford it. Three different times he lit signal flares to get the attention of passing ships. But each time the waves were too high and the ships couldn't see his canoe.

His wife, Viktoria, never lost hope. She was sure he was ok and even posted entries on their website. Viktoria kept track of the weather conditions and estimated where Gabor might be.

On March 25th 2012, Gabor landed on the island of Antigua. It took 76 days to cross the Atlantic alone in his canoe. He was even three weeks ahead of schedule! Congratulations to Gabor Rakonczay on making a difficult journey through the Atlantic.

title: Ancient Transportation
text:
Ancient Sumerians and the Wheel

In ancient times, the people who lived near the Tigris and Euphrates rivers were known as Sumerians. About 3000 B.C., they changed transportation forever--they invented the wheel. They attached wheels to carts that could be pulled by people or animals. Wheeled carts made it possible to move larger loads than the early farmers could pack on an animal's back.

The Sumerians began to grow more crops than they needed for themselves so they could trade their extra crops for tools or different kinds of food. They also built chariots with two or four wheels in which people could ride. Of course, wheels worked best on smooth paths of dirt or stone. They didn't turn very well in sand. Chariots became an important tool for war and helped empires expand their power.

Roman Roads

The Roman Empire was huge! The empire was all the countries and areas Rome took over in wars. It was so big that it took a very long time for the Romans to get from one place to another. So they had a great idea. They built lots of roads that connected all the parts of the empire. They also built chariots pulled by horses that could go very quickly over the paved roads. All of this helped the Romans to travel more quickly and smoothly as they went from here to there. This helped them trade and travel between different lands and cultures easily.

Water Travel

Once people learned how to build rafts for fishing, they began to build other types of boats. They made wooden oars to paddle the boats through the water. For many years, Europeans and Asians used boats as an important way to move goods and people along major rivers.

Around 2000 B.C., the Polynesians invented the sail. They used boats with sails to travel over the South Pacific. Sails made water travel faster and easier. Over time, people all over the world began using sails.

title: The Steamboat
text:
In 1787, John Fitch showed the first steamboat to a crowd near the Delaware River in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The boat was 45 feet long and was pushed along by a steam engine that turned 12 paddles. When these paddles turned, the boat moved along the river.

In 1807, Robert Fulton created a steamboat that could carry passengers and freight (a load of goods). His first steamboat was called the Clermont. Many people thought the steamboat would fail and were surprised when it succeeded.

The steamboat made life much easier for people living near the rivers. It could bring people and goods up and down the rivers much more quickly than a wagon could bring them on land. It was also cheaper to travel by steamboat. The invention of the steamboat helped Americans settle in new towns all over the country.

title: How important is water?
text:
There is one main thing that makes life on Earth possible. That's water! Water is everywhere and all around you, but anywhere you find LOTS of water is an ecosystem. Plants, animals and people depend on it. Think about oceans, lakes, bays, gulfs and coasts. Most of the water on Earth is salt water. Right now we don't know how to take the salt out so we can drink it. The question is how much water on Earth is drinkable water? Well, start with 100 pieces of macaroni. Take out 97. That represents the salt water. Now, take out two more pieces that represent the ice in the North and South poles. The last piece of macaroni represents all the groundwater on Earth (which is where our drinking water comes from). Not all of that water can be used for drinking water. Paint a very thin line on the edge of the macaroni. That represents the actual available fresh water on Earth. Now you know why we need to take care of our water supply!

Did you know that water can clean itself? That means it is renewable. It happens every time it goes through the water cycle. In fact, the water we have on Earth now is the SAME water we have always had on Earth. It just keeps going through the water cycle and cleaning itself. The next time you get a drink, think of this--you are drinking the same water the dinosaurs drank! So if people would just try a little harder, like ending the habit of throwing garbage and toxic waste in rivers and streams, our water could clean itself. That's not only good for our water, it's good for us!

title: Transportation of the Future
text:
What will transportation in the future be like? Well, have you ever ridden on a train? Trains of the near future will probably all be levitation trains. They look like they are flying in the air a few inches above the train rail. They do that through the use of magnets, very powerful magnets!

What can we do about traveling short distances? One idea is to make covered bike tunnels that would use the push of the wind to help the bikers go faster! This would be good for the environment and give people some exercise! How about using a “space elevator”? A company called LiftPort Group is looking into ways to build an unusual elevator into space. It would actually hang from the ground and fall into space for 62,000 miles! This could work because of the spin of the Earth. Now that would be quite an elevator ride!

How about cars? That is an area where things are really going to change! In 2015, Tesla introduced cars with autopilot. Some people believe that solar cars may be available someday. Do you think a flying car is possible? Imagine zipping around in the air going 300 miles an hour!

The future has some exciting changes in store for all of us in the area of travel. Hang onto your seat belts… here it comes!

title: Institutions - Then and Now
text:
Did you know that many institutions began in ancient times? Read the stories below and this week's lesson to find out how ancient civilizations influenced our modern institutions.

Cities

Once people learned how to grow crops, they were able to stop wandering around to look for food. Then it wasn't long before they started making products they could sell. People would then take those products and sell them so they could buy what they wanted. They could also take their products to trade, called bartering, for something they wanted. Selling and trading are ways to get something you want that you do not have.

Commerce

Once people started to make or raise products to sell or trade, groups of people started to live together in one place. This was the beginning of towns and cities. More and more trade started happening. Commerce is another word for "trade" or "business." In ancient times, people traded things they had plenty of for things they needed. They might trade crops they did not need or things they made like baskets or pots to sell or trade. Sometimes they traveled great distances to trade. As cities grew larger, people found that they could actually earn a living by making goods and selling them in their own communities. This was the beginning of the first businesses. Can you name some businesses in your community?

title: Institutions - Then and Now
text:
Guilds

During medieval times (A.D. 400 to 1400), many people who did the same kind of work belonged to groups called guilds. Members of merchant guilds sold goods that were produced by other people, sometimes from places far away. Members of craft guilds made items that people needed like shoes or clothes. There were even guilds that made bread. Today, some workers belong to unions - groups of people who do the same kind of work, like construction workers or airline pilots.

Universities

The schools we call universities began hundreds of years ago in Europe. The first universities were called studia generalia, schools where students came from all over the world to study. The first true university was in Bologna, Italy, in the 11th century. The University of Paris opened in about A.D. 1150, and Oxford University in London was founded around 100 years later.

Soon there were universities all over Europe. The first university in the United States was Harvard University, which was founded in 1636. Is there a university where you live?

The Christian Church

About 2,000 years ago, the Christian Church began in Jerusalem, Israel, when Jesus Christ was alive. The people who followed him became known as Christians. They wanted to share their beliefs with others, and soon there were churches all over the world. Today about 1.6 billion people are of the Christian faith. The Christian Church is one of many religions in the world today.

title: The Bellows
text:
When early metalworkers first started heating metal and pounding it into useful shapes, they discovered something very interesting. In order to make the fire hot enough to heat the metal, they needed to blow on it. Blowing on a hot fire with your lips can be very tiring--and very hot--work! These early blacksmiths put their heads together to think of a better way to blow on the fire to make it hot enough for them to do their work.

As early as around 3000 B.C., the first blacksmiths found a way to make a hand-operated bellows, an invention to blow on the fire for them. These bellows were made of a leather bag with pleated, or folded, sides. The bag was attached between two wooden handles in a special way that made it possible for the bag to be opened and closed, allowing air to get into the bag and stay there until it was forced back out again. There were small vent holes that controlled where air came in and where it went out. The bellows made it possible for the blacksmith to blow on the fire without having to use his mouth at all!

Later on, a blacksmith would often hire a helper just to work the bellows while he heated and hammered the hot metal into the proper shape. Today, modern air compressors have replaced most of these hand-held bellows.

title: Guilds Lead the Way
text:
Guilds were very important during medieval times. People who worked in the same trade would group themselves together into a guild to make sure the products and services they offered were good quality and sold at a price that was fair. If you were a member of a guild, it was a sign that you did good work and gave you a lot of respect in your town. Members of a guild would check on other members to make sure their work was good. If it wasn't, or if they were cheating people, the guild member could be fined, made to do the work over or could even be thrown out of the guild. Being thrown out of a guild meant that you could no longer work in your own town!

When people were members of a guild, they knew the guild would take care of them if they were sick, and if they died, they knew the guild would take care of their families.

If you lived in medieval times and you wanted to learn a trade, you would become an apprentice when you were about 12 years old. You would leave your parents to live with the guild member, and he would be your teacher. Your parents would pay the guild member to teach you, so you would have to work very hard. You might live with the guild member for up to 14 years. When the apprenticeship was all finished, you would then be a journeyman. At that point you could actually be paid for your work. When you saved enough money, you could open a business of your own.

Only people who were members of a guild could sell in a town. But on market days anybody could sell their products, even if they were not skilled. All they needed was someone willing to buy their product. A big fair was held each year that brought people from all around. That was a great time to shop in any town!

title: The Job of a Museum Director: ‘A Little Bit of Everything’
text:
The Campbell House Museum is a beautiful Civil War-era home in St. Louis, Missouri. The wealthy Campbell family lived there from 1854 to 1938. Studies Weekly asked Andrew Hahn, the director of the museum, about his job.

SW: How is a house museum different from other types of museums?

AH: A house museum is different because it gives you an opportunity to get the full experience of the past. If you go to an art museum, you can see paintings from the past that may tell a story about history or a particular event. But when you come to a house museum, you get the full picture of what it was like to live in the past. When people come here, they get to experience what it was like to be welcomed into the house or to work in the house. The house was so well preserved, and the Campbells’ collection is still here. This is their house and how they lived in it.

SW: What does a museum director do?

AH: I do a little bit of everything. We have to raise money so that we can keep the doors open and pay the utility bills. I write the checks for all the bills, and I organize our volunteers who do most of the work at the house. We do research, so I look into the Campbell story and read old documents and newspapers that tell stories about the past. I even take out the trash!

title: We Depend on Each Other
text:
What would life be like if your family had to take care of all of its own needs? Could you grow all of your own food? Make all of your own clothes? Build your own transportation and get fuel to make it run?

Many years ago, families had to do just that. If they couldn't make or grow it themselves, they had to do without. Today, most people in the world live very different lives than those of our early ancestors. We now depend on each other to take care of our needs.

Your state produces many items that are sold to other states and countries. In turn, other states and countries sell us things that we can't produce ourselves. By working together, people are able to meet many of their needs and wants. A need is something you must have to live, like a home, food and clothing. A want is something that you would like to have, (like a new TV) but you could live without.

Let's find out what we share with others, and what they share with us to keep everyone well and happy.

title: Has Amelia Earhart’s Plane Been Found?
text:
A research group that looks for historical aircraft has been trying to solve one of the greatest mysteries of the 20th century. What really happened to Amelia Earhart? Earhart was the first woman to try to fly around the world. She disappeared without a trace while flying over the Pacific Ocean in 1937.

Earhart and Fred Noonan, her navigator, could have landed somewhere near Gardner Island, now called Nikumaroro. Others believe they crashed into deep water. By using technology to study a 1937 photo of the island's shore, researchers may have new evidence in the case. The photo shows what may be the landing gear of her Lockheed Electra airplane sticking out of the water. This could mean Earhart and Noonan lived on the island for some time after the crash. Artifacts have also been found on the island that could have belonged to Earhart and Noonan.

The oceanographer who found the undersea wreckage of the Titanic says the photograph might be the clue that helps us find out what really happened. Underwater robotic submarines and mapping equipment will help the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery look for the plane's remains. Perhaps an old photograph and new technology will help solve a 75-year-old mystery!

title: Economic Interdependence
text:
Communities Work Together

As you look around your neighborhood, you can see the many ways people depend on each other. Who built the sidewalks you walk on every day? What about the food you eat? Where did it come from? Who built the house you live in and the school you attend? Look at your clothes. Where did they come from?

Because we are all good at some things and not as good at others, we are able to give, but must also receive. We work at what we are good at and rely on others to help us with the things we aren't as good at doing. Those who are good at building and programming computers take care of the needs of those who are not. Those who are good at growing things provide food for those who aren't able to do so. We each use our resources and talents to help fulfill the needs of our communities.

Communities may also need to rely on each other because of scarcity. Scarcity means there just isn't enough of something that people want or need. This means choices have to be made based on those wants and needs. For example, if there aren't enough bananas because the crop failed in South America, then shoppers in this country have to either buy another kind of fruit or pay a higher price for the bananas they buy. When products are scarce, the price usually goes up.

Every community and country in the world depends on other communities and countries for some of the things they need. Some communities may grow more than enough oranges for their own area, but may not have enough oil to make gas for their cars. They can sell their oranges to other communities, but then will need to buy the oil they need from another community.

What Does Your Community Provide for Other Communities?

Your state sells many products to other communities around the nation and the world. Products that are sold to other communities are called exports. Why are some products sold locally, but other products have to be sent to us? Well, some things depend on the weather. If you live in an area that has cold, long winters, you won't be growing bananas! Bananas need very warm and wet climates. They could never survive a cold winter. But you might grow corn that can be sold to other communities that don't have the weather, or the right kind of land to grow corn. What are some of the things your state grows or makes that can be sold to other communities?

What Does Your Community Get from Other Communities?

Products you would like to have, but are not made or grown in your community, must be brought to you from other places. This is called an import. Your state may import lumber, medicine, oil, coal and many other items that cannot be made in your area. If there is no oil or coal under the ground in your community, it needs to come from somewhere else if you are going to use it. That means you need to import it. What are some of the products your community has to import?

Working Together, We Can Take Care of Our Needs

In the past, people took care of all their own needs. Today, people use the resources they have to produce certain products or services (work provided by someone for pay). They then ship what they don't need to those who aren't able to produce these products at all.

By working together, each community is able to get the things it needs and wants. When two or more groups depend on each other to fulfill each other's needs, it is called interdependence. Almost all people, communities and countries these days are interdependent.

title: Examples of Economic Interdependence
text:
Here are some examples of economic interdependence in ancient civilizations:

Around 4000 B.C., the Sumerians discovered copper and started shipping it to people who didn't have any. It was such a rich trade that they named the main shipping river "copper river." The Sumerian word for "copper" is "urudu," which is the root word for "Euphrates" River.

In Egypt, people wove and pounded the flat fibers of a plant called papyrus to make paper. In 600 B.C., the Greeks started buying their papyrus from a city called Byblos.

During medieval times, people often belonged to groups called guilds. Members of merchant guilds brought products to market for others and sold them to the community. Members of craft guilds, such as bakers, carpenters, blacksmiths and cobblers, were excellent at making certain things. Guilds helped the community by providing the goods and services needed for everyday life.

title: Government Goods and Services
text:
Every day, we often use government goods and services without thinking about it. Some examples are the school you attend, if it is a public school, and the road that you took to school; they are provided for you by the government. People who work pay a part of their income to the federal government in the form of taxes. When you buy something, you pay a little more than the price tag says because you are also paying a small tax (sales tax) that will help the government provide goods and services to everyone.

Many of the goods and services provided by the government are known as public services. Businesses that are owned by people are considered private enterprises (businesses). An example of this would be going to the library in your community. It does not cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. If you were to go to a bookstore, however, things would be a little different. The bookstore owner is in business to make money. That person probably wouldn't allow you to borrow the book you wanted to read. Instead, you would buy it. The bookstore is not public, but is instead private enterprise. Other public services provided by the government include the police and fire departments, parks, the water department and public health department.

title: Samuel Wilson - The Man Behind the Cartoon
text:
You've probably seen pictures of Uncle Sam wearing red, white and blue and saying, "Uncle Sam Wants You!" Who is Uncle Sam, anyway? Most people think he's just a cartoon.

The people who live in Troy, New York, know Uncle Sam was real. Samuel Wilson moved to Troy in 1789 and opened a meatpacking business a few years later. He supplied meat to troops during the War of 1812. That's when soldiers started joking that the letters "U.S." on the boxes stood for "Uncle Sam."

In 1832, the first pictures of Uncle Sam appeared in newspapers. He had a long, white beard. He wore a tall, star-spangled hat and a red-, white- and blue-striped suit.

For more than 100 years, Uncle Sam has been asking Americans to stick together during times of war and to fight for freedom and justice. The members of Congress made Uncle Sam an official national symbol in 1961. They also said Samuel Wilson of Troy was the inspiration for the character.

Today, some people in Troy are trying to raise money to build an Uncle Sam Museum. One of them is George Jacques III, who is a veteran of WWII. He is working to raise money for the museum, and he even built a model of the way he thinks the museum should look.

title: Forms of Government
text:
Continued from the cover story:

Absolutism

During the 16th and 17th centuries, many people believed in the divine right of kings. That meant that people thought God had picked the monarch (king or queen) that ruled their country. Because they believed God had picked that person, the choices made by the monarchs could not be questioned. The people of the country had to do everything the king or queen said. If they didn’t, they were thought to be going against God. This kind of government became known as absolutism.

By the 18th century, absolutism was the kind of government used in many countries. Louis XIV of France and Catherine the Great of Russia were absolute monarchs.

Communism

Does the word communism remind you of any other word? How about community? That’s because those two words are related. During the 19th century, many people believed that everyone should be equal and should be able to have everything needed. That belief led to the development of communism.

Communism is a form of government in which everyone in the community owns all the goods and property. Citizens share the goods and property, depending on how much they need. In other words, a family of six would get more food than a family of three. There should be no rich people or poor people, and no one should be more important than anyone else.

In 1917, a group of workers called Bolsheviks took power in Russia. The government they formed was called communism. Other nearby countries also began using that word to describe their governments. In 1949, a man named Mao Tse Tung became the leader of China. He formed a government that was called communism, too. The problem was that none of these countries were really communist. The people who lived in these countries were not treated fairly at all. In fact, many people did not always have what they needed just to live. However, the people who ran the government had more than they needed, and some became rich. This form of government ended up being so unfair that most countries that were using communism have moved on to another kind of government.

Totalitarianism

In some countries where a leader had a lot of power, some people started to believe that the government should have even MORE power. They believed the people who lived in a country should have no say over anything. They thought the government should have power over every part of a citizens’ life. When a government controls every part of a citizens’ life, it is called totalitarianism.

In this kind of government, people are told how to run their businesses, how to act and what to believe. The government even got to say what art, music and books people could use! People who lived in the country did not have the right to protest when they did not like the government’s choices. Anyone who spoke out against the government could be put in prison or even killed.

Three countries had a totalitarian government for a while during the first half of the 20th century. In Italy, Benito Mussolini ran the country from 1922 to 1943. Mussolini was the one who made up the name totalitarian to describe his kind of government. In 1933, Adolf Hitler rose to power in Germany. He was one of the world’s most cruel and powerful leaders until his death at the end of World War II in 1945. From 1924 to 1953, Joseph Stalin led the totalitarian government of the Soviet Union (Russia and several nearby countries).

title: The Price of Democracy: Paying Your Taxes
text:
During the early years of our nation, not much was paid in taxes. For a short while, our country used the taxes paid on carriages, sugar, tobacco, property, corporate bonds and slaves to support itself. It wasn't until after the War of 1812 that our nation began to tax the sale of items such as gold, silverware, jewelry and watches. Congress began to rely on tariffs (taxes on items shipped or received) on imported goods to run the government. In 1862, during the Civil War, Congress issued the first income tax law. Depending on how much money you would make, the income tax began at 3 percent and rose with your level of income. In the same year that income taxes began, the office of Commissioner of the Internal Revenue was established. This particular office has the power to assess, collect and levy taxes; enforce tax laws; and take property or income from people who don't pay their taxes. For a while, income taxes were eliminated and brought back more than once between 1868 and 1895. However, in 1913, the income tax became permanent when it was re-introduced as the 16th Amendment to the Constitution. This amendment gave Congress the right to tax the incomes of individuals and corporations.

The federal government collects taxes to gain revenue, or money, to help pay its expenses. The amount of money that is overspent by our government is called the federal deficit. Some of the expenses the government must pay are for federal programs that help and protect the citizens of our country. The Department of Health and Human Services has programs such as Headstart for young children, assistance for needy families, foster care and child abuse. The Department of Veterans Affairs helps veterans and their families with benefits and services. The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) tries to stop illegal drugs from entering our country. Other programs include air-traffic safety and security, federal prisons, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and national defense and security for protecting America against the threats of terrorism or war. Our government has many programs that are supported by various taxes that are collected. Our country would be very different without the help of many of these programs.

title: Forests
text:
What is an ecosystem anyway? Well, it is an area made up of all the living (bugs, plants, animals) and non-living (water, dirt, rocks) organisms in that area. It can be as small as the area under a rock, or as big as the ocean. One of the most important ecosystems on Earth is our forests. Why? Because forests, especially rain forests, produce most of the oxygen on Earth, and oxygen is what you need to breath.

Forests are usually made up of layers. First of all is the forest floor. You can think of this layer as the waste basket for all the layers above it. It includes dead and decaying plants and animal droppings. It is the place where soil is made! Lots of animals live there, as well as animals like earthworms and beetles that live below the surface and help break down material so it can become soil. The herb layer is the wildflowers, ferns and other low-growing plants. Rabbits and chipmunks love it there. The shrub layer is made of shrubs that grow up to 8 feet high. It is home to caterpillars, as well as birds. Last of all is the tree layer (canopy) which shades the whole forest.

Do you remember the fact that most of our oxygen comes from forests? The problem is many forests are being cut down to sell the lumber for money. In a democracy, people have the right to protest the government if they decide to cut down all the trees in a forest. This has stopped much deforestation (that's what it is called when you cut down all the trees) in the world. However, in communist countries, where the people have no say, deforestation happens a lot! In Tibet, when that country was taken over by the Chinese communists, the Chinese cut down 45 to 80 percent of all Tibet's trees to sell and use. The people couldn't say anything to stop it. People in a democracy can protect their environment by speaking out! It is the job of all of us to tell our government when we think something is wrong. Not all people have that right.

title: Forms of Government
text:
Democracy

The Greeks invented democracy. The word democracy means “government by the people.” This form of government has been around for more than 2,500 years. In a democracy, people have the right to vote, write letters to people in the government and protest when they do not like the way something is being done. They also have a responsibility to obey the laws and to help make their country a better place to live. In democratic countries, the people believe citizens should have a say in their government.

The United States and France were the first modern countries to become democracies. Today, many countries all over the world have some kind of democratic government.

There are many other kinds of government. Most of these do not let the citizens have any voice about what happens to them or to their country. This week we have learned a little about democracy, but now we are going to learn about absolutism, communism and totalitarianism. There is a big difference between democracy and these kinds of government!
