title: Fake or Real News?
text:
Have you ever read something online, like on social media sites, that sounded fishy? Maybe it was real, but it could be fake news! The big danger, though, is news that sounds real but isn’t. Fake news is becoming common because anyone can post things online. Fake news can be in the form of a story. Fake news can be a photo or video that has been changed. The problem is that these fake items look real. Fake news can cause problems and it spreads misinformation.

Sam Wineburg, a professor, did some research. He found that 80 percent of students cannot tell the difference between real and fake news. Do you want to become a media-savvy person? You have to be able to find out if news is real or fake. How do you do that? You have to become a detective and search for the truth. You can learn about the author or company that posted the news. You have to think about the purpose of the news. Is there a hidden plan to get you to buy something or to make you think a certain way? Your teacher or a trusted adult can help you learn how to spot fake news. It takes a little time, but democracy depends on real information! Do your part and discover what is real and what is fake!

title: Why Did People Come to Iowa?
text:
Since the state first became a territory, Iowa has welcomed immigrants from many lands. Immigrants are people who leave their own countries to live in another country. We know that people have been coming here for hundreds of years, but why have people chosen to leave their homes to settle in Iowa?

There are several reasons why immigrants have chosen to leave their native countries and come to Iowa. One very important reason is that Iowa had cheap land, and many immigrants, especially those from Europe, wanted the chance to own their own land. In Europe, land was very expensive, and only the very wealthy families could afford to have land of their own. In Iowa, almost anyone could afford to buy land and use it any way they chose.

Another reason that many immigrants chose to leave their countries to come to Iowa was for religious freedom. During the 1800s, many people left Sweden because the leaders of the Lutheran Church were charging large church taxes, and they didn't believe these taxes were fair. In 1847, many immigrants left Holland because they were being forced to belong to the state church, and they didn't want to join. Many of these immigrants came to Iowa and started the town of Pella, where they could worship as they chose.

Still other immigrants left their countries to come to Iowa because they didn't agree with the government in their home countries. In Germany, boys were forced to join the military and were treated very harshly, so many families chose to leave their country rather than have their sons serve as soldiers.

Perhaps the most important reason why people came to Iowa was to have a better life. Many immigrants were very poor and could not afford to feed their children unless they "hired them out" to work for other people. This meant that many families couldn't be together, and families had to be broken up. In Denmark, children were often hired out to work at as young as nine years of age. Once they left their families to work, they usually never came home to stay again. Many Danish immigrants came to Iowa to keep their children from having to leave home to work. They wanted to come to a place where they could keep their families together.

The first immigrants to Iowa came mainly from northern Europe and Great Britain. Today, most of Iowa's immigrants come from Southeast Asia and Latin American countries. Most of the immigrants from Southeast Asia have come to Iowa to escape war and great suffering in their native countries. Many of these immigrants have fled their countries because their governments have been taken over by communism, and their freedoms have been taken away. Most Latin American immigrants have come to Iowa in search of better jobs and a better future for their children.

title: Gateway to the Eastern United States
text:
Immigrants wanting to enter the United States had to first pass through a station in New York. At this station, they were asked questions to test their knowledge about America and their education and skills. They were checked for disease and to see if they were escaped criminals or had bad intentions. If they checked out okay, the immigration officers let them pass into New York and start new lives. Otherwise, they had to stay at the station until things were straightened out, or they were put back aboard a ship and deported.

As the numbers of immigrants grew, the station had to be moved to Ellis Island.

The Ellis Island complex started out as Oyster Island in Upper New York Bay. In 1892, the island became headquarters for new immigrants to the United States. The flow of immigrants soon outgrew the capacity at Ellis Island, and two additional islands had to be created. The two artificial islands were created by dumping Earth and rock into the bay near the original Ellis Island. About 16 million immigrants entered the United States through the Ellis Island complex from the 1890s until about 1915. In 1954, the station was finally closed, and immigration was moved to Manhattan. In 1990, Ellis Island was dedicated as a museum. Tourists may see documents and artifacts that help re-create the amazing job these islands performed for so many years and for so many grateful people.

title: Move Over, Brothers Grimm—New Fairy Tales Found
text:
There's a magical world out there full of elves, evil queens and beautiful princesses! If you enjoy "Cinderella," "Little Red Riding Hood" and "Rapunzel," you have already discovered the work of the Brothers Grimm. These German fairy tales and legends were collected by the Grimm brothers and put into popular books about 200 years ago.

A new world of fairy-tale magic has just been revealed. Researchers found a collection of 500 stories gathered by Franz von Schonwerth, a German historian who did his work at the same time as the Grimm brothers. Because Schonwerth was a historian, he wrote the stories exactly as the German people told them to him. The Grimm brothers changed some of the stories to make them less frightening for children. The Grimm brothers admired Schonwerth's work. Jacob Grimm said, "Nowhere in the whole of Germany is anyone collecting (fairy tales) so accurately, thoroughly and with such a sensitive ear." Schonwerth's collection was never as popular as the Grimm brothers' books. His three volumes of stories collected dust for 150 years until they were rediscovered.

Schonwerth's collection includes a story of a beautiful girl who gets away from a witch by turning herself into a pond and another tale about a turnip princess. As soon as the stories are translated into English, you will have a whole new collection of fairy tales to read!

title: Turkey
text:
The turkey is a large game and poultry bird that is related to the grouse and the pheasant. Some people believe that the turkey got its name from the "turk turk" sound it makes when it is startled.

The wild turkey is native to North America, and it is a popular game bird here in Iowa. Turkeys raised in captivity cannot fly, but wild turkeys can fly for short distances at speeds of up to 55 miles per hour.

Turkeys have a great sense of hearing, an excellent sense of taste, great vision, and a terrible sense of smell. They also have a loud voice! A turkey's gobble can be heard up to a mile away. Turkeys eat insects, seeds, plants and fruit.

Millions of turkeys are cooked and eaten in the United States each year at Thanksgiving. The turkey industry makes several billion dollars every year raising and selling turkeys.

At one time, Benjamin Franklin suggested that the turkey, not the bald eagle, be considered the national symbol of our country. He said that although the turkey was "vain and silly," it was better than the "cowardly" bald eagle.

title: About how many Iowans today are descendants of immigrants?
text:
Every Iowa citizen, unless he or she is American Indian, is a descendant of immigrants. All of our ancestors came to America from another country at some time or another. People from many parts of the world have come together in Iowa and have joined their cultures, foods, languages, and beliefs to help make up the society we know today.

(A descendant is someone who is born after a previous generation. You descended from your parents.)

title: Vesterheim Museum and Library
text:
Decorah is located in northeastern Iowa, and it was settled by immigrants from Norway. To help preserve their Norwegian history and culture, immigrants founded the Vesterheim Museum in Decorah in 1877. "Vesterheim" means "western home" in Norwegian, and it is used to describe the new home that the Norwegian immigrants made for themselves in Iowa.

The Vesterheim Museum is a single ethnic group in the entire United States. It takes up 15 historic buildings in downtown Decorah and is a wonderful place to visit to see what the Norwegian culture is like.

The museum has more than 24,000 objects in its collection. Vesterheim displays fine and folk art, clothing, metal working, carvings, books, photographs, and household items from the homes of actual Norwegian immigrants.

The museum also has a library of Norwegian books, which include many editions of the Norwegian-language Bibles brought to Iowa from Norway. There are also books that were of interest to the immigrants that were published in America. The library also has many books on Norwegian folk art such as rosemaling, woodcarving, knife-making, and weaving. Rosemaling is a type of art where people paint flowers and colorful designs on bowls, cabinets, and other items made of wood.

Vesterheim is a place to remember some of Iowa's hard-working and talented immigrants.

title: Iowa's Immigrants
text:
Since Iowa first became a territory, immigrants have flocked here seeking land and a better life. Immigrants from all over the world have helped to settle Iowa and make our state what it is today. Let's explore some of the largest groups of immigrants to enter our state and find out what they have contributed to Iowa.

German Immigrants

Many German immigrants came to Iowa to escape the requirements for military service for all German boys. The boys who were required to serve in the military received very harsh and unfair treatment, and many families wanted to come to a place where their children would be treated better.

The Germans were the largest group of immigrants to come to Iowa. They were good farmers and hard workers, so most Iowans were glad to see them come. Most German immigrants settled in right away and started their own farms and businesses.

Although the German immigrants were glad to be in America, they also longed to keep their German traditions and culture alive. Many German immigrants joined the Turner Society, a German-American organization that met each week to sing German songs, speak the German language, and visit with other German immigrants. These immigrants were Americans, but they still liked to view themselves as Germans.

German influence can be felt in many of our Iowa cities today, especially in Dubuque, Davenport, and Burlington. Turner Halls, places where the Turner Society met, old German churches, and breweries can be found in these Iowa towns.

Scandinavian Immigrants

The Scandinavian immigrants came to Iowa from the countries of Sweden, Norway, and Denmark. The first of the Scandinavian immigrants to arrive in Iowa were the Swedes, who settled in New Sweden. This group was led by Peter Cassel, and he and his group soon bought land and began farming the area.

Not long after the first Swedes arrived, a second group, led by Anna Dalander, planned to join them. Peter Cassel sent directions to Mrs. Dalander, but she and her group of 41 people got lost and ended up in Boone County. Winter was coming on, and the only cabin Mrs. Dalander and her group could find was one belonging to Thomas Gaston, the only white settler in the area at the time. He told them that they were lost and invited them to spend the winter with him. He had extra food that he sold to the group, and they stayed until spring came. After staying the winter, the group decided not to try to find Cassel and his group, but to settle where they were. They called their community Swede's Point, which is now the town of Madrid.

The Norwegians were the next Scandinavians to come to Iowa. They settled in northeastern Iowa near the present-day city of Decorah. Other Norwegian immigrants settled in Story County, near Story City and Huxley. The Norwegians were proud of their heritage and built the Vesterheim Museum to display items that were important to them and their history.

The Danes came to Iowa about the same time as the Norwegians and settled in Shelby and Audubon Counties. The city of Kimballton still honors its Danish heritage by flying the U.S. and Danish flags side by side. Elk Horn has a windmill that was brought here to Iowa in 30,000 pieces from Denmark and then put back together here. It stands as a reminder of the Danish culture (the beliefs, language, arts, and relationships that a group of people from the same society or country share).

In 1847, many Dutch immigrants came to Iowa in search of religious freedom. They started the community of Pella, which still preserves its Dutch heritage today. The city holds a large Tulip Festival each spring, and during this time, the town dresses in Dutch costumes, including wooden shoes, to show the world that it is proud of its ancestors.

Other Immigrants

Before 1880, most immigrants to Iowa came from northern Europe and England. After this time, immigrants began to come from southern and eastern Europe as well. People came to Iowa from Italy, Croatia (now called Yugoslavia), Hungary, Poland, Lithuania, and Russia. There were many Italians who came to Iowa around 1900. The Italian immigrants tended to settle in cities rather than on farms. Most Italians found jobs in coal mines or on the railroads.

The Italian immigrants were glad to find these jobs because many wanted to send their money home to Italy for other members of their families to use to travel to Iowa. The Italian immigrants worked hard to earn the money they needed to bring their families here to join them.

Iowa's small number of African American immigrants came here searching for work. They settled mainly in the river towns of Keokuk, Burlington, and Muscatine. Many worked on the railroad, on steamboats, and as business owners. African Americans often set up their own restaurants and barber shops. The largest number of African Americans found jobs in the coal mines. Many of these African Americans settled in Buxton, a large coal camp where the number of African American miners outnumbered the number of white miners for a time.

In recent years, immigrants have come to Iowa from all over the world, but particularly from Latin American countries and from Southeast Asia. These two groups of immigrants have also come looking for work and for a better life for their children. They have brought with them their languages, cultures, foods, and religions, which have enriched our state and helped us to understand different cultures throughout the world.

title: Paperweight
text:
plastic or glass cup

paper and cardboard

shells, rocks, etc..

glue

string or twine

Find a cup that you want your paperweight to be in. Make sure you ask your parent(s) if you can use it. Take your glass or plastic cup and trace around the bottom of it on the piece of paper.

Cut out your circle of paper and trace around it again onto the cardboard.

Glue the cardbaord on top of the piece of paper. This way the white paper shows on the bottom of your paperweight instead of the cardboard.

Gather your rocks, shells or whatever you have chosen to put in the paperweight. Glue them down onto your cardboard, making sure your glass fits over the items. Let the items dry for a week before finishing the paperweight.

Glue the bottom lip of the cup (glass or plastic) onto the cardboard. Make sure you glue it securely so it doesn’t fall off.

Take a piece of string or twine and glue it around the bottom of the glass. This will cover and secure the seam between the cup and the cardboard.

Put your paperweight on any desk or table. You can be creative and put any thing you like in your paperweight; shells, flowers, leaves, small toys, buttons, etc. These make great gifts!

title: What Did Religion Do for Early Iowans?
text:
When the first European settlers came to America, they came here with many different religious beliefs. Settlers from many different countries soon made the United States their home, and each group brought its different religious beliefs when the settlers arrived.

The writers of the Constitution decided that it would be best for the country if there was no set state church. This seemed strange at first to most new settlers, as the countries they had come from all had their own official state churches. The governments of these countries charged taxes to be used to support the state church, and the schools taught the beliefs of that church during regular school lessons. It didn't matter if the citizens of that country believed in the state religion or not—they still had to pay taxes to support the state church.

The United States of America has no state church. Our government makes certain that everyone is free to practice the religion of his or her choice, and taxes are not used to support any church. This is called the separation of church and state.

The early settlers in Iowa were allowed to practice whatever religion they chose, and religion played a large role in helping Iowa get settled. When Iowa was still part of the frontier, churches were often the only real organizations in the area. Churches often made rules to help the settlers get along with each other and preserve peace. There were very few police or law officers on the frontier, so it was important that people agree upon certain ways to behave so that there was order in the new settlements. Churches helped people to agree on how they should behave.

Churches also provided recreation for the early settlers. Recreation is what we do to relax and refresh our minds and bodies. Members of the early churches in Iowa got together to relax and enjoy each other's company. They had picnics, potluck suppers, and church socials. These events brought the early settlers together and gave them the opportunity to get to know each other better.

Churches in early Iowa also helped to educate the children on the new frontier. Church buildings were often used as schools during the week and as churches on Sunday. Later on, many of Iowa's colleges were started by churches. The Methodists started Iowa Wesleyan, Cornell College, Simpson, Upper Iowa, and Morningside. The Presbyterians are responsible for founding the University of Dubuque, Coe College, and Buena Vista. The Lutherans started Luther College and Wartburg College. Central University in Pella was first founded by the Baptists and then taken over by the Dutch Reformed Church and renamed Central College. The Dutch also started Dordt College, and Northwestern. Drake University was started by the Disciples of Christ, and the Quakers started William Penn College. The Catholics founded Clarke, Loras, Marycrest, St. Ambrose, Briar Cliff, and Mt. Mercy. Without churches in early Iowa, the education of our citizens would have suffered greatly.

Churches in early Iowa also took stands on moral issues and helped our state be more aware of right and wrong. Churches took stands against slavery, against breaking the Sabbath Day, against gambling, and against drinking. They also tried to help feed those who were hungry and motivate people to live better lives. Religion in early Iowa helped to make our state a better place to live.

title: The ‘Irish’ Saint Who Wasn’t Really Irish
text:
People parade in New York City and turn the rivers green in Chicago every year on St. Patrick's Day. This saint (holy person) lived 1,500 years ago. But did you know St. Patrick wasn't even Irish?

Patrick was born in Britain to wealthy parents. When he was 16, Irish pirates attacked his home and took him prisoner. They took him to Ireland and held him captive. He worked as a shepherd and became a Christian. After six years he escaped and went back to Britain. But he had a dream in which an angel told him to go back to Ireland as a missionary (person who does religious work in other countries). After Patrick became a priest, he did just that. Many Irish at that time practiced a nature-based religion, so Patrick used some of their symbols to teach them about Christianity. For example, they worshiped the sun. So he put the sun on a cross. This is where the Celtic cross comes from. Historians think he died on March 17 about A.D. 460. Irish villagers mourned his death every year on that day.

The Irish people have always been great storytellers. These stories often became more exaggerated over the years. The story of St. Patrick chasing the snakes out of Ireland is one of these exaggerated stories. St Patrick's Day started out as a religious holiday, but today he is remembered all over our nation with parties and parades. Does your community celebrate St. Patrick's Day?

title: Eastern Goldfinch
text:
The eastern goldfinch was declared Iowa's state bird in 1933. The goldfinch was chosen as the state bird because it can be found all over the state during all seasons of the year. The male goldfinch is more brightly colored than the female goldfinch. The goldfinch lives in Iowa year round and doesn't fly south for the winter. It eats seeds and harmful insects, and farmers particularly like the goldfinch because it eats weed seeds. The more weed seeds the goldfinch eats, the fewer weeds the farmer will have to deal with.

Most other members of the finch family build sloppy nests, but the goldfinch makes a very neat, cup-shaped nest. It then lines the nest with soft thistle down and lays four to six pale, bluish-white eggs in the nest. The eggs usually hatch in late August, and after about three weeks, the new birds leave the nest to brave the world on their own.

title: Why did the Methodist Church have the most members of any church on the Iowa frontier?
text: The Methodists had the most members of any other church on the Iowa frontier because the Methodist circuit riders, or traveling preachers, brought the message of the church to settlers all over the state. These circuit riders preached the gospel, performed marriages, and conducted funerals throughout Iowa, and many settlers decided to join the Methodist Church after listening to these traveling preachers.

title: The Amana Colonies
text:
The Amana Colonies were established in eastern Iowa in 1855 by the Community of True Inspiration. They were called the Inspirationalists, and they came from Germany and settled in Iowa because they felt that they could live the way they wanted to here, in a simple and honorable way.

The Inspirationalists eventually bought about 26,000 acres of land and settled seven villages in the area. They lived together in a communal way, meaning that all land and buildings were owned by the community, and everyone worked for the good of the group. The group called the settlements "The Amana Colonies" because "amana" means "believe faithfully." The colonies lived together in harmony for nearly 80 years before the leaders voted to stop communal living in 1932.

Today, people still live and work in Amana, and the Amana Society provides medical, dental, and burial insurance for its members. The colonies are a major Iowa tourist site today, and visitors come from all over to see the Museum of Amana History, the Community Church Museum, the Communal Agriculture Museum, the Communal Kitchen and Coopershop Museum, the Amana Arts Guild Center, the Mid-Americana Barn Museum, and the Industrial Machine Shop Museum. These museums are full of beautiful antiques, handmade crafts, old tools, and items used in days gone by. Visiting the Amana Colonies is like stepping back in time!

title: Religion in Iowa
text:
Let's look at some of the early churches in Iowa and explore the contributions they made in making our state what it is today.

The Mormons

The Mormons are members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and they came to Iowa seeking religious freedom. The church was founded by Joseph Smith in New York in 1830, and the members of the church had been persecuted by their neighbors since its earliest beginning.

The Mormons had settled in Nauvoo, Illinois, and had created a large and thriving city. Settlers from neighboring cities didn't like the fact that the Mormons had their own army, the Nauvoo Legion, and they resented Joseph Smith's claims that God would someday give the Mormons land to build a holy city called Zion. Some wanted to force the Mormons to move on.

In 1844, an angry mob murdered the Mormon leader Joseph Smith and his brother, Hyrum. The mobsters continued to threaten the Mormons living in Nauvoo, and the group finally fled to Iowa, seeking safety. The Mormons had plans to move west, but they built important settlements in Iowa where they stayed while they prepared for their journey. The first groups to head west built bridges, marked roads, dug wells, and even planted crops to be harvested by groups of Mormons who would follow later. Important settlements were built at Garden Grove, in Decatur County, at Mt. Pisgah, in Union County, and at Council Bluffs, along the Missouri River.

Although the Mormons didn't stay in Iowa, they helped to settle both southern and western Iowa for settlers who followed later. Many pioneers who traveled west later on used the bridges, wells, and trails made by the Mormon pioneers.

The Catholics

Most of Iowa's first Catholics came here from Ireland. Catholic miners from Ireland came to Dubuque to work in the lead mines in the area and then settled there. Father Samuel Mazzuchelli was a priest from Italy, and he came to Dubuque to help care for the Catholics living there. He built St. Raphael's Church and then built several more churches in the area before he died from an illness in 1864.

More and more Catholic immigrants continued to come to Iowa, so the Catholic Church created the Iowa Diocese. A diocese is a region or territory under the direction of a Catholic bishop. The first Catholic bishop in Iowa was Mathias Loras, a very hard-working and spiritual man. Loras College is named after this Catholic bishop.

Irish and German Catholics were soon joined by Czech and French Catholics as well. Each group often built its own Catholic church so that it could continue to worship in its native language. Many cities had several Catholic churches, each representing a different immigrant group.

The Catholics built churches and schools and helped provide educational opportunities for settlers in Iowa.

The Congregationalists

The Congregationalists believed that each congregation, or church, had control over itself and that the bishop of each congregation could decide how to run his church. The leaders of the Congregational Church, now called the United Church of Christ-Congregational, were well-educated and trained for their roles as ministers. They worried about the lawless and often Godless frontier and wanted to do something to provide religion to the region. They formed the American Home Mission Society and raised money to send missionaries to the frontier.

The first Congregational church in Iowa was built in 1838 in Denmark. In 1843, a group of 11 college students from Massachusetts came to Iowa to help bring religion to the settlers here. They founded churches and became leaders in the community. They built schools and eventually started Iowa College, which is now Grinnell College. The Congregationalists helped to bring education to the new frontier and made sure that there were schools here for those who desired an education.

The Methodists

The Methodist Church had the most members of any church on the Iowa frontier. The Methodists built their first church in 1834 in Dubuque. They chose local members to help teach Bible classes and lead church services but relied on circuit riders, or traveling ministers, to take care of the needs of many congregations.

The circuit riders would travel from congregation to congregation, never staying long in one place, caring for the needs of the Methodist settlers. Because these traveling ministers were able to take care of large groups of people who lived in many different towns, the Methodist Church grew very quickly in Iowa. By the Civil War, there were 90,000 Methodists in Iowa. The Methodists provided much-needed support for the early settlers of Iowa and gave them a connection to their neighbors.

There were other churches that had members in Iowa as well. The Lutherans, the Mennonites, the Amish, the Quakers, the Baptists, and the Jews all had members among the Iowa settlers, and each group made important contributions to settling the untamed frontier that became Iowa.

Consider the reasons people settled in this area and what moral issues they felt were important. Complete the cause-and-effect chart below.

title: Walnut Box
text:
Materials

walnuts

pliers or knife

glue

small piece of felt

lace, ribbon, string

Instructions

1. Get a walnut that is big enough to put something inside. It can be storebought or off a tree.

2. Find something to pry the walnut open, maybe some pliers or a knife. (If using a knife have a teacher or parent help you.) Try not to crack the walnut shell, you want it to stay intact.

3. When you get the walnut open, take out the nut part. You can eat it if you like walnuts.

4. Take a small square of felt and glue it on to make a hinge between the two walnut shells. This makes the shells able to open and close.

5. Find something to decorate the walnut with; lace, ribbon, string or twine. Glue the decoration around the opening of each shell. You can overlap and layer more than once to make a beautiful design.

What are you going to keep inside? You can keep coins, gum or candy!

title: McGuffey’s Readers
text:
What school supplies do your parents buy for you each time another school year rolls around? Pencils? Notebooks? Glue sticks? Chances are that you may be asked to bring some of these items to school, but has your teacher ever asked you to buy your own textbooks and bring them to school? That is just what happened in Iowa's early schools, because the first public schools didn't provide textbooks for their students. If families couldn't afford to buy textbooks for their children, they simply had to do without or use their creativity to supply reading material. Some students brought medical books, Bibles, or even old calendars from home if they weren't able to get regular textbooks.

As more people moved to Iowa and more students began attending school, the school system improved. By 1900, public schools were providing textbooks for the children. Very popular textbooks of this period were McGuffey's Readers, a series of books written to help children learn to read while teaching them important values at the same time.

William McGuffey was a professor of moral philosophy at the University of Virginia. He developed the McGuffey Readers after studying children and finding out what types of stories and poems appealed to them. He published his first readers in 1836 and continued to write them for many years. Eventually, he came up with a series of six books, called "readers," and a spelling book, to be used with elementary school children. He also developed a high school reader for older students. The most interesting thing about McGuffey's Readers was that each story or lesson in the books included a moral. A moral is a lesson that teaches a proper behavior or the difference between right and wrong. Some of these morals were that children should obey their parents, that they should be honest and work hard, that they should show respect for their country, and that they should honor the flag.

McGuffey's Readers also taught students to keep their bodies healthy and avoid habits such as smoking, using chewing tobacco, and drinking alcohol. One poem included in McGuffey's Readers uses birds as an example of being healthy and happy by avoiding alcohol. A verse reads, "Why do they twitter and sing, do you think? Because they've had nothing but water to drink." Another verse teaching students to stay away from tobacco reads, "Tobacco is a filthy weed that from the devil does proceed. It drains your purse, it burns your clothes, and makes a chimney of your nose."

Most parents agreed with the messages included in McGuffey's Readers and were pleased to have their children learning such morals as they learned to read. The readers also told the students that they needed to be good citizens, keep trying, do their best, and make the world a better place. McGuffey's Readers were used in at least 37 states and were the most widely used reading books of this time period in the United States.

title: Fighting Extremism with Education
text:
Extremism or radicalism means pushing an idea as far as it can go. Extremists are people who do this, and they often do not accept or tolerate other people’s ideas. They have hurt others and even killed because they didn’t agree with their beliefs.

Many brave individuals all over the world have dedicated their lives to fighting extremism by promoting education. Malala Yousafzai is one of these brave individuals. She believes that through education, people can learn to understand and accept one another.

Malala Yousafzai is a young Muslim woman. She was born and raised in Pakistan. In 2009, when Malala was 12 years old, the area of Pakistan she lived in was taken over by the Taliban. The Taliban are a religious extremist group who want to force their radical views onto other people. They believe that women should not receive an education, and Malala disagreed. When the Taliban came into her city and forbade girls from being able to attend school, she spoke up and campaigned for girls’ education. This put her in a lot of danger, but she did not let that stop her from speaking up for what she knew was right. At the age of 14, Malala was shot by a member of the Taliban and almost died.

On October 10, 2014, Malala was made a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for her dedication to education rights. More recently, in 2017, the United Nations named her the youngest ever official Messenger of Peace.

title: Cedar Rapids
text:
The city of Cedar Rapids is located in east-central Iowa. Cedar Rapids is the second largest city in Iowa and has been one of the fastest-growing areas in the Midwest. It is one of the leading manufacturing regions in the country.

Cedar Rapids is known for its good education system and especially for the strong music programs found in its schools. The Symphony School, a project that involves both the public schools and the Cedar Rapids Symphony, was founded to help students receive music training. Members of the symphony teach music classes in the schools and give private lessons to students as well. Students involved in these music programs also receive vouchers, or coupons, for symphony tickets.

Cedar Rapids also has many wonderful museums that focus on educating children in fun ways. The Iowa Children's Museum offers hands-on exhibits that help children learn and use science, language, and reading skills and also allow children to role-play, pretend, and work with art and music. The Science Station offers educational exhibits that teach visitors about science and make it fun. The Science Station offers workshops for school groups and has special weekend events that students can attend.

title: Aster
text:
The aster is a family of plants that includes many beautiful flowers, as well as some plants that are used for food. Most people think of daisy-like or star-shaped flowers when they think of asters, but lettuce, endive, chicory, and artichokes are types of asters as well.

The most famous flowers of the aster family are wild asters, daisies, chrysanthemums, marigolds, and zinnias. All these types of flowers can be found in Iowa, either growing wild in fields throughout the state or planted in flower gardens around our homes and buildings.

Most asters bloom in the late summer or early fall, and each plant produces many blooms, or flowers. The aster usually has a yellow disk in the center and is surrounded by petals in colors such as purple, blue, pink, yellow, and white.

Most asters are perennials, which means they come back each year and bloom again without having to be replanted. The most common types of aster planted in flower gardens are the New England aster, which is purple, and the New York aster, which is violet or blue.

title: What were the first Iowa school buses like?
text: Children were first bused to school in the late 1800s, when small, one-room schools were closed down, and the children were sent to larger schools farther away from the students' homes. At first, students rode to school in hacks. Hacks were horse-drawn wagons that transported the students to school each day. Later on, vans and buses were used. Iowa school children of today ride to school on the very familiar "big yellow school bus."

title: Education in Iowa
text:
Historically, Iowa has prided itself on a high-quality school system. Students have been given good educations, and a large percent of them have left school literate, or able to read. For a long time, Iowa has ranked near the top in the nation for quality education, so let’s take a look at how some early schools began!

Early Schools

The first school in Iowa was built in 1830 in Lee County. The school was a small log cabin, and the first teacher at the school was a man named Berryman Jennings. He came to Iowa from Kentucky when Dr. Isaac Galland, a doctor in the area, promised him a room with meals. Dr. Galland also promised him that he would allow Jennings to study from his medical books when he wasn't teaching. Jennings wanted to become a doctor, so he was grateful for the chance to study the doctor's books.

Other small log-cabin schools soon opened throughout Iowa, and the students were taught mainly by memorizing lessons. There were no desks at first, but just benches for the students to sit on. The girls sat on one bench, and the boys on another. The children weren't divided up into grades, but each student worked at his or her own pace. When a student finished a lesson, then he or she would move on to the next one. The school would have a blackboard in the front, usually just a wooden board painted black, and each student brought his or her own slate to write on. The students would be asked to go to the front of the room for "recitations," and they would recite from memory what they had just learned. They would also work arithmetic problems on the board and give public speeches.

The teachers weren't paid much money for their work in the early schools. They usually received about $20 or $30s per month, and some teachers had to accept their payment in butter, chickens, or other types of farm goods. The teachers usually stayed at the homes of the students, taking turns staying at each home. The families of the students would give the teacher a room and would provide all of the meals for the teacher as well. The more students a family had in the school, the longer the teacher would stay at that home.

School was usually divided up into three terms: fall, winter, and spring. During fall and spring terms, many of the older students, especially the boys, would stay out of school to help with the farm work at home. During the winter term, most students were in school, including boys as old as 18 and 19 years old. Once students reached the level of eighth grade in their studies, they could take tests to see if they were qualified to graduate. Most students who graduated from eighth grade never went on to receive any more education.

Academies and High Schools

If students wanted to receive more education after completing the eighth grade, they could sometimes choose to attend an academy. Academies were schools for students who had completed the eighth grade and were set up and run by different churches. Boys and girls often went to separate classes and studied religion along with their regular subjects, such as English, history, and math. Strict moral standards were enforced at these academies, and students were expected to live by the standards of the church that ran the academy.

In 1856, the first high school in Iowa was opened in Tipton. Other high schools opened over the years, but it took a lot of time before many students in Iowa actually attended high school. Most parents believed that an eighth-grade education was enough and didn't think that it was necessary for their children to go on to high school. By 1920, people had changed their minds about high schools, and soon there were high schools in all of Iowa's larger cities and in many of our towns as well. By this time, most Iowa students were attending high school.

Colleges and Universities

By 1850, Iowa had begun to open colleges and universities for the few students who needed higher education. Most people at this time didn't go to college, but people who wanted to become doctors, teachers, and government workers needed to attend college. Many of the first colleges and universities in Iowa were built and run by churches. These schools offered a good religious education along with training for a profession.

The state government also set up colleges and universities in Iowa. The University of Iowa opened in Iowa City in 1855 and taught classes to train doctors, lawyers, and other business workers. The Iowa Agricultural College, which is now Iowa State University of Science and Technology, was set up to teach courses in farming and provide training for more physical jobs. The Iowa State Normal School, which became the University of Northern Iowa, was established in the 1870s to train teachers for our schools. All of the colleges and universities in Iowa helped prepare students for careers and helped them to be more successful in life.

title: Leaf Designs
text:
Materials

dried leaves

glue

cardstock paper

phone book or newsprint

toothpicks

Directions

1. Go around the yard and find some neat leaves that you like. Gather all different sizes, shapes and colors.

2. Put your leaves between some pages of an old phonebook or between newsprint. Put some heavier books on top of them to make them flat and dry. Let you leaves dry there for at least a couple of days before making your leaf picture.

title: Henry Agard Wallace
text:
Henry Agard Wallace was born in Adair County on Oct. 7, 1888. He came from a family of farmers and was always interested in agriculture (science of farming) and improving methods of farming.

Henry graduated from Iowa State Agricultural College and went on to join his father and grandfather as a writer for the farming magazine called Wallaces' Farmer. During this time, Henry became interested in figuring out how much corn a farmer had to feed each pig to fatten it up enough to sell. He taught himself statistics and soon was able to figure out how much corn a farmer could afford to feed each pig and still make a profit (money made from a business after all expenses have been paid) when he sold the pig for pork. His figures helped farmers figure out how many pigs they could afford to raise on the corn they grew and allowed them to predict how much money they would make at the end of the year. During the early 1920s, Henry began working on solving another problem. He wanted to find ways to create better, more productive types of corn for the Iowa farmer to plant. He began experimenting with creating hybrids. Hybrids are plants that are created by crossing with each other two different varieties of the same type of plant with each other. Henry took pollen from one type of corn and used it to fertilize the silk of another type of corn until he was able to develop hardy hybrids.

Henry kept experimenting until he grew plants that were larger, stronger, and more resistant to disease than other corn plants of the time. He also worked to produce ears that were longer and had more kernels per ear and whose kernels were bigger than other types of corn. Eventually, Henry Wallace entered his hybrids in corn contests all over Iowa. When he won these contests, farmers wanted to buy his seed and plant it themselves. Soon Henry started Wallace's Pioneer Seed Corn Company and sold hybrid corn seed throughout the state.

As word of the amazing new corn seed spread throughout the Corn Belt, or the states of Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, and Indiana, more and more farmers began buying their seed from Wallace and planting hybrid corn in their fields. Before 1933, less than 1 percent of all the corn planted in the Corn Belt was hybrid corn. Within 10 years of the time Henry Wallace made his hybrids famous, 78 percent of the corn grown in the Corn Belt was hybrid corn. By 1965, nearly 100 percent of all the corn planted in the Corn Belt was hybrid corn. Henry Wallace's experiments with creating a better corn had changed the way farmers grew corn forever.

Henry Wallace became famous for his work and later went on to serve as the United States Secretary of Agriculture, vice president to President Franklin D. Roosevelt, and Secretary of Commerce under Roosevelt and Harry S Truman. He even ran for president in 1948 as the Progressive Party candidate. Henry Wallace died in 1965 after being diagnosed with Lou Gehrig's disease. A true scientist to the very end, Henry kept detailed notes and journals telling about each new development of his disease in the hopes that his notes would someday help doctors find a cure for the disease.

title: Amazing Little Soybean
text:
Iowa has long been known for its corn, but it's becoming famous for its soybeans as well. While corn has always been a popular grain, the amazing little soybean is beginning to make a name for itself.

Foods made from soybeans are becoming more popular with Americans because they are so healthy. Soy foods are rich in protein and are good for both heart and bone health. People who are interested in living active lives and in living longer believe that soybeans can help them take better care of their bodies.

Studies done by the Soyfoods Council and the United Soybean Board show that:

More Americans are trying soy foods each year.

Soy products are being used in place of meat more often than ever before.

Chips and snacks made from soy are becoming popular with snackers who want to stay healthy.

Frozen desserts, yogurt, drinks, and soups made with soybeans are expected to become popular in the near future.

Iowa companies that process soybeans and sell soy ingredients to companies that make soy foods are finding great success in the soybean business. Some of these companies process up to two tons of soy ingredients every hour, 20 hours a day, six days a week, just to keep up with the demands of its customers.

The companies make soy flour and other soy ingredients that are later added to bread, pasta, snacks, candy, energy bars, and health foods. These soy processing companies buy soybeans from our farmers and also pay them to grow special types of soybeans to be used only in their products.

title: The Soybean
text:
The soybean first became important in Iowa during World War II. Farmers began growing soybeans as a substitute for other protein foods that were more expensive.

The soybean is native to the warm, tropical regions of the world and has been grown in Asia for at least 5,000 years. There are more than 2,500 varieties of soybeans being grown throughout the world. The soybean is easy to grow and harvest, and it produces large crops. It can be grown anywhere that corn can be grown, and it has become a very popular crop here in Iowa.

Soybeans can be used in dozens of ways. Soybeans are used to make soy sauces, soybean meal, vegetable oil, tofu (bean curd), miso (fermented soybean paste), soy milk, and coffee substitutes. The plant is also used as a feed for animals and as a fertilizer. Soybean oil is used to make glycerin, paints, soaps, rubber substitutes, plastics, printer ink, and many other products.

title: What is the 4-H Program?
text: The 4-H program was started in about 1900 to help farm children take pride in their farms and learn skills that would help them be better farmers. The club is for both boys and girls nine to 19 years old. The pledge of the 4-H program is, "I pledge my Head to clearer thinking, my Heart to greater loyalty, my Hands to larger service, and my Health to better living, for my club, my community, my country, and my world." Members of 4-H clubs still learn skills such as breeding and raising chickens and cattle, growing vegetables and fruits, canning and preserving foods, and making handicrafts and needlework.

title: Dyersville
text:
Dyersville is located in eastern Iowa near Manchester. Dyersville is a beautiful town that offers something for everyone.

One of Dyersville's most famous attractions is the National Farm Toy Museum. The museum, established in 1986, is home to thousands of farm toys and exhibits. The museum is dedicated to honoring farmers and makers of farm toys. The displays include tractors, farm tools, trucks, miniature farm scenes, information about making farm toys, and even a large pedal tractor exhibit. The museum also includes a theater where visitors can enjoy a movie telling about the museum and about the history of farming. Another famous Dyersville attraction is the site of the baseball diamond used in the popular movie "Field of Dreams." The famous baseball diamond, made right in the middle of an Iowa cornfield, was created for the movie in Dyersville in 1988, and visitors still come to see the field and throw out a ball or two.

Dyersville also offers many other interesting things to do and see. The Dyer-Botsford Historical House and Doll Museum has a collection of around 1,000 dolls, and the Becker Woodcarving Museum displays the work of Iowa woodcarver Jack Becker.

Dyersville has many beautiful trails and outdoor areas to enjoy as well. The Heritage Trail runs 26 miles east from Dyersville to Dubuque. The trail is open during all seasons of the year and is very popular with bicyclists and hikers alike.

Dyersville is another great Iowa town to visit and explore!

title: Early Farming
text:
After about 1865, when the Civil War was over, Iowa was no longer a pioneer state waiting to be settled. It had become a state full of growing farming communities. The rich Iowa soil supported farms throughout the state, and farm families worked hard, year round, to make sure their farms produced a good profit.

Early Iowa Crops

Most farmers in the early 1900s practiced a type of farming called diversified farming. Diversified farming meant that farmers raised many different crops so that if one crop failed, or didn't produce well, they would still have other crops to use or sell.

When farmers first started raising crops in Iowa, they concentrated on wheat and did well, but when other states, such as North and South Dakota, Kansas, and Nebraska, started growing wheat as well, most Iowa farmers switched to corn as their main crop. Iowa's climate and soil proved to be perfect for growing corn, and Iowa farmers always grew plenty of it.

Besides selling the corn, and keeping some to eat, Iowa farmers also used the corn they grew to feed to their pigs. The farmers found that corn made perfect pig feed and that they could often make more money feeding their corn to their hogs and then selling the hogs than they could by just selling the corn itself. Hogs became another prime Iowa business. Iowa farmers also raised barley, oats, and hay. These grains were used as feed for the animals on the farm, and any extra could be sold to other farmers as animal feed as well.

Many Iowa farmers also raised sheep, both for their wool and for their meat. Farm families also raised cows for milk and meat, chickens for eggs and meat, and horses for work and transportation. Horses were used for pulling all types of farm machinery, from plows and corn planters to hay rakes. Horses also pulled wagons and buggies and carried the farmer and his family to town.

Iowa Farmers were Self-Sufficient

Most Iowa farm families were almost completely self-sufficient, which means that they were able to provide for nearly all of their own needs. Because they raised a little of everything, most families had nearly everything they needed right there on their farms. The only things that most farmers had to buy at the local store were coffee, flour, sugar, and salt.

Besides raising crops such as corn, barley, oats, and hay, farmers also planted large vegetable gardens. The farm women planted potatoes, tomatoes, beans, pumpkins, squash, and other vegetables to keep the family going throughout the year. They also planted fruit trees and spent much of the summer and fall canning and preserving fruits and vegetables for winter.

Farm families usually had eight to 10 cows that they milked each day. Whole milk was used in cooking and for drinking, but cream was separated from some of the milk to be used for making butter and cheese. Cream was sometimes sold to the local store or to neighbors. The skim milk, leftover after the cream was taken from it, was usually fed to the pigs.

Farmers raised chickens and ate the eggs or sold or traded them at the local store in exchange for groceries. Often, children had the job of taking care of the chickens and gathering the eggs. Chickens were also used as meat for the family.

In the winter, the farmer usually butchered both a hog and a cow to provide meat for the next few months. The women would bottle the meat, using every possible part of the animal and wasting nothing. One common farm saying was that the farmer's wife used all of the pig but the squeal!

Farm Families Relied on Each Other

Because farming was hard work, neighboring families often helped each other and relied on each other for both work and entertainment. Most farmers couldn't afford to buy their own threshing machines, which were machines that separated the kernels of grain from the stalk. Because these machines were expensive, five or six farm families often joined together and bought a threshing machine to be shared. Each family then took turns using the machine to thresh their grain, and the other families came to help. The men worked together out in the fields, and the women prepared huge meals for the men. This way, each farmer got his turn with the machine and received much-needed help with the work.

Farm families also shared holidays and special times together. Socials and programs were often held at the country school, and all the families joined together to bring food and prepare programs. School children memorized songs, poems, and skits to entertain the families, and everyone enjoyed socializing with their neighbors.

Farmers stuck together and worked hard to earn a living. Times have changed for Iowa farmers today, but our farmers still work hard and are still willing to help their neighbors when the need arises.

title: Stained Glass Window
text:
Materials

Directions

1. Cut two pieces of waxed paper, approximately 10 by 12 inches, into an interesting shape. Use a utility knife to shave pieces of crayons of different colors onto one of the waxed paper sheets. (Have a teacher or parent help you. These knives are very sharp and cause painful cuts.) Spread the shavings evenly over the waxed paper. Sprinkle colored glitter over the areas between the shavings.

4. Place the finished design against a window to let the outside light create a stained glass effect.

title: The Stagecoach
text:
Between 1833 and 1870, the most popular way to travel across Iowa and other Midwestern states was by way of a stagecoach. Stagecoach lines ran east and west across the states of Iowa, Wisconsin, Missouri, and Nebraska. The largest stagecoach company in the area was the Western Stage Company, which employed about 1,500 people, owned 600 coaches, and used about 3,000 horses to pull the coaches.

The Western Stage Company used only the finest vehicles of the time, the Concord Stage. The Concord Stage was built in Concord, New Hampshire, and each one cost $1,050 each—a huge amount of money for the early 1800s. The Concord Stage had the finest wheels of any stagecoach made at the time. They were made of white oak and dried carefully to make certain that they would be strong and stable. The spokes in each wheel were made by hand and fit into the rim of the wheel so well that it was impossible to see the joint. While the wheels on other stagecoaches often warped or split during trips in bad weather, the wheels of the Concord Stage kept on rolling.

The body of the Concord was a strong, solid oval made of wood and reinforced with iron bands. The body rested on leather braces that cradled the carriage and rocked it back and forth as the stagecoach traveled along. Many people believed that this was done to make the ride more comfortable for the passengers, but the leather braces were really used to keep the stagecoach from bumping into the horses and injuring them.

The inside of the Concord Stage was about four feet wide and four and one-half feet high. There were three seats inside the coach, each seating three people, so the stage carried nine when fully loaded. The stage often allowed one extra rider to sit beside the driver as well. The seats inside were padded, but were still very hard and uncomfortable. The middle seat was the most uncomfortable, as it had no backrest, so those who arrived late always had to sit in this section. Each Concord Stage had windows that were covered with leather curtains to keep out dust, rain, and snow. The curtains didn't do a very good job of keeping the passengers comfortable, however, and the journey was usually either too hot, too cold, too dusty, or too wet. When the curtains were down, the coach was dark and stuffy inside, yet if they were open, the passengers choked on the dust from the horses.

Besides transporting passengers, the coaches also carried mail from city to city along their routes. Mail sacks, sometimes weighing as much as 250 pounds, would be carried in the leather "boot," or trunk, at the back of the coach. The most valuable and important mail was usually kept under the driver's seat.

The coaches were capable of going as fast as 15 miles per hour, but they usually only averaged about three and a half miles per hour on most trips. The stagecoach would stop about every 15 miles to change horses, and passengers could take a brief rest and get something to eat. On long trips, passengers would stop at stations for the night and start out again in the morning.

By 1870, the railroad had reached Iowa, and most people chose to travel by train rather than by stagecoach. In 1870, the Western Stage Company went out of business, and the era of the stagecoach in Iowa was over.

title: Has Amelia Earhart’s Plane Been Found?
text:
A research group that looks for historical aircraft has been trying to solve one of the greatest mysteries of the 20th century. What really happened to Amelia Earhart? Earhart was the first woman to try to fly around the world. She disappeared without a trace while flying over the Pacific Ocean in 1937.

Earhart and Fred Noonan, her navigator, could have landed somewhere near Gardner Island, now called Nikumaroro. Others believe they crashed into deep water. By using technology to study a 1937 photo of the island's shore, researchers may have new evidence in the case. The photo shows what may be the landing gear of her Lockheed Electra airplane sticking out of the water. This could mean Earhart and Noonan lived on the island for some time after the crash. Artifacts have also been found on the island that could have belonged to Earhart and Noonan.

The oceanographer who found the undersea wreckage of the Titanic says the photograph might be the clue that helps us find out what really happened. Underwater robotic submarines and mapping equipment will help the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery look for the plane's remains. Perhaps an old photograph and new technology will help solve a 75-year-old mystery!

title: Cardinal
text: One of the most strikingly beautiful birds of Iowa is the cardinal. Sometimes called the "redbird" because of its bright red color, the cardinal can often be found at backyard bird feeders and nested in parks around the state. It is easy to spot the cardinal just about anywhere it goes. It is a bright scarlet color with a black throat and a black face. The male is a brighter, more vibrant red, while the female is more of a rusty brown. Both male and female cardinals have red crests on top of their heads, and their beaks are red as well. Cardinals stay in one place all year long and don't migrate when the seasons change. The female builds her nest out of twigs and grass in bushes or low shrubs. The female lays three to four eggs at a time, and she sits on the eggs for about two weeks until they hatch. Both the male and the female take care of their young, and most cardinal parents raise between two and four "broods," or groups of young hatched at the same time, per year. The cardinal is another beautiful native of the great state of Iowa!

title: Why was it sometimes dangerous to travel by steamboat?
text:
Traveling by steamboat could be dangerous because explosions would sometimes occur on the boats, injuring many passengers. Steamboats used the power of steam to turn the giant paddles that pulled the boats upstream. Large boilers (or containers) were used to heat water until it turned to steam.

If the boilers got too hot, they would sometimes explode and burn the passengers with boiling water. These explosions could often start the boat on fire as well, and the steamboat pilot would try to turn the boat toward the shore so that the passengers could jump off and swim to safety.

title: Boone
text:
If you travel about 15 miles west of Ames and 35 miles north of Des Moines, you will find the city of Boone.

Boone is home of the Boone and Scenic Valley Railroad, which is Iowa's very own working railroad museum. Visitors can ride the train on a 15-mile round-trip ride over two amazing bridges and through the Des Moines River valley.

The Kate Shelley Memorial High Bridge is also located in Boone. The bridge is one of the the longest and the highest double-track railroad bridges in the United States. The bridge is suspended 185 feet above the Des Moines River and runs 2,685 feet across.

The Kate Shelley Railroad Museum is a restored depot dedicated to 15-year-old Kate Shelley, a young Iowa girl who warned a passenger train of danger and saved the lives of many people. The museum has a working telegraph, many railroad artifacts, and other interesting displays.

The Boone County Historical Center is another great place to visit. Built in 1907, the building houses exhibits of natural and geological history, American Indian history, and military and local events as well. If you like history and old trains, don't miss visiting the city of Boone!

title: Early Transportation
text:
Getting to Iowa in the early 1800s wasn't always an easy task. Early settlers came here by way of steamboats, stagecoaches, and covered wagons. When the railroads came to Iowa in the 1850s and 1860s, transportation in Iowa improved, and people were able to get from place to place much more quickly and easily.

Steamboats

In 1823, the first steamboat began running on the upper Mississippi River. Soon steamboats began carrying food and guns from St. Louis to forts upriver and furs and lead down river to cities. Not long after the steamboats started running on the rivers, people began using them to travel west from states such as New York and Pennsylvania. Settlers moving to Iowa liked taking the steamboat because they could bring heavier items, such as furniture, that couldn't be brought easily by wagon.

Immigrants also enjoyed using steamboats because they were a cheap way to travel to Iowa. Also, they didn't have to worry about purchasing horses and wagons for the trip west.

Steamboats were a simple and major method of transportation (way of moving people or things from place to place) until the 1870s, when the railroads were all completed. After this time, most people preferred to travel by train than by steamboat.

Railroads

The first railroad in America was built in 1831 in Baltimore, Maryland. People soon realized that the railroad was the best way to transport goods and people quickly and efficiently, and railroads began springing up all over the East. As these railroads were finished, the citizens of Iowa began thinking that if they could build their own railroad that would join up with the Illinois railroads, they would be able to benefit from this great new "iron horse" as well. ("Iron horse" was the name for the train.)

Four major railroads began construction on railroad lines that would cross the state of Iowa and connect to the railroad lines farther east. Building the railroads was expensive and difficult. It took the Dubuque and Pacific Railroad 17 years to build a railroad that stretched 400 miles. In spite of how slowly the work went, the companies involved knew that their work would eventually pay off.

By 1870, the four major railroads had each completed lines that connected Iowa's western border to the railroads in the East. Soon after this, shorter railroad lines, called commuter lines or interurbans, were built. These lines were built to transport people from town to town so that they could do their shopping, visit friends, or conduct business. When the railroad came to Iowa, it helped our citizens in many ways. It allowed them to travel during any season without having to worry about rain, snow, dust, or mud. It also provided transportation for farmers to send crops and animals to cities in the East where they could be sold for a profit.

With the development of the railroad, coal mines soon opened up as well. During the 1800s, all trains burned coal, so coal mining became a big business in Iowa as long as the coal-burning trains were used.

Businesses used by farmers also increased because of the railroad. Meat-packing plants and grain-processing factories opened throughout Iowa to help the farmers throughout our state and the Midwest. The railroads carried animals to the meat-packing plants for slaughter and then carried the meat East to be sold. Trains also carried grain to the processing plants and then carried the processed grain to the east as well.

By 1900, railroads had changed the lives of nearly every person living in Iowa. By this time, there wasn't a person living anywhere in Iowa who lived more than eight miles from a railroad!

Stagecoaches

The stagecoach was a very popular means of transportation between 1833 and 1870. People who wanted to get from place to place quickly, and in relative comfort, used stagecoaches for their travels. Stagecoaches were also the main method of transporting mail from place to place. Once the railroads were completed, most people stopped using stagecoaches because trains were much faster and more comfortable. After 1870, the Western Stage Company, Iowa's largest stagecoach line, closed its doors, and other companies soon followed. The stagecoach era in Iowa ended after lasting for nearly 40 years.

title: David Bushnell and the Turtle
text:
A submarine was used in the American Revolution? Absolutely. David Bushnell, American patriot and inventor, used reason and logic to build the first military submarine.

David Bushnell was born on a farm in Connecticut in 1740. He experimented with underwater explosives during college and built a submarine that would carry them. Bushnell's vessel was nicknamed "the Turtle" because it was shaped like two wooden turtle shells joined together, standing on end. Its hull filled with water to submerge and was pumped out by the operator to rise. Two propellers and a rudder were used to guide it.

Benjamin Franklin and others were impressed with Bushnell's invention. When British warships blockaded New York Harbor in 1776, the Turtle was called into action. The submarine operator was supposed to use a giant screw to attach the powder keg (called a mine) to the bottom of the British flagship, the HMS Eagle.

The plan seemed like a failure when the mine could not be fastened to the ship. However, the gunpowder made a frightening explosion underwater. The British quickly moved their warships from the area. Although it didn't work as planned, Bushnell's invention did have an effect on the British navy.

Bushnell then turned his skills to improving underwater mines. These were placed in harbors to protect American rivers and forts. General George Washington was pleased with Bushnell's work and gave him a commission (job) in the Army.

Today David Bushnell is given credit for inventing the first military submarine and for making valuable contributions to the American Revolution. You can visit a replica (an accurate model) of the Turtle in the Connecticut River Museum in Essex, Connecticut. By yourself or with a partner, think of a person who has used reason and logic to develop something that helped America.
