title: My Favorite Person or Event in History
text: Imagine that you could go visit any person or event in history. Draw a picture of where you would go or who you would visit. Tell why you chose that person or place. Good luck!

title: Fort Osage at Sibley
text:
Fort Osage is located near the town of Sibley, about 20 miles northeast of Kansas City. William Clark, one of the famous explorers who traveled west, picked the spot where Fort Osage should be built. He and his partner, Meriwether Lewis, chose the spot because it was on a hill, about 70 feet above a bend in the Missouri River. Building a fort here would make it easy to see any enemy coming from miles around.

Fort Osage was built in 1808. United States soldiers lived in the fort to protect and guard the new territory (part of the United States that hasn't become a state yet) from any enemies that might want to attack. The soldiers at Fort Osage also made friends with the Osage Indians and traded with them. The Osage Indians came to the fort to trade furs and skins for cloth, tobacco, knives and other things that they could only get from white people.

Fort Osage was a busy place. Explorers, government officers, trappers, traders and many American Indians came to the fort in the 19 years that it was open. George Sibley was in charge of all trading that went on at the fort, and he was able to help the government make money because of his careful record keeping. The town of Sibley was later named after him.

The United States government closed Fort Osage in 1822. It was used for storage for several years and then was left empty in 1827. The Native Sons of Kansas City, a group of men who work to protect the history of this area, started rebuilding Fort Osage in 1941. The rebuilt fort became a national historic landmark in 1961.

Visitors can now tour the fort and learn more about the history of the Osage Indians, the first settlers in the area and the Lewis and Clark expedition.

title: Can Facebook Save Dying Languages?
text:
Can you say a few words in Siletz Dee-ni? No? How about saying "hello" in Aka? If you can't, you're not alone! These two languages and 3,500 more could become extinct by the end of this century. Almost 80 percent of the world's population now speaks only one percent of the world's 7,000 languages. This has happened because of globalization. Globalization means that countries are more connected through trade, money and workers. When countries work together, people must be able to communicate with each other. That means many people have to learn another language. English is the main language used throughout the world for business and the Internet.

Why is this a problem? When the last person who is able to speak a particular language dies, some of the knowledge that is found within that language dies with them. A language contains the history of its people, how they used their environment and their beliefs and ideas. Technology may just save many of these languages from extinction! With YouTube, Facebook and other forms of social media, languages that are spoken by even 5 or ten people can be taught to others around the world.

National Geographic has been working on the Enduring Voices Project. Its goals are to record native speakers of endangered languages into talking dictionaries and help communities learn ways to save their languages from extinction. What language do you want to help save?

title: American Indians in Missouri
text:
The American Indians who lived in Missouri and across America in the early days of this country lived together in tribes, or communities, much the same way we do today. Although each community was different from other communities in some ways, American Indian communities also shared many beliefs, values and ways of living in common. This week, we will look at how the tribes of Missouri were the same in some ways and different in others. There were two main American Indian tribes who lived in Missouri before the Europeans came. The Missouri Indians and the Osage Indians both made their homes in Missouri.

Shared Ways of Life of the Missouri American Indian Tribes

Homes and Farms

Both the Missouri and the Osage tribes built houses for their families. The Missouri tribe lived in houses called wigwams. A wigwam was made of a frame of young trees bent to form a half circle. The frame was then covered with bark or reeds woven together to make mats. These wigwams looked a lot like upsidedown baskets.

The Osage tribe built long houses for their families. A long house was made of a wooden frame with bark, skins and mud on the outside. The long houses were about 100 feet long, and several families lived together inside. Both the Missouri and the Osage tribes planted crops to feed their families. It was the job of the women to plant corn, beans and squash and to prepare them once they were ripe.

Differences Between Tribes

Hunting Habits

"Missouri" means, "the people who have big canoes." The Missouri people were great hunters, but they spent more time farming than hunting. They spent the summers in one place, growing crops and gathering berries, nuts and wild fruit.

In the winter, the Missouri tribe would go on hunting trips, tracking bison, elk, deer and wild turkeys. When they traveled, they often used dogs to pull a travois, a type of sled or trailer used to carry their belongings. Dogs were also used as watchdogs. Often, dogs would even end up being used for food.

The Osage tribe spent much more time hunting than did the Missouri tribe. The entire tribe went on the hunts. They went on a spring hunt, which began in March and lasted until May. In May, they came back to their villages to plant corn, beans and pumpkins. In the summer, the Osage went on another hunt and came back to the villages in the fall to harvest their crops. After the harvest was over, the Osage went on one more hunt in the fall, but returned to their villages again once the coldest weather hit. The Osage Indians stayed at home during the winter. The Osage were great horsemen, and they used horses to carry their belongings when they went on their hunts. The Osage were famous for their riding skills.

Physical Differences

The Missouri Indians were known for wearing animal skins, blankets and buffalo robes. They also made bracelets out of bone, copper, beads and brass. The Osage called themselves the "Little Ones," which may have been a joke, for Osage people were large and had broad shoulders. They have been described as looking like giants, as many of them were more than six feet tall, and some were as tall as seven feet! They were strong and healthy people, and it wasn't uncommon for the Osage men to run 60 miles in one day or shoot an arrow all the way through a full-grown buffalo.

The Osage women also took very good care of themselves and were known for their beauty. Missouri American Indian tribes were different in many ways, but they all lived in communities, built houses for their families, grew crops to survive and hunted animals for both their meat and their skins.

title: Kenora, Ontario, Canada
text:
Kenora, a beautiful city in Ontario, Canada, was once the home of the Ojibwe Indian Tribe. The Ojibwe people settled here to be near Lake of the Woods, a good source of water and animals that came to drink there.

The first European to come to Kenora was a Frenchman named Jacques de Noyon. In 1688, de Noyon visited Lake of the Woods on a trip into the wilds of what was then an unknown area. He found the Ojibwe people and saw the large amounts of furs and skins they had gathered.

In 1836, the world-famous Hudson's Bay Company built a fur-trading post on the Winnipeg River. This post was later moved to the site of the present city of Kenora in 1860. When the railroad came through Kenora, the town began to grow. Businesses in the area used the railroad to send timber, fur and fish to people in the East.

Today, lumber and fish are still important to the city of Kenora. Fishing is a popular sport and people come from all over Canada and the United States to fish in Lake of the Woods. Tourists also come here to hunt, swim, water ski and boat.

The Ojibwe people came to Kenora because of the many furs, skins, fish and trees near Lake of the Woods. Many of the people who live in Kenora today came here for the very same reasons.

title: Sacagawea
text:
Sacagawea was a Shoshone Indian woman who helped the great explorers Lewis and Clark on their journey to explore the West. Sacagawea had been born and raised in the West and knew about the land, the best paths to travel and how to get along with different American Indian tribes.

Sacagawea, her French husband, Toussaint Charbonneau, and their young baby traveled along with Lewis and Clark as they explored the land called the Louisiana Purchase. America had bought the huge chunk of land from the French, and President Thomas Jefferson asked Lewis and Clark to go west and find out what this new piece of America was like. Sacagawea made the journey much easier for the explorers. She showed them shortcuts that saved them a lot of time when traveling. She also talked to different American Indians along the way, persuading them to give the group fresh horses, food and other supplies. When food was hard to find, she found roots, berries and other plants to keep the men from going hungry.

Sacagawea was a great help to Lewis and Clark on the journey West. She used her skills to make the journey faster, safer and more comfortable for these great explorers of the new American West.

title: The Atlatl
text:
"Atlatl" is an Aztec Indian word that means "spear thrower." Before the bow and arrow were invented, early American Indians used the atlatl to help them hunt animals for food. The atlatl was a special spear thrower that let the American Indians throw their spears farther and with more power than they could by using their arms alone. Historians believe that people have been using the atlatl for more than 40,000 years. The American Indians even used the atlatl as a weapon against the Spanish when they came to the New World in the late 1400s. A spear thrown with an atlatl could pierce the metal armor worn by the Spanish soldiers.

Today, many people have rediscovered the atlatl. They hold competitions to see who can use the atlatl to throw a spear the farthest and who can come closest to hitting the center of a target.

title: Squanto
text:
Kidnapped by Spanish explorers as a young man and sold into slavery in Spain, Squanto managed to escape from slavery and return to his people. When he got back to America, he found that all of his tribe had died from smallpox, so he went to live in a nearby Wampanoag Indian village.

Squanto made friends with the settlers at the Plymouth settlement in Massachusetts and taught them to plant corn and to find and prepare seafood. Without his help, the Pilgrims might easily have starved to death.

Squanto also arranged a treaty, or an agreement, between the settlers and the local American Indians that helped the two groups get along with each other. This treaty remained unbroken for 50 years. Squanto performed many other acts of friendship for the English colonists before he died in 1622.

title: Families in Japan
text:
When a Japanese husband and wife have a child, they stop calling each other by their first names. Instead, they call each other "otousan" ("father") or "okaasan" ("mother"). They do this to show that being a parent is more important than being a husband or a wife.

Japanese parents teach their children that the group they belong to is much more important than each separate person is. The children must always do what is best for the group. Parents and teachers tell the children that they must behave well or it will make their families and their friends look bad.

Japanese children study hard and doing well in school is very important. Children go to school all day and into the evening. They eat lunch together in their classroom and spend part of their school day cleaning the rooms, halls, toilets and yards of the school.

Japanese children are taught to show great respect for their parents and grandparents. Many Japanese families have their grandparents living with them, and the family takes care of them in their old age.

Japan is a great place to learn how to work, study and show respect for others.

title: Trip to an American Indian Village
text: Imagine that you traveled back in time to an American Indian village in our state. What did you find there? Were the people friendly? Draw the people and things you saw on your trip back to the American Indian village.

title: Independence
text:
Independence started as a small settlement only three miles from the Missouri River. The town grew quickly during the 1840s when many pioneers started heading west. Independence became known as the "jumping-off point" for those starting on the long trip west.

Before Independence started building stores and trading posts, it was home to a religious group called the Mormons. The Mormons were members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, a church started by Joseph Smith. They are often called Mormons after their book of scripture, The Book of Mormon. The Mormons came to Independence to practice their religion in peace. The Mormons built houses, schools and churches and even started the first newspaper in the area. When other settlers living in Independence got worried that the Mormons were trying to take over, they drove them out of Jackson County.

After Lewis and Clark's trip to explore the Louisiana Purchase, Americans began heading west by the hundreds. Independence was sometimes called the "Queen City of the Trails" because it was the place where the Santa Fe, the Oregon and the California Trails began. Brave pioneers who were ready to head into the wilderness came to Independence to buy supplies and load their wagons before getting on the trail. Today, Independence is full of interesting historic sites. Visitors can tour the National Frontier Trails Center to find out more about the Santa Fe, California and Oregon Trails. They can also see real Santa Fe Trail swales, or ruts in the rock made by wagons traveling along the trail. Independence was also the hometown of Harry Truman, who became the 33rd president of the United States in 1945. The Truman Home and the Truman Presidential Museum and Library are fun places to learn more about one of Independence's greatest citizens.

title: Celebrating a Hero’s Trip Around the Earth
text:
It was 1957 when the Soviet Union launched the first spacecraft into orbit. Americans were shocked! The space race had just begun and we were already behind! In 1961 President John F. Kennedy announced that the U.S. planned to land a man on the moon by the end of the decade. The Russians responded by first launching a dog into orbit, and later two men. The race was on!

On Feb. 20, 1962, a Marine Corps fighter pilot from Ohio stepped up to put his life on the line. John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth. The success of his Mercury mission was one of the first steps to landing a man on the moon in July 1969.

John Glenn served as the U.S. senator from Ohio for 24 years, but he longed to go back into space. In 1998 at the age of 77 he was able to see that dream come true. He traveled on the space shuttle Discovery and became the oldest person to ever go into space! On Feb. 20th, 2012, America celebrated the 50th anniversary of John Glenn's first orbit. Mr. Glenn and the remaining members of the Mercury mission space team were given a hero's welcome at Cape Canaveral in Florida. Because of Mr. Glenn's service to our country as an astronaut and a senator, he has been called an American hero.

title: Explorers in Missouri
text:
The first people who explored and settled in America and Missouri came here for many different reasons. Some came here looking for gold and other ways to get rich. Others, like the Pilgrims, came here searching for a place to worship God in their own way. Some came to America hoping to find freedom from unfair governments. A few even came here hoping to find good health and a long life. This week, we will look at several different explorers and settlers to discover what they hoped to find when they came to America and Missouri.

Columbus

When Columbus set out on his journey across the ocean, he hoped to find a new way to get to the Far East. If his plan worked, Spain would have a new way to get to China. Sailors could sail west and bring back all kinds of gold, spices and silks to sell in Europe. Columbus didn't realize that North and South America were blocking the way!

Ponce de Leon

Ponce de Leon, a Spanish sailor, was an unusual explorer. He didn't sail west looking for gold, freedom, or honor. He came looking for a way to stay young forever.

Ponce de Leon had heard legends (stories that may or may not be true) about the Fountain of Youth. The Fountain of Youth was a spring that was supposed to make anyone who drank from it stay young and healthy forever. He explored the Bahamas, searching for this famous spring. Instead of finding the Fountain of Youth, Ponce de Leon became the first European to explore Florida.

Cartier

Jacques Cartier sailed northwest from France hoping to find a new trade route to Asia. A trade route is a pathway that can be used for traders to bring their goods back and forth. Like Columbus, Cartier wanted to find a new way to get to all the wealth and riches that could be found in China and other Asian countries.

Cartier landed near the mouth of the St. Lawrence River. He thought that if he sailed up the river, he would reach the open sea. He hoped to reach Asia by using this waterway.

In 1534, Cartier sailed up the St. Lawrence River and found that it never reached the ocean. His plans to sail to China were blocked by the American continent. He never found his trade route, but Cartier claimed Quebec for France.

Early Missouri Explorers and Settlers

The first French explorers to come to North America hoped to find gold and silver. They didn't find any of these valuable metals, but they found something that made them almost as rich . . . fur!

Explorers like Louis Jolliet came to the Missouri area looking for furs from animals such as beaver, mink and otter. These furs were very popular in Europe at this time. People loved to wear hats and coats made of fur. They also used these expensive furs to trim their dresses and other clothing. Many early French settlers came to Missouri hoping to get rich by trapping, trading and selling the furs they found here. Other early settlers came to Missouri hoping to convert (to change someone's religion) the American Indians to their church. Missionaries for the Catholic Church who came to Missouri built churches and helped the American Indians work with the leaders of the French government. Both the fur traders and the Catholic missionaries helped to explore and settle Missouri.

The first settlers came to America and Missouri for many different reasons. Those who had the courage to stay did their best to make their dreams come true here in a new and sometimes frightening land.

title: Timbuktu, Mali, Africa
text:
Timbuktu is a city in the Western African nation of Mali. You may have heard someone say something like, "Trash is scattered from here to Timbuktu," and wondered exactly what that meant. Timbuktu is in a very out-of-the-way place, far from other large cities. People often use the word"Timbuktu" to describe something that is far away, or out in the middle of nowhere.

Timbuktu wasn't always such an out-of-the-way place. The city of Timbuktu was once the center of learning, wealth and religion in Africa.

The city started in the 1100s as a camp for African nomads, or people who traveled from place to place. Later, as Mali became a rich African kingdom, Timbuktu became an important city for trading gold and salt. People came from all over northern Africa to trade in the wealthy city.

Besides the many traders who came to Timbuktu to do business, many wise men, artists and members of the Muslim religion came here as well. Timbuktu was a beautiful city with large buildings, interesting people and wonderful places to eat and sleep.

Today, Timbuktu really is near the middle of nowhere. The famous city has crumbled, and its wealth is gone. Small traders still bring their camels, loaded down with salt, to the city to trade, but there is no longer any gold here to trade for. A few brave visitors still make the trip to Timbuktu, hoping to find out more about this city in the middle of nowhere.

title: Jacques Marquette
text:
Father Jacques Marquette was a Catholic priest who explored the Missouri area with his friend, Louis Jolliet. These two Frenchmen were the first Europeans to explore the Mississippi River area. Jacques Marquette was born in Laon, France. He had heard about the New World, and he wanted to see it for himself. In 1666, Marquette got his wish when he was sent to the Catholic missions in Canada.

While working as a missionary in Canada, Father Marquette met a French trader named Louis Jolliet. Jolliet wanted to explore the land to the south and find new American Indian tribes to trade with for furs.

Marquette went with Jolliet on his trip, hoping to convert (to change someone's religion) the American Indian tribes to the Catholic Church. The two men spent much time talking to the American Indians living in the Great Lakes area. These American Indians told Marquette and Jolliet about a river they called the Mississippi, which in their language meant, "The Father of the Waters." Marquette and Jolliet decided to explore this new river. The two explorers traveled down the river, taking careful notes about everything they saw. By the time the Frenchmen turned back, they had explored an area that no white person had ever seen. They had also learned that the Mississippi River did not lead to the Pacific Ocean, but that it led to the Gulf of Mexico, something that no one had known before this. After they returned to Canada, Father Marquette drew a map of the Mississippi River. This map showed an American Indian village near the spot where the Missouri River joins the Mississippi. He called this place "Ou Missouri." Today, we call it Missouri.

title: The Zipper
text:
Most of the world's greatest inventions happened because someone had a problem that needed to be solved. The zipper is one invention created for this very reason.

Whitcomb L. Judson loved machines and gadgets. He spent much time tinkering with new ideas for making life easier.

Whitcomb had a friend with a problem. His friend had a stiff back that made it impossible for him to bend over and use both hands to hook up the hooks on his shoes. Whitcomb set out to solve this problem for his friend.

After working for a few weeks, Whitcomb came up with a special slide fastener that could be opened and closed with just one hand. By 1893, Whitcomb had received a patent, or license from the government giving him and only him the right to make and sell his new invention.

After a few years, other inventors came up with even better "hookless fasteners." Because they were so easy to "zip" up, the fasteners soon became known as zippers. By the 1920s, zippers were used in galoshes (rubber boots), clothing, luggage and bags. Today, the zipper is found on almost everything, from pants to dresses to tents. Whitcomb Judson's invention helped his friend and people everywhere who needed an easy way to open and close almost anything.

title: Cesar Chavez
text:
At the age of 10 years old, Cesar Chavez became a migrant worker when his father lost his farm in Yuma, Arizona. A migrant worker moves from place to place, working in the fields when the crops are ready.

Cesar moved to California, working in the fields, orchards and vineyards to earn money for himself and his family. He joined many different groups that tried to help the migrant workers get more money, better houses and shorter working hours.

After years of work, Cesar Chavez started the United Farm Workers of America, the first successful farm workers' union in United States history. A union is a group that works for fair pay, safe places to work and good working hours for men and women working at the same type of job. The union started by Cesar Chavez is still around today and works to make sure that farm workers are treated fairly.

Cesar and his union started strikes against fruit and vegetable growers who refused to give farm workers fair pay, reasonable working hours and safe places to live. A strike happens when workers refuse to come to work until the owners of the company promise to give them what they are asking for. These strikes made people across the nation aware of the needs of the farm workers and helped to bring important changes to the farm industry.

title: Sharing Public Space: Vitus Bering and Russian Colonies in Alaska
text:
Imagine traveling 6,000 miles over land with supplies for an expedition, and THEN sailing through frigid seas to look for a new world. This was the job given to Vitus Bering, a Danish navigator who sailed for the Russian navy. Peter the Great, czar (ruler) of Russia, asked Bering to explore the eastern coast of Russia. He was wondering if land connected Asia and North America.

Bering's first trip began in 1725. After spending three years getting his supplies to eastern Russia, Bering sailed along the coastline. He didn't see any land to the east, and he didn't realize he was sailing in the narrow passage between Russia and Alaska. This waterway is now called the Bering Strait.

Bering led another expedition in 1741. This time his ship landed on Kayak Island, off the coast of Alaska. They explored some of the Aleutian Islands and met the native people there, the Aleut. He was the first European to arrive in present-day Alaska.

Bering died before returning to Russia, but his voyages paved the way for Russian settlements in North America. Many fur traders came to the area. In 1799 the Russian government established a fur-trading operation in Alaska. Furs from foxes, sea otters and seals were very valuable.

Unfortunately, the Russians took advantage of the native people just as some Europeans had done in settling New England. The Russians took over their lands and forced them to hunt for furs. They also brought new diseases, which killed many natives.

Today, the Aleut people continue to live along the western coast of North America, and their population has grown. What might have been different if the Russians and the Aleut had shared public space fairly? Where in your community is there a debate over public land? How should such debates be handled?

title: Saint Genevieve
text:
Saint Genevieve is Missouri's oldest city. The city was the first permanent European settlement in Missouri. It is located on the Mississippi River in Ste. Genevieve County, about 60 miles south of St. Louis. Ste. Genevieve was settled around 1735 and has a very rich history. The French first settled here because of the salty water found in the springs on Saline Creek. The French used this salty water to keep their food from going bad and to help preserve their animal skins.

Settlers also came to Ste. Genevieve for the rich farming soil. By 1788, Americans began moving to Ste.Genevieve. They had heard about the fine farmland here and wanted to see it for themselves. When America bought Missouri from France as part of the Louisiana Purchase in 1803, more Americans than ever before began settling in Ste. Genevieve. The Ste. Genevieve Museum has many interesting exhibits that teach about the early history of the area. The museum has prehistoric American Indian items, old papers and things used long ago by the people of Ste. Genevieve. There are also beautifully restored French homes, built as early as 1784. Tours are given of both the outside and inside of these historic buildings. The Bolduc House and the Felix Valle House are both great examples of the types of houses that the early settlers once built.

The citizens of Ste. Genevieve enjoy celebrating their French heritage with many festivals and events throughout the year. The King's Ball has been held each February for nearly 300 years and is still held today. A Spring House Tour is open to the public each year, and La Fete Francaise, a festival with French food and entertainment, is also held in the spring. Bastille Day is celebrated in July, and Jour de Fete, one of the largest craft fairs in Missouri, happens every August. Fall Harvest is celebrated in October, and a Christmas Walk is held each December.

Ste. Genevieve is a beautiful city that preserves some of Missouri's earliest history.

title: Early Missouri Communities
text:
When settlers first started coming to Missouri, it was at the edge of the frontier. A frontier is the end of the settled part of a country and the beginning of the unsettled area. After America bought the Louisiana Purchase from France, many people were excited about moving west. Missouri became a very busy and interesting place for settlers and for those who were getting ready to go west. This week, we will find out more about some of Missouri's early communities. See if you can find out why each community was settled, how it was the same as where you live now, and how it was different from your community today.

St. Louis

Missouri's second oldest city is the city of St. Louis. St. Louis was settled in 1764 by a French merchant named Pierre Laclede. Laclede and his partner planned to set up a trading post, and Laclede chose this spot on the Mississippi River to build their settlement. Laclede sent his 14-year-old clerk, Auguste Chouteu, to the spot to clear the land and build the first buildings of the settlement. Chouteu brought 30 workers with him and supervised them in the building of the town of St. Louis. St. Louis later became a great fur-trading center and, even later, the Gateway to the West. St. Louis is still one of America's oldest and most important cities.

Franklin

Franklin was once the great "jumping off point" for the Santa Fe Trail. Many pioneers who were heading west started their trip in Franklin. They came here to buy supplies before heading out on the Santa Fe Trail. Franklin was a wild and lawless town, where drinking, gambling and fighting were a way of life. The town also made much money building and selling wagons. Farmers got rich selling their crops to hotels and restaurants and to people who were ready to head out on the trail.

In 1828, the Missouri River flooded and washed the town of Franklin away. Missouri's "jumping off point" was moved to the city of Independence.

St. Joseph

St. Joseph is found on the Missouri River along the western border of our state. St. Joseph is famous for being one of the "jumping off" points for the trip west and for being the home of the Pony Express. It was founded in 1826 by Joseph Robidoux and was incorporated as a city in 1843. The Pony Express was a way of getting mail across the country in record time. Young riders would saddle up their horses and ride from St. Joseph, Missouri, to San Francisco, California, in 8-10 days. The mail normally took at least 25 days to travel this far!

When the railroad came to St. Joseph, the city also became a popular spot for people to catch a train heading west. There were beautiful hotels and fancy restaurants in St. Joseph to take care of the needs of these travelers.

St. Charles

In 1821, St. Charles was chosen as the first capital of the state of Missouri. At the time, St. Charles was at the center of the state, and people thought that this was the best spot for the center of the government.

St. Charles also became the center of education for young women in Missouri. Mary Easton Sibley, the wife of a successful businessman, decided that it was time the young women of Missouri had a chance to go to school, just like the boys. She began teaching young women in her home in St. Charles. As the school grew, she and her husband, George, built Lindenwood University, a school for young women. Today, Lindenwood College still stands in St. Charles, but both girls and boys now go to this school.

title: Montreal, Quebec, Canada
text:
The famous French explorer Jacques Cartier arrived in what is now Montreal in 1535. About 100 years later, in May of 1642, the first French settlers came to Montreal. They shot guns to scare away any evil spirits that might already be living here and dedicated the island to the Virgin Mary. They named the spot "Ville-Marie," or the City of Mary. Over the years, Montreal was controlled by France, England and even the United States. Today, Montreal is part of the country of Canada.

Montreal has some neighborhoods in which most people speak French, and some neighborhoods in which most people speak English. There are strict laws about which languages can be used in business, in government and in schools. Many people have very strong feelings about which language should be used.

Today, Montreal is a famous meeting place for people from countries all over the world. Many conventions, or meetings of large groups of people, are held in Montreal each year. The city makes money from its airport, hotels, restaurants, convention centers and shopping malls.

title: Daniel Boone
text:
"I have never been lost, but I will admit to being confused for several weeks." - Daniel Boone

Born near Reading, Pennsylvania, Daniel was one of the greatest American trailblazers of all time. A trailblazer is someone who goes first and makes a path for others to follow.

In 1769, a friend of Daniel's named John Findley asked him to help him blaze a trail to Kentucky. Boone, Findley, and five other men set out along the small trails and pathways leading through the Cumberland Gap in the Appalachian Mountains into Kentucky. They found a "hunter's paradise" filled with buffalo, deer, wild turkey and meadows that were perfect for farming. Daniel was so excited about this new land that he promised to bring his family back here to live.

A few years later, Daniel and 30 other woodsmen (men who lived in the wilderness and knew about the land) were hired to build what became known as the "Wilderness Road" into the heart of Kentucky. By 1775, Daniel had built a fort and a small town called Boonesborough. He soon moved his family here to live. When Kentucky became part of the United States, Daniel lost all his land. His son, Daniel Morgan Boone, had moved to St. Charles, Missouri, and he invited his parents to come and live there. Daniel and his wife Rebecca went to Missouri, where Daniel became a judge. Daniel died in Missouri, but his body was later buried in Kentucky, the "hunter's paradise" that he loved so much.

title: The Steamboat
text:
In 1787, John Fitch showed the first working steamboat to a crowd gathered near the Delaware River in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The first steamboat was 45 feet long and was pushed along by a steam engine that turned 12 paddles. When these paddles turned, the boat moved along the river.

In 1807, Robert Fulton created the first steamboat that could carry passengers and freight (a load of goods). His first steamboat, called the Clermont, traveled from New York Harbor, up the Hudson River, to Albany and back. Many people thought that the steamboat would fail, and they were surprised when it was a success.

The steamboat made life much easier for people living near the rivers. It could bring people and goods up and down the rivers much more quickly than a wagon could bring them on land. It was also cheaper to travel by steamboat than by wagon. The invention of the steamboat helped Americans settle in new towns all over the country.

title: George Washington
text:
"First in war, first in peace and first in the hearts of his countrymen." - Henry Lee George Washington was born in Westmoreland, Virginia, in 1732. His father died in 1743, and George went to live with his half brother, Lawrence, at Mount Vernon.

George wanted to be a sailor, but became a surveyor (someone who measures and marks the land) instead. After surveying for a short time, George joined the army and became a lieutenant colonel. He was only 22 years old, but he learned quickly and did very well. By 1755, George became a colonel and then the commander-in-chief of the Virginia militia (small army). George decided to quit the army for a while and began serving in the Virginia House of Burgesses.

When the Revolutionary War started, George was chosen as the commander-in-chief of the Continental Army. He was a great leader and helped the United States win its independence from England. His men loved him and respected him for his honesty and his leadership skills.

After the war ended, George served as president of the convention that wrote the U.S. Constitution, the paper that tells how our country should be run. He was later elected as the first president of the United States. Because he was our first president, he is often called "The Father of Our Country."

title: Athens, Greece
text:
Athens is a large city in the country of Greece. In Athens, the men are the leaders, both at home and in the government. The most important job of the women is still to take care of the home and raise the children. The men go to work and make money to take care of the family.

After work, Greek men usually meet at their favorite coffee houses to have some refreshments and visit with their friends. The women often get together with their friends as well. They go to church activities, let their children play together, join together to cook a meal or just visit.

Men are in charge of the money in the family. The women are in charge of the home and the children. Many women now have jobs and work outside their homes, but it is still the woman's job to run the household and raise the children. Women also have the right to own land, vote, hold jobs and speak out in public, just like women in the United States.

title: The Job of a Museum Director: ‘A Little Bit of Everything’
text:
The Campbell House Museum is a beautiful Civil War-era home in St. Louis, Missouri. The wealthy Campbell family lived there from 1854 to 1938. Studies Weekly asked Andrew Hahn, the director of the museum, about his job.

SW: How is a house museum different from other types of museums?

AH: A house museum is different because it gives you an opportunity to get the full experience of the past. If you go to an art museum, you can see paintings from the past that may tell a story about history or a particular event. But when you come to a house museum, you get the full picture of what it was like to live in the past. When people come here, they get to experience what it was like to be welcomed into the house or to work in the house. The house was so well preserved, and the Campbells' collection is still here. This is their house and how they lived in it.

SW: What does a museum director do?

AH: I do a little bit of everything. We have to raise money so that we can keep the doors open and pay the utility bills. I write the checks for all the bills, and I organize our volunteers who do most of the work at the house. We do research, so I look into the Campbell story and read old documents and newspapers that tell stories about the past. I even take out the trash!

title: St. Charles
text:
Before Missouri became a state, many different cities hoped that they would be chosen as the capital of the Missouri Territory. The leaders of Missouri agreed that the permanent capital should be in the center of Missouri, but it would take some time to build the capitol building. While the capitol was being built in Jefferson City, St. Charles was chosen to serve as the temporary capital of Missouri.

St. Charles was a good place for the first capital. St. Charles is found on the Missouri River at the end of Boonslick Road, so it was easy to get to both by boat and by wagon. A building owned by some St. Charles businessmen became the temporary capitol building. The second floor was divided into different sections to be used by the Senate, the House of Representatives, the governor and different committee groups.

Today, the original capitol building has been restored to look as it did in the 1800s. Visitors to St. Charles can now take a tour of the historic building. St. Charles was also the spot where the explorers Lewis and Clark met to start their famous journey to explore the West. Each year, St. Charles holds a special celebration to remember Lewis and Clark. People come from miles around to enjoy the excitement. Everyone gathers near the river, and tents are set up with foods, crafts and games from the 1800s. Cannons and muskets are fired, military groups raise and lower the flag and drummers and buglers perform each day. Today, St. Charles is a busy city of more than 60,000 people. St. Charles is the county seat of the fastest-growing county in Missouri. St. Charles is a great place to go to see what Missouri was like before it became a state!

title: Joplin Works to Rebuild After a Deadly Tornado
text:
On May 22, 2011, a tornado hit the city of Joplin, Missouri. It wasn't just any tornado. It was a monstrous EF-5, with winds over 200 miles an hour. This huge tornado was almost a mile wide and cut a path over 22 miles long. It crushed almost 1/3 of the city, killed 162 people and destroyed almost 8,000 buildings. It is considered one of the deadliest tornadoes in over 50 years.

Joplin is working hard to rebuild. Think about all of the parts that make a city work. In addition to houses and businesses, cities need electricity, sewers, roads, hospitals, parks and government buildings. In January 2012 federal and civic organizations in Joplin got together to give the "ok" to a plan called Joplin Area - Next Steps Plan. The plan outlined how to replace what was destroyed in the tornado. 4,000 building permits have been given to homeowners so they can begin construction on new homes. After the tornado hit, 530 businesses were either destroyed or badly damaged. The good news is that 420 of those businesses have reopened. Work has begun on a new hospital. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is helping to clean up waste and keep the area safe for residents.

The people of Joplin will never forget that terrible day. Recovering from something this devastating is difficult, but Joplin is showing how it's done!

title: Studying History
text:
As we study the history of Missouri, America and the world, we find that there are many things to think about. Have you ever wondered how we know what happened long ago? Or why things happened in the order they did? Or why people see the same event in different ways? This week, we will be learning how to find out what happened in the past, how to organize these events and why different people see the same event in different ways.

Thinking "Chronologically"

When we study history, it is important for us to be able to ask, "What happened first?" "What happened next?" and "What happened last?"

Putting events in order of when they happened is called organizing them chronologically. Chronological order is a lot like ABC order. Only instead of organizing a list of words by which letter they start with, you organize a list of events in order from which happened first to which happened last.

Using a timeline makes it easy to see which things happened first and happened later. A timeline is a list of events, starting with the first and ending with the last.

Look at the timeline below. It shows the main events that happened during the Civil War. You will see that the timeline is in chronological order, with the events that caused the war at the beginning and the surrender of the South at the end.

Primary or Secondary

When we try to find out what happened in the past, we need to look in many different places. We can read journals, letters and reports. We can also look at pictures, read books, watch movies and listen to people tell about their experiences. All these different places to get information are called sources.

Each of these sources can be put into one of two groups: primary sources and secondary sources. Primary sources are actual records that have survived from the past, such as letters, journals, photographs and articles of clothing. Primary sources come from people who actually lived through an event. "Primary" means "first," or "main," so primary sources are usually the first places we should research when trying to find out what happened.

Secondary sources are created sometime after an event has happened by people who weren't actually there. "Secondary" means "less important," or "coming later," so we usually look at secondary sources after we have already looked at the primary sources first. Some secondary sources are textbooks, history books, research papers and movies.

Both primary and secondary sources are good places to look for information when we are studying the past.

Point of View

When we study history, we also notice that our sources don't always agree on what happened, why it happened, or why it is important. If two people were part of the same event in history, how could they tell different stories about this event?

Each person who tells a story has a different point of view about what happened. Point of view is the way that a person sees things.

When we study the Civil War, we notice that those in the North had a different point of view from those in the South. We also see that those who owned slaves had a different point of view from those who were held as slaves.

If this seems strange to you at first, think about your life today. Do you have a different point of view about some things than your parents? Do you think you have a different point of view about what happened on September 11 than someone who lives in Africa, Afghanistan or France? Do you think that you see the Civil War differently than a child who actually lived through it?

When we read what different people have written about things that happened in the past, we need to look at what their point of view was. Then we can understand the things they say.

title: Chihuahua, Mexico
text:
Chihuahua is the capital of the state of Chihuahua, Mexico. Chihuahua is in the northern part of Mexico, in a little valley surrounded by hills.

Chihuahua is known for playing a part in many of the changes that have happened in Mexico's government over the years. During the Revolution of 1810, Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, a famous priest who fought against the government, was put in prison in Chihuahua. The brave priest was held for 98 days and was fed only bread and water. He was later executed, or killed, for trying to get rid of the Mexican government. The night before he was executed, he wrote a poem on his cell wall thanking his guard for being so kind to him. Today, a flame is kept burning on the patio of the Government Palace to remind those who visit of the price Hidalgo y Costilla paid for their liberty.

Chihuahua was also part of another Mexican revolution, fought more than 100 years later. The famous bandit Pancho Villa fought to get rid of a government that he felt treated the people unfairly. He had a home in Chihuahua where he often hid from the Mexican army. The mansion still stands, and many visitors tour here. The car that Pancho Villa was in when he was shot to death is also on display.

Chihuahua is a city where visitors can see the past and the present, all at the same time!

title: Kit Carson
text:
Christopher Houston "Kit" Carson was born on Christmas Eve 1809. He spent most of his young life in Boone's Lick, Missouri. When he was only nine years old, his father died, and he had to work to survive. He was apprenticed (sent to work for someone so that he could learn to do his job) to a saddle maker in Franklin when he was 14 years old. But he hated the job. He ran away to Independence with hopes of joining in the excitement of the western frontier. When Carson got to Independence, he was thrilled to find traders and frontiersmen who told him exciting stories about Santa Fe. Santa Fe was a Spanish settlement located in what is now the state of New Mexico. Because Carson had run away from his job and had no education, he decided to join a wagon train and find out for himself what Santa Fe was like.

After going west, Kit Carson became a fur trapper. He got to know the West so well that he started working as a guide for others who wanted to come here. A guide is someone who shows others the way. Kit Carson was hired by the famous explorer John C. Fremont and helped guide him in his explorations through Oregon, California, the Central Rocky Mountains and the Great Basin. Kit Carson was a great western pioneer who became famous for his exciting adventures on the wild frontier. People still remember the famous trapper, explorer and guide from Franklin, Missouri, who ran away to explore the West.

title: The Sewing Machine
text:
Can you imagine having to sew all of your own clothes with just a needle and thread? Before the invention of the sewing machine, that is exactly what clothing makers had to do.

In 1755, an American inventor named Charles T. Wiesenthal designed a double-pointed needle, with a sharp point on each end, to make sewing faster. In 1830, a Frenchman named Barthelemy Thimonnier used this double-pointed needle to make the first sewing machine. He attached the needle to a rod connected to a wheel. When the wheel turned, the needle went up and down, sewing stitches.

By 1846, Elias Howe, an American inventor, had figured out how to make the first lockstitch sewing machine. This machine pulled the stitches tight so that they didn't come loose later. It was used in clothing factories to make sewing faster and easier.

In 1851, Isaac Merritt Singer, a Boston machine maker, built the first small sewing machine that could be used at home. He made it easy for people to have their very own sewing machines for making their own clothes at home. The Singer Sewing Machine Company went on to become the world's largest maker of home sewing machines. Just think of all the time, money and energy saved by the invention of the sewing machine!

title: Jonas Salk
text:
Jonas Salk was born in New York City in 1914. After graduating from medical school, he became a professor of epidemiology (the study of diseases and how to control them) at the University of Michigan. He later began teaching at the University of Pittsburgh, where he made the first polio vaccine. Polio is a disease that attacks the nervous system, often leaving its victims paralyzed. A vaccine is a special medicine that keeps people from getting certain diseases. The polio vaccine was first given to children in 1953, and it turned out to be a great success. Today, babies and children regularly get the polio vaccine to protect them from this terrible disease.

In 1963 Dr. Salk built the Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California, to study diseases and ways to stop them. He left his home in Pittsburgh and spent the next 30 years in the San Diego area trying to find ways to protect people from contagious illnesses, or sicknesses that can be passed from person to person. He died in 1995.

Dr. Jonas Salk made the world a better place by fighting the germs that make us sick.

title: Kansas City
text:
Kansas City is the largest city in Missouri. Its nickname is "The Heart of America" for a couple of reasons. First, Kansas City is at nearly the exact center of the North American continent. That makes it the "heart" of America. Next, Kansas City is also the point where many forms of transportation come together and the place where many people meet as they come and go. Many great and important railways, waterways and freeways meet in Kansas City. So it is the "heart" of American transportation (something that carries people or things from place to place) as well.

Kansas City was named after the Kansa Indians, who once lived in the area. The people who settled the city first called it "Westport," then "Kansas," then "the City of Kansas," and finally "Kansas City."

Kansas City straddles (stands on) both sides of the Missouri River, so there are many bridges connecting the two parts of the city. Kansas City also has many beautiful parks and fountains. In fact, those who live here say that Kansas City has more fountains than any city except Rome, Italy.

Kansas City can have very interesting weather. It is very hot and humid in summer, but the fall weather is mild and comfortable. Winter can bring blizzards and cold temperatures, and spring usually brings one or two tornadoes per year to the Kansas City area.

Kansas City is the center for many types of businesses. It has huge grain silos that ship grain all over the world. Kansas City also has flour mills, livestock (cattle, horses, sheep and hogs) markets, steel plants, motor-vehicle assembly plants, oil refineries and printing and publishing companies.

Jazz music has also had a home in Kansas City since the 1920s. Famous jazz musicians like Scott Joplin, Charlie Parker and Count Basie all came from Kansas City.

When you visit Kansas City, be sure to see the Historic Union Train Station, the Union Cemetery and the Vietnam Veterans' Memorial.

title: Fake or Real News?
text:
Have you ever read something online, like on social media sites, that sounded fishy? Maybe it was real, but it could be fake news! The big danger, though, is news that sounds real but isn’t. Fake news is becoming common because anyone can post things online. Fake news can be in the form of a story. Fake news can be a photo or video that has been changed. The problem is that these fake items look real. Fake news can cause problems and it spreads misinformation.

Sam Wineburg, a professor, did some research. He found that 80 percent of students cannot tell the difference between real and fake news. Do you want to become a media-savvy person? You have to be able to find out if news is real or fake. How do you do that? You have to become a detective and search for the truth. You can learn about the author or company that posted the news. You have to think about the purpose of the news. Is there a hidden plan to get you to buy something or to make you think a certain way? Your teacher or a trusted adult can help you learn how to spot fake news. It takes a little time, but democracy depends on real information! Do your part and discover what is real and what is fake!

title: Chandigarh, India
text:
Families who live in Chandigarh, India, enjoy spending time together, just like we do here in the United States. There are some differences between Indian and American families, though. Many parents in the United States pitch in and do the housework together, but not in India.

In India, the mother is almost completely in charge of everything around the house. She takes care of cooking, cleaning, shopping and anything else that must be done to keep the household running. The father doesn't get involved in these chores.

The job of the father in India is to support the family by earning money. Most dads in India believe that their work on the job is the most important thing in their lives. When they come home at night, however, they leave their work at work and enjoy spending quiet time with their families. They don't bring their work home with them like many American fathers do.

They also spend a lot of time talking to their children and learning how their children feel about things. Indian fathers see themselves as the head of the family, and they try to stay connected to their children.

title: Santiago, Chile
text:
Santiago is the capital of the South American country of Chile. The city is the center of the country's economy, or money-making activities.

Chile has one of the best economies in South America. The country has a great climate for growing many types of fruits and vegetables, especially grapes. Some of the grapes grown in Chile are made into wine, but most of them are shipped to North America as table grapes, or grapes to be eaten fresh. Chile's grapes get ripe just in time for Christmas, so most of the grapes we eat over the holidays come from here.

Chile also makes money by selling fish, wheat, potatoes, corn, sugar, beets, onions, beans, copper, wood and clothes to countries all over the world. The country uses its natural resources, like a good climate and rich soil, to help produce things that it can sell to make money. Santiago, Chile, is a good example of a city that uses what it has to get what it needs.

title: J.C. Hall
text:
Joyce C. Hall was a man who never liked his first name because everyone thought it was a girl's name. Because of this, he went by his initials, J.C., when he got older.

When J.C. was only 18 years old, he took $3,500 that he had saved and went to Kansas City to start his own business selling picture postcards. He had heard that Kansas City was a good place to start a business because it had hardworking people and because it had many railroads to use for shipping goods. J.C.'s brothers soon joined him in Kansas City, and the Hall Brothers Company was on its way. The Halls were some of the first people in the greeting card business to offer cards and envelopes sold together. J.C. made sure that all his cards were the best that could be made. This is the reason he chose the slogan (a catchy sentence to help people remember a company) "When you care enough to send the very best" for his company.

Hallmark Cards is now the world's largest greeting card company with its headquarters located in the Crown Center in Kansas City, Missouri. Besides greeting cards, Hallmark also makes picture albums, ornaments, gift wrap, party supplies, art supplies and crayons. Hallmark Entertainment also produces television specials and videos.

title: The Typewriter
text: Christopher Sholes invented the typewriter in 1867. He was a printer who believed that it would make life much easier for people who did a lot of writing if they had a machine to help them. Christopher built the first typewriter using keys attached to metal letters. When someone struck the keys with their fingers, the typewriter printed the letters on a piece of paper. The keys were arranged in alphabetical order, but this arrangement didn't work out very well. When the keys were struck, they often jammed together because many of the keys used most often were too close together. James Densmore, a friend of Christopher, suggested splitting the keys so that the keys used most often were mixed in with the keys that weren't used as much. The two men built a new typewriter with the keyboard arranged as it is today, and the problem of jammed keys was solved. After the invention of the computer, most people stopped using the typewriter, but we still use the same "QWERTY" letter arrangement on our computer keyboards today.

title: Sam Walton
text:
Sam Walton, the founder of Wal-Mart, believed that "individuals don't win, teams do." Born in Oklahoma in 1918, Walton went on to build a team that made him the second richest man in the world.

After graduating from college in 1940, Sam Walton began running a variety store, and in 1962, he opened the very first Wal-Mart in Rogers, Arkansas.

Sam Walton believed in offering his customers name-brand products at low prices and found that customers loved the idea. He didn't keep all the profits (money leftover when all the store's bills were paid) for himself when the company did well. Instead, he passed the savings along to the customer by cutting the prices of his products. He also gave his employees stock (shares, or part ownership) in the company so that they could make money when the store did well.

Wal-Mart is now the largest retail store in the world. Sam Walton's desire to share the money his stores made with his customers, as well as his employees, helped make him one of the most successful businessmen in the world.

title: Using Our Resources
text: Draw a picture of how you use our natural resources. You could be a farmer using the land, a miner searching for gold, a banker or a teacher. How are you going to use our natural resources to bring in capital to our state? Draw it for us!

title: Our Resources
text:
This week, we will be learning about the economy of our state. The economy of a community is its ability to earn money by using its resources. Resources are things that are found in a community that can be used to make money, or capital. We will learn about natural, human and capital resources and how people use them to get the things they need and want.

Natural Resources

Natural resources are the riches that are found naturally in an area. These riches include land, forests, mineral deposits, water and wildlife.

Human Resources

Human resources are the people who live in an area. The people who live in a community may be the most important resource of all. Without human resources, natural resources would be of no use. It takes people to plant and harvest crops, dig ditches and move water, break rocks to mine minerals, and sail the oceans and rivers to catch fish. Human resources, or people, choose what to do with the natural resources found in a community.

Capital Resources

Capital resources are the riches and wealth that people own. This capital can be land, jewelry, factories or anything that is valuable and could be sold. People use their capital resources to buy the things they need and to make changes that will help them to earn even more capital. The more capital a person, business or community has, the more they can do with their natural and human resources.

Using Our Resources

Most of Missouri's early settlers were farmers. They came to Missouri and used its great natural resources of good soil, plenty of rain and pleasant sunshine to help them grow good crops. Missouri's early farmers also used their own capital resources, or money, to buy seeds, tools and farm equipment. They also put in plenty of their own human resources, or strength, clearing and plowing the land, planting their seeds and harvesting their crops. By using all these resources, Missouri's first farmers could raise enough food to keep themselves alive and to make some money as well.

Today, Missouri farmers still use these same resources to raise crops and make money to support their families. Missouri raises and sells soybeans, corn, cattle, hogs, wheat and dairy products. In fact, Missouri has more farms than all other states except Texas! Missouri also uses its natural, capital and human resources to make cars and trucks, vending machines and airplanes and to mine (dig out of the Earth) lead, coal and zinc. We also use our resources to entertain tourists. Missouri has built hotels, theaters and amusement parks to make money from tourists who come here to enjoy our great state.

People chose to settle in Missouri because it had the natural resources they needed to survive. They built communities in places that had good soil, plenty of water, and a mild climate. Communities that had what people needed to live well continued to grow and succeed. Today, our Missouri communities use their natural, human and capital resources to make money and get the things they need and want.

title: Springfield
text:
Springfield is located in southwestern Missouri in Greene County. It is Missouri's third-largest city and has become quite a tourist attraction in the last few years. It has gentle mountains, green forests, blue lakes and clear streams that make it a place people love to come and see.

Springfield is also home to many large companies. Famous companies like Kraft Foods, 3M, Bass Pro Shops, MCI Worldcom, Springfield Remanufacturing, General Electric and Reckitt Benckiser all have large factories here in Springfield, giving jobs to many people who live here.

Springfield has many exciting and interesting places to visit. One popular tourist site is Fantastic Caverns, a cave that allows visitors to ride rather than walk through on a 50-minute tour. Tourists ride through an ancient underground river bed in train-like cars, viewing the cave formations from their seats as they ride by.

Another interesting place to see in the Springfield area is the Laura Ingalls Wilder Museum and Home. This is the home where the "Little House" books were written. The museum also has family pictures, Pa's fiddle, Laura's handwritten manuscripts (handwritten original copies) of her books and other interesting family items. If you have ever read any of the "Little House" books, you will enjoy your visit to this historic location.

If you like animals, Springfield has a place for you, too. Wild Animal Safari is a drive-through animal park where visitors can drive through more than 400 acres of wild animals and birds in their own natural habitats. There are more than 3,000 wild animals including bears, lions, kangaroos and exotic birds that can be seen from the comfort of your own car. The park is an amazing sight for anyone who enjoys animals.

Springfield has many other things to see and do. If you feel like seeing more of our beautiful state, be sure to put Springfield on your list!

title: What a Piggy Bank!
text:
Do you have a piggy bank at home? How much money do you think is in someone's piggy bank? If you think a few dollars worth of coins might be hiding inside one of these, then hold onto your hats.

A type of Viking piggy bank called a bucket has been found on the Swedish Island of Gotland in the Baltic Sea. An archaeologist found it using a metal detector. Other treasures from Viking times had been found on the island, including a treasure of almost 6,000 coins discovered during the 1880s. Well, when people know treasure could be buried somewhere, then they hunt for themselves! The Gotland county administrative board decided that they had better find whatever Viking treasure might still be on the island before treasure hunters looted any more of it. What they found has been described as "fantastic" by Swedish archaeologists.

Buried about 12 inches under the ground, they found a bronze bucket from the Viking era filled to the brim with silver coins. The bucket is about 9 inches wide by 7 inches deep archaeologists think it contains thousands of coins. They think the coins were probably minted in Germany between A.D. 1000 and 1040. The archaeologists estimate that just one of the coins could be worth hundreds of U.S. dollars. The scientists plan to study the treasure even more to unravel more secrets from the past!

title: Using Our Resources
text:
Have you ever wanted something that you just couldn't have? Maybe you were at a picnic and wanted a glass of lemonade, but your little sister just drank the last glass. What did you do? You may not have been able to drink lemonade, but you had other choices about what to do. You could drink root beer or water or even go without. When there isn't enough of something to go around, we have to look at other ways to get what we need and want.

Scarcity

When we say that something is scarce, we mean that there isn't much of it or that it can't always be found. When we want something that there just isn't much of, we face the problem of scarcity, or not having enough of something to go around.

If you love watermelon and want to eat it all year, you may find that there are times when watermelon is scarce, or that you have a hard time finding it in the store. Because watermelon grows well during the summer season, you can probably find it then without a problem. But if you try to buy it in December, you may not be able to find it at all. If you do happen to find a watermelon, you will probably have to pay a very high price for it because it is scarce, or hard to come by.

Choice

When you find that you can't get what you want, what choices must you make? If you can't find watermelon, you must choose to eat something else. If you find watermelon at the store in December, but it costs more money than you want to spend, you must decide how much you really want to eat watermelon. If you only have a certain amount of money to spend on food, you must decide if you are willing to give up buying other foods so that you can have the expensive watermelon.

Opportunity Costs

When you make a decision about what you will buy, you not only choose to buy the watermelon, but you also choose NOT to buy something else. The same is true about nearly any choice you make. If you choose to read a "Harry Potter" book, you also choose NOT to read another book until later. If you choose to go swimming with your friends, you also choose NOT to go to a movie with your brother, if he is going at the same time.

When we make choices, we need to look at what we are choosing, but also at what we are choosing to give up. When we choose one thing, we also choose to give up the next best choice. This is called opportunity cost. We give up the opportunity, or chance, to do one thing when we choose to do another.

Conserving Our Resources

Making choices about how to use what we have doesn't only apply to money. We must also make important choices about how to use our resources. For example, if our state has a certain amount of water, we must make decisions about where this water will be used. Should it be put into reservoirs and used to make power? Or should it be put in canals to be used by farmers?

Should our trees be cut down for lumber to bring money into our state? Or should they be left alone to keep the landscape beautiful and keep the air fresh? Should we cut some down and leave others alone?

People who help run our state must make important decisions like this each year. They must look at what we have and make decisions based on what they will give up by making each choice. Keeping these opportunity costs in mind helps our leaders make wise decisions about how to use our resources.

1. You have to decide whether you're willing to pay the high price, or choose to buy something else.

2. Watermelons are scarce during the winter, so in order to get some, you may have to pay a high price.

3. When you choose to buy watermelon you also choose not to buy something else. This is called opportunity cost.

title: How to Make a Five-Pointed Star
text:
A five-pointed star is a symbol of our flag and nation. There is one star for each state on our flag.

Materials

Square Paper

Scissors

Directions

1. To make a five-pointed star, start by folding a square piece of paper in half as shown. To find the center, fold lightly in half (flap A to flap B) and unfold.

2. Next, use the found center as a pivot point and fold A over B as shown. The way to tell if you are folding the correct angle is to look at the flap on A. It should be twice as big as the B flap that is showing.

3. Fold B back over A. Now fold the piece with flaps A and B over the C section.

4. Cut at an angle on the dotted line as shown. Open it up, and the result will be a perfect five-pointed star.

Extra Activity: You can decorate your stars and use them to add some life to your classroom at school bedroom at home.

title: Cairo, Egypt
text:
Cairo is the largest city in the Middle East and Africa. There are more than 60 million people living on only 3 percent of Egypt's land.

Cairo is an important trade city. Cairo uses the Nile River to move goods and supplies from place to place easily and quickly. The city was also the spot where the first railroad in Africa was built. The railroad connected Cairo to Alexandria.

Today, Cairo has a busy airport and many railroads and highways. Cairo makes most of its money by selling goods to other countries. Cairo grows and sells food products, tobacco and cotton to countries around the world. The city also sells chemicals, plastics, metals and cloth. The main countries that trade with Cairo are the United States, Italy, France, Greece, Germany, England and Japan.

One of Cairo's biggest problems today is its huge population growth. There are so many people living here that getting enough water for everyone is becoming a real worry. It is also very difficult to get from place to place within the city. More than 15 million people travel to the center of the city each morning to go to work. This kind of crowd is very hard to manage! By planning ahead and working together, the city of Cairo hopes to solve the problems that come with so many people living in one place.

title: George Washington Carver
text:
George was born a slave in 1864 in Diamond Grove, Missouri, and was raised by his owners, Moses and Susan Carver. George's father had died in an accident soon after George was born, and his mother was kidnapped. When the slaves were freed in 1865, the Carvers continued to raise George and care for him. They taught him to read and write. And when he turned 11 years old, they sent him to a school for African American children in Neosho.

After George graduated from college, Booker T. Washington asked George to go to the Tuskegee Institute to teach school. The Tuskegee Institute is an agricultural college (a college that teaches people how to farm and care for animals) for African Americans. George moved to Alabama, where the school was located, and soon became head of the Tuskegee agricultural department.

Around 1914, George began doing research on the peanut. He figured out how to make more than 300 products from the peanut, including a milk substitute, face powder, printer's ink and soap. George Washington Carver is still remembered today for his research on peanuts.

George never married, but spent most of his money trying to help young African American students have the chance to go to school. He is a great example of someone who worked hard and overcame great odds to find success.

title: Blue Jeans
text:
Levi Strauss was a man who sold fabric, or cloth. When he decided to head West during the California Gold Rush, he brought a few bolts of cloth with him to sell to people along the way. By the time he reached the gold fields of California, he had sold all of his cloth except a roll of canvas, a heavy cloth used for making wagon covers and tents.

Levi Strauss found that the miners who spent their days digging and panning for gold wore their pants out very quickly. They wanted work pants that wouldn't wear out in just a few weeks. Levi Strauss looked at the roll of canvas and had a great idea - he would make pants for the miners out of the heavy cloth!

Soon, miners began flocking to Levi, asking him to make pants for them. When he ran out of canvas, Levi started using a new kind of cloth from Italy called "genes." Levi changed the spelling to "jeans," and the first blue jeans were born. Later, rivets (small metal fasteners) were added at the pockets to keep them from ripping. Today, the popular pants are worn by men, women and children all over the world.

title: Abraham Lincoln
text:
Abraham Lincoln was born on Feb. 12, 1809, in a log cabin in Kentucky. He had less than a year of formal schooling, but went on to become the president of the United States.

Lincoln is known as one of the nation's greatest presidents. He saved the United States from being permanently torn apart during the Civil War. He also signed the famous Emancipation Proclamation, a law that freed the slaves in the Confederate states.

Lincoln was very kind to the South after they lost the Civil War and promised that he would do his best to bring the nation back together again. Lincoln didn't get the chance to do as he had promised. This is because he was assassinated, or killed because of his beliefs. He was shot on April 14, 1865, while watching a play at Ford's Theater in Washington, D.C., and died the next day.

Abraham Lincoln, often called "Honest Abe," was a leader who used humor, good judgment and kindness to guide the United States through very difficult times.
