En los años 1770, antes de asistir al Segundo Congreso Continental, Mason escribió la Declaración de Derechos de Virginia. En este documento se describían los derechos de la gente. Tuvo influencia en el contenido de la Declaración de Independencia.

Cuando se comenzó a escribir la Constitución, Mason estaba preocupado porque no se había incluido una lista de derechos garantizados en el nuevo documento. Mason era antifederalista. Estaba preocupado porque pensaba que el nuevo gobierno tenía demasiado poder por sobre los estados. Cuando los delegados votaron para aceptar la nueva Constitución sin una declaración de derechos, Mason se negó a firmar. Argumentó que los estados no debían aceptar el nuevo documento a menos que se incluyeran enmiendas para proteger los derechos individuales. Después de la aceptación, se añadió a la Constitución una declaración de derechos basada en la sugerida por Mason, que protegía los derechos de todos los estadounidenses. Esta es la misma la Carta de Derechos que tenemos hoy.

title: Elbridge Gerry
text:
Elbridge Gerry venía de una familia grande de Massachusetts con 11 hijos. Creció viendo a su padre actuar como un importante líder en la comunidad. Gerry asistió a la universidad cuando era joven. Cuanto más aprendía, más creía que estaba justificado que los colonos se resistieran a las normas injustas impuestas por el gobierno británico. Gerry sirvió en varios puestos en el gobierno local después de graduarse. Fue elegido para servir como delegado de Massachusetts en la Convención Constitucional de 1787 en Filadelfia, Pensilvania.

Como antifederalista, Gerry estaba preocupado por el documento propuesto para la Constitución. Veía varios temas que consideraba que le daban demasiado poder al gobierno nacional. Rechazó firmar el documento si no se agregaban varias enmiendas. En 1791, se agregaron las enmiendas conocidas como la Carta de Derechos.

Después de la aceptación de la Constitución, Gerry fue elegido para formar parte de la Cámara de Representantes en el nuevo Congreso. Después fue vicepresidente de James Madison desde 1812 hasta su muerte en 1814.

title: James Madison
text:
A James Madison se lo conoce como el "padre de la Constitución". Muchas de las ideas de la Constitución eran las ideas originales de Madison sobre los derechos y libertades que debían tener las personas. Nuestros derechos y responsabilidades se definen y protegen en la Constitución, gracias, en gran medida a Madison. Él era un delegado muy activo en la Convención Constituyente. Tomó notas, llevó archivos e hizo más de 150 discursos. Cuando se terminó la Constitución, James Madison sabía que le esperaba el trabajo arduo de convencer a todos los estados para que la aprueben. Trabajó junto con John Jay y Alexander Hamilton en la escritura de los Papeles Federalistas, que eran una serie de ensayos que apoyaban al nuevo gobierno. Madison escribió 29 de los 85 ensayos. Virginia fue uno de los últimos estados en ratificar la Constitución, y los ensayos de James Madison ayudaron a conseguir los votos finales.

Madison y los demás federalistas se esforzaron por mantener el sistema de controles y equilibrios entre los tres poderes del Estado y proteger los derechos de los ciudadanos. En 1789, fue elegido miembro de la Asamblea de Virginia y trabajó para crear la libertad de religión en su estado natal. Sirvió como Secretario de Estado durante la presidencia de Thomas Jefferson. En 1808, fue elegido como cuarto presidente de los Estados Unidos.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text:
Thomas Jefferson estudió muchas materias, como ciencias, arquitectura, derecho, música, historia, idiomas, astronomía y matemáticas. Creía que todos tenían el derecho a recibir educación y que todos podían aprender. Jefferson fue el autor principal de la Declaración de Independencia. Él fue uno de los primeros estadounidenses en expresar la idea de que todas las personas nacen con ciertos derechos que nunca se le pueden quitar. Sentía que la única manera de lograr su meta era crear una nación nueva e independiente. Sus ideas de "vida, libertad y búsqueda de la felicidad" influirían más tarde en los Artículos de la Confederación y en la Constitución.

Durante la Revolución estadounidense fue gobernador de Virginia. Trabajó para formar una alianza con Francia. También trabajó conjuntamente con su compañero fundador James Madison para crear la libertad e igualdad de religión en Virginia. Después de la Revolución estadounidense fue embajador en Francia. Ayudó a establecer una relación comercial entre los dos países. Aunque no estuvo presente en la Convención Constituyente, creía firmemente en la Constitución. Estaba de acuerdo en que todo el poder que no se le da al gobierno nacional le pertenece al estado o la gente.

Regresó a los Estados Unidos para servir como primer Secretario de Estado de George Washington. Fue vicepresidente de John Adams hasta que, en 1800, fue elegido presidente de los Estados Unidos.

Durante su presidencia, los Estados Unidos llegaron a tener más del doble de su territorio por la Compra de Luisiana. También trabajó muy duro para evitar la guerra de los Estados Unidos con Francia e Inglaterra. Después de su presidencia, fundó la Universidad de Virginia y vendió su colección personal de libros. Más tarde se convirtió en la Biblioteca del Congreso.

title: Europa antes de la Exploración hacia el Oeste
text:
En los años 1400, el mundo entero estaba en movimiento. El las Américas, África, Asia y Europa los imperios crecían. Los imperios fueron los patrocinadores, eso quería decir que les pagaban a las personas para estudiar, explorar o crear arte para la gloria del imperio. Este patrocinio llevó a nuevos avances en el conocimiento e intercambios de ideas a través de las rutas de intercambio. Una ruta de intercambio es una zona que usan los comerciantes por motivos económicos.

En las Américas, surgían nuevos imperios. Cerca de los Grandes Lagos, la Confederación iroquesa estaba ganando más control sobre el intercambio. El comercio se estaba expandiendo por todo el continente incluyendo lo que ahora es México y América del Sur. En América Central, estaba en expansión el Impero Azteca. Los gobernantes aztecas fueron mecenas de muchos grandes poetas. En América del Sur, estaba en expansión el Imperio Inca. Los gobernantes incas fueron mecenas de inventores que desarrollaron nuevas tecnologías para el cultivo, medicamentos y construcción de puentes. El imperio usaba estos nuevos conocimientos para aumentar el comercio y las ideas de intercambio.

Al otro lado del Océano Atlántico, en África, se estaba expandiendo el Imperio Songhai. El comercio de sal y oro a través del Sahara hizo rico al imperio. Los líderes de Songhai fueron mecenas de educación. Bajo los Songhai, miles de eruditos y estudiantes se reunían para estudiar en las famosas bibliotecas de la ciudad de Tombuctú.

En los 1400, la mayoría de la población del mundo estaba en Asia. China e India tenían las economías más importantes del mundo por su comercio. Comerciaban especias, sedas, oro y otros bienes por toda Europa. En los 1400, el Imperio Otomano crecía entre Asia y Europa. Los Otomanos ganaron rápido el control del comercio entre Asia y Europa. Los Otomanos hicieron detener el comercio con Europa.

Para los comerciantes de Europa, perder el control comercial con Asia fue difícil. Pero Portugal y España vieron una oportunidad. Estos países buscaron nuevas rutas hacia Asia a través del mar. Los patrones de Portugal esperaban ganar dinero con el comercio en África y encontrar un camino para llegar de África a Asia en barco.

Para 1490, Fernando e Isabel eran el rey y la reina de España. España acababa de terminar su guerra religiosa contra los cristianos. Habían tomado propiedades de judíos y musulmanes en España, y eso les dio la posibilidad de ser patrones muy importantes. Fernando e Isabel querían nuevas rutas de comercio y más ingresos. Solo necesitaban un método correcto y pagarle a la persona correcta para que lo intentara.

Un emprendedor llamado Cristóbal Colón tuvo una idea inusual. Pensaba navegar hacia el oeste a través del Océano Atlántico y llegar a India por ese camino. Colón estaba buscando un mecenas. Colón fue a hablar con la Reina Isabel y el Rey Fernando.

Isabel y Fernando acordaron ser los mecenas de Colón. Ellos pagaron los barcos que usó Colón. También pagaron las herramientas y la tripulación para el viaje. Colón hizo un acuerdo con Fernando e Isabel. El acuerdo decía lo que tanto España como Colón recibiría si el viaje tenía éxito. Este acuerdo aclaraba que España y Colón compartirían las ganancias de cualquier cargamento que trajera.

Colón zarpó (se subió al barco y se fue) de España en 1492. Su viaje pondría en marcha los mayores cambios en el gobierno, el conocimiento y el comercio jamás vistos en el mundo.

title: Semana 9 Pregunta guía
text: ¿Por qué exploraron los europeos?

title: La Era de los Encuentros
text:
A finales del 1400, los países de la costa del Atlántico de Europa competían entre ellos por el poder y la riqueza. Portugal era líder en exploración. En 1488, un barco de Portugal navegó hasta el extremo sur de África. Después, en 1492, España le pagó a Cristóbal Colón para que navegara hacia el Oeste por el Océano Atlántico. Colón estudió todas las posibilidades. Creía que podía llegar a India navegando hacia el Oeste. Hasta ese momento, Europa, no sabía que había más continentes entre el océano Atlántico y la India. Cuando Colón encontró tierra, pensó que había llegado a la India. Por eso fue que le llamó "indios" a las personas que encontró.

Colón trajo a Europa evidencias de su viaje. Compartió sus aventuras y se hizo famoso en Europa. Una vez que Colón y su tripulación contó lo que lo que habían aprendido en el viaje, otros exploradores los siguieron.

Portugal, Inglaterra y Francia mandaron exploradores por el Atlántico. Muchos de los primeros exploradores creían que llegaban a Asia. En 1503, un explorador llamado Américo Vespucio se convención de que la tierra que estaba explorando era otro continente. Américo Vespucio afirmaba que era un "nuevo mundo". La gente más adelante llamó a las tierras "América" en honor a su afirmación.

Los exploradores compartían información que ayudaba a otros exploradores. Colón abrió un nueva puerta a la aventura. Muchos lo siguieron y compartieron sus conocimientos.

1. Cristóbal Colón

España le pagó Cristóbal Colón para que navegara a través del Atlántico en 1492. Colón esperaba llegar a la India navegando hacia el Oeste. Pero en cambio, sus barcos llegaron al Caribe. Allí, Colón encontró a los taínos. El viaje de Colón despertó el interés de exploración en Europa y dio lugar a muchos otros viajes y colonias.

2. John Cabot

Aprendiendo de Colón, John Cabot estaba interesado en encontrar una ruta más corta a través del océano. Inglaterra patrocinó a Cabot para que navegara a través del Atlántico Norte en 1497. Cabot pensaba que había llegado a Asia, pero en realidad estaba en lo que hoy es Canadá. Su viaje demostró que había una ruta hacia el norte de las Américas. Encontró a los indígenas americanos de los Bosques del Este.

3. Pedro Álvares Cabral

En 1500, Portugal le pagó a Pedro Cabral para que llevara 13 barcos a la India para comerciar. El plan de Cabral era navegar alrededor de África, pero en el camino, sus barcos navegaron hacia adentro del Atlántico. Al tomar la dirección incorrecta Cabral llegó a las costas de América del Sur. Encontró habitantes de Tupiniquim.

4. Jacques Cartier

Francia esperaba encontrar un paso en el Noroeste para llegar al Océano Pacífico a través de América del Norte. En 1534, Francia le pagó a Jacques Cartierpor esa búsqueda. Cartier navegó río arriba por lo que hoy es Canadá. No encontró una ruta al Pacífico, pero encontró a los habitantes de Mi’kmaq y la poderosa Confederación Iroquesa. El comercio entre Francia y América del Norte empezó con los viajes de Cartier.

5. Francisco Vásquez de Coronado

A partir de 1540, Coronado dirigió una expedición para España en busca de las Siete Ciudades de Cibola, de las que se decía que estaban llenas de asombrosas riquezas a la espera de ser tomadas. En el camino, la expedición descubrió el Gran Cañón y encontró muchas aldeas de indígenas americanos, pero allí no había oro. Coronado pasó por Arizona, Nuevo México cruzó el Oeste de Texas y el Mango de Oklahoma, y luego entró en Kansas alrededor de lo que es hoy Liberal. Su viaje lo llevó por lo que es hoy Plains, Meade, Fowler, Minneola, y Dodge City.

title: Las herramientas del descubrimiento
text:
Cientos de años atrás, los exploradores viajaron por los océanos. ¿Cómo sabían dónde estaban? Los avances en tecnología, matemáticas y de medición de los años 1400 hicieron posible que se pudiera navegar largas distancias. Colón es un ejemplo del uso de buenos métodos porque fue uno de los primeros navegantes en llevar un registro detallado de su viaje.

Algunas de las herramientas que usó Colón ayudaron a la navegación celeste, es decir, usar el sol, la luna y las estrellas para encontrar una posición. Los marineros usaban un instrumento llamado astrolabio con el que apuntaban al cielo. Usando el sol durante el día y la estrella del Norte por la noche, los marineros apuntaban el indicador del astrolabio al objeto celeste (planeta o estrella) escogido, después leían un dial (marcación) para determinar su latitud. El cuadrante era otra herramienta que usaban los exploradores. El cuadrante se usaba para determinar la altitud, la altura de un punto fijo sobre el nivel del mar.

Estas herramientas permitieron avances en la cartografía o al hacer los mapas. El propósito original de los mapas no era que fueran exactos en tamaño o proporción. En cambio, mostraban quién tenía control sobre las tierras. Cuando los mapas ya mostraban las distancias exactas y otros detalles, eran más fáciles de seguir. Una vez que se inventó la imprenta fue más fácil obtener los mapas.

Incluso los nuevos barcos en los que navegó Colón ayudaron a la exploración. La carabela, un barco con proas y vigas anchas, era más pequeña, más ligera y más fácil de navegar que los barcos más antiguos. Como eran ligeras y más pequeñas también eran más rápidas. La mayoría de los barcos tienen un tipo de vela, pero las carabelas tienen dos. Al tener velas triangulares y cuadradas las carabelas pueden navegar contra el viento. También les permitía nadar por la orilla y en aguas abiertas. Aunque eran pequeñas, tenían tablas gruesas y podían transportar muchos bienes o personas.

title: Efectos de la exploración europea
text:
Los habitantes de las Américas satisfacían sus deseos y necesidades usando los recursos de la tierra que tenían a su alrededor. Tenían sociedades vibrantes y extensas rutas comerciales. Tenían arte, historia y protección para sus comunidades. Tenían gobierno y religión. Alimentaban a sus familias cazando animales y recolectando bayas, nueces y frutas. Cultivaban maíz, calabazas, judías, tomates, patatas y algunos granos. Crearon herramientas de los recursos que tenían a su alrededor. Viajaron caminando o en barco por las vías navegables.

Los europeos usaban los recursos naturales para fabricar bienes. Como los indígenas americanos, también tenían sociedades vibrantes y extensas rutas comerciales. Tenían arte, historia y protección para sus comunidades. Tenían gobierno y religión. Alimentaban a sus familias cultivando y comerciando. Los europeos domesticaban animales para tenerlos en sus granjas. Esto significa que no querían cazar para comer. Tenían caballos para trabajar en la granja y en le mercado. Cultivaban granos, trigo, avena y cebada. Los europeos desarrollaron diferentes medios de transporte. Usaban carretas y carros por tierra y barcos por el mar. Fabricaban bienes de metal y madera. Usaban muchos de sus recursos para explorar lugares nuevos a través del océano.

Cuando se encontraron estas dos sociedades, hubo consecuencias nacionales e internacionales. Los dos grupos intercambiaron ideas de diseño de herramientas y transporte. Los europeos trajeron animales domesticados, cerdos, pollos y caballos en los barcos. Los habitantes de las Américas les dieron plantas, comida y metales preciosos. Las dos culturas usaron el lenguaje de señas y los gestos para comunicarse.

La tolerancia de las diferencias entre las dos culturas podría haber incrementado los intercambios positivos. Pero, los europeos no eran tolerantes con las diferencias que encontraban. Creían que los pueblos de las Américas eran inferiores porque eran diferentes. La intolerancia causó conflictos y muchos indígenas americanos en cautiverio o muertos.

La introducción de animales domesticados en las Américas provocó un desequilibrio en el ecosistema. Soltaron los cerdos para que coman en los bosques. Cada vez hubo más cerdos hasta que agotaron la vegetación. Los otros animales que se alimentaban de esa vegetación no tenían nada para comer.

El caballo era un animal nuevo en las Américas. El caballo llegó a ser muy popular enseguida porque era una ayuda en la vida diaria de los pueblos de las Américas. Usaban caballo como transporte y para trabajar. Los caballos llegaron a ser un recurso de intercambio valioso. Los caballos se multiplicaron rápidamente. Todavía hay descendientes de estos caballos en la costa Este y en las tierras del Oeste de los Estados Unidos.

El intercambio más mortífero fue involuntario. Los europeos trajeron enfermedades con ellos. Ellos habían desarrollado inmunidad a muchas bacterias y virus a lo largo de los siglos. Los pueblos de las Américas nunca habían estado expuestos a gérmenes tan mortíferos. Viruela, tuberculosis, influenza, y otras cepas de enfermedades eran fácilmente transportadas por personas sin saberlo. Los historiadores estiman que las enfermedades mataron al 90 por ciento de la población nativa en 150 años.

title: Semana 10 Pregunta guía
text: ¿Qué intercambios se establecieron como resultado de la era de la exploración?

title: El intercambio colombino
text:
En 1494, un hombre que navegó a través del Océano Atlántico regresó a su hogar con historias salvajes de todo tipo. Describió el nuevo mundo que había visto, lleno de plantas, animales y comida desconocidos. Contó sobre las personas que había conocido allí. Este hombre no era Cristobal Colón ni un miembro de su tripulación. Era Taíno de las Bahamas a quien Colón capturo y llevá a España. No sabemos su nombre real porque Colón lo llamó Diego Colón.

Después de regresar a su país, Colón les contó a sus amigos y familiares sobre España. Describió "las grandes iglesias, fortalezas e iglesias" y "las personas y caballos y animales". Vio una tierra desconocida de "tierras y comida... y corridas de toros". Todo era nuevo para él, así como los pueblos nativos y sus tierras natales era nuevos para los europeos. Como las personas viajaban entre los continentes, ellos intercambiaban ideas sobre tecnología, religión y formas de vida.

Como los europeos exploradores llegaron a diferentes partes de América del Norte, llevaron a pueblos de diferentes grupos, como los iroqueses y Patuxet a través del océano a conocer Europa. No era solo curiosidad lo que había entre los pueblos de las Américas y Europa. Apenas se conocieron, vieron oportunidades de satisfacer sus deseos y necesidades. Los pueblos de los dos lados del Atlántico rápidamente intercambiaron bienes, personas, plantas, animales y enfermedades.

Este intercambio entre las Américas, Europa, África y Asia se llama Intercambio Colombino. Se llamó así por Cristóbal Colón. El Intercambio Colombino tuvo un impacto enorme sobre la vida de todas las personas del mundo. Sin él, Italia nunca hubiera inventado la pizza e Irlanda nunca hubiera cultivado patatas. Los indígenas americanos nunca hubieran montado a caballo.

Los animales como los caballos, ganado, ovejas y cerdos cambiaron la vida económica de las Américas. La crianza de animales comenzó a ser un nuevo recurso para comer. Los caballos cambiaron la forma en la que las tribus como los Sioux y los Comanche cazaban y viajaban. Montar a caballo era una forma de transporte mucho más rápida que caminar llevando una manada de bisontes

Los colonos europeos también trajeron con ellos la caña de azúcar, aceitunas, cítricos, bananas y abejas. Colón trajo la caña de azúcar a La Española en 1493. La caña de azúcar crecía bien en las Américas y se vendía bien en Europa.

Muchas plantas de las Américas también tuvieron un gran impacto en Europa, África y Asia. Por ejemplo, en las Américas las plantas como las patatas, tomates y maíz cambiaron la forma de comer de los pueblos. A los dos lados del Atlántico, las nuevas plantas en granjas y asentamientos se propagaron y cambiaron incluso las que crecían en la naturaleza. El mundo no fue nunca el mismo debido al Intercambio Colombino.

title: Demanda en Europa
text:
España mandó exploradores a través del Atlántico para abrir el comercio con India y ganar dinero. En cambio, el descubrimiento de las Américas tuvo un impacto aún mayor en la economía europea. A medida que llegaban nuevos bienes de las Américas, las personas corrían a comprarlos.

Al principio, la mayoría de las cosas que venían de las Américas eran bienes de lujo para los ricos. Los europeos trajeron oro y plata. A los compradores ricos de Europa también les gustaban las pieles de los animales de las Américas. En las Américas, las cosechas como el tabaco también se hicieron populares. Muchas personas deseaban probar nuevos bienes y por eso los precios aumentaban. Trajeron la caña de azúcar, originaria de Asia, al clima cálido del Caribe y creció muy bien. La gente de Europa estaba dispuesta a pagar precios altos por el azúcar. La alta demanda hizo que los productores de la caña de azúcar de las Américas desearan aumentar sus provisiones.

Algunas cosechas de las Américas solamente eran populares entre ciertas personas o en ciertos lugares. A los europeos ricos al principio no les gustaban las patatas. Pero, las patatas eran un buena comida porque tenían muchas calorías y crecían bajo tierra. Esto evitaba que las destruyera el mal tiempo. Poco a poco, las patatas se extendieron a muchos países. Las patatas nunca tuvieron un precio tan alto como el azúcar. Como la gente aprendió como prepararlas y cocinarlas para hacer comidas aumentó su producción.

Los europeos no hicieron del maíz una compra popular. Muchos europeos usaron el maíz como ingrediente en otros platos y para alimentar animales. El maíz se aceptó en Asia y África como una importación de Europa.

La demanda de Europa de diferentes bienes de las Américas tuvo un impacto en la vida de las Américas. La forma de dividir la tierra, la forma de trabajar de la gente y las ideas sobre quién tenía derechos estaban influenciados por la demanda económica en los países europeos.

title: Why Is It Important to Study Geography?
text:
Geography is the study of places and the relationships between people and their environments. The study of geography also includes how things change over time. Studying geography helps us understand the world around us. We can use geography to understand the past and answer important questions about the world and its people. Using geographic tools, such as maps, globes, graphs, diagrams, aerial and other photographs, and other geographical representations helps us to organize our thinking about the world into spatial terms.

Studying geography helps us to understand history, economics, culture, and government. No matter the time period, geography has played a role in the actions of people and the events of government and economics. Wars were started over resources from the land. Location played a key role in building the colonies in the United States. Representation in government is based on regions and places. Transportation systems modified the land to bring goods and services to markets. The creation of settlements, territories, states, and nations are all linked to geography.

Geographic skills and concepts can also help people solve local, state, or international problems. Studying geography can help experts answer questions concerning environmental change, population distribution, proper use of natural resources, and political discussions. Studying geography helps you to become a responsible citizen of your local community, state, and the world. You can learn about current events and apply your knowledge of geographic concepts to current events by watching the news, reading the newspaper, or researching current events using reliable and credible sources.

According to former president Barack Obama:

The study of geography is about more than just memorizing places on a map. It's about understanding the complexity of our world, appreciating the diversity of cultures that exists across continents. And in the end, it's about using all that knowledge to help bridge divides and bring people together.

This week, you will practice using geographic skills and tools. As you work through this week, think of ways that geographic skills and tools can help you understand the world around you.

title: Physical Characteristics of the United States
text:
Physical characteristics describe the natural environment of an area. Landscapes, plants, climate, and animals are physical characteristics. Bodies of water, including rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans, are also physical characteristics. Some examples of landforms are mountains, plains, valleys, and deserts. A place's physical characteristics also include climate, vegetation, ecosystems, and animal life. These characteristics are all connected and help geographers describe different areas on the Earth’s surface.

Climate is the average weather conditions of a place over an extended period of time. While the weather can change in just a few hours, climate usually takes hundreds, thousands, and even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperature, precipitation, and wind in an area. Precipitation includes rain, snow, and sleet.

Ecosystems are communities of living organisms within a region. Living organisms include animal and plant life. Many factors affect living organisms within an ecosystem. These include climate, type of soil, water, and other growing conditions. In an ecosystem, plants and animals depend on each other for survival.

Physical characteristics are all connected and help geographers describe different areas on Earth’s surface. They are what makes Earth interesting and unique. The physical characteristics of an area influence its human characteristics. A place’s human characteristics come from human ideas and the interactions people have with their environment.

The United States is a diverse country with many unique physical characteristics that impact the way people live and interact with their environment.

title: Mountains
text:
A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean. It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They are formed from movement of the Earth's crust. Mountains are shaped over time by weather. Rich minerals are found in the core of mountains. Mountain peaks are often covered in snow. The snow melts and sends water down the sides in streams, creeks, and brooks.

There are many mountain ranges in the United States. The Rocky Mountain range is the biggest mountain range in North America. It begins in Canada and extends through central New Mexico. Many of the peaks are more than 12,000 feet high. Mount Elbert in Colorado is the tallest peak in the range at 14,433 feet. Thousands of tourists flock to the Rocky Mountains each year to explore their natural wonders.

The Appalachian Mountains are located in the eastern part of the United States. The highest peak is Mount Mitchell at 6,684 feet. The Appalachian Trail runs the length of the mountain range, which is about 2,000 miles long. Outdoor adventurers and hiking enthusiasts hike the Appalachian Trail throughout the year.

title: Rivers and Lakes
text:
Rivers and lakes have played a vital role in the history, economy, and actions of governments in North America for thousands of years. There are many rivers in the United States that continue to play a vital role in the nation’s economy, history, and culture.

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. Combined with the Mississippi River, it forms one of the largest river systems on Earth. The Missouri River travels through the heart of the Great Plains. The Missouri flows southeast from its source in Montana. It ends in Missouri, where it joins the Mississippi River.

The Mississippi River is the second-longest river in the United States. Its name comes from a Chippewa word meaning "Father of Waters." The Mississippi River formed when glaciers melted about 12,000 years ago. The Mississippi River is nearly 2,400 miles long and travels through 10 states before it pours into the Gulf of America.

The Rio Grande is the fourth-largest river in the United States. The name "Rio Grande" is Spanish for "great river." The Rio Grande begins its journey high up in the southern Rocky Mountains and travels south toward the Gulf of America. The Rio Grande cuts the state of New Mexico almost in half. The rest of this river's path forms the border between Texas and Mexico.

The Great Lakes, which include Lake Erie, Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, and Lake Superior, are located in the northern United States. The Great Lakes cover over 94,000 square miles and contain about 6 quadrillion gallons of water. The lakes hold about 21 percent of the Earth's fresh water and 84 percent of America's fresh water. The deepest lake is Lake Superior at 1,330 feet. Lake Erie's average depth is only 70 feet.

Lake Okeechobee is another important lake in the United States. Lake Okeechobee is located in southern Florida and covers 730 square miles, making it the 10th-largest freshwater lake in the United States. It is home to hundreds of plant and animal species. Because of its abundant supply of fish, Lake Okeechobee is one of the state’s premier fishing destinations.

title: Oceans and Gulfs
text:
Oceans and gulfs are important bodies of water in and around the United States. Oceans are bodies of saltwater. Oceans cover most of the Earth's surface. The United States is bordered by two oceans. The Atlantic Ocean borders the United States on the East Coast. It is the second-largest ocean on Earth. Like the other bodies of water in the United States, the Atlantic Ocean helps the U.S. economy by providing a trade route with other countries. Atlantic coastal areas are popular tourist destinations for Americans and visitors from around the world.

The Pacific Ocean is on the western border of the United States. The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth. It covers over 60 million square miles. Like the Atlantic Ocean, the Pacific Ocean plays a major part in the U.S. economy. The Pacific Ocean is a vital trade route between the United States and other countries.

A gulf is a deep inlet of water that connects the coastal areas to a larger body of water, such as a sea or ocean. The Gulf of America sits between Florida and Mexico. It covers about a half-million square miles of water. The Gulf shares a border with five states. It has 33 major tributaries, or rivers, that flow into it. This includes the Mississippi River. These tributaries have been used as travel routes for thousands of years, making the Gulf of America a gateway to expansion.

title: Deserts and Plains
text:
A desert is a place where there is less than 10 inches of precipitation in a year. The dryness keeps the soil from being high in nutrients. Deserts usually have high temperatures and are hot during the day. At night, the temperature is lower, and the desert is colder.

The Mojave Desert is located in parts of southern California, Nevada, Arizona, and Utah and extends into Mexico. It is the driest desert in North America. It receives less than two inches of rain each year. The Mojave Desert is home to Death Valley. Death Valley lies 282 feet below sea level, making it the lowest point in North America. It is also the hottest place on Earth. Despite its dry and extremely hot climate, hundreds of plant and animal species call the Mojave Desert home. The plants and animals of this region have adapted to the harsh conditions of the desert in order to survive.

The Great Plains are very different from the Mojave Desert. A plain is a large area of flat land with few to no trees. The Great Plains is a large area east of the Rocky Mountains that is very flat. It extends from Mexico to Canada and eastward to Illinois. It is primarily grassy with few trees. The soil is usually very good in the plains due to the abundant amount of grass material that grows there. It is a great place for growing crops like corn and wheat.

title: Human Characteristics of the United States
text:
A place's human characteristics are a result of people’s ideas, choices, and actions as they interact with the physical environment. In other words, where people live and the kinds of houses they build are human characteristics. The kind of work people do and the activities they do for fun are also human characteristics of a place.

When we discuss a place's human characteristics, we also examine its economic, political, and cultural characteristics. A place's political characteristics are organized by where people live. This includes cities, states, and countries. Cultural characteristics include a place's religion, language, arts, and celebrations. A place's economic characteristics are based on natural resources. These natural resources are used for goods and services and a place's resulting economy.

The United States is made up of 50 states and numerous territories in the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. Each state in the United States has its own capital and state government. State governments are responsible for providing safety and security for those in the state, maintaining justice and order within the state, and providing members of the community with goods and services to meet their wants and needs.

States within the United States vary greatly in population, culture, and economic activities. California is the most populated state in the United States, with a total population of over 39 million people. In contrast, Wyoming has the smallest population in the United States, with only 579,000 people living in the state.

The United States is also made up of 14 territories. A territory is an organized area of land under the control of another state or country. At present, the United States has 14 territories. Puerto Rico is the most heavily populated of the U.S. territories around the world. As of 2020, Puerto Rico’s population totaled 3,194,034 people. The smallest U.S. territory by population is American Samoa. It has a permanent population of 55,140 people.

Geography plays a large role in the human characteristics of an area. It affects where people decide to live, the natural resources they can use, and the way they make a living.

A natural resource is any material from the Earth that people can use. Some examples are trees, coal, oil, natural gas, plants, and gold. Natural resources are important to make life better for the people in a community.

To survive, animals must eat. Whether they are gathering their food or finding and catching prey, it is hard work. Frequently, animals fail in their hunts. Hunting gets easier when animals work in a team. Dog species are most famous for this type of pack hunting. Humpback whales also hunt in groups. They circle a school of fish, blowing bubbles. The bubbles make a curtain around the fish so that they cannot swim away. Then, the whales swim through the middle with their mouths open. The fish have nowhere to go except inside a whale’s mouth. All the whales help, and all take turns eating.

Animals form groups for protection. They protect each other in two ways. The first is active protection. Elephants, bison, and dolphins all do this. When a predator comes close, the adults form a protective circle around the young and weak members of the group. If the predator gets close, the strong adults will attack. However, they will not leave the circle. Another form of protection is used by antelopes and minnows. They live in large groups so they can hide in the crowd. An individual animal has a smaller chance of being caught because others in the group could be caught instead. Groups provide protection to individuals.

title: George Washington Gets His Start
text:
Young George Washington of Virginia was ambitious. This means he wanted to make an impression on the world. He wanted a life as a British military officer. Being a British officer would give him status, respect, and wealth. When Virginia Lieutenant Governor Dinwiddie wanted to send a message to the French Army in the Ohio Country, he chose Washington to deliver it.

In May 1754, Dinwiddie sent young Lieutenant Colonel George Washington, his second-in-command Captain Adam Stephen, and a company of Virginia militia to build a fort at the forks of the Ohio. This would send the message to the French that the Ohio Country belonged to Virginia. The French were not welcome.

Washington was joined by Tanaghrisson, the Half-King of the Iroquois Confederacy. Tanagrhisson knew a French patrol’s location. Washington took some of his men and followed Tanaghrisson.

After the death of Jumonville, Washington and his company of men reunited. They quickly built a small fort in a meadow. Fort Necessity became Washington’s first point of defense against the French.

Jumonville’s half-brother, Louis Coulon de Villiers, led 600 French troops and 100 of their American Indian allies from Fort Duquesne to Fort Necessity. He would meet with the people who killed his brother.

In a rain-soaked meadow, the Virginia militia waited. The constant rain ruined the gunpowder in the muskets. They had no means of defense. When the French force came, there was little Washington could do to save the lives of his men. The French presented Washington with a document written in French. The document gave conditions for surrender. Washington did not speak French. Washington signed the document, not knowing that it also blamed him for the assassination of Jumonville. An assassination is when someone is killed for political or religious reasons.

On July 4, 1754, he led his defeated men back to Virginia. It was not a very good beginning for a man who wanted to be a British army officer. His actions with Jumonville sparked the French and Indian War.

How does this activity relate to our phenomenon?

Weather is the state of the atmosphere in a specific location at one time. It is the combination of many factors happening in the air and sky. These factors can include temperature, wind, rain, snow, and more. In a specific location, the weather can be different in each season.

Weather follows specific patterns, or repeats itself in a specific location. For example, we know that it is usually warm and sunny in Florida, even in the winter time. This is a pattern that repeats. Another pattern of weather is in the state of Alaska. Parts of Alaska have cold, windy, and snowy weather the whole year. This pattern continues to repeat.

Scientists use patterns to make predictions for the future. Weather patterns help scientists make predictions that help inform people. For example, we know it has been warm and sunny in Florida during December. We can make a prediction that it will continue to be warm and sunny in Florida during the next month of December. This prediction can be helpful to people who will be in Florida during December.

title: Rain in the Desert
text:
Scientists use weather patterns to make predictions about weather in the future. These predictions are important and helpful to people. For example, a scientist may predict that hurricanes are more common in the summer than winter. They base this on previous weather patterns. So, people know that they should be more prepared for a hurricane in the summer months than in the winter months. People may decide to buy a first-aid kit or extra non-perishable food. They may be more cautious planning certain outdoor activities in summer. They might travel with emergency supplies in summer. People who live in areas where hurricanes happen know they are more likely to hit during summer.

This does not mean that a hurricane could never happen in the winter. It means that summer is when hurricanes are more likely. Scientists continue to track weather patterns. As they gather more data, they learn more. They can be more accurate in what they predict. They continue to inform the public about weather patterns. This is important information for people. It helps them make decisions in their daily life.

text: Over the last 200 years, human beings have infiltrated the homes of many animal species. Human beings build roads, homes, and communities in places that were previously the homes of many forms of wildlife. Across North America, people have built their communities in places that have prevented animals from being able to come together with other animals. This can cause problems for future generations of that species if animals can’t get to other animals to be able to mate. It can also cause problems for species that are migratory. For example, caribou herds. need to be able to move from place to place to get enough food. If a road is blocking them from moving, they will likely go over the road to be able to get more food. When animals cross roads, many are killed in car accidents. This is devastating for the animals and the people involved. To solve this problem, many states have invested in wildlife bridges or underpasses. They are roads built over or under a road where lots of wildlife can pass. These bridges are very successful in restoring ecosystems to their natural state and in preventing the deaths of animals trying to get around the roads.

title: Extended: Coming Together for the Next Generation
text:
Even animals that live alone must find a mate to reproduce. Some species form groups at this time to make it easier for males and females to find each other. The grouse is one example. This bird usually lives alone. During mating season, the males come together and fight over specific territory. Once they have their designated spots, they perform for the females. The females then walk around and pick the male they prefer. When mating season is over, the grouse separate and continue living alone.

Another reason many species live in groups is to raise their young together. It takes a lot of time, energy, and resources to raise young from birth to adulthood. During that time, both offspring and parents are easier prey. Forming a group to share the responsibility of raising the young helps all members of the group. Prairie dogs are great examples of this. A prairie dog community is one large extended family with siblings, cousins, grandparents, aunts, and uncles. The young are raised in a nursery. All the adults take turns watching and teaching the nursery. Others go out to hunt and gather food. All members of the group share responsibilities to survive.

title: Florida's State Government
text:
Florida’s state government is responsible for making important decisions for the people of Florida. State governments are modeled after the federal government and consist of an executive, legislative, and judicial branch. The seat of Florida’s state government is located in the state’s capital, Tallahassee.

Executive Branch

The executive branch is responsible for signing bills into law, appointing judges, proposing the state budget, organizing the state militia, and overseeing all agencies that work within the government. The executive branch is led by the governor and lieutenant governor. A governor is the leader of a state government. The governor of Florida makes decisions about how the state should be run and appoints people to certain positions in the government.

Florida’s lieutenant governor assists the governor in running the state government. The lieutenant governor has four main responsibilities. If the governor cannot fulfill their responsibilities, the lieutenant governor takes their place until the governor’s term is over. The lieutenant governor can also serve as the head of any state government department that the governor assigns them to. The lieutenant governor also works with the Department of Economic Opportunity to support workforce development projects and encourage economic development in the state. The lieutenant governor is also responsible for helping to maintain and pass the state’s yearly budget.

The executive branch also includes the secretary of state, attorney general, and chief financial officer, all of whom are elected by the people and serve four-year terms. The secretary of state is responsible for elections, record-keeping, and safeguarding the state archives. The attorney general of Florida is the head of law enforcement for the state. The chief financial officer for the state of Florida is responsible for overseeing all of the state’s financial decisions and funds.

Legislative Branch

The legislative branch is responsible for making laws for the state. Florida’s legislative branch is made up of the state House of Representatives and the Senate. The House of Representatives consists of 120 elected members that represent districts throughout the state. Florida’s state Senate is made up of 40 senators. Members of the legislature are elected by the people. Members of the House of Representatives serve for two years, while members of the senate serve for four years. Each year, members of the House of Representatives and Senate meet to make new laws and amend existing laws. They also develop and pass a balanced state budget every year, as required by the Florida constitution.

Judicial Branch

The state judicial branch’s job is to interpret or explain what the laws of the state mean. This branch is made up of judges and courts. Florida’s judicial branch is led by the Florida Supreme Court. Supreme court justices are appointed by the governor and a special committee, whose members are selected by the governor. They serve for a term of six years, but there is no limit to the number of terms they can serve. The justices ensure that the correct procedures were followed. If problems or disagreements cannot be resolved within the state, people take their cases to the U.S. Supreme Court.

title: Local Governments in Florida
text:
A local government is a government that serves the people of a town, city, or county. There are three main types of local government in Florida: counties, municipalities, and special districts.

County Governments

The state of Florida is divided into 67 counties. Each of these counties is made up of different cities, towns, and communities. County governments are responsible for assisting the state government in meeting the needs of those who live within the county’s boundaries.

County governments are run by a board of commissioners, who are elected by the voters of their county. County governments are usually responsible for keeping records. This means that counties keep track of births, deaths, marriages, and business licenses. County governments are also in charge of voting, vehicle registration, and collecting taxes on land and property. Many counties also offer health and welfare services, like nursing care, immunization, and childcare classes. Some counties also run the public library system.

Municipalities

Each town or city within a county has its own form of government, which are called municipalities. Municipalities are run by a mayor and a city council, who are selected by the people. Leaders of a municipality work with one another, as well as county and state leaders, to uphold the laws of the city’s charter. Municipal governments in Florida are responsible for public safety and services within their community, including police and fire departments, parks, and sanitation services.

Special Districts

Special districts are created by the state to serve a specific purpose. Special districts usually serve a single purpose. In Florida, special districts often cover more than one county. One of the most important special districts in Florida are water management districts. The state is divided into five water management districts, which are responsible for conserving water from Florida’s rivers, lakes, and underground aquifers. Florida also has special districts to help with fires, mosquito control, housing, and community development programs.

title: The Court System
text:
The judicial branch of the United States and Florida is made up of courts and judges. The purpose of the courts is to interpret laws and settle conflicts. How does the court system work? First, citizens bring their problems to the state trial courts. These trial courts are located in the county you live in. The judges in the trial courts listen to the problem, or case, and both sides of the story. They think about the evidence that each side presented and then make a decision based on what they heard. Judges' decisions solve conflicts and provide consequences for those people who break the law.

If a person does not agree with the trial court's decision, they can file an appeal. This appeal goes to one of the five Court of Appeals in the state of Florida. Sometimes the Court of Appeals keeps the trial court's decision. Other times, they overturn the original outcome. If a person is still unhappy after the Court of Appeals' decision, they can apply to take their case to the state supreme court.

Florida’s supreme court has seven judges, called justices. They make decisions on cases and solve problems that people bring before them. The Florida Supreme Court takes cases that have first gone through the trial courts and Court of Appeals. Justices on the Florida Supreme Court decide cases in two ways: by opinion or by order. In both types of cases, the judges must meet to analyze the case and determine the verdict.

If a case cannot be resolved by the state courts, it can be elevated to the Supreme Court of the United States. The U.S. Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States. It upholds and interprets the laws of the Constitution. It also ensures that the rights of all Americans are protected. Currently, the Supreme Court is made up of nine judges. Supreme Court justices work together to determine the outcome of important court cases. The Supreme Court reviews thousands of cases each year.

title: Who Represents Florida in the National Government?
text:
There are many elected officials that represent the interests of Floridians in the federal government. Each state, including Florida, is represented by elected officials in the legislative branch of the federal government. Floridians are represented by two senators in the United States Senate. Senators serve six years, but there is no limit to the total number of terms that they can serve.

Officials are also elected from Florida to the U.S. House of Representatives. The number of representatives from each state is based on population. States with smaller populations have fewer representatives than states with larger populations. Currently, there are 27 representatives from Florida that represent the state and its citizens in the House of Representatives. Each member of the House represents a specific area in their state known as a congressional district.

title: Communication Systems
text:
Communication technology has always been important in economics. For many centuries, people could only communicate and trade with one another using time-consuming methods like overland caravans or ocean-going vessels. Despite the length of time it took to trade and communicate, people began to rely on the goods and ideas produced on the other side of the world. Tea produced in Asia became a key influence for the American Revolution. Chinese scientists invented the compass and astrolabe. These innovations spread to other cultures and made ocean travel possible for Europeans.

As communication technology improved, global trade increased. The transmission of ideas and information increased as well. Starting in the mid-1800s, communication technology began to grow rapidly. Samuel Morse invented the telegraph. He also invented a code for the telegraph that would become a globally understood mode of communication. Morse’s invention allowed people to communicate over great distances. The telegraph and Morse code became one of most important communication methods for sailors and navies.

From the telegraph to the internet, communication technology has dramatically increased the exchange of goods and ideas. Modern communication technology lets you order goods from anywhere in the world and keep track of it from the warehouse to your doorstep. With an internet connection, you have access to ideas from across the globe. The internet and other forms of modern communication allow people to share important ideas like universal human rights. Other types of communication happen through these mediums too. The Olympics are broadcast in real time, news outlets report on events almost instantaneously, and social media allows you to connect with people from all over the world. The role of communication technology has always been vital to a global society, but innovation and collaboration have made communication even more effective.

title: Government in the United States
text:
The purpose of government is to provide safety and security for those in the community from threats outside of the community, maintain justice and order within the community, and help the members of the community meet their wants and needs. The government of the United States is a constitutional republic.

A constitutional republic is a form of government based on a written document that determines the power and functions of an elected representational government. The written law of the Constitution is enforced by representatives chosen by the people. At every level, the people's consent is what gives the government power to act. This is known as popular sovereignty. A constitutional republic must balance individual rights with the common good. Effective leaders work to meet the needs of citizens and protect their rights.

Americans have different customs, traditions, and ethnic origins. Americans are united by the principles of a constitutional republic. The Constitution states that citizens need to respect individual rights and freedoms. Authority from the people limits the actions of the government, which protects their rights of liberty and freedom. By creating and enforcing laws, citizens can ensure their rights are protected. Respecting the rights of others means that everyone is treated equally. The principles of fairness, equality, and justice have influenced new laws and policies over time at the local, state, and national levels of government.

Fairness, equality, and justice are principles that have influenced government and laws. Fairness is a fundamental American value. Fairness is about making sure that everyone has what they need to be successful. Our government supports fairness by making laws to keep things fair for everyone. All people should be treated equally.

Equality means that all people are treated the same, regardless of who they are. Our government provides services and protection to all citizens. Justice means that people behave in a way that is fair, equal, and balanced for everyone. Fairness, equality, and justice are democratic values. These values guide our government. They protect the rights of citizens.

According to one of the Founders, John Adams, “Government is instituted for the common good … not for profit, honor, or private interest of any one man, family, or class of men.” The common good is when people think about what is best for everyone. It refers to decisions that benefit most members of a community. Our government supports the common good through laws. If citizens work together toward the common good, freedom and self-government can be successful. Everyone in the community benefits.

Another important facet of the United States government is rule of law. John Adams stated that “The rule of law means a government of laws and not of men.” Rule of law is based on fairness, equality, and justice. It means that the government is accountable to the law. The government can only use its power as defined by laws. There are four important ideas with the rule of law:

Laws have to be adopted and approved through government processes.

Laws have to be clear, and everyone needs to know about them.

Laws are applied equally for all citizens.

When there are disputes about the law, individuals will have representatives who are neutral to deliver the best outcome.

In the United States, we have a federal government that leads our country. The federal government shares its power with state governments. The federal government has the power to:

print money

declare war

build the military

make treaties (agreements with foreign countries)

make and enforce laws for doing business between the states and foreign nations

make laws to enforce the Constitution

State governments control laws within each state. They also have elected officials. The leader of the state is the governor. The governor appoints officials and signs or vetoes bills passed by the state legislature. The governor is also the commander-in-chief of the state’s military. Each state has its own constitution. Like the United States Constitution, state constitutions must enforce laws in ways that protect the rights of citizens.

We also have local governments. They lead our towns, cities, and counties. Cities and towns elect leaders called mayors. People also elect city managers, town councils, and county commissioners. These officials address community concerns, help out in the community, and act as a voice to the community. Local governments are in charge of police and fire departments, public transportation systems, road maintenance, community parks, trash removal, and building codes.

title: Checks and Balances
text:
The writers of the U.S. Constitution wanted to limit the power of government so that the United States would be strong and endure. Articles I, II, and III of the Constitution separate the government into three branches.

This ensures that branches of government share power equally. In order for these branches to work together, the Founders created a system of checks and balances. This means that each branch of the government has to be in agreement with the other two.

Each branch has the power to stop certain actions of another branch. This happens if a branch believes those actions are unconstitutional or not in the best interest of the country. The system of checks and balances helps make sure that no branch of government becomes more powerful than the others.

Congress can pass a law, but the president must approve it. Congress can also override the president's decision to veto, or reject, a law. The Supreme Court has the power to strike down a law that has been approved by both Congress and the president if it believes the law is unconstitutional. The president appoints justices to the Supreme Court, but Congress must approve the choices. Because of this system of checks and balances, U.S. citizens can be sure their rights are always protected.

title: Place
text:
The theme of place refers to how we describe what a location is like. This theme includes the physical and human characteristics of a place. How is one place different from another place?

Each place has different physical characteristics that are part of its natural environment. These might include forests, mountains, oceans, and rivers. Landforms, bodies of water, climate, soils, biomes, natural vegetation, and animal life are all part of a place's physical characteristics.

A place's human characteristics come from human ideas and interactions that people have with their environment. People make choices about where to live and how to meet their basic needs.

A place's human characteristics include the political boundaries of states, cities, and towns. Human characteristics also include buildings, bridges, homes, and other manmade features of a place.

title: Climate
text:
When we study the weather of a place, we want to know if it is warm or cold, sunny or rainy. Climate is a physical characteristic of a place. Climate is the weather pattern of an area that develops over many years. While the weather can change in just a few hours, the climate takes hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperature, precipitation (rain, snow, sleet), and wind in the area. We can understand the climates of the world by looking at a graph that shows the patterns in weather over 12 months.

Let’s look at a graph describing climate zones around the world. This graph shows how many regions of the world have the same kind of climate. For example, four regions of the world have a polar climate in them.

title: Planning an Investigation
text:
Scientists do investigations to better understand the natural world. Read about how one scientist did her investigation. Then answer the questions below.

Erin Smith

Erin Smith is an inventor and scientist. She is currently at Stanford University studying neuroscience and computer science. She is also the inventor and founder of FacePrint. FacePrint is an invention that can help identify Parkinson’s disease and other neurological diseases. It uses video technology to identify changes in facial expressions caused by disease. The technology helps detect the disease early. Smith developed the technology as a high school student.

Starting Young

Smith started doing scientific research when she was ten years old. “My mom and I turned our kitchen into a makeshift lab and spent hours searching for answers to my many questions,” she explains. “My ideas spanned any and everything I was curious about and started small. Science research was an art form to me that I quickly fell in love with. Then, when I was in high school, I had the idea for FacePrint after watching a video of Parkinson’s disease patients on YouTube [...] I noticed that whenever they would smile or laugh it came off as emotionally distant.”

Investigation Process

Smith began to research after that. She spoke with doctors and family members of people who had Parkinson’s disease. She also read medical journals to get as much information as possible. Smith came up with a hypothesis, or idea to be tested. She then decided which variables to test. Smith's success has come as she's worked hard to find answers to her questions. She has done this through research and investigation.

Advice to Young Scientists

“Learn to really cultivate your curiosity. I think every invention or research project I've had came through curiosity," Smith says. "That's really where the best ideas come from. And secondly, start pursuing your ideas today, even if it's just a small step forward. There are so many really amazing, impactful ideas that never turned into reality just because there's no perfect time to start. So start today.”

title: Let's Write
text: The American Indians and European settlers treated each other unfairly long ago. In your opinion, what could the settlers and American Indians have done differently in order to share land and resources harmoniously?

title: Spanish Missionaries Come to Florida
text:
In 1565, after many years of failed expeditions and colonization attempts, Spanish explorer Don Pedro Menéndez de Avilés landed on the east coast of Florida with 1,000 soldiers, settlers, and Catholic priests. King Philip II of Spain tasked Menéndez with reclaiming the area for Spain, driving the French out of the area, and establishing the first permanent Spanish settlement in Florida. Menéndez quickly achieved all of these goals. He established the first permanent settlement in what is now the continental United States, the town of St. Augustine.

Menéndez achieved two of the primary goals of exploration. He gained access to new resources, which could be sent back to Spain, and brought glory to the Spanish empire. The final goal of exploration was to spread Christianity to the native peoples of the Americas. The Roman Catholic Church held immense power over people across Europe and the Americas during the Age of Exploration. Not only did it influence the Christian religion, but its power found its way into the culture as well.

Church leaders preached that a person must belong to the Roman Catholic Church in order to go to heaven. If a person didn't belong, their soul would not be saved. This concept frightened many of the Church’s followers so much that they were willing to do as the Church demanded. The Church required a great deal from people. Everyone was expected to give funds to the church. Even those who were without money were supposed to pay this tax. Many had only crops to give, but others handed over the money and struggled to live without it.

The Church amassed a vast fortune. It could use this money as it pleased. At times, the funds were used to help the less fortunate, but funds were also used to build churches and missions across the globe. The pope, who is the leader of the Catholic Church, had the ear of many monarchs, especially the Catholic monarchs of Spain. Not only was he their spiritual advisor, but he also gave his opinion on all matters of state. The Church had as much power as, if not more than, kings, queens, and emperors. It used its influence and vast fortune to send missionaries and construct missions across the Americas with the purpose of converting the Native Americans to Christianity.

On his initial expedition to Florida, Menéndez brought Spanish priests and friars with him. These religious figures established the first Catholic parish in what is now the United States at St. Augustine in 1566. They also established small religious settlements known as doctrinas near Native American villages to begin the work of converting the native population to Christianity. Doctrinas consisted of a church, kitchen area, and homes for the friars. Friars and priests also established visitas. A visita was a small outpost constructed in a Native American village that included just a church or chapel.

The priests and friars that came with Menéndez needed additional help to convert the large population of Native Americans they encountered in Florida. Missionaries were sent by the Catholic Church to Florida to assist them. Missionaries were religious figures who wanted to convert others to their religion. These missionaries belonged to one of two Catholic religious orders: the Franciscans and the Jesuits.

In 1573, the first Franciscan missionaries arrived in Florida. Their goal was to establish missions across Florida, starting in St. Augustine. Missions were small settlements that centered around religious activities and education. The missions had three primary goals. The first goal was to convert Native American tribes to Christianity. The second goal was to claim the area and ensure that it remained in Spanish control. The third goal was for them to serve as centers to teach Native Americans about Spanish culture, history, and laws so they could become Spanish citizens.

The first Franciscan mission was completed in 1578. Mission Nombre de Dios was built near the settlement of St. Augustine to convert the local Timucua tribe in the area. It also served as one of the primary religious centers of St. Augustine. The construction of Mission Nombre de Dios was the start of Florida’s extensive mission system. Over the next 100 years, the mission system of Florida continued to grow.

title: Spanish Missions of Florida
text:
From the late 1500s to the late 1600s, Spanish missionaries founded over 100 Catholic missions across the colony of Florida, which extended north into present-day Georgia and west into present-day Alabama. Goods, people, and ideas moved between the missions of North Florida and St. Augustine, the Spanish capital, and along the Camino Real. Camino Real is Spanish for “royal road” or “king’s highway.” By the mid-1600s, Florida was home to over 70 Franciscan missionaries, who ministered to roughly 25,000 Native Americans from various tribes.

Spanish Missions in Florida

The table includes information about prominent missions constructed in Florida, including present-day Georgia and Alabama, from 1587 to the late 1600s. Each mission was established to serve one of the major Native American tribes of northern Florida.
