Daily Life in the Spanish Missions

Daily life in the Spanish missions of Florida centered around religious activities, education, and work. The primary goals of the mission system were to convert Native Americans to Christianity and provide all settlers with religious services and instruction. Each day started with prayer and religious services. The priests and friars also led the settlers of the mission in religious instruction every day. Settlers from the surrounding communities often came to the missions to attend church services and religious ceremonies, such as baptisms, marriages, and funeral services.

The missions were responsible for supporting themselves. The settlers in each mission had to grow or raise their own food, make their own tools and clothing, and build their own facilities. Most missions included a large garden or farmland to grow crops needed for survival. Settlers in Florida’s missions often grew corn, wheat, and other vegetables. Most missions raised livestock, including cattle, chickens, goats, and sheep. Land outside of the mission was used for grazing and housing livestock.

Settlers in the missions also produced their own clothing and tools. Women were often in charge of making clothing for their families and others in the mission. Cotton and wool were spun into yarn, which was then woven into cloth for making clothes. Craftsmen made tools from iron and used them to produce furniture, cooking utensils, fences, and anything else that was needed for life in the mission. The missions were expected to provide goods, crops, livestock, and free labor to the settlers of St. Augustine.

Effects of the Mission System on the Native American Tribes of Florida

Missions in Florida impacted the native population in many ways. Before European exploration and colonization, most Florida Native American tribes were nomadic and hunted, fished, and gathered wild plants for food. They were now expected to stop these traditions and live the same way as the Spanish in established villages as farmers and laborers. They were forced to become laborers for the missionaries and Spanish settlers. They were forced to farm and harvest crops. At this time, many Native American tribes of Florida did not engage in agriculture and did not know how to plant and harvest crops. They were also expected to convert to Christianity and give up their own religious beliefs.

Spanish missions in Florida were also overrun with European diseases. Smallpox, yellow fever, and measles epidemics were common occurrences in the 1600s. Franciscan friars estimated that almost half of the Timucua population of Florida died from these diseases between 1614 and 1617. Additional epidemics in the mid-1600s decreased the Native American population even further. The decline in the native population of Florida led to labor and eventually food shortages in the missions and colonial settlements.

Many tribes were willing to work with the missionaries and settle in the missions, but there were many Native American tribes that were not. They were unwilling to give up their cultural beliefs, traditions, land, and resources to the Spanish and work as laborers. Tensions between members of the Apalachee tribe and the Spanish led to open hostilities in 1647. During the 1650s, several Timucua tribes rebelled against the Spanish government and missionaries. Armed battles took place between the Timucua and the Spanish. After years of fighting, the Timucua were defeated in 1655. The remaining members of the Timucua either escaped the Spanish and joined other tribes or were sold into enslavement.

Decline of the Mission System

Disease and hostilities between the Spanish and the native population of Florida led to a dramatic decline in Florida’s mission system. As British colonization expanded into South Carolina and Georgia, Spanish missions were destroyed, and many Spanish colonists escaped to St. Augustine. By 1706, all mission activities outside of St. Augustine were stopped by English settlers or local Native American tribes. In just over 100 years, all Spanish missions in the Americas were disbanded, and the mission system came to an end.

title: Fray Francisco Pareja
text:
One of the most important figures of Spanish life in Florida was Fray Francisco Pareja. He played a vital role in the mission system near St. Augustine and was one of the few missionaries who fostered good relationships with the Native American tribes of Florida. Fray Francisco Pareja was a Franciscan friar from Spain. He arrived in Florida in 1595 to work in the missions in St. Augustine. He was assigned to minister to the Timucua at Mission San Juan del Puerto.

During his time in Florida, Pareja became fluent in the Timucuan language. He used this knowledge to write several books to help other missionaries learn the language. His books also helped the missionaries in St. Augustine to teach the Timucua Spanish. In a letter written by Pareja in 1599 to the Spanish king, he noted that “many Indian men and women have learned to read in less than six months, and they write letters to one another in their own language.” One of his books, which was written in 1613, is one of the oldest surviving books written in any Native American language.

Fray Francisco Pareja spent 30 years in Florida working to bridge the gap between two very different cultures.

title: Castillo de San Marcos
text:
During its first 100 years, St. Augustine came under constant attack by privateers and pirates. This was due to the city’s strategic location and the competition between the major powers of Europe to control North America. Several forts were constructed to protect the city from 1565 to the mid-1600s. Each of these forts was constructed of wood, which made them vulnerable to enemy attack.

In 1668, St. Augustine was attacked by the British privateer Robert Searles. Searles and his crew kidnapped African residents, sold them into enslavement, robbed homes, churches, shops, and government buildings, and destroyed the wooden fort located along the Matanzas River. Searles' attack on the city was the final straw for the settlers. They petitioned the queen of Spain to supply funds to build a stone fort to protect the city. Queen Mariana of Spain agreed. She gave her permission and funds to build a stone fort in St. Augustine.

Construction of the fort began in 1672. The first task was to gather stone to construct the fort. Coquina was mined from nearby Anastasia Island for the fort. Coquina is a type of limestone cemented with small shells. Local craftsmen, skilled laborers, Native Americans, enslaved and free Africans, convicts, and soldiers worked tirelessly for 23 years to build the fort, which was finally completed in 1695.

The Castillo de San Marcos still stands along the banks of the Matanzas River. It is the oldest masonry (stone) fort in the continental United States. About 650,000 people visit the Castillo de San Marcos each year to learn about the history of the fort and the city of St. Augustine.

title: The Founding of Pensacola
text:
With the completion of the Castillo de San Marcos in 1695, St. Augustine became a bustling city. During this time, numerous missions were established from St. Augustine to present-day Tallahassee. Spanish control of Florida was firmly established, but the Spanish government hoped to create a stronghold in the western part of Florida. The Spanish also wanted to prevent the French from settling near the Mississippi River. They decided to return to Pensacola, the site of Tristan de Luna’s failed settlement.

In 1698, Spanish explorers returned to the area to establish a new settlement. They constructed two forts to protect the area from enemy attacks. After constructing the military fortifications along Pensacola Bay, the Spanish soldiers moved farther inland and laid out plans for the town.

Life in early Pensacola was not easy. The Spanish were forced to turn to their French rivals for assistance. The French settlers in present-day Mobile, Alabama gave the Spanish much-needed supplies. Because of this, the settlers were able to remain in the area. By 1704, nine Spanish families and hundreds of Native American families lived in Pensacola. A hospital was established to care for the sick. The settlers established a church and a mission near the city.

Life changed drastically in 1719. During the early 1700s, the major powers of Europe were in constant conflict with one another. The War of the Quadruple Alliance pitted England, France, Austria, and Holland against Spain. Spanish colonies in the Americas were attacked by the French and English, including Pensacola. France took possession of the city from 1719 to 1721, but it was returned to Spain following the conclusion of the war.

It took several years for Pensacola to fully recover from war, illness, and turmoil and become a thriving city.

title: Fort Mose
text:
When the British colony of Carolina was established in 1663, colonists flocked to the new colony. They established large farms and plantations, where they grew cotton, rice, and indigo. Africans were enslaved by merchants and were brought to the Carolina colony to work on these large plantations. This work was grueling and extremely difficult. Most enslaved Africans were treated very poorly. They had no rights. They were not allowed to own property or learn to read, and they were not paid for their labor. Many enslaved Africans actively searched for a way to escape the plantations.

Some enslaved Africans did escape and made it to St. Augustine, hoping for protection from the Spanish government. The first group arrived in St. Augustine in 1687. This situation presented the Spanish government with an idea. To encourage enslaved Africans to leave their plantations in the Carolina colony, King Charles II of Spain decreed that enslaved Africans who escaped from British colonies would be welcomed in Florida, as long as they became Catholic. Men were also required to serve in the colonial militia or as laborers for four years.

Many enslaved Africans took advantage of this proclamation. By 1738, over 100 enslaved Africans had reached Florida and were granted their freedom. The newly freed Africans settled in St. Augustine. As their community grew, the Spanish governor of Florida, Manuel de Montiano, established a community for the formerly enslaved Africans near the city. Gracia Real de Santa Teresa de Mose, known as Fort Mose, became the first town for free Africans created by a government in what is now the United States.

The people of Fort Mose were important allies of the Spanish. They fought alongside the Spanish militia against English, French, and Native American forces who sought to gain control of St. Augustine. By 1759, the community at Fort Mose grew to a population of 67 villagers. Their lives were very similar to those of their Spanish neighbors. They attended church services and planted and harvested crops.

In recent years, archeologists have excavated the settlement. They have found many artifacts that show what life was like at Fort Mose, including metal belt buckles, glass bottles, pottery, and metal nails. Today, Fort Mose is one of Florida’s many state parks where people can learn about the history of the state and its people.

title: Tensions Rise Across the World
text:
For Europeans, the North American continent was a place of growth, expansion of freedoms, and a provider of opportunities. The empires of Spain, England, France, and the Netherlands competed with each other to control the vast resources this land could give them. The countries sent representatives to explore and claim the land and its resources for the sponsoring monarch. Little consideration was given to the empires of Native Americans who already lived there.

By the year 1750, North America was dominated by European and powerful Native American empires. Spain still held control of Florida and lands in the western part of the continent. British colonies extended along the Eastern seaboard from Georgia to Maine. France controlled the Louisiana Territory. The Iroquois Confederation controlled much of the Great Lakes region.

The powerful empires of Europe and North America established a trade system that benefited each one of them. The expert Iroquois hunters brought furs and leather to the English and French traders. The traders brought European manufactured goods for exchange. The Spanish established trade networks throughout Florida, the Caribbean, and Central and South America. Raw materials were sent to Spain to make manufactured goods. These goods were sent back to the Americas to be used by colonists and Native American tribes that the Spanish traded with.

The competition for resources and control of land in the Americas ultimately led to armed conflict. Alliances were formed between the major powers of Europe and the powerful Native American nations in North America. Eventually, these armed conflicts spread to Europe. Many nations became involved in one of the first global conflicts in world history.

title: Rights of Citizens
text:
People have many different rights. These include unalienable, civil, political, and economic rights. Rights have different functions. Unalienable rights, also called natural rights, are rights that people are born with and cannot be taken away. The Declaration of Independence defines these rights as the right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

Civil rights protect people from the actions of government, organizations, or other people. The United States government, organizations, and other people cannot prohibit the rights of citizens to:

vote

a fair trial by jury

government services

due process of the law (legal actions or proceedings that must be followed)

serve in the military

serve in public office

equality through the law

assemble or petition the government

freedom of speech

freedom of religion

freedom of the press

Political rights allow people to participate freely in government. People can protect their civil rights through political rights. These rights are defined in the Constitution and the Bill of Rights at the federal level. They are defined at the state level in state constitutions. Examples of political rights include:

voting

serving on a jury

holding political office

attending a protest

petitioning the government through action and/or speech

supporting a social or political issue

expressing an idea in speech and the press

joining a political party

equal access to public services

Economic rights are financial choices and privileges that individuals may select without government interference. These rights enable people to make use of civil and political rights. Economic rights include the right to:

own property

change employment

operate a business

join a labor union

access polling places

meet basic wants and needs

multiple economic opportunities

not being required to pay fees and taxes based on race, gender, ethnicity, religion, or sexual orientation

title: Voting
text:
Voting is one of the most important civic responsibilities that people have. Voting is a formal process in which a group of people makes a choice. This helps inform decisions in their community. An important part of voting is being informed about issues and the people who are running for public office. Voter guides provide background information on the candidates and ballot measures. These guides list the candidates running in each race and offer details on each one’s experience and goals. You can also be informed by listening to speeches, reading the news, and learning how each candidate feels about important issues. Good voters gather information from reliable sources. They use this information to inform their opinion.

To vote, citizens must first register in their state as a legal voter. Citizens must be at least 18 years old and live in the community where they are voting. All citizens can vote. This is a right and a responsibility of being a citizen. Many people throughout history have made many sacrifices so that all citizens can vote, regardless of gender, race, or economic status.

During elections, citizens find out the voting location in their community. A voting location is also known as a polling place. This might be at a school or community building in their neighborhood. There they vote on issues and candidates. At the polling place, citizens have to prove their identity because they can only vote one time per election. How you submit your vote differs by location. You might vote using a computer or a paper ballot.

Presidential elections are held every four years. They are always on the second Tuesday in November. National elections take place every two years on even-numbered years. State and local elections can occur at other times throughout the year. This includes primary and special elections. The right to vote is a privilege and a responsibility of all citizens.

title: Being Informed
text:
It is the responsibility of citizens to be engaged and to learn about what is happening in their community, state, the nation, and the world. This means understanding social, political, cultural, and environmental issues. There are different ways to stay informed. One way is to read and watch the news. There are different news sources available. You can read newspapers and magazines. The news is also available in print and on the internet.

The best way to stay informed is to research a topic. You can investigate issues to learn more about them. You can explore many sources and opinions to better understand the issue. Staying informed also means choosing news sources carefully. Make sure to choose sources that are credible, or reliable. That way, you know the information is correct. You can also talk to an expert to help you understand a topic more clearly.

Staying informed is a very important responsibility for all citizens, especially when it comes to voting. Citizens must be informed on the opinions of candidates and how they will address community issues. Then, citizens can make the best decision when voting in local, state, or national elections.

title: Serving on a Jury
text:
One responsibility U.S. citizens have is to serve on a jury when they are summoned. Juries are important because they help decide if someone who has been accused of a crime is guilty of breaking the law. This is an important part of our country’s legal system. It can only work properly if responsible citizens participate in the process. People who are at least 18 years old are sometimes called to jury duty. A jury is a group of six to 12 people chosen to help decide a court case. In the United States, you are guaranteed a “jury of your peers.” This means that the jury will be made up of citizens just like you.

If you are selected to serve on a jury, you will participate in hearing the court case. Sometimes, this might only be a few days, but in some rare cases, they can go on for months. After everyone has heard both sides of the issue, the jury deliberates, or discusses what they saw and heard, to make a decision. Jury members should use reason and logic when making their decision. In a criminal court, a jury must reach a unanimous decision. This means that all jurors agree on the verdict, or outcome. Juries must deliberate until they reach a unanimous decision. If they cannot, the case may have to start all over with another trial and a different jury. It is very important to take being on a jury very seriously.

title: Paying Taxes
text:
Another responsibility that citizens have is paying taxes. A tax is a percentage of money that a person pays to the government. There are many different types of taxes. You pay taxes on items you buy or items you already own. Sales taxes are taxes you pay on things you buy. There are also taxes you pay every year on things you already own, like property taxes. Property taxes are taxes you pay for owning a house or a car.

Federal income taxes are taxes you pay to the federal government. Some states require residents to pay state income taxes. State income taxes are taxes you pay to the state you live in. Florida does not require residents to pay state income taxes. The state relies on federal, local, and other taxes to pay for public services.

Taxes help to fund public services. If it weren't for taxes, you wouldn’t be able to go to public school. You wouldn't have a town library where you can check out books for free. You also wouldn't have roads to drive on or garbage pick-up to take away your trash. In your community, taxes pay police officers and firefighters to keep you safe. Taxes also maintain local parks and provide clean water to drink. Being able to earn an income helps you buy the things you want and need. Paying taxes contributes to the well-being of your community, state, and country.

title: Shadows by Day
text:
Draw a time …

… when you had to change your schedule or plans because it got dark outside sooner than you expected. Discuss why you think this happened with a partner.

Shadows form when the light from a light source, like the sun, is blocked. Shadows created by the sun change throughout the day. This is because the sun moves across the sky in an arch, rising in the east and setting in the west. But in reality, the sun isn’t moving; the Earth is! Imagine a line that goes from the North Pole, straight through Earth’s center, to the South Pole. The planet rotates, like a top, around this line. This line is called the Earth’s axis. One rotation of the Earth on its axis takes 24 hours, or one day. As the Earth turns, one side is always facing toward the sun and the other side is always facing away from the sun. This creates day and night. When the Earth rotates toward the sun, the rising sun creates long shadows. Over the course of the day, the shadows grow shorter, then longer again as the sun sets. All the while, the shadows are moving in the opposite direction as the sun. When the Earth turns away from the sun, shadows disappear and night falls.

The axis of the Earth also changes the sun’s position in the sky throughout the year, but this isn’t caused by the planet’s rotation. Earth not only rotates but also moves around the sun. Its pathway, or orbit, is an almost circular trip that lasts one year (365 days). When the Earth travels around the sun, it is revolving, or completing a revolution. We can observe this pattern in the shadows on Earth as well. At certain times of the year, the sun reaches its highest point in the sky. This creates shorter shadows and longer days. In the opposite months, the sun never hits its peak. The days are short and the sun stays low, forming longer shadows.

title: Night Lights
text:
Listen to your teacher read the article aloud. Be sure to follow the listening strategies.

Listening Strategies:

Set a purpose for reading.

Listen for key words.

Take notes by writing or drawing.

Our planet’s movement gives us Earthlings quite the show. During the day, the sun appears to move across the sky, creating shadows and magnificent colors at sunrise and sunset. At night, the Earth turns away from the sun, offering a brilliant display of objects in space.

Our planet completes one rotation per day. When the Earth is facing the sun in its rotation, it’s daytime. The sun is the only star in our daytime sky that we can see. As the Earth rotates, it begins to face away from the sun, allowing other stars to come into view. Daily, constellations rise in the east and set in the west. What else follows this pattern?

Our planet also completes one revolution around the sun every 365 days. That means Earth is in a different position in space each day. Although the difference in its position from day to day is very small, the difference in its position from season to season is much bigger and more noticeable. In December, the Earth is located on the opposite side of the sun as it is in June. Therefore, the constellations that are visible in December are different from the ones visible in June. From night to night, the sky may look the same, but it’s not. The constellations are constantly shifting. These changes become more obvious with each passing month and season.

The stars aren’t the only celestial objects that follow observable patterns. The moon shines brightly almost every night. It follows a pattern too! The moon, like the sun, seems to rise in the east and set in the west. But unlike the sun, the moon is actually moving. It travels in an orbit around the Earth. Each revolution of the moon takes about 28 days. Like the Earth, the moon changes position as it revolves. Its position, as well as the sun’s and Earth’s positions, affects its shape both daily and monthly.

The next time you’re out at night, remember to look for patterns in the sky!

title: What Is Culture?
text: Culture is the beliefs, traditions, and celebrations of a group of people. There are many characteristics of culture. Architecture, arts, literature, music, and language are some. Religion, clothing, and food are others. Culture reflects a group’s way of life. It includes things they produce and use. It also includes the skills and traditions passed down to younger generations. People use resources around them to meet their needs. Local plant and animal resources are used to make food, clothing, and shelter. A group’s culture develops using these resources.

title: Language
text: Language is an important part of culture. When people move, they bring their languages with them. For example, explorers from Spain traveled around the world. Now, people speak Spanish all over the world. Early pilgrims to the United States spoke English. American Indian populations in these places now speak English as well as their native languages. Another example is the French language. It is an official language in 29 countries. The movement of language impacts culture.

title: Celebrations
text: One way people express culture is through celebrations. Geography influences how people celebrate and what the celebration is about. Some cultures celebrate the seasons. Other cultures celebrate planting and harvesting crops. As people move from place to place, they bring their cultures and celebrations with them.

title: Religion
text: Religion is another part of culture. Religion is a system of beliefs that a group of people share. Different cultures have different religions. Five worldwide religions are Buddhism, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Christianity. There are many other important religions throughout the world. Religion impacts culture in the ways that people celebrate.

title: Clothing
text: Environments people live in affect the way they dress. People in hot climates wear lightweight clothing to keep cool. People in colder climates wear heavy clothing to keep warm. The material of clothing reflects local resources. Grasses, palm fronds, pigskin, and cloth made from natural fibers are some things people use. Dye for cloth can be made from local plants. Traditional or ceremonial clothing is often very well made and decorated. It reflects the traditional skills of the people.

title: Patriot Day

title: Ethnic Celebrations
text: Our country has many ethnic groups. Each group has a unique culture. They have different foods and celebrations. They have different histories, traditions, and beliefs. There are many ways to learn more about different ethnic groups. It is important to respect their culture. You can attend their celebrations. You can join them to eat their traditional foods. You can listen to their stories.

title: Birthday Celebrations
text: Cultures have different birthday traditions. Some celebrate birthdays with a cake and gifts. Others celebrate with traditional foods. Some birthdays have piñatas. Some have birthday songs. In Mexico, they sing "Las Mañanitas." In the U.S., we sing "Happy Birthday."

title: New Year Celebrations
text: Many countries celebrate the new year. In the U.S., we celebrate New Year's Day. It is on January 1. The Lunar New Year is celebrated in East Asia. Jews celebrate Rosh Hashanah. Diwali is celebrated in India.

title: Celebrating the Seasons
text: Many people celebrate the change of seasons. They have different seasonal holidays. They celebrate winter holidays. The fall season is celebrated with harvest festivals. Summer and spring are also celebrated by many.

title: Plant Structures
text:

Directions: Read the two articles and use the text as evidence to answer the comprehension questions.

External Structures

Have you ever wondered why plants look so different from one another? Why do some plants have thorns while other plants have bark? Why do some plants have colorful petals while others have colorful fruit?

Plants have external structures just like animals. These structures support their ability to survive, reproduce, grow, and behave. Depending on the environment in which a plant lives, their external structures will vary to provide the most support.

Plants have four main external structures:

a root system

a stem or trunk and branches

leaves

a reproductive structure such as a flower, fruit, or cone

A root system absorbs water and nutrients that the plant needs for survival and growth. Root systems also help anchor the plant to the earth and provide support against environmental factors such as weather and predators. Root systems vary from plant to plant depending on the environment. Some root systems stay near the surface, while other root systems reach deep into the ground.

The stem or trunk and the branches of a plant provide support for the plant. Supporting the plant is very important. The stems or trunks and branches of plants are usually protected with sharp hairs, thorns, spines, or bark. Some plants may also have a coating that is slimy or waxy to defend against predators. The stem, trunk, and branches have internal structures as well, such as tubes. These help deliver nutrients and water throughout the plant.

A leaf has several purposes. A leaf provides food for the plant using sunlight. Leaves also act like lungs in animals do. They exchange air and help the plant breathe. Leaves can also sweat. This helps the plant get rid of any extra water. The stems, trunks, or branches on a plant protect the leaves.

Plants reproduce, or create new plants, using flowers and fruit or cones. They use the fruit or cone to create pollen or seeds. The flower, which is made up of colorful petals, will attract insects or birds to help the plant spread the pollen or seeds.

These external structures work together with internal structures to help the plant. The main internal structures of a plant are structures it uses for reproduction.

Internal Structures

Internal structures that help in plant reproduction are found in the flower. The stamen is a small stalk that produces pollen at the top. This is the male part of a plant. Plants usually have a few stamens.

Another internal structure is the pistil, which is the female part of the plant. It is usually found in the center of the flower.

Pollen travels from the stamen to the pistil and starts to make a seed. Some plants will produce a fruit or cone as a covering for the seed. Fruits and cones protect the seeds and allow them to grow before they are released. Once they’re free, the seeds will begin to grow into new plants.

Plants also have tubes in the stems and branches. These tubes help the plant transport nutrients throughout the plant.

Comprehension Questions

What might happen if one structure fails?

title: Phenomenon Explanation
text:
Ponderosa pine tree

Ponderosa pine trees have a widespread root system with one main deep root to collect nutrients and water. Their trunks are covered in a thick bark to protect against cold weather, diseases, and predators. The ponderosa pine tree has branches that curve down so that snow can fall off of them. Their pine needles serve the same function as leaves, providing food for the tree from sunlight and exchanging air. Ponderosa pine trees produce both male and female pine cones. The male pine cone contains pollen, which it releases in early spring. The pollen attaches to the female pine cone, which is where the seed forms. The pine cone protects the seeds from predators and the weather until they are ready to be planted.

Black bear

Black bears have thick black fur to protect them from cold weather and strong hind legs, which they use to stand up so they can smell, hear, or see better. Black bears also have short, curved claws, which they use for climbing trees to find food or escape danger. They also use them to pull apart rotten logs to find insects. Black bears find their food with a keen sense of smell and excellent eyesight. Black bears can see in color and in detail up close. Black bears have different kinds of teeth that they use for eating both plants and animals. Black bears have an excellent memory when it comes to finding food and remembering where food sources are located. This helps their stomachs stay full as they prepare for hibernation.

Using evidence from the diagrams, phenomenon video, and observations you have made throughout the unit, make a claim about the external and internal structures of the black bear and ponderosa pine tree and how these structures may or may not support their survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction.

title: Animal Senses
text:
Directions: Read the article. Use the text as evidence to answer the questions. Then complete the "Animal Senses Sort" activity.

Have you ever watched an animal? Maybe you observed a pet such as a dog or cat. Maybe you have watched an animal outside your window, like a bird, deer, or squirrel. While you were observing this animal, you probably noticed that it was constantly moving, looking around, and possibly twitching its ears or nose.

Why do animals move around so much? Why do they always seem to be looking around or twitching their ears? Why are animals often seen sniffing the air or ground? All of these behaviors are signs that animals are using their five senses.

Animals have five senses, just like humans. They have the ability to hear, see, taste, touch, and smell. Animals use their senses to gather information about their surroundings. They can also pick up on changes in the weather and temperature!

An animal that is constantly looking around may be scanning the area for predators, prey, or food sources. Animals that move their ears around are listening for any noises in the surrounding area. They may be listening for predators, prey, or other members of their pack or family. Animals that sniff the air or ground are trying to pick up odors or smells. They may be trying to track other animals or find a travel route. Animals will also taste different types of plants, vegetables, or fruits to find a new food source. Animals gather all sorts of information from their surroundings using their senses!

The next time you observe an animal, pay close attention to which senses they are using. Try to figure out what kind of information the animal may be gathering.

title: Sensory Receptors and the Brain
text:
Clementine Investigation

Draw how you used your sense of smell to know that this object was a clementine.

Directions: Read the article about animal senses. Then use the text as evidence to answer the questions.

Animals have five senses. They have the ability to hear, see, smell, taste, and touch. But how do these five senses work? Animals have specialized parts in their bodies that respond to information in their environments. These are called sensory receptors. The nose, mouth, eyes, skin, and ears all have sensory receptors. These specialized parts of an animal's body are able to pick up on information in the environment. This includes light and shadows, smells, sounds, types of tastes such as bitter or sweet, and feelings such as hot and cold or soft and hard. When a sensory receptor picks up a piece of information, it sends the information to the brain. If the brain recognizes the information, it makes a decision on what behavior the animal should have next based on past experiences. If the information coming to the brain is new, the brain makes the best decision it can. It then stores the information as a memory.

Let’s examine how this works. A bear is hungry and looking for food. The bear sees a brown piece of fruit. The bear’s eyes, or sight receptors, have picked up this information of brown-colored fruit. The information is sent to the bear’s brain. In the bear's brain, a memory is triggered. The bear remembers the last time it ate brown fruit. It tasted sour and rotten. The bear's brain decides that the bear should not eat the fruit. The bear keeps looking for food.

In this example, the bear's sight receptors and brain worked as a system to come up with the best behavior the bear should have in response to brown fruit. If the bear did not have the memory of eating rotten food, the bear may have eaten it and created a new memory. The bear would use the memory in future situations.

Animals use their senses and sensory receptors to gather information from the environment. They send this information to the brain. Then, they respond to that information in a way that supports their survival.

Comprehension Questions

What is a sensory receptor?

What kinds of information do sensory receptors collect from the environment?

What happens once a sensory receptor detects a piece of information?

What does the brain do once it receives information? How does the brain decide what to do?

How do the sensory receptors, brain, and behavior of an animal work together as a system?

title: Mexico’s Physical and Human Features
text:
Mexico is the northernmost country of Latin America. It is very rich in history. The ruins of ancient civilizations attract many tourists. There are many cities that attract visitors. Mexico City is the city where the most people live. In fact, more people live in Mexico City than in any other city in North America. The warm, sandy beaches bring many tourists as well.

Mexico has water on two sides. The northern border is shared with the United States. Guatemala and Belize lie to the southeast. Mexico has mountains and volcanoes. The Sierra Madre Occidental and the Sierra Madre Oriental are two mountain ranges in Mexico. Mexico also has high and rolling plateaus. It has tropical rain forests, dry deserts, and fertile valleys.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe Mexico?

title: Mexico’s Climates
text:
The climate in Mexico ranges from a dry climate to a tropical climate. There are big differences in these climates. Some are very wet, and some are very dry. Mexico is divided into three main climates. This is what each climate is like:

Tropical

The average temperature is above 77 degrees Fahrenheit. The average yearly rainfall is about 50 inches.

Temperate

The average temperature is 64 to 77 degrees Fahrenheit. The average yearly rainfall is about 25 inches.

Dry

The average temperatures of a dry climate vary. Some places are very cold, and some are very hot. The dry climate has little rain.

title: Mexico’s Biomes
text: There are different climates in Mexico. This means there is a wide variety of plants and animals living there. There are forests in the forest biome of Mexico. One of the most famous animals in Mexico is the monarch butterfly. Every year, millions of monarch butterflies migrate to Mexico. The butterflies hibernate in the forest for the winter. Some of these forests have pine trees and bears. Some of these forests are rainforests that have huge, broadleaf trees and monkeys. Rabbits, snakes, and scorpions live in the sandy desert biomes of Mexico. Whales, rays, and tropical fish are some of the many animals that live in Mexico’s oceans.

title: Mexico’s Natural Resources
text: Mexico is rich in natural resources. Some of its biggest natural resources are silver, copper, oil, and agricultural products. Agriculture is the business of growing crops and raising livestock. Mexico has a diversity of agricultural crops. The biggest produce market in North America is in Mexico. The United States gets much of its produce from Mexico. Some of Mexico’s main crops are corn, tomatoes, and chili peppers. Mexico has two special crops that are rarely grown outside of the country. They are called maguey and henequen. They are both kinds of agave plants. Mexico also has some highly productive oil fields. Oil is an important natural resource. A lot of oil is used to make fuel for cars.

title: Mexico's Landmarks
text:
One very famous place in Mexico is called Teotihuacán. The name means “The City of the Gods” in the Aztec language. However, the city was not built by the Aztec people. It was built by a much older culture whose name no one knows. The city was built about 2,000 years ago. About 200,000 people lived in this city, making it one of the largest cities in the world at the time. The city has several pyramids, but the largest is the Pyramid of the Sun. This pyramid is one of the largest in North America. It is 216 feet tall. This city is one of Mexico’s ancient man-made landmarks.

Did you know that Mexico is home to the world’s largest underground river system? The Sac Actun river system is 95 miles long. It flows through a maze of underground limestone caves. These caves can be accessed by holes in the earth called cenotes. There are over 100 cenotes leading to the river system. The Mayan people used cenotes for all of their water needs. Cenotes are one of Mexico’s natural landmarks.

title: Mexico: Mixed Cultures
text:
Mexico was and is home to many Native American people. The Maya were one of the early peoples. They built large pyramids. Many of these pyramids still stand today. The Aztecs were one of the later Native American peoples. The Aztecs once lived in a large city that is now the capital city of the country, Mexico City. The Aztecs were conquered by Spanish explorers from Europe in the 1500s. Many Spanish people moved to Mexico after this time. The cultures of the Native Americans and the Spanish Europeans mixed. Many Mexican people are mestizos. Mestizo means having a mix of Native American and Spanish heritage.

Language

Spanish is the official language of Mexico. However, there are more than 50 Native American languages in Mexico. These languages are still spoken today.

Food

Mexico’s food is a mix of Spanish and Native American food. Corn, beans, and squash were eaten by the Native Americans. They are still eaten by Mexicans today. Rice, beef, and onions were brought to Mexico by the Spanish. They are also still eaten by Mexicans today.

title: What Is a Region?
text:
We organize the Earth into regions to help us to learn about our world. A region is an area that has similar characteristics. Some regions are organized based on their physical features, such as landforms, climate, or biomes. Some regions are organized by their human features, like population, culture, or language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

The United States is often divided into five regions. These regions are organized based on state political boundaries. They are the Northeast, the Southeast, the Midwest, the Southwest, and the West.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe regions of the United States?

title: The Northeast
text:
Physical features

The landforms of the Northeast include highlands, mountains, and plains. The Green Mountains and the White Mountains in this region are part of the Appalachian Mountains. Niagara Falls and the Adirondack Mountains are also landforms in the region. The Atlantic Ocean, Lake Erie, the Hudson and Androscoggin Rivers are some of the bodies of water in the Northeast.

Human Features

The Northeast Region has some famous human features as well. One World Trade Center, which is 1,776 feet high, is in this region. The Erie Canal and the Statue of Liberty are also here.

Climate and Biomes

Winters are cold in the Northeast. Summers, however, are warm or hot. The region gets a lot of precipitation. Pines and chestnut oak trees abound in the region. Some of the animals found there are black bears, red foxes, white-tailed deer, and chipmunks.

Natural Resources

Natural resources like lumber, granite, and coal are abundant in the Northeast. Other resources there include seafood, maple trees, and quartz.

Culture

The Northeast Region is diverse in culture. Food, clothing, arts, and celebrations from all over the world can be seen in the Northeast. Native American culture still thrives in some parts of the region.

title: The Southeast
text:
Physical features

Mountains, wetlands, plains, highlands, and plateaus are some of the physical features of the Southeast Region. The Smoky Mountains and the Okefenokee Swamp are both in this region. The bodies of water in the region include the Gulf of America and the Atlantic Ocean. There are also rivers, lakes, and streams.

Human Features

The human features of the Southeast Region include large cities with big industrial areas. There are also agricultural areas and large shopping centers. Walt Disney World, The Mercedes-Benz SuperDome, and Cape Lookout Lighthouse are found in this region.

Climate and Biomes

Although winters are mild in the region, summers are hot. It rains a lot. However, there are times when the region experiences drought. Citrus, pines, and hardwood trees are some of the plants that grow in the region. Panthers and alligators thrive in the swamps. Other wildlife commonly found in the region are salamanders, bats, and black bears.

Natural Resources

The region has soil that is rich in minerals. Peanuts, cotton, and sugar cane grow well in the region. Other natural resources include oil and natural gas, coal, and seafood.

Culture

The culture of the Southeast Region is diverse. It grew out of African American, European, Cajun, and Hispanic cultures. Today, there are cultures from all over the world in the Southeast Region.

d

title: The Midwest
text:
Physical Features

There are 12 states in the Midwest. Peninsulas, the Great Plains, and highlands make the Midwest unique. Part of the Ozark Mountains is in this region. So are the Badlands. The bodies of water in the region include four of the Great Lakes. Many rivers also flow through the region, including the Mississippi River.

Human Features

Three of the human features of the Midwest are the Mackinac Bridge, the Soo Locks, and Mount Rushmore. There are also large residential, industrial, commercial, and agricultural areas.

Climate and Biomes

Climate in the region varies from east to west. The western part of the Midwest is drier. Winters in the region are mostly cold. Summers are hot or warm. There are not a lot of forests in the Midwest. There are, however, many types of grass and shrubs. Mesquite and sagebrush are common in this region. Wildlife found in the region includes bison, elk, wolves, black bears, prairie dogs, and white pelicans.

Natural Resources

The Midwest has a lot of natural resources. The soil is rich. There is also an abundance of water. Coal, oil, natural gas, and precious metals are other natural resources in the Midwest.

Culture

The Midwest has people from all over the world. Native American culture was the first to grow in the Midwest. Many Europeans came later and brought their culture. Each group from Europe brought its own style of building. Languages from different parts of the world can be heard in the region. Food, celebrations, and art come from all over the world.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe regions of the United States?

title: The Southwest
text:
Physical Features

The Southwest Region covers Arizona, Oklahoma, New Mexico, and Texas. The Gulf of America is one of the main bodies of water in the region. The Santa Cruz River, the Gila River, and the Colorado River also flow through the region. There are lakes and streams as well.

The region has plains, plateaus, highlands, mountains, and deserts. The Grand Canyon, the Petrified Forest, and the White Sands are in this region.

Human Features

Some examples of human features in the region are the Alamo and Pueblo-style houses. The region also has dams and reservoirs, like Coolidge Dam and Elephant Butte Reservoir. They help provide power and water to people in this region.

Climate and Biomes

Much of the Southwest is very hot in the summer and warm in the winter. The mountainous areas get colder. Much of the Southwest gets very little rain or snow. Plants that grow here are mostly shrubs and brushes. However, there are yucca and cactus plants. There are also juniper and evergreen oak trees. Some of the animals that survive conditions in the region are the Gila monster, glossy snake, and Albert’s squirrel. There are black bears, elk, and bighorn sheep as well.

Natural Resources

The main resources of the Southwest Region are oil, natural gas, coal, and uranium. The soil is also good for raising some crops and cattle.

Culture

Native American and Spanish cultures are common in the region. People from all over the world have brought their culture to the region. However, place names, celebrations, food, and agriculture show a lot of Native American and Spanish influence.

title: The West
text:
Physical Features

The West has mountains, volcanoes, plains, highlands, and waterfalls. Mount Saint Helens, the Rocky Mountains, Bryce Canyon, Pikes Peak, and Redwood Forest are in this region. Earthquakes sometimes occur here. Bodies of water in the region include the Pacific Ocean, the Great Salt Lake, the Colorado River, and the Yukon River.

Human Features

Some of the human features here are the Hoover Dam, the Space Needle, and the Golden Gate Bridge.

Climate and Biomes

The West has many different climates. The northern part is usually very wet and the southern part is usually very dry. The temperature is warm year-round in one part of the region. In another part, it is cold year-round. Plants found in the region include coconut palms, cedar, redwood, and Joshua trees. Animals like whales, caribou, and moose thrive in the West Region. So do animals like mountain lions, bears, monk seals, and nene geese.

Natural Resources

The diverse soils in the region produce pineapples, potatoes, and apples. The Pacific Ocean provides seafood. Other natural resources in the West include lumber, oil, natural gas, and precious minerals.

Culture

Native American culture is the first to have grown in this region. It can still be felt in the names of places and animals. However, cultures from all over the world are also present. There are pieces of art, music, food, and celebrations from all over the world.

title: Human Features
text: In addition to physical features, we also describe places using human features. The human features of a place are a result of people’s ideas, choices, and actions as they interact with the physical environment. They are the things that are made or built by humans. Where people live, the kinds of houses they build, the kind of work they engage in, and the activities they do for fun are the human features of a place. Bridges, factories, buildings, and parks are also human features.

title: Essential Question
text: What are human features of places?

title: Political Features
text: Political features, including cities, states, and countries, are organized by where people live. These can be seen on a political map. Many people in the world live in cities. Cities are organized into states. States come together to form a country. Political maps show the borders of cities, states, and countries. A political map can also show how some borders have been created using the physical features near them. For example, oceans, rivers, and mountain ranges can also create borders of countries or states. These borders help us by showing where one area stops and a new one begins.

title: Population
text:
Population tells us how many people live in a certain area. Look at the population map of North America. Can you find Mexico City in Mexico? This city has the largest population in all of North America.

By looking at the map colors and the map key, we can see that the United States is the most populated country in North America. More than half of the people who live in North America live in the United States.

Canada is the biggest country when it comes to square feet, but it has a smaller population than Mexico or the United States.

The populations of the Caribbean island nations are much smaller individually. If you count all the Caribbean region together, the total population is higher than Canada’s.

title: Man-Made Landmarks
text:
Man-made landmarks are different from landforms. They are things like buildings, statues, towers, and walls. Man-made landmarks are well-known places. They are often used to help people know where they are. This means they can be used to give directions.

Take a look at the list of man-made landmarks in North America. Use one symbol to mark the ones you have heard of or seen. Use a different symbol to mark the ones you would like to know more about.

title: Settlement
text:
People move for different reasons. Throughout history, people have explored new places to find resources. Most people move to places they already know about. For example, many people from Europe moved to North America after explorers traveled here. We call this kind of movement from one place to another migration.

A number of factors affect where people settle. The climate plays an important role. The amount and types of resources available are also important. Historically, communities grew around water and other important resources. Water is necessary for people to survive. It is needed for growing food and for transportation. Places with more resources can support larger populations.

title: Essential Question
text: How does the environment influence settlement patterns?

title: A World at War
text:
In 1754, England, France, and many Native American tribes of the Iroquois and Wabanaki Confederacies went to war over control of a vast amount of important land in North America. They fought over the Great Lakes, Ohio River Valley, and St. Lawrence River. The states of Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan, Indiana, and the provinces of Quebec and Ontario represent this area today. The land was very valuable for farming, hunting, timber, and furs for the fur trade.

The French armies were much smaller than those of the British. The majority of Native American tribes sided with the French, and in many battles, the Native American warriors outnumbered their French allies. The French and Native American alliance won many of the early battles in the war. The tribal warriors knew the land better, and their style of fighting was more efficient than the British fighting style. They were able to surprise the British in many attacks. Also, the Native American warriors were very brave and fought well.

This war was fought in several different theaters. A “theater of operations” is the military term referring to land and sea areas that are invaded or defended during a war. The American theater of this war is called the French and Indian War because battles were fought between England, France, and their Native American allies.

In 1756, the war spilled over into Europe, Africa, and even Asia. This theater of the war is referred to as the Seven Years’ War. The major powers of Europe scrambled to create alliances to oppose their enemies. Great Britain allied with Prussia, Portugal, and several other smaller central European countries. The French formed an alliance with Austria, Russia, Spain, Sweden, Saxony, and the Mughal Empire of Asia.

In 1759, the tide of war began to turn in North America. The British captured the Canadian city of Quebec. Another factor for British success was that French allied Native American warriors were catching deadly diseases, like smallpox. Great Britain and its allies won several key victories in Europe against Spain, Russia, and Austria. In 1760, the Iroquois joined forces with the British. The Iroquois were old enemies to the Odawa, Ojibway, Potawatomi, and Huron, but the Iroquois had large war parties that helped the English army. The war ended with the French surrender of Montreal in 1760. Fighting in Europe came to an end in November 1762.

The Treaty of Paris in 1763 officially ended the war between England, France, and their allies. A treaty is a formal document that creates an agreement between two nations.

The French gave up all their land in North America east of the Mississippi River. However, France was allowed to keep the city of New Orleans as part of its colonial holdings. During the war, British forces captured Havana, Cuba. Havana was Spain’s busiest port in the Americas. The Spanish agreed to cede the colony of Florida to the British in exchange for Havana. With this exchange, the British gained all territory east of the Mississippi River.

After taking possession of Florida, the British felt the territory was too large to govern as one colony. They divided the colony into two colonies, which they named East Florida and West Florida. The territory of East Florida extended along the panhandle from the Atlantic Ocean to the Apalachicola River. West Florida extended along the panhandle from the Mississippi River and the Apalachicola River. St. Augustine was named the capital of East Florida, and Pensacola became the capital of West Florida.

West Florida was largely forgotten by the British. The soil in West Florida was not good for farming. Thick pine forests also made it difficult to clear the land for farming and building large settlements. Furthermore, there were fewer settlements in this area of Florida. The British focused their attention on expanding their interests in East Florida. The British governor of East Florida, James Grant, offered land grants to British colonists who agreed to settle and establish farms in East Florida. Many colonists from Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, and other British colonies settled in the area during this time.

The new government of Florida also legalized slavery, which encouraged plantation owners to migrate to the new colony. Large plantations and small farms were established by new settlers. They grew various crops, including cotton, rice, citrus fruit, and sugarcane. The government of East Florida also established trade networks with the Native American tribes of the territory. British East Florida thrived, and even West Florida grew into an important military outpost. However, British control of Florida was short-lived. Control of the colony would change hands again just 20 years after the British obtained the colony from Spain.

title: The American Revolution
text:
The Treaty of Paris in 1763 officially ended the war between England, France, and their many allies. After the war, France and Spain gave lands they had claimed to England. Many British colonists took advantage of the new lands. The British Parliament realized it didn’t have enough money in the treasury to pay for war expenses. Raising taxes, creating new taxes, and collecting taxes were the only ways the government could get enough. Because the war had been fought to protect the colonies, Parliament decided that the colonists were responsible for paying the war debt. Following the French and Indian War, many British soldiers remained in the colonies to enforce the new taxes placed on the colonists.

Some British officers noticed that the colonists weren’t paying their taxes. The officers let Parliament know. Many colonial merchants wouldn’t pay the taxes at the harbors on goods coming in from Great Britain. Some colonists smuggled goods into their warehouses. They bribed tax collectors to look the other way. Parliament was not happy with the colonists and decided this could not continue. Over the next few years, Parliament created laws, known as Acts, to collect taxes.

From 1764 to 1770, various levels of conflict rose between Parliament and the colonists. Parliament felt it was within its right to tax the colonists based on the cost of keeping them safe during the French and Indian War. The colonists felt differently. Some colonists felt they should pay the various taxes. Others felt that the taxes and Parliament’s actions weren’t fair. Many colonists did not believe that Parliament treated the colonists as British citizens.

Many colonists wanted to have direct representation in Parliament where decisions were made and taxes were created. Parliament was supposed to represent all British citizens, but it claimed the colonies did not need representation. “No taxation without representation!” became the repetitive answer from the colonists to each of Parliament’s actions.

At first, communication between all the groups (Parliament, King George III, colonial legislatures, and the people) was very open. As the decade and actions of Parliament continued, communication between all parties broke down. As communication decreased, conflict increased. The conflict between the colonies and Parliament led to open rebellion and the American Revolution.

Timeline of the American Revolution

1764 to 1767: Parliament passed multiple acts that restricted trade, required the colonies to pay additional taxes on certain goods, such as paint, paper, glass, lead, and tea, and provide food and lodging for British troops. As a result, many colonists began to actively boycott, or refuse to buy, British goods.

1768 to 1769: Parliament suspended multiple colonial assemblies for opposing British policy and boycotting British goods.

March 5, 1770: Boston Massacre: Colonial civilians were shot and killed by British soldiers.

1773: Parliament passed the Tea Act to tax tea in the colonies.

Dec. 16, 1773: Colonists in Boston dumped crates of British tea into Boston Harbor to protest the tea tax.

May to June 1774: Parliament passed the Coercive Acts in response to the Boston Tea Party.

September 5 to Oct. 26, 1774: Colonial delegates met in Philadelphia at the First Continental Congress. Congress urged the colonists to defy the Coercive Acts and form militias. Delegates drafted a petition to King George III in response to the Coercive Acts.

April 1775: The first shots of the American Revolution were fired at the battles of Lexington and Concord.

May to July 1775: Delegates met again in Philadelphia for the Second Continental Congress. During their meeting, delegates received word of the Battle of Bunker Hill, which was fought outside of Boston between colonial and British forces. After this battle, Congress formed the Continental Army and appointed George Washington as commander of all colonial forces. Congress drafted a petition to send to the king to avoid going to war.

December 1775: In response to the colonial petition, Parliament banned trade with the colonies.

July 1776: Congressional delegates wrote and signed the Declaration of Independence. The Declaration of Independence listed the grievances, or issues, that the colonists had with the British government. It also stated that if the king could not address these grievances, the colonists would dissolve all ties with Great Britain and form their own country. East and West Florida remained loyal to the British government.

December 1776 to January 1777: The battles of Trenton and Princeton were fought in New Jersey, resulting in the first major Continental victory.

October 1777: Patriot forces surrounded British troops near Saratoga, New York, and won a decisive victory. This victory helped persuade the French to join the Patriot cause.

December 1777 to March 1778: Washington and the Continental Army wintered at Valley Forge near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. This was a difficult time for the Continental Army. They were undersupplied. Almost 2,000 soldiers died from disease, while many others deserted and went home. Washington and his foreign allies worked hard to turn the ragtag Continental forces into a professional army before the spring of 1778.

June 1779: Spain joined the American Revolution, creating an alliance with the American colonists and the French. In exchange for their support, the Spanish hoped to regain control of Florida and other colonies that they lost as a result of the Seven Years’ War.

September 1780: Patriot forces defeated British and Loyalist troops at Kings Mountain near the border of North and South Carolina. The American victory forced British troops to retreat into South Carolina and prevented them from advancing farther north into Virginia.

May 1781: Spanish forces under the command of Bernardo de Gálvez captured Pensacola and drove the British out of the territory.

Oct. 19, 1781: British General Cornwallis surrendered to General George Washington at Yorktown, Virginia. His defeat meant that the entire British Army was beaten.
