title: What Is Research?
text:
Research means studying something thoroughly. There are many steps in research. These include asking questions, gathering answers, organizing information, and presenting ideas. When you are doing research, start with questions. You need to figure out what you want to know. This means you need to ask questions. Then, you begin seeking answers. You gather information to answer your questions. Next, you need to organize the information. This means presenting your information in a way that others can understand easily.

Let’s practice. Your challenge is to investigate how people perceive places. Perceive means how people see or think about something. An example is what someone thinks about America. People may form these opinions by talking to Americans, listening to the news, or reading stories, poems, or legends.

How might you research what people perceive?

title: Essential Question
text: How do people view places?

title: Ask Questions
text:
Questions help you focus your research. For example, your research question is: How do people view a place? Your first question would be: Which place? Let’s research how people perceive Florida.

Questions also help you decide what information you need to look for. What questions could you ask to help you answer your research question?

title: Gather Answers
text:
There are many primary and secondary sources you can use to find information. There are books, journals, and images. You can also use technology and maps. Artifacts and information at museums may also help. In addition, you can interview someone who knows about your topic.

The best way to understand an issue is to use several sources and perspectives to research it. Look for sources that are credible and reliable. A credible source is unbiased and backed by evidence. A reliable source is something you can trust to be accurate. It is also important that your source is relevant, or related to the topic you want to learn about.

title: Organize Information
text:
After you have gathered your information, you need to organize your ideas. This means you put the information in order. You need to decide which information is important. What is fact? What is an opinion? Be sure the information is useful. Your information should help you answer your questions.

Write out all your main ideas. Create an outline of the main ideas. Put them in an order that is clear. Then, write or present your information in that order. Add supporting details or examples to each main point.

title: Present Your Information
text:
Once your information is organized, you need to decide how to present it. Think about the sources you have gathered. Could you use charts, tables, maps, or graphs to organize and present your information clearly? Also consider using stories, pictures, and artifacts. What would make your presentation interesting and informative? Will you create a written or oral presentation?

Brainstorm how to share the information you have found. Use a separate piece of paper to write down your resources and make a plan.

title: We Share Cultures
text: Sometimes, the United States is called a "Melting Pot" or a "Salad Bowl." In a melting pot, ingredients mix and combine together. The United States is full of lots of different cultures and types of people. They all combine to make one united country.

title: Human Features
text: Human features include the number of people who live in a place and their ideas. People make choices about where to live. They use their ideas to build the place. People make choices on how to meet their basic needs. They meet their needs by using the physical features of the place. The way people build their homes is part of the human features of a place. So are the clothes they wear and the foods they eat. A new park in your neighborhood is a human feature. Our transportation systems are, too. Human features tell us about people and culture.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe where I live?

title: Political Maps
text: Many people in the world live in cities. Political maps show the borders of cities and states. Political maps also show us where each country is. Political maps show us where one border stops and a new one begins.

title: What Is a Country?
text: What is a country? A country is a place that has its own flag. However, states have their own flags, too. A country has a capital city. States have capital cities as well. What is different about a country, then? A country is an area of land that has its own government, and nobody controls it from the outside. It also has a leader who is not controlled by anybody from outside. Most countries have their own money. The United States, Mexico, and Canada are all countries. So are some of the nations in the Caribbean.

title: Your Ancestors Shared Their Cultures
text: As people moved to the United States, they brought new ways of doing things. They shared new food, languages, and much more with each other. Now we can all enjoy the cultures our ancestors brought with them.

title: What Is a Capital City?
text:
A capital city is the location where a state or country's government meets to work. It is the most important city in a country or state. It is where you can find the government leaders. On maps, capital cities are often represented by stars. The capital city of the United States is Washington, D.C. States have capital cities, too. The capital city of Florida is Tallahassee.

Look at the map. Find Canada and Mexico. What are their capital cities? Can you find other capital cities?

title: Land Use
text:
Land use is a human feature. Land can be used for different purposes.

Communities where people live are called residential. Residential areas have houses, apartments, and schools.

Some areas of land are labeled as industrial. Industrial areas are where people make things. Warehouses, factories, and storage buildings are found in these areas.

Commercial areas are used for services. Gas stations, grocery stores, and hotels are found in commercial areas.

Recreational areas are where people play, relax, or do sports. Parks, swimming pools, and lakes are recreational areas.

Agricultural land is used for growing crops and raising animals. Crops and animals depend on temperature, rainfall, and soil. Access to clean water is very important to agricultural communities.

title: Why Do People Move?
text:
In geography, people study movement. This means studying how people, resources, and ideas move. People move for many reasons.

Sometimes people choose to move. Pull factors are the good things that attract people to a place. Pull factors are things like better jobs or education. Other pull factors are safety or more resources for a better life.

Sometimes people move because they have to. Push factors are the bad things that make people leave a place. Some push factors are war, natural disasters, and religious persecution.

title: Essential Question
text: Why do people move?

title: Exploration
text: People have explored new places throughout history. Many people went looking for resources. Others wanted to expand their empires. Some wanted to share their religion. Exploration is traveling to learn about an unfamiliar place.

title: Settlement
text: People choose to live in certain areas. These settlements depend on the physical environment. They also depend on the availability of natural resources. People settle in places that make life better for them. Traditionally, communities have grown around water and other important resources. Water is necessary for people to survive. It is important for growing food and for transportation. Where there are more resources, the population grows.

title: Migration
text:
Most people move to a place they already know about. Many early settlers in North America were from Europe. They moved after explorers traveled here. We call the movement from one place to another migration.

New transportation has made moving much easier. People move across the world or country for a new job. Migrant workers are people who move wherever the jobs are. College students often move when they go to school.

Migration is one way people, ideas, and materials move.

title: What Is a Region?
text:
We organize the Earth into regions. This helps us learn about our world. A region is an area with common features. Some regions are organized by physical features. Landforms and climate are physical features. Some regions are organized by their human features. These include population and culture.

The United States is often divided into five regions. These regions are based on location and state boundaries. They are the Northeast, the Southeast, the Midwest, the Southwest, and the West.

title: Essential Question
text: What is a region?

title: The Northeast
text:
Physical Features

There are 11 states in the Northeast Region of the United States. Many of the states have beaches along the Atlantic Ocean. There are also rivers, lakes, streams, waterfalls, and mountains in the region. The Northeast has a temperate climate in its northern part. Winters are long and cold with ice storms and snowstorms. The southern part of the region is milder. It has cool winters and hot summers. Plants in the Northeast include different species of large trees and ferns. Black bears, red foxes, and chipmunks are some of the animals in the Northeast.

Human Features

The first people to live in the Northeast Region were Native Americans. Forestry, coal, and granite industries have brought many people to the region. Wide toll roads cover the Northeast. Bridges, tunnels, and the Erie Canal allow travel over, under, and by water. This helps the movement of people, goods, and services. The population of the Northeast Region is about 56 million. High-rise apartment buildings in large cities provide shelter for many people. Rural areas have more space with large farms and forests that are used for industry and recreation.

title: We Share Languages
text: Most people in the United States speak English. Many people speak both English and Spanish. In different parts of the country, you may hear Chinese, French, Vietnamese, and many other languages. Different cultures make the United States an interesting place to live.

title: The Southeast
text:
Physical Features

The Southeast Region has 12 states. The region has beaches. Freshwater sources in this region include lakes and rivers. The Appalachian and the Blue Ridge Mountains are some of the landforms. There are also barrier islands, swamps, and wetlands. The climate of the Southeast Region is tropical. Summers are long, hot, and humid. The region has many national forests. Snakes, crocodiles, alligators, and black bears are some of the animals in the Southeast.

Human Features

The Choctaw, the Creek, and the Cherokee were the first people to live in the Southeast Region. The Spanish arrived around 1513. Enslaved Africans were brought to this region for the first time in 1619. All these people influenced the culture of the Southeast Region.

The fertile soil and mild climate of the region are great for farming. Cotton, wheat, corn, fruit and nuts bring money to the region. Manufacturing is another important industry. Cars, airplanes, and medical equipment are made here. The population of the Southeast Region is about 97 million.

title: The Midwest
text:
Physical Features

The land in the Midwest is mostly flat. There are 12 states in the region. There are rolling hills, high mountains, and deep valleys in the region. Six of the 12 states are within the Great Lakes area. In summer, it gets hot and humid in the Midwest. In winter, it can get really cold.

Human Features

The Chippewa, Lakota, and Blackfoot were some of the Native American tribes that first lived in the region. There is a lot of farming in the region. The land is very fertile. People grow wheat, soybeans, and corn. Others raise hogs and dairy cows. A lot of vehicles and machines are also made in the Midwest.

title: The Southwest
text:
Physical Features

The Southwest Region has four states. Part of the Gulf of America is in the region. There are also 10 rivers and a few lakes. Landforms in the region include high mountains, valleys, and barrier islands. The region is home to the Grand Canyon as well. Rainfall is mostly seasonal in the Southwest. Only a few places get rainfall in summer. Most areas get their rainfall in winter.

Human Features

The culture of the region shows the influence of the Native Americans who first lived there. We can see this influence in three main ways. There are still stone and mud homes. The food eaten in the region has Native American influence, too. Also, some cities and towns have Native American names. Mining coal, oil, and natural gas have brought many jobs to the region. Farming is an important industry there, too.

title: The West
text:
Physical Features

Eleven states make up the West Region. Many of the states lie along the Pacific Ocean. There are many islands too. The region also has many rivers and waterfalls. There are lakes, hot springs, and geysers as well. The West is home to mountain ranges, valleys, and canyons. The West Region has diverse climates. Some places are hot and humid. Other places are hot and dry. There are also places that are very cold.

Human Features

Many Native American tribes and nations live in the West. They were the first people there.

Forestry, fishing, ranching, and mining are important industries. Many people in the West have jobs in entertainment and tourism, too. Amusement parks, ski resorts, and national parks bring lots of tourists. There are also many farmers. The region is famous for potatoes, pineapples, almonds, grapes, and cotton.

title: Specialization
text:
Communities have different resources. They use these resources to produce goods and services. Many communities and businesses focus on making one product or service to sell. This focus is called specialization.

Many Florida communities have good land and climate. They use these resources for growing things. They grow many products more easily than in other climates. Businesses in Florida specialize in growing these products to sell to other communities. Florida grows 57 percent of the citrus sold in the United States. Florida also grows more sugarcane than any other state.

title: Essential Question
text: Why does the United States trade with other nations?

title: Interdependence
text:
Most communities sell their specialized products to other communities. Interdependence is when people depend on others to provide products to sell. People, businesses, and countries can depend on each other.

A factory can specialize in making car tires. That means tires are all the factory does. Car tires would not be very useful without a car. A car without tires would not be very useful, either. Specialization creates interdependence. The car company needs tires to create cars. The tire company needs to sell its tires. People buy and sell different things. This helps people get everything they need.

title: Markets
text: A market is a place where people sell goods and services. A store where you buy groceries is a market. There are other kinds of markets, too. A market is not always a store. Some people buy and sell things on an online market. Everyone who buys or sells goods or services is part of a market. A local market includes people who live near you. Other markets can include all of your state or country. The international market includes millions of people from different nations of the world.

title: Trade
text:
Most countries and states don’t make everything their citizens need and want. Each place has its own resources. Sometimes people have to buy things from other states or countries. Some places have oil and coal. Other places have fish, fruits, and vegetables. Trade is when people buy and sell goods and services between places. It's also when people exchange a good or service for something they want or need.

People around the world depend on each other. The United States does not produce everything Americans need and want. The United States trades with other countries. We get goods from other countries. We send goods to other countries, too.

title: Imports and Exports
text: Trade depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods that are brought in from another country or state. Exports are goods that are sent out of a state to be sold. We depend on each other to trade. We barter the resources we have for the resources we need.

title: We Share Foods from Long Ago
text: Long ago, Native Americans ate what they could hunt or grow. They fished and hunted animals like rabbits, turkeys, and deer. They grew corn and beans. We still eat some of these foods today.

title: We Share Foods from Today
text: In a big city, you might see a large variety of restaurants. There could be a Japanese restaurant, a Chinese restaurant, an Italian restaurant, and a Mexican restaurant side by side or across the street from each other! They all offer different foods for us to try.

Maybe you can try new restaurants or read books about faraway places. Take what you come up with and write it on the lines below!

title: Essential Question
text: How does our environment affect how we live?

title: Clothing
text: Our environment affects the clothes we wear. When it rains, you wear a rain jacket. When the sun shines, you wear shorts.

title: Adapting to Our Environment
text: Our environment affects the way we live. We adapt to our environment. This means we change the way we live to meet our needs.

title: Shelter
text: Houses are built differently in different environments. Some people live where it is windy. Their houses may be built with cinder blocks. Some people live near water. Their houses may be built on stilts.

title: Food
text: The food we eat depends on our environment. People who live near bodies of water might eat more seafood. People who live in warmer places might eat more tropical fruits.

title: Activities
text: The activities that people do depend on their environment. People who live near forests can go hiking. People who live near the ocean can go surfing.

title: Transportation
text: Our environment affects how we get from place to place. People might ride on public transportation in a big city. They might ride trains or buses. People might drive cars in the country.

title: Tools That Help Us Adapt
text: We use tools to help us adapt to our environment. We use umbrellas when it rains. We use hats to keep the sun out of our eyes.

title: Timelines
text: A timeline shows things in the order that they happen. They can show past, present, and future events. Timelines can show days, weeks, months, and years.

title: Essential Question
text: How do people and places change over time?

title: You Change Over Time
text:
You grow and change over time. You were a baby. Now you are a child. You will grow to be an adult.

Draw a picture of you in the past. Draw a picture of you in the present. Draw a picture of you in the future.

title: Families Change Over Time
text: Families change over time. Brothers, sisters, cousins, and pets can come into your family. Aunts, uncles, and other parents and grandparents can also come into your family. All families are different.

title: Our Class Changes Over Time
text: Our class changes over time. New students join our class. Some students move away. We learn new things.

title: Neighborhoods Change Over Time
text: Neighborhoods change over time. New houses and roads are built. New families move in. Other people move out. Communities get bigger. People use the land for different things.

title: Resources
text:
A resource is a material that people can use. Resources help us meet our needs and wants. It is important for people and communities to use resources wisely.

Many things that we use to meet our needs come from nature. We call these natural resources. Natural resources are things like minerals, trees, and animals. These resources give us food to eat and materials to build with. The wind and the sun are also natural resources. They help us meet our needs.

It is important for people and communities to use resources wisely so they will be there for us to use in the future.

title: Essential Question
text: How do resources affect people's choices?

title: Resources and Work
text: Natural resources are used in the jobs people do. In many places, important industries are created because of the local natural resources. Let’s look at how that happens.

title: Agriculture
text: Agriculture is another word for farming. It is growing crops and raising animals. Farmers need healthy soil, clean water, and good weather. These are natural resources. Farmers also grow plants like orange trees and cotton. Oranges can be sold to grocery stores. Cotton can be sold to people who make clothes.

title: Manufacturing
text: Manufacturing is creating goods in factories. Workers take resources and process them to make something new. Most factories use machines to process, or change, resources. One factory might take trees and turn them into paper. Another factory will use plastic and metal to make computer parts. Cotton from plants can be turned into clothing or blankets. Oranges can be made into orange juice. The orange juice is then sold in stores.

title: Tourism
text: The tourism industry takes care of people who are traveling. Beautiful natural resources often make people want to visit a place. People also travel to do activities. Some go to oceans to fish. Others travel to beaches to relax and play. People who travel need goods and services. Tourists use transportation services. They need hotels and other places to stay. Tourists go to restaurants to eat. Tourists also like guides to show them around. All these services are jobs people do.

title: Aerospace
text:
The aerospace industry is important in Florida. It deals with air and space travel. There are over 16,000 aerospace companies in Florida. Rocket engines are made in West Palm beach. Jets are researched and made in Melbourne.

The aerospace industry uses many natural resources. Cape Canaveral is a natural resource. It is natural land that is a good place for launching rockets into space.

Even the weather is a natural resource that affects the aerospace industry. For example, aircraft and rockets cannot take off in stormy weather. Many flights get canceled in bad weather.

title: Trade, Logistics, and Transportation
text:
Florida has around 150 airports. This means airplanes can easily travel to and from Florida. It is surrounded by the sea on three sides. This means ships can easily travel to and from Florida. There are also good roads in Florida. This means trucks and cars can easily travel to and from Florida.

These natural and man-made resources make Florida a great place for international trade. International trade is trading goods and services between countries. Over 200 countries buy Florida-made goods and services. Getting these goods and services to and from these countries is made easy by Florida’s resources.

Florida is a leader in logistics and transportation. Logistics means managing the movement of resources. These resources can be goods or data. Transportation means moving goods or data from one place to another. Florida’s location and road system make transportation easier.

title: Florida Becomes a State
text:
Florida experienced great changes during the early to mid-1800s. In 1821, Spain ceded Florida to the United States. The U.S. government combined East and West Florida to create one territory. Andrew Jackson was appointed the military governor of the new territory. Jackson was tasked with establishing a territorial government, organizing Spanish and British land claims in the new territory, and arranging the peaceful transfer of power from Spain to the United States. This was not an easy task for Jackson. He faced many challenges during his short time as the military governor of the territory.

Many Spanish, Native American, and African settlers, who had lived in Florida for several years, were unhappy with the changes. They did not trust the new territorial officials, and they were upset with the influx of new settlers to the territory. Spanish military and government officials were unwilling to work with Jackson and the new government. They left Florida to settle in other areas of the Spanish empire.

The Seminole and other Native American tribes of Florida were wary of Jackson and the new government of the territory. Jackson led U.S. troops into Florida to oppose Native American resistance during the First Seminole War. The territorial government of Florida hoped to restrict the movements of the Seminole Tribe by forcing them onto a reservation in South Florida. The Seminole refused to leave their ancestral homeland. As a result, two more wars were fought between the Seminole and the United States for total control of the territory.

African settlers were also wary of the new government. Many African settlers were formerly enslaved people who had escaped enslavement and gained their freedom in Florida. The Spanish government protected these people, but the free African population of Florida was unsure if the United States would offer the same protections as the Spanish government. Many feared that they would be returned to their former enslavers or forced back into enslavement. During the 1820s, about 150 African settlers left Florida and settled in Cuba. They did this to keep their rights as Spanish citizens. Others stayed and fought to keep their rights and property.

Jackson worked quickly to complete his tasks. He did not want to stay in Florida long. In 1822, William P. Duval replaced Jackson as the new governor of the territory. Duval’s mission was different from Jackon’s. He wanted to encourage more American settlers to come to Florida. He also hoped to establish a new capital and increase economic activities in the territory. If he could complete these goals, then Florida could become a state.

In order to become a state, the population of a territory had to be at least 60,000. In 1821, Florida was home to about 8,000 people. The territory had a long way to go to reach a population of 60,000. Duval knew this, so he focused his initial efforts on creating a capital and building a strong territorial government. In 1824, Duval and government officials decided to create a new capital between St. Augustine and Pensacola. A site was chosen near the former location of Mission San Luis. The new capital was named Tallahassee, a Creek word that means “old field” or “old town.”

After Tallahassee was established as the capital and the town began to grow, settlers poured into the area from other states. The land around the new capital city was very fertile. Settlers established farms and plantations in the area. Plantation owners from Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, and the Carolinas came to Florida in search of more land. They brought thousands of enslaved people with them to work on their plantations. Cotton was the primary crop grown on the plantations around Tallahassee. It quickly became the main cash crop grown in the territory.

When the Second Seminole War ended in 1842, hundreds of Native Americans were forced to move to Indian Territory in Oklahoma or move to a reservation established by the government. The land that once belonged to Native Americans was bought by new settlers. By 1845, the population of Florida had exceeded 60,000. The territorial government had already created a draft of the possible state constitution, so it was time for Florida to petition Congress to become a state.

On March 3, 1845, Florida became the 27th state in the Union. William D. Mosley was elected governor of the new state. David Levy Yulee and James D. Westcott Jr. were selected as the first senators to represent Florida in the national government. The state was on its way to becoming an important part of the country. Statehood also had a big impact on the people, economy, geography, and culture of Florida.

title: Changing the World: The Steam Engine
text:
New forms of technology changed the way people traveled to and from Texas. Science advanced in the 1800s to control steam pressure. Steam was created by burning coal under a boiler of water. The heated water would boil and create steam. The steam pressure was then used to move mechanical parts, like wheels. This technology paved the way for the steam engine to be invented in England.

Americans imported the first steam engine from England in 1829. This triggered a new industry. Entrepreneurs began experimenting with how the steam engine could be used to make work easier. Many new jobs were created because of the steam engine.

The steam engine was used to create better transportation on water and on land. Boats powered by steam engines did not need to depend on the wind or currents. They could travel up to five miles per hour. Steamboats revolutionized transportation and shipping around the country.

The steam locomotive could move more cargo and do it faster than horses or oxen. Transporting goods and people became faster. The dependability of these machines led to predictable schedules for getting goods to market. The northern states used this new technology to increase manufacturing. Other states and areas of the country, including Florida, wanted to harness the power of the steam engine to make transportation and travel easier. Steam power transformed the geography, economy, and culture of Florida during the mid-1800s.

title: Railroads Reach Florida
text:
Even before Florida became a state in 1845, thousands of people came to the area in search of economic opportunity. At this time, traveling to and through Florida was not easy. There were very few roads, and the existing roads were not reliable. Traveling to Florida by ship often took weeks or months. Florida’s early lawmakers looked for an easier way to move goods and people around the state.

In 1836, the first railroad line was completed in Florida. This happened before Florida became a state. It connected the town of St. Joseph, the location of present-day Port St. Joe, to the Apalachee River. This railroad was the first to use a steam engine in Florida. The main purpose of this railroad was to transport cotton from plantations around St. Joseph to the river. From there, boats carried the cotton up and down the Apalachicola River.

Another rail line was completed in 1837 between Tallahassee and St. Marks to move goods, people, and fresh water to the capital more quickly. Cotton was the main commodity transported by the Tallahassee Railroad. By the end of 1837, about 30,000 bales of cotton were transported by the railroad from St. Marks to Tallahassee. In 1839, another rail line was constructed to connect Port Leon to the Tallahassee Railroad. The construction of these early rail lines was the start of the transportation revolution in Florida.

title: Steamboats Sail Through Florida
text:
During the early 1800s, sailors began using the steam engine to power their ships. Steamboats were first used to transport people and goods throughout Florida beginning in 1829. Companies established routes and travel schedules for cargo and people wishing to travel. The first steamboat companies were located along the east coast of Florida. They sailed up and down the St. Johns, Kissimmee, Ocklawaha, and Suwannee Rivers.

Steamboats were also used to connect Florida to important port cities in the South, including Savannah, Georgia, and Charleston, South Carolina. The steamboat Florida transported cargo and passengers along the Atlantic Coasts of Florida and Georgia, making multiple stops daily along its route. Steamboats quickly became a more reliable form of transportation than traveling overland to Florida. As a result, thousands of people migrated to Florida during this time. The population grew from 34,730 in 1830 to 54,477 by 1840.

The economy of Florida also grew with the use of steamboats. Goods produced in Florida could travel to markets across the South more quickly. Goods and supplies could also reach Florida faster than they had ever done before.

title: Innovative Inventions
text:
New inventions and innovations developed during this time period made life easier for people in Florida and across the world. Some of these were the cotton gin, the steel-tipped plow, and the ice-making machine.

The Cotton Gin

In 1793, Eli Whitney invented a machine that simplified the work of removing cotton seeds from harvested cotton. Southern plantations grew cotton using the work of enslaved people. One enslaved worker could only remove seeds from about one pound of cotton a day. At this speed, farmers did not make much money from cotton. Then, Whitney built the cotton gin. The cotton gin was a large wooden box with a crank on the side.

The machine could separate the seeds from cotton quickly. It could process 50 pounds of cotton a day. This meant more cotton could be grown, harvested, and sold. The cotton industry expanded. Whitney’s invention revolutionized cotton production across the country.

The Steel-Tipped Plow

Farming in Florida was tougher than anyone expected. To prepare a field for planting, farmers used a plow, a tool with a blade that turns the soil over and creates rows for planting. Plows were pulled by horses or oxen. They had blades made of cast iron. The iron plows did not work well on the prairie, though. The iron couldn’t cut through the tangled prairie grass roots or the sticky soil. Farmers had to stop every few minutes to clear their plows of the sticky mess.

Farmers across the country struggled with this problem for years. Then, a blacksmith named John Deere solved the problem. John Deere was from Vermont, but he was unsuccessful in setting up a business there. Like so many others, he saw moving west as an opportunity to start fresh. He settled in Grand Detour, about 100 miles outside of Chicago, Illinois. One day, he was sharpening blades at a sawmill. There, he found a broken steel saw blade. The blade had been polished smooth after passing through so much lumber. It reminded Deere of other work he’d done polishing steel tines on a hayfork.

Polishing that steel hayfork made it pass through the soil easily to gather more hay. He wondered if polished steel on a plow blade might do the same thing. He designed a large plow with a steel blade on it and called it a “grasshopper plow.” He sold this first steel-bladed plow to a local farmer in 1838. That farmer told his friends how well it worked cutting through the grass and sticky soil. By 1855, Deere’s factory was filling orders for 10,000 plows a year. John Deere’s invention made farming the prairie possible.

Ice-Making Machine

Another invention that revolutionized Florida was the ice-making machine invented by Dr. John Gorrie. Gorrie was a doctor who studied tropical diseases, such as yellow fever and malaria. His studies brought him to Florida. During this time, many settlers suffered from yellow fever, which was caused by mosquitoes. Gorrie settled in Apalachicola in 1833 and began working on a cure for yellow fever.

From his studies, Gorrie knew that yellow fever and other tropical diseases were worse during warmer seasons of the year. He was convinced that colder environments could help people who suffered from tropical diseases. Gorrie began helping sick patients by placing ice in a bowl and hanging it from the ceiling to cool down the room. During this time, ice was not easy to transport to Florida. Gorrie knew he had to come up with a different way to get ice for his patients.

Gorrie invented a machine that could be powered by steam, wind, or water to produce ice. He received a patent for his device in 1851. His device helped hundreds of patients suffering from yellow fever and other tropical diseases. Gorrie’s device was studied by future inventors and was one of the inspirations for modern refrigeration and air-conditioning.
