title: Magnetic Poles
text: Magnets have two sides. Each side is called a “pole.” One side is called the north pole, and the other side is the south pole. If you put the north and south poles of two magnets together, they attract one another. This means magnetic force pulls them together. When you put the north end close to the north end of another magnet, you will feel the magnets push apart. This is called repulsion.

title: Why Did People Move to America?
text: People from Europe wanted to explore the land in North America. Then people from Europe wanted to live here. People move to new communities for different reasons. Sometimes the reason is for safety. Sometimes the reason is for new opportunities. Sometimes the reason is adventure. A group of people from England came to America in 1620 to start a new life.

title: Essential Question
text: What was life like for people who moved to early America?

title: The Pilgrims
text: In 1620, 102 people came to America on a ship called the Mayflower. They wanted to be free to worship in their own church. They wanted a chance to build a new home. They also wanted land to farm and make a living. They created a village called Plymouth. It was by the ocean in what we call Massachusetts today. We call these people the Pilgrims.

title: Food
text:
When the Pilgrims arrived, they only had the food they brought from England. This was food like cheese, dried meat, and flat, hard bread. They tried to hunt and fish in Plymouth. The Pilgrims found some corn that had been stored by the Wampanoag Native Americans. They took the corn. There was not enough food for all the Pilgrims.

Some Native Americans came to help the Pilgrims. Samoset was a Native American who met the Pilgrims. He spoke English. He told the Pilgrims about the land. Samoset introduced the Pilgrims to the Wampanoag Native Americans who lived there. Their chief was called Massasoit. He made a peace treaty with the Pilgrims. The Wampanoag showed the Pilgrims how to plant corn. They also showed the Pilgrims good places to fish and hunt. The Wampanoag taught the Pilgrims many skills. The Pilgrims needed these skills to survive in America.

title: Shelter
text:
Every person needs shelter from the sun, cold, and weather. The Wampanoag built homes using wooden frames covered with woven mats. These materials were natural resources of the land. They built wetus, or wetuash, in dome shapes. Several families lived together in each wetu.

The Pilgrims used the Mayflower for shelter until a meeting house was built. Then, they all lived together in one building. Later, each family built a simple cabin. They also used the natural resources of the land to build their cabins.

title: Clothing
text:
The Pilgrims didn’t have many clothes. They wore what they brought from England. There were no stores where they could buy new clothes. Men and boys wore long-sleeved shirts, pants, and hats. Women and girls wore long skirts or dresses, aprons, and a white cap called a coif.

The Wampanoag had clothes made from natural resources like hides and furs. Wampanoag men and boys wore breechcloths and leggings. Wampanoag women and girls wore knee-length skirts. Sometimes they wore leggings to keep warm. The whole tribe wore moccasins to protect their feet.

title: Education
text:
Wampanoag children learned from their parents. They worked in the fields and in their homes. They learned stories about their culture and history after the work was done.

Pilgrim children also learned from their parents. They worked to build their houses and farms. The children learned to read from the Bible after the work was done.

title: Changes Over Time
text:
The Pilgrims were not the only people who left England and came to America. More and more people came. Soon there were 13 colonies. The people cleared land by cutting down trees and large plants. This gave them room to plant more crops and build more houses.

Life in the colonies was very hard at first, but it got easier. The people learned how to live in their new land. They built better homes. Some people opened shops. The shops sold clothes, tools, food, and other things people needed. In 1635, the first public school opened in America.

title: Needs and Wants
text:
A need is something that you have to have every day. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us warm or cool.

Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler to help you be successful each day.

A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. A want is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

title: Essential Question
text: How do we use money?

title: Goods and Services
text:
Goods are things that are made for people to buy and use. Goods include clothing, furniture, and toys. Goods are also things we eat or drink. Fruits, vegetables, and milk are examples of goods we consume.

A service is work that one person does for someone else. Services are actions such as a haircut, car repair, and teaching. If you send a package to someone else, you pay for a delivery service. If you have a cell phone, you pay for cell phone service. You might choose to have your pizza delivered. That’s a service too.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
The people who make goods or provide services for other people are producers. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are created for other communities.

The people who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers can buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. When you get a haircut, you are buying a service. This makes you a consumer. You are also a consumer if you buy a book.

People can be both producers and consumers. For example, a baker is a consumer when they purchase flour, sugar, and supplies to make their baked goods. A baker is a producer when they sell their baked goods.

title: Supply and Demand
text:
The price of a good or service depends on two things. First, it depends on how much of the good there is for people to buy. That’s called supply. Next, it depends on how many people want or need it. That’s called demand. When the supply is low and the demand is high, the price goes up. When the supply is high and the demand is low, the price goes down.

When the newest smartphones come out, many people want them. There is a large demand. At clearance sales, stores want to get rid of products that haven’t sold. In this case, there is a larger supply.

title: Scarcity and Surplus
text:
Scarcity is when there is more demand for something than supply. In other words, it is not having enough of something people want or need. Sometimes, scarcity can be a big problem. If basic resources like food or water are scarce, it is hard for people to live. When goods and services become scarce, families have to decide what they need most. Families have to make choices about how to spend their money to meet their needs.

Surplus is when the supply of a good or service is more than the demand. In other words, there is more than people need or want. A surplus of a good or service usually makes the price go down.

title: Trade
text:
Our country does not produce everything we need. We have to buy things from other countries. That is called trade. Trade is when you buy, sell, or exchange a good or service for something else you want or need. Businesses, states, and countries trade goods and services all around the world. Trade between countries is a very important part of a nation’s economy. Because of interdependence and trade, our community is affected by events around the world.

Bartering is trading goods without the use of money. In early cultures, people were able to get many things they needed and wanted through bartering. Today, we use money to buy what we need because it is much easier to use.

title: Imports and Exports
text: International trade depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods brought in from other countries. Exports are goods sent out to other countries to be sold. Rice, oil, and computers are made in Asia and imported to the United States. They are imports. Cars, airplanes, and machines are made in the United States and exported to other countries.

title: Human Features
text: Human features are how people change where they live. We build cities and towns. We also build roads, buildings, and houses.

title: Essential Question
text: What are human features?

title: Houses
text: We build houses. They give us shelter and a place to sleep. Houses are a human feature.

title: Roads and Bridges
text: We build roads and bridges. They help us get from place to place faster. Roads and bridges are human features.

title: Buildings
text: We build buildings. We build stores so we can buy what we need. We build schools so we have places to learn. Buildings are human features.

title: Recreation
text: We build playgrounds, pools, and parks. We build places where we can have fun and relax. These places are human features.

title: Florida in the 1850s
text:
The mid-1800s was a time of great change in Florida. After 24 years as a territory, Florida became the 27th state in the Union in 1845. Technological advancements and new forms of transportation brought more settlers to Florida. Between 1821 and 1850, the population of Florida increased from 8,000 to 87,445. By 1860, the population rose to 140,424. Wagon trains, ships, and railroads brought new settlers to Florida by the thousands.

The majority of the new settlers who came to Florida migrated from the southern states, including Georgia, North and South Carolina, and Alabama. A small portion of these new settlers immigrated to Florida from Europe and the Caribbean. There were many factors that encouraged people to settle in Florida. The motivations for people migrating are called “push-pull factors.” A push factor could be considered a forceful or negative reason that drives a person from a place. Usually, a push factor is when a person’s way of life is in danger. The danger could be because of war, persecution, famine, or any other factor that endangers the welfare of a person or a family.

A pull factor could be considered an attraction or draw to a place. Usually, a pull factor is when a person wants something more in their life. Leaving a location would then be considered a positive. A pull factor could be the availability of land, new jobs, better climate, fewer natural disasters, and other things. Push-pull factors work together. We consider them when we study movement. Historians look at push-pull factors to analyze the past.

From 1800 to 1850, many things were happening around the world. Countries in Europe were experiencing continual wars. Living in the path of armies and fighting was a push factor for many people to emigrate to America. The pull factor in America was that people would not be living in a war zone.

In Great Britain, people were being pushed off their rented land. Often, landlords found they could make more money by using the land for animals. In some cases, the landlord paid for the tenants to emigrate. Some tenants emigrated to Australia. Some emigrated to America. In Ireland, there was a major famine when the potato crops failed. Millions of Irish people were pushed by starvation to emigrate to all parts of the world. The pull factor in America was that there were more resources there than they had in Ireland.

Land in Florida was plentiful and affordable. Many settlers came to the state with the hopes of establishing large farms and plantations. The economy boomed as a result of the influx of settlers and the use of new technology to produce goods and move them to markets. Florida continued to grow quickly throughout the 1800s.

The population of settled cities, including Pensacola, Apalachicola, and St. Augustine, increased. New towns were established by settlers moving to the state. Quincy, Marianna, Monticello, Jacksonville, and Tampa were all established during this time. The rapid growth of the state had a large impact on the people, places, and culture of Florida.

title: The Growth of Florida's Cattle Industry
text:
Spanish explorers were the first to bring cattle to Florida during the 1500s. Juan Ponce de León brought several heads of cattle with him to Florida in 1521. Many historians and cattle ranchers in Florida today believe that the cattle Juan Ponce de León brought with him were the first domesticated (kept as a pet or tamed) cattle in what is now the United States.

Spanish settlers brought more cattle to Florida when they settled St. Augustine in 1565. Missionaries raised cattle with the help of the local Native American tribes of the area. Settlers began to raise their own cattle and establish large cattle farms. During the 1600s, Florida’s cattle ranchers began to export their cattle to Cuba and other Spanish settlements in the Caribbean. These cows were given the name “cracker cow.” They could survive in the hot and humid climate of Florida and adapted to the plains of the area.

The open plains and large fields of the Florida panhandle and peninsula were ideal for cattle ranching. Within 100 years, Spanish settlers established 34 cattle ranches that raised about 20,000 head of cattle. The largest cattle ranches were located near present-day Tallahassee, Gainesville, and St. Augustine. Other ranches were established along the St. Johns River. This allowed ranchers to transport their cattle to Spanish settlements and forts more quickly.

Many Spanish cattle ranchers left Florida when Great Britain gained control of the colony in 1763. Thousands of head of cattle were left behind. Native American tribes gathered the cattle and developed their own herds. Members of the Seminole Tribe were very skilled cattle ranchers. Cattle ranching became an important economic activity for the tribe during the 1700s. The Seminole were the top producers of Florida cattle during this time. By 1775, it is estimated that the Seminole possessed a herd of about 7,000 to 10,000 head of cattle. They established their own ranches near present-day Micanopy, Florida.

When Florida became a territory and later a state, many settlers from the United States came to Florida in search of new pasture land for their cattle. The cattle roamed freely throughout the plains. Cowboys and cattle ranchers would round up the cattle to take them to market. They would often take their cattle to markets in Georgia and Alabama. Other cowboys and cattle ranchers would take their cattle to Tampa and Punta Rassa Port, where they would be shipped by boat to Cuba and other areas of the Caribbean.

Florida cowboys received a unique nickname during the early 1800s. These new cattle ranchers and rustlers were known as “Florida Crackers.” Historians are unsure where the term actually came from, but they agree there are two possibilities. To rustle up, or gather, their cattle, Florida cowboys would use long whips. The whips would make loud cracking sounds that could be heard across the plains. This is one possible origin of the nickname. The other possibility comes from the cracked corn they would use to make different foods and drinks.

“Cracker cowboys” were very skilled at raising cattle. They adapted to the land that many people refused to live on because of the harsh conditions. They used resources from the environment to build their homes. They also used smaller, lighter ponies to move easily around the plains and swamps of Florida. Cracker cowboys and their families lived off the land. They hunted, fished, and gathered wild plants.

By 1860, Florida cattle herds ranged from 5,000 to 50,000 head of cattle. As of January 2020, there were over 1,000,000 head of cattle in the state of Florida!

title: William Bartram
text:
Another pull factor that brought settlers to Florida was the writings of William Bartram. Bartram was a well-known naturalist, explorer, and author who wrote about his extensive travels through the American southeast. From a young age, Bartram was a skilled artist. He often drew pictures of plants and animals near his home in Pennsylvania. In 1765, Bartram accompanied his father on an expedition to Florida. He drew illustrations of the plants, animals, and natural features of Florida for his father. This trip made him interested in exploring the American South even further.

Between 1773 and 1777, Bartram traveled through present-day North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, and Mississippi. He collected seeds, plants, and roots of native plants and wrote about the natural environment of each area. He also described the interactions he had with the Native American tribes he encountered. He described the culture, traditions, government, and economic activities of the tribes.

In 1791, Bartram published a book about his travels through the American South. His descriptions of the plants, animals, people, and environment encouraged hundreds of settlers to leave their homes and settle in Florida. Today, Bartram’s works still serve as a valuable source of information for people studying the history of Florida.

title: The Lumber Industry
text:
Another important industry that developed during this time was the lumber industry. Before the 1800s, Florida was covered by about 27 million acres of forests. Lumber was essential to build homes, ships, churches, and towns. The first sawmill in Florida was established in 1819. A sawmill is a factory where logs are turned into lumber, which is used for building. The first sawmill in Florida was located near Jacksonville. It was built close to Six Mile Creek. The sawmill was powered by water from the creek.

Florida’s lumber industry grew quickly after it became a territory of the United States. As more settlers came to Florida, the need for lumber grew. They established sawmills around Pensacola, the St. Johns River, and along the Gulf Coast. Large pine and live oak trees were harvested, cut into lumber, and used to create new settlements across Florida. By 1835, there were 25 sawmills in the Pensacola area alone. One mill, owned by Joseph Forsyth and Andrew and Ezekiel Simpson, sent over 900,000 feet of lumber to market each year by the end of the 1830s.

In 1860, there were close to 90 sawmills throughout the state. By the end of that year, lumber added $1,476,645 to the state’s total economy. The steam engine and new forms of transportation made it easier for mill owners to get their products to markets across the country. Florida’s economy continued to grow because of the abundance of lumber in the state.

title: Pioneer Life in Florida
text:
The early American, European, and Caribbean settlers who came to Florida are often referred to as pioneers. Pioneers are people who are among the first to do something. Many of the early pioneers who came to Florida hoped to create a new life for themselves and their families. Some settled in established cities, while others settled along the Florida frontier.

Life for those who settled along the frontier was much more challenging than life in the city. Frontier pioneers relied on the environment and natural resources around them to survive. Each member of the family had a role to play. Men were often responsible for clearing the land, raising cattle, planting crops, hunting, and building homes. Women were primarily in charge of the house and taking care of the children. They were responsible for making clothing, cooking, growing crops in the family garden, harvesting crops on the farm, and tending to the smaller animals around the farm or homestead. Women also served as teachers for their children along the frontier because there were very few established schools.

Children helped around the house and homestead. They assisted their parents with the household chores and on the farm. Boys were often taught to hunt and fish. Girls helped their mothers make clothing, cook, and take care of the house. Like the cowboys of the frontier, these pioneers were often referred to as “Florida crackers” because they engaged in cattle ranching and used cracked, or dried, corn in many of their recipes.

title: Slavery in America
text:
For centuries, the rights of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness were denied to many people. Men, women, and children were enslaved. To be enslaved is to be forced to work against your will. In America, enslaved people were considered to be the legal property of another person. The enslaver had full control over the liberty and freedom of the enslaved person. This was in direct opposition to the self-evident truths in the Declaration of Independence.

In the 1600s, the continent of Africa was home to many tribes, kingdoms, and empires. They traded with each other and with foreign countries. The ocean ports in West Africa were open for trade with European countries. There was competition and rivalry between many of the African countries. Rival tribes raided towns and villages to destroy resources. They captured or kidnapped men, women, and children from enemy villages.

The Europeans purchased these captives and brought them to colonies in the Americas. This was known as the Middle Passage of the European triangular trade route. The captive men, women, and children were enslaved for the rest of their lives. For nearly 200 years, this system of trade from Africa continued.

On Jan. 1, 1808, the United States Congress passed the Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves. This law stopped the importation of people from Africa to be sold into slavery. However, millions of enslaved people already lived in the United States. Most had been born into slavery and were descendants of enslaved African men and women. They were enslaved for life, as their children and grandchildren would be. They were the property of the white men who bought and sold them. They had no freedom or liberty. Their clothes, food, and shelter all came from their enslavers. Slavery would continue to be legal in the United States for another 57 years.

The new American government protected the rights of white citizens. The government also continued to legally deny unalienable rights to Black people. They were denied rights based on their families of origin and the color of their skin. This system continued for many years and only ended after the Civil War, a bloody conflict that tore the nation apart. By 1860, the total population of Florida was 140,424 people. The Black population of the state was about 63,000 people. Of these 63,000 people, about 62,000 were enslaved. The number of enslaved Africans was almost half of the total population of the state at this time. Legalized slavery had a profound impact on the people of Florida for many years.

title: The Rise of the Plantation System
text:
The majority of Florida’s enslaved population lived on large farms called plantations. Plantations often specialized in growing cash crops, such as cotton. Cash crops are crops grown only for their financial value, not for the farmer to use and live off of. The fertile soil and thousands of acres of available land in the Florida panhandle attracted many plantation owners from other southern states. Many who relocated to Florida brought with them a large labor force of enslaved African people to work on their new plantations.

The majority of plantations in Florida primarily grew cotton. Tobacco and sugar were also grown as cash crops on the state’s plantations. Vegetable gardens supplied food for those who lived on the plantations. In 1842, the federal government offered 160 acres to anyone willing to settle in south Florida to cultivate the land. Many settlers and plantation owners from South Carolina took advantage of this offer. They moved to present-day Marion and Hernando Counties. The large plantations they established there had a big impact on Florida’s economy. Crops produced on Florida plantations were shipped by boat, wagon, and railroad to markets across the country.

The number of plantation owners who owned 30 or more enslaved persons doubled from 200 in 1850 to 400 by 1860. As more plantations were established in Florida, the population of enslaved Africans rose. This caused tension between people who believed the institution of slavery was right and those who wanted to abolish, or put an end to, it. Tensions between the people who supported and opposed slavery eventually led to open hostilities and civil war.

title: Technology Changes New Jersey
text:
New Jersey, like many other states in the nation, has an important transportation network. Roads and railways help businesses distribute their goods and resources throughout the country. New Jersey’s coastline also has natural harbors and human-made ports. Harbors and ports allow boats and people to transport goods from the land to the ocean. Ports and harbors are also found in other places in the United States and the world. This allows boats to transfer goods and resources from one port to another.

Another way New Jersey uses its access to the coast is to create wind farms. There are strong winds that blow in off the ocean. New Jersey takes advantage of the wind by creating wind farms in the ocean. These large turbines generate and store electricity. They are placed close to large coastal populations. Energy can be supplied for populations quickly and efficiently. This technology can provide electricity for thousands of homes. Offshore wind farms provide a way to create a clean source of energy.

title: Government: What Is It, and What Does It Do?
text:
We need rules in school. Rules help us work together in an orderly way. They keep us safe and help us manage problems. Our communities need the same things. Governments were created to perform these functions or tasks. A government is a group of citizens who lead a community. Governments serve the needs of the people in a community. Governments create laws, which help provide order. They protect people and their property.

The United States government provides safety and security for the people of the country. It also maintains justice and order. It protects people and their property. The government also provides services.

title: Essential Question
text: Why do we have government?

title: The Government Creates Laws
text:
A primary focus of all governments should be to promote the common good. The common good means working to create laws and rules that benefit everyone.

The United States government makes laws and rules that guarantee and protect the rights of people. For example, it is against the law to steal. This law protects people's property. Laws and rules also provide safety and security. For example, it is against the law to injure another person on purpose. This law keeps people safe. Laws in the United States say people are to be treated equally. The government is responsible for making sure all people are treated fairly under these laws. For example, it is against the law to treat a person unfairly because of the color of their skin. This law helps everyone to be treated equally.

Holding people and the government responsible for their actions is important.

title: The Government Establishes Order
text: The laws the government creates help us work together in an orderly way. Imagine if there were no traffic laws. How would we drive on the roads? Laws help establish the way that we do things in our community. In the United States, everyone has to obey the same laws. The laws apply to everyone equally. The laws have to be written down.

title: The Government Provides Security
text: A function of government is to help its citizens feel safe. Governments create laws that protect people and their property. They also provide services to help do this. Fire departments are government services. If your house catches fire, the fire department will help you. The police help provide security. The military is a part of our government. It protects our whole country.

title: The Government Provides Services
text:
The United States government creates services for the public. Government services help provide order and keep us safe. They create opportunities in the community for work. These services support our health. Governments use tax money to provide these services. There are many examples of government services.

Schools: Governments use tax money to help provide schools with buildings, classroom furniture, and playground equipment.

Public Libraries: Governments pay for libraries. Libraries provide books and research services. They also provide educational and entertainment resources.

Recreation: Governments provide places of recreation. They provide public parks, playgrounds, and sports fields.

Fire Department: The fire department is an important government service that protects communities. Firefighters protect life, property, and the environment.

Police: The police department helps fight crime. Sometimes, police officers patrol neighborhoods. They make sure drivers are obeying traffic laws.

Public Sanitation: The government cleans and maintains roads. This government service keeps us safe. Trash pick-up and street sweeping are government cleaning services. Governments pay to help keep our public places clean.

title: Economic Boom
text:
In the late 1800s, Florida experienced a period of rapid economic growth, often called a “boom.” This economic boom had several causes. Florida has a warm climate, making it the best place in the United States to grow certain crops. The Florida peninsula is surrounded on three sides by water, which provides access to useful resources. The state was also relatively untouched by large-scale development at the time, which left many natural resources untouched and ready to be cultivated. The growing population of immigrants provided an increasing number of laborers for these new industries. Many more people sought to spend their leisure time in a state with sunny skies and warm beaches.

Timber

The climate of Florida provided the perfect conditions for vast forests of pine, oak, and cypress trees. Florida’s timber industry can trace its beginnings back to Spanish colonization in the mid-1700s. During the late 1800s, towns began to pop up through northern Florida to support the work of felling these large forests. Sawmills turned those trees into lumber for use around the nation in the construction of houses, ships, and more.

Citrus

Timber was not the only product the trees of Florida produced. The warm, wet climate supported citrus trees, especially orange trees. Oranges are not native to Florida or North America. They spread from Asia throughout the world. Spanish settlers introduced oranges and other citrus fruits to Florida in the 1500s. During the late 1800s, the citrus industry suffered because of strong frosts. The cold weather threatened to destroy the citrus groves. Chinese immigrant Lue Gim Gong worked to develop frost-resistant oranges, grapefruits, and other fruits and flowers. He is credited with saving Florida’s citrus industry.

Tourism

Florida’s climate supported more than the timber and citrus industries. It also attracted people as they enjoyed the state’s warmer winter months and miles of beaches. Tourists from northern states flocked to luxury resorts in Florida, like Henry Plant’s Kissimmee Hotel in Tampa and Henry Flagler’s Hotel Ponce de León in St. Augustine. Flagler expanded his offerings to tourists by establishing a series of hotels throughout Florida in the late 1800s.

Phosphate Mining

Florida does not have many mining operations because it is not generally rich in the kinds of resources that need to be mined out of the ground. One exception is phosphate, which does occur naturally in central Florida. It was difficult work in the 1800s, as it was usually mined by hand and carried out in wheelbarrows. Like the timber industry, phosphate mining supported the creation of towns where workers would live. The creation of these towns was often developed by the mining companies themselves. Phosphate from Florida was used to make fertilizer and was shipped all over the world.

Sponge Diving

Sponge diving is another industry with strong immigrant roots in Florida. Greek divers were brought to Florida to harvest the sea sponges that live in the warm waters around the Florida Keys and in the Gulf of America. These sponges were used for bathing and treating wounds. The town of Tarpon Springs quickly grew to be the center of sponge fishing in Florida. The Greek immigrants came to the town and brought their food and traditions with them. The descendants of these early Greek immigrants continue to preserve the traditions of their ancestors.

Shrimping

Shrimping was another Florida industry that came from immigrant families harvesting precious resources from the waters of the coast. Beginning in Fernandina, along the Atlantic Coast of North Florida, Greek, Italian, and other immigrants began pulling drag nets along the ocean floor. The shrimp they brought up were shipped around the country, introducing this regional food to national markets. The shrimping industry in Florida created the demand for more shrimp boats. St. Augustine served as the center of shrimp boat building for many years.

Wrecking

With all of this activity in the waters of Florida, people were bound to lose their ships and boats to underwater obstacles and poor navigation. Some Floridians made their living on the misfortune of these wayward sailors. Salvaging goods and rescuing people from shipwrecks, or “wrecking,” became a lucrative industry in Florida. Wrecking became especially popular in the Florida Keys. The shallow waters and reefs of the Florida Straits caused many ships to wreck. Wreckers received a payment equal to a portion of the goods they retrieved from stranded ships.

title: What Is Government?
text: A government is a group of people who make decisions for a community. They serve the needs of the people in the community. In the United States, adult citizens vote for people to represent them in the government. The representatives make decisions based on the law. The people agree to follow their representative’s decisions. This agreement is called consent of the governed. At every level, people’s consent is what gives the government power to act.

title: Essential Question
text: Why do people form governments?

title: Transportation Boom
text:
With the growth of the various industries in Florida came the development and expansion of new and existing transportation methods in the state. If you were harvesting shrimp or sponges, you wanted to get your goods to markets in other states. The timber and cattle industries relied on transporting their products as well. Tourists wanted faster ways to travel to and among Florida’s many hotels and points of interest. As Florida developed, new transportation networks grew to meet the demand for moving people and goods inside and outside the state.

Railroads

In the 1800s, the most popular way to move people and goods long distances over land was by railroad. Soon, passengers and products were traveling across the country as fast as the trains could carry them. As a state still fully developing its economy, Florida saw great growth in its network of railroads at this time. The first major effort at railroad construction in Florida occurred from Jacksonville through the panhandle to the west. Towns that were settled along the new route were given the names of prominent men involved in the railroad, such as Bonifay, Chipley, and DeFuniak Springs.

The route was chosen in part because it ran through the forested northern part of the state where sawmills turned the forests of Florida into valuable timber. The railroad provided vital access to the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of America. Companies could get the timber from Florida out to national and international markets much faster with a dependable railroad system. Goods shipped into ports like Jacksonville and Pensacola could more quickly move along the rail lines to the interior areas of the state.

In addition to goods and materials, the railroads provided passenger access to Florida. Several men took it upon themselves to single-handedly expand Florida’s railroads in order to provide easier access to their hotels. Henry B. Plant connected his hotels along the Gulf Coast of Florida, and Henry Flagler did the same along the Atlantic Coast. Both men connected their railroads to railroads in Georgia, linking Florida with the rest of the country. William Chipley was the main force driving the development of the railroad connecting the panhandle to the rest of the state.

Bridges

The many low-lying areas and waterways of Florida presented a challenge to the railroad builders. They could not simply lay track on solid ground in Florida. Rivers and swampy areas required the construction of bridges that could span the distances and hold the weight of the trains and their cargo.

Flagler undertook perhaps the most ambitious bridge-building project to that point. He wanted to connect the city of Miami to Key West. This would require multiple bridges, hopping over miles and miles of open water to connect the islands. The Overseas Railway was completed in the early 1900s. Railroad companies became bridge-building companies, too. The construction of these bridges throughout Florida laid the foundation for the boom in road building as automobiles became popular at the turn of the century.

Ships

In the 1800s, Florida had more ocean coastline than any other state. As railroads were still developing, many Floridians used the waterways for transportation. The railroads connected to port cities like Pensacola, Jacksonville, and Miami. Immigrants from Caribbean islands and European countries like Greece and Italy arrived by ship at Florida’s ports. These immigrants came to work for the growing industries of Florida and allowed those industries to ship their goods to markets far away.

In addition to its coastline, Florida also boasted miles of inland waterways. The rivers provided access to areas that were otherwise inaccessible. Major rivers like the St. Johns and Apalachicola Rivers served almost as highways would today, with heavy steamboat traffic moving goods and people along them. Steamboats could also travel along the shallow coastlines, further connecting the cities and towns of Florida. Steamboats remained a popular way to explore Florida’s inland areas through the 1800s.

Transportation Network

The growth of Florida’s population and economy in the late 1800s drove the growth of the state’s transportation network. Travel on land and water combined to provide people and goods with a system of transportation within the state. This system also connected Florida with the rest of the country and the world.

Timber and citrus could travel by railroad to the major ports to be shipped around the world. Tourists could arrive in St. Augustine or Tampa for vacation on railroads from the north. Immigrants could make their way to Florida by ship to the many ports along the state’s lengthy coastline and find work at one of the many stops along the railroad. Florida’s industries and transportation network grew together in the late 1800s, each one helping the other to develop and prosper.

title: Henry Plant
text:
Many people came to Florida after the Civil War to take advantage of the economic boom that was happening in the state. One of these people was Henry Plant. Plant was born in Connecticut in 1819. He began working on steamboats and in the shipping industry at an early age.

In 1854, Plant purchased his first company and began investing in the railroad industry. He purchased his first railroad, which traveled out of Savannah, Georgia. He extended this line to Jacksonville, Florida. Plant realized that building railroads in Florida would be a very successful enterprise, and he hoped to make a lot of money from the economic boom happening in the state.

Plant started the Plant Investment Company in 1882 to acquire and build new rail lines in Florida. He built the company headquarters in Sanford, Florida. Thousands of people came to Florida to work on Plant’s railroads. The new rail system also made it easier for people to reach the state. Plant had a profound impact on Florida, but he had the greatest impact on the city of Tampa.

In 1889, Plant extended his railroad to Tampa. He also renovated and expanded the port to allow more steamships and large ships to enter the port. These upgrades to the port allowed Plant to ship goods to Cuba, Jamaica, and other states located along the Gulf of America more quickly. His vast network of land and sea travel was known as the Plant System. Many industries benefited from the Plant System, including the state’s citrus, lumber, phosphate, tourism, and timber industries.

Because of his success, Plant was named the “King of Florida” by Success magazine in 1898. Plant’s impact on Florida can still be seen today.

title: Henry Flagler
text:
Henry Flagler created a network of railroads that influenced virtually every industry in Florida. Flagler was born in Hopewell, New York, in 1830. In 1852, Flagler became a partner in his brother’s business. He made enough money to start his own company, called the Flagler and York Salt Company. Within a few years, the Flagler and York Salt Company ran out of funds, and Flagler was forced to close his salt mines. This failure did not keep Flagler from seeking new business opportunities.

Flagler went back to working in the grain business and quickly began to make money again. In 1870, Flagler used the money he earned to invest in the oil business. This would prove to be one of the best business decisions of Flagler’s career. Flagler made a fortune because of these investments.

In 1878, Flagler and his wife visited Jacksonville, Florida. Flagler fell in love with the area and knew that it could become a popular tourist destination with his help. In 1888, Flagler completed construction on a luxury hotel in St. Augustine. That same year, he purchased the Jacksonville, St. Augustine, and Halifax Railroad to bring guests to his new hotel. Within a decade, he built three more luxury hotels in Daytona and Palm Beach. He expanded his railroad to reach his new resorts. This was the first time that reliable transportation reached this part of Florida. By 1896, Flagler’s railroad, which he renamed the Florida East Coast Railroad, reached Miami.

Flagler achieved great success in Florida during the 1880s and 1890s, but he hoped to achieve even more during the early 1900s. In 1905, Flagler began construction on the Over-Sea Railroad to Key West. It was completed in 1912, and the state of Florida was finally connected from Pensacola in the west all the way to Key West in the south. Flagler achieved his dream of bringing tourists, goods, and businesses to Florida. Today, Florida is a popular tourist destination thanks in large part to the efforts of Henry Flagler.

title: Population Boom
text:
As more reliable transportation came to Florida, the economy boomed, and more businesses were established around the state. Florida’s economic growth encouraged more people to move to Florida during the late 1800s. The population grew from 140,424 inhabitants in 1860 to 391,422 in 1890. Many of these new settlers migrated to Florida from other states. Thousands of immigrants also came to Florida from Europe and the Caribbean during this time.

The largest group of Caribbean immigrants to settle in Florida during this time came from Cuba. Many factors led Cuban immigrants to leave their homes and travel to Florida. Cuba is only 90 miles south of Florida, so it was easier to travel to than many other countries. Florida businesses were in desperate need of more workers and encouraged immigrants to come to the state. During the late 1800s, many people in Cuba pushed for independence from Spain and freedom for enslaved people. This conflict led to the Ten Years’ War. Thousands of Cubans fled to escape the war and the economic hardships it created.

One Cuban immigrant who settled in Florida during this time was Vicente Martínez-Ybor. Ybor was a cigar manufacturer. During the 1860s, he left Cuba and built new cigar factories in Florida. He employed thousands of Cuban refugees in his factories and encouraged many more to immigrate to the United States. In 1885, Ybor established a town outside of Tampa, where he built his largest cigar manufacturing plant and housing for his employees.

As it grew, Ybor City also embraced immigrants from other countries, including Italy, Germany, Russia, and China. This made it one of the most diverse cities in the southern United States. Cuban immigrants also created their own communities in Miami and Key West. By 1895, 2.3 percent of Florida’s population was originally from Cuba.

A small group of Greek immigrants settled in Tarpon Springs in the 1890s. Tarpon Springs was settled in 1876 by American farmers, but it quickly became a favored destination of Greek immigrants. Many of the early Greek settlers came to the city to work as sponge divers. Other Greek immigrants settled in the area to open businesses that catered to the sponge divers and their families. Today, one in 10 residents is descended from Greek immigrants.

Compared to the rest of the population, Tarpon Springs has the largest percentage of people with Greek ancestry of any city in the United States.

title: Why Do We Have Government?
text: We need rules in school to help us. The rules help us work together in an orderly way. They keep us safe and help us manage problems. Our communities need the same things. Governments were created to perform these functions, or tasks. They create laws to help provide order. They protect people and their property. Governments also help resolve conflicts.

title: The Government Creates Laws
text:
A primary focus of all governments should be to promote the common good. The common good means working to create laws and rules that benefit everyone.

Our government makes laws and rules to protect the rights of citizens. Laws and rules also provide safety and security.

Laws in the United States say people should be treated equally. The government is responsible for making sure all people are treated fairly under these laws.

title: The Telegraph
text:
The telegraph simplified the way people sent messages to one another. The telegraph was originally invented in England in the 1830s. In 1838, American inventors Samuel F. B. Morse and Alfred Lewis Vail developed a new type of telegraph, using electricity to communicate over long distances.

Morse developed his own alphabet to use with the telegraph called Morse code. Morse code is an alphabet with letters that are represented by long and short signals of sound or light. It is transmitted by pressing the key on the telegraph machine, which creates a radio wave. This technological pattern allowed scientists to use long and short waves to create the Morse code alphabet and transfer information.

Morse and Vail constructed the first telegraph line between Washington, D.C., and Baltimore, Maryland. On May 24, 1844, Vail received the first message over the line. Floridians hoped to tap into this new technology to make communication easier across the state and connect Florida to the rest of the country.

Florida entrepreneurs and businesses hoped to expand the telegraph to Florida and connect the frontier with the rest of the country. In the early 1870s, telegraph lines were installed across the Florida prairies to connect North Florida to Punta Rassa, south of Fort Myers. From there, an undersea cable was built to connect Florida to Havana, Cuba. This telegraph line furthered international trade in Florida.

title: The Government Establishes Order
text: One of the main functions of government is to create laws. Laws help us work together in an orderly way. Imagine if there were no traffic laws. How would we drive on the roads? Laws help establish the way that we do things in our community. In the United States, everyone has to obey the same laws. The laws have to be written down and applied equally.

title: The Government Provides Security
text: A function of government is to help its citizens feel safe. Governments create laws that protect people and their property. They also provide services to help do this. If your house catches fire, the fire department is there to help you. The police help provide security. The military is a part of our government. It protects our country.

title: The Government Provides Services
text:
Governments help provide things we need and want. Governments create services that support the well-being of the public. Governments use tax money to provide these services.

Government services include public transportation, police, and fire departments. Creating roads and traffic lights and providing trash pick-up are also usually government services. Many governments provide places of recreation. They are things like public parks and playgrounds. Local governments give us schools and libraries too.

title: Government Impacts Daily Life
text: Look at the scenarios. Explain how the government affects us in each scenario.

title: The United States Government: A Constitutional Republic
text: The government of the United States is a constitutional republic. This form of government is based on a written constitution. This document determines the power and functions of the government. Adult citizens vote for people to represent them in the government. The officials make decisions according to the laws of the land. The Constitution is the law of the land for the United States. The people agree to abide by the decisions of their representatives. This agreement is called consent of the governed. At every level, people’s consent is what gives the government power to act. The idea that the American people give the U.S. government its powers comes from the Declaration of Independence.

title: Essential Question
text: How does the national government work?

title: The Constitution Guides the United States Government
text:
In the United States, how the government should act is written in documents. How the communities should act are also written in documents. These documents are called laws. The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law of our country. Its purpose is to describe the duties of the government and the rights of the people being governed. It defines the basic responsibilities and structure of the government.

The United States Constitution shows how the government must work. The Constitution says there must be three branches of government. These three branches are called the executive, judicial, and legislative branches. The branches share power. This way, each branch has limits, and no branch has too much power. This is called the separation of powers. The separation of powers creates a system of checks and balances in the government.

In the United States, we have a federal government that leads our whole country. The federal government shares its power with state governments. The federal government and the U.S. Constitution serve as a model for state governments and constitutions throughout our country. Florida has a state constitution that guides the state.

The federal government has the power to:

print money

declare war

build the military

make post offices and stamps

make treaties (agreements with foreign countries)

make and enforce laws for doing business between the states and foreign nations

make laws to enforce the Constitution

title: The Executive Branch
text:
Each branch of the government was designed to address specific issues and concerns. Each branch has its own structure, processes, and leaders.

The executive branch enforces our country’s laws. It is also in charge of the military. The head of the executive branch is the president of the United States. The president is chosen by voters. The president and vice president are elected together for four years. They may serve up to two terms for a total of eight years. The president creates a group of advisors called a cabinet. Cabinet members are often experts in their fields. They help run the executive branch by leading departments. For example, the Department of Defense is in charge of the military.

The president has veto power. A veto means saying “no” to a bill. A bill is a plan for a law.

title: The Legislative Branch
text:
The legislative branch makes laws and sets taxes. Congress is the legislative branch of our national government. It is divided into two parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives. Two senators are elected from each state. A state's number of representatives depends on how many people live there. Larger states send more representatives. Smaller states send fewer. Today, there are 100 senators in the Senate and 435 representatives in the House. All of them were elected by the people of their states.

The legislative branch also approves how tax money is spent. They vote on which programs and projects the government can spend money on.

title: The Judicial Branch
text:
The judicial branch interprets the laws, or decides what laws mean. It also determines whether laws follow the Constitution.

The judicial branch is made up of judges and courts. The Supreme Court is the highest court in the land. The Supreme Court is made up of leaders called justices. They are chosen by the president and approved by senators. They work in the Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.

title: Voting, Elections, and Appointments
text:
The Constitution is not just a list of rights and laws for everyone in our country. It also tells us how our leaders should be chosen. At the national level, citizens vote to elect the president. They also elect representatives to serve in the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Citizens interested in serving in the government participate in a campaign process. Each candidate shares what they believe about different issues. Citizens study each candidate carefully and vote for the one who best represents their viewpoints. The candidate with the most votes wins! To vote, citizens need to be 18 years old or older. Citizens can vote for leaders of their community, state, or country.

An appointed official is chosen by our leaders. The leaders have to agree on public appointments. For example, the president can nominate a member to the cabinet but Congress has to approve the appointment. People who have an appointed office serve for a set period of time.

title: Florida State Government
text:
We have a national government that leads our country. We also have state governments that lead our states. We have local governments that lead our counties, cities, and towns. We have representatives at all levels of government.

Florida is led by a state government. Floridians elect leaders to represent them in our state government. These representatives work to make life better for everyone who lives in our state. Florida's government is modeled after the national government. Its powers and responsibilities are separated between three branches.

title: Essential Question
text: How do state and local governments work?

title: The Florida Constitution
text:
The current Florida constitution is our state’s sixth constitution. It was written in 1968. It explains the rules for Florida’s government.

The Florida Constitution:

organizes the state government into three branches that share power equally

works for the common good and protects citizens’ rights.

explains how the state can make laws.

requires the governor to balance the budget. (The state cannot spend more money than it collects.)

describes how the state government divides and shares power with counties and cities.

is responsible for public education, conservation of natural resources, and other public services.

title: Branches of State Government
text:
Florida’s government is divided into three branches: legislative, executive, and judicial. These three branches balance and check on each other so that no branch has more power than another branch.

The legislative branch makes the laws and can change laws that already exist. Legislators are representatives and senators. Voters elect representatives to serve two-year terms and senators to serve four-year terms.

The executive branch enforces (carries out) the laws. The governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, chief financial officer, and commissioner of agriculture make up the executive branch. The governor is the head of the executive branch of our state government.

The judicial branch decides what laws mean, how to apply the laws, and which punishments are needed for the guilty. Judges and justices make up the judicial branch. The Florida Supreme Court is the highest court in the state of Florida. It is similar to the U.S. Supreme Court. It decides whether laws go against the state's constitution.

title: Florida Local Government
text: We also have local governments. Local means belonging to one community. They lead our towns, cities, and counties. Cities and towns elect leaders called mayors. People also elect city managers, town councils, and county commissioners. These officials address community concerns. They help out in the community and act as a voice to the community. Local governments also work to provide services to members of the community. These services can be police and fire departments. They can also be public bus systems, road maintenance, and trash removal.

title: Branches of Local Government
text:
Many local governments have a city charter. The city charter is like the Constitution. It defines how the local branches of government work together.

The executive branch of the local government includes the mayor and the city manager. Local communities elect the mayor. The city manager is generally appointed by the mayor or the city council.

The city, town, and county council members represent the legislative branch. Together, they create the city or town council’s policies.

Local courts represent the judicial branch. The judicial branch decides whether someone is guilty of a crime. It protects all citizens' rights.

title: Changes for Native Americans
text:
The first people to live in North America were Native Americans. They lived here for thousands of years. Then other people started coming to America. Many people came from countries in Europe.

People who move to a new country are called immigrants. Many people have come to America since the first European immigrants arrived in the 1500s. These settlers and the Native Americans had different ways of living. This often caused problems.

As more and more people came to America, many things changed for the Native Americans. For example, immigrants brought germs that made many Native Americans sick. Many Native Americans died. Many aspects of Native American culture changed with the increasing population.

title: Essential Question
text: How did immigrants change the lives of Native Americans?

title: How Did Immigration Affect Native American Culture?
text: Native Americans made everything they needed from the land. There were no stores to buy things ready-made. However, as immigrants came, the Native Americans' lives changed.

title: The Constitution
text:
The Constitution of the United States is the country's law. It protects our natural rights. It defines our civil rights.

The Constitution has three parts.

The preamble explains the purpose of the document.

The Articles explain how the government should be run. They define the power of the government. The Articles ensure that no branch has too much power. The Constitution checks the balance of power. It helps the power remain with the people.

The Amendments are changes made after the Constitution was written.

title: Essential Question
text: How do important documents protect our liberty and rights?

title: The Bill of Rights
text:
The Bill of Rights is the first 10 amendments to the Constitution. It was created to limit how the government can control our lives. It ensures the basic rights of the people. It explains our rights as citizens.

You have rights in school because of the Bill of Rights. You have the right to free speech. This means you can say what you think. It is important to be respectful when you say what you think. You have the right to be treated fairly no matter what color your skin is or where you are from.

title: The First Amendment
text:
The Constitution says that everyone has the right to be treated equally. No matter what we look like or where we come from, we should all have the same opportunities.

The First Amendment identifies and protects five important rights of citizens. It protects freedom of religion. It protects freedom of speech and press. It protects the right to assemble and petition the government.

title: Freedom of Religion
text: The First Amendment states that we have freedom of religion. This means Americans have the right to worship in their own way. We are free to worship how or where we want. We have the responsibility to respect others’ beliefs.

title: Freedom of Speech
text: One of our most important rights is the right to free speech. Freedom of speech is the right to express your thoughts and opinions. Freedom of speech does not mean we can say anything we want to. We have the responsibility to tell the truth. We have the responsibility to use our words to make things better and not to hurt others.

title: Freedom of the Press
text: Another right we have is freedom of the press. This right protects people who report the news. This right also protects other people. It protects the right of people to express their opinions and beliefs. We can write or print our opinions in newspapers, books, on TV, or online.

title: Right to Assemble
text: Citizens have the freedom to assemble. We can meet together on public property. As citizens, we have the right to be together to talk about things. We can hold rallies, or gather in special groups. The Constitution protects this right. We have the responsibility to make sure our meetings are peaceful.

title: Right to Petition the Government
text: The Constitution protects the rights of the people. People can bring their concerns to the government. We have the right to ask the government to change if we don't agree with their decisions.

title: Week 15 Guiding Question
text: Why did English settlers choose to live on the North Atlantic seaboard?

title: Wampanoag and the Patuxet
text:
About four years before the Pilgrims arrived, the Wampanoag Nation suffered an epidemic that killed 100 percent of the population of many villages. The Pilgrims did not know that the place they chose to build their colony was also the site of one of those villages. Surviving Wampanoag members who lived nearby helped the Pilgrims learn to adapt to their new environment.

The help the Wampanoag gave the Pilgrims became very important to the survival of Plymouth Colony. The following were important people involved in interactions between the Wampanoag and the Pilgrims.

Samoset (1590-1653)

It must have been a surprise for the Pilgrims in the spring of 1621 when a tall Native American man walked up and said, "Welcome, Englishmen." Hearing one of the native people speak English was probably the last thing they expected to happen! This man was Samoset, a Patuxet. He told the Pilgrims that he came from a place that was about a five-day walk from there. He explained that the place they chose as their new home had once been a Patuxet village. He told them that a disease had killed the Patuxet a few years before. He promised to bring Massasoit, the leader of the Wampanoag, to meet and talk with them.

A few days later, Massasoit arrived with 60 men. At first, there was a standoff between the two sides. Neither group completely trusted the other. Finally, Edward Winslow offered to stay outside with some of the Wampanoag while Massasoit and 20 unarmed men entered the village to talk to John Carver, the first unelected governor of Plymouth Colony.

Massasoit (1580-1661)

Massasoit was the Great Sachem, or most important leader of the Wampanoag. He was around 41 years old when he met the Pilgrims. In Edward Winslow’s journal, a primary source, he described Massasoit:

"... in his best years, an able body, grave of countenance and spare of speech.... In his Attyre, a little or nothing differing from the rest of his followers, only a great Chaine of white bone Beades about his neck, and at it behinde his necke, hangs a little bagg of Tobacco ..."

The Pilgrims explained to Massasoit that they only wanted peace and trade with his people. They negotiated a treaty that benefitted both groups.

Squanto (1580-1622)

Squanto, who called himself Tisquantum, was a Patuxet. Before the Pilgrims arrived, Squanto was one of a group of Patuxet and Nauset kidnapped by an Englishman named Thomas Hunt. Hunt took the captives to Spain to sell as slaves. Spanish priests heard about the captives from America. They took custody of Squanto and others to try to convert them to Christianity. Somehow, Squanto escaped to England. He learned English and was employed by the Newfoundland Company to work with its governor in their colony. From Newfoundland, he made his way back to his homeland in 1619 to find that all of his people had died.

Squanto was a big help to the Pilgrims at Plymouth. He acted as an interpreter, or translator, between the English and the Wampanoag. He showed the Pilgrims good places to fish. He taught them the best way to plant crops. William Bradford wrote: "Squanto continued with them, and was their interpreter ... He directed them how to set their carne, wher to take fish, and to procure other comodities, and was also their pilott to bring them to unknowne places for their profitt, and never left them till he dyed."

title: William Bradford and Record-Keeping
text:
William Bradford was one of the Separatist colonists on the Mayflower. He was a leader in the Separatist church. He made contributions to the community in the first difficult year. For all this, the colonists made him their first elected governor. The election of the governing offices established a representative government in Plymouth. Bradford had five assistants who advised him. They helped Bradford guide the growth of the colony and its new government.

Bradford held meetings to keep the members of the community informed and to hear the concerns of the people. Only white men who owned property could vote in the town’s government. This form of government, which was called a “town meeting,” allowed more people to be part of the decision-making process. This was a step toward a form of participatory government called democracy. Although their social and legal systems were democratic in nature, they were still closely tied to their religious beliefs.

As an official of Plymouth, Bradford kept accurate records and journals. These notes recorded events, trade, and negotiations with the Wampanoag and other Native Americans in the region. They give historians a great opportunity to understand how Plymouth Colony grew to be successful.

Bradford’s records are still used today. With the help of his careful recordkeeping, millions of people can trace their ancestry back to the men, women, and children of Plymouth Colony.

title: Native American Lands
text:
Native Americans had great respect for the Earth and all life on it. They used the land they lived on in many different ways. Some farmed the land. They stayed near the same location for a growing season that was three to four months long. Some hunted game in the forests and the waterways. They used each part of an animal to meet their needs for clothing, tools, weapons, utensils, and bedding. They also gathered wild fruits, nuts, and berries. The fruit was dried and preserved to eat in the winter. The land provided for their wants and needs.

These resources were sometimes used by multiple groups at the same time. The Native American nations would create alliances over the resources and the land. Other times, Native Americans defended the lands to protect their access to these resources. However, the Native Americans believed that land was not something to be owned. They had no units of measurement for measuring land. For Native Americans, land use was shared or fought over, but the land itself was never owned.

The Europeans wanted the land for their farms and domesticated animals. More importantly, they wanted to use the resources for economic gain. The Europeans had a system of measurement for land. Surveying created boundaries. These lines could be marked clearly so everyone could know and follow the rules of ownership.

When Europeans came to America, they brought the idea of land ownership with them. Native Americans frequently negotiated and traded the same area of land to many different Europeans, just as they did with fellow Native Americans. These differences caused confusion between the two groups. Europeans thought they were buying rights to own the land. Native Americans thought the Europeans were paying for the right to use the land temporarily. They considered the negotiated cost a “user's fee.” This fee would give the colonists access to the land for hunting, fishing, and using some of the resources. It was not for ownership. This cultural difference often led to Native Americans being brought into the colonial courts on charges of breaking a negotiated contract.

Not every colonist or colonial government negotiated or traded with Native Americans for the land. There were many instances of colonial governments selling land to new settlers that had not been negotiated for with the local Native American nations.

All Native American land was acquired by Europeans through negotiation, trade, or force. These opposing views of how to use the land brought each side to various levels of conflict from court testimony to bloodshed and war.

title: Week 19 Essential Question
