title: Indigenous People’s Trade Routes
text:
For thousands of years, American Indians operated huge trade networks to get what they needed from other people in the Americas. For example, people in what is now North Dakota quarried a hard stone called flint near Knife River. The stone was so valuable in ancient times that 4,000 years ago, it was being traded far from the quarry. Copper and obsidian have also been discovered far from their natural locations. This proves a trade system existed.

Another example of trade comes from the Hohokam tribe in what is now Arizona. The Hohokam traded buffalo hides for seashells. Neither resource comes from Arizona! The hides came from tribes on the Plains. Plains tribes often traded bison robes, dried meat, and tallow with other tribes for corn and squash. The shells came from the Mojave tribe in California. By trading with both groups, the Hohokam became middlemen within a larger trade route. Middlemen took goods from one group to another during trade.

Trade was an essential part of the government. Agreements had to be made in order to trade safely. But not all trade was peaceful. Sometimes tribes would go to war to control trade routes and resources. Eventually, peace would be made with chiefs making agreements for their bands.

Rivers and Trails

Rivers were extremely important when native people needed to travel. Many traveled by canoe on major rivers like the Mississippi, Ohio, Columbia, and Missouri. Some canoes could haul thousands of pounds of goods for trade. Rivers were the “highways” for tribes. If rivers were the highways, paths were like the smaller “roads” we use today. Paths crossed all over North America.

Native peoples made and named other paths. One well-known route stretched from the forests by Lake Erie to the South Carolina coast. This trail, called the Trading Path, appeared on maps in the 1700s. Parts are still marked today.

Trails often followed the “military crest” of the ridge. Trails ran alongside, but not on the ridge tops. This way, a person could travel along the trail without being seen by those on the other side of the ridge. Many American Indians disciplined themselves to walk heel-to-toe in a single file. This left the smallest marks on the ground and allowed them to travel without being seen.

Trading Sites

Trade was very important to tribes. They exchanged food, goods, and information. Some locations were more permanent trading locations, while others moved where the people went.

One example of a permanent trading station is the straits of Mackinac. The straits of Mackinac is where Lakes Michigan and Huron meet. This area in the Great Lakes attracted tribes from all over the eastern woodlands to trade. The Odawa and Chippewa had villages at Mackinac and conducted the trade.

Most of the trade happened when native people went to other villages or designated areas for trade. These areas were often convenient locations along travel routes. One such site, the Dakota Rendezvous site, was held along the James River.

title: Many Nations
text:
Before European contact, North America was home to hundreds of tribes of Native Americans. A tribe is a name for a group of families and communities that have a common language, religion, and government. Languages, beliefs, and governments could have had differences within the same region.

Each tribe had its own myths on creation. For example, the Natchez believe they came from the sun. The Cherokee believe water is spiritually important. These Indigenous peoples also spoke many different languages, not just one. Some believe there were over 250 languages in North America at one time. When one group of people met another, they might have used hand gestures to communicate.

Each individual tribe used their region’s resources to meet their wants and needs. Some tribes planted crops. Some followed migratory animals that they hunted for food and supplies. Native Peoples fished, gathered berries, hunted, and made good use of the resources around them.

Although many of the same resources were used within the same region, no two tribes looked exactly the same. Some tribes used trees and woven grasses to make long, rectangular dwellings. Others within the same region made dome-shaped houses out of the same materials.

Each tribe put their distinct mark on the appearances of their families and communities. Some tribes would wear their hair long and make their clothing out of animal skins. Other tribes made their clothing from plant fibers. Visually, each tribe’s appearance made them distinct and recognizable to both friend and foe, even within the same region.

The natural resources of a region would have influenced the economic and cultural customs of each tribe. Animals of each region were, and still are, used in tribal stories and beliefs. For example, alligators are prominent in the Everglades of the Southeastern region. However, other areas of the Southeastern region do not have alligators at all. The Calusa tribe revere the alligator in the Southeast, but the Cherokee, who do not live near alligators, revere the owl. This reverence is based on the environment and the available resources of each region.

As you learn about American Indian tribes this week, you may find that there were many commonalities between them. As you study, remember each tribe was unique and extraordinary. Further analysis will help you to learn about the distinct culture and individuality of each tribe.

title: Governments of Indigenous People in North America
text:
Native Americans had organized communities. Women played many different roles within the tribes. Some tribes had women in their government as leaders and advisors. In other tribes, women supported family and community survival.

Long ago, some Native peoples lived in small, independent groups. Other tribes formed large confederacies. The smallest native political unit was the individual. They had complete freedom to make their own decisions. Next was the band or village. A band was a group of people of the same tribe who were closely connected, often by family ties. They might fish, hunt, and grow food together. There were leaders for different duties. Bands had one chief for war and a leader during peacetime.

Clans were larger groups of distant relatives. The clan elders were chosen to make decisions for the group. Clans were often shared by many tribes. Bands or clans joined together to form tribes.

A tribe was a group of people connected by a common language, belief, land, and culture. Tribes didn’t always have just one specific leader. They worked together to make major decisions, like going to war, choosing who to trade with, or choosing how to use natural resources.

A chiefdom was a group of tribes under one leader, or chief. For the Haudenosaunee, or the Iroquois, a woman might not be the chief of her tribe, but women helped make decisions on who their chief should be. The chief’s authority often stayed in the same family. The Iroquois believed authority was passed down through the matriarchal line. That means the power was passed through the mother's line. Cultures like the Navajo also passed authority down through the mother’s side. Other cultures were patriarchal, or passed authority down through the father’s side of the family.

For most tribes, if a chief wasn’t doing well for their people, that chief would be removed. With some groups, women made the decision to change the chief.

Some tribes joined together to form confederacies. Hundreds of years ago, the Mohawk, Onondaga, Cayuga, Oneida, and Seneca fought. To end the wars, an Iroquois woman named Jigonhsaseh, Chief Hiawatha, and the prophet the Great Peacemaker convinced the tribes to unite.

The Iroquois created a constitution called the Great Law of Peace. This agreement included a balance of power between bigger and smaller groups, a two-branch legislature, procedures for passing laws, and more.

As the Cherokee were being pushed west, groups of Cherokee women asked the leaders of their tribes to not give the land away.

No matter the structure, the purpose of having a government was the same: to provide safety and security for those in the community. How each group’s government achieved this varied. Some restricted freedoms and liberties, while others ensured them to provide safety and security. Both Native American men and women worked together to provide safety and security for their people.

A government also provides justice and maintains order within the community and helps the members of the community meet their wants and needs. Every community, past and present, has a form of government. The amount of authority given to government leaders varies based on the community. Each tribe chose leaders in different ways. Leadership varied between men and women in the government. Leadership authority was based on age, wisdom, leadership skills, or heredity. Each tribe chose the best leader to ensure the safety of the community.

Authority was distributed across the community, and leaders had authority over smaller numbers of people. A chief had authority over more people than a band leader. In a confederacy, the leaders had authority over a great number of people from many communities or nations. Women worked right alongside the men. The goal was to provide safety, justice, and welfare for the people.

title: Customs and Traditions
text:
The tribes of North America have many different cultures and traditions. Each tribal group has its own beliefs, rituals, and traditions. Many traditions are connected with the land the tribes call home. This connection to their homeland is similar for many tribes. Native American tribes are different in many ways, but they also share many similar customs and traditions. Tribes have marriage ceremonies, funerals, and rites of passage for youth. Tribal culture includes language, storytelling, and the arts, celebrations, food, and clothing.

Language

Before the arrival of Europeans in North America, there were approximately 500 different Native American languages spoken by millions of Indigenous peoples. The languages of various tribes were diverse. Some languages were spoken within a very small area, while others were spoken by large numbers of people across the continent. Many Native American languages are still spoken today. However, many languages have also become extinct after the European colonization of North America. Today, many tribes are trying to bring back their original languages.

Storytelling and the Arts

The arts and storytelling are a large part of Native American culture. Native peoples living in North America did not use an alphabet to communicate, but they did have symbols that were part of stories. These symbols were placed on important, ceremonial items or painted on rocks. They mainly used the spoken word to communicate and to preserve their history and traditions. Often, their speeches took the form of stories. Many stories explained their beliefs and the creation of the world. Some stories represented actual events that happened in the tribe’s past. Some represented relationships between families and their ancestors. Other stories are more like religious stories for the tribes. These stories have lessons on how to be a good person and treat everything with respect. Elders often taught these stories to children. Animals, birds, and the environment were often part of these important stories, creating a special bond to the land.

Throughout North America, Native peoples made beautiful pieces of art from natural materials around them. They used shells, porcupine quills, or feathers for decoration. Jade, turquoise, and other stones were used to create their art. They crafted jewelry and other items from silver, turquoise, and gold. Some cultures were known for creating elaborate sculptures out of stone, wood, and other materials. Many tribes wove baskets and made pottery. But not all the things made by Native peoples were simply art. Many items were used in ceremonies and considered very sacred. These sacred items are only used for special occasions, like a funeral. Early Native American art continues to influence artists, and many tribes continue to create art in the same way as their ancestors.

Ceremonies and Celebrations

Native American tribes had their own individual ceremonies and celebrations, but many tribes celebrated for common reasons. Ceremonies and celebrations were often held to honor their ancestors and celebrate the natural elements around them. Many holidays honor the sun, rain, and harvest.

Dancing, singing, and praying are very important in Native American ceremonies. Many ceremonies are performed to help people who are sick. Some ceremonies are to celebrate when a child becomes an adult. When warriors came back from battle, special ceremonies were performed to help them not be angry. There were celebrations for a good harvest, giving thanks for the food. When a young hunter killed their first deer or bison, a special feast would be held to honor the animal and the new hunter for the community.

Food

Native Americans across North America relied on the land for food. Tribes hunted, gathered, and farmed for food. Many of the foods Native Americans ate were based on the seasons. Seasonal crops and hunting patterns played a huge role in community activities. Members of each tribe worked together to provide food for the community. Many of the foods that we enjoy today can be traced back to the crops grown by Native Americans. These include corn, potatoes, tomatoes, peanuts, wild rice, squash, and beans.

Clothing

Before European exploration, Native American tribes used natural resources from the land to create clothing. Native American clothing represented the natural environment in which they lived. Clothing was practical and reflected the climate where they lived. Native Americans used animal products, such as fur, feathers, bones, teeth, and claws to make clothing and jewelry. They also used plants like tree bark and various grasses to make woven fabrics. Native Americans wore different forms of clothing for different purposes. Many tribes wore decorative headdresses, masks, and clothing for ceremonies and celebrations.

title: Innovations
text:
Tools

Native American tribes created and used many tools before Europeans arrived in North America. Various tools were used for hunting, fishing, farming, and in everyday life. Native American tools were made from stone, wood, animal bones and antlers, and shells. They created drills and chisels to build homes, canoes, and weapons. Sewing needles were made of animal bone. They used them to sew clothing, shoes, and fishing nets. Many tribes also had specific tools for grinding corn, nuts, and other plants for eating and medicinal purposes.

Agriculture

Native farmers studied wild plants and learned which foods would grow well in certain areas. They also learned how to create new plants from old ones. Great Lakes peoples cultivated wild rice. The Iroquois grew crops in small mounds called milpas to prevent soil erosion. Tribes of the Northeast used fish to fertilize their crops. This allowed them to grow in sandy soil. Many native cultures created irrigation systems to water their crops. They built canals, pipelines, reservoirs, and dams to bring water from distant sources to their farms.

Medicine

Native peoples found many ways to use plants as medicine. Native Americans knew which plants and herbs would cure common ailments, such as fever, pain, burns, and wounds. Black willow bark was brewed into a tea and consumed to prevent pain. Sage was used to cure stomach issues and skin rashes. Some tribes used milkweed plants to treat sore throats and prevent coughing.

Transportation

Before the arrival of Europeans, water was the main mode of transportation for Native Americans. Waterways were vital to the movement of people and goods. American Indians have used canoes for thousands of years. Their invention made transportation, trading, and fishing much easier. Tribes used materials from the environment they lived in to make canoes. Bark canoes were very popular because they were lightweight. They could also be made from materials in forested areas. Sometimes, people used animal skins to wrap around the stick frames of their canoes. In the northeastern United States, birch bark was very popular.

Canoes were also made by digging out the inside of large logs. This was long, hard work. The final canoe, called a dugout, was very heavy. The Native Americans of the Pacific Coast made dugout canoes from cedar. Cedar is wood that naturally resists water and rot. People burned the inside of a log. Then they used sharp-edged rocks or shells to scrape out the burned part. Another interesting canoe was made with planks that were carefully split from a log and sewn together with strands of animal hide. The cracks between the planks were filled with a substance like tar made from plant materials and mud. A swift canoe could take travelers 150 miles or more after a long, hard day of paddling!

title: Lives of Indigenous People
text:
For thousands of years before European exploration of the Americas, people called these continents home. These first peoples were very diverse. They had many names that identified their communities. These communities were called tribes.

Today, the Indigenous peoples of North America are often called Native Americans, Native Hawaiians, or Native Alaskans. Each Indigenous tribe has its own unique customs and culture. These tribes lived, moved, and called the Americas home long before Europeans arrived.

Each tribe or nation had a different way of life. Still, cultures that had developed by the 1400s shared many similarities.

Each tribe had a sophisticated society of families, markets, and governments. They had celebrations and remembrance ceremonies. Oral histories of heroes and the past were passed down in each tribe. Trade and communication were established to meet their wants and needs. Safety and security were part of each community. Entertainment and work were mixed into their days. All the things that mark a vibrant society in any time period were present in the native tribes of North America.

title: Tribes of the Northeast
text:
Native Americans of the Northeast, or Eastern Woodlands, lived in a land rich in fresh water, including the Great Lakes. The land was also good for farming and had many types of trees and other plants.

Many tribes lived in the Eastern Woodlands. These included the Iroquois, Algonquin, Penobscot, Chippewa, Odawa, and Powhatan. They grew corn, beans, and squash. The tribes used all the natural resources around them to meet their basic needs. They used birchbark to build canoes and cover their homes. They burned wood to stay warm and cook food. They used tools for work and as weapons. The animals they hunted fed the people. The animal hides, or skins, were used to make clothes, containers, and bags. Everything was used, and nothing was wasted.

Eastern Woodlands tribes lived in larger villages in the summer and smaller family groups in the winter. The houses were different from tribe to tribe. Some tribes lived in wigwams, which are small, dome-shaped homes. The Chippewa lived in wigwams. Tribes lived in wigwams when they moved to hunt, fish, and gather natural resources. Other tribes lived in larger, more permanent longhouses. The Iroquois lived in longhouses. Many people could live in a single longhouse. The homes fit the lifestyles of each community.

title: Essential Question
text: How were family and community structures of Indigenous peoples similar to and different from one another?

title: Tribes of the Southeast
text:
The Southeast region of the U.S. includes land from the Ohio River to the Gulf of Mexico and from Texas to the Atlantic Ocean. The Native Americans who lived in this area had access to excellent soil for growing crops. Many of them were farmers. Corn was an important crop and was traded with other tribes. Southeastern tribes hunted and fished for their proteins. The land was also rich in plants that were made into medicines to help heal people. Because this area is a mixture of forests and grasslands, homes ranged from grass huts to wooden houses.

One of the largest tribes of the Southeast was the Creek tribe. Many early Creek tribes built large earthen mounds throughout the region. These mounds were part of large ceremonial complexes. The Creek lived in log cabins made from lumber, mud, and tree bark. Like other tribes, the Creek adapted to their environment and used the resources available where they settled. The Creek were expert farmers and planted crops such as corn, beans, and squash. They also hunted and fished for food.

title: Native American Land
text:
Native Americans had great respect for Earth and all life on it. They used the land they lived on in many different ways. Some farmed the land. They stayed near the same location for a growing season that was three to four months long. Some hunted game in the forests and the waterways. They used each part of an animal to meet their needs for clothing, tools, weapons, utensils, and bedding. They also gathered wild fruits, nuts, and berries. The fruit was dried and preserved to eat in the winter. The land provided for their wants and needs.

These resources were sometimes used by multiple groups at the same time. The tribes of North America created alliances over the resources and the land. Other times, tribes defended the lands to protect their access to these resources. However, the Native Americans believed land could not be owned. They had no units of measurement for measuring land. For Native Americans, land use was shared or fought over, but the land itself was never owned.

The Europeans valued the possession of land for their farms and domesticated farm animals. More importantly, they wanted to use the resources for economic gain. The Europeans had a system of measurement for land. Surveying created boundaries. These lines could be marked clearly so everyone could know and respect the ownership.

When Europeans came to America, they brought the idea of land ownership with them. The Indigenous people of North America frequently negotiated and traded the same area of land to many different Europeans, just as they did with fellow Native Americans. This caused considerable confusion. Europeans thought they were buying rights to own the land. Native Americans thought the Europeans were paying for the right to use the land. They considered the negotiated cost a “user's fee.” This fee would give the colonists access to the land for hunting, fishing, and using some of the resources. It was not for ownership. This misunderstanding often led to Native Americans being brought into the colonial courts on charges of breaking a negotiated contract.

Not every colonist or colonial government negotiated or traded with Native Americans for the land. There were many instances of colonial governments selling land to new settlers that had not been negotiated for with the local tribal nations.

All Native American land was acquired by Europeans through negotiation, trade, or force. These opposing views of how to use the land brought each side to various levels of conflict from court testimony to bloodshed and war.

title: Essential Question
text: What was daily life like for those who settled in the Southern, Middle, and New England Colonies?

title: Mercantilism
text:
The American colonies were chartered to trade with England. Colonists sent raw materials to England. These raw materials would be used in England to make manufactured goods that would be exported to the English colonies. This economic system is called mercantilism. In the mercantile system, governments want to increase exports, or what they sell to other countries. They also want to decrease imports, or what they buy from other countries. That keeps more money flowing into their economies. When a country sells more than it buys, it has a favorable balance of trade.

Mercantilism in the colonies meant that the colonies could not sell their raw materials to anyone but the English. They were not allowed to import anything except from England. This guaranteed only English goods were sold in the colonies. To keep this balance, England also charged tariffs. A tariff is a tax on goods coming from another country. Tariffs were added to the cost of the goods. This made the goods more expensive.

Each colony in America had a deep-water sea port. Large ships criss-crossed the Atlantic with goods to and from these ports from all over the world. A port was essential to the economy in each colony. Each port had a royal customs office at the docks. This office checked and taxed all cargo being brought on or off ships. This ensured the royal customs officer knew exactly what was being shipped. This also guaranteed the royal customs officer knew where the ships were going.

England created rules to make sure they would have a favorable trade balance. These rules were called the Navigation Acts. They required:

Only England or English colonial ships could carry cargo between England and the colonies.

Certain goods, including tobacco, rice, and furs, couldn’t be shipped to foreign nations unless they went through England or Scotland first. The English government would pay bounties, or rewards, to Americans who produced certain raw goods while raising tariffs on the same goods produced in other countries.

American colonists would not compete with English manufacturers in large-scale manufacturing.

This favorable trade balance created a network of trade routes between England, Africa, and America and the West Indies. It was referred to as triangular trade because there were three connecting routes. Each part of the triangular route had a name. The voyage from Europe to Africa was called the Outward Passage. Ships carried manufactured goods for trade in Africa. Enslavers traded people for these manufactured goods. The enslavers captured men, women, and children. They were then sold to become enslaved workers for the colonies. The Middle Passage, as it was called, went from Africa to the West Indies and American colonies. The Inward Passage then shipped raw materials to England.

In the triangular trade system, as in the Columbian Exchange, England benefited greatly from the natural resources of America. Each section of the colonies had specialized goods they provided in this trade triangle. The geographic location, the climate, and the population of the colony determined what goods it produced. American colonies built economies based on supply and demand. This system was regulated by the government to make sure England made a large profit. The mercantile system made many colonists in the Americas and investors in England rich. It was the drive for wealth that created mercantilism. The people made choices without considering what the true cost would be in people’s lives.

title: Ensign Joseph Coulon de Jumonville
text:
Ensign Joseph Coulon de Villiers de Jumonville was born in New France into a military family. His older half-brother became the military leader at Fort Duquesne in the Ohio River country in what is now Pittsburgh. They were very well known in the French army and the French government.

On the morning of May 27, 1754, Jumonville was with 35 French soldiers near Fort Duquesne. He awoke that morning to gunfire. Virginia militia soldiers and their American Indian allies were in the midst of the French soldiers.

What happened that morning has many conflicting reports. This is what is known: Jumonville and some of his soldiers were killed. How did this happen? The French said one thing. The Virginians said another. The American Indians said something entirely different from the others.

According to the Articles of Capitulation, the document that outlined the terms of the surrender of Fort Necessity, Jumonville’s brother Louis Coulon, sieur de Villiers stated, “...Since the English have in their power an officer and two cadets, and, in general, all the prisoners whom they took when [they] assassinated Sieur de Jumonville they now promise to send them with an escort to Fort Duquesne....”

Jumonville was an important person in France. His death sparked a series of events that set the world on a course for war.

title: Tanaghrisson the Half-King
text:
Tanaghrisson the Half-King was an important person in the Iroquois Confederacy.

The fur trade was necessary for Tanaghrisson and his people. He told the French he was their friend and ally against the British. This protected his family and kept them trading with the French. Then, when the British came, Tanaghrisson and his people also became friends and allies with the British. This allowed his people to trade with the British. Tanaghrisson was trading with both the French and the British. He was also a scout and ally for young George Washington when Washington was in the Ohio Country.

In May 1754, Tanaghrisson told Washington a French military party was nearby. He led Washington and his men to meet Ensign Joseph Coulon de Jumonville’s camp.

Tanaghrisson left Washington and his men at Fort Necessity following the death of Jumonville. He moved his people away from the Ohio River to an area in the Allegheny Mountains near Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, where he died in the fall of 1754.

title: Conestoga Wagons
text:
The Conestoga wagon was built by German settlers who lived in Pennsylvania, near the Conestoga River. Its main purpose was hauling up to six tons of freight. Skilled craftsmen built these wagons with U-shaped floors. Gates on either end of the “U” helped keep goods in the wagon from shifting and sliding around during transport. The gates could easily be lowered to make loading and unloading easier. Waterproof canvas was stretched over wooden hoops over the wagon to protect the contents from inclement weather.

Four to six horses were generally used to pull the wagons. Unlike later prairie schooners, or “covered wagons,” as they are commonly called, drivers of Conestoga wagons did not ride on the wagon itself. Instead, the driver traveled with the wagon in one of three ways. One was to walk on the left side of the wagon, where the brake was installed. Another way was to stand or sit on a “lazy board,” also on the left side, which was a piece of wood they could pull out to ride on. Finally, they could ride on the horse closest to the front left side of the wagon to be close to the brake.

Conestoga wagons were used in much the same way truck trailers are used for hauling goods today. The wagons were so large they often didn’t or couldn’t move out of the way of oncoming traffic. Other wagons and travelers had to move over to pass the Conestoga wagons. They moved to the right so the left side of each vehicle faced the center of the road. This practice was the origin of why Americans drive on the right side of the road and the driver’s seat is on the left side of the car!

As more and more people began to make their way into the West, common farm wagons were modified for families to move across the Plains. Farm wagons were lighter and more practical to use than the Conestoga wagons, which were too heavy. These modified farm wagons were called prairie schooners or covered wagons. They typically had flat floors and riding boards in front for the driver to sit on. Prairie schooners became the most common type of wagon used by pioneers moving west in the 1800s.

title: Needs and Wants of a Community
text:
Just like individuals, communities have needs and wants. Goods and services meet community needs and wants. Goods are things that people buy to meet their needs and wants. People produce goods like food, clothing, furniture, and toys to meet the wants and needs of a community.

A service is work that a person does for someone else. Communities provide services to people. Important community services include providing water, electricity, schools, and hospitals to meet people’s needs.

A community must evaluate if something is a want or a need. Communities work together to provide goods and services. Together, they examine needs and the possible resources available to meet those needs. Community members share their opinions. They talk, give demonstrations, write articles for the newspaper, or put up signs to make their wants or needs known.

When all of the opinions are heard, people begin to compromise to reach a positive outcome. In a compromise, everyone gives something up to create a solution. When we compromise, we think about what is best for the group. We don't just think about what we want individually.

Needs and wants can change due to personal, environmental, and economic events. If your parents lose their job, they may not have enough money to spend on wants. Basic human needs, like food, water, shelter, and clothing, become the main priority. Resources can become scarce, or not available, after a natural disaster or in times of war. It can be difficult for people to meet their basic needs. Communities must work together to share resources and help each other.

title: The Civil Rights Movement
text:
In last week's lesson, you learned about the Civil Rights Movement, which helped African Americans gain their legal rights as citizens. It also helped people of different races begin to understand one another so that they could work together to make our state and our country better places to live. You studied Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., who spoke some very famous words on Aug. 23, 1963, at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C. He even mentioned our state in part of his speech:

"I have a dream ... I have a dream that, one day down in Alabama, little black boys and black girls will be able to join hands with little white boys and white girls as sisters and brothers."

Many others worked with King in the Civil Rights Movement. Some were ordinary people who joined together to try and create a peaceful revolution. Others held government positions that allowed them to help change unfair laws. One was a man named Thurgood Marshall. In 1967, he was appointed to the Supreme Court by President Lyndon B. Johnson. Thurgood Marshall was the first African American to serve on the Supreme Court. Throughout his life, he worked within the law to give equal rights to people who had been treated unfairly since the time of slavery. His work helped end segregation in our country. Marshall died in 1993, but his legacy lives on in our schools, our businesses and our courts.

In this week's lesson, you will learn about the results of the hard work and dedication of the civil rights workers. You will hear about how the Civil Rights Act of 1964 ended segregation in schools and other public facilities and how the passage of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 gave all eligible adults the right to vote. You will also learn about the Civil Rights Act of 1968 that gave African Americans the right to live wherever they wanted to live. So turn the page and find out more about how things have changed for all Americans.

title: King Makes Her Mark
text:
Coretta Scott King, who died in 2006, was one of the great leaders of the Civil Rights Movement. After Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination in 1968, she carried on her husband's work for almost 40 years. She wanted to fulfill his dream of a country where all people had equal rights. King gave hundreds of speeches in our country and overseas and was active in several civil rights organizations. She also wrote and published two books, The Words of Martin Luther King, Jr. and My Life with Martin Luther King, Jr.

King was born April 27, 1927, in Heiberger, Alabama, which is northwest of Montgomery. She spent her childhood on her parents' cotton farm with her sister Edythe and her brother Obie. The children helped pick the cotton during hard times to help make ends meet.

As a child, King walked five miles each day to school. She was a hardworking, intelligent student. She loved music, played the piano and trumpet, and sang in her school's recitals. In 1945, she graduated from Lincoln High School as valedictorian, or the top student, of her class.

King attended Antioch College, where she majored in music and education. After graduation, she won a scholarship to study concert singing in Boston, where she met Martin Luther King Jr. They were married in 1953.

The next year, they moved to Montgomery, Alabama, where Dr. King began his work as a minister and civil rights activist. Through the years, besides raising her four children, Coretta Scott King walked beside her husband in marches, gave speeches, and organized a series of freedom concerts, which told the story of the Civil Rights Movement.

title: Freedom Riders
text:
The first group of Freedom Riders was organized in 1947 in Washington, D.C. It was set up to test the enforcement of a U.S. Supreme Court decision. The court had ruled that segregation in interstate travel was unconstitutional. African American and white people boarded buses together to ride through the South. As they traveled, they tested each city’s compliance with the law.

The Congress of Racial Equality (CORE) revived the Freedom Riders initiative in 1961. They wanted to test another Supreme Court decision from 1960. This ruling said that segregation at terminals for buses that traveled between states was also unconstitutional. This time, women were included among the riders. African American and white riders began their trip in Washington, D.C. They planned to travel through the southern states to New Orleans and stop at bus terminals along the way. African American riders would attempt to use white-only restrooms, lunch counters, and waiting areas.

The ride was fairly uneventful through Virginia and North Carolina. When the riders reached Rock Hill, South Carolina, an African American rider named John Lewis, a white rider named Albert Bigelow, and another African American rider tried to enter a whites-only waiting room. These three were violently attacked by white people waiting in the terminal.

As the ride continued, the group split onto two buses, a Trailways bus and a Greyhound bus. When the Greyhound bus arrived in Anniston, Alabama, a mob of 200 white people was waiting at the bus terminal. The driver kept driving past the terminal. The mob followed in cars. The tires on the bus were blown out. When the bus stopped, someone threw a bomb onto the bus. The Freedom Riders all escaped the burning bus, but then they were attacked by the mob. The Trailways bus riders also met with mob violence when they reached Birmingham, Alabama. The violence increased in Montgomery, Alabama.

Photographs of the burning bus were printed in newspapers and broadcast on television. The nation’s attention was drawn to the Freedom Riders. Hundreds of new Freedom Riders joined the cause. Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy ordered 600 federal marshals to go to Montgomery to stop the increasing violence. Pressure from the government and the shocked public resulted in regulations established by the Interstate Commerce Commission to be respected. There were no more segregated facilities in bus terminals.

title: Role of Government in Economics
text:
The government's main economic role is to use money and funds to provide services to citizens. We use government goods and services every day. An example is the school you attend, if it's a public school. The road you took to school is another example. The government provides these goods and services. People who work pay a part of their income to the federal government in the form of taxes. When you buy something, you pay a little more than the price tag says. This is because you're also paying a small tax, called a sales tax. Sales tax helps the government provide goods and services to everyone.

Many of the goods and services the government provides are known as public services. An example of this is going to your community library. It doesn't cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. Other public services provided by the government include the police, fire and water departments, parks, and public health departments.

Businesses people own are considered private enterprises. What are some private businesses in your area? Think about the restaurants, stores, and gas stations you visit.

title: Supply and Demand
text:
The price of goods and services changes. Most of the time, the price of goods and services depends on supply and demand. Supply is the amount of product that is available. Economists look at several things when they study supply. They look at the product being sold. Next, they want to know who is selling it. Finally, they study the market for the product. Economists study prices being charged for a product and how much it costs a company to make it.

Demand is the amount of product people actually want or need. When there is a greater demand for a product than producers can supply, a shortage occurs. Shortages usually mean prices go up as people compete to buy it. When there's a greater supply of something than a demand for it, it's called a surplus. A surplus usually means prices go down. Producers lower prices to boost sales.

title: Creating a Budget
text:
A budget is a plan for how to spend money wisely. A budget shows how much money you have and how you're going to use it. When planning a budget, try to balance the money you earn, called income, and money you spend, called expenses. You can make a budget for each week, month, or even a year. To make a budget, think about how much money you will make for the time period of the budget. Then think about things you will need to spend money on. Most people include money they will spend on housing, clothing, food, and transportation.

You will also want to think about money to spend on things you want. Wanted items include things like movie tickets, video games, and eating out. A good budget will also note the amount of money you will save. Saving money is important. People need to be prepared to pay for things they might need in the future. Using a budget helps you think about what you want to do with your money. It also helps to keep you from spending more than you have. A budget helps you plan for the future. By sticking to a budget, you will make more responsible money choices.

title: Goods and Services
text:
Goods are items you can use or consume to meet your needs and wants. They are produced using human, natural, and capital resources. Goods can also be things people grow. In the United States, goods fall into two categories. These are private and public goods. Private goods are items you can buy from a business with your own money. Private goods include food, clothing, furniture, and toys. Public goods are paid for by taxes, not individual consumers. Public goods include law enforcement, sewer systems, and public parks.

A service is work that one person does for someone else. Services are actions, such as haircuts, car repairs, medical check-ups, mail delivery, and teaching. Services provided by the government are known as public services. These include hospitals, schools, police and fire stations, trash pickup, and public transportation. An example of a public service is going to your community library. It doesn't cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. Businesses owned by people are considered private enterprises.

How do companies compete to provide goods and services to consumers? Specialization lets companies make more and better products. They make more money if they make more of a product to sell. When a company makes more money, they can hire more workers. Then, more people have money to spend on things they need and want. Many companies may specialize in the same goods and services. This allows consumers to make choices. They can choose goods and services they wish to purchase based on price, availability, and quality.

The United States produces many goods for consumers around the globe. It produces billions of dollars worth of public and private goods, industrial supplies, automobiles, and agricultural products. These goods are used by consumers in our country. They are also exported to countries all over the world.

title: Static Electricity
text:
Things I’m still wondering about static electricity

Answers to my questions from the article

Static electricity is a ____________ of electric charge on the _________ of an object. Particles can have a positive or negative charge. They are happiest when the amount of particles with a positive and negative charge in one space is equal. When two objects rub against each other, the particles move from one place to another. This creates an imbalance, which creates static electricity. For example, think of rubbing a balloon and a sweater together. The balloon gains particles with a negative charge. It becomes a negatively charged object. Paper is a positively charged object. So, when you bring the balloon close to the paper, the objects pull toward each other. The paper jumps up to the balloon. The opposite happens when you set two negatively charged balloons close together. They will push away from each other. This is because likes repel and opposites attract.

Lightning is a natural example of static electricity. A storm cloud has charged particles in it. When the particles start moving toward each other, they cause a spark. Because the cloud is so big and there are so many particles, it is a very big spark that we can see from the ground.

title: Earnings and Income
text:
How do people pay for their needs and wants? People must work in order to earn money. People work in many jobs to earn money. You could work in a restaurant or grocery store. You could farm the land and grow crops. You could maybe open your own business. You can also become a teacher, veterinarian, doctor, lawyer, or computer programmer. The possibilities are endless!

Money that you receive for working is called income. You can do many things with your income. Most people use their income to meet their needs. This includes your home, electricity, food to eat, and transportation. Medical services, like visiting the doctor or going to the dentist, also cost money.

You can also use your money to buy things you want. Some people choose to save a portion of their income for the future. You can earn money to buy goods and services you need and want. People have many choices about how to save and spend their income. Part of the income people earn is collected by the government in the form of taxes. Taxes pay for the community, state, and national services.

title: Banks
text:
A bank is a business that deals with money. Banks provide many services to their customers. A bank's primary function is to hold their customers' money in accounts. It is safer to keep your money in a bank than to keep it at home. Banks also lend money to people in the form of loans. Loans are a type of debt in which the person borrowing the money agrees to pay it back within a certain amount of time. They also agree to pay interest. These are additional fees people agree to pay to borrow money. People use loans for many reasons. Some examples are paying for college, buying a home, or purchasing a car.

There are three main types of banks. The first is a commercial bank. These banks serve both businesses and individuals. They offer checking accounts, loans, and saving accounts to their customers. The second kind of bank is a savings bank. These banks are similar to commercial banks. Savings banks mostly offer savings accounts and loans.

The third type of bank is called a credit union. Credit unions were started to help people borrow money. People in the same type of employment put their savings together and loan it to others within that organization. In other words, they operate their own banks. Today, credit unions provide many of the same services as commercial and savings banks. However, they are nonprofit organizations. This means that all the members of the credit union share any profit they make.

title: Paying Taxes
text:
A tax is a percentage of money that a person pays. There are many different types of taxes. You pay taxes on items you buy or items you already own. Sales taxes are taxes you pay on things you buy. There are also taxes you pay every year on things you already own, like property taxes. Property taxes are taxes you pay for owning a house or a car.

Federal income taxes are taxes you pay to the federal government. State income taxes are taxes you pay to the state you live in. Both state and federal income taxes are based on how much income you earn every year.

Taxes pay for public services. If it weren't for taxes, you wouldn’t be able to go to public school. You wouldn't have a town library where you can check out books for free. You also wouldn't have roads to drive on or garbage pick-up to take away your trash. In your community, taxes pay police officers and firefighters to keep you safe. Taxes also maintain local parks and provide clean water to drink. Being able to earn an income helps you buy the things you want and need. Paying taxes contributes to the well-being of your community, state, and country.

title: Role of Government in Economics
text:
The government's main economic role is to use money and funds to provide services to citizens. We use government goods and services every day. An example is the school you attend, if it's a public school. The road you took to school is another example. The government provides these goods and services. People who work pay a part of their income to the federal government in the form of taxes. When you buy something, you pay a little more than the price tag says. This is because you're also paying a small tax, called a sales tax. Sales tax helps the government provide goods and services to everyone.

Many of the goods and services the government provides are known as public services. An example of this is going to your community library. It doesn't cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. Other public services provided by the government include the police, fire and water departments, parks, and public health departments.

Businesses people own are considered private enterprises. What are some private businesses in your area? Think about the restaurants, stores, and gas stations you visit.

title: Location
text:
People use geographic representations, such as maps and globes, to acquire, process, and report information from a spatial perspective. Maps help people learn about an area and determine where something is located. Geographers describe places with both relative and absolute location. The relative location of a place tells us where a place is relative to, or compared to, something else. When we are describing the relative location of a place, we use words such as "by," "near," "above," and "below." If your friend tells you that their house is “down the street and across from the supermarket,” they are using relative location.

A place's absolute location is its exact location. Absolute location is more helpful when you're trying to find an unfamiliar place. The absolute location of a place could be its physical address or coordinates. Coordinates are numbers and letters located along the margins of a map that help you find a place's location. Coordinates can be used on a map with a grid line system. A grid line system, called longitude and latitude, is also used to find a place's absolute location. Vertical lines of longitude go around the Earth from the North Pole to the South Pole. Lines of longitude show how far east or west places are from the Prime Meridian. We call these lines meridians. Horizontal lines of latitude show how far north and south places are from the Equator. Cartographers use these lines to divide a map into small squares. These squares can be labeled with numbers, letters, or both. These squares make finding a location easier.

title: Prime Meridian and Longitude
text:
Cartographers draw lines on a map from the North Pole to the South Pole. This helps us be more specific in our mapping. One of these lines, the Prime Meridian, divides the world in half vertically. These halves are called the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere.

Absolute location uses latitude and longitude lines to pinpoint where something is located. These lines are measured in degrees. Each degree is divided into 60 minutes, and each minute has 60 seconds. The Earth is divided into 24 different time zones. The reason for this division is because the Earth rotates on its axis once a day. A time zone is one of the ways that the world is divided and is based on what time it is in a given location. The starting point for these time zones is the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, also called Greenwich Mean Time. Theoretically, every 15 degrees east or west of Greenwich means one hour more or less. In practice, however, time zones do not go through the middle of countries. Larger countries have multiple time zones. For convenience, time zone boundaries often follow political boundaries instead of longitude lines.

The International Date Line is another imaginary line on Earth's surface. It defines the boundary between one day and the next. The International Date Line is located halfway around the world from the Prime Meridian.

title: Equator and Latitude
text:
We divide up the world for mapping purposes. Imagine a horizontal line that runs around the middle of the world. Cartographers draw this imaginary line on many of the maps they make. They call this line the Equator. The Equator divides the Earth into hemispheres. A hemisphere is a division on Earth between north and south or east and west.

The Northern Hemisphere includes all of the land and oceans that are north of the Equator. The Southern Hemisphere includes everything to the south. The Equator crosses parts of South America, Asia, and Africa. Horizontal lines of latitude run east and west around the Earth. These lines show how far from the Equator places are. We call these latitude lines parallels.

title: Essential Question
text: What are the physical characteristics of a place?

title: Physical Characteristics
text: Physical characteristics describe the natural environment of an area. Landscapes, plants, climate, and animals are physical characteristics. Bodies of water, including rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans, are also physical characteristics. Landforms are also a physical characteristic of an area. Some examples of landforms are mountains, plains, valleys, and deserts. These characteristics are all connected and help geographers describe different areas on the Earth’s surface. Physical characteristics are what make the Earth interesting and unique! A physical map shows the world's major physical features. Look at the physical map of the United States. Can you locate the rivers? Can you identify the surrounding oceans?

title: Resources
text: Resources help living things survive. Living things use resources to make what they need and want.

title: Natural Resources
text:
A natural resource is something found in nature that people can use. There are many types of natural resources in the world around us. These include soil, plants, coal, water, natural gas, and even animals. We use natural resources to meet our needs and wants. Sometimes, we use natural resources just as they are. For example, we use water to drink and for cooking and cleaning. We also eat fruits and vegetables that grow naturally in our environment.

We use some natural resources to make products that make our lives easier. We burn coal and use natural gas to power and heat our homes, schools, and businesses. We use trees to build furniture and houses. Trees are also used to make paper and books. We also use natural resources to make some of the items we use daily. This includes cell phones, computers, clothing, and even your toothbrush!

Natural resources can be either renewable or nonrenewable. Renewable resources are those that can be renewed, or replaced. Trees are an example of a renewable resource. This is because new trees can be planted to replace those we cut down. Even though renewable resources can be replaced, it's important to use our resources wisely and not waste them.

Nonrenewable resources are resources that cannot be easily replaced. Oil and natural gas are two examples of nonrenewable resources. It took millions of years to form these resources. Once we use them all up, they're gone forever.

It's important to learn to conserve, protect, and use our natural resources wisely. Then there will be enough of them in the future. Conserving our natural resources also helps us protect the environment.

title: Ecosystems
text:
Ecosystems are communities of living organisms within a biome. Living organisms include animal and plant life. Many factors affect living organisms within an ecosystem. These include climate, type of soil, water, and other growing conditions. In an ecosystem, plants and animals depend on each other for survival.

There are two categories of ecosystems found on Earth. Ecosystems that are primarily on land are called terrestrial. Ecosystems in water are called aquatic. Terrestrial ecosystems include grasslands, deserts, forests, tundras, and mountains. Terrestrial ecosystems vary greatly in their climate, vegetation, and animal life.

Oceans are the largest aquatic ecosystems on Earth. Oceans can be warm or cold. They are home to plants like seaweed and animals like fish, whales, turtles, and sponges. Freshwater ecosystems are rivers, lakes, streams, and ponds. They are home to animals like fish, frogs, and birds. Many plants grow in or near fresh water.

title: Climate
text:
Climate is a physical characteristic of a place. Climate is the average weather conditions of a place over an extended period of time. While the weather can change in just a few hours, climate takes hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperatures, precipitation, and wind in an area. Precipitation includes rain, snow, and sleet. There are five climate zones found on the Earth. These are tropical, dry, temperate, continental, and polar.

Tropical climates are hot, wet, and humid. This is because these areas have high average temperatures and large amounts of rainfall. Areas located around the Equator usually have a tropical climate.

A dry climate zone has very little precipitation. Places with a dry climate experience very little rainfall. Temperatures vary depending on a location's latitude and longitude. These areas can be very cold or very hot.

Areas with a temperate climate have warm summers and cold winters.

Continental climates are dry. They have very hot summers and very cold winters.

Polar regions are cold and dry. They are in the far north and far south of the world. These regions are extremely cold throughout most of the year. Even though snow falls through the winter, the climate is relatively dry.

A person who studies climate is called a climatologist. Climatologists study and observe an area's climate over a long period of time. Climatologists also make predictions about future climate patterns. Climate affects trade, agriculture, clothing, and the foods people eat. Climate is a big part of our daily lives.

title: Essential Question
text: What rights and responsibilities do I have?

title: Natural Hazards of the United States
text:
People move to and live in areas that meet their needs. However, many places around the world also have hazards, or dangers. The environment can cause natural hazards. A natural hazard is a dangerous event in nature. Some examples of natural hazards include hurricanes, tornadoes, wildfires, and earthquakes.

People have to think about the hazards of an area when they choose a place to settle. These hazards can be dangerous and cause massive amounts of damage. Hazards can affect homes, schools, industries, and the natural environment. There are many natural hazards that affect people in the United States. These are hurricanes, tornadoes, earthquakes, floods, and blizzards. No matter the natural hazard, it is important to be prepared. You should always have a safety plan in place and an emergency kit assembled to deal with natural hazards that you may encounter.

Hurricanes

Hurricanes are strong storms that form over the ocean. These storms can cause heavy rain, high winds, and flooding. When hurricanes hit land, they can be devastating to cities and coasts. As a hurricane moves through an area, it can also produce thunderstorms and tornadoes.

Tornadoes

Tornadoes are devastating storms with high winds that usually form over land. Tornadoes form very quickly. Sometimes, they give only a few minutes of warning before they strike. The United States has more tornadoes than any other country, about 800 per year. Most occur in a region nicknamed "Tornado Alley." The region spans the Great Plains, from Texas through the states of Illinois, Indiana, and the Dakotas.

Earthquakes

In the United States, most earthquakes happen along the fault lines in California, Oregon, and Washington. However, earthquakes can happen anywhere. An earthquake occurs when tectonic plates beneath the Earth’s surface shift suddenly. This causes waves of movement along the Earth's surface. Rocks and soil vibrate in response to the movement. The movement of the waves through the land causes buildings and roads to vibrate and shake.

Floods

Floods occur when water rises in an area and has no place to go. Floods are caused by many different factors. Some of these are heavy rain, hurricanes, rapidly thawing snow, ice jams, and broken dams or levees. Flooding can happen over a few hours, days, or weeks.

Droughts

People use surface water and groundwater to meet their wants and needs. If there isn't much snow or rain, the groundwater can be diminished. This means it is used up and not replaced. If groundwater decreases over a period of time, it is called a drought. A drought creates a shortage of water, which can lead to problems. Drought affects people, animals, plants, and even the soil. Droughts can last for months or even years.

title: Human Characteristics
text:
A place's human characteristics are a result of people’s ideas, choices, and actions as they interact with the physical environment. In other words, where people live and the kinds of houses they build are human characteristics. The kind of work people do and the activities they can enjoy are also human characteristics of a place.

When we discuss a place's human characteristics, we also examine its political, cultural, and economic characteristics. A place's political characteristics are organized by where people live. This includes cities, states, and countries. Cultural characteristics include a place's religious beliefs, languages, arts, and celebrations. A place's economic characteristics are based on natural resources. These natural resources are used for goods and services and contribute to a place's resulting economy.

title: Rural, Suburban, and Urban
text:
People form communities based on how they use the land they live on. Rural communities have large spaces of undeveloped land. This land is used for farms that grow food for the urban and suburban communities. Houses are far apart in rural communities. Businesses are built together in a town. There are not usually many public transportation options. Roads connect goods and people with the towns. In 2020, the U.S. census recorded that about 14 percent of the total population of the United States lived in rural areas.

A suburban community is formed when there are fewer businesses and people living in one location. There are less-developed areas with fewer buildings. Living space on the land has areas with no buildings. These spaces include yards, parks, and open lots or fields. Transportation systems in the suburban community are smaller. Highways connect goods and people to areas of business and houses. There is some land available for families to have small farms and grow food. Food is brought in to help feed the population in suburban communities.

When many people live in one location, the land is known as an urban area. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, an urban area has a population of 50,000 people or more. Urban areas can also be called cities. In cities, buildings for businesses and homes are developed to be close together. Tall buildings with many floors, or stories, are built so many people can live on smaller pieces of land. Transportation in urban areas is organized to move as many people and goods as possible in and out of the city. There is less land available to grow food in urban areas. Food for many people has to be brought into the city.

Many cities in the United States started as rural settlements. New York City is an example of a town that grew to be a city. For thousands of years, Algonquian tribes inhabited the area. The first European explorer arrived in present-day New York City in 1524, opening the door to European colonization of the area. The Spanish, French, English, and Dutch explored the areas for 100 years before the first European settlement was established by Dutch fur traders in 1624.

Dutch settlers from the Netherlands established a colony that they called New Amsterdam on Manhattan Island in 1625, where the Lenape people lived. This settlement eventually became New York City. The Dutch settled in this area because of its proximity to a deepwater port along the Hudson River. They built trading posts, a fort, and various mills near the Hudson River. This allowed the settlers to easily access trading posts, defend their settlement, and use the river to power their mills. Today, New York City is the largest city in the United States. Over eight million people live in the city.

Denver, Colorado, is another example of a city that grew from a small frontier settlement. In 1858, a group of miners discovered gold at the base of the Rocky Mountains near Cherry Creek. Word soon spread of the discovery, and the area grew rapidly. That same year, miners established Denver City on the eastern banks of the Cherry River, where the Cheyenne, Arapahoe, and Ute tribes lived.

In 1870, the Denver Pacific Railroad constructed a railroad that connected Denver to the Transcontinental Railroad. This greatly increased trade and transportation into the city. As a result, the population of Denver grew from 4,759 in 1870 to 106,713 in 1890. Railroads also allowed merchants, miners, and farmers to send their products to market all around the country. Today, Denver has a population of 711,463.

title: Depending on the Environment
text:
Humans have basic needs. People need food, clothing, and a place to live. The physical environment influences where people settle, their jobs, and their lifestyle. The physical environment includes landforms, climate, and weather. People depend on the environment to meet their needs. The natural features and resources available in an area provide materials, food, and clothing for people living there.

People usually choose to live close to resources that help them meet their basic needs. One example is the need for water. Throughout history, towns and cities have been established near bodies of water to meet basic human needs. These places provided a source of clean water and waterways used for transportation and trade. This made these locations desirable places to live. Resources found in the environment make our lives easier.

title: Test
text: The Trail of Tears Ride is a special event. It remembers the who were forced to leave their land. This event reminds people of the journey. The ride goes through towns and cities. People come to watch as the riders pass by.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
A producer is someone who makes a good or provides a service. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are used for other communities. Farmers, factory workers, car mechanics, and doctors are producers. The person who cuts your hair is also a producer.

People who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. People often depend on trade with others to meet their wants and needs. People can be both a producer and a consumer. When we buy groceries, gas, clothing, or toys, we are buying goods. When we go to the doctor, have our car fixed, or get a haircut, we are using services. When you get a haircut, you're a consumer because you're buying a service.

Both consumers and producers affect the prices of goods and services. For example, a company that produces bicycles may raise the price of their product if there's a metal shortage. A shortage is when something you need can’t be found in the amount needed. Consumers may stop buying bikes if the price is too high. Then the company might have to lower prices to get more sales. When a consumer doesn't buy enough of a good or service it may cause producers to lower the cost of it. If consumers are buying too much of a product, a producer might increase the product's price.

title: Adapting to the Environment
text: People adapt to their environment to meet their basic needs and to survive. This means people change how they live based on their environment. Everything from plants and animals to the weather can change the way people live. People must adapt to the climate. They must change the ways they live based on the climate where they live. People around the world wear different clothes, eat different foods, and live in different houses. People do all of this based on their environment. The jobs they do relate to their environment, too. Forestry, mining, and drilling are examples of jobs that were created based on a place's natural resources.

title: Modifying the Environment
text: People modify their environment to meet their needs. This means they change the place where they live. For example, people build dams to provide water for growing food. People also build homes and schools. They set up irrigation and farming systems. They build roads and bridges to travel from one area to another. They cut down forests for lumber and to make farmland for growing crops. All of these interactions modify the environment in some way.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text:
When humans settle in an area, they begin to interact with the environment in many different ways. They use the land around them to help fulfill their needs. When people make changes to the environment, they modify it. These changes can have positive and negative impacts.

Positive Impacts on the Environment

People can have a positive impact on their environment. Some ways to do this are by cleaning up litter, protecting endangered species, planting trees, and growing your own plants and vegetables. Other things that can have a positive impact on the environment are conserving water and electricity, using reusable water bottles, and buying locally grown food. When we use natural resources wisely, we positively impact the environment.

It is a good idea to use natural resources more responsibly. One example is implementing recycling programs in communities. About 70 percent of all the garbage we throw away can be recycled. The best way to keep our landfills and garbage dumps from taking over the environment is to recycle as many items as possible. People can work together to protect natural resources and have a positive impact on the environment.

Various efforts have been made to conserve resources and protect the environment in California. In 1999, the California legislature passed the Marine Life Protection Act. This act established marine-protected areas throughout the state to protect marine animals, their natural habitats, and the ecosystems in which they live. Organizations like Environment California are working to create programs that promote clean air initiatives, drinking water conservation, and the development of cleaner energy sources.

Negative Impacts on the Environment

In many ways, people’s interactions with the environment can be negative. We change the environment when we cut down trees, remove stone, and use natural resources. Agriculture and mining can also pose a threat to the environment. These activities can change the landscape in ways that make it no longer usable. Gold mining has had a significant impact on the environment of California. While many people came to California to seek their fortunes during the Gold Rush, some of the methods they used to look for gold had a negative impact on the environment that can still be seen today.

People also produce a lot of trash. Trash often ends up in landfills and garbage dumps. Trash can also produce harmful chemicals that can pollute the soil, water, and air. People have to be careful to balance their needs with available resources found in their environment. This helps people avoid having a negative impact on the environment.

title: Opportunity Cost
text: People make choices on how to spend their money. Sometimes we want more than one thing at a time. This means we have to make a choice. We have to decide what to keep and what to give up. Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you make a choice. Imagine you have $20. Your friends want to go see the new movie, but there is also a book you would like to buy. Before you can make a choice, you need to find out how expensive each option is. You might ask a friend or family member for advice. If you are patient, the price may drop in a few weeks. It might be a good idea to wait for that to happen. Whichever you choose, you also have to think about the opportunity cost. It can be a hard choice!

title: Movement
text:
Movement is the study of how people, resources, and ideas move. People move for different reasons. Sometimes people choose to move because there are better jobs, more freedom, or different resources in other places. Sometimes, people are forced to move. They may move because of war, natural disasters, or persecution.

Throughout history, people have explored new places for various reasons. They explored to find resources, spread religion, or expand their empire. As exploration increased, human interactions became more frequent. Exploration led to settlements in new places. When people choose to move to a new place, they usually try to go somewhere they already know about. We call this kind of movement from one place to another migration.

Migration is one way people, ideas, and materials move. Ideas move with people as they travel from place to place. Ideas also move through communication and technology.

Goods are moved from place to place in many ways. Moving goods can be as simple as carrying a basket of peaches to a market or as modern as transporting goods on a jet.

When we study movement, we ask questions like “Why and how do people, ideas, and materials move?” and “What is the result of this movement?”

title: Push-Pull Factors
text:
People move from one area to another for many reasons. Geographers call these reasons push-pull factors. Push-pull factors help us understand how and why people move. Some factors may be pushing, or driving us away, from the places we know. We usually think of push factors as negative. Push factors include war, natural disasters, and religious persecution.

Factors that pull us to a new community are usually positive. Pull factors include better jobs, more freedom, or different resources. Push-pull factors can be simple or complicated. However, they are always important. They can also be influenced by various factors. These factors are economic, political, and environmental. People may move to a new community due to many push-pull factors.

Migration is the movement of people, ideas, and goods from one place to another. People migrate to different areas because of push-pull factors. People can migrate to new cities, states, and even countries. Migration to and from an area can affect communities. A large increase in population may put a strain on natural resources. However, large amounts of people leaving an area may also put a strain on local businesses. When people migrate, they bring many different cultures together to create a new community.

title: Roger Sherman
text:
Roger Sherman signed the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, and the United States Constitution. Sherman was on the Committee of Five to write the Declaration of Independence. He was on the committee to write the Articles of Confederation. At the Constitutional Convention in 1787, he introduced the idea of a bicameral legislature, where states have representation based on population and a national senate where each state has two senators.

Sherman was known to be hardworking, dedicated to service, and extremely sensible. He was a self-taught surveyor, lawyer, and merchant. He served in the Connecticut House of Representatives and the General Assembly.

At the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia in 1787, Connecticut was considered a middle-sized state: smaller than Virginia, Massachusetts, and Pennsylvania, but larger than Delaware or Rhode Island. Sherman was vocal in protecting states’ rights over the federal government. Sherman supported Alexander Hamilton’s proposal of having the federal government pay the state debts for the revolution. One of his greatest contributions was the introduction of the compromise for a bicameral legislature.

Thomas Jefferson described Sherman as: “a man who never said a foolish thing in his life.” John Adams called him a best friend and “one of the strongest pillars of the revolution.”

Sherman served in the new House of Representatives and then the Senate until his death in 1793.

Roger Sherman once said: “When you are in the minority, talk; when you are in the majority, vote."

title: William Paterson
text:
William Paterson was born in Ireland and immigrated to Pennsylvania with his parents in 1745. Paterson attended Princeton College and knew many of the other Princeton alumni, including Aaron Burr and James Madison. Paterson became a lawyer in New Jersey. He was selected to be a delegate to the first Congress of New Jersey. He helped write the New Jersey constitution. He became attorney general for the new state. His energy and commitment to law earned him the opportunity to represent New Jersey at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia in 1787.

Paterson opposed representation according to the population of the state. Being from the smaller state of New Jersey, Paterson feared there would be too much control from the larger states. He proposed that each state have only one vote. A unicameral legislature would be an equalizer for small states and large states. His proposal was incorporated into Roger Sherman’s Great Compromise of a bicameral legislature. A house of representatives and a senate was adopted by the convention.

As a Federalist, Paterson helped ratify the Constitution and went on to serve in the Senate. Paterson was the first senator to resign from office to become the governor of New Jersey. By 1793, Washington asked him to serve on the Supreme Court of the United States. He resigned the governorship to become an associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court from 1793 to 1806.
