title: Distribution of Land in the Colonies
text:
During the colonial era, colonists saw the land as readily available for free, white men. In England, the monarch decided who owned property. When colonists sailed to America, they hoped to seize opportunities that came along with land ownership. If they owned land, these men could vote and hold government offices.

In the New England Colonies, early colonists received 50 acres of land. They took the greatest risks to be there, so this land was meant as a reward. Families obtained land if they promised to farm and improve the property. The land was surveyed, and then land deeds were processed by the royal governor’s office. These deeds were sometimes recorded in the colony’s government records.

In the Middle Colonies, proprietors could sell or gift land to others. The proprietor determined the price, and the measurement of the land was recorded in the proprietor’s office. Individuals could then resell part or all of the land. This was one way people could speculate, or purchase large tracts of land and then resell them in smaller parts for profit.

In the Southern Colonies, the headright system was established by the governor and the colonial government. The government gave 50 acres of land to adult men. They were also given 50 acres for each person who worked for them. A clerk in the governor’s office recorded land measurements and transfers. Large land ownership became known as a plantation.

title: Mercantilism
text:
The American colonies were chartered to trade with England. Colonists sent raw materials to England. These raw materials would be used in England to make manufactured goods that would be exported to the English colonies. This economic system is called mercantilism. In the mercantile system, governments want to increase exports, or what they sell to other countries. They also want to decrease imports, or what they buy from other countries. That keeps more money flowing into their economies. When a country sells more than it buys, it has a favorable balance of trade.

Mercantilism in the colonies meant that the colonies could not sell their raw materials to anyone but the English. They were not allowed to import anything except from England. This guaranteed that only English goods were sold in the colonies. To keep this balance, England also charged tariffs. A tariff is a tax on goods coming from another country. Tariffs were added to the cost of the goods. This made the goods more expensive.

Each colony in America had a deep-water seaport. Large ships crisscrossed the Atlantic with goods to and from these ports from all over the world. A port was essential to the economy in each colony. Each port had a royal customs office at the docks. This office checked and taxed all cargo being brought on or off ships. This ensured the royal customs officer knew exactly what was being shipped. This also guaranteed the royal customs officer knew where the ships were going.

England created rules to make sure they would have a favorable trade balance. These rules were called the Navigation Acts. They required:

Only England or English colonial ships could carry cargo between England and the colonies.

Certain goods, including tobacco, rice, and furs, couldn’t be shipped to foreign nations unless they went through England or Scotland first. The English government would pay bounties, or rewards, to Americans who produced certain raw goods while raising tariffs on the same goods produced in other countries.

American colonists would not compete with English manufacturers in large-scale manufacturing.

This favorable trade balance created a network of trade routes between England, Africa, and America and the West Indies. It was referred to as triangular trade because there were three connecting routes. Each part of the triangular route had a name. The voyage from Europe to Africa was called the Outward Passage. Ships carried manufactured goods for trade in Africa. Enslavers traded human beings for these manufactured goods. The enslavers captured adults as well as children. They were then sold to become enslaved workers for the colonies. The Middle Passage, as it was called, went from Africa to the West Indies and American colonies. The Inward Passage then shipped raw materials to England.

In the triangular trade system, as in the Columbian Exchange, England benefited greatly from the natural resources of America. Each section of the colonies had specialized goods they provided in this trade triangle. The geographic location, the climate, and the population of the colony determined what goods it produced. American colonies built economies based on supply and demand. This system was regulated by the government to make sure England made a large profit. The mercantile system made many colonists in the Americas and investors in England rich. It was the drive for wealth that created mercantilism. Merchants involved in the triangle trade pursued wealth. They gained wealth by neglecting the well-being of indentured servants and enslaved people.

title: Daily Life in the Colonies
text:
Life in the early 1700s was very different from when the colonies were first established. There was a greater trade balance. This meant more manufactured goods were available from England, like paper, sugar, and tea. Colonists could trade for or buy things. They didn’t have to make everything themselves.

Every city had a newspaper, which included news, weather, opinions, and advertisements. Even though most people could read, they often gathered at a local meeting house to hear the news read out loud.

Farmers sold their produce at markets. Families in the city would have a kitchen garden. They would still go to the market to purchase or trade with items such as meat, vegetables, and preserved fruit. Much of the preparation was done before foods arrived in city kitchens. This eased the workload of women and children.

Colonists’ daily diets included dried or salted meat and corn mush or bread. Meals might include a stew or pie filled with meat and vegetables in gravy. The drink of choice was apple cider. People rarely drank water because it was not clean. People living in cities often got sick from bad water.

Craftsmen took in apprentices to teach them a trade. These boys acted as servants in a craftsman’s household and shop. They ran errands, tended fires, cleaned, and learned the trade. Blacksmiths, silversmiths, glassworkers, and printers were all open for apprenticeships.

Boys had two shirts, one for work and one for church. Socks were mended until they couldn’t be mended anymore. Women and girls usually had only one dress and a few aprons. Aprons protected their dresses for church on Sundays. When children outgrew their clothing, they passed it down to their siblings.

Shoes were individually made by village shoemakers to a general size. There were no right or left shoes. They did not fit well and had to be tied or buckled to stay on. Only the very wealthy could have shoes made to fit their feet.

The average lifespan of a colonist in the 1700s depended on their work situation, their wealth, and luck. Poor and enslaved people died young from disease, accidents, or being overworked. Those who had easier work could expect a longer life. Although life had gotten better since the early days of colonization, it still wasn't easy. Every day presented its own difficulties.

title: The Mayflower Compact
text:
The Mayflower Compact was only 166 words long, but it is one of the most famous documents from early American history. A compact is an agreement or contract between individuals or groups of people. Why was the Mayflower Compact so important to Plymouth Colony?

The Pilgrims’ ship was supposed to land in the chartered area of Virginia. Instead, the ship landed in a place not legally governed by the Virginia Company. Pilgrim leaders realized that if they didn’t set up some temporary rules, there would be no order, and the colony might fail. The 41 adult male passengers and crew came together and created a set of laws that everyone would agree to obey. All of the men signed the document. Women were not allowed to sign, vote, or hold government offices.

The Mayflower Compact is an example of self-government. Self-government means people work together to pass laws for themselves that benefit all citizens. This is the central idea behind our government today.

The settlers lived up to the Compact, and the colony survived. One year later, a man named John Pierce expanded the Mayflower Compact so the English government would support it. The Mayflower Compact continued to be used to govern Plymouth Colony for more than 70 years.

title: Enslavement
text:
Prince Henry the Navigator was a Portuguese duke. Although he was called the Navigator, he never went to sea. Prince Henry did control a large amount of money for an organization called the “Order of Christ.” This organization brought navigators and geographers together. They would plan expeditions to unexplored regions along the Atlantic coast south of Portugal. They hired a sea captain named Bartolomeu Perestrello and his ship for their expeditions.

The early voyages sent Perestrello to the mid-Atlantic islands, such as Madeira and the Azores. These explorations were followed by routes along the west coast of Africa.

As a result of their exploration, the Portuguese began to colonize new areas. Beginning in 1445, the Azores rapidly filled with colonists. They developed a rich sugar-producing colony. The sugar was exported to European markets. The Portuguese also established trading posts along the west coast of Africa.

These trading posts were to trade Portuguese goods to traders in Africa. The Africans traded enslaved people in exchange for these goods. The enslaved captives were taken to sugar plantations on the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores. Many enslaved people were also taken to Spain and Portugal. By the mid-1550s, 10 percent of Portugal’s population was enslaved men, women, and children.

Exploration of the Americas created a new market where traders could sell enslaved people. The first recorded ship carrying 200 enslaved people sailed to the Caribbean in 1525. Sold into a lifetime of enslavement, they worked on sugar plantations. This early trade by Portuguese ships began the system of bringing enslaved people across the Atlantic.

title: Climate
text: Climate is a physical characteristic. Climate is the weather pattern that develops in a place over many years. The weather can change in just a few hours. The climate takes hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperature, precipitation (rain, snow, sleet), and wind in the area. People make decisions about food, clothing, and shelter based on the climate. We use climate maps to learn about what different places are like. We can learn about different climate zones around the world.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text:
Thomas Jefferson was born in Virginia in 1743. He became a leader in the colonial government at age 25.

In 1776, Jefferson became a member of the Continental Congress. This is the group that was organized to write the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson was chosen to write the declaration that was sent to the king of England. It told the king that the 13 Colonies wanted to break away from England.

After the Revolutionary War, Jefferson served as a minister to France. He was elected president of the United States in 1800. Jefferson was very familiar with the French because of the time he had spent in France. This helped him make a deal to buy territory that France owned and expand the United States.

Jefferson is remembered as a talented writer and statesman. He was the third president of the United States. He was one of the great Founders of our nation.

title: The Louisiana Purchase
text: In 1801, the United States didn't look like it does today. It was much smaller. The Mississippi River was the western border of our country. Spain controlled Florida and much of the Southwest. France claimed the land west of the Mississippi River. Settlers shipped supplies and goods up and down the Mississippi River to the port of New Orleans. President Jefferson thought it would be dangerous for another country to control this important shipping route. Instead of trying to take it by force, Jefferson asked France to sell the land. In 1803, France made a deal to sell the United States even more land than Jefferson had originally asked for. The United States paid $15 million for the land. This sale is called the Louisiana Purchase. The purchase doubled the size of our country. The new territory stretched from the Mississippi River all the way to the Rocky Mountains.

title: Lewis and Clark
text: Before the Louisiana Purchase happened, President Jefferson had already planned to send a group to explore the western frontier. He chose his secretary, Meriwether Lewis, to lead the group. Lewis chose William Clark as his co-captain. Lewis and Clark had served in the military together. About 40 other men joined Lewis and Clark. Their group was called the Corps of Discovery. Their expedition became known as the Lewis and Clark Expedition. President Jefferson instructed Lewis and Clark to explore the land. Jefferson told them to draw maps, study the plants and animals, and observe the American Indians living in the area. Jefferson also told them to look for new travel routes and existing trading posts or settlements.

title: The Lewis and Clark Expedition
text: In May 1804, the Corps of Discovery began their journey. They took glass beads, mirrors, and cloth to trade with American Indian tribes they met. The first winter of their exploration wasn't easy. Some members of their group had diseases or injuries. It was very cold. There was little to eat, and the men were afraid they would die. However, they survived the winter, and the expedition reached the Pacific coast. They stayed there for the second winter. Then, they returned home to share their findings. They brought journals, sketches, and maps of their journey. They recorded information about 300 new kinds of plants and animals. After returning to Missouri, the men were treated as heroes. The expedition was very important. It helped settlers learn about the new land and the people who lived there. They now had maps that would make traveling through the Louisiana Territory easier. Settlers could now move even farther west. The expedition wasn't good news for everyone. American Indians had already been pushed west by the settlers. Now even more American Indians were forced to move off the land. They had to live on reservations. Reservations are areas of land set aside by the U.S. government.

title: Sacagawea
text:
Sacagawea (Bird Woman) was a Lemhi Shoshone woman. She was an interpreter and guide for the Lewis and Clark expedition. At age 12, Sacagawea was captured and enslaved by an enemy tribe. She was then sold to a French Canadian fur trader named Toussaint Charbonneau. Lewis and Clark hired Charbonneau as an interpreter for their expedition. Sacagawea was brought on the trip as an interpreter because she spoke Shoshone. However, Sacagawea was never paid for her work. Sacagawea played an important role in the expedition. In addition to interpreting, she was very good at finding edible plants and herbs. This skill helped the explorers during their travels.

On May 14, 1805, the expedition boat she was in tipped over and filled with water. Supplies and documents fell into the water. Sacagawea stayed calm. She saved the supplies and documents from being lost to the river. About a week later, Lewis and Clark showed their appreciation by naming a part of the Musselshell River after her.

title: Louisiana: Past and Present
text:
Life in Louisiana in the past was both different and similar to life in Louisiana today. Before French settlers came to Louisiana in the 1700s, most of the people living here were American Indians. There were many groups, or tribes. People with ancestry from these tribes still live in Louisiana today. The Chitimacha tribe still live on some of the same lands their ancestors did. Today, many different groups of people live in Louisiana. Some things have changed as new groups have moved into Louisiana. Other things have stayed the same.

Food

Differences:

In the past, many people hunted animals for their food. Today, most food is bought from a grocery store.

Similarities:

American Indians harvested and ate potatoes and corn in the past. Potatoes and corn are still popular foods in Louisiana today.

Recreation

Differences:

Today, much of our recreation is based on technology. People watch movies. People play video games. Those things hadn’t been invented in the past.

Similarities:

Like people living in Louisiana today, American Indians in the past played games and went to sporting events. Wrestling was a popular sport in the past. Wrestling is still popular today.

Holidays

Differences:

In the past, each group or tribe had its own different celebrations and traditions. Today, we have many national holidays that we celebrate as a whole country.

Similarities:

It was important to American Indians in the past to honor their dead. They had a holiday in the early part of November that was dedicated to honoring their ancestors. It was called the Feast of the Souls. Today, we honor people who died fighting in wars on a day called Veterans Day. This day is also in November.

title: Louisiana: Many Cultures
text: Louisiana's culture is unique. The music has different rhythms and beats. There are many lively festivals. The food is known for its spicy taste. The buildings were made with influences from around the world. Why is our culture so special? There's a good reason. It has been shaped by many different cultures that have mixed together right here in Louisiana. When the Louisiana Purchase was made, new land was added to our country. This land was different from much of the other land. People of American Indian, European, African, and Latin American descent made a unique and mixed culture. This culture added diversity to the United States.

title: Ancient Egyptian Government
text:
In 3150 B.C.E., King Namer unified Egypt. After that, the government of Egypt didn’t change much. The king was the ruler of Egypt. The king was considered a connection between the people and the gods. The people believed that the laws the king passed were the will of the gods.

The vizier was second-in-command. The vizier chose the many officials and scribes who administered the government’s rules, laws, and decrees.

The king and vizier ruled over regional governors, known as nomarchs. Nomarchs ruled over the mayors of towns. Egypt also had a police force.

The government was supported by the farmers. They gave a large portion of their harvest to the nobles who owned the land. The nobles would give some of the harvest to the government. The government would use the harvest for trade or distribute it back to the community.

Sometimes ancient Egypt would break up into warring kingdoms. This happened three times during its 3,000-year history. These were dark periods in Egyptian history. The periods when Egypt was unified were more peaceful.

title: The Layers of the Ocean
text:
My observations from the video:

1.

2.

3.

Just like a cake, the ocean has layers. These layers are also called zones. Differences in density and temperature create these zones. The amount of salt causes the differences in density. Different amounts of sunlight reach each zone. This causes the differences in temperature. Let’s investigate these layers.

The sunlight zone is the first zone. Sunlight can shine down about 600 feet below the ocean's surface. The sunlight hitting this layer means that there are a variety of organisms because there is a lot of food. The food comes from algae and phytoplankton. These organisms use the sun’s energy to make food. It is an important adaptation. Algae and phytoplankton become food for small animals. Small animals become food for medium-sized animals. Medium-sized animals become food for large animals. The amount of light means that it is easy to see the creatures that live in this layer. These creatures have adapted their color and patterns to try and blend in. This is important for hiding, both for animals trying not to get caught and those that are trying to catch food.

The next zone is the twilight zone. It is from about 600 to 2,000 feet deep. In this layer, there is very little sunlight. Without much sunlight, the water gets colder. There is also less oxygen in this layer, which plants and animals need to survive. The animals in this low-light environment have some special adaptations. Some make their own light, like fireflies do. Some animals in this layer have specialized eyes for seeing in the dark.

The midnight zone goes from 2,000 to 10,000 feet below the surface of the ocean. Sunlight no longer reaches the water at this depth. The midnight zone is completely dark. The lack of sunlight makes this layer cold. The creatures living here cannot be picky eaters because there is not very much food. They have to eat anything that comes their way! Some of the creatures living here don’t even have eyes because there is no light. The water pressure is also very high because there are thousands of feet of water on top of this layer. The animals here have adapted to these conditions. They tend to be blobby and pale.

title: Ocean Adaptations
text:
Animals that live in the ocean have physical and behavioral adaptations to live in this habitat. A physical adaptation is a characteristic of an animal’s body that helps it survive in its environment. A behavioral adaptation is something an animal does to help it survive in its environment. text: Legends say that Menes was the first king of Egypt. The legends also say that he was the one to unite Upper and Lower Egypt into one country. But no one has found any proof that he actually lived. He may just be a myth. If Menes was a myth, then Narmer was the first king of Egypt. He lived 5,000 years ago. Narmer accomplished a lot. He united the two halves of Egypt. He married a princess. He started big construction projects. He started trading with other countries.

title: Pharaohs
text:
The word “pharaoh” means “great house” in ancient Egyptian. It refers to the rulers' large palace. Early in ancient Egypt, the rulers were called kings. Around 3000 B.C.E., the title “pharaoh” came into use. This is also when Upper and Lower Egypt became united. For this reason, pharaohs were also called the “lords of two lands.”

Early on, ancient Egyptians considered the pharaohs to be living gods. Later, they thought of the pharaohs as representatives of the gods. Pharaohs had total control of religion and government.

The pharaohs used writing and art to show their authority. They had artists show them performing impressive acts. The pharaohs are commonly shown as warriors, killing enemies or fighting lions. These works of art might not be accurate histories. Instead, they were used to show the idea that the pharaohs were powerful.

Not every pharaoh was from ancient Egypt. When Egypt fought wars with other countries, sometimes it lost. Those other countries sometimes put their own rulers in charge. Also, not every pharaoh was male. Hatshepsut and Cleopatra were two women known to have ruled ancient Egypt.

title: Nomarchs
text:
Like the United States today is divided into states, ancient Egypt was divided into districts called “nomes.” Egypt had 42 individual nomes. Each was ruled by a person known as a nomarch. A nomarch was like the governor of the nome. Nomarchs had many responsibilities. They collected taxes, managed local courts, and led a local army.

Unlike in the United States, these leaders were not elected. For some time, the position of nomarch was passed down in families. Nomarchs became very rich and powerful. This system made the central government of ancient Egypt weaker. One of the rulers of ancient Egypt, King Sesostris III, changed the system. Under his rule, the king or vizier appointed the nomarchs. After that, the nomarchs were more loyal to the king. The central government of ancient Egypt became stronger.

title: Military Service
text:
Not all men in Egypt were farmers. Many men were also soldiers in the army. Being a soldier was dangerous work. Soldiers did not want to die outside of Egypt. They believed this would make it harder to find their way to the afterlife.

The army wasn’t just for soldiers. People who made weapons also worked for the army. When Egypt started using horses and chariots, the army hired people to build the chariots.

The army’s job was not to take over other lands. The army mainly protected Egypt from other countries.

For hundreds of years, Egypt had one of the most powerful armies in the world.

title: Rules and Laws in Early Civilization
text:
Ancient Egyptian law was based on the idea of ma’at, or harmony. To live in harmony, a person needed to live a good life of balance. This meant living in balance with their community and the gods. The people believed that the gods themselves created this rule of ma’at at the beginning of time. They created laws to make sure everyone was living in harmony.

Since the law came from the gods, breaking the law was not just going against the government. It was breaking a religious law. The punishments for breaking the law were harsh. Murderers were fed to crocodiles. Someone guilty of theft could have their hand, foot, or nose cut off. Knowingly lying in court could be punished by drowning.

There were three levels of courts. The lowest court, the seru, was a group of elders in rural communities. Next was the kenbet, or regional court. The djadjat was the imperial court. This court decided what the laws were.

There were no lawyers in ancient Egypt. There was a police force that enforced the rules. They brought accused criminals to the courts. Judges listened to witnesses and weighed the evidence to make their decisions. Someone accused of a crime was considered guilty until proven innocent. A false charge or false witness was a very serious offense.

How do we use patterns to send messages? We can send messages through sound and light waves, using patterns. Waves transfer energy over long distances without being changed or disturbed. When a person wants to send a message using waves, they first need to come up with a pattern or symbol to represent the message. Often, a pattern is made for each letter of the alphabet. Once the pattern is made, the message can be encoded. Encoding is when each letter or word of the message is converted into the pattern. Once the message is encoded, it is ready to be sent. Flashing a light, using long or short beeps, tapping, using musical instruments, or using patterns of numbers to send an image or text are all examples of transferring messages using light, sound, and radio waves. When the wave reaches the receiver, the message is ready to be decoded. Decoding a message is when the patterned message is turned back into everyday language. The decoder must know the pattern that was used to encode the message. If the message was encoded and decoded accurately, then it was a successful pattern!

title: Landforms and Bodies of Water
text:
Landforms

The United States is a diverse country with many unique physical characteristics that impact the way people live and interact with their environment. Landforms are natural features that make up the Earth's surface.

A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean. It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They are formed by the movement of the Earth's crust. Mountains are shaped over time by weather. Rich minerals are found in the cores of mountains. Mountain peaks are often covered in snow. The snow melts and sends water down the sides to form streams, creeks, and brooks.

There are many mountain ranges in the United States. The Rocky Mountain range is the biggest mountain range in North America. It begins in Canada and extends through central New Mexico. Many of the peaks are more than 12,000 feet high. Mount Elbert in Colorado is the tallest peak in the range at 14,433 feet. Thousands of tourists flock to the Rocky Mountains each year to explore their natural wonders.

The Appalachian Mountains are located in the eastern part of the United States. The highest peak is Mount Mitchell, at 6,684 feet. The Appalachian Trail runs the length of the mountain range, which is about 2,000 miles long. Outdoor adventurers and hiking enthusiasts hike the Appalachian Trail throughout the year.

A desert is a place where there is less than 10 inches of precipitation in a year. The lack of water makes the soil low in nutrients. Deserts usually have hot temperatures during the day and colder temperatures at night.

The Mojave Desert is located in parts of southern California, Nevada, Arizona, and Utah and extends into Mexico. It is the driest desert in North America. It receives less than two inches of rain each year. The Mojave Desert is home to Death Valley. Death Valley sits 282 feet below sea level, making it the lowest point in North America. It is also the hottest place on Earth. Despite its dry and extremely hot climate, hundreds of plant and animal species call the Mojave Desert home. The plants and animals of this region have adapted to the harsh conditions of the desert in order to survive.

The Great Plains are very different from the Mojave Desert. A plain is a large area of flat land with few to no trees. The Great Plains region is a large area east of the Rocky Mountains that is very flat. It extends from Mexico to Canada and east to Illinois. It is primarily grassy with few trees. The soil is usually very good on the plains due to the abundant amount of grass material that grows there. It is a great place for growing crops like corn and wheat.

Bodies of Water

Rivers and lakes have played a vital role in the history, economy, and actions of governments in North America for thousands of years. A river is a large, flowing body of water that moves across the land. There are many rivers in the United States that play a vital role in the nation’s economy, history, and culture.

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. Combined with the Mississippi River, it forms one of the largest river systems on Earth. The Missouri River travels through the heart of the Great Plains. The Missouri flows southeast from its source in Montana. It ends in Missouri, where it joins the Mississippi River. The Mississippi River is the second-longest river in the United States. Its name comes from a Chippewa word meaning "Father of Waters." The Mississippi River is nearly 2,400 miles long and travels through 10 states before it pours into the Gulf of Mexico.

The Great Lakes, which include Lake Erie, Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, and Lake Superior, are located in the northern United States. The Great Lakes cover over 94,000 square miles and contain about six quadrillion gallons of water. The lakes hold about 21 percent of the Earth's fresh water and 84 percent of America's fresh water. The deepest lake is Lake Superior, at 1,330 feet. Lake Erie's average depth is only 70 feet.

Oceans and gulfs are important bodies of water in and around the United States. Oceans are large bodies of salt water. Oceans cover most of the Earth's surface. The United States is bordered by two oceans. The Atlantic Ocean borders the United States on the East Coast. Like the other bodies of water in the United States, the Atlantic Ocean helps the U.S. economy by providing a trade route with other countries. Atlantic coastal areas are popular tourist destinations for Americans and visitors from around the world. The Pacific Ocean is on the western border of the United States. The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth. It covers over 60 million square miles. The Pacific Ocean is a vital trade route between the United States and other countries.

A gulf is a deep inlet of water that connects coastal areas to a larger body of water, such as a sea or ocean. The Gulf of Mexico is between Florida and Mexico. It covers about half a million square miles of water. The Gulf of Mexico shares a border with five states. It has 33 major tributaries, or rivers, that flow into it, including the Mississippi River. A bay is a coastal body of water partly surrounded by land that feeds into a large body of water. The Chesapeake Bay is the largest bay in the United States. It covers over 4,000 square miles and holds approximately 15 trillion gallons of water. Over 150 rivers empty into the Chesapeake Bay. It is also home to over 3,700 plant and animal species.

title: A Day in Washington
text:
Draw a time …

… when you knew, based on the weather, that it was going to rain. How could you tell?

Reading Strategies

Circle pronouns that show a firsthand account.

Highlight sentences that show subjective points of view (influenced by feelings or opinions).

Put a star next to sentences that are facts.

Firsthand Account

I would describe today’s walk to school in one word: WET! I should have known when I saw the dark clouds rolling in. Luckily, I always have my umbrella with me. But listen: I’ll take all that rain and cloudy weather. It means the greenest green you’ve ever seen! Even on the road to my house, there are vibrant, leafy forests lining the street. Mossy forest walks are my favorite. All those clouds in the overcast sky are just a result of living by the ocean. Being so close to an ocean also makes for some really cool beach days. During one field trip to the coast, we learned about all the awesome ecosystems and living things that are just a short drive away! The ocean creates landforms, like beaches, and affects my town's climate. Wind off the ocean carries warm, moist air into the sky and creates a ton of clouds. In Washington winters, you barely see the sun. Almost every day is completely overcast. But some days, the clouds disappear and the sun shines through, giving us a crystal-clear view of the majestic mountains in the east.

Secondhand Account: Online Encyclopedia

A satellite image provides a clear visual of plant life in the western part of Washington. The plants are evidence that this area receives plenty of precipitation. Increased precipitation in western Washington also shapes the Cascades through weathering and erosion. Precipitation originates from clouds. Water from the surface of the ocean heats up and turns into water vapor in a process called evaporation. Wind currents from the Pacific Ocean blow warm, moist air inland. The water vapor collects in cool, higher air. The result of this process is clouds! All the gases on Earth, like the air in the wind and clouds, are components of the subsystem known as the atmosphere. People living in western Washington are no stranger to cloudy days. On average, Seattle has 308 “mostly cloudy” days per year. That means 84 percent of the year is overcast.

But not many people realize that the eastern part of Washington has a completely different climate. This area, right across the Cascades, is known for its dry desert conditions. Some of its cities receive as little as 5 to 10 inches of rain per year. In the summer, temperatures are high and very little rainfall occurs. The winter is short and cold, with snow. This desert is just a few hours’ drive from an area so lush it earned Washington its title as the Evergreen State.

title: The Water Cycle
text:
After your teacher’s demonstration, observe the bag you placed in the sunlight. Use your bag and the article to draw a model of the water cycle and answer the questions that follow.

The hydrosphere describes all of the water on Earth in any state of matter: solid, liquid, or gas. This includes the ocean, glaciers and other ice formations, water that is deep underground, and more. Water moves through different spheres in the water cycle. The first step of the cycle is evaporation. Liquid water in the ocean evaporates and turns into water vapor. Water vapor then moves into the atmosphere. In the atmosphere, the air gets cooler the higher up you go. As the water vapor cools, it collects on particles of dust or pollution. These wet particles become droplets of water and are visible as clouds. This step is known as condensation. When the droplets become too heavy, they fall back to the Earth as precipitation (rain, snow, sleet, or hail). Precipitation then seeps into or “runs off” the land, going from higher to lower areas, until it eventually collects in the ocean. From there, it starts the water cycle all over again with evaporation. As water cycles, it influences living things, impacts climate, and shapes Earth’s landforms.

Draw your model. Be sure to label the steps of the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection. Use symbols to show how matter moves through the system.

What spheres are interacting in the water cycle?

title: Rain Shadow
text:
Let’s Discuss:

What do you know about shadows? What are they? How could the mountain range in the phenomenon be acting as a shadow?

When a section of the geosphere becomes a desert because a mountain or mountain range blocks precipitation to that region, it is known as rain shadow. Evaporation creates water vapor in the air. Warm, moist air is blown inland by winds that usually travel in a specific direction, also called prevailing winds. As the wind blows the warm air toward a mountain or mountain range, it is forced up to a higher level, where the air is cold. Cold air cannot hold as much moisture as warm air. At colder temperatures, water vapor in the air condenses to form clouds. The clouds start to pass over the mountain peaks, releasing precipitation as they move. The further the clouds travel, the less moisture remains in them. The wind continues down the other side of the mountain, forcing the air down. The air warms up, so the clouds disperse or fade away. Rain shadows form on the leeward side of mountains because this side does not receive precipitation.

Summarize how the hydrosphere interacts with both the geosphere and atmosphere to result in a rain shadow.

title: Weather
text:
Unlike climate, weather refers to the short-term atmospheric conditions in an area or specific location. When discussing the weather, three primary factors should be considered. These factors are temperature, precipitation, and wind. Temperature is the measurement of how hot or cold it is outside. A thermometer is a tool used to measure temperature.

Precipitation is water that falls from clouds. It comes in the form of rain, snow, sleet, or hail. The form it takes depends on the temperature. This is part of the reason meteorologists pay attention to the temperature. If it’s fairly warm outside and it starts to precipitate, it will rain. If it’s cold outside and it precipitates, it can snow.

Wind is air moving outside. Wind direction is the direction the wind is blowing. To measure the wind direction, you can use a weather vane. This can determine what kind of weather is blown toward or away from where you live. We measure the speed of the wind because the wind affects how the weather will change. Wind direction is measured using the directions north, south, east, and west. The wind speed is measured using an anemometer and recorded as miles per hour.

A scientist who studies the weather and weather patterns is called a meteorologist. Meteorologists study current weather patterns and provide weather forecasts for the near future. Meteorologists often work for news stations and outlets to provide the weather forecast for viewers across the country or specific areas.

title: Tribes of the West
text:
Many Native American tribes lived in the West. The West includes parts of Nevada, Idaho, Oregon, Utah, California, Colorado, Montana, and Wyoming. This area is very diverse, with mountains, rivers, coasts, and deserts.

Tribes relied on the region's abundant resources to establish a way of life. Many western tribes gathered, hunted, and fished for food. Coastal areas and the rivers of the Great Basin provided many fishing opportunities for Native peoples. Tribes hunted large animals, such as bison, deer, and elk. They also gathered wild berries and nuts for food.

Many tribes followed large herds of animals and moved throughout the region. They lived in easy-to-move lodge homes, such as tepees or wickiups. A wickiup consisted of a wooden frame covered with woven leaves and brush. Some tribes lived along the Pacific coast.

Tribes of the Western region engaged in trade with one another. The tribes of the Great Basin traded shells, animal hides, furs, clothing, and baskets for other items. They used resources found in their environment for clothing. They traditionally wore furs in colder climates and seasons. In warmer areas and warmer parts of the year, they wore clothing made from bark, grasses, and animal skins.

Like other Native Peoples, tribes of the West have a deep connection with their environment. Sacred sites that are important to the beliefs of the tribes, like mountains, sequoia trees, and rivers, are given special respect.

title: Northwest
text:
The Northwest region includes Alaska, Oregon, and Washington. These states border the Pacific Ocean. The Northwest has many kinds of natural resources. One of the most important resources is forests. The lumber from these trees is turned into houses, furniture, pencils, paper, musical instruments, and other important items. About 1 million Americans work in the lumber industry.

There are other important natural resources in the Northwest. Many crops are grown in the Northwest, such as fruits, vegetables, nuts, wheat, and other grains. Washington has well-known apple tree orchards. The state is our nation's top apple grower. People who live in coastal areas earn money through the fishing industry. Mining and the oil industry also play a large role in the economy of the region.

Tourism is an important industry in the Northwest. People from around the world travel to visit tourist sites throughout the region. The natural wonders and national parks of the region attract thousands of tourists each year. The tallest point in the United States is Denali. It is located in Alaska. Many people travel to cities like Seattle, Washington, and Portland, Oregon. They visit museums, cultural centers, and human-made wonders, like the Seattle Space Needle.

title: Research and Ideate
text:
Floods

Floods happen when water moves on to dry land. Too much rain or snowfall can cause floods. The water from the rain or snowfall flows into rivers, streams, or oceans. When the water rises in those rivers, streams, and oceans, flooding can happen in the nearby areas. Snow or ice melting too fast can also cause flooding.

Flooding can be powerful when the water pushes into dry land. Sometimes this can harm nearby structures, like businesses, homes, and roads.

Flooding can happen over a few days or weeks. Flash floods occur more quickly. Flash floods can be unsafe because people do not have time to prepare or to leave the area that is being flooded. Flash floods often occur near hills or rivers.

If your area is likely to flood, it is a good idea to prepare. When you prepare, you will be more likely to keep yourself and your belongings safe.

text:
Trade Routes’ Impact Today

We still use a lot of native trails and trade routes. Many major city roads and U.S. highways follow the same paths American Indians took thousands of years ago! For example, Interstate 94 (I-94) between Chicago and Detroit is on top of an old path native peoples used 11,000 years ago! Another example is Interstate (I-75) from Michigan to Florida. This is also on top of an old native path. The original name for this route was “the Great Path.”

title: Lexile Text - Kent
text:
The first inhabitants of what is now New York City were the Lenape. They were also called the Delaware by European settlers. The Lenape traditionally lived in southern New York. Many of their villages were located close to the Hudson River. Their territory included various counties in present-day southeastern New York, the five boroughs of New York City, and parts of Long Island. The Lenape were divided into different groups, including the Munsee, Hackensack, Wappinger, Esopus, Massapequa, Canarsee, Minisink, and Rockaway. Lenape is an Algonquain language. The Algonquain language family includes languages spoken in the eastern and middle parts of North America.

The Lenape had their own government. The leader of the different groups was the sachem, or chief. Sachems were responsible for performing specific ceremonies. They settled arguments within the tribe. They also managed relationships with other tribes. Lenape groups also had shamans. A shaman is a religious or spiritual leader of a tribe. Shamans were healers, teachers, and prophets who told the future. They were messengers who communicated with the spirit world. The elders of each village also held a special role in the tribe. They were counselors and helped the sachem make decisions for the tribe.

The Lenape had a matrilineal kinship system. This meant that someone was only related to people on their mother's side of the family. Inheritances and positions of power were passed from a mother to her children. There were three matrilineal clans in Lenape society: the Turtle clan, the Wolf clan, and the Turkey clan. The head sachem was always from the Turtle clan. The turtle was an important animal among Lenape people. It represented the Earth and its power to give life.

The Lenape religious tradition influences many aspects of the people’s culture. The Lenape believe in a creator god called Kishelëmukong. They also believe in some lesser spirits, called manitou or manëtu. Most animals, plants, and some objects are thought to have manëtu. For example, there are manëtu called “the thunder beings,” or pethakhuweyok. The winds of the four cardinal directions are also considered manuëtu. They are called Grandfather of the North, Grandfather of the East, Grandfather of the West, and Grandmother of the South.

The Lenape divided work responsibilities between men and women. Men hunted and fished seasonally. Different animals and birds were hunted at certain times of the year. Men also fished in the Atlantic Ocean and nearby rivers, bays, and sounds. Lenape women farmed and prepared food from the forests. The land they farmed belonged to the women. Women cultivated corn, beans, squash, and tobacco. Tobacco was mostly used for ceremonial purposes or as offerings to spirits. The women also picked berries and nuts. Many wild berries and nuts grew in the area. These included strawberries, blueberries, cranberries, walnuts, and chestnuts. When they were not planting or harvesting, women also went to the forest to tap trees for maple sap. The Lenape women would make the sap into maple syrup.

title: Fossil Fuels and Oil
text:
Fossil Fuels

Fossil fuels are ________ resources. Examples of fossil fuels are ______, ______, and ________.

Nonrenewable resources are ________ sources that ________ be replaced in a short amount of time.

Nonrenewable Resources

Directions: Obtain and combine information (from articles, charts, images, and online research) on how oil is used as an energy source as well as the effects of using oil on the environment. Record information in the chart titled “Nonrenewable Resources.”

What Is Oil?

Oil is a thick, black, liquid fossil fuel found in underground rock chambers. It is formed from the remains of tiny ocean plants and animals.

In some places, oil rises to the Earth’s surface. This is the case at the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, California. Big pools of thick oil can be found there, along with preserved animal remains from thousands of years ago.

To access most oil, big oil rigs (machinery used for oil drilling) drill deep into the earth. Then, pumps pull the oil up from the rock chambers where it was buried. Some of these oil rigs and pumps are on land. Others are in the ocean.

Oil cannot be used right after it is taken from the ground. Instead, it must be refined, or separated into fuels and other products. Gasoline for your car, jet fuel, home heating oil, diesel fuel for trucks, and kerosene for lamps are all refined oil products. Oil is also used in many other products, like plastics, medicines, cosmetics, and paints.

Once an oil company finds a good place to drill for oil, it can usually extract oil there for about 30 years. Although oil is difficult to find because it is located deep beneath Earth's surface, once it is found, it is a reliable source of energy

The Positive and Negative Effects of Using Oil on the Environment

Positives:

Oil platforms can be used as artificial reefs, creating a home for many marine animals and plants.

Negatives:

When oil products (such as gasoline) are burned, they release toxic gases and fumes into the air.

Drilling and shipping can result in oil spills that affect the surrounding land and bodies of water. Oil spills can destroy habitats and kill many animals or make them very sick.

Ways technology is trying to help:

Fully electric cars depend on a rechargeable battery to run instead of gasoline.

Hybrid cars can run off of gas or electric energy from a battery and burn less gas overall than normal cars.

title: Coal
text:
Directions: Obtain and combine information (from articles, charts, images, and online research) on how coal is used as an energy source as well as the effects of using coal on the environment. Record information in the chart titled “Nonrenewable Resources.”

What Is Coal?

Coal is a black or brownish rock created from the slow breakdown of ancient plant and animal remains. Like other fossil fuels, it must be obtained underground through a process called mining. There are two ways of mining coal: underground mining and surface mining. Underground mining is used when the coal is located deep below the Earth’s surface. Miners use elevators that go through mineshafts to travel deep into the Earth. They then use big machines to remove the coal and bring it to the surface. Surface mining is used when the coal is located near the Earth’s surface. To get to the coal, the area is cleared of trees and soil so the coal can be cut from the ground.

Coal is a very reliable source of energy that provides electricity. About half of the electricity in the United States comes from coal. The electricity you use in your home to power lamps, TVs, and other appliances may come from coal. Coal is turned into electricity when it is burned in power plants. When coal is burned, it leaves behind other products that can be used to make plastic, cement, and more. In some countries, coal is also burned in homes to produce heat.

Coal is a useful source of energy. It is the most plentiful fossil fuel, and it provides a lot of energy when it is burned. Coal is also easy to transport via truck or train. However, the positive aspects of using coal must be weighed against the negatives. The process of retrieving coal from the Earth is extremely dangerous for miners, and there are many negative effects of using coal on the environment.

The Positive and Negative Effects of Using Coal on the Environment

Positives:

Coal is the most abundant fossil fuel.

It is a very reliable fuel.

Underground mining does not immediately destroy the landscape like surface mining does.

Negatives:

When coal is burned, it releases toxic gases and fumes into the air.

Surface mining will completely destroy habitats because the landscape is ripped apart.

Surface mining can cause landslides.

Underground mining is extremely dangerous for miners.

Underground mining can poison local water supplies.

Ways technology is trying to help:

Some coal power plants are working to separate out toxins that are produced when coal is burned. Removing these toxins could reduce acid rain and other forms of pollution.

Some scientists are researching the possibility of trapping carbon dioxide released by burning coal before it can enter and heat up the atmosphere.

title: Natural Gas
text:
Directions: Obtain and combine information (from articles, charts, images, and online research) on how natural gas is used as an energy source as well as the effects of using natural gas on the environment. Record information in the chart titled “Nonrenewable Resources.”

What Is Natural Gas?

Natural gas is a colorless, odorless gas found in pockets between rocks below the Earth’s surface. Sometimes natural gas can be trapped in pockets that are miles long. In order to get the natural gas, the pockets must be split apart. This can be done through a process called fracking. Fracking is when high-pressured water is used to split apart the rocks underground, releasing the trapped gas.

Natural gas is often used to heat homes and water sources, and it is also used to power many stovetops and ovens. Natural gas is also burned to generate electricity, providing power for lights, TVs, air conditioners, and other appliances.

Natural gas has several benefits. It is relatively cheap to obtain and is much cleaner than oil or coal. Natural gas is also easy to transport in pipelines that run above or below the ground.

However, the positive aspects of using natural gas must be weighed against the negative. Natural gas is extremely flammable, so gas companies must be very careful to avoid leaks or explosions.

The Positive and Negative Effects of Using Natural Gas on the Environment

Positives:

It is a very reliable fuel.

Negatives:

Fracking can cause earthquakes.

Highly toxic wastewater from fracking can leak into local water supplies that are used for drinking or bathing.

When natural gas is burned, it releases toxic gases and fumes into the air.

Ways technology is trying to help:

Advanced technologies such as satellites and sensing devices are used to discover natural gas pockets so fewer wells need to be drilled.

title: Renewable Resources and Solar Energy
text:
Renewable Resources

Renewable resources are ________ sources that are replaced in a ______ amount of time. Examples of renewable resources are ______, ______, ______, and ________.

Directions: Obtain and combine information (from articles, charts, images, and online research) on how solar energy can be used as an energy source as well as the effects of using solar energy on the environment. Record information in the chart titled “Renewable Resources.”

What Is Solar Energy?

Solar energy is when sunlight is converted into electricity. Sunlight flows through a solar panel, which transforms the sunlight into electric energy that can be used to power buildings.

If you examine a solar panel, you will see that it is made up of tiny solar cells. One solar cell can only generate enough electricity to power a watch, but when the cells are combined to make a panel, they can provide much more electricity. Solar panels can be installed on the tops of houses and used to generate enough electricity to power everything in the house. On solar farms, which are large areas with hundreds of solar panels, enough electricity can be generated to provide energy for commercial buildings or multiple homes.

In 2009, Taiwan installed roughly 8,800 solar panels on the roof of a sports stadium. These solar panels provide enough electricity to power the entire stadium. When the stadium is not using the electricity, the solar panels are instead used to power the majority of the surrounding neighborhood.

Solar energy has many advantages. It is a renewable source of energy because the sun is always available. In one day, the sun sends enough energy to Earth to power the entire world for 40 years! Solar energy does not cause pollution, and it will last for billions of years. Solar energy does have a few drawbacks, however. First, it is only available when the sun is shining, so a backup system is needed on cloudy days and during the night. Second, solar energy is spread out over all the Earth. To use it effectively, the energy needs to be collected and concentrated into small areas. Third, while houses can be fitted with solar power panels, the process is very expensive.

The Positive and Negative Effects of Using Solar Energy on the Environment

Positives:

Solar energy does not release any harmful substances into the air, land, or water.

Negatives:

Solar farms use valuable space that could be used for planting crops.

Solar farms can displace plants and animals.

Ways technology is trying to help:

Some devices, such as watches, lights, and chargers, can use solar energy instead of electricity.

Solar power plants in North Africa could produce enough electricity for all of Europe.

title: Hydroelectricity
text:
Directions: Obtain and combine information (from articles, charts, images, and online research) on how water can be used as an energy source as well as the effects of using water as an energy source on the environment. Record information in the chart titled “Renewable Resources.”

What Is Hydroelectricity?

Hydroelectricity is when water is used to make electricity. To produce hydroelectricity, engineers will first find a large river or lake. Then they will build a dam. A dam is a very large wall that blocks the flow of water. Engineers can control how much water flows through the dam. When water flows through the dam, it spins a turbine. The turbine is connected to a generator, which converts motion into electricity. The water then returns to the river on the other side of the dam. Dams are a major source for generating electricity.

Hydroelectricity provides electricity to millions of homes, schools, offices, and businesses every day. In some parts of Canada, 90 percent of electricity is produced from water! Also, hydroelectricity is often one of the first types of electricity that is introduced into developing countries.

Hydroelectricity has many advantages. It is a reliable, renewable energy source because water is readily available and can be controlled by dams. Hydroelectricity does not release any harmful materials into the air, land, or water, so it is safe for humans and the environment. However, hydroelectricity does have drawbacks. Building dams is expensive, and once they are built, dams can cause extensive damage and changes to the local environment. Dams prevent fish from swimming upstream, which is critical to reproduction. Dams also flood the areas where they are built, destroying wetland habitats and forcing animals to relocate.

The Positive and Negative Effects of Using Hydroelectricity on the Environment

title: Cause and Effect
text:
Roses and Thorns

Why do some rose stems have thorns while others do not? Some roses have adapted, or changed, over time. There are two main reasons. One of the reasons is that roses with thorns are more likely to survive than roses without thorns. This is because the thorns protect them from predators. The smell of roses attracts animals. These animals are less likely to eat roses with thorns than roses without thorns.

Another reason that some roses have adapted to grow thorns is to help the plants get more sunlight. The thorns stick into other nearby plants. This allows the rose plant to grow above the nearby "stuck" plant. The taller rose plant is able to soak in more sunlight, so it is more likely to survive. It is clear that rose thorns are an adaptation that has occurred over time. The adaptation has caused roses with thorns to be more likely to thrive and survive than roses without thorns.

title: Cause and Effect
text:
Peacocks and Plumage

Have you ever seen a peacock? It is the male of the peafowl species. When you think of a peacock, you probably think of long, colorful tail feathers, or plumage. Why do some peafowl have large, colorful tails and other peafowl do not? The answer comes down to adaptation, or changes over time that help a species survive. Peacocks have adapted and developed larger, more colorful tails. The reason for this is that it makes them more attractive to the peahens (females). A large, colorful tail helps the peacock attract the peahen. The peacock will spread his tail as large as he can for the peahen. Then, the two are more likely to mate and produce offspring. This helps the peafowl species reproduce and survive. This is a part of the process called natural selection.

title: Dr. Juan Angel del Regato
text:
Juan Ángel del Regato fue uno de los médicos más reconocidos en la historia de la radioterapia estadounidense. Nació en Camagüey, Cuba, el 1 de marzo de 1909. Su madre fue Damiana Manzano Núñez, originalmente de Yucatán, y su padre fue Juan del Regato Castanedo, fotógrafo y operador de proyector de películas de profesión.

Juan Ángel del Regato recibió su educación secundaria en el Instituto de Segunda Enseñanza en Santa Clara, Cuba. Realizó estudios de medicina en la Universidad de La Habana, de 1926 a 1930. En el otoño de 1929, se convirtió en un estudiante internista en el Instituto del Cáncer. Poco después, se le ofreció la posición de tecnólogo radiológico. Cuando la Universidad fue cerrada en 1930, debido a la controversia política, fue enviado por la Liga Cubana Contra el Cáncer a continuar sus estudios en la Universidad de París. Recibió su título de médico en 1937. Su tesis era sobre la radioterapia exitosa en el tratamiento de cánceres inoperables del antro maxilar. Después de dos años, recibió el diploma en Radio Fisiología y Radioterapia de la Universidad de París.

En marzo de 1938, el doctor del Regato fue al Chicago Tumor Institute invitado por Max Cutler. Luego, se dedicó a entrenar y capacitar a los futuros oncólogos estadounidenses y extranjeros en una serie de cursos de seis meses. En ese entonces, solo había 39 radiólogos en los Estados Unidos.

El doctor del Regato trabajó como becario de investigación en el National Cancer Institute, y como director de Radioterapia en el Ellis Fischel State Cancer Hospital en Columbia, Missouri. Dirigió también el Penrose Cancer Hospital, en Colorado Springs, de 1949 a 1974. Luego, llegó a ser profesor de Radiología en la universidad estadounidense University of South Florida, Tampa, Florida y después fue profesor emérito de Radiología en 1981. El doctor del Regato fue el primero en establecer un programa de capacitación en oncología radioterápica. Capacitó a una primera generación de oncólogos radioterápicos reconocidos hoy como líderes en el campo. También fue un distinguido médico de la Administración de Veteranos.

El doctor del Regato fundó la asociación American Club of Therapeutic Radiologists, en 1958, un club con 54 miembros iniciales. Este club de radioterapeutas se reunía periódicamente y creció en número, hasta convertirse en la organización American Society of Therapeutic Radiologists, más tarde American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO).

El doctor del Regato recibió varios honores y premios a través de su carrera. Estos incluyen medallas de oro de las siguientes organizaciones: Radiologic Society of North America (1966), the American College of Radiology (1968), the American Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology (1977). También, recibió reconocimientos como el American Medical Association Scientific Achievement Award (1993).

title: Gloria Estefan
text:
Gloria María Milagrosa Fajardo García, nació el 1 de septiembre de 1957 en La Habana, Cuba. Su padre fue un policía militar en Cuba y su madre fue maestra. Ella tenía solo 16 meses cuando salió de Cuba. Sus padres se vieron obligados a inmigrar a Miami, Florida, debido a la situación política de la isla. Al llegar a los Estados Unidos, su padre se unió al ejército estadounidense y fue enviado a Vietnam. Luego, como familia, se mudaron un tiempo a Texas mientras su padre servía en el ejército.

Asistió a las siguientes instituciones escolares: St. Michael-Archangel School y Our Lady of Lourdes Academy, en Miami. Gloria continuó sus estudios de psicología y comunicaciones en la Universidad de Miami (University of Miami). También trabajó como intérprete en el Servicio de Inmigración y Naturalización e impartió clases de guitarra tres noches por semana. Conoció a su esposo y padre de sus hijos, Emilio Estefan, durante un evento musical. Emilio pertenecía a una agrupación llamada “Miami Latin Boys”. Emilio invitó a Gloria a integrarse al grupo como vocalista principal. Una vez que Gloria aceptó, el grupo cambió de nombre a “Miami Sound Machine”. Se casó con Emilio Estefan en 1979 y desde entonces es conocida profesionalmente como Gloria Estefan.Tuvieron un hijo, Nayib (nacido el 2 de septiembre de 1980) y una hija, Emily ( nacida el 5 de diciembre de 1994).

La carrera artística de Gloria Estefan fue impactada por un accidente, el 20 de marzo de 1990. Un tractor chocó con el autobús en el que descansaba la banda durante una tormenta de nieve en Pennsylvania. El accidente le causó la fractura de dos vértebras cervicales, por lo cual tuvo que someterse a varias operaciones. Ella continuó su carrera a pesar de eso y se convirtió en una de las artistas más importantes de su era.

Durante su carrera, Gloria Estefan vendió más de 100 millones de discos en todo el mundo y ganó siete premios Grammy. También recibió una estrella en el Hollywood Walk of Fame y otra en Las Vegas Walk of Fame, además de la Medalla de Honor del Congreso de Ellis Island. Gloria Estefan también recibió varios premios. Entre ellos están el Hispanic Heritage Award, un MTV Video Music Award, dos ECA Awards, y el American Music Award por su trayectoria artística. Fue incluida en el Songwriters Hall of Fame y ha recibido múltiples Billboard Awards por sus éxitos en las listas.

Los logros de Gloria Estefan no solo han sido en su carrera artística. También tuvo éxito en sus obras filantrópicas. Ella y su esposo iniciaron una fundación filantrópica en 1997. Gloria Estefan fue elegida Persona del Año 2008, por la Academia Latina de la Grabación, por su labor "filantrópica, profesional y logros culturales". En el año 2015, fue premiada con la Medalla de la Libertad junto con su esposo.

Los Estefan también han contribuido al estado de Florida con sus negocios. Entre ellos la cadena de restaurantes de comida cubana, Bongos, el restaurante Larios on the Beach y el hotel Cardozo. Por los mismos, la Cámara de Comercio del Gran Miami les otorgó el premio "The Sand in My Shoes" ("Arena en los zapatos").

title: Lydia Cabrera
text:
Lydia Cabrera nació el 20 de mayo de 1900 en La Habana, Cuba. Ella fue una académica reconocida en todo el mundo. Escribió muchas obras sobre la vida popular y la cultura afrocubana. Lydia Cabrera es considerada una figura importante en la literatura cubana. Durante su carrera, escribió el trabajo de investigación más completo e importante sobre las religiones y el folclore afrocaribeños. Reconoció en sus obras la riqueza de la cultura africana y sus contribuciones vitales a la identidad cubana.

Lydia era la menor de ocho hijos. Su padre fue Raimundo Cabrera Bosch, un escritor, jurista, abogado y ex-activista por la independencia de Cuba. Él fue miembro de los intelectuales independentistas, conocidos como la "generación de 1868", y fundador de la revista literaria y política Cuba y América.

Cuando Lydia era joven, fue una lectora entusiasta y recibió su educación primaria en su hogar. Su educación fue influenciada por el nacionalismo y la cultura de su padre. Su amor por el arte fue influenciado por su hermana Emma. Lo que más impactó su vida profesional fueron las historias, el idioma y las tradiciones africanas y afrocubanas de sus niñeras.

A los 14 años, Lydia completó su escuela secundaria y comenzó a auditar cursos universitarios. Estudió por un tiempo en la Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes San Alejandro. En sus ratos libres escribía, bajo el seudónimo de Nena, en la revista Cuba y América. A los 18 años, publicó sus artículos en el Diario de la Marina.

En 1927, a los 27 años, viajó a París para tomar clases en la Escuela del Louvre (L'Ecole du Louvre). También realizó investigaciones sobre el arte y la religión de Japón y la India. Lydia permaneció en Francia durante 11 años. Allí escribió Cuentos negros de Cuba, una colección de 22 cuentos populares, la cual se publicó en 1940 en La Habana. Su segunda obra de ficción, ¿Por Qué? Cuentos Negros de Cuba, Colección del Chicherekú, fue publicado en 1948. El Monte se publicó en 1954. Este libro describe su notable estudio sobre la religión de la santería. En el mismo se discute la fusión de las deidades yorubas de la santería con los santos católicos romanos y su farmacopea herbal (información sobre sustancias medicinales).

Lydia Cabrera fue reconocida y honrada internacionalmente por sus contribuciones a la literatura, la etnología y la antropología. Durante la Revolución cubana de 1959, ella se vio obligada a huir del país. A partir de entonces, vivió en España y Estados Unidos, principalmente en Miami, donde continuó trabajando por el resto de su larga vida. Lydia Cabrera recibió varios doctorados honorarios, incluyendo uno de la Universidad de Miami (University of Miami) en 1987. Murió en Miami, el 19 de septiembre de 1991.

title: Mel Martínez
text:
Melquiades R. Martínez nació el 23 de octubre de 1946 en Sagua la Grande, Cuba. Su padre era veterinario y practicaba con su familia la religión católica. Debido a la persecución religiosa en Cuba hacia los católicos, los padres de Martínez lo enviaron a los Estados Unidos en 1962, a través de la Operación Pedro Pan. Martínez tenía tan solo 15 años y solo hablaba español cuando llegó a un centro de refugiados en Matecumbe Key en los Cayos de la Florida. Vivió con dos familias diferentes en Florida, hasta que sus padres llegaron a los Estados Unidos en 1966.

Mel Martínez terminó la escuela secundaria en una escuela católica local con un excelente dominio del inglés, y se matriculó en Florida State University. Estudió una licenciatura en Relaciones Internacionales en 1969 y en Leyes en 1973 en Florida State University. Fue presidente de Florida Academy of Trial Lawyers de 1988 a 1989. Martínez también presidió la corporación Orlando Housing Authority y formó parte de la junta directiva de Orlando Utilities Commission. Conoció a su esposa, Kitty, mientras eran estudiantes en Florida State University. La pareja tuvo tres hijos y adoptaron a niños refugiados de Cuba y Vietnam.

En 1998, Mel Martínez ganó las elecciones como gobernador de Orange County. En este cargo, Martínez pudo reducir algunos de los impuestos a la propiedad en Orange County. También despidió a un jefe del departamento de bomberos que se negó a promover los derechos de las mujeres y de las minorías.

El presidente Bush nominó a Martínez como Secretario del Departamento de Vivienda y Desarrollo Urbano de EE. UU. (HUD). Fue confirmado unánimemente por el Senado de los Estados Unidos el 23 de enero de 2001. En este cargo, Martínez fue un firme defensor de la propiedad de la vivienda y del avance de las iniciativas público-privadas con servicios religiosos y comunitarios.

El 12 de diciembre de 2003, Martínez renunció a su cargo en el Departamento de Vivienda y Desarrollo Urbano de EE. UU. (HUD) para postularse a un cargo en el Senado, el cual ganó. En su discurso de victoria dijo lo siguiente: "Solo en los Estados Unidos puede un niño de 15 años llegar solo a nuestras costas, sin hablar el idioma, con una maleta y la esperanza de un futuro más brillante, y ascender para servir en el Gabinete del Presidente de los Estados Unidos. Y solo en Estados Unidos puede ese mismo muchacho hoy estar a un paso de hacer historia como el primer cubanoamericano en servir en el Senado de los Estados Unidos."

Mel Martínez se jubiló del Senado el 9 de septiembre de 2010. Actualmente, se desempeña como presidente de JP Morgan Chase & Co. para el Sureste de los Estados Unidos y América Latina.

text:

Natalia went home after helping her friends in the community garden. She kept thinking about how big the pumpkins they’d planted had grown. However, she had her own plant to take care of, and lately, it wasn’t doing well.

Her plant was called a spider plant, and it had been a gift from her mother. Natalia was worried because she knew her mother would not be pleased if it died. She had been giving the plant new water regularly, and she kept it in a corner of her bedroom, close to her bed, so she could check on it often. Why was it still wilting? Natalia thought about some of the questions from her conversations with friends in the community garden. Maybe her plant needed more light!

She decided to put her plant closer to a window. Sure enough, in a couple of weeks, her plant was looking great: healthy and green. She realized for the first time that something was special about her plant. It wasn’t growing in any dirt! “How could that be?” she wondered. The garden had dirt, but her plant didn’t.

title: Jan Baptist’s Willow
text:

Jan Baptist van Helmont was a scientist living in the 1600s. Like all good scientists, he had questions. He wondered where plant material came from. Other scientists at the time thought plants ate soil to grow. Van Helmont wasn’t sure that was true. He decided to perform an experiment to find the answer.

Van Helmont began his experiment with a baby willow tree and some soil. He weighed both of them. The tree weighed five pounds, and the dirt weighed 200 pounds. He then let the tree grow undisturbed for three years. During that time, he gave water to the tree in an area with plenty of light and air.

After three years, van Helmont weighed the tree and the soil again. He discovered that the tree had gained 164 pounds, but the soil had only lost four ounces. With these results, he concluded that the tree did not gain 164 pounds from the soil. He said, “One hundred and sixty-four pounds of wood, barks, and roots arose out of water only.”

What point was van Helmont trying to make with his experiment? (Hint: In science, this is sometimes called the experiment’s claim.)

In science experiments, it's important to track and record all data, especially matter that is transported into a system. What data should van Helmont have documented in addition to the weights of the plant and soil?
