title: Distribution of Land in the Colonies
text:
In colonial America, land was readily available for free white men. In England, the king decided who owned property. When colonists sailed to America, they hoped to seize opportunities that came along with land ownership. If they owned land, these men could vote and hold government offices.

In the New England Colonies, early colonists received 50 acres of land. They took the greatest risks to be there, so this land was meant as a reward. Families obtained land if they promised to farm and improve the property. The land was surveyed, and then land deeds were processed by the royal governor’s office. These deeds were sometimes recorded in the colony’s government records. If landowners ever wanted to sell property, white men and free African men could buy it.

In the Middle Colonies, proprietors could sell or gift land to others. The proprietor determined the price, and the measurement of the land was recorded in the proprietor’s office. Individuals could then resell part or all of the land. This was one way people could speculate, or purchase large tracts of land and then resell them in smaller parts for profit. Free African men were permitted to own land if a landowner was willing to sell property to them.

In the Southern Colonies, the headright system was established by the governor and the colonial government. The government gave 50 acres of land to adult men. They were also given 50 acres for each person who worked for them. A clerk in the governor’s office recorded land measurements and transfers. Large land ownership became known as a plantation.

title: Cycle of Debt
text:
There are factors that determine the price of a commodity or product. Some of these factors include the cost of production, the quality of the product, and how many products will be available in the future. The most critical factor is demand, or the desire people have to buy a product. If there is no demand, it doesn’t matter how much of a product there is or what it costs. If no one wants it, it won’t sell.

In Great Britain, there were large companies that bought and sold one valuable product: tobacco. These companies were called brokerages. Only brokerages could buy American tobacco. Tobacco farmers worked with brokerage firms to get the tobacco from the plantation to Great Britain. The broker would decide how much the plantation owner’s tobacco was worth.

In the 17th century, no direct payment was involved. The brokerage house worked like its own bank. The plantation owner would be given credit for the value of the tobacco. This amount of credit was recorded by the brokerage house.

Manufactured goods had to be purchased from Great Britain and shipped to the colonies. If there was anything the plantation owner and his family wanted to buy from Great Britain, they made a list and gave it to the broker. The broker purchased the items using the credit from that year’s tobacco sales.

The owner had to trust the broker with these purchases. There were no prices on the list, so the owner didn’t know how much each item would cost. The broker would purchase only the best for his client. Most of the time, the cost of the items was more than the owner had in his account. The broker promised that the planter could pay off the rest when he returned with the next year’s crop. The plantation owner would then be in debt to the broker. This process often repeated the next year. So, the plantation owner would always be in debt to the broker. It was extremely difficult to reverse this cycle.

title: Life in the Middle Passage
text:
In the first 300 years after Columbus reached the Americas, ships that crossed the Atlantic almost always came from Europe. However, most didn’t sail straight from Europe to the Americas. The sea currents and wind directions made sailing south toward Africa easier and faster than sailing directly west across the Atlantic. This route presented opportunities for trade by staying near the continents. European traders found a market with the nations in West Africa.

This voyage from Europe to Africa was called the Outward Passage. Ships carried tools, weapons, cloth, and other goods to Africa. Merchants and soldiers would pressure African leaders to trade those goods for people who had been captured in wars or kidnapped.

People were imprisoned and held as products to be traded. The European traders did not care about the welfare of the people they considered “cargo.” These men, women, and children were put in dark, dank ships. The living conditions were inhumane. The traders who held the Africans against their will were transporting them to be sold to new owners in the West Indies and American colonies. The voyage from Africa to the colonies in the Western Hemisphere was called “the Middle Passage.”

No words can describe the terror and hopelessness felt by the African men, women, and children who experienced the Middle Passage. Nothing can justify the choices the European traders and colonists made in the past that impacted so many lives. No words can be expressed for those who survived, except to learn of their suffering and share in their sorrows.

title: Lives of Enslaved Africans
text:
The life of a person who was enslaved changed little from day to day. Enslaved people were considered property by the people who enslaved them. They were clothed, fed, and sheltered by what the enslaver wanted to provide. The workday was structured by the enslaver.

There were public consequences for outward defiance. This was done to create fear within the enslaved people so they did not want to rebel against their enslavers. Sometimes, enslaved people fought back and rebelled against their enslavers and living conditions. This caused enslavers to fear future rebellion. It also proved that enslaved Africans not only desired their freedom but were willing to risk their lives to get it back.

There were many other ways that enslaved adults and children resisted their enslavers and their situation. Some resisted by breaking tools used for cultivating cash crops. Others planned and escaped from the enslavers. Escape was very dangerous. If successful, there was freedom. If unsuccessful, there was extreme punishment. The enslavers tried to control everything.

Enslaved people were taken from their homes, families, cultures, and everything they had known. They were bought and sold as property to people in a strange new land. Everything in their lives was turned upside down. They were forced to work in an unfamiliar environment with unfamiliar people. They had to learn how to use unfamiliar tools, grow new crops, and learn a new language. Sometimes, they also had to adjust to a different climate.

In addition to all the loss and change they experienced, enslaved people also knew they would never see their homes again. The one thing the enslavers could not take from the enslaved people was their memories. They kept the celebrations and traditions of their communities and cultures alive. They remembered the stories, songs, and skills they learned in Africa. Enslavers tried to stop the African people from expressing their cultural identities. Despite these efforts, the enslaved Africans continued to preserve their memories and culture. These were things no enslaver could ever take from them.

title: Daily Life in the Colonies
text:
Life in the early 1700s was very different from when the colonies were first established. There was a greater trade balance. This meant more manufactured goods were available from England, like paper, sugar, and tea. Colonists could trade for or buy things. They didn’t have to make everything themselves.

Every city had a newspaper, which included news, weather, opinions, and advertisements. Even though most people could read, they often gathered at a local meeting house to hear the news read out loud.

Farmers sold their produce at markets. Families in the city would have a kitchen garden. They would still go to the market to purchase or trade with items such as meat, vegetables, and preserved fruit. Much of the preparation was done before foods arrived in city kitchens. This eased the workload of women and children.

Colonists’ daily diets included dried or salted meat and corn mush or bread. Meals might include a stew or pie filled with meat and vegetables in gravy. The drink of choice was apple cider. People rarely drank water because it was not clean. People living in cities often got sick from bad water.

Craftsmen took in apprentices to teach them a trade. These boys acted as servants in a craftsman’s household and shop. They ran errands, tended fires, cleaned, and learned the trade. Blacksmiths, silversmiths, glassworkers, and printers were all open for apprenticeships.

Boys had two shirts, one for work and one for church. Socks were mended until they couldn’t be mended anymore. Women and girls usually had only one dress and a few aprons. Aprons protected their dresses for church on Sundays. When children outgrew their clothing, they passed it down to their siblings.

Shoes were individually made by village shoemakers to a general size. There were no right or left shoes. They did not fit well and had to be tied or buckled to stay on. Only the very wealthy could have shoes made to fit their feet.

The average lifespan of a colonist in the 1700s depended on their work situation, their wealth, and luck. Poor and enslaved people died young from disease, accidents, or being overworked. Those who had easier work could expect a longer life. Although life had gotten better since the early days of colonization, it still wasn’t easy. Every day presented its own difficulties.

title: The Laws of Slavery
text:
Before 1640, a man, regardless of his skin color, could buy land in a colony in America. Enslavement of another person was a socially accepted practice but had no legal basis. Over time, the number of captured and enslaved Africans increased as the economics of the colonies increased. In Virginia, enslavers felt laws should be in place to keep the Africans enslaved. By the 1700s, the laws of Virginia had begun to distinguish Black people from white people. This is important in the history of law. It was the first time in America that a person was defined by the color of their skin. This legal distinction has had a long-term impact on millions of lives. This gave legal grounds for future generations of people of African descent to be denied natural and civil rights in the United States of America.

Let’s look at other laws that affected enslaved and free Africans in the colonies.

1641 Massachusetts Colony made slavery legal.

1660 Connecticut did not allow people of African descent to serve in the militia.

1670 Virginia made lifetime enslavement the “normal” condition for people of African descent.

1680 Virginia declared the status of a child was determined by the status of the mother. If the mother was enslaved, the child would be, too.

1696 South Carolina required enslavers to provide clothing for their enslaved people. Enslavers were also allowed to treat and punish enslaved people any way they wished.

1702 New York made it illegal to do business with an enslaved person without permission from their enslaver.

1705 New York made it legal to execute freedom seekers who were caught.

1723 Enslaved people in Virginia were not allowed to meet together in large groups.

1740 South Carolina made it illegal to teach enslaved people to read and write.

title: How Do I Build Empathy?
text:
It is important to practice showing empathy to others. When you spend time with other people, you get to know them. You get to know what they like and dislike. This helps you understand how they see the world around them. It helps you become an empathic person. Being an empathic person helps you to be a better friend.

Here are some ways to practice empathy:

Ask lots of questions.

Get feedback from others.

Try to think in terms of “us” and not “them.”

Consider what you have in common with your classmates.

Work in a team or in groups.

Ask yourself, “How would that make me feel, so I can feel that with them?”

title: Democratic Principles
text: Americans are a diverse group of people. We come from many places. We have many customs and traditions. We share some similar ideas, or beliefs. We believe in truthfulness, equality, and justice. We also believe in respect and working for the common good. These beliefs help unite us in our communities. They help the country work successfully.

title: Truthfulness
text: Truthfulness is saying and doing what is right. It is being honest about what really happened. An honest person does what they say they will do. They don’t lie, cheat, or steal. It can be hard to tell the truth, but it is important. When we are truthful, others will trust us. Being truthful is responsible and brave.

title: Equality
text: Equality means treating all people with fairness and kindness. It means that all people have access to what they need to succeed.

title: Justice
text: Justice is about applying the law fairly. People are judged equally. They are not treated differently because of their beliefs or appearance. Justice makes things equal and balanced for all people.

title: Respect
text: Respect is knowing all people are important. It is accepting other people’s beliefs and values. You can respect others even if you believe in different things. Respect is caring about others’ health, well-being, and feelings. Respecting yourself is important, too. Your health, well-being, and feelings are important. When you respect yourself, it is easier to respect others.

title: The Common Good
text: In democratic communities, each person has to think about other community members. They have to think about what would be best for everyone. Thinking about what is best for everyone is known as the common good.

title: Young Entrepreneurs
text:
You don’t have to be an adult to start a business. People as young as five years old have become entrepreneurs by starting their own businesses. Some businesses have grown and become successful.

Take child entrepreneur Hannah Grace. Grace was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes when she was just a baby. At the age of 10, she started making her own health and beauty products to sell. She created a business called Hannah Grace BeYOUtiful and donates 20 percent of every purchase to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Fund.

Maya Penn founded her business, Maya’s Ideas, when she was just eight years old. Today, Penn is 19 and CEO of her own company, which sells fashion accessories that are environmentally sustainable. Not only does she run her own business, but Penn also donates 10 percent of her profits to charities and to help the environment.

When he was nine years old, Moziah Bridges wanted an eye-catching fashion accessory. Because of this, he got the idea to create Mo’s Bows. Bridges’s company sells all kinds of things, including bow ties, pocket squares, and other apparel. Today, despite his company’s international success, Bridges intends to graduate high school and continue his education by going to college to study fashion design.

Nohbo Drops were created by Benjamin Stern. Stern came up with the idea while he was sitting in his ninth grade biology class. Nohbo Drops are packets for shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and shaving cream that dissolve in water. They don’t contain chemicals that harm the environment, and they help to eliminate plastic waste.

These young people didn’t find success overnight. Their businesses started with an idea. They worked and improved their ideas until they were able to create businesses out of them. Hannah Grace had to try over and over to find a successful recipe for her bath bombs and beauty products. Moziah Bridges started out with an eye-catching bowtie and worked to design and create other accessories. Entrepreneurs work hard, often for years, before their businesses take off. Some businesses don’t make it, but with a good idea, hard work, and dedication, anything is possible.

title: Potoo Bird
text:
A solar oven uses light to heat and cook food. They are also called "solar cookers". Solar ovens are usually used outside in direct sunlight. They can also be used with very strong lamps. Solar ovens use energy by trapping light. The trapped energy is converted to heat. The more light, the more heat energy. As heat energy is gathered, it increases the temperature inside of the solar oven.

Solar ovens can be made from different materials. Metal sheets, wood, and metal bowls can all be used. They can even be made from recyclables, like cardboard boxes, cardboard tubes, and tin cans. Solar ovens can come in various sizes, shapes, and designs. It all depends on the materials used. All designs trap light. They convert the light energy to produce heat.

For a solar oven to cook food, the food may need to be cut up into tiny pieces. Tiny pieces of food cook faster than large pieces. Solar ovens also work best with food that does not need to be stirred, flipped, or rearranged while cooking. Stirring or moving food requires the oven to be opened. When the solar oven is opened, all the trapped energy is released. Lastly, depending on the light source, solar ovens may need to be moved or adjusted so that they are always in direct light.

Solar ovens rely only on light to cook food, so they are an affordable, easy-to-move, and efficient device for cooking.

title: Working Together
text:
People think and believe different things. Sometimes these differences can cause conflict. Conflict is a disagreement. Conflict can happen between two people or between groups. It can even happen between nations.

One way to prevent conflict is to treat others with respect. In school, we show respect when we take turns, play with everyone, and follow rules. It is important to show respect even if we have different opinions. We can follow democratic principles and work together to prevent conflict.

title: Steps to Solving Problems
text:
When problems arise, there are steps we can take to help:

State the problem.

Identify the cause of the problem.

Suggest solutions for the problem.

Attempt to solve the problem.

Reach out to experts (teacher, parent, adult, community helpers) to brainstorm possible solutions.

title: Consensus and Compromise
text:
Talking and negotiating are two ways to solve problems. People and groups can talk and negotiate. People can try to come to a consensus. Consensus is when most of a group has the same opinion. Consensus is also when the whole group agrees to a solution.

People can have different ideas and opinions. Differences can make it hard to solve problems. People don't always agree on one solution. When this happens, people can compromise. Compromise means changing the way we think about a solution. In a compromise, both sides give something up to create a solution. We compromise when we think about what is best for everyone, not just ourselves.

title: What Is a Region?
text: Geographers organize the Earth into regions to help us learn about our world. A region is an area that has similar characteristics. Some regions are organized based on their physical characteristics. Physical characteristics include landforms, climate, and biomes. Some regions are organized by their human characteristics. These include population, culture, and language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

title: Regions of the United States
text:
The United States is a very big country. It covers almost 4 million square miles! We can divide the U.S. using physical or political boundaries. Boundaries mark the positions of regions on the continent.

The United States is divided into six regions: Northeast, Southeast, Midwest, Southwest, Northwest, and West. Most regions are divided using common geographic characteristics. Each area has its own unique physical geography, climate, vegetation, and natural resources.

title: Northeast
text:
The Northeast region has 11 states. The bigger states are New York and Pennsylvania. The smaller states are Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Rhode Island, and Vermont. The Northeast region is bordered by Canada to the north. The Southeast region is to the south, and the Midwest region is to the west. The Atlantic Ocean is to the east.

Much of the Northeast region is mountainous. The major mountain ranges are the Allegheny Mountains, the Pocono Mountains, the Adirondack Mountains, and the Catskills. The Northeast region has many rivers. Some of them are the Delaware, the Kennebec, the Hudson, the Connecticut, the Niagara, the Penobscot, and the Ohio.

The Northeast has the largest number of people. However, it is the smallest region in the area. The Northeast has many large cities. There's a large amount of technology and manufacturing in the region.

The Northeast has a diverse climate. It has all four seasons. The average precipitation is 20 inches per year. The abundance of water sources affects the climate and economy. Water helps agriculture and other industries. Water is very important for transportation. People and goods can be transported by boats, ships, and ferries. The Northeast is also home to many forests, wetlands, and beaches.

title: Southeast
text:
The Southeast region has 12 states. The inner southeast states are Arkansas, Kentucky, Tennessee, and West Virginia. Eight southeastern states border either the Atlantic Ocean or the Gulf of Mexico. The states that border the Gulf of Mexico are Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, and Louisiana. The states that border the Atlantic Ocean are Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Florida.

Water is a great resource for both work and play in the Southeast. Fishing and visiting the beach are very popular activities. Florida borders both the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. Its beaches are world-famous. North Carolina’s beaches are historic. The Wright Brothers flew the world’s first airplane at Kitty Hawk on North Carolina’s Outer Banks.

Agriculture is a major industry in the Southeast. This region has mild winters and hot, humid summers. This makes the Southeast an ideal spot to grow crops. The Southeast has long been known for growing cotton. Did you know the nation’s peanut supply comes from the Southeast? Georgia farmers produce nearly half of all peanuts grown in the U.S. With mostly flat land, there are hundreds of thousands of acres dedicated to growing cotton and peanuts. Other important crops are corn, sorghum, and citrus crops, like oranges and grapefruit.

Many businesses have opened up in this part of the country. Why here? People like to live in places with good weather that offer many things to do. Automobile manufacturing is an important industry in the Southeast. Eleven different car companies have factories in the region. They have thousands of people working for them. All those people build more than one million cars each year. Other big employers with headquarters in the region are banks, beverage companies, and retail stores.

title: Midwest
text:
The Midwestern states are different from the rest of the nation. They feature fertile soil, big rivers, and thousands of lakes. The Midwestern Region contains 12 states. Half of these states border the Great Lakes. These states are Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, and Ohio. States that don't border the Great Lakes are North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri, and Iowa.

The Great Lakes are an important physical feature of the Midwest. The term “great” is no exaggeration. They are so big that at their widest points, you cannot see the other side. Lakes Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, and Superior hold more than 80 percent of the fresh water in the United States. The Great Lakes provide drinking water for 48 million Americans and Canadians. They have a big impact on the economy of the Midwest. More than $50 billion is spent on recreation at the Great Lakes each year. Fishing and boating are two of the biggest activities. It is estimated that over 1 million jobs are connected to the Great Lakes.

Many of the states in this region have rich, fertile soil. Where does it come from? The rivers provide it. Three of the largest rivers in the U.S. cross the Midwest. The Missouri, the Mississippi, and the Ohio Rivers help drain the lands. Regular flooding deposits nutrients into the soil. Parts of the region get heavy rainfall in the spring and summer. These rivers carry that water away. Unfortunately, annual flooding can cause major issues for people who live in those areas. Both the Missouri and the Ohio are tributaries of the Mississippi. This means they flow into the Mississippi. The Mississippi eventually flows south into the Gulf of Mexico.

Part of the Midwest region is very hilly. South Dakota’s Black Hills feature the rugged Badlands National Park. Rolling hills can be found in many states. Some of these are the remains of glaciers. As glaciers inched forward thousands of years ago, they left their mark on much of the Midwest. Flat land can make for good farming, but the landscape also produces lots of wind. Many states have fields of wind turbines that produce electricity as they spin. Other types of wind common to the Midwest are not so helpful. Tornadoes are a dangerous menace across the Midwest. They have been known to strike in nearly every state. Tornadoes seem to occur frequently in this region during May and June.

title: Southwest
text:
The states that belong to the Southwest region are Arizona, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas. This region uses its natural resources to make products and provide services. Mining and oil drilling are very important. Texas and Oklahoma produce much of the nation’s oil. The Southwest is also rich in minerals, such as coal, copper, and silver. Mining and oil companies provide jobs for workers in this region. These companies also sell their products to other companies throughout the nation and the world.

Most of the land in the Southwest is too dry to grow crops. There are some areas that receive enough rainfall water. However, others use irrigation ditches and canals. This helps to bring water in from other places to grow crops. The Southwest grows many crops. These include cotton, lettuce, melons, grapefruit, onions, nuts, hay, and more. These crops are shipped across the nation and the world. This brings millions of dollars into the Southwest’s economy. Ranchers here also raise dairy and beef cattle, pigs, sheep, and chickens. If you eat brown shrimp, chances are they were caught along the Texas coast!

Tourism brings millions of dollars into the economy of the Southwest. Tourists from colder climates enjoy visiting these states during the winter months. When it is cold and snowy back home, it is often warm and pleasant in the Southwest. Visitors come to the Southwest to see Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona and Carlsbad Caverns National Park in New Mexico. These locations and many others bring money into the economy. They also provide jobs for people in the area.

title: West
text:
The West region includes the states of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Utah, and Wyoming. The West has many kinds of natural resources. Many large industries that support the region have been created around these resources. Some of these include fertile soil, plenty of sunshine, and enough water for farming. Crops grown in the West include wheat, potatoes, cabbage, and onions. Many farmers also raise beef and dairy cattle, sheep, chickens, and turkeys.

The West has a large population. In order to provide water for all those people, massive dams have been built. The Oroville Dam in California and the Hoover Dam at the Nevada-Arizona border create huge reservoirs. They also generate inexpensive electricity for the population. Rich deposits of gold, various metals, oil, and natural gasses are found in the West. Mines and oil wells throughout the region provide jobs for workers. They also supply these valuable natural resources to people across the United States and around the world.

Tourism is an important industry in the West. It brings tourists from all over the country and the world. Some popular sites are Yellowstone National Park, beaches in California and Hawaii, Utah’s Zion National Park, and the rugged Rocky Mountains. You can be sure tourists spend plenty of money while they’re there. They create jobs for people who work in hotels, lodges, restaurants, recreation stores, and national parks.

title: What Is Government?
text: A government is a group of people who make decisions for a community. They serve the needs of the people in the community. In the United States, adult citizens vote for people to represent them in the government. The representatives make decisions based on the law. The people agree to follow their representative’s decisions. This agreement is called consent of the governed. At every level, people’s consent is what gives the government power to act.

title: Why Do We Have Government?
text: We need rules in school so we can work together in an orderly way. Rules keep us safe and help us manage problems. Our communities need the same things. Governments were created to perform these functions, or tasks. Governments create laws for our communities. These laws help provide order. Governments protect people and their property. They also help resolve conflicts.

title: The Government Creates Laws
text:
A primary focus of all governments should be to promote the common good. The government works for the common good by creating laws and rules that benefit everyone.

The government makes laws and rules to protect the rights of citizens. Laws and rules also provide safety and security.

Laws in the United States say people should be treated equally. The government is responsible for making sure all people are treated fairly under these laws.

title: The Government Establishes Order
text: One of the main functions of government is to create laws. Laws help us work together in an orderly way. Imagine if there were no traffic laws. How would we drive on the roads? Laws help establish the way that we do things in our community. In the United States, everyone has to obey the same laws. The laws have to be written down and applied equally.

title: The Government Provides Security
text: A function of government is to help its citizens feel safe. Governments create laws that protect people and their property. They also provide services to help do this. If your house catches fire, the fire department is there to help you. The police help provide security. The military is a part of our government. It protects our country.

title: The Government Provides Services
text:
Governments help provide things we need and want. Governments create services that support the well-being of the public. Governments use tax money to provide these services.

Government services include public transportation, police, and fire departments. Creating roads and traffic lights and providing trash pick-up are also usually government services. Many governments provide places of recreation. They are things like public parks and playgrounds. Local governments give us schools and libraries too.

Courts of law are government services that help solve conflicts. People can take conflicts to a court. There, a judge listens to both sides of the conflict. Then the judge interprets the law to resolve the conflict.

title: Types of Government
text: A government is a group of people who lead a community. The role of government leaders is to serve the needs of community members. Three types of government systems are representative democracy, monarchy, and dictatorship. Each government system works differently. Most of these government systems make and enforce laws. As we look at these types of governments, pay special attention to the services provided by the government. Also, pay attention to the role of citizens in each of these types of governments.

title: Democratic Principles Unite People
text:
The United States is home to a diverse group of people. U.S. citizens

come from many places. They have many customs and traditions. They are all united by democratic principles. Some of these principles are fairness, equality, justice, the rule of law, and the common good. These foundational principles help communities work together successfully. They help the government run well.

title: Fairness, Equality, and Justice
text:
Fairness is a fundamental value in the United States. Fairness means making sure everyone has what they need to be successful. We demonstrate fairness in our classroom, school, and community. For example, students are allowed to wear hearing aids in class. This is fair because it gives students the support they need to succeed. The government demonstrates fairness by making laws and policies to help all citizens be successful.

Equality means all people have the same opportunity and tools to succeed. In your school, everyone deserves the same education. Every student can check out books in the library. They can order from the same lunch menu. It would be unequal if everyone did not have the same opportunities. It is the responsibility of the government to provide the same opportunities to everyone.

Justice means applying the law fairly. People are judged equally. They are not treated differently because of their beliefs or appearance. Government should make sure the law is applied equally and in a balanced way for all people.

Fairness, equality, and justice are democratic values. These values guide the government. They protect the rights of citizens.

title: Rule of Law
text:
Rule of law means citizens and government leaders must obey the same laws. Everyone, including those who make and enforce laws, should follow the same rules. The consequences for breaking the law should be the same, too. Everyone must also be treated equally under the laws.

The United States government follows the rule of law. The Constitution is the supreme law of the United States. This means the government can only use its power as defined by the Constitution.

The rule of law has four important ideas:

Laws have to be adopted and approved through government processes.

Laws have to be clear, and everyone needs to know about them.

Laws are applied equally for all citizens.

When there are disputes about the law, individuals will have representatives who are neutral in order to deliver the best outcome.

title: The Common Good
text: The United States Constitution establishes the conditions for government. According to the Constitution, people give authority, or power, to the government by electing representatives. A representative is someone who makes choices and acts for other people. The representatives must choose what is good for the freedom and liberty of many people instead of what is good for a few. This is called common good. In a democratic community, citizens behave in a way that supports the common good. In the United States, the government works for the common good through policies and laws.

title: Colonial Charters
text:
As European countries established colonies in the Americas, English colonists started new lives across the sea. Some colonists were motivated to make money and gain a higher status in society. Other colonists came to practice their religion freely and avoid persecution. Many others sought the chance to get land of their own, which was very difficult in Europe. Regardless of the motivation behind their decision, why people decided to come to the colonies, all of them came as a result of a charter.

A charter was a legal document given by the king of England. It gave land to a company or individual to create a colony. The charter included the geographic location for the colony. It also laid out the terms between the king and the government in the colony. The charter gave each colonist the rights and privileges of an English subject. The purpose of the colony was also described in the charter. Finally, the charter detailed the conditions for paying taxes to the king. The charter was the document of ownership or deed for the colony, its constitution, and the financial contract between the king of England and the colony.

The charters provided two important things. First, they guaranteed the colonists the same rights as citizens in England. This included the right of representation in government. Second, the charter allowed for an elected legislature, as long as the laws the legislature made did not go against the laws of England.

People who wanted to start a colony had different options. One option was to form a company. A company was made up of investors who provided ships, tools, food, water, and protection for the people who would move to America. Wages for the colonists were also paid with the investors’ money. The colonists were required to meet the goals of the charter. They worked for the company and lived by the rules of the charter. The colonists remained the king’s subjects but lived and worked across the ocean. They worked to provide the company with products such as furs, lumber, and agricultural products. The company would then sell the products back in England for profit. These profits were used to pay the company’s investors and the king. The colonies that were established by company charter included Virginia, Plymouth, Massachusetts Bay, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Delaware.

At this time in England, there was great conflict over what church a person attended on Sundays. An official state church had been created that every person in England was supposed to attend. In colonies, the king’s people weren’t there to enforce that law. They could attend the church they wanted instead of the church the king said they must attend. The colonists had more freedom to choose what religion to practice. This freedom was included in the charter.

Another form of charter created a proprietorship. In this case, the king gave a charter to a person as a reward for services to the king. The person given the charter was called a “proprietor,” meaning “owner.” The charter gave the proprietor all the rights to govern the colony, choose the purpose for the colony, and the conditions of paying taxes to the crown. The colonies that were established by proprietors included New York, New Hampshire, Maryland, North Carolina, New Jersey, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania.

Some of the colonies established by companies and proprietors later became royal colonies. The king rewrote their charters so that all of the profits and authority became his. These royal colonies included New Hampshire, New York, New Jersey, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

title: Essential Question
text: Who moved to and settled in North America? Why did they choose to live where they did?

title: Economies in the Colonies
text:
While it is true that many colonists came to America in search of religious freedom, they also sought economic freedom. The geography and climate in America were different from what they were used to in Europe, but the colonists soon adapted. They found ways to make their environment work for them, using the land and natural resources to develop their economy.

In the New England Colonies, farms were small. They barely produced enough for the families who lived on them. Agriculture was not a big part of the economy in this region. Access to the sea did give rise to maritime trade. Fishing and whaling became profitable industries. Large forests provided lumber for shipbuilding. Sawmills were built and powered by water to cut trees into lumber. Oak and maple woods were used for ship frames, and tall white pines were perfect for the masts and planking of the ships. Cargo ships also required wooden barrels and crates for storage. Over time, the New England Colonies became an ideal place for factories to build and process goods. Boston was a major port and center of activity in this region.

With the richer soil in the Middle Colonies, more food could be produced on the land. Farms were bigger and more productive, providing grains to all of the colonies. Large mills called grist mills were needed to process the grain into goods like flour and bran. Before grist mills, grain was processed by hand with a grindstone. Grist mills used water-powered machinery to process a larger amount of grain faster and easier than older methods. The Middle Colonies were busy with trade, too. Colonists utilized the forested areas. They sold the trees for lumber. They also trapped small animals for their fur, which was in demand in Europe. Coal and iron mining boosted the economy. Ports in Philadelphia and New York City were important centers of trade and grew quickly. They attracted more than just merchants, though. All sorts of people flocked to these larger towns. During the colonial period, these same towns became influential centers of culture and thought.

In the Southern Colonies, the economy was almost entirely dependent on agriculture. Some colonists had small family farms. However, most grew cash crops during long growing seasons. These are crops grown only for their financial value, not for the farmer to use and live off of. Some of the cash crops grown in the Southern Colonies were tobacco, rice, sugarcane, and indigo (a deep purple-blue dye). While crops like tobacco and sugarcane needed to be dried or ground down, indigo required a chemical process to extract the color and make it into a marketable product. This made cash crops very labor intensive to grow and process. To make a profit, large areas of land had to be planted. This developed into a plantation system. Each plantation was a large farm. People worked on their own farms. Sometimes, they had indentured servants to help them. When the colonists realized that their plantations required more labor, enslaved people were captured from Africa and forced to work in the colonies. To trade and sell their crops, the Southern Colonies made use of their natural sea ports. Charleston, South Carolina, was a major port for the Southern Colonies.

title: Daily Life in the Early Colonies
text:
What was daily life like for the people of British Colonial America? As the colonies were getting started, daily life was very hard. People had to figure out how to survive.

Colonial farmers woke up early, ate, and started their work in the fields. The work they did depended on the season. In the spring, they would plow and plant the fields. They worked with their hands or with the help of an ox or horse. During fall, they harvested their crops. Year-round, they tended the fields, took care of livestock, chopped wood, fixed fences, and made house repairs.

Tradesmen worked long hours in villages. Depending on their trade, they had different tasks. For instance, blacksmiths spent their days making tools like axes and hammers for fellow tradesmen and average citizens. Most tradesmen trained apprentices as well.

Since there weren’t many women in the colonies, they often had more significant roles than in Europe. Without a strong and productive wife, a family would struggle to survive. Daily, women were responsible for raising their children, preparing meals, making and washing clothes, preserving food for winter, and fetching water.

Children had very little playtime. By the age of three or four, they had to get up early and work alongside their parents. Boys often helped their fathers with work on the farm as well as with hunting and fishing. Girls, on the other hand, usually helped their mothers and learned housekeeping skills.

Indentured servants worked on farms and large plantations. It was hard work to use the hoe, scythe, ax, and plow to cultivate and harvest crops. These people had very little freedom. Nearly every aspect of their lives was strictly controlled by the people who indentured them.

Enslaved African Americans were forced to work in the fields or the home of their owner. Once someone was enslaved, they were enslaved for life. They had no rights and were often mistreated.

title: American Geography and Resources
text:
Early colonists in America had to use every available resource to get what they needed to survive. American Indians had been using natural resources for centuries. What resources were available to the colonists?

New England Colonies

In the New England Colonies, the Appalachian mountain range is close to the coast. The shoreline is rocky with small beaches. The mountains are snow-capped in winter and are covered in thick forests. The soil is rocky and thin. The weather is harsh in the winters and mild in the summers. Because of the cold winters, the animals have thick furs and many birds migrate south. The ocean and streams are home to a variety of wildlife.

Middle Colonies

The Appalachian Mountains are farther from the ocean in the Middle Colonies. The soil in the meadows is fertile and deep. Where rivers flow into the ocean, there are deep, natural harbors. The mountains are lower and don't have snow-capped peaks. There are thick, dense forests, and thickets provide protection for deer, small game, and birds. Chesapeake Bay is a home for birds and sea life.

Southern Colonies

In the Southern Colonies, the Appalachian Mountains are a greater distance from the coast. The hills extend from the foot of the mountains to the coastal plain. The waterways from the mountains come to the coast and provide deep harbors. In the hills, the soil is fertile and deep. Mild winters give way to long, hot summers. The birds from the north find homes in the south during the winters. The ocean currents are warm and bring many varieties of sea life.

title: The Workforce in the Colonies
text:
As the colonial charters said, profit was necessary for the colony to survive. There was plenty of land but few workers to manage it. Over time, the introduction of new people and economic systems supplied the colonies with a stable workforce. This workforce included families, indentured servants, free men, apprentices, women, and enslaved people.

Families were often the first source of labor that the colonists had. All members of a family were expected to contribute to their homes, farms, small businesses, or a combination. Learning business, farming, or a craftsman’s trade was typically passed from father to son.

Indentured servants were men and women whose journey from England to the colonies was paid for by another person. In exchange, they signed a contract with that person that required them to work on farms or in households for a certain number of years. Protected by the law, this contract of indenture was a legal and binding agreement. Once their debt of passage (about $2,500 today) had been repaid, the contract was complete. Then, the servant was free to live and work in the colonies. Sometimes, they would receive land, money, weapons, clothes, or food upon the contract’s completion.

Free white men in America were no longer bound by the restricted social class system of England. In England, men from lower-class families had few opportunities to advance in society. In America, new laws favored ambitious men who worked and contributed to the success of the colony. These men, according to the charter, could own land. With that land, a man could become a farmer, a merchant, or join another profession. Land ownership also meant new rights and privileges, like voting, for these men.

Apprentices were another common labor source in America. Often, orphans or younger sons of large families were contracted to master craftsmen for years to learn a specific trade. These contracts were drawn up, signed before the courts, entered into a deed book, and considered binding. As part of the contract, an apprentice agreed to work for a master without pay. Masters were obligated to provide basic education (reading, writing, and arithmetic), room and board, and sometimes tools or clothes upon completion of the apprenticeship.

Enslaved people were kept in bondage and forced to work on farms and later on plantations. Enslaved people came from Africa, where they were captured and sold into slavery. Under the law, these people were considered property. They had no freedom or rights. These people were enslaved for life. Any children they had were also enslaved. When indentured servitude became unsustainable, many landowners looked to enslaved Africans as a profitable labor source.

title: A Proprietary Charter
text:
A colonial charter could be given to an individual by the monarch. This type of charter was known as a “proprietary charter.” A proprietor is an owner of property. The charter gave a person the rights to land in America. The monarch gave up all ownership or claim to the land. Being the owner of the land, the proprietor could sell or keep any parts of the colony.

The borders laid out in the charter were important because they showed the extent of the land the proprietor owned. When borders were not specific, it led to conflict between colonies.

The proprietor could also decide what type of government would lead the colony. The government had to honor the rights of Englishmen, provide representation for the people, and not go against the king. This meant that the proprietor could be the governor of the colony, or the proprietor could choose someone else to be their representative. The governor would then have a council or legislative body to advise him and report from the people. The authority of the council would depend on whether the proprietor wanted to give them authority.

Taxes in the colonies were set by the charter. In a proprietary colony, certain taxes went to the proprietor. Taxes could only be generated if the land had people. People paid taxes and produced goods and services. Many proprietary colonies gave away land to motivate people to settle and live there.

Some taxes would go to the British government. To attract people to live in America, however, the king also exempted colonists from paying taxes. This meant colonists were not taxed by the British government for a period of years.

The charter also gave the proprietor the choice of who could settle in the colony. William Penn chose to open Pennsylvania to all people, regardless of their religion. The Calverts chose to give preferential treatment to people of the Catholic faith in Maryland. The proprietor determined the businesses, products, and services in their colony.

The colonies that were established by proprietors included New York, New Hampshire, Maryland, North Carolina, New Jersey, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania.

title: A Royal Charter
text:
In a royal charter, the monarch gave themselves a colony. The charter defined the boundaries of the colony that would most benefit the monarch. Sometimes, boundaries overlapped with previous boundaries set by a previous charter. This ultimately led to conflict, which the monarch would resolve.

A royal charter defined the government structure of the colony. The colonists would have the rights of Englishmen and some form of representation to be their voice in the colony. The monarch would appoint a royal governor to be the crown’s representative in the colony. The royal governor would have the authority of the king in the colony. There would be some type of council of men who were elected by the people to give counsel to the royal governor. The royal governor did not have to heed anything the council said. The royal governor could also suspend or dissolve the representative council.

In Virginia, this council was called the House of Burgesses. In the New England Colonies, there were town meetings and town councils.

The monarch could encourage people to live in a royal colony with land giveaways, tax exemptions, and other means to populate the colony to generate goods and services. The monarch determined the religion that would be followed in the colony. As the head of the Anglican Church of England, the monarch would choose the Anglican church to be the official religion of a royal colony. At the beginning, this influenced who came to live in the colonies, but eventually, other protestant religions were tolerated.

Taxes were determined by the monarch. There were rarely individual taxes in a royal colony. The monarch wanted the taxes from the import and export of goods and services. The royal governor would appoint tax collectors and customs house officials as part of his duties.

New York and Georgia began as royal charter colonies. Eventually, the king revoked (took away) many company charters to give royal authority to the colony. This proved to be in the best interest of the monarch.

title: Consequences of the French and Indian War
text:
France

The French gave up all their land in North America east of the Mississippi River.

France retained New Orleans.

The British government promised to allow all French citizens to practice Catholicism.

French ships continued to fish off the coast of Newfoundland.

French-speaking Catholics (Acadians) were forced by the British to leave Acadia (Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Prince Edward Island); of 14,100 Acadians in the region, 11,500 were displaced.

France no longer had to pay to maintain a military presence in Canada.

Great Britain

The British gained all territory east of the Mississippi River.

The British gained Florida.

Plans to give the British government more control over the colonies were set in motion.

The military was left with little respect for the colonial militias.

Great Britain authorized a permanent army of 10,000 Regulars to stay in America to enforce the proclamation line.

Subjects were guaranteed free rights of navigation on the Mississippi River and through the port of New Orleans.

The British government was left with a large debt from war costs.

The terms of trade with the Native Americans were changed by limiting the goods available for trade.

Native Americans

The Proclamation of 1763 tried to keep colonists out of Native American lands in the Ohio Country.

The tribes who allied with the French lost a trading partner and French protection.

The tribes who allied with the British won continued British alliances.

The tribes could no longer play the French and British against each other.

The terms for trading changed now that the Native Americans could only deal with the British; the British limited available goods for trade.

Colonists

French invasion in the colonies was no longer a threat.

Colonial interests no longer aligned with British interests for the future of the colonies.

The Proclamation of 1763 prohibited expansion and settlement across the Appalachian Mountains.

The militia had little respect for the British military.

The colonists became united against a common foe and were more powerful.

The Proclamation of 1763 prohibited the colonies from issuing any more land grants; only representatives of the king could negotiate land purchases.

Britain expected the colonies to pay the debt from the war.

title: The Intolerable Acts
text:
In response to the damage of the tea cargo in Boston, Parliament created the Coercive Acts. These acts were designed by King George III to punish Massachusetts colonists for the tea party and their continued resistance to his actions and his government. Because of this, the acts also became known as the “Intolerable Acts.”

The following was directed at Massachusetts:

Boston Port Act (June 1, 1774): closed off the port of Boston, eliminating commerce and trade in the city.

Administration of Justice Act (May 20, 1774): granted a change of location to Great Britain or a British Colony in the event of a jury trial.

Massachusetts Government Act (May 20, 1774): repealed the colony’s charter and created an unprecedented amount of royal control.

Quartering Act (June 2, 1774): allowed new royal governor General Thomas Gage to house British soldiers in private homes, inns, and other buildings without permission from colonists.

Quebec Act (June 22, 1774): designated the western region north of the Ohio River as part of Quebec and allowed Catholics to practice their religion freely in Quebec; this upset colonial Protestants.

Each colonial legislature called for a meeting of representatives. This was called the First Continental Congress. Representatives gathered in Carpenters' Hall in Philadelphia on Sept. 5, 1774. Twelve of the 13 colonies sent delegates.

The first order of business was to write a petition to King George to remove the recent Acts applied to Massachusetts. Each colony had protested the Tea Act in some manner, but Massachusetts was receiving the punishment. The delegates at the congress knew the king could do the same to each of their colonies at any time.

The delegates continued to prepare. They agreed that if the offending Acts of Parliament were not repealed, the colonies would boycott British goods. The congress also recommended that each colony continue to defy Parliament and the king. They also recommended that each colony prepare a militia of Patriots and to begin gathering supplies for them.

The delegates of the congress sent their petition to King George through Benjamin Franklin, who was in London as an agent for the Pennsylvania colony.

At the end of the congressional session in October 1774, the members agreed to meet in a second continental congress the following May, in 1775.

title: All About Measurement?
text: When you measure something, you use numbers to show its size or amount. You can measure length. You can measure weight. You can measure how hot or cold it is. Scientists and engineers measure. It helps them be accurate.

title: Customary System of Measurement
text: The United States uses the customary system of measurement. It can also be called the U.S. standard of measurement. Length is measured in inches, feet, yards, and miles. Weight is measured in ounces and pounds. Volume is measured in cups, pints, quarts, and gallons. To measure temperature, it uses degrees Fahrenheit.

title: Metric System of Measurement
text: Most of the world measures using the metric system. The metric system is used in science. The metric system uses meters to measure length. It uses grams to measure weight and liters to measure volume. To measure temperature, it uses degrees Celsius.

title: Measuring Length
text: Rulers measure length. Metric rulers and metersticks use centimeters (the numbers). The numbers between the lines are millimeters. Many rulers use one end as "zero." Other rulers start at zero, a little ways from the end. Look for zero on the ruler you are using. If there is no zero, the end of the ruler is zero. Lay the ruler so that zero is at one end of what you are measuring. Read the line nearest the end of the object. Readings can be in centimeters (cm) or millimeters (mm). It all depends on what is being asked.

title: Measuring Length Activity
text: Choose an object to measure. First, measure the object in centimeters. Second, measure the object in inches. Record your data.

title: Measure and Graph
text:
Scientists and engineers like to be as accurate as possible. Sometimes it is not necessary. You can use a measuring skill called estimating. When you estimate, you make a guess based on the information you have about something. Estimating needs previous knowledge. Estimating is used when you don’t need to know exactly how many, just about how many.

Use rulers and a meterstick to measure different items in inches, meters, and feet. First, guess what you think the length will be. Write down your guess. Then, write down the actual measured length.

title: Graphs
text: A graph is a type of picture that shows organized data. Scientists and engineers create graphs. Graphs help them better understand their data. There are many types of graphs. The most common are bar graphs, line graphs, and pictographs. Bar graphs organize data into bars. They help scientists compare data. Graphs support scientists’ conclusions. Graphs help others clearly see the results of their investigation. Measure the following objects in centimeters. Then, draw a bar graph of the data.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text:
Thomas Jefferson was born in Virginia in 1743. He became a leader in the colonial government at age 25.

In 1776, Jefferson became a member of the Continental Congress. This is the group that was organized to write the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson was chosen to write the declaration that was sent to the king of England. It told the king that the 13 Colonies wanted to break away from England.

After the Revolutionary War, Jefferson served as a minister to France. He was elected president of the United States in 1800. Jefferson was very familiar with the French because of the time he had spent in France. This helped him make a deal to buy territory that France owned and expand the United States.

Jefferson is remembered as a talented writer and statesman. He was the third president of the United States. He was one of the Founders of our nation.

title: The Louisiana Purchase
text: In 1801, the United States didn't look like it does today. It was much smaller. The Mississippi River was the western border of our country. Spain controlled Florida and much of the Southwest. France claimed the land west of the Mississippi River. Settlers shipped supplies and goods up and down the Mississippi River to the port of New Orleans. President Jefferson thought it would be dangerous for another country to control this important shipping route. Instead of trying to take it by force, Jefferson asked France to sell the land. In 1803, France made a deal to sell the United States even more land than Jefferson had originally asked for. The United States paid $15 million for the land. This sale is called the Louisiana Purchase. The purchase doubled the size of our country. The new territory stretched from the Mississippi River all the way to the Rocky Mountains.

title: Lewis and Clark
text: Before the Louisiana Purchase happened, President Jefferson had already planned to send a group to explore the western frontier. He chose his secretary, Meriwether Lewis, to lead the group. Lewis chose William Clark as his co-captain. Lewis and Clark had served in the military together. About 40 other men joined Lewis and Clark. Their group was called the Corps of Discovery. Their expedition became known as the Lewis and Clark Expedition. President Jefferson instructed Lewis and Clark to explore the land. Jefferson told them to draw maps, study the plants and animals, and observe the Indigenous cultures living in the area. Jefferson also told them to look for new travel routes and existing trading posts or settlements.

title: The Expedition
text:
In May 1804, the Corps of Discovery began their journey. They took glass beads, mirrors, and cloth to trade with the Indigenous people they met. The first winter of their exploration wasn't easy. Some members of their group had diseases or injuries. It was very cold. There was little to eat, and the men were afraid they would die. However, they survived the winter, and the expedition reached the Pacific coast. They stayed there for the second winter. Then, they returned home to share their findings. They brought journals, sketches, and maps of their journey. They recorded information about 300 new kinds of plants and animals.

After returning to Missouri, the men were treated as heroes. The expedition was very important. It helped settlers learn about the new land and the people who lived there. They now had maps that would make traveling through the Louisiana Territory easier. Settlers could now move even farther west. The expedition wasn't good news for everyone. Indigenous people had already been pushed west by the settlers. Now even more were forced to move off the land. They had to live on reservations. Reservations are areas of land set aside by the U.S. government for Indigenous communities to live in.

title: Phenomenon Explanation
text:
Collisions

Did you know that collisions are happening around you all the time? Some collisions are less noticeable than others. Right now, you may have a pencil in your hand. Are you tapping your pencil? That’s a collision! When you write on paper with your pencil, that’s a collision too: your pencil collides with the paper. When you get up and push your chair in, your feet will collide with the floor, and your chair may collide with the desk.

Other collisions are more noticeable because they involve more energy. For example, one collision that may catch your attention is a door being slammed shut. This collision can cause a loud noise. It can also cause the door frame to shake or the door to bounce back open.

Any time two objects collide, energy is transferred. How much energy is transferred depends on how much speed an object had before the collision. Objects with greater speeds have more energy due to motion and therefore will transfer more energy during a collision.

The moment two objects collide, or come into contact with each other, the transfer of energy between them causes the speed and direction of each object to change. Some energy will also transfer to the air, causing sound and heat to be produced.

Look around you. When and where do you see objects changing direction or speed? When and where are sounds made? These could be indicators that a collision has just occurred!

Think about your daily life. What are some collisions that you cause or see happening during a normal day? List 2-3 daily collisions.

title: Tribes of the Southwest
text:
The landscape of the Southwest varies between deserts, valleys, plateaus, and coastal areas. Tribes such as the Apache, Pueblo, Navajo, and Hopi lived in this area. These tribes found different ways to use the resources of their environment. People on the coast fished for food. People who lived in the plateau areas were skilled in using acorns for food. They hunted for antelope, rabbits, and deer.

Many tribes in this region lived in homes built of dried clay called adobe. Adobe is a mixture of straw, water, and clay baked into hard bricks. Some tribes built adobe homes into the rock cliffs in the area. Other tribes built hogans made of wood and packed dirt. Like other tribes across the continent, these tribes utilized the resources around them to build their homes.

The tribes of the Southwest also farmed the land. Water can be a scarce resource in the Southwest. Southwest tribes were very resourceful and found ways to irrigate farmland. They gathered water from rivers and underground water sources to grow crops. They grew many crops, like corn, pumpkins, beans, squash, melons, and other types of fruit. After contact with the Europeans, some tribes raised cattle, sheep, and horses. One example of a tribe that raised livestock is the Hopi of Arizona.

title: Tribes of the Midwest
text:
Peoples of the Midwest lived on grasslands called plains. The plains of North America are ideal for farming and hunting animals that graze for food. These tribes utilized large areas to hunt. They often moved with the animals they hunted. The main source of food and materials for these tribes was bison. They used every part of the bison to meet their needs. Bison skin was used in tepees, clothing, containers, and blankets. Bison dung was used as fuel for fires. These tribes lived in tepees because they could be packed up and moved easily.

Many tribes inhabited this region long before Europeans, including the Wichita and the Caddo. These tribes also farmed the land. They traditionally grew corn, pumpkins, beans, and squash. They also hunted deer, antelope, and bears. Some tribes lived in more permanent villages. These villages had homes that couldn't be transported like the tepee could.

title: Tribes of the Northwest
text:
Northwest peoples lived in a land full of plants, fish, and wild animals. Tribes such as the Tlingit, Haida, and Puyallup had very distinct cultures. They ate bear, elk, and deer. They fished in the rivers for salmon and captured whales and sea lions from the ocean. People used the land and resources around them to build their homes. Clothing was made from local materials, like woven grass and animal skins.

Tribes of the Northwest, like the Suquamish people, lived in shelters called longhouses during the fall and winter. During the spring and summer, they lived in portable shelters similar to teepees and wigwams. The homes were especially useful when hunting game because they could be set up and taken down quickly. The tribes traveled frequently throughout the year, harvesting and securing food.

They were very skilled at using natural resources to meet their needs. The ocean, mountains, and land all are part of the history and traditions of these tribes. A unique tradition of the Northwest tribes is the building of totem poles. Totem poles help tell the tribes’ histories and stories.

title: Arctic Tribes
text:
Arctic tribes lived in parts of northern Canada, Alaska, and Greenland. The Inuit, Yuit, and Aleut are examples of Arctic tribes. The land of the Arctic and Subarctic regions remains frozen most of the year.

In the Arctic, food was not available in large amounts year-round. The Native Peoples who lived in this region had a very special understanding of how to get food in such a unique area. They traveled great distances to hunt animals like seals and caribou. They were also experts at fishing. Plants are not as abundant in the Arctic, but they do exist. Many tribal people gathered when a large animal, like a whale, was caught. They used all parts of the whale and its resources. When food was scarce, communities would organize into small units.

In similar ways to other tribes, Arctic tribes used pelts for their clothes. This kept them warm in the cold climate. Seal hides were very valuable because they were waterproof.

Many Arctic tribes, like the Inuit, used dogs for transportation. For fishing, however, they made wood-carved kayaks. They also traveled on sleds and toboggans. The Arctic tribes adapted to their environment. They used the natural resources for survival and trade. They thrived in all seasons.

title: Can You Persuade Me?
text:
Persuading a person to change their thinking is not an easy task. We need evidence and facts to support the claim we are trying to make. This is why it's so important to look at as much evidence as we can and ask good questions. There are many ways to persuade an audience.

Two common ways are persuading with reason or with emotion. Either way, the goal is to create a call to action for people to help us change a problem using your solution. A call to action means getting people to act in a way that we need them to so a problem can be solved.

Reason

“Just the facts, please” is a phrase we might often hear. It relates to facts the reader should know when it comes to understanding a problem we're trying to solve. A writer needs to give reasons and present the facts when writing to persuade readers. This is known as persuasion through reason. Reason means to use evidence to change someone’s mind and call them to action. Think about how you will use facts to persuade your audience.

Emotion

This form of persuasion relies on how you feel about a problem or letting someone else know how it affects you personally. This reaches out to a person’s empathy to persuade them to change their mind. Remember, empathy is connecting with another person's thoughts and feelings. These emotions could show how a problem makes you or someone else feel. Will you persuade your audience through emotion or through reason?

The complexity of your problem will help you decide what the best way is to persuade your audience and support your claim. No matter how you persuade your audience, it's still important to consider all the evidence. That way, your claim is supported with facts and evidence.
