title: Geneticists Then and Now
text:
The Father of Genetics

Gregor Mendel lived from 1822 to 1884. Mendel was passionate about learning and science. Mendel joined the Augustinian Abbey of St. Thomas, in Austria. This monastery was a center for new ideas and discoveries. While there, Mendel taught science. He also did research. Mendel’s great addition to the scientific world began in 1856 with his study of garden peas. Mendel studied how traits of peas were influenced by the mixture of different plants. He was the first scientist to discover that the traits of an offspring are influenced by its parents.

Dog Genetics

Takeshi Kawakami lived from 1925 to 2009. He was a senior research scientist at Embark Veterinary. Embark is a dog genetics company. They use samples of dog DNA to predict a dog’s size and appearance. They also test risks of disease based on a dog’s DNA. Kawakami was passionate about his work. He said, “It is fun to see a great variety of dog breeds with different colors and sizes. Unfortunately, some breeds are suffering from various diseases. These include blindness, deafness, and joint problems. Genetics offers a powerful tool to prevent those diseases. Genetics inform breeders which pairs of dogs can have an increased risk of genetic diseases. It is a great feeling that my research can help society and improve a dog’s life.”

title: Analyzing and Comparing Primary Sources
text:
When you have analyzed your sources, it is time to evaluate them. To evaluate means to determine which information is most useful to you. To begin this process, you should review all of the information you gathered from your research. This information is your evidence. Evidence is information or data that supports an argument. It is important to use evidence when you make a claim. Remember, a claim is a statement you make about what you believe. Claims must be supported with evidence.

Evidence from your sources should be ranked by which pieces are most helpful in supporting your claim. Once your evidence is organized, you can use corroboration. Corroboration means finding evidence from multiple sources to support your claim. In order to find evidence from multiple sources, you must compare and contrast evidence.

Comparing is examining two or more events, people, places, or ideas to identify how they are the same. Contrasting is examining events, people, places, or ideas to see how they are different. Historians often compare and contrast multiple sources.

Historians also compare and contrast multiple perspectives of the same event. Being able to compare and contrast historical events allows historians to compare and contrast past events to current events. This can deepen their understanding of history. It can also provide a more accurate view of history.

title: Patrick Henry
text:
Patrick Henry was a member of the Virginia House of Burgesses. Henry was known for his passion for liberty and his fiery speaking style.

On March 23, 1775, he met with his fellow legislators, saying:

They tell us, sir, that we are weak; unable to cope with so formidable an adversary [the British Army]. But when shall we be stronger? Will it be the next week, or the next year? Will it be when we are totally disarmed, and when a British guard shall be stationed in every house? … The battle, sir, is not to the strong alone; it is to the vigilant, the active, the brave.

He concluded with a statement that has lived on for 250 years: “I know not what course others may take; but as for me, give me liberty or give me death!”

title: Types of Economic Systems
text: An economic system is the way communities and governments organize resources, goods, and services. Resources, goods, and services are then given to the people. Governments often determine the type of economic system a country uses. There are many types of economic systems people around the world use. However, most people use one of three types of economic systems. These three types are traditional, command, and market economies. Each system shares the same basic features. However, each one has specific characteristics that separate it from the others.

title: Traditional Economy
text:
Some nations manage goods and services through a traditional economy. Traditional economies are the oldest economic systems in place. They reflect a community's or nation's cultural heritage and beliefs. In a traditional economic system, land is inherited. People use or trade what they produce themselves. Instead of using money, people trade goods and services for other goods and services.

There are countries that still function with a traditional economy. Many of these countries have large areas of rural land. They rely heavily on farming and agriculture to meet the needs of citizens. Though some traditional economies still exist, most countries have replaced them with other economic systems.

title: Command Economy
text:
In some countries, the government controls economic activity. Such activity includes labor, resources, prices, and distribution of goods and services. This system is called a command economy. The government determines what will be produced. It also determines how much products will cost and who will receive resources and products.

The idea of a command system is for the government to ensure the needs of all citizens are met. Command economies are often seen with governments that control the freedom and liberty of the citizens. Command economies are often seen in countries with many valuable resources. These could be resources like minerals and oil.

title: Market Economy
text:
In a market economy, the government does not have direct control of resources. This prevents the government from becoming too powerful and claiming total control over the economy. Regulations and economic rules are created by the people. They decide what to produce. They can decide how much to produce. They also decide the price of their products and where to sell them. Supply and demand plays a large part in the decisions made in a market economy.

Market economies encourage economic incentives. An economic incentive is something that is offered to people to help them make a decision about goods and services. Economic incentives can be positive or negative. Positive economic incentives reward people for buying from a certain company. An example is when grocery stores offer "buy one, get one free" deals, coupons, or discounts. Stores do this because they want more people to come in and spend money at their store. The customer's positive economic incentive is saving money. Negative economic incentives are used to encourage people to do something or act in a certain way. However, these incentives cost money. For example, if you return a book to the library after the due date, you're required to pay a late fee. The late fee is the negative economic incentive.

In a market economy, governments cannot regulate fair trade or create laws to protect the economy. This can create a large imbalance of wealth between citizens. No countries in the world have a true market economy. Most economies are a mixture between a market economy and a command economy. The U.S. economy has many market economy characteristics. But even in the United States, the government has some control over goods and services.

title: Free Market
text:
The free market system is an important aspect of a market economy. Free market systems only work if a country's laws and its citizens' values support them. If this type of market doesn't exist, the system will fail. Six characteristics of a free market system make it successful. These are private property, specialization, voluntary exchange, price system, market competition, and entrepreneurship.

Private property is the first fundamental component in a free market system. It influences everyone to care for the things we own. Private property also provides us with incentive. Incentive is what motivates us to make the decisions we make. If a business doesn't take care of its office building or breaks equipment, it must pay to replace them. This gives the business incentive to care for things it uses.

Specialization means businesses focus on creating certain types of products or providing specific services. This allows companies to become experts in their field. They can also produce more goods over time. Companies that specialize in one or many products are able to save money on goods and resources. They can provide higher wages to their employees.

Voluntary exchange is another important element of free market systems. Voluntary exchange means people must exchange goods or currency to acquire resources they need. Consumers have the choice to purchase goods and services. It's not forced upon them by businesses or government regulations.

Creating a price system is crucial for a free market economy's success. Prices provide guidance for producers and consumers. Prices show the market how much customers value the producer's goods. They also provide clues for economists about whether a market is healthy or not. Prices also provide incentives for businesses and consumers. Most consumers try to shop for bargains if prices rise. This keeps businesses from overcharging their customers.

A free market system must have competition within the market to work properly. Competition between producers lowers product prices and creates more options for consumers. It can also make resources and products more valuable.

A free market economy's final characteristic is entrepreneurship. Entrepreneurship is the act of developing, organizing, and managing a new business. Entrepreneurs are people who create and run businesses. They must be able to adapt to changing markets and meet customer demands.

title: Capitalism
text: Capitalism is very similar to a market economy. Capitalism is an economic system where businesses are owned by private companies or people. Companies or people also control resources and the means of production. Capitalism's focus is for businesses to make the most profit possible. In capitalism, the market determines which businesses are successful and make a profit. Under capitalism, businesses must compete with one another for consumers. This gives consumers access to a wider variety of products. Buyers, sellers, consumers, and producers must work together. Doing this makes a capitalistic system successful.

title: United States System of Economics
text:
The United States is considered a free market system. A free market system is an economy where the government places few restrictions on businesses. This results in companies competing to earn customers, which leads to lower prices and better products. In the United States, the individual is the most important resource. Individuals consume, or use, the products. Individuals are the workers who produce, or make, the goods. Labor is done by people who then get paid a wage. That money is used to purchase goods and services. In the United States, businesses can set their own prices and determine what goods and services they wish to sell.

The United States’ economy is also made up of private businesses. Business owners produce goods or services to make a profit. Larger businesses often allow people to purchase part of the business by buying stocks, or a share in the business. This makes the person a stockholder. This means they own part of the company.

Another important part of a free enterprise system is banking, which is regulated by the government. Many individuals have checking accounts they use to pay for goods and services. Many individuals also have savings accounts, where they can earn interest on the money they set aside. They can then make larger purchases or save for retirement.

title: Young Entrepreneurs
text:
You don’t have to be an adult to start a business. People as young as five years old have become entrepreneurs by starting their own businesses. Some businesses have grown and become successful.

Take child-entrepreneur Hannah Grace. Grace was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes when she was just a baby. At the age of 10, she started making her own health and beauty products to sell. She created a business called Hannah Grace BeYOUtiful and donates 20 percent of every purchase to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Fund.

Maya Penn founded her business, Maya’s Ideas, when she was just eight years old. Today, Penn is 19 and CEO of her own company, which sells fashion accessories that are environmentally sustainable. Not only does she run her own business, but Penn also donates 10 percent of her profits to charities and to help the environment.

When he was nine years old, Moziah Bridges wanted an eye-catching fashion accessory. Because of this, he got the idea to create Mo’s Bows. Bridges’s company sells all kinds of things, including bow ties, pocket squares, and other apparel. Today, despite his company’s international success, Bridges intends to graduate high school and continue his education by going to college to study fashion design.

Nohbo Drops were created by Benjamin Stern. Stern came up with the idea while he was sitting in his ninth grade biology class. Nohbo Drops are packets for shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and shaving cream that dissolve in water. They don’t contain chemicals that harm the environment, and they help to eliminate plastic waste.

These young people didn’t find success overnight. Their businesses started with an idea. They worked and improved their ideas until they were able to create businesses out of them. Hannah Grace had to try over and over to find a successful recipe for her bath bombs and beauty products. Moziah Bridges started out with an eye-catching bowtie and worked to design and create other accessories. Entrepreneurs work hard, often for years, before their businesses take off. Some businesses don’t make it, but with a good idea, hard work, and dedication, anything is possible.

title: Language
text:
Language is another important part of culture. Today, more than 7,000 languages are spoken around the world. Some languages are spoken within a very small area. Others are spoken by large numbers of people in the world. The most commonly spoken languages in the United States after English include Spanish, Chinese, and many others.

Most people have a primary language they speak. We call this their native language. This is the first language they learned. They can speak it fluently. Some people learn a second or even third language in addition to their native language. When people learn another language, they also learn about the culture it represents.

As people move from place to place, they bring their culture and their languages with them. Multiple languages can be represented in one area. Many streets, cities, towns, and states in the United States take their names from other languages. This brings together cultures from around the world in one place. The movement of languages continues to impact culture today.

They make sure everyone is following the rules. They make sure drivers are obeying traffic laws. Many police departments visit schools. They teach students how to stay away from drugs and crime.

title: Citizenship
text: Governments can only work well when citizens are responsible. Citizens of the United States have rights and responsibilities. Rights are freedoms that every person has. Responsibilities are things people are expected to do. Citizens have the responsibility to behave in certain ways. Responsible citizens actively participate in their communities.

title: Rights of Citizens
text: Rights are freedoms every person has. Important documents outline and protect rights. Citizens of the United States have the right to “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.” This means you have the right to think and speak freely. You can help make decisions in your community, state, and country. You have the freedom to do the things that make you happy.

title: Responsibilities of Citizens
text: Responsibilities are things we are expected to do. Responsible citizens show respect for people and property. They get involved in making their communities better. Responsible citizens participate in local government. They learn about what is going on. They also interact with elected officials.

title: Traits of Responsible Citizens
text: Responsible citizens are honest and trustworthy. They treat everyone equally. They respect the rights and property of others. Responsible citizens are fair and treat others kindly. They volunteer and work together for the common good.

title: Active Participation
text: Citizens can make a difference when they actively participate in their communities. Many citizens volunteer and serve their communities. They stand up for each other. They stay informed about what is happening. They share their opinions. Adult citizens vote for officials who they believe will help their communities.

title: Becoming a United States Citizen
text: There are many paths to United States citizenship. If you are born in the United States, you are a citizen. People who are born outside of the United States can apply for citizenship. This process can take a long time and cost money. New citizens have to know what citizenship means.

title: Being a Responsible Citizen Now!
text: You belong to many communities. You are a citizen in your classroom. You are also a citizen in your school and local communities. As a citizen, you can express your opinions respectfully. Your suggestions can improve both your school and your community. You can vote when making classroom decisions. As a citizen of a classroom, you can collaborate with others. You can participate in classroom activities as well.

title: Taking Action
text:
Let’s Discuss:

Many of the issues you read about in the previous activity take place on a global scale. They can seem overwhelming when people consider the question “What can we do to help?” Many communities are taking action to help resolve the plastic waste problem.

Why do you think solutions created within small communities can still help solve the worldwide plastic problem?

Reading Strategies:

Underline the problem.

Circle the solution.

Star the scientific ideas that each community uses to help protect their environment and resources.

In the time given, read as many articles as you can. As you read, use the reading strategies to annotate the articles. Then, answer the questions that follow.

Ocean Day in Huntington Beach

For locals, Huntington Beach, California, is a favorite place for summer activities. However, the area also suffers from major plastic pollution.

This community recognizes that pollution in their area can harm ocean environments. Local elementary school students choose to help. They want to make a measurable difference to reduce plastic pollution on their beaches. Each year, on Ocean Day, they work to do just that.

Students from almost 600 elementary schools in Orange County spend a day picking up plastic and other waste from the beach. In 2022, they picked up more than 115 pounds of trash on Huntington State Beach! Ocean Day inspires students to be more careful with the plastic they use. They learn that they can make a difference with small actions every day.

Sabin Elementary School Activists

Three fifth graders in Portland, Oregon, have taken action to educate their community about plastic waste. It all began with an exhibition project at Sabin Elementary School. Louisa Andersen, Heidi Kirshman, and Louisa Brown learned a sad truth: Eight million tons of plastic end up in the ocean each year. They decided to share the grim facts about plastic pollution in the ocean with a larger audience.

Their project prompted people to think about the issues created by plastic waste. It asked: What can we do to fix the causes of these issues? They said that people can cut down on plastic use by buying larger containers of food instead of purchasing individual packages. The students also provided information about organizations dedicated to cleaning up the oceans. They encouraged people to donate to these organizations.

Cash Daniels

As a child, Cash Daniels made a shocking discovery: The river near his home in Chattanooga, Tennessee, was full of garbage! There were discarded toys, cassette tapes, and much, much more. He decided to find out whether just one person, like him, could make a difference.

Plastic pollution in water sources, like Cash’s river, can contaminate drinking water and nearby ecosystems. Cash wondered how much trash he could collect in only several hours a week. For one whole year, he and his friends cleaned up nearly 1,000 cans each week. But Cash’s group set their sights on even bigger numbers. They asked other kids around the globe to join them to pick up one million pounds of trash by the end of 2022!

A Times Kid of the Year finalist in 2021, Cash is an example to kids everywhere. He hopes that sharing his mission will help people think twice before littering. He believes kids are the future of conservation. He said, "Kids may be a small part of the population, but we are 100 percent of the future and we can change the world!"

New Use for Plastic Across the Globe

There are huge amounts of recyclable plastics being made around the world. However, only a fraction of them actually end up recycled. So, people started asking themselves: How can I reduce, reuse, and recycle? Through their personal curiosity and innovation, many new uses for plastic waste have been discovered.

Nzambi Matee is an engineer and biochemist in Kenya. She founded a company that mixes plastic waste with sand to create lightweight bricks. These bricks are even stronger than concrete. In India, Monisha Narke created a program to turn plastic and paper cartons into furniture. Their benches, desks, and chairs are donated to local schools. The program also works to educate and inspire kids to decrease their plastic use. In Uganda, most plastic waste ends up in gutters. Faith Aweko, a founder of “Reform Africa,” employs local women to create sellable goods out of plastic bags. They collect about 661 pounds of bags each month. The bags are washed and dried, then processed into leather-like material. This material is sewn into reusable backpacks, shopping bags, and more.

Every new idea for reusing plastic waste contributes to reducing plastic pollution worldwide.

Local Law Changes

The biggest source of global plastic pollution is single-use plastics: grocery bags, bottles, straws, silverware, and more. People across the United States are trying to reduce this litter. In 2011, officials in San Jose, California, created an ordinance, or local law, that banned single-use plastic bags. Pharmacies, grocery stores, and other retailers were all required to stop handing them out. If they violated this law, they could be fined up to $1,000. A year later, surveys showed that bag litter was reduced by 89 percent in storm drains; 60 percent in creeks and rivers; and 59 percent in city streets and neighborhoods. Community members can always reach out to their local officials to change or create laws that help protect the Earth and its resources.

title: Engineering Problem: Community Pollution
text:
Types of Pollution

How many different types of pollution do you know about? Trash left in open or public places, or litter, is one of the most common forms of pollution. But even when people throw away their waste properly, it can pollute the land. Land pollution occurs when huge amounts of solid materials, like paper, plastic, food, etc., are thrown away and landfills are needed to store the waste. Another type of pollution is air pollution. It is produced mainly when fossil fuels are burned, by power plants and cars, for example. Other types of pollution include water pollution, plastic pollution, noise pollution, and even light pollution. Factories, farming, construction, and other parts of everyday human life have had large impacts across all of Earth’s systems. But with the help of science, local communities can take steps to reduce pollution. Sometimes this starts just by identifying the cause and effect of pollutants. Pollutants are harmful substances that pollute the Earth. What pollutants do you see in your town?

Engineering Scenario: Local communities can use science ideas to protect the Earth’s resources and environment. Create a solution to reduce pollution in your community.

title: Conducting Research
text:
Addressing the Plastic Problem

How does pollution affect your daily life? The effects may be hard to see. Long ago, people didn’t have cars, factories, plastic, or even electricity. But as humans evolved, so have their needs. With more people on Earth comes the need for increased food production, access to clean drinking water, housing, jobs, and more. All of these needs raise the demand for newer and better technology and materials. And these innovations have come — but at a heavy price. In everyday life, the amount of waste from packaging, electricity and air conditioning, new clothes, and devices has increased drastically.

Tackling the harmful effects that humans have on the planet is in everyone’s best interest. Preserving Earth’s environments and resources ensures that the world is a healthy, beautiful place to live. Scientists and engineers work hard to come up with solutions to the problems created by humans. For example, technologies designed to harness energy from renewable resources have improved and are continuing to advance. This reduces the burning of fossil fuels that contributes to air pollution. Other technologies, like scrubbers, have been developed to remove pollutants from the air.

Small communities don’t have labs and large amounts of money to build advanced technology. Instead, to combat the harmful effects of pollution, they can practice the Three Rs: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. They can also do community cleanups, prevent pollution before it happens by educating and informing the public, and, finally, work to pass laws to control behaviors that contribute to pollution.

title: Symbols and Values
text: Patriotic symbols remind us about the love we feel for the United States of America. These symbols represent important values, like freedom and justice. Our customs and celebrations also reflect our values. They remind us what it means to be an American.

title: The Bald Eagle
text: The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States. The nation’s founders chose the bald eagle. It is on the Great Seal of the United States. The bald eagle is a symbol of dignity and strength.

title: The Statue of Liberty
text: The Statue of Liberty is a symbol of freedom. It reminds us of our American beliefs. The Statue of Liberty was given to the United States by France. It represents hope for people who are seeking a better life in America.

title: The Rose
text: The rose is our national flower. Our lawmakers decided this in 1986. President Ronald Reagan announced the decision in a special ceremony. It was at the White House Rose Garden. President Reagan said the rose symbolizes life, love, and devotion. He also said it symbolizes beauty and eternity.

title: Uncle Sam
text: Uncle Sam is not a real person. Uncle Sam is a patriotic symbol. The image of Uncle Sam began as a poster. The poster was designed to make people want to serve their country. Uncle Sam reminds us to be patriotic and actively participate in government. The red, white, and blue colors of the poster remind us of the American flag.

title: The Liberty Bell
text:
The Liberty Bell is a symbol. It represents American independence and freedom. It first rang in the tower of Independence Hall. The words “Proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof” are written on the bell.

The first name of the Liberty Bell was the State House Bell. The bell was first cast in London, England. Then it was shipped to Philadelphia. The first time it was rung, it cracked. The broken bell was melted down and remade again. This happened two more times. The third time it cracked was when they rang the bell for George Washington’s birthday.

title: The Turkey
text:
The turkey is a large bird that is native to North America. Some people believe that the turkey got its name from the "turk turk" sound it makes when it is startled.

In the United States, millions of turkeys are eaten each year at Thanksgiving. Many of these turkeys come from farms. Turkeys also live in the wild. Wild turkeys live in the woods. They can be found in many parts of the United States.

Most turkeys raised on farms cannot fly. Wild turkeys can fly short distances. They can fly at speeds of up to 55 miles per hour. Turkeys have a great sense of hearing. They also have an excellent sense of taste and great vision. However, they have a terrible sense of smell. They also have a loud voice! A turkey's gobble can be heard up to a mile away. Turkeys eat insects, seeds, plants, and fruit.

Benjamin Franklin believed the turkey should be the national symbol of the United States. Franklin said the turkey was an intelligent and noble bird. He felt that the bald eagle should not be the choice. Bald eagles are scavengers. Scavengers eat animals that are already dead. He said that although the turkey was "vain and silly," it was better than the "cowardly" bald eagle. Obviously, not everyone agreed. The bald eagle stands proudly as a symbol of the United States today.

title: History of the Statue of Liberty
text:
The Statue of Liberty is on Liberty Island in New York Harbor. It was a gift from France. The statue was made in France and completed in July 1884. Then it was disassembled, packed in large crates, and shipped to New York. It arrived in June 1885. The pedestal, or base, of the statue was made and paid for by Americans. It was completed in April 1886. The Statue of Liberty was finally dedicated on October 28, 1886.

The Statue of Liberty is now a well-known landmark for the United States. It has become one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world. It is a symbol of freedom, inspiration, and hope.

title: Founders
text: The Founders were people who loved the country. They were responsible citizens. The Founders worked together to build a new nation. They were the first leaders of the United States. The Founders believed in American principles. They believed in freedom, equality, and justice for all. The Founders helped make the United States a free country.

title: George Washington
text: George Washington was an active member of his community and nation. He was a general in the army. He was involved in writing the Constitution. George Washington felt that the Constitution was so important that he was willing to sign it. George Washington became our first president.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text: Thomas Jefferson was a man who loved books. He believed that education was for everyone. He enjoyed studying science. Thomas Jefferson is the author of the Declaration of Independence. Thomas Jefferson was our third president.

title: John Hancock
text: John Hancock was one of the signers of the Declaration of Independence. His signature is the largest on the document. John Hancock helped to create the Navy. He was the president of the Continental Congress. He helped the authors of the Declaration of Independence. Together, they made good decisions about the words in the Declaration of Independence.

title: John Adams
text: John Adams went to college. He became a lawyer. John Adams helped Thomas Jefferson write the Declaration of Independence. His signature is on the Declaration of Independence. John Adams was George Washington’s vice president. John Adams was the second president of the United States.

title: Benjamin Franklin
text: Benjamin Franklin was one of our Founders. Benjamin Franklin was a scientist and inventor. He was also a politician, journalist, and businessman. Benjamin Franklin owned a newspaper company. He helped spread information. Benjamin Franklin is known for helping with the writing of the Declaration of Independence. He also helped with the drafting of the Constitution. Benjamin Franklin brought consensus and compromise during their meetings. He signed both of these important documents.

title: James Madison
text: James Madison was our fourth president. He was known as the “Father of the Constitution.” Many of the ideas in the Constitution came from him. James Madison believed that citizens have both rights and responsibilities. Our rights and responsibilities are defined and protected in the Constitution.

title: Alexander Hamilton
text: Alexander Hamilton and George Washington were good friends. Hamilton was Washington's right-hand man in the Revolutionary War. Alexander Hamilton worked hard for the Constitution to become law. Alexander Hamilton signed the Constitution. He wrote articles that were published in Benjamin Franklin's newspapers. Alexander Hamilton became the first secretary of the U.S. Treasury. His picture is on our $10 bill.

title: Essential Question
text: Who were the Founders? Why are they important?

title: Essential Question
text: What is the meaning behind our national symbols?

Georgia is a unique state. From the Blue Ridge Mountains to the Barrier Islands, the land we know today as Georgia supports diverse plants and animals. For thousands of years, many different American Indian cultures and civilizations have called this land home. These groups explored Georgia’s landscape and learned to use the land and its features to their advantage. From navigating rivers to blazing trails through mountain ridges, American Indians created vibrant and diverse cultures. As explorers from Europe came to Georgia’s shores, they quickly found that this was a promising place to settle. The biggest benefit of solar ovens is that they cook food by using only energy from light. Solar ovens have other benefits too. They are simple, efficient, and portable. title: The United States Government
text:
The government of the United States is a constitutional republic. This form of government is based on a written constitution. The Constitution determines the power and functions of the government. Adult citizens vote for people to represent them in the government. The officials make decisions according to the law of the land. The Constitution is the law of the land for the United States. In a republic, people agree to abide by the decisions of their representatives. This agreement is called consent of the governed. At every level, people’s consent is what gives the government power to act. The idea that the American people give the U.S. government its powers comes from the Declaration of Independence.

The United States uses a federal system. In a federal system, national and state governments divide the responsibilities. Each government is responsible for different things. Tribal nations have their own governments. There are also local governments that lead the counties, cities, and towns. There are representatives at all levels of government. The national government and the U.S. Constitution serve as a model for state governments and constitutions throughout our country.

title: Three Branches of Government
text:
Executive Branch

The executive branch enforces our country’s laws. It is also in charge of the military. The head of the executive branch is the president of the United States. The president is chosen by voters. The president and vice president are elected together for four years. They may serve up to two terms for a total of eight years. The president creates a group of advisors called a cabinet. Cabinet members are often experts in their fields. They help run the executive branch by leading departments. For example, the Department of Defense is in charge of the military. The president has veto power. A veto means saying “no” to a bill. A bill is a plan for a law.

Legislative Branch

The legislative branch makes laws and sets taxes. Congress is the legislative branch of our national government. It is divided into two parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives. Two senators are elected from each state. A state's number of representatives depends on how many people live there. Larger states send more representatives. Smaller states send fewer. Today, there are 100 senators in the Senate and 435 representatives in the House. All of them were elected by the people of their states. The legislative branch also approves how tax money is spent. They vote on which programs and projects the government can spend money on.

Judicial Branch

The judicial branch interprets the laws, or decides what laws mean. It also determines whether laws follow the Constitution. The judicial branch is made up of judges and courts. The Supreme Court is the highest court in the land. The Supreme Court is made up of leaders called justices. They are chosen by the president and approved by senators. They work in the Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.

title: Elections and Appointments
text:
The Constitution is not just a list of rights and laws for everyone in our country. It also tells us how our leaders should be chosen. At the national level, citizens vote to elect the president. They also elect representatives to serve in the House of Representatives and the Senate.

An appointed official is chosen by our leaders. The leaders have to agree on public appointments. For example, the president can nominate a member to a position in their cabinet, but Congress has to approve the appointment. People who have an appointed office serve for a set period of time.

title: The Structure of National Government
text:
The Constitution says that the United States should have three branches, or divisions, of government. Each branch has its own structure. Each branch also has its own leaders and processes. The three branches of government are the executive, legislative, and judicial branches. The three branches were designed to balance the power of each branch. This prevents one person or group of people from having all of the power to make decisions.

Each branch of government has limits on what it can do. This means the legislative, executive, and judicial branches have to work together for the common good. Each can influence laws and actions of the government. No single branch can make an independent decision that would affect the people. This separation of powers provides a means of sharing decision-making, called checks and balances.

title: How a Bill Becomes a Law
text: In the United States, ideas for laws come from citizens. An elected representative from Congress writes down ideas to make our country better. We call this written idea a bill. The bill needs approval from both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The bill goes to the executive branch if it is approved. If the executive branch agrees with the bill, it is signed into law. The executive branch can veto, or say no, to the bill if they don't agree. If that happens, the bill goes back to Congress.

title: Types of Maps
text:
There are many different kinds of maps. You can use them to explore the world. Some maps display the characteristics of physical environments. Other maps show where people live and how they interact with their environment.

A physical map shows the natural features of an area. These maps show the natural features of a place. Natural features include landforms, mountains, valleys, lakes, and streams.

Historical maps are created to represent historical events in the time period they occurred.

Some maps show the climate of a region. Climate is the study of weather over time. A climate map shows whether a place is usually warm or cold and wet or dry.

A political map shows the borders of regions, countries, states, and cities. There are even maps of counties, townships, and neighborhoods.

A population map is used to show the overall distribution of the population within a particular area or region. Most maps use colors or symbols, such as circles or stars, to represent the varying populations. Population maps are useful for the government to plan how to distribute resources.

Cultural maps identify community cultures and resources. These maps are used to help plan and implement the distribution of resources. Cultural maps also connect cultural groups based on their beliefs and values. Cultural maps illustrate the relationships between how people, places, and the environment interact.

title: Diving Deeper: What Does It Mean to Have Empathy?
text:
People can have different perspectives and points of view about the same problem. It's important to respect other people's perspectives and points of view. This is called empathy. Empathy is the ability to understand and share somebody else's feelings. A good example would be to think about a problem that is not your own and ask, "How does that make them feel?" This helps you to understand the problem from their perspective.

One of the fundamental rights protected by the Bill of Rights is freedom of speech. Citizens have the right to express their opinion. However, does that give us the right to say whatever we want without consequences?

title: America Helps Win World War I
text:
In the beginning of the 20th century, farms and factories were growing, and new inventions were springing up everywhere. Life looked good to Nebraskans, but then, something changed. In 1914, a war started in Europe. On one side were the Allied Powers of Britain, France, Russia, and some other European nations. On the other side were the Central Powers of Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria, and Turkey.

Much of the fighting took place on the smooth, rolling lowlands of Belgium and France. This meant that the ground troops had nothing to hide behind, so they dug huge networks of trenches or long narrow ditches. Soldiers lived in those trenches. They ate and slept in them. Anyone who ventured out of the trenches into "no man's land" was quickly killed.

During the war, the German navy came up with a new and dangerous weapon: the U-boat. When ships sailed in the Atlantic Ocean, the U-boats, or submarines, usually attacked them. It didn’t matter if the boat was a military or civilian ship. In 1915, a U-boat sank the Lusitania, a British passenger ship carrying many U.S. passengers. This made many Americans want to go to war. Eventually, President Woodrow Wilson decided to declare war on Germany. The United States joined the Allied Powers. It became part of what was then called the Great War and what is now called World War I.

Millions of workers left the farms and factories in Europe to fight in the war. There was a huge demand for food and supplies for these soldiers. American businesses and farmers helped meet these demands. Nebraskan farmers produced more food to feed both our country and the troops overseas. Nebraskans also did their part to support the war effort. Over 57,000 Nebraskans went to Europe to fight the Central Powers.

On November 11, 1918, at 11 a.m. the Armistice was signed. It signaled the fall of the Central Powers. The war had ended groundwork for the next great war, World War II.

title: September 11, 2001: The Day the World Stopped
text:
The morning of Sept. 11, 2001, began like any other day in the United States. People made their way to work. Students boarded buses or walked to their schools. Thousands of people arrived at airports to board planes. They were going on business trips, vacations, or family visits.

Among those passengers were 19 members of the terrorist organization Al-Qaeda. They had declared war against the United States, and they were about to carry out their largest attack ever. Their leader, Osama bin Laden, created a plan for them to fly hijacked airplanes into important buildings in the United States.

The 19 terrorists boarded four planes leaving major airports in the cities of Boston, Massachusetts; Washington, D.C.; and Newark, New Jersey. Once in the air, the hijackers took over the airplanes. In most hijackings, the terrorists would demand money or the release of other terrorists in prison. The passengers thought they would be safe by following instructions.

Instead of making demands, the Al-Qaeda terrorists turned the airplanes back toward New York City and Washington, D.C. They intentionally flew two of the airplanes into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City. They crashed the third airplane into the military complex known as the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia..

Flight 93, the fourth airplane hijacked that day, was delayed on take-off and was running behind the other three. The passengers on Flight 93 found out that the terrorists were crashing into buildings instead of making demands. They decided to launch a counterattack on the hijackers. The passengers and crew of the plane caused the airplane to crash in an empty field in Pennsylvania rather than into another building. There is no way to know how many lives were saved by the passengers and crew of Flight 93.

The reaction to the terrorist attacks was immediate. Within seconds of the first airplane hitting the North Tower of the World Trade Center, first responders rushed to the scene. Firefighters, paramedics, and police officers converged on the burning building. Even after the second airplane hit the South Tower, first responders continued to make their way into the collapsing World Trade Center.

They helped as many people as possible to evacuate the buildings and surrounding area. Many first responders were still in the buildings helping the victims when the towers collapsed from the attacks.

The government grounded all flights in the United States. Every airplane in the air was ordered to land wherever they could. Passengers ended up stranded at whichever airport they landed. No one knew if there were more hijackers, so air travel stopped in the entire country. Important government buildings were evacuated in case they were targets, too.

The news about the attacks was shared on television. There were very few internet news sites and no social media like we have today. Instead, people focused on the videos and pictures on their TVs. Television stations cut into their regular programming to cover the news. People in the United States and around the world stopped everything to watch their televisions. All day, and for days after, the world watched together as more information about these attacks came out.

Every passenger on the four flights lost their lives that day. Many people in the buildings died from the impact of the airplanes, and many died when the towers fell. Nearly 3,000 people from over 80 countries were killed in the attacks that day. Many more people were injured. The terrorist attacks on Sept. 11, 2001, were the single largest loss of life resulting from a foreign attack on United States soil.

On Sept. 12, 2001, cleanup began. The World Trade Center site became known as Ground Zero. It took rescue workers and volunteers nine months to remove the rubble and debris from Ground Zero. Today, there is a memorial at Ground Zero. It is dedicated to all of the people, including first responders, flight passengers, and workers, who lost their lives that day.

The USS New York’s hull was built from 7.5 tons of steel recovered from Ground Zero. It is a San Antonio-class ship with an amphibious dock. This means that the ship can sail the ocean but also dock with the land. The New York transports marines around the world. The ship’s motto is “Never Forget.”

title: Tribal Government
text:
Some Native American tribes in the United States are considered sovereign nations. A sovereign nation means there is a government that has authority over a geographic region. Tribal nations have their own governments. Many also have constitutions. Tribal governments within the United States also have to follow laws created by the federal government and the U.S. Constitution. The U.S. Congress has final authority on Native American nations. The federal government has a responsibility to protect the rights of Indigenous tribes. Tribal members are often invited to join local, state, and national groups. This is to make sure that laws passed there are fair to their tribes.

There are different types of tribal government. Generally, the leaders of tribal nations are known as chiefs, presidents, or governors. Often, a group of leaders form a council. Tribal councils make laws for their nations. Tribal councils also decide how to spend money on roads, water, and electricity. Tribes also have their own court system and police who help interpret and enforce tribal laws. Some tribal councils tax their people. They use the money to pay for police officers, education, and healthcare for the people.

title: Essential Question
text: How are tribal, state, and local governments organized?

title: State Government
text:
Each state in the U.S. has a state government. State governments are modeled after the federal government. They each have an executive, legislative, and judicial branch. These three branches balance and check each other so no branch has more power than another branch.

The executive branch enforces (carries out) the laws. The governor, lieutenant governor, and other appointed public officials make up the executive branch. The governor is the leader. The executive branch signs bills into law and appoints judges. They also propose the state budget, organize the state militia, and oversee state agencies.

The legislative branch makes the laws and can change laws that already exist. Legislators are called representatives or senators. Voters elect representatives to serve two-year terms and senators to serve four-year terms.

The judicial branch decides what laws mean, how to apply the laws, and which consequences apply to people who are guilty. Judges and justices make up the judicial branch. The state supreme court is the highest court in the state. It is similar to the U.S. Supreme Court. It decides whether laws go against the state's constitution.

title: Local Government
text: Local means belonging to one community. Local governments lead our towns, cities, and counties. The structures of local governments can be different depending on the community. Some cities and towns elect leaders called mayors. People might also elect or appoint city managers, town councils, and county commissioners. Local government officials address community concerns. They help out in the community and act as a voice to the community. Local governments work to provide services to members of the community. These services can be police and fire departments. They can also be public bus systems, road maintenance, and trash removal.

title: County Government
text:
Most states are divided into counties. Each county is made up of different cities, towns, and communities. County governments are responsible for assisting the state government. They help meet the needs of those who live within the county’s boundaries. County governments are often run by a board of supervisors. Members of a board of supervisors are elected by the people who live in their county.

County governments are usually responsible for keeping records. They keep track of births, deaths, marriages, and business licenses. County governments are also in charge of voting, car registration, and collecting taxes. Many counties also offer health and welfare services. These can include nursing care, immunization, and childcare classes. Some counties also run the public library system.

title: City Government
text:
Many cities and towns have their own local government. Some have a charter. A charter is a document similar to the Constitution. It defines how the local branches of government work together. It can also include important rules and laws for the community.

Local governments can differ depending on the size, type, and needs of the community. Some cities and towns have three branches of government. The executive branch of the local government may include an elected mayor or a city council. It may also include roles like a city manager. Often, the city manager is appointed by the mayor or the city council.

In some communities, city, town, and county council members represent the legislative branch. They create the city or town council’s policies. Local courts and magistrates represent the judicial branch. The judicial branch decides whether someone is guilty of a crime. It protects all citizens' rights.

Local governments are responsible for providing safety, health, and welfare services. The local government can tax people and businesses. Tax money is used to provide services to the people. Some government services are parks and recreation, sanitation, and street maintenance.

title: What Plants Need to Grow
text: Have you ever grown a garden before? Gardens take work. You need to plant seeds in a sunny spot. You have to water the seeds each day. Then, right before your eyes, new plants will grow! That must mean every plant needs lots of daily sunlight and water, right? This is not true! So why would we think this? It is easy to believe this because we have seen it happen. We can see that if a plant in a sunny spot gets watered daily, it grows. It may even sprout some beautiful flowers. Is this true for all plants, though? Think about plants in Alaska. Sometimes it can be dark in Alaska for up to 22 hours a day. What about plants in a desert? Sometimes a plant might go days or months without any water. Plants in those environments have to be able to survive without daily sunlight or water. Dandelions in Alaska open to soak up as much sunlight as possible during the short time there is light. In the desert, a cactus will store water to use for long periods when there is no water. In areas where sunlight and water are not always available, plants adapt to their surroundings. Plants store the resources to survive.

title: Concept Correction
text: Have you ever baked cookies? You may have had to use melted butter. How do we melt a block of butter? We can heat it up on the stove or in a microwave. After it is heated, butter looks different. It looks like a yellowish liquid. Some people might think it is not even butter at all. Some people think that when you melt something, it makes a new substance. This is because the substance looks different than it did at first. This may lead them to believe that adding heat to something causes an object to change forever. Why would we think this? It is not true! If I melt a block of butter, all I did was just that: I melted it! It is still butter. If I cool it again, it can be hard butter again. Sometimes, applying heat to a substance will cause a change we cannot reverse. If we burn a piece of paper, we cannot reverse that. The paper is now burned and turned to ash. It is gone. But, there are times when a change caused by heat can be reversed. Some materials, like butter, change when heated and return to their original state when cooled.

title: The Founders
text: The Founders are important people in U.S. history. They worked hard to create the government. They wrote and signed the country's important documents. These documents still protect citizens' rights today.

title: Essential Question
text: Why are the Founders important people in United States history?

title: George Washington
text: George Washington was the first president of the United States. He helped write the Constitution. George Washington signed the Constitution.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text: Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence. He was the third president. He helped the country to grow.

title: John Hancock
text: John Hancock signed the Declaration of Independence. He helped to make decisions about the Declaration of Independence.

title: John Adams
text: John Adams was one of the writers of the Declaration of Independence. He was the second president of the United States.

title: Benjamin Franklin
text: Benjamin Franklin also helped to write the Declaration of Independence. He signed the Declaration of Independence. He also signed the Constitution.

title: James Madison
text: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States. He believed that citizens have rights and responsibilities. He is known as the “Father of the Constitution.”

title: Alexander Hamilton
text: Alexander Hamilton worked hard to help the Constitution become law. He signed the Constitution.

title: Struggle to Control a Continent
text:
In 1750, the American continent was home to the great Iroquois Confederacy. The seven nations that made the confederacy dominated the smaller nations. Their homeland extended from the Great Lakes to the Mississippi River, over the Appalachian Mountains, and south to Georgia. The confederacy had elaborate trade systems. Their alliances with other nations created security and protection for the people. The Iroquois used the many waterways as trade routes. The network of waterways let people travel, connect, and trade.

The Allegheny River and the Monongahela rivers meet to form the large Ohio River. This place was known as the Forks of the Ohio. The land surrounding the rivers was called the Ohio Country. The Ohio River flows southward to join the Mississippi River, which flows down to the Gulf of Mexico. The Iroquois knew the Forks of the Ohio gave access to the continent.

Into this vast empire of the Iroquois Confederacy came two empires from Europe. The French and the British established trade with the Iroquois. Furs, pelts, and leather were traded for European-manufactured goods. This trade balance was favorable to all.

The French were in the northeast region of the continent in present-day Canada. They were also in the Gulf of Mexico in the settlement of New Orleans. The French wanted to connect the northern trade routes with the settlement of New Orleans. This meant they would need to have control of the Ohio Country in western Pennsylvania to reach the Mississippi River.

The British Empire had established colonies on the eastern borders of the Iroquois Empire. The Appalachian Mountains, at first, kept them to the sea coast. In the 1750s, the Iroquois found the British moving westward into the Ohio Country. The British came into the Iroquois land and built permanent trading posts that expanded into settlements. Settlements used the resources the Iroquois needed for their people. The animals left. The resources were consumed, leaving nothing for the Iroquois to live on or to trade with.

Three empires wanted the same territory. One empire was trying to maintain control of the Ohio Country. The other two empires struggled to possess it. Caught in a three-way struggle for power, each empire would do whatever it took to win. Alliances, betrayals, secrets, and lies would cost human lives. They worked against each other in a three-way fight for control. Why? Because whoever controlled the Mississippi would control the continent.

While reading the article, use the map to find the locations discussed in the text.

title: Mary Jemison
text:
Mary Jemison and her family were settlers in an area of the Ohio Country now known as Gettysburg. This was the homeland of the Iroquois Confederacy. The American Indians did not want British settlers to be on their land. In the 1750s, members of the Iroquois Confederacy attacked the intruders to get them off the land. The Jemison family’s home was attacked by members of the Shawnee tribe and their French allies. Mary was taken captive, and her family was killed.

The raiding party and their captives traveled over the mountains about 200 miles to Fort Duquesne at the forks of the Ohio River. Mary was sold by the Shawnee to a group of Seneca. She was adopted and made a member of their nation. Mary spent her life with the Seneca in the southern Ohio Country. She married Sheninjee, a Seneca warrior, and had two children. Mary and her husband left their home in the south. Sheninjee was afraid that white people would come and take Mary. They traveled on foot 700 miles to her husband’s homeland near the Genesee River in western New York. On the trip, Sheninjee was killed in an accident. Mary and the children continued to the Genesee. Sheninjee’s family welcomed her. Later in her life, Mary was given the chance to return to the British settlements. She refused. Mary lived the remainder of her life with her family, the Seneca.

title: Ensign Joseph Coulon de Jumonville
text:
Ensign Joseph Coulon de Villiers de Jumonville was a member of a prominent military family in the colony of New France. Jumonville began his military service at the age of 15, serving under his father for a number of years. Jumonville’s older half-brother served as the military leader at Fort Duquesne, located in the Ohio River country in what is now Pittsburgh.

On the morning of May 27, 1754, Jumonville led 35 French soldiers from Fort Duquesne to detain British forces in the area. He awoke that morning to gunfire. Virginia soldiers and their Native People allies were in the midst of the French soldiers.

There are many conflicting reports from that day. What is known is that Jumonville and some of his soldiers were killed. The French had their theories as to how this happened, while the Virginians told a different story. The Native Americans had a completely different story than the French and the Virginians.

According to the Articles of Capitulation, the document that outlined the terms of the surrender of Fort Necessity, Jumonville’s brother Louis Coulon de Villiers stated, “Since the English have in their power an officer and two cadets, and, in general, all the prisoners whom they took when [they] assassinated Sieur de Jumonville they now promise to send them with an escort to Fort Duquesne.”

Jumonville’s death sparked a series of events that set the world on a course toward war.

title: Tanaghrisson the Half-King
text:
Tanaghrisson the Half-King was another important individual during the French and Indian War. Tanaghrisson was a member of the Seneca Tribe. The Seneca Tribe was part of the Iroquois Confederacy. He was chosen by the confederacy to lead the native peoples living in the Ohio River Valley.

The fur trade was necessary for Tanaghrisson and his people. He told the French he was their friend and ally against the British. This protected his family and kept them trading with the French. Then, when the British came, Tanaghrisson and his people also became friends and allies with the British. This allowed his people to trade with the British.

Tanaghrisson traded with both the French and the British, but ultimately sided with the British during the French and Indian War. He served as a scout for the British, including a young British officer named George Washington. In May 1754, Tanaghrisson told Washington a French military party was nearby. He led Washington and his men to meet Ensign Joseph Coulon de Jumonville’s camp.

Tanaghrisson left Washington and his men at Fort Necessity following the death of Jumonville. He moved his people away from the Ohio River to an area in the Allegheny Mountains near Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, where he died in the fall of 1754.

title: George Washington Gets His Start
text:
Young George Washington of Virginia was ambitious. This means he wanted to make an impression on the world. He wanted a life as a British military officer. Being a British officer would give him status, respect, and wealth. When Virginia Lieutenant Governor Dinwiddie wanted to send a message to the French Army in the Ohio Country, he chose Washington to deliver it.

Dinwiddie sent young Lieutenant Colonel George Washington, his second-in-command, Captain Adam Stephen, and a company of Virginia militia to build a fort at the Forks of the Ohio. This would send the message to the French that the Ohio Country belonged to Virginia. The French were not welcome.

In May 1754, Washington was joined by Tanaghrisson, the Half-King of the Iroquois Confederacy. Tanagrhisson knew a French patrol’s location. Washington took some of his men and followed Tanaghrisson.

After the death of Jumonville, Washington and his company of men reunited. They quickly built a small fort in a meadow. Fort Necessity became Washington’s first point of defense against the French.

Jumonville’s half-brother, Louis Coulon de Villiers, led 600 French troops and 100 of their American Indian allies from Fort Duquesne to Fort Necessity. He would meet with the people who killed his brother.

In a rain-soaked meadow, the Virginia militia waited. The constant rain ruined the gunpowder in the muskets. They had no means of defense. When the French force came, there was little Washington could do to save the lives of his men. The French presented Washington with a document written in French. The document gave conditions for surrender. Washington did not speak French. Washington signed the document, not knowing that it also blamed him for the assassination of Jumonville. An assassination is when someone is killed for political or religious reasons.

On July 4, 1754, he led his defeated men back to Virginia. It was not a very good beginning for a man who wanted to be a British army officer. His actions with Jumonville sparked the French and Indian War.

title: French and Indian War (1754–1763)
text: The war called the French and Indian War in American history is also called the Seven Years’ War in Europe. Conflicts over the Ohio Country began in 1754. However, the war for control of North America officially started in 1756. It ended when the Treaty of Paris was signed in 1763. This timeline lists information about some of the most important events of the war.

title: The Ohio Company: Land Speculation
text:
The Charter of Virginia showed that Virginia borders stretched all the way to the Pacific Ocean. The land was waiting for settlers to live there and use the rich resources. Wealthy colonists in Virginia created a land speculation company called the Ohio Company. The Ohio Company bought land in the Ohio Country from King George II. This gave them the legal basis to sell land to settlers at a higher price. The members of the Ohio Company would become very wealthy. However, two other empires claimed the same land: the Iroquois Confederacy and the French.

Royal Lieutenant Governor Dinwiddie of Virginia was an officer in the Ohio Company. Two of George Washington’s brothers were also investors. If the French gained full control of the Ohio Country, the Ohio Company could not sell any land. They would lose all their investments. No one would be wealthy. It was very important for the French to be forced out of the Ohio Country.

title: What Makes a Good Citizen?
text:
Good citizens help our governments to work well. A citizen is an official member of a country, state, or community. Citizens have the responsibility to behave in certain ways. Civic virtues are personal behaviors and actions that help improve communities. For example, good citizens are friendly and kind. They are willing to donate their time to help others. Good citizens respect others and themselves. They treat others civilly, or politely. They work together for the common good. They are responsible in their daily lives.

Citizens have the responsibility to participate in government. They educate themselves about government issues. They vote in elections. They respectfully hold public officials to their word. Good citizens are necessary for successful communities.

title: Essential Question
text: How do citizens participate in government?

title: Respecting Diversity
text:
Respect is showing all people they are important. When you respect someone, you treat that person with kindness. You show that you care about the person's feelings by respecting their beliefs and traditions. You can respect others even if you believe in different things. Respect is an important quality to practice every day.

You should also respect yourself. Having self-respect means you see the good things about yourself. When you respect yourself, it is easier to show respect to others. When you feel good about yourself, you are happy and treat others kindly. Respecting yourself also means admitting when you do something wrong. It means learning from your mistakes.

title: Voting
text: In the United States, voting is a right. When citizens turn 18 years old, they can vote. Voting is the way we choose our leaders. Voting gives people a chance to make their voices heard. Voters have the responsibility to learn about issues and the people they are voting for. If we don't have all the facts, we may find out later that we voted for something we didn't want. In some countries, people are not allowed to vote. Voting is an important civic responsibility in our system of government.

title: Volunteering
text:
Citizens who want to give something back to the community can volunteer, or donate their time to help others. Many people volunteer because they want to help others in need. There are many ways you can volunteer in your community.

People can volunteer for drives. Different types of drives collect things for people in need. Some volunteers help with community clean-ups. Other volunteers serve in community fire departments and neighborhood watch programs. The list of volunteer jobs is very long. If you want to give back to your community, find out about where you could volunteer. Someone will really appreciate your help!

title: Serving in the Military
text: Some people choose to be participating citizens by joining the United States military. A military is a group of people who are given power to defend a country. People choose to serve in the military in different ways. Some military members help when there is a natural disaster. Other military members fight in combat to protect the United States. We honor military members who choose to serve our country on special holidays, like Veterans Day.

title: Running for Political Office
text:
Citizens interested in serving in the government participate in a campaign process. People who want to be elected are called candidates. Candidates need to meet official requirements for the government job, or office, they want. Before election day, candidates spend a lot of time campaigning. This means they let voters know who they are and what they believe about different issues. They talk about what they would like to do if they win the election. They might use signs, flyers, billboards, and commercials to campaign. They also give speeches and often have debates with other candidates.

Citizens study each candidate carefully. They vote for the person who best represents their viewpoints. The candidate with the most votes wins. Citizens can vote for leaders of their community, state, or country.

title: Paying Taxes
text:
Taxes are money people pay to the government. The laws of our state and our country say citizens must pay taxes. There are many types of taxes. When we purchase items at a store, we pay a sales tax. People who have a job pay an income tax. Citizens who own land or buildings pay a property tax.

Tax money is used for many things. Taxes pay government workers. Taxes also help pay for services like libraries, trash pickup, and police and fire departments. Schools use tax money to buy books and supplies. Tax money also helps repair school buildings and pay teachers and staff. Many other parts of a community, like roads and parks, also rely on tax money. Responsible citizens obey the law and pay their taxes. The money from taxes helps make our communities better.

title: What Are Maps?
text:
The world is a big place. You would have to travel 25,000 miles to go around the middle of the Earth. A globe is a 3D model of the Earth that helps us visualize our planet. Globes show the location of water, land, and countries.

Maps are models of places around the world. They are usually drawn on a flat surface. Maps show the sizes and shapes of countries. They show locations of features of the Earth. They also show the distances between places.

We use many different types of maps. Maps can help us find things like roads, cities, and national parks. Other maps show landforms, boundaries, and weather patterns. Each map looks different and provides specific information.

title: Essential Question
text: How do maps help us learn about the Earth?

title: Reading Maps
text:
A person who creates a map is called a cartographer. Like the author of a book, a cartographer has a point of view and a purpose. A cartographer decides what to include on a map. Map tools help us read and understand maps and globes. Map tools include the title, legend/key, compass rose, cardinal directions, and scale.

The title of the map tells us what the map is about. The map’s legend/key explains what the symbols and colors on the map represent. Most maps also have a compass rose. The compass rose is a symbol that shows the cardinal directions: north, south, east, and west. The scale is a map tool that shows distance. Distance is how far one place is from another. The scale measurement represents a real distance. For example, one inch on a map might represent 100 miles on Earth.

title: Thematic Maps
text:
There are many different kinds of maps.

A population map shows us where people live.

A political map shows the dividing lines or borders that governments make between cities, states, and countries.

A physical map shows the natural features of a place, such as landforms, mountains, valleys, lakes, and streams.

A climate map shows whether a place is usually warm, cold, wet, or dry. Climate is the study of weather over time.

title: Be a Cartographer!
text: Use the things you've learned this week to be a cartographer. Make a map of your classroom, school, or community.

title: The Great State of Nebraska
text:
Artifacts are objects that people have left in places where they lived. Artifacts show that people have lived in Nebraska for at least 13,500 years. Native American tribes developed the area for thousands of years, leaving spear points and other artifacts behind. French and Spanish explorers tried to claim the land in the 1500s. The United States bought the land from France in 1803 as part of the Louisiana Purchase. Eventually, in 1862, families traveling on the Oregon Trail were given land in Nebraska to come live and farm on. Nebraska officially became a state on March 1, 1867. The state’s name comes from a Native American word that

means “flat water,” referring to the Platte River that runs through the state.

Nebraska did not adopt a state flag until 1925. That's 58 years after it became a state! Nebraska’s state flag is a blue rectangle with a golden state seal in the center. The state seal shows different parts of the state and its history. The seal’s design shows a blacksmith with an anvil and hammer, the Missouri River, a settler’s cabin, wheat, corn, and the Rocky Mountains. The seal

also shows the state motto: “Equality Before the Law.”

title: "Beautiful Nebraska"
text: A state song often shows the attributes and wonders of the state. It can be played at state events, celebrations, and sporting events. Our state song is called “Beautiful Nebraska.” A man named Jim Fras wrote the song one day on a drive through the country near Lincoln, Nebraska. Fras parked his car and lay in the tall grass. As he looked up into the blue sky, a melody popped into his head. He rushed home and began to write the song on his piano. “Beautiful Nebraska” was made our state song in 1967, and it is still being taught in schools today!

title: Meadowlark
text: Did you know Nebraska has the same state bird as five other states? Our state bird is the meadowlark. This bird has a long, pointed beak, yellow cheeks, and a yellow throat. Adult meadowlarks have a black “V” on their chests. The meadowlark makes its nest on the ground in the grass. It mainly eats insects like caterpillars and grasshoppers, but it will also eat seeds and berries. This bird has a flute-like song that is made up of around 7-10 notes. The meadowlark became our official state bird in 1929.

title: Goldenrod
text: The goldenrod was made Nebraska’s state flower in 1895. These yellow wildflowers grow in the meadows and along the roads of Nebraska. They can grow to be 2-3 feet tall. Their bright colors attract insects like butterflies and bees, which help pollinate the plants. Farmers often plant the goldenrod near their crops to attract these insects. Native Americans also had many uses for the goldenrod. They used it to act as a painkiller to treat bee stings. They chewed on it to help relieve toothaches too. The goldenrod is also the state flower for Kentucky and South Carolina. In midwestern states, it is said that when the goldenrod starts to bloom, it will soon be time for children to go back to school!

title: Little Bluestem
text: Our state grass is called the little bluestem. It is the state grass of Kansas too! This grass grows in small clumps of tall stems. Each clump of grass has about 100-300 stems in it. The grass is a blue-green color but changes to red or purple in the winter months. During the months of August to October, the grass grows fuzzy, white flowers. The tall stems of the little bluestem offer insects protection from predators and weather. Many butterfly species choose to lay their eggs in the grass.

title: The Honeybee and Catfish
text:
Nebraska made the honeybee its state insect in 1975. We share the honeybee as our state insect with 17 other states! Honeybees play an important role in Nebraska. They produce beeswax to make candles and cosmetics. They also make honey! One of the bees' most important jobs is to pollinate the crops and wild plants.

The state fish of Nebraska is the channel catfish. The catfish is named for its whisker-like barbels, which look like a cat’s whiskers. The sensitive barbels help the catfish find food. These dark-colored fish live in lakes and larger rivers. They like to eat insects, fish, frogs, and plants. The catfish is one of North America’s most fascinating and spectacular types of fish.
