title: Animal Migration
text:
Why do animals leave their homes? Often, animals migrate because of the seasons. The weather might be too hot, cold, or dry during certain times of the year. To survive, they must migrate to find food.

One animal that migrates is the pronghorn.

Pronghorn are found only in North America. Migration is an important part of the life cycle of pronghorn. These animals have the longest land migration in the continental United States. Herds of pronghorn migrate 150 miles each way between Wyoming’s upper Greater Green River Basin and Grand Teton National Park. This migration route is called “The Path of the Pronghorn.”

Pronghorn need open plains, fields, and grasslands to survive. Between summer and winter, the pronghorn must migrate between these places to survive the winter.

This is a long trip. It has become even harder. Pronghorn used to only have to worry about cold weather or predators when they migrated. The path the pronghorn take has been changed by humans. Humans have added fences and highways. A major highway has been built right through a key section of their migration route.

Scientists and engineers have been collecting data on this problem for many years. In five years, 702 pronghorn and mule deer were killed while trying to cross Highway 191.

This problem is expensive! About 1,800 vehicles collide with wildlife each year. Several people have died. Hundreds of people have been injured. In this area alone, drivers spend approximately $350,000 per year on vehicle repair and medical bills. These expenses are because of accidents involving animals trying to cross the highway. However, the route needs to stay open, and the highway cannot be moved.

Your job is to look at the solutions that have been proposed. Decide which solution is the best for meeting the criteria and constraints of the problem.

title: The Pronghorn Overpass
text:
In the case of “The Path of the Pronghorn” problem, scientists chose to build the overpass over the highway. They built fences along the highway. The fences funnel the pronghorn to the overpass.

Scientists decided that the cost to build the fences and overpass could be justified. This solution could restore the ecosystem. It could reduce accidents, which would reduce costs to life and property. The animals could still follow their migration route. Cost was a constraint.

How They Did the Math

On average, about 100 animals are hit on roads each year.

Each crash causes an average $10,000 in damage.

The value of each deer is about $3,000.

You Do the Math:

100 animals hit each year X $3,000 value = $_______________________________ (Amount A)

$10,000 in damage X 100 crashes resulting in damage = $___________________________ (Amount B)

$______________ Amount A + $_____________ Amount B = $_____________ (Amount C)

$_____________ Amount C X 20 years = $_________________ (Amount spent without the overpass)

This is how much it would have cost if the bridge had not been built. Scientists determined they could save money over time that could go toward the cost of the bridge.

If you didn’t pick this solution, you didn’t get the answer wrong. Some parts of the country use one of the other solutions. No solution is right or wrong. Solutions are chosen based on how well they meet the criteria and constraints. They also consider input from the people who would pay for the solution.

Once the bridge was built, scientists did a wildlife study. They tracked the overpass, using cameras. They wanted to see if the animals were using the overpass. Over 9,000 animals used the overpass during a three-month study. That means that 9,000 animals were safe from cars.

Scientists and engineers work hard to find great solutions to problems like these. Maybe you would like to be a scientist or engineer and help find solutions to problems.

title: Cottonwood
text: The cottonwood tree has played an important part in our state’s history. Early pioneers would use cottonwood trees as landmarks to find their way to Nebraska. These pioneers would then plant cottonwood trees on the new land they claimed. The cottonwood was made our state’s tree in 1972. Cottonwood trees still grow throughout all of Nebraska. These trees have thick trunks and diamond-shaped leaves. The wood of the cottonwood tree is soft. It may not be the best to build with, but it makes great firewood. The cottonwood tree can grow to be 80-100 feet tall. That is slightly taller than the White House.

title: Whitetail Deer
text: The whitetail deer was made Nebraska’s state mammal in 1981. Ten other states have also made the whitetail deer a state symbol. This is an incredible animal that can run up to 40 miles per hour. That is about how fast your car drives down the street! These animals can be quite shy. If you get too close, they will probably run away. Whitetail deer eat weeds, grasses, nuts, and fruits. The whitetail deer is important to our state because both Native Americans and early settlers relied on the deer for food and furs. The deer continue to help our state by helping plants and forests grow.

title: Blue Chalcedony
text: Blue chalcedony (kal-sed-o-nee) was named Nebraska’s state gemstone in 1967. It is commonly called the blue agate. These stones have bands of blue and white. If you are out looking for a blue agate, the beautiful blue stone is usually hidden beneath a rather ugly exterior. You might need to crack the rock open to find the blue stone. Blue agates are often used to make jewelry and can be found in northwestern Nebraska.

title: Mammoth
text:
Did you know Nebraska has a state fossil? Our fossil is the mammoth. Mammoths were a kind of elephant that lived during the Ice Age. These creatures have since gone extinct, which means they are no longer living anywhere in the world. Mammoths had longer tusks than elephants, and some mammoths had thick fur that covered their bodies. These creatures stood over 13 feet tall and weighed around 22,000 pounds. That is about how much a semi-truck weighs! Mammoth fossils have been discovered all over our state.

The largest mammoth fossil in the world was discovered near Lincoln, Nebraska, by chickens. Yes, you read that right: chickens. In 1921, a farmer named Henry Kariger noticed his chickens were pecking at something on a hill. Kariger investigated a little further and realized it was the jaws and teeth of a giant animal. This is now on display at the University of Nebraska State Museum and was given the name "Archie." The mammoth was made the official state fossil on Nebraska’s 100th birthday, March 1, 1967.

title: What is Data?
text:
To learn about a topic, data needs to be collected. What is data? Data is information. Data guides and directs scientists in their search for answers. Other professionals also use data. These professionals are teachers, authors, businesspeople, politicians, artists, athletes, doctors, and farmers. Data is different, depending on the investigation. When collecting data, it is important to be consistent. Consistent means doing something the same way every time. Imagine if you were measuring how much it rained each day for a week. On the first day, you measured the rain in inches; on the second, in centimeters; and on the third, in feet. The results of your data would not be consistent. To be consistent, you have to use one single type of measurement to measure how much it rained. It is important to keep track of your data in an organized place. Scientists use their science notebooks to keep all their information in one place. They write clear tables and notes. Collecting clear and organized data is important in all scientific investigations.

title: Organizing Data
text:
Graphs are used to organize data that scientists have collected. By creating a graph, it is easier to see patterns in the data. There are many types of graphs. Two common types are bar graphs and pictographs. Bar graphs organize data into bars. They help scientists compare data. Pictographs organize data with pictures. They help scientists see the data. Graphs support scientists’ conclusions. Graphs help others clearly see the results of an investigation.

title: Rules
text: Rules explain what or how to do things. Rules help us to make choices. We have rules at home and school. Rules teach us how to learn, work, and play together.

Juneteenth is short for “June 19th.” It is a special day for African Americans. In 1863, President Lincoln signed an important document. It set enslaved people in the United States free. It was called the Emancipation Proclamation. General Granger brought the news to Texas. He landed at Galveston on June 19, 1865. Finally, formerly enslaved people were free in every state.

African American communities have celebrated Juneteenth for many years. They hold church services and parties. Some cities hold big celebrations with parades. In 2021, the President of the United States made Juneteenth a national holiday.

title: People and the Resources of Nebraska
text:
Humans have basic needs. People need food, clothing, and a place to live. The natural features of an area influence how people meet their basic needs. They also influence the jobs that people have and their lifestyle.

People depend, or rely, on the environment around them to meet their needs. People usually choose to live close to resources that help them meet their basic needs. One example is the need for water. Throughout history, people have established towns and cities near bodies of water to meet this need.

People modify their environment to meet their needs. This means they change the place where they live. For example, people build roads and bridges to make travel from one area to another easier.

People also adapt to their environment to meet their basic needs and to survive. This means people change how they live based on their environment. People wear different clothes, eat different food, and live in different houses, depending on the environment they live in. The jobs that people have often relate to their environment.

For example, some of Nebraska’s major cities are located along the Platte River. These communities were created because of the resources around them. The Platte River provides transportation and water to meet daily needs. A community located along the river’s floodplain would have good fertile soil for growing crops and supporting farms. People moving west had a big part to play in how the resources of Nebraska were used to create the cities and towns we live in today.

title: Omaha
text: The city of Omaha is located along the banks of the Missouri River. This river creates the border between Nebraska and Iowa. The city is also surrounded by several lakes. Being located near a water source made this area a great place to settle. The area was originally the home of the Omaha Native American tribes. In March of 1854, the United States signed a treaty with the Omaha tribe. The treaty stated that the tribe would give up all their lands west of the Missouri River. On July 4, 1854, Omaha became an official city. The fur trade was one of the initial businesses that supported the growth of the city, especially after Lewis and Clark wrote that this area would be a good place to create a trading outpost. The city quickly became a jumping-off point for the many people migrating westward. When the Union Pacific railroad was built, many more opportunities for the city to grow came with it. The railroad connected many cities together. Quickly, the need for housing, schools and stores became apparent. The grassy fields and water supply of the area brought cattle to Omaha. Ranchers would bring the cattle to the city to sell. A new industry developed as stockyards, or fenced sections of land for cattle to be kept, and packing plants brought new business to Omaha.

title: Lincoln
text: Lincoln is the capital city of Nebraska. The city was named after President Abraham Lincoln. It is located in a wetlands valley, where the Salt Creek flows into the Platte River. There are saline deposits, or salt flats, in the area northwest of Lincoln. Around 1853, early settlers had the idea of manufacturing salt from these flats. Unfortunately, the idea proved to be unsuccessful. In 1867, the Haymarket opened. The market's main purpose was providing a place where your crop of hay could be weighed before it was sold. You could buy a wagon, camping supplies, and hay all in one place. The large, open spaces and low hills make growing alfalfa and raising cattle an ideal resource for this area of Nebraska.

title: Fort Kearny
text: Fort Kearny was built twice. Its first location was on a route that very few people heading west used. So the decision was made to move the fort to a new location in a wooded area next to the Platte River. There were three advantages to this new area. The land was slightly elevated so flooding would be less of a problem; there were plenty of trees to support building needs; and the natural hay bottoms supplied food for feeding animals. In 1848, the new fort was built. It was used by many who followed the Oregon Trail. Some days, as many as 500 teams of oxen passed through the fort. Fort Kearny was an important landmark in Nebraska. It was the only fort between the Missouri River and the Rocky Mountains.

title: Grand Island
text: Grand Island, Nebraska, was named after a large island in the Platte River. French fur traders called it La Grand Isle. Grand Island is part of the Great Plains region. Before the area was settled, you could see field after field of prairie grass. Wagon trains brought people from many different cultures through this growing city. As news of the railroad spread, people began to create settlements along the path of the railroad. A group of German immigrants from Iowa were one such group. People were looking to become landowners, something they couldn’t do in their own countries. The island in the river disappeared when dams across the river were built to control flooding. Nebraska is a region of low, flat hills. Flooding was a problem for many cities that had been built along the rivers. Grand Island’s location along the river and its wetlands was an ideal location for the sandhill crane migration.

title: Scottsbluff
text: Just past the towering 300 feet of Chimney Rock is the town of Scottsbluff. This is one of the last major cities you will see as you head west out of Nebraska. Located in Nebraska’s panhandle, Scottsbluff has a higher elevation than most other cities in the state and was also created as a railroad station in the western part of Nebraska. To mark the spot, the railroad left an abandoned train car next to the tracks as its first depot. The climate of Scottsbluff is perfect for growing and processing sugar beets. Many people refer to the area around Scottsbluff as the “Sugar Valley” because sugar beets are farmed and processed there.

title: North Platte
text:
The city of North Platte is located in the Great Plains region of the state, where the North Platte River and the South Platte River meet. The climate, the Ogallala Aquifer, and the rich soil make this region of Nebraska an ideal place to grow corn.

Access to a regular water source and open fields also supported the growth of the cattle industry. The railroad also played a role in helping establish the city. The largest railroad yard in the world is Bailey Yard, located in North Platte. Bailey Yard is a place where trains are repaired, crews on the trains change places, and train cars get sorted for final destinations. The central location makes this a great place for trains to drop off and pick up new cargo.

title: North Platte River
text: The Platte River has provided for inhabitants of Nebraska for centuries. The 700 miles of river run through Wyoming, Colorado, and Nebraska. The Platte River flows into the Missouri River, which joins the Mississippi River, until eventually it meets the Gulf of Mexico. The seven dams across the Platte River provide electricity for neighboring cities. Pioneers traveling west had to cross this river as part of their journey. To get across the river, they either swam with their horses or tied the wagons together to create floating ferries. This didn’t always work well. Later, when there were actual ferries or bridges, people would charge a toll to others wanting to cross the river. The trail created by those going west follows the path of the river. So, if you drove along I-80 in Nebraska, some of the things you saw would be similar to what the pioneers saw. The consistent source of water and the support of the towns along the way made the journey west possible.

Pennsylvania is home to some of the greatest performing artists in the world. In fact, the first building that showed movies was built in Pittsburgh in 1905! The first movie tickets cost five cents and it helped lead to the movie industry that we have today. Pennsylvanians have influenced the world of music, acting, singing, and dance. Some of these famous people include:

Marian Anderson: Marian was one of the finest singers in the world in the 1930s. She was born in Philadelphia. Even as a performer, she faced discrimination because she was Black. After returning from a tour of Europe, Anderson was denied the chance to sing at Constitution Hall because of her race. When Eleanor Roosevelt, the US President’s wife, found out, she quit the organization that denied Anderson and asked her to sing at the Lincoln Memorial on Easter in 1939. It was one of the most important performances in history.

Martha Graham: Martha Graham was born and raised in Allegheny, Pennsylvania. She was a famous dancer and choreographer. A choreographer is someone who creates dances for others. She created a new way of teaching dance called the “Graham Technique.” Her style of teaching dance is still used today. Graham even received the Presidential Medal of Freedom for her contributions to dance and the performing arts.

John Coltrane: Coltrane is considered one of the best jazz musicians in the world. His musical style influenced generations of artists. He moved to Philadelphia after high school and made his mark in the music industry. Coltrane faced some problems in his life, but music helped him overcome them. He became a force for good and his music helps people through their problems today. John Coltrane was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for his contributions to music in 2007.

title: Newton’s Discovery
text:
Let’s Discuss:

“Dropping the ball” is an idiom. What does it mean? How does this idiom illustrate the effects of gravity?

Read the article with a partner. Then, identify the author’s point and evidence. Discuss which evidence would help support your claim to make sense of the phenomenon.

Issac Newton was a scientist who asked great questions. He is famous for many things and there are many stories about him. According to one of these stories, one day in 1666, Newton sat under an apple tree, making observations about the world. When one of the apples fell to the ground next to him, he began his scientific inquiry. He asked himself, “Why did the apple fall down, not sideways or up?” From this simple question, Newton began to understand the invisible force on Earth that draws everything toward its center. We call this unseen force gravity.

The main piece of evidence supporting Newton’s claim was the apple. The apple fell down and stayed down. You can see the same principle when you jump, drop objects, or even when you do nothing at all. Gravity causes everything to fall straight down and remain there. Because the Earth is round, the idea of “down” changes based on the perspective of the observer. People live all around the Earth, and they all observe objects falling straight “down.” Gravity’s force applies to all things on Earth, drawing them toward the center of the planet.

But what causes gravity? Gravity on Earth is actually caused by the planet itself. Earth is so large that it draws everything in toward its center. This is known as gravitational pull. When you are far, far away from the Earth, its gravity isn’t as strong. Astronauts appear weightless because they are actually in a constant state of falling! Things in outer space float because they are far away from any large objects, such as Earth, so the gravitational pull is weak. You can see this on a large scale when nearby objects in space are pulled toward the Earth. But here on the ground, the evidence of gravity is as simple as watching an apple fall from the tree.

title: Conducting Research
text:
Gravity and Weight

Gravity from Earth is always drawing objects down, toward its center. But not all objects on Earth are the same. That means Earth's gravity affects some things more strongly than others. The more matter (or stuff inside it) an object has, the more Earth’s gravity will pull it down. This is observed as weight. The weight of an object is a measurement of gravitational force. When you weigh an item on a scale, you are actually measuring the amount of gravitational pull Earth has on that object. Humans have used Earth’s gravitational pull as a useful tool for centuries. The weight of an object can be used to trigger certain functions in simple machines. For example, animal traps work by using the weight of an animal to release a lever or door to a cage. Weight sensors can also detect when gravity triggers an alarm, indicating the presence of something, like a car approaching a drive-through window at a fast food restaurant. Gravity acts on all objects, whether it's a trap door falling or the slight, almost unobservable downward motion of a sensor.

title: Food in Nebraska
text:
Hundreds of years ago, Indigenous tribes were the only people in the area we now call Nebraska. The land was covered with wild grass. Millions of bison roamed the plains of North America. Indigenous peoples hunted the bison for food. They also grew crops. They ate squash, corn, and turnips. They cooked sunchokes, which come from the roots of sunflower plants.

In the 1800s, settlers began to plant farms where there had only been wild grass. Almost all of the bison were killed by hunters. Instead of bison, people raised cattle and pigs for meat.

Today, people in Nebraska still eat the crops that Indigenous people ate long ago. Nebraska is especially famous for its corn. Many people in Nebraska also love to eat steak made from cattle.

Bierocks, or runzas, are a popular food in Nebraska that is not well-known in other parts of the United States. A bierock is a baked bread pocket filled with hamburger, cabbage, and onions. Bierocks were originally made hundreds of years ago in Russia. They were brought to America by immigrants from Germany.

Some famous foods were invented in Nebraska. The Tin Roof sundae is made from vanilla and chocolate ice cream, marshmallow sauce, and peanuts. It was created over 100 years ago in Potter, Nebraska. The Reuben sandwich is a corned beef sandwich that was invented in an Omaha hotel in the 1920s. The first powdered drink mix was invented in Hastings, Nebraska, in 1927.

Today, Nebraskans eat food from many cultures. Nebraska has people who can trace their ancestry to every part of the United States and all over the world. You can find restaurants that serve food from Asian, European, African, and South American countries.

title: Sports in Nebraska
text:
Many people in Nebraska love to play and watch sports. If you like to play, you can join a team at your school!

The most popular football team in Nebraska is the University of Nebraska Cornhuskers. They are one of the most successful college football teams in American history. The Cornhuskers started playing football more than 130 years ago, in 1890. They have won the national college football championship five times.

The Cornhuskers have fans in every part of Nebraska. When there is a football game at the Huskers’ home stadium, thousands of people go to Lincoln to attend the game. The stadium can hold more than 89,000 people. The Cornhuskers’ team colors are red and white. When the stadium is full, everything looks red. The stadium has been full for every football game since 1962.

The University of Nebraska women’s volleyball team is just as successful as the football team. The Cornhuskers’ volleyball team started in 1975. They have won more games than any other women’s college volleyball team. Like the football team, they have won five national championships.

The College Baseball World Series is a special event that happens every year in Omaha. This is a championship tournament for the best college baseball teams in America. Thousands of fans also come to Omaha from all over the country. Fans celebrate and cheer for their teams. Millions of people watch the games on television.

Some famous athletes grew up in Nebraska. Bob Gibson is one of the best baseball pitchers of all time. He was from Omaha. He went to college at Creighton University, in Omaha. In high school and college, Gibson played both baseball and basketball. He played professional basketball for the Harlem Globetrotters, but then he decided to be a professional baseball player. When he played for the St. Louis Cardinals, he won the award for the best pitcher in the league twice. His team also won the World Series twice. He is a member of the Baseball Hall of Fame.

Gale Sayers played high school football in Omaha. He became a running back for the Chicago Bears in the National Football League. Sayers had to retire from his professional football career after just seven seasons because he was injured. However, he was such a good player that he became the youngest person to be chosen for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Tom Osborne is from Hastings, Nebraska. He played football in high school and at Hastings College. Then he became a football coach at the University of Nebraska. Osborne was the Cornhuskers’ head coach for 25 years. He was the University of Nebraska’s most successful coach.

title: Music in Nebraska
text:
In Nebraska, people have always loved music! Native Americans made the oldest music in Nebraska.

When settlers started coming to Nebraska in the 1850s, they worked hard to build homes, farms, and ranches. Music and dancing gave them opportunities to spend time together and rest from their work. They played instruments like the guitar, the banjo, and the fiddle. They brought pianos and organs to play music in their homes. People also liked to play brass instruments, such as the trumpet, the trombone, and the tuba. Every town had a brass band that played in concerts and performed for special celebrations. Nebraskans also built theaters and opera houses in cities and towns across the state.

Many kinds of music were popular in Nebraska during the 20th century. Starting in the 1920s, North Omaha was an important city for African American music, especially jazz and blues. Many jazz musicians lived in North Omaha. Jazz performers came to Nebraska from other parts of the United States and the world. Rock music and country music also became popular throughout our state. Rock and country bands from cities like Lincoln, Fremont, and Omaha have become famous. There are classical orchestras in Omaha, Lincoln, and Kearney, and there is an opera company in Omaha.

People have come from all over the world to live, work, and study in Nebraska. They have brought the world’s music with them. We can listen to music from places like Mexico, Cuba, Scotland, Italy, Brazil, and the Caribbean. You can find almost any kind of music right here in Nebraska.

title: Native Dance in Nebraska
text:
Dance is a treasured and sacred tradition for Native Americans. Styles of Native American dancing have been passed down for hundreds or even thousands of years. Each tribal group has its own styles of dance. Some dances are for family celebrations, like marriages and birthdays. Some dances prepare the tribe for hunting. Dances can show gratitude for the land. Native American dances can also be just for fun!

One of the oldest Native dances is the Grass Dance. This dance comes from the tribes of the Great Plains. The Ponca, Omaha, Winnebago, and Iowa are tribes in Nebraska who dance in this style. The Great Plains were once covered in long, tall prairie grass that flowed back and forth like waves in the wind. The Grass Dance is a beautiful, flowing dance. The dancers hop from one foot to the other, following the rhythm of the drum and the singers. Their heads, arms and shoulders sway back and forth. The tassels on their brightly colored clothing move like grass.

One place to see traditional Native dancing is at a powwow, an event where members of the tribe meet to celebrate their culture. There are often dancing competitions at powwows.

title: Languages and Religion in Nebraska
text:
People from many parts of the world have come to live in Nebraska. They have brought their cultures, languages, and religions. When these were added to the cultures of the Native Americans who were already here, a wonderful combination of languages and heritages was created that exists in Nebraska today.

Most people in Nebraska speak English. But other languages have also been part of Nebraska for a long time. In the 50 years between 1865 and 1915, nearly 25 million people came to America to live. Most of these people came from Europe in search of a better life. Some of the largest European immigrant groups spoke German, Swedish, Czech, Danish, or Russian. There were also immigrants who spoke Italian or Greek. People from all of these places built towns where these languages were spoken along with English.

European immigrants had strong religious beliefs. Most people from Ireland, Italy, and Czechia were Catholic. Many German, Swedish, and Danish immigrants were Lutheran. Many other Germans were Catholic or Mennonite. Many immigrants from Greece and Russia were Orthodox Christians. All of these religions have many followers in Nebraska today.

Other religious groups have also grown in Nebraska. There are thousands of Jews, Muslims, Buddhists, and Hindus. There are also many people who do not belong to any church.

Many Black people migrated to Nebraska, especially after the Civil War. At that time, African Americans were not allowed to worship in white people’s churches. Black Nebraskans founded their own churches, including many Baptist and African Methodist Episcopal churches. These churches are still important in the lives of many Nebraskans.

Native American languages were spoken in Nebraska before any European languages. These Indigenous languages include Omaha-Ponca, Pawnee, Dakota-Lakota, Chiwere, Cherokee, and Ho-Chunk. Very few people speak these languages now, but members of Native American tribes are working to teach these languages to more people. Many Native Americans also preserve Indigenous religious beliefs.

During the 20th century, people came to Nebraska from even more places. People from Latin America brought the Spanish and Portuguese languages. Spanish is now the second-most spoken language in Nebraska. Thousands of Nebraskans speak Vietnamese, Chinese, Arabic, or Tagalog (a language from the Philippines). Some Nebraskans also speak languages from India and Africa.

title: Coordinate Grid System
text:
The first theme of geography is location. Location refers to where a place is. An absolute location is the exact spot where something is on the Earth. Absolute location is helpful when you're trying to find an unfamiliar place. We can find the absolute location on a map by using vertical and horizontal lines. Horizontal lines of latitude run east and west around the Earth. These lines show how far from the Equator places are. We also call latitude lines parallels. Cartographers also draw lines of longitude on maps from the North Pole to the South Pole. We call these lines meridians.

Cartographers use latitude and longitude lines to divide a map into a grid. A grid is two sets of lines that cross each other to make small squares. Grids make finding a location easier. A coordinate grid system uses letters and numbers to label the grid lines.

title: Important Lines of Latitude
text: We divide up the world for mapping purposes. Imagine a horizontal line that runs around the middle of the world. Cartographers actually draw this imaginary line on many of the maps they make. They call this line the Equator. The Equator divides the map of the world into halves, called the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere. The prefix “hemi-” means half, so a hemisphere is half a sphere. The Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle are two important lines of latitude that are to the north of the Equator. The Tropic of Capricorn and the Antarctic Circle are lines to the south.

title: Important Lines of Longitude
text: Many maps also include important lines of longitude. The Prime Meridian is one of these lines. It divides the world into halves, called the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere. The vertical lines of longitude that go from the North Pole to the South Pole show how far east or west places are from the Prime Meridian.

title: Cardinal and Intermediate Directions
text: Cardinal directions are the four main points on a compass. These directions are north, south, east, and west. They help us to locate places around the world. North and south refer to the poles of the Earth. Intermediate directions are between the cardinal directions. They include northwest and northeast. They also include southwest and southeast. Both cardinal and intermediate directions can be located on a compass rose.

title: Other Important Lines
text:
We use latitude and longitude lines to find absolute location. Longitude lines measure the Earth's rotation in degrees. Each degree is 60 minutes. Each minute also has 60 seconds. The Earth rotates fully around its axis once a day. This takes 24 hours. That is why Earth is divided into 24 different time zones. A time zone shows what time it is in a particular location. The Prime Meridian is the starting point of the time zones. From the Prime Meridian, we add one hour per zone towards the east. We take one hour away towards the west.

Larger countries have many time zones. The United States has six time zones. It would be difficult for smaller countries to have different time zones. In order to make things easier, time zone boundaries often follow political boundaries instead of longitude lines.

The International Date Line is another imaginary line drawn on a map of Earth's surface to show the boundary between one day and the next. The International Date Line is located halfway around the world from the Prime Meridian. It isn’t straight because it follows political boundary lines.

title: What Are Natural Features?
text: Natural features of the Earth are parts of the Earth's surface. Natural features are created in different ways. The Earth's surface is changing every day. Wind, rain, drought, volcanoes, and earthquakes all shape Earth's surface. People have named types of natural features by the way the land forms. Mountains, valleys, deserts, and oceans are all natural features on Earth's surface.

title: Mountains
text:
A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean.

It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They are formed from movement of the Earth's crust. Mountains are shaped over time by weather. Rich minerals are found in the core of mountains. Mountain peaks are often covered in snow. The snow melts and sends water down the sides in streams, creeks, and brooks.

title: Natural Resources and Mountains
text: Mountains may contain a variety of biomes. A biome is a community of plants and animals living together. Taller mountains have colder weather. When the weather is cold, plant life is limited. Further down the mountain slopes, the temperature is warmer, and plant life increases. This makes it easier for animals to find food and shelter there.

title: Valleys
text: A valley is a low area between mountains. It is often created by a river or stream. It can also be created when two mountains are formed close together. Valleys are usually “V”-shaped. They collect the soil and plants that are moved down the mountains by weather.

title: Valleys and Natural Resources
text:
Valleys are home to many animals. These animals find shelter in the trees and grasslands. The soil has nutrients, which help plants grow. Streams from mountains form rivers in valleys.

Valleys are protected by the mountains. The weather in a valley is often mild. As a result, plants and animals thrive there.

title: Regions of Nebraska
text:
Physical Nebraska

A lot of people think Nebraska looks like a pan turned upside down. The skinny part on the left is called the “panhandle.” The larger part, to the right, is called the “pan.” Other states also have a panhandle, such as Idaho and Oklahoma.

Nebraska is part of the Great Plains flatland that makes up the center of the United States. These Great Plains extend from northern Canada to southern Texas and include parts of thirteen states in the central United States.

But that doesn’t mean Nebraska is entirely flat. Nebraska's land slopes gently downward from west to east. The rivers flow toward the Missouri River, Nebraska’s eastern border. If you live in Richardson County, the southeastern point of our state, you live about 875 feet above sea level. But if you traveled westward to Panorama Point in Kimball County, the southwestern point of the panhandle, you’d be standing more than one mile above sea level. That’s a difference of more than 4500 feet!

Nebraska has five major geographic regions.

Badlands

In the far northwestern area of our state, you will find the Badlands, which make up a big part of our neighbor to the north, South Dakota. These steep, rocky hills have been carved into strange and beautiful shapes by erosion. One part of Nebraska’s badlands is called Toadstool Geologic Park. The Badlands are used as a rangeland where livestock are raised.

High Plains

The High Plains are found in the panhandle. They extend westward into Wyoming and Colorado. In the southwest corner of this region, you can find our state's highest point, Panorama Point, which is more than one mile above sea level. You can see the Rocky Mountains from Panorama Point. You can also find Chimney Rock and Scotts Bluff in the High Plains.

The Sandhills

The Sandhills region is the largest area of grass-covered sand dunes in North America. It is also one of the largest in the world! This area consists mostly of hills and ridges of grass-covered sand (sod). The Sandhills are dotted with valleys, lakes, rivers, and streams. There are two national forests and several wildlife refuges there but not many people. It covers about one-fourth of our state. Cattle ranching is the main industry in this region.

Loess Hills and Plains

Loess is a rich, windblown soil that is perfect for farming. The Loess Hills and Loess Plains include low to moderate hills. Grand Island, one of Nebraska's largest cities, is located in this region. Near Grand Island, millions of ducks, geese, and sandhill cranes stop by the Platte River every spring during their migration north.

Central Lowlands

Eastern Nebraska is part of the Central Lowlands that extend into South Dakota, Iowa, Missouri, and Kansas. This area was once covered by a glacier and has deep deposits of loess. The region includes rolling hills and many rivers and streams that flow into the Missouri River. Nebraska's two largest cities, Omaha and Lincoln, are found in this region.

title: Cities in Nebraska
text:
Omaha

Omaha, Nebraska's largest city, was settled in 1854. It is named for the Native Americans who lived there until their lands were given to settlers. Because of its location on the Missouri River, it has played a big part in the history of our state and our country. It was one of the "jumping-off" points for the Oregon Trail. One-third of Nebraska's population lives in and around Omaha and Lincoln.

There are many things to see and do in Omaha. Two popular places are the Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium and the Joslyn Art Museum. There are also water parks, a planetarium, a children's museum, botanical gardens, a wildlife refuge, a nature center, and many parks. You can also visit the Great Plains Black History Museum, one of the most complete exhibits on Black history found in the West. Through photos and objects from the past, you can learn more about the African American experience on the Great Plains.

Lincoln

Lincoln is the second largest city in Nebraska and its state capital, or where state leaders meet to discuss laws. Lincoln’s state capitol building, sometimes called the “Tower of the Plains,” is considered one of the most beautiful public buildings in the country. Visitors can see a great view of the city from the 14th-story observation deck.

The city of Lincoln was named after President Abraham Lincoln. The city’s children’s museum has a three-story apple tree, a real airplane, and a water exhibit. The Lincoln Children’s Zoo has lots of ways to see the animals up close, including a train. There are also nature centers, a natural-history museum, a planetarium, parks, and even a go-kart raceway.

The main campus of the University of Nebraska is located in Lincoln. In 1869, when it first opened, the University only had 20 students, but today, it has more than 24,000 students.

Grand Island

Grand Island is one of Nebraska’s largest cities. It was originally built on a 40-mile-long island formed by the Wood River and a channel of the Platte River. However, the city was moved. It is now located near the spot where Interstate 80 leaves the Platte River. Each spring, millions of ducks, geese, and hundreds of thousands of sandhill cranes stop near Grand Island on their way north. Many people travel to Grand Island to see these birds.

The Stuhr Museum of the Prairie Pioneer is a living history museum in Grand Island. It has more than seventy historic buildings brought from all over Nebraska, such as churches and stores. Tourists can talk with people dressed in pioneer-era clothing. They can explore buildings displaying antiques, such as early steam engines, tractors, and farming tools. There is also a replica of a Pawnee earth lodge that would have been home to up to fifty people.

North Platte

North Platte stands where the two branches of the Platte River (the North Platte and the South Platte) meet and continue their journey together across the state. Since the city was found right on the Oregon Trail, thousands of immigrants traveled through it. The railroad also went through town, bringing in all sorts of people and giving the town a wild reputation.

North Platte was once Buffalo Bill's favorite retreat. There, you can visit the Buffalo Bill Ranch State Historical Park, where you can see his beautiful home, visit his big red barn, and even ride horses during the summer. Cody Park has a life-size statue of Buffalo Bill along with a railroad museum with one of the biggest steam locomotives ever built.

Speaking of railroads, North Platte is home to Bailey Railroad Yards, one of the world's largest classification yards. A classification yard is a place where incoming train cars are sorted and placed in outgoing lines that will lead them to their final destination.

Red Cloud

Just a few miles from the Kansas/Nebraska border stands the famous Nebraska city of Red Cloud. It is best known as the town author Willa Cather grew up in. She graduated from the University of Nebraska and published twelve novels and many short stories. Her stories were often about her experiences in Red Cloud. In her stories, she gave Red Cloud various names, such as Sweet Water, Hanover, Frankfort, Moonstone, Haverford, Black Hawk, and Skyline. Visitors to Red Cloud can tour Cather's childhood home.

title: History of Transportation in Nebraska
text:
Transportation has changed a lot over the history of Nebraska. The Native Americans used a complex network of trails to get where they wanted to go on foot. If they wanted to go faster, they would take a canoe on a river.

When the European settlers came, they brought their own kinds of boats. The earliest kind were shallow keel boats that had a keel or ridge along the bottom that helped it move in a straight line.

In the 1800s, steamboats showed up. They could carry several tons of supplies along rivers that were deep enough.

Settlers also used heavy wagons to get supplies across the plains. It took from six to twelve oxen to pull a heavy wagon, which could carry from three to five tons.

From 1841-1866, many wagons came through Nebraska as settlers followed the Oregon Trail to the western United States. About 500,000 emigrants (people moving from another region) passed through Nebraska on their way west. The Oregon Trail followed the Platte River.

In 1861, United States leaders planned a transcontinental railroad. The eastern part of the railroad started in Omaha and headed west along the Platte River Road, which was part of the Oregon Trail. Now, people would be heading west on a train instead of walking alongside wagons.

In 1957, the Oregon Trail and the Platte River Road were used again. This time they were designated as the path for a transcontinental highway called I-80. In 1974, Nebraska was the first state to complete its section of I-80. Nebraska has 3,553 miles worth of highways within its borders. That’s almost enough highway to drive from Seattle, Washington, to Guatemala City in Central America!

Article Research

Read each article. Then, answer the questions, using the text as evidence.

Solar Ovens

A solar oven, or solar cooker, uses light to heat and cook food. Solar ovens are typically used outside in direct sunlight. They can also be used with very strong lamps. Some solar ovens use energy by trapping light. The trapped energy is converted to heat. The more light, the more heat energy. As heat energy is gathered, it increases the temperature inside of the solar oven.

Solar ovens can be made from different materials, such as metal sheets, wood, and metal bowls. They can even be made from recyclables, like cardboard boxes, cardboard tubes, and tin cans. Solar ovens can come in various sizes, shapes, and designs. It all depends on the materials used.

For a solar oven to cook food, the food may need to be cut up into tiny pieces. Tiny pieces of food cook faster than large pieces. Solar ovens also work best with food that does not need to be stirred, flipped, or rearranged while cooking. Stirring or moving food requires the oven to be opened. When the solar oven is opened, all the trapped energy is released. Lastly, depending on the light source, solar ovens may need to be moved or adjusted so that they are always in direct light.

Solar ovens rely only on light to cook food, so they are an affordable, easy-to-move, and efficient device for cooking.

How do solar ovens work?

Do solar ovens produce, or make, their own energy?

Why are solar ovens most successful with cooking food that does not need to be stirred?

Horace Bénédict de Saussure

Horace Bénédict de Saussure was born on February 17, 1740, in Geneva, Switzerland. As a young man, he would often travel to the Swiss Alps, a large mountain range, to collect and study plants. He also hiked mountains in the Alps to study glaciers. Saussure experimented with heating and cooling. He invented many scientific tools and instruments to study temperature, wind, clouds, fog, and rain.

In 1767, Saussure invented the first known solar oven, then called a hot box. He was intrigued by greenhouses: large, glass houses that trap heat to grow plants in cooler environments. Saussure wondered why no one had tried trapping energy to cook food. He experimented by creating a small glass box to trap light that could be used as heat. His experiment was very successful. He was able to create a box that got hot enough to cook fruit! Saussure continued to experiment with the solar oven. He carried it to the top of a mountain to see if the colder temperatures limited how hot the oven could get. Saussure found that the air temperature did not affect the temperature inside the solar oven. The solar oven was able to get just as hot at the top of the mountain as it was at the bottom. All the solar oven needed was direct light.

Saussure continued to study the Earth. He remained a well-known scientist until his death in January 1799. To this day, Horace Bénédict de Saussure is recognized for his inventions and investigations on Earth, weather, and the Swiss Alps.

What inspired Saussure to create a solar oven?

What did Saussure learn by bringing a solar oven to the top of a mountain?

Solar Ovens Today

Solar ovens are an efficient device for cooking food and cleaning water. While they can be made and used by people all over the world, some countries especially rely on them. Three countries that use solar ovens are India, Chad, and China.

India uses solar ovens to cook food for large groups of people. The design is simple and affordable. When compared to cooking on a stove, solar ovens can make thousands of meals for a fraction of the cost. Solar ovens also help reduce air pollution. They do not release any toxins or smoke. That is because they convert light to heat. Their basic design makes solar ovens good for the health of people and the environment. In Western India, the Shirdi government built the world’s largest solar oven. It can cook enough food for 20,000 people a day!

Chad, a country in northern Africa, has about 50,000 solar ovens. They are used by refugees to cook food in a safer, healthier way. Using a solar oven instead of a traditional fire pit decreases the risk of fire outbreaks. It reduces the production of smoke too. This helps to keep people safer and healthier. Another advantage of solar ovens over traditional fire pits is that solar ovens do not require firewood. This means people do not have to leave their camps to look for wood. It helps to keep them safe.

Solar ovens are also used in Zhangye, a rural part of northwestern China. Zhangye is a very sunny but underdeveloped town. That means they do not have as many resources for cooking and cleaning. The solar ovens use the light to cook food. They provide this town with a clean and efficient way to cook food and purify water.

The simple yet effective design of the solar oven gives many people around the world a safe, healthy, and cost-effective way to cook food and clean water.

How do solar ovens continue to help people today?

The Benefits of Solar Ovens

The main benefit of solar ovens is that they cook food by using only the energy from light. They're built in a simple, efficient, and portable design. Solar ovens have other benefits too. They are relatively inexpensive to make. They can be used to clean water and sterilize medical equipment. They also decrease negative effects on the environment and increase human health and safety.

In some parts of the world, cleaning resources are less available. That makes finding clean drinking water difficult. By using solar ovens, people are able to clean their own water. Water can be collected in a pan and placed in a solar oven. The solar oven heats the water, bringing it to a boil. When water is boiled long enough, any bacteria or germs in the water are killed. Once the bacteria is killed, the water is safe to drink.

The same is true for medical equipment. Medical equipment can be cleaned and sterilized in a solar oven with water. As the water heats up in the solar oven, it creates steam. The hot steam then disinfects the medical equipment.

Solar ovens do not require electricity, gas, wood, or coal to run. That means solar ovens do not emit any waste, smoke, or toxins into the air. This makes them much more environmentally friendly. Solar ovens also do not need fuel. That means trees don't need to be cut down and coal doesn't need to be mined.

All this makes solar ovens a safe and healthy choice. People using solar ovens do not have to worry about breathing in smoke, collecting firewood, or paying for electricity. Solar ovens are useful and beneficial in all parts of the world.

What are two benefits of using a solar oven?

Using a Lamp to Power a Solar Oven

While solar ovens normally use sunlight, they also work with light from a lamp. In a typical set-up, energy transfers from the sun to the solar oven as light. When light enters the solar oven, it's trapped. The energy is converted into heat. When solar ovens use a different light source, such as a lamp, the path of energy is a little more complicated.

The path of energy starts with the lamp. Some lamps use batteries. A battery does not produce energy but, rather, stores energy in a chemical state. When the battery is placed in the lamp and the switch is turned on, there is a complete loop, or path, for energy to flow. The stored energy in the battery is carried through the electric currents in the lamp's wires. The electric currents carry the energy to the light bulb, which converts the energy to light. The energy then travels from the lamp as light to the solar oven, where the energy is trapped and converted to heat.

Lamps that do not use batteries will often plug into an outlet. The outlet carries electric currents. When you insert the plug into the outlet, you complete a full loop, or pathway, for energy to travel. The electric currents from the wall outlet travel through the wires of the lamp.

In any of these scenarios, energy is transferred. That energy is converted in order to produce heat. That heat cooks the food in the solar oven.

Sketch the path of energy when a battery-powered lamp is used with a solar oven. Label the types of energy.

Do batteries produce energy?

title: Additional Research
text:
Properties of a Solar Oven

In what ways are these solar ovens similar? Why are these similarities important? If you look closely, you will notice that each of these solar ovens has an angled wall with a shiny background. Why?

When light from the sun or another light source hits the shiny, angled wall, it is directed inside the oven toward the food. This increases the amount of light that hits the food.

If you look closely at each of these images again, you may also notice that each solar oven has a lid that allows the solar oven to be tightly sealed. Why is this important? Once light energy is directed into the oven, the energy needs to be trapped inside in order to create heat. Sealing the oven off and making sure there are no spaces for energy to escape is critical in creating a solar oven that can reach and maintain high temperatures.

If you examine each one of these images again, you may notice that each solar oven contains a dark floor. Why is this? The dark floor absorbs the light that enters the box. When light is attracted to the dark floor, the energy is converted to heat energy. The heat rises and cooks the food.

title: Thinking Like a Historian
text:
In many ways, a historian is like a detective. Historians seek to ask and answer questions about the past. When historians study the past, they also learn about a society’s culture, beliefs, and economy.

Historians identify, select, analyze, and evaluate sources to understand the past. When we study people and events in history, we think like a historian and gather relevant information from sources to determine their meaning. We can determine if the evidence we are examining is credible and reliable.

There are different kinds of historical thinking skills. They include chronological, analytical, critical, and historical thinking.

title: What Are Needs?
text:
What are some of your basic needs? Food, shelter, clothing, sleep, love, education, safety, medical care, and others may come to mind. A need is something that you have to have every day to survive. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water to survive. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us safe by keeping us warm or cool. Needs are something you must have to have in order to survive.

In addition to your basic needs, you might also have other needs. Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If both of your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler to help you be successful each day.

title: What Are Wants?
text:
A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. It is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

Sometimes it's difficult to decide whether you want or need something. Each of us makes these choices throughout the day. We go through the process of determining the positive and negative consequences of purchasing our wants. We evaluate if it is still a need or a want. Then, we make a choice of what would be best for us.

title: Needs and Wants of a Community
text:
Just like individuals, communities have needs and wants. Goods and services meet community needs and wants. Goods are things that people buy to meet their needs and wants. People produce goods like food, clothing, furniture, and toys to meet the wants and needs of a community.

A service is work that a person does for someone else. Communities provide services to people. Important community services include providing water, electricity, schools, and hospitals to meet people’s needs.

A community must evaluate if something is a want or a need. Communities work together to provide goods and services. Together, they examine needs and the possible resources available to meet those needs. Community members share their opinions. They talk, give demonstrations, write articles for the newspaper, or put up signs to make their wants or needs known.

When all of the opinions are heard, people begin to compromise to reach a positive outcome. In a compromise, everyone gives something up to create a solution. When we compromise, we think about what is best for the group. We don't just think about what we want individually.

Needs and wants can change due to personal, environmental, and economic events. If your parents lose their job, they may not have enough money to spend on wants. Basic human needs, like food, water, shelter, and clothing, become the main priority. Resources can become scarce, or not available, after a natural disaster or in times of war. It can be difficult for people to meet their basic needs. Communities must work together to share resources and help each other.

title: Choosing Between Wants and Needs
text:
Each day, everyone must make decisions about needs and wants. The most important thing is that we take care of all of our basic needs first. Afterward, we can start taking care of our wants. When you make a decision, you usually can’t have it both ways. For example, you can’t eat junk food and still be healthy. Likewise, you can’t spend money on new furniture for the house and still have enough left to buy groceries. By choosing one thing, you decide not to choose the other, at least for the time being.

When adults get paid, they look at how much they must spend on their needs. They often create a budget, or a plan for keeping track of their money. A budget lists all of their expenses, or things that must be paid for the month. A budget also lists resources, or money they have available for spending that month.

Additionally, there are items that aren’t part of the regular monthly budget. When making responsible decisions, families first pay for everything they need. Then, they can use what's left over to buy things they, and you, want. To make good choices, we must learn to see the difference between needs and wants. We must plan wisely so all of our needs are taken care of before we start fulfilling our wants.

title: Needs Drive the Economy
text:
In the past, people took care of their own needs. They grew their own food, built their own homes, and made their own clothes. Today, people use the resources they have to produce products or services. Communities work together to produce goods and services.

Communities import goods that they need. In exchange, they export goods and products to other communities around the world. By working together, each community is able to meet the needs and wants of its citizens. This helps to support the economy and makes the community more successful.

title: Meeting Needs and Wants
text:
People face many challenges when trying to meet their needs and wants. One challenge is the availability of resources. As our human population grows, our wants and needs for different materials increase. Due to this increase, humans are using more of the Earth’s resources.

In addition to increased resource use, the Earth’s resources are also changing. Climate can impact the growth of crops and other food sources. Natural hazards can have a negative impact on what resources are available. All of these factors can prevent people from meeting their wants and needs.

People have personal financial resources they use to meet their wants and needs. The amount of wealth people have limits the choices they make. The more money you make, the more opportunity you have to meet your wants and needs. A person with very little money has limited personal financial resources. This person has to decide what needs and wants are most important for their survival. For example, a person may have to decide if they should purchase food for the week or repair a car.

title: Star Light, Star Bright
text:
Reading Strategy

Underline evidence that is relevant to making sense of the phenomenon.

The sun is the only star in our solar system. Stars are natural objects out in space that give off their own light. Our star shines so bright that it provides light and heat energy essential for life on Earth. Although the sun appears as small as a pea to us, it is massive. It only appears smaller to us because Earth is approximately 93.5 million miles away from the sun. But even at this distance, we are close enough to the sun that during the day, all other stars become invisible. Our star seems to be the biggest and brightest. In reality, the sun isn’t the biggest and brightest star in space. As big as the sun is compared to Earth, it is only average-sized compared to other stars.

So why do all the other stars we see seem tiny and dim in comparison to our star? They are so far away that the distances between them and us are hard to imagine! The solar system is so big that scientists have to use scales to describe how far away other stars are. Even then, the scales they use are huge. Imagine the sun as the size of a pea. At this scale, the Earth would be a tiny dot that can only be seen under a magnifying glass and the nearest star (other than the sun) would be about 125 miles away. That’s 2,200 football fields!

In reality, our nearest solar neighbor is 4.2 light-years away. A light-year is a unit of distance that records how long it takes for light to travel somewhere. Scientists use light-years to measure the extremely long distances from Earth to other stars. That is why all the other stars we see in the sky appear small and dim. Objects that are closer to you always appear bigger than objects that are far away. You might have noticed this while riding in a car at night. If a car is coming toward you, its headlights will grow brighter and larger the closer it gets.
