title: Who Are Scientists and Engineers?
text:
Science is the search for knowledge. Knowledge of general truths or the operations of fundamental laws is used to solve problems through the use of science and engineering practices. Science is the study of the physical world or life and its processes. During their investigations, scientists gather evidence and look for patterns.

People who study science are called scientists. Scientists use systematic methods of study to collect data and make observations. They work to develop theories that help them order or unify related facts. As scientists explore, they answer their questions. Answers to those questions might lead to new questions and answers. As they gather more facts, they are better able to understand how and why something happens or happened. Science provides the basis of much of modern technology that makes our lives easier.

There are many types of scientists. Different types of scientists have different disciplines. A plant scientist is called a botanist. They understand the properties of plants, how plants function, and the habitats of plants. They have developed better varieties of plants and fertilizers. A physicist is a scientist who studies motion and forces. They learn what matter is and why it behaves the way it does. Physicists work with specialized and expensive equipment to study how they can improve manufacturing processes or products.

Engineering is applying science to solve problems. You use what you have learned in science to help you. You use your science skills to solve problems. Engineering is creating or building complex, scientific equipment to bring a solution to a problem.

Engineers apply their scientific knowledge to solve problems. Engineers use principles of science to design structures, machines, and products for practical use. There are different types of engineers. Many branches of engineering overlap. Aerospace engineers create vehicles, aircraft, and rockets that go into space. They work closely with electrical engineers to develop guidance, navigation, and power systems. They work with civil engineers to plan airports and other public facilities. Biomedical engineers create devices to help solve medical problems. They work with chemical engineers to understand how chemical properties interact with each other and with the human body. They have developed new surgical techniques and lifesaving machines. Medical professionals, such as doctors and nurses, use these devices to help others. As new science and technologies develop, new fields of engineering are being created.

You are a scientist and an engineer. Like scientists, you make observations during your investigations. You ask questions and seek answers. You see the world around you and you wonder about it. Like engineers, you see problems that need solutions. You can design tools and methods to solve those problems. Scientists and engineers are not just people in lab coats. They are people like you who are curious about the world around them. They make tools, materials, techniques, and power sources that make life better.

You are a scientist and engineer! Draw a picture of yourself as a scientist or engineer.

title: Tools and Safety
text:
Scientists use many tools to observe things. Tools are devices used to solve a problem. Some of these tools are microscopes, magnifying glasses, binoculars, and telescopes. These tools help scientists look closely at objects that are near or far away. Microscopes magnify objects and details that are too small to be seen by the eye. Physicians and biologists use microscopes to examine cells and tissues. Magnifying glasses make close objects appear larger. They are used to study objects close-up. Scientists use magnifying glasses to study tiny germs and insects. Binoculars and telescopes are used to view objects that are far away. Biologists use binoculars and telescopes to view migrating animals. Astronomers use telescopes to view stars, galaxies, and planets.

Scientists also use tools to help them measure. A ruler or meterstick helps them measure length. Length can be measured using the U.S. standard of measurement: inches, feet, yards, and miles. Length can also be measured using the metric system. The metric system measures length using millimeters, centimeters, meters, and kilometers. Scientists measure objects to make comparisons, like how much a certain animal grows each year.

A thermometer measures temperature. There are three different systems for measuring temperatures: Fahrenheit, Celsius, and Kelvin. The United States uses Fahrenheit to measure temperature. Most of the world uses Celsius to measure temperature. Scientists often use Celsius and Kelvin scales to measure temperatures.

Scientists also use tools to help them stay safe. Safety tools include goggles, lab coats, and gloves. These tools protect the scientists’ eyes, clothes, and hands. When exploring underwater, scientists use tanks filled with oxygen to help them breathe and wet suits to protect their skin.

Engineers also use many different tools to help them build things. They use tools to help them measure and to keep themselves safe. They wear hard hats to protect their heads and earmuffs or headphones to keep their ears safe. They wear masks to keep their lungs safe. They wear gloves and goggles to keep their hands and eyes safe. When you engineer your own project, you will use engineering tools. Using these tools correctly will keep you safe.

It is important to be safe while you do science and engineering. Follow your class rules and your teacher’s instructions. Use the safety tools to protect you. Read the directions. Never taste or smell materials unless your teacher instructs you to do so. Be careful with sharp objects. Keep your hair and clothes tied back. Clean up spills immediately. Tell your teacher about accidents or if you see something that is not safe. Clean up your workstation when you are finished. Wash your hands after every activity. These things will help you not get hurt and will keep your classmates safe. You can learn better when you are safe.

text:

title: Week 5 Inquiry Question
text: What characteristics can be used to define a region?

title: Agriculture in Nebraska
text:
Here in Nebraska, agriculture, or growing crops and raising animals, is a big business. There are about 46,000 farms and ranches in Nebraska. They produce enough grain and meat to feed millions of people. When Americans sit down to a big dinner, chances are that something on the table comes from Nebraska.

Nebraska’s single most important agricultural product is beef, which brings in almost 11 billion dollars each year. Cattle ranches can be found in every region of the state. There are so many cattle in Nebraska that they outnumber people three to one! But the cattle aren’t raised just for their meat. They are also used to make fishing line, leather, and biodegradable outboard motor oil. Nebraska also raises hogs, poultry, sheep, and dairy cattle.

You probably already know Nebraska’s most important crop. If you don’t, the mascot of the University of Nebraska-Lincoln’s football team might give you a hint. That’s right: corn is Nebraska’s top cash crop. It is grown mainly in the eastern part of the state, since there is more rainfall there. But irrigation, or using canals and pipes to bring water to a farm, helps farmers in central and western Nebraska grow corn, too. In fact, there are 21,500 corn farmers tending 9.81 million acres of cropland in the state. Besides being food for humans and livestock, corn can also be used to make bioplastics and ethanol. Nebraska is the second-largest producer of ethanol.

Soybeans are grown in the east, while other edible beans, such as Great Northern beans, are grown in the west, along with sugar beets. Other major crops include wheat, grain, sorghum, rye, and oats.

Let’s not forget Nebraska’s sweetest product: honey. Our honeybees produce more than two million pounds of honey each year. That’s not bad when you consider that one bee produces just one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey over its lifetime (about three weeks).

title: Soils in Nebraska
text:
Nebraska's most important natural resource is the land itself. Nearly all of the land in the state (about 95 percent) is used for farming or ranching. Very few states in America use that much of their land for agriculture. This means that the soil in Nebraska is very important to the farmers and ranchers who live there.

Soil scientists separate soil particles into three sizes. The largest is sand, the second-largest is silt, and the smallest is clay. Each of these particle sizes is present in all soil, but the proportions are different depending on the type of soil.

Most soil in Nebraska is loess, which is made of 20 percent or less of clay, the rest being roughly equal parts sand and silt. Loess is blown into an area by wind and then held down by grasses and other small plants. That’s how Nebraska gets most of its topsoil.

But if loess can blow in, it can also blow out. This is called erosion. Farmers and ranchers need to make sure their soil doesn’t erode. They do this by not plowing under their fields after they are harvested. That way, the old roots can keep the loess down. Farmers can also plant rows of trees to slow down the wind near the ground.

Soil in parts of northwestern Nebraska is made mostly of sand, which is why it’s called the Sandhill Region. This region is best suited to be rangeland for raising cattle. The eastern part of Nebraska has more clay in its soil and is good for growing crops that use a lot of water, such as corn and soybeans. The soil in western Nebraska is mostly made of silt. It is best-suited to growing crops that use less water, such as dry beans and sunflowers.

Each state has a state soil. Nebraska’s state soil is called Holdrege. It is made up mostly of clay and silt. It is found in central and southern Nebraska. It stores water well and is great for growing corn.

title: Weather and Climate
text:
What’s the difference between weather and climate?

Weather is what is happening outside your window right now. Is it hot, cold, wet, dry, calm, stormy, clear, cloudy, or windy? Whatever it is, that is the weather. The weather can also change. In Nebraska, it can change very quickly. In December 2017, the temperature in Scottsbluff fell more than 50 degrees in one day, from 48 to -2 degrees Fahrenheit! Sudden changes in weather can also occur in the form of hailstorms, blizzards, thunderstorms, and tornadoes. Nebraska has an average of 45 tornadoes each year.

Climate is the pattern of weather conditions in an area over a long period of time. We know about the climate of Nebraska because meteorologists, or scientists who study the weather, have been recording weather conditions for many years.

Many words can be used to describe Nebraska's climate: extreme, harsh, unruly. Only the hardiest settlers were able to survive here. The Native Americans learned to survive Nebraska's hard winters long before the settlers came. The temperatures in our state can be severely cold in the winter (as low as -45 degrees Fahrenheit) and very hot in the summer (more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit). Nebraska also experiences both droughts and flooding.

Despite these extremes, Nebraska has pleasant spring and fall seasons; low humidity, moisture in the air, and long growing seasons. Temperatures in the southern part of the state are generally warmer than in northern Nebraska. Nebraska's rainfall is considered light, with the state average being about 23 inches per year. Eastern Nebraska receives about 28 inches of rain each year, while the western part receives only about 16 inches.

title: Precipitation
text:
Since Nebraska relies so much on agriculture, water is essential to the state’s well-being. The amount of rainfall, or precipitation, is different depending on which part of the state you’re in. In the western part of Nebraska, only about 16 inches of precipitation falls each year. It is a semiarid climate. But in eastern Nebraska, about 28 inches of rain falls each year. It is a humid climate.

Water is always moving through a cycle that takes it from the earth to the sky and back again. We call it the hydrologic cycle, or the water cycle. “Hydro” means water.

The water cycle begins with the sun. The sun heats the Earth and begins changing water from a liquid to vapor. This is called evaporation. The vapor rises high into the sky, leaving behind salt, pollution, or other impurities it might have been mixed with.

The vapor meets up with other water vapor, and it combines to form clouds. When the clouds cool down, the vapor turns back into liquid and falls to the ground as rain, snow, or hail. In some parts of the world, large mountains stand in the way of clouds. When the clouds are stopped by the mountains, they drop their moisture.

When the snow melts and rain falls, it trickles down the sides of mountains and hills. It gathers into cracks and low places and becomes creeks, streams, and rivers. The little rivers join others to form larger rivers. And where does all this rushing water go? To the lowest place it can find. This is usually a lake or the ocean. But sometimes it just soaks into the ground.

The water cycle cleans our water so that living things can use it. However, when pollution is in the air, clean rain washes the impurities back to the earth, and sometimes that rainwater isn't safe to use. When pollution soaks into the ground, underground layers of clean water become dirty.

A huge part of Nebraska’s water supply is made up of groundwater. The state sits over the top of the gigantic High Plains Aquifer, also called the Ogallala Aquifer. An aquifer is a pocket of groundwater, like an underground lake. The High Plains Aquifer stretches beneath eight states, but it is at its biggest beneath Nebraska. It provides drinking water to 82 percent of the 2.3 million people who live in the High Plains. It provides irrigation to numerous farms and ranches in Nebraska.

The aquifer is very large, but it could dry up if it is overused. Farmers, ranchers, and scientists have found ways of using less water so that we can have plenty of water in the future.

title: Airports in Nebraska
text:
There are approximately 82 public airports in Nebraska. The biggest is Eppley Airfield, near Omaha. The airport was built in 1929. A stunt pilot, Eugene Eppley, built up a national chain of hotels and donated one million dollars to the airport in 1960. The money paid for a new terminal and a runway long enough for jets to land on. Since transcontinental flights had become popular by then, the airport expanded to service the jets. Now, Eppley Airfield hosts nearly four million airline travelers each year.

Lincoln has the second-largest airport in Nebraska. Lincoln’s connection to aviation started in 1910 at the Nebraska State Fair. Arch Hoxey, a Nebraska native, flew one of the Wright Brothers’ planes multiple times at the fair. During one flight, his plane crashed into the roof of a building, but he survived. In 1922, a young man named Charles Lindbergh came to Lincoln to learn how to fly. Five years later, in 1927, he became the first person to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.

The Lincoln Municipal Airport was dedicated in 1930. Its first terminal was built in 1941. The airport as we now know it was built in 1974. It has a 12,901-foot runway. The runway was built that long so it could act as an emergency landing site for the Space Shuttle. But the Shuttle has never needed it.

The Central Nebraska Regional Airport is Nebraska’s third-largest airport. It is in Grand Island. It started in the 1920s as a grass field, but it now serves hundreds of flights each year. Twenty-three percent of the flights that go in and out of the airport are passenger airlines. The rest are general aviation and military flights.

Far toward Nebraska’s western border is the Western Nebraska Regional Airport. It was established in Scottsbluff in 1934. During World War II, it was a military airbase, where the Air Force trained aircrews to fly B-17 and B-24 bombers. It became very popular on August 21, 2017, when it was in the path of a total solar eclipse.

title: The Building of I-80
text:
It’s about 450 miles from Omaha to the western border of Nebraska’s panhandle. During the 1800s, it would take settlers about a month to cross that distance if they traveled 15 miles every day. Today, it takes about six and a half hours to make the same trip if you’re driving on Interstate 80.

As it was being built, many things affected which route I-80 took. The federal government required that I-80 connect Omaha, Lincoln, Grand Island, and other major cities along the Platte River. But it was left to Nebraska officials to choose the actual route between those points.

The problem was that no matter which route the highway took, it would affect something. Some towns wanted to be connected to the rest of Nebraska through I-80. Other towns wanted to be left alone. Sometimes the planned route would cut a farm in half. Sometimes it would go through a city park or neighborhood. Sometimes it would encounter a pioneer or Native American cemetery. Sometimes it would expose fossil beds. In all these cases, problems had to be solved. The bones of four previously unknown prehistoric animals were uncovered during I-80’s construction.

Starting at Fort Kearny, in central Nebraska, I-80 follows the path that hundreds of thousands of settlers followed during the 1800s. It was called the Great Platte River Road. The Transcontinental Railroad later followed this same route. As you drive west from Fort Kearny you can see the same landscape the settlers saw. They followed this route partially because they could get water from the Platte River. It was part of the California, Oregon, and Mormon Trails west.

title: Lincoln, Nebraska
text:
Lincoln, the capital city of Nebraska, was named after President Abraham Lincoln. It is the second-largest city in Nebraska, with a population of over 286,000. The people of Lincoln are known for being caring and helpful. City leaders have worked hard to create a culture of equity and inclusion and a place where everyone feels welcome.

Lincoln is a modern and well-functioning city with specific plans in place to encourage growth, to protect the environment, and to help businesses and people succeed. Lincoln has a strong economy. There are many jobs in the service and manufacturing industries. The main campus of the University of Nebraska is located in Lincoln. It brings in students from all over the world and provides jobs for many people. Other industries in Lincoln include finance, insurance, publishing, railroads, and information technology. In fact, some of the state’s biggest and most successful tech companies are in Lincoln.

Outdoor recreation is a large part of what makes Lincoln an exciting place to live. There are over 6,000 acres of parks and 130 miles of trails. There are rivers and lakes, public pools, golf courses, and countless other outdoor activities. Spending time outdoors is linked to improved health and well-being. Lincoln was named the “Happiest City in America” by a top health magazine.

The city is also filled with museums, theaters, and other cultural centers, like gardens, art shows, and a children’s zoo. If you are a sports fan, you can go to a rodeo, run a marathon, watch soccer, hockey, or baseball, or cheer for the famous Huskers football team. There is something for everyone in this exciting city!

title: Week 10 Inquiry Question
text: Why do people choose to live in Nebraska?

title: The Population of Nebraska
text:
When people are deciding where to live, they look for a place that has physical characteristics and natural resources that can provide the things they need and want. Families look for places that give them opportunities to make a good life for themselves. Why do people choose to live here in Nebraska?

Population

Nebraska is the 16th-largest state in the country by area, but it ranks 37th by population. The population is the number of people living in an area. When Nebraska was organized as a territory, its population was about 3,000. Six years later, in 1860, the population had jumped to nearly 30,000 people. After the Civil War ended in 1865, the Homestead Act led to another increase in population. Over time, the numbers have gone up slowly but steadily, and now there are close to two million people living here.

Nebraska’s Largest Cities

Over half of the people in Nebraska live in the state's three largest counties: Douglas, Lancaster, and Sarpy. About one in three people live in its two major cities: Omaha and Lincoln. The next-largest cities are Bellevue, Grand Island, and Kearney. Many cities have fewer than 3,000 people, and hundreds of towns in Nebraska have fewer than 1,000 residents. The land between populated communities is filled with farms and ranches, rolling hills and prairies, wetlands, wildlife reserves, and state and national parks.

Omaha: 479,529

Nebraska's biggest city was settled in 1854. It was named for the Omaha Tribe, one of the Indigenous tribes who originally lived there. Over the years, the city of Omaha has welcomed many different groups of people who came to earn a living and find a home. Germans, Scandinavians, Mexicans, and many others have added to the unique blend of cultures in Omaha.

Lincoln: 286,388

Lincoln was founded in 1856 as the village of Lancaster. When Nebraska was granted statehood in 1867, the village was chosen as the capital and renamed Lincoln. The capitol building, built in 1932, has been called one of the most beautiful public buildings in the country.

Bellevue: 63,970

Bellevue began as a fur trading post and was founded in 1822. It sits on rolling hills overlooking the Missouri River. It is the oldest town in Nebraska and the oldest town in America west of the Missouri River.

Grand Island: 51,250

In the 1850s, as wagon trains rolled through what used to be called “The Great American Desert,” a group of German-speaking immigrants heard about the plans to build a transcontinental railroad. They stopped and formed a town near the east end of an island on the Platte River. Today, Grand Island is known as the hub of central Nebraska.

Kearney: 33,783

This city began in 1848 as a fort built along the Oregon Trail. It provided protection to thousands of pioneers, Pony Express riders, and prospectors traveling west. For a period of time during the Gold Rush, as many as 500 wagons might stop by in a single day! In the 1880s, it was one of the biggest and busiest communities in Nebraska.

title: Changing Demographics
text:
Diversity

The population of Nebraska continues to become more diverse. When a state is diverse, it means the population includes people from many different backgrounds and cultures. Information from the 2010 and 2020 censuses shows how Nebraska’s demographics are changing. Demographics are data that tells us about the characteristics of a population.

Immigration

Immigrants come from all over the world and settle in the United States. Sometimes people come for job opportunities or to be close to family members. These reasons are called “pull factors.” Nebraska has a diverse immigrant population. Immigrants make up seven percent of our state’s population. About one in 14 modern Nebraskans was born in another country. Historically, German Americans were the largest immigrant group in Nebraska. We also have the largest Czech American population in the United States. Some of the top countries of origin of immigrants today are Mexico, Guatemala, and India.

Sometimes, people come because of problems in their home countries. These problems are things like war, violence, or natural disasters. We call these “push factors.” Nebraska has been a national leader in welcoming refugees who have been forced to leave their countries. In 2016, Nebraska took in a higher share of refugees than any other state. Lincoln has America’s largest population of Yazidi refugees and Yazidi Americans. Omaha has welcomed a significant number of Karen refugees from Burma.

Immigrants are an important part of our community. They add billions of dollars to Nebraska’s economy. They help strengthen our labor force and fill the need for young workers across the state. Over one-third of people who have immigrated to Nebraska are now U.S. citizens. Immigrants work in many industries, including manufacturing, production, computer and mathematical sciences, health care, educational services, and construction.

title: Population Growth Over Time
text:
In the early 1800s, Native American communities, a few fur traders, government officials, and church missionaries lived in Nebraska. In 1854, the land was officially opened for settlement. Westward expansion and the Gold Rush pushed people into the Nebraska Territory, and over the next 35 years, nearly one million settlers moved to Nebraska.

Since the 1900s, the population of Nebraska has risen slowly. In fact, the state’s growth has been consistently slower than the United States’ average. In 1940, the census showed that the population had actually dropped from what it was 10 years earlier. A census is a measure of people living in a certain area. In 2021, the U.S. Census Project released data showing that for the first time in over 100 years, Nebraska’s population was growing at the same rate as the rest of the nation.

Scholars at the University of Omaha study each census and other data in order to predict how the population might change in the future. Population predictions, also called projections, help a state to plan and prepare for the changes. In 2015, using the current population structure and applying birth, death, and migration rates, scholars projected that the population of Nebraska would reach two million in 2030.

title: Population Density
text:
Population size is the number of individuals in a population. Population density is the average number of people living in each square mile. The number is found by dividing the total population by the land area. Population distribution is how people are spread across a specific area. It shows the pattern of where people live.

This population map shows the pattern of human settlement in the United States. It shows the average number of people who live on one square mile of land. The dark red areas of the map show where the most people live, or the most dense populations. The light yellow areas of the map show where few people live.

This population map shows the settlement pattern in our state. Nebraska’s surface area is approximately 77,354 square miles. That makes it the 16th-largest state in the U.S. in terms of size. What do you notice about the distribution of people across the state?

Jack found some beans that he believed were magic. He decided to plant them, even though his mother disagreed. The next morning, Jack woke up to a beanstalk that reached all the way to the clouds. It was enormous! Jack decided to explore the beanstalk. He climbed and climbed until he reached the top. On top of the clouds, he found a castle that was large enough to be home to a giant. He explored the clouds around the castle and found a golden goose that seemed to lay golden eggs. He decided to go back down to the ground to show the goose to his mother.

On his way back to the beanstalk, Jack felt the clouds begin to shake under his feet. He slowly turned around and saw the giant that inhabited the huge house. Before the giant noticed him, Jack scurried down the beanstalk with the goose. He ran back home, yelling, “There is a giant on the beanstalk!” The whole town, who were confused about the beanstalk to begin with, were startled by the news and decided to call a town meeting. They requested that Jack come to the meeting and explain to them what was happening.

When Jack arrived, the townspeople began discussing the dangers that this beanstalk had created for the community. What if it fell? How many resources was it taking from the town? Worst of all, what if the giant came down and attacked the town to get his golden goose back? Jack realized he had made a mistake by planting this beanstalk.

What should the town do to handle the situation of the beanstalk? How should it be removed without the giant coming down? Should the goose be returned? Should Jack get in trouble?

title: Natural Features of Nebraska
text:
Water

Nebraska has 22,000 miles of streams. In the Sandhills Region alone, there are hundreds of small and shallow lakes.

The two major rivers in Nebraska are the Missouri and Platte rivers. The Platte River is made up of two branches, the North Platte and the South Platte. The river begins in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado. They empty into the Missouri River, which is the eastern border of Nebraska.

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. It flows from Montana all the way to the Mississippi River. It provided transportation early in the settlement of the United States. Now, it also provides electricity, water, and recreation.

Sandhills

Sandhills cover roughly one-fourth of Nebraska, or about 19,600 square miles. The area is large enough to hold both Vermont and New Hampshire. The sandhills were shaped by erosion into low hills and ridges. There is a thin layer of soil over the sandhills that allows grass to grow. The grass makes excellent feed for cattle. In fact, cattle outnumber people in the sandhills area.

Mountains

Courthouse Rock and Jail Rock in Morrill County were among the first landmarks seen by settlers as they headed west through Nebraska. However, the most famous Nebraska landform is Chimney Rock, which is 500 feet high. It is located in the western part of Nebraska, near the Wyoming border. The Sioux name for it meant “the hill that is hard to go around.” From the base of the bluff, settlers traveling the Oregon Trail would get their first glimpse of the Rocky Mountains.

Plains

Plains are vast stretches of mostly flat land. The plains of Nebraska have a cold, semi-arid climate. They receive 10-20 inches of precipitation each year. Though Nebraska’s plains are flat, they have a high elevation. Steady, and sometimes intense, winds blow across the plains. The winds make the plains a perfect place for wind farms, which use windmills to produce electricity.

title: How Are Goods Produced?
text:
People have grown corn in North America for thousands of years. It is a very useful crop. Only one percent of the corn grown in the U.S. is for people to eat. The other 99 percent gets used in other products that we use every day. Corn is used to meet many different types of needs.

There are three basic types of corn. Corn grown for people to eat is called sweet corn. It has more sugar in its kernels and doesn’t pop. The corn grown for making other products is called field corn, or dent corn. When this type of corn is dried, the kernels become dented. The third type of corn is popcorn. This type of corn has a higher moisture content in its kernels, which causes them to pop when heated.

Sometimes we eat sweet corn right off the cob. Sweet corn can be frozen or canned for later use, too. We use whole kernels of field corn to feed animals or turn into other products. But most field corn gets processed, or changed, to make it more usable. Processed corn becomes an ingredient in other products. It can be turned into ethanol fuel. It can be turned into a starch or a syrup. Corn starch and corn syrup are added to many products. There are about 4,000 products in your grocery store that list corn as an ingredient!

Today, people get most of their food from grocery stores. With ships, airplanes, and refrigerated trucks, food can travel around the world. This makes our food supply more interdependent. Interdependent means that people and communities depend on each other to provide what they need. One farmer does not grow all the kinds of food we need. They usually grow just one kind of food and then export it, or ship it, to other places. Our grocery stores have food from all over the world. We can buy apples from Washington. We can buy bananas from Ecuador. Corn from Nebraska gets transported to other parts of the United States. It also gets transported around the world.

title: Farm to Table
text:
How Is Corn Produced?

Nebraska is a great place for farming. It has some of the most fertile soil in the nation. Over 90 percent of the land in the state is farmland. Nebraska is the nation’s third-largest producer of corn. Nebraska farmers plant corn in the spring so that the soil will be warm. Farmers use technology to help them plant the corn in straight rows. This helps with pollination and harvesting. Farmers hook a planter up to a tractor, and a GPS system shows them exactly where to plant the kernels. Each kernel needs the right amount of space to get enough nutrients, water, and sun.

Over the summer, the corn plants grow. Their leaves take in heat and sunlight. Their roots soak up water and nutrients. Each plant will grow two ears of corn. Hundreds of long plant fibers, called corn silks, grow from each ear. The silks get pollinated. Once they are pollinated, each silk forms a new kernel. These kernels grow on the cob until they are ripe.

Processing: How Is Corn Harvested?

Field corn gets harvested when the whole plant, including the kernels, dries out. Sweet corn is different. The ears and plants are still green at harvest time. The kernels are still soft. Farmers know to harvest sweet corn when the silk on the end of the ears turns brown.

Sweet corn can be harvested by hand or by machine. As the ears are picked, workers sort them by hand. They pack the ears into crates that weigh about 42 pounds each. Each crate holds about five dozen ears of corn.

As soon as an ear of corn is picked, the sugar in its kernels begins to change into starch. Starchy corn is less sweet. Temperatures are usually hot when farmers harvest sweet corn in late summer. It is important to cool the ears within hours of the harvest because cooling slows the process of sugar becoming starch. Farmers run cold water through crates of packed ears to cool them down.

Distribution: How Does Corn Get to Market?

The clock starts ticking on fresh sweet corn as soon as the harvest begins. Farmers store the crates of cooled ears in sheds. Sweet corn can be stored for 5–8 days. The sooner farmers can ship the corn, the better.

Fresh sweet corn ships in refrigerated trucks or rail cars. Shipping temperatures are kept at around freezing so that the sugars inside the kernels can stay sweet.

Once the corn reaches stores, employees set the corn out. Stores buy sweet corn by the crate. They sell the corn to the customers, who can cook it right away, store the ears in the fridge, or freeze them.

title: Entrepreneur: "Buffalo Bill" Cody
text:
William F. Cody was born in 1846 in the state of Iowa. Cody wasn't able to attend much school. His father died when he was just 11 years old. To help support his family, he began hauling goods on a wagon freight train. For a while, he worked for the famous teamsters Russell, Majors, and Waddell. He rode for the Pony Express when he was only 14 years old.

Cody was a skilled marksman, and while he was still in his teens, he got a job as a professional bison hunter for the railroad. Bison meat was used to feed the men working on the Kansas Pacific Railroad. His great skill earned him the nickname "Buffalo Bill." "Buffalo" is another name for bison.

Cody was a scout in the Union Army during the Civil War. Army scouts served as guides and traders. They delivered messages to other army camps. Cody was commended for his endurance, courage, and heroism as an Army scout. After serving in the war, he was often hired as a guide on bison hunts. Wealthy people would pay him large fees to lead them.

In 1882, Cody, or, as many now called him, Buffalo Bill, organized North Platte's Fourth of July celebration, called "The Old Glory Blowout." He must have enjoyed putting on that show, because the next year, he organized his "Wild West Show," which ran for the next 30 years! Buffalo Bill took his show all over the country. It became very popular. His "Wild West Show" eventually employed nearly 700 people.

With the money Buffalo Bill made from his show, he built a large ranch that people can still visit today: Scout's Rest, near North Platte. His ranch proved to be very profitable. He raised cattle and thoroughbred stallions. He even planted 1,200 acres of corn, alfalfa, and oats. The ranch and big red barn have been restored. They have become a state park, where you can see some of "Buffalo Bill" Cody’s possessions and memorabilia.

title: Ethanol
text:
Corn ethanol is produced when water is added to corn flour and the mixture is heated. The starch in the corn gets broken down into sugars. After those sugars go through another process, they become an alcohol called ethanol.

Ethanol is a common ingredient in many personal care products. It helps hairspray stick to hair. It kills bacteria and many viruses, so it is in hand sanitizer. For the same reason, ethanol is used in many cleaning products. It is found in some types of paint because it helps the paint dry smoother and faster.

The biggest use for ethanol is as fuel. Ethanol is added to gasoline to help the gas burn efficiently in the engine and create less pollution. This means we can use less gasoline. About 31 percent of the corn grown in Nebraska is used to make ethanol. There are 24 ethanol plants in Nebraska, making our state the second-largest ethanol producer in the U.S.

title: Cornhuskers
text: The legacy of the Cornhuskers began in 1890, when the University of Nebraska-Lincoln’s football team defeated a YMCA team from Omaha. It was the only game they played that year. They played only one game in 1891, too. They didn’t even have a coach until 1893. In fact, they weren’t even called the Cornhuskers to begin with. Over the years, they have been called the Tree-Planters, Rattlesnake Boys, Antelopes, Old Gold Knights, and the Bugeaters. It wasn’t until 1899 that Charles "Cy" Sherman, a sports journalist, used the nickname “Cornhuskers,” and the name stuck. Huskers football has a big impact on the economy of Nebraska, especially in Lincoln. One of the positive ways that sports influence communities is by bringing people together. Millions of dollars are spent every year when people come to games. People need places to stay and food to eat. They have to buy tickets to the game. This creates jobs and opportunities for local businesses.

title: Memorials and Monuments
text: Memorials are symbols or ceremonies that remind us of important people or events in which people died. Monuments can be a type of memorial. Monuments are buildings, structures, or sites that honor people and events in history. National memorials and monuments honor the country's history. People can visit national memorials and monuments. They can learn why these places are important to the United States. Knowing the history of our country helps to unite us as citizens.

text: Why do we celebrate patriotic holidays?

title: Patriotic Celebrations
text: We celebrate the history of the United States. We celebrate important events that shaped the nation. We celebrate heroic people who protect our freedom. We honor people who made a difference in the lives of others. We celebrate in many ways.

title: We the People Face Challenges
text:
After the Constitutional Convention, George Washington of Virginia was unanimously elected the president of the United States. The first Congress met and began the business of governing. There were many challenges facing the new federal government. Some of those challenges were because of new laws. Some challenges were inherited from the old system.

One challenge inherited from the old system was the debt created from the war. The cost of keeping an army supplied during the Revolutionary War had added up. Under the Articles of Confederation, the individual states were responsible for paying off this debt. However, the Confederation Congress did not have the power to collect tax money. The new federal government, however, had a taxation system in place. The new secretary of the treasury, Alexander Hamilton, created a plan. To give the new government a positive financial system, he suggested that the war debt be paid in full. After much debate, he persuaded the federal government to pay off the debt. To pay the debt, the Bank of the United States was established, and a system of currency, or money, was created that is still in place today. To strengthen the United States, Hamilton proposed that the United States promote manufacturing. He also advocated that the country limit its trade dependency on manufactured goods from Europe.

Another challenge the new government faced was how to balance the demands of manufacturing and agriculture. Manufacturing favored the northern states but diminished the agricultural plantation system of the southern states. Thomas Jefferson, in contrast, promoted policies that favored agriculture and the southern states. Hamilton and Jefferson’s opinions created two different ways of thinking that eventually led to two political parties. The two parties were the Federalists and the Democratic Republicans. Hamilton led the Federalists. Jefferson led the Democratic Republicans.

By 1798, Washington had retired as president. John Adams, a Federalist, was the second president. Thomas Jefferson, a Democratic Republican, was vice president. The two parties had such differing opinions on every topic that there was constant conflict in the government. The Federalists accused the opposing views of the other party as being disloyal to the Constitution.

Congress passed the Alien and Sedition Acts. These Acts targeted immigration and immigrants living in the United States. The Acts also made it a crime for American citizens to “print, utter, or publish ... any false, scandalous, and malicious [hostile] writing” about the federal government. These legal actions were a direct challenge to the First Amendment, especially freedom of speech and the press. Many newspaper journalists who supported Jefferson’s political party were arrested and shut down for printing material that opposed the Federalists.

John Adams ran for re-election in 1800 against Thomas Jefferson and Aaron Burr. Jefferson and Burr received the majority of votes in a tie. As directed in the Constitution, the election went to the House of Representatives to break the tie. After weeks of discussion and voting, with a tie occurring each time, Alexander Hamilton stepped up to endorse Thomas Jefferson over his friend, Aaron Burr. This swayed enough House members to vote for Jefferson as president. Burr conceded defeat and became vice president. The first peaceful transfer of power occurred after a very tense election process. Burr’s peaceful concession strengthened the Constitution and the new country.

The Alien and Sedition Acts were repealed, or not renewed. President Jefferson began his administration by looking to give more power to the states. However, as time passed, an opportunity would come that made Jefferson stretch the authority of the presidency. He made the largest land purchase in the history of the United States.

title: The Northwest Ordinance, 1787
text:
When the new United States government signed the Treaty of Paris with Great Britain in 1783, they gained more than just the land within the 13 American Colonies. They also received a large area of land west of the colonies that came to be known as the Northwest Territory. The question of what was to happen with this unorganized territory was one of the first major issues faced by the new country. The answers to this question would impact all future U.S. land claims and territories.

Each new state wanted to gain as much land as they could for themselves, and Virginia was moving aggressively to claim as much of the Northwest Territory as they could. Small eastern states like Connecticut and Rhode Island had no realistic claim to the territory because they were separated from it by other states.

Because of this, they opposed the enlargement of states like Virginia. Giving those states more land would make them more powerful in the new national government. As a democracy, the states with more land and more people would have a larger say in how the country was run.

To further complicate issues of land in the West, soldiers from the Continental Army were given pieces of land for their service during the Revolutionary War. Those former soldiers and other settlers moving west began claiming land for themselves. Some argued that they had bought the land from Native Americans, while others simply chose an empty piece of land upon which to build their homestead. This led to arguments and disputes over land ownership.

To solve these problems, Congress passed the Northwest Ordinance of 1787. The Ordinance laid out the process by which the Northwest Territory, and future territories, would be admitted as a state to the country. It also ensured that each new state would be equal to all other states, which is not something that was guaranteed before the ordinance was passed.

Each territory would have a governor and other government officials appointed by the U.S. Congress. Once 5,000 free men were living in a territory, it would need to have an elected legislative body. Finally, once the population reached 60,000 people and a state constitution had been drafted, the territory could apply for statehood. The ordinance also outlawed slavery in any newly created territory, which would have major consequences as there was increased conflict over the issue of slavery between the states into the 1800s.

However, the specific question of what to do with the Northwest Territory remained. Using the guidance of the Northwest Ordinance of 1787, Congress eventually annexed Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Minnesota into the United States from the land that originally made up the Northwest Territory.

title: Jefferson Becomes President
text:
The election of Thomas Jefferson in 1800 was the first peaceful transfer of power for the United States. There were many disagreements over the presidency between the two major political parties, the Federalists and the Democratic Republicans, or Anti-Federalists. After many weeks, both sides came to a compromise and Jefferson was elected president. Jefferson was a firm believer in the tenets of the Constitution. He wished to strengthen these principles through his presidency. His first goal as president was to create peaceful cooperation between the Federalists and the Democratic Republicans. This was not an easy task. In many ways, it wasn't successful because both groups had opposing beliefs and ideas.

Jefferson also had to attend to U.S. foreign policy issues. Foreign policy is how one country interacts with other countries. During his second term, Washington had signed a Proclamation of Neutrality that prevented the United States from entering foreign conflicts. Jefferson agreed that the United States should remain neutral and not enter foreign wars. France and Great Britain were at war with one another. The United States refused to enter the conflict.

Jefferson and his cabinet hoped to maintain a friendship with both countries. This angered Great Britain. The British Navy blockaded European ports. This affected American trade immensely. The British also seized American goods and forced American sailors to work on British vessels. In response, Jefferson asked Congress to expand the U.S. Navy and restrict the import of goods from Great Britain.

Jefferson served a second term as president from 1804 to 1808. Hostilities between France and Great Britain continued, as did their issues with U.S. neutrality. Both countries attacked American ships and seized their cargo. Jefferson encouraged Congress to act. In 1807, the government passed the Embargo Act. An embargo is an order to stop ships from delivering goods. The law stated that goods couldn't be shipped to any foreign port.

The United States hoped that both France and Great Britain would be devastated without American supplies. Unfortunately, the Embargo Act backfired. Great Britain and France survived without U.S. goods. The U.S. economy, on the other hand, suffered greatly due to the act, angering American citizens. President Jefferson repealed the Embargo Act before leaving office in March of 1809.

title: The Supreme Court
text:
Established by the United States Constitution, the Supreme Court began to take shape with the passage of the Judiciary Act of 1789. At this time, a position on the Court was not seen as glamorous. The networks of courts under the Supreme Court required the Justices (members of the Court) to visit frequently. This required days of travel in poor conditions.

At first, the Justices would not stay in the Court for their life appointments as suggested in the Constitution. This changed when outgoing president John Adams appointed John Marshall as Chief Justice in 1800. John Marshall served as Chief Justice for 34 years until 1834. Several of his fellow Justices served for more than 20 years.

As the country grew and the government implemented the Constitution, there were many judicial reviews conducted by the Supreme Court. The justices reviewed the laws to determine if they were in agreement with the Constitution. When a law was not in line with the rights of the people as outlined in the Constitution, the law was labeled as unconstitutional. It was no longer considered a law. When a law was “upheld” by the Supreme Court, it meant it supported the rights protected in the Constitution and was considered law.

These reviews provided a check and balance of power designed by the Founding Fathers.

title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
text: Martin Luther King Jr. was an important person in United States history. He believed in equal rights for all people. He taught people that everyone should be treated equally. He used words to solve problems. He was born on January 15, 1929. On the third Monday in January, we honor and remember his work.

title: Foreign Policy
text:
It is important for nations to get along with each other for many reasons. Foreign policy is the government’s guidelines for business with other countries. Some countries wanted to be friends with the new United States. Others wanted to challenge the new government.

The continued rivalry of the governments in Europe caused concern in America. The British were still occupying areas of Canada. France had colonies in the Caribbean. Spain had colonies in Mexico and the southwest territory of North America. These colonies were gaining independence. The United States was concerned that the other European governments would try to restore the colonies.

President James Monroe issued a foreign policy order in 1823 known as the Monroe Doctrine.

“The American continents, by the free and independent condition which they have assumed and maintain, are henceforth not to be considered as subjects for colonization by any European powers.”

This policy described that any attempt by a European power to exert its influence in the Western Hemisphere would, from then on, be seen by the United States as a threat to its security.

The Monroe Doctrine is still a part of U.S. foreign policy today.

title: The First Census: 1790
text:
A government based on representation has to have an accurate count of its population. To determine the members in the House of Representatives, a census would be required. Article 2 of the U.S. Constitution requires a complete count of the population every 10 years. Aug. 2, 1790, was the first census day. Under the direction of Thomas Jefferson, the then-secretary of state, the census was taken in the original 13 states. They also included the districts of Kentucky, Maine, Vermont, and the Southwest Territory (Tennessee).

The 1790 census wanted the following information:

Name of the head of the family

Number of free white males 16 years old or older

Number of free white males younger than 16 years old

Number of free white females

Number of all other free persons

Number of enslaved persons

The census determined that there were four million people in the country in 1790. This census gives us a glimpse at the families and settlements of the new nation. The census records are available today through the United States Census Bureau.

title: Veterans Day
text: A veteran is any person who has served in the military. November 11 is the day we honor veterans. We remember their sacrifice and service for the country. We can show our respect by flying the American flag.

title: Juneteenth
text:
Juneteenth is short for “June 19th.” It is a special day for African Americans. In 1863, President Lincoln signed an important document. It set enslaved people in the United States free. It was called the Emancipation Proclamation. General Granger landed in Galveston, Texas, on June 19, 1865. He issued orders to free enslaved people in Texas.

African American communities have celebrated Juneteenth for many years. They hold church services and parties. Some cities hold big celebrations with parades. In 2021, the president of the United States made Juneteenth a national holiday.

title: Labor Day
text: Labor Day is a holiday. We celebrate Labor Day on the first Monday in September. On this holiday, we remember workers throughout the country’s history. Labor Day honors those who work hard to make the country strong and prosperous. Labor Day honors workers’ well-being.

title: Independence Day
text: The Fourth of July is also called Independence Day. The Declaration of Independence was voted on and accepted on July 4, 1776. This is the day we celebrate the United States becoming a country. We honor the people who worked for freedom. Many people celebrate this holiday. People watch parades and spend time with family and friends. People also watch fireworks.

title: Memorial Day
text: Memorial Day is a national holiday. We celebrate Memorial Day on the last Monday of May. We honor the people who died while serving the country.

title: How the War Was Fought in the South
text:
In the summer of 1778, the British soldiers realized that they were not winning the war in the Northern and Middle Colonies. So, they turned their attention to the Southern Colonies. Many southern colonists remained loyal to the soldiers and provided additional support to them. The British military was confident that it could defeat the Patriot forces in the south.

Fighting in the Southern Colonies was different from fighting in the Northern or Middle Colonies. The weather, land, and plants were different. The southern states were also less populated.

The geography of the Southern Colonies had wide, rolling hills and open fields. There were large areas of thick woodlands, and there were also great areas of marshland. The natural features of the South were spread farther apart than features found in the close terrain of the Appalachian Mountains. Movement was easy in the fields, but the marshes and swamps were more difficult to navigate. The woodlands were so thick that wagons couldn’t travel through them.

The Southern Colonies had a large number of Loyalists in each colony. The British army appealed to their loyalty and asked the Loyalists to share information about their Patriot neighbors. This created a great amount of tension between neighbors and friends. Friendships were questioned, and in the name of the king, some friendships ended.

The Patriot forces were usually outnumbered by the British forces. The British forces were also better trained, so the Patriot forces had to find other ways to win.

Typical battles during the Revolution required two armies to face each other in an open field. However, the Patriot forces learned another strategy from the American Indians. A small group of Patriots would hide in the underbrush and launch a surprise attack on the larger British army. Then, the Patriots would run back into the forest and marshland, letting the British soldiers chase them. They weakened the British army this way. Patriot soldiers also attacked British supply lines, which made it hard for the British soldiers to receive the food and support they needed.

British generals felt the American Patriots were not honorable in the way they fought. However, the Americans were fighting for independence. They believed they had to use the strategies that would help them win.

title: Nebraska Settled
text:
The area we now know as Nebraska was part of the northern half of the Louisiana Purchase. Nebraska was named after the Otoe tribe’s name for the Platte River. People who lived east of the Missouri River thought Nebraska was a big desert and an undesirable place to live. Many Native Americans who had been forced off their lands in the east had been sent to live on this “undesirable” land. Other Indigenous tribes had lived on these lands for centuries.

In the 1840s, settlers east of the Missouri River started to realize that Nebraska had fertile soil and good weather for farming and ranching. Many of them wanted to move to Nebraska.

The Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854

For the American government, figuring out how to organize settlement in the west wasn’t easy. There was the big issue of slavery. The states that had already been settled were divided over slavery. The southern states, were slave states, where enslaved people could be bought and sold as property. Enslaved people had no rights. They could not own property or vote. They were not even thought of as people. The states in the north were considered free states. This meant that it was not legal to own enslaved people in these states. The disagreement about whether slavery should be allowed anywhere in the United States was becoming more and more contentious. That disagreement would eventually become the Civil War.

Pro-slavery people and anti-slavery people could not agree on whether Nebraska should allow slavery. How would they solve this argument? In 1854, the United States Congress passed the Kansas-Nebraska Act. This law said that when the Kansas and Nebraksa territories wanted to join the Union as states, the people in those territories would vote on the slavery question.

The Kansas-Nebraska Act made it possible for more people from the east to settle in Nebraska. It also added more fuel to the fire between slave states and free states. The Nebraska Territory became a place where pro-slavery people and anti-slavery people argued and sometimes fought.

The Homestead Act of 1862

The U.S. government wanted to encourage people from the east to move to Nebraska. In 1862, Congress passed a law called the Homestead Act. The law said that people could own 160 acres of land in the western territories just by moving there, living there for five years, and paying a low price for the land. Thousands of people came to Nebraska because of the Homestead Act. Most came from the eastern part of the United States, but some came from other countries. After a few years, there were thousands of small farms in the Nebraska Territory.

The Homestead Act hurt the Native American tribes who lived in the Nebraska Territory. It took away land that the U.S. government had given to them. It gave that land to white settlers.

title: Timeline of Settlement and Statehood
text:
8000 B.C.E.: The earliest known time when Indigenous peoples lived in the area we now call Nebraska

1682 C.E.: The Kingdom of France claims a huge part of North America, including the land that would become Nebraska.

1762: Spain receives the land from France at the end of the Seven Years’ War.

1800: The land is returned to French control.

1803: France sells the land to the United States. It is called the Louisiana Purchase. This brings almost 800,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River into the U.S. government’s control. Native Americans are still the only people living in Nebraska.

1804: The Lewis and Clark Expedition visits Nebraska. Lewis and Clark are explorers sent by the U. S. government to map the western part of North America.

1825-1892: Treaties between Native American tribes and the U.S. government force tribes to give up land. Native Americans are forced to leave or live on reservations in Nebraska.

1840s: White settlers from the United States travel through Nebraska on their way to settlements in Oregon, California, and Utah.

1854: Congress passes the Kansas-Nebraska Act, opening the Nebraska Territory to settlement.

1862: Congress passes the Homestead Act. This law makes land available for white settlers from the east to start farms and ranches in Nebraska.

1867: Nebraska is admitted to the Union as the 37th state.

Some tribes are using the land they get back to teach people about their history. Many tribes have built museums or villages to show what life was like for them in the past. Museums are places that hold objects found in nature. They also display things that the tribes have created. People can visit them to see baskets and tools that tribes would have used. Clothing and jewelry created by the tribes are also displayed. These things are called artifacts. Members of the tribe run these museums. They use the museums and artifacts to teach others about the history and traditions of their people. They use them to share the story of who they are and where they come from.

text: Emotions are what you feel. Happy is an emotion. Sad is an emotion. Mad is an emotion. You can pay attention to your feelings.

text: How do you feel today? You can notice how you feel. You can learn words to say how you feel.

text: You can share how you feel. You can use your words to say how you feel. You can write or draw to show your feelings.

title: Weathering
text:
Reading Strategies

Identify the cause-and-effect relationship.

Highlight or underline the cause in blue.

Highlight or underline the effects in red.

Answer the questions.

Weathering is an unstoppable force on Earth. The breaking of rocks and sediment can be caused by many things: wind blowing rocks against each other or plants growing in the cracks of rocks, for example. But among these, water is often the main cause of weathering rocks.

Have you ever been driving down a mountain road and seen a sign warning drivers of falling rocks? Signs like these are common in mountain areas. Drivers have to be especially careful in the spring. This is because in spring, snow from the winter begins to melt. As the snow melts, the water can seep into the cracks of rocks. In the spring, the temperatures cool down enough at night to freeze the melted snow. Once the water freezes inside of a crack, the water expands, forcing the rock to crack more and more. This freeze-and-thaw process repeats over and over until gravity helps pull apart the rocks and make them fall down.

Weathering through water and ice can happen in cities, too. Potholes form when water gets into the ground beneath the pavement. Water becomes bigger (or expands) when it freezes. Repeated freezing and thawing can cause roads and sidewalks to crack. This happens mostly in areas with snow or freezing temperatures. Although weathering cannot be stopped, engineers have designed solutions to help prevent the harmful effects of weathering. At the White House in Washington, D.C., a method called whitewashing was used to fill in cracks. This prevented moisture from seeping in that would lead to more cracking. In places where there are mountains, rockfall netting is sometimes used. This is wire mesh that can stretch across a mountain face. Engineers use this tool in places where falling rocks are common. The mesh hugs the mountainside, keeping everything in place while also catching falling rocks. Netting like this helps protect drivers and keep roads clear of debris.

Summarize to explain the process of weathering in the phenomenon. Support your explanation with evidence from the article.

How do you think the rocks and dirt got onto the sidewalk?

title: Erosion Stations
text:
At each station, read the article then follow the directions for each investigation with your group.

Water Erosion

The force of water has the strength to weather and erode rocks. As water moves, smaller pieces of rocks are carried with it. The rocks crash into each other as they are moved and break into even smaller pieces. Streams, rivers, and other bodies of water transport rocks to different locations. This is how V-shaped canyons are formed. Slowly, a river’s current erodes and carries away pieces of its shores. The river beds become wider and deeper.

Erosion is nature’s rock polisher. After hundreds or even thousands of years, the water in oceans, rivers, and rainfall can smooth down the rough edges of rocks and even mountains. Large amounts of rainfall can change the shapes of rivers through erosion. Sea arches form because of the crashing force of waves. Erosion is also very important for carrying nutrients and minerals from soil into water sources. This can benefit plant life and ecosystems.

Investigation Directions:

In the container of sand, create a slope of about 45 degrees.

Measure the depth of the sand in centimeters. Record this data in the table.

Pour the cup of water down the slope in one area.

If you don’t see a difference, pour another cup of water.

As you investigate, identify the cause and effects of the erosion.

What natural process does the water represent?

What are its effects? What did it create?

Measure the new depth of the sand where the water flowed down the slope. Record this data in the table.

Complete the rest of the table.

Do you think this type of erosion is happening in the phenomenon? Why or why not?

What landforms are created by water erosion?

How do you think the results of the investigation would change if you poured more or less water? What would be the effect of a stronger flow of water?

Does this process happen quickly or slowly?

Ice Erosion

Ice erosion is different from weathering that happens when water freezes and thaws. Instead of breaking rock, ice moves rock. For example, glaciers are landforms made from ice and snow. Believe it or not, due to gravity, glaciers are slowly, slowly moving down mountainsides. As they move, they act like giant bulldozers. They push rock and soil with them as they go. When the weather warms up, glaciers can move more easily. When the temperature cools down, rocks are frozen into glaciers, giving them a rough, sandpaper-like texture. This allows glaciers to erode mountains even more by grinding down the earth. Glaciers carve a U-shape through mountains and create valleys. This process can take thousands of years.

Investigation Directions:

In the container of sand, create a slope of about 45 degrees.

Lay a string down to split the area in half.

Measure the depth of the sand on each side of the string in centimeters. Record this data in the table.

On one side of the string, take turns gently pushing the ice down the slope.

As you investigate, identify the cause and effects of the erosion.

What natural process does the ice represent?

What are its effects? What did it create?

Measure the new depth of the sand where the ice was pushed down the slope. Record this data in the table.

Complete the rest of the table.

Do you think this type of erosion is happening in the phenomenon? Why or why not?

What landforms are created by ice erosion?

Does this process happen quickly or slowly?

Wind Erosion

Have you ever been outside in really windy weather? Sometimes the wind blows dust in your eyes. That dust is made up of rock sediments that are being eroded by the wind. The wind is blowing them to another place. As the wind picks up the sediment, it is also driven into other rocks. When the sediment crashes into the rocks, the rocks weather and erode, bit by bit. This process is slow and can take thousands of years or longer! Wind erosion creates beautiful rock formations all around the world. For example, hoodoos, or tall, thin towers of rock, have been formed by weathering and erosion. Bryce Canyon National Park, in Utah, is a great place to see hoodoos. The same force of erosion that creates these landforms will also eventually destroy them.

Investigation Directions:

Measure the weight of one piece of chalk on the scale. Record this data in the table.

Measure ½ cup of salt in the plastic container. Add the piece of chalk and close the container tightly with the lid.

Take turns shaking the container vigorously for 2-3 minutes.

As you investigate, identify the cause and effects of the erosion.

What natural process does the shaking represent?

What are its effects? What did it create?

Remove the chalk piece from the container and weigh it again. Record this data in the table.

Complete the rest of the table.

Was there a difference between the weight of the chalk before and after you shook the container? If not, how could you tell if erosion took place?

Do you think this type of erosion is happening in the phenomenon? Why or why not?

What landforms are created by wind erosion?

Does this process happen quickly or slowly?

The history of Latin America has been greatly influenced by Indigenous peoples for thousands of years. During the Age of Exploration, European and African cultural influences were introduced. Many new customs and traditions were created. Some of the new cultural customs were positive. Many others had a negative impact on the Indigenous peoples of Latin America and the enslaved Africans that were brought to the region through the Atlantic slave trade. The culture and history of Latin America have often been characterized by the themes of conflict and change. These themes continued through the 20th and 21st centuries.

When Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected president, he started something called the New Deal. This was a plan to provide jobs for people all over the United States. Many jobs were available to the citizens of Georgia. These jobs helped people survive through this difficult time.

The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) was a New Deal program. It was established on March 31, 1933. It provided jobs for millions of single young men between the ages of 18 and 25. The CCC operated in Missouri. At least 136 camps were established. They worked on improving the different natural areas. They also worked on different infrastructure improvements.

One great legacy, or long-lasting impact, left by the CCC in Missouri was its state parks. The Corps established around 12 state parks. Most of these state parks can be found in the Ozarks region of Missouri. Big Spring State Park was one of the first state parks. It had extensive changes to the infrastructure including gravel roads, providing different areas with water, a flood control system, many cabins, and a fire tower.

The CCC brought many opportunities to the state of Missouri. It gave the unemployed young men an opportunity to work, while creating state parks that people enjoy today.

title: Mount Rushmore
text:
Mount Rushmore stands in the beautiful Black Hills of southwest South Dakota. The Black Hills have been a sacred place for many groups of people throughout history, including the Lakota Sioux tribe. The environment of the Black Hills is rich in natural resources. The Lakota Sioux respected the land and used its abundant resources for survival long before the creation of Mount Rushmore.

Mount Rushmore celebrates the American ideals of leadership, courage, and strength. Mount Rushmore honors four of our nation’s leaders. Large carvings of presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln are on permanent display at Mount Rushmore.

Each president was selected to represent different phases of American history. Washington was chosen to represent the founding of America. Jefferson represents the growth of the United States. Lincoln represents the success of the Union during the Civil War and the abolishment of slavery in the United States. Roosevelt represents the development of the United States during the 20th century.

Construction began in 1927. The granite carvings were created by drilling into the face of the hills and using explosives to blast through the mountain rock. The work was difficult and dangerous. Workers climbed hundreds of steps each day just to reach the site. Men held onto ropes to do most of the dangerous work. The original design included full-body carvings of each president and engravings that commemorated important events in American history. These ideas were abandoned due to a lack of funding and the difficulty of the work.

In March 1941, Gutzon Borglum, the designer of the monument, died before the project was completed. His son Lincoln completed the project in October 1941. The Sioux did not want the monument built on their ancestral lands, but their protests were ignored. To help preserve their culture, the Sioux began construction on the Crazy Horse Memorial in 1948. The monument commemorates the courageous actions of the Oglala Lakota warrior Crazy Horse.

title: Human-Environment Interaction
text: Humans have basic needs. We need food. We need clothing and a place to live. We use resources in our environment to meet these needs. We might use trees to build our houses. We use cotton and wool to make clothes. We use places with good soil and climates to grow all kinds of food. All our interactions with our environment have consequences.

title: Essential Question
text: How do people interact with their environment?

title: Adapting to the Environment
text: People adapt to their environment. The word adapt means people change how they live depending on their environment. People wear different kinds of clothes. People build different kinds of houses. In doing so, people can adapt to the climate.

title: Modifying the Environment
text:
People modify their environment to meet their needs. Modify means to make a change. When people clear the land to build a home, they are modifying the environment. When people create irrigation for farms, they are modifying the environment. When people cut down trees to make a new road, they are modifying the environment. Review the images to see how we use and modify our environment to meet our needs.

Humans clear the land to create farms. They grow plants and raise animals for food on farms.

Humans build dams. They use the water from dams for drinking and growing crops.

Humans mine the land for minerals and resources we use in daily life.

Humans build homes to live in. They also build commercial buildings to work in. These buildings help provide shelter and jobs.

Humans build roads. They use these roads for travel and to transport goods.

Humans drill the land for oil and natural gas. They use this energy for transportation and heating.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text:
There are consequences when humans modify the land. A consequence is something that happens because of something else. Consequences can be good, bad, or both.

Humans modify the land to get the resources they need. They use resources to produce energy and food. They can create faster transportation. These are all good consequences for humans.

Human modifications can also damage the environment. Humans create pollution. They can use too many natural resources. These are bad consequences for the environment.

We need to use Earth’s natural resources wisely. We can help our environment by planting new trees. We help our environment when we pick up trash and recycle. We hurt our environment when we pollute lakes and rivers. It is our responsibility to modify the land around us carefully.

title: This is a title
text:
Sit still. Can you feel yourself moving? Believe it or not, the land you are on is slowly drifting. All the continents drift. Even the land deep below the ocean is moving. The Earth’s outermost layer of rock, or its crust, is made of large pieces. These pieces are floating on magma. When the pieces move, they can move toward, away, or slide past other pieces. Different types of movements create different landforms. After millions of years, this slow movement has created big effects. We can see the effects in the patterns of where Earth’s features have formed.

Sometimes two pieces of crust pull away from each other. This usually happens under the ocean. It results in a long, thin opening. Magma can then seep up from deep within the Earth. The magma fills in the opening. This creates ocean ridges. It can also form seamounts. Pieces of the Earth can also move toward each other. They collide when this happens. One plate is forced below. The other one is forced up. If this happens on land, it forms large mountain ranges. It can happen along continental boundaries. It can also happen in the middle of continents, like the Himalayas in Asia.

Pieces of the Earth can also slide past each other. As they do, a huge amount of energy is built up. Every so often, this energy is released. This makes an earthquake. This type of movement happens along the Pacific coast of the United States. Earthquakes occur frequently in California. Patterns of Earth’s major landforms are caused by the pattern of Earth’s pieces.

Mountains

A mountain is a tall, rocky landform larger than a hill. It generally has steep slopes and is at least 1,000 feet taller than the area surrounding it. A mountain chain is a line of mountains, one right after the other, forming a chain. These are also sometimes called mountain ranges.

Volcanoes

A volcano is a mountain or hill, typically in a cone shape. However, unlike other mountains and hills, volcanoes have vents that allow lava, rock pieces, hot steam, and other gases to escape. Volcanoes form in many shapes and sizes, and not all volcanoes spew lava. The majority of volcanoes are found in a region of the Earth called the Ring of Fire. This area is very high in volcanic and seismic, or earthquake, activity.

title: Mapping Earth’s Features: Ocean Features
text:

The Ocean Floor

The ocean floor is often thought of as flat and shapeless. However, the bottom of the ocean has many diverse features, with areas as deep as the Grand Canyon and mountains as tall as Mount Everest. Underwater mountains are known as seamounts. Seamounts are generally extinct volcanoes. They are considered seamounts because their peaks are below the surface of the ocean. One seamount, however, grew beyond the surface of the ocean into an island. Mauna Kea is a dormant volcano. Measured from its base on the ocean floor to its peak, it is even taller than Mount Everest!

Trenches and ridges are two other types of undersea landforms. An ocean trench is a deep, long, sunken crevice in the ocean floor. An ocean ridge is a submarine mountain chain that is formed when parts of the ocean floor spread, allowing magma to seep through, pushing land higher and higher.

text:
Journal Prompt
