title: Juneteenth
text:
Between 1861 and 1865, the United States was a divided nation engaged in a civil war. A civil war means that citizens within a country are in rebellion against each other. Twenty-two states remained loyal to the United States, while 11 joined the newly formed Confederate States of America. The cause of the war was over the legalization of enslaving people. The question was: Could states decide on their own if enslaving people was legal? This question led to armed conflict between the United States and the Confederate States of America.

On Jan. 1, 1863, President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation, a legal document that freed the enslaved people in the rebellious states of the Confederacy. Word of this proclamation was slow to reach all of the enslaved people in the Confederate States. On June 19, 1865, the news of emancipation finally reached Galveston, Texas. This day became known as “Juneteenth.”

Juneteenth has been celebrated in many African American communities since 1865 to commemorate the emancipation of the enslaved peoples of the United States and to preserve the history and traditions of African Americans. On June 17, 2021, President Joe Biden signed the Juneteenth National Independence Day Act into law, making Juneteenth a national holiday.

title: Plastic Pollution
text:
Think of some things that you do every day, like brushing your teeth and hair, playing sports or games, eating food, writing, or riding your bike. Chances are, some or all of the objects you used in these activities have something in common: plastic. Plastic is one of the most widely used materials in the world.

In the 19th century, many everyday objects were made of valuable stones or gems, like marble and jade. Plastic was an excellent replacement for these hard-to-find materials. It has useful properties, and it is inexpensive to produce. The first plastics were invented in the mid-1800s but didn’t become commonplace until the 1930s. Most plastic is made of chemicals that come from nonrenewable resources, such as oil, natural gas, or coal. These materials are heated to create a new substance. The process can be changed to create different types of plastics.

Despite all the benefits of plastic, plastic waste is creating a monumental pollution problem on Earth. Since the invention of plastics, about 8.3 billion metric tons of them have been produced. That's about as heavy as 25,000 Empire State Buildings! Plastic pollution is caused by mass production; overuse of single-use plastics, such as food packaging, plastic bags, and plastic bottles; and not properly disposing of plastic waste. This leads to the collection of plastic litter in massive amounts. But it doesn’t stop there. It is estimated that one-third of plastic is washed into water sources or blown away by the wind.

Natural materials, like wood or paper, biodegrade, or are decomposed by bacteria. Plastic, however, does not biodegrade. This means it takes hundreds of years for plastics to break down in landfills. Because they are matter, broken-down plastics cannot be completely destroyed. Instead, they turn into tiny particles called microplastics. Microplastics cycle through Earth’s systems in the air, water, and soil. They are even consumed by living things.

title: Plastic Pollution in the Geosphere and Biosphere
text:
The majority of plastic waste is found in the geosphere in landfills. This waste will remain in landfills for hundreds of years because plastic materials are made of chemicals that do not biodegrade. This means bacteria cannot decompose them. Over time, however, plastic does break down into tiny particles called microplastics. The largest of these microplastics are five millimeters, about the size of a pencil eraser. The smallest are like bacteria: so small that they can’t be seen with the naked eye. When plastic litter is left sitting out or is pushed by wind or water, microplastics can be carried into the soil. This can affect the growth and root systems of plants.

Even before breaking down into microplastics, plastics can release harmful chemicals into the soil. These chemicals can leak into crops that are planted in the soil or go even deeper into groundwater sources. That means without healthy, chemical-free soil, we can lose some vital resources, such as food crops and fresh water.

In addition to the land and plants, plastic pollution can also affect wildlife. This can be extremely harmful. Wildlife may mistake plastic for food or accidentally eat plastic that is attached to their food sources, like plants. Because plastic cannot be digested, it cannot pass through an animal that consumes it. This can hurt or even kill the animal. In addition, wildlife can get stuck or become tangled in plastic litter, causing injuries or worse.

title: Plastic Pollution in the Hydrosphere
text:
Plastic cannot biodegrade, or be decomposed naturally by bacteria. This means the majority of plastic waste will sit in landfills for hundreds of years before breaking down. However, these and other plastics are sometimes carried by wind or water into the ocean. Unfortunately, they pollute the ocean’s surface and floor and can wash up on beaches. Trash in the ocean either sinks or is cycled by currents to other waters around the world. In the northern Pacific, between California and Hawaii, is the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. With a surface area twice the size of Texas, it is the largest collection of plastic pollution in the world. Bottles, bags, and wrappers are the most common marine debris found in oceans and on beaches. Marine debris is any solid material that is purposely or accidentally thrown away or left in marine environments. These plastics damage habitats for ocean life.

Over time, the sun and waves break down plastics into smaller and smaller pieces. These tiny particles are less than five millimeters in length and are known as microplastics. Some of these microplastics are so small that they can’t be seen with the naked eye. Microplastics turn areas of the ocean into plastic soup. The majority of the plastic in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch is made of these tiny particles. Microplastics have even been found in rainwater and can be cycled through the hydrosphere and atmosphere in the water cycle.

At any size, plastics have harmful effects on almost 700 species of marine animals. Research has suggested that microplastics may be affecting the ability of ocean microorganisms to absorb extra gases. These gases are released from factories, cars, and breathing and can harm the Earth. Ocean microorganisms help protect the planet by taking in some of these gases. In addition, plastic pollution can lead to injuries or even death for marine animals. Whales, fish, sea turtles, birds, and other animals can mistake plastic for prey and eat the plastic. This can lead to starvation. Many dead animals have been found with plastic still in their bellies. Marine creatures can also get trapped in plastic and other debris.

title: Plastic Pollution in the Atmosphere
text:
Have you ever seen a plastic bag or wrapper blowing in the wind? What about the plastic you can’t see? Plastic is made from chemicals, which means that bacteria cannot naturally decompose, or biodegrade, it. Because of this, most plastic waste is put into landfills. The rest, if it is not recycled, can be burned. The problem with burning plastic is that as its chemicals are burned, harmful toxic gases are released into the atmosphere. Not only does the destruction of plastic contribute to pollution, but the creation of it does too. Fossil fuels, such as coal and other nonrenewable resources, are used to create plastic. This process releases more dangerous gases into the atmosphere. These harmful gases can settle on crops and in waterways, negatively affecting those valuable resources and posing a threat to human and animal health as well.

Plastic use is widespread in many areas of everyday life. You might not think that driving to the grocery store would contribute to the plastic pollution problem. However, as tires rub against the road and eventually wear down, particles of plastic break off of them into the air. These particles are tiny. The smallest are the size of bacteria, invisible to the human eye, and the largest are five millimeters, or the size of a pencil eraser. They are known as microplastics. According to research from Portsmouth Hospitals Trust in the UK, people can inhale up to 7,000 microplastic particles every day from common items, such as clothes or furniture.

This happens in the ocean, too! Microplastics floating on the ocean’s surface are tossed or blown into the air by waves or wind. Traveling microplastics can enter the atmosphere and remain there for up to six days. That is plenty of time for them to spread, harming farmland, water sources, and environments. Plastic has also become a key material in space travel because of its lightweight property. However, even space has become polluted with unused or non-working items, many of them containing plastic. Many scientists are searching for solutions to the problem of space debris.

title: My Body Can …
text: My body can see and smell. My body can talk. My body can jump and run. What else can my body do?

title: Ecosystems in Nebraska
text:
An ecosystem is made up of the connections between organisms and their environment. Some of these connections are how animals share resources, how they help each other, and how they use plants, rocks, soil, water, and other materials.

One connection that all ecosystems share is with the sun. It is the main source of energy for all ecosystems. Plants use sunlight as energy to make their food. This helps them grow. Then, plants get eaten by animals, animals get eaten by other animals, and so on. This interaction is how an ecosystem works.

In Nebraska, the sun shines an average of 223 days a year. This means that the four ecoregions of Nebraska get enough sunlight to support the plants and animals that live there. An ecoregion is an ecosystem with a specific type of geography that receives the same amounts of rain and sun. Nebraska has four ecoregions: the shortgrass prairie, the sandhills, the mixed grass prairie, and the tall grass prairie. Each of the regions supports Nebraska’s various types of plant and animal life. Nebraska is home to the following species:

60 types of amphibians and reptiles

80 fish species

400 types of birds

85 types of mammals

32 mollusk species

1,470 types of plants

Tens of thousands of insect types

Ecologists study the relationships between organisms and their environment. They ask questions to help them understand the connections within ecosystems and describe what each ecosystem is like. Then they can start to understand how ecosystems work and how they are connected to the rest of the planet.

title: Weathering and Erosion Shape the Land
text:
Weathering and erosion are constantly changing the environment of Nebraska. Physical weathering occurs when rock is worn down by heating, cooling, frost, or crystal growth. Erosion is when sand, silt, or gravel are removed by wind or water.

One place in Nebraska where erosion and weathering can be seen is Scotts Bluff. The rock of the bluff expands and contracts due to heating and cooling. This causes cracks to appear. As the cracks grow, they cause the rock to crumble. The temperatures around Scotts Bluff can range from below 0° F in the winter to around 100° F during the summer.

Erosion from wind and water also occur at Scotts Bluff. Wind and water can move silt and sand to new locations. Moving water erodes the ground, depositing sediment further down the river. Over time, rivers can change their course. The North Platte River has created new channels over the past 10,000 years.

Erosion also affects people. Erosion can damage roads, bridges, and other human-made structures. Erosion also takes away the soil farmers need to grow crops. Scientists and farmers have developed methods for reducing erosion.

title: Rivers
text:
Rivers are a vital part of life. Nebraska’s rivers are home to many plants and animals. Four of the biggest rivers in Nebraska are the Missouri River, the North Platte River, the White River, and the Niobrara River.

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. Every river in Nebraska eventually empties into the Missouri River. But portions of the Missouri River’s banks often collapse. This makes it difficult to ship freight down the river. The government stabilized the river’s banks, but the project affected nearly 555,000 acres of wildlife habitat. The numbers of many species along the river declined, including the pallid sturgeon, the least tern, and piping plovers.

The North Platte River begins in Colorado and continues through Wyoming and Nebraska for 716 miles. The North Platte River supplies freshwater to the wetlands and lakes for the river otters and the trumpeter swans. The grasslands that grow near the river are home to many insects like dragonflies, butterflies and tiger beetles.

The White River is 580 miles long and has a distinctive white-gray color. This color comes from volcanic ash, clay, and sand in the water. Flowing through South Dakota and Nebraska, the White River begins near the Badlands. Because there is very little rainfall in western Nebraska, not much water flows along the White River. But when thunderstorms come along, the river can suddenly become large and fast. There are different species of fish in the White river and occasionally you can spot a hawk diving in to get his dinner.

At 568 miles long, the Niobrara River runs through Wyoming and Nebraska. Erosion is a particularly dire issue for the Niobrara River. The severe erosion has caused cliffs and rock-filled rapids to form on parts of the river. The steep valley sides of the river have created 230 waterfalls along the river banks. The Niobrara river supports some of the only forests in Nebraska. This makes it a great home for white-tailed deer, squirrels, coyotes and beaver.

title: Wetlands
text:
Nebraska is home to diverse types of wetlands, such as fens, oxbows, playas, marshes, and forested swamps. There are three types of wetlands: marine, tidal, and non-tidal. Marine wetlands can be found along coastal shallows. Tidal wetlands can also be found along the coast, but further inland, They are affected by tides. Non-tidal wetlands are found inland. They are not affected by the ocean. Nebraska has non-tidal wetlands.

Wetlands retain water and help prevent erosion and flooding. They provide a habitat for 70 percent of Nebraska’s threatened and endangered species, including piping plovers and whooping cranes. Wetlands are filled with life. Millions of birds use Nebraska’s wetlands for breeding grounds, nesting grounds, and migration stopovers.

Groundwater is filtered through wetlands. The water that leaves wetlands is of higher quality than the water that enters. Most of Nebraska’s drinking water is from groundwater filtered by wetlands. Much of the pollution that enters wetlands becomes a harmless gas. Since they offer natural filtration, wetlands are being used more often to help in wastewater treatment.

Wetlands are so important that many federal, state, and local laws have been passed to protect them. Some of these laws are the Clean Water Act, the Farm Bill, and State Title 117. These laws have helped prevent the loss of Nebraska’s wetlands. There are many ways to help conservation efforts, including restoration, protection, and education.

Volunteer programs have been formed that focus on the conservation of Nebraska’s wetlands. If there were no wetlands, there would be less drinking water for people and less irrigation water for farms. We would also lose a wildlife habitat. The risk of flooding would increase. We would lose many recreational opportunities, such as boating and fishing.

title: Forests
text:
When most people think of Nebraska, they think of grasslands and farming. However, Nebraska has forests as well. The types of forests found in Nebraska are different from the forests found in many other states. Nebraskan forests are smaller and have fewer trees. These forests are still remarkable and grow a variety of trees, such as cottonwood, Douglas fir, ponderosa pine, elm, ash, walnut, oak, aspen, birch, jack pine, and red pine,

There are two national forests in Nebraska: the Nebraska National Forest and the Samuel R. McKelvie National Forest. These forests are unique because they were human-made. In 1890, a professor at the University of Nebraska named Charles E. Bessey had the idea to plant trees and create forests in Nebraska. Bessey believed the forests would provide timber, increase animal habitats, and help limit soil erosion.

He acquired two pieces of land in the sandhills and began creating a forest. In 1902, he started cultivating the seedlings for his forest. However, he ran out of money and had to abandon his project. Ten years later, someone rediscovered his forest. The trees he had planted were still growing strong. The project was restarted. It is now called the Nebraska National Forest.

Forests suffer from diseases like wilt and blight that kill many trees. Insects, such as emerald ash borer beetles, can cause significant damage to forests. Tracking insects and diseases can help determine the health of Nebraska’s forests.

Drought and an increasing number of dams are causing trees such as the eastern red cedar to take over the habitat of cottonwoods. Herbicides used on crops can damage nearby trees. Fires are another threat to forests. One fire prevention technique is leaving large strips of land where trees are not planted (called fire lanes). Cattle can be grazed in these areas to keep the grass short.

title: Wildfires and Ecosystems
text:
Fires are a serious concern for the grasslands of Nebraska. While fire can cause much destruction, scientists say that wildfires can be as beneficial as water. An environment deprived of water will become a desert. Without wildfire, the grasslands can become overgrown. In both cases, a valuable ecosystem is lost.

The oak savannas and oak woodlands of Nebraska are kept in balance when maintained by wildfire. Due to human settlements and increased laws and protections regarding fire, the oak woodlands have grown into forests. This has reduced the habitat for the native plants and wildlife around them. Heavy grazing has damaged many of the savannas. Like prairies, savannas are a fire-dependent ecosystem.

In 2012, wildfires destroyed thousands of acres of grasslands and forests in Nebraska. People feared the region had been severely damaged. But a study done by the University of Nebraska-Lincoln discovered that the plants had recovered quickly. They were as healthy as plants from regions unharmed by fire.

There are planned fires that can help keep ecosystems healthy. Nebraska has Prescribed Burn Associations that participate in controlled burns and help spread knowledge about this practice.

title: Times of Drought
text:
Droughts are periods of dry weather that can last for weeks, months, or years, depending on the precipitation an area usually receives. Without precipitation, wetlands, lakes, rivers, and other sources of water become dangerously low. Drier weather increases the risk of wildfires and causes them to spread faster.

An extended drought can destroy crops and harm livestock. Farmers have to spend more money for irrigation. When crops decrease, the price of food goes up. People’s physical and mental health can be affected by a drought. Drought conditions can force people to leave their homes and move to new cities.

In Nebraska, the longest recorded drought lasted 348 weeks (from Feb. 5, 2002, to Sept. 30, 2008). That means Nebraska experienced six years of drought.

Charles H. Morrill wrote about living through a drought in the 1890s. Crops were ruined. Farmers had to buy grain to feed their livestock, or they had to sell their animals at low prices. This made it hard for farmers to pay for their farms. Real estate prices all around Nebraska went down because of the drought. Banks went out of business. The financial strain became a financial depression. Nebraska began to see prosperity again in the 1900s.

title: Week 6 Inquiry Question
text: How do ecosystems interact with each other?

title: How Nebraska Became a State
text:
There are 50 states in the United States of America. The people in each state can vote in national elections. Each state has representatives in the U.S. Congress.

Before Nebraska became a territory or a state, it was part of the Louisiana Purchase. The Louisiana Purchase was a huge piece of land that the U.S. bought from France in 1803.

For many years, Native Americans were the only people who lived in the land of the Louisiana Purchase. In the 1830s, white settlers began moving into the territory. Many of them wanted to make Nebraska part of the United States. Nebraska became a territory in 1854.

Six years later in 1860, some people wanted to make Nebraska a state. They thought it would be useful to have representatives in the U.S. government and have their own state officials. Other people worried that becoming a state would make Nebraskans have to pay more taxes. The people voted against becoming a state.

Many people in other states wanted Nebraska to become a state. They wanted the United States to keep getting bigger. In 1864, the U.S. Congress passed the Nebraska Enabling Act. It listed the conditions Nebraska would need to meet to become a state. The first thing Nebraska needed was a constitution. A state constitution defines the basic laws and principles for a state. A constitutional convention gathered in Omaha to begin writing a constitution. However, most of the delegates that came were against statehood, so they ended the convention quickly without writing a constitution.

After the Civil War, the Republican Party became the popular party in Nebraska. Republicans wanted Nebraska to become a state so that there would be more Republican representatives in Congress. Republicans needed help to pass laws protecting the rights of people who had been enslaved and freed during the war. Another vote was taken on Nebraska statehood. The people of Nebraska voted to adopt a state constitution. They won by only 100 votes.

Nebraska’s constitution only allowed white men to vote. The U.S. Congress passed an act that said if Nebraska’s constitution allowed Black men to vote, Congress would admit Nebraska as a state. The U.S. president, Andrew Johnson, vetoed this act. But Congress, which was largely Republican, passed it anyway. Nebraska rewrote its constitution to allow Black men to vote. Nebraska became a state on March 1, 1867. It was the 37th state to join the Union.

title: Week 17 Inquiry Question
text: What do you need to become a state?

title: Nebraska’s Unicameral Legislature
text:
While Nebraska was a territory, it used a two-house, or bicameral, legislature. This means that there were two groups of lawmakers. In order for a bill to become law, it had to be approved by both groups. The U.S. Congress is also a bicameral legislature. All of the states have used the bicameral system in their legislatures.

When Nebraska became a state in 1867, it kept the bicameral system. The two houses in the Nebraska Legislature were called the Senate and the House of Representatives. The Senate had 13 members, and the House of Representatives had 39 members.

In the early 1900s, people were exploring many new ideas to make government better. Some people introduced the idea of having one house instead of two houses in the legislature. It would be a unicameral legislature.

The unicameral system got a boost in Nebraska when U.S. Senator George W. Norris started supporting it. He had traveled to Australia where he had seen a unicameral legislature at work. Norris said that in bicameral systems, the two houses often don’t agree on exactly what a law should say, so committees get together to negotiate it. The problem is, these committee meetings aren’t public, so some of the most important parts of lawmaking occur without public oversight. These meetings wouldn’t happen if there were just one group of lawmakers, he said. Norris wanted voters and the media to have access to all lawmaking meetings.

Norris said that he wore out two sets of tires traveling around Nebraska supporting a unicameral system. When the people of Nebraska voted on whether to have a unicameral legislature in 1934, the proposal passed in over 90 percent of the state’s precincts and counties. In the same year, 21 other states voted on a unicameral system. It only passed in Nebraska.

Some scholars think that one of the reasons the unicameral system passed in Nebraska is that the Great Depression was at its peak. People hoped a smaller government would save the state money. Only 43 people would be elected to the unicameral legislature instead of 133. The first unicameral session cost about half what the last bicameral session cost.

Nine decades after it passed, Nebraska’s unicameral system is still working. Lots of representatives from other states have come to watch our government at work, but no other states have adopted it yet. However, most U.S. city, county, and school district governments use a unicameral system.

title: The Three Branches of State Government
text:
Our Government

The state of Nebraska has a constitution that is patterned after the U.S. Constitution. A constitution is a plan for how the government should work. Our constitution divides the government into three branches or parts. These three branches share the power of governing so one person or group of people won’t become too powerful and force their will upon others.

The Executive Branch

The governor is the head of the executive branch of government in our state. The governor’s job is to carry out the laws of the state of Nebraska. Our state’s governor is elected by the people and serves for a term of four years. A term is the length of time that an elected official stays in office. The governor chooses people to work with them to help run the state. The governor also has veto power. This means the governor can reject any bill. A bill is a proposal for a law.

The Legislative Branch

The legislative branch makes the laws. The people in the Nebraska Legislature are called senators. They are elected by the people in their district to serve a four-year term. Today there are 49 districts in Nebraska, so there are 49 senators in the legislature. Senators write bills and then vote on whether these bills should become laws.

The Judicial Branch

The job of Nebraska’s judicial branch is to interpret, or explain, the laws of our state. The judicial branch is made up of judges and courts.

The highest court in Nebraska is called the Supreme Court. There are seven judges on the Supreme Court. These judges review the most important cases from the other courts in Nebraska and decide if they have been handled correctly. They can also review laws passed by the legislature to see if they agree with Nebraska’s constitution. If a law doesn’t agree with the constitution, then the Supreme Court rejects the law. Supreme Court judges serve six-year terms.

Checks and Balances

No branch of government has all of the government’s power. Each branch can do things that the other branches cannot do. The branches have to cooperate to get things done. When the branches have to share the power, it is harder for people in the government to abuse their power. This is called the principle of checks and balances. The government works best when power is balanced among the three branches.

title: Public Goods and Services
text:
Governments are established to provide public goods and services. Public goods and services are things that are available to everyone, such as roads, sanitation, schools, defense, police, and fire protection. There are sometimes debates about whether governments should provide particular public goods and services or whether businesses should do so instead. Public goods and services need taxes to support them, and not everyone uses public goods and services the same amount. Sometimes it might be more efficient for businesses to provide public goods and services only to those who need them. But businesses are run for profit, not for the public good. So some public goods and services need to be provided by the government.

In the U.S., different levels of government provide different public goods and services.

The federal, or national, government is in charge of making currency (money), signing treaties with foreign nations, overseeing international trade and trade among states, and creating military branches.

State governments are often tasked with overseeing trade within the state, conducting elections, supporting public health, establishing local governments, education, and issuing licenses for things like marriage, driving, and hunting.

However, government roles are not always clean-cut. Some roles that both the federal and state government share include creating courts, collecting taxes, and building highways. For example, both the Nebraska state government and the federal government worked on and paid for the part of Interstate 80 that goes through Nebraska.

City and county governments provide local public goods and services, such as the police force, sanitation, education, libraries, roads, bridges, and street lighting.

title: The Constitution of Nebraska
text:
A constitution is the highest law of a state or a country. It describes the structure of the government, and it describes the rights of the people. Every state in the United States has a constitution. Nebraska had a constitution even when it was a territory, before it became a state. Our country also has a constitution.

Nebraska’s constitution begins by listing the people’s rights. Some of the rights the constitution protects are the right not to be a slave, the right to vote, the right to speak freely, and the right to follow a religion.

Our constitution organizes the state government in three branches: the legislative branch, the executive branch, and the judicial branch. The constitution sets the basic rules for governments of counties and cities. It also says that the state must create free schools for all children.

Taxes pay for government services. The constitution makes the basic rules for taxes in Nebraska.

The constitution can be amended. An amendment is a change in the constitution. Our Nebraska constitution has been amended many times: 228 times. We amend the constitution when we see ways to improve the government. One of the most important amendments to Nebraska’s constitution was the amendment that created our unicameral legislature.

title: Native American Heritage Day
text:
There are four recognized tribes in Nebraska: the Omaha Tribe, the Santee Sioux Nation, the Ponca Tribe, and the Winnebago Tribe. These tribes are an important part of Nebraska’s history and play a large role in Nebraska today. Nebraska has a rich Native American heritage. A heritage is a collection of traditions, achievements, and beliefs that are part of a group’s history. That’s why Nebraska celebrates Native American Heritage Day each year on the day after Thanksgiving.

The days and weeks leading up to Native American Heritage Day are a time for schools, libraries, community groups, and other organizations to hold events honoring the lives and cultures of Nebraska’s Native American tribes. Some tribes hold special ceremonies in which their flags are displayed. Tribes often play music and perform ceremonial dances at these events. Everyone can participate in honoring the people who are Indigenous to Nebraska by learning about important tribe members and their stories. Visiting local museums or memorials is a great way to discover more.

title: Essential Question
text: How can maps help us describe places?

title: Physical Characteristics
text:
Physical characteristics tell us what a place looks like. They are part of the natural environment. Continents and oceans are the largest physical characteristics on Earth. A continent is a landform. An ocean is a body of water.

A continent is a large area of land. There are seven continents in the world. Some of them are Africa, Antarctica, and Asia. The others are Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.

An ocean is a large body of water. There are five oceans in the world. They include the Arctic Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Indian Ocean. The Pacific Ocean and the Southern Ocean complete the list.

title: Bodies of Water
text:
Bodies of water are large areas of water. Some important bodies of water are oceans, rivers, and lakes.

Oceans are the largest bodies of water. They cover about 71 percent of the Earth. Imagine the world as a huge pizza. If you divided it into four equal parts, the oceans would cover almost three!

Rivers are flowing bodies of water. This means the water in them moves. Rivers usually run from mountains toward oceans.

Lakes are large areas filled with water. They are surrounded by land. Unlike rivers, the water in lakes tends to remain still or move very slowly.

title: Landforms
text:
Landforms are features on Earth’s surface. They include mountains, valleys, plains, and islands.

Mountains are landforms. They rise above the surrounding land. A mountain usually rises at least 1,000 feet above sea level.

Hills are also areas that rise above the surrounding land. Their tops are usually rounded. They are similar to mountains, but not as high.

Valleys are low areas between hills or mountains. Mountains and hills can prevent rain from falling in valleys.

Plains are large areas of flat land. They grow a lot of grass. Plains are found on all continents. They cover a large portion of the land on Earth.

Islands are areas of land surrounded by water. They are not connected to a continent.

title: Climate
text: Climate is a physical feature of a place. Sometimes we want to study a location’s weather. We may want to know if it is warm or cold. We may want to know if it is sunny or rainy. The weather can change in just a few hours. The climate of a place, on the other hand, takes years to change. Climate is the weather pattern of an area. It tells us what the weather is like over a long period of time. Climate includes the temperature and how windy it usually is. Rain and snow are also part of the climate. Understanding the climate helps people make decisions about food, clothing, and shelter.

title: Biomes
text: We call the plants, animals, and climate of a place a biome. The types of plants that grow in a place depend on the climate. Animals are also affected by climate. In a biome, plants and animals live together. They depend on each other for the things they need.

title: Week 23 Inquiry Question
text: What do the celebrations of a state tell you about that state?

title: Nebraska Statehood Day
text:
Nebraska was the 37th state to join the United States. President Andrew Johnson signed the proclamation for statehood on March 1, 1867, just two years after the end of the Civil War. Each year, Statehood Day gives Nebraskans the opportunity to reflect on what makes Nebraska such a special place. Susan Shore, wife of Governor Pete Ricketts, said, “We have gone from sod houses to skyscrapers, from pioneers to groundbreaking innovation, and feeding a few to feeding the world. We have so much of which we can be proud.” This is an important time for us to think about our rich culture and way of life.

Nebraskans can reflect and celebrate in many ways. Students throughout Nebraska participate in classroom and school activities. Some students participate in statewide art and essay contests. One state tradition is the Statehood Day Dinner at the State Capitol. The Capitol rotunda, or a round room, is filled with tables and chairs. More than 250 people come to a special dinner that celebrates Nebraska and recognizes Nebraskans who have made a difference. Check out your local city centers to discover Nebraska Statehood Day events happening near you!

title: George Norris Day
text:
In 1955, the members of the United States Senate chose five senators who they thought were most important to American history. They wanted to display their pictures in Washington, D.C. By this time, hundreds of senators had served the country. George W. Norris, a senator from Nebraska, was one of the five chosen.

Norris served in the senate for 30 years, from 1913 to 1943. He was a progressive Republican. Although he identified as part of the Republican Party, he felt those ties lightly. He had strong anti-war ideas and didn’t support the U.S. entering World War I. Norris became known as an independent who made decisions based on each policy and situation instead of only following his party’s decisions.

Perhaps the most important thing Norris did while in office was helping to create the Tennessee Valley Authority Act, or the TVA. After the Great Depression, many Americans were rebuilding their communities and farms. The TVA helped people in the Tennessee Valley learn better farming techniques. It built dams that controlled flooding, made sure trees were planted, and helped people get electricity to their homes.

Norris also campaigned for a unicameral government in Nebraska. This means there is one house, or chamber, in the local government instead of two. All other legislatures in the United States are bicameral. Norris believed a Senate and a House of Representatives was too much like the British Parliament.

John F. Kennedy, who became the 35th president of the United States, said, “Nothing could sway [Norris] from what he thought was right, from his determination to help all the people, from his hope to save them from the twin tragedies of poverty and war.”

January 5 is George W. Norris Day in Nebraska.

title: Juneteenth, Veterans Day, Memorial Day
text:
lWe have many celebrations that are unique to Nebraska, but we also celebrate many national holidays! National holidays are set aside to commemorate historical or religious occasions, to provide thanks, or to simply have fun. In the United States, we have established certain days for the whole country to celebrate. A few of these holidays are Juneteeth, Veterans Day, and Memorial Day.

Juneteenth

Juneteenth is a holiday that celebrates the end of slavery in the United States. This holiday is also known as Emancipation Day. During the Civil War, President Lincoln issued the Emanciation Proclomation, which made slavery illegal. The Confederate states did not want to follow this new law and tried to keep it a secret from enslaved people . However, the news of freedom began to spread, and people celebrated with prayer, song, and dance.

In 1866, the first Juneteenth celebration took place in Texas. This celebration included prayer meetings and singing of spirituals. Participants wore new clothes in order to show their new freedom. Other states began to celebrate Juneteenth as well, making it an annual tradition. The United States government declared Juneteenth a national holiday in 2021. It is celebrated on June 19. In addition to celebrating the end of slavery, Juneteeth also honors the contributions and achievements of African Americans. People celebrate today with family gatherings, educational events, speeches, religious services, and prayer.

Veterans Day

World War I, the “war to end all wars,” officially came to an end on June 28, 1919. However, the fighting stopped months earlier, on November 11, 1918. Therefore, Nov. 11 became known as Armistice Day. The day was set aside for Americans to show their appreciation to the country’s World War I heroes. The national celebrations included parades, speeches, and public prayer meetings. After later wars in the 20th century, the name of the holiday was changed to Veterans Day. Today, every November 11 is set aside as a day of “celebration to honor America's veterans for their patriotism, love of country, and willingness to serve and sacrifice for the common good.”

Memorial Day

This national holiday started on May 30, 1868, when General John A. Logan established Decoration Day. It was a day to decorate the graves of Civil War soldiers. In 1950, this holiday became known as Memorial Day. President Harry S. Truman proclaimed the day to be a day of prayer for peace. Memorial Day became a federal holiday in 1971. We celebrate Memorial Day each year on the last Monday of May. Many cities have established traditions and celebrations for this day. Some of these traditions are putting flags and flowers on the graves of those who served in the military, flying the U.S. flag at their homes, visiting monuments dedicated to war veterans, and marching in parades. One of the ways the United States celebrates Memorial Day is for the president or vice president to give a speech about the freedoms we enjoy and express thanks to all those who work to protect it.

title: Rodeos and County Fairs
text:
Fairs have their roots in times before the Middle Ages! During this period of European history, fairs were places where merchants could gather and buy, sell, and trade goods with the public. These fairs were often associated with religious days and had festivities to celebrate.

Fairs have evolved over time and from country to country. The first American state fair was held in the early 19th century in Pittsfield, Massachusetts. It was organized by Elkanah Watson and featured a sheep shearing demonstration. This fair promoted more public gatherings, where people could bring their livestock for judgment and awards. Watson furthered his vision of fairs to include technology, livestock, agriculture, and merchants that would buy and sell goods.

Now, each state has multiple fairs each year. The Nebraska State Fair is our state’s oldest fair. It began in 1859, when Nebraska was still a territory! This fair takes place over 11 days and ends on Labor Day. The Nebraska State Fair has had many locations but can now be found in Grand Island.

One of the most popular attractions at Nebraska fairs is the rodeo. A rodeo has horse and bull competitions. Some of these events include barrel racing, team roping, and bull riding. These competitions have judges who give riders awards. In 1921, the citizens of Burwell wanted to put their town on the map by holding an annual rodeo. It is now the biggest rodeo in Nebraska. It has been going for more than 100 years.

For centuries, fairs have provided an opportunity to bring communities together each year. Citizens come together to socialize, learn, and enjoy local food and entertainment. Fairs are a great way for us to remember Nebraska’s heritage and the richness our state has to offer!

title: Crane Watch Festival
text:
Every March, 400,000 to 600,000 sandhill cranes make a stop on the Platte River in Nebraska. That is over 80 percent of the world’s sandhill cranes! They make their way there to rest and to feast on the grains left in the cornfields. The cranes stay in Nebraska for over a month, fattening up on food, before making their way to their nesting grounds in Alaska and Canada.

These fascinating birds are three to four feet tall, about the height of a first grader at your school. Sandhill cranes have long legs and long necks. Their feathers are gray and tan. A unique feature of this bird is the red feathers around its eyes. Each sandhill crane also has a long black beak, which helps it find food in the fields and marshes. Female sandhill cranes lay two eggs a year.

For more than 50 years, Nebraska has held a festival inviting people from all over the world to come and learn about sandhill cranes. This festival is unique in that it has no loud music. The festival is kept quiet to respect the environment of the birds. Visitors can go on bird watching tours and listen to speakers share information about the cranes. You can even bring your own binoculars and use one of the festival’s “discovery stations.” These stations are boxes large enough for people to stand in. The boxes have rectangular windows cut out so that visitors can watch the cranes. These discovery stations allow visitors to watch the birds up close without disturbing them in their natural habitat. Nebraska is fortunate to be a pit stop on the sandhill cranes’ long journey!

title: Landforms
text: Landforms are big areas of land. Mountains are landforms. Valleys and plains are landforms. Deserts are landforms.

title: Bodies of Water
text: Bodies of water are places where water collects. Oceans and lakes are bodies of water. Ponds and rivers are bodies of water.

title: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
text:
Ruth Bader Ginsburg was born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1933. She was the daughter of an immigrant father and a mother from New York. Her family valued education, and Ginsburg spent her childhood excelling in school. After high school, Ginsburg pursued higher education at Cornell University, where she graduated in 1954 at the top of her class.

Following graduation, Ginsburg began a family with her husband. Just a few years later, Ginsburg enrolled in Harvard Law School. During her time at law school, her husband, Martin, became ill with cancer. Ginsburg completed her own studies while keeping Martin up to speed on his law studies as well. She did all of this while also raising their young daughter and maintaining their home. In addition to these challenges, Ginsburg faced discrimination as one of only nine women in her law class of 500 students. She transferred to Columbia Law School in New York when her husband got a job there.

Despite these hurdles, Ginsburg once again graduated top of her class. Despite this, she had trouble finding employment in the 1950s as a Jewish woman. Ginsburg eventually returned to Columbia Law School, first as a research associate and then as a professor. After Ginsburg spent some time as a judge in the United States Court of Appeals, President Bill Clinton appointed her to the Supreme Court in 1993. She was the first Jewish woman to serve as a Supreme Court Justice. She spent much of her career fighting for women’s rights. Ruth Bader Ginsburg served as a United States Supreme Court justice for over 27 years, until her death in 2020.
