title: Pennsylvania's Road to Independence
text:
Pennsylvania has long held the nickname of the “Keystone State.” In architecture, a keystone is the stone at the top of an arch that locks the rest of the arch together. This word often gets used to refer to something that is very important. A keystone can refer to an idea that connects many other parts. Or it can be the thing on which every other part relies. Pennsylvania earned this nickname because of the role it played in the early history of the nation.

Pennsylvania’s geography made it an ideal place for colonial leaders to meet and debate the future of the American colonies. It was central, sitting between the most northern and southern colonies. There were established roads in the colony, along with a port in Philadelphia. This made travel to the colony easier.

The port in Philadelphia was important for more than just travel. Trade made the city an economic center. With the circulation of goods came the circulation of ideas. People were drawn to the city for this reason. Philadelphia grew to become an intellectual and artistic center as well.

The political leadership in the state was another important element that made Pennsylvania an important meeting ground. Events like the Boston Tea Party and the Boston Massacre years earlier made many people in the North angry. Northern colonies dealt with a heavy military presence. In the South, people were more conservative in their motivation to act. The moderate politics in Pennsylvania made it the best place for everyone to talk.

The most notable leader living in Philadelphia at the time was Benjamin Franklin. He had been trying for decades to get the colonies to unite and work together. He had cultivated a network of news and information on both sides of the debate. His network of friends and sources were members of the colonial and royal governments in every colony. He had his own newspaper, The Pennsylvania Gazette. This enjoyed a wide readership throughout the colonies as well. All of his connections and efforts made his town the place to meet.

So it was Philadelphia where the Founding Fathers came in 1776. When Robert Morris arrived, he said, "You will consider Philadelphia … to be to the United States what the heart is to the human body in circulating the blood." It is from this heart that the Founders did determine the course of the nation and signed the Declaration of Independence.

title: Population of Our Community
text: Do many people live in our community or do few people live in our community? Write the population of our community.

title: The Liberty Bell
text: The famous bell found at Independence Hall in Philadelphia is not the original bell made for the building. Colonial leaders ordered a bell from London in 1751 to celebrate the 50-year anniversary of William Penn granting the colony charter privileges. The first time they rang the bell it cracked. So, local metalworkers John Pass and John Stowe melted the whole thing down and made a new one. That second bell is the one that hung in what we now call Independence Hall. It rang to signal lawmakers it was time for their meetings. It rang to call the people in the town together to hear the news read out. It rang when the Declaration of Independence was signed. This inspired the bell to earn its name. In the 1830s, people in Philadelphia fighting against slavery began calling it the Liberty Bell. They wanted to remind people about the Declaration of Independence. They also wanted to remind them of the message engraved on the bell, “Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land Unto All the Inhabitants thereof." In 1840, a thin crack formed in this second Liberty Bell. Metalworkers actually widened this crack in an attempt to repair the bell. Their efforts were unsuccessful. The Liberty Bell was silenced forever. However, the engraved message and symbolism of the bell continue to inspire people around the world.

title: Valley Forge
text:
The year of 1777 was tough for General George Washington’s volunteer Continental army. His soldiers had fought fiercely but lost two important battles that allowed the British to capture the city of Philadelphia. The Continental Congress had to flee from the city. Winter was quickly approaching. The colonial army no longer had access to the comforts of life in the city of Philadelphia. Washington had to find a place for his exhausted soldiers to rest and recover. This was a difficult situation for the general, though. The British Army had the practice of quartering their troops in private homes when they occupied a place. To quarter soldiers means to be required by the government to provide food and housing for troops. This is done without private citizens’ consent. British soldiers had often quartered in the homes of colonists even prior to the War of Independence. One of the grievances listed against King George III in the Declaration of Independence was, "For quartering large bodies of armed troops among us." Washington would not do as the British did and quarter his troops. So, in spite of the winter weather ahead, he and his soldiers would set up camp.

Why Valley Forge?

Washington and his advisors selected Valley Forge, Pennsylvania, for the army to camp during the winter of 1777-1778. Valley Forge is located 18 miles from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Staying close meant the colonists could monitor the British army as they occupied the city. Being located on higher ground also gave them an advantage. They could see the British coming and could defend from attacks. The nearby Schuylkill River also protected the Valley Forge camp from British invaders.

Living Conditions at Valley Forge

By December 1777, more than 12,000 soldiers of the Continental Army, along with 400 women and children, lived at Valley Forge. They built over 1,500 cabins and other buildings. This created the fourth largest “city” in the colonies. Valley Forge was a diverse military camp. Alongside civilians and officers lived soldiers from all backgrounds: there were both free and enslaved Black soldiers, Indigenous people, and European immigrants.

Life at Valley Forge was not easy. The winter weather of 1777 was harsh. The U.S. government had little money to support the troops. This meant that the Continental Army and the people of Valley Forge could not get the supplies they needed. Many residents of Valley Forge became sick because of the lack of resources for hygiene and nutrition.

Even with these hardships of cold, hunger, and disease, General Washington would not quarter his troops in nearby homes and farms. He went through the channels of government to obtain what funding he could to provide for them. He and his staff remained loyal to the ideals in the Declaration of Independence.

The Outcome of the Winter at Valley Forge

During the long winter at Valley Forge, the Continental Army needed to stay active. So they trained. The soldiers learned new military strategies from a man named General Baron von Steuben. Washington appointed von Steuben to train the army at Valley Forge. This Prussian general taught the troops new ways to fight the British and how to fight as a unified army. Every day they ran drills and marched in the mud and snow.

The Continental Army faced many hardships at Valley Forge. They had entered the valley being defeated in battle, poor in health, and poor in spirits. By the time the troops left Valley Forge in June 1778, they were stronger, united, and focused on winning the war.

title: Crossing the Delaware
text:
Only months after colonial leaders signed the Declaration of Independence, General Washington faced the prospect of losing the revolution. Colonial troops retreated to Pennsylvania from several battles recently lost to the British. The troops were discouraged. Funding from the Continental Congress was low, so troops lacked basic necessities, such as food, blankets, and shoes. Many soldiers were due to return to their homes in the new year. General Washington needed a victory. So, he planned a daring attack.

On the night of Dec. 25, 1776, Washington ordered troops to cross the Delaware. The plan was to capture the Hessian troops stationed on the other side at Trenton, New Jersey. Not everything went as planned. The evening started with heavy rains. Temperatures dropped from 33 to 29 degrees Fahrenheit. Sleet and snow began to blow. The wind was fierce out of the northeast. “It blew a perfect hurricane," as one soldier put it. Large chunks of ice in the river made the crossing slower. The troops were far behind schedule. Still, they persisted in the four-hour march from the crossing to Trenton and caught the Hessians unaware. Not only did the troops gain military ground, they captured supplies such as muskets, gun powder, and food. This victory renewed the troops' and leadership's commitment to the war effort.

title: Hessian Soldiers
text:
In the 1700s, German soldiers were considered to be some of the best soldiers in the world. Armies were expensive to maintain. Many German leaders hired out their soldiers to fight all over the world.

When war with the American colonies began, the British army had just fought a war with France. They needed more soldiers to fight against the American colonists. The British army hired German soldiers to fight for them in America.

Many German soldiers came from an area called Hesse-Kassel. Because of this, all German soldiers became known as Hessians.

Hessian soldiers helped the British win several early battles during the American War for Independence. The Americans held captured Hessian soldiers in camps around Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. This was a good location for camps. It was far from the fighting and had a large German-speaking population. After the war, some Hessian soldiers decided to stay in America.

title: Pennsylvania Long Rifle
text:
The Pennsylvania long rifle (or American long rifle) was invented in the early 1700s by Martin Mylin, a German immigrant. It was first made in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The rifle’s barrel measured between five and six feet in length, as long as the total length of the common musket.

The long rifle was an innovation. Grooves or rifling were added to the inside of the barrel. Rifling caused it to shoot up to five times farther than a musket and was more accurate. It was quickly adopted by the Continental Army. Specially trained soldiers, known as riflemen, used it against British and Hessian soldiers. Colonel Daniel Morgan led these respected troops. “These are said to be all expert riflemen,” wrote John Adams, “and by means of the excellence of their firelocks [rifles], as well as their skill in the use of them …”

Daniel Boone, born in Oley Valley, PA, carried a Pennsylvania rifle as he explored the Appalachian Mountains. He played a large role in the settlement of Kentucky. The long rifle eventually became known as the Kentucky rifle because of Boone’s association with that territory.

title: Women of the American War for Independence
text:
Women from all backgrounds helped win the American War for Independence, often in surprising ways. In society of the 1700s, women often weren’t allowed to vote, participate in politics, or even attend school. This was based only on their gender. Women’s roles in the 1700s included taking care of their families, running the household, cooking for and feeding their families, and more. Although society kept women from participating directly in the war, many helped America win its Independence from the British.

Some women helped the war effort from their homes. While the men went off to fight, the women had to keep the family farms, shops, and other businesses running. Sarah “Sally” Franklin, the daughter of Benjamin Franklin, took on the role of hostess for her father’s many political gatherings. She also played a big role in relief efforts. In 1780 she led the Ladies Association of Philadelphia to sew clothing for the Continental Army. Another woman who used political connection to help the war effort from home was Esther Reed. She was the wife of the Pennsylvania governor at the time, Joseph Reed. She led a bold fundraising campaign. Women in Philadelphia went house to house collecting funds to support the Continental Army. In the summer of 1780 the women raised $300,000.

Sometimes women followed their husbands to battle when they joined the Continental Army. These women were known as “camp followers.'' They were an important part of army life. They would cook, clean, mend uniforms, and give medical aid. Sometimes they would even serve in battle. Two famous female war heroes were from Pennsylvania. Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley (also known as Molly Pitcher) was from Cumberland County. She supported the Continental Army when her husband joined the troops from Pennsylvania. When her husband was wounded, she fired cannons for hours at the Battle of Monmouth. Another famous female patriot from Pennsylvania was Margaret Cochrin Corbin. She was from Franklin County. She fought alongside her husband when he joined the First Company of Pennsylvania Artillery. When he was killed in battle, she took his place, firing the cannon. She was also eventually wounded and later became the first female recognized as a veteran of battle by the U.S. government!

Sometimes being a woman was an advantage for spying. British soldiers didn’t suspect women as spies. Lydia Darragh used her status as a woman to spy on the British when they occupied Philadelphia. She would carry flour by the British headquarters and gather as much information as she could. She would then walk five miles to give the information to American supporters, who would then tell General Washington. Washington personally chose Ann Simpson from Bucks County to carry secret messages to his generals in eastern Pennsylvania. She would hide messages in sacks of grain or in her clothes. She was never caught.

Countless women helped support the Continental Army by sewing clothes, supplying food, and raising money. The Continental Army was underfunded, so contributions from women throughout the country made a huge difference. Some women gave even more. Sarah Simpson Cooke of Northumberland County turned her house into a hospital in 1778. There she cared for wounded soldiers, widows, and orphaned children. These are just a few examples of how women changed the course of the war and history in the United States.

title: Maya Lin and The Vietnam Memorial
text:
One of the most important artists of our time is Maya Lin, an Asian American woman. She designed the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C. Lin saw a contest advertised while she was attending school at Yale University. The contest allowed anyone in the nation to enter a design for the Vietnam Veterans Memorial. Lin submitted her design and it was chosen out of almost 1,500 entries.

Lin’s parents came to the United States from China in 1949. They left just before the Communist Party took control of China. Lin was born and raised in Athens, Ohio. Besides the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, she has designed many other sculptures and buildings across the nation.

title: Chinatown
text:
Gold was discovered in California in 1848. Thousands of people went to California to search for gold. This was called the Gold Rush. Asian immigrants sailed across the Pacific Ocean to take part in the Gold Rush. Japanese and Filipino miners were a small portion of immigrants who came to California. The majority of Asian immigrants came from China. In 1852, over 20,000 Chinese immigrants came to California to work in the mining industry.

Many Chinese immigrants and workers settled in San Francisco. By 1870, the city’s population of people of Chinese descent was more than 12,000. Chinese immigrants created a community for themselves in the city known as Chinatown. This was a 12-block area stretching from California street to Broadway. Many Chinese immigrants living in San Francisco retain many of their cultural customs and traditions. For example, residents celebrate Chinese New Year with firecrackers and a colorful dragon parade.

title: Roger Y. Tsien
text: Roger Y. Tsien was born in New York City to Chinese immigrant parents. His father was an engineer and his mother was a nurse. The family moved to Livingston, New Jersey and that is where Tsien was raised. Tsien’s parents bought him a chemistry set and he experimented in his basement and backyard with chemicals and reactions. His interest in chemistry continued through high school, and Tsien won the national science fair prize called the Westinghouse Prize. Tsien’s interests branched out to include the study of biology during college. He earned degrees at Harvard and Cambridge Universities. After this, Tsien worked at UC Berkeley and then UC San Diego. In 2008, Tsien won the Nobel Prize in chemistry with his fellow researchers, Osamu Shimomura and Martin Chalfie. They discovered the natural protein that jellyfish use to glow fluorescent. Then, they figured out how to transfer this protein to other organisms. This process is used in many different scientific processes. Unfortunately, Tsien died in 2016.

title: Patsy T. Mink
text: Patsy T. Mink was born in Paia, Hawaii to Suematsu Takemoto and Mitama Tatyama Takemoto. Patsy was a Pacific Islander of Japanese descent. She graduated from college hoping to become a doctor but went to law school instead. She attended the University of Chicago Law School and was the first Japanese American to do so. While there, she married John Francis Mink. Because John was white and their marriage was interracial, she was rejected from working at many law firms. She set up her own law practice and then became involved in politics. Mink was the first Asian American woman to be elected to the U.S. House of Representatives. She served from 1965-1977 and 1990-2002. She spent her time legislating for causes she believed in including education, women’s rights, and equality.

title: Railroad Workers
text:
The Pacific Railway Act gave the work of building this railroad to the Central Pacific Railroad in California and a new company called the Union Pacific Railroad. The Central Pacific Railroad would start building railroad tracks in Nebraska, heading east. The Union Pacific would build tracks heading west. The two tracks would eventually meet at Promontory Summit in Utah. The building of the railroad was a difficult and challenging feat of engineering. It was also treacherous and backbreaking work.

The Central Pacific Railroad hired over 11,000 Chinese immigrants to complete the work. Many of the immigrants came to California during the Gold Rush. Others were recruited by railroad representatives in China. The Chinese railroad workers were very skilled at their jobs. They worked 10 to 12 hours a day, six days a week. They often laid 10 miles of track per day, despite the harsh working conditions and extreme natural elements they encountered. Their pay was $30 a month. The company then deducted fees for food and lodging. These workers were integral to building the transcontinental railroad, and would eventually help to build other railroads throughout the United States.

title: Dalip Saund
text:
Dalip Singh Saund was an Indian American activist who worked for the rights of Asian Americans in the United States. Dalip was born in India in 1899. He and his family were Sikh, a religion originating from India. Saund studied at the University of Punjab in India. He immigrated to the United States in 1920 to continue his education. He attended the University of California, Berkeley, and received his Ph.D. in mathematics in 1924. At the time, it was difficult for Asian Americans to find work in many areas. Because of this, Saund moved to southern California to farm.

During the 1940s, he worked with local leaders to change public policy towards Asian Americans and Indian immigrants. At this time, immigrants from India were not allowed to become citizens, so Saund fought for the right to become a U.S. citizen. He formed the Indian Association of America which championed citizenship for Indian immigrants. Eventually, Saund and his organization succeeded. Congress passed a law allowing Indian immigrants to become citizens in 1946. Saund became a citizen in 1949. A few years later, he was elected judge of a local court.

In 1956, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives. Saund was the first Indian American and Asian American to serve in the U.S. Congress. He served three terms before his death in 1973.

title: Citizens, Leaders, and Policies
text:
The word “govern” means “to control the actions” of something or someone. That means you are the governor of yourself. Whenever you control your own behavior in a way that makes life better for yourself and the people around you, you’re governing yourself. You “govern” yourself all the time. Governing ourselves is part of being a citizen.

Of course, your parents and teachers do a little governing as well. Parents and teachers have rules for you to follow, too. Your parents govern while you are at home, and teachers govern their classrooms during the day. Any place where there are rules to protect you or tell you what to do, you are under a government.

Local governments make rules and laws that govern your town or city. City governments usually include a mayor and a group of council members. County governments are led by supervisors or commissioners. These leaders are in charge of the police, firefighters, and schools in your community. They make sure that trash gets collected and the roads stay safe. The governor and the legislature lead the state government. The national government oversees the entire country and is led by the president and Congress.

All of us should understand what our local, state, and national governments do. Leaders in government make laws and policies that affect all of us. A policy is a plan for solving a problem. Laws and policies are rules that a community lives by. All of us need to live by good rules. As citizens, we can share our opinions about policies. When we share our opinions, we can influence our government’s policies.

Government is a way for us to work together to solve problems. With a government, we can accomplish things together that none of us can do all by ourselves.

title: Week 25 Inquiry Question
text: Why is it important to be involved in a community?

title: Speed Limits and Seat Belts
text:
Rules for traveling on the road are one way that policies help us to be safe.

People started driving cars early in the 1900s. At that time, most people walked wherever they went. Some people used horse-drawn carts or rode bicycles. When big, heavy cars became popular, people could see that streets would be more crowded. It would be dangerous without new rules.

Leaders in the government made rules of the road so people could walk, ride bikes, and drive cars without crashing into each other. Nebraska’s first speed limit for cars was made in 1905. The speed limit was 10 miles an hour.

Leaders in government keep studying ways to make driving safe. Today, cars are faster, and so are speed limits. We can have faster speed limits because we have learned how to build better, safer roads.

We also keep improving the rules of the road. To make sure that people know how to drive a car safely, we require drivers to get a license. We have learned that seat belts protect everyone who rides in a car, so every state has laws that require people in cars to wear seat belts.

title: Government Helps Every Citizen
text:
Let’s think about some of the benefits we share because of government policies.

The Beauty of Parks

Have you ever visited a marshland full of graceful birds? Have you ever gone hiking, camping, or hunting in a place full of wildlife? Have you ever visited a park in your city where you can play and relax under a tree? Parks make these experiences possible for all of us. Local governments create parks in our cities and towns. Our state government creates larger state parks where wild animals can live and people can enjoy nature.

Police Protection

Imagine that you’re driving with your mom. Suddenly, she spots something in a store window that she wants to see. She parks the car and you both go in. A few minutes later, you walk out again. But, instead of climbing into the car again, you can only stare in shock at the empty parking space where the car used to be. Someone has stolen the car! When your mom sees that empty parking space, she’s likely to make an urgent call to the local police force. Police officers will work to find your car and bring the person who stole it to justice. The local police force provides a valuable service to the people of our community. It’s a service that’s provided and paid for by our government.

Safe Roads

Maybe you’ve been driving along when suddenly some orange cones narrow your two-lane road down to one lane. You may even think it’s a little inconvenient. But you also might see, on the other side of the cones, people in hard hats and coveralls working on the part of the road that you’re not allowed to drive on. Maybe they’re filling potholes. Maybe they’re installing a guardrail to protect your car from oncoming traffic. Maybe they’re laying a completely new road. Building and repairing roads are just two more things the government does for us and our community.

Public Utilities

Have you ever wondered where the water comes from when you turn on a tap, or where we get the electricity that powers our lights? Electricity, water, and natural gas are called public utilities because they are things that everyone needs to use. Governments make rules to ensure that public utilities are safe and available to everyone.

Libraries

Where would you go to find a book you want to read? You could go to a bookstore, but first you might want to check the public library. Many communities decide that it is a good policy for everyone to have access to books and the knowledge books contain. Government carries out the policy by building public libraries. By creating libraries, we work together to give everyone the chance to learn.

title: Public Schools
text:
You probably never complain about having to wake up in the morning to go to school, right? Well, if there’s ever a morning when you do, think about this: You are lucky enough to live in a place where the government provides an education for everyone your age.

When our country began in the 1700s, there were no free schools. Children could not go to school unless their families could pay for their education. During the 1800s, people in America started to realize that our country works better if everyone has an education. Americans decided it is a good policy to make schools free for all children.

We get a free education from kindergarten to 12th grade. That’s because the government uses some of the money we pay in taxes to pay for schools and teachers. Some colleges even get money from the government.

Why is education something the government is willing to spend so much money and energy to provide? When people are educated, they can help make their town, state, and country better for everyone. Education helps us understand the issues we vote about. Education helps us have informed opinions about whether government policies are good or bad. We can be better citizens when we can read, write, and do mathematics. Knowing about the history of our communities helps us know what our communities need now.

Going to school is not always easy, but the work is worth it. Even tests are valuable. As students, we take tests to make sure that we are learning the things we need to know. Tests also help teachers do a better job of teaching. Every year, students in public schools take tests to help make our schools the best they can be.

title: Citizens Get Involved
text:
Every state has public issues that the people need to address. A public issue is any problem or decision that a group of people face. Different states face different issues. An important part of what our leaders do is to work on solving these concerns. Nebraska has faced a lot of issues over the years. People in Nebraska have not always agreed on how to deal with taxes, education, and how to use the land. Citizens can argue over how to solve these issues.

It is good to pay attention to the important issues your state faces because the solutions may impact your daily life. For example, lawmakers might propose a new law to help the environment. That law might change how your community handles trash. The law may also mean new taxes or fines. While voters may want to make the environment better, it may also be hard for them to pay more taxes. The decision can be very difficult.

Most communities face choices over how much they should raise or lower taxes. Those communities also have to choose how to spend tax money. People often disagree about where to spend the money.

It is our job, as citizens, to learn about the issues and share our ideas. You can share your opinion with leaders by telling them. Write an email or a letter and send it directly to the leader. Many leaders have offices with phone numbers you can call to share your ideas.

Another important way to influence policy is by talking to other people who are also affected by the policy. You can express your opinion on social media. You can talk about the policy with your friends. You can find other people who are also interested in the policy so you can work together with them. Other people who care about the same thing will help you learn more about the issue. They can help you find the government leaders who are responsible for making decisions about the issue.

The issues facing Nebraska are always changing. Do you know what issues the state faces right now? What do you think our leaders should do about them? Think about writing a letter to your mayor, city council or governor with some ideas.

title: What Is Lobbying?
text:
When you hear about government policy, you’ll hear people talk about “lobbying.”

People who try to convince government leaders to support a policy are lobbying. When you write an email or make a phone call to government leaders about your policy ideas, you will be lobbying too!

Persuading people to support your ideas takes planning. Good lobbyists are good at following a plan.

First, you need to learn about the issue you’re interested in. The more you know about the issue, the better you’ll be able to make good suggestions and answer questions about what should be done.

You also need to find out which leaders you should contact. Find out who the mayor is. Find out which city council member represents the area where you live. If you have suggestions for improving a park in your neighborhood, you’ll want to get in touch with the leaders who work on parks.

One of the most important things that a good lobbyist does is persevere. If some people don’t agree with you at first, don’t be discouraged. Keep sharing your ideas.

Remember that people don’t always agree about what the best policy is. A government leader’s job is hard because it is hard to know what is best for everyone. When you talk to leaders, you won’t always get your way. However, policy decisions will usually be better when leaders know what you think.

title: Human Features
text: Human characteristics include the number of people who live in a place and their ideas. People make choices about where to live. They use their ideas to build the place. People make choices on how to meet their basic needs. They meet their needs by using the physical features of the place. The way people build their homes is part of the human features of a place. So are the clothes they wear and the foods they eat. A new park in your neighborhood is a human feature. Our transportation systems are, too. Human features tell us about people and culture.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe where I live?

title: What Is a Country?
text: What is a country? A country is a place that has its own flag. However, states have their own flags, too. A country has a capital city. States have capital cities as well. What is different about a country, then? A country is an area of land that has its own government, and nobody controls it from the outside. It also has a leader who is not controlled by anybody from outside. Most countries have their own money. The United States, Mexico, and Canada are all countries. Some of the Caribbean islands are countries.

title: What Is a Capital City?
text:
A capital city is the location where a state or country's government meets to work. It is the most important city in a country or state. It is where you can find the government leaders. On maps, capital cities are often represented by stars. The capital city of the United States is Washington, D.C. States have capital cities, too. What is the capital city of your state?

Look at the map. Find Canada and Mexico. What are their capital cities? Can you find other capital cities?

title: Land Use
text:
Land use is a human feature. Land can be used for different purposes.

Communities where people live are called residential. Residential areas have houses, apartments, and schools.

Some areas of land are labeled as industrial. Industrial areas are where people make things. Warehouses, factories, and storage buildings are found in these areas.

Commercial areas are used for services. Gas stations, grocery stores, and hotels are found in commercial areas.

Recreational areas are where people play, relax, or do sports. Parks, swimming pools, and lakes are recreational areas.

Agricultural land is used for growing crops and raising animals. Crops and animals depend on temperature, rainfall, and soil. Access to clean water is very important to agricultural communities.

title: Urban, Suburban, Rural
text:
People live in three main types of communities. They are urban, suburban, and rural. Urban is a word we use to describe a city. Urban communities have many tall buildings. There are a lot of people living close together. They often have freeways and public transportation systems.

A suburban community is a group of neighborhoods near a big city. Suburban areas are less crowded. There is more space for homes and businesses. There are usually large roads and many cars. Many suburbs have public transportation systems.

Rural communities have fewer people. They often have fewer buildings too. There are small towns, farms, and open spaces. Rural communities have smaller roads, but many people have cars. Few rural areas have public transportation systems.

title: Essential Question
text: Why do people move?

title: Why Do People Move?
text:
In geography, people study movement. Movement is how people, resources, and ideas travel from one place to another. People move for many reasons.

Sometimes people choose to move. Pull factors are the good things that attract people to a place. Pull factors are things like better jobs or education. Other pull factors are safety or more resources for a better life.

Sometimes people move because they have to. Push factors are the bad things that make people leave a place. Some push factors are war, natural disasters, and religious persecution.

title: Exploration
text: People have explored new places throughout history. Many people went looking for resources. Others wanted to expand their empires. Some wanted to share their religion. Exploration is traveling to learn about an unfamiliar place.

title: Settlement
text: People choose to live in certain areas. These settlements depend on the physical environment. They also depend on the availability of natural resources. People settle in places that make life better for them. Traditionally, communities have grown around water and other important resources. Water is necessary for people to survive. It is important for growing food and for transportation. Where there are more resources, the population grows.

title: Migration
text:
Most people move to a place they already know about. Many early settlers in North America were from Europe. They moved after explorers traveled here. We call the movement from one place to another migration.

New transportation has made moving much easier. People move across the world or country for a new job. Migrant workers are people who move wherever there are jobs. College students often move when they go to school.

Migration is one way people, ideas, and materials move.

title: Migration Patterns
text: This is a population map of North America. It shows patterns of human settlement. Look at the legend. The beige areas of the map show where very few people live. The blue and dark red areas of the map show where the most people live. People usually choose to settle where resources are easily accessible.

title: Population Map Activity
text:
Use the population map and the legend/key to answer the following questions.

1. What do the beige areas of the map tell you about the population?

2. Which color on the map shows you where the most people live?

3. What do you think is happening in the beige areas? Why don’t people want to settle there?

title: Essential Question
text: What is culture?

title: Cultural Characteristics
text: There are many different characteristics of culture. Architecture, fine arts, literature, music, and language are part of culture. Religion, clothing, and food are also part of culture. Culture is how a group of people act and what they believe.

title: Clothing
text:
The environments people live in affect the way people dress. Traditional clothes were made from the resources in an area. People who kept sheep often made clothes out of wool. Others used grass and palm fronds.

Some people made cloth from tree bark. Color dye for the cloth was made from local plants.

The style of clothing is also affected by the environment. Those who live in a warm environment wear lightweight clothes. Those who live where it gets cold need heavier clothing to keep warm.

title: Food
text: Our foods come from the resources around us. Many cultures eat the same foods. However, how they prepare and preserve the food may be different. For example, many people eat tomatoes. Some make sauces for pizza or spaghetti. Others may use diced tomatoes as a topping on a taco.

title: Celebrations
text: One way people show their culture is through their celebrations. They celebrate things that are important to them. Some cultures celebrate the seasons. Others celebrate special events or people. When people move, they bring their culture and traditions with them. Many states have unique celebrations.

title: Language
text: Language is an important part of culture. As people move around, they bring their languages with them. Language helps people share information. The words people use help them share their experiences with others. Language can be used to bring cultures together.

title: Arts and Folktales
text:
We can learn about different cultures through their art. Artists draw what they see around them. They draw the people, animals, and celebrations they see.

Literature comes from the stories people share. Stories can also be used to share beliefs and ideas. When these stories are told over and over, they become folktales. These shared stories become part of their culture.

title: Beliefs
text: Religion is another part of culture. Religion is a system of beliefs. Different cultures have different beliefs. Many celebrations and traditions come from a group's beliefs or religion. These celebrations can influence culture.

title: What Is a Region?
text: We organize the Earth into regions. Doing so helps us to learn about our world. A region is an area with similar characteristics. Some regions are organized by physical characteristics. Landforms, climate, and biomes are physical characteristics. Some regions are organized by their human characteristics. These include population, culture, and language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

title: Essential Question
text: What is a region?

title: North America
text: The North American region is made up of three large countries and some groups of islands. The larger countries are Canada, the United States, and Mexico. All three countries share important mountain ranges. The Rocky Mountains start in Canada. The Sierra Madre mountains go through both the United States and Mexico. North America is surrounded by oceans. The Pacific Ocean is west of North America. The Atlantic Ocean is east of North America. A group of islands called the Caribbean are in the Atlantic Ocean. A group of islands is called an archipelago. Greenland and many other islands are to the northeast of Canada. There are also important lakes and rivers in North America. The five Great Lakes connect Canada and the United States.

title: South America
text: South America is in the Southern Hemisphere. It is home to the Amazon River and the Andes mountains. The continent is bordered by three bodies of water. It has the Pacific Ocean on its west side. The Atlantic Ocean is to the east. The Caribbean Sea is to the north. The Amazon Rainforest is also in South America. The forest has a variety of plants, animals, and insects. Mount Aconcagua is the highest point in the Americas. It is part of the Andes mountain range in South America.

title: Africa
text: Africa’s geography has mountains, valleys, and bodies of water. The Atlas Mountains are in the north. These mountains are between the Mediterranean coast and the Sahara desert. There are also many mountains in east Africa. Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest of these. The longest river in the world is in Africa. This river is the Nile. Some rivers in central Africa gather into Lake Victoria. Lake Victoria is Africa’s largest lake.

title: Europe
text: Thousands of years ago, most of northern Europe was very different. It was covered by giant masses of ice, called glaciers. Over time, the ice melted away. The landscape changed. We now call it the European Plain. South of the European Plain is a long mountain range. These mountains include the Alps and two active volcanoes. Iceland, Great Britain, Ireland, Sicily, and Corsica are islands of this region. The European region gives us examples of physical features found all around the world.

title: Antarctica
text: Antarctica is a region covered in ice. The South Pole is in Antarctica. The continent has a long range of mountains. The mountains divide the continent into east and west sections. The Antarctic Peninsula is on the north end of Antarctica. It stretches toward the southern tip of South America. Although Antarctica is very cold, it has an active volcano. You can see lava flow there. No continent is as dry and windy as Antarctica.

title: Oceania
text: The region of Oceania is in the Southern Hemisphere. Oceania is made up of thousands of Islands. Australia, New Zealand, and New Guinea are the largest islands. Australia is the only island that is also a continent. Oceania has many climate types. There are many rainforests. There are many animals in the region that cannot be found anywhere else. Oceania also has many coral reefs.

title: Asia
text: Asia is the largest continent. More than half of all the people in the world live in Asia. The Himalayas are located in Asia. They are the tallest mountains in the world. Asia also has several large peninsulas. A peninsula is land surrounded on three sides by water. Two of Asia’s peninsulas are the Arabian Peninsula and the Korean Peninsula.

title: Our Government of Laws
text:
Our system of government works through laws. In our country, we say that everyone is equal under the law. The law protects our freedom. The law sets rules for what the government can do. The law also sets rules for what people can do. When people respect the law and try to improve the law, our society is better.

The government’s job is to make our laws and to make sure that laws are applied fairly to everyone.

In Nebraska, we have three branches of government. These are the legislative branch, the executive branch, and the judicial branch. Each branch of government has a part in making sure our laws work well.

The Nebraska Legislature is the legislative branch. The Legislature meets at the Nebraska State Capitol in Lincoln. Members of the Nebraska Legislature are called senators. They are elected by the people. Senators listen to Nebraska’s citizens to find out how our laws need to change. Senators write proposed laws, which are called bills. They debate and vote on bills. If most of the senators vote for a bill and the governor agrees, then the bill becomes a law.

The governor is the head of the executive branch. The governor is elected by the people. After a bill becomes a law, the executive branch carries out the law. Many laws make rules for things that

the government must do, like building roads, running schools, and collecting taxes. People who do these things are part of the executive branch.

The judicial branch is the system of judges in our courts. Judges are chosen by the governor. Later, the people vote on whether to keep a judge. A judge’s job is to settle disputes about the law. When people disagree about what the laws require, judges decide what the laws mean. Judges also decide the punishment when people break the law.

title: Essential Question
text: Who are some people who have influenced communities?

title: The Code Talkers
text:
During World War I, the United States used codes to send secret messages. The messages had important information about military plans. Countries that were fighting against the United States learned how to break the codes. They were able to learn the secret information. One day, a U.S. commander heard Choctaw soldiers talking in their native language. He realized that the Choctaw language would be totally unknown in Europe. The Choctaw soldiers were trained to use their words as a code. They sent and received important messages in that code.

During World War II, the U.S. government asked Native American soldiers from many different tribes to create codes. The most complicated code used the Navajo language. Very few non-Navajo people knew how to speak it at the time. Navajo soldiers were trained as Code Talkers. No other army could break the code. Like the Choctaw soldiers, the Navajo and other Indigenous soldiers used their languages to protect American troops.

title: Langston Hughes
text: About 100 years ago, many African Americans moved to big cities in the northern United States. New York City’s Harlem neighborhood was a popular place for Black artists, writers, and musicians to live. These creative people made art about their history and community. One of the most well-known Harlem writers of this time was Langston Hughes. He was born in Missouri in 1901 and moved to Harlem in 1922. He wrote poetry, plays, books, and newspaper articles. Hughes wrote differently from many other authors at the time. He used language that everyone could understand, which made it easier for people to read his work. The subjects he wrote about were different, too. Before Hughes, there were not many well-known African American writers. Langston Hughes wrote about feelings and experiences many African Americans shared. His writing helped give a voice to the Black community in the United States. The work of Langston Hughes still inspires readers and writers today.

title: Week 18 Inquiry Question
text: How does a bill become a law?

title: From Bill to Law
text:
Government action and decisions are put into effect by creating a bill that can become a law. A bill is a draft of a law presented to a legislature. There’s a special process that every citizen should know in order to be an informed, active participant in the processes of government.

The process of making a law starts in the legislature. The Nebraska Legislature is often called the Nebraska Unicameral. Unicameral means “one room,” or “one house.” All the other states in the United States have bicameral legislatures. That means they have two houses, or groups, of lawmakers who have to agree with each other to make a law. In Nebraska, the legislature has one house of lawmakers, called senators. In 1933, Nebraskans decided to use a unicameral legislature because they thought it would be more efficient and less expensive. They also thought a unicameral legislature would be more open to public view.

Every bill starts with an idea. Citizens can contact their elected senators to propose an idea for a law that will make their community, state, or country a better place. Then, the senators can write a bill based on the proposal of the groups of citizens they represent.

title: Introducing a Bill
text:
Preparing a bill for the Legislature is called “introducing the bill.” There are several steps in the process of introducing a bill.

A senator brings an idea for a bill to a bill drafter. Bill drafters work for the Legislature. Bill drafters are lawyers who help senators write bills. The senator and the drafter work together to write the bill. They try to make sure that the wording is right. If the wording of the bill is not right, the law will be unclear and won’t accomplish its purpose.

Copies of the bill are printed on paper and published on the internet. That makes it possible for other senators and members of the public to read the bill.

Experts who work for the legislature study the bill to figure out if it will affect the state’s plans for spending money. These experts write a report called a fiscal note.

Now the bill is ready for all the senators to study and talk about it.

title: Alice Stokes Paul
text: Alice Stokes Paul was born in New Jersey in 1885. She grew up believing that women should have the right to vote. When she was an adult, she helped plan the first protest at the White House. A protest is when a group of people gather together to show that they disagree with something. During protests, people might hold signs or chant a message about their ideas. Alice Paul’s protest lasted for more than two years. Women dressed in white and stood silently outside the White House. They were there six days a week, even in rain or snow. The women held signs and banners that asked for the right to vote. These women were called the Silent Sentinels. Around 2,000 women participated between January 1917 and June 1919. In 1920, the 19th Amendment passed. This amendment allowed women to vote in federal elections. Today, grateful voters still leave notes on Alice Paul’s grave.

title: Committee Hearings
text:
Senators divide up the work of studying bills by separating into smaller groups called committees. There are 14 permanent committees in the Legislature. Each committee has a different subject area. Bills about farming and ranching go to the Agriculture Committee. Bills about schools go to the Education Committee. Bills about taxes go to the Revenue Committee.

One job of a committee is to have public meetings where the committee discusses bills. These meetings are called hearings. In hearings, senators talk about what they think is good or bad about a bill. They talk about how they want to change or improve a bill.

Members of the public can go to hearings and listen to what the senators say. People can speak at hearings. They can express their opinions to members of the committee. All the discussion at a hearing is recorded. It is printed in the record of the bill, so everyone knows what senators and members of the public said at the hearing.

After the hearing, senators vote on the bill. If most of the senators on the committee support the bill, they send the bill to the entire Legislature to be debated.

title: Booker T. Washington
text:
Booker T. Washington was born into slavery in Virginia in 1856. He learned how to read in his spare time. At age 16, he walked 500 miles to a school in Virginia. He convinced the headmaster to let him work as a janitor to help pay for his tuition. Washington worked and studied hard to become an educator and leader.

When he was an adult, Washington was hired to lead the Tuskegee Normal School. A “normal school” was a school that trained teachers. The Tuskegee Normal School was one of the few schools that taught African American educators. Washington encouraged each student to do their best work. He believed education was important for African Americans. Booker T. Washington said, “I have learned that success is to be measured not so much by the position one has reached in life as by the obstacles which he has overcome.”

title: Legislative Debate
text:
The full Legislature debates and votes on a bill at least two times before it can pass. There are 49 senators in the full Legislature.

The first time senators debate a bill, they talk about possible changes to the bill. These changes are called amendments. The first debate is important because it is a time for senators to make compromises. Often, senators disagree about the details of a bill. When senators give up a little bit of what they want so everyone can have the things they agree about, it is called a compromise. Senators make amendments to a bill because they are making a compromise.

If at least 25 senators vote for a bill after the first debate, the amendments are put into the bill and printed for everyone to read and study.

In the second debate, the senators have another chance to talk about the bill and decide whether it is a good idea. They also have another chance to make amendments. At the end of the second debate, the senators vote on the bill. If at least 25 senators vote for the bill, it is sent to the governor.

title: Clara Barton
text: Clara Barton was born in Massachusetts in 1821. When she was young, her brother fell and got hurt. They did not live close to a doctor. She took care of her brother and became interested in nursing. As an adult, she traveled to Europe and learned about the International Red Cross. The International Red Cross began in 1863. Its goal was to help people who were hurt by war. Clara Barton felt inspired by the International Red Cross. When she returned to the United States, she helped start the American Red Cross. The American Red Cross was founded on May 21, 1881. It still helps people today. The American Red Cross helps provide emergency services and disaster relief. People in the American Red Cross also teach first aid and collect blood donations. Wherever there is a disaster, the American Red Cross shows up to help.

title: Ed Roberts
text:
Ed Roberts was born in 1939. When he was 14, he was paralyzed by a disease called polio. He could not use much of his body from his neck down. He had to use a mechanical lung to breathe. At that time, people with disabilities did not have many opportunities to learn and work. Ed Roberts had to fight for his right to get an education. He took high school classes on the phone and did very well. However, his high school almost did not let him graduate because he did not complete physical education classes. When people at his university discovered he had a disability, they almost didn’t let him attend. Roberts had to insist on his right to learn.

Ed Roberts’ courage opened the way for other people with disabilities. He helped create change in his community. His work helped make organizations respect the rights of people with disabilities.

title: Selena
text:
Selena Quintanilla-Pérez was born in Texas in 1971. She began singing in her family’s band when she was about eight years old. The Quintanilla family performed Tejano music. Tejano music combines music styles from Mexico, Europe, and the United States. When Selena began singing, Tejano music was popular in Mexico and the southwestern U.S. However, Selena wanted everyone to enjoy her music. She began recording songs in English and in Spanish so her music could reach more people. Soon, music-lovers everywhere knew the name Selena.

Selena’s hard work and talent spread Tejano music across the world. Today, she is remembered as an important cultural figure.

title: Mary Golda Ross
text: Mary Golda Ross was born in 1908 in Park Hill, Oklahoma. She was Native American, and she lived with her grandparents in Cherokee County. There weren’t many female engineers around that time, but Ross soon knew she wanted to become an engineer. There were no Native American female engineers she could look up to. Ross, however, was not discouraged. She went to a university and became an engineer. She became one of the first female engineers to work at a company that made aircraft for the military. Later, she worked for NASA. Her skills helped the space program of the United States. Mary Golda Ross became an inspiration for her community and for others who wanted to follow in her footsteps.

title: The WASP
text:
In 1941, American men went to fight in World War II. American women replaced the men in airplane factories. Many women built airplanes. In 1942, there was a shortage of combat pilots. A program was created to train some women to fly military airplanes. These women were known as the Women Airforce Service Pilots (WASP). Their job was to fly planes from factories to military bases. They also tested planes that had been repaired. Another job was towing targets behind their planes. This gave ground and air gunners shooting practice. The gunners sometimes used real ammunition. It was a dangerous job.

To become a member of the WASP, a woman had to be between 21 and 35 years old and in good health. She also had to have a pilot’s license. Twenty-five thousand women applied, 1,830 were accepted, and 1,074 graduated. Thirty-eight members of the WASP lost their lives during the war.

It has taken a long time for the Women Airforce Service Pilots to be recognized for their service. They petitioned the government many times. Finally, in 1977, the government officially granted them veteran status. This allowed members of the WASP to receive military benefits. The WASP Museum was created at Avenger Field, Sweetwater, Texas, in 2005. They received the Congressional Gold Medal in 2009.

title: The Governor’s Approval or Veto
text:
After the Legislature passes a bill, the governor has five days to decide what to do with the bill. If the governor signs the bill or does nothing with it, the bill becomes a state law. If the governor does not want the bill to become law, the governor may reject the bill. The governor’s rejection is called a veto.

A vetoed bill goes back to the Legislature. The senators can debate and vote on the bill again. They can still pass the bill into law. However, after a veto, 30 senators must vote for the bill to make it a law.

After a bill becomes a law, it is printed with the other laws of Nebraska in books and on the internet. Everyone can read and study the laws.

title: Phenomenon
text: When ingredients of dough are mixed, the dough rises.

title: Phenomenon Introduction
text:
Rules:

Ask as many questions as you can.

Do not stop to discuss, judge, or answer your questions.

Change your statements into questions.

Circle your best question.

My Questions:

title: Constitutional Amendments
text:
Changes to the state or federal constitution are a special kind of law called constitutional amendments. The process for making constitutional amendments is different from the process for passing regular bills.

The constitution is the highest law of a state or a country. A constitution makes the basic rules for how the government works, and it describes the basic rights of the people. Changing the constitution is a big decision, so it requires an extra amount of support.

State Constitutional Amendments

When a senator proposes an amendment to the Nebraska Constitution, the process starts like it does for a normal bill. The amendment is sent to a committee. If the committee votes for the amendment, the full Legislature debates and votes on the amendment. A regular bill passes if 25 senators vote for it. However, it takes 30 votes to pass a constitutional amendment.

Even if the amendment gets 30 votes in the Legislature, the process is still not over. The people also have to vote on it. A constitutional amendment that passes in the Legislature is put on the ballot for a general election where Nebraskans can vote yes or no. If most of the voters in the election vote yes, the amendment becomes part of the Nebraska Constitution.

Federal Constitutional Amendments

Changes to our nation’s constitution start in the U.S. Congress, which is the nation’s legislature. If the members of Congress vote for a constitutional amendment, the legislatures of the states can vote on it. This process is called ratification. For a federal constitutional amendment to become law, three-fourths of the state legislatures must vote to ratify it. That means 38 of the 50 state legislatures must vote for it. The federal constitution has been amended 27 times.

title: Plan and Predict
text:
Investigation Materials:

1½ cups warm water

2 Tbsp sugar

1 Tbsp yeast

3½ cups flour

1 tsp salt

Investigation Steps:

Mix the warm water and sugar.

Stir in the yeast. Let the mixture sit for five minutes.

Add flour and salt to the mixture. Mix until the dough is smooth, then let it rise for 10 minutes.

Roll the dough into a loaf and let it rest for another 10 minutes before putting it into the oven.

Bake at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 15-20 minutes.

Investigation Plan:

What are the ingredients for the investigation?

What do you think the effect will be when the ingredients are mixed together?

title: Dough Investigation
text:
As you complete your investigation trial:

After each step, record the effect (or effects) of combining the ingredients and the new properties of the solution or mixture.

Step 1: Mix the warm water and sugar.

Vocabulary:

Step 2: Be sure the water is still warm. Stir in the yeast. Let the mixture sit for five minutes.

Step 3: Add flour and salt to the mixture. Mix until the dough is smooth, then let it rise for 10 minutes.

title: Cause and Effect
text:
Draw a time …

… when you mixed two or more materials together and it had an unexpected effect. What change was unexpected?

Vocabulary:

A chemical change is ____________________________________________.

How did adding yeast to the mixture affect your dough? How did excluding yeast from the mixture affect your teacher’s dough? Fill in the separate effects on the table. Then, record the observable evidence you saw that led you to those conclusions.

Reflect and Connect

How has your understanding of the phenomenon changed from today’s activity? What new evidence do you have?

title: Changes in Matter
text:
Mixing matter causes a change that can either be physical or create a new substance. When mixing causes a physical change, the appearance of the substance may be different, but the matter still has the same properties as it did before. In other words, a new substance is not formed. For example, when you make a salad, you mix lettuce, other vegetables, and dressing. Although the ingredients are called by a different name (“salad”) when mixed together, that doesn’t mean it’s a new substance. The items you mixed did not change; they have the same properties as before. The lettuce is still green and leafy, the dressing is still liquid, and so on.

When matter is mixed and becomes a new substance, its properties do change. The new substance has different properties than the separate items that were mixed together. This is called a chemical change. There are clues to help you decide whether a mixture is a new substance. Here is what to look for:

A gas is formed.

There is a color change.

There is a temperature change.

A solid is formed.

Light or odor is released.

But the biggest question you need to ask is, “Is this material the same substance that it was before?” Imagine ripping a piece of paper into tiny bits. Those bits are still paper, just smaller. This is a physical change. Nothing new has been created. Now, imagine throwing those bits of paper into a fire. Suddenly, the color of the paper changes, the temperature increases as it burns, and you can see and smell the smoke as it is released. The paper is no longer paper at this point. It has become ash, which is something new.

Answer the following questions, citing evidence from the article. Be sure to use the correct punctuation when you quote the article.

Why is mixing a salad considered a physical change?

What are some things that might happen after a chemical change?

We made dough by mixing ingredients. Was that an example of a physical or chemical change? How do you know?

title: Essential Question
text: How do resources meet our needs and wants?

title: Needs and Wants
text:
A need is something that you have to have every day. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us safe by keeping us warm or cool.

A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. A want is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book.

title: Resources
text: A resource is something that people or businesses use. Resources help us meet our needs and wants. It is important for people and communities to use resources wisely.

title: It’s Alive!
text:
Reading Strategies

Circle clues that show a new substance is made.

Underline the causes of a new substance.

Yeast is a living organism. It may not look like it is living because it doesn’t appear to eat and breathe, but in the right conditions, it will! Yeast is a fungus. It comes “alive” when it is mixed with warm water and food to eat. The temperature of the water is very important because if the water is too hot or too cold, the yeast will die. Another important ingredient that yeast needs is sugar. Yeast “eats,” or consumes, sugar for energy. After it consumes the sugar, it puts out a gas. The gas is visible as bubbles. This is why a dough mixture rises over time: because it is being filled with many tiny gas bubbles. Gas bubbles are evidence that a new substance is being made.

Reflect and Connect

What causes dough to rise after it is mixed? Cite evidence from the text, using the correct punctuation.

title: Natural Resources
text: Many things that we use to meet our needs come from nature. We call these natural resources. Natural resources are things like minerals, trees, and animals. These resources give us food to eat and materials to build with. The wind and the sun are also natural resources that help us meet our needs.

title: Human Resources
text: People who use their skills to make something are human resources. People who use their skills to provide a service are also human resources. Farmers, builders, and clothing manufacturers are examples of human resources. So are teachers, doctors, and computer programmers.

title: Phenomenon Explanation
text:
Phenomenon: When ingredients of dough are mixed, the dough rises.

Write:

A short response to explain the phenomenon. Your explanation should address what causes the dough to rise, supported by evidence and reasoning. Be sure to use the following terms:

chemical change

substance

Explanation:

Evidence and Reasoning:

Applied Science Writing

Write about a chemical change and a physical change you have seen in your home, school, or community. Describe how you knew the changes were physical or chemical.

title: Capital Resources
text: Capital resources are the tools we use to help us make or do things. These tools help us build or put things together. Machines like lawn mowers and computers help us do our work. They are examples of capital resources.

title: Resources in the Community
text: Communities don’t always have everything their citizens need. Each community has its own resources. Some communities have lumber and coal. Others have fish, fruits, and vegetables. We depend on each other for the resources we need. We use many resources in our community. If our community does not have enough resources, we can get them from other communities.

title: Essential Question
text: How do resources affect the jobs we do?

title: Goods and Services
text:
Goods are things that are made for people to buy and use. Goods include clothing, furniture, and toys. Goods are also things we eat or drink. Fruits, vegetables, and milk are examples of goods we consume.

A service is work that one person does for someone else. Services are actions such as a haircut, car repair, and teaching. If you send a package to someone else, you pay for a delivery service. If you have a cell phone, you pay for cell phone service. You might choose to have your pizza delivered. That’s a service too.

title: Mining
text: Mining means digging into the ground to get useful minerals. A mineral is a natural resource that forms inside the Earth’s crust. There are many kinds of minerals. Some examples are iron, coal, and salt. Diamonds and gold are minerals, too. Miners dig tunnels or pits into the earth so they can reach the minerals. Then, they use machines and tools to take the minerals out of the ground. People in other industries can use the minerals to make things. More than 60 minerals are needed to make a single computer. Minerals can also become part of airplanes, jewelry, vitamins, and much more.

title: Natural Resources and Work
text: People can do different kinds of work to earn money. Work is how people meet their needs. People choose the kinds of jobs they want to do. Some people have jobs making goods, or things we want or need. Other people provide services we want or need. Natural resources are used to create many goods and services. Let’s look at how that happens.

title: Agriculture
text: Agriculture is another word for farming. It is growing crops and raising animals. Farmers need healthy soil, clean water, and good weather. These are natural resources. Farmers grow the plants that we eat. Farmers also raise animals that give us things like milk and eggs. These goods can be sold to grocery stores. They can also be sold to bakers and restaurants.

title: Processing and Manufacturing
text: Manufacturing is creating goods. This is often done in factories. Workers take natural resources and process them to make something new. Most factories use machines to process, or change, resources. One factory might take trees and turn them into paper. Another factory might use trees to make furniture. Wool from sheep can be turned into clothing or blankets. Wheat can be turned into flour. The flour can then be then turned into bread or cake.

title: Tourism
text: Tourism is an industry that takes care of people who are traveling for fun. Beautiful natural features and resources often make people want to visit a place. People also travel to do activities. Some go to rivers, lakes, and oceans to fish. Others travel to mountains to ski. People who travel need goods and services. Tourists use transportation services, like airplanes and taxis. They need hotels and other places to stay. Tourists often go to restaurants to eat. Some tourists like guides to show them around. All these services are part of the tourism industry.

title: Oil Industry
text: The oil industry is the name we give to everyone working with oil, which is a natural resource. Some people work to get crude oil. Other workers refine oil. This means they make crude oil into something we can use. Oil is used to make many products. It is used to make gas for cars. It is also used to make crayons and bike tires.

title: Feelings
text: Happy is a feeling. Sad is a feeling. You have different feelings every day.

title: Choose Your Feelings
text: You are in charge of your feelings. It is normal to have lots of different feelings. If your toy breaks, you might feel sad. You might feel happy when you play with a friend. Think about how you like to feel.

title: Happy Thoughts
text: When you want to feel happy, what do you think about? Think about your favorite things. What makes you smile?

title: Smile
text:
A frown shows you are sad. A smile shows you are happy. When you smile you share your happiness with others.

Draw how you feel when someone smiles at you.

title: Your Attitude in Action
text: Your emotions reflect your attitude. Your attitude is how you act while you have feelings. You can show a positive attitude by saying please and thank you.

title: Markets
text: A market is a place where people buy and sell goods and services. A store where you buy groceries is a market. There are other kinds of markets, too. A market is not always a store. Some people buy and sell things on an online market. Everyone who buys or sells goods or services is part of a market. A local market includes people who live near you. Other markets can include all of your state or country. The international market includes millions of people from different nations of the world.

title: Essential Question
text: How do producers and consumers affect each other?

title: Producers
text: People who make goods or provide services are producers. A farmer might produce apples or blueberries to sell. A baker might produce apple or blueberry pies. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are used for other communities.

title: Consumers
text: People who buy goods and services are called consumers. When you buy apple juice or apple pie to eat, you are consuming. Consumers buy goods and services in their communities. They also buy goods and services from other communities. People can trade to meet their wants and needs.

title: Buying and Selling
text:
When you sell something, you are a producer. When you buy something, you are a consumer. People buy things based on their needs and wants. They make decisions based on what resources are available. The price of a good or service also affects their choices.

People can be both producers and consumers. A baker is a consumer when they purchase flour to make their bread. A baker is a producer when they sell their bread.

title: Producing or Consuming?
text: Look at the images. Identify the people. Are they producing or consuming?

title: Opportunity Cost
text:
Most of the time, we want many things. However, we usually can’t get everything we want. This means we have to make choices. Our choices are affected by the price and by what is available.

Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you make a choice. For example, imagine that you wanted to play at the park. Instead, you chose to go swimming. The opportunity cost of swimming is giving up the park and the enjoyment of playing there.

title: Essential Question
text: What affects how much things cost?

title: Supply and Demand
text: The price of a good or service depends on two things. First, it depends on how much of it there is for people to buy. That’s called supply. Next, it depends on how many people want or need it. That’s called demand. When the supply is low and the demand is high, the price goes up. When the supply is high and the demand is low, the price goes down.

title: Surplus
text: Surplus is when there is more of something than people need or want. A surplus of a good or service usually makes the price go down.

title: Scarcity
text: Scarcity is not having enough of something. Scarcity usually makes prices go up. When goods and services become scarce, families have to choose carefully. They have to decide what they need most. Sometimes scarcity can be a big problem. If food or water is scarce, it is hard for people to live.

text:

title: Engineering Design Process
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

Do you have any problems that you need to solve? Engineering may be able to help you! When you engineer something, you plan or build in a skillful way. Engineering is using science to find solutions, or answers to a problem. Engineering requires the use of scientific knowledge. It is also often called “applied science.” Technology is the machinery and equipment made by using scientific knowledge. Science isn’t the only tool that engineers work with, though. They also use things like wrenches, hammers, pliers, and drills. Measuring tape, levels, and vices also come in handy. These tools allow engineers to make their products as exact as possible. We interact with engineered products daily; they make our lives much easier!

Engineers follow a certain process. A process is a series of steps or actions that lead to a specific outcome. The engineering design process is steps that engineers use. It helps them to find the best possible solution to a problem. A problem is a question or challenge meant to encourage inquiry, consideration, or development of a solution. The whole engineering design process revolves around the problem. So, in order to start the engineering design process, you first have to identify the problem. One way to solve a problem is to collaborate. This is the ability to work together as a group to solve problems. A group is a number of individuals gathered together, usually for a purpose.

Write about a problem you had and the solution you used to fix it. Was technology involved? Why or why not?

Write about a problem we can solve as a class using the engineering design process. How might we do it?

title: Define
text:
Read the article. Answer the questions. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

The first step in the engineering design process is to define the problem. We define a problem in order to better understand it. Defining the problem also allows us to come up with solutions. When we define something, we are usually trying to find the meaning of a word or phrase. You can also define something by determining its important parts. When we define a problem, we look at the important parts of the problem. In order to define a problem, it is important to communicate. When you communicate, you share what you know about a topic. Communicating about a problem can help you figure out the important parts. You might be able to figure out how to address the important parts better. When you communicate to define a problem, you might ask questions. Or, you might share your ideas about what you think is happening. As you communicate you may learn new things that can change your thinking. It may change how you define the problem.

Look at the image. What observations can you make? What questions can you ask? Record your thoughts.

Define the problem for this week.

Solutions usually have criteria and constraints. Criteria are the standards on which judgments or decisions may be based. Constraints are rules or standards created to check, restrict, or compel one to avoid some action or behavior. Design solutions usually have constraints. They might be time, money, or material availability. List the criteria you will follow and the constraints you’ll have to overcome. What are the criteria and constraints for your design solution?

title: Ideate
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

The next step of the engineering design process is ideate. They use the information they gathered. To ideate, they form an idea about a possible solution. Scientists and engineers talk with one another. Doing so helps their ideas develop. Those ideas can grow into a strong design solution. Sometimes when scientists ideate, they learn even more about the problem they are trying to solve. That helps develop the solution more.

Come up with some ideas on how Alana can get her materials home safely. Be sure to take into consideration your criteria and constraints.
