title: Plan
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

Engineers collect all the ideas from their group. Then, they choose the idea that they think will make the best product. An ideal solution is the standard of perfection. Sometimes, a group may decide they like part of one person’s idea. They may also like a part of another person’s idea. You can combine ideas and then write down your group's plan. A plan includes drawings, labels, and descriptions and should be detailed. Another engineer should be able to look at your plan and create your product. Make sure your group has the same plan. Also, make sure everyone understands your design.

Use the space provided to develop a plan for your design solution. Be sure to take into consideration your criteria and constraints.

title: Create
text:
During the “Create” step of the process, you get to create a prototype. To create means to make something new. A prototype is the first draft of a product. Be creative, but stick to your plan as much as possible. Write down all of the materials you use in the design. Be sure to also include how much of each material you use.

Engineers sometimes work in groups. They listen to others and communicate their own ideas. When you work in a group, you need to participate, too.

title: Test
text:
After creating your prototype, it is time to see if it works. Check if the product solves the problem. If you want to know if your product works, you do a simple test. When you do a simple test, you examine, observe, or evaluate something to see if it works. When you test, you may take measurements. You may also write notes. You should always write what happens to your product as you perform tests. We call this collecting data. The data shows if your prototype works.

Sometimes a test results in failure. A failure is when something doesn't work as intended. Tests can also result in success. A success is when the product achieves its purpose.

Use the chart to collect your data.

How many things can your bag hold?
Did you complete your design solution in the time allotted? Yes / No

title: Improve
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

Have you noticed there is always a new phone advertised on TV? Why do you think that happens? The newest phones always have the best technology. Companies have engineers constantly improving their previous products. Improve means to make it better. To reflect on your product is to think about what worked and what did not work when you tested it. After engineers reflect, they refine. To refine something is to gradually improve it or make it better. Engineers go back to their plan, make changes, improve the creation, test again, and then reflect and refine again in order to optimize their product. To optimize something means to make it as perfect, effective, or functional as possible. This process can happen multiple times to make a product the best it can be.

Looking at your data from the “Test” step, where could your design solution be improved? Why? How? Use the space provided to improve your design.

[DRAWING SPACE]

What materials will you use? How will your product work better after the improvements?

[WRITING SPACE (LINED; minimum 4)]

title: Communicate
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

After you complete the steps in the engineering design process, it is important to communicate, or to share information about something with others. One way to share your findings is to write a reflection in your journal. What went well? What didn’t go well? What materials worked? What materials didn’t work? What would you do differently if you had a chance to try again? Communication is a great tool for learning! Communicating gives us opportunities to share our thinking, discoveries, and provide feedback. Feedback can be positive, something that could be improved, or neutral. People can learn from each others' experiences. You might even find an idea of merit, or something to deserve or be worthy of praise or high value, that worked well for someone else that you could try next time.

In group work, it is especially meaningful to communicate. Talk about your group’s experience building the product. On a separate sheet of paper, write down what your group talked about. Make a list of positive feedback and a list of things to improve.

title: Engineering Design Process
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

Do you have any problems that you need to solve? Engineering may be able to help you! When you engineer something, you plan or build in a skillful way. Engineering is using science to find solutions, or answers to a problem. Because engineering requires the use of scientific knowledge, it is often called “applied science.” Science isn’t the only tool that engineers work with, though. They also use things like wrenches, hammers, pliers, screwdrivers, and drills. Measuring tape, levels, vices, and utility knives also come in handy. These tools allow engineers to make their products as exact as possible. We interact with engineered products daily; they make our lives much easier!

Engineers follow a certain process. A process is a series of steps or actions that lead to a specific outcome. The engineering design process includes steps that engineers use. It helps them to find the best possible solution to a problem.

The six steps of the engineering design process are:

Define

Ideate

Plan

Create

Test

Improve

Humans have built amazing things using the engineering design process. This process wasn’t their only useful tool, though. They also had knowledge, creativity, imagination, flexibility, and teamwork on their side! The structures created by humans are sometimes hard to believe, even when you’re standing right next to them. The technology we use now is very different than what people used when the structures were created. Technology is the machinery and equipment made by using scientific knowledge.

The whole engineering design process revolves around the problem. A problem is a question or challenge meant to encourage inquiry, consideration, and development of a solution. So, in order to start the engineering design process, you first have to identify the problem. One way to solve a problem is to collaborate. To collaborate means to work together as a group to solve problems. A group is a number of individuals gathered together, usually for a purpose.

Write about a problem you had and the solution you used to fix it. Was technology involved? Why or why not?

Identify a problem we could solve as a class using the engineering design process. How might we do it?

title: Define
text:
Read the article. Answer the questions. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

The first step in the engineering design process is to define the problem. We define the problem in order to better understand the problem and to come up with solutions. When we define something, we are usually trying to find the meaning of a word or phrase, but you can also define something by determining its important parts. When we define a problem, we look at the important parts of the problem. To define a problem, you first have to look at the important parts of a situation that needs to be solved (or an engineering scenario). Communicating about that scenario can help you figure out its important parts and how to address them better. When you communicate, you share knowledge or information about a topic. When defining a problem, communication might involve asking questions or sharing ideas about what you think is happening in the engineering scenario. As you communicate, you may learn new things that can change your thinking and how you define the problem.

Look at the image. What observations can you make? What questions can you ask? Record your thoughts.

Using the engineering scenario for this week, define the problem.

Solutions usually have criteria and constraints. Criteria are the standards by which we know that our solution is successful. Constraints are the limitations or boundaries that engineers face when designing solutions to problems. Constraints occur naturally during the engineering design process. They might be time, money, or material availability. What are the criteria and constraints for your design solution? List the criteria you will follow and the constraints you’ll have to overcome.

title: Ideate
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

The next step of the engineering design process is to ideate. At this stage, engineers use the information they gathered to define the problem to help them ideate, or form ideas about a possible solutions. Engineers talk with one another to help their ideas develop or grow into a strong design solution. After all the possible solutions have been ideated, engineers compare them to see how well each one meets the criteria and constraints of the project. They may make adjustments to their ideas or even combine solutions. Doing so helps develop the solution more.

Come up with some ideas on how Alana can get her materials home safely. Be sure to take into consideration your criteria and constraints.

title: Plan
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

The third step in the engineering design process is to plan. You’ve explored many possible solutions to the problem. Now, it is time to choose one as your plan. Pick the ideal solution that you think will work the best. An ideal solution is one that you feel will best solve the problem while also meeting the criteria and constraints. The object that you make to solve the problem is called your product. If you are working in a team, make sure that you have the same plan for your product and that you work together. Meet and discuss the solutions that each person has come up with. Decide which one is the best solution as a group. If your solution isn’t chosen, that is okay! Continue to help your group throughout the process.

When engineers plan, they usually create a model by drawing or sketching their ideas. Eventually, their drawings and sketches are finalized into an official construction plan that is sometimes referred to as a blueprint. Engineers work with architects and construction managers before a blueprint is approved. Once it is approved, they send the blueprint to the builders.

As you sketch, pay close attention to each part of your design. These parts need to work together in order to solve the problem. Once you have drawn your design, label each part with additional details to explain your picture. Make sure that you list the supplies that you will need to design your solution. Write down the steps that you will take to create your product. This plan is like an instruction manual so that others can recreate your work. You may also plan for how you will test your solution against the criteria and constraints.

Use the space provided to develop a plan for your design solution. Be sure to take into consideration your criteria and constraints.

title: Create
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

During the “Create” step of the process, engineers bring their products to life. Now, it’s your turn to create the first draft of your product. This is called a prototype. Be creative, but stick to your plan as much as possible. Write down all of the materials used in the design. Be sure to also include how much of each material you use.

Engineers often work in groups. They listen to others and communicate their own ideas. When you work in a group, you need to participate, too. To be an effective and helpful team member, remember these guidelines:

Help your group with the product.

Communicate your thoughts.

Ask your group for ideas.

Listen to your team members respectfully.

Work cooperatively. Take turns and share materials.

Consider giving each person in the group a job so that no one gets left out.

Say something if someone takes over the project and doesn’t let others participate.

If a group member isn’t involved, invite them to help out.

Treat your materials with respect.

Take only what you need, and try to avoid waste. Share materials with other students or groups.

title: Test
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

Now that you’ve created your design, it’s ready to be tested! The “Test” step of the process helps you see if your product works like it is supposed to. A simple test determines if something works through examination, observation, or evaluation. Remember to be safe! Before testing, make sure that your work area is clear. As you begin to test your product, gather and record information in your notebook about what happens. This is called collecting data. You could choose to simply take notes or to represent your data visually with graphs and charts. Then, you should evaluate the data, or decide what fixes or changes you should make to your product. At this time, you can also compare your data with another student or group to see what did and did not work in their testing. Ask yourself: Did the product work? Did I solve the problem? Can I make the product better? Write down any problems that you encountered during testing. Write down things that went well, too. Taking notes will help you improve your product; the more notes you write, the better!

Sometimes a test results in failure, or an inability to perform a normal or intended function. Tests can also result in success. Success is the accomplishment of an aim or purpose.

Test your prototype. Use the chart to collect your data.

title: Improve
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

After gathering and evaluating information from testing, your product can now be improved. Because you want the best possible solution to the problem, look at your design and ask yourself: How can I improve my product? Also consider how you could improve your product using your collected data. Make sure that you record any changes that you make to your product.

When you improve your product, sometimes you need to go back to the drawing board and refine it. To refine something means to gradually improve it or make it better. Luckily, the engineering design process is flexible! If you decide to simply make improvements, you can move on and complete your project. However, if you figure out that you need to start from scratch, you can still return to the asking, ideation, or planning stages

Once you have created your new product, test it. If there are still improvements to be made, then you can optimize it as many times as you need to. To optimize something means to make it as perfect, effective, or functional as possible. Even if you do not find a solution to the problem, that is okay. We can learn from our mistakes and try again.

Looking at your data from the “Test” step, where could your design solution be improved? Why? How? Use the space provided to improve your design.

What materials will you use to improve your product? How will your product work better after the improvements?

title: Communicate
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

After you complete the steps in the engineering design process, it is important to communicate what you learned with others. One way to communicate your findings is to write a reflection in your journal. What went well and what didn’t go well? What materials worked or didn’t work? What would you have done differently? Communication is a great tool for learning! To communicate means to tell someone about something through words, images, or videos. Communicating gives us opportunities to share our thinking, discoveries, and provide feedback. Feedback can be positive, suggestions for improvement, or neutral. People can learn from your experiences, and you can learn from others’ experiences. You might even find an idea that worked well for someone else that you could try next time.

In group work, it is especially meaningful to communicate. Talk about your group’s experience building the product. On a separate sheet of paper, write down what your group talked about. Make a list of positive feedback and a list of things to improve.

Read the article. Circle the vocabulary words and underline their meanings.

The engineering design process is a cycle that you continue to move through. After gathering and evaluating information from testing, the product can now be improved. Because you want the best possible solution to the problem, look at your design and ask yourself: How can I improve my product? Also, consider how you could improve your product using your collected data. Either way, make sure that you record any changes that you make to your product.

When you improve your product, sometimes you need to go back to the drawing board and refine it. To refine something means to gradually improve it or make it better. Luckily, the engineering design process is flexible! If you decide to simply make improvements, you can move on and complete your project. However, if you figure out that you need to start from scratch, you can still return to the asking, ideation, or planning stage.

Once you have created your new product, test it. If there are still improvements to be made, then you can go through this cycle again to optimize it as many times as you need to. To optimize something means to make it as perfect, effective, or functional as possible. Even if you do not find a solution to the problem, that is okay. We can learn from our mistakes and try again.

Looking at your data from the “Test” step, where could your design solution be improved? Why? How? Use the space provided to improve your design.

What materials will you use to improve your product? How will your product work better after the improvements?

title: Communicate
text:
Read the article. Circle the vocabulary word and underline its meaning.

Through successes and even failures, engineers are proud of their work. Both failures and successes lead to new learning, ideas, and innovations. But if engineers never share their discoveries with others, will it make a difference? Of course not! Engineers communicate their work to their bosses, clients, and coworkers. To communicate means to tell someone about something through words, images, or videos. By communicating, we can share our thinking, discoveries, and provide feedback. Feedback can be positive, suggestions for improvement, or neutral.

After working on your product, it is time to share your hard work. In group work, it is especially meaningful to communicate. On a separate sheet of paper, write down what your group talked about. Make a list of positive feedback and a list of things to improve.

title: Test 4
text:
You can see patterns in the sky by looking up from your place on earth.

The sun rises in the east to start the day. It is high in the sky in the middle of the day. It sets in the west. Then it is night.

The moon also rises in the east and sets in the west. You can see it day or night.

Stars also rise in the east. They set in the west.

The sun, moon, and stars all seem to move across the sky from east to west. This pattern happens over time.

Virginia was the location of many battles in the American Civil War. By 1863 the farmland of northern Virginia was destroyed. Crops were not planted. Orchards were not harvested. Soldiers from all over the Confederacy joined the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia. Companies of soldiers from Texas, Louisiana, Alabama and Arkansas joined General Robert E. Lee’s command. He was desperate for supplies to care for the soldiers.

Lee was aware of the richness of Pennsylvania farms. No fighting had occurred in Pennsylvania. There were many supplies available for the confederate troops.

Additionally, Harrisburg was not far from the state border. Capturing a northern city would be a victory for the Confederate States of America (CSA). The Confederate position in Pennsylvania would endanger the safety of Baltimore, Maryland and Washington, DC. It was a daring risk for General Lee. Lee turned the Confederate army north to invade Pennsylvania.

General Lee used the physical features of the Blue Ridge Mountains to his advantage. The Army of northern Virginia moved northward from Winchester, Virginia on the west side of the Appalachian mountains. The mountains shielded the 75,000 man Army from being seen by the 90,000-man Federal army that was on the east side of the mountains.

Major General George Meade wanted to keep the Federal army to the east to protect Washington DC. Meade knew Lee’s men were moving north, unsure of the target. The Federal army moved north to pursue or follow the Confederate army in hopes of catching up.

The Confederate Army entered Pennsylvania. They traveled to Chambersburg in the Cumberland Valley. Parts of the army continued to move north and east to occupy Camp Hill and York, Pennsylvania. The CSA army confiscated or seized needed supplies as they went through the farms of Adams and York counties. Small companies of the Confederate army used the roads to easily move about the Pennsylvania countryside.

Twelve roadways converged or met at a location in Gettysburg, Adams County. Gettysburg is centered in the valley of two ridges of the Allegheny mountains. The ridges run north-south with patches of woods, fields, and farmland. There are areas of large granite boulders coming out of the ridges and fields. Streams make their way down the ridges to create wetlands and rivers.

To the west of Gettysburg was “Seminary Ridge”. It was named for the Lutheran college for ministers that was located there. To the east of Gettysburg, about three miles away, is “Cemetery Ridge” and Culp’s Hill” . They were named for the graveyard and the farm located there. To the south of Cemetery Ridge are the small tree-covered mountains known as “Big Round Top” and “Little Round Top”. The town and farms can all be seen from Little Round Top.

The Confederate Army camped on Seminary Ridge. The Federal Army chose Cemetery Ridge, from Culp's Hill to Little Round Top. The two armies met in a battle on July 1, 2, and 3, 1863.

It was the physical features of Gettysburg that attracted both armies to the location. The hills, woods, streams, and granite boulders had created a marketplace for a town. The same physical features of the landscape set up a place for two armies to clash. Each tried to use the physical features to their advantage. The battle of Gettysburg became a turning point for the American Civil War. It also became a symbol of care and respect for those who fought.

title: Baron Friedrich von Steuben
text:
Like the Marquis de Lafayette and Casimir Pulaski, Friedrich Wilhelm von Steuben was another key European ally for the Continental Army during the American Revolution. Von Steuben was born in the kingdom of Prussia, a country that encompassed areas of present-day Germany, Poland, and other eastern European countries, in 1730.

At the age of 17, von Steuben joined the Prussian Army. He led troops during the Seven Years’ War and served as a member of King Frederick of Prussia’s council on war matters. During the Seven Years’ War, von Steuben gained extensive knowledge on military strategies and tactics. He would later use this knowledge to aid the Continental Army during the American Revolution.

After the Seven Years’ War, von Steuben served as the Grand Marshall (someone in charge of running court affairs) to the Prince of Hohenzollern-Hechingen, a small state in what is now Germany. Von Steuben earned several awards during his service, including the title of baron. However, from 1775 on, von Steuben began to look for work in the military.

He looked into several armies around Europe, but no positions opened up for him. Eventually, he met Silas Deane and Benjamin Franklin in France, who were there as ambassadors for the United States. Although there was no guarantee of rank or pay if he volunteered to serve, von Steuben eventually decided to take his chances and set sail for America.

Upon his arrival in the United States, von Steuben presented himself before the Continental Congress. With his military experience, as well as a letter of introduction from Benjamin Franklin, the congress arranged to have von Steuben paid after the war. They sent him to the camp at Valley Forge to help General George Washington get his troops trained.

Von Steuben first inspected the conditions of the camp, the soldiers, and their equipment. Then, he got to work writing standardized drills for the entire Continental Army to use. Copies of these drills were sent out to every company and officer. This helped organize the army and ensure all of the soldiers received the same training.

Von Steuben’s methods, organization, and discipline met with great success. The Continental Army showed marked improvement under his direction, and the soldiers liked him for personally working with the troops, which was uncommon at the time.

Thanks to von Steuben’s contributions, the Continental Army went from a ragtag group of farmers and volunteers to a disciplined and well-trained military force.

title: Casimir Pulaski
text:
Another foreign soldier who had a profound impact on the American Revolution was Casimir Pulaski. Pulaski was born in Poland in 1745. He was a member of a prominent Polish family with ties to the Polish government. From a young age, Pulaski’s father trained him to be an expert horseman. These skills served Pulaski well in the conflicts he experienced later in life.

At this time in history, Polish politics were heavily influenced by the Russian monarchy. Pulaski’s father was a supporter of Polish independence and instilled these beliefs in his son. In 1772, Pulaski fought against Russian control of Poland. This rebellion failed, and he fled to France. While living in France, Pulaski met American diplomats Benjamin Franklin and Silas Deane, who were serving as the American ambassadors to the French government. Franklin and Deane convinced Pulaski to join the Patriot cause for American independence.

In 1777, Pulaski sailed to Boston and traveled to meet George Washington, hoping to receive a military commission. He proved himself a capable soldier at the Battle of Brandywine in Pennsylvania and was given the rank of brigadier general by the Continental Congress. He also spent the winter of 1777-1778 at Valley Forge. While at Valley Forge, Pulaski assisted Washington in reorganizing his cavalry forces. Because of his expertise and military prowess, Washington sent Pulaski to South Carolina with a small cavalry force to assist continental troops in the Southern Colonies.

In the fall of 1779, Pulaski traveled to Savannah, Georgia, and assisted colonial forces during the siege of the city. On the last day of the siege, he was struck down by British gunfire and died from his injuries. Pulaski is remembered as an influential figure in the fight for Polish and American independence.

title: World War II
text:
World War II

In 1939, another terrible war began in Europe. Again, the United States was determined to stay out of the war, but something happened on December 7, 1941. It left America no choice but to fight back. On that date, Japanese airplanes dropped bombs on the United States naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. Thousands of Americans were killed, and many American ships were sunk. Twenty-two Nebraskans lost their lives on the battleship USS Arizona during the bombing. After the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, the United States declared war on Japan.

With many of the men off fighting the war, thousands of women took over their jobs, doing work they had never done before. In Nebraska, women worked in factories to make airplanes and other essential supplies. One of those airplanes was the Enola Gay. The B-29 Superfortress was built at the Martin factory in Omaha. This plane would be used to attack Japan.

I can remember the B-29s were a particular fascination to me because they were in Grand Island … During school hours, if a plane went over, the whole school was dismissed for a few minutes to go out and watch the plane go over.

— Geraldine George Sorensen, Grand Island grade school student

Nebraska’s location between the Rocky Mountains and the Appalachian mountains made it the perfect place to build airfields for the U.S. Army. It had favorable weather conditions and acres of open land. The cities of Ainsworth, Alliance, Bruning, Fairmont, Fort Crook, Grand Island, Harvard, Kearney, Lincoln, McCook, Scottsbluff, and Scribner all built airbases. This created new jobs for people living in Nebraska.

It is truly an amazing sight to see these Army air bases suddenly rise into view from farms, cattle ranges, or hayflats. As one drives across the state, there first appears an orange and black checkerboard water tank rising above the horizon. Then the blue-green glass windows of a control tower come into sight. Hangars housing big war birds [airplanes] are seen, their arched domes across the sky.

— Lt. Howard J. Otis, Air Force Public Relations Officer, July 1943

Japan signed the final terms of surrender on board the battleship USS Missouri on September 2, 1945. People all over the world breathed a sigh of relief and hoped for peaceful times.

title: The Civil Rights Movement
text:
The American Civil Rights Movement was a response to discriminatory laws that were put in place after the Civil War ended. These laws segregated Black people from white people. Segregation is the practice of separating one group of people from another.

Brown v. Board of Education

In 1951, Oliver Brown filed a lawsuit against the Topeka Board of Education. His daughter had not been allowed to attend a school close to their house because she was African American. Thurgood Marshall was one of the key lawyers in the case. Marshall argued that segregated schools could never be equal.

Marshall presented the case to the U.S. Supreme Court in 1954. Chief Justice Earl Warren responded that segregation violated the equal protection clause of the 14th Amendment. The court ordered schools across the United States to integrate.

Montgomery Bus Boycott

In 1955, a woman named Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a public bus for a white passenger, as the law at that time required. She was arrested. The civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. organized a bus boycott in response to her arrest.

The boycott lasted 381 days. It ended when the Supreme Court ruled that segregation on buses was illegal.

Little Rock Nine

In 1954, in Brown v. Board of Education, the Supreme Court said segregation was against the Constitution. One of the first places people complied with the ruling was Little Rock, Arkansas. Nine African American students who had attended a segregated school were chosen to go to Little Rock Central High School in 1957. They became known as the Little Rock Nine. Until then, only white students had attended Little Rock Central High. Crowds of people who did not like integration tried to stop the students from getting to their classes. The governor sent the Arkansas National Guard to prevent the students from going inside the school. President Eisenhower intervened with the authority of the executive branch. The students were able to go to class, but people continued to bully and threaten them every day. This did not stop the Little Rock Nine. They continued to attend their new school. They helped ensure that all Americans had access to a quality education.

The De Porres Club

Mildred Brown was the African American owner, publisher, and editor of the newspaper The Omaha Star. The newspaper was founded in 1938. The Omaha Star was a place where activists could communicate and keep communities updated and involved. She met with city leaders and presidents as she fought for equal rights. She founded the De Porres Club to challenge discrimination and make African American voices heard. The club had a long history in Omaha’s Civil Rights Movement.

title: Thinking Like a Historian
text:
Historians study many types of sources to unlock the mysteries of the past. Written sources are the most common type of sources used by historians. These sources provide written evidence about specific events, time periods, and people throughout history. Written sources include books, newspaper articles, journals, letters, and important documents.

Historians also use visual sources. These include maps, photographs, paintings, and videos. Historians use these sources to study events and learn more about the past. Additionally, they analyze oral histories to learn more about events and people. Oral histories are interviews, recorded on audio or video, with someone who experienced an event in the past.

Historians use artifacts to understand the past. Artifacts are man-made objects that help us learn about past civilizations and how they developed. They can also be ordinary objects used in the past by people working or interacting with others. Artifacts help us understand what people’s lives were like. Artifacts can include tools, pottery, artwork, clothing, and jewelry. Historians work with archaeologists to determine the purpose of different artifacts. Archaeologists are scientists who excavate and study items left behind by people throughout history.

title: Patterns in Movement: Did You Know?
text:
Have you ever been on a swing? You swing your legs and go back and forth. The harder you swing your legs, the higher you will go. If you continue this motion, you will follow the same pattern: back and forth, back and forth, and so on. If you keep swinging your legs, you will eventually stop, right? You will be surprised to know that the laws of physics say otherwise. You will actually keep going until a force causes you to stop! That force could be you or something around you.

Let’s look a little deeper at this example and see how it differs from what you might have thought before. When you use your legs to swing back and forth, your legs create a constant motion. If you continue that constant motion, then you will continue going back and forth until you stop pumping your legs. The swing does not start moving side-to-side or follow any other pattern without some kind of other force acting on it. For example, the wind could change your movement, or you might start twisting the swing around. This is true for other objects too, such as rolling a ball around in a bowl. It is important to remember that the object will always continue on its path until a force stops it. So what stops the swing when you quit swinging your legs? Believe it or not, it’s gravity!

title: Migration
text: Migration is the movement of people, ideas, and goods from one place to another. People can migrate to new cities, states, and even countries. Migration to and from an area can affect communities. A large increase in population may put a strain on natural resources. Many people leaving an area may put a strain on local businesses. When people migrate, they bring many different ideas and cultures together. This mixing of cultures creates a new community.

title: Essential Question
text: Why do people move from one place to another?

title: Reasons for Movement
text: Movement can be small or large. People move for many reasons. Geographers call these reasons push-pull factors. Push-pull factors help us understand how and why people move. Push and pull factors are different for every person. What could be a pull factor for one person could be a push factor for another.

title: Push Factors
text: Push factors are a reason people move. They are things that push people away from a place. A push factor could be moving to avoid harmful situations. This type of push factor includes war, natural disasters, and religious persecution. Other push factors include poor economics and a lack of natural resources.

title: Pull Factors
text:
A pull factor is something that encourages people to move to another place. Factors that pull people to a new community are usually positive. Pull factors include better jobs, more freedom, or different resources.

Pull factors can also be influenced by various details. These factors are personal, economic, political, and environmental. However, they are always important.

text: Create a list of your movements within the day. Think about the reasons for your movement. Is it a push factor or a pull factor? Write the action under the appropriate column. Be prepared to explain your reasoning.

text:

title: Working Together
text:
No two people are exactly the same. We each have different beliefs and experiences. Sometimes, people and communities experience conflict because of their differences. Conflict is a disagreement between individuals or groups. Conflict can happen between two people, or it can even happen between nations. Although it can be difficult, overcoming conflict is possible.

In order to overcome conflict, we need to have a plan. A plan helps us to solve a problem step by step. We also need to make decisions while we plan and while we work through the conflict. Decision-making skills and problem-solving skills go together. When we use both sets of skills and work together, we find solutions to many types of problems.

title: Consensus and Compromise
text: Consensus and compromise are two possible ways to find a solution. Consensus is when most people in a group have the same opinion or agree to the same solution. However, consensus isn’t always possible. People often have different opinions about how to solve a problem. It can be hard to agree on a solution. When we can’t agree, we have to compromise. When we compromise, we change our thinking about a solution. In a compromise, everyone gives up something to create a solution. When we compromise, we think about the common good, not just about what we want.

title: Essential Question
text: How can we solve problems?

title: Conflict Resolution
text:
When conflicts arise, there are steps we can take to solve the problem.

First, we need to clearly identify the problem. This means we need to state what the problem is. We also need to gather information to identify the cause of the problem.

Next, we need to think about solutions to the problem. There are many ways to solve a problem. It is important to gather information about each possible solution. Information helps us to consider the advantages and disadvantages of each solution. We need to know which solution is the best. We might consider things like which solution costs less or would last longer. We often try to choose the solution that most people agree with. However, it is not always easy for people to agree on a single solution.

Once we pick a solution, it is time to implement it. Some solutions require experts or money. Experts can tell us how much money is needed. They can also show us the right way to implement the solution.

After we try a solution, we need to evaluate the results. To evaluate means to see how well it has worked. If the solution hasn’t worked, we need to consider why. Once we know why it didn’t work, we can fix it. Evaluating a solution can also mean collecting more data and starting the process again.

title: Practice Solving a Problem
text:
Jack found some beans that he believed were magic. He decided to plant them, even though his mother disagreed. The next morning, Jack woke up to a beanstalk that reached all the way to the clouds. It was enormous! Jack decided to explore the beanstalk. He climbed and climbed until he reached the top. On top of the clouds, he found a castle that was large enough to be home to a giant. He explored the clouds around the castle and found a golden goose that seemed to lay golden eggs. He decided to go back down to the ground to show the goose to his mother.

On his way back to the beanstalk, Jack felt the clouds begin to shake under his feet. He slowly turned around and saw the giant that inhabited the huge house. Before the giant noticed him, Jack scurried down the beanstalk with the goose. He ran back home, yelling, “There is a giant on the beanstalk!” Everyone in the town, who was confused about the beanstalk to begin with, was startled by the news and decided to call a town meeting. They requested that Jack come to the meeting and explain to them what was happening.

When Jack arrived, the town began to discuss the dangers that this beanstalk had created for the community. What if it fell? How many resources was it taking from the town? Worst of all, what if the giant came down and attacked the town to get his golden goose back? Jack realized he had made a mistake by planting this beanstalk.

What should the town do to handle the situation of the beanstalk? How should it be removed without the giant coming down? Should the goose be returned? Should Jack get in trouble?

Clearly identify a problem: What is the problem?

Gather information about the problem: Why is the problem happening? What do I already know about the problem? What else should I find out?

List and consider solutions: What are possible solutions to the problem? What are the advantages and disadvantages of each solution?

Implement a solution: Which solution would be the best for this situation? How could we make the solution happen?

Evaluate your efforts: How did the solution work? How could we improve the solution in the future?

Before the giant noticed him, Jack scurried down the beanstalk with the goose. He ran back home, yelling, “There is a giant on the beanstalk!” Everyone in the town, who was confused about the beanstalk to begin with, was startled by the news and decided to call a town meeting. They requested that Jack come to the meeting and explain to them what was happening.

When Jack arrived, the town began to discuss the dangers that this beanstalk had created for the community. What if it fell? How many resources was it taking from the town? Worst of all, what if the giant came down and attacked the town to get his golden goose back? Jack realized he had made a mistake by planting this beanstalk.

What should the town do to handle the situation of the beanstalk? How should it be removed without the giant coming down? Should the goose be returned? Should Jack get in trouble?

title: What Is an Interview?
text:
An interview is a type of conversation that focuses on asking and answering questions. The answers to the questions help people to learn about a person, topic, or event. Interviews are often used in news shows. An interview with a person who talks about their experiences is a primary source. Primary sources are needed to study history.

This week, you will be a historian. You will be interviewing an adult who has been an eyewitness to history. You will develop questions. You will listen and summarize the interview. You will share the information of the person’s experiences.

title: Essential Question
text: How is continuity and change a way to study the past?

title: Invisible Forces: Did You Know?
text: If you have ever been to the beach or a lake, you may have seen someone walking around with a metal detector. They swish this long-armed machine back and forth across the shore hoping to find something valuable buried in the sand. That metal detector acts as a magnet. It can detect when metals are around and where to dig for them. People have found gold, silver, and copper with metal detectors! The name “metal detector” implies it is able to detect all metals. Items that are magnetic are almost always some sort of metal. However, many metals are not magnetic at all. For example, most soda cans are made out of aluminum. Aluminum is a very thin and weak metal. Think about how easily it can be crushed! Aluminum is metal, but aluminum cans are not magnetic. Even if you put a magnet next to it, the magnet will not stick to the can. Before assuming a metal is magnetic, test the object with a magnet and record what happens. If they come together, the object is magnetic. If it does not, then it is not magnetic!

title: The 72nd Pennsylvania Infantry Regiment
text:
The 72nd Pennsylvania Infantry Regiment was a group of volunteer soldiers who served in the Union Army. Infantry refers to soldiers who are trained to fight on foot. Many of these soldiers were firefighters from Philadelphia. The 72nd was involved in many battles during the Civil War. These included battles in Antietam, the Overland Campaign, and Gettysburg. At Gettysburg, they defended an area known as “the Angle” and helped defeat the Confederate forces there. They also helped stop “Pickett’s Charge,” when the Confederate Army attempted to take Cemetery Hill from Union control. The 72nd's soldiers helped secure the Union Army’s defenses, and the Confederate Army was stopped.

The surviving members of the 72nd Infantry Regiment wanted a monument built to honor and remember their role in the battle. The correct placement of a monument was important to the soldiers who fought there. The former soldiers wanted their monument placed exactly where they fought. Many did not agree with the planned location of their monument. They took the group responsible for placing the monument to court. The case made it all the way to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, the highest court in the state. The former soldiers of the 72nd Infantry won their court battle. Their monument was placed where they wanted it on the battlefield as part of the Gettysburg National Military Park.

title: Motion: Did You Know?
text: When we think of the word force, we often think of motion. For something to move, there has to be a force acting on it, right? For example, if someone is riding their bike down the street, the motion of them pedaling their bike forces the bike to go forward. If the bike is not moving and is propped up with the kickstand, there is no motion, so there must be no force, right? If you think this, you might be surprised to learn that the laws of physics say otherwise! Did you know that you can actually have things happening that we cannot see, and those things can be considered a force? Using the bike example, let’s take a deeper look at how forces are at work even when the bike is propped up by a kickstand and not moving. First, the kickstand is holding the bike up. Without the kickstand, the bike would just fall to the side. The force of the kickstand on the ground allows the bike to remain standing up. There is no motion, but the weight of the bike is balanced by the kickstand. If someone goes to use the bike, kicks up the kickstand, and is not actually holding the bike, it will fall due to no forces keeping it up. Even an object at rest will have some kind of force acting on it.

title: Surviving as a Group: Did You Know?
text:
Every living organism needs four simple things: food, water, shelter, and sleep. If all living organisms have those things, they will survive. If a predator comes around, they can hide or fight. It’s natural for organisms to have predators. Organisms must know how to take care of themselves.

Not every living organism is out for themselves. Many organisms, including larger animals like lions, zebras, buffalo, and wolves, thrive together and not alone. There are many animals that actually form groups to live together. They survive longer that way. Their species then continues to live on through the generations and thrive because they have worked together. For example: a pride of lions. A pride will have one male lion who is usually the king of the pride. This means he is the most dominant and in charge of the pride. However, he cannot protect the whole pride by himself. He has to rely on other male lions to help protect the females and cubs. If a herd of buffalo came charging at the lions, the lions could better defend themselves if there was a group of them rather than just one single lion.

Every living organism needs food, water, shelter, and sleep to survive. They also need protection from predators. Often, protection comes in numbers. Organisms' chances of survival are often better together.

title: Trait Adaptation: Did You Know
text: You’ve probably heard that bats hunt at night, hang upside down, and can’t see. Bats do often hang upside down and hunt at night. However, they are not blind. We think that bats are blind because bats fly in the dark, when eyesight is not very helpful. We have been told this, and it has been accepted over time. However, some bats have better eyesight than humans do. Some bats within the same species have certain characteristics that actually help them survive. Some bats, such as the vampire bat, actually have such sensitive vision that they see better at night than during the day. Flying fox bats have huge eyes that allow them to see almost all of the way around their heads. Bats also have excellent hearing. They use echolocation to hear their prey. Vision and hearing allow bats to hunt when it is dark. If they did not have these traits, they would not be able to survive.

title: Fossils: Did You Know?
text:
Fossils are all over our planet. We can find them at the beach or in the mountains. Sometimes, we might find them in our own backyard. When we find one, we think we have found an animal or plant from the past. Did you know that what you’re looking at is not actually the plant or animal? A fossil is actually a rock!

Ancient organisms lived all over the planet. Soon after they died, they were covered in sediment. Over long periods of time, the minerals from the sediment seeped into the remains. The remains become fossils. Fossils can be organisms such as plants or animals.

Fossils are clues to the past. We are not looking at the exact plant or animal as it was. We are looking at a preservation or imprint of the hardest parts of that animal or plant in rock. We can use fossils to help us understand more about what life was like for that plant or animal at the time.

title: Interview: Supporting Questions
text: Create questions on the topic you have chosen. Have the questions be open. This means they cannot be answered by a “yes” or “no.” For example: “What types of toys did you play with when you were my age?” instead of “Did you play with toys?” Write your questions in the order you want them to be asked.

title: Traits and the Environment: Did You Know?
text:
We have learned that from the time we are born, we learn our traits from our parents. Our parents tell us what to eat, drink, and do. Organisms also inherit traits from their parents. However, traits are not just inherited from parents. The environment can impact an organism and cause its traits to change over time.

Let’s look at the example of flowering plants. A plant, such as a dandelion, can grow in an area where there is sunlight and water. It will continue to grow and reproduce. It will produce bright, beautiful flowers. If there is a drought, however, there will be less rain. The plants will not have as much water as they usually do. The dandelions are still growing. However, without the water they are used to, they grow smaller. They may not have big, beautiful flowers anymore. They may not have as many nutrients. They may reproduce smaller offspring. They will continue to reproduce that way unless they receive more water. The environment can really change the way a plant grows, regardless of the traits it inherited from its parents.

text:
Set up a time to talk with the eyewitness.

Remember to be respectful.

Ask one question at a time.

Actively listen to the person.

Ask if there is anything else the person would like to share.

Take notes. Include the name of the person and the years they are talking about.

Thank the person for being interviewed.

title: Specialization
text: Communities have different resources. They use these resources to produce goods and services. Many communities and businesses focus on making one product or service to sell. This focus is called specialization. For example, communities with good land and a good climate often use their resources to grow crops. States in the Midwest have the resources to grow soybeans, corn, and other grains. On the west coast, grain doesn’t grow as well. However, communities can grow fruit and nuts. Fruit also grows well in the southeastern United States. Businesses specialize in growing these products to sell to other communities.

title: Essential Question
text: Why does the United States trade with other nations?

title: All About Respect
text:
Respect can be a feeling. You can feel respect for another person. When you respect someone, you accept that they have opinions and differences, and you want to treat them with kindness. Everyone can demonstrate respect. You can show others respect through your words and actions. When someone is different from you, you can ask them questions to learn more about them. You can support your peers in their healthy behaviors and encourage others to be respectful as well. In what ways have others shown you respect?

title: Ocean Water Survival: Did You Know?
text: Have you ever thought about how animals came to be in their environment? How did the polar bear come to be in the Arctic? In the Arctic, it is cold, icy, and there is an ocean full of fish to eat. How did the desert tortoise come to be in the desert? In the desert there is not a lot of water, but lots of plants for them to eat. Animals could move from one place to another and thrive. All they have to do is adapt to their surroundings. Did you know that animals cannot just adapt and live anywhere? Animals will only live in an area that supports their needs. For example: polar bears tend to be found in cold, icy areas like the Arctic. The primary diet for a polar bear is fish. There is a vast ocean for them to find the food they need. Polar bears also have a very thick coat, so they prefer a colder environment. For the desert tortoise, they can store water in their bodies. They can use the stored water for months without worrying about getting more. They eat the plants found around them. Both the animals would not survive in their habitats if they did not have their needs met. The next time you’re thinking about why an animal is found where it is, consider what the animal needs. Consider how its needs are being met.

title: Interdependence
text:
Most communities sell their specialized products to other communities. Interdependence is when people depend on others to provide products to sell. People, businesses, and countries can depend on each other.

A factory can specialize in making car tires. That means tires are all the factory does. Car tires would not be very useful without a car. A car without tires would not be very useful, either. Specialization creates interdependence. The car company needs tires to create cars. The tire company needs to sell its tires. People buy and sell different things. This helps people get everything they need.

title: Trade
text:
Most countries and states don’t make everything their citizens need and want. Each place has its own resources. Sometimes people have to buy things from other states or countries. Some places have oil and coal. Other places have fish, fruits, and vegetables. Trade is when people buy and sell goods and services between places. It's also when people exchange a good or service for something they want or need.

People around the world depend on each other. The United States does not produce everything Americans need and want. The United States trades with other countries. We get goods from other countries. We send goods to other countries, too.

title: Imports and Exports
text: Trade between countries depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods that are brought in from another country. Exports are goods that are sent out of a country to be sold. We depend on each other to trade. We barter the resources we have for the resources we need.

title: How Can People Make a Difference in Their Community?
text: Communities have problems, just like people do. The members of every community can work together to solve their problems. They can listen to everyone’s ideas. This helps them come up with the best solution. Every citizen can be involved in solving their community’s problems.

title: Essential Question
text: What impact can I have on my community right now?

title: Decision Making
text: We have to make decisions to solve problems. Good information can help us make decisions and solve problems. Graphs, maps, charts, and diagrams give good information. Look at the decision-making model. It shows steps to make good decisions. These steps also help us solve problems.

title: Identify, Gather, List, and Consider
text: Every community has its own problems. Ask an adult about problems they see in your community. Create a list of the problems. Ask a lot of questions. Gather as much information about the problems as you can. Ask where to find more information. Ask about possible solutions.

title: Consider and Implement a Solution
text:
Everyone has the ability to solve problems. Students worldwide have solved problems in their communities. When you see a problem and tell an adult, you are helping to solve it.

There are some problems in your community you can solve on your own. When you see such a problem, you take action. You do not wait for someone else to solve the problem. You come up with a plan. Then, you do your very best to reach your goal. We can work together to solve problems.

title: Evaluate
text: After you have implemented your plan, you look at the result. You review your solution and evaluate it. This means that you decide if the solution you chose worked well. Create a report that shows your process and evaluation.

title: Environmental Changes: Did You Know?
text:
The Amazon Rainforest in South America is one of the most diverse ecosystems in the world. It is home to over a million different species of insects, plants, and animals. The rainforest thrives because all the species work together to survive. Some might believe that when a new organism comes into the area, everything remains the same. Others may think that humans moving into the area would not impact the animals or plants. However, when a new organism moves into an area, it can impact organisms already living there. These changes can even have life-threatening outcomes.

One change to the rainforest has been because of logging. Humans cut down trees to use for lumber. The lumber is used to build homes, schools, and other buildings. When those trees are removed, it disrupts the entire ecosystem. Insects living within the trees are forced out. Without the trees that used to provide shade or shelter, animals who sought the trees' protection become exposed. Some animals are forced to move elsewhere. Species that once thrived no longer have shelter, food, or protection.

We might see changes to the environment as something that benefits us. However, there are millions of other organisms that are impacted by this change.

title: Patterns of Weather: Did You Know?
text: Every year the seasons come and go. During seasons that are colder, there can be more rainfall. During seasons that are hotter, there is less. We often think that because we have data from previous years, we can always tell what the weather will be during a certain time of year. This is not completely true though. We can use data from previous years to see what we might expect from the weather. However, we cannot really tell until the weather actually happens. For example: California may experience El Niño in late September and early October. El Niño is a time when there are warm winds and increased rainfall. El Niño happens every two to seven years. However, they do not occur on a regular schedule. Another area may have several feet of snow in one year. The next year, there may not be as much snow. Scientists continue to record the patterns of weather. However, until the weather happens, we cannot assume that it will always be the same.

title: Weather and climate: Did You Know?
text: When you get ready for school in the morning, the first thing you might do is look outside. What is happening outside can help you decide what you’re going to wear that day. If it is cloudy and cold, you might put on a jacket. If it is hot, you might make sure you are wearing shorts. What you are thinking about when you decide what to wear is the weather. Sometimes we think weather and climate are the same thing, because we often hear the words used in place of each other. However, climate is similar to weather, but it is not the same. When you look outside, you are using the weather to help you decide what to wear. Weather is the day-to-day conditions. Weather can change without warning. For example: it might be a beautiful, sunny, summer day, but then a thunderstorm rolls through. There might be some rain, but it quickly passes. Then you are back to playing outside. The climate is like weather, but over a long period of time. Scientists look at rainfall, temperatures, wind, snow, and other factors. They record the data and get an average of an area's climate. Scientists know that some parts of the planet have warmer climates, such as South America or Africa. They know some parts of the planet have colder climates, such as Alaska and Russia. Day-to-day weather can always change. Climate changes more slowly. Climate is what scientists refer to when tracking an area’s weather over long periods of time.

title: Weather Hazards: Did You Know?
text: Humans are in constant need of water. They build dams to store extra water. A dam is a structure that can hold back water. It is usually built on a river and can form a reservoir. The water can be used later when it is needed. When there is too much rain, the dam can hold that water. The dam can reduce flooding and possibly save lives. Some people believe dams are built not to cause harm and will last forever. However, human-made structures, like the dam, can still have lasting consequences. Animals, fish, and plant life changes when a dam is built. Dams can reduce the impact of natural hazards, like heavy rainfall. However, that does not mean they last forever. In 2021, the Aqua Dam in Louisiana failed. There was a major storm that caused the dam to fill up higher than it was used to. Higher water means more water weighing against the dam. The Aqua Dam could not take the pressure of the water and broke. The failure caused major flooding below the dam. Hundreds of people had to leave their homes and belongings. Unfortunately, humans cannot completely eliminate natural hazards like heavy rainfall or flooding. However, we can build solutions to help reduce the impacts of natural hazards.

title: Organizing Regions
text:
We organize the Earth into regions to help us learn about our world. A region is an area that has similar characteristics. Dividing large areas of the world into regions makes it easier for us to study them. Some regions are organized based on their physical characteristics. Physical characteristics can include landforms, climate, or biomes. Some regions are organized by their human characteristics. These human characteristics may include population, culture, or language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

Regions can have political boundaries, such as cities, states, countries, and continents. Regions can also be organized by systems of people, goods, and ideas. Some examples are metropolitan areas, suburbs, and neighborhoods. Regions can be categorized by historical context. An example of this is the original 13 Colonies. The Colonies were organized into the Northern, Mid-Atlantic, and Southern regions. Regions can also be organized by imaginary borders and cultural characteristics, such as the “Deep South.” This indicates not only a geographic location but also implies certain traditions, beliefs, and manners.

title: Getting Help When You Need It
text: Asking for help is a critical skill to learn. Everyone needs help to accomplish tasks they are given. Asking for help when you need it takes courage. It may be hard at first, but with practice it gets easier. Letting others help you can create friendships. Getting help when you need it can help you reach your goals.

title: Be Safe When You Ask For Help
text:
Different people can help you with different things. Be cautious and smart when you ask for help. When you have a problem and need help, you can ask yourself, “who would be the BEST person to help me with this?” No matter what you need help with, you should always try to ask people you know and trust. If no one you know and trust is around when you need help, ask someone whose job is to help like police officers, security guards, or employees.

To stay safe, there are some people you should not ask for help like a stranger who makes you feel uncomfortable or someone you don’t know who offers you a ride in their car. Never get in a car with someone you don’t know. You can make smart choices and stay safe when you ask for help.

title: Gray Kangaroo Measurements
text:
Directions: Read the article. Underline vocabulary words and their definitions.

Length is the distance between two points. To determine the length of an object, you have to measure how long it is from point to point. For example, you can measure the distance between two houses. You can measure the distance between your toes and the top of your head, too. To measure length, you can use the metric system or the customary system.

There are two systems of measurement. In the United States, we typically use the customary system. We measure length using inches (in), feet (ft), yards (yd), or miles (mi). A standard ruler or a yardstick can be used to measure length in the customary system. The ruler equals one foot. The yardstick is as long as three rulers, or three feet. Both tools are divided into inches. It is harder to convert between different units in the customary system. The system requires more memorization. For example, you have to remember that there are 12 inches in one foot, three feet in one yard, and 1,760 yards in one mile.

You can also use the metric system, a decimal measuring system, to measure length. In the metric system, length is measured in millimeters (mm), centimeters (cm), meters (m), and kilometers (km). A metric ruler or a meterstick can be used to measure length in the metric system. These tools are labeled with two different units: centimeters and millimeters. Centimeters are marked with numbers and longer lines, just like inches on standard rulers. The smaller lines in between the centimeters represent millimeters. There are 10 millimeters in one centimeter, 100 centimeters in one meter, and 1,000 meters in one kilometer.

Growth Chart of Gray Kangaroo

When a gray kangaroo is born, it is the size of a grape! It will grow to be 60 times bigger when it is an adult. A kangaroo spends almost one year in its mother’s pouch as it grows. Scientists study the growth of baby kangaroos by collecting data, or information. Data can be examined and used to inform decision-making.

How much does the tail grow (in millimeters) from the time it is first measured at 20 days to when the kangaroo begins to emerge from the pouch at 260 days?

How much does the tail grow (in millimeters) from when the kangaroo begins to emerge from the pouch to when it permanently leaves?

If a typical grape is 3 cm in length, how much smaller is a baby kangaroo than a grape?

title: Essential Question
text: What is a region?

title: Physical and Human Characteristics
text:
We describe a place using physical and human characteristics. The physical characteristics of a place include landforms, bodies of water, and climate. Physical characteristics also include biomes and natural resources.

People create the human characteristics of a place. These characteristics are a result of people’s ideas, choices, and actions as they interact with the physical environment. Human characteristics include where people live and the work they do. They also include the kinds of houses people build and the activities they do for fun. Bridges, factories, buildings, and parks are also examples of human characteristics. Each place on Earth is different because of its human and physical characteristics.

title: What Is a Region?
text:
Organizing the Earth into regions can help us learn about our world. A region is an area that has similar characteristics. Some regions are organized based on their physical characteristics, such as landforms, climate, or biomes. Some regions are organized by their human characteristics, like population, culture, or language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

The United States is often divided into six regions. These regions are organized based on state political boundaries. They are the Northeast, the Southeast, the Midwest, the Southwest, the West, and the Northwest. Alaska is part of the Northwest Region. Hawaii is considered part of the West.

title: Northeast: Physical Characteristics
text:
There are 11 states in the Northeast Region of the United States. Many of the states have beaches along the Atlantic Ocean. There are also rivers, lakes, streams, waterfalls, and mountains in the region.

The Northeast has a temperate climate in its northern part. Winters are long and cold with ice storms and snowstorms. The southern part of the region is more mild. It has cool winters and hot summers.

Vegetation in the Northeast includes different species of large trees. There are also fungi, mosses, and ferns. The states closest to Canada have maple trees, too.

Animals that thrive in the Northeast include black bears, red foxes, white-tailed deer, and chipmunks.

title: Northeast: Human Characteristics
text:
The first inhabitants of the Northeast Region were Indigenous peoples. They survived mostly by farming and hunting. Forestry, coal, and granite industries have brought many people to the region. Maple syrup and cranberry juice are also produced there.

Wide toll roads cover the Northeast. Bridges, tunnels, and the Erie Canal allow travel over, under, and by water. This helps the movement of people, goods, and services.

The population of the Northeast Region is about 56 million. High-rise apartment buildings in large cities provide shelter for many people. In contrast, rural areas have more space with large farms and forests that are used for industry and recreation.

title: Southeast: Physical Characteristics
text:
The Southeast Region has 12 states. The region has beaches on the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. Freshwater sources in this region include lakes and rivers. The Appalachian and the Blue Ridge Mountains are some of the landforms. There are also barrier islands, swamps, and wetlands.

The climate of the Southeast Region is tropical. Summers are long, hot, and humid. Thunderstorms and hurricanes are frequent. The region has many national forests. It is a good region for trees.

Animals in the Southeast include snakes, crocodiles, and alligators. There are also black bears, panthers, and even flying squirrels.

title: Southeast: Human Characteristics
text:
The Choctaw, the Creek, and the Cherokee were the first people to live in the Southeast Region. The Spanish arrived around 1513. Enslaved Africans were brought to this region for the first time in 1619. All these people influenced the culture of the Southeast Region. Art, architecture, cuisine, and language have come from all these cultures.

The fertile soil and mild climate of the region are great for farming. Agriculture used to be the main industry. Cotton, tobacco, and corn still bring money to the region. Companies that manufacture cars, airplanes, and medical equipment attract many people to the region today. The population of the Southeast Region is about 97 million.

title: Human and Whale Weight Gain
text:
Directions: Read the article. Underline vocabulary words and their definitions.

Weight measures the amount of matter or substance that makes up an object. In the metric system, the base unit for weight is the gram. One gram weighs about the same as two paper clips. Like the meter, the gram can be converted into smaller and larger measurements. The kilogram, for example, equals 1,000 grams. Grams and kilograms are the most commonly used units for measuring weight. Just like units of length, units of weight are often abbreviated:

gram = g

kilogram = kg

To convert kilograms into grams, multiply the number of kilograms by 1,000.

Ounces, pounds, and tons are used to measure weight in the customary system. These units are abbreviated as:

ounce = oz

pound = lb

ton = t

Like with length, it is more difficult to convert between customary units. For example, you have to remember that there are 16 ounces in a pound. You also have to remember there are 2,000 pounds in a ton.

Growth Chart of a Blue Whale

Blue whales are some of the fastest-growing mammals in the world. When they are born, they weigh 2.5 tons! Baby blue whales can gain weight at a rate of about 10 pounds per hour. That's 250 pounds per day for the first 6-12 months of their lives. Blue whales will reach their final weight when they are between 5 and 15 years old. Blue whales have a lifespan of 110 years.

Directions: Convert each weight measurement from tons to pounds. Then, answer the questions, using the data from the chart.

Analyze and Interpret Data

We can analyze and interpret data to make sense of scientific concepts or events. When we analyze data, we look for and identify patterns. When we interpret data, we make sense of the patterns using logical reasoning.

Interpret: What do you think these patterns mean?

title: Lion Sleep and Sightings
text:
Directions: Read the article. Underline vocabulary words and their definitions.

Time is the way we measure how long something takes. We can measure how long it takes for a student to run around the school, how long it takes to bake cupcakes, or how long it takes for someone's hair to grow. To measure time, we use seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, and years! Both the metric and customary systems use the same measurements to track and record time.

We can use tools such as stopwatches and timers to measure time. To convert between different units of time, you have to memorize a few rules. There are 60 seconds in one minute and 60 minutes in one hour. There are 24 hours in one day. How many minutes are in a day?

How Much Do Animals Sleep?

Did you know that some animals, such as lions, sleep three quarters of the day? That means that the average lion sleeps for 18 out of the 24 hours in a day, or 1,080 minutes!

Let’s take a look at how much other animals sleep in a day.

The lowest number is the start of the number line. The highest number is the last number on the number line. Then, fill in the numbers between the highest and lowest.

To record your data, put an “X” over the number line above the matching number. If a number repeats in the data, add another X on top. title: Home Range and Body Weight
text:
Directions: Read the article. Underline vocabulary words and their definitions.

Area is the amount of space inside a shape, or the measurement of a surface. Perimeter measures the distance around the outside of a two-dimensional shape. Imagine a playground that is fenced in. Measuring the area tells us how much space you have to play. Measuring the perimeter tells us how much fence was needed to surround the playground.

We can find the area of a shape by multiplying the length by the width. We can use this equation: area (a) = length (l) x width (w). Area is measured in square units. We can find the perimeter of a shape by adding the side lengths together. We can use this equation: perimeter (p) = side (s) + side (s) + side (s) + side (s). Perimeter is measured in units.

We can still solve for area or perimeter when we have missing side lengths. To do that, simply view either formula as an equation with an unknown factor.

Animal Enclosures

In the wild, animals have a home range. A home range is the area or space that animals in the wild use. An animal's home range can include its favorite spots to eat, sleep, or find mates. Several factors determine how big an animal's home range is. Some of the factors are what the animal eats and its habitat. At the zoo, zoologists cannot give animals their entire home range. However, they do try to provide animals with enough space to create a mini home range.

Otters typically need about 2,500 square feet of space for an enclosure at a zoo.
