title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe a region?

title: Midwest: Physical Characteristics
text:
The Midwest Region has 12 states. The land is mostly flat. In parts of the Midwest, there are also rolling hills, high mountains, and deep valleys. Some states in the Midwest have rivers as their borders. Six of the 12 states fall within the Great Lakes area.

The Midwest has a humid continental climate. In summer, it gets hot and humid. In winter, it can get really cold. There is a large difference between the temperatures in summer and winter.

There are prairie grasses all over the region. This makes the soil fertile. Blueberries, corn, and asparagus grow very well in the Midwest.

Animals that live here include bison, prairie dogs, and black bears.

title: Midwest: Human Characteristics
text:
The population of the Midwest is about 68 million. The Chippewa, Lakota, and Blackfoot were some of the Native American tribes living in this region before Europeans arrived.

The Midwest is known for some of the finest architecture in the United States. Many of the architects were from Europe. The buildings often show the style of the architect’s home country.

Since the land is fertile, there is a lot of farming in the region. People grow wheat, soybeans, and corn. Others raise hogs and dairy cows. It is one of the most important areas of agricultural production in the world. There are also many manufacturing industries. A lot of vehicles and machines are made in the Midwest.

title: Southwest: Physical Characteristics
text:
The Southwest has four states. The Gulf of Mexico and 10 rivers are the region’s main bodies of water. There are also a few lakes. Landforms there include high mountains, plateaus, valleys, and seven barrier islands. The region is home to the Grand Canyon.

There are both dry and tropical areas in the region. Rainfall is mostly seasonal. In summer, only the tropical areas receive rainfall. Other areas get most of their rainfall in winter.

Blue palo verde, Texas ebony, Arizona cypress, and white oak are trees that grow in the region. Cotton, lettuce, melons, and grapefruit also do well there.

Swift foxes, black-tailed prairie dogs, and Texas horned lizards are some of the animals found in the Southwest.

title: Southwest: Human Characteristics
text:
There are more than 42 million people living in the Southwest Region. Indigenous peoples who live in the Southwest have influenced the culture of the region. The stone and mud homes and the food eaten in the region show this cultural influence. This influence can also be heard in the names of cities and towns in the Southwest.

Coal, oil, and natural gas abound in the region. Agriculture and mining are big industries there, too. Oil, however, is the most important industry. There is also a growing aerospace manufacturing industry.

title: Northwest: Human Characteristics
text:
Many different people lived in the Northwest before Europeans came. The Pacific coast provides fresh seafood. Forests provide wood for homes and furniture. Over 68 million people now live in this region.

Grapes, apples, and potatoes grow well in the Northwest. Oil, coal, and natural gas are important resources. Gold and zinc can also be found in this region. Agriculture, mining, and logging are big industries for the region. Manufacturing and healthcare provide jobs, too. The region is also known for dams that provide water and electricity.

Tourism is a big business in the Northwest. People travel there to ski, climb rocks, and observe wildlife.

title: Northwest: Physical Characteristics
text:
There are three states in the Northwest. All these states have beaches along the Pacific Ocean. There are many rivers, lakes, and waterfalls.

Mountains and valleys are all over the region. Some of the mountains are volcanoes.

This region has temperate and polar climates. The temperate areas have redwood, Douglas fir, and western hemlock trees. The polar areas have lichens, mosses, and sedges.

Polar bears, walruses, cougars, black bears, grizzly bears, wolves, and moose can all be found in the Northwest Region.

title: The West: Physical Characteristics
text:
Eight states make up the West Region of the United States. The Pacific Ocean gives the region many islands and coastlines. The region also has many rivers and waterfalls. There are lakes, hot springs, and geysers, too. The West is home to mountain ranges, valleys, and canyons.

The West has dry, temperate, and tropical climate areas. The dry areas have Joshua trees and cacti. The temperate areas have redwood, Douglas fir, and different kinds of juniper trees. Coconuts, pineapples, and sugarcane grow in the region's tropical areas.

Animals in the region include elk, wolves, and bighorn sheep. There are also bison, rattlesnakes, and horned lizards. There is a lot of marine life, too.

title: The West: Human Characteristics
text:
The population of the West is about 58 million. European settlers moved there in large numbers looking for gold. Many American Indians lost their homes. Copper, coal, oil, and natural gas are still found here. The region is also famous for potatoes, pineapples, almonds, and grapes.

A transcontinental railroad was once built to connect this region to the eastern United States.

Forestry, fishing, and ranching are some industries in the region. Entertainment and mining are also important in the region. Amusement parks, ski resorts, and national parks bring in a lot of tourists. The region’s islands also provide a tropical getaway.

title: Essential Question
text: How does data help historians learn about the past?

title: The Census
text:
The U.S. Census is the count of how many people live in the United States. This count is done every 10 years. A list of questions called a survey is sent to every home. If the survey isn’t returned, a census worker visits the home. The worker helps the people living there to fill out the survey. The survey asks who is living at the address. It asks for important information about the people.

The census is important. The U.S. Constitution requires a census. The House of Representatives is based on the number of people in a district or region. Regions grow or shrink in population. This causes the number of representatives to be adjusted.

Census information is made public. People can use census details in many ways. Businesses can determine if they should expand or downsize. Social scientists can use the information to learn about people and communities. Individuals can use census data to find ancestors and family members.

Population information is available from every census since 1790. The data is considered a primary source for research.

title: Data, Data, Everywhere
text:
The census counts people and collects information about each person who is counted.

Let's look at the questions on the 2020 Census:

Who lives in the household?

How are they related to each other?

Age, sex, and race?

Own or rent the house?

Phone number?

The Census of 1880 had 26 questions. Questions from 1880 asked for the number of people living in the dwelling as well as their ages, sexes, and races. Other questions included whether the people in the dwelling could read and write. They answered what country they were born in. They also wrote their occupations. In 1880, the most populated city was New York City. San Francisco was ranked ninth in population.

The actual counting of people was done by individuals. This process sometimes took years to finish. In 1890, counting everyone was done using an electronic punch card system. A modern computer was first used in 1950. Today, the use of computers makes the census count go faster. Computers also help share the information collected in tables, charts, and maps.

A line graph shows the increase or decrease of something over time.

A bar graph is used to compare things between different groups.

A pie chart is another method of displaying information. A pie chart is round. It represents the total number of things counted. The slices show parts of the totals. The larger the slice, the greater the number. The smaller the slice, the smaller the number.

A map can also display data. A map can represent larger or smaller numbers by using different colors.

A table chart gives data in columns and rows. Each column and row is labeled with the type of information shown.

title: Who We Were
text:
The government did a census in 1910. It asked questions about age and place of birth. Each person reported whether they could read and write. The census helped identify Civil War veterans 50 years after the war.

Native Americans who were living in the United States answered a separate census. It was titled “Indian Population." People identified their tribe and their language. They also indicated whether they owned land.

There have been 23 federal census surveys. Information from each year tells us about who was living in the United States. Information from the census can provide a glimpse of life in the past. The census can identify who lived next door to each other. There is information on occupations, ancestry, number of children, and education levels. Census data helps us to know that people came from all over the world to live in the United States.

title: Who We Are
text:
From the 2020 Census form: “The goal of the 2020 Census is to count everyone just once and in the right place. We want to ensure that everyone in your home who should be counted is counted — including newborns, roommates, and those who may be staying with you temporarily.”

Census data also provides a glimpse of life now. For example, the population in California in 2020 had grown since the 2010 census. California has more people than any other state. There is great ethnic diversity in the cities and suburbs. In many rural areas, there is less ethnic diversity.

title: Who We Will Be
text: As we look at the census data from 100 years ago, we can see that some things stay the same and some things change. The United States will continue changing and growing as new people arrive from all over the world. Some towns will become larger. Some will become smaller. Governments and companies use census data to help predict what the population of an area will be like in the future.

title: Ordinary Man, Extraordinary Times
text:
Paul Revere was an ordinary businessman in Boston. As a silversmith, he worked with metal to create household items like teapots and silverware. He was also part of the messenger and alarm system for the Sons of Liberty. On April 18, 1775, he was needed. The Sons of Liberty received word that British troops were going to Concord to destroy the colonists’ supply of munitions stored there. The Minutemen needed to be warned. Also, Sons of Liberty leaders Samuel Adams and John Hancock were both staying nearby to hide from the British. They could be arrested and sent to England for treason and also needed to be warned.

British soldiers patrolled the roads to Concord. The ride from Boston was a dangerous task. Revere and Sons of Liberty messenger, William Dawes, took two routes to go the 18 miles to Concord. They successfully warned Adams and Hancock. Dr. Samuel Prescott joined as they continued their ride. However, British patrols stopped them. Prescott and Dawes escaped. Dawes was injured, so only Prescott made it with the message for the Concord militia. The patrol kept Revere, questioning him for several hours. They finally released him—without his horse—to return to Boston.

Revere convinced the soldiers he wasn’t a messenger. His quick thinking saved his life. He continued to work with the Sons of Liberty. He was an ordinary man living in an extraordinary time.

title: Essential Question
text: How does land use influence change in communities?

title: Urban Communities
text: People form communities based on how they use the land. When many people want to live in one location, the land is known as an urban area. Urban areas can also be called cities. In cities, buildings for business and homes are developed to be close together. Tall buildings with many floors or stories are built so many people can live on smaller pieces of land. Transportation in urban areas is organized to move as many people and goods as possible in and out of the city. There is less land available to grow food in urban areas. Food for many people has to be brought into the city.

title: Suburban Communities
text: A suburban community is formed in areas outside of a city. Suburbs have fewer businesses and people living in one location. There are fewer developed areas with tall buildings. Living spaces have open areas with no buildings. These spaces are yards, parks, and open lots or fields. Transportation systems in the suburban community are smaller. Highways transport goods and people to business and residential areas. There is some land available for families to have small farms and grow food. Food is brought in to help feed the population in the suburban community.

title: Rural Communities
text: Rural communities have large spaces of undeveloped land. This land is used for large farms that grow food for the urban and suburban communities. Houses are far apart in rural communities. Businesses are built together in a town. There are not usually many public transportation options. Roads connect goods and people with the towns.

title: San Francisco: Part One
text: San Francisco is an example of a town that grew to be a city. The Ohlone Tribe lived in the bay area. World explorers from Spain, England, and Russia traveled to the area in the 1700s. Russian traders made their home in the region. The Spanish explorers claimed the land northwest of Mexico for the king of Spain. By 1821, Mexico was independent from Spain. The Mexican government claimed the bay as part of their country. In 1835, a small settlement of many different origins named the land Yerba Buena. During the Mexican-American War, the United States acquired the land from Mexico. The American military renamed Yerba Buena “San Francisco.”

title: San Francisco: Part Two
text:
The discovery of gold in California in 1848 brought thousands of people to the state. San Francisco was the place of entry. Many went to the goldfields in the mountains. Many stayed in the town and found work taking care of all the new settlers.

Buildings were constructed with no plan for the organization of blocks or streets. The land was being used as new needs occurred. There were many conflicts with such rapid population growth. Elections took time and organization. The government was disorganized. People would construct a building quickly with no regard for safety. Over time, the city became more organized.

Streets and highways were built to move people and trade in and out of the city. Railroads were built to connect San Francisco with the state and the country. The harbor became organized for bringing people and goods safely to the city. Today, the many transportation systems can be seen on a map.

California attracted people from all over the world. Many settled in the San Francisco area. The rich diversity of food, music, and customs made San Francisco an exciting place to live and work. The diversity is seen today in architecture, restaurants, places of worship, and community festivals.

title: Communication Over Time
text: Communication means to talk and listen to other people. How we communicate has changed over time. Inventors created better ways to communicate.

title: Essential Question
text: How have the ways people communicate changed over time?

title: Pony Express
text: The Pony Express made sending mail faster. Pony Express riders would ride horses. They could deliver mail in about 10 days. Before the Pony Express, mail could take months to arrive.

title: Telephone
text: Alexander Graham Bell invented one of the first telephones. It was big and did not have numbers. Phones have changed over time. Today, a cell phone fits in your pocket.

title: Telegraph
text: The telegraph helped people to communicate over long distances. It used electricity and wires. Samuel Morse helped invent the telegraph. He also created a code to send messages.

title: Computer
text: The first computer was much bigger than today's computers. One computer took up a whole room. Over time, people made computers smaller. Now we have computers that fit in our hands.

title: Internet
text: The internet gives us more ways to communicate with others. We can send emails. We can video chat to connect with people far away.

title: How I Communicate

text: How can I learn about people who made a difference?

title: What Is Inquiry?
text: What is inquiry? Inquiry is a way to investigate a problem. It is a way to ask for more information. An inquiry has three parts. These are asking questions, gathering evidence, and presenting ideas. When you are planning an inquiry, it is important that you start with a question that you want to know more about. Your inquiry should be about something or someone interesting. Your inquiry should really make you think.

title: Evidence
text: Evidence provides us with facts about something. It helps us find answers to our questions. Tasks are steps we take to help us gather evidence. Tasks also help us gather answers for our inquiry. First, tasks include making a list of our questions. Next, tasks help us identify the sources that give evidence. Last, tasks help us create a plan to share what we have learned.

title: Culture
text: Culture is how people live. It is what people believe. It is how they celebrate. Every family has a culture. People show culture in many ways.

title: Essential Question
text: What is culture?

title: Celebrations
text: Celebrations are part of a culture. Some cultures celebrate special days or people. These celebrations make the culture unique. Sharing your celebrations is important.

title: Traditions
text: A tradition is the way something is done. Traditions come from those who lived before us. We celebrate traditions. We might decorate for a celebration as a tradition.

title: Food
text: Food is part of culture. Food can show where your family came from. Food can show how you celebrate. You can share your culture when you cook a meal for someone.

title: Language
text: Language is part of culture. People speak different languages. The language you speak is part of your culture. Speaking to others in your language helps you share your culture.

title: Oral Histories
text: Oral histories are part of your culture. Elders tell stories to their families. The stories help you feel like you are part of the history. They connect you to your family and culture.

title: Beliefs
text: Beliefs are a part of your culture. Beliefs are important ideas that guide behavior. They help you know how to treat others and live your life.

title: Stories
text: People share their cultures by sharing stories. Stories can be shared out loud or written. Stories can teach about our culture. They can teach what we believe.

title: Essential Question
text: How do folktales and legends show the beliefs, languages, and traditions of communities?

title: Folktales
text: Folktales are stories passed down from generation to generation. They are told over and over. Folktales share people's beliefs. They often teach a lesson about choices.

title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
text: “The Boy Who Cried Wolf” is a folktale. This folktale teaches us a lesson. It teaches us to always tell the truth.

title: Legends
text: Legends are stories. They share culture and beliefs. Legends are often about important events from the past. They can be about important people. Legends try to explain why things happened.

title: Miwok Legend: “Creation of Man”
text: The Miwok share their culture through legends. Their legends show the Miwok traditions and beliefs. One Miwok legend is "Creation of Man." It tells the Miwok belief of how man was created.

title: The Tortoise and the Hare
text: “The Tortoise and the Hare” is a folktale. Put the folktale pictures in order. What lesson does this folktale teach?

title: Pennsylvanian Innovations and Inventions
text:
Innovation is the process of taking something that exists and improving it to make something new. Invention is the process of creating something totally new. Invention and innovation almost always overlap.

The inspiration for invention and innovation comes from problems that need to be solved. The solutions inventors and innovators develop can make work easier or better. Their ideas can also change the way people live.

The first step to problem solving is problem finding. Innovators and inventors spend time thinking about possibilities of what could be. Innovators and inventors ask questions that may not have easy answers. They keep searching until a possible answer is found. Innovators and inventors don’t give up. When something doesn’t work, it is not a failure. Thomas Edison, a talented inventor, said he discovered “... several thousand things that won’t work,” before he went on to find the one that did.

Innovation can happen in products, services, art, technology and processes. Not all innovators are successful in their lifetimes. Sometimes the public isn’t ready to accept new things. The innovation has to be proven to be practical and improved. In the 1880s, washing hands to prevent illness was a new innovation. It was such a simple thing. Many people thought it was too simple and it wouldn’t make a difference. We know today that washing hands is one of the best ways to prevent the spread of germs. Many people mocked and laughed at the innovators who introduced washing hands. It took time for people to recognize how effective this innovation was and to then accept it. Innovators and inventors could lose friends and support from the community. To continue with the innovation or invention meant taking a risk, or chance. The innovators for washing hands continued despite the risk. Many lives have been changed because they accepted the risks.

Sometimes innovations and inventions can receive a patent. A patent is a government certificate that grants the right of ownership. The patent makes the innovator or inventor the owner of the idea. Anyone who wants to use a patented idea has to pay the patent owner. The United States Patent and Trademark Office provides information on the patenting process. In 2020, the Patent Office processed 646,244 applications. Only 388,900 of the applications were given patents. Thomas Edison would possibly say, “Those are just 257,344 applications that didn’t work.”

title: Innovation in the Arts
text:
Nickelodeons

As new inventions and innovations made work easier, people had more time for entertainment. Thomas Edison invented moving picture photography. Innovators used the motion picture invention to record stories from the stage. These became known as “movies.” The first theater building that showed movies was built in Pittsburgh in 1905 by John P Harris. The cost to see a movie was five cents, or a nickel. The theater became known as a “nickelodeon.” Nickelodeons were built across the country. Nickelodeans helped innovators create more movies and a new industry was started. One hundred years later, the industry continues to grow. According to the National Association of Theatre Owners, in 2005 there were 6,000 movie theaters in the United States. Today, Pennsylvania continues to encourage film production throughout the state.

Marian Anderson

Marian Anderson was born in Philadelphia in 1897. Anderson had a successful singing career, performing in a variety of styles of music. Anderson sang in large theaters with new innovative microphones and speakers. This helped Anderson be heard by more people in larger audiences. Anderson was very popular in European theaters. She sang to sold out concerts repeatedly throughout the 1930s.

When Anderson returned to the United States, she was scheduled to have a concert in Washington DC. However, when she arrived, the concert hall authorities wouldn’t let her perform because of her race. This discrimination

led Anderson to perform the first outdoor concert on the Lincoln Memorial steps. The concert gave an opportunity for Anderson to be an innovator. The new sound equipment made it possible for thousands to hear her sing.

Anderson was the first to use the Lincoln Memorial steps as a place to promote equality and civil rights. The Lincoln Memorial was also used by Martin Luther King, Jr and, most recently, in support for Black Lives Matter.

Martha Graham

Born in 1894, Martha Graham grew up in Allegheny, Pennsylvania. She was a famous dancer and choreographer. A choreographer is someone who creates dances for others. She created a new way of teaching dance called the “Graham Technique.” This technique involved studying movement, muscles, and how the body naturally worked. Traditionally, music was created and dances were made to follow the music. Graham’s technique was to interpret the emotion that the music created. Dance became powerful athletic movements from the dancer. Costumes changed to allow for greater movement. Eventually, music was created after the dance had been choreographed. Graham created the art of modern dance we see today.

John Coltrane

In 1943, John Coltrane came to Philadelphia with his saxophone. Coltrane had lived in North Carolina. He was influenced by the religious music of his community. Gospel Blues came from the African American communities in the South. The music was emotional, joyful, and sad. Coltrane played with no written music. He used his saxophone to make the listener feel deep emotion. Coltrane practiced every day. He challenged himself to become a musician who could interpret his emotions into sound. He said, “... there are always new sounds to imagine, new feelings to get at.” Coltrane’s innovations with music inspired many to continue to seek combining music and emotion.

Mary Cassatt

Mary Cassatt was born in Pittsburgh in 1844. Her family lived in various locations in Pennsylvania over her lifetime. At age 15, Cassatt began studying art at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts in Philadelphia. Cassatt studied with the intention of being a professional artist. In 1860s America, this career path was unusual for a woman. Cassatt did independent learning to gain artistic skills. She sought out instructors who would teach a woman. Cassatt struggled in her early career until she joined a group of artists known as “impressionists.” As opposed to exact copies, the impressionist artists tried to capture the light,

movement, people, and objects they saw as they saw them. This group helped inspire Cassatt to do more challenging pieces of art. As Cassatt gained skills and confidence. She eventually developed her own style of art. She used different types of paint, ink, and papers. Cassatt supported other women becoming artists. Later in life, Cassatt supported getting women the right to vote. She proved to herself and others that a woman could successfully influence a community in many ways.

Andy Warhol

Andy Warhol was born in Pittsburgh in 1928. His parents immigrated from Slovakia. Warhol grew up loving photography and movies. Warhol went to the Carnegie Institute of Technology. He was ambitious and wanted to be a commercial artist making advertisements. Eventually, Warhol took his focus on objects for sale to another level in the art world. Warhol took a photo of a can of soup and created images in different vibrant colors. He took portraits of famous people and used the same technique. Warhol ‘s innovation was taking ordinary objects and creating color and larger than life, fun images. This became known as Pop Art. Warhol successfully made Pop Art a part of America that can be seen everywhere, from posters in college dormitories to the walls of museums. The Andy Warhol Museum is located in Pittsburgh.

title: George Westinghouse and KDKA Radio
text:
Born in Central Bridge, New York, in 1846, George Westinghouse became fascinated with technology at an early age. After serving in the Civil War, he moved to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in 1867. There, Westinghouse launched his career as an inventor. He received a patent for inventing a brake system for trains to use. Before Westinghouse's air brake, each car in a train had to have its own brakeman to apply the brakes at the same time. This caused many accidents. Westinghouse created a system using pressurized air to apply brakes at the same time in each car. His air brake enabled trains to stop with accuracy. This air brake was quickly bought by every railroad. In 1884, George Westinghouse started the Westinghouse Electric Company. Its focus was to improve the system that delivered electricity. He partnered with Nikola Tesla in creating alternating current. This is the delivery used today for electricity.

Westinghouse continued looking for innovations, including in communication. Telephone and radio were being used as communication methods. At the time, telephones were connected by a system of wires. Radio was wireless. Westinghouse took a chance on radio. Radio waves could be sent out from a station to be received by anyone with a radio receiver. So, Westinghouse started building receivers. He then created the first commercial radio station in the world. KDKA began broadcasting in October, 1920.

KDKA played music, broadcasted sports, weather forecasts and advertisements. The success of KDKA encouraged other companies to invest in radio. By 1921, eight radio stations were operating across the United States. Today there are over 15,445 radio stations in the United States. Westinghouse's efforts to innovate opened new avenues of communication and success for others.

title: Violet Oakley
text:
Violet Oakley was born in New Jersey in 1874. She moved to Pennsylvania to attend the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts. Oakley also studied at Drexel University in Philadelphia. While at Drexel, Oakley studied art under the illustrator Howard Pyle. An illustrator is a person who draws or creates pictures. Pyle called Oakley and her roommates the “Red Rose Girls." This is because they lived in the Red Rose Inn in Villanova, Pennsylvania.

In 1906, Oakley became the first female artist in history to be asked to paint in a public building. She was asked to paint a series of murals in the Pennsylvania State Capitol. A mural is art that's painted or drawn directly on a wall. Although Oakley designed the murals for the Capitol building, she did not personally paint on the walls. Back then it was not socially acceptable for a woman to oversee the work of men in public. So, Oakley created the designs and gave instructions ahead of time. At night, after the work crews had finished for the day, she was allowed to go in. She could then inspect their work on her murals and make corrections.

Her work at the capitol was only the beginning. Banker Charles Yarnell asked her to paint a series of murals in his home. Oakley titled these murals “Building the House of Wisdom.” Today these murals are in the Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia. They are some of Oakley’s most famous pieces.

Violet Oakley changed how women were received in the art community. Her passions extended beyond art. She was passionate about racial equality, women's rights, economic and social justice, and international government. Oakley helped found many art organizations in Philadelphia. She was a great supporter of the Woodmere Art Museum. Her life partner Edith Emerson was the museum director for over 30 years. Oakley’s studio in Philadelphia is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Violet Oakley died on February 25, 1961.

title: George Westinghouse and KDKA Radio
text:
It's hard to imagine what life would be like without electricity. Although he did not invent electricity, we can thank George Westinghouse for today's modern electrical system. Born in Central Bridge, New York in 1846, Westinghouse moved to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in 1867. At an early age, Westinghouse became fascinated with technology. After serving in the Civil War, Westinghouse launched his career as an inventor.

His first patent was for the rotary steam engine. A rotary steam engine delivers power created by steam to machines using shafts, pulleys, and belts. Once he received his first patent, Westinghouse never looked back.

By 1884 Westinghouse started the Westinghouse Electric Company. The company's focus was to improve the system that delivered electricity. Before his death in 1914, Westinghouse had over 360 patents. He also owned over 50 companies.

The KDKA radio station in Pittsburgh is credited with being the first commercial radio station in the United States. It was owned by the Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company in East Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The Westinghouse Company used the radio station to help sell their radio receivers. KDKA began playing music. They also started broadcasting sports, church services, and weather forecasts. The success of KDKA encouraged other companies to invest in radio. By 1921, eight radio stations were operating across the United States. Today there are over 15,445 stations in the United States.

title: Violet Oakley
text:
Violet Oakley was born in New Jersey in 1874. She moved to Pennsylvania to attend the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts. Oakley left the academy to study at Drexel University in Philadelphia. While at Drexel, Oakley studied art under the illustrator Howard Pyle. An illustrator is a person who draws or creates pictures. Pyle called Oakley and her roommates the “Red Rose Girls”. They received the nickname because they lived in the Red Rose Inn in Villanova, Pennsylvania. Encouraged by friends, Oakley and her roommates moved to Mount Airy, Pennsylvania.

In 1906, Oakley became the first female artist in history to be asked to paint in a public building. She was asked to paint a series of murals for the Governor’s Reception Rooms in the Pennsylvania State Capitol. A mural is art that's painted or drawn directly on a wall.

Her work at the capitol was only the beginning. Banker Charles Yarnell asked her to paint a series of murals in his home. Oakley titled her murals at the Yarnell Estate “Building the House of Wisdom”. Today the murals are in the Woodmere Art Museum in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The murals are some of Oakley’s most famous pieces.

Violet Oakley changed how women were received in the art community. She was not just passionate about her art, however. She was also passionate about racial equality, women’s rights, economic and social justice, and international government. Oakley helped found many art organizations in Philadelphia. She was a great supporter of the Woodmere Art Museum. Her life partner Edith Emerson was the museum director for over 30 years. Oakley’s studio in Philadelphia is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Violet Oakley died on February 25, 1961.

title: The Inventions of Benjamin Franklin
text:
Benjamin Franklin was born on January 17, 1706, in Boston, Massachusetts. He grew up in a large family and was the 10th of 17 children in his family. Franklin learned to read and write as a young child. He had to leave school when he was 10 years old and continued learning by reading as much as he could. At age 12, he became an apprentice at his older brother's print shop. An apprentice is someone who is learning a trade or art by experience under a skilled worker. Franklin moved to Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, to work as a printer when he was 17. He made his permanent home there. His curious nature led him to wonder and explore the world around him. He would often experiment with new inventions to help make life easier for everyone.

Swim fins

The first swim fins were one of Franklin’s earliest inventions. As a young boy, he loved swimming and made paddles that he could attach to his hands. These paddles helped him swim faster and move easier through the water. Franklin loved swimming and swam regularly all throughout his life.

The Lightning Rod

Franklin famously flew a kite in a rainstorm to collect proof of the electricity of lightning. This led him to hypothesize ways to protect houses from lightning strikes. A hypothesis is an informed guess or explanation for why something happens. Franklin thought that lightning would be attracted to a long metal rod that could stick up from the top of a building. Attaching this to a pole would lead the electricity down to the ground, instead of onto the building. This saved the building from catching on fire.

Bifocal Glasses

Franklin loved reading all his life. Reading glasses made this pass time easier. He didn’t like switching between his regular glasses and his reading glasses, though. To solve this problem, he had two pairs of glasses combined. The top half was for seeing distances and the bottom half was for reading. He wrote to a friend that he was, "happy in the invention of double spectacles, which serving for distant objects as well as near ones, make my eyes as useful to me as ever they were."

The Franklin Stove

During Franklin’s lifetime, the way to heat a home in winter was with a fireplace. The fireplace was a stone or brick hole in the wall of the house. Smoke and heat from the burning wood went up an attached chimney. Franklin used his knowledge of science to invent a better way to heat buildings. Franklin lined the fireplace with iron plates. Positioning the iron plates away from the bricks created warm air. This warm air was then funneled back into the room.

This is Franklin’s recollection of the invention:

In order of time, … in 1742, [I] invented an open stove for the better warming of rooms, and at the same time saving fuel, as the fresh air admitted was warmed in entering, I made a present of the model to Mr. Robert Grace, one of my early friends, who, having an iron-furnace, found the casting of the plates for these stoves a profitable thing, as they were growing in demand. To promote that demand, I wrote and published a pamphlet, entitled "An Account of the new-invented Pennsylvania Fireplaces; … their Advantages above every other Method of warming Rooms demonstrated; …," etc. This pamphlet had a good effect. Gov'r. Thomas was so pleas'd with the construction of this stove, as described in it, that he offered to give me a patent for the sole vending of them for a term of years; but I declin'd it from a principle which has ever weighed with me on such occasions, viz., That, as we enjoy great advantages from the inventions of others, we should be glad of an opportunity to serve others by any invention of ours; and this we should do freely and generously.

title: Needs
text: A need is something you have to have to live. Food and shelter are needs. Clothes and water are needs. People meet their needs in different ways.

title: Essential Question
text: How do people meet their needs?

title: Wants
text: A want is something you would like to have but do not need. Not everyone wants the same things. You may want a video game. Your friend may want a soccer ball.

title: What It Takes to Be a Champion
text:
Consider what it takes to be a champion. Is it all about being the best athlete on the team? Is a champion the person who gets the most hits or scores the most goals? Maybe that is the case on the field. Actually, being a true champion is about something more. Many accomplished athletes were either from Pennsylvania or made their mark there. There are famous baseball players, golfers, football players, and others. These athletes worked hard and practiced to become well-known in their individual sports. They were athletic champions, but they were also much more than that. Champions are people who help make their community a better place.

Many athletes use their fame to help others in need, even if they don’t know them. Many athletes brave discrimination based on their race or gender to participate in their sport. Discrimination is when someone is not allowed to do something because of their race, gender, or other factors. While many athletes struggle against challenges, they work hard to overcome them to help others. They often encourage and inspire others to never give up. Many athletes gain fame because they have won awards, events, and titles. However, what makes someone a real champion is how they make a positive impact outside of their sport. True champions are people who have courage and perseverance, believe in themselves, and also make personal sacrifices to help others. These characteristics combined make a champion on and off the field.

title: Making Choices
text: Sometimes we have to choose between needs and wants. We see how much money we have. We choose what we want or need most.

title: Meeting Our Needs
text: People meet their needs in different ways. Some people make their own goods. Some work for money to buy goods. Others trade to get what they need and want.

title: Producing
text: Some people produce their own goods. This meets their needs. They plant fruits and vegetables to get food. They sew their own clothing. They build their own houses.

title: Working
text: People have jobs. They work at their jobs to earn money. They use the money to buy things they need and want.

title: Trading
text: Trade is when you buy or sell a good or service. People trade to meet their needs. People use money to make trade easier.

title: Little League Baseball
text:
Little League Baseball was born in Pennsylvania. Eleven of the 12 teams in the first Little League World Series in 1947 were from Pennsylvania. Over 2,500 people watched the first championship.

The Little League program we know today was started in 1939 by a lumberyard clerk named Carl E. Stotz. Stotz watched his nephews play catch in the backyard in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. Sitting on the porch steps, Stotz yelled to his nephews, "How would you like to play on a regular team with uniforms, your own cap, a new ball for every game, and bats your size?" Stotz looked for support for his idea from local businesses. Soon, his amateur youth baseball league was born. It was not long before news of the program spread. By 1957, Little League games were being played in 50 states. The first National World Series tournament was held in 1959 in South Williamsport. Stotz held the position of commissioner of the league until 1955. Williamsport, Pennsylvania, is the permanent home of the annual Little League World Series.

Today, more than 2.5 million youth in more than 30 countries play Little League. Little League baseball teaches the importance of good sportsmanship and fair play. Playing baseball is fun for millions of children. It is even better when it’s played with respect and good sportsmanship.

title: Roberto Clemente
text:
Some athletes are famous not only for what they do on the field but also for their actions off the field. Roberto Clemente is an example of this.

Early Life

Clemente was born in 1934 in Carolina, Puerto Rico. He was an excellent athlete as a child. He played in the Puerto Rican Baseball League at age 17. The Los Angeles Dodgers signed Clemente when he turned 18. The following year, the Pittsburgh Pirates signed Clemente. He played there for the next 17 years.

Early Career

As a Puerto Rican, Clemente faced discrimination. He fought to overcome his challenges to become known as one of the best players in Major League Baseball history. He could really hit the ball. He was a great outfielder. He was an even better teammate. His award record shows just what an outstanding player he was. Clemente won baseball’s Most Valuable Player award, four batting titles, and two World Series titles. He was also awarded Best Outfielder 12 years in a row. As good as he was in baseball, though, Clemente was even more of a champion outside of the game.

Charity Work

Clemente did a lot of charity work. He loved Puerto Rico and wanted to give back. He traveled home often to help children learn the sport of baseball and more. He believed that sports could be a way out of poverty for others, just as it was for him. When he worked with children in Puerto Rico, he talked about the importance of being a good person and a good athlete. When asked about his charity work, Clemente said, “I get kids together and talk about the importance of sports, the importance of being a good citizen, the importance of respecting their mother and father. Then we go to the ballfield and I show them some techniques of playing baseball."

When an earthquake struck the country of Nicaragua in 1972, Clemente focused on helping the people there. Hundreds of thousands of people were left homeless and in need. Clemente worked to bring needed medical supplies, food, and water to the country. Although Nicaragua was over 1,500 miles from Puerto Rico, Clemente said that he felt a duty to help fellow Latinos in need. On Dec. 31, 1972, Clemente boarded a small plane loaded with supplies from Puerto Rico to deliver them to Nicaragua. The plane crashed just off the coast. Unfortunately, Clemente did not survive the crash. The world was saddened by the news of his death.

Continuing Roberto Clemente’s Work

After Clemente’s death, many people wanted to honor him for his achievements both on and off the field. Normally, players have to be out of the sport for five years or more before anyone can nominate them to the Baseball Hall of Fame. However, the Baseball Writers of America held a special vote in the months after Clemente’s death. They voted Clemente into the Baseball Hall of Fame. To honor his charity work, the Roberto Clemente Award was created. Every year a baseball player who volunteers in their community receives this award. Major League Baseball teams also honor his memory every September 15 with Roberto Clemente Day. Clemente’s advice to young people shows how he lived his whole life: “Any time you have an opportunity to make a difference in this world and you don’t, then you are wasting your time on Earth.”

title: Women of Pennsylvania Baseball
text:
Baseball has been part of life in Pennsylvania since the 1830s. The Athletic Club formed in Pennsylvania in 1860. It was one of the earliest professional baseball teams. Women and men of many different backgrounds played baseball. By 1883, there were two baseball teams in Philadelphia composed only of Black women. Both teams were called The Dolly Varden. These were the first teams like this in the country. These women played baseball in a time when both their gender and race severely limited their opportunities. The Kansas Timesnewspaper noted their toughness, saying “none of the women flinched” on injuries that would have “doubled up men.”

Women’s professional baseball continued in Pennsylvania. In 1922, the Philadelphia Bobbies were an all-women’s team. The team’s name, Bobbies, came from a popular women’s hairstyle of the time, the “bob.” The Bobbies traveled all over the country, challenging men’s baseball teams to games. They even traveled to Japan in 1925 to play baseball. This was a unique opportunity for any professional athletic team at the time.

During World War II, women’s baseball continued through the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League (AAGPBL). This league began in 1943 and lasted until 1954. Popular players included Dorothy “Dot” Kovalchick from Sagamore in Armstrong County, Pennsylvania. Another was Betty Jane “Curly” Cornett, also from Western Pennsylvania. These female players kept baseball alive during the war. They also helped keep up morale. As talented athletes, they could show their skills and entertain millions of fans. While women had played baseball before the AAGPBL formed, this league was an opportunity for women to play regularly all over the country. Having women as athletes in public became normal. These women paved the way for female athletes in the U.S. in the decades that would follow.

title: Kobe Bryant
text:
Kobe Bryant was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania in 1978. He played high school basketball in the Lower Merion School District, a suburb of Philadelphia. After high school, he entered the NBA (National Basketball Association) to play basketball professionally. He played for the Los Angeles Lakers for 20 years. Bryant's dad was Joe “Jellybean” Bryant. He was also a former professional basketball player.

Bryant was also a star off the basketball court. In 2017, a poem he wrote was made into a short film. In 2018, this film won an Academy Award. It is called Dear Basketball. Bryant’s foundation, the Kobe and Vanessa Bryant Family Foundation, works to improve the lives of young people and families through sports.

On Jan. 26, 2020, Bryant was in a helicopter crash. Tragically, Bryant, his 13-year-old daughter Gianna, and seven others died. His legacy lives on through the Mamba and Mambacita Sports Foundation.

title: Arnold Palmer
text:
Arnold Palmer was one of golf’s most successful players. He was born in Latrobe, in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, on Sept. 25, 1916. He was the first golfer to win one million dollars as a professional golfer.

Although best known for his golfing, Palmer did much more. During his legendary golf career, Palmer and his wife, Winnie, started the Arnold and Winnie Palmer Foundation. This foundation had a special focus. It worked to help children who suffered from health problems. The foundation’s motto was, “A life well played.”

Arnold Palmer will be remembered for his contributions to golf. However, he will also be remembered for his deeply giving spirit. That was what extended beyond the game and into the lives of thousands of children.

title: Jim Thorpe
text:
James “Jim” Francis Thorpe was not born in Pennsylvania. However, he left his mark on the state. Thorpe was born in the Indian Territory of Prague, now Oklahoma. He was a member of the Sauk and Fox tribes. Thorpe’s Indigenous name is Wa-Tho-Huk, which means “Bright Path.” Thorpe attended and played football at Carlisle Indian Industrial School in Carlisle, Pennsylvania. In 1912, Thorpe won Olympic Gold Medals in both the pentathlon and decathlon. He was the first Native American to win an Olympic Medal.

Thorpe played professional baseball and football. In 1920, he served as president of the American Professional Football Association. Thorpe’s legacy has inspired generations of Native American athletes.

The town of Jim Thorpe in Carbon County, Pennsylvania, is named in honor of Thorpe’s accomplishments.

title: Edith “The Kid” Houghton
text:
Edith Houghton was just 10 years old when she joined a major league baseball team in 1922. The youngest of 10 children, Houghton grew up playing baseball. She lived right across the street from a baseball park. She was playing baseball by age six. By age nine, Houghton was giving hitting, fielding, and throwing demonstrations before Philadelphia Police games. At the age of 10, she won the key infield position with the Pennsylvania Bobbies.

She earned the nickname “The Kid” because she was so young. Newspapers reported, “Little Miss Houghton, the 10-year­-old phenom, covered plenty of ground at shortstop for the visitors and made herself a favorite with the fans by her splendid fielding and ability at the bat.” Houghton wasn’t just some kid who could play baseball. When she was a teenager, she played for the Passaic Bloomer Girls, an all-female team that played against men’s baseball teams. One reporter noted,

“This Miss played as good a brand of ball as any male player has displayed at Maple Shade this season. In addition to pasting out five hits, including two doubles and a screaming homer, she handled six tries at short in major league fashion.”

When World War II broke out, Houghton enlisted in the WAVES (Women Accepted for Volunteer Emergency Services) as part of the U.S. Navy. She served as a clerk. She also played baseball for her WAVES department. Houghton worked her way up the ranks in the Navy WAVES to the chief storekeeper, and finally became Chief Master of Arms. She continued to play in the Navy Baseball League. At one point, she even played with a broken ankle and while suffering from appendicitis!

After WWII, Houghton approached the Philadelphia Phillies to be a talent scout. This meant she would find new players for the team. The team hired her, and she became the first female Major League Baseball scout. She traveled all over the country for the Phillies from 1946 to 1952. Houghton left scouting for the Phillies in 1952. Then, she re-enlisted in the U.S. Navy as a reserve during the Korean War. She served in the Navy for 20 more years. In 1972, she retired from the Navy after rising in the ranks to Chief Petty Officer. Houghton moved from Philadelphia to Sarasota, Florida. She died on February 2, 2013, just eight days before her 101st birthday. Houghton is honored today among the women who changed both how we look at sports and service in the U.S. Armed Forces. She was a trailblazer for women in all aspects of her career.

title: Leadership in Nebraska
text:
A leader’s job is to help people do things together. Leaders also help people solve problems. We have many things to do and many problems to solve. That’s why we have many different leaders. We should understand who our leaders are and what they do. You might even become a leader yourself!

In your classroom, your teacher is a leader. The teacher leads the class in learning. Think about how your teacher helps your class. A teacher shares information that you need to learn. Teachers also listen to your questions so they understand how to help you.

A leader focuses on a particular area of activities. Your teacher is a leader in education. There are leaders in every group in our society. Just like teachers in a classroom, other leaders try to help people learn and accomplish things. There are political leaders, business leaders, religious leaders, scientific leaders, and artistic leaders. We have all of these kinds of leaders in Nebraska.

We need many leaders because there are so many different people. Think about the many ways that people are different. Some people live in cities, while others live on farms or ranches. Some people are older, while others are younger. There are people with many different racial or religious backgrounds too. These are just a few of the many differences that make our culture so interesting.

Our differences give us different ideas about the best ways to solve problems. We choose leaders to represent our different needs. All of us need to be represented when important decisions are made.

This week, we are learning about some of the different kinds of leaders who help all of us in Nebraska do good things together.

title: Week 19 Inquiry Question
text: How do leaders affect a state's progress?

As the country grew, people used the natural resources of the land. Towns formed near harbors, streams, and rivers. The water was used for drinking, irrigating crops, and transporting people and goods. Towns were often near natural resources like forests or minerals. People also built farms in fertile valleys.

Communities change over time. The population of a town can grow or shrink according to needs and resources. First, people build places to live and work. Then, they build community buildings. Places for government, education, and worship are usually some of the first buildings in a community.

As more people come to live in a community, they need more medical and safety care. Communities build hospitals, fire departments, and police stations. A growing community also needs places to buy food and goods.

People change the land to make things convenient. They build things like bridges, tunnels, and shopping malls to help communities meet their needs.

title: Tribal Leaders
text:
Thousands of Native Americans live in Nebraska. Leaders of Native American tribes in Nebraska have a special responsibility to represent their people.

There are four Native American reservations in Nebraska. A reservation is land set aside for a tribe’s use. These reservations belong to the Omaha Tribe, the Winnebago Tribe, the Ponca Tribe, and the Santee Sioux Tribe. Many Native Americans in Nebraska belong to other tribes or do not live on reservations. However, each of these tribes has a government that is

separate from the state and federal governments. Leaders of a tribe are responsible for the tribe’s land, water, law enforcement, and money. Tribal leaders talk to other government leaders in Nebraska to represent their tribe’s needs.

Every tribe chooses their leaders to organize the tribe’s needs and help members of the tribe strengthen each other. One of the most important roles of tribal leaders is to help preserve their tribe’s language and traditions.

title: Leaders in State Government
text:
Our government is organized to give everyone a voice in solving problems. The Nebraska Legislature has 49 senators. Each senator comes from a different area of the state, called a legislative district. The people in each district elect a senator to be their leader in the Legislature.

Each senator’s job is to represent what the people in their district think is most important. People in different parts of the state have different needs. What’s best for ranchers might not be what’s best for farmers. What’s best for people in western Nebraska might be different from what people in eastern Nebraska need. People in big cities might have different problems than people who live on farms or ranches. Our Legislature is designed to take everyone’s needs into account when solving problems.

Our government also has other leaders. The governor is elected to represent everyone in the state. We also have judges who help us understand and obey the law.

Advocacy groups are groups of people who want to teach others about the importance of certain issues. One group might be interested in helping small businesses grow in Nebraska. Another group might work to help people enjoy art and music. Another group might want to protect the environment. The number of different issues people care about is almost endless. Leaders of advocacy groups are important because they help solve the many problems that people care about.

title: State Leaders
text:
Nebraska went from a territory that had 33 legislators in 1854 to having 133 legislators as a state in 1875. With the introduction of the unicameral system in 1936, that number dropped to 43. Today, there are 49 legislators, called senators. Each senator represents about 35,000 citizens.

A senator can only serve two terms in a row. One term lasts for four years. However, a senator can run for election again after being out of the legislature for four years. Senators come from many walks of life. Some are attorneys, farmers, ranchers, businesspeople, and educators.

Senators work during a 90-day legislative session in odd-numbered years and a 60-day session in even-numbered years. While they are not in session, they are expected to talk with the people they represent, conduct studies, and research bills they plan to present at the next session. For this work, they get paid about $12,000 annually.

title: Red Cloud
text:
Red Cloud was a great Native American leader in the 1800s. He was born in 1822, near what is now North Platte, Nebraska. He was a member of the Oglala Sioux Tribe. The Oglala Sioux lived in a region that included areas of Nebraska, Wyoming, Montana, and South Dakota.

Red Cloud became a leader of his people when they came into conflict with other people who wanted the same land that the Oglala Sioux were living on. In 1858, explorers found gold in Montana. The U.S. government started making a trail and building forts along the way to Montana. The trail crossed the land where Red Cloud’s tribe lived. The Oglala Sioux decided to defend their land in a war that was called “Red Cloud’s War.” Red Cloud’s people won the war. The U.S. Army stopped trying to build the trail to Montana.

After the war, settlers continued to move onto Native American land. The U.S. government did not keep its promises to protect Native tribes’ land. However, Red Cloud did not continue to fight wars. He saw that there were far more Americans than Native Americans. Even though Red Cloud knew that his people were very brave, he believed that they would be destroyed if they continued to fight.

Red Cloud became a leader who spoke out against the U.S. government’s broken promises. He traveled many times to Washington, D.C., and other American cities in the east. He became a diplomat for his people.

By the end of his life in 1909, Red Cloud was famous as a leader in both war and peace.

title: Advocates for the Arts
text:
People who work in the arts can make our culture better by helping everyone see the world in new ways. There are many kinds of artists. Painters make pictures. Musicians compose and perform music. Writers tell stories and share information about the past and present. Sculptors make statues. Architects design buildings. Each of these arts can give us wonderful experiences.

Leaders in the arts help artists share their work with the world. Leaders can help people find artistic work that enriches everyone’s lives. The Nebraska Arts Council is one of the advocacy groups that helps the arts in our state.

Almost 50 years ago, the Nebraska Legislature passed a law that created the Nebraska Arts Council. The Council supports school field trips to attend art events and exhibits. The council also gives money to towns and cities in Nebraska to hold musical concerts and art shows. There are many people in our state who would not be able to enjoy artistic events without support from groups like the Nebraska Arts Council.

title: Willa Cather
text:
Willa Cather was one of Nebraska’s great artists. She wrote stories, novels, and poems. Some of her most famous books are about life in Nebraska during the end of the 1800s and the beginning of the 1900s.

Cather was born in Virginia. In 1883, when she was only nine years old, her family packed up everything they owned and moved to Webster County, Nebraska. She went from living in a town full of other people to living in the middle of the huge, empty prairie. Cather and her family were the only other people for miles around. Her father wanted to be a farmer.

Living in such a large, empty landscape had a big impact on Cather. When talking about her childhood on the prairie, she said:

This country was mostly wild pasture and as naked as the back of your hand. I was little and homesick and lonely and my mother was homesick and nobody paid any attention to us. So the country and I had it out together and by the end of the first autumn, that shaggy grass country had gripped me with a passion I have never been able to shake.

Life out on the prairie was hard for Cather at first, but she eventually grew to love it.

Cather attended college at the University of Nebraska in Lincoln. She wanted to learn how to write so she could write about life on the prairie. After college, Cather moved to New York City. She started working as a journalist and a teacher. During that time, she worked hard to get a book published. Her first published book was a book of poems. Later, she published many novels. My Antoníais one of her most famous books. My Antonía is a novel about a boy who moves from Virginia to Nebraska in the 1880s. The story shows us the hard work, difficult challenges, and exciting experiences of people who lived in our state long ago.

title: Economics and Geography in Nebraska
text:
Economics and geography work together. Economics is how money is made and spent. Geography is the way weather, land, and people interact. So, if a farmer wants to make money in the geography of eastern Nebraska, what would be the best crops to grow? What would be the best crops to grow in western Nebraska?

Western Nebraska gets less rain and snow each year than eastern Nebraska. So, it is best to grow crops that need less water in western Nebraska. This is why farmers grow proso millet in the panhandle of Nebraska. Proso millet does not need much water, and it grows quickly. Soybeans grow best in eastern Nebraska, where there is more precipitation. Soybeans need a lot of water.

What if a rancher wants to make money in Nebraska? Where is the best place to raise livestock? Cattle can be raised anywhere in Nebraska. All they need is grass to feed on, and Nebraska has plenty of that. For example, the Sandhill Region isn’t a great place to raise crops, because the soil is too sandy. However, the region is full of grass and small lakes. It has everything cattle need to grow. On the other hand, pigs mostly eat grains, so pig farms are mostly in eastern Nebraska, where more grain is produced.

Geography also affects the economics of the service industry in Nebraska. The service industry is made up of businesses offering things like credit card transaction processing, insurance, and banking. These industries tend to be located in densely populated areas, such as Omaha and Lincoln. Cities are where lots of people need these services and where there are enough people to be employed by these businesses.

title: Specialization in Nebraska
text:
Nebraska’s geography is unique in the United States. It is made up largely of vast stretches of plains and sandhills. Nebraska doesn’t get a lot of precipitation, but it has an enormous underground water source. This unique geography means that Nebraskans have to specialize.

To specialize means to focus your efforts on a narrow range of skills or products. When you specialize at something, you practice it a lot. You get very skilled at it. A musician might specialize in playing the guitar. An athlete might specialize in playing football. A person who makes things in a factory might specialize in welding or painting parts of a machine.

What do Nebraskans specialize in? Since 92 percent of Nebraska’s land is used for growing crops or livestock, one in four Nebraskans specialize in agriculture. They usually specialize in either growing crops or raising livestock. Farmers who raise crops often specialize in a few crops. Some farmers specialize in growing corn one year and then specialize in growing soybeans the next year. Soybeans put nitrogen back in the soil to help the next crop of corn grow. Many ranchers in Nebraska specialize in beef. But there are also farms that specialize in raising pork. Dairy cows, sheep, goats, and poultry are other livestock that farmers specialize in.

However, farmers and ranchers also need to specialize in how to raise crops and livestock in Nebraska. When white settlers first came to Nebraska, they brought farming methods from other places. Those methods often did not work. Nebraska does not get a lot of precipitation, and the soil is very different. People had to learn how to irrigate the land and how to keep soil from blowing away in Nebraska’s winds.

Scientists at Nebraska’s universities specialize in researching new ways to make the most of Nebraska’s land. They study how to keep livestock healthy, how to best grow and rotate crops, how to prevent disease and erosion, and many other things. Then scientists and farmers work together to see how the research can help on Nebraska’s farms.

title: Week 31 Inquiry Question
text: What goods and services does Nebraska create and share with others?

title: Trade in Nebraska
text:
Most communities can’t produce everything they need. Nebraska has plenty of cows, corn, and soybeans, but bananas, coconuts, and seaweed can’t be grown there. In order to get those things, we have to buy them from other places. Buying and selling things is called trade. Trade is part of the economy wherever people live.

Nebraska trades with every other state in America. It also trades with almost every other country in the world. Nebraska exports $1.6 billion in goods to Canada each year. Some of those goods are natural gas, agricultural machinery, and animal meats. Nebraska also exports services to Canada, such as insurance services, financial services, and computer services. Nebraska imports $1.2 billion in goods from Canada. Some of those goods include lumber, animal feed, and plastics.

Overall, Nebraska exports $8 billion worth of goods and services to other places in the world. Most of Nebraska’s exports are foods, such as soybeans, beef, and corn. Nebraska also exports machines, chemicals, transportation equipment, and computer products.

Nebraska also trades in education and research. In 2019, almost 2,000 Nebraska college students studied in universities outside the United States. In 2020, more than 5,000 students from outside the United States came to study in Nebraska universities.

title: Beef in Nebraska
text:
Beef is the largest industry in Nebraska. It’s such a big industry that cattle actually outnumber humans in the state by more than three to one. Three counties in Nebraska raise more cattle than any other county in the United States. Cherry County is at the top, raising almost 166,000 cows. Custer County raises 100,000 cows, and Holt County raises 99,000. Beef sales bring in more than $12 billion to Nebraska each year.

Nebraska specializes in raising beef because everything needed to get beef to the store is right here. More than 24 million acres of Nebraska are made up of grasslands, and cattle love to eat grass. At one point in their lives, cattle are fed corn. Nebraska grows more than 1.5 billion bushels of corn each year. Almost half of this corn goes to feed cattle. Many meat packing plants are also located in Nebraska.

But cattle aren’t raised just for beef. Every part of a cow is used to make various products. Some things made from cows include paintbrushes, tennis racket strings, and shampoo.

title: Crops in Nebraska
text:
We already learned about corn in a previous issue of Studies Weekly, so let’s learn about some of the other crops grown in Nebraska.

Soybeans

After corn, soybeans are the most grown crop in Nebraska. Nebraska produces almost 300 million bushels of soybeans each year. Soybeans are used to make cooking oil, margarine, and shortening. About one-tenth of Nebraska’s soybeans go to feed the state’s livestock and poultry. Soybeans are especially useful in Nebraska because their leaves capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. This brings nitrogen into the soil. Soybeans are often planted between corn harvests because corn needs a lot of nitrogen to grow. Soybeans have many uses. They can be made into ink, plastics, and even fuel for vehicles. In fact, one bushel of soybeans can make 1.5 gallons of biodiesel fuel.

Wheat

The Great Plains area, of which Nebraska is a part, is often called the Breadbasket of America. This is because so much wheat is grown here. Nebraska grows two types of wheat: hard red winter wheat and hard white winter wheat. It is called winter wheat because it is planted in the fall and harvested in early summer. These kinds of wheat need a period of cold to produce grain. Nebraska harvests around 65 million bushels of wheat each year. A bushel of wheat can make 64 loaves of bread. Nebraska exports about half its wheat to other countries.

Beans

Beans have been grown in the Great Plains region for centuries. Native Americans grew them along with corn and squash. Today, Nebraska is the top producer of great northern beans in the nation. Nebraska also produces pinto beans, black beans, pink beans, and garbanzo beans. Beans are mainly grown in the western part of Nebraska, where there is little precipitation. The beans usually need to be irrigated.

Sugar Beets

Chemist Rachel Lloyd was the mother of sugar beet cultivation in Nebraska. Her studies in 1890 showed that Nebraska was a good place to grow sugar beets. In the five years, after her studies were published, Nebraska went from producing 700,000 pounds of sugar beets to eight million pounds. Today, Nebraska is seventh in the nation for producing sugar beets. Most of Nebraska’s sugar beets are grown in the state’s panhandle area. More than half the sugar produced in the United States comes from sugar beets.

title: Beekeeping in Nebraska
text:
The honeybee was first brought to the U.S. from Europe in the 1620s, about 400 years ago. They are now the most numerous bee species in America. In 1975, the Nebraska government named the honeybee as the state’s official insect. This is because Nebraska relies so heavily on agriculture, and honeybees make a lot of agriculture possible through pollination.

Plants share pollen with each other in order to reproduce, or make, new plants. Pollination is the process of spreading pollen to other plants.Though many of Nebraska’s main crops, such as corn, are pollinated by the wind, plenty of other crops need bees for pollination. Some of these crops include alfalfa, sunflowers, and sweet clover. Honeybees are also essential to pollinating some things that you probably enjoy eating, such as watermelon, cantaloupe, apples, cherries, and pears. Worker bees only live for 6-8 weeks. Bees spend so much time flying around as they pollinate that they travel the equivalent of one and a half times around the Earth.

Nebraskans first started cultivating honey in the 1880s. There are now an estimated 700 beekeepers in Nebraska, who raise about 115,000 colonies of bees. Each bee colony has about 60,000-80,000 individuals, and each worker bee produces about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey. That may not seem like much, but, depending on the weather and plant life, these colonies can produce between five and 11 million pounds of honey each year. That’s an average of 75 pounds of honey per colony.

Bees can thrive in many places, even in your own backyard. Backyard beehives are legal in Omaha, though you do need a permit. The University of Nebraska-Lincoln even has a beekeeping program that helps people learn to start and maintain their own colonies. If you want to help your local bees, plant lots of flowers around your house. The more plants they can choose from, the healthier they’ll be.

title: Quillwork and Beadwork in Nebraska
text:
Some of the most unique goods produced in Nebraska are quillwork and beadwork.

Early in Nebraska’s history, Native American women used porcupine quills to decorate items of clothing and make accessories. They would dye the quills with plants and soak the quills so that they could be bent. Sometimes they would weave the quills together. Sometimes they would wrap them around an object, such as a strip of rawhide. It was difficult, time-consuming work.

It was also important work. Quilling was considered a sacred act. Women with excellent quilling skills had a high status. They made visual representations of their tribes’ legends and history so that people could remember them.

Native American women also drilled holes through small stones, shells, and bones to create an early form of beadwork. When the Europeans arrived, they brought beads with them. Native Americans used the beads to create intricate designs and patterns. Today, they are well-known for their beadwork.

Nebraska is a great place to find Native American quillwork and beadwork. You can find everything from beaded dresses to quilled boxes and quilled jewelry to beaded moccasins. Both men and women participate in beading and quilling today.

text: We have needs and wants. Sometimes there is not enough money for both. Sometimes there are not enough goods and services to buy. We have to make a choice.

title: Supply
text: Supply means how much of a good or service there is to buy. Supply affects the price of the good or service.

title: Demand
text: Demand means how many people want or need goods and services. If the demand is high, the price could go up.

title: Scarcity
text: Sometimes producers do not make enough goods and services. This is called scarcity. Scarcity can make the price of a good or service go up.

title: Opportunity Cost
text: Sometimes, we do not have enough money to buy what we need and want. We have to make a choice. We have to give up something. What we give up is the opportunity cost.

Boxes of apples go onto refrigerated trucks or shipping containers. Then, they travel by road, boat, or plane to other communities. Apples need to be kept cool while they travel, but not frozen. At the wrong temperature, they might turn mushy or taste different. When the apples reach their destination, refrigerated trucks take them to stores.
