title: A Changing Nebraska
text:
Nebraska has gone through significant changes in the time humans have inhabited it.

Archaeologists have found evidence that humans started living in the Nebraska area about 10,000 years ago. This was during the last ice age. These people were hunter-gatherers who hunted mammoths, ground sloths, and camels.

The Ice Age ended about 9,000 years ago, and many of the animals these people hunted went extinct. They started hunting different, often smaller, animals, such as deer and antelope. The climate in the Nebraska area changed to become the way we know it today.

About 1,000 years ago, these first peoples began to farm to supplement their hunting. They developed pottery for storage and cooking. They also developed weapons, including the bow and arrow.

Between 900 and 1450 CE, the Great Plains area had a population boom. Archaeologists say that there were actually more people living in the Great Plains area then than there are now. This is called the Central Plains Village Tradition period. Archaeologists have found about 5,000 village sites from this period in Nebraska.

However, around 1400 CE, most of these people suddenly left the area. Nebraska was largely deserted by humans until the Pawnee, Omaha, and Oto tribes arrived in the 1600s.

By 1680, tribes in Nebraska were introduced to horses and began to use them for hunting. Contact with Europeans happened around this time as well. The Native Americans in the Nebraska area first interacted with the Spanish and French. Sometimes, they traded with them, and other times, they fought with them. The French eventually claimed a large area of land that included what is now Nebraska and then sold it to the United States in 1802. This area of land was called the Louisiana Territory.

The Nebraska area was considered the “Great American Desert” for many years after the Louisiana Purchase. Few settlers moved there. But in the mid-1800s, the Gold Rush and the promise of land in the Oregon Territory caused hundreds of thousands of people to travel through Nebraska. Some of them stayed. In 1860, about 29,000 settlers were living in the area. Soon, there were enough citizens to make Nebraska into a territory. In 1867, Nebraska became a state. It had a population of 123,000. Today, Nebraska has a population of 1.9 million.

title: Farm Equipment Over Time
text:
Agriculture has always been important to Nebraska’s people. For hundreds of years, Native Americans fashioned tools made of animal bone and stone to cultivate crops such as squash and corn. When white settlers came to Nebraska, they were used to farming areas with more precipitation. They had to learn new agricultural methods to be successful here.

In 1850, most farmers had two main tools. One was a horse-drawn walking plow. Farmers used this to till their fields. The other tool was a harrow. A harrow is a frame with spikes that is dragged across the plowed ground. It breaks up dirt clods and smooths out the soil. Farmers had to plant and harvest their crops by hand. It would take 75–90 hours of labor to plant enough corn to produce 100 bushels.

By 1890, new tools had been developed to help farmers. One was the two-bottom plow. It had two plows on it, allowing the farmer to till the ground twice as quickly. Disk harrows had also been invented. They were more efficient than spike harrows, but they also made it easier for the wind to blow topsoil away. Planting could now be done with a horse-drawn machine, but harvesting was still done by hand.

Enough progress had been made by 1930 that farmers only had to spend 15–20 hours of labor to plant enough corn to produce 100 bushels. However, they needed more equipment. One farmer could grow enough food for 10 people.

Until the 1940s, most farming was done with horses. However, by then, tractors became affordable enough for most farmers to buy them. By 1975, a farmer could use a five-bottom plow, a 20-foot disk harrow, a planter, and an herbicide (weed killer) applicator. Then, they could harvest their crops with a motorized combine. Now, it took only three and a half hours of labor to eventually produce 100 bushels of corn.

Today, farm equipment uses the Global Positioning System (GPS) and geographic information systems (GIS) to do their work. GPS applications can help farmers plan for the best use of their land, map their fields, and keep track of soil conditions and crop yields. Many tractors and combines can drive themselves, using GPS. A farmer today can grow enough food for 130 people.

title: Irrigation Over Time
text:
Major Stephen Long, who led an expedition through the Nebraska area from 1819 to 1820, called it “the Great American Desert.” He said it was “totally unfit for cultivation.” However, today, Nebraska is one of America’s top producers of corn, soybeans, and wheat.

The main thing that has made Nebraska into such a successful agricultural state is irrigation. Early settlers of Nebraska farmed land that was near streams and rivers. They dug ditches that brought some of this surface water to their crops.

Later settlers had to find water under the ground. They dug wells. Sometimes they found water, and sometimes they didn’t. However, even if they did find water, the wells didn’t help their crops much because the water had to be brought up to the surface one bucket at a time.

By 1870, windmills had solved the settlers’ problem. A windmill’s blades are attached to a rotor, which is attached to a pump. As the wind turns the blades, the rotor powers the pump, which brings water up from the well.

In 1889, the Ogallala Aquifer was discovered. The Ogallala Aquifer is a huge collection of underground water, enough to fill Lake Huron. Most of it is located beneath Nebraska. Farmers now had a large supply of water to draw from, but sometimes, they had to drill down hundreds of feet to reach it. Then they would have to install supporting walls to keep the well from collapsing. This could be expensive.

In 1949, one of the most important advances in irrigation was invented. Frank Zybach was born in Columbus, Nebraska. He invented what he called the “Zybach Self-Propelled Sprinkling Apparatus.” Now, this invention is called “center-pivot irrigation.” This irrigation tool is an enormous sprinkler that can water a 100-acre field. The sprinkler moves on wheels in a circle until the entire field has been watered. The four major suppliers of center-pivot sprinklers are all in Nebraska.

Today, Nebraska has more than six million irrigated acres, the most of any state.

title: How Agribusiness Works
text:
The entire process of producing food and bringing it to the world is called agribusiness. Each part of the agribusiness process is called a sector. Food production takes up the greatest amount of physical space in Nebraska. However, all agribusiness sectors are essential and provide many jobs in our state.

A farm can’t grow crops without first having the seeds, fertilizer, equipment, and workers it needs. Farms get these essentials from the inputs sector, which is made up of businesses and cooperatives. The input sector provides the products and workers that farms need to grow their crops.

Farms are the production sector. Farms produce crops and livestock for the market. When the harvest comes, farms send their products to the processing sector.

The processing sector takes the farms’ products and turns them into the kind of food that people and animals can eat. For example, grain processors make raw wheat into flour. Bakeries can then make that flour into bread.

Once the food is ready for consumers, it goes to the marketing sector. The marketing sector is made up of stores, restaurants, and other places that advertise and sell food.

The support sector helps all the other sectors. It includes universities and government agencies that conduct research. Their findings can help farmers use their land more efficiently, cut their costs, or raise higher-quality crops. They can also help the other agribusiness sectors to better process and deliver food. The University of Nebraska-Lincoln offers degrees in many sectors of agribusiness, including agricultural economics, animal science, food science, and mechanized systems management.

Cooperatives are another aspect of the support sector. Cooperatives are groups of farmers that join together to buy supplies at better prices. They also join together to manage their own input, processing, and marketing sectors.

title: Nebraska Scientists
text:
Ida A. Bengtson

Ida A. Bengtson was born in Harvard, Nebraska, in 1881. She went to the University of Nebraska and earned degrees in mathematics and languages. Then, she went to work for the U.S. Geological Survey Library, but she grew tired of it. She entered a university program in bacteriology and biochemistry. In 1919, she earned a Ph.D., the highest academic degree. She was the first woman to be hired at the United States Public Health Service’s Hygienic Laboratory.

Bengtson is mainly known for her research into typhus, an infectious disease that killed thousands of soldiers during World War I. She also found the bacteria that causes trachoma. Trachoma can cause blindness. While doing trachoma research, she helped more than 1,000 people fight this disease.

Perry London

Perry London was born in 1931 to a Jewish family in Omaha. In high school, he wrote an academic article that got him a full college scholarship. It even got published in an academic journal. After earning a Ph.D., he studied people who selflessly helped others. He focused on Christians who risked their lives to save Jews from the Holocaust during World War II. Some risked their lives even if the people they were saving were complete strangers. London found that these people were adventurous. They were also somewhat different from the rest of the people in their communities. Their uniqueness gave them a different perspective.

Clark S. Larsen

Clark S. Larsen was born in Omaha in 1952. He found his calling when he went on an archaeological dig right after high school. He went with the Nebraska State Historical Society to Fort Atkinson. They discovered human bone fragments there. He found out that scientists can learn a lot from bones. He earned a Ph.D. in biological anthropology. For the rest of his career, he studied bones dug up from archaeological sites around the world.

Kay M. Brummond

Kay M. Brummond grew up in Herman, Nebraska, and graduated from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln in 1985. She has a Ph.D. in chemistry. She has been a professor specializing in synthetic chemistry at multiple universities. Besides her research, she focuses on encouraging women to enter the sciences. She was awarded the ACS National Award for Encouraging Women into Careers in the Chemical Sciences in 2021.

title: Communication and Computer Technology Advances in Nebraska
text:
Nebraska has played a large role in developing communications and computer technology.

It started with Jay W. Forrester. He grew up on a Nebraska cattle ranch and graduated from the University of Nebraska. He was one of the pioneers of early computers. He invented magnetic-core memory storage, which was a way of storing information on a computer. His invention led to today’s RAM (random access memory) technology. The computer Forrester worked with in 1949 was quite different from the computers we use today. His computer was so large that it filled a two-story building. He is a member of the Inventor’s Hall of Fame and has received many awards and honorary degrees.

In 1948, the federal government decided to locate the Strategic Air Command (SAC) near Omaha. The purpose of the SAC was to lead military operations in case of a nuclear war. So, an advanced communication system that could withstand a nuclear blast was built for it. In 1992, one of the first fiber-optic cable networks in the U.S. was built on that system.

A Nebraska company named Level 3 Communications used that system to create a 16,000-mile fiber-optic cable network that served many major cities in the United States. Omaha became a major center for telemarketing. Ameritrade, one of the largest online brokerage companies in the U.S., is also based in Omaha.

Nebraska is also the home of some online gaming companies. One of them is called SkyVu. It has produced games that have received more than 20 million downloads.

title: Learning About History

title: Life Long Ago and Today
text: We do many things the same as people did long ago. We have fun. We learn at school. How we do these things has changed over time.

title: Essential Question
text: How are our lives different from those who lived in the past? How are they the same?

title: Clothing
text: Children's clothes have changed over time. How are they the same? How are they different?

title: Having Fun
text: Children in the past did not have video games. They played tag. They played with marbles. Think about the games you play. Are they the same? Are they different?

title: Learning
text: Children long ago learned to read and write in school. They also learned math. Do you learn these things at school?

title: Food and Water
text: People long ago grew their own food. They got water from a well. Today, we have grocery stores. We have water faucets.

title: Clubs
text: A club is a group of people who like the same thing. Long ago, children formed clubs. What clubs are at your school?

title: Rules and Laws
text: We have rules and laws. Rules and laws change over time. Long ago, roads did not have traffic lights. Today, traffic lights tell drivers when to stop.

title: Washed Away: Did You Know?
text: Rocks are found everywhere. They are found in all habitats all over the world. Some people think rocks are the thing that change the shape of the land. For example, the Colorado River has many large rocks in it as it flows through the Grand Canyon in Arizona. The rocks cause rough water in the river. The rocks cause rapids and even cut through the land. This leads to the belief that rocks are what make the shape of the land. What is really happening is the water is changing the land. The water carries rocks as it flows. This process is called weathering. Water may freeze and crack the rock. Powerful winds can cause small pieces of rock to break over time. The rock then gets picked up by wind and water and moved elsewhere. During the weathering process, rocks may change the way an area looks. However, it is actually wind and water that change the shape of the land.

title: Maps and Models: Did You Know?
text:
A map is a great tool to look at the features of our world or the city we live in. When we look at a map, we see water and land. Maps can help us when we travel places. A map of the United States shows many mountain ranges. Other countries have many mountain ranges too. Mountains seem to look the same size on a map.

A map is a visual representation of the areas on our planet. Maps are models. Models do have limitations. On a map, the Rocky Mountains might only be about two inches long. On the same map, the Himalayas might also be only about two inches long. The Rocky Mountains have some of the tallest peaks in the United States. The Himalayas have some of the tallest peaks in the world. Mt. Everest is almost 30,000 feet tall. It’s located in the Himalayas. In the Rocky Mountains, the tallest peak is Mt. Elbert. It is only about 14,000 feet. Mt. Everest is almost twice the size of Mt. Elbert.

Maps are not meant to be used to show the size of land features or the depths of oceans. They are meant to show where things are located.

title: Liquid Water, Solid Water: Did You Know?
text: Water is one of the basic needs for human life. Water is found all over the world. It is in oceans, rivers, lakes, and ponds. It’s easy to think that humans will never run out of water. We think this because we can see water all over the Earth. If we stand on the East or West Coast of the United States, we will see an endless ocean. However, the ocean is made of salt water. This is not water that humans can drink. We get our water in many forms. We can get our fresh water from underground water, springs, rivers, lakes, and rain. We can build structures, such as reservoirs, to store fresh water to be used later. However, the reservoirs can dry out. This happens if there is a drought and people do not conserve water. We can conserve water by taking shorter showers. We can turn the sink off when we are not using the water. We can avoid using sprinklers and hoses for longer than needed. We use a lot of fresh water for things other than drinking. Humans need water, but our planet does not have an endless supply. We have to make sure we store and save our water so we can continue to survive.

title: What Plants Need to Grow: Did You Know?
text:
It is time to grow a garden in the window sill! We put the plants up on the window sill, where they will get enough sunlight. We also make sure to water them each day. Right before our eyes, they grow. We may think all the plants needed was some sunlight and water every day. We think this because it is all we can see. We see that a plant that is watered daily and placed in a sunny place will grow. It may even grow some beautiful flowers.

How do plants survive in areas where there is little sunlight? How do plants survive in areas where there is little water? In the Arctic, it is dark for up to 22 hours a day during the winter. In deserts, a plant can sometimes go for days or months without any water. Plants have to have a way to make sure they can survive without the daily sunlight and water. In the Arctic, a flowering plant is going to open and soak up as much sunlight as possible when it can. In the desert, a cactus will store water within it to use for long periods when there is no water. Where sunlight and water are not guaranteed every day, plants will adapt to their surroundings. They will use stored resources to survive.

title: Pollinators: Did You Know?
text: You may have heard the saying, “Save the Bees!” We have heard that if bees go extinct, then humans and animals are doomed. Many people believe that bees are the only pollinator. That’s because sometimes they are the only pollinators people ever talk about. A pollinator is an animal that moves pollen from one flower to another. Pollen allows plants to reproduce. However, bees are not the only ones pollinating. We might think they are because bees are the first thing that comes to mind. Other animals and insects move pollen from one plant to another. Butterflies, birds, and flies do their part in helping to move pollen. So do beetles, ants, and even bats! More plants means more oxygen to breathe. More oxygen is better for all living things.

title: Habitats: Did You Know?
text: Sometimes we think that animals only live in one area. For example: we may think that snakes only live in the desert. They are reptiles, and we’ve learned that reptiles live in the desert. However, different types of snakes actually live all over the world. They live in forests, deserts, and the plains. Sometimes when we learn about the different habitats, we also learn about the animals found in that habitat. However, we do not often learn that those animals could survive in other areas. For example: a raccoon can often be found in the mountains or forest. They live in wetlands too. Wetlands are not always found in forests. Wetlands are often on the coast of the continent where the ocean and freshwater meet. They can also be found near lakes. Raccoons can also live in the city. Animals can be found in multiple habitats. Over time, they can migrate and adapt to their new area. It is easy to just say that animals are only found in one specific habitat. However, animals can migrate, adapt, and build a life in a new habitat.

title: Rapid Change, Slow Change: Did You Know?
text: At some point, you may hear someone say, “Our streets are flooding!” after a severe storm. That is one type of flooding. Another type is a flash flood. Some people might think both types are the same thing. After all, both are called “floods.” However, they are actually two different things. Earth has a way of surprising us sometimes. Flooding in a neighborhood might happen overnight due to heavy rainfall. A flash flood in the desert could happen much more quickly. In 2017, a family was hiking in Payson, Arizona. Payson is surrounded by a forest. The area can get large amounts of heavy rainfall. The rain can come quickly and without warning. The family thought it was just another rainstorm. So much rain fell in such a short amount of time that they could not get to safety. The mountain had a lot of burnt areas from a recent fire. The land was very dry. Plants and trees had not grown back. Water from the rain caused a landslide. It was far different than what we might see outside our front window after a night of heavy rainfall. It is important to know that events on Earth can happen very quickly. Other events can happen very slowly. If we understand how things happen, we can be prepared.

title: Introduction to Medieval Europe
text:
Prior to the Middle Ages, most of Europe was a part of the Roman Empire. Eventually, the Western portion of the Roman Empire fell and Europe was divided or broken up into smaller entities. The era known as the "Middle Ages" describes the time period between the fall of the Western Roman Empire and the subsequent Age of Discovery, Age of Exploration, religious reform, and Renaissance. The study of the Middle Ages or medieval Europe is interdisciplinary. This means that understanding Europe’s history during this period requires studying more than just the events of the past, it requires a study of Europe’s geography, economy, political systems, and culture as well.

The basic geography of Europe has not changed significantly from the medieval era, but it has had a significant influence on the events of the past. At the beginning of the Middle Ages, Europe was politically fragmented. However, political boundaries and authorities would change dramatically over the course of the medieval era. Culturally, religion would play a significant role in Europe, particularly influencing the formation and authority of political structures. Christianity was beginning to take hold in the Middle Ages and it would spread all throughout Europe in the medieval era. The economy of Europe, like its religion, was intricately connected to the political systems that began to emerge in this era.

title: Timeline
text:
476 C.E.: The fall of the Western Roman Empire

800 C.E.: Charlemagne, King of the Franks, is crowned Holy Roman Emperor.

1066 C.E.: William of Normandy, a French Duke, conquers and becomes King of England.

1096 C.E.: Start of the First Crusade

1215 C.E.: King John of England signs the Magna Carta.

1337 C.E.: The Hundred Years' War begins between England and France.

1347 C.E.: The Black Death begins in Europe.

title: Europe’s Geography
text:
Geography is the study of the Earth and its people. The study of geography includes how the Earth changes over time. To examine this change, it is necessary to understand how humans interact with the natural characteristics of an area. No matter the time period, geography has played a role in the actions of people and the events of government and economics.

Some of Europe’s most important geographic features have influenced the choices that people have made. Europe is a peninsula or a piece of land surrounded by water on three sides. Europe is surrounded by the Baltic Sea, the North Sea, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Mediterranean Sea. Other important features are the Alps, North European Plain, the English Channel, and the Ural Mountains. One example of how geographic features have influenced the history of Europe can be found among the Vikings. The Vikings were a group of people from Scandinavia. Because they were surrounded by water in their homeland, Vikings developed ships. They eventually designed a ship that could travel beyond their Scandinavian coasts. This ship was called the longship and it was swift, had a square sail, and was able to cross large bodies of water. The Vikings crossed the North Sea, ventured into the Atlantic Ocean, and began raiding the coastal countries of mainland Europe. Another important geographic feature that helped Vikings be successful while raiding was the fact that Europe has a lot of rivers and most of them are navigable. Navigable rivers can be used for transportation because they are deep enough for boats with few natural dangers. The Vikings used these navigable rivers to raid inland and made it to cities like Paris.

The natural resources of an area are also key features in the geographical study of an area. Europe has many natural resources that have influenced the growth of economics. One of the largest continuous stretches of plain on Earth is known as the European Plain. The plain provided resources like good soil and forests. These were vastly important in the medieval era. Soil provided good ground to grow crops. Agricultural crops were the main source of income for people in the Middle Ages. The forests of the European Plain provided building materials and fuel for heat. Europeans developed technologies that harnessed natural resources and made life easier in the Middle Ages as well. For example, watermills and windmills used water and wind to power mills. These mills had wheels attached to them that were powered by the wind or water and once the wheel was spinning, it could grind grain into flour.

title: Maps of Europe
text:
Physical Map

This is a physical map of Europe. It shows the natural features found in Europe like landforms, mountains, valleys, and bodies of water.

Resource Map

This is a resource map of Europe. A resource map shows some of the natural resources available in an area. Although this is a current resource map of Europe, the only major difference between this resource map and a resource map from the Middle Ages would be the availability of timber. Timber, or wood, was an invaluable resource in the medieval era. Timber was used so much in that period that the forests of Europe have decreased significantly since then.

Climate Maps

These are both climate maps. Climate is the study of weather over time. The first map contains a modern understanding of the European climate. The second map from the Middle Ages is called a Macrobian or Macrobius Map. The Macrobian Map shows how medieval scholars understood the climate of the world. The yellow area represented a frozen climate, the blue area represented a temperate climate, and the red represented a hot and dry climate. Medieval Europeans believed that only the top two climates (yellow and blue) were livable.

Historical Map

This is a historical map of the world, drawn around 1295. Ptolemy was a geographer and astronomer in the second century or around the year 150 C.E. He wrote a book about geography that had a revolutionary idea in it: astronomy could be used to calculate distances and estimate the size of the world. Latitude and longitude lines were placed on the map to allow people to understand the distance and placement of continents around the world. Although Ptolemy’s maps were lost, the text was preserved by Muslim scholars. Medieval monks used Ptolemy’s text, math, and astronomy to recreate his world map. This map was more accurate than other maps from the period.

title: Europe’s Economy
text:
Economy is the production and trade of goods and services. During the Middle Ages, Europe produced little that anyone outside of the continent wanted. However, Europeans sought to import items from other parts of the world including silks from China, cotton from India, and spices from Southeast Asia. Gold was mined out of West Africa and was sought after by monarchs across Europe.

Towards the end of the Middle Ages, Chinese inventions would soon be sought after around the world. The Chinese invented paper and printing methods. Paper in the form of papyrus or parchment had been used for centuries, but it deteriorated rather quickly. The new Chinese paper used finely ground wood pulp and it lasted much longer. Although trade was important, most of the economy of Europe was based on agriculture. People began using livestock like oxen and horses. A job that would take all day to do by hand (like plowing a field) would be shortened considerably when using a horse. Some of the most important agricultural products raised in Europe were grain and sheep. The grain was used to make flour, which made bread. Bread was the food that fed most Europeans. Sheep were raised for their wool. Wool made the majority of clothing for Europeans. The spinning wheel allowed people to spin thread from wool, which made cloth. A technological improvement in the spinning wheel allowed people to spin thread much faster, increasing the production of cloth.

title: European Political Systems
text:
A government or political system has the authority to control or direct the actions of the people who live within its political boundaries. After the unity of the Roman Empire ended in Western Europe, many different political authorities gained power. For the majority of the Middle Ages, minor political authorities ruled small tracts of land. However, in the 8th and 9th centuries, two Kings created a larger, unified empire called the Holy Roman Empire. The rulers were a father named Pepin and his son Charlemagne.

Political boundaries also changed quite often because there were many conquests during the Middle Ages. The Visigoths, the Ostrogoths, and the Vandals are often credited with the fall of the Western Roman Empire, which began the medieval era. However, these were not the only conquerors during the Middle Ages. Other groups like the Vikings, also called the Normans, the Franks, the Saxons, and many others were migrating and conquering new territories throughout Europe. Migration and conquest are undertaken for many reasons. In the study of geography, these reasons are called push and pull factors. Push factors are the things that drive people away from a certain area, and pull factors are the things that draw people to a certain area. For example, it is believed that the Visigoths and Ostrogoths invaded Roman territory because they were driven from their homeland by the Huns, another invading group, who were seeking, or being pulled, to find resources.

title: Culture in Europe
text:
Culture is the shared beliefs, customs, traditions, and celebrations of a group of people. There are many different characteristics of culture including, architecture, language, art, religion, celebrations, food, and clothing. To try and describe Europe in terms of a single culture is very difficult. Because communication and movement were not easy to accomplish in this era, most cultures were localized. For example, there wasn’t a single language for all of Europe. In fact, there was rarely a single language for a unified political area. If you lived in England in the early medieval period you spoke Old English. However, if you lived in the southeastern part of England you spoke a dialect of Old English called Kentish. If you lived in the southwest, you spoke West Saxon, Merican in the midlands, and Northumbrian in the north, all of which were dialects of Old English. If you lived in England during the later medieval period you could speak Middle English, Anglo-Norman (a dialect of French), or Latin.

Over the course of the middle ages, however, there were some cultural developments that spread among the majority of people living there. For example, Christianity spread and it became a very prominent part of European culture. Roman Catholicism, a Christian religion, became the focal point of architecture, art, and celebrations in Europe. Although there were people who belonged to different religions like Judaism and Islam, their populations were much smaller than the Roman Catholic population. During the 1100s Gothic architecture developed in Europe. This style of architecture commonly has vaulted ceilings, pointed arches, and ornate decorations like gargoyles and stained glass. Monumental buildings like the Notre Dame Cathedral in France, Westminster Abbey in England, and the Duomo in Italy are all Gothic-style buildings constructed during the Middle Ages.

title: Christianity
text:
In Judaism, the Tanakh, or scriptures, talk about the coming of an important person called the Messiah. The prophecy says that this person would come at a critical time in history and save the Jews from oppression. Around 30 C.E. a group of Jews believed that the Messiah had come, and his name was Jesus of Nazareth. Nazareth was a city in the north of Judea. Jesus’ teachings made him unpopular with Jewish leaders in Jerusalem and with the Roman authorities who had taken Judea as a part of their Empire. He was killed by the Romans after the Jewish leaders had accused him of speaking against Roman rule.

The group of Jews that believed Jesus was the Messiah were called disciples and apostles. After Jesus died, the apostles started teaching others about Jesus. It was their belief that Jesus was the world’s Savior and after he died, he was resurrected, or raised from the dead, and then ascended into heaven.

They believed that Jesus could take away people’s sins, if they followed his teachings. Eventually, those that believed in Jesus of Nazareth were called Christians. This title comes from the Greek word Christ, which means Messiah.

Christianity continued to grow, particularly in the Mediterranean World, but Christians were often persecuted or mistreated. Eventually, Christianity was accepted by Roman leadership when Constantine I made Christianity legal and even converted to Christianity later in his life. In the Medieval Era, some significant changes happened within Christianity. In the Middle Ages, Christianity spread out of the Mediterranean world into northern Europe. Monasteries and nunneries were formed, and Christianity began to be involved in the political systems of Europe.

title: The Spread of Christianity
text:
The spread of Christianity began with the life of Jesus of Nazareth, who traveled through Judea preaching his gospel. After his death, his apostles did the same, except they preached throughout the Mediterranean world. The spread of Christianity continued through the Middle Ages. In fact, Christianity required its followers to go out and spread the message of Jesus and his teachings. The people who are sent to convert others to their religion are called missionaries. Christianity had reached Britain by 410 C.E. From Britain, it traveled throughout Ireland and then back into the main European continent. It found its way to Germany, Russia, and Sweden.

Many of the most famous missionaries like St. Patrick in Ireland, Gregory the Great in Britain, and St. Boniface in Germany traveled throughout Europe to share their views with people. By the year 1200 C.E., nearly all of Europe had been exposed to some form of Christianity. However, some people practiced previous beliefs, by worshiping multiple gods along with the Christian God, and celebrating pagan (non-Christian) holidays.

title: The Great Schism
text:
The 11th century was a critical century for Christianity. It was the beginning of the crusades and it was the time period of something called the Great Schism. Up until this point in Christian history, there wasn’t one central leader. There were five bishops from five cities in the Mediterranean, they were the bishops of Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem. They led the Church as a group but believed that the bishop of Rome had inherited his role from Peter, Jesus’ chief apostle. So, although they believed all decisions should be made together, they acknowledged, at least in part, that the Roman bishop was more closely connected to the origins of Christianity. This would lead to issues among the Church leaders.

Other issues arose in the 11th century. Communication was becoming more difficult between Constantinople and Rome because there was no longer a unified empire to protect travelers. There were also more and more doctrinal issues arising as the Christian Church grew. In the year 1054, all of these issues reached a critical point. The western church, led by the bishop of Rome, also called the pope, threatened to excommunicate the bishop of Constantinople, the leader of the eastern church. Excommunicate means to officially exclude someone from membership, usually of a church. This was offensive to the bishop of Constantinople because he felt that the pope did not have the power to excommunicate anyone, and he told the pope so. The pope responded by actually excommunicating the bishop of Constantinople. Then the bishop of Constantinople excommunicated the pope in return. This break between the eastern and western churches was called the Great Schism. The western church would be called the Roman Catholic Church and the eastern churches would be called Orthodox Churches.

title: Monasteries and Convents
text:
Monks and nuns played an important role in medieval Christianity. Monks are men and nuns are women who both cut ties with regular life and dedicate themselves to their religion. Monks live in monasteries and nuns live in convents. Monks and nuns lead single lives. They often spend their days devoted to prayer, worship, and work. Besides the hours set aside for prayer, monks and nuns attend Mass or church services, often attending Mass multiple times a day.

Monasteries and convents are often safe havens for people accused of crimes, orphans, or homeless people. Many schools, orphanages, and refugee camps have been established by nuns or monks. Some of those institutions are in existence today, having stood the test of time. These places have been helping people since medieval times.

Many medieval monks and nuns based their lives on the rules of St. Benedict, set down in the 6th century, and became members of the Benedictine Order (a special group within the church). Some of the members of this group took vows to live in poverty and silence. Other monastic orders developed during this era. These orders, such as the Dominicans and Franciscans, were modeled after the lives of various important religious figures.

In the Middle Ages, monks and nuns were typically some of the most educated people. They were trained to translate religious and historical texts. Some monks even went beyond just translating into writing their own texts on topics like science, religion, and history. One monk, famous for his writings, was the Venerable Bede. He wrote about science, faith, and historical events.

Before anyone invented the printing press, the only way someone could reproduce a book was to copy the entire book by hand. Some monasteries focused solely on transcribing, or copying, versions of spiritual works, like the Bible. Monks worked in a place called a scriptorium hunched over a desk copying books page by page. It was very difficult to erase their mistakes. They didn’t even have paper as we have it today. Instead, they wrote on parchment or vellum (skins of animals).

title: Week 3 Framing Question
text: What are three ways that Christianity influenced the history of Europe?

title: The Roman Catholic Church
text:
The Roman Catholic Church became the most influential church in western Europe. The leadership of the Roman Catholic Church was hierarchical. At the very top of the hierarchy was the bishop of Rome, or the pope. After the pope came cardinals, archbishops, and all of the other bishops. Then came priests and deacons. Sometimes the people who joined a monastery were members of the clergy (deacons or priests), but often they were not. This often depended on which monastery they were joining. The job of the clergy was to teach the gospel and to help people be forgiven of their misdeeds.

In the medieval era, the Roman Catholic Church played a large role in the daily lives of Europeans. Some of the doctrines or teachings of the Church helped to cement this influence. First, there was an afterlife, and second, to have a good afterlife (go to heaven), you had to obey the rules of the Church. The Church had many spiritual rules, which required a great deal from the people. One of these rules was a church tax. Everyone was required to pay 10 percent of their income to the Church. This was a great sacrifice, especially for the poor. Another condition to reach heaven was that every person had to participate in the church sacraments. In the Roman Catholic Church, there are seven sacraments: baptism, confirmation, eucharist, penance, anointing of the sick, matrimony, and the holy orders. A person could only have the sacraments performed for them by a Roman Catholic priest.

Most towns and villages had a priest that lived in or around them. The priest oversaw the religious lives of people and performed the sacraments. When people sinned, they were required to seek forgiveness. Priests determined the penalties, called penance, for people’s sin. The penance required by the priest might be something like saying a specific prayer, fasting, or going on a pilgrimage, which is a spiritual journey.

In the Middle Ages, the Church would also gain great influence among the nobility of Europe. The pope instructed and influenced many monarchs. Not only was he their spiritual advisor, but he also gave his opinion on political matters. Records show that during the medieval period, there were frequent disagreements that took place between monarchs and the pope. Some were won by the pope and others by the monarch.

title: Charlemagne
text:
Charles the Great, or Charlemagne, was the King of the Franks, a Germanic tribe in western Europe. He inherited the kingdom when his father, Pepin III, died. Both Charlemagne and his father were Christians. Pepin had become King of the Franks when he forcibly took the throne from the previous king. He did this after the pope wrote a letter giving Pepin advice or permission to remove the previous king for incompetence.

When Charlemagne took the throne, the pope was struggling against invaders called the Lombards. Charlemagne came to the aid of the pope and defeated the Lombards. In 800 C.E. Charlemagne was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III. By having the pope crown him emperor, Charlemagne represented both the former power of the Roman Empire and Christianity. The pope benefited from crowning Charlemagne as well, because he received protection from his enemies through Charlemagne’s military.

Charlemagne waged wars for much of his life. He spent nearly 30 years fighting the non-Christian Saxons. Eventually, he defeated them and then forced them to convert to Christianity. In fact, most of the people that Charlemagne waged war with were not Christians, and once they had been defeated, they were required to convert to Christianity.

Charlemagne also donated to the poor across Europe and the Middle East. He promoted education and literacy. He believed this would help people, especially the clergy, become better Christians. He created a large library supported by monks who transcribed books. He paid people to create art. Charlemagne is also credited with writing a short set of laws for his people.

title: The Holy Roman Empire
text:
The Holy Roman Empire began in 800 C.E. with the coronation of Charlemagne. It lasted, in one form or another, until 1806. However, the peak of the Holy Roman Empire’s power and land ownership came under the reign of Charlemagne.

As previously stated, one of the greatest accomplishments of the court of Charlemagne was official support for literacy and education. Monks and other scholars in the Holy Roman Empire acquired and found writings from the previous Roman Empire. Then, they transcribed them onto vellum or parchment. Many of the writings from scholars in the Roman Empire were written on papyrus scrolls. Papyrus was very fragile and as it got older, it disintegrated. The vellum and parchment used in medieval Europe were much more durable (long-lasting) than papyrus. Some of the copies of Roman writing created during Charlemagne’s rule are the oldest versions in existence and are the only reason we know about those writings today.

Charlemagne also sought to standardize writing. Before the reign of Charlemagne, spelling and writing varied from person to person. Writing and spelling could only be standardized when all monks were educated in the same way. During the reign of Charlemagne, all monks began to use the same letters when they copied manuscripts. The type of script they used was called Carolingian Minuscule. Minuscule is what we would call lower-case letters today.

Charlemagne and his successors to the Holy Roman Empire were also noted for their belief that they had been chosen by God to lead. They believed they were accountable to God for how they treated their subjects. They also believed that they were mandated to make all of their subjects become Christians. Charlemagne wanted everyone in the realm of the Holy Roman Empire to be Christian for another reason: he believed that when everyone belonged to the same religion, it created cultural and political unity. This was not a new idea and had been used in many other Kingdoms and Empires, but it was something Charlemagne and his successors enforced.

After Charlemagne’s death, he left his imperial throne to his son Louis the Pious. However, during Louis’ reign, the Holy Roman Empire would become less powerful and would never regain its former size or strength. There were many reasons that the Empire declined, but here are a few:

The Empire was too large. As with many Empires, when the state becomes too large, it becomes difficult to enforce the laws on its fringes. The Empire was at its largest after Charlemagne’s conquests. It would be his successors who had to deal with how to administer to such a large Empire, and they did not do it well. This inability to enforce their rule would lead to a new political system called feudalism.

Louis the Pious’ sons fought multiple wars of succession. Louis had made a plan to split up the leadership of the Empire between his sons. None of his sons were satisfied with the areas they were given. They fought amongst themselves before Louis’ death and after. These wars were expensive and weakened the power of each son.

Conflict between church and state grew after Charlemagne’s death. During the reign of Charlemagne, it was clear that Charlemagne believed he was both a political and religious leader, chosen by God. He was not worried about any church authority telling him what to do, as his authority was unchallenged. After Charlemagne’s death, a new question arose from both political and religious authorities: does the church preside over the government, or does the government preside over the church? Louis the Pious also believed that he had been called by God to lead, but he submitted to church authorities in a way that Charlemagne never did. In fact, after the death of his nephew, Louis felt such sorrow that he submitted to public penance. A church authority commanded Louis to wear sackcloth and ashes. From this moment forward, the church’s power would continue to increase.

title: Spotlights
text:
There are many organizations that serve Nebraska. Here are a few you can learn about.

Wildlife Rescue Team

The Wildlife Rescue Team has been working in Nebraska since 1979. They are a volunteer organization that raises orphaned animals. They also rehabilitate injured wildlife. Both orphaned and injured animals are released back into the wild when they are grown or healed. People can report an orphaned or injured animal to the Wildlife Rescue Team, who will come and take the animal to a shelter. People can also volunteer their time to help the orphaned and injured animals.

Community Action Partnership

In Lancaster and Saunders counties, there is an organization that helps members of various communities. The Community Action Partnership has programs in four main areas: early childhood education, homelessness prevention, financial and family well-being, and hunger relief, or healthy food access. Volunteers can work in any of these four areas. The goal of the organization is to empower community members.

Center for People in Need

The Center’s mission is to fight poverty in Lincoln. They focus on helping people in the community get access to educational training. This training helps people improve their work prospects. The Center helps distribute food through the Food Bank of Lincoln and also funds a diaper bank, where parents can get diapers for their babies. These supplies help families who are facing financial difficulties. Volunteers can help at the food bank or diaper bank, and people with special skills can help educate others.

Habitat for Humanity

Habitat for Humanity is a program that builds homes and helps improve communities for low-income families. Habitat for Humanity does not give away homes for free. It helps people in need afford homes. It can do this with the help of donations and volunteers. Many people, clubs, and businesses volunteer to help Habitat for Humanity. Families who buy the homes also help build them. Habitat for Humanity is trying to help fix the problem of poverty and homelessness.

title: The North Platte Canteen
text:
One of the biggest volunteer efforts of World War II happened right here in Nebraska!

At first, the United States did not become involved in the war. Many Americans wanted to stay out of it. However, Japan attacked the United States on December 7, 1941. By the next day, most people in America were eager to defend the country. They were ready to join the fight.

People in Nebraska started thinking right away about how they could help the war effort. On December 17, 1941, a group of Nebraskans came together at the North Platte train station because they had heard that a group of National Guardsmen from Nebraska were coming on the train that day. It turned out to be a group of National Guardsmen from Kansas. Even though it wasn’t the group of soldiers they were expecting, the Nebraskans gave the Kansas guardsmen all of the food, sweets, and Christmas presents they had brought for their own guardsmen. The event gave Rae Wilson the idea to start a canteen, or cafeteria, that would offer free food to every soldier on every troop train that came through North Platte.

During the war, many items were rationed because they had to go to the troops: sugar, butter, meat, coffee, and gasoline. Rationing meant that most people could only get specific amounts of these things. Even though these items were scarce, several communities from around 200 miles of the train station provided food, drink, cakes, cookies, and other items to the canteen. The canteen was in service from 1941 to 1946. By the end of the war, six million troops had passed through North Platte and been served by the canteen.

title: Week 7 Inquiry Question
text: How do people adapt to their environment?

title: Native American Communities
text: Historically, Native Americans used the land in different ways to meet their wants and needs. Some tribes used the land to hunt and gather plants for food. Some used the oceans, rivers, or lakes to get their food. Others farmed the land to grow crops like corn, beans, squash, and pumpkins. Indigenous groups settled where there was fertile land, mild weather, and water.

title: Essential Question
text: How has my community changed over time?

title: Europeans Came to North America
text:
Many European explorers came to North America on boats. These ships landed in natural harbors on the east and west coasts. On the east coast, many of the explorers were from France, England, the Netherlands, and Spain. Spanish explorers also traveled along the west coast. Some explorers came by land. They traveled north from what is now Mexico or south from what is now Canada.

People from all over the world came to North America. They wanted to settle on land where Indigenous tribes were already living. There was great conflict over the land and the right to live there. The newcomers brought diseases that infected the Native Americans. It is thought that up to 90 percent of Native Americans in some areas died from such diseases. Weakened and outnumbered, the Indigenous peoples had their land taken by the new settlers.

title: Cities Grew in Diversity
text:
Spain built the first successful European settlement in what is now the continental United States. It is called St. Augustine. People still live there today. The settlement was built on the coast of what is now Florida. On the coast, boats could reach it easily. Harbors were usually the first areas where Europeans built settlements.

Some people came to the United States to claim and farm the land. Others hunted and trapped animals so they could send fur back to Europe. Some came to harvest natural resources, like minerals and wood. Many people had jobs working on the ships that came in and out of the harbors. Others brought resources to the ships to trade for other goods. Cities grew out of the harbor areas, and more people needed food to eat and places to live. Farms produced a surplus of food that was transported to the cities. Communities built railroads to help move people and goods. Settlers from Asia and Latin America came to find work building railroads and harvesting food.

Not everyone came to North America by choice. Europeans brought enslaved people from western Africa to work on farms and plantations. Everyone who came to America brought their experiences, cultures, and traditions into the country. The United States became a diverse place.

title: Growth of a Community
text:
As the country grew, people used the natural resources of the land. Towns formed near harbors, streams, and rivers. The water was used for drinking, irrigating crops, and transporting people and goods. Towns were also located near natural resources like forests, mines in the mountains, or farms in the valleys.

Town populations increase or decrease because of resources. Towns grew with family homes and places to work. Then, the town would build community buildings. Places for government, education, and worship were some of the first buildings in a community.

As more people came to live in a community, they needed more medical and safety care. Communities built hospitals, fire departments, and police stations. A growing community would also need food markets and places to buy things.

Towns made changes to the land to make things convenient for people. They built bridges, tunnels, and shopping centers to help people meet their needs.

title: Decline of a Community
text:
Sometimes resources in an area are exhausted, or used up. With no resources to create jobs, people move away. They are pulled to other areas with more resources and jobs. Towns with no resources cannot keep up with the wants and needs of the people. Houses are for sale with no buyers. Shopping centers close because there is no business. School buildings have fewer students. There are many empty businesses. Over time, some towns completely disappear.

As one area declines, another area can be growing. Every community goes through periods of growth and decline.

title: Bodie, California
text:
The town of Bodie, California, was established in 1859. First a mining camp, the town grew quickly because of the silver and gold that was found there. Miners from far and wide moved to Bodie to get jobs mining the gold. The miners brought their families. Housing was built quickly for the families. By 1879, Bodie's once-small mining population grew to almost 10,000 people.

Over 2,000 buildings were built to meet the wants and needs of those living in the community. There were general stores, banks, mining offices, and union and social halls. There were also churches and a newspaper office. These were just some of the buildings that made up the town of Bodie.

Bodie saw many years of growth. However, by 1920, the town's population had declined to only 120 people. The gold and silver mines were exhausted. With no jobs, people were pushed out of Bodie and pulled to other more prosperous areas of the state. Today, Bodie is one of California's State National Parks. Only 110 buildings remain in the park.

title: Essential Question
text: What are ways businesses influence change in communities?

title: Goods and Services
text:
People use resources to produce goods and services to provide for their needs and wants. Goods are things made for people to buy and use. Goods include food, furniture, and houses. Services are work that a person does for someone else. Services are actions like haircuts, car repair, and teaching.

In the United States, there are private and public goods and services. Private goods and services are provided by businesses. You buy them, and then you own them. Private goods include things like clothing, cars, and toys.

Public goods and services are paid for by taxes, not individuals. They are shared by the community. Schools, police stations, and public transportation are public goods. Another example is your public library. The items at the library belong to the community. It doesn't cost you money to borrow things from your local library. The government provides this service to the community through money collected from taxes.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
The people who make goods or provide services for other people are producers. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are created for other communities.

The people who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers can buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. When you get a haircut, you are buying a service. This makes you a consumer. You are also a consumer if you buy a book.

People can be both producers and consumers. For example, a baker is a consumer when they purchase flour, sugar, and supplies to make their baked goods. A baker is a producer when they sell their baked goods.

title: Economic Activities
text:
What things are produced in a community? How are things produced? Who receives the goods that are produced? The study of economics answers these questions.

Producers depend on trade with others to meet their needs and wants. People make choices based on their needs, wants, and the availability of resources. What consumers buy often determines what goods and services are produced.

Every community has different types of economic activities. Some of these activities are agriculture, manufacturing, and research and development. Other economic activities are healthcare services and tourism.

title: Types of Economic Activities
text:
Agriculture is the business of growing crops and raising animals. Fruits, vegetables, flowers, and cotton are agricultural products. Dairy farming and beekeeping are agricultural businesses. Natural resources are important to agriculture.

Manufacturing is using raw materials to make products or goods to sell. Cars, computers, and toys are all manufactured products.

Research and development is about creating new services or products. It can also be about improving existing services or products.

Healthcare is a service industry. It includes all the goods and services used to treat people who are sick.

Tourism is providing goods and services to travelers. Some places have tourist attractions based on unique physical characteristics in their area, such as oceans, mountains, and national parks. Other tourist attractions, like theme parks, are human-made. Tourism strengthens the economies of cities, states, and countries.

title: Your Own Business
text:
The United States has a free enterprise system. A free enterprise system means that businesses, goods, and services are determined by people’s needs and wants. This also means that people are able to start their own businesses. There are rules and fees, but the government doesn't tell people what businesses they can create.

Businesses create goods and provide services. The money it costs to run a business is known as expenses. The money businesses earn is called income. Income is used to pay business expenses. Profit is the money left over after a business pays all its expenses. Some businesses make a large profit. Sometimes businesses don’t make a profit and take a loss. A loss is when the expenses of the business cost more than the income a business makes. The prices a business charges affect how much profit they can make.

title: Entrepreneurs
text:
An entrepreneur is someone who comes up with an idea and then uses this idea to start a business. Entrepreneurs are people who have a vision about something new or helpful they can offer their community. They combine the natural, human, and capital resources in an area to produce goods and services. They make decisions about what to produce based on the needs and wants of people in their area.

Entrepreneurs have many reasons for wanting to start their own businesses. Some entrepreneurs want to build something of their own. Others feel they can make a lot of money working for themselves. Others have a solution to solve a problem. There are big opportunities and risks involved in being an entrepreneur. Successful entrepreneurs often have a great impact on their communities.

title: Let’s Coexist: Did You Know?
text: Have you ever noticed that wolves, lions and many other pack animals live together, work together and get along for the benefit of the group? These are pack animals so they will always want to work together, right? You may be surprised to find that all organisms, even the same kind, do not have to get along to live in the same environment. Why do we think this? We think this because we often do not see the day to day interactions between organisms. We really never see the same animals competing against each other for resources. It happens every single day. You probably already know that organisms will only stay in areas that meet their needs. For example, bears that eat berries or fish will not live in an area that does not have these resources. If they cannot get the food they need, they will move to an area that does. There are other bears though that also need those resources too. They will compete for the resources as necessary and some may have to move on. It is important to remember that within an ecosystem, organisms will compete for resources and feed on one another if they have to. They will only stay where their basic needs for food, water and shelter are met. Organisms can live together within the same ecosystem because of their needs but they will not always get along.

title: Ga Du Gi and Ella Bird
text:
For some people, being rich and famous is a way to earn the admiration of other people. For Cherokee people, earning respect and admiration is about living a life based on the principle of Ga Du Gi. This means a Cherokee person should always look to benefit others, to join together and work for one another’s benefit.

Ga Du Gi is a concept that Ella Bird, born and raised in the Snowbird community located in present-day Graham County, NC, has lived her whole life by. A mother of ten children, (five girls, five boys) and a fluent Cherokee speaker, Ms. Bird has passed down her knowledge of plants, language, quilting, and traditional foods. Her favorite meals involve pinto beans and fried potatoes. She has also taught younger generations of Cherokee about harvesting food from the mountains surrounding her home, including spicy mustard greens, turnip greens, polk salad, delicious sochan, and ramps. Ramps are potent onion-flavored bulbs that grow in North Carolina’s mountains during the early part of springtime, and can be eaten raw or cooked.

The Cherokee people will bestow the title of Beloved Man or Beloved Woman to someone who follows Ga Du Gi and is highly respected for their service to the community, their integrity, and their good character. Historically, a Beloved Woman would have an important voice when the Nation deliberated whether or not to go to war. One of Ms. Bird’s most respected characteristics is that she is slow to anger and thus, would have been very cautious before deciding to go to war. It is extremely rare for somebody to be honored with the title of Beloved Man or Woman. People who receive one of these titles are carefully selected for their honesty and wisdom, and only 11 people have received such a title since 1943. Ella is one of only three living Cherokee people that have been given the title of Beloved Woman for living a life full of admiration and respect.

title: Respect
text:
Being unkind, being rude, or bullying is not healthy. Being kind and respectful to peers and teachers is important and builds relationships. Sometimes bullying or disrespect can look like trying to show humor at the expense of someone else's feelings. While you may notice that some people treat others this way, it is not good for your wellness or the emotional or social health of others.

Being respectful means being kind and thoughtful to others. Respect can also mean that you admire, or look up to, someone.

To whom should you show respect? Everyone deserves respect. No one is better than any other person. When you choose to show respect to others, they are more likely to be respectful to you. Being a good listener, being kind to people who are different from you, and appreciating others who believe or act differently than you are all ways of showing respect.

title: Respecting Differences
text:
No two people are the same. People’s clothes, skin colors, beliefs, abilities, talents, and interests all make them different from each other. Can you imagine what it would be like if everyone looked, sounded, and acted the same? What a boring world that would be!

People may also differ from you in how they choose to express themselves. You can choose to show everyone respect, whether or not you agree with their beliefs or behaviors. You can stand up for your own ideas and opinions while still being respectful to others. Respect doesn’t always mean agreement. When you are respectful, you can be friends with people who are different from you.

Some people choose to treat others poorly if they are different. Teasing or gossiping about someone because they are not the same as you is wrong and harmful to yourself and others. This kind of behavior is often called bullying. The effects of bullying are very harmful and can be long-lasting. Respecting differences between people can protect you and others from the negative effects of bullying.

title: Embracing Similarities
text:
There is no one exactly like you. Even though this is true, you do have similarities with all people.

Imagine you could talk to anyone in the world. If the two of you decided to fill out a Venn diagram together, you might be surprised at the results. After labeling the circles with your names, you would each write your differences in those circles.

But what about where the circles overlap? Would you have things in common?

You might share lots of similarities with some people. With others, you might have to say, “We both have eyes,” or, “We both have knees.”

This means you can connect with and respect everyone around you. You can focus on what you have in common instead of only focusing on how you are different from others. Finding ways to connect with people can help you feel and show respect toward them. Give it a try!

title: Handling Misunderstandings with Respect
text:
When you have disagreements or misunderstandings with others, you can choose how to act. Some people are disrespectful during a disagreement or misunderstanding, but that can damage relationships. Disrespect could be:

Yelling

Name-calling

Gossiping about the person

Choosing not to see the other person’s perspective

Using violence

You can choose to maintain respect for each other as you work through a misunderstanding or disagreement. Handling a misunderstanding with respect may include some of these things:

Calmly expressing your side of things

Listening to the other person with the intent of understanding their perspective

Apologizing when necessary

Striving to find a win-win solution

Solving a misunderstanding respectfully doesn't mean you have to simply agree with the other person. You can have a conflict with someone and still be respectful. You can even feel and express frustration while maintaining respect. Even adults have a hard time with this sometimes. You can be an example to everyone around you by solving all your misunderstandings using calm, respectful words.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text:
Thomas Jefferson was born in Virginia in 1743. He became a leader in the colonial government at age 25.

In 1776, Jefferson became a member of the Continental Congress. This is the group that was organized to write the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson was chosen to write the declaration that was sent to the king of England. It told the king that the 13 Colonies wanted to break away from England.

After the Revolutionary War, Jefferson served as a minister to France. He was elected president of the United States in 1800. Jefferson was very familiar with the French because of the time he had spent in France. This helped him make a deal to buy territory that France owned and expand the United States.

Jefferson is remembered as a talented writer and statesman. He was the third president of the United States. He was one of the Founders of our nation.

title: The Louisiana Purchase
text: In 1801, the United States didn't look like it does today. It was much smaller. The Mississippi River was the western border of the country. Spain controlled Florida and much of the Southwest. France had claimed the land west of the Mississippi River. Settlers shipped supplies and goods up and down the Mississippi River to the port of New Orleans. President Jefferson thought it would be dangerous for another country to control this important shipping route. Instead of trying to take it by force, Jefferson asked France to sell the land. In 1803, France made a deal to sell the United States even more land than Jefferson had originally asked for. The United States paid $15 million for the land. This sale is called the Louisiana Purchase. The purchase doubled the size of the country. The new territory stretched from the Mississippi River all the way to the Rocky Mountains.

title: Lewis and Clark
text: Before the Louisiana Purchase, President Jefferson had already planned to send a group to explore the western frontier. He chose his secretary, Meriwether Lewis, to lead the group. Lewis chose William Clark as his co-captain. Lewis and Clark had served in the military together. About 40 other men joined Lewis and Clark. Their group was called the Corps of Discovery. Their expedition became known as the Lewis and Clark Expedition. President Jefferson instructed Lewis and Clark to explore the land. Jefferson told them to draw maps, study the plants and animals, and observe the Indigenous peoples they met. Jefferson also told them to look for new travel routes and existing trading posts or settlements.

title: The Lewis and Clark Expedition
text:
In May 1804, the Corps of Discovery began their journey. They took glass beads, mirrors, and cloth to trade with the Indigenous people they met. The first winter of their exploration wasn't easy. The first winter, the corps experienced freezing temperatures, high winds, and storms. The corps members were sick and had injuries. They kept going to reach the Pacific coast. They stayed there for the second winter. Then, they returned home to share their findings. They brought journals, sketches, and maps of their journey. They recorded information about 300 new kinds of plants and animals.

After returning to Missouri, the men were treated as heroes. The expedition was very important. It helped settlers learn about the new land and the people who lived there. They now had maps that would make traveling through the Louisiana Territory easier. Settlers could now move even farther west. This expansion wasn’t good news for everyone. Indigenous peoples had already been pushed west by the settlers. Now, even more were forced to move off their land.

title: Sacagawea
text:
Sacagawea was a Lemhi Shoshone woman. She was an interpreter and guide for the Lewis and Clark expedition. At age 12, Sacagawea was captured and enslaved by an enemy tribe. She was then sold to a French Canadian fur trader named Toussaint Charbonneau. Lewis and Clark hired Charbonneau as an interpreter for their expedition. Sacagawea was brought on the trip as an interpreter because she spoke Shoshone. Sacagawea played an important role in the expedition. In addition to interpreting, she was very good at finding edible plants and herbs. This skill helped the explorers during their travels.

On May 14, 1805, the expedition boat she was in tipped over and filled with water. Supplies and documents fell into the water. Sacagawea stayed calm. She saved the supplies and documents from being lost in the river. About a week later, Lewis and Clark showed their appreciation by naming a part of the Musselshell River after her.

title: Louisiana: Many Cultures
text: Louisiana's culture is unique. The music has different rhythms and beats. There are many lively festivals. The food is known for its spicy taste. The architecture of the buildings was influenced by places all around the world. Why is the culture so special? There's a good reason. It has been shaped by many different cultures that have mixed together, right here in Louisiana. When the Louisiana Purchase was made, new land was added to the country. This land was different from much of the other land. People of Indigenous, European, African, and Latin American descent made a unique and mixed culture. This culture added diversity to the United States.

title: Louisiana: Past and Present
text:
At the time French settlers came in the 1700s, many Indigenous peoples lived in Louisiana. The Louisiana Purchase altered the shape of our nation and the lives of Louisiana’s native peoples. Some tribes left or were forced to move to different lands. Some tribes stayed, and some of their descendants still live in Louisiana today. The Chitimacha are the only native people in Louisiana to still live on a section of their original homeland. Today, many different groups of people live in Louisiana. Some things have changed as groups have moved in or out of Louisiana. Other things have stayed the same.

Life in Louisiana today is both similar to and different from life in the past.

Lands and Home

Louisiana's original inhabitants were close to nature. They relied on and respected it. Mountains formed natural borders. Rivers provided food and trade routes. Families lived in houses made of wood, grasses, and reeds.

Food

While the men hunted, the women grew and gathered food. Their main crops were corn and potatoes. A tribe's territory often shaped its traditions. Those who lived along the rivers or coast could fish or catch alligators. Those who lived in wooded areas hunted for deer and bear.

Clothing

Hunting was an important source of food but also provided clothing, tools, and jewelry. The women made clothes from animal skins. They also used cloth, feathers, and bark.

Recreation

Indigenous communities of the past played games and went to sporting events. Wrestling, racing, and archery were popular sports. Music and dancing were central to these events.

Celebrations

Many tribes had a celebration in the early part of November to honor the dead with dance, song, and food. Families gathered in cemeteries to visit graves and then returned home to a great feast.

title: Physical Characteristics
text:
The theme of place refers to how we describe a location. The physical characteristics of a place are part of its natural environment. What is the landscape like? Are there unique landforms or bodies of water? What are the common plants and animals? What are the weather patterns? What are the natural resources?

Landscapes, plants, climate, and animals are physical characteristics. These things give a location its unique appearance and meaning. Places on Earth are different because of their different physical characteristics.

title: Climate
text: Climate is a physical characteristic. Climate is the weather pattern that develops in a place over many years. The weather can change in just a few hours. The climate takes hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperature, precipitation (rain, snow, sleet), and wind in an area. People make decisions about food, clothing, and shelter based on the climate. We use climate maps to learn about what different places are like. We can learn about different climate zones around the world.

title: Resources and Environment
text:
Economics is the study of the production and trade of goods and services. There are many sub-topics that can be used to understand how economics has influenced history. Some of these topics are: trade, money, business, resources, and labor.

The resources available within a geographic area are going to limit the economic choices that people can make in that area. For example, the area that is now Saudi Arabia gets less than 6 inches of rain per year. In comparison, the state of Georgia gets anywhere from 50 to 60 inches of rain per year. For this reason, the land that Saudi Arabia occupies is also called the Arabian desert. It is very difficult to engage in agriculture in this area, so historically, the people who lived there were nomads. They followed herd animals to oases and good grazing lands. It might seem like this would make it impossible for the economy of Arabia to move away from nomadic herding. However, Arabia had a few other resources that would allow it to trade extensively with other nations. These items were frankincense and myrrh.

Frankincense and myrrh are harvested from a family of trees called Burseraceae. When these types of trees are cut or the bark is damaged, sap flows out of the tree and hardens. Once the sap has been harvested, it is sold and is usually burned for its desirable smell. Both frankincense and myrrh were considered to be luxury goods because they came from such a specialized tree. Only the very wealthy could afford frankincense and myrrh. Those who sold these goods also became wealthy. So, the nomads of Saudi Arabia became wealthy despite living in a very harsh environment. This is just one example of how the availability of resources affects economic growth.
