title: Juneteenth
text: The Emancipation Proclamation declared that on Jan. 1, 1863, all enslaved people would be free. News of the proclamation was slow to reach many parts of Texas. In some other places, the news was hidden by slaveholders to preserve slavery. Two and a half years later, on June 19, 1865, federal troops arrived in Galveston, Texas. African Americans celebrated when they heard the news that the Civil War had ended and that enslaved people were free. Juneteenth is a short way of saying "June nineteenth." In 2021 it became an official national holiday. It is a day for African Americans to celebrate not only their freedom but their history, culture, and achievements. It is a day for all Americans to think about equality and justice.

title: The Real Story of Thanksgiving
text:
Thanksgiving today is very different from what happened in the Plymouth Colony in the fall of 1621. The Pilgrims’ first year was very difficult. Most of the colonists were still living on the ship. Only half of the colonists who arrived on the Mayflower made it through the winter. The Wampanoag Indians helped them adapt and survive. Colonists were taught how to extract sap from maple trees, cultivate corn, and how to avoid poisonous plants. To celebrate their first harvest, Governor William Bradford organized a feast.

Our harvest being gotten in, our governor sent four men on fowling, that so we might after a special manner rejoice together, after we had gathered the fruits of our labors; they four in one day killed as much fowl, as with a little help beside, served the Company almost a week, at which time amongst other Recreations, we exercised our Arms, many of the Indians coming amongst us, and amongst the rest their greatest king Massasoit, with some ninety men, whom for three days we entertained and feasted, and they went out and killed five Deer, which they brought to the Plantation and bestowed on our Governor, and upon the Captain and others. And although it be not always so plentiful, as it was at this time with us, yet by the goodness of God, we are so far from want, that we often wish you partakers of our plenty. -Edward Winslow, Pilgrim chronicler

The Wampanoag who were invited to the feast had also experienced a difficult year. They had lost many of their people because of disease. The Wampanoag were welcomed in the village and so was the deer they brought to the feast. For three days, they shared in a celebration to give thanks.

title: Farm to Market
text: The food grown on farms is transported to urban and suburban markets. The system of highways, seaports, and airports creates the routes from farm to market. Consumers purchase products from all over the world. Producers send products all over the world. This great system, or network, of producers and consumers is called interdependence. Each depends on the other for success. Sometimes, this is also called a supply chain. We will be learning about interdependence using apples, a natural resource.

title: Essential Question
text: How does interdependence influence cost?

title: Production: How Are Apples Grown?
text:
Some parts of the United States are good for growing natural resources. One of these natural resources is apples. Washington, in the Northwest region, produces more than half of the apples grown in the United States. Apples grow best in climates where winter is cold and summers are warm. To produce a good crop, most apple trees need about 1,000 hours of chilling time. Chilling time means the weather is above freezing but below 45 degrees Fahrenheit.

Apple trees grow in orchards, or pieces of land where fruit and nut trees grow. In order to plant an orchard, an apple producer needs plenty of open land with good soil. They also need access to lots of fresh water.

The apple producer cares for the trees. They make sure the trees stay healthy and get enough water and sunlight. In spring, they also help to make sure the flowering apple trees are pollinated. Pollination is necessary for producing fruit. Bees are the best natural pollinators. Some apple orchards have their own beehives. Many apple producers rent hives from beekeepers.

In the United States, apples usually begin to ripen starting in July. Different types of apples become ripe at different times. People can harvest fresh apples through the fall. Usually, producers harvest apples by hand instead of using machines. The people who do the work of picking apples are known as human resources. A human resource is a person who works and does important tasks for a company or organization.

title: Processing: How Are Apples Harvested?
text:
When apples are ripe, workers pick them off the trees. Scientists and engineers have tried to build apple-picking machines. However, most apple producers use human resources to harvest apples. Picking by hand is still the best way to keep the fruit from getting bruised.

Once they are picked, the apples go to a processing building. The apples go into a water chute, where moving water pushes the floating apples through the next steps of processing. The water chute also cleans dust off the apples. The apples are examined to make sure they have no insect holes or bruises. Sometimes this is done by people. Many large apple producers have machines that scan the apples to make sure they’re ready to go to the market. The tools and machinery used to process a product are called capital resources. Then, the apples are sorted by color, size, and shape. The apples go into bins with other similar apples. Then, the bins go into a cold storage room.

When the apples are ready to go to the market, they go to a packing facility. Workers look them over one last time to make sure they look good enough to eat. Then, they put a sticker on each apple and hand-pack them into boxes.

title: Distribution: How Do Apples Get to Market?
text:
Boxes of apples go onto refrigerated trucks or shipping containers. They travel by truck, boat, or plane to other communities. Apples need to be kept cool but not frozen while they travel. At the wrong temperature, they might turn mushy or taste less fresh. When the apples reach their destination, refrigerated trucks take them to stores. Then, consumers can buy them and bring them home.

Apples that don’t look nice but are still fresh and safe to eat don’t just go into the trash. They are processed into other goods. The apple producer might sell them to a different producer. Apples can be turned into juice or applesauce. They might be combined with other ingredients and turned into a pie. Those producers have their own processes for getting their apple goods to consumers.

title: Civic Responsibility
text:
A civic responsibility is something that citizens are expected to do in the community. All citizens are expected to make choices for the common good. Members of a community are expected to obey laws. We are all expected to work to improve our communities.

Some civic responsibilities are enforced. This means that there are consequences if we do not follow them. Obeying the law and serving on a jury are enforced responsibilities. A jury is a group of citizens who are selected to decide a court case.

We vote to elect public officials. However, voting is not enforced. It is by choice. Volunteering is also by choice. It helps the community and people in need. Serving in the military or holding a public office are also things citizens can do to help their community.

text:

This is when French explorers camped and held a small celebration not far from the future site of New Orleans. Over time, people have added unique traditions that have helped shape the holiday into what it is today.

Mardi Gras is celebrated with music, parades, events, and activities throughout Louisiana. North Louisiana is known for a parade featuring a royal court of pets. A tradition popular in southwest Louisiana involves dressing in colorful costumes and begging for ingredients to make gumbo. For the final ingredient, runners chase after a live chicken. King Cake, a braided pastry decorated in gold, purple, and green, is one of the most popular treats of the Mardi Gras season.

title: Politics and Economics
text:
The relationship between politics and economics is different in each country and time period. Politics focuses on the distribution of power and the relationships that exist between the holders of power. Economics focuses on the availability and distribution of resources in order to meet society’s needs. However, although politics and economics are two different systems, one often affects the other.

For example, laws are sometimes passed to ensure that everyone involved in a certain trade or profession keeps the same rules and follows the same guidelines. This ensures that trade is fair for everyone. This is just one example of how politics affects economics.

In contrast, a group that produces a certain good or provides most of the labor for a company can ask the government to create rules or laws. They can also exert their will by refusing to work until their demands are met. This is an example of how economics can affect politics.

Trade has always been a necessary part of the economy. When a certain good can’t be produced within a country, that country must trade for it. Governments are often involved in trade, making sure that laws aren’t broken and that each party benefits from the trade. For example, a spice merchant in the medieval period might discover that there is a demand for spices in a city in another country. If they went to that city to trade, they could take business away from local spice merchants already there. To make sure they wouldn’t disrupt the local economy, the political power could require foreign merchants to pay a fee, obtain a license, or charge the same prices as other merchants in the city.

The involvement of politics in economics varies from country to country and from era to era. In the United States, we currently have a free market economy. In this system, the government is not allowed to influence the market in specific areas, such as competition between businesses, where a person chooses to work, and what products or services each company makes. In other countries, the government is much more involved in establishing and controlling the economy. In some countries, there are laws that dictate where a person must work, what the price of a certain product is, and which businesses can operate. This can often reduce or eliminate competition.

How closely politics and economics interact differs around the world and has changed throughout history. One thing that is often true about their relationship: political systems want their economies to succeed and often meet the wants and needs of their citizens.

title: Feudalism
text:
After the collapse of the Roman Empire, and a brief period of unity during Charlemagne’s rule, the governing power across western Europe splintered. Territories became divided into smaller kingdoms. Kings ruled over these small kingdoms and delegated or assigned power to members of the nobility. This created a system we now call “feudalism.”

Kings gave parcels of land within their kingdom to noble lords in exchange for their loyalty and service, usually through military support. These nobles, under similar terms, then gave pieces of their land to lower-born lords to manage and oversee. The king or lord who gave the land was known as the overlord, while the lord who received the land was a vassal.

Nobles and lords, to some extent, took on the roles of kings over their fiefs, or parcels of land granted to them. They took care of the people who lived on their lands, made laws, and collected taxes. The lord of a fief lived in a large manor house that was surrounded by the villages and farming communities of the region.

Knights were essentially the military personnel of the feudal system, and their primary function was to protect the lords and nobles, the land, and sometimes the king. Knights were considered the lowest members of the nobility, but they were a step above peasants. They could be granted land and wealth from the lord they served.

At the bottom of the feudal system were the lowborn peasants, or serfs, who worked and farmed the land they lived on. In exchange for protection and use of the land, the serfs paid rent, farmed, gave a portion of their food to their lord, and paid taxes. Peasants in the feudal system had very few freedoms. It was difficult to leave the land where they lived and worked, even for short periods of time. Marriage was restricted to people who had the same feudal lord. There were many other restrictions. So, although they were not enslaved, many historians classify peasants in the feudal system as “unfree” because of their limited freedoms.

Through the system of feudalism, kings and lords established a network of alliances that made their kingdoms loyal and strong.

title: Manorialism
text:
While feudalism was more of a political system of power and land ownership, manorialism, or the manor system, was the economic and agricultural part of the feudal system. Kingdoms relied on manors to supply food to the rest of their people. A kingdom was similar to a state, and a fief was like a county within that state. Within a fief, there could be one or more manors, or large houses with lands attached to them. A manor was owned and managed by a vassal or lord. Each manor was responsible for providing enough food to feed itself, as well as sending a portion of what it produced to the king. The layout of a manor had to be meticulously planned and laid out to make sure it was as successful and as productive as possible. The size of a manor could vary between 1,200 and 1,800 acres.

The manor consisted of the main manor house, the village or villages surrounding it, and the farmland, meadowland, and woodlands around that. The manor house was where the lord and his family lived. Close by were the homes of the peasants. The manor house sometimes had the appearance of a castle, made of sturdy materials like stone or brick. It contained many rooms: bedrooms, a dining hall, a kitchen, a food storage room, a chapel, and servant's quarters. In contrast, a peasant's house was typically a one-room hut with dirt floors and doors, and their windows were usually holes covered with curtains, not glass. Near the village were the work buildings, such as a flour mill, blacksmith forge, church, and lumber mill. Surrounding the village and manor house were the fields where crops were grown and livestock grazed.

Manors had a three-field rotation system. The most common crops grown were wheat, barley, and rye. The first field was planted in the fall with a specific crop, the second field was planted in the summer with a specific crop, and the third one would be left empty to let the soil rest. All three fields were rotated every year so nutrients could be replenished in the soil. The best parts of the land were farmed for the nobles, and the poorer parts were farmed by the peasants to feed themselves. Sometimes, if harvest times were going extremely well, the peasants were allowed to sell their share of the crops in nearby cities or towns to make extra money for their families.

title: Knights
text:
Knights had a unique role in the feudal system. They weren't royalty, but they weren't peasants, either. They were technically a lower class of noble-born men who had chosen to train for knighthood, a type of military service.

Knights could be given land by the king or by the lord they served. In exchange for the land, they pledged their loyalty and promised to fight for the king or lord when needed. When there were military issues in the kingdom, or wars to be fought, knights were called into service. They were expected to fight at least 40 days out of every year during times of war or conflict.

It took a long time to become a knight. At the age of about seven, boys were chosen and sent away from their homes for training. For seven years, they trained as pages. Pages learned courtly manners, how to ride horses, and how to read, write, fight, and do other tasks. They used wooden weapons and fake wooden horses to ride. Around the age of 14, they began the next stage of their training as a squire.

Squires continued to train with wooden weapons, but they also assisted and served the knight training them by bringing their meals to them, caring for their armor and weapons, and accompanying them onto the battlefield. Squires also began learning the code of chivalry.

The code of chivalry was the honorable behavior expected of a knight. It included things like protecting the weak, respecting women, and always being honest. They had to live with honor, obey the king, and work for the greater good. They had to swear oaths and vows to uphold these values.

At the age of 21, the squire advanced into knighthood. Here, they received instruction from experienced knights in warfare strategies, the best ways to defeat an enemy, how to think critically in battle, and how to attack and conquer castles.

Because of the values they defended and fought for, knights have been memorialized in countless poems, stories, songs, and paintings throughout history.

title: Class Systems
text:
Social classes of the Middle Ages can be divided into three basic levels: the upper class, the middle class, and the lower class. Each level had its own branches and levels according to a person’s power and standing in the society. The upper class, for example, consisted of the king at the very top, with members of the nobility below that. The middle class consisted of knights, merchants, scholars, and professionals, such as doctors, and craftsmen, such as blacksmiths and carpenters. The lower classes were made up of the peasantry, which mainly included farmers. There was also a Roman Catholic hierarchy that existed in medieval society, though most Church clergy would exist in the upper and middle classes, not the lower classes.

Societal roles were rigidly set during the Middle Ages. No one of lower birth could rise to a class higher than the one they were born into. A peasant could never rise to become a knight, and a knight could never rise to become a noble lord.

For centuries, feudalism kept the different social classes separated. Poor serfs of the peasant class were easily distinguished from wealthy lords of the nobility. People married and had families within their own social classes, and it was extremely rare for someone to marry below their station. Practices like this kept the wealth and power within the upper classes and kept the peasant class poor. However, as the economy grew and changed over time, members of the lower nobility and even peasants began to be able to purchase fabrics and items that previously only members of the upper class could afford. People started having a harder time telling the classes apart.

Because of this, rules were created about clothing, shoes, and hats that helped people identify what class a person belonged to. They called these rules sumptuary laws. The laws dictated the color of clothing, types of fur, the height of a hat, shoe length, and even the number of buttons a person of a social class could wear. Members of the peasantry could only wear plain, dull colors, such as grays, browns, and blacks. Only royalty and nobility could wear brighter colors, such as purple.

Despite the rules and laws that worked to keep classes divided, many people pushed back against the system in order to live their lives more freely and achieve success for themselves.

title: Guilds
text:
In medieval times, groups called “guilds” existed. There were typically two types of guilds: merchant guilds and craft guilds. Merchant guilds were made of traders and sellers within a particular region that dealt in a variety of goods. Craft guilds functioned somewhat differently; they were groups of people who specialized in a particular type of work. There might have been a craft guild made up of bakers or blacksmiths who were considered experts at the one thing they did.

Guilds had structures and rankings: apprentices at the bottom, journeymen in the middle, and masters at the top. Apprentices were educated by the masters and received food, clothing, and a place to live; they were expected to work without pay. Once their years of service were completed, they advanced to the next level (journeyman). As a journeyman, one could be paid for the work. The ultimate goal was to become a master, which was a difficult goal to achieve. Typically, guild masters were important men in society. Guilds only admitted new members into the guild after they had proved their skills to the guild masters. Setting the expectation for the work process allowed guilds to establish set wages, working hours, working conditions, and expectations for the quality of the product.

Guilds were important because they drove the economy by providing goods of higher quality at a set price. Guilds developed monopolies for what they were doing, often eliminating local competition. Merchant guilds could require outside traders to pay fees to trade and sell in their regions, or even ban them entirely if they chose to. Typically, the two types of guilds worked together for the common good of all.

title: "Le Morte D'Arthur"
text:
CHAPTER V.

How Arthur was chosen king, and of wonders and marvels of a sword taken out of a stone by the said Arthur.

...there was seen in the churchyard, against the high altar, a great stone four square, like unto a marble stone; and in midst thereof was like an anvil of steel a foot on high, and therein stuck a fair sword naked by the point, and letters there were written in gold about the sword that said thus:—Whoso pulleth out this sword of this stone and anvil, is rightwise king born of all England…

…so it happened that Sir Ector, that had great livelihood about London, rode unto the jousts, and with him rode Sir Kay his son, and young Arthur that was his [foster] brother;...Sir Kay lost his sword, for he had left it at his father’s lodging, and so he prayed young Arthur for to ride for his sword. I will…said Arthur, and rode fast after the sword, and when he came home, [no one was there]. Then was Arthur wroth, and said to himself, I will ride to the churchyard, and take the sword with me that sticketh in the stone, for my brother Sir Kay shall not be without a sword this day. So when he came to the churchyard, Sir Arthur alighted and tied his horse to the stile…And so he handled the sword by the handles, and lightly and fiercely pulled it out of the stone, and took his horse and rode his way until he came to his brother Sir Kay, and delivered him the sword…When Sir Ector beheld the sword, he returned again and came to the church, and there they alighted all three, and went into the church. And anon he made Sir Kay swear upon a book how he came to that sword. Sir, said Sir Kay, by my brother Arthur, for he brought it to me. How gat ye this sword? said Sir Ector to Arthur. Sir, I will tell you. When I came home for my brother’s sword, I found nobody at home to deliver me his sword; and so I thought my brother Sir Kay should not be swordless, and so I came hither eagerly and pulled it out of the stone without any pain…Now, said Sir Ector to Arthur, I understand ye must be king of this land. Wherefore I, said Arthur, and for what cause? Sir, said Ector, for God will have it so; for there should never man have drawn out this sword, but he that shall be rightwise king of this land. Now let me see whether ye can put the sword there as it was, and pull it out again. That is no mastery, said Arthur, and so he put it in the stone; wherewithal Sir Ector assayed to pull out the sword and failed.

title: Week 5 Framing Question
text: Why was the Mediterranean world a crossroads of cultures, religions, and political powers?

title: Monarchy
text:
In the feudal system, some of the lords were actually kings or monarchs. A monarch is a leader who inherits power from a near relative, usually a father. Monarchs become kings or queens when the former monarch dies. The monarch is the head of the government or political system until their own death. Monarchs can also abdicate their throne, or give up their position.

In the Middle Ages, monarchs often ruled by force. If the monarch did not have a large enough military or enough money, then this form of authority did not work. So, many monarchs had to balance their own will with the needs of other powerful lords. Sometimes the result was compromise, but often it was conflict.

In most monarchies, there was a common belief called divine right. Divine right was the concept that the monarch’s right to rule came directly from God. Essentially, both the monarch and their subjects believed that God had chosen the monarch. God chose the ruler by making sure that they were born to the family of the former monarch.

Eventually, absolute monarchies would develop. These are governments where the monarch had most, if not all, of the power and could make laws without any else’s input. The monarch decided who paid taxes and how much. The monarch decided when to wage war and the subjects were required to fight on their behalf. While some of these governments survived through the early modern period, many evolved, and some were even overthrown.

title: Magna Carta
text:
England has been a monarchy for more than 1,000 years. However, it evolved from an absolute monarchy to a parliamentary monarchy in the year 1215 C.E. A parliamentary monarchy is a governmental system that limits the power of the monarch through a hereditary or elected body called a parliament. In this system, a parliament helps make the laws. In 1215 C.E., a group of English nobles believed King John was abusing his powers. King John taxed them extensively, and if they couldn’t pay, he either seized their property or punished them severely. The nobles surrounded London and forced King John to negotiate and sign a document called the Magna Carta. The English nobles who made King John sign the Magna Carta are considered the first members of Parliament.

The Magna Carta stated that everyone in England, including royalty, had to follow English law. This might seem like a small change, but it limited the power of the monarch. Under the Magna Carta, the monarch was subject to the laws of the government, just the same as a peasant. The act of signing the Magna Carta also gave some of the monarch’s power to the members of Parliament. The Magna Carta also stated that every “freeman” had the right to justice and a fair trial. The word “freeman” applied to very few people because most peasants were not free. However, this was the foundation for later reforms, which allowed trial by jury for all people. Later, Parliament would further limit the power of the monarchy.

title: Geography
text: Changes outside of Europe had a significant impact on its history during the Middle Ages. The area encompassing the larger Mediterranean world, including Southwest Asia and Northern Africa, was a crossroads of cultures, economies, and empires. One of the reasons that this area was such an important part of world history was because this was the area where three significant monotheistic religions began: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

title: Monotheistic Religions
text:
Judaism, Christianity, and Islam had their beginnings in the Mediterranean world. All three of them are monotheistic religions, meaning they believe that there is only one God. Judaism originated nearly 4,000 years ago in modern-day Israel and Palestine. The followers of Judaism are called Jews. One of the main figures in Judaism is Abraham. Jews believe that God promised Abraham that he and his people would be given the land of Canaan and that they would prosper. In return, Abraham promised to worship God and obey his commandments. This covenant, or promise, was passed down through Abraham’s family, all the way to modern Jews.

Christianity has Jewish roots. It began with a man named Jesus of Nazareth, who many people believed was the Messiah, prophesied in Jewish holy books. This means they also believe in Abraham and that he was given a promise from God.

Islam began in the Mediterranean world. Muhammad was born in Mecca in 570 C.E. Islam teaches that when Muhammad was around 40 years old, he spent time meditating in a cave and was visited by an angel. The angel, Gabriel, gave him messages or revelations about God and how to worship God. Muhammad recited these messages to his followers, who collected them into a book. The book became the Islamic holy book of faith, the Quran. Followers of Islam are called Muslims. In Islam, like Judaism and Christianity, Abraham is one of the key figures in their religious story. Jews and Muslims are descendants of Abraham. Jews are descended from Abraham’s son Isaac, and Muslims are descended from another of Abraham’s sons, Ishmael. The Quran talks about Abraham being the first prophet. In Islam, Muhammad was the final prophet chosen by God.

Muhammad taught the people to be strict monotheists. He also talked of rewards in heaven for those who followed God. Following God required that Muslims do five certain things, called the pillars of Islam: first, a Muslim must declare their belief in God and that Muhammad is His prophet; second, they must pray five times a day; third, they must give charity; fourth, they must fast during Ramadan; and fifth, they must make a pilgrimage to Mecca at least once during their lifetime. Muhammad gained many followers but angered those who worshiped many gods. However, when Muhammad died in 632 C.E., most people of the Arabian Peninsula practiced Islam and called themselves Muslims.

title: The Spread of Religion
text:
Muhammad wanted his followers to spread the Islamic religion beyond the Arabian Peninsula. So, Muslim armies expanded into other territories, conquering the people and establishing the Islamic religion in these areas. Islam also spread because the people who lived in the Arabian Peninsula were nomadic or worked as caravan traders.

Timeline of the spread of Islam:

570 C.E. Muhammad is born.

610 C.E. Muhammad is visited by the angel Gabriel and receives his first revelations.

622 C.E. Muhammad escapes Mecca and migrates to Yathrib (later known as Medina).

630 C.E. Muhammad returns to Mecca, destroys the idols in the Kaaba, and dedicates it to God.

633 C.E. Muhammad dies. Muslims elect Muhammad’s father-in-law, Abu Bakr, as caliph.

638 C.E. Muslims take over former Byzantine territories: Syria, Palestine, and Lebanon, as well as Sasanian territory in Iraq.

641 C.E. Muslims defeat the Byzantine army in Egypt.

655 C.E. Islam starts spreading through North Africa.

661 C.E. Ali is killed, and the Umayyad dynasty begins its rule.

711 C.E. Muslims conquer Spain and India.

732 C.E. Charles Martel (grandfather of Charlemagne) defeats the Muslims at the Battle of Poitiers, also called the Battle of Tours.

750 C.E. The Abbasids defeat the Umayyads and move the capital of the Caliphate to Baghdad.

756 C.E. Abd al-Rahman I establishes Umayyad rule in the Iberian Peninsula.

909 C.E. The Fatimid dynasty conquers Cairo and the rest of Egypt.

1071 C.E. The Seljuk Turks defeat the Byzantine Emperor at the Battle of Manzikert and take over much of Anatolia.

1095 C.E. Pope Urban II calls for the first crusade.

1099 C.E. The Christian Crusaders take Jerusalem from the Muslims. Control of Jerusalem will change hands again in 1187 (Saladdin takes Jerusalem), 1228-1229 (Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II signs a treaty with al-Kamil for control of Jerusalem), and 1244 (Europeans lose Jerusalem for the final time).

1453 C.E. Ottoman Turks conquer Constantinople, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, and change its name to Istanbul.

title: Crusades
text:
In the 11th century, the Byzantine Empire was fighting enemies from all sides. In 1095, the Byzantine emperor, Alexius I, appealed to Rome for help to fight the empire’s enemies. Pope Urban II used this Byzantine appeal to promote a war that would free Christians in the eastern Mediterranean from Islamic authority. Urban gave a speech to the people of France where he said that Christian pilgrims (people going on a religious trip) traveling to Jerusalem were in danger of Muslim persecution. Urban said this must not be allowed and a war for the liberation of Jerusalem must happen. These military expeditions were called the Crusades.

The European nobility, as well as ordinary citizens, responded to Pope Urban II’s appeal in large numbers. Some were persuaded to fight because of a promise from the pope that their sins would be forgiven. Others sought adventure and wealth. The journey from France to Jerusalem was 3,000 miles and took almost two years. In all, eight major crusader expeditions occurred between 1096 and 1291.

The First Crusade took place from 1096 to 1099 C.E., ending with the crusader capture of Jerusalem. The crusaders killed many of the Muslim and Jewish inhabitants of the city. A second Crusade took place in 1147 and lasted just two years. The kings of France and Germany led forces to take Muslim-held cities north of Jerusalem. Even after leading a force of 50,000, the Christians were defeated.

In 1189, a third Crusade was called. Jerusalem had recently been retaken by Muslims. This time, three powerful western European kings banded together, including King Richard I of England (Richard the Lionheart), King Philip II of France, and Emperor Frederick I of the Holy Roman Empire. Even with this combined strength, the Christian army only managed a truce. Jerusalem remained under Muslim control, but Christians were permitted access to Jerusalem.

The Iberian Peninsula, where today we find Spain and Portugal, had been under Muslim rule since the eighth century. However, Pope Urban II encouraged many crusaders to help Christian kings in the north of Spain to fight against Muslim rulers in the southern parts of the Iberian Peninsula. The crusaders were very successful and occupied most of Iberia. The Kingdoms of Castile, Aragon, Navarre, Leon, and Portugal would be ruled by Christian kings. This would prove to be devastating to the Jewish and Muslim populations who lived there.

After about 200 years, the Crusades ended, but the Christians did not recapture Jerusalem or any of its surrounding territories. The results of the Crusades were captured lands, lost lives, gained riches, and castles built. Europeans also gained new knowledge from the Islamic world. They translated many books from Arabic into Latin. This information led to advances in medicine, geography, math, and science. Trade increased as Europeans brought back paper, the compass, glass mirrors, and silk. They shared food that Europeans had never seen before such as sugar, oranges, lemons, melons, peaches, and apricots. They also brought back spices such as cinnamon, ginger, pepper, and cloves. Some of these new goods and ideas would influence Europe and lead to the Age of Discovery.

title: The Caliphates
text:
Islam spread through conquest, but it also spread because the people who lived in the Arabian Peninsula were nomadic or worked as caravan traders. Arab Muslims brought their ideas, inventions, and foods to those they conquered or met in their travels. Within about 150 years, Arab Muslims spread their religion throughout North Africa, Southwest Asia, and into Europe. They were very successful in conquering the Persian and Byzantine empires because the two empires had long fought one another to a point of weakness. Military conquests ended up including Palestine, Lebanon, and Syria. Eventually, they ended up moving into parts of Iraq, Egypt, and Armenia.

The first caliphate was the Umayyad Caliphate. It took power after the dispute between Sunni and Shia Muslims. When the Umayyads took control, they stopped the practice of electing the caliph, made the caliph a hereditary position, and moved the capital of the Islamic Empire to Damascus. The Umayyad held power until 750 C.E., when they were taken over by the Abbasid Caliphate. However, the Umayyads kept control of the Iberian Peninsula when a member of the Umayyad family, Abd al-Rahman I became the founder of the Umayyad dynasty there. The Abbasids conquered areas to the east, including making more incursions into Byzantine territory. Eventually, the Abbasid Empire would be split into two: the Fatimid Caliphate and the Abbasid Caliphate. Various Muslim Caliphates and groups would take power until the end of World War I throughout Southwest Asia: the Seljuk Turks, the Almohad Caliphate, the Mamluk Sultanate, and the Ottoman Empire.

Timeline:

632-661 C.E. Rashidun Caliphate

661-750 C.E. Umayyad Caliphate

750-1258 C.E. Abbasid Caliphate

909-1171 C.E. Fatimid Caliphate

1121-1269 C.E. Almohad Caliphate

1261-1517 C.E. Mamluk Sultanate

1517-1924 C.E. Ottoman Caliphate

title: The Convivencia
text:
The Quran says that people cannot be forced to convert to Islam. Most Muslim leaders were tolerant of people who belonged to other religions. In the Iberian Peninsula, Jews and Christians were allowed to worship as they chose. This period in Iberia is remembered as a unique era of religious tolerance. It becomes especially significant when compared with the period after it, when Jews and Muslims were forced to convert to Christianity or leave their homes in the Iberian Peninsula.

Although Jews and Christians were allowed to worship as they chose, they did not have all of the rights and freedoms that Muslims did. They were forced to pay a tax that allowed them to practice their religions. Even with this tax, Jews in the Iberian Peninsula were very fortunate in comparison to the Jews throughout the rest of Europe. At best, Jews across Europe were tolerated. They usually lived apart from their Christian neighbors and couldn’t participate in regular society. They were prohibited from holding office and couldn’t marry a Christian. They could not participate in politics, and at worst, they often faced violence. Mobs of Christians attacked Jews in the town of Worms, Germany, and hundreds were killed. Both England and France, and later Spain, expelled Jews from their lands.

However, in the Iberian Peninsula at this time, Jews and Christians were not persecuted for their beliefs. Without fear of persecution, Jews made great strides in the advancement of cultural and scientific developments. This tolerance attracted more Jews to settle in al-Andalus from all over Europe and North Africa. In al-Andalus, the name given to Muslim Spain, Jews rose high in the ranks of society. Some even held high posts in government. Jews showed talents that included medicine, the arts, and sciences. Members of the Jewish faith in al-Andalus created poetry and wrote books on philosophy. One such author, Ibn Gabirol, was thought to be one of the world’s foremost philosophers. His work, Fons Vitae, was later included in Christian teachings. Jews also served as translators of many scientific publications, translating them from Arabic into Latin, French, Spanish, Italian, and Portuguese. A Jewish doctor helped write an Arabic version of a teaching text and reference manual that was used around Europe.

The period of tolerance declined and eventually formally ended in 1492, when Muslims lost control of Granada, the last Muslim Kingdom in Iberia. Through a series of royal decrees and edicts, the rulers in Spain sought to get rid of the Jewish and Islamic faiths. Some 300,000 Jews and Muslims (up to a quarter of the Spanish population) had to convert to Catholicism or flee Spain or were killed in the Spanish Inquisition.

title: Week 1 Framing Question
text: Why did groups of early humans leave Africa and how did they travel across the world?

title: Prehistoric Humans
text:
The story of humanity began a long, long time ago, in prehistoric times. Prehistoric means the time before people started writing. Imagine a family group or small tribe who created their tools out of sticks and stones and made blankets and clothing from animal skins. By day, they hunted animals and gathered plants, seeds, and berries to eat. At night, they huddled around fires to keep warm.

The earliest evidence of modern humans has been found in Africa. Archaeologists are scientists who study the evidence people leave behind. They do this to learn about how people lived a long time ago. They have found human fossils that date to more than 230,000 years old. Some evidence suggests that there may have been people in Africa even earlier.

Africa is the world's second-largest continent. It is located south of Europe. The Atlantic Ocean, the Indian Ocean, the Red Sea, and the Mediterranean all border Africa. This continent is the home of the Nile, the world’s longest river, and the Sahara, the world’s biggest desert.

title: Hunting and Gathering
text:
Early humans were nomads, or people who wandered from place to place to find resources. They relied on hunting animals and gathering plants for food. This is a difficult way to survive. One problem is that plants bloom in different places during different seasons of the year. Animals follow where the plants are thriving, so the humans had to move as well.

The larger the group, the more food they would need to hunt and gather, so these nomadic groups would have been small. People probably lived and traveled in groups of 20 or 30. Some would hunt. Others would gather. Working together gave these small groups a greater chance for survival.

These groups are often called hunter-gatherer societies. Researchers believe that these nomadic people were not completely isolated. Small groups would have interacted with other groups. They might have shared or traded resources. They might have formed friendships with other hunter-gatherers.

In many ways, these early groups were similar to the communities humans create today. They gave people a way to support each other. They could help protect one another from danger. They could raise their children together. They could teach one another new things and learn from each other. Human society today has grown more complex, but we still share those similarities with our early ancestors.

title: Why Migrate?
text:
Today, people move and live all over the world. There are not many places without humans and even fewer places that humans haven’t explored. Despite how it may seem today, it took time for people to spread across the globe.

Early humans traveled over land and water in a process called migration. Migration is the movement of groups of people or animals over time. But why do people migrate? Why not stay in one place?

There are many reasons people move to new places. In early human history, most of the reasons involved the very survival of the people. People need water, food, and clothing. They need resources to build shelters. Early humans relied on plants and animals for survival, so if their resources moved, the people had to move with them.

Another main reason for migration appears to have been the effects of climate change. Many researchers believe that there were shifts in global climate around the time of the first permanent migrations. As areas of Africa were becoming drier, there was not enough food and water for all the people. This could explain why some groups began to leave Africa over 100,000 years ago. As the climate in Africa heated up, cooler regions in Asia and Europe became more appealing. These areas could support more plants, which also attracted more animals. Humans slowly began to migrate into these areas.

Competition and conflict with other tribes or groups may have also forced people to find new lands. The number of people who could live in one area was limited by the resources available there. Once a group got too large, it may have been harder for them to stay together. It is also possible that different groups did not get along. This conflict might cause one group to move away from another.

Many factors motivated people to spread across the continents. Moving animal herds, plant growth, changing weather patterns, and human interaction are some of these factors.

title: Where Did They Go and When?
text:
Movement out of Africa began around 125,000 years ago. Researchers have identified this movement as the first step toward humans migrating throughout the world. The dates when humans arrived in different parts of the world are estimates. Dating historical evidence is complicated. Sometimes researchers form different opinions using the same evidence. Sometimes they find new evidence that tells a different story. Sometimes new tools and technology change our understanding of when things happened.

Groups of humans moved outward from Africa toward areas where they could find food and resources. As the first people left Africa, they arrived in southwest Asia between 100,000 and 70,000 years ago. Sometime later, these groups began to spread through Asia. These migrations did not happen quickly. Instead, they occurred over many generations and thousands of years. The next groups migrated from south Asia to Australia and Europe.

It took longer for early humans to spread as far as North and South America. This might be because of their distance from Africa. Groups probably traveled by both land and water to get to these places. The people who finally arrived in the Americas likely arrived between 15,000 to 20,000 years ago.

title: Land Bridges
text:
Today, there are permanent human settlements on every continent except Antarctica. How did they get there? The world’s continents are separated by oceans or other bodies of water. If early humans migrated out of Africa, how did they get to places like Australia and the Americas? Many researchers believe that hundreds of thousands of years ago, the continents and oceans looked very different. The world was colder then, and more water was trapped in glaciers. Because there was less liquid water in the oceans, the sea levels were lower.

At certain points in history, sea levels could have been low enough that land was exposed between continents. This land that connects two continents is called a land bridge. It acts as a natural bridge between two larger landforms. We have land bridges today, such as the Panama isthmus, which connects North and South America. One theory claims that these early land bridges helped humans migrate between continents.

The most well-known land bridge from this theory is the Bering Land Bridge. It connected Asia and North America where Alaska is today. This land bridge would have been there for thousands of years. For a long time, researchers have believed that humans lived on the land bridge and traveled across it. Now some researchers are questioning that. They say that plants did not grow there until much later. This means the area would not have had animals for food and wood for fuel during the long crossing. Other scientists believe the land bridge was blocked by a huge wall of ice. That means hunter-gatherers may not have used the land bridge to travel to America.

title: Boats
text:
An artifact is any object made by a human. As archaeologists search for evidence of early humans, they find artifacts. The latest findings suggest that some groups traveled over the oceans and seas. This could help explain how they were able to leave the African continent and eventually spread around the world. Traveling by water would have been dangerous for early humans. Researchers are still working to find proof that migrating groups traveled by water.

Archaeologists have found evidence of humans living on certain islands dating back tens of thousands of years. Early stone tools and other objects prove that humans were there. These islands were separated from the mainlands, even when sea levels were lower. This suggests that early humans used boats or rafts to reach those islands. There was no other way for humans to get there other than over water.

One of the problems is that no one has found the remains of these boats. They would have been made of wood, which might not survive long enough in a natural environment to be found today. Another problem is that the coastlines are in a different place now since the Earth is warmer and there is more water in the oceans. It is possible that the evidence that could help solve the mystery is buried beneath the ocean.

title: Weapons, Tools, and Fire
text:
Weapons and Tools

The earliest tools humans had were their hands. However, hands were not enough to protect people against large animals like bears. The earliest people probably threw things like sticks and stones at dangerous animals. It took many years before they found ways to sharpen these sticks and stones and use them as tools. One useful type of stone was flint. Flint was easy to break into flat, sharp pieces. Those pieces could be used as arrowheads, spear tips, scrapers, and knives.

A New Discovery

Some of history’s most important discoveries happened by accident. This may have been the case with fire. The first fires humans experienced may have been from lightning strikes or forest fires. Eventually, hunter-gatherers learned how to use fire and start it on their own. Life changed quite a bit for anyone who learned how to start a fire. Fire gave them protection, since they probably used it to frighten away dangerous animals. Humans also learned to use fire for light, warmth, and cooking. There is some debate as to when people began to use fire. Some experts think humans first used fire over 300,000 years ago.

Connections

In colder areas, fires provided much-needed warmth. People would have gathered around them, which encouraged them to interact with one another. The light from fire allowed hunter-gatherers to stay active longer into the night after the sun went down, giving them more opportunities to connect with others in their communities.

title: Asking Questions
text:
The story of how early humans lived and populated the Earth is fascinating. You may have noticed while reading this week that some ideas are well-understood and agreed-upon, but other ideas are debated. Some details are still only theories, and many facts are yet to be discovered. So how do we learn the truth about prehistoric times? There is no time machine we can use to go back and gather facts. Instead, we must learn about how people lived in the past through clues left in the present.

One problem with researching the past is that archaeologists are like detectives working from an incomplete set of clues. Some clues are hidden underground or underwater. Other clues have disintegrated over time. Just bits and pieces of people’s lives have survived for us to learn from. Despite the challenge of studying the past, archaeologists continue in their work. They ask questions, study artifacts, and develop and test their theories.

In the same way, you can ask questions about people and events in the past. You can ask what people did. You can ask why an event happened. By asking questions, you can develop your own claims. A claim is a statement you make about what you believe. Your next step is to research and look for evidence to support your claim. You can look at photos, artifacts, and other primary sources. A good investigator also checks to see if someone has already answered their questions. You can find secondary sources in media centers and books. You can do research online. The more evidence you gather, the stronger your claims will be.

Because we don't have all the answers yet, you have the opportunity to look for answers and develop your own theories of how our early ancestors lived and how they migrated across the world.

title: Week 2 Framing Question
text: How does having or not having resources affect a society's development?

title: The Agricultural Revolution
text:
For many years, early humans lived a nomadic lifestyle. They hunted wild animals. They picked whatever plants, nuts, or berries they could find. They used very simple tools made from stone and bone. They lived in temporary shelters. When the food ran out in one area, they moved on. Eventually, humans stopped moving and chose instead to settle and grow food. The transition from hunting and gathering to farming is called the Agricultural Revolution or the Neolithic Revolution.

People began to build more permanent shelters. They lived beside lakes or rivers where they could fish and plant seeds and roots in the moist soil. Gradually they learned how to clear large areas of land and run water to the plants so that they would grow more easily. They tended the trees and gathered fruit. They also learned how to tame and raise animals and use them for farming or for food.

Building a settlement was very different from being a hunter-gatherer. It took time and work to build homes, clear the land, and grow crops. This new lifestyle allowed groups to get bigger. As populations grew, more food and resources were available. This meant people could share what they had. Small settlements got bigger and gradually became villages and towns.

Major changes happened in these early agricultural communities. Humans developed new tools to make farming easier. Groups organized themselves and decided who would do what type of work. They created rules for how to work and trade with others.

Today, food and goods are still traded between cities, states, and countries. In modern societies, people usually have one type of work, instead of many different jobs. We have governments to organize and protect people. The societies we live in now are directly related to the changes of the Agricultural Revolution.

title: Why Call It a Revolution?
text: A revolution often refers to a fight or war to change a country or government, like the American Revolution. In the 1930s, an archaeologist named Gordon Childe chose the term “revolution” to show the great impact that the change from hunting to agriculture had on the human population. It’s important to remember that the Agricultural Revolution wasn’t a single point in history. It happened in different regions of the world at different times. It happened with small, gradual changes. For a while, even after people understood how to farm, groups continued to hunt and gather for part of the year and grow crops during the other parts. Today, there are still nomadic societies in the world.

title: Weather, Climate, and Environment
text:
Today we have scientists and advanced technology to help us predict the weather. We have shelters to keep us safe and dry in a storm. What did early humans do? How did the weather affect them? Early humans depended on their environment. Weather was very important to them. Indigenous communities in the Americas tracked weather patterns. Ancient Egyptians carved descriptions of storms and flooding. Many early civilizations believed the weather was controlled by the gods.

Weather refers to things like sunshine, rain, heat, cold, and wind. Climate is the average weather conditions or weather patterns of a place over an extended period of time. While the weather can change in just a few hours, climate can take hundreds or even thousands of years to change.

Many researchers believe migration and the change from nomadic life to farming were due to changes in climate. Today, climate is still one of the biggest factors that influences where people live and what activities they do.

The term “climate change” today often refers to the long-term change in climate caused by human activities and their use of resources. As early farmers improved their methods, they changed their environment. They cleared larger areas of land. They used natural resources to make tools, furniture, and buildings. Some scholars say that the Agricultural Revolution, an event that occurred many thousands of years ago, had lasting effects. They say the shift in land use from forests to farmlands and permanent settlements could be seen as the very beginning of climate change caused by humans.

Perhaps early humans were more aware of their impact on their surroundings and environment than we are today. Did they try to live in harmony with nature, or did they change their landscape in negative ways? Is there anything we can learn about climate and the environment today by looking to the past?

title: Geography’s Role in History
text:
Geography

In every part of the world and every time period in history, geography has played an important role in the lives and actions of people. Geography is the study of places on Earth and the relationships between people and places. Physical geography is about the features that occur naturally on the Earth. It focuses on things such as landforms, forests, oceans, lakes, plants, and animal life. Human geography is the study of how people interact with the land and use resources. It focuses on how humans change the places they live in. For example, building homes, clearing fields to plant crops, and making roads is all part of human geography. Studying the geography of ancient civilizations gives us clues to their history, economics, culture, and government.

As nomadic tribes began to settle and build more permanent homes, they had to consider location. The physical geography influenced which plants grew and which animals lived in an area. It determined the resources they would have access to and even what kind of advantages they’d have if another group attacked them.

Resources

Resources are anything that comes from the Earth that humans can use to survive or make life better. Getting resources has been an important part of life since prehistoric times. People do whatever is necessary to get the resources they need to survive. Many civilizations started near rivers where the people had water for survival and rich soil for growing food. Rivers, and other natural features such as mountains, could also provide protection during an invasion. People made tools from rocks, bones, and plants. They built monuments from stone.

Early settlements adapted to use the resources around them. In areas where there were fewer trees, people built homes made of grasses or mud. In areas where the water was far away, people dug channels to carry the water to the city. Some ancient civilizations began in areas that did not have mountains, so they focused on building walls instead.

Studying geography helps us to understand the past and answer important questions about the world and its people. Geography influenced the way ancient societies lived—where they settled, and what kind of houses they built. It even influenced the food they ate, the clothing they wore, the art and music they created, and the games they played.

title: Tools of the Farming Trade
text:
Have you ever worked in a garden? Imagine that you didn’t have any tools to work with. What would you use to plant all of those seeds? Your situation would be very similar to what ancient farmers dealt with. They may have gotten the idea to farm from watching seeds sprout after the seeds fell on fertile ground. When the time came to plant a lot of seeds at once, they knew they needed some tools.

Farmers sharpened sticks, stones, and bones and used them to dig. This made farming easier. When the crops grew, they probably used those same tools during the harvest. The next generations of farmers made those tools better. They may have attached stones to long sticks to make a shovel or a hoe. Others used grasses and sticks to make baskets to carry water. Traders may have come, offering clay pots or tools made out of iron. Farmers also started using animals to help prepare fields and to carry heavy loads.

As time passed, farming and agriculture slowly became more advanced. Today, scientists have learned how to engineer plant species. Computer-run irrigation systems control how crops get water. Tractors and other farming equipment have heaters and air conditioning. Many farms even use wind and sunlight as ways to generate power.

title: Food Surpluses
text:
Scarcity is when there is more demand for something than there is a supply. It is not having enough of something people want or need. When food or water is scarce, it is hard for people to live. Surplus is when the supply of a good or service is more than the demand. There is more of something than people need or want.

Better farming tools and techniques during the Agricultural Revolution helped people grow more food with less work. The increase in food production led to food surpluses. People had more food than they needed to keep their communities fed. To protect their surpluses, they created places and systems to store their extra crops. Having food storage made it even more important for people to stay in one place. They couldn’t just move at a moment’s notice as hunter-gatherers did. But with all of the food they were producing now, they didn’t need to.

title: What Is a Civilization?
text:
When early humans learned to farm and grow their own food, their lives changed completely. As more groups settled in the same area, they helped each other farm. This meant some of them had time to focus on tasks other than growing food.

People began to make tools and other useful items. As more people joined the community, they organized themselves, shared ways of living, and created systems to protect everyone. Some people became artisans. This meant they used special skills to make things with their hands. Others became leaders and created rules for everyone to follow. These ancient communities grew and prospered. Over time, small villages became cities. Then, with the right conditions, they grew into large civilizations.

title: What Do Civilizations Have in Common?
text:
What are the right conditions that allow a community to develop into a large civilization? Civilizations are complicated. They have many layers and factors that influence their successes and failures. Scholars and historians do not all agree on an exact definition of “civilization.” Most scholars do agree there are characteristics that civilizations share. Some of these characteristics are a stable food supply, specialization, government, infrastructure, technology, social structure, and a system of communication.

Culture is also an important characteristic. Most ancient civilizations were shaped by shared beliefs, common activities, and forms of art. In different places civilizations have grown, changed over time, and eventually disappeared. Even though they are gone, what ancient civilizations learned, built, and accomplished has become an important part of our history.

title: What Is an Empire?
text:
When can something be classified as an empire? An empire is a civilization that expands its borders and conquers other societies and large amounts of land. The term “empire” comes from the Latin word “imperium.” This word refers to power and military authority. The main point of imperial growth is to conquer new territories and gain control over people. This control can be military, economic, or cultural. It can also be a combination of these factors. For a civilization to become an empire, all the lands it conquers must be ruled by one central government. The ruler of the government is often called an emperor.

Ancient Rome grew from a city-state to become an empire. The rulers of Rome conquered lands and people around the Mediterranean. They expanded the borders of Rome as far away as Britain.

Ancient Greece was not an empire. Some city-states in ancient Greece established colonies around the Mediterranean but each one had its own government. There was never one central ruler who was in charge of all the Greek territories.

Ancient Egypt was not an empire. It had one government, with the Pharaoh as a central ruler, but the ancient Egyptians did not conquer large amounts of territory. They benefited from their life along the Nile River. They had no need to expand their borders.

title: Cause and Effect
text:
People, places, ideas, cultures, and technology change over time. To understand patterns of change in history, historians often ask the following questions:

What events or changes happened?

What caused those changes?

What were the results?

How did people benefit or suffer from the changes?

Historians try to understand what started a change or led to an event in history. This is called a cause. They also want to understand the outcome or what happened because of an event or a change. This is called an effect. In a text, the words “because,” “since,” “so,” and “then” often signal a cause and effect relationship. You have already read about many cause and effect relationships. Here’s one example. Because Africa’s climate got warmer, humans and animals then migrated to cooler places. Can you think of more?

As you read about the characteristics of ancient civilizations, look for causes and effects that help explain how and why things changed. Remember, history is not always a clear timeline of events that lead from one thing to the next. Sometimes, looking at the things that stay the same throughout history is as important as looking at how things change.

title: Stable Food Supply
text:
Civilizations need a stable food supply. When there is enough food, a community can thrive. The people of Mesopotamia planted grains, such as wheat and barley, that could feed many people. They built irrigation systems to get water to their crops. They also invented the plow. All this made planting and harvesting easier. Farmers also domesticated pigs, goats, geese, and cattle. Domesticate means to tame animals and raise them for eggs, dairy, and meat.

As tools improved, farmers were able to consistently produce enough food for all the people in the valley. As a result of this stable supply of food, there was an increase in population. Larger and more complex societies began to form. People began to organize themselves and work together to find new ways to improve their settlements.

title: Specialization and Trade
text:
Because communities had plenty of food, people had time to do tasks outside of farming. People made baskets for gathering grains and tools for farming. They made clothing, crafts, and works of art. Soon people began to focus on doing one specific task that they were good at. This is called specialization. One person in town might make tools. Then others in the town could use those tools to weave cloth. The cloth was then used to make clothing.

An example of job specialization from the Indus Valley was making pottery. The potter dug the clay from the nearby rivers and then shaped it into containers for storing food and water. Clay pots were much better than stone pots because they were thin and lightweight. Before long, potters began to make extra containers so they could trade or sell them. Specialization is an important characteristic of a civilization. It added more variety to communities. It allowed them to be more efficient, so they could grow even larger.

title: The Barter Economy
text:
Imagine living in a society with no money system. If you needed a new pair of sandals, a pitcher for water, or someone to help you dig a channel, what would you do? In early communities, there was no money. People began to use extra goods, like food or handmade items, and barter for other things they needed.

Bartering is when people trade goods or services instead of using money. For example, a farmer in Ancient China could give rice to a carpenter in exchange for a carved table. When bartering, both people needed to agree that the trade was fair and that the goods or services had an equal value.

The trade and bartering system began with small exchanges between social groups. Eventually it expanded into complex trade routes. The Silk Road was a trade route where people could get materials from different parts of the world. Merchants would travel in caravans or on ships laden with goods. They bartered for items that could then be taken back to their lands and used there.

title: Measurement, Conversion, and Data
text:
Measurement Systems

Objects have different properties, such as size, weight, and volume. Properties can usually be measured. Measurement is the size, length, or amount of something. For example, the volume of a milk carton measures one cup. This one-cup measurement comes from the United States’ customary system. Did you know that there are other ways to measure objects? The same milk carton measures eight fluid ounces and 236 milliliters in other systems.

The U.S. customary system is based on Great Britain’s imperial system. The imperial system was built around how big or small a country's leader was. However, different leaders were different sizes. Each country ended up with a unique measurement for one foot. This made it difficult to share data.

To fix this, French scientists set up the metric system. The metric system uses decimals and multiples of 10. The system is also based on a measure called the meter.

It is common to use the metric system, especially in science. Under the metric system, the base units of measurement are the meter, liter, and gram.

Converting Metric Units

The metric system was created so that everyone could use the same measurements. Before the metric system, converting between units was hard. Each conversion required a different number. The metric system uses only one number to convert between units: 10.

This is made possible through the use of prefixes. A prefix can go in front of any unit. It indicates how small or large the unit becomes. For example, the unit for volume is the liter. Kilo- is a prefix that means 1,000. So, one kiloliter is 1,000 liters.

Another example: the meter is the unit for length. Centi- is the prefix that means one hundredth (0.01). So, one centimeter is one hundredth of one meter. Another way to think about it is to divide one meter into 100 parts. A centimeter is one of those parts. Just like with kilo-, centi- can be used with any unit. Remember: to convert metric units, all you need to do is multiply or divide by 10. If you move to a bigger unit, you divide by 10. If you move to a smaller unit, you multiply by 10. Look at the conversion table to see how you can move from larger to smaller units by 10.

Conversion Practice

Imagine that your principal has decided to have all of the carpets in the school cleaned. The carpet cleaners need to remove all of the desks from your classroom. Using a metric ruler, measure the width of your desk and the door frame in centimeters to see if the desks can be removed from the classroom. Record these measurements in the following table. After measuring, convert your measurements into meters and millimeters. Record the conversions in the following table.

Recording Data

Once data has been collected, it has to be recorded. Many scientists then graph their findings to show others what the test results were. Graphing also allows scientists to see what patterns there are in the information, and if there are relationships. There are multiple types of graphs, and some lend themselves to information better than others. A pie chart is a graph that is used only when the evidence adds up to a perfect 100, making a whole circle, or pie.

title: Length, Area, and Line Plots
text:
Length

Have you ever wondered how far your favorite restaurant is from your house? This distance is called length. To find the length of an object, you have to measure how long it is. You could measure the length of your classroom or the length of a pencil. These lengths, however, would likely be measured in different units.

The base unit for measuring length in the metric system is the meter. The millimeter, centimeter, and kilometer are three commonly used units based off of the meter. These units are often abbreviated because abbreviating them is easier than writing them out every time. Here are the abbreviations for the four main metric units of length:

millimeter = mm

centimeter = cm

meter = m

kilometer = km

To measure length in the metric system, you use a metric ruler or a meterstick. These tools are labeled with two different units: centimeters and millimeters (cm and mm). Centimeters are marked with numbers and longer lines, just like inches on standard rulers. The smaller lines in between mark millimeters. There are 100 centimeters in a meter. There are 1,000 millimeters in a meter. To convert meters to centimeters, multiply the number of meters by 100.

Once the lengths of two sides of an object are calculated, you then can calculate the area of that object. The area of an object is found by multiplying length by width.

Area Practice: Find the area of Alana’s dog pen. The dog pen is 2.2 m by 2.2 m. What is its area?

Line Plots

One type of graph is a line plot. A line plot shows the frequency of data along a number line. Line plots are best used when comparing fewer than 25 numbers.

Line Plot Practice: Some of the students in Claire’s class are making friendship bracelets to sell. Claire brought all the random pieces of string she had from home. When she and the other students went to sort the string pieces, they noticed that the pieces had a variety of lengths.

Use the following data to complete the line plot.

String Lengths: 6½, 6½, 7, 5, 7, 5½, 7, 5, 6, 6½, 6½, 6½, 5, 5½, 7

title: Cities and Government
text:
As specialization and trading became more common, more people started to gather in one place to make it easier. This was the beginning of cities. Cities were an important characteristic of civilizations. As cities grew, people built larger structures. They made buildings to store the extra grain from the farms. They made marketplaces for people to sell and buy. People also developed forms of government to provide services and to create systems and rules. Some of the first governments were created to help resolve trade disagreements or conflicts over property.

Often the city rulers believed that their authority and power came from the gods. Ancient Greeks believed each city had a god to watch over it and protect the citizens and the government. The people showed their thanks by building temples to honor the gods.

title: Infrastructure and Technology
text:
Infrastructure refers to the basic structures that people create in an area so they can live and work and meet their needs. Aqueducts are an example of infrastructure in Ancient Rome. An aqueduct is a series of pipes, canals, and bridges that transports fresh water into the city.

In ancient times one of the most important structures was a road. Making roads was not an easy task. It often meant building bridges across rivers, cutting through forests, or digging tunnels through mountains. But roads made it much easier for people to travel and transport goods. Another benefit of roads was innovation and technology. In ancient terms, the word technology refers to the thoughtful designing or making of techniques or tools for people to use. As people thought of new ways to build roads, they created new technology to make the work easier.

title: Weight and Bar Graphs
text:
Weight

Weight is how heavy an object is. It is measured by using a scale. In the metric system, the base unit for weight is the gram. One gram weighs about as much as two standard paper clips. Like the meter, the gram can be converted into smaller and larger measurements. The kilogram, for example, equals 1,000 grams. Grams and kilograms are the most commonly used units for measuring weight. Just like units of length, units of weight are often abbreviated:

gram = g

kilogram = kg

To convert kilograms into grams, multiply the number of kilograms by 1,000.

Weight on the Moon

Find the weight of each object on the moon by multiplying the Earth weight by 0.165.

Bar Graphs

Another type of graph is a bar graph. A bar graph contains two lines that make a 90-degree angle. Along the two lines are labels for what is being studied. The horizontal line shows what is being measured, and the vertical line shows the amount.

Data on a bar graph is represented by horizontal or vertical bars of different sizes. Use the weight measurements from the chart to fill in the bar graph.

title: Social Structure
text:
Another characteristic of a civilization is the division of people into classes. Classes can mean groups of people divided by the kind of work they did. Classes can also mean groups of people divided by how much money they made.

Details of each level vary from civilization to civilization. Although, they do follow similar patterns. Those in the highest classes were usually the rulers and leaders. They made decisions that affected the entire society. Middle classes included people with specialized skills, artisans who made goods, or merchants who traded the goods. The lower classes included people who worked common jobs. These were often weavers, sailors, bricklayers, farmers, or shepherds. People were treated differently at each level. Those at the top had more opportunities and power. In some societies, the lowest classes of people were treated unfairly.

Some scholars who study ancient Egypt believe that it lasted so long because everyone understood their place and did what was needed to keep the balance. During most of Egypt's history, this system worked and the civilization prospered. When those at the top neglected the members of the lower class, the system began to break down.

title: Volume and Pictographs
text:
Volume

Have you ever drunk soda from a two-liter bottle? Do you know what a liter is? The liter is the base unit for volume in the metric system. Volume is how much space something takes up. For example, soda takes up two liters of space in a two-liter bottle. The milliliter is another unit for measuring volume in the metric system. These two units are abbreviated as:

milliliter = mL

liter = L

Compute and record the volume of different objects based on the length, width, and height of the objects.

Volume = Length (L) x Width (W) x Height (H)

Cubic Units

Cubic units are also used to measure volume. One cubic unit has a length, width, and height that measure one unit each.

Pictographs

Pictographs use pictures or symbols to record data on a graph. The same picture or symbol is used for the entire graph or a part of the graph. The picture represents a quantity that is defined in a key found on the graph.

title: Communication and Writing
text:
When people in an ancient society spoke the same or similar language, it made communication and leadership easier. Yet spoken language had limitations. It could only be used between people who were next to each other and once the words were said, they had to be remembered or they were gone.

As societies became more complex and cities grew larger, people needed a way to record events and remember trade deals. This is how the first forms of writing came to exist. Different ways of writing were developed in different parts of the world. Some of the first systems used drawings to represent objects or phrases. Other writing systems used symbols to represent sounds or letters.

The development of writing systems caused many changes. Written language was used for spreading news and information. It was used to count populations and track food storage. Rules were written down so that people could remember them.

Much of what we know about ancient civilizations today comes from different forms of written communication. Writing has given us a better picture of the people that came before us.
