title: Recognize Emotions in Others
text: Everyone shows their emotions in different ways. You can be observant and notice people’s emotions. What can you pay attention to? You can listen to their words. You can look at their surroundings. You can watch someone’s body language and facial expressions. The way people sit or stand can show how they feel. Sometimes the best way to know how someone else is feeling is to ask. You can be a good friend and family member by noticing other people’s feelings.

title: Self-Regulate Your Emotions
text: When your body gets too hot, it sweats to cool down. When your body gets too cold, it shivers to warm up. Your body self-regulates to keep your temperature from getting too hot or too cold. You can self-regulate, or manage, your emotions, which helps you stay in control of them. Pay attention to how you feel. Pause and ask yourself: “How do I feel? Why do I feel that way?” If you don’t like the way you feel, you can self-regulate your emotions and start to feel better.

title: How to Self-Regulate
text: You experience positive and negative emotions. Happiness and excitement are examples of positive emotions. Sadness and anger are examples of negative emotions. Negative emotions can be overwhelming sometimes. Have you ever had to do something hard? How did you get through it? Did you ask for help? When you can’t figure out a math problem, you ask your teacher. When you can’t reach something, you ask someone taller to help. You can ask for help when your emotions are hard for you to handle. You can talk to a teacher, a parent, or guardian you trust. Talking, drawing, and exercising are all good ways to cope with your emotions.

title: British Victories, American Defeats
text:
In 1777, the Continental Army had setbacks in their fight for independence from Great Britain. The British wanted to divide the New England colonies. This would prevent supplies and reinforcements from reaching the Continental Army. The British troops were under the command of General John Burgoyne. They moved from Canada into New York to stop the American military. They took control of Fort Ticonderoga on July 5, 1777. This fort was near Lake Champlain, in northern New York. This was a blow for the Continental Army because of the fort’s strategic location.

At the same time, British General William Howe and his soldiers moved to stop the colonial government in Philadelphia. On September 11, 1777, Howe’s army defeated Washington and his troops at the Battle of Brandywine Creek. Washington was forced to retreat. Howe moved toward Philadelphia and occupied the city. The Continental Congress fled to York, Pennsylvania. The Continental Army needed a decisive victory to encourage the colonists to continue fighting for their independence.

In 1777, The British army was the best fighting force in the world. The Continental Army was not trained and had few supplies. However, the colonists were fighting for their independence. The training and supplies did not matter to them. Early in the war, the British commanders had many victories. The victories allowed the British to gain control of roads and transportation routes in the northern colonies. It was hoped that this would prevent the Continental Army from getting supplies and support from the towns.

The Continental Congress was meeting in Philadelphia. The British army captured the city. This forced the Congress and the Continental Army to leave the city. Congress moved to York, Pennsylvania. The Continental Army moved to Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. It was in Valley Forge that the Continental Army would succeed or fail.

title: Hard Times at Valley Forge
text:
Following the Continental victories, Washington and his troops traveled to Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. This is where they set up their winter camp. The British troops remained in Philadelphia for the winter. In Philadelphia, the British commanders quartered their soldiers in the homes of the colonists. At Valley Forge, Washington’s men lived in crudely built log huts. The soldiers were exposed to the harsh winter weather. Washington had the soldiers stay in these huts instead of taking over the homes of their fellow Patriots.

Washington’s troops were exhausted from long marches and battles with the British by the time they made camp. Most had no shoes, and their clothes were old and torn. There was not enough food for the 12,000 soldiers. The harsh conditions led to sickness and disease like typhoid, influenza, or smallpox. It is estimated that about 2,000 soldiers didn’t make it through the winter.

Despite the difficult conditions, Washington did everything he could to inspire his troops. He convinced Congress to send needed supplies to the camp. He worked tirelessly to train his soldiers. He persuaded foreign soldiers to help him train his army. Two of these men were the experienced Prussian officer Baron von Steuben and French officer Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de La Fayette. By the spring of 1778, Washington’s forces were reenergized. They were prepared to face the British once again.

title: The Tide of War Changes
text:
The luck of colonial forces stationed in the southern colonies changed under the command of General Nathanael Greene. In 1780, Patriot forces defeated a Loyalist army at Kings Mountain, South Carolina. Greene saw a chance to beat the British after this victory. He sent half of his army west of Kings Mountain. Those soldiers won the Battle of Cowpens in January 1781.

Cornwallis and Greene's soldiers fought at Guilford Courthouse, North Carolina, in March 1781. The British won the battle. They suffered heavy casualties. Greene retreated to South Carolina to resupply. Cornwallis marched into Virginia on May 20, 1781. He fortified his position. Cornwallis was unaware that the Continental Army was moving toward Virginia in the hopes of ending the war.

title: Mindfulness
text: Practicing mindfulness means being in tune with your thoughts and feelings in the moment. You can be mindful by paying attention to the things around you. Yesterday is in the past. Tomorrow is in the future. Thinking too much about the past or the future is the opposite of mindfulness. When you focus on today, you are being mindful.

title: Steps to Practicing Mindfulness
text:
If you feel distracted or stressed, try practicing mindfulness. Here are a few steps you can take:

Stop what you are doing.

Close your eyes.

Ask yourself: “How do I feel right now?”

Look around and notice the sounds, space, objects, and people that surround you.

Great job! You are on your way to being mindful!

title: Why Mindfulness Matters
text: When you practice mindfulness, you will see benefits. A benefit is something positive that happens as a result of practicing something. Practicing mindfulness helps your mental and emotional well-being. It can even help your academic and social well-being. Mindfulness can help you make good choices. When you are aware of what is going on around you, you can make wise choices. Mindfulness can help your social well-being. When you are focused on the people you are with, you can notice and accept their differences.

title: Let’s Practice
text:
There are so many ways to practice mindfulness. Anything that helps you stay focused on the present moment is a great tool. Let’s practice a couple ways you can practice mindfulness. First, let’s do some stretching:

Stand up.

Close your eyes.

Reach your hands to the sky.

Take three deep breaths and notice how your body feels.

How do you feel?

Reach down and touch the floor.

Notice how you feel. Are you feeling any emotions?

Stretching and breathing can be a great way to practice mindfulness.

title: What Is Well-Being?
text:
Well-being is the feeling of being healthy, safe, comfortable, and happy. Well-being is learning about the five areas of our development. These include social, emotional, academic, physical, and mental areas. You need to learn how to stay healthy in these five developmental areas.

Your well-being can feel unbalanced if you neglect taking care of one area of your development. Learning about keeping your mind and body healthy helps you thrive. Thriving is when you learn new skills. Thriving is living and feeling your best.

Learning about well-being is like building your muscles. Building muscles takes time and work. First, you need to learn skills. Next, you need to practice what you learn. Then, you need to continue learning. The more you practice well-being skills, the easier they are to do.

title: Physical Well-Being
text: Your body has physical needs to stay healthy and safe. Your body needs food, water, oxygen, and sleep. Your body has systems, and each body part has a function. You can learn to make choices about your physical health to help you feel your best. Getting enough physical activity is a great way to stay healthy and strong.

title: Mental Well-Being
text:
Your brain is connected to your whole body by nerves. Nerves are like roads that send messages from your toes and fingertips all the way to the brain. Nerves also send messages from your brain to your body.

Different parts of your brain do different things. One part of your brain is in charge of learning, another part is in charge of emotions, and another is in charge of keeping you alive and safe.

Protect your brain; wear a helmet. Make good choices about physical activity and nutrition. Attempt to learn new things every day. The more you practice a new skill, the easier it is for your brain to remember how to do it.

title: Academic Well-Being
text:
Academic well-being includes your ability to show you have learned something. Each year, you learn new skills. You build on what you learned the year before. First, you learn what numbers are. Next, you learn how to add and subtract numbers. Then, you learn how to multiply numbers.

Learning new skills might seem hard. You have brain cells called neurons. When you learn new skills, your brain has to build new neurons. The new neurons form new connections in your brain. These are called neural pathways. These pathways help you remember a new skill. When you practice or share the skills you have learned, your brain builds more and more connections. The skill you learned becomes easier because your brain can process, or think, how to do it faster.

Each of us has different strengths and weaknesses. Each person's needs are different. Some tasks come very easily to one person but are very difficult for another person. You can always build new neural pathways. The more you practice, the stronger those pathways become.

title: Social Well-Being
text: Social well-being is about learning how to interact with others. You can learn how to build and maintain healthy relationships. You choose how you treat friends and family. Social well-being is learning about connection and belonging. You can build positive connections by being kind and respectful of others.

title: Emotional Well-Being
text: Emotional well-being is learning to identify how you feel. Your brain has a control center for your emotions. This control center helps you label your emotions. When you label your emotions, you can communicate to others how you are feeling. Then, you can learn how to self-regulate your emotions. Self-regulation means learning to manage your emotions. Your brain helps you learn about positive behaviors. It also helps you avoid negative behaviors.

title: Cause and Effect
text: Spending time practicing these five parts of well-being will help you thrive. Practicing self-reflection and problem-solving will help you be more self-aware. Your health and well-being are connected. When you take care of your physical well-being, your body feels strong. When you feel strong, you can think faster. When you can think faster, you can make better decisions and build better relationships. As you learn skills to help you take care of your well-being in each area, you will become more self-aware, build self-confidence, and be willing to show respect and empathy for your peers. You will also be more willing to try new things and learn new skills.

title: The Siege of Yorktown
text:
In May 1781, Cornwallis led 7,000 British troops out of North Carolina. They retreated to Yorktown, Virginia. Yorktown was on the coast. It could be attacked by French ships. The British set up their defenses and waited for reinforcements. French ships moved toward Yorktown through the Chesapeake Bay. The ships blocked British supply lines.

George Washington sent 4,500 troops to Yorktown. They were led by Marquis de Lafayette. They would prevent the British army from leaving. Washington sent other troops to join the French fleet in the Chesapeake Bay. Washington arrived in Yorktown on September 28, 1781. He besieged the city for 11 days. Unable to defend the city, Cornwallis surrendered on Oct. 19, 1781. His surrender brought the American Revolution to an end. It became a significant event in the fight for American independence from Great Britain.

title: The Treaty of Paris, 1783
text:
After the Siege of Yorktown, the British wanted to end the war with the American colonists. The war was expensive. The British Parliament didn’t want to pay for the fight to continue. In 1782, representatives from each country met in Paris, France. They discussed terms to officially end the war. In 1783, the representatives signed the Treaty of Paris. Each side compromised in order to end the conflict. With the end of the war, the 13 Colonies could take their first steps as a new, independent nation.

Conditions of the Treaty of Paris, 1783

United States

The United States of America became an independent nation.

The U.S. gained fishing rights off the British-Canadian coast.

The Mississippi River was opened to both U.S. and British citizens.

American debt owed to British creditors would be resolved.

Colonists who remained loyal to the king during the war would be treated fairly. Property that had been taken from them during the war would be returned.

Great Britain

Britain recognized its former colonies as an independent nation.

Britain gave up its territory east of the Mississippi River to the United States.

The Mississippi River was opened to both U.S. and British citizens.

The British remained in control of their colonies in Canada.

Britain returned the territory of Florida to Spain.

title: Human-Environment Interaction
text:
Human-environment interaction explores the relationship between people and the environment. It includes how people depend on, modify, and adapt to the environment. People need food, shelter, and clothing. They depend on natural resources from the environment to meet these basic needs. People sometimes modify their environment to meet these needs. For example, people build homes, schools, roads, and railroads to meet their needs for shelter, education, and transportation. They set up irrigation canals and farming systems to meet agricultural needs. In some places, people build solar plants or drill for oil under the Earth’s surface to meet their needs for energy.

People adapt to their environment when they respond to the climate and natural resources available in different areas. Sometimes, the environment changes the way people live or where they live. The environment can affect the kinds of clothes people wear, the jobs they have, the buildings they build, and the foods they eat.

When humans settle in an area, they begin to interact with the environment in many different ways. They use the land around them to help fulfill their needs. When colonists first came to America, they settled in areas with access to fresh water, soil that would be good for farming, and other natural resources that would meet their needs. When people make changes to the environment, they modify it. This can include clearing trees for farming or building. People can also modify their environments by planting and growing crops, raising livestock, or fishing.

In many ways, human interaction with the environment can be negative. People use the natural resources in their environment, such as trees for lumber, to meet their needs. However, if this is overdone, natural resources can be depleted, or used up. Sometimes, conservation efforts are needed to prevent natural resources from being depleted. In doing this, we can preserve natural resources and continue to use them in the future.

Agriculture and mining can also pose a threat to the environment. These things can change the landscape in ways that make it no longer usable. For example, poor farming practices and overgrazing in the Plains region turned the land into what was called the “Dust Bowl” in the 1930s. Because of this, new conservation and farming practices were implemented in the U.S. to restore farming soil and prevent a dust bowl from ever happening again.

Pollution is another negative impact people can have on the environment. Trash can be very harmful to the environment. People have to be careful to balance their needs with available resources found in their environment.

Humans sometimes move a non-native species into a habitat where it doesn‛t belong. These are known as invasive species. Invasive species compete with native species for resources. When this happens, the native species don‛t have enough food or space to live, and they can become endangered. This can have a negative impact on the natural environment.

People can also have a positive impact on their environment. Some ways to do this are cleaning up litter, recycling, planting trees, carpooling, and using organic pesticides for gardening and farming. When we use natural resources wisely, we positively impact the environment.

title: Adapting to the Environment
text:
People adapt to their environment to meet their basic needs in order to survive. This means people change how they live based on their environment. Everything from plants, animals, weather, and climate can change the way people live. The clothes that people wear, the foods they eat, and the houses they live in are often determined by the environment where they live. The jobs that people do often relate to their environment, too. Forestry, mining, farming, and fishing are examples of jobs that were created based on a place’s natural resources.

People have adapted to the environment of Ohio for thousands of years to meet their needs. Native People tribes adapted to the environment of Ohio in many ways. They created warm clothing from animal skins to wear during the winter months. They used the materials available from their environment to build homes. They used available resources to construct canoes. The Ottawa tribe used the bark of the birch tree to construct canoes. These canoes were used to transport goods and were exchanged as trade items.

European immigrants adapted to the unique environments they encountered in the United States. They built homes based on the needs created by the environment. Homes in the wooded and forested areas of the Northeast and Midwest were often constructed from logs, which were lumbered from the large number of available trees. Homes were insulated to keep out the cold. Settlers in the south often built homes with large windows. These windows allowed breezes to move through the home and cool it down.

title: Depending on the Environment
text:
Humans have basic needs. People need food, clothing, and a place to live to survive. The physical environment, including landforms, climate, and weather, influences where people settle, the jobs they work, and their lifestyles. People depend on the environment to meet their needs. To depend means to rely on something. The natural features and resources available in an area provide materials, food, and clothing for people living there.

People usually choose to live close to resources that help them meet their basic needs. One example is the need for water. Throughout history, towns and cities have been established near bodies of water to meet basic human needs. These places provided a source of clean water, and waterways were used for transportation and trade. This made these locations desirable places to live. Resources found in the environment make our lives easier.

One city that grew as a result of its proximity to water is Cleveland. The city of Cleveland was first surveyed in 1796 before Ohio was a state. At first, the town grew slowly along the banks of Lake Erie and the Cuyahoga River. When the Erie Canal was completed in 1825, it connected Cleveland to other cities along the lakes and along the east coast of the United States. The natural resources available around Cleveland made it a convenient place for railroads and ships to load and unload goods.

The city of Boston, Massachusetts, was founded in 1630 by Puritan immigrants. Boston is located on the Shawmut Peninsula, where the tribe of the same name lived. This area was ideal for settlement. It provided the Puritans with access to fresh water and navigable waterways. These were vital for trade. The natural harbor near the city was deep enough for ships to enter. It could also support many docks and wharves for years to come.

Like Cleveland and Boston, San Francisco was settled in its current location because of its proximity to water and a natural harbor. In 1769, Spanish explorers quickly realized that the natural resources of the area and the protected deepwater harbor would be very valuable to the Spanish Empire. Settlers arrived in the area in June 1776. They constructed a presidio, or fort, and the Mission San Francisco de Asís. San Francisco Bay, where the Yelamu tribe lived, provided the early settlers with many ways to meet their needs. The bay allowed the early settlers to travel easily to other Spanish settlements and conduct trade.

title: Modifying the Environment
text:
People modify their environment to meet their needs. This means they change the place where they live in order to meet their wants and needs. For example, people build dams to provide water for growing food. People also build homes and schools. They set up irrigation and farming systems. They build roads and bridges to travel from one area to another. They cut down forests for lumber and to make farmland for growing crops. All of these interactions modify the environment in some way.

Many Native People tribes that lived in desert areas created irrigation systems to water their crops. The Hohokam people, who lived in present-day Arizona and Mexico for over 1,000 years, constructed irrigation canals. The irrigation canals carried water from the Salt and Gila Rivers to water nearly 110,000 acres of land. Archeologists have uncovered some irrigation canals that measure 15 feet deep and 45 feet wide.

Ohio has a long history of mining activity, which has modified the environment in many ways. Coal mining began in Southeast Ohio in 1800. By 1870, there were coal mines in over 30 counties in the southern part of the state. Miners dug deep caverns in the Appalachian Plateau to reach large deposits of coal. During the late 1800s, miners began to use blasting techniques and explosives to extract coal from the mines. Efforts to mine coal greatly modified the environment of southeastern Ohio.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text:
When humans settle in an area, they begin to interact with the environment in many different ways. They use the land around them to help meet their needs. When people make changes to the environment, they modify it. These changes can have positive and negative impacts.

Positive Impacts on the Environment

People can have a positive impact on their environment. Some ways to do this are by picking up trash, creating programs to protect endangered species, planting new trees and vegetation, and growing vegetable gardens at home. Other things that can have a positive impact on the environment are conserving water and electricity, using reusable water bottles, and buying locally grown food.

It is a good idea to use natural resources more responsibly. One example is implementing recycling programs in communities. About 70 percent of all the garbage we throw away can be recycled. The best way to keep our landfills and garbage dumps from taking over the environment is to recycle as many items as possible. People can work together to protect natural resources and have a positive impact on the environment.

Negative Impacts on the Environment

In many ways, people’s interactions with the environment can be negative. We change the environment when we cut down too many trees, plow fields for farming, or dig trenches to redirect water. Mining can change the environment by causing pollution and slag buildup.

People also produce a lot of trash. Trash often ends up in landfills and garbage dumps. As certain materials break down, they can produce harmful chemicals that seep into the soil and groundwater.

In order to avoid having a negative impact on the environment, people have to be careful with available resources and how they use them.

title: Essential Question
text: How do people adapt to, depend on, and modify their environment to meet their needs?

title: Geography
text:
Geography is the study of Earth and its people and how things change over time. A geographer is a scientist who studies the Earth, its people, and how they live and work in their environment. Geographers ask questions and make claims that are supported by evidence. There are different themes of geography that serve as a framework to help us understand the world around us. These themes help us ask and answer important questions about the world and its people. They give us a way to study the past. The themes of geography are location, place, human-environment interaction, movement, and region.

No matter the time period, geography has played a role in the actions of people and the events of the world. In ancient times, location was critical as people first began to settle and build permanent homes. Wars were fought over places and resources. As civilizations grew, humans changed their environment to meet their needs. Religions and cultures spread through the movement of trade and exploration. Political boundaries were organized based on regions. The success and failure of settlements, civilizations, and empires can be tied to the themes of geography.

“The study of geography is about more than just memorizing places on a map. It's about understanding the complexity of our world, appreciating the diversity of cultures that exist across continents. And in the end, it's about using all that knowledge to help bridge divides and bring people together.” — Barack Obama, 2012

title: Tools of Geography
text:
As we study the themes of geography, we can organize our thinking about the world using different tools. These include maps, globes, graphs, diagrams, photographs, and other geographical representations. These tools can help us find and explain connections between ideas, events, and developments in world history.

A globe is a round model of Earth. Globes show us where water, land, and countries are located. Globes are useful when you need to see Earth in a more accurate, spherical shape. Maps are drawings of places around the world. They can show large areas, like continents, or small areas, like cities. All maps have some distortion or inaccuracy because you cannot perfectly represent a three-dimensional Earth on a two-dimensional map.

There are many different kinds of maps. You can use them to explore the world. Maps can show the physical characteristics of a place, like landforms or bodies of water. They can help us see the borders of regions, countries, or states. Maps can show elevation, which means height above sea level. They can show the climate, or the weather over a long period of time. A person who creates a map is called a cartographer. A cartographer decides what to include on a map.

title: Week 5 Framing Question
text: How does geography impact the actions of people?

title: Location
text:
This theme of geography answers the question “Where is it?” Location refers to the position of something on the surface of the Earth. Maps and globes are the best way to show location. Two terms we use to talk about locations on maps are “relative” and “absolute.”

The relative location tells us where a place is relative to, or compared to, something else. We use words such as “near,” “by,” “above,” and “below.” For example, ancient Egypt was located near the Nile River, in the northern part of Africa below the Mediterranean Sea. The absolute location of a place is more precise. We often use a coordinate grid, or horizontal and vertical lines on a map, to say exactly where something is. For example, the absolute location of the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is 29°58′45″N, 31°08′03″E. Let’s learn what that means.

Lines of latitude lines are horizontal. They run from east to west. The line at 0° latitude is called the Equator. The Equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres. The Northern Hemisphere includes all of the land and oceans that are north of the Equator. The Southern Hemisphere includes everything to the south.

Lines of longitude are vertical. They run from north to south. The line at 0° longitude is called the Prime Meridian. It divides the Earth into two more hemispheres. The Eastern Hemisphere includes all of the land and oceans that are east of the Prime Meridian, and the Western Hemisphere includes everything to the west. Egypt is located in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres of the Earth.

title: Place
text:
This theme of geography answers the questions “What is this place like?” and “What makes it unique?” All places have features that make them different from other places. Two terms we use to describe places are “physical characteristics” and “human characteristics.” Every place has physical characteristics that are part of its natural environment. These might include physical features and landforms like forests, mountains, oceans, and rivers. Climate, soils, biomes, natural vegetation, and animal life are also physical characteristics.

Places can also have human characteristics. These are features that come from human ideas and actions. They include things that humans have created or defined, such as structures and systems, boundaries and borders, cities, states, and countries. They also include cultural characteristics, like ways of life, belief systems, languages, arts, and traditions.

Maps are a great way to study physical characteristics. This map shows the features of Ancient Mesopotamia as well as the political features, like borders of regions and names of cities.

Photos are a great way to study human characteristics. This photo of a palace wall in Nimrud, Mesopotamia, shows us the art style and the written language of the civilization. It also gives us a look at the clothing, hairstyles, transportation, and practices of the culture.

title: Human-Environment Interaction
text:
This theme of geography answers the question “How do people change their environment?” and “How does the environment affect the way people live?” There are three concepts in human-environment interactions: depending on, adapting to, and changing the environment we live in.

Humans depend on the natural environment for their basic needs: food, shelter, and clothing. Early humans had to adapt their way of life to the natural resources found in their environment. The people who lived near oceans learned to fish. The people who lived near rich soil learned to farm. Choices about what to wear and what food to eat also reflected the environment they lived in. When early humans settled in an area, they changed the environment around them to meet their needs. Ancient Romans cut down trees to build homes. They grew crops to provide food. They dug tunnels and channels to carry drinking water and carved roads throughout the land to move goods and supplies.

Diagrams are a useful tool for learning about human-environment interaction. Diagrams are images or drawings that help us visualize information. They can show parts, relationships, steps in a process, or how things work. This diagram shows how Roman roads were made, layer by layer.

title: Movement
text:
This theme of geography answers the question “How do people, things, and ideas get from place to place?” Ancient civilizations and the relationships between them were shaped by the constant movement of people, materials, and ideas.

Throughout history, people have moved to new places for various reasons. They may choose to move to find resources, better opportunities, or to expand their territory. Sometimes people are forced to move to a new place. They may move because of wars, natural disasters, or religious persecution.

Materials are moved from place to place in many ways. It can be as simple as a farmer carrying a basket of grain to a market or as complex as a merchant sailing the seas to trade goods. Ideas move with people as they go from place to place. As people traveled and civilizations expanded, human interactions became more frequent, and ideas began to spread from one culture to another.

Hundreds of years ago, there were a series of travel routes called the Silk Road. They wound across the continent of Asia and through the Mediterranean Sea and the Indian Ocean. People used the routes to trade gold, ivory, spices, animals, medicines, and foods. This trade also helped to spread culture, technology, and ideas.

Graphs and charts are tools that can help us track movement and growth over time. The size of Ancient China and the constant travel made it difficult to govern. The rulers began to count and chart the number of people living in China as far back as 2,500 B.C.E. The most well-known census was done during the Han Dynasty in 2 C.E. It recorded over 59 million people.

title: Region
text:
This theme of geography helps to answer the question “What do places or areas have in common?“ Dividing large areas of the world into regions makes it easier for us to study them. A region has some kind of similarity or characteristic that unifies it. These characteristics could be physical features or human characteristics or both. A region could be located within specific physical boundaries, like a state or a country. A region can also exist without physical boundaries. A geographer who studies language might divide the world into language regions. Another geographer might look at features like climate, plant life, or soil and divide areas into natural regions accordingly.

In ancient Greece, there were natural barriers like mountains, and the sea, and political boundaries like tribal divisions. This influenced the formation of three different regions.

We also organize regions by hemispheres and continents. The Earth is divided into continents, or large bodies of land. Many geographers divide the world into seven continents. They are Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia, Africa, South America, and Europe. The continents of Europe and Asia are different from the others. They are not separated by water, but they are considered separate continents because there are differences in the look of the people and their customs and culture. However, some geographers feel Europe and Asia should be one continent, and they call it Eurasia. They count only six continents. Others count five continents, with North America and South America combined as a single continent called the Americas.

title: Map Tools
text:
Maps can tell us a lot about the world. A map’s title helps us know the purpose and the kind of information we will find on the map. Most maps use symbols to show important places or landforms. Cities are often labeled with a dot. Roads and travel routes are marked using lines that show the path. Different colors are used to show boundaries, areas, or regions. Cartographers include these markings in the map legend. A map legend is a list of all the symbols or colors that appear on the map that explains what each represents.

A very important part of every map is the compass rose. A compass rose is a symbol that often looks like a flower or star, and it shows directions on a map. A compass rose shows the cardinal directions. The cardinal directions are north, south, east, and west. It may also show the intermediate directions. Intermediate directions fall between each cardinal direction. They are northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest.

A map scale is often part of the map legend. It helps us figure out distances. A map scale shows the relationship between real-life distances and the distances shown on the map.

title: Types of Maps
text:
There are many different kinds of maps. You can use them to explore the world. Some maps display the characteristics of physical environments. Other maps show where people live and how they interact with their environment.

A physical map shows the natural features of an area. Natural features include landforms, mountains, valleys, lakes, and streams.

A political map shows the borders of regions, countries, states, and cities. Some political maps represent even smaller divisions, such as counties, townships, and neighborhoods.

Some maps show the climate of a region. Climate is the study of weather over time. A climate map shows whether a place is usually warm or cold and wet or dry.

A population map is used to show the overall distribution of the population within a particular area or region. Most maps use colors or symbols, such as circles or stars, to represent the varying populations. Population maps are useful for the government to plan how to distribute resources.

Cultural maps identify community cultures and resources. These maps are used to help plan and implement the distribution of resources. Cultural maps also connect cultural groups based on their beliefs and values. Cultural maps illustrate the relationships and interactions between people, places, and the environment.

Historical maps are created to represent historical events in the time period they occurred.

Political maps are organized by where people live. They show political features, including cities, states, and countries. Many people in the world live in cities. Cities are organized into states. States come together to form a country. Countries are grouped together to organize continents. Political maps show the borders of cities, states, and countries.

A political map can also show how some borders have been created using the features near them. For example, oceans, rivers, and mountain ranges can also create borders of countries or states. These borders help us by showing where one area stops and a new one begins.

title: Latitude and Longitude
text:
Lines on a Map

Mapmakers have given Earth a system of lines running both north and south and east and west. The lines that run across the globe from east to west are called parallels of latitude because they run parallel to each other.

Look at the world map and notice how the lines are labeled. Each line of latitude and longitude has a number assigned to it that shows where it is located. We measure latitude and longitude with numbers and the word "degrees." The middle line of latitude is the Equator. It divides Earth in half. The Equator is at zero degrees latitude. Lines above the Equator are labeled N for north latitude. Lines below the Equator are labeled S for south latitude. The larger the number, the farther north or south the line is from the Equator. The zero degree line for longitude is called the Prime Meridian. Lines to the west of this line are labeled W for west longitude. Lines to the east of the Prime Meridian are labeled E for east longitude. These lines are numbered by degrees, the same way the lines of latitude are numbered. The lines cross at different points and help us find things on maps and globes. Lines on maps of large areas often do not show every degree; the numbers skip by fives or tens to form the grid.

To find a location on the map, all you need to know are the latitude and longitude numbers. Latitude numbers are always listed first, followed by longitude. You can use a compass rose to make sure that you are looking in the correct direction when finding north, south, east and west. Using latitude and longitude numbers, you can find any place in the world.

Sometimes an alphanumeric grid is used to describe the locations on a map. An alphanumeric grid uses grid lines for latitude and longitude, but there are numbers and letters along the margins of the map.

Go to N, 28. Koalas live on this continent. Which two hemispheres is it in?

Go to J, 18. Famous pyramids are on this continent in the Eastern Hemisphere. Which continent is it?

Coordinates

Modern navigation systems make use of lines of latitude and longitude to pinpoint a particular location on the Earth’s surface. It is given as geographical coordinates.

A coordinate can be simply written as 10°N, 70°W. However, most locations on the Earth do not sit exactly on the lines of latitude or longitude. They are found within the square created by the crossing lines. To accurately pinpoint locations, the lines of latitude and longitude are divided into degrees, minutes, and seconds. This is called the DMS format. An example of this format is: 41°24’12.2″N, 2°10’26.5″E. The first half is the line of latitude and is read as 41 degrees, 24 minutes, 12.2 seconds north. The line of longitude is read as 2 degrees, 10 minutes, 26.5 seconds east.

Another format is decimal degrees (DD.) The space between each line of latitude or longitude, representing 1°, is divided and expressed as decimals. An example of this format is: 41.40338, 2.17403. The first coordinate (latitude) is read as north because it is positive. If the number is negative, it represents south of the Equator. The second coordinate (longitude) is read as east because it is positive. If the number is negative, it represents west of the Prime Meridian.

If you went to the above coordinates, you would see this elaborate church in Spain, designed by the famous architect Antoni Gaudí.

Reading Coordinates in a Digital Space

Today's online digital maps often provide coordinates in both DMS and DD formats.

The location of the George Washington Cable House in New Orleans would be 29° 55′ 34.87″ N, 90° 5′ 13.8″ W in the DMS format and 29.926353, -90.087167 in the DD format.

title: Prime Meridian and Time Zones
text:
Cartographers draw lines on a map from the North Pole to the South Pole. This helps us be more specific in our mapping. One of these lines, the Prime Meridian, divides the world in half vertically. These halves are called the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere.

Absolute location uses latitude and longitude lines to pinpoint where something is located. These lines are measured in degrees. Each degree is divided into 60 minutes, and each minute has 60 seconds. The Earth is divided into 24 different time zones. The reason for this division is because the Earth rotates on its axis once a day. A time zone is one of the ways that the world is divided and is based on what time it is in a given location. The starting point for these time zones is the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, also called Greenwich Mean Time. Theoretically, every 15 degrees east or west of Greenwich means one hour more or less. In practice, however, time zones do not go through the middle of countries. Larger countries have multiple time zones. For convenience, time zone boundaries often follow political boundaries instead of longitude lines.

The International Date Line is another imaginary line on Earth's surface. It defines the boundary between one day and the next. The International Date Line is located halfway around the world from the Prime Meridian.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text:
When humans settle in an area, they begin to interact with the environment in many different ways. They use the land around them to help fulfill their needs. When people make changes to the environment, they modify it. These changes can have positive and negative impacts.

Positive Impacts on the Environment

People can have a positive impact on their environment. Some ways to do this are cleaning up litter, protecting endangered species, planting trees, and growing your own plants and vegetables. Other ways to have a positive impact on the environment are conserving water and electricity, using reusable water bottles, and buying locally grown food. When we use natural resources wisely, we positively impact the environment.

Many people have encouraged others to use natural resources more responsibly. One example is implementing recycling programs in communities. About 70 percent of all the garbage we throw away could be recycled. The best way to keep our landfills and garbage dumps from taking over the environment is to recycle as many items as possible. People can work together to protect natural resources and have a positive impact on the environment.

Negative Impacts on the Environment

In many ways, people’s interactions with the environment can be negative. We change the environment when we cut down trees, remove stone, and use natural resources to create building materials. Agriculture and mining can also pose a threat to the environment. These can change the landscape in ways that it can no longer be used.

Many industries create pollution that seeps into the air, water, and soil. People also produce a lot of trash. Trash often ends up in landfills and garbage dumps. Trash can also produce harmful chemicals that can affect the soil, water, and air. People have to be careful to balance their needs with available resources found in their environment. This helps avoid negative impacts to the environment.

title: Depending On, Modifying, and Adapting to the Environment
text:
Depending on the Environment

Humans have basic needs. People need food, clothing, and a place to live. The physical environment influences where people settle, their jobs, and their lifestyle. The physical environment includes landforms, climate, and weather. People depend on the environment to meet their needs. The natural features and resources available in an area provide materials, food, and clothing for people living there.

People usually choose to live close to resources that help them meet their basic needs. One example is the need for water. Throughout history, towns and cities have been established near bodies of water to meet basic human needs. These places provided a source of clean water and waterways used for transportation and trade. This made these locations desirable places to live. Resources found in the environment make our lives easier.

Adapting to the Environment

People adapt to their environment to meet their basic needs and to survive. This means people change how they live based on their environment. Everything from plants and animals to the weather can change the way people live. People must adapt to the climate. They must change the ways they live based on the climate where they live. People around the world wear different clothes, eat different foods, and live in different houses. People do all of this based on their environment. The jobs they do relate to their environment, too. Forestry, mining, and drilling are examples of jobs that were created based on a place's natural resources.

Modifying the Environment

People modify their environment to meet their needs. This means they change the place where they live. For example, people build dams to provide water for growing food. People also build homes and schools. They set up irrigation and farming systems. They build roads and bridges to travel from one area to another. They cut down forests for lumber and to make farmland for growing crops. All of these interactions modify the environment in some way.

title: Ancient Transportation
text:
There were many reasons for people to move in every ancient culture. Walking was the first means of getting from one place to another. However, the environment sometimes made it difficult for people to walk to some places. As a result, communities developed new technologies and ways to overcome the natural obstacles to movement.

Animals

Some people had to cross large, sandy deserts. They used camels. Horses and elephants were also used to carry goods and people. Dog sleds were used in cold climates in North America. They used dogs that can survive the climate.

The Wheel

In ancient times, the people who lived near the Tigris and Euphrates rivers were known as Sumerians. About 3000 B.C.E., they changed transportation forever: they invented the wheel. They attached wheels to carts that could be pulled by people or animals. Wheeled carts made it possible to move larger loads than the early farmers could pack on an animal's back. These new tools changed the lives of everyone, from farmers and traders to generals and emperors.

The Sumerians also built chariots with two or four wheels in which people could ride. Of course, wheels worked best on smooth paths of dirt or stone. They didn't turn very well in the sand. Chariots became an important tool for war and helped empires expand their power.

Roads

Around the fourth century B.C.E., the Romans took a giant step forward in improving the use of chariots and carts by building a huge network of roads. The Roman Empire was so big that it took a long time for the Romans to get from one place to another. So they built roads that connected all the parts of the empire. Historians estimate that the Romans built over 55,000 miles of roads over the next several centuries. Every time the Roman army conquered a new region, they used supplies from local areas to build roads that connected the new land to the capital city of Rome. Some of these roads are still used today by bikers, sightseers, and even cars!

Water Travel

Once people learned how to build rafts for fishing, they began to build other types of boats. They made wooden oars to paddle the boats through the water. For many years, Europeans and Asians used boats as an important way to move goods and people along major rivers. Sails were invented by the Sumerians. Around 4000 B.C.E., Egyptians also used a sailcloth system to pull basic log boats along rivers. Around 2000 B.C.E., the Polynesians used boats with sails to travel over the South Pacific. Sails made water travel faster and easier. Over time, people all over the world began using sails.

title: How Do I Feel?
text:
We all need to pay attention to how we feel. We call these feelings emotions. Everyone experiences different emotions at different times. Think of something that makes you feel happy. Think of something that makes you feel comfortable. What makes you feel happy and comfortable might not for someone else. Observing your own emotions helps you to understand yourself better. When we know how we are feeling, it helps us understand our own emotions. There are things you can do to help you manage your emotions positively.

Sometimes we feel more than one emotion at a time. When this happens, you can ask, "How do I feel?" and you can wonder why you feel that way. Listening to your body and the way you feel can help you identify your emotions.

title: My Emotional Vocabulary
text: There are many words we can use to tell others how we are feeling. These words describe our emotions. Emotions can be lumped into five categories. They are "joy," "sadness," "anger," "fear," and "disgust." We use these vocabulary words to describe our feelings. We can use our emotional vocabulary to help others understand us. Emotional vocabulary also helps us understand others. Using the right words to label our feelings helps others know exactly how we feel.

The physical properties of temperature can make a big difference in the kitchen! When ice cream is fresh, it has a different texture from when it has been sitting on the counter for an hour. When the temperature changes, so does the texture. Cake batter is another example of how a food can have a different texture when its temperature changes. After heating the cake batter in an oven, it turns into a cake! If the correct temperature is not used when cooking foods, people could get sick. For example, chicken needs to have an internal temperature of 165° Fahrenheit to be safe to eat. Temperature is a physical property of food. It really matters when you are cooking, baking, and eating!

title: Communicating My Emotions
text:
Talking to other people can help you identify how you feel. Your thoughts can be affected by the people in your life. Your peers and family can impact your thoughts and emotions. Even media can influence you. It can help people understand how you feel when you talk about your emotions. Communicate how you feel honestly. When you understand your own emotions, you can be kind. You can also be more understanding of others.

You can communicate how you are feeling with your body language. You can communicate with your facial expressions. Learn and use emotional vocabulary words to help you. Using words to tell others how you feel is helpful.

title: Introduction to the Ancient Near East
text:
Thousands of years ago, people began living in organized groups for the first time in written history. A group known as the Sumerians settled between two rivers in the Ancient Near East. The area is now called Mesopotamia, which means “land between two rivers.” This land is often referred to as a “cradle of civilization.” The term “cradle” means it is where one of the first civilizations was born.

The Sumerians were not the only group to develop in Mesopotamia, but their culture influenced many future civilizations. They invented soap, the sailboat, and the wheel. They created the first schools and the first aquarium. Sumerians came up with new tools and techniques for farming. They developed one of the first known forms of writing. At one point, their city of Uruk had between 40,000 and 80,000 people. It may have been the largest city in the world at the time.

The Sumerians prospered in the Near East for thousands of years. Eventually, people called the Amorites and Babylonians took control of the region. Over time, the Sumerians and all that they had accomplished were forgotten. For many years, no one saw any evidence of Mesopotamia. Then, in the 1840s, archaeologists working in that area became interested in some huge mounds of sand. As they dug deeper and deeper into the mounds, a forgotten world began to emerge. They discovered many written records, artifacts, and structures. Scientists have been able to use this evidence to piece together many details about this ancient civilization.

title: Observing Emotions in Others
text:
Recognizing how other people feel is important. You need to be aware of what others around you are feeling. When you know how others are feeling, you can show them empathy. Empathy is the ability to understand and share somebody else's feelings. Showing empathy helps you create strong friendships.

To understand how people are feeling, we follow some steps:

First, when we talk to others, we watch their faces and their body language. We listen to the tone of their voice.

Next, we infer, or make a guess, about their feelings based on what we see and hear.

Then, we ask questions. If you see someone smiling, you can infer that they are feeling happy. You could ask them, “Are you having a good day?”

title: Self-Regulating My Emotions
text:
Understanding our feelings comes with responsibility. We have a choice in how we show our emotions. The words we use should tell people how we feel but not hurt them. Remember that emotions are there to help us.

Review the following example scenarios. Think of an appropriate way to show your feelings in each scenario.

You are angry because you didn't make the team.

You are happy that your basketball team won a game.

You are sad that your family is moving to a new house.

title: Overcoming Emotional Obstacles
text:
It is important to let yourself feel your emotions. However, the way we act can sometimes be hurtful to the people around us. It is helpful to breathe and think before you act on your emotions. This helps you respond appropriately to your emotions.

The media you view can impact your thinking and behavior. The people in your life can too. If you view media that shows people being unkind to one another, you may think that is appropriate. Look for examples in your life of people who treat others with kindness. When you see others being respectful, you have a good example to follow.

You can train yourself to overcome emotional obstacles (difficulties). You can train yourself to "push pause" and think before you act. If you see someone being unkind, you can “push pause” and take a breath. Next, think about how to respond. Instead of yelling the first words you think of, "push pause" to help you choose your response.

title: What Is Well-Being?
text:
Well-being is learning about how to be healthy, happy, safe, and about being your best self. You are constantly growing, changing, and learning new skills. Your body and brain are developing. Sometimes, these changes can feel difficult to manage. Well-being includes five areas of development: physical, mental, academic, emotional, and social. Well-being is about learning how to manage these areas and how they affect your health.

Keeping your well-being balanced helps you to thrive. Thriving is when a person lives and feels their best. Your well-being can feel unbalanced if you neglect, or ignore, one area of your development. You can learn to thrive by setting a routine. A wellness routine is a set of healthy habits you repeat often. By wearing a helmet, keeping yourself clean, wearing sun protection, and improving your mindset, you can take care of your physical well-being. You can learn and practice new skills to enhance your health and wellness often.

title: Physical Well-Being
text:
Your body needs physical things to keep you healthy and safe. Your body needs food, water, oxygen, and sleep. We also need exercise and ways to keep our bodies moving.

Most people’s bodies know how to breathe on their own; it is automatic. Oxygen keeps your body running well and keeps you alive.

You can protect your body by getting enough sleep and eating healthy foods. You can protect your body by wearing helmets, life jackets, and sunscreen when needed. You can stay healthy by making wise choices to keep your body clean and brush your teeth morning and night.

Taking care of your physical well-being is taking care of your body. You can make healthy choices that will keep your well-being balanced.

title: Mental Well-Being
text:
Your mental well-being is all about how you think and learn. Your brain is like a supercomputer, and it is connected to your whole body by nerves. Nerves are like roads that send messages all through your body to the brain and back. Nerves also send messages from your brain to your body.

Every part of your brain has a different job. One part of your brain helps you learn new things. Another part of your brain helps you recognize and regulate your emotions. A different part of your brain helps you make smart and safe choices to keep you alive.

The more you learn and practice, the more your brain can do. The first time you learn to do something, it might be hard. However, the more you practice, the easier it is for your brain to remember how to do something.

title: Academic Well-Being
text:
Academic well-being is your ability to learn and show that you remember new things. In each grade, you learn new skills. You build on what you have learned the year before. When you learn new skills, your brain has to build new cells. These cells are called neurons. These new cells form connections in your brain. The connections help your brain remember what you’ve learned. As you retain, or remember, things you have learned, your brain makes room for more learning. This improves your academic well-being. The more you learn and practice, the stronger your brain becomes.

Each person has individual challenges, strengths, and weaknesses. This means that each person approaches academic well-being a little bit differently. In addition, we all have different likes and dislikes. We have all grown up with different resources and tools to develop our individual knowledge. Some tasks may come easily to one person but could be difficult for another person. The brain is amazing and can always learn how to adapt and overcome challenges if a person is willing to learn, practice new skills, and work hard.

title: Emotional Well-Being
text:
Emotional well-being involves learning about how you feel. It means being able to label, observe, and communicate your emotions, thoughts, and feelings. When you know how you feel, you can talk about it. This helps you learn how to manage your emotions.

You can learn to adapt or eliminate any harmful ways you manage your emotions. Doing this is called self-regulating your emotions. Learning to self-regulate your emotions is learning how to pay attention to how you feel and make choices about how you respond. Doing this helps you communicate your feelings to others in an appropriate way.

Your emotional well-being can be influenced by others. It is important to learn how to observe other people's emotions or feelings. You can talk about the impact they have on you. You can learn how to process criticism and navigate challenging situations.

title: Social Well-Being
text:
Social well-being is about learning how to interact with other people. It is important to feel belonging, attachment, and connection. It is also important to be able to resolve conflict and manage your responses to different social situations.

We can learn how to build and maintain healthy relationships. We do this with friends and family. Social well-being helps us learn about our own sense of belonging. It also helps us connect with others. Learning how to have positive connections takes work. Social well-being is learning to be kind and respectful to others.

Because of technology, there are many different ways to interact with others. You can interact digitally, through apps and online platforms, and you can interact face to face or over the phone. Interacting digitally is very different from interacting face to face, but it is still a part of your social well-being. When you interact with others, you learn how to treat others with kindness, while standing up for yourself and making good choices. You will likely encounter conflict, which requires you to collaborate, or work with your friends, to find solutions to the problems. Learning how to manage all of these skills will help you develop your social well-being.

title: Cause and Effect
text:
It is important for everyone to develop skills in well-being. A person who spends time developing these areas of well-being will be able to thrive. Taking care of your well-being means learning how to self-reflect and solve problems. It means being able to communicate and work with others.

The five areas of well-being work together to help you thrive. When you take care of one area of well-being, your capacity to learn, grow, and develop in other areas also increases. Taking care of your body's physical needs impacts your ability to thrive academically. You can think in the classroom and learn new things because your body has enough fuel and feels safe. Can you think of other ways your areas of well-being impact one another?
