text: Steven, Claire, Miguel, and Alana have a big dodgeball game coming up against the fifth graders. They need to figure out which material to build their fort with that will withstand the dodgeballs.

title: Ibn Battuta
text:
Who was Ibn Battuta?

Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier, Morocco, in 1304. He was a Muslim traveler and scholar. He traveled the world, going from his homeland to Arabia, East Africa, and India. What is even more significant about Ibn Battuta’s travels was that he wrote about his experiences. His writings are translated from Arabic into English.

This is a portion of Ibn Battuta’s writing that pertains to East Africa:

The sultan at the time of my visit was Abu'l-Muzaffar Hasan, who was noted for his gifts and generosity. He used to devote the fifth part of the booty made on his expeditions to pious and charitable purposes, as is prescribed in the Koran, and I have seen him give the clothes off his back to a mendicant who asked him for them. When this liberal and virtuous sultan died, he was succeeded by his brother Dawud, who was at the opposite pole from him in this respect. Whenever a petitioner came to him, he would say, "He who gave is dead, and left nothing behind him to be given." Visitors would stay at his court for months on end, and finally he would make them some small gift, so that at last people gave up going to his gate.

title: Connections: Cultures in the United States
text:
The cultures that exist in the United States today took a long time to evolve. They are still growing and changing. They developed through a long process of cultural diffusion.

Indigenous communities had their own unique cultures when settlers arrived in the Americas. As the Europeans from various countries came over, they too had their own unique cultures. As the cultures blended, they began to evolve into the cultures we are familiar with today.

The ancient civilizations of North, Central, and South America were advanced and well-established when the Europeans arrived. Most Europeans did not value the cultures of the Indigenous communities. They wanted to assimilate the people into their own culture. Assimilation is when people force other people to become like them. Some Europeans didn't want to force the Indigenous people to be like them. They wanted to move them out so they could have the land as their own and live without the influence of others. These attitudes eventually led to the American colonist culture dominating the Indigenous American cultures.

Often we don’t realize it, but the cultures of Indigenous people greatly influenced the cultures we know today. Indigenous ideas and values can be found in the art, music, and everyday lives of people everywhere. Many of the foods grown in the Americas were cultivated by ancient civilizations and have remained a part of the American diet. Even some holidays and festivals can be traced back to Indigenous traditions.

Since the arrival of the first settlers, millions more have migrated to the United States. They too have influenced our culture. People from Africa, Asia, and various parts of Europe have come, and all have contributed to the present culture. To this day, Scandinavian culture can be found in the names of towns all over the midwestern United States. There are French-speaking communities in New England, Maine, and Louisiana. In the Southwestern states, we find examples of beautiful Spanish architecture. People take pride in their cultures. The United States has many cultures that exist together and blend together. This is one thing that makes our country such a beautiful, rich place to live.

It is important to value the many things that make up the cultures of our countries. It is important to value diversity, as well as be proud of our unique and varied heritages.

title: Major World Religions
text:
Judaism

Judaism originated nearly 4,000 years ago in the near eastern region of Canaan (modern-day Israel and Palestinian territories). Judaism is one of the oldest religions in the world. Judaism is based on the belief in a covenant made by Abraham, their patriarch, with God. A covenant is a promise between a man and God. God promised Abraham that he and his people would be given a promised land and would be made prosperous. The main figures of Judaism are Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the prophet Moses, who received God's laws at Mount Sinai. The most important Jewish book of scripture is the Torah.

Christianity

Christians believe in the teachings of Jesus Christ. He lived in Palestine about 2,000 years ago. The life and teachings of Jesus are found in the Gospels. The Gospels are the books that were written by Jesus's disciples between 20 and 100 years after his death. The Gospels are the four first books of the New Testament. Christians also believe in the Old Testament. The Christian Bible consists of the Old and New Testaments. Christianity is not only the largest religion in the world but also the largest religion in Europe. There are about 565 million Christians living in Europe.

Islam

Islam had its origins in the Middle East in the 7th century C.E. Muslims believe in the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. He lived most of his life in the town of Mecca in western Saudi Arabia. Muhammad died in the year 632 and was buried in Medina, Saudi Arabia. The sacred book of Islam is called the Koran. The teachings of Islam cover every part of a person's daily life, including the foods they should eat, the clothes they should wear, what education they should receive, and the manners they should use. Those who follow the religion of Islam are called Muslims, which means "one who submits." Muslims believe in submitting themselves to Allah, or God. Islam is a growing religion. It is the second largest religion in Europe.

Hinduism

1 billion people practice Hinduism. This means that Hinduism is one of the largest religions in the world. It all began in ancient India. Some Hindus believe their religion never had an origin or beginning. They feel their beliefs are timeless. Hinduism allows for many differing viewpoints. It is considered one of the most tolerant, accepting religions in the world. Some followers are polytheistic. This means they believe in many different Gods and Goddesses. Others believe there are only three Gods that form a trinity. These Gods are Brahma, Shiva, and Vishnu. Other Hindus believe that all of the Gods and Goddesses are different sides to a single, powerful God. One of the most important beliefs in Hinduism is the idea of karma. Hindus believe their past and present actions play a role in their future.

Buddhism

Buddhism is another of our world’s oldest religions, and it also began in India. Buddhism is sometimes described as a nontheistic religion. People of a nontheistic religion do not believe in a god who either created the world or judges people. Buddhism does not have a traditional god in the same way that Christianity or Islam do. Instead of a personal god, they have Buddha. Buddha was a man named Siddhartha Gautama. He went on a journey to find personal enlightenment. Personal enlightenment is peace and spiritual understanding. Buddhism is a spiritual and religious tradition that has over 400 million believers across the world.

title: Archaeology: How Do We Know?
text:
There are no newspapers, photos of people, or even records to prove that humans came to America around 20,000 years ago. How do we know that they were here so long ago? How do we know anything about their lives?

People leave clues that help us understand them long after they are gone. Sometimes, ancient peoples left clues in stories passed down to their descendants. They also left behind innovations we still use today. Some of these include crops, like corn, and medicines. People left behind objects they made, too. We call this archaeological evidence.

An archaeologist studies things left behind by people who lived a long time ago. Some objects, called artifacts, get covered by earth or water for thousands of years. Many become fragile. To avoid damaging them, archaeologists rarely use their hands to observe artifacts. Instead, they use dry brushes and other tools to clean them. This helps make sure that they won’t remove things like leftover paint and food from the artifacts. For example, stone tools that archaeologists find can reveal traces of foods that people ate.

Archaeologists often recognize patterns. They study differences between earlier objects and later, more advanced ones. They find evidence of trade by tracking the movement of similar artifacts. For example, Knife River flint comes from what is now North Dakota. Artifacts made from this flint have been found throughout the western United States. They have also shown up as far east as Ohio and Pennsylvania. This evidence suggests that people traded flint all across the country.

But archaeologists don’t only study objects. They also study structures and human-made features. They do this at archaeological sites or other places where there is evidence of past human activity, Structures like native peoples’ homes can suggest whether a certain group had more of a small close-knit community or a large, complex society. Features like fireplaces or storage pits can also help scientists imagine what daily life in ancient cultures was like.

Archaeologists study artifacts carefully. It’s important to show respect to people from the past and their descendants. Sometimes when archaeologists dig, they unearth sensitive things. They may find places where people are buried. Some people think burials should be examined for evidence. Others think they should be left alone. New technology has helped archaeologists with this problem. Today, they can often scan areas without digging. Not having to dig allows them to show more respect for burial places.

When combined with other forms of evidence, artifacts can tell a story. Archaeology has proven that the early peoples who lived in the Americas were skilled. They built complex societies, traded goods with other ancient peoples, and had vibrant, sophisticated societies in America for thousands of years.

title: Sources
text:
The best way to understand an issue is to research it. This means gathering information from several sources. The internet puts a wealth of information about almost any topic right at your fingertips. Type your topic into a search engine, and it will reveal many sources. But some sources are better than others.

As you look for information, look for sources that are credible and reliable. A credible source is one that readers can trust. The information is written by experts. The intent is to teach or inform, and the information provided is reliable and accurate. Government agencies, universities, and mainstream news organizations are generally considered credible. You also want to look for relevant information. This means that it is directly related to the topic you want to learn about.

Some sites that look credible may not be. Anyone can write a blog or an article on the internet. These postings do not go through the same editing process as credible sources do. Check the URL. Government sources usually end in .gov, and educational organizations use .edu. These sources may have more reliable information than sites ending in .com or .org.

Look for clues about why an article was written. Look for research or sources cited at the end of the information. Read about the author. If no author or citations are provided, you should question the reliability of the source.

Additionally, look for unbiased articles that are willing to consider both sides of an issue. Biased articles include only the facts that support one point of view. Their goal is not to help people understand the issue. Rather, it is to convince people that their opinion on the issue is correct. Keep in mind the author’s purpose as you read. Analyze what the person is writing, and look for other sides of the issue. This can help you balance different ideas.

title: Essential Question
text: What responsibilities do community members have?

title: Being Informed
text:
As citizens, it is our responsibility to know what is happening around us. This means understanding our community’s social, political, cultural, and environmental issues. There are different ways to stay informed. One way is to read and watch the news. There are many news sources available today. Some are newspapers and magazines.

The best way to stay informed is to investigate issues to learn more about them. You can explore many sources and opinions. This would help you understand issues better. Staying informed also means choosing news sources carefully. Make sure to choose sources that are credible, or trustworthy. You can also talk to an expert in the field you wish to learn more about.

Staying informed is a very important responsibility for all citizens, especially when it comes to voting. Citizens must be informed about how candidates wish to address community issues. This helps citizens to make the best decision when voting in local, state, or national elections.

title: Models of the World
text:
Geography is the study of places and the relationships between people and their environments. The study of geography also includes how things change over time. Studying geography helps us understand the world around us. We can use geography to understand the past and answer important questions about the world and its people.

Using geographic tools, such as maps, globes, graphs, diagrams, aerial and other photographs, and other geographical representations, helps us to organize our thinking about the world into spatial terms. Studying geography helps us to understand history, economics, culture, and government. No matter the time period, geography has played a role in the actions of people and the events of government and economics. Wars have been started over resources from the land. Location played a key role in building the colonies in the Western Hemisphere, or North and South America and the water surrounding them. Representation in government is often based on geographic regions and places. Transportation systems modified the land to bring goods and services to markets. The creation of settlements, territories, states, and nations are all linked to geography. Geographic skills and concepts can also help people solve local, state, or international problems. Studying geography can help experts answer questions concerning environmental change, population distribution, proper use of natural resources, and political discussions.

There are different ways we can study the world’s geography. A globe is a model of the Earth. Globes show us where water, land, and countries are located. Globes are useful when you need to see the Earth in a more accurate, spherical shape.

Maps are drawings of places around the world. They show where places are located and how to get there. Maps help us find the direction we need to travel. They can show large areas like continents or small areas like cities. Maps can show elevation, which shows height above sea level. They can show the population, or how many people live in a place. They can also show the climate, or the weather over a long period of time.

This week, you will practice using geographic skills and tools. As you work through this week, think of ways that geographic skills and tools can help you understand the world around you.

title: Essential Question
text: What tools can be used to understand the geography of a place?

title: Why Do We Use Maps?
text:
A cartographer, is a person who creates and decides what to include on maps. The original purpose of maps wasn’t to be accurate in size or proportion. Instead, they showed who had control of the land. Once maps showed more exact distances and details, they were easier to follow. Maps worked to show the different sizes and shapes of countries, along with the distance between places and how long it took to get to certain locations. The invention of printing also made maps easier to obtain.

Maps are used for a variety of different reasons, depending on the purpose of the map. Meteorologists, or scientists that study the weather, use weather maps to help tell people about the forecast or to study patterns of weather. Travel agents use maps of destinations to help vacationers plan routes around roads, national parks, or to cities. City planners or housing developers use maps to design houses, streets, parks, and buildings for an area.

One of the first and largest engraved maps of the Western Hemisphere was completed in 1562 by Diego Gutiérrez, a cartographer who was commissioned by the Spanish and by Hieronymus Cock from Antwerp, who was considered a noted engraver. Many elements are showcased in the map as to who held control of the different regions through the Western Hemisphere. The Spanish and French coats of arms are displayed in the top left corner, and Portugal’s coat of arms is displayed in the bottom right corner. The map’s political features show that the cartographer knew of major rivers, such as the Amazon River, and major mountain ranges, such as the Appalachian Mountains. The map also describes different stories of the oceans, mythological sea creatures, and various sea battles that have taken place.

title: Political Features
text:
Political features, including cities, states, and countries, are organized by where people live. Political features can be seen on political maps. Many people in the world live in cities. Cities are sometimes organized into counties, and counties are organized into states or provinces. States and provinces come together to form a country. Political maps show the borders of cities, states, and countries.

A political map can also show how some borders have been created using the physical features near them. Oceans, rivers, and mountain ranges can also create borders of countries or states. One example would be how the Rio Grande in the United States marks part of the border for Mexico. These borders help us by showing where one area stops and a new one begins.

title: Types of Maps
text:
Map tools help us when we use maps and globes. Map tools include the title, legend, compass rose, and scale. The map’s title helps us know the map’s purpose and the kind of information we will examine on the map. The map’s legend or key explains what the symbols and colors on the map represent. Maps have a compass rose. The compass rose is a symbol that shows the cardinal directions: north, south, east, and west. The compass rose can also show the intermediate directions of northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast. You can tell the distance on a map by looking at the scale.

There are many different kinds of maps. You can use them to explore the world. Some maps display the characteristics of physical environments. Other maps show where people live and how they interact with their environment.

A physical map shows the natural features of an area. Natural features include landforms, mountains, valleys, lakes, and streams.

Some maps show the climate of a region. Climate is the study of weather over time. A climate map shows whether a place is usually warm or cold and wet or dry.

A population map is used to show the overall distribution of the population within a particular area or region. Most maps use colors or symbols, such as circles or stars, to represent the varying populations. Population maps are useful for the government to plan how to distribute resources.

Cultural maps identify community cultures and resources. These maps are used to help plan and implement the distribution of resources. Cultural maps also connect cultural groups based on their beliefs and values. Cultural maps illustrate the relationships and interactions between people, places, and the environment.

Historical maps are created to represent historical events in a certain time period.

A political map shows the borders of regions, countries, states, and cities. Some political maps represent even smaller divisions, such as counties, townships, and neighborhoods.

title: Aerial and Digital Images
text:
Geographers use many tools to study the physical and human features of the Earth. We can study the features of the world from a spatial perspective. Spatial perspective is the study of geographic features of an area using multiple tools. These tools include maps, globes, and satellite images.

Technology presents new and exciting ways to learn about the world. We can use GPS to help us study the world. GPS stands for Global Positioning System. The GPS is made up of over 18 satellites that are orbiting, or circling, the Earth in space. These satellites send information to stations on the ground on Earth. This allows scientists to take very specific measurements of different locations all over the Earth. With the newest GPS systems, scientists can pinpoint a place on Earth to the nearest centimeter. You can also use GPS to find how long it takes to get from one place to another.

Geographic Information Systems, also known as GIS, are a way of visualizing data on maps. As soon as people invented computers capable of doing it, they began using computers to map information. If you have data or information that matches locations on a map, you can use GIS to make a visual representation of that data on a map. Looking at the data on top of a map can show new relationships and patterns that might not have seemed obvious at first. Without the ability to map and visualize data, it can be difficult to understand it. Trends and patterns in data can often be missed if you do not understand the physical relationship between the various points of information.

Any information that can be mapped can be visualized through GIS. Many different careers rely on GIS data and visuals. City planners can use GIS to map the riders on public transportation like buses and subways to make sure their transportation plans meet people where they are. Biologists observe the presence of endangered species and plan protection strategies through the information they learn using GIS. Archaeologists use GIS to map the presence of historical sites and artifacts. Archaeologists dig in the ground and dive into bodies of water to look for artifacts. They also use GIS to make detailed digital models of the sites where they find these artifacts. Mapping the data through GIS allows them to visualize the entire site and find patterns they might otherwise miss. Recreating sites digitally also allows them to limit how much they disturb fragile historical sites.

Governments in a state or province use GIS data to identify areas threatened by natural hazards. This helps them create and share evacuation routes with citizens. It also allows counties to share other important information, like flood zones and access to important services like fire stations and schools.

By using geographic tools, we can view the world from many different perspectives. This can help us determine how things work to make a place unique.

title: What are Natural Features
text: Natural features of the Earth are parts of the Earth’s surface. Natural features are created in different ways. The Earth’s surface is changing every day. Wind, rain, drought, volcanoes, and earthquakes all shape Earth’s surface. People have named types of natural features by the way the land forms. Mountains, valleys, deserts, and oceans are all natural features on Earth’s surface.

title: Mountains
text:
A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean.

It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They are formed from movement of the Earth’s crust. Mountains are shaped over time by weather. Rich minerals are found in the core of mountains. Mountain peaks are often covered in snow. The snow melts and sends water down the sides in streams, creeks, and brooks.

title: Valleys
text: A valley is a low area between mountains. It is often created by a river or stream. It can also be created when two mountains are formed close together. Valleys are usually “V”-shaped. They collect the soil and plants that are moved down the mountains by weather.

title: Natural Resources and Mountains
text: Mountains may contain a variety of biomes. A biome is a community of plants and animals living together. Taller mountains have colder weather. When the weather is cold, plant life is limited. Further down the mountain slopes, the temperature is warmer, and plant life increases. This makes it easier for animals to find food and shelter there.

title: Landforms and Natural Features Activity
text: Compare and contrast a mountain and a valley. Draw pictures that show how they are similar or different.

title: Valley and Natural Resources
text:
Valleys are home to many animals. These animals find shelter in the trees and grasslands. The soil has nutrients, which help plants grow. Streams from mountains form rivers in valleys.

Valleys are protected by the mountains. The weather in a valley is often mild. As a result, plants and animals thrive there.

title: Essential Question
text: How do natural features influence movement and resources?

title: Culture and Beliefs of Ancient Egypt
text:
Ancient Egyptian society revolved around religious beliefs. Like many ancient cultures, when Ancient Egyptians did not understand the cause of some natural event, they credited it to a god. They built massive monuments and temples to worship and honor their gods. Their art focused primarily on their religion, depicting a wide variety of gods with different powers and responsibilities.

As Egyptian religion developed, each town adopted its own local god. As towns grew, some gods gained more prominence than others. They were given the largest monuments, with many priests and priestesses honoring them.

One of the earliest and most important gods was Osiris. He was credited with causing the Nile’s yearly flood. The flood brought the waters and soil that allowed Egyptians to grow their crops. Isis, wife of Osiris, was another major god. According to Ancient Egyptian myth, she brought Osiris back to life and saved their son, Horus, from death.

Gods were often paired up to symbolize opposing forces. For example, Horus was the god of life and order, while Set was the god of chaos and disorder. When Horus was saved from death by Isis, he went on to defeat Set and become king of Egypt. Horus symbolized the royal power of the pharaoh. Pharaohs were considered to be descendants of Horus. Together, Osiris, Isis, and Horus were the royal family of Egyptian gods. Many representations of them decorate Ancient Egyptian tombs and monuments.

Symbols were an important part of Egyptian beliefs and traditions. Gods and pharaohs are shown in paintings, inscriptions, and sculptures as holding a scepter. One version of this scepter symbolizes power over Egypt. Another version symbolizes godly power. Gods and pharaohs are also shown wearing headgear, such as crowns, symbolizing their status. For example, Horus and pharaohs are shown with a cobra head on their headgear to symbolize their royalty.

Ancient Egyptian art focused on their belief in many gods and goddesses. Much of what we know about Ancient Egyptian religious belief comes from studying their statues and the art on the walls of tombs and monuments.

title: Week 10 Framing Question
text: Why was religion so important to the Ancient Egyptian way of life?

title: The Afterlife
text:
The discovery of Tutankhamun’s tomb was the first step in learning about the process the Egyptians believed people went through to access everlasting life. By studying the illustrations and artifacts in Ancient Egyptian tombs, archaeologists have pieced together Ancient Egyptian beliefs about the afterlife.

For Ancient Egyptians, the first step to accessing the afterlife was to construct a tomb for the dead. It would hold the person’s body and the things they would need for their journey to the afterlife. Mummifying the body was a precise and complicated process. If the body was not properly prepared, it was believed it would not survive the dangerous journey into the afterlife.

Originally, mummifying the body and storing the necessary items to make the journey was limited only to pharaohs. As time went on, it became possible for the wealthy to afford a tomb, mummification, and other essential items for passage into the next life.

As the soul progressed toward the afterlife, Ancient Egyptians believed it would encounter dangerous mythical creatures, so weapons were buried with the body to help the soul fight them. Passing this challenge brought the soul to seven gates. A magic spell for each gate would grant access to the Hall of Osiris, where the soul would be judged.

Living a good life was important to the Ancient Egyptians, and it was one of the main criteria for passing the final judgment and entering the afterlife. Ancient Egyptians believed that bad acts made the heart heavy and good acts made the heart light. The soul was required to confess its crimes to a group of 42 gods. If the soul passed the judgment of the gods, its heart would be weighed against a feather. A heavy heart, weighed down by crimes and evil deeds, would weigh more than the feather. Then that person’s soul would be consumed, and they could not enter the afterlife. A good person’s heart would weigh less than the feather. Their soul would then become immortal and join Osiris, the other gods, and the pharaohs in the afterlife.

title: Mummification
text:
For the Ancient Egyptians, the mummification process was an important part of preparing a dead person’s soul to go to the afterlife. Mummification was thought to preserve the soul within the body. Without the soul, the person would not be able to make the journey to the afterlife. It was a scientific, multi-step process that shows that Ancient Egyptians understood much about how the human body works.

The process took 10 weeks. To start with, many bodily organs were removed to make sure they would not cause the body to decompose. Since moisture causes the body to decay, a mixture of salt and baking soda was used to dry it out. Long strips of linen were then wrapped around the body.

The best mummifications preserved a body well enough that we can get an idea of what the mummified person looked like when they were alive, even a few thousand years after their death. Tutankhamun died during the New Kingdom era, when mummification was practiced at its highest level. It's one reason why the discovery of his tomb was so important. The preservation of his body revealed much about Egyptian mummification.

title: The Pyramids
text:
The most popular symbols of Ancient Egypt are the pyramids. The pyramids were built as tombs for pharaohs. When a pharaoh died, their body was mummified and placed deep within the pyramid. From there, the Ancient Egyptians believed the pharaoh began a journey into the afterlife.

The sides of the earliest pyramids were made of large steps. They were constructed during the Old Kingdom era, more than 1,000 years before the famous pharaohs of the New Kingdom, such as Hatshepsut, Akhenaten, and Tutankhamun. Each level of the step pyramids was smaller than the one below it.

The most famous pyramid is the Great Pyramid at Giza. It is the largest Egyptian pyramid. It has smooth sides. The Great Pyramid was built under the direction of King Khufu. It was the tallest structure on Earth until the 1800s. It is composed of over two million stone blocks. Each block weighs over two tons. The blocks fit together so well that they do not need cement to hold them together.

How the pyramids were constructed has long been a mystery. Moving the 4,000-pound blocks from where they were quarried in the Eastern Desert to the construction site was a feat all on its own. Yet the Ancient Egyptians then placed the blocks hundreds of feet up, atop the pyramids.

Archaeologists and historians originally thought that most of the labor used to construct the pyramids came from enslaved people. But the historical record seems to show that Egyptian farmers were also expected to spend part of each year working on the pyramids. They were well-fed and taken care of while they worked.

The pyramids preserved much of the information we have today about Ancient Egypt. The tombs within the pyramids contain hieroglyphics describing daily life in ancient times, including the labor of different workers and common religious practices and traditions.

title: The Sphinx
text:
The pyramids are not the only massive stone structures built during the Old Kingdom that still stand at Giza. Near the pyramids crouches a large stone lion with a human head. It is called the Sphinx. Unlike the pyramids, which are made of many blocks, the Sphinx is made of one giant piece of limestone. It was carved out of a limestone formation that occurs there naturally. No one knows for sure who is responsible for the construction of the Sphinx. Leading archaeologists believe it was Khufu’s son, King Khafre. A nearby pyramid built by Khafre contains stone quarried from the Sphinx.

The Sphinx is over 60 feet tall and almost 250 feet long. Its lion body and human head are meant to represent Ra-Horakhty, a form of Ra, the sun god. Though it is very large, parts of the Sphinx are missing. Archaeologists found a broken stone beard and a cobra symbol from the Sphinx’s headdress during excavations in the 1800s. Archaeologists also found bits of paint on the Sphinx, leading them to believe that it may have been completely painted at one point.

For much of modern history, the Sphinx was buried up to its neck in sand. Digging it out proved to be a difficult task. Early attempts failed when the sand that had been removed simply flowed back into the digging area. The Sphinx was finally dug out in the 1930s. Further archaeological excavations uncovered a settlement where the workers who carved the Sphinx lived. As many as 2,000 workers may have been involved in the construction of this famous and impressive structure of Ancient Egypt.

title: Papyrus
text:
The Nile River and delta provided ancient Egyptians with the water and soil they needed to grow crops. The shallow waters along the Nile provided another resource: a reed known as papyrus. This plant could be used to make a variety of goods, including rope, cloth, and sails.

Today, the word “papyrus” most often refers to a paper-like material. The English word “paper” actually comes from the word “papyrus.” Fibers from the papyrus plant were woven together in a crisscross pattern and then pressed together into flat sheets. These sheets were pasted together to form a scroll of papyrus paper. The finished scrolls could be up to 100 feet in length. Papyrus makers were important craftspeople in ancient Egypt.

Papyrus was used to record many types of information. Scribes used it to record government proceedings. Merchants used it to record the details of their business dealings. Archaeologists found surviving papyri (the word for more than one papyrus sheet or scroll) that tell the story of the Great Pyramid at Giza’s construction.

Papyrus became a very important tool for record keeping. Egyptians harvested the plant from the banks of the Nile River and became specialists in making it into paper-like sheets and scrolls. Egyptian merchants sold and traded papyrus throughout the ancient world, sometimes as far away as Greece and Rome.

The dry Egyptian environment, and especially the tombs of pharaohs, allowed many papyrus scrolls to survive. Archaeologists have discovered some that date back as far as 3000 B.C.E.

title: Hieroglyphics
text:
Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics were one of the first written languages in human history. Developed around 3000 B.C.E., the use of hieroglyphics dates to the very beginnings of Ancient Egyptian society.

Hieroglyphics used different kinds of symbols. Some of them represented entire words or concepts. Others stood for certain sounds in a spoken language. Important concepts, ideas, or people had their own hieroglyphs. For example, gods like Anubis and Osiris had their own hieroglyphs. The words “sun” and “house” also had their own symbols. Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics included more than 700 different symbols.

Original hieroglyphics were complex. Some of the symbols had details that made them time-consuming to produce. They were most often carved into the walls and statues of pharaohs’ tombs

Different forms of hieroglyphics developed over time. One form was called hieratic. It was usually written with reed brushes on papyrus. It was used for business records, letters, and other common writings. Later, other scripts, such as demotic and coptic, developed. These scripts brought in alphabets and written languages from other parts of the ancient world.

Eventually, hieroglyphics went out of use. People forgot what the symbols meant. Their meanings remained a mystery until an important discovery in the early 1800s. The discovery was a large slab of darkly colored stone with three different kinds of writing on it. It was a government decree from 196 B.C.E. The decree was written in three different languages: original hieroglyphics, demotic script, and Greek. Researchers Thomas Young and Jean-Francois Champollion were able to use their knowledge of Greek to translate the demotic and then the hieroglyphics. This gave archaeologists and historians the ability to translate the hieroglyphics on papyrus and tomb walls. Their translations provided a fuller picture of the life and culture of Ancient Egypt. The stone became known as the Rosetta Stone, named for the city near which it was found.

title: Jean-Francois Champollion
text:
Born in 1790, Jean-Francois Champollion helped change what the world knows about ancient Egypt. Soon after Champollion was born, a magician said that one day Champollion would become famous. He was correct. Champollion is credited with discovering the meaning of the ancient Egyptian writing called hieroglyphs. He helped us understand the world of the ancient Egyptians.

As a young boy, Champollion was often sick, so he couldn't go out and play sports. There weren't computers and video games at the time. So Champollion spent his days in the world of books. He learned to read Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese, Syriac, and Chaldean, all by the time he was a teenager. He could also read Latin and Greek. Champollion was just a young boy when the Rosetta Stone was found. He announced then that he would be the first person to translate the hieroglyphic writing. Champollion spent years trying to figure out the meaning of the Egyptian hieroglyphs. Studying the three different writings on the stone, of which only Greek could be read, Champollion determined they were the same message. He used the Greek as a key to deciphering the hieroglyphic writings.

Champollion was working on an Egyptian dictionary and grammar book when he died in 1832.

title: Hounds and Jackals
text:
Dating back to about 1800 B.C.E., Hounds and Jackals is a board game that has been found in several Egyptian tombs. It is sometimes called the Game of 58 Holes. Although no directions have been found, it appears to be similar to Chutes and Ladders, a game you may have played when you were younger. Archaeologists think players rolled a die to move five pieces from the holes at the very top of the board to the holes near the top of the palm tree. Players moved pegs shaped like the heads of hounds or jackals along the holes in the board. The first person to get all five of their pieces to the top of the tree was the winner.

Try playing Hounds and Jackals. With a partner, make 10 markers: five hound heads and five jackal heads. Choose who will use which markers and place them at the top of the board. Take turns rolling a die and moving one piece at a time. If you roll a 1 or a 6, take an extra turn. Move only on your side of the board. If you get to a space with a connecting line, you must slide your piece to the other end of the line. That's good if you get to slide from #10 to #24, but not so good if you have to slide from #24 to #10. No one really knows how this game was played, so feel free to make up your own rules. Just be sure to agree on them before you begin to play.

title: Columbus
text:
Surveyors first laid out the plan for Columbus in 1812, but the city was not officially created until 1816. It was chosen as the capital of Ohio because of its central location. It was also close to several rivers and other transportation routes. These transportation options allowed the city to grow quickly in its early years.

Immigrants began moving to Columbus because the land was cheap. Many businesses sprang up. Railroads were built across the country in the 1800s. Columbus became a crossroads where multiple railroads met. People and goods traveled along these railroads through Columbus. This created more economic opportunities and allowed the city to grow.

In the 20th century, major roads and interstate highways were built. This helped Columbus to grow even further. Suburbs and nearby communities eventually became part of Columbus. It is now the most populous city in the state. It is home to major businesses, universities, and other important institutions.

title: Essential Question
text: How have communities in Ohio changed over time?

title: Cleveland
text:
Cleveland was established in 1796. It grew slowly along the banks of Lake Erie and the Cuyahoga River. By 1820, there were only a few more than 600 people living there. In 1825, the Erie Canal was completed. It connected Cleveland with other cities along the Great Lakes and the East Coast. The natural resources available around Cleveland made it an ideal place for railroads and ships to load and unload goods.

The area around Cleveland had a lot of coal and iron ore. These resources made Cleveland a major industrial center. The city grew quickly during the late 1800s. Many people moved there to work in the steel industry. By 1920, it had the fifth-largest population in the United States.

A strong economy and a healthy transportation network attracted people. Cleveland’s population reached almost one million by the middle of the 1950s. However, many factories in Cleveland closed in the 20th century. The economy of the United States moved away from manufacturing. Many cities like Cleveland struggled to support new jobs and opportunities. The city’s population has continued to decrease during the 2000s.

title: Cincinnati
text:
Cincinnati became a city in 1819. It is located on the Ohio River. The river was a major travel route to the west. Businesses were opened to sell supplies to explorers and settlers going west. Immigrants from Germany and Ireland moved to the city during the 1800s.

The rural areas around the city produced livestock. These were brought to Cincinnati to be processed and sold. The meatpacking industry used the river to quickly move its products to markets around the country. Railroads arrived in the 1800s and made Cincinnati’s economy even stronger. The city also produced iron and clothing during the late 1800s.

The population of Cincinnati has not changed much since the late 1800s. However, the area surrounding the city has grown. The city’s population has stayed the same because many businesses moved outside the city. Companies and workers left the city for the suburbs.

title: Toledo
text:
Toledo was established in 1836. It is located on one end of the Wabash and Erie Canal. The city relied on water transportation during its early years. This is because of its location. Travel on the lake and along the canals of Ohio connected Toledo to Cincinnati and other major cities.

The area around Toledo was known as the Great Black Swamp. Citizens had to deal with diseases from the stagnant water and insects. The swamp also made travel difficult. To solve the problem, large ditches were dug to drain the swamp. The people then gained access to the natural resources in the swamp, especially trees for lumber.

Railroads became the preferred way to move goods in and out of Toledo in the 1800s. They were faster and more reliable than the water routes. The city became a center of manufacturing. Toledo has maintained its importance as a center of manufacturing and trade. This is due to its location on Lake Erie. Toledo’s economy struggled after WWII. However, its population continued to grow.

title: Akron
text:
Akron was established in 1825, when the Erie Canal was being built. Many of the canal workers were Irish immigrants who lived in Akron. The canal connected Akron to Cleveland. This made Akron a destination for goods from around the area. Businesses processed crops from the area. The products were then shipped along the canal. Factories moved goods through Akron as well.

The arrival of railroads improved the city’s economy. Major industries and companies called Akron home. The B.F. Goodrich Company and the Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company opened in Akron. This made the city a major center supporting the growing automobile industry. In the late 1800s and early 1900s, many people moved to Akron to work in these industries. As a result, Akron grew and prospered.

The city contributed to the World War II manufacturing effort. Many of the things the army needed were made there. Unfortunately, many of these manufacturing industries closed after the war. Akron saw its population decrease in the second half of the 1900s as people moved away to find jobs.

title: Connections
text:
The medieval and early modern periods of history were full of remarkable change, development, and growth around the globe. During this period, languages, religions, and cultures spread throughout the world. There were also significant advancements in technology. As cities grew, so did the agricultural skills and technology necessary to feed the rising global population. To understand the global changes that took place during this era, we will ask questions about the geography, economics, politics, and religions of societies we want to learn more about.

We already know that geography plays a significant role in the choices people make and that geography has influenced history. This week we will learn some foundational principles about economics, politics, and culture. We will also examine how political, economic, and cultural choices and trends have influenced history and led to many of these transformative changes during the medieval and early modern time periods. The role of geography will still be a significant factor while we consider new themes of economics, politics, and culture.

title: Economics
text:
Economics is the study of the production and trade of goods and services. There are many sub-topics in economics that can be used to understand how economics has influenced history. Some of these topics are: trade, money, business, resources, and labor. Economic development has followed a historical trend. First, economies start on a local level. This type of economy is often called a traditional economy, and in this system, land is the most important commodity. Agricultural goods are produced on the land, which are used to feed people. In order to produce agricultural products, people used the only other resource available to them: their own labor. As agricultural tools improved, fewer laborers were necessary to produce food, more people were fed, and new areas of labor were created. Instead of everyone working as agricultural laborers, people were now working as craftsmen, religious leaders, tradesmen, or luxury good producers.

This historical trend continued. As more labor-saving technology was produced, people engaged in new economic activities. A new merchant class emerged, and new businesses were created, like insurance agencies and law firms. Eventually, people would have leisure time, which increased the amount of people working in hospitality fields. During this trend, civilizations moved from traditional economies to more complex economic systems, like market economies. Most of the civilizations that we will study during the medieval and early modern period followed this economic pattern from traditional, agricultural economies to market systems. Ultimately, the world would become so interconnected that people could specialize enough that they only produced one good. They could rely on global trade networks to provide the rest of their necessities.

title: Trade and Increasing Interactions
text:
Trade has always been a crucial part of economic systems. Trade is the buying, selling, or bartering of goods or services. People and civilizations have been trading for centuries. It is one of the mechanisms that connected the world and led to the exchange of not just goods and services, but also ideas and technology. Most of us would assume that this trade happened between close neighbors, but starting in the first century C.E., trade increased between distant regions. The silk road connected China with Europe and Africa, as did the sea and spice trades. The resources available within a geographic area influence the economic choices that people make, including when people trade and who they trade with.

Silk Road

The silk road got its name because the most popular commodity traded from China to Southwestern Asia and Europe was silk. The silk road actually had multiple roads or routes from China across Central Asia to all parts of the world. The silk road connected traders from Europe, the Arabian Peninsula, and Africa. Caravans of traders would cross to large trading cities in Central Asia and sell or barter their goods. The Chinese produced silk, gems, pearls, and jade. Central Asian goods were horses, donkeys, and ivory. Southwestern Asian and European goods were glassware, grapes, and coral.

Sea and Spice Trade

In addition to land trade routes, people also traded by sea. Sea traders were important because there were some spices that only grew on islands in Southeast Asia, which made sea trade a necessity. Cinnamon grew in what is now Sri Lanka, cloves and nutmeg grew in the spice islands, or islands that are now part of modern-day Indonesia.

Ideas, Philosophies, and Technology

Along these trade routes, goods were not the only thing exchanged. People shared religion, ideas, and technology. For example, Buddhist missionaries traveled from India along the silk road. Their influence caused many Chinese people to convert to Buddhism. Technologies like paper and the compass were Chinese inventions that were moved along the silk road. Paper and the compass would change cultures worldwide, including influencing Portuguese and Spanish explorers during the Age of Exploration.

title: Politics and Governments
text:
Societies have created many different types of governmental systems. These different types of government reflect the values and beliefs of the societies that created them. Some forms of government are unique to certain times and places. Others have been reused, recycled, or reformed by other communities. When the ancient Romans created the Roman Republic, it was a completely new form of government. However, many other societies have created their own republic governments since then. In fact, the United States has a republic government.

The purpose of government is to create systems that manage the rights and liberties of individuals. Governments create mechanisms that help them meet their own wants and needs as well as the wants and needs of the people. These mechanisms include judicial systems, elections, and political parties.

Governments have the authority to control or direct the actions of citizens. A government’s authority comes from the law, morality, custom, or consent of the people. Laws are the formal rules of a society that all citizens must follow. The government enforces the consequences for breaking laws. The laws that a government creates reflect the values and customs of the society they come from.

Some of the first recorded government laws were created in Mesopotamia in approximately 1771 B.C.E. The leader of Mesopotamia at that time was a man named Hammurabi. The laws of Hammurabi were written down as “if-then” statements. For example, one law stated that if you stole an ox from your neighbor, then you would owe the owner 30 times the value of the ox. Like all laws, this law reflects the values of the society. Because of the high price of replacing stolen property, this law would likely have prevented people from stealing in the first place. It shows that people in Mesopotamia valued property. The high price for stealing an ox may also show that Mesopotamians valued working animals as a very important type of property.

This year as we study world civilizations from 500 C.E. to 1500 C.E., we have learned and will continue to learn about many types of governmental systems. As we study them, we will understand more about the customs and values of the societies and people that lived with these governments.

title: Culture
text:
Culture is the shared beliefs, customs, traditions, and celebrations of a group of people. It includes the architecture, religion, language, stories, music, and food created by that group. Culture is often influenced by the place where the group lives. People create art from local resources. They tell stories to explain the world around them. They cook food from the plants grown on the land where they live. For example, people who live near the ocean tend to eat more fish than people living inland, while people who live in areas with large grasslands rely heavily on farming and often raise cattle for food. People in different parts of the world also flavor their foods with different spices.

We often describe the human geography of places and regions by their cultural traits. When people move from one place to another, they bring their cultures with them, so elements of different cultures often combine to create new traditions and customs. As we continue to study the history of the medieval world, this is one of the most common things that you will see about culture: it is a blend of ideas and influences. It is rarely unchanging. As Islam reached different parts of Africa, it’s language blended to make new languages, like Swahili. Its religious ideals led to the creation of long-lasting universities and libraries in West African empires. Another example of evolving culture can be seen in European history. As exposure to different spices grew, food staples changed. Recipe books in medieval Europe used natural sweeteners like honey in most recipes. This changed when they were exposed to sugar. Sugarcane is a plant native to Southeast Asia, but Europeans began replacing honey with sugar in their recipe books.

title: Essential Question
text: How have the ways people communicate changed over time?

title: Communication
text: Communication has always been important to communities. Cultures developed their own languages and writing systems. Written messages were carried between people. There have been many communication inventions over time. The telegraph and the photograph were two of the earliest inventions. Things like the radio, motion pictures, and television came next. Today, we have computers, the internet, and smartphones. These inventions make communicating with people around the world much quicker and easier. Most people now have nonstop access to information from every corner of the world. They use computers and smartphones. Sharing ideas across the world has become much easier.

title: Evolving Communication
text:
Before the telegraph, people communicated by letters. The telegraph was the first way to send messages over very long distances. Samuel Morse invented the telegraph in 1837. The telegraph sent messages using Morse code. Morse code is a system of dots and dashes.

The typewriter is a machine. It was invented to make life easier for people who did a lot of writing. Christopher Sholes invented the typewriter in 1867. It made creating documents much cheaper. It created new jobs, especially for women.

Alexander Graham Bell invented the first telephone in 1876. People could talk to each other without being in the same place. News and other important messages were delivered instantly. Families and friends could communicate quickly and easily.

The satellite was invented in Russia in 1957. Satellites send signals around the world. Satellites can also take images from space. The images help us predict the weather. We can prepare for storms and hurricanes.

The cell phone was invented in 1973. The first cell phones were very big. Today, most cell phones can fit in a pocket. Cell phones can help us find directions without a map. We can call people if there is a problem. We can take photos and videos to send to friends and family.

The internet helps us communicate with others. It was invented in 1983. Before the internet, people wrote letters or called each other on the telephone. Now we send emails, which arrive immediately. We can video chat and connect with people far away. We can search for information or jobs from home.

title: Essential Question
text: What geographic tools can you use to learn about a specific place?

title: Relative Location
text: People use geographic representations, such as maps and globes, to collect, process, and report spatial information. Maps help people learn about an area and determine where something is located. Geographers describe places with both relative and absolute location. The relative location of a place tells us where a place is relative to, or compared to, something else. When we are describing the relative location of a place, we use words such as "by," "near," "above," or "below." If your friend tells you that their house is “down the street and across from the supermarket,” they are using relative location. You can also use cardinal and intermediate directions to describe the location of human and physical characteristics of a place. For example, when describing Ohio’s location within the United States, you could say, “Ohio is located in the northern part of the United States to the south of the Canadian border.”

title: Alphanumeric Grids
text:
Geographers use many tools to determine location on maps. One of these tools is called an alphanumeric grid. An alphanumeric grid is a grid that uses grid lines with letters and numbers to help you describe an absolute location on a map. Like a map that includes a coordinate grid, lines on an alphanumeric grid map form small squares. These squares can be identified using coordinates that contain one letter and one number. When using an alphanumeric grid, you should determine the letter, then the number of the coordinate. For example, the capital of Ohio is located at E, 15. Use the map to answer the analysis questions.

What state is located at E, 6? _________________________

What coordinates could you use to find the location of Colorado? ________________________

What state is located at D, 15? ________________________

What coordinates could you use to find the location of Georgia? __________________________

What state is located at G, 8? ________________________________

title: Types of Maps
text:
There are many different kinds of maps. You can use them to explore the world. Some maps display the characteristics of physical environments. Other maps show where people live and how they interact with their environment.

A physical map shows the natural features of an area. Natural features include landforms, mountains, valleys, lakes, and streams.

A political map shows the borders of regions, countries, states, and cities. Some political maps represent even smaller divisions, such as counties, townships, and neighborhoods.

Some maps show the climate of a region. Climate is the study of weather over time. A climate map shows whether a place is usually warm or cold and wet or dry.

A population map is used to show the overall distribution of the population within a particular area or region. Most maps use colors or symbols, such as circles or stars, to represent the varying populations. Population maps are useful for the government to plan how to distribute resource.

Cultural maps identify community cultures and resources. These maps are used to help plan and implement the distribution of resources. Cultural maps also connect cultural groups based on their beliefs and values. Cultural maps illustrate the relationships and interactions between people, places, and the environment.

Historical maps are created to represent historical events in the time period they occurred.

title: Good Citizens
text: A citizen is a person who belongs to a country, state, or community. We need good citizens for our governments to work well. The Constitution and laws of the United States give many rights and freedoms to people living in the United States. People who are citizens of the United States have additional rights and benefits. Some of those benefits are the right to vote, to run for office, and to work for the government. Being a U.S. citizen gives you the freedom to travel and to ask for help and protection from the government.

title: Week 7 Framing Question
text: How do good citizens treat others?

title: Becoming a Citizen
text: If you are born in the United States, you are a U.S. citizen. If your parents are citizens, you can be a citizen no matter where you were born. People who are born outside of the United States can choose to become citizens. There are requirements, steps, and checklists along the way. There are certain things you have to learn and do. The process can take time and cost money. New citizens need to know what citizenship means. When they become citizens, they are expected to do certain things and to behave in certain ways. They must support and defend the Constitution and the laws of the United States. Good citizens participate in their communities. They should show respect for the different cultures, religions, and opinions of other citizens. They should honor the freedoms and opportunities that citizenship gives them.

title: Serving on Committees and Volunteering
text:
Citizens who want to give something back to the community can volunteer, or donate their time to help others. Many people volunteer or work on committees because they want to help others in need. There are many ways you can volunteer in your community. Many volunteer organizations need committees of people to help keep them running.

People can volunteer for drives. Different types of drives collect things for people in need. Some volunteers help with community clean-ups. Other volunteers serve on committees to help community fire departments or neighborhood watch programs. Food banks collect canned goods or deliver food to people in need. Other programs teach people to read. Some volunteers even build homes for families who need a place to live.

The list of volunteer jobs is very long. If you want to give back to your community, find out about where you could volunteer. Someone will really appreciate your help!

title: Civil War
text:
When Europeans came to the United States, settlers in both the north and south brought people from Africa and forced them to do manual labor. As time went on, the northern part of the U.S. focused on manufacturing. It became less reliant on the work of enslaved people. The south focused on agriculture. It relied heavily on the work of enslaved people.

Most northerners came to feel that enslaving people was wrong. They were called abolitionists. As abolitionists gained political power, white people in the south began to worry. They thought the federal government would try to make slavery illegal. This would deeply affect the southern economy.

The Republican Party was formed specifically to abolish slavery. Abraham Lincoln was the Republican candidate for the presidency. He said he would allow slavery to continue in states where it was already legal, but he would not let it spread. But when Lincoln was elected, southerners thought he would make slavery illegal nationwide. They felt this would infringe on their states’ rights. So, many of the southern states seceded, or left, the United States. They formed their own country, the Confederate States of America.

Lincoln wanted to keep the United States together. In 1861, he sent Union troops to Fort Sumter in South Carolina, which was the first state to secede. Confederate troops attacked Fort Sumter and drove the Union troops out. This battle began the Civil War.

Northerners thought the war would be short, but it lasted four years. It involved more than 400 conflicts. More than 600,000 people were killed during the war. It ended in 1865. The Confederate general Robert E. Lee surrendered to the Union general Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Courthouse, Virginia.

title: Abraham Lincoln
text:
Abraham Lincoln had very little formal education. He grew up on the frontier of Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. He read every book he could find on any subject. At age 19, Lincoln took a flatboat of goods on the Mississippi River to the South. It was the first time Lincoln had ever seen people who were enslaved and being sold as property. He never forgot the sight, and it had a major impact on him.

Lincoln served a short time in the Illinois militia and then studied to be a lawyer. He met and married Mary Todd in 1842. Mary’s father was a wealthy banker, politician, plantation owner, and enslaver in Kentucky.

Lincoln was elected to the Illinois State Legislature from 1834 to 1842. He was then elected to the U.S. House of Representatives from 1847 to 1849. Lincoln’s political views were anti-slavery. He believed the federal government should control the legalization of enslaving people.

He ran for the U.S. Senate against Stephen A. Douglas in 1859 but lost. Instead, in 1860, he was nominated to run for president as a Republican. He was elected president of the United States even though his name was not on the ballot of nine southern states.

Lincoln was president during the Civil War and wrote the Emancipation Proclamation, which freed enslaved people in the southern states. Abraham Lincoln was assassinated just five days after he received news that the Civil War had ended. While watching a play, he was shot by John Wilkes Booth. Thousands of people across the nation participated in ceremonies to honor Lincoln.
