title: Emancipation Proclamation
text:
Following is some of the text of the Emancipation Proclamation. It is a document that freed the enslaved people in the Confederate southern states. However, it did not free the enslaved people who lived in states still loyal to the Union. President Abraham Lincoln told the Confederate states that if they rejoined the Union, he would not issue the Emancipation Proclamation. But they did not rejoin. Lincoln issued the Proclamation after the Battle of Antietam on September 17, 1862. The Proclamation was only temporary. Congress outlawed slavery permanently with the 13th Amendment in 1865.

January 1, 1863 By the President of the United States of America: A Proclamation.

… That on the first day of January, in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and sixty-three, all persons held as slaves within any State or designated part of a State ... in rebellion against the United States, shall be then ... and forever free; and the Executive Government of the United States, including the military and naval authority ... will recognize and maintain the freedom of such persons, and will do no act or acts to repress [stop] such persons . . . in any efforts they may make for their actual freedom.

… I hereby enjoin upon the people so declared to be free to abstain from all violence, unless in necessary self-defence; and I recommend to them that, in all cases when allowed, they labor faithfully for reasonable wages.

. . . I further declare and make known, that such persons of suitable condition, will be received into the armed service of the United States to garrison forts, positions, stations, and other places, and to man vessels of all sorts in said service.

And upon this act, sincerely believed to be an act of justice, warranted by the Constitution ...

In witness whereof, I have hereunto set my hand and caused the seal of the United States to be affixed ...

By the President: ABRAHAM LINCOLN WILLIAM H. SEWARD, Secretary of State

title: Free Citizens Vote
text:
The original Constitution said that enslaved people could not vote. They could not vote because the Constitution considered them three-fifths a person and two-fifths property.

During the Civil War, Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation. It said all enslaved people in the Confederate states were free. But the Constitution had to be changed to make all enslaved people in the U.S. free. It also had to be changed so that African Americans could vote.

The first thing the federal government did was pass the 13th amendment in 1865. It said, “Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude … shall exist within the United States.” This amendment freed enslaved African Americans.

The government made African Americans full citizens by passing the 14th Amendment in 1866. It said, “All persons born or naturalized in the United States … are citizens of the United States.” It said that no state could take a citizen’s rights away. Until the 14th Amendment was passed, no non-European people could be citizens.

After African Americans had been freed and given citizenship, one step still remained. The federal government gave them the right to vote by passing the 15th Amendment in 1869. It said, “The right of citizens of the United States to vote shall not be denied … on account of race, color, or previous condition of servitude.”

title: New Members of Congress
text:
More than 2,000 African Americans were elected to government office between 1868 and 1877. They were elected to local, state, and national positions.

In 1868, there were more African American politicians elected to South Carolina’s state legislature than white politicians. Some of these African Americans were free men before the war. Others had been enslaved.

On February 25, 1870, Hiram Revels of Mississippi became the first African American to take the oath of office for the U.S. Senate. Revels took the place of Jefferson Davis. Davis had resigned from the Senate to become president of the Confederacy. Revels had been a chaplain in the Union Army during the Civil War.

Joseph Rainey of South Carolina was the first African American elected to the House of Representatives. A month later, Jefferson Long of Georgia joined him. Rainey served the longest of any of the African American representatives from the southern states. He worked to establish schools and equal opportunities for emancipated African Americans.

Besides Revels, Rainey, and Long, 16 more African American men were elected to the national capital. Every new member of Congress has to learn the workings of the House and the Senate. Few members of Congress worked with them or treated them as equals. They weren’t given many opportunities to influence laws. They were often met with opposition. Being an African American leader at this time took great courage.

title: Tourism
text:
Tourism is the business of encouraging people to travel for fun. Tourism is an economic activity. People travel to places different from where they live. Cities, states, and even countries have created businesses and resorts for people to shop and stay. These locations are sometimes based on a place's unique physical characteristics. This includes places like oceans, mountains, and national parks. Some tourist attractions are human-made.

Tourism changes a place's physical environment. The more people visit a place, the more accommodations are made. Bringing in visitors requires additional roads, hotels, restaurants, stores, and sites for people to visit. Tourism is an industry that brings a lot of money to cities, states, and countries. It strengthens the economy.

title: Foundations of Government
text:
Government has three major purposes. The first is to provide safety and security for those in the community from threats outside of the community. Second, a government should maintain justice and order within the community. And third, it should help the members of the community meet their wants and needs. The founders of our country created a government to protect the rights of citizens.

There are many different types of government. However, the function of all governments should be to make laws and rules that guarantee and protect the rights of citizens. The government should make sure all people are treated fairly under those laws.

The focus of a government should be to promote the common good. The common good means working to create laws and rules that benefit everyone. To promote the common good, governments provide services to citizens. Examples of services include schools, police and fire departments, public transportation, sanitation, libraries, and more.

Governments protect citizens by creating the rule of law. Rule of law means that both citizens and government leaders must obey the same laws. Everyone must follow the same rules. Every citizen has the same consequences if they break the law. This creates equality under the law.

The roles and responsibilities of governments are outlined in legal documents called constitutions. The United States has a constitution that sets up the federal government. A state constitution is a written contract between the government and the people. State constitutions define the rights and responsibilities of the state government. The people of a state have specific needs, strengths, and ideals. The state’s constitution reflects those.

Pennsylvania has had four different constitutions since 1776. The current constitution was approved in 1968. This constitution has been amended, or changed, 49 times to meet the changing needs of the people of Pennsylvania.

The Pennsylvania Constitution is divided into multiple sections. The first is called the Preamble. A preamble is an introduction to a document that explains its purpose. The current preamble states:

We, the people of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, grateful to Almighty God for the blessings of civil and religious liberty, and humbly invoking His guidance, do ordain and establish this Constitution.

The remaining text is divided into 11 articles or sections.

Section

Purpose

Article I

Lists the rights of every person that are protected by the state government

Article II

Sets up the general assembly

Article III

Sets up the procedures for the passage of laws and defines education as a responsibility of the state

Article IV

Sets up the executive branch of the government

Article V

Sets up the judicial branch of the government

Article VI

Sets up the procedure to establish local governments

Article VII

Establishes the methods of elections

Article VIII

Sets up taxation and finance

Article IX

Sets up the provisions for local governments (area governments, townships, municipalities, and Philadelphia)

Article X

Provides guidelines for private corporations in the state

Article XI

Details the amendment process

title: Pennsylvania's Government Today
text:
Pennsylvania’s state government is responsible for making important decisions for the residents of the state. Pennsylvania is called a commonwealth. This term was used in its first constitution. It was written in 1776, before the United States was formed. The Pennsylvania Constitution divides the government into three branches. The division creates a separation of powers. This allows for a system of check and balances within the state government.

Executive Branch
The executive branch is responsible for signing bills into law, appointing judges, and proposing the state budget. It also oversees all agencies that work within the government. The executive branch is led by the governor and lieutenant governor. A governor is the leader of a state government. The governor of Pennsylvania makes decisions about how the state should be run. The governor also appoints people to different positions in the government. The lieutenant governor helps the governor run the state and leads the meetings of the state senate. If anything ever happened to the governor, the lieutenant governor would act in the governor's place until the governor's term was over.

The executive branch also includes the attorney general, auditor general, state treasurer, and superintendent of public instruction. All of these are elected by residents and serve four-year terms. The attorney general is the head of law enforcement for the state. The auditor general is responsible for ensuring that taxes and other funds are spent legally and properly. The state treasurer is responsible for overseeing all the state’s financial decisions and funds and collecting taxes. The superintendent of public instruction regulates all schools, colleges, and universities in Pennsylvania.

Legislative Branch
The legislative branch is responsible for making laws for the state. Pennsylvania’s legislative branch is called the General Assembly. The General Assembly is the House of Representatives and the Senate. Each representative who serves in the General Assembly is elected by residents. The House of Representatives consists of elected members based on population. They represent districts throughout the state. Pennsylvania’s Senate is made up of 50 senators. Each year, members of the House of Representatives and Senate meet to make new laws and amend existing laws.

Judicial Branch
The job of the state’s judicial branch is to interpret or explain Pennsylvania’s laws. They use those laws to manage conflicts involving residents, companies, and the government. This branch is made up of judges and courts. Judges are elected by the people during general elections. There are many levels of courts in the state that resolve conflict. The highest court in the state is the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

title: Taxes and Government Services
text: One way the government can be sure to protect and meet citizens’ needs is through taxes. Taxes are money that citizens pay to the government. Taxes are also added to the cost of goods and services. The government uses tax money to pay for community services that help people. Government services ensure safety, well-being, and opportunities for citizens to participate in the community. Examples of government services include police and fire departments. Health services are provided by the government and funded by taxes. Parks provide recreation and protect wildlife. Schools and libraries are also government services. Roads, bridges, and transportation services are maintained through taxes paid to the state and local governments.

title: Pennsylvania's Local Governments
text:
The people of Pennsylvania live in school districts, counties, and municipalities.

School districts are responsible for education. A locally elected school board determines what is taught in that district. They also make decisions about after-school activities, faculty, and administration.

Each county’s government is a division, or region. It is designed to conduct elections and provide for the welfare of the people. County governments are responsible for health services and social programs. They also oversee emergency services, law enforcement, courts, and prison facilities.

Cities, boroughs, towns, and townships are divisions of a county. They're all called municipalities. This level of government affects the daily lives of people more than other levels of government. Municipalities make decisions on public safety, zoning, and maintenance of roads and bridges.

Municipalities are the areas where voting in elections occur. Citizens vote in their communities at identified polling locations. Polling locations are places where people can go to vote. The votes are counted by municipal authorities. Results are given to the county officials. Those officials then give the results to the state office of elections.

title: Working to Solve Problems
text:
Issues in a community can impact the daily lives of residents. Common community issues in Pennsylvania include transportation, water quality, and access to clean water. Funding for education and rising taxes are also common issues. Citizens can work with their local, state, and federal leaders to solve problems. People can attend meetings and contact their representatives. This can help make sure their opinions and ideas are heard.

One way that we can solve problems is by engaging in civil discourse. Civil discourse helps people have conversations about their community. Civil discourse should be respectful of other people’s opinions. It should consider different points of view. You practice civil discourse by talking in appropriate ways with other people. It helps build understanding about an issue or problem. Although there are people with different opinions, practicing civil discourse reminds us to treat others with respect. Steps that people can use to work together to solve problems in their community include:

State the problem in a way that everyone can understand.

Identify potential causes for the problem.

Reach out to experts to brainstorm possible solutions. Some experts may include teachers, parents, and community helpers.

Suggest solutions to address the problem and create a plan.

Attempt to solve the problem.

Reflect on the plan and make changes if needed.

Citizens and elected leaders can work together to overcome issues. They can improve conditions in communities, states, and countries. They can do it by practicing civil discourse and community problem-solving.

title: Rights and Responsibilities
text:
People have many different rights. These include unalienable, civil, political, and economic rights. Rights have different functions. Unalienable rights, also called natural rights, are rights that people are born with and cannot be taken away. The Declaration of Independence defines these rights as the right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

Civil rights protect people from the actions of government, organizations, or other people. The United States government, organizations, and other people cannot prohibit the rights of citizens to:

vote

a fair trial by jury

government services

due process of the law (legal actions or proceedings that must be followed)

serve in the military

serve in public office

equality through the law

assemble or petition the government

freedom of speech

freedom of religion

freedom of the press

Political rights allow people to participate freely in government. People can protect their civil rights through political rights. These rights are defined in the Constitution and the Bill of Rights at the federal level. They are defined at the state level in state constitutions. Examples of political rights include:

voting

serving on a jury

holding political office

attending protests

petitioning the government through action and/or speech

supporting social or political issues

expressing ideas in speech and the press

joining a political party

equal access to public services

Economic rights are financial choices and privileges that individuals may select without government interference. These rights enable people to make use of civil and political rights. Economic rights include the right to:

own property

change employment

operate a business

join a labor union

access polling places

meet basic wants and needs

multiple economic opportunities

not be required to pay fees and taxes based on race, gender, ethnicity, religion, or sexual orientation

Responsibilities

Voting
Voting is a formal process. It allows people to express their opinions and choose elected leaders. It helps leaders make decisions for a community. It's important to be informed about current issues and the people who are running for public office.

To vote, citizens must first register as a legal voter in their state. Citizens must be at least 18 years old. They need to live in the community where they are voting. All citizens can vote. It is a right and a responsibility of being a citizen. Many people throughout history have made many sacrifices so that all citizens can vote, regardless of gender, race, or economic status.

During elections, citizens find out the voting location in their community. A voting location is also known as a polling place. This might be at a school or community building in their neighborhood. There, they vote on issues and candidates. At the polling place, citizens have to prove their identity. They can only vote one time per election. The final step for citizens is to submit their vote.

Serving on a Jury
One responsibility that citizens have is to serve on a jury when called. Juries are important. They help decide if someone who has been accused of a crime is guilty of breaking the law. This is an important part of our country’s legal system. It can only work properly if responsible citizens participate. People who are at least 18 years old are sometimes called to jury duty. A jury is a group of six to 12 people. They are chosen to help decide a court case. In the United States, people are guaranteed a “jury of your peers.” This means that the jury will be made up of citizens from the same area.

If you are selected to serve on a jury, you will participate in hearing the court case. Most of the time, this will only be a few days. In some rare instances, cases can go on for months. After everyone has heard both sides of the issue, the jury deliberates. Deliberate means to discuss what they saw and heard and make a decision. Jury members should use reason and logic when making their decision.

In a criminal court, a jury must reach a unanimous decision. This means that all jurors agree on the verdict, or outcome. Juries must deliberate until they reach a unanimous decision. If they can’t, the case may have to start all over with another trial and a different jury.

Volunteering
Responsible citizens who want to give back to their community, state, country, or the world can volunteer. That means they donate their time to help others. Many people volunteer because they want to help others in need. There are many ways that people can volunteer in their community. Food banks collect canned goods. They also deliver food to people in need. Other programs teach people to read. Some volunteers even build homes for people.

Public Service
Citizens can participate in their community and solve community problems through public service. Public service is when people perform activities to make their community a better place. Any citizen can perform public service, regardless of their job. Public service can also include serving in government offices, elected positions, and in the military.

title: What Makes a Good Citizen?
text:
Good citizens help our governments work well. Citizens have the responsibility to behave in certain ways. Civic virtues are personal behaviors and actions that help improve communities. For example, good citizens are friendly and kind. They are willing to donate their time to help others. Good citizens respect others and themselves. They treat others civilly, or politely. They work together for the common good. They are responsible in their daily lives.

Citizens have the responsibility to participate in government. They educate themselves about government issues. They vote in elections. They respectfully hold public officials to their word. Good citizens are necessary for successful communities.

title: Voting
text:
Voting is one of our most important civic responsibilities. Voting is a formal process in which a group of people expresses their opinion. This helps inform decisions in their community. An important part of voting is being informed about the issue and the people that are running for public office. Voter guides provide background information on the candidates and ballot measures. These guides list the candidates running in each race and offer details on each one’s experience and goals. You can also be informed by listening to speeches, reading the news, and learning how each candidate feels about important issues. Good voters gather information from reliable sources. They use this information to inform their opinion.

To vote, citizens must first register as a legal voter. Citizens must be at least 18 years old and live in the community where they are voting. All citizens can vote. This is a right and a responsibility of being a citizen. Many people throughout history have made many sacrifices so that all citizens can vote, regardless of gender, race, or economic status.

During elections, citizens find out the voting location in their community. A voting location is also known as a polling place. This might be at a school or community building in their neighborhood. There they vote on issues and candidates. At the polling place, citizens have to prove their identity because they can only vote one time per election. How you submit your vote differs by location. You might vote using a computer or a paper ballot.

Presidential elections are held every four years. They are always on the second Tuesday in November. National elections take place every two years, on even-numbered years. State and local elections can occur at other times throughout the year. This includes primary and special elections. The right to vote is a privilege and a responsibility of all citizens.

title: Location
text:
People use geographic representations, such as maps and globes, to acquire, process, and report spatial information. Maps help people learn about an area and determine where something is located. Geographers describe places with both relative and absolute location.

The relative location of a place tells us where a place is relative to, or compared to, something else. When we are describing the relative location of a place, we use words such as “by,” “near,” “above,” and “below.” If your friend tells you that their house is “down the street and across from the supermarket,” they are using relative location.

A place’s absolute location is its exact location. Absolute location is more helpful when you’re trying to find an unfamiliar place. The absolute location of a place could be its physical address or coordinates. Coordinates are numbers and letters located along the margins of a map that help you find a place’s location. Coordinates can be used on a map with a grid line system. A grid line system, which uses lines of longitude and latitude, is also used to find a place’s absolute location. Vertical lines of longitude go around the Earth from the North Pole to the South Pole. These lines of longitude show how far east or west places are from the Prime Meridian. We also call these lines “meridians.” Horizontal lines of latitude show how far north and south places are from the Equator. Cartographers use these lines to divide maps into small squares. These squares can be labeled with numbers, letters, or both. These squares make finding locations easier.

title: Coordinate and Alphanumeric Grids
text:
Geographers use many tools to determine location on maps. Coordinates help geographers determine the absolute location of a place. Coordinates can help you find a place’s location on a map. A coordinate grid uses lines of latitude and longitude to locate places on a map. The grid lines indicate where a place is located. You can use the coordinate grid on the map provided to determine the locations of places in South America. What lines of latitude and longitude intersect, or cross, in Brazil?

Geographers also use alphanumeric grids to determine location. An alphanumeric grid is a grid that uses grid lines with letters and numbers to help you describe an absolute location on a map. Like a map that includes a coordinate grid, lines on an alphanumeric grid map form small squares. These squares can be identified using coordinates that contain one letter and one number. When using an alphanumeric grid, you should determine the letter, then the number of the coordinate. For example, La Paz, the capital of Bolivia, is located at I, 5.

title: Climate
text:
Climate is a physical characteristic of a place. Climate is the average weather conditions of a place over an extended period of time. While the weather can change in just a few hours, climate takes hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperatures, precipitation, and wind in an area. Precipitation includes rain, snow, hail, and sleet.

There are five climate zones found on the Earth. These are tropical, dry, temperate, continental, and polar. Tropical climates are hot, wet, and humid. This is because these areas have high average temperatures and large amounts of rainfall. Areas located near the Equator usually have a tropical climate. Dry climate zones, on the other hand, have very little precipitation. Places with a dry climate experience very little rainfall.

Temperatures vary depending on a location’s latitude and longitude. These areas can be very cold or very hot. Areas with a temperate climate have warm summers and cold winters. Continental climates are dry. They have very hot summers and very cold winters.

Polar regions are cold and dry and are located in the far north and far south of the world. These regions are extremely cold throughout most of the year. Even though snow falls through the winter, the climate is relatively dry.

A person who studies climate is called a climatologist. Climatologists study and observe an area’s climate over a long period of time. Climatologists also make predictions about future climate patterns. Climate affects trade, agriculture, clothing, and the foods people eat. Climate is a big part of our daily lives.

title: Equator and Latitude
text: We divide up the world for mapping purposes. Imagine a horizontal line that runs around the middle of the world. Cartographers draw this imaginary line on many of the maps they make. They call this line the Equator. The Equator divides the Earth into hemispheres. A hemisphere is a division on Earth between north and south or east and west. The Northern Hemisphere includes all of the land and oceans that are north of the Equator. The Southern Hemisphere includes everything to the south. The Equator crosses parts of South America, Asia, and Africa. Horizontal lines of latitude run east and west around the Earth. These lines show how far north or south places are from the Equator. We call these latitude lines parallels.

title: Climate
text:
Climate is a physical characteristic of a place. Climate is the average weather conditions of a place over an extended period of time. While the weather can change in just a few hours, climate takes hundreds, thousands, and even millions of years to change. Climate includes the average temperature, precipitation, and wind in an area. Precipitation includes rain, snow, and sleet. There are five climate zones that we find on the Earth. These are dry, continental, temperate, tropical, and polar.

Tropical climates are hot, wet, and humid. This is because these areas have high average temperatures and large amounts of rainfall. Areas located around the Equator usually have a tropical climate.

A dry climate zone is hot with little precipitation. Places with dry climates experience very little rainfall. Temperatures vary depending on a location's latitude and longitude. These areas can be very cold or very hot.

Areas with a temperate climate have warm summers and cold winters.

Continental climates are dry. They have very hot summers and very cold winters.

Polar climates are cold and dry. They are in the north and south of the world. These regions are extremely cold most of the year. Even though snow falls through the winter, the climate is relatively dry.

Climate affects trade, agriculture, farming, the way people dress, and food consumption. Climate is a big part of our daily lives!

title: Plant Survival: Did You Know?
text: When was the last time you tried to grow a flower or plant? Maybe you put it in a cup on the windowsill or in your front yard. Did you make sure it would get enough sunlight? Did you water it every day? Why did you put the plant in soil? Was it because that’s where the plant gets its “food,” or the material it needs to grow? Some people may think this, but it’s not quite true. Soil provides plants with three things: access to water, access to nutrients, and a solid foundation for the roots. That’s it. The material that plants use to grow tall doesn’t come from the soil; it comes mostly from the air and water! But you may be wondering, “How could plant matter come from the air?” Remember that the air is filled with invisible gas particles, which are matter. Plants take in air through their leaves and water through their roots. Then, the parts that make plants green absorb the sun’s energy to turn the air and water particles into food. Sunlight doesn’t provide any matter to plants to help them grow, but its energy gets this process moving. Without all of these elements, plants would not be able to survive and grow. Did you notice that soil wasn’t mentioned? Soil can certainly help plants, but it isn’t necessary. Plants don’t “eat” soil. Just like other organisms, plants have needs. And if those needs aren’t met, they will not thrive.

title: Who Were the Sumerians?
text:
Many ancient cultures are associated with the land of Mesopotamia. The Sumerians, Assyrians, Akkadians, and Babylonians interacted with each other for thousands of years. The Sumerians were the first group to organize themselves in southern Mesopotamia. They settled the area around 4000 B.C.E. Their neighbors, the Akkadians, who later settled in the north, called Sumer the “land of the civilized people.”

We don’t know where the Sumerians came from before they settled in Mesopotamia. One of the reasons is that their language isn’t similar to any other language we know about. Languages are one of the main ways researchers track where people come from and where they go. Because the Sumerian language isn’t like any other known language, we can’t connect the Sumerians to any other place or people.

Mesopotamia was centrally located between the Egyptian civilization and the Indus Valley civilization. The exchange of knowledge, languages, and cultures that took place in Sumer had a lasting impact on writing, technology, communication, trade, religion, and law. By the time the Sumerians were conquered by invading forces thousands of years after settling in the area, they had established a culture that would go down in history as a powerful and innovative influence.

title: Week 7 Framing Question
text: What factors helped the Sumerians build a successful civilization?

title: Innovation and Growth
text:
The people of Mesopotamia were inventive. In an effort to improve their lives, they created new things. They must have observed existing problems and then proposed and tested solutions to them. This is similar to the way people today use the scientific method. We refer to these inventions and innovations as technology.

Sumerian farmers needed stronger tools. They learned how to work metal. They made bronze hand tools, like hammers, sickles, axes, and hoes. By 3000 B.C.E., they had invented the plow. All of these inventions and new technologies made it easier for them to grow more food. This led to economic growth and prosperity for everyone.

The Sumerians were some of the first people to use copper. Archaeologists have found evidence of copper-making in the ruins of 6,000-year-old Sumerian cities. Some of the objects discovered include copper chisels, razors, and weapons, such as spearheads and arrows.

Historians believe the wheel was invented because of a need for more pottery. Placing the clay on a wheel that could be turned helped people create pottery faster than they could when they were just using their hands. They could now make large quantities of pots and jars to collect and store food. This supported a larger population in the cities and gave them surplus items that could be used for trade. At some point, the potter’s wheel was adapted and used to make carts and, later, chariots, for transporting goods and traveling.

Sumerian shepherds spent their evenings looking at the stars. They made some of the world’s first astronomical discoveries. They mapped the stars into constellations and were aware of at least five planets. The Sumerians were the first to develop the system of tracking time with 60-second minutes and 60-minute hours.

title: Trade and Transportation
text:
New tools and inventions helped the Sumerians become strong traders as well as good farmers. Traveling on land was difficult and sometimes even dangerous. Since they lived between the Euphrates and Tigris Rivers, the people of Mesopotamia began to look for ways to transport their goods by water. They started by building simple wooden boats. Then they wanted to travel faster and needed to be able to guide the boats when the water was rough, so they added a sail. The sailboats helped the people travel greater distances.

Merchants could then travel over land and sea to trade. Mesopotamians developed some of the first trade routes in the world. Some trips were short, but sometimes they traveled for months at a time. Their trade routes reached east to India, west to the Mediterranean, north to the Caspian Sea, and south to ancient Ethiopia.

The land where the people of Sumer lived was arid and bare, with little wood or stone. So they traded crops, pottery, and other surplus items for these needed materials. They also traded for gold, silver, copper, and other valuable metals and gemstones.

With the materials and resources brought back from other areas, there was more innovation to meet wants and needs. Sumerian craftspeople specialized and became potters, jewelers, artists, blacksmiths, and weavers. Two important roles were bricklayers and builders. As the economy became more advanced, the Sumerian population grew. As there was not much stone or wood, the people built with mud bricks. They learned how to create large quantities of brick at a time. They began to build complex cities.

title: City-States
text:
The people of Mesopotamia built city-states. A city-state is a large town or city and includes nearby farms and houses. Each city-state had a strong wall around it for protection. Each city-state operated like a small country and was ruled by a different leader. Sumerian city-states shared a common language, but they each had their own laws and worshiped different gods or goddesses. They often traded with one another. They also fought with one another. Sometimes city-states joined together to form alliances. This made them stronger against invading forces.

Two of the strongest Sumerian city-states were Ur and Uruk. Ur was an important city-state in southern Mesopotamia. It was near the mouth of the Euphrates on the Persian Gulf. This made it an important center of trade. Archaeologists have discovered a cemetery with royal tombs containing treasures in gold, silver, bronze, and semiprecious stones. These artifacts are evidence that the people of Ur had wealth, a strong economy, and a highly developed society.

The city of Uruk was also located in the southern region of Sumer. It is considered the world’s first big city. By 3,000 B.C.E., Uruk had 40,000–50,000 people, and after another few hundred years, it grew to have 50,000–80,000 inhabitants. For comparison, that is similar in size to the modern city of Lake Charles, Louisiana. Uruk is most famous for its legendary king Gilgamesh, the origin of writing, and the building of great stone structures.

Sadly, these city-states, built mostly with mud bricks, did not stand up to time. As centuries passed, structures eroded, and sand covered many of the ruins. No one saw evidence of the Sumerians until just a few hundred years ago.

title: Sumerian Writing
text:
In 1877, archaeologists were given permission to excavate the mound of Tello. Over the next 25 years, they explored the entire area and uncovered the Sumerian capital of Lagash. They found many important artifacts that provided information about the people of Sumer. Among the most valuable discoveries were approximately 30,000 clay tablets with Sumerian writing on them.

Cuneiform

About 3500 B.C.E., people in Sumer began keeping records of goods and trading. Scribes (writers) used sharp sticks to carve images, or pictograms, into wet clay tablets to represent objects or ideas. When the clay dried, the writing became permanent. Important information could then be shared from one place to another without messengers needing to remember all the details.

Drawing detailed pictures into the clay took time. So the Sumerians made it easier by pressing wedge-shaped symbols into the clay to represent the pictures. By 1800 B.C.E., there were more than 700 written symbols. These symbols are called cuneiform. The Sumerians wrote detailed information about crops, livestock, and trade. They wrote about breeding and sales, including who bought their animals, how many animals were sold, and how much the animals were sold for.

The Epic of Gilgamesh

The Sumerians also used tablets to write down stories, such as the Epic of Gilgamesh. In 1850, 12 clay tablets were found. They were inscribed with the tale of a hero’s journey. It tells of the adventures of two warriors, King Gilgamesh and his friend Enkidu. It is considered one of the oldest examples of written literature.

Code of Hammurabi

Cuneiform was also used to write the Code of Hammurabi. The Code was a collection of laws. Some of them became the basis for present-day laws. The laws did not allow for excuses or mistakes. Around 1780 B.C.E., King Hammurabi, the ruler of the Babylonians, ordered the laws to be written on a huge black stone. It was displayed for all to see, so no one could say they did not know the law. The laws were based on the principle of “an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.” This principle meant that any punishment should be equal to the crime.

title: Sumerian Religion
text:
The people who lived in ancient Mesopotamia were polytheistic. That means they worshiped many different gods and goddesses. The Sumerians believed their gods controlled wars, diseases, crops, and flooding. When bad things happened, people believed the gods were angry. The Sumerian people believed that the gods lived on mountaintops. When they moved away from the mountains and into the Fertile Crescent, the people must have worried that the gods would not follow them to the flat land. Sumerian leaders decided to build mountains of their own as places for the gods to live. The first ziggurat was built around 3000 B.C.E. The word “ziggurat” means “man-made mountain.” Ziggurats were built as temples or dwelling places for the gods. They were usually tall and had several tiers, or levels. There were stairways for the gods to travel to and from heaven. These temples quickly became the most important part of each city. One of a ruler’s most important jobs was to take care of their ziggurat.

Ancient Mesopotamians also believed in life after death and thought they could take possessions with them into the next life. They believed in a land below our world, often known as the "Great Below." They trusted that everyone went there after death, no matter their social status or their actions during life.

title: Ancient Israelites
text:
Remember that the region of Mesopotamia was home to many cultures in addition to the Sumerians. The Akkadian Empire had a strong influence across Mesopotamia for almost 200 years. The Babylonian Empire formed north of Sumeria and the Assyrian Empire north of that. The history of the Jews also began in Mesopotamia. A prophet, named Abraham, is considered the father of the Jewish civilization. He was born around 2000 B.C.E. in Ur.

The Sumerians believed in many gods, but Abraham believed in one true God. He left Ur and traveled to a new land, known as Canaan. Abraham had many descendants. Around 1200 B.C.E., they lived as twelve separate tribes along the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea. However, there were larger nations nearby, and the tribes needed to defend themselves. So they gathered under one government and became known as Israel.

By 1000 B.C.E., Israel had separated into two kingdoms, one in the north and one in the south. The northern kingdom was called Israel. The southern kingdom was called Judah. In 722 B.C.E., the Kingdom of Israel was conquered by the Assyrians. In 586 B.C.E., the Kingdom of Judah was conquered by the Babylonians, and the people of Judah were forced to leave their homeland. A few hundred years later, Cyrus the Great, emperor of Persia, allowed them to return to their homeland.

In the years that followed, the Israelites faced more conquest, change, and heartbreak and were eventually scattered all across the world. The people relied on their laws and beliefs to help them through these hardships. The Israelite faith became the religion known today as Judaism. The followers of Judaism are known as Jews. Judaism would eventually influence both Christianity and Islam.

title: Important Achievements of the Ancient Israelites
text:
During their time in exile, the Israelites began to write sacred texts. They wrote about their history and religion. The writings are gathered in what we know today as the Hebrew Bible, or the Tanakh. It is the most important work of ancient Hebrew literature. Hebrew is a very old writing system. It is written and read from right to left. Many words in English come from Hebrew. Some of these include “amen,” “cherub,” “hallelujah,” “camel,” and “cider.”

The Israelites dedicated themselves to agriculture and raising livestock. The area they lived in was dry, and there was little water, so they had to work hard to farm the land. They relied heavily on water from the River Jordan. They grew olives and grapes, grains, and lentils. They invented olive presses and wine presses. Hebrew writers called Canaan “a land flowing with milk and honey.”

Israelites valued music and used it in celebrations and religious ceremonies. They played harps, tambourines, and flutes. Artisans made goods from gold, copper, and ivory. Common themes in ancient Israelite art include plants and animals and symbols adapted from Egyptian art. The ancient Israelites are also known for their skills in building. They built royal palaces, great homes for the nobles, city walls with gated entryways, and large temples. These large structures were often built with stone that was cut into brick shapes using a chisel and a hammer. King Solomon’s temple was built in Jerusalem out of cut limestone, cedar wood, and gold.

The ancient Israelites were also known for their military. Iron was the most common metal available, and it was used to create armor and weapons. One of the most important developments was the iron chariot. Before the iron chariot, most battles were fought using hand-to-hand combat with spears, swords, or axes. But when the iron chariot was introduced, battle styles changed. Each chariot had two horses in front and a driver, or charioteer. Behind the driver was a soldier with a bow and arrows.

title: The Akkadian Empire
text:
Geography

The people of the Akkadian Empire first lived in northern Mesopotamia. Their army marched south. They took control of cities along the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. The empire spread until it covered all of Mesopotamia. Upper Mesopotamia begins in the foothills of the mountains of Turkey. Those mountains are where both the Tigris and Euphrates rivers begin. The region is full of gentle hills and flat, alluvial plains. Alluvial plains are created when rivers deposit rich soil to an area over time. Upper Mesopotamia is also home to one of the world’s largest salt flats, the Sabkhat al-Jabbul. Salt flats form in areas like deserts. This is where water evaporates at a rate greater than rain falls.

Religion

The Akkadian people were polytheistic. They worshiped a group of gods. They thought the gods had human forms and emotions. Gods could become happy or angry. Akkadians believed they needed to serve the gods and keep them happy. The people also believed that their king was their gods’ representative. This belief meant kings like Sargon were very powerful. Rulers often became even more powerful by appointing friends and family members to powerful positions.

Economy

The Akkadians relied on agriculture in their economy. The alluvial plains of Upper Mesopotamia were a good place to grow many types of grain. The Akkadians also used the land of the people they invaded to the south. Fields in southern Mesopotamia were irrigated. They produced enough food for trade. Akkadians built friendships and trading deals with people in many places. Many of these people spoke both the Sumerian and Akkadian. This made it easier to build roads, a postal system, and a calendar. These all became useful tools that made the economy even stronger.

Political and Social Structure

Sargon established the idea of an Akkadian dynasty. A dynasty is a series of rulers from the same family. His idea was that the power to rule the empire should be passed down from father to son. This idea worked for around 140 years. Then the empire declined and collapsed. Five different kings ruled during that time. Sargon and his descendants built and maintained the empire by using military power. Female relatives were given positions of religious influence, such as high priestess. Sons and male family members became governors and leaders. They were appointed to manage land, control trade, and oversee the growth of communities. Experts do not know much about how the rest of society worked. Historians think people were divided into different social classes. These classes had different amounts of power. The ideas that advanced the Akkadians resulted in new patterns that would be repeated throughout history. Can you think of what some of those patterns might be?

title: The Continuing Legacy of Mesopotamia
text:
Mesopotamia gave birth to a lot of civilizations over the centuries. Babylon was one of these. It was a great center of power, wealth, and culture. Its importance also made it a target for attack and invasion. Babylon's book of history has five major chapters, with many different groups of people in charge.

Amorites Expand Babylon: 1894 B.C.E. to 1595 B.C.E.

King Hammurabi ruled from 1792 to 1750 B.C.E. In addition to writing a strict code of law, Hammurabi did many important things while he was king. He conquered all of the city-states in the area. He helped Babylon grow until it included southern Mesopotamia and land that is now known as northern Iraq. After Hammurabi's death, Amorite control continued for another 150 years. It was broken when the Hittites conquered Babylon in 1595 B.C.E. The Hittites were a group that used iron weapons.

Kassites Take Charge: 1570 B.C.E. to 1158 B.C.E.

The Kassites began their 400 years of rule in about 1570 B.C.E. During this time, Babylon became a center of literature and religion. The Kassites introduced the use of horses. They were the first to use boundary stones to mark their territory. They may have been the first to use molded bricks to form figures on their temples. They helped Babylon become famous for its art, architecture, science, astronomy, jewelry, textiles, and medicines.

Assyrians Rise to Power: Around 1200 B.C.E. to 612 B.C.E.

The Assyrians rose to power and battled with Babylon for hundreds of years. Their capital was the city of Nineveh. The Assyrians were among the first warriors to ride horses and carry iron weapons. After Babylonian King Nebuchadnezzar I died in 1103 B.C.E., the Assyrians kept control for a while, but they eventually withdrew.

Chaldeans Seal Babylon's Fate: 627 B.C.E. to 539 B.C.E.

Like the Akkadians, the Chaldeans were a Semitic-speaking group that lived in Mesopotamia. One of their leaders was Nebuchadnezzar II. He is best remembered for conquering Syria and Palestine and destroying Jerusalem in 587 B.C.E. The Chaldeans sent the captured Jews to Babylon. Some people believe that Nebuchadnezzar was the person who built the Hanging Gardens of Babylon. The Hanging Gardens were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. The ancient Greeks described these gardens as sitting on top of towers that were 400 feet square and 75 feet above the ground. Nebuchadnezzar II also rebuilt the great Temple of Marduk. This was to honor Babylon's god. Under Nebuchadnezzar's rule, Babylon was the greatest business center of the Middle East.

Babylon Dies: Around 300 B.C.E.

The Persian emperor, Cyrus the Great, took control of Babylon in 539 B.C.E. About 200 years later, the empire fell to Alexander the Great. Alexander wanted to make Babylon his capital. He appreciated the city’s greatness. He ordered his people to tear down the temple and rebuild it even larger and grander. When Alexander died in 323 B.C.E., all of his plans fell apart. Babylon was eventually abandoned. One of the greatest empires in ancient history had come to an end.

title: The Assyrians
text:
For hundreds of years, different groups fought for control of Babylon. The Assyrians were the most successful of these groups. They ruled from 1200 B.C.E. to 612 B.C.E. Assyrian kings ruled over the land, had great wealth, and led powerful armies. Many historians think that Assyria was the greatest Mesopotamian empire.

Geography

The Assyrian Empire began in the city of Assur. The city was named after the temple of the god Assur. The city was located on the western bank of the Tigris River. As years passed, the empire grew until it reached all the way through Mesopotamia, from present-day Türkiye to Egypt. The Assyrians built a new capital where the Tigris and Khosr rivers meet. The new capital was called Nineveh. It was surrounded by great farmland. Assyrian leaders spent more time fighting wars and taking over new lands. They never took advantage of the fertile plains.

Politics and Government

The Assyrians were one of the first warrior people of the ancient world. They wanted to build an empire and were not afraid to use violence. They fought other city-states and took over a lot of new land. One reason they won so many battles was because they had iron weapons. Most of the people they fought against used bronze, which is much weaker. Assyrians also attacked cities with battering rams and wheeled towers. Battering rams could break through walls. Towers protected soldiers as they moved closer to a city.

Economy

Many Assyrian towns and cities became important centers of trade. These cities made a lot of money for the empire. The city of Nineveh was built where the Tigris and Khosr rivers meet. It was also on a major highway for people traveling to and from the Mediterranean Sea. It became an important place. It united people from both the East and the West. Traders who used the city as a place to buy and sell goods often became very rich.

title: The People of Phoenicia
text:
Sea Traders

The Phoenicians did not have much room for growing their own crops. Without much land for farms, they turned to the Mediterranean Sea and became traders. Phoenician traders traveled to many different civilizations all over the region. They used sand along the coast to make glassware to trade. They became master glassblowers. They were the first to mass-produce glass for trading. They also traded metal objects, pottery, cedar timber, and wood products. They came home with silver, ostrich plumes, ivory, and tin. They also brought back an Egyptian form of paper called papyrus.

Ancient Rest Areas

If you were traveling by sea as much as the Phoenicians did, wouldn’t it be nice to have a home away from home: a place where you could stop, repair your ship, and get fresh food and water? The Phoenicians established colonies along the Mediterranean Sea to do just that. Look at the maps to see some of the Phoenician colonies. The Phoenicians used the North Star to help them navigate out on the open sea. Closer to shore, the sailors used the coastline to keep track of where they were as they traveled from village to village.

The Purple People Get Their Name

The Phoenicians were famous for making a beautiful purple dye. Clothes and fabrics in that color became highly prized. Some experts think that Cleopatra used a purple sail on her ship. Roman Emperor Nero wrote a law that made it illegal for anyone but him to wear the color.

The purple dye is also where the Phoenicians got their name. The Greeks who bought the reddish-purple cloth called the traders “phoinikes,” which means “red people.” As time passed, the name changed into the word “Phoenician.”

Legend of the Origin of Purple

The legend about the first discovery of purple dye features Melqart, the god of the city of Tyre. He was walking along the shore of the Mediterranean Sea with his dog and his girlfriend. His dog came upon a murex snail and quickly chomped down on it. The dog’s mouth and teeth turned a beautiful shade of purple-red. His girlfriend demanded that Melqart make her a robe of the beautiful color, or she’d have nothing more to do with him. Melqart gathered some of the murex snails and had his people create the first robe made of purple cloth. The color purple might not seem like an important thing to history. Do you think this discovery was relevant to the history of the Phoenicians?

The Phoenician Alphabet

In the time of the Phoenicians, writing systems were mostly based on pictures. Imagine having to do your homework in pictures; that would take lots of time. The Phoenicians needed a quick and easy way to record their purchases and sales, so they developed an alphabet. Their alphabet contained 22 letters, and each symbol stood for a sound. Writing was done horizontally, from right to left, with no spaces between words. Later, dots and dashes were added to separate words and make it easier to read. Although Phoenicians first used wax tablets as paper, they eventually used Egyptian papyrus instead. The Phoenicians shared their writing system with everyone they met as they traveled the Mediterranean Sea. That’s why the Phoenicians are often called the “carriers of civilization.” Other cultures, such as the Greeks and the Romans, adopted the Phoenician writing system but tweaked it a bit. Over time, that alphabet changed and became the one we know today. Although the Phoenicians invented the alphabet, they left behind very few written records of their rich culture.

Life in Phoenicia

Phoenicia did not have a central government or leader. Each city-state had its own temples, gods, and a king. Different city-states worshipped different gods and goddesses. The king was at the top of the social structure. Workers and merchants made up the middle class, and servants made up the lower class. Women could become high priestesses in the temples. Phoenicia eventually came under the control of leaders like Cyrus the Great and Alexander the Great.

title: Inventions, Innovators, and a Growth Mindset
text:
Innovation is taking something that exists and improving it. Invention is the creation of something totally new. Invention and innovation almost always overlap.

Before the invention of the modern light bulb, people could only see by sunlight or firelight. Then, Thomas Edison changed the world. Edison created many light bulbs that didn’t work, but he didn’t give up. Edison demonstrated a growth mindset. A growth mindset is a way of talking to yourself that helps you accept growth and change. He even said, “I have gotten a lot of results! I know several thousand things that won’t work!”

Innovations are essential to cultural and technological progress. Society needs people who use their setbacks as motivation to make a lasting impact on the world.

title: The Code of Hammurabi
text:
Although the Code of Hammurabi is not the oldest written set of laws, it is probably the best-preserved. Toward the end of his life, King Hammurabi, the ruler of the Babylonians from 1792 to 1750 B.C.E., collected all of the ancient Sumerian laws and ordered the laws be written on a huge black stone. More than six feet tall, the stone pillar is called a stela and was placed where everyone could see the laws, even though few people could read. Many legal historians consider it to be a primitive, or ancient, constitution.

The stone was covered with 282 paragraphs of laws written in cuneiform. The laws showed that there were different classes of people and different punishments depending on your class. The code was used as a basis for some modern laws. It covers legal decisions about family law, such as marriage and divorce, and economic laws about trade, taxes, and prices. It also covers criminal law about such things as theft and violence. In fact, these historical codes are so well-respected that a wall of the U.S. Supreme Court Building shows an image of Hammurabi receiving them. The Code of Hammurabi was excavated in 1901 by French archaeologist Jean-Vincent Scheil. Today, it can be seen in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

title: Exploring Space
text: The Chinese were the first to invent and use rocketry technology. They invented it around 800 C.E. In 1300 C.E., gunpowder began to be used in Europe. It was used in rockets, cannonballs, and bombs. Germany was one of the European countries that refined rocketry. The United States and the Soviet Union both used and improved Germany's rocket technology. By 1955, rocketry had improved to the point that both the Soviet Union and the United States began working on launching satellites into space. The Soviet Union was the first. They launched Sputnik I into Earth’s orbit in 1957. The United States put its first satellite in orbit on January 31, 1958.

title: Week 31 Framing Question
text: What was the impact of the Space Race?

title: Neil Armstrong
text:
Neil Armstrong was born in 1930 in Ohio. As a child, he wanted to grow up to fly airplanes. He went to college at Purdue University. Then, he served as a Navy pilot from 1949 to 1952. Later, he became the test pilot for the X-15 rocket plane. Armstrong became an astronaut in 1962. Seven years later, Armstrong did something that no one had ever thought possible: he walked on the moon.

It was the first time a human had ever stepped foot on the moon. As he stepped onto the moon's surface, Armstrong said, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." Armstrong retired from the astronaut program in 1970. He continued working for NASA. Later, he taught at the University of Cincinnati. Armstrong received many awards. One of these awards was the Medal of Freedom. This was for his walking on the moon, where no person had gone before.

title: Human Computers
text:
In the 1940s and 1950s computers hadn't been invented. People had to solve problems and do calculations by hand. These people were called human computers. Human computers worked for many organizations. One of these organizations was called NACA. NACA stands for National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics. NACA came before our current space program, NASA.

NACA hired human computers to help them figure out how to launch a rocket into space. NACA needed to know exact details about how much fuel was needed and what path to take. The human computers figured out the answers. Most of the human computers were women.

One of these women was Dorothy Vaughan. She was hired to work for the NACA in 1943. Vaughan taught herself programming. She later became the first African American supervisor for NASA.

Mary Jackson joined Vaughan’s team. Jackson was also an African American woman who worked as a human computer. Her goal was to become an aerospace engineer. To achieve this goal, Jackson worked hard to get permission to take advanced courses in a "whites only" college. There, she earned her engineering degree. She became NASA's first African American female engineer.

Katherine Johnson joined the team of human computers in 1953. She was a physicist, space scientist, and mathematician. She was so good at her job that she was asked to help calculate astronaut John Glenn's orbit around the Earth. She also helped astronauts land on the moon.

These women had to overcome racial barriers during the Space Race. They worked hard and opened the door for others to succeed.

title: Sally Ride
text:
As a child, Sally Ride loved sports and science. Ride was always encouraged to explore her interests by her parents. They bought her a chemistry set and telescope.

As a young adult, she went to Stanford University. There, she majored in physics. She also played on the women's tennis team. After she graduated in 1978, she applied to work for NASA. Eight thousand people applied to work for NASA. Ride and only 34 other people were picked for the job. In 1983, Ride became the first American woman to go into space. She traveled into space on the space shuttle, Challenger. Ride later developed a robotic arm that space shuttles would use to launch and retrieve satellites.

title: Mae Jemison
text:
Mae Jemison was born in Alabama in 1956. Jemison grew up wanting to learn more about the world around her. She knew she wanted to be a scientist at a young age. She earned a scholarship to Stanford University at age 16. She faced discrimination because of her race and gender. Jemison did not let this hold her back. She graduated from Stanford with a degree in chemical engineering and African American Studies. She then went on to earn a medical degree at Cornell University.

In 1987, Jemison applied to NASA’s astronaut program. Over 2,000 applications were submitted. She was accepted as one of 15 candidates. Jemison made history in 1992, when she became the first African American woman to go into space. She worked as a mission specialist on the space shuttle Endeavor.

She later left NASA and continued to inspire and encourage others. She taught environmental studies at Dartmouth College. She started The Jemison Group. This was her own consulting company that uses science and technology to create social change.
