title: The First People of Pennsylvania
text:
The rich natural resources in Pennsylvania have always pulled people to the area. Humans have long interacted with this environment. They adapt and change the natural and physical features to meet their wants and needs.

The original inhabitants of Pennsylvania were the Lanape people, sometimes called the Delaware. Over 10,000 years ago, the Lenape settled in what is now Eastern Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, and Delaware. They call themselves Leni Lanape, which means “original people” in the Algonquin language. Dozens of other Algonquian-speaking peoples throughout North America descend from the Lenape. Many see the Lenape as the “grandfather” of the Algonquin Nations. The Lenape made pipes and ornaments out of copper. They stored food and tobacco in pottery. They created dye from plants to make records.

Other native groups in the region were part of the Iroquois Confederacy. This confederacy was a group of native tribes who formed a democratic government centuries before the European explorers arrived in North America. The people of the Iroquois Confederacy called themselves the Haudenosaunee. This means “people of the longhouse.” They built very large houses and lived in large family groups. Women played a big role in their society. They influenced decisions about planting, harvesting, war, and other matters. Clan mothers were the elderly women who led extended family groups. They arranged marriages, counseled clan members, and selected the chiefs.

The Seneca were the largest group in this confederacy. They lived in what is now Western New York and Northern Pennsylvania. While they were known to be fierce warriors, the Seneca also knew how to make peace. They valued language and became skilled speakers. They also valued art, sports, and dance.

The Tuscarora were also part of the Iroquois Confederacy. They were originally from what is now North Carolina. When they joined the confederacy, the Tuscarora traveled north. Over the many years they traveled, they built settlements along the way. This included places in Pennsylvania. Their final home was along the banks of the Niagara River, near the Seneca. Though they traveled for a long time, the Tuscarora have deep ties to the land. Their name comes from this connection. They called themselves Skarureh, meaning “hemp people.” They used what is known as Indian hemp, or milkweed, to make rope, cloth, and other objects.

Another Iroquoian-speaking group in Pennsylvania was the Conestoga. They were sometimes called the Susquehannock because they lived on the banks of the Susquehanna River. This was a major trading route. Although the tribe no longer exists, descendants of the Conestoga may still be among the Seneca or Lenape today. The name Conestoga comes from the Iroquoian phrase meaning "people of the cabin poles."

Each of these groups followed the Eastern Woodland lifestyle. This means their lives were tied to the seasons and the land. Eastern Woodland groups did not have a concept of land ownership. Rather, they saw themselves as caretakers of the land. They got everything they needed from the land. Their shelter, food, clothing, and tools all had to be grown, caught, or made from what was in the environment. Woodland groups built villages with longhouses. They used the thin pine saplings common in the region to make the frames. Then they covered the frames with bark. In these villages, the people farmed the rich soil. During the colder months, the people left the villages. They formed camps to hunt, following the animals and resources of the land. Each spring, they returned to their villages to replant their crops.

title: Immigration over Time
text:
Just as place names or artifacts can tell us about the people who inhabited a place, numbers can also tell a story. Look at the charts below. They include numbers taken from Pennsylvania census data from over 150 years. They show the countries where the largest groups of immigrants to Pennsylvania came from. The rich resources have always pulled people to live in Pennsylvania. Large cities have also provided immigrants with many opportunities for jobs. However, events outside of Pennsylvania and the U.S. also affect immigration trends. These push factors can include famines, wars, and environmental or economic disasters. Having family, friends, or people from their home country in a place can influence where people decide to settle. Familiar people can make it easier to adapt to a new country and language. This can explain why the same countries of origin often appear in the top groups of immigrants to the state.

Look at the charts collected from census data. How many countries were in the top five places of origin? Which country sent the most immigrants to Pennsylvania over the 150 years of data collection?

title: Pennsylvania Dutch
text:
Many people came to the Pennsylvania colony from German provinces in the 17th and 18th centuries. A lot of them practiced non-traditional Protestant beliefs. This made them religious minorities in their homeland. Many European governments did not approve of their religious practices at the time. The governments’ attitudes pushed the people to leave. The government of the Pennsylvania colony had a high degree of religious tolerance. This was a pull factor for these immigrants. By 1790, about one-third of the population of Pennsylvania was from Germany.

These immigrants all spoke German, or Deutsch, as it is called in the German language. The word is pronounced as “doych,” which sounds a lot like the English word “Dutch.” English speakers near the German settlers heard them saying “Deutsch.” They eventually started calling them and their language “Dutch.”

Many of the German immigrants spoke different dialects of German. A dialect is a regional variety of a language. A dialect can have different vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation from other dialects of the same language. As all these German speakers came together, different dialects influenced their language. Some words from English were also introduced into their language. What formed was a new German language unique to these American immigrants. The language was called "Pennsylvania Dutch," or "Pennsylvania German." It was then handed down through the generations. It is the first language for many who still belong to these religious groups today.

title: The Amish of Pennsylvania
text:
Amish immigrants came to Pennsylvania in the early 1700s. They left Europe because their religious practices were unpopular there. Pennsylvania was more welcoming, and they found the rich soil for farming.

The Amish value humility and simplicity. They hold a religious belief in separating themselves from things that distract them from these values. For this reason, the Amish dress simply and do not use many forms of modern technology. Family life is another important value the Amish hold. This leads adults to choose jobs that do not require them to travel away from their homes for long periods of time. Most Amish adults work from home in jobs such as farming, carpentry, or handcrafting.

The value of separating themselves from the world led the Amish to set up their own settlements. They arrange settlements by church districts. Each district is composed of around 30 to 40 families. The baptized members of a district select the leaders for the district. Those leaders help district members review and determine the ordnung for their district. The ordnung is the set of rules that guide Amish life. It is a German word that means order, or discipline.

To preserve their separation from the world, the Amish set up their own schools. They designed the education to help children prepare for adulthood in Amish society. Most school buildings are very simple and have only one classroom. The lessons enforce values of humility, heritage, and cooperation in the community. Amish children study English at school, as Pennsylvania Dutch is their first language. Formal education usually ends for Amish children around the age of 14. At this age, they may begin training for a trade. A trade is a job that requires specialized skill.

title: Essential Question
text: What are physical characteristics and how do they differ from place to place?

title: Plains
text:
A plain is a large area of flat land with few to no trees. The largest plains in the United States are the Great Plains. The Great Plains region is a large area east of the Rocky Mountains that is very flat. It extends from Mexico to Canada and eastward to Illinois. It is primarily grassy with few trees. The soil is usually very good in the plains due to the abundant amount of grass material that grows there. It is a great place for growing crops like corn and wheat.

Large areas of northern and western Ohio are dominated by plains. The Till Plains encompass most of western Ohio. The Till Plains formed thousands of years ago, when glaciers that once covered Ohio melted. When the glaciers melted, it left behind a rich layer of sediment, or soil-like material deposited by water, wind, or glaciers. This layer of sediment left behind by melting glaciers is called till. The layer of till deposits makes the soil of the Till Plains very good for growing crops. Farmers in this area grow large amounts of corn, grain, and soybeans.

Northern Ohio is dominated by the Lake Plains. The Lake Plains border Lake Erie and extend south toward the Till Plains. Like the Till Plains, much of the soil of the Lake Plains is rich and fertile because of sediment left behind by melting glaciers. Many of Ohio’s farms are located in this area. Because of their proximity to Lake Erie, the Lake Plains are home to the largest ports in Ohio: Cleveland and Toledo.

title: Mountains
text:
A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean. It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They are formed by the movement of the Earth's crust. Mountains are shaped over time by weather. Rich minerals are found in the cores of mountains. Mountain peaks are often covered in snow. The snow melts and sends water down the sides to form streams, creeks, and brooks.

There are many mountain ranges in the United States. The Rocky Mountain range is the longest mountain range in North America. It begins in Canada and extends through central New Mexico. Many of the peaks are more than 12,000 feet high. Mount Elbert in Colorado is the tallest peak in the range at 14,440 feet. Thousands of tourists flock to the Rocky Mountains each year to explore their natural wonders.

The Appalachian Mountains are located in the eastern part of the United States. They extend south from Canada to Georgia. The highest peak is Mount Mitchell at 6,684 feet. The Appalachian Trail runs the length of the mountain range, which is about 2,000 miles long. Outdoor adventurers and hiking enthusiasts hike the Appalachian Trail throughout the year.

title: Plateaus
text:
Plateaus are landforms with flat tops that rise above the surrounding land. One way that plateaus form is when tectonic plates collide. The friction creates heat, which causes solid rock to melt and rise to the surface. They can also be created through volcanic eruptions, erosion, or weathering. When the top of a mountain is weathered away by water or ice, the result may be a plateau.

The Appalachian Plateau sits at the foot of the Appalachian Mountains. This plateau extends from New York to Alabama and dominates the eastern half of Ohio. The Appalachian Plateaus was formed by weathering, erosion, and deposition. Deposition is the process in which sediment carried by wind or water settles in an area. Because the northwest edge of the plateau in Ohio was covered by a glacier, it has a flat, smooth surface. By comparison, the southern part of the plateau houses huge cliffs and deep gorges that were formed over time by water.

In Ohio, this part of the Appalachian Plateau is called the Allegheny Plateau because it lies west of the Allegheny Mountains. The Allegheny Mountains are a range of mountains within the Appalachian Mountains. The Allegheny Plateau has many large deposits of coal, salt, oil, and gravel. Because of this, mining has been one of the largest industries of the Allegheny Plateau for hundreds of years.

title: Rivers
text:
Rivers have played a vital role in the history, economy, and actions of governments in North America for thousands of years. A river is a large, flowing body of water that moves across the land. There are many rivers in the United States that play a vital role in the nation’s economy, history, and culture.

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. Combined with the Mississippi River, it forms one of the largest river systems on Earth. The Missouri River travels through the heart of the Great Plains. The Missouri flows southeast from its source in Montana. It ends in Missouri, where it joins the Mississippi River.

The Mississippi River is the second-longest river in the United States. Its name comes from a Chippewa word meaning "Father of Waters." The Mississippi River formed when glaciers melted about 12,000 years ago. The Mississippi River is nearly 2,400 miles long and travels through 10 states before it pours into the Gulf of Mexico.

The Rio Grande is the fourth-largest river in the United States. The name "Rio Grande" is Spanish for "great river." The Rio Grande begins its journey high up in the southern Rocky Mountains and travels south toward the Gulf of Mexico. The Rio Grande cuts the state of New Mexico almost in half. The rest of this river's path forms the border between Texas and Mexico.

Ohio is home to thousands of rivers. The longest is the Ohio River, which flows for 981 miles from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Cairo, Illinois, where it flows into the Mississippi River. The Ohio River forms the borders between Ohio and West Virginia and Ohio and Kentucky.

title: Lakes
text:
A lake is a body of water with land on all sides. The Great Lakes, which include Lake Erie, Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, and Lake Superior, are located in the northern United States. The Great Lakes cover over 94,000 square miles and contain about six quadrillion gallons of water. The lakes hold about 21 percent of the Earth's fresh water and 84 percent of America's fresh water. The deepest lake is Lake Superior at 1,330 feet.

Lake Okeechobee is another important lake in the United States. Lake Okeechobee is located in southern Florida and covers 730 square miles, making it the 10th-largest freshwater lake in the United States. It is home to hundreds of plant and animal species. Because of its abundant supply of fish, Lake Okeechobee is one of the South’s premier fishing destinations.

There are many natural and human-made lakes in Ohio. The largest is Lake Erie, which shares approximately a 150-mile long border with Ohio. It is the 13th-largest lake in the world. Lake Erie provides drinking water for over 11 million people.

title: Glacial Grooves
text: Glacial grooves occur when sediment and rocks are trapped in glaciers. As the glaciers melt, the ice, sediment, and rocks leave behind scratches and deep cuts in the bedrock underneath. Glacial grooves are found throughout the United States, from Alaska to Maine and even in California. The glacial grooves found on Kelleys Island, Ohio, are one of the state's most unique physical characteristics. These glacial grooves formed about 18,000 years ago, when many of the glaciers that covered Ohio began to melt. Scientists and geologists have studied the glacial grooves for many years to learn more about the last ice age and how it impacted areas of North America.

title: Rock Arches
text:
Rock arches, also called rock bridges, are natural features that form when portions of a rock erode, or wear away, from weather or water. The remaining rock has a large hole in it that looks like a window through the rock. The United States is home to many natural rock arches. One of the most recognizable arches is Delicate Arch, located in Arches National Park in Utah. Delicate Arch is a sandstone arch. The opening of the arch is 46 feet high and 32 feet wide.

Ohio is home to many natural rock arches. The largest of Ohio’s rock arches are located at Hocking Hills State Park, 50 miles southeast of Columbus, Ohio. Rockhouse, an Ohio cave system, extends throughout Hocking Hills State Park. There are seven rock arches that are part of the Rockhouse cave network. Thousands of people visit this natural wonder each year, making it one of Ohio’s most popular tourist destinations.

title: Essential Question
text: What is the type of criteria that can describe a region in North America?

title: What is a Region?
text:
Geographers organize the Earth into regions to help us learn about our world. A region is an area that has similar characteristics. Some regions are organized based on their physical characteristics. Physical characteristics include an area's landforms, climate, and biomes. Some regions are organized by their human characteristics. These include population, culture, and language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

Prehistoric environments that no longer exist can be studied by geographers through their regions. Paleogeography is the study of these ancient environments. It is studied by examining plate tectonics, or the movement of the Earth's crust. Geographers look at how these geographic regions are constantly created, changed, or destroyed over time. The supercontinent Pangaea, which existed millions of years ago, is an example of one of the paleogeographic regions that geographers have studied. Pangaea split and broke apart into the continents we see today.

title: Regions of North America
text:
The third-largest continent in the world is North America. This area extends from Canada, through the United States, Mexico, and the Aleutian Islands, to the Isthmus of Panama. This region has many physical characteristics and can be divided into five physical regions: the mountainous west, the Canadian Shield, the Great Plains, the eastern region, and the Caribbean.

North America has a variety of natural wonders that make up the great features of this region. Denali, the highest peak in the continent, stands at 6,194 meters, or 20,320 feet. The Great Lakes hold a huge amount of the planet’s fresh water. Deep canyons stretch throughout Cooper Canyon in the Mexican state of Chihuahua.

title: Regions of Canada
text:
Canada is considered the second-largest country on Earth, with nearly four million square miles of land. Canada has many different geographic areas, with the southern border along the United States being the longest border between two countries. Canada is divided into sections called provinces. Canada’s 10 provinces are divided between three territories. Each province and territory has its own capital city.

Canada is made up of five distinct regions. The Atlantic provinces have four territories and make up most of Canada’s Atlantic coastline. This area is rich with natural resources, such as fish and farmland. These key resources have made up a huge part of Canada’s history and development. The capital of Canada, Ottawa, is located in Central Canada. More than half of the population of Canada lives in this area. Manufacturing and industry are the major resources of the area, with three-quarters of all manufactured goods for Canada being created in this region.

The prairie provinces of Canada are made up of three territories. This region has the most fertile farmland in the world and is rich in energy resources. Saskatchewan is the country’s largest producer of grains and oilseeds. The West Coast region is made up of British Columbia and is known for its majestic mountains. It is Canada’s gateway to the Pacific Ocean. This region contains the Port of Vancouver, which is Canada’s largest and busiest port. Billions of dollars in goods are handled in this port each year.

The last region in Canada is the Northern Territories region. This region has one-third of Canada’s land mass and only has a population of 100,000 people. This area is called “Land of the Midnight Sun.” This is because during the summer months, daylight lasts up to 24 hours.

title: Regions of the United States
text:
The United States covers almost four million square miles and is made up of 50 states and six regions. The U.S. can be divided using physical or political boundaries. Boundaries mark the positions of regions on the continent. The six regions of the United States are the Northeast, Southeast, Midwest, Southwest, Northwest, and West. Most regions are divided using common geographic characteristics. Each area has its own unique physical geography, climate, vegetation, and natural resources.

The Northeast region has 11 states and is bordered by Canada and the Atlantic Ocean. This region has the largest population within the U.S. Technology and manufacturing are major industries within this region.

The Southeast region is made up of 12 states and has many businesses that opened up due to the climate and outdoor activities. Automobiles, agriculture, banks, and beverage companies are a few industries that have made the Southeast their home.

The Midwest region contains 12 states and has three of the largest rivers in the U.S. crossing through it: the Mississippi River, the Missouri River, and the Ohio River. These rivers allow many of the states in the Midwest to have rich and fertile soil.

The Southwest region contains four states. This region relies on its natural resources. A majority of the United States' oil production comes from Texas and Oklahoma.

The Northwest is made up of three states and has one of the most important resources: forests. The lumber industry is made up of about one million American workers. Washington is considered the U.S.’s top apple-producing state.

The West is made up of eight states and has many types of natural and human resources. Tourism is an important industry for the West. Some popular sites are Yellowstone National Park, beaches in California and Hawaii, and Zion National Park in Utah.

title: Regions of Mexico
text:
Mexico’s location is considered to be one of the most dynamic tectonic areas on Earth. Two major volcanic peaks are Citlaltepetl, which is considered the highest peak, and Popocatepetl, which is still an active volcano.

Mexico is divided into nine major regions: Baja California, the Pacific Coastal Lowlands, the Mexican Plateau, the Sierra Madre Oriental, the Sierra Madre Occidental, the Cordillera Neo-Volcanica, the Gulf Coastal Plain, the Southern Highlands, and the Yucatan Peninsula.

The Baja California region has arid land and is extremely difficult to navigate, due to its vast landscape of sharp peaks and sloping mountains.

The Pacific Coastal Lowlands region has highly productive farmland, due to its lowlands of coastal terraces and small, irrigated basins.

The Mexican Plateau region is the largest region and is the most populated.

The Sierra Madre Oriental region is a range of mountains that have major deposits of copper, lead, and zinc.

The Sierra Madre Occidental region is made up of a variety of gorges, with the most complex system being the Copper Canyon.

The Cordillera Neo-Volcanica region is rich in silver, lead, zinc, copper, and tin deposits. This region has an active volcanic range with a volcano called Paricutin that formed between 1943 and 1952.

The Gulf Coastal Plain is wider than the Pacific side and has lagoons and low-lying swampy areas.

The Southern Highlands region is made up of mountain ranges and plateaus. This region is also home to the Mexican Riviera and is a major tourist destination for Mexico.

The Yucatan Peninsula has a terrain that is thick with limestone. This leads to erosion that creates caverns and sinkholes. The islands of Cozumel and Mujeres are found in this region near Cancun.

title: Regions of the Caribbean
text:
The Caribbean is south and east of the continental United States. This region has 26 island nations. There are lakes and rivers on many of these islands. There are also mountains, volcanoes, coral reefs, and rainforests in the Caribbean. The regions are divided into the Greater Antilles and the Lesser Antilles.

The Greater Antilles include the four large islands of Cuba, Jamaica, Hispaniola, and Puerto Rico. The Lesser Antilles region includes the smaller islands in the eastern and southern areas of the Caribbean. Tourists come to visit the Caribbean year-round to see the beautiful physical features there.

The population of the Caribbean varies greatly depending on the place. It ranges from over 10 million people in Cuba to fewer than 5,000 people in Montserrat. Most of the countries in the Caribbean manufacture and process oil and agricultural goods for other countries. Many of the people living on the islands work in the tourism industry.

title: The Moravians of Pennsylvania
text:
Moravian history begins in the 1400s with the invention of the printing press. Moravians place a high value on learning. They began printing books in their own language, including the Bible. Back then, the Bible was only printed in Latin and read to people by a priest. Many people did not like how the Moravians were doing things. It led to difficulties. The Moravians had to move to new places.

Like the Amish and Mennonites, Moravians believe in simple living and non-violence. Moravians also believe in missionary work. Beginning in the 1700s, Moravians sent missionaries all over the world. This missionary effort led their leader and some followers to come to Pennsylvania. They excelled in farming and trades like carpentry and pottery making. They settled Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, in 1741. It is still the North American center of the Moravian church and missionary work. From Pennsylvania, Moravian missionaries preached to enslaved people and Native Americans.

title: History in Town Names
text:
We can learn a lot about a place from its name. Sometimes a place gets its name from its geographical features or how it is used. For example, a settlement between two rivers was often named for having a port to transport canoes and cargo over land. Port Allegheny, Port Matilda, and Portage are all settlements named for economic activity.

The name of a place can tell us about who originally lived there. Some towns and areas still have the names the Native Americans gave them. Names like Conshohocken, Shamokin, and Wyomissing all come from Indigenous languages. Many of Pennsylvania’s rivers and other landmarks have Indigenous names. The Lackawanna, Kiskiminikis, and Susquehanna Rivers and Mount Nittany all take their names from the native tribes who lived near there.

French, English, and German immigrants came to Pennsylvania. They built communities that looked a lot like where they came from. Some of the names they gave these places came from their old homes. For example, several counties in Pennsylvania get their names from the shires in England where immigrants came from. Berks, Bucks, and Chester are just a few.

Looking at the names of towns gives us some information about the immigrants who settled there. Many town names in Pennsylvania end in “-burgh,” “-ton,” or “-ville.” These all have origins in European languages. In the German language, a burg (or burgh) is a fortified town. Fortified means strengthened. These places were early trading posts. The ending “-ton” comes from the English language, meaning town. In French, "ville" means village. Combining these word endings with an important feature or leader gave settlers their town name.

Some towns were named after an event or landmark in the area. There are many interesting town names throughout the state.

Flourtown is named after a flour mill located in the area.

State College gets this name for being the home of a state university, Penn State.

Bala Cynwyd was settled by Welsh immigrants. Cynwyd is a town in Wales, and "bala" is a Welsh word that means outflow of a lake.

Burnt Cabins in Center County tells its history in its name. Its name comes from an event that took place in 1750. Several settlers illegally built cabins on land reserved for the Native American population. People burnt these cabins down to avoid breaking an agreement with local tribes.

When we learn about a place's name, we find more than just a word. We find the history and the people of that place as well.

title: Census Data
text: The U.S. constitution requires that the government complete a census every 10 years. A census is a complete count of the population. Knowing the number of people living in a place is useful. Taking a census is an opportunity for more than just counting the total number of people, though. A census can also look at different groups of people within the population. This can help people understand a lot about a place. A census can count people by age groups, the types of jobs they have, or the ways they travel or interact with technology. Looking at these categories can help elected officials understand the needs of a community.

title: Lenses of Social Studies
text:
You are many things. You are a student. You are a friend. You are also a reader and a writer. You are part of a diverse world filled with many cultures, ideas, and beliefs. This year, you will study what it is like to be part of that world. Your knowledge of the world around you will grow.

You will study social studies through different lenses to help you understand the world. Looking at a subject through many lenses gives you a better understanding of it. You will examine social studies through the eyes of a historian, geographer, and a political scientist. You will also see how a social scientist, an economist, and a problem solver look at social studies.

title: Essential Question
text: What are the lenses of social studies?

title: Historian
text:
Historians study the past. They help us understand how people thought and lived over time. They ask questions to understand the past, such as:

What happened?

When did it happen?

Why did it happen?

How did things change?

What did we learn from it?

In many ways, a historian is like a detective. They seek to ask and answer questions about the past. When historians study the past, they also learn about a society’s culture, beliefs, and economy. Historians study sources to understand the past.

Like a historian, you will use different types of sources to study the past. You will learn about people and events of the past. These people and events have had a large impact on our communities, our state, and our country. You will use many types of sources to understand the past. Then, you will apply that learning to the future.

title: Geographer
text:
This year, you will look at the world through a geographer’s lens. Geographers study the interaction between people and the environment. They use various tools to answer questions about the world. Some of these tools are maps, globes, graphs, and diagrams. Sometimes, they use photographs as well.

Geographers ask questions, such as:

Where is it?

How do we use or interact with it?

Why is it important?

Looking at the world as a geographer will help you understand how geography affects communities in Ohio, including yours.

title: Political Scientist
text:
A political scientist studies how a government works. They want to understand how community leaders make laws for their people.

Political scientists ask questions, such as:

How will laws help our community?

Who has the power to create a law?

How are laws enforced?

For example, the United States is a representative democracy. This means people elect leaders who represent them in the government. The purpose of the government is to protect citizens’ rights. It also promotes the common good.

The values of the nation are defined in documents. Documents written during the nation’s history protect citizens’ rights. Ohio has a government that makes laws for the state. Ohio’s important documents protect the rights of citizens.

This year, you will use the lens of a political scientist to study Ohio. You will study how government and laws affect Ohio.

title: Social Scientist
text:
Social scientists study all parts of a person. Some of these parts are academic, social, emotional, physical, and mental. They analyze the effects of behaviors and emotions on individuals and groups.

Social scientists ask questions, such as:

How did that event or action impact people?

What are the consequences of these actions or events?

How can I see this from a different perspective?

What are the facts, and what is my interpretation of the situation?

What is within my control, and what is not within my control?

Looking at a topic through the lens of a social scientist can help you. You can see how events and the actions of individuals have impacted Ohio.

title: Economist
text:
An economist studies money and finance. Economists make claims about the economy. They look at the production of goods and services in a community. They look at available resources. They determine how resources can help fix problems. Economists help people make responsible financial choices.

Economists ask questions, such as:

What resources are in our community?

How do people make money?

Why do people use different products?

What businesses are needed in our community?

This year, you will study social studies through the lens of an economist. This will help you learn. You can learn the things that have influenced economic growth and decline in Ohio.

title: Problem Solver
text:
All problems have a solution. A problem solver is anybody who has solved a problem before. People who are good at solving problems think creatively. Creative thinkers are people who look at a problem using many different lenses. They are willing to try various strategies to solve a problem.

Problem solvers might ask questions, such as:

How did this problem begin?

What is the problem happening now?

What kind of laws might help solve the problem?

How has the problem impacted people?

What resources are in our community that we could use to help solve the problem?

How can I think differently about the situation to help solve the problem?

You have the power to solve problems too. Social studies will challenge you to see things through a problem solver’s lens. This will help you to understand and appreciate different ways of thinking.

title: The Lumbee
text:
North Carolina’s Lumbee Tribe consists of 55,000 members and is the largest tribe in the state. The tribe lives in the counties of Robeson, Hoke, Cumberland, and Sotland. The name of the tribe comes from the Lumbee River, which runs through Robeson. The Lumbee have been recognized as a tribe by North Carolina since 1885. That same year, the Lumbree created a school. They wanted a school that would support the members of the tribe. Two years later, the Croatan Normal Indian School was created. Today, that school is the University of North Carolina at Pembroke. Education is important to the Lumbee.

Several different tribes, including the Siouan-, Algonquian-, and the Iroquian-speaking tribes, make up the peoples of the Lumbee. In the early days of the tribe, farming was their way of life. Crops consisted of cotton, tobacco, hay, and corn. Today, they continue to be a thriving community. The tribe has its own government and tribal services, much like services you would find in any community. Their community provides support for the tribe through housing programs, vocational or job training, and water and power services. They have their own schools and hold elections for their leaders.

The Lumbee Tribe shares their cultural traditions with the world every year, at the Dance of the Spring Moon Powwow. This powwow includes dancing demonstrations, drumming contests, and a church service on Sunday morning for visitors to attend. Coming together is a central part of the Lumbee culture. They consider themselves a spiritual people. Participants at the powwow can also participate in a stickball game. This powwow helps keep their culture alive.

Culture, tradition, and history are important to the Lumbee. You can see evidence of this in the preamble to their constitution:

In accordance with the inherent power of self-government of the Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina ("Tribe"), the Tribe adopts this Constitution for the purposes of establishing a tribal government structure, preserving for all time the Lumbee way of life and community, promoting the educational, cultural, social, and economic well-being of Lumbee people and securing justice and freedom for the Lumbee people.

title: The Mennonites of Pennsylvania
text:
The Mennonites formed in Europe in the 1500s. Like the Amish, they believe church members should not serve in the military and that church and government should be separate. Governments were unfriendly to their beliefs. Often, Mennonites were forced to live away from villages in areas with poor soil for farming. They had to learn how to build up the soil to produce crops. Many Mennonites immigrated to Pennsylvania. There, they gained opportunities to form religious communities and farm fertile soil. In 1683, Mennonites founded Germantown. It is the oldest Mennonite community in North America.

Today, there are different groups of Mennonites. Old Order Mennonites dress plainly and do not use modern technology. Conservative Mennonites also dress plainly and live in closed settlements. They do, however, use many forms of modern technology. Conference Mennonites dress in modern clothing styles and use modern technology. All three groups are committed to the same values. The most important of these values are non-violence and service.

title: Goods and Markets
text:
People rely on the resources around them to meet their needs and wants. Before European colonization, Native American tribes made everything they needed from the available natural resources. There are different natural resources available across the country. There can be a surplus, or more resources than needed. People can trade this surplus for resources that are scarce, or less available. In order to meet needs and wants, people establish trade networks. They can trade resources they have in surplus and find those that are scarce. Native Americans created trade networks among the different tribes. The paths they took to meet with each other and make trades spread all over North America.

People who work and make items for trade are called producers. The items for trade are called goods. Producers need to attract consumers, or people to receive the goods for use. So, they bring the goods to market, or a place where people trade. This could be at a junction, or where two or more travel routes crossed. Markets can be large or small. There were many large markets and trading centers in early Pennsylvania. Kittanning was one such trade center in Western Pennsylvania. The junction of the Great Shamokin Path and Venango Path was another trade center.

There are different ways for people to pay for goods. In most markets, people pay with a form of money. Money can be whatever society decides is valuable and acceptable for exchange. Indigenous tribes that lived in Pennsylvania and beyond traded with wampum. Wampum were special beads made of polished shells and used as money. Another option was trading. Bartering is the act of trading something for goods without using money. Bartering has been used for thousands of years, when money was not available. This type of market is known as a traditional market system. A traditional system has markets that are the same from generation to generation.

Markets in early America were centers for producers and consumers to meet with goods. Markets were also centers for communication and the exchange of ideas and news. People communicated through common language or through a form of sign language. Entertainment was also exchanged in the form of music, dance, and stories. These exchanges helped cultures grow and expand.

title: Trading Paths and Trading Centers
text:
Waterways were like highways to the people who lived in early Pennsylvania. Water was a good way to travel. It was also a good way to move goods from one place to another. Pennsylvania's watersheds provide many rivers and streams. These waterways connected people in the different regions. People also traveled over land by different paths. The places where waterways crossed footpaths became places of trade. Kittanning, Venango, Logstown, Conewago, Shamokin, Towanda, and Lackawanna were all known trading centers.

Look at the map of Pennsylvania.

Use one color to identify waterways.

Identify footpaths with a different color.

Circle where the lines cross each other.

title: Transportation and Trade
text:
When Europeans came to Pennsylvania, they had manufactured goods available for trade. Markets and trade centers then became permanent buildings called trading posts. Quantities of goods for trade increased. Trading posts became places for settlements and towns to grow. The population in these areas rose. With more people, the demand for goods at the markets continued to increase. To accommodate the increased demand, more goods needed to be produced. More goods for consumers would mean greater profits, or earnings, for the producer. Producers had to transport more goods to the markets. This created a need for larger vehicles to carry the goods.

Larger vehicles required more than foot paths to reach the market. People built roads to accommodate them. The ridge and valley region made transporting goods to market difficult. The dense forests made creating roads difficult. People cut the trees and hauled them away. However, the stumps and roots of the trees remained in the ground. This made the roads bumpy. The first roads in Pennsylvania were bare ground, which turned to mud with rain and traffic.

In 1795, the Philadelphia and Lancaster Turnpike changed Pennsylvania’s roads. This 62-mile road was the first in the United States with a hard surface. The project took two years to complete. Roads were expensive to build. So, people had to pay a toll, or fee, to travel on them. “Toll houses'' were built along the route. A long pole called a "pike" was placed across the road at each toll house. This prevented people from traveling any further on the road. Once a traveler paid the toll, the pike was moved or turned, and the traveler could move on. This type of road that used tolls and pikes was called a turnpike.

Better roads and larger vehicles for transporting goods benefited consumers at a market. When there are more choices, the producers have to maintain quality. Producers also have to keep prices low to attract consumers.

title: Amendments
text:
When Congress created the Constitution, they knew that some changes might be needed in the future. They included a process to add or change parts of the original Constitution. Changes to the Constitution are called amendments. Amendments are additions designed to make a document better. Today, there are 27 amendments to the Constitution of the United States. The first 10 amendments are known as the Bill of Rights. These amendments to the Constitution were created by the writers to protect the rights of citizens and create our government's structure.

There have been many changes to the Constitution in its 200-year history. However, it is not easy to amend the Constitution. In order to make an amendment to the Constitution, an amendment must be presented to the Congress. Both parts of Congress, the Senate, and House of Representatives, vote on any changes. If two-thirds or more of the members of Congress agree on the change, then it moves on to the president. If the president does not agree, she or he can veto, or vote, against the change. All current amendments have gone through this process. This process makes sure all citizens have the ability to participate in government decisions.

title: Capital Resources
text: Capital resources are the tools we use to help us make other things. Capital resources include tools, buildings, machinery, or equipment. These items are man-made. This means they do not occur naturally in the environment. They have to be created before they can be used to build other things. The process to make paper uses lots of capital resources. The saws and machines used to cut and deliver the trees are capital resources. The equipment that makes the paper is also a capital resource. The company uses trucks to deliver the finished paper to customers. The trucks, factory, and machines are all capital resources.

title: Manufacturing
text:
Manufacturing is the business of using raw materials to make products or goods to sell. There are many types of manufacturing companies. Some examples of manufactured products are cars, computers, toys, and soft drinks. Some manufacturing products are made from natural resources. Others are made from man-made resources.

People often work in factories to manufacture goods. They work together to make products for consumers to purchase. Workers depend on each other. They need to do their job well so the product is made correctly.

One example of this is the automobile industry. To build an automobile, workers must assemble 15,000 manufactured parts! This is done quickly and efficiently through an assembly line. An assembly line is a way of putting together a product in a factory by moving it along a line of workers. Each worker adds or adjusts a part until the product is finished. Once production is complete, automobiles are tested for safety. This is done before sending them to businesses where consumers can purchase them.

Some products are made with parts from other countries. For example, a car plant makes cars. However, it may get a lot of parts from overseas. Parts like the car battery or the car tires could be made in another country, such as China. These parts are shipped to the U.S. to be manufactured into a car you can drive. This is known as importing. The batteries and tires are imports. The car factory in America uses them to manufacture cars.

title: Tourism
text:
Tourism is the business of encouraging people to travel for fun. Tourism is an economic activity. People travel to places different from where they live. Cities, states, and even countries have created businesses and resorts for people to shop and stay. These locations are sometimes based on a place's unique physical characteristics. This includes places like oceans, mountains, and national parks. Some tourist attractions are man-made.

Tourism changes a place's physical environment. The more people visit a place, the more accommodations are made. Bringing in visitors requires additional roads, hotels, restaurants, stores, and sites for people to visit. Tourism is an industry that brings a lot of money to cities, states, and countries. It strengthens the economy.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
A producer is someone who makes a good or provides a service. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are used for other communities. Farmers, factory workers, car mechanics, and doctors are producers. The person who cuts your hair is also a producer.

People who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. People often depend on trade with others to meet their wants and needs. People can be both a producer and a consumer. When we buy groceries, gas, clothing, or toys, we are buying goods. When we go to the doctor, have our car fixed, or get a haircut, we are using services. When you get a haircut, you're a consumer because you're buying a service.

Both consumers and producers affect the prices of goods and services. For example, a company that produces bicycles may raise the price of their product if there's a metal shortage. A shortage is when something you need can’t be found in the amount needed. Consumers may stop buying bikes if the price is too high. Then the company might have to lower prices to get more sales. When a consumer doesn't buy enough of a good or service it may cause producers to lower the cost of it. If consumers are buying too much of a product, a producer might increase the product's price.

title: Information Technology
text:
Another important section of the U.S. economy is information technology. Information technology is the study and development of computer systems to store, retrieve, and send information. Millions of people work for thousands of U.S.-based information technology companies. The largest information technology companies in the United States include Apple Inc., Microsoft, Oracle, Cisco Systems Inc., and Adobe Inc.

Inventors and entrepreneurs Steve Jobs and Stephen Wozniak founded Apple Computers in Silicon Valley, California. In 1975, the first build-your-own computer kit came out. Wozniak and Jobs built their first personal computer in the Jobs’ family garage. Today, Apple is one of the richest companies in the world and employs over two million people. It designs, manufactures, and sells personal computers, mobile devices, and computer software programs.

In 1975, software engineers Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft. They developed software for some of the early personal computers on the market. In 1980, Microsoft partnered with the International Business Machines Corporation (IBM). Together, they developed software for personal computers. The development and distribution of personal computers skyrocketed following this partnership. Today, Microsoft is still one of the leading producers of computer software and employs over 181,000 people.

These companies employ thousands of people in the United States and add billions of dollars to the country’s economy each year.

title: The Pennsylvania Turnpike
text:
The Pennsylvania Turnpike extended the original 62 miles of turnpike built in 1795. The ridge and valley region in the state made east-to-west travel difficult. There were so many mountains to go over and waterways to cross. To make transportation easier, road engineers made tunnels through the mountains. They also built bridges over waterways. Today, the Pennsylvania Turnpike is a vital roadway for transporting goods to market.

Look at the map of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. Identify how many tunnels are a part of the turnpike.

title: Prime Meridian and Longitude
text:
Cartographers draw lines on a map from the North Pole to the South Pole. This helps us be more specific in our mapping. One of these lines, the Prime Meridian, divides the world in half vertically. These halves are called the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere. Absolute location uses latitude and longitude lines to pinpoint where something is located. These lines are measured in degrees. Each degree is divided into 60 minutes, and each minute has 60 seconds.

The Earth is divided into 24 different time zones. The reason for this division is because the Earth rotates on its axis once a day. A time zone is one of the ways that the world is divided and is based on what time it is in a given location. The starting point for these time zones is the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, also called Greenwich Mean Time. Theoretically, every 15 degrees east or west of Greenwich means one hour more or less. In practice, however, time zones do not go through the middle of countries. Larger countries have multiple time zones. For convenience, time zone boundaries often follow political boundaries instead of longitude lines. The International Date Line is another imaginary line on Earth's surface. It defines the boundary between one day and the next. The International Date Line is located halfway around the world from the Prime Meridian.

title: Conestoga Wagons
text:
In the same way that we have different types of motor vehicles for different purposes today, there used to be different types of wagons. There were small buggies for driving around town and bigger wagons for farm work and longer trips. The increased demand to bring more goods to market made innovations in vehicles necessary. Larger wagons were needed. The roads these wagons would travel on weren’t smooth. Tree stumps, roots, and rocks were left in the road bed. There were few bridges for crossing the many waterways. Wagons had to be strong enough to go on these rough roads and to go through the streams.

It was in Conestoga, Pennsylvania, that such a vehicle was constructed. Known as the Conestoga Wagon, it was like the freight truck of its day. The length of the wagon was 13-16 feet. The sides of the wagon were four feet high. The curved floor stopped goods from shifting or falling out. A waterproof canvas pulled over wooden arches protected the goods from the weather. Its brakes and steering system were specially designed to handle long hauls over rough terrain. The height of the wheels made it possible to go over the stumps and rocks in the road. A typical farm wagon would need two to four horses to pull it. A Conestoga wagon needed six to eight big horses, or up to a dozen oxen to pull it. It took 23 days to get from Philadelphia to Pittsburgh.

title: Canals and the Allegheny Portage Railroad
text:
The many waterways in Pennsylvania required wagons to go through streams as they traveled, or they required bridges for crossing. To use the waterways more efficiently, canals, or passages, were dug to connect rivers. Canals were 40 feet wide and six feet deep to float boats packed with goods for trade. The system of canals was built in the 1820s to the 1850s. This was before there was heavy machinery that could help in the digging process. These canals were dug by hand. People used shovels and picks. They loaded wagons with the dirt to be hauled away.

Canal boats carried more goods to markets than wagons. The waterways and canals were effective. There was still a problem, though. The ridge and valley area of the state presented difficulties for water transportation. There were waterways on either side of the mountains. It was important to figure out how to connect the canal systems on both sides of the mountains.

Owners of the Pennsylvania Main Line Canal first wanted to make a tunnel through the mountain. The tunnel could then be flooded and create a canal. However, this project was very expensive, so they never pursued it. In England, a series of incline planes, or slopes, had been built up and down mountains. People used these planes to pull the canal boats over the mountains. People used this idea to build the Portage Railroad between Hollidaysburg and Johnstown.

Look at the images to discover how the Portage Railroad moved canal boats over the mountains.

Innovation and Invention

The ropes used to pull the canal boats up the mountain were made of hemp fibers. The fibers would wear over time and break. It was very dangerous when the rope hauling a canal boat broke. Not only could the goods get damaged or lost, but people involved could get injured, or worse. John Roebling worked as an engineer. He realized the dangers of the hemp fiber ropes pulling these heavy loads. Roebling invented a rope made from metal. He twisted thin, metal cords together to form a large rope. This was stronger and safer for using on the inclines. Roebling eventually would use this innovation to build bridges. The Brooklyn Bridge was possible because of the Allegheny Portage Railroad.

title: Important People and Places
text:
Our values and beliefs are represented in our symbols. Citizens know about and honor important events and people in our country’s history. We honor these events and people through celebrations and holidays. We also recognize them by building monuments and memorials to honor them.

National memorials and monuments are symbols of our nation. They were built to remind us of important events and people in our history. Memorials and monuments teach us why these people are important to America. Knowing the history of our country helps to unite us as citizens. Symbols of the United States make us feel patriotic. We feel patriotic because of the freedoms we enjoy.

title: Liberty Bell
text:
The Liberty Bell was made in England in 1752 for the Pennsylvania Assembly. It weighs 2,000 pounds and is made of copper and tin. The Liberty Bell is a symbol for the United States. It represents American independence and freedom. It first rang in the tower of Independence Hall. The words “Proclaim Liberty Throughout All the Land Unto All the Inhabitants thereof” are engraved on the bell.

The first name of the Liberty Bell was the State House Bell. After the bell was created in England, it was shipped to Philadelphia. When the bell arrived, it was placed in Liberty Hall. It was used to signal meetings or call citizens together. The first time it was rung, it cracked. The broken bell was melted down and remade again. This happened two more times. The third time it cracked was when they rang the bell for George Washington’s birthday.
