title: Specialization and Trade
text:
Instead of visiting one country, fly over South and Central America to get a big-picture view of the beauty and natural resources found in each country. Most South American countries are known for coffee, cattle, and sugarcane. Some countries have unique resources, such as Brazil’s natural petroleum and Peru’s llamas. Bolivia is rich in mineral resources, such as copper and zinc, while off the coast of Venezuela, you can find oil and pearls.

Latin American countries don’t all have the same resources or produce the same goods, so the best strategy to get what you need is specialization. Specialization is a method where a country focuses on producing a few products well. Then, they trade their “specialized” products with other countries to gain what is needed. For example, Venezuela could trade some of its oil to gain copper from Bolivia.

Besides natural resources, Latin American countries can specialize in manufactured goods. Medical supplies, pharmaceuticals, clothing, aircraft, and computer machinery are all manufactured in Latin American countries. Costa Rica is a top manufacturer of electronics and computer chips. Honduras produces textiles, and Guatemala is a producer of automotive parts. When Latin American countries trade amongst themselves, they save on shipping costs and work together as a powerful trade bloc with other countries. Several times in history, Latin American countries have attempted to work together to produce better trading conditions between their countries. They have formed free trading groups to encourage specialization and teamwork.

Unfortunately, trade among Latin American countries sometimes decreases. This puts them in competition instead of working together for a better economy for the whole continent. However, the Pacific Trade Alliance, the countries of Chile, Columbia, Mexico, and Peru, are working together to increase trade within Latin America and other countries. Hopefully, more countries will join the alliance for better trade arrangements. Some Latin American countries are small and produce similar items, so the majority of the trading is from other countries, such as India, China, and the United States.

Latin American countries trade a lot with the United States. The United States gains use of their natural resources and labor force. Because pay is lower in Mexico, many manufacturers can produce automobiles and electronics more cheaply in Mexico than in the U.S. Many American companies moved production to Mexico to lower their costs. Carmakers have moved their assembly lines for that reason. Also, since a product costs less to make in Mexico, the car or computer will be cheaper for the buyer in the United States.

On the other hand, Latin American countries that trade with the U.S. have a twofold gain. First, Latin Americans have a greater market for their products by importing to the U.S. Second, since the imports are tax-free (for some countries), they can sell their products for a greater profit. Profitable businesses create jobs. If the pay is good enough and the working conditions are safe, these jobs help the people in those countries to provide for their families.

Don’t just fly over and see the beauty of Latin America. Get to know the specializations of each country, whether it’s the llamas in Peru or the pearls of Venezuela!

title: Rainforest Preservation
text:
One group that is devoted to saving the rainforests is The Rainforest Foundation Fund.

The Rainforest Foundation Fund began in Brazil in 1989 after a native tribesman from the Kayapo approached the musician, Sting, his wife, Trudie Styler, and filmmaker Jean-Pierre Dutilleux with tales of the tribe’s struggles with mining and logging companies. The organization was founded with the mission to help indigenous people gain land rights to their ancestral homes. How do they accomplish this mission? The organization provides funds to programs that defend land rights, promote development of indigenous communities, and/or challenge activity that may damage the land.

The benefits of this approach have been proven. The fight to save the Kayapo land led to the protection of 6.7 million acres of Brazil’s rainforest. Drone footage and satellite images show that lands protected by the indigenous tribes have significantly lower rates of deforestation than lands that are not protected. In 2015, there was 12 times less deforestation on protected lands.

Students and parents can join in the fight to save the rainforest by visiting websites dedicated to the cause. There are simple things you can do like spreading the word on social media and participating in fundraising events. You can also avoid purchasing items that were created in a way that is harmful to the rainforest.

title: Natural Resources of the Rainforest
text:
The Amazon Rainforest is the largest rainforest on our planet. Because of its location along the equator and its tropical climate, this rainforest has the highest biodiversity of any place on Earth. This means that several million species of plants and animals make it their home. So it makes sense that humans would explore this area to find useful natural resources.

You may be surprised by just how many products from your daily life are products of the rainforest. Brazil nut trees grow almost exclusively in the Amazon. The trees produce fruits that are about the size of baseballs. Inside the fruits are a number of seeds, which we know as Brazil nuts. Local forest-based communities collect and sell the nuts. Brazil, over half of which is covered by rainforest, grows one third of the world’s coffee beans and exports large numbers of oranges, papayas, sugarcane, and soybeans. An astounding number of other fruits and vegetables come from the rainforest, including bananas, citrus, avocados, cashews, tea, palm and coconut oil, and flavorings, such as cocoa, vanilla, and spices.

Plants are one of the greatest natural resources we utilize from the rainforest, not just for the food they provide. Plants also provide the materials needed to produce numerous medicines. Twenty-five percent of all drugs are derived from plants that grow in the rainforest. Some medicines even come from rainforest animals. Picture this: a dangerous viper of the rainforest bites a person, and they collapse from a massive drop in blood pressure. A drug company hears about it and decides to figure out which compounds in the venom are responsible for lowering blood pressure. The drug company then uses those compounds to make heart medicine for people with high blood pressure.

Here are some other facts about natural resources that come from the Amazon Rainforest:

Twenty percent of all freshwater is located in the Amazon Rainforest.

Minerals, such as gold, copper, tin, iron ore, bauxite, nickel, and manganese, are mined from the forest.

Valuable timber is harvested from the rainforest, including mahogany, rosewood, and teak.

Oil is shipped from the Amazon to many countries for refinement, including the U.S.

title: Geographic Features of Latin America
text:
While the term “Latin America” may suggest a single location, we know that Latin America is actually a very diverse group of countries. Latin America includes Mexico, Central and South America, and some of the Caribbean nations. That means Latin America stretches from moist tropical beaches to rugged mountains thousands of feet high to deserts so dry that rainfall has rarely been recorded.

When you think about geography and Latin America, your thoughts might turn to the soaring heights of the Andes. The longest mountain chain in the world, the Andes run the entire length of the South American west coast. Climbing as high as 22,000 feet above sea level, this mountain range creates a barrier for rain and snow. The Atacama Desert, located in the country of Chile and on the immediate eastern slope of the Andes, is the driest non-polar area on the planet. Precipitation falls on the western slopes and leaves nothing for the land to the east. Yet not far from this desert, high up in the clouds, lies the famed mountain city of Machu Picchu. The Inca Empire built this amazing complex in the 15th century but abandoned it after they were conquered by the Spanish. Today, it is a very popular tourist stop.

Travel east of the Andes, and you can’t help but run into the enormous Amazon basin. Highlighted by the world’s second-longest river, which also shares its name, the Amazon basin is home to the largest rainforest on Earth. It’s so big that you could nearly fit the entire United States (minus Alaska) inside! Countless animal and plant varieties call this rainforest home. Unfortunately, much of it is disappearing because of deforestation (the cutting down of trees) and global warming. Most of the basin is located in the Portuguese-speaking country of Brazil, the most populous of all the Latin American countries.

Continue north out of South America, and you reach the isthmus that is Central America. An isthmus is a narrow strip of land bordered by large bodies of water on both sides. In the country of Panama, ships can travel through a massive canal that connects the Pacific Ocean to the Caribbean Sea and Atlantic Ocean. Finished in 1914 by the United States, the canal allows ships to skip several thousand miles of travel since they need not go all the way around the South American continent to get from one ocean to the other.

Central America connects to the North American continent in Mexico. The nation’s capital, Mexico City, sits more than 7,000 feet above sea level in the highland plateau of the sprawling Sierra Madre Mountains. It is the largest city in the Western Hemisphere, with more than 21 million people, and it’s the largest Spanish-speaking city in the world. On clear days, you’re sure to notice Mount Popocatepetl, just 40 miles away. This volcano rises nearly 18,000 feet and is capped with snow even in the hottest months.

Sail across the Gulf of Mexico and anchor near the palm trees and sandy beaches of the many island nations that are part of Latin America. These include Cuba, Puerto Rico, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, Jamaica, the Bahamas, and the Virgin Islands, to name just a few. Many of these countries are popular tourist destinations because of their tropical climate and sandy beaches. Volcanic eruptions formed most of the islands. Evidence of this can be found in the form of volcanic peaks or rich volcanic soil excellent for growing sugar cane, bananas, and coffee beans.

title: Impact of Destruction on Other Countries
text:
You may think that since you live in the United States, cutting down trees in the rainforest does not affect your life. There are actually several ways that the loss of rainforest habitat impacts the global community.

Loss of trees affects the water cycle. Trees pull moisture out of the soil and return it to the atmosphere through transpiration. Disturbing this balance can lead to droughts in various parts of the world, depending on weather patterns.

The loss of habitat caused by deforestation is responsible for the extinction of hundreds of plant and animal species. With each species that vanishes, so too does a possible cure for a life-threatening disease.

Deforestation is a large contributing factor to global climate change due to its impact on the carbon cycle. When trees are cut down, carbon dioxide levels increase, which in turn causes temperatures to rise. Over time, as more deforestation occurs and more carbon is released, the world warms up, affecting the lives and habitats of humans, plants, and animals alike.

title: The Amazon River and Rainforest
text:
“There is something in a tropical forest akin to the ocean in its effect on the mind. Man feels so completely his insignificance there and the vastness of nature.” Henry Walter Bates spoke these words as he first explored the Amazon Rainforest. He soon came to realize just how unique an ecosystem the forest was. Its unique location, steady climate, incredible biodiversity, and abundance of natural resources set it apart from any other place on our planet.

The Amazon Rainforest, the largest rainforest in the world, is located in South America. Its boundaries stretch from the foothills of the Andes Mountains in the west to the Atlantic Ocean in the east. The Guiana Highlands form the northern boundary, while the Brazilian Highlands mark its southern edge. Within these borders lies the mighty Amazon River and the almost 1,100 tributaries that feed it. The rainforest covers 2,300,000 square miles, almost the entire Amazon River basin (an area that drains into a river).

The climate in the rainforest is pretty predictable: rain and humidity! On average, the Amazon receives 120 inches of rainfall in a year. There is really no “rainy season,” but there is a “rainier season,” usually from January to May. All this moisture has to evaporate sometime. This leads to very high rates of humidity (the amount of water vapor in the atmosphere). The average humidity is between 77 and 88 percent. This causes high temperatures to feel hotter and cool temperatures to feel colder. However, because the rainforest is located along the equator, the true temperature doesn’t change much. It hovers around 80 degrees Fahrenheit year round. There is very little difference in temperature as the seasons change. In fact, there is a wider range of temperature between daytime and nighttime than between seasons!

The Amazon Rainforest is home to an astonishingly high number of plant and animal species. In fact, 10 percent of all known plants and animals call the Amazon home. There are several million species of insects, plants, birds, fish, and mammals, and there are still some organisms in the rainforest that are unrecorded by science. There are also plants that exist in the rainforest that do not exist anywhere else in the world.

There are several natural resources found within the rainforest. Many of the plants in the forest have healing properties and are used to create medicine. Other plants produce tasty fruits and nuts that are harvested and shipped to other countries. Around 80 percent of our favorite foods have their origins in the rainforest: coffee, chocolate, rice, tomatoes, potatoes, bananas, black pepper, pineapple, and corn. Timber from the trees is used to create lumber for building. There are oil and gas reservoirs as well as gold, copper, tin, iron ore, nickel, and bauxite.

title: Geography of Mesoamerica
text:
The continent of North America includes more than the U.S. Mesoamerica, or middle America, includes Mexico and the countries of Central America. The land has a very diverse geography. Much of it is mountains, dividing the land into a wet region (tropical forests) and a dry region (high deserts).

Mesoamerica developed completely separate from Europe and Afro-Eurasia. About 15,000 years ago, humans crossed over from Asia and made their way south into Central America. Unlike other continents, the Americas had no beasts of burden. There were no cattle, oxen, camels, or horses to help people do work. So the people of Central America had to survive in a unique way, very differently from people in other parts of the world.

Linguists, those who study languages, believe there may have been more than 120 different languages in Mesoamerica, making communication difficult amongst groups of people. Some of them learned to use a type of writing called "rebus" writing (called logosyllabic script), a type of communication using pictures instead of words. This form of writing is considered to be the most sophisticated and highly developed writing system in the pre-Columbian Americas.

The groups that lived in Mesoamerica did share some things in common. They all farmed maize (corn), beans, and squash. They shared a common origin story, calendar, writing system, and a sport played with a hoop and a ball.

One of the most important civilizations in Mesoamerica was the Maya. The Maya were an advanced civilization: they built stepped pyramids, used the sun and stars to navigate, created an accurate calendar, and developed the concept of zero in mathematics.

The Maya lived mostly in the highlands of Guatemala and the jungles of the Yucatán peninsula. Historically, they began as nomadic farmers, moving from place to place and planting crops when and where the conditions were right. After a while, the Maya became a sedentary group, staying in one place to farm crops, such as chili peppers, avocados, onions, and cacao, which is used to make chocolate.

title: Indigenous Spirituality
text:
Religion was part of daily life for the indigenous peoples of the United States and Canada. It influenced the ways they lived, hunted, celebrated, and even expressed themselves. For many, there was little separation between daily life and their relationship with the spirits. Religion taught people that they were spiritually connected to and must respect all living things.

The Northwest people were well known for their carved ceremonial masks. These masks were used in social gatherings and for performing religious ceremonies. These ceremonies often took the form of dance. The greatest ceremony of the Plains people was the Sun Dance. The people would dance and try to get a vision from the spirits about how to live the rest of their lives.

Also closely tied to religion for these people was the practice of medicine. A tribe would have a medicine man or woman. This person was also known as a shaman. They would consult the spirits about how to heal people or where to find food or other supplies.

The arrival of Europeans marked a major change in native customs and religions. Tens of millions of indigenous people died due to sickness. European programs of slavery and extermination were employed. Europeans and their missionaries usually looked upon native spirituality as worthless superstition inspired by the Christian devil, Satan. Many of the surviving natives were forced to practice Christianity.

Today, many American Indians are Christians, while others combine traditional native practices with Christianity. Pan-Indianism is a recent and growing movement which encourages a return to traditional beliefs and seeks to create a common native religion.

One Big Family

The native peoples of North America were linked together through clans. Clans were groups whose members claimed a common ancestry. Sometimes, the claim was many generations deep, and clans were very large. Some tribes traced their lineage through female lines (matrilineal) and others through male lines (patrilineal).

Some tribes named the clans after animals who symbolized the strengths and duties of that clan. For example, the Ojibwa originally had seven clans. The Crane and the Loon clans were given the power of chieftainship. They worked together to give the people a balanced government. The members of the Fish clan were the teachers, and the Bear clan acted as the police force. Because the Bear clan members were guarding the land, they learned which plants were safe and useful. The people of the Hoof clan were peacemakers who also cared for members in the tribe. The Martin clan took care of feeding the tribe through hunting and gathering. They were also the warriors of the Ojibwa. Leading the people in their spiritual lives was the job of the Bird clan. The seven clans of the Ojibwa people worked together to build a strong nation. They provided law and order. They became the guardians of the teachings and principles of their way of life.

Clans were an important part of the structure of many native cultures. Villages often organized themselves though the clans. Clan members made important decisions for other members, including who was an appropriate marriage partner or who could claim property. The clan also supervised some ceremonies for the young people of the clan. Clan members were very loyal to those in their clan and would be willing to help or defend other clan members in need.

Today, some people still follow their clan duties. In many tribes, however, the clan system has all but vanished.

title: Indigenous People of Central and South America
text:
There were originally five major empires in Latin America. The Inca and Chibcha lived in South America. The Maya, the Toltec, and Aztec were in Central America. The Inca were the largest and most advanced and civilized when the Europeans arrived. At one point, the Inca Empire extended from northern Ecuador to central Chile, and from the Andes Mountains to the Pacific coast. According to their legends, the Inca came up from the south and settled in the Peruvian highlands around Cuzco. They began to expand around 1100 CE. The Inca were most powerful around the 15th century. Their economy was built on agriculture. Because they lived in mostly mountainous areas, they had special ways to use the land. The Inca terraced their crops. They also used methods of irrigation. The Inca developed great urban centers and well-kept networks of roads. They were skilled in architecture. They refined and worked metal. The Inca were also advanced in weaving, pottery, and other arts. Although the Inca were highly civilized, the Spanish destroyed them by the year 1532 CE.

The other major South American civilization was the Chibcha. The Chibcha were less advanced than the Inca. They had a complex system of cities in the area that is now Bogotá, Colombia. The Chibcha civilization spanned a time of wealth and peace. Although they were wealthy, they had not begun to use stone for building like other major empires. Their nicest homes were constructed from decorated wood.

The Maya were the first big empire in Central America. They had many flourishing city-states in what are now Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico. They made great advances in architecture, sculpture, mathematics, and astronomy. They developed a complex writing system that modern-day researchers have studied. In fact, researchers can now understand about 75 percent of surviving Maya texts. The Maya thrived until about 800 CE when they deserted their cities. No one knows why or what happened to them.

Central America's second major empire belonged to the Toltec. The Toltec were invaders. They came out of the mountains and defeated the biggest city at the time, Teotihuacán. Then they took control of the abandoned Maya cities. The Toltec were leaders in agriculture, craftsmanship, and many other things. Later tribes admired the Toltec. Sometimes, they would claim to be descendants to receive social privilege. The Toltec fell for an unknown reason by 1100 CE.

That’s around the time when the Aztec (or Mexica) came in. The Aztec came from the north, following their sun god, Huitzilopochtli, to the shores of Lake Texcoco. When they first came, they were not liked by other groups in the surrounding area. They sought peace on an island in Lake Texcoco. There, they saw an eagle perched on a cactus, eating a snake. They took that as a sign from their gods and established Tenochtitlán, their island capital. The Aztec ruled central Mexico from this spot, and Tenochtitlán became their major political and social center. Aztec society thrived on the cultivation of maize, a type of corn. The language of the Aztec was Nahuatl. It is still a popularly spoken language among native people in Central America. Mexico City is now built on top of the ruins of the Aztec capital, Tenochtitlán.

title: People of the Arctic
text:
The people of the Canadian Arctic are known as the Inuit, which means “the people.” About 50,000 Inuit live in northern Canada. This region is known as Inuit Nunaat, meaning “Inuit homeland.” They make their living through traditional means, such as hunting, fishing, and trapping. They also work in government, tourism, and mining. The Inuit have enjoyed the benefits of governing themselves over the last 30 years.

In Alaska, there are five different groups of natives: Northwest Coast Indians, Inupiaq, Yupik, Aleuts, and Athabascans. These groups together make up about 16 percent of Alaska’s population. They too have benefitted from land claims agreements. These understandings have allowed the native tribes to live a modern lifestyle. Still, much of the native culture has remained the same. They hunt, fish, and gather plants. This activity provides almost half of the food they eat.

title: Changes in the Amazon
text:
We already know a few things about the Amazon Rainforest. It is the largest tropical rainforest in the world. It receives between 80 and 430 inches of rain each year. It also has the most species. You can find more than 300 reptile species, 500 mammal species, and 175 lizard species living here. There are also more than 30 million insects crawling, leaping, and buzzing around the Amazon. One third of all the world's bird species also live in the region.

The Amazon Rainforest gets its name for the river that runs through it. The Amazon River, which is 4,080 miles long, begins in the Andes of Peru and travels to the Atlantic Ocean at Belem, Brazil. The river empties 28 billion gallons of water every minute into the ocean. Such an amount of freshwater lessens the salt in the Atlantic for about 100 miles offshore.

Two hundred indigenous (native) tribes call the Amazon Rainforest home. The Yanomami are one of the largest groups. The Yanomami live in the rainforests of southern Venezuela and northern Brazil. Two other groups are the Matis ("Jaguar People") and the Huaorani blowgun hunters. They are mostly isolated from outsiders, but that is starting to change.

The countries of Bolivia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Colombia, Brazil, Peru, Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana all share the rainforest. Brazil has the largest section, with 60 percent of the Amazon. Every minute, 60 acres of the Amazon Rainforest are being cut down to make room for more farmland or to sell timber. Destruction of the rainforest is having a very negative effect on indigenous cultures. These tribes are losing the place they have called home for thousands of years. Additionally, contact with the modern world is causing thousands of tribespeople to die from diseases that were previously unknown to their cultures. Many of the tribes’ youth are choosing to leave their homelands for a new world that has just been introduced to them.

title: Today's Maya
text:
More than seven million Maya descendants live in Mesoamerica today, spread all over Central America. They still speak about 30 of the 100 original dialects that made up the ancient Mayan languages. Many live simple lives, farming the land for sustenance, but others have adapted to the 21st century, living in cities and using technology.

The largest groups of Maya descendants live in parts of Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador. Even though they left their ancestral home and dissipated throughout Central America, they have been able to maintain their culture. The ancient Maya language is still spoken, though it is at risk of disappearing. Traditional art is still practiced as well. The ancient religion underwent a significant change when the Spanish forced Christianity upon the inhabitants of the lands they conquered. However, some Maya today practice a blend of Catholicism and their old ways. Some still pray to the corn god for a bountiful harvest.

Only one group still embraces the old ways: the Lacandon. They number about 300 and live in the rainforests of southern Mexico. They still hunt with bows and arrows and live in harmony with nature, occasionally interacting with the outside world by selling some handmade items. Some fear that this group will eventually lose their culture and become integrated into the 21st century way of life.

title: Democracies, Monarchies, and Dictatorships
text:
Democracies

You have probably heard people call the United States a democracy. The word “democracy” comes from two Greek words, meaning “people” and “authority.” In a democracy, the citizens are the ones who elect representatives to run the government. Also, any citizen can be elected to the government; you do not have to be a certain race or from a certain family. In our country, citizens over 18 years old can vote for who they think would do a great job leading our nation. People vote for officials who have the same beliefs as them or feel the same way they do about important issues.

Monarchies

A monarchy is another form of government. A queen or king runs a monarchy. The citizens in a monarchy do not elect their queen or king. Instead, the queen or king are born into their position in the royal family and will pass the crown to a son or daughter. In some monarchies, the people may also vote to elect the members of Parliament. The members of Parliament and the prime minister run the country with the help of the monarch. In other monarchies, the king or queen holds more power. But there are usually representative bodies of some kind. So, while different from a democracy, a monarchy's citizens do have some power to elect decision makers.

Dictatorships

A dictatorship is another form of government that is different from a democracy. In a dictatorship, one person or a small group is in charge of making every decision for the nation. Unlike a democracy, the citizens of a dictatorship cannot decide who is in charge of the government. In fact, they cannot even express their personal opinions about government officials. This type of government is also not guided by a constitution. Cuba and North Korea are both countries with dictatorships.

title: Totalitarianism in Latin America
text:
Many of the modern countries in Latin America began through a revolution, just as the United States did. A revolution is when people gather together and use force or go to war to change something in their own country. The people revolted against their governments in this case. They didn't want to be ruled by a monarchy hundreds or thousands of miles away. Sound familiar?

The new countries set up many kinds of governments. A common kind of government that was established is called a totalitarian government. A totalitarian government is any kind of government in which one person or a small group of people has all the power. They create, explain, and enforce the laws. This means that there is no way for the people to control that person or group. A totalitarian ruler is sometimes called a dictator. Dictators hold so much power that they can easily mistreat their people. Dictators are very hard to replace because people usually don't get to vote or, at least, vote in fair elections. Often, a dictator comes to power as a result of a battle or military takeover.

The only country in Latin America that is still ruled by a dictator is Cuba. Cuba is a communist country, and their leader is Miguel Díaz-Canel. Díaz-Canel served as a Cuban politician before taking office as president in 2019. The two leaders before him, Raúl Castro and Fidel Castro, were brothers. Díaz-Canel is the first president to not be a member of the Castro family since 1976.

title: Scarcity
text:
Countries don’t always have all of the food or resources they need for their citizens. These countries usually trade with other places to get the supplies they don’t have. Most countries need to trade with others in order to give their citizens things they need and want. That means people have access to more goods and services. Problems occur when there are not enough resources to go around. Scarcity is having a very small supply or not enough of something for everyone.

Scarcity of a major resource can affect an economy. Think about what might happen when an area does not get enough rain. Farmers have a harder time growing crops. That means less food for people to eat. People are also less likely to visit lakes, rivers, or water parks. Those people spend less money on gas, souvenirs, and hotels. Many power plants also depend on water. Less rain makes it harder for those places to produce electricity. That can cause energy prices to go up.

When supplies are scarce, people have to make difficult choices. They may have to give up something in order to get whatever is in scarce supply. For example, when water is scarce, families may not be able to water their lawns or take as many showers. These sacrifices, or trade-offs, are sometimes called the opportunity cost. Can you think of a time when you had to give up something in order to get something that was scarce?

Scarcity and weather are not the only factors to consider. The rate of unemployment and the amount of savings and debt all factor into economic performance. Countries have to decide what the costs and benefits are of each decision they make. No one wants people to go hungry, but sometimes hard decisions have to be made that are for the good of all.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors influence the culture of Ohio?

title: Architecture
text:
One of the many ways people can express and preserve their culture is through architecture. Architecture is the style and design of a building. Buildings provide shelter. They are also a place where people gather for celebrations, government functions, and education.

We can learn about a culture's beliefs when we look at their buildings' architecture. When different cultures come together in an area, they create buildings and homes using their country's common architecture. Cultures combine different elements and natural resources to create new architectural styles. This makes the landscape around them unique. Economic activities and resources can also determine the architecture of a building.

When European explorers and settlers came to the Americas, they brought their architecture, or building style, with them. They also took what they knew and blended it with what they learned from native peoples.

The English, French, and Dutch used clay tiles for their roofs at times, but the ones you'll probably recognize right away are Spanish clay tiles. They are often a red, brown, or orange color, and they are curved instead of flat. These tiles were used for many roofs in the Southwest and West regions. When the Spanish settled these areas, they knew that the tiles would absorb the heat of the sun. This style of roof tile is still in use today.

Many homes that were constructed along the Atlantic Coast during the colonial period often used the federal style of architecture. Federal-style homes were constructed of brick or wood siding and were very rectangular in shape. Hundreds of federal-style homes and buildings have been preserved throughout the eastern United States and serve as a reminder of the architectural styles used during the nation’s history.

Ohio has many buildings that represent different architectural styles. During the early 1800s, many settlers came to Ohio from New England. They built homes and buildings in the same style they used in New England. The federal style was the preferred style of architecture for many settlers. In the mid-1800s, architects began to construct buildings using the gothic style of architecture. The characteristics of gothic architecture include large stone structures, towers, and archways. Buildings in Ohio still reflect this cultural influence.

Today, there are many buildings in Ohio that are easily recognizable because of their architecture. The former headquarters of the Longaberger Company is located in Newark, Ohio. The Longaberger Company makes wood baskets, furniture, and other home goods. The former company headquarters is one of the most recognizable buildings in Ohio. The building resembles a picnic basket.

title: Arts and Literature
text:
We can learn about a culture by studying its art and literature. Artists are important to communities. They help us understand culture through art and artistic celebrations. Artwork expresses the traditions of different people. Artists help us learn about how different cultures live, work, and think. Sculptures, photographs, paintings, and sketches reflect the fine art of a culture. Artists draw the images they see around them. Examples are images of people, places, traditions, and celebrations from their culture or other cultures. This allows people from around the world to study the culture of different places.

Literature includes the stories people write and share. Reading, telling, and listening to stories are ways people share their ideas and beliefs with each other. Stories, such as folk tales, myths, and legends, are important to many cultures. These are passed down from one generation to another through storytelling. Shared stories become part of a place's and community's culture. Authors use elements from their own culture in their writings. This allows people from around the world to experience different cultural ideas.

Many American writers have become famous throughout the world for their work. One of the most famous American writers is Mark Twain. When he was 18, Twain became a riverboat captain piloting boats up and down the Mississippi River. His travels inspired some of his most popular works, including The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. He used the landscape of the Mississippi River as the setting for his books.

Many famous authors and illustrators have called Ohio home. Robert McCloskey was a native Ohioan. He was an author and illustrator of children's books. McCloskey’s most famous works include Blueberries for Sal and Make Way for Ducklings. McCloskey received the Caldecott Medal, the highest award given by the American Library Association for children’s book illustrations.

Like authors, American artists have shaped the culture of the United States in many ways. Alice Schille was a famous artist from Ohio. She attended and graduated from the Columbus Art School. After graduating, she started her long career teaching art at the Columbus Art School and began her successful painting career. Schille was a watercolor artist who specialized in painting landscapes and portraits. She was inspired by the people and places of Ohio.

Artists' and authors’ works continue to shape and change the cultural heritage of our country’s communities.

title: Language
text:
Language is another important part of culture. Today, more than 7,000 languages are spoken around the world. Some languages are spoken within a very small area. Others are spoken by large numbers of people in the world.

Most people have a primary language they speak. We call this their native language. This is the first language they learned. They can speak it fluently. Some people learn a second or even third language in addition to their native language. When people learn another language, they often also learn about the culture it represents.

As people move from place to place, they bring their cultures and their languages with them. Multiple languages can be represented in one area. Many streets, cities, towns, and states in the United States take their names from other languages. This brings together cultures from around the world in one place. The movement of languages continues to impact culture today.

The most common language spoken in Ohio is English, but the state’s cultural diversity is reflected by the number of languages spoken in the state. Spanish is the most common non-English language in Ohio, followed by West Germanic languages, such as Yiddish and Pennsylvania Dutch, Mandarin, Cantonese, and Arabic.

title: Religion and Beliefs
text:
Religion is another important part of culture. Religion is a system of beliefs that a group of people shares. There are many different religious beliefs practiced around the world. Some of these are Buddhism, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Christianity.

People from various cultures have different religious beliefs. Religion influences culture in various ways. Many celebrations and traditions come from a cultural group's beliefs or religion. The food we eat, the way we dress, and where we live can also be influenced by religion.

People who share common religious beliefs often form communities. This can create new cultural experiences. Traditions and celebrations can blend when different religious groups in a community come together. Citizens must respect other people’s religious beliefs.

Many people who live in the U.S. today consider themselves to be religious. Many different faiths are practiced in the U.S., such as Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Sikhism, and other religions. Eastern religions such as Taoism, Confucianism, Hinduism, and Buddhism, which are practiced widely across Asia, are more popular in western states like California because of the large number of Asian immigrants who live there.

Ohio is home to a large Amish population. Amish immigrants came to Ohio in the early 1800s. They left Europe because their religious practices were unpopular there. Ohio was more welcoming and they found rich soil for farming. The Amish value humility and simplicity. They hold a religious belief in separating themselves from things that distract them from these values. For this reason, the Amish dress simply and do not use many forms of modern technology. Family life is another important value the Amish hold. This leads adults to choose jobs that do not require them to travel away from their homes for long periods of time.

title: Celebrations
text:
One of the ways people demonstrate their culture is through celebrations. Culture is very important to communities. Cultural communities often celebrate the same holidays in similar ways. Geography often influences how people celebrate and what the celebrations are about. Some cultures celebrate the seasons. Other cultures celebrate planting and harvesting crops.

As people move from one place to another, they bring their culture and celebrations with them. Many places in the United States have unique cultural celebrations. One example of a cultural celebration found in the United States is a Native People’s powwow. A powwow is a modern Native People ceremony where people celebrate, dance, compete, and socialize.

The Cherokee tribe hosts an annual powwow in July in North Carolina. Thousands of visitors attend this powwow each year to watch traditional tribal dances and enjoy Cherokee art, music, and customs. The United Tribes Technical College in Bismarck, North Dakota, organizes a powwow each year. Over 70 tribes gather to compete in Native People dance competitions.

Scandinavian culture is celebrated each year at Norsk Høstfest. This cultural festival is held in Minot, North Dakota. The festival features Scandinavian food, art, and music.

Other celebrations preserve the traditions of immigrants who came to the United States in search of better opportunities. Many Greek immigrants created festivals to celebrate their Greek heritage. One of the largest Greek festivals in the United States is held in Columbus, Ohio, each year. Visitors can enjoy Greek food, crafts, and traditional dance at the festival.

The Germania Society of Cincinnati hosts the Christkindlmarkt each year. The Christkindlmarkt is a Christmas market where visitors can buy Christmas decorations and German products and sample traditional German food.

title: Food
text:
Food is an important element of culture. In most places, the food people eat is based on the natural resources around them. People who live near the ocean tend to eat more fish than people living inland. The climate also dictates what grows well. This explains why people around the world eat differently. Food staples in East and Southeast Asia include rice and fish. Europeans eat more wheat and potatoes. People who live in areas with large grasslands rely heavily on farming and often raise cattle for food. People in different parts of the world also flavor their foods with different spices.

Food can also play an important role in cultural celebrations and holidays. People use special ingredients and recipes to prepare important meals. Many cultures use specific tools for eating and cooking. This helps maintain cultural traditions. When people move to new places, they bring their recipes and food traditions with them. This allows people from many cultures to enjoy new dishes and types of food.

Foods with a Mexican or Hispanic flavor are part of American cuisine. Pupusas (corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans, or pork) from El Salvador are sold at small shops throughout the country. Other favorites include carne asada (Mexican grilled beef strips), fish tacos, and burritos. Because of the large population of Hispanic immigrants in New York, there are many restaurants that feature traditional foods from Cuba, Puerto Rico, Columbia, the Dominican Republic, and other Latin American and South American countries.

"Soul food" is a name given to traditional foods that African Americans have been cooking for years and years. Most soul food is based on recipes created by African Americans who lived in the South. Foods such as fried chicken, fried green tomatoes, okra, black-eyed peas, and grits are all popular soul foods that have become a part of America's cookbook.

Many Native People tribes are working to preserve traditional foods and dishes for people to enjoy today. Some of the dishes are more traditional, such as acorn soup, frybread, fish, and bison, while others have been given a modern twist, such as venison meatballs, chia seed pudding, and maple and butternut squash.

There are many traditional foods and recipes that reflect the culture of Ohio. One of the most famous recipes to come out of Ohio is the buckeye. Buckeyes are made from peanut butter balls dipped in chocolate. They earned the name “buckeyes” because they resemble buckeye nuts. Buckeye nuts grow on the Buckeye tree, which is the state tree of Ohio.

Cincinnati is famous for its chili. Cincinnati chili is traditionally served over noodles and onions and topped with cheese. Restaurants around the country now serve this style of chili, which originated in Ohio.

title: Clothing
text:
The way people dress can be affected by the environments they live in. People use different resources to make clothing. Traditionally, people made clothing from the resources in their environment. Grasses, palm fronds, animal skins, and cloth made from plants are some of the resources used to make clothes. Color dye for cloth was made from local plants. People in tropical and dry climates wore lightweight clothing to keep themselves cool. People who lived in a continental or polar climate made and wore heavier clothing to stay warm.

Clothing also reflects a community's cultural beliefs and traditions. Many cultures and religious groups wear clothing that reflects their beliefs and history. They use materials from the environment to make traditional clothing.

For many ethnic groups, their culture's traditional clothing is usually only worn for special occasions, such as weddings, funerals, graduations, festivals, or other special celebrations. Some examples of traditional Asian dress you may see include the Japanese kimono, the Korean hanbok, the Chinese hanfu, and the Vietnamese áo giao lĩnh.

Traditional Mexican clothing for men includes things like the poncho, sombrero, and the elaborately embroidered three-piece charro suit. This is usually worn on the Day of the Dead. Some popular traditional clothing for women includes things such as the huipil, which is a loose, embroidered tunic worn with a skirt, or the Mexican folklore dress, which is often very colorful with a long, flared skirt for dancing.

Traditional Native People clothing has a wide range of styles and decorations from tribe to tribe. Today, most traditional clothing is only worn on special occasions. Some examples of traditional clothing used by different tribes include elaborate headdresses, skirts made of animal skins or plant fibers, and the use of feathers, shells, or beads for ornamentation. Special clothing reserved for certain ceremonies is called “regalia.”

The Amish have strict rules about their clothing and the attire they can wear. Amish clothing reflects the beliefs of humility, simplicity, and separation from the wider world. Clothing is made at home from plain, dark fabrics. The Amish do not use zippers to fasten their clothing because of their beliefs in simplicity. Instead, they use straight pins, snaps, and buttons.

title: Introduction to North America
text:
Indigenous people lived all across North America during the period from 500 to 1500 C.E. They lived in diverse communities. They had distinct governments, economies, and traditions. The focus of the next few weeks of study will be on the Indigenous groups from the Northeast, Plains, and Southeast sections of North America.

Governments

Indigenous Americans used many different systems to organize their communities. Some native peoples lived in small, independent groups. The smallest native political unit was the individual. Individuals had complete freedom to make their own decisions. Next was the band or village. A band is a group of people of the same tribe who are closely connected. Often they’re connected by family ties. Bands might fish, hunt, and grow food together. Bands had leaders for different duties. Bands had one chief for war and a different one for peace.

Clans are larger groups of distant relatives. Clan elders were often chosen to make decisions for the group. Bands or clans join together to form tribes. A tribe is a group of people connected by a common language, belief, land, and culture.

A chiefdom is a group of tribes under one leader, or chief. The chief’s authority often stayed in the same family. Some cultures passed authority down through the father’s side of the family. Other cultures passed authority down through the mother’s side. For most tribes, if a chief was not doing well for their people, that chief would be removed. Many chiefs had to earn their right to lead their people.

Some tribes also joined together to form confederacies. A confederacy is an alliance between various groups. One example of a confederacy was the Haudenosaunee, or Iroquois. Each tribe in the confederacy had its own leadership, but during times of conflict or distress, the tribes came together and made decisions in a council of chiefs.

Language

Before the arrival of Europeans in North America, there were approximately 500 different Native American languages spoken by millions of Indigenous people. The languages of various tribes were diverse. Some languages were spoken within a very small area, while others were spoken by large numbers of people across the continent. In the Northeast, there were two large language families: Algonquian and Iroquois. Within these language families, tribes or bands would speak distinct dialects of the language. In the Plains, there were more language families, including Algonquian, Siouan, Caddoan, and Uto-Aztecan. Members of the Southeast tribes spoke Muskogean, Siouan, Iroquoian, and Caddoan languages. Language patterns show connections between tribes in multiple areas of North America.

title: Week 13 Framing Question
text: What did most Native North American tribes have in common?

title: Timeline
text:
Because most Indigenous peoples in North America did not have written records, the history of these peoples comes from oral history, archaeological sources, and European settlers’ records.

3000 B.C.E.–1000 C.E.: This era is known as the Woodland Period.

1000 B.C.E.–1500 C.E.: The Adena and Hopewell cultures build mounds in the Ohio River Valley.

650 C.E.–1400 C.E.: The Cahokia, another mound-building culture, builds large mounds to support a city of 20,000-30,000 people.

1000 C.E.: Vikings arrive in Mi’kmaq land in the area known as Newfoundland.

1450 C.E.–1660 C.E.: The Haudenosaunee confederacy begins sometime during these years.

1492 C.E.: Columbus arrives in the Caribbean.

1501 C.E.: A Portuguese explorer kidnaps and enslaves Haudenosaunee people.

1503 C.E.: Fishers begin fishing for cod in Newfoundland.

1513 C.E.: Spanish conquistadors reach Florida.

1598 C.E.: The horse reaches the plains.

title: Trade Routes
text:
Trade was very important to Indigenous peoples. They exchanged food, goods, and information. For thousands of years, Native Americans operated huge trade networks to get what they needed from other tribes. For example, people in what is now North Dakota quarried a hard stone called flint near Knife River. The stone was so valuable in ancient times that 4,000 years ago, it was being traded far from the quarry. Copper and obsidian have also been discovered far from their natural locations. This proves a trade system existed.

Another example of trade comes from the Hohokam tribe in what is now Arizona. The Hohokam traded bison hides for seashells. Neither resource comes from Arizona! The hides came from tribes on the Plains. Plains tribes often traded bison robes, dried meat, and tallow for corn and squash. The shells came from the Mojave tribe in California. By trading with both groups, the Hohokam became middlemen within a larger trade route. Middlemen took goods from one group to another during trade.

Trade was an essential part of the economy and government. Often, governments made trade agreements. But not all trade was peaceful. Sometimes tribes would go to war to control trade routes and resources. Eventually, leaders would make peace treaties for their people.

Rivers and Trails

Rivers were extremely important when people needed to travel. Many traveled by canoe on major rivers like the Mississippi, Ohio, Columbia, and Missouri. Some canoes could haul thousands of pounds of goods for trade. Native peoples also made trading paths. One well-known route stretched from the forests by Lake Erie to the South Carolina coast. This trail, called the Trading Path, appeared on maps in the 1700s. Rivers and other trading paths crossed all over North America.

Trails often followed the “military crest” of the ridge. Trails ran alongside but not on the ridge tops. This way, a person could travel along the trail without being seen by those on the other side of the ridge. Many Native Americans disciplined themselves to walk heel-to-toe in a single file. This left the smallest mark on the ground and allowed them to travel without being seen.

Trading Sites

Some trading locations were more permanent, while others moved where the people went. One example of a permanent trading station is the straits of Mackinac. The straits of Mackinac is where Lakes Michigan and Huron meet. This area in the Great Lakes attracted tribes from all over the eastern woodlands to trade. The Odawa and Chippewa had villages at Mackinac and conducted the trade. Trade was well-established and vital to Native Americans across North America.

title: Environment and Respect for the Land
text:
As in other areas of the world, the geography and environment where Indigenous peoples lived influenced their governments, economies, and cultures. For example, the people in the Northeast were surrounded by dense forests, which some tribes used to build their homes, called longhouses. Other tribes in the same region gathered food from the forest. One way they did this was by tapping trees and gathering sap to use in their food.

Native North American peoples have a deep respect and connection to nature and the land they live on. The natural world played a vital role in their sacred beliefs and everyday lives. They cared for the land and used their resources wisely. They believed that if they took care of the Earth, the Earth would take care of them. Many tribes used the same name to describe the Earth, “Mother Earth.”

Native Americans did not believe in individual land ownership. The land was used by tribes and belonged to the tribe. Products from the land were communal and shared among the bands that lived there. Because tribes relied so much on the land for their resources, they needed lots of land to get those resources. Tribes would cover millions of acres to get food, fuel, water, and other resources. A certain area may be used for several years. Then the tribe would leave so the area could replenish itself. Eventually, the tribe would come back to that area when it was ready.

title: Culture: Customs and Traditions
text:
The native peoples of North America have many different cultures and traditions. Each group has its own beliefs, rituals, and traditions. Many traditions are connected with the land the tribes call home. This connection to their homeland is similar for many tribes. Most North American tribes are different in many ways, but they also share many similar customs and traditions. They have marriage ceremonies, funerals, and rites of passage for youth. Their cultures all include language, storytelling and the arts, celebrations, food, and clothing.

Storytelling and the Arts

The arts and storytelling are a large part of Native American culture. Native peoples living in North America did not use an alphabet to communicate, but they did have symbols that were part of stories. These symbols were placed on important, ceremonial items or painted on rocks. People mainly used the spoken word to communicate and to preserve their history and traditions. Often, their speeches took the form of stories. Many stories explained their beliefs about the creation of the world. Some stories represented actual events that happened in the tribe’s past. Some represented relationships between families and their ancestors. Other stories are more like religious stories for the tribes. These stories have lessons on how to be good people and treat everything with respect. Elders often taught these stories to children. Animals, birds, and the environment were often part of these important stories, creating a special bond to the land.

Throughout North America, native peoples made beautiful pieces of art from natural materials around them. They used shells, porcupine quills, or feathers for decoration. Jade, turquoise, and other stones were used to create their art. They crafted jewelry and other items from silver, turquoise, and gold. Some cultures were known for creating elaborate sculptures out of stone, wood, and other materials. Many tribes wove baskets and made pottery. But not all the things made by native peoples were simply art. Many items were used in ceremonies and considered very sacred. These sacred items are only used for special occasions, like a funeral. Early Native American art continues to influence artists, and many tribes continue to create art in the same way as their ancestors.

Ceremonies and Celebrations

Native American tribes had their own individual ceremonies and celebrations, but many tribes celebrated for common reasons. Ceremonies and celebrations were often held to honor the people’s ancestors and celebrate the natural elements around them. Many holidays honor the sun, rain, and harvest.

Dancing, singing, and praying were very important in Indigenous ceremonies. Many ceremonies are performed to help people who were sick. Some ceremonies were to celebrate when a child became an adult. When warriors came back from battle, special ceremonies were performed to help them not be angry. There were celebrations for a good harvest, giving thanks for the food. When a young hunter killed their first deer or bison, a special feast would be held to honor the animal and the new hunter for the community.

Food

North American Indigenous groups relied on the land for food. Tribes hunted, gathered, and farmed for food. Many of the foods they ate were based on the seasons. Seasonal crops and hunting patterns played a huge role in community activities. Members of each tribe worked together to provide food for the community. Many of the foods that we enjoy today can be traced back to the crops grown by Native Americans. These include corn, potatoes, tomatoes, peanuts, wild rice, squash, and beans.

Clothing

Before European exploration, Native American tribes used natural resources from the land to create clothing. Native American clothing represented the natural environment in which they lived. Clothing was practical and reflected the climate where they lived. Native Americans used animal products, such as fur, feathers, bones, teeth, and claws, to make clothing and jewelry. They also used plants like tree bark and various grasses to make woven fabrics. They wore different forms of clothing for different purposes. Members of many tribes wore decorative headdresses, masks, and clothing for ceremonies and celebrations.

title: Needs and Wants
text:
A need is something that you have to have every day. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us warm or cool.

Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler, to help you be successful each day.

A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. A want is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

title: Week 21 Framing Question
text: How do geography and resources influence a state?

title: Resources
text:
A resource is a material that people can use. Things like soil, air, and water are resources. People depend on resources to survive. There are three categories of resources. They are natural, human, and capital resources. It is important for people and communities to use resources wisely so that we will have enough in the future.

Many things we use to meet our needs come from nature. They are natural resources. Natural resources include things like soil, water, natural gas, and coal. These things make our lives easier. We burn coal and use natural gas to power and heat our homes. We make furniture, houses, and books out of trees. Some of the items we use every day, like cell phones, computers, and clothing, come from natural resources. Natural resources can be renewable, nonrenewable, or flow.

Renewable resources can be replaced, like trees. New trees can be planted to renew those we cut down.

Nonrenewable resources cannot be easily replaced. Oil and natural gas are examples. It took millions of years to form these resources. Once we use them all up, they are gone forever.

Flow resources are part of Earth’s natural processes. They must be used where they occur. Wind, running water, and solar energy are flow resources.

Capital resources are the tools that help us make other things. These items are man-made. This means they do not occur naturally in the environment. They need to be created before they can be used. Capital resources include tools, buildings, and machines. Machines like lawnmowers or ovens are capital resources. Buildings like factories and warehouses are other examples.

Human resources include people, their ideas, and their skills. Teachers, doctors, and farmers are examples of human resources. Scientists and inventors are also human resources. They are creative people who have developed new technologies to improve lives. For example, new types of transportation and communication have changed our lives. We can fly products to and from other countries within one day. We can video chat with people on the other side of the world. Human creativity and innovation are some of the greatest resources we have.

title: Scarcity and Opportunity Cost
text:
Surplus is when the supply of a good or service is more than the demand. In other words, there is more than people need or want. A surplus of a good or service usually makes the price go down.

Scarcity is when there is more demand for something than there is supply. In other words, it is not having enough of something people want or need. Sometimes, scarcity can be a big problem. If basic resources like food or water are scarce, it is hard for people to live. When goods and services become scarce, families have to decide what they need most. Families have to make choices about how to spend their money to meet their needs.

We often have to make choices on how to spend our money. Sometimes we want more than one thing at a time. This means we have to make a choice about which thing to buy. Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you make a choice. Imagine you have $20. Your friends want to go see a new movie, but there is also a book you would like to buy. You can’t afford both. If you decide to buy the book, you give up the movie. The movie is the opportunity cost.

title: Industrial Revolution
text:
Territory and businesses in the United States expanded during the late 19th century. From this period into the early 20th century, industrialization changed in the United States. Industrialization meant that more factories were being built. This meant goods were being produced faster. Factories needed supplies to produce goods and transportation to ship them to customers.

Advances in steel production made steel cheaper. The process also produced more steel in less time. Steel production became a big business. Railroads could expand using steel that cost less. More machines for factories could be purchased because steel costs were lower.

The expanding availability of electricity changed the lives of Americans. Many inventions used electricity. These inventions made life easier. Alexander Graham Bell found a way to use electricity to transmit sound from one place to another through wire. He had invented the telephone. Thomas Edison experimented with electricity until he perfected the light bulb. This type of light bulb could be safely used in homes. Electric streetcars began to replace horse-drawn carriages. The first radio waves were successfully transmitted across the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Week 22 Framing Question
text: How do people contribute to the progress of government and society?

title: More Effects of the Industrial Revolution
text:
During this time, many factories were built. These factories used an assembly line system. Before the creation of the assembly line, a product had to be made by hand. One worker, or a group of workers, would create the entire product, one at a time. In an assembly line, the product moved along a moving belt or track. Each worker along the line had one task. They would do this task over and over as the product came to them. For example, if a car was being built, the basic frame would begin moving on the assembly line. Each worker along the line would add their part to the car. By the end of the line, the car would be complete. Using the assembly line process, more cars could be created in a shorter period of time.

Not all of this growth was good for some businesses. Some of the people who ran bigger businesses made deals with suppliers. These deals gave them exclusive access to resources. This hurt the smaller companies that needed the same resources. These giant corporations became monopolies. Becoming a monopoly allowed a business to control the prices and availability of a product. The companies often made illegal payments to the government and other business officials. They made these illegal payments in order to grow their businesses and get rid of the competition. When these actions were publicly revealed, the federal government created laws to end monopolies.

title: Free Enterprise
text:
The free market system is an important aspect of a market economy. Free market systems only work if a country's laws and its citizens' values support them. Six characteristics of a free market system make it successful. These are private property, specialization, voluntary exchange, price system, market competition, and entrepreneurship.

Private property is an important part of a free market system. We learn to care for the things we own. Spending money on the things we own gives us a reason to take care of the things we own. If a business doesn't take care of its office building or it breaks equipment, the business must pay to replace them. This gives the business incentive to care for the things it uses.

Specialization means a business focuses on creating one type of product or providing specific services. This allows the company to become experts. They can also produce more goods over time. Companies that specialize in one product are able to save money on the goods and resources needed to make their product.

Voluntary exchange is another important part of a free market system. Voluntary exchange means people must exchange goods or currency to pay for or get the resources they need. Consumers have the choice to purchase goods and services.

Creating a price system is crucial for a free market economy's success. Prices provide guidance for producers and consumers. Prices show the market how much customers value the producer's goods. Most consumers try to shop for bargains if prices rise. This keeps businesses from overcharging their customers.

A free market system must have competition within the market to work properly. Competition between producers who make similar products lowers product prices. This creates more options for consumers. It can also make resources and products more valuable.

A free market economy's final characteristic is entrepreneurship. Entrepreneurship is developing, organizing, and managing a new business. Entrepreneurs are people who create and run businesses. They must be able to adapt to changing markets and meet customer demands.

title: Trade, Imports, and Exports
text:
Our country does not produce everything we need. We have to buy things from other countries. That is called trade. Trade is when you buy, sell, or exchange a good or service for something else you want or need. Businesses, states, and countries trade goods and services all around the world. Trade between countries is a very important part of a nation’s economy. Because of interdependence and trade, our community is affected by events around the world.

Bartering is trading goods without the use of money. In early cultures, people were able to get many things they needed and wanted through bartering. Today, we use money to buy what we need because it is much easier to use.

International trade depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods brought in from other countries. Exports are goods sent out to other countries to be sold. Rice, oil, and computers are made in Asia and imported to the United States. They are imports. Cars, airplanes, and machines are made in the United States and exported to other countries.

title: GIS Technology
text:
Geographic Information Systems, also known as GIS, are a way of visualizing data on maps. As soon as people invented computers capable of doing it, they began using computers to map information. If you have data or information that matches locations on a map, you can use GIS to make a visual representation of that data on a map. Looking at the data overlaid on a map can reveal new relationships and patterns that might not have seemed obvious at first.

Without the ability to map data and visualize it, it can be difficult to understand what the data is representing. Trends and patterns in the data can often be missed if you do not understand the physical relationship between the various points of information. Any information that can be mapped can be visualized through GIS.

Many different people in many different careers rely on GIS data and visuals to do their work. City planners can use GIS to map the riders on public transportation, like buses and subways, to make sure their transportation plans meet people where they are. Biologists can observe the presence of endangered species and plan protection strategies through the information they learn from GIS.

Archaeologists use GIS to map the presence of historical sites and artifacts. Archaeologists dig in the ground and dive in bodies of water, looking for artifacts. They use GIS to make detailed digital models of the sites where they find these artifacts. Mapping the data through GIS allows them to visualize the entire site and find patterns they might otherwise miss. Recreating the site digitally also allows them to limit the amount they disturb the fragile historical sites.

County governments in the state use GIS data. This data allows the counties to share important information and gives them access to important services like fire stations and schools.

title: Thomas Edison and Electric Lights
text:
Technology fascinated Thomas Edison from an early age. He began conducting science experiments when he was only 12.

When he got older, Edison built a laboratory. He hired assistants to help him work on new inventions and improve existing technology. Soon, Edison decided he needed more space for equipment. He built a much larger laboratory. It was the first lab of its kind. It had buildings for a carpenter, blacksmith, glassmaker, and more. Today, many research and development laboratories still use this laboratory design Edison created at Menlo Park.

One of Edison’s first inventions was the phonograph. The phonograph was the first machine to record sound. The voice recording Edison made was the poem “Mary Had a Little Lamb.” People began calling Edison “The Wizard of Menlo Park” because of his incredible inventions.

Edison turned his attention to electric lights. The first incandescent light bulb had already been invented by a British scientist in 1840. However, it was too expensive for regular use. Edison created many, many light bulbs that didn’t work. But Edison didn’t give up. After a lot of hard work, Edison and his assistants invented the first long-lasting electric light bulb.

Edison patented more than 1,000 inventions in his lifetime. Many were created by his hardworking assistants. Without the inventions created at Edison’s laboratories, the world would not be the same.

title: Alexander Graham Bell and the Telephone
text: Alexander Graham Bell was the first person to patent a device that could transmit speech electronically. His device was called the telephone. Bell wanted to improve the telegraph. As a result, he invented the telephone. The telegraph could only receive and send one message at a time. Bell had a good knowledge of sound and an understanding of music. This allowed him to think about the possibility of transmitting multiple messages over the same wire at the same time. This is how the multiple telegraph was developed. Bell and his assistant, Thomas Watson, began to explore the idea of a device that would transmit speech electrically. In 1875, Bell and Watson proved that different tones would vary the strength of an electric current in a wire. Bell discovered he could hear sound over a wire. His discovery led to the end of the multiple telegraph and the beginning of the telephone. Today, telephones can be found all around the world.

title: Henry Ford and Automobiles
text:
Henry Ford was born in 1863. He grew up on a farm in Dearborn, Michigan. At the age of 16, he left home to study machines. Later, he returned home. Here, he continued work on the farm and in factories. He also operated and serviced steam engines. In 1891, he began working as an engineer at the Edison Illuminating Company in Detroit.

In his free time, Ford worked on a gasoline-powered automobile. He called his invention the “Quadricycle.” It was the very first of its kind. His invention drew a lot of attention from investors. They helped support him as he built more vehicles. Some of them formed the Detroit Automobile Company. Ford worked there until 1902. In 1903, he created his own company, called the Ford Motor Company.

In 1913, Ford developed a new system of making cars in his factory. He began using a moving assembly line. This meant each worker had one job to do in the car's assembly. Using this idea, factories made cars more quickly than if they were assembled one car at a time. Ford believed that this mass production would make his company very successful.

Ford also had ideas about how to treat workers in his car factory. He offered them up to $5 a day to work for him. At the time, this was a very large wage to be paid for a day's work. Ford wanted to be sure his own employees could afford to buy one of the cars they were helping to produce.

Henry Ford's ideas about using assembly lines to produce goods are still used around the world.
