title: Entrepreneurs
text:
An entrepreneur is someone who comes up with an idea and then uses this idea to start a business. Entrepreneurs are people who have a vision about something new or helpful they can offer their community. They combine the natural, human, and capital resources in an area to produce goods and services. They make decisions about what to produce based on the needs and wants of people in their area.

Entrepreneurs have many reasons for wanting to start their own businesses. Some entrepreneurs want to build something of their own. Others feel they can make a lot of money by working for themselves. Others have a solution to solve a problem. There are big opportunities and risks involved in being an entrepreneur. Successful entrepreneurs often have a great impact on their communities.

Entrepreneurs also fund their businesses with capital resources by themselves. The entrepreneur becomes the sole, or only, owner. If a person with a business idea joins with others to make it happen and share profits, it is a partnership. Entrepreneurs hold the responsibility of the business by themselves.

title: Interest
text:
Did you know that you can earn income by lending someone some of your money? Interest is another form of income that people might earn. Sometimes, people need to borrow money in order to buy things they need or want. They may borrow money from a bank, a company, or another person, who is often called a lender. The loan, or money borrowed, must be paid back to the lender within a certain amount of time.

The person borrowing money has to pay interest on the loan. Interest is the amount of money a lender or financial institution receives for lending money. For example, if a person borrows $100 from a bank, the bank will charge interest on that loan. When that person pays back the loan, they will have to pay $100 plus the interest charged. You might be wondering where banks get the money that they loan to people and businesses. That money can come from you. If you have a bank account that earns interest, the bank is paying you to allow them to use your money.

Interest rates can change over time. Higher interest rates cost the borrower more money. This gives the lender higher income. It costs money to borrow money to pay back over time. With some credit card debt, the interest will eventually cost more than the amount borrowed. Smart consumers stay aware of their interest rates.

title: Goods and Services
text:
Goods are items you can use or consume to meet your needs and wants. They are produced using human, natural, and capital resources. Goods can also be things people grow. In the United States, goods fall into two categories. These are private and public goods. Private goods are items you can buy from a business with your own money. Private goods include food, clothing, furniture, and toys. Public goods are paid for with taxes, not individual consumers. Public goods include law enforcement, sewer systems, and public parks.

A service is work that one person does for someone else. Services are actions, such as haircuts, car repairs, medical check-ups, mail delivery, and teaching. Services provided by the government are known as public services. These include hospitals, schools, police and fire stations, trash pickup, and public transportation. An example of a public service is going to your community library. It doesn't cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. Businesses owned by people are considered private enterprises.

How do companies compete to provide goods and services to consumers? Specialization lets companies make more and better products. They make more money if they make more of a product to sell. When a company makes more money, they can hire more workers. Then, more people have money to spend on things they need and want. Many companies may specialize in the same goods and services. This allows consumers to make choices. They can choose goods and services they wish to purchase based on price, availability, and quality.

The United States produces many goods for consumers around the globe. It produces billions of dollars worth of public and private goods, industrial supplies, automobiles, and agricultural products. These goods are used by consumers in our country. They are also exported to countries all over the world.

title: Different Lenses
text:
Compelling questions are often very big. It helps us to think about them in different ways.

For example, historians look at the past to see how people solved problems. They look at different periods of time. They think about how past events have shaped the present.

Historians ask:

What happened?

When did it happen?

Why did it happen?

How did things change?

What did we learn from it?

Geographers study the interaction between people and the environment. Knowing how people and the environment impact a problem is important.

Geographers ask:

Where is it?

How do we use or interact with it?

Why is it important to us?

Political scientists study how a government works. They help community leaders make laws for their people.

Political scientists ask:

How will laws help our community?

Who has the power to create a law?

How are laws enforced?

Well-being scientists study the whole person: academic, social, emotional, physical, and mental. They analyze the effects behaviors and emotions have on people or groups of people.

Well-being scientists ask:

How did that event or action impact people?

What are the consequences of these actions or events?

How can I see this from a different perspective?

What are the facts, and what is my interpretation of the situation?

What is in my control, and what is not in my control?

Economists think about resources, money, and finance. They look at the production of goods and services in a community. They look at available resources and how they can help fix a problem.

Economists ask:

What resources are in our community?

How do people make money?

Why do people use different products?

What businesses are needed in our community?

title: Essential Question
text: What would motivate people to take creative risks that lead to innovations and inventions?

title: Essential Question
text: How is the government designed to protect rights and promote the common good?

title: Essential Question
text: How does Ohio's location and its transportation systems influence the movement of people, products, and ideas?

title: Moving People, Goods, and Ideas
text:
Like people, ideas can travel around the world by means of transportation and communication. Transportation is the movement of goods and people from one place to another. Advancements in transportation allow people to move farther and faster than they ever have before. Goods can also travel faster to many locations. Farmers and factories can ship their products by railroad, truck, or plane throughout the country and the world. Cities have been created and have grown because of these new types of transportation. People can now reach places they never would have been able to before.

Moving ideas and information is called communication. Communication and technology are an important part of studying movement within geography. We use communications systems when we communicate with people. These systems spread information between large numbers of people. The internet is a good example. People communicate in many different ways. We don’t always communicate in spoken or written messages. We are able to connect with people around the world like never before. Technology makes it possible to share information with groups of people throughout the world.

Because of its strategic location and abundance of resources, Ohio’s transportation systems are a vital link in the movement of people, goods, and ideas throughout the United States and the world.

title: Transportation on Land
text:
Ohio Railroads

Before America's introduction to the steam locomotive in 1820, Ohio relied heavily on water transportation. People and goods traveled via Lake Erie, the Ohio and Erie Canal, and other smaller canals and rivers. However, not all parts of the state had access to canals and waterways. People wanted access to railroads to ship goods across the state and nation.

The Erie and Kalamazoo Railroad was the first railroad to be completed in Ohio in 1836. However, it wasn't until the 1840s that construction on rail lines in Ohio began in earnest. Some of Ohio's largest railroads included the Cincinnati, Hamilton, and Dayton Railroad (CH&D) and the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway. The CH&D was primarily used for passenger transport, while the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway was used mainly for transporting coal.

Today, railroads are still used for transporting goods and people. Many of the first rail lines and companies were purchased or merged with other companies over the years. Today, Ohio railroads are used mainly to transport goods, but some lines are also used for passenger transportation.

Roads and Highways

The first federal highway, the National Road, started construction in 1811. The first roads, though, were mainly mud. Sometimes, the roads would be built from plank logs. Roads steadily improved over the years, and by 1891, Ohio became the first state to use concrete to pave a street. However, it wasn't until the Ford Model T came on the scene that our state roads started changing. Starting in 1908, the Model T was a cheaper car that more people could afford. This increased the demand for better roads. Over time, asphalt roads replaced the old dirt roads.

With the passage of the Interstate Highway Act of 1956, more roads and highways were constructed to connect major cities across the U.S. As more and more highways and roads were built to connect cities and towns across the nation, railroads began to fall out of use for transporting goods and people. Today, 113,435 miles of highway cross through Ohio, including Interstates 70, 71, 75, 76, 77, 80, and 90.

Moving goods and people is still important in Ohio today. We still use trains to ship goods, but trucks carry most of our state’s products. In fact, trucks are sometimes called the "backbone" of our nation. This is because trucks carry most of the things we buy to places around our state and nation. Whether you buy food, clothes, video games, or anything else you can think of, trucks probably used one of the interstates to get it to your local store.

title: Transportation on Water
text:
In 1807, a man named Robert Fulton created a steamboat that could carry passengers and freight. His first steamboat was called the Clermont. The invention of the steamboat helped Americans settle in new towns all over the country. The steamboat made life much easier. It could bring people and goods up and down rivers much more quickly than a wagon could bring them on land. It was also cheaper to travel by steamboat. By 1830, steamboats were the most common form of river transportation. Steamboats helped develop the country’s trade system by delivering goods faster and cheaper than by horse and wagon.

Before canals were built, western farmers transported their crops with horses and wagons over the mountains to states in the East. That cost a lot of money and took a long time. Digging canals, or human-made waterways, between rivers made things easier. Before the invention of the steamboat, ropes tied to horses or mules were used to tow, or pull, boats as they walked on a path next to the canal.

The first canal in Ohio opened in 1827, making a waterway between Cleveland and Akron. Canals made it much faster and less expensive for farmers to move their crops. Canals also doubled the speed of travel to about four miles per hour. That doesn't seem very fast now, but it was really something back then.

In less than 25 years, workers built 1,000 miles of canals to connect cities and towns in Ohio. Building canals also made the land worth more, and lots of people started moving to Ohio. Many settlers got jobs digging the canals or working on the canals after they opened. Others started businesses around the canals. The canals also carried iron ore from the Great Lakes area and coal from the Appalachian Mountain region. Ohioans used these resources to start the local steel industry. More industry meant more stores and other businesses, too. The population of Ohio went from around half a million to two million in only 30 years.

Today, most of the canals are no longer in use, thanks to interstate highways and trucking. Some steamboats are still operational as tourist attractions, and a short stretch of canal is still used in the Muskingum Valley. However, roads and automobiles are the most common way for goods and people to move around the state and country.

title: Transportation in Air
text:
Many experiments were carried out over the years by people hoping to harness the power of flight. They involved anything from paper wings to gliders made of wood and canvas. However, brothers Wilbur and Orville Wright, from Dayton, Ohio, successfully achieved the first powered flight on Dec. 17, 1903. Although their first airplane wasn’t much more than a glider, it had a powered motor attached to it. This allowed them to actually fly rather than merely glide on wind currents.

Airplanes started out as a means of entertainment for the public. They were very unsafe and frequently crashed. As plane designs and safety improved, planes began to be used for more practical purposes. During WWI, some planes were used to gather information and map areas of land in enemy territory. Not much fighting was done in the air, but airplanes quickly proved to be a step toward the future.

Further advances and increases in airplane safety led to their use in military, commercial, and passenger transportation. Today, thousands of planes fly across the country and the world every day. Traveling by plane is the fastest way to travel across long distances. Journeys that once took several weeks or even months can now be made in a matter of hours.

Flight technology has also been used to transport people and resources into space. Resources such as satellites and the International Space Station were launched into space thanks to modified aviation technology. Now, these valuable resources orbit the Earth and give us access to tools such as the internet and the Global Positioning System.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
A producer is someone who makes a good or provides a service. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are used for other communities. Farmers, factory workers, car mechanics, and doctors are producers. The person who cuts your hair is also a producer.

People who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. People often depend on trade with others to meet their wants and needs. People can be both a producer and a consumer. When we buy groceries, gas, clothing, or toys, we are buying goods. When we go to the doctor, have our car fixed, or get a haircut, we are using services. When you get a haircut, you’re a consumer because you’re buying a service.

Both consumers and producers affect the prices of goods and services. For example, a company that produces bicycles may raise the price of their product if there’s a metal shortage. A shortage is when something you need can’t be found in the amount needed. Consumers may stop buying bikes if the price is too high. Then the company might have to lower prices to get more sales. When a consumer doesn’t buy enough of a good or service it may cause producers to lower the cost of it. If consumers are buying too much of a product, a producer might increase the product’s price.

title: Interdependence
text:
Interdependence

Interdependence is mutually relying on each other to get things done. A tire factory specializes in tires. Every community and country in the world depends on other communities and countries for some of the things they need. In the United States, many states specialize in specific agricultural products and manufactured goods that they can send to other states in exchange for different goods.

Some areas of the United States have natural resources that allow them to make or grow certain things. Countries trade goods and services. People cannot make and grow everything they need. They depend on each other. Specialization creates interdependence and world trade.

Many areas of the United States specialize in growing or producing specific products. Car manufacturing requires parts produced around the country to create automobiles. Tires manufactured in Ohio, airbags produced in Utah, and transmissions built in South Carolina are shipped to facilities in Michigan to build automobiles.

Our country does not produce everything we need. We have to buy things from other countries. That is called trade. Trade is when you buy, sell, or exchange a good or service for something else you want or need. A nation’s economy depends on its ability to trade with other nations. Trade depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods that are brought in from another country. Exports are goods sent to another country to be sold. In other words, imports are things you need or want but do not produce. So, you must buy those things from somewhere else. Exports are things you produce or have that you can sell for money or barter for other goods.

title: Opportunity Cost
text:
Opportunity Cost

People make choices on how to spend their money. Sometimes we want more than one thing at a time. This means we have to make a choice. We have to decide what to keep and what to give up. Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you make a choice. Imagine you have $20. Your friends want to go see the new movie, but there is also

a book you would like to buy. Before you can make a choice, you need to find out how expensive each option is. You might ask a friend or family member for advice. If you are patient, the price may drop in a few weeks. It might be a good idea to wait for that to happen. Whichever you choose, you also have to think about the opportunity cost. It can be a hard choice!

title: Spending Choices
text:
Spending Choices

You need to buy a new pair of shoes. How do you pick which ones to buy? The least expensive ones? The ones with the coolest advertisement? The ones that your favorite athlete or celebrity is wearing? All of these factors and more can influence how we spend our money. Every time you spend money on something, you are making a choice.

Some of the factors that influence your spending choices are advertisements and commercials that companies or individuals use to call attention to their product or service. Others include price, or the cost, and peer pressure, or influence from your friends or other individuals. The decision to spend your money on a product or service is an important one and should be based on good information. If you make a decision that is not based on good information, you might end up wasting your money on a product or service that is not right for you.

title: Scarcity
text:
Scarcity is not having enough of something. Sometimes scarcity can be a big problem. If food or water is scarce, it is hard for people to live. When goods and services become scarce, families have to decide what they need most. Families have to make choices about how to spend their money to meet their needs.

The scarcity of a major resource can affect an economy. An area that doesn’t get enough rain can affect the economy. Without rain, farmers have a harder time growing crops. That means less food for people to eat. Less rain can also affect tourism. People will be less likely to visit lakes and rivers. There will be less money coming to gas stations, souvenir stores, and hotels. Many power plants depend on water. Less rain makes it harder for those places to produce electricity. That can cause prices to go up.

When supplies are scarce, people have to make difficult choices. They may have to give up something in order to get whatever is in scarce supply. People have a choice of what they want to buy. Every choice has value to each person. When a person makes a choice, they are valuing that product over the others. The products a person gives up is opportunity cost.

title: Barter
text:
Bartering is trading goods without using money. In early cultures, people were able to get many things they needed and wanted through bartering. Merchants would often travel on ships laden with goods. These goods were bartered for items that could be taken back. Then they would be either bartered for other goods or traded for money. People, towns, and even countries bartered for items they did not produce or grow.

Bartering is still going on today. People, companies, and even countries barter for things they need or want. Countries that raise great amounts of beef may barter with countries that grow large amounts of grain. Companies may trade services to support one another.

People who work pay a part of their income to the federal government in the form of taxes. When you buy something, you pay a little more than the price tag says. This is because you’re also paying a small tax, called a sales tax. Sales tax helps the government provide goods and services to everyone.

title: Essential Question
text: How can you describe the physical environments in North America?

title: Physical Environments of North America
text:
Physical characteristics describe the natural environment of an area. Landscapes, plants, climate, and animals are physical characteristics. Bodies of water, including rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans, are also physical characteristics. Landforms are also a physical characteristic of an area. Some examples of landforms are mountains, plains, valleys, and deserts. These characteristics are all connected and help geographers describe different areas on the Earth’s surface. Physical characteristics are what make the Earth interesting and unique. A physical map shows the world’s major physical features.

The countries in North America each create boundaries and borders in different ways. Canada has 10 provinces and three territories, the United States has 50 states, Mexico has 31 states, and the Caribbean has 13 sovereign (independent) states and 17 dependent territories.

North America is surrounded by oceans. The Pacific Ocean is located west of North America, and the Atlantic Ocean is east of North America. The Gulf of Mexico is south of North America. The Gulf of Mexico is a body of water between Mexico, the United States, and the Caribbean islands. There are also important lakes and rivers in North America. The five Great Lakes connect Canada and the United States.

Canada, the United States, and Mexico share important mountain ranges. The Rocky Mountains start in Canada and go down the western side of the United States. The Sierra Madre mountains go through both the United States and Mexico.

title: Climate of North America
text:
North America is a large continent with a variety of different climate zones. One of the most important factors in determining climate is the distance from the Equator. Areas close to the equator are generally much warmer and get more precipitation. The climate gets colder and drier as you move away from the Equator toward the North and South Poles. North America stretches from the tropics, which are close to the Equator, all the way to the Arctic Circle, near the North Pole. Because of this, the continent's climate varies depending on where you are.

In the far northern regions of North America, it is generally cold, and the precipitation that does fall is often snow. Areas of Alaska and Canada experience very cold winters and cool summers. Closest to the North Pole, the climate stays so cold that the ground is permanently frozen, which is called permafrost. The plants that do live in this area, like certain trees and bushes, have to survive on less heat and water.

In the far southern regions of North America, it is usually warm with more precipitation in the form of rain. Countries in this area of the continent, such as Mexico and Guatemala, experience warm winters and hot summers. Closer to the Equator, the climate stays warm and wet enough to never get frost. The plants in this area thrive on warmer temperatures and abundant precipitation.

In between these two extremes, the climate is considered temperate. A temperate climate is in between very warm and very cold climates. Because a large portion of North America sits somewhere between the far northern and far southern regions, the temperatures and precipitation levels are somewhere in between as well.

In these areas, the climate is impacted by distance from the ocean as well as how high the land is above sea level. Here, you will find forests with warm summers and cool winters. In the higher elevation of mountain ranges, like the Rocky Mountains, there are climates similar to the cold climates of the northern regions. Mountain ranges block rain clouds in certain areas, creating hot and cold deserts that get very little precipitation. Near the oceans, the climates often feature more precipitation as the moisture from the large bodies of water fall on the land nearby.

title: Landforms and Bodies of Water in the United States
text:
The United States is a diverse country with many unique physical characteristics that impact the way people live and interact with their environment. Landforms are natural features that make up the Earth's surface.

A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean. It takes millions of years for mountains to form. Rich minerals are found in the cores of mountains.

The Rocky Mountain range is the biggest mountain range in North America. It begins in Canada and extends through central New Mexico. Many of the peaks are more than 12,000 feet high. Mount Elbert in Colorado is the tallest peak in the range at 14,440 feet. Thousands of tourists flock to the Rocky Mountains each year to explore their natural wonders.

The Appalachian Mountains are located in the eastern part of the United States. The highest peak is Mount Mitchell, at 6,684 feet. The Appalachian Trail runs the length of the mountain range, which is about 2,000 miles long. Outdoor adventurers and hiking enthusiasts hike the Appalachian Trail throughout the year.

A desert is a place where there is less than 10 inches of precipitation in a year. Deserts usually have hot temperatures during the day and colder temperatures at night.

The Mojave Desert is located in parts of Southern California, Nevada, Arizona, and Utah and extends into Mexico. It is the driest desert in North America. It receives less than two inches of rain each year. The Mojave Desert is home to Death Valley. Death Valley sits 282 feet below sea level, making it the lowest point in North America. It is also the hottest place on Earth. Despite its dry and extremely hot climate, hundreds of plant and animal species call the Mojave Desert home.

The Great Plains are very different from the Mojave Desert. A plain is a large area of flat land with few to no trees. The Great Plains region is a large area east of the Rocky Mountains that is very flat. It extends from Mexico to Canada and east to Illinois. It is primarily grassy with few trees. The soil is usually very good on the plains due to the abundant amount of grass material that grows there. It is a great place for growing crops like corn and wheat.

Bodies of Water

Rivers and lakes have played a vital role in the history, economy, and actions of governments in North America for thousands of years.

The Missouri River is the longest river in the United States. Combined with the Mississippi River, it forms one of the largest river systems on Earth. The Missouri River flows from Montana to Missouri, where it joins the Mississippi River. The Mississippi River is the second-longest river in the United States. It travels through 10 states before it pours into the Gulf of Mexico.

The Great Lakes, which include Lake Erie, Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, and Lake Superior, are located in the northern United States. The Great Lakes cover over 94,000 square miles and contain about six quadrillion gallons of water. The lakes hold about 21 percent of the Earth's fresh water and 84 percent of America's fresh water.

Oceans and gulfs are important bodies of water in and around the United States. Like the other bodies of water in the United States, the Atlantic Ocean helps the U.S. economy by providing a trade route with other countries. Atlantic coastal areas are popular tourist destinations for Americans and visitors from around the world. The Pacific Ocean is on the western border of the United States and is a vital trade route between the United States and other countries.

A gulf is a deep inlet of water that connects coastal areas to a larger body of water, such as a sea or ocean. The Gulf of Mexico covers about half a million square miles of water. It has 33 major tributaries, or rivers, that flow into it, including the Mississippi River. A bay is a coastal body of water partly surrounded by land that feeds into a large body of water. The Chesapeake Bay is the largest bay in the United States. Over 150 rivers empty into the Chesapeake Bay.

title: Canadian Shield
text:
The northern part of North America is covered almost entirely by the country of Canada. The massive geological formation that makes up most of Canada is called the Canadian Shield. The Shield is made up of rock from the Earth’s crust. It formed over billions of years and was originally mountainous. Forces of erosion and the friction caused by the movement of glaciers have flattened this region into what it is today. Because it is made up of the Earth’s crust, it is rich in natural resources. Gold, copper, and iron are just a few of the many mineral deposits in the Canadian Shield.

The climate of the Canadian Shield is influenced by the region’s distance from the Equator. The Shield is in the northern region of North America, far from the Equator. This close to the Arctic Circle, temperatures are colder. In the farthest northern reaches of the Canadian Shield, the ground remains frozen all year long. This frozen soil is called permafrost, and it makes plant growth almost impossible.

Farther south, the climate remains cold, but it is warm enough to thaw the soil during the summer months of the year. With enough rain and snow, this region gets warm enough to support forests of certain trees. These forests usually consist of only one or a few varieties of tree species that can survive cold winters or periods with little precipitation.

While it has generally been flattened by geological forces, the Canadian Shield is quite rocky with many hilly areas, lakes, and rivers. The rugged terrain limits the ability of people to use this area for agriculture.

title: Caribbean
text:
The Caribbean is located in the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean. This series of small islands is located south of the Gulf of Mexico and the Florida coast. Mountains cover the large islands. Some islands have active volcanoes, lush rainforests, and waterfalls. Pico Duarte is the highest mountain peak in the region. It reaches 10,000 feet into the sky.

Beaches in the region are popular. They have different kinds of sand. Volcanic rock formed the black sand beaches. Parrot fish created the white sand by using their beaks to scrape off coral rock. Red shells, broken into tiny grains by the surf, make the pink sand. Large coral reefs in the region are home to colorful and diverse marine life. Sharks, sea turtles, and sea horses are native to the reefs.

The Caribbean is home to the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. forest system. It is called the El Yunque National Forest. It gets its name from the Taíno god Yukiyú. This forest is located in Puerto Rico. It is rich in plants and animals. There are 23 plants and animals there that are not found anywhere else in the world. Eight large rivers flow through this rainforest. About 600,000 people visit this rainforest every year. Rainforests are one of the Caribbean's natural landmarks.

The Caribbean has a mostly tropical climate. Tropical climates are warm, wet, and humid. The average temperature stays almost the same all year. In most places in the Caribbean, there is a dry season and a wet season. The dry months are usually from February to May, and June to November is the wet season. Hurricanes can happen during the wet season. The temperatures vary in the Caribbean islands. However, the average high temperature is about 82°F (28°C). Generally, the best time to visit the Caribbean is during its driest months. There are many islands in the Caribbean. The amount of rain that falls depends on the physical environment of the island. The islands of Aruba, Bonaire, and Curaçao get the least amount of rain. In fact, their climate can be very dry. These islands are also much less likely to experience hurricanes.

title: Mexico
text:
North America’s land mass narrows down in the south where it connects to South America. Mexico makes up the largest portion of this land bridge. The country is home to a varied climate, with some of the wettest and driest climates in North America. Mexico lies along the Tropic of Cancer, the northern line of the region known as the tropics. The tropics are characterized by year-round warm temperatures and more-than-average precipitation. The northern half of Mexico is outside the tropics, and the southern half is inside the tropics.

Northern Mexico, outside the tropics, is dominated by an arid, desert climate. The driest areas are two deserts: the Sonoran and Chihuahuan Deserts. Some areas of these deserts receive as little as 10 inches of rain per year. The deserts exist partially because of the Sierra Madre mountain range. The eastern and western ranges of the Sierra Madres run in parallel lines from north to south, blocking moisture from getting to the deserts and creating a rain shadow.

Southern Mexico is located south of the Tropic of Cancer inside the warm, wet tropics. As a result, this region of Mexico generally receives more precipitation than northern Mexico. The inland areas of southern Mexico are characterized by a temperate climate with differences marked mainly by changes in elevation. Higher elevations are cooler and lower elevations are warmer throughout the year. The coastal areas of southern Mexico get enough rainfall to be characterized as a tropical climate. The tropical climate zones of the country receive multiple inches of rain each month.

Mexico has two major peninsulas with very different climates. A peninsula is a landform surrounded by water on three sides. The peninsula known as Baja California, on the west side of Mexico, is almost exclusively north of the Tropic of Cancer. It is almost entirely covered by the arid Sonoran Desert. On the eastern side of Mexico, the Yucatan Peninsula juts out into the Gulf of Mexico in the tropics and features a tropical climate with excessive summer rain.

title: Biomes of North America
text:
The type of vegetation that grows in a place depends on the climate, type of soil, and other growing conditions. Animals are also affected by climate. The climate, vegetation, and animals in a place together form a biome. In a biome, the plants and animals depend on each other for survival. Grassland, freshwater, desert, forest, tundra, mountain, and marine are all examples of biomes. Biomes are part of the physical characteristics of a place.

There is a wide variety of plants and animals in Canada's biomes. There are different types of forests in the forest biome of Canada. Squirrels, moose, and wolves live in these forests. There are also many pine trees in the forests. In the mountain biome, there are grizzly bears and cougars. Trout, pike, and bass are some of the types of fish that live in Canada’s freshwater biome. Canada’s tundra biome is home to polar bears, snowy owls, and arctic hares. Very few plants live in the tundra because it is cold and dry. One plant that can survive in the tundra is moss.

The United States has a variety of biomes that make up the physical characteristics of its regions. Grassland, freshwater, desert, forest, tundra, and mountain make up the different biomes. Grassland biomes are found in warm, dry climates. There are many different types of wild grasses, shrubs, and some trees. These plants provide food for animals that live in grassland biomes.

Fresh water is water that is not salty. Freshwater biomes include lakes, ponds, rivers, and streams. They provide homes to a huge variety of plants and animals. These animals include different fish, frogs, and water lilies.

Desert biomes are dry areas where there is less than 20 inches of rainfall per year. Desert plants and animals have adapted to use less water. Deserts can be either cold or hot.

Forest biomes are areas with many trees. Forests provide homes for animals like deer, monkeys, and birds. Different temperatures and amounts of rainfall make different kinds of forests.

Tundra is the coldest biome. It has very little rain, a very short growing season, and extreme winds. Few plants, animals, or people can survive in the tundra year-round. Some animals survive because of their thick fur. Others migrate to warmer habitats during colder seasons.

Mountain biomes are diverse. Taller mountains have colder weather. When the weather is cold, plant life is limited. Farther down the mountain slopes, the temperature is warmer, and plant life increases. This makes it easier for animals to find food and shelter there.

There are also different climates in Mexico. This means there is a wide variety of plants and animals living there. One of the most famous animals in Mexico is the monarch butterfly. Every year, millions of monarch butterflies migrate to Mexico. The butterflies hibernate in the forest for the winter. Some of these forests have pine trees and bears. Some of these forests are rainforests that have huge, broadleaf trees and monkeys. The sandy desert biomes of Mexico are home to rabbits, snakes, and scorpions. Whales, rays, and tropical fish are some of the many animals that live in Mexico’s oceans.

The Caribbean has freshwater, forest, and mountain biomes. Most of the plants growing in these biomes are tropical. There are rainforests with many plants and animals. Parrots and monkeys live in the rainforests. Palm trees grow on the sandy beaches. The ocean has many animals, such as sea turtles and rays. Many sea animals make their homes in and around coral reefs. A great variety of plants, animals, and insects form the wildlife of the Caribbean. The Caribbean is an example of a diverse biome.

title: Young Entrepreneurs
text:
You don’t have to be an adult to start a business. People as young as five years old have become entrepreneurs by starting their own businesses. Some businesses have grown and become successful.

Take child entrepreneur Hannah Grace. Grace was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes when she was just a baby. At the age of 10, she started making her own health and beauty products to sell. She created a business called Hannah Grace BeYOUtiful and donates 20 percent of every purchase to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Fund.

Maya Penn founded her business, Maya’s Ideas, when she was just eight years old. Today, Penn is 19 and CEO of her own company, which sells fashion accessories that are environmentally sustainable. Not only does she run her own business, but Penn also donates 10 percent of her profits to charities and to help the environment.

When he was nine years old, Moziah Bridges wanted an eye-catching fashion accessory. Because of this, he got the idea to create Mo’s Bows. Bridges’s company sells all kinds of things, including bow ties, pocket squares, and other apparel. Today, despite his company’s international success, Bridges intends to graduate high school and continue his education by going to college to study fashion design.

Nohbo Drops were created by Benjamin Stern. Stern came up with the idea while he was sitting in his ninth grade biology class. Nohbo Drops are packets for shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and shaving cream that dissolve in water. They don’t contain chemicals that harm the environment, and they help to eliminate plastic waste.

These young people didn’t find success overnight. Their businesses started with an idea. They worked and improved their ideas until they were able to create businesses out of them. Hannah Grace had to try over and over to find a successful recipe for her bath bombs and beauty products. Moziah Bridges started out with an eye-catching bowtie and worked to design and create other accessories. Entrepreneurs work hard, often for years, before their businesses take off. Some businesses don’t make it, but with a good idea, hard work, and dedication, anything is possible.

title: How a Bill Becomes a Law
text:
Government action and decisions are put into effect by creating a bill that can become a law. A bill is a draft of a law presented to a legislature. There’s a special process that every citizen should know in order to be informed, active participants in the processes of government.

Every bill starts with an idea. Citizens can contact their elected representatives to propose an idea for a law that will make their community, state, or country a better place. Then, the representative can write a bill based on the proposal of the groups of citizens they represent. Once legislators write the bill, they must present it to the house in which they are a member. For example, a senator would present the bill to the Senate, and a representative would present the bill to the House of Representatives.

The bill needs approval from both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The bill goes to the executive branch if it is approved. In the federal government, the executive branch is the President of the United States. The governor is the executive branch in your state. If the executive branch agrees with the bill, it is signed into law. The executive branch can veto, or say no, to the bill if they don't agree. If that happens, the bill goes back to Congress.

A bill becomes a law with public opinion as part of the entire process. If representatives are responsive to the common good of the people they have been elected to serve, they can be continually elected to Congress. If representatives are not responsive, at every election, the people have the opportunity to elect someone else who will better represent them.

title: Volunteering
text:
Citizens who want to give something back to the community can volunteer, or donate their time to help others. Many people volunteer because they want to help others in need. There are many ways you can volunteer in your community.

People can volunteer for drives. Different types of drives collect things for people in need. Some volunteers help with community clean-ups. Other volunteers serve in community fire departments and neighborhood watch programs.

The list of volunteer jobs is very long. If you want to give back to your community, find out about where you could volunteer. Someone will really appreciate your help!

title: Analyzing Primary Sources
text:
Analyzing primary sources helps us understand events, people, and places during a specific time period. Arizona became a territory of the United States in 1866. Following its annexation by the United States, Arizona became a bustling territory. People from around the country and the world came to Arizona in search of gold and precious metals. The following source is an excerpt from Emma Hildreth Adams’s book To and Fro in Southern California, written in 1887. This source details Adams’s journey through Arizona on her way to California. Examine the primary source and answer the analysis questions.

Arizona is one of the richest mineral lands of the world. Leaving gold and silver out of the question, it is affirmed that the Territory's annual yield of copper alone will in a few years reach the vast sum of twenty-five million dollars... Tucson is an un-America, and, on a small scale, extremely cosmopolitan city. A resident of the place avers [states] that on its streets may be heard eighteen different languages. Americans, Mexicans, Germans, Russians, Italians, Austrians, Frenchmen, Spaniards, Greeks, Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese, Africans, Irishman, and Sandwich Islanders are all here, being drawn to the spot by the irresistible mining influence.

title: Searching for Answers
text:
It’s important to know what to look for when answering a compelling question. Supporting questions can help focus your research. The compelling question can also guide you. Consider a question like: Why did the 13 colonies declare their independence from England? To answer this question, you would look for the events that led up to the colonies declaring independence in your sources. Then, you check whether those events impacted the decision to declare independence. Supporting questions could be:

What events led to the 13 colonies declaring independence from England?

Who were the major participants?

What was the outcome of the 13 colonies declaring independence from England?

title: Presenting Your Information
text:
After you have analyzed and evaluated your sources, you have to organize and explain your conclusions. You do this by creating a main idea and adding supporting details to back up your idea.

The main idea is the answer to your compelling question. You can use the compelling question to create your main idea. If your compelling question is “Why did the 13 colonies declare their independence from England?” then the main idea would be:

1. Actions by the British government drove the 13 colonies to declare their independence from England.

Once you decide on your main idea, you add evidence that supports your idea.

1. The colonists did not like the taxes they had to pay.

2. The colonists wanted to trade with other countries.

You need to present your main idea and supporting evidence carefully to justify your claim. Your main idea comes first. Your evidence comes after that.

Our example of a compelling question is “Why did the 13 colonies declare their independence from England?” Our main idea is “Actions by the British government drove the 13 colonies to declare their independence from England.”

You can then add evidence that the colonists didn’t like the taxes they had to pay. You can also explain that the colonists wanted to trade with other countries.

The order for presenting our information is: the main idea, the first piece of evidence, and the second piece of evidence.

title: Budgeting for a Third Grader
text:
What might budgeting look like for someone in third grade? Let's take a look.

First, you write down how much money you receive. Do you do chores? Do you receive an allowance? Maybe you receive money for your birthday or other special occasions. This is your income.

Then, you need to look at what you have to pay for. Maybe you have music lessons that you help pay for. Maybe you have a pet that you help take care of. You might be saving money for something like a new bike or game. You could also donate money. After paying for the important things, you can allocate money for other things you want.

title: Introduction to the Northeast
text:
The indigenous peoples of the Northeast, or Eastern Woodlands, lived in a land rich in fresh water, including the Great Lakes. The land was also good for farming and had types of trees and other plants.

Many tribes lived in the Eastern Woodlands. This area was home to many different tribes, including the Iroquois, Algonquin, Illiniwek, Chippewa, Odawa, Kickapoo, Miami, Lenni Lenape, and Powhatan. They grew corn, beans, and squash. The tribes used all the natural resources around them to meet their basic needs. They used birch bark to build canoes and to cover their homes. They burned wood for cooking and to stay warm. They used tools for work and as weapons. The animals they hunted provided food for the people. The animal hides, or skins, were used to make clothes, containers, and bags. Everything was used and nothing was wasted.

Eastern Woodland tribes lived in larger villages in the summer and smaller family groups in the winter. The houses were different from tribe to tribe. Some tribes lived in wigwams, which are small, dome-shaped homes. The Chippewa lived in wigwams. Tribes lived in wigwams when they moved to hunt, fish, and gather natural resources. Other tribes lived in larger, more permanent longhouses. The Iroquois lived in longhouses. Many people could live in a longhouse. The homes fit the lifestyles of each community.

title: Week 14 Framing Question
text: How were the cultural features of the Northeast tribes influenced by the geography of the Northeast?

title: Tribal Structures
text:
There were varying forms of government among the indigenous people of the Northeast, but one of the most famous governments was the Iroquois or Haudenosaunee Confederacy. Hundreds of years ago, the Mohawk, Onondaga, Cayuga, Oneida, and Seneca fought many wars. To end the wars, a woman named Jikonhsaseh, Chief Hiawatha, and a prophet called the Great Peacemaker convinced the tribes to unite. Each group had its own leadership, but the leaders made big decisions in the Grand Council of the Chiefs. The Iroquois created a constitution called the Great Law of Peace. This agreement included a balance of power between bigger and smaller groups, a two-branch legislature, procedures for passing laws, and more.

The Potawatami also formed a confederacy. They formed their confederacy with the Ojibwe (keepers of the faith), and the Odawa (keepers of the trade). They called their alliance the Three Fires Confederacy. The Three Fires were often in conflict with the Haudenosaunee Confederacy. The Haudenosaunee were powerful and the Potawatomi were forced to migrate after losing to the Haudenosaunee Confederacy. The Potawatomi had originally been in what is now Michigan but moved to regions of Illinois and Wisconsin.

The Lenni Lenape had a matrilineal kinship system. Among the Lenape, this meant that someone was only related to the people on their mother's side of the family. In other matrilineal societies, this also meant they lived with their mother’s family. It is not totally clear if the Lenape people only lived with their mother’s family. However, it is clear that inheritances would be passed from the mother to her children, instead of from the father to his children. In fact, the authority of a Lenape sachem, or chief, passed matrilineally. For example, when one sachem died, the new sachem would be chosen from among his sisters’ sons. There were also three matrilineal clans in Lenape society: the Turtle clan, the Wolf clan, and the Turkey clan. People’s clan membership was determined by their mother’s family line. The head sachem was always from the Turtle clan. The turtle was an important animal among Lenape people because it represented the Earth and its power to give life.

title: Economy
text:
Like many other Woodland societies, the Lenape divided work responsibilities between men and women. Men hunted in the forests around the Delaware River. They hunted and fished seasonally. Deer, bear, elk, beavers, rabbits, raccoons, turkeys, ducks, and geese were all hunted at certain times of the year. Men also fished in the Delaware River for shad, salmon, and sturgeon. They also fished in the Atlantic Ocean for shellfish and herring.

Lenape women farmed and prepared food from the forests. The land they farmed belonged to the women. Women cultivated corn, beans, squash, and tobacco. Tobacco was mostly used for ceremonial purposes or as offerings to spirits. The women also picked berries and nuts. Wild strawberries, blueberries, cranberries, walnuts, and chestnuts all grew in the area. When it was not the season for planting or harvesting, women also went to the forest to tap trees for maple sap. The Lenape women would make the sap into maple syrup.

Since the land was sacred, the Ho-Chunk were careful with it. They harvested only what they needed. They traveled with the seasons. They moved their villages to conserve, or protect, an area’s natural resources from destruction. This allowed plants to regrow and animals to repopulate.

They also divided the labor. The men hunted, and the women gardened and tanned animal hides. One notable skill among the Ho-Chunk was jewelry making. The men made silver and copper jewelry for both men and women. The ornaments showed the status of the wearer, especially the earrings.

title: Language
text:
The tribes of the Northeast spoke a variety of languages and dialects. A dialect is a way of pronouncing, and speaking a language that is unique to an area or community. For example, Lenape is an Algonquain language, but the people spoke different dialects. The Algonquain language family connects many tribal languages all across the eastern and middle part of North America. A language family is a group of languages that share a common ancestor or parent language.

Among the Lenape there were three dialects: Munsee, Unami, and Unalachtigo. The Munsee-speaking people lived in the northern territory of the Lenape. This encompassed parts of modern-day New York, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey. Munsee means, “the people of the stony country.” The Unami lived in the central portion of New Jersey and part of Pennsylvania. Their name translates as, “the people down river.” The third group of Lenape were the Unalachtigo, or the Nanticokes. They lived in the southern portion of the territory, which included the modern states of Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Delaware. Their name means “people near the ocean.” All the Lenape, no matter which dialect they spoke, lived close to the Delaware River. While not all Lenape live in the same region now, they do share a common history and many cultural characteristics.

The Miami Tribe spoke another Algonquian language. Their original territory was just south of Lake Michigan, in present-day Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, and Ohio. According to tradition, the Miami people came from the water. The Miami name for themselves is Myaamia, which means, “the downstream people.” The Myaamia legend says their people climbed out of the St. Joseph’s River near Lake Michigan. Language had meaning; even singular words contained many ideas and feelings.

title: Religion
text:
Many indigenous groups of the Northeast held deep religious beliefs. Most of these religious beliefs were influenced by the natural world. The Lenape believed in a creator god called Kishelëmukong. They also believed in some lesser spirits called manëtu or manitou. Most animals, plants, and some objects are thought to have manitou. For example, there are manitou called “the thunder beings,” or pethakhuweyok. The winds of the four cardinal directions are also considered manitou. They are called Grandfather of the North, Grandfather of the East, Grandfather of the West, and Grandmother of the South.

The Illiniwek were highly religious. They believed in a Master of Life, as well as individual spirits to whom they prayed for help. They had religious traditions and ceremonies for weddings and burials. These ceremonies often involved gifts. The Illiniwek did not value personal wealth. A person who could give away possessions earned great respect. When a person died, the Illiniwek buried with them gifts of things they might need in the afterlife. These gifts often included tobacco, a bow and arrow, corn, or a kettle.

The most important religious ceremonies involved the calumet. This was a stone pipe that represented the god of peace and war. The Illiniwek performed the calumet dance at public celebrations. The dance was also performed to strengthen bonds with other tribes and to unite the tribe for war. Dancers formed a circle, with the main dancer holding the calumet in the center. Then, the dancers performed a mock battle to the beat of drums. After the dance ended, the chief would give the pipe to an honored guest at the ceremony as a token of peace.

An important leader of the Kickapoo tribe was the shaman. A shaman communicated with the spirit world, predicted the future, and cured the sick for the band. Sometimes the shaman’s authority was greater than a chief’s.

The Kickapoo believed in a Great Manitou in the spirit world who ruled over everything. Lesser manitous were in the four winds, fire, sky, moon, stars, and Grandmother Earth. Wisaka was Great Manitou’s son and created the Earth and everything in it. The Kickapoo performed many ceremonies such as the Bison Dance. This ceremony asked for both protection during the hunt, as well as a plentiful hunt.

title: Oral Traditions
text:
Passing knowledge, beliefs, and history from generation to generation this way is called oral tradition. Older people in the group would often tell stories to the younger ones, handing down the lessons and traditions in their history. Many stories explained beliefs about creation or other religious customs. Sometimes as the stories got passed down, different versions of a history or a belief emerged. Two versions about creation were recorded by Europeans who met and lived around the Lenni Lenape in the 1600s and 1700s.

The first story says that a woman fell down from the heavens. As she fell, she continued to float in the air searching for a place to rest. She couldn’t find one. Finally, some sea creatures decided to help her. A large tortoise came to the surface of the sea and let the woman rest there. The dirt, plants, and shells of the sea gathered around the turtle. This mass grew until it became the earth, the home of the Lenape people.

The second story says that a turtle came up to the surface of the sea from the deep part of the ocean. As the water drained from the turtle’s back, a tree began to grow. The tree’s roots sent out two sprouts. One sprout grew into a man. The second sprout grew into a woman. These were the first ancestors of the Lenape people. In both versions of the story, the turtle represented Earth. The turtle was a very important and respected symbol among Lenape people.

title: Mound Builders
text:
A group of ancient people lived at the end of the medieval period, from around 100 B.C.E to 500 C.E. These people demonstrated their culture and heritage by building complex mounds. Some mounds were for burial. Some were made in the shapes of animals. Other mounds were used as foundations for temples. Mounds were sometimes built to enclose cities, too. The native people of this time were skilled artists. They made beautiful artwork using materials from faraway places, such as the Gulf of Mexico. The mounds extend throughout the Ohio and Mississippi River Valleys. This culture is often called the Hopewell culture.

Another mound building group lived from about 650-1400 C.E. in a large city that once stood near present-day Collinsville, Illinois. On the site, there are 51 human-made mounds that date from 800-1350 C.E. Some mound builders like the Adena and Hopewell built effigy mounds that were shaped like animals. The people at Cahokia built flat-topped pyramid-type mounds.

The Mounds probably held religious and cultural significance to the society. The tallest at the site is called Monks Mound. It is more than 90 feet tall, 1,000 feet long, and 700 feet wide. The mound was built entirely by human power. In addition to holding cultural significance, the top of the mound was likely the home of the chief. At the height of its power, Monks Mound was surrounded by a community of about 20,000-30,000 people. This was bigger than the city of London at the time. The reason that historians propose these ideas about Cahokia are from the archaeological artifacts in and around these mounds.

title: Introduction to Ancient China
text:
Archaeologists think the earliest people migrated to China from the north. Two river valleys, the Yangtze and the Yellow River Valleys, are known as the cradles of Chinese civilization. Evidence shows that hunter-gatherers were not nomadic in these areas. As early as 5000 B.C.E., small villages began to form along the rivers. Chinese mythology tells of supernatural or half-god emperors who taught the people how to make fire, build homes, and grow crops. Just like in other civilizations, as a surplus of food grew, so did the population. Most scholars agree that the people began to unify along the Yellow River around 2000 B.C.E. They needed to solve the problem of the destruction caused every time the river would overflow. A legendary king, Yu the Great, designed systems to control the floods and water the fields. He is believed by many to be the first leader of the Xia dynasty.

Soon villagers began to trade goods. This helped the people grow in wealth. Throughout the ancient period of China’s history, the Yellow River Valley was the heart of the Chinese world. It became the center of Chinese culture, society, and learning. Chinese civilization began to spread across the rest of the country. Over time, powerful families gained control of the government. New dynasties filled China's history. The Shang dynasty started silk culture, created bronze weapons, and invented a system of communication. The Zhou dynasty changed the system of government and military. The achievements and rich cultures of these early societies are still deeply felt today.

title: Essential Question
text: How do geographical tools help us learn about our world?

title: Reading Maps
text:
A person who creates a map is called a cartographer. Like the author of a book, a cartographer has a point of view and a purpose. A cartographer decides what to include on a map. Map tools help us read and understand maps and globes. Map tools include the title, legend/key, compass rose, cardinal directions, intermediate directions, and scale.

The title of the map tells us what the map is about. The map’s legend/key explains what the symbols and colors on the map represent. Most maps also have a compass rose. The compass rose is a symbol that shows the cardinal directions: north, south, east, and west. There are other directions in between these directions. They are called intermediate directions. For example, northeast is between north and east. Southwest is between south and west. The scale is a map tool that shows distance. Distance is how far one place is from another. The scale measurement on a map represents a real distance. For example, one inch on a map might represent 100 miles on Earth.

title: Physical Maps
text:
A physical map shows us where natural features are located. Natural features are things like bodies of water and landforms. Bodies of water include rivers, lakes, and oceans. Landforms are things like mountains and plains. Green, brown, and blue are the most prominent colors on a physical map.

A physical map can help people plan hiking or fishing adventures. Hunters use physical maps as well. Surveyors and geologists use physical maps too.

title: Political Maps
text:
A political map shows us the borders between cities, states, and countries. Borders are created by governments. Some borders are also natural features. Mountains, rivers, and lakes may divide one place from another.

Political maps also show us where capital cities are located. Capital cities are often represented with a star. Major roads and waterways are often included on political maps. Pilots, boat captains, and drivers are some of the people who may use political maps.

title: Alphanumeric Grids
text:
Cartographers put imaginary lines on maps. These make maps easier to read. There are lines that go from west to east (or left to right) and lines that go from north to south (or top to bottom). These lines cross to create small squares called grids. These grids have letters and numbers. This is called an alphanumeric grid system. An alphanumeric grid makes finding a location easier.

Which city is located near the coordinates 4, A?

title: Essential Question
text: How does a community change over time?

title: American Indian Communities
text: American Indians used the land in different ways to meet their needs. Some groups used the land to hunt and gather plants for food. Some used the oceans, rivers, or lakes to get their food. The Erie, the Shawnee, and the Kickapoo got fish from the Ohio River and lakes in the area. They also farmed the land to grow crops. They mostly grew corn and squash. Most tribes settled in areas with fertile land, mild weather, and water.

title: Europeans Came to North America
text:
Many European explorers came to North America. Their ships used natural harbors on both the east and west coasts. Many of those who landed in the east were French, English, Dutch, or Spanish. Spanish explorers also traveled along the west coast. Some explorers came to what is now the United States by land. They traveled north from what is now Mexico or south from what is now Canada.

People from all over the world came to North America. They wanted to settle on land where Indigenous peoples were already living. There was great conflict over the land. Indigenous people in the Ohio area joined to fight the British in 1763. The Shawnee, the Wyandot, and others all fought to defend their lands.

The Europeans also brought diseases. Many American Indians got infected. It is thought that up to 90 percent of American Indians in some areas died from such diseases. Weakened and outnumbered, the Indigenous peoples had their land taken by the Europeans.

title: Interdependence
text:
Interdependence is mutually relying on each other to get things done. A tire factory specializes in tires. Every community and country in the world depends on other communities and countries for some of the things they need. In the United States, many states specialize in specific agricultural products and manufactured goods that they can send to other states in exchange for different goods.

Some areas of the United States have natural resources that allow them to make or grow certain things. Countries trade goods and services. People cannot make and grow everything they need. They depend on each other. Specialization creates interdependence and world trade. Many areas of the United States specialize in growing or producing specific products. Car manufacturing requires parts produced around the country to create automobiles. Tires manufactured in Texas, airbags produced in Utah, and transmissions built in South Carolina are shipped to facilities in Michigan to build automobiles.

Ohio is a leading producer of fabricated metals, including steel, iron, and aluminum. One of the primary components of making steel is iron. Ohio has many natural deposits of iron ore throughout the state. Ohio’s large deposits of coal were also used to fuel furnaces in factories. Because of Ohio’s access to the necessary natural resources, steel became one of the leading products manufactured in Ohio in the late 1800s. Today, Ohio’s steel industry manufactures and ships steel building materials, tools, and parts for various types of equipment all over the United States and the world.

Our country does not produce everything we need. We have to buy things from other countries. That is called trade. Trade is when you buy, sell, or exchange a good or service for something else you want or need. A nation’s economy depends on its ability to trade with other nations. Trade depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods that are brought in from another country. Exports are goods sent to another country to be sold. In other words, imports are things you need or want but do not produce. So, you must buy those things from somewhere else. Exports are things you produce or have that you can sell for money or barter for other goods.

title: Essential Question
text: What goods and services help you meet your needs and wants?

title: Cities Grew in Diversity
text:
The Spaniards built the first successful European settlement in what is now the continental United States. It is called St. Augustine. People still live in St. Augustine today. The settlement was built on the coast, where boats could reach it easily. Harbors were usually the first areas where Europeans built settlements.

Some people came to the United States to farm the land. Others hunted and trapped animals for fur to send back to Europe. Some came to harvest natural resources, like minerals and wood. Many people had jobs working on the ships that came to the harbors. Others brought resources to the ships to trade for other goods.

Cities grew near harbors and other waterways. Many big cities in Ohio grew near the Ohio River and Lake Erie. The first European settlement in Ohio was Marietta. It was located where the Ohio River and the Muskingum River meet. It is still there today. People in cities needed food to eat and places to live. Rural farms produced food that was transported to the cities. Communities built railroads to help move people and goods. Settlers came from Asia and Latin America to find work. Some helped in building railroads and harvesting food.

Ohio’s cities grew even more diverse when rubber and steel factories opened. People moved to Ohio from different parts of the world to find work.

Not everyone came to North America by choice. Europeans brought enslaved people from western Africa to work on plantations. Everyone who came to America brought their experiences, cultures, and traditions into the country.

title: Growth of a Community
text:
As Ohio’s towns grew, people made use of the land’s natural resources. Big towns rose near the Ohio River and Lake Erie. The people used the water for drinking, planting crops, and transportation. Some cities grew near natural resources. Cleveland grew near iron ore. Akron is near rubber. Toledo has trees for lumber.

A city’s population increases or decreases depending on the availability of resources. Towns grew with family homes and places to work. Then, the towns would build community buildings. Places for government, education, and worship were some of the first buildings in a community.

People continued to move to Ohio’s cities over time. This meant that more healthcare and public safety services were needed. Hospitals, fire departments, and police stations were built. As the cities grew, they built shopping malls, entertainment centers, and restaurants.

As Ohio grew, more changes were made to the land. These changes made life convenient for people. Bridges, tunnels, and airports were built to help people meet their needs.

title: Decline of a Community
text:
Sometimes resources in an area are exhausted, or used up. With no resources to create jobs, people move away. They are pulled to other areas with more resources and jobs. Towns with no resources cannot keep up with the wants and needs of the people. People try to sell houses, but there are no buyers. Shopping centers close because there is no business. School buildings have fewer students. There are many empty businesses. Over time, some towns completely disappear.

As one area declines, another area can be growing. Every community goes through periods of growth and decline. For example, Akron grew quickly during WWII. This is because the military needed its resources. After the war, Akron’s population declined. People left to find new jobs elsewhere.

title: Shawnee, Ohio
text:
Shawnee, Ohio, was a small town in the 1800s. It was a busy coal-mining community of around 4,000 people. Work in the mines drew people to Shawnee. The town became a center of activity and culture. Railroads connected the town to the rest of the state. Citizens enjoyed opera shows and stores along the town’s Main Street.

Activity at the mines began to decrease in the 1900s. People began to move away from Shawnee to look for work. The people who remained in Shawnee mostly worked in nearby towns and cities. Some operated the few remaining businesses in the town. Empty buildings are common along the streets of Shawnee today. Some consider it a ghost town. A few hundred people still live there, but much of the town has been abandoned.

title: Essential Question
text: How can people spend, save, or invest their income?

title: Geography of Ancient China
text:
China is surrounded by several natural landforms. The Gobi Desert is to the northwest, the Himalayan Mountains are to the southwest, and the Pacific Ocean is to the east. In ancient times, the mountains and the desert were both impassable. This means that humans did not have the technology to cross them. These natural barriers kept China isolated from the rest of the world for many years.

The largest river in China is the Yang Zi, or Yangtze. It flows for over 3,900 miles. China’s largest modern city, Shanghai, is located at the river’s mouth. Another important river is the Huang He, or Yellow River. It collects silt as it flows. The mud has a yellowish color, giving the river its name. The earliest villages and towns developed along these rivers.

China is a vast country with a huge range of terrains and physical features, from mountains and plateaus to plains and deserts to river valleys and coastlands. It borders 14 other countries, including India to the southwest, just beyond the Himalayas. Mount Everest, Earth's highest mountain above sea level, is located in the Himalayas. The Plateau of Tibet sits between the Himalaya and the Kunlun mountains. It makes up about one-fourth of China's land. It is the tallest plateau in the world. China also has just about every type of climate on Earth, from subarctic to tropical. Based on the area and the time of year, the weather and climate can vary greatly. Typically, the southern part of China is warmer than the northern part of China. The climate in the ancient river valleys was ideal for farming. The summers were not too hot, and there was enough rainfall for crops to grow. All these factors helped shape Chinese civilization.

title: Rivers and Rice
text:
Two of the most important physical features of Ancient China were the Yangtze and the Yellow Rivers. They provided fertile soil, fish to eat, and hemp for clothing. The rivers were also used for transportation and for protection. They were at the center of thousands of years of Chinese history. They are featured in Chinese art and literature. The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia and the third-longest in the world. It is very wide and difficult to cross. It created a natural boundary between northern and southern China. The Yellow River is China’s second-longest river. Because it was so important to the beginning of Chinese civilization, the Yellow River is often called “Mother River.” It is also called “China’s Sorrow” because it brought raging floods that destroyed farms and villages.

Archaeologists have found evidence that the Yangtze River Valley was the origin of the early fishing, hunting, and gathering economy in China. The rivers provided everything the people needed to adapt and live as farmers. As early as 5000 B.C.E., people began to grow rice in the warm, wet climate. This is believed to be the first area in the world where rice was grown. From the river regions, rice farming spread across central and southern China and into southeast Asia. In time, it also spread into Korea and Japan. Rice is grown in fields flooded with water, called “paddy fields.” Growing rice requires a large amount of work and constant irrigation. As the farming of rice and other crops improved and developed, agriculture gradually replaced hunting and gathering as the main economy.

title: China’s Mighty Mountains
text:
Mountains have pros and cons. They can be used as an advantage in war by making it difficult for other countries to invade. However, they can also enclose a civilization and isolate it from interaction and trade with other societies. Mountains can cut off entire areas of a country from the rest of the same country.

Much of China is hilly and isolated by mountains. There are many mountain ranges in China. One of the most famous is the Himalaya range, which runs across the southwestern part of China. These mountains create a natural boundary between India and the Tibetan Plateau. The Himalayas have the highest elevation in the world.

For many thousands of years, landscape paintings have been an important part of Chinese art. The Chinese term for "landscape" is made up of two characters: 山 (shan), meaning "mountains,” and 水 (shui), meaning “water." Mountains are the "heart" and central focus of Chinese landscape paintings. The rounded peaks point up to the heavens. Rivers and, sometimes, waterfalls flow through and around the mountains and reflect the traditional belief in harmony with the natural world.

In ancient times, mountains were considered sacred and powerful. They attracted the rain that watered the crops. People believed that hidden in their slopes were magical fruits and plants that promised healing and long life. Legends tell of mystic beings and supernatural spirits who lived deep in the mountains. Caves were seen as doors to other realms. From early times, Chinese people have roamed the mountains seeking peace, enlightenment, and immortality.

title: Geography's Influence on China's Cultural Identity
text:
One of the greatest world civilizations developed in the vast, varied land of China. The size and geographic features of China have shaped its events, given it a distinctive character, and helped create a unique cultural identity.

One thing that makes Chinese history unique is its continuity over time. Many practices and traditions in ancient civilizations have developed but later changed or vanished. But in China, Confucianism, ancestor worship, and other cultural elements stayed unchanged right up to the early 20th century. Many of the beliefs and systems that exist in China today can be traced back to ancient origins.

Another contrast between this civilization and others is the writing system. Many ancient civilizations developed writing systems that were based on or influenced by cuneiform. The Chinese developed a completely different form of writing. This is because one of the most important geographic factors that has shaped China is how far away it was from other developing civilizations. Contact with other civilizations was limited. For a long time, the Chinese people had to work out their own progress and survival without help or influence from other parts of the world. Rugged mountain terrain taught the people to work hard and be innovative. Harsh deserts and dry grasslands molded powerful warriors and military leaders. Crowded river valleys taught people thrift, exactness, and the need to live together in respect and harmony.

title: The Earliest Dynasty
text:
In the study of history, there are often two or more sides to every story. People come from different backgrounds and have unique perspectives. Our life experiences can influence our thoughts about important issues. People looking at the same evidence can reach different conclusions. Viewpoints can even change as people get more information. All of this can lead to historical events being interpreted differently by people with different viewpoints. As historians, we should always try to study and compare different viewpoints.
