At its narrowest point, the strait is only 750 meters across. What makes such a small body of water so important? Not only does the Bosporus connect the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, it also separates Asian Turkey from European Turkey. It is a continental boundary between Asia and Europe. It is one of only two passages between the Black and Mediterranean Seas. Throughout history, civilizations have relied on the passage to build strong trading economies.

If traders could use the strait, armies and navies could as well. Empires built castles or fortifications on the European side to defend the city of Constantinople from invaders. Today, this city is known as Istanbul. The Bosporus continued to attract interest from governments and generals as the world went to war in the 20th century, too.

Today, the Bosporus is a very busy place. On its southern end, it is bordered on both shores by the bustling city of Istanbul. It is the main waterway for ships that transport fuel to European countries from Russia and western Asia. Around 48,000 ships make their way through the strait each year, including several thousand oil tankers. The tankers and trading vessels share the channel with a rich population of tourists and fish. Several species of fish use the Bosporus as a seasonal migration route from the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara. Shores on both sides are lined with resorts and villages. Cross a bridge and enjoy your vacation on another continent!

title: Pericles: The Value of Democracy
text:
Sometimes a leader needs to honor citizens who have died in battle. The leader may give speeches at soldiers’ funerals. These talks can be very emotional. They are also important. A leader who is good at speaking can take the time to remind their nation about why they went to war. The Athenian leader Pericles was a very good speaker. He gave powerful talks about freedom and democracy. One of his most famous speeches is known as Pericles’ Funeral Oration.

Pericles gave this speech in 431 B.C.E. at a large funeral for the soldiers who had died in the first few battles of the Peloponnesian War. He shared his belief that neither poverty nor class should control how successful a person could become.

Pericles spoke of the value of trust and the importance of government rule by laws that favored many people, not just a few. He said that justice came when people settled disagreements fairly.

We know about what Pericles said thanks to a historian named Thucydides. Thucydides heard the speech and wrote it down. He knew that Pericles’s ideas were important for the citizens of Athens. These ideas were unusual at the time. Most nations and empires were ruled by kings or emperors. Athens would set an example for others, including the United States.

In the speech, Pericles said, “Our constitution does not copy the laws of neighboring states; we are rather a pattern to others than imitators ourselves. Its administration favors the many instead of the few; this is why it is called a democracy.” What are some ways these ideas are similar to our country’s idea of government?

title: Urban, Suburban, Rural
text:
People live in three main types of communities. They are urban, suburban, and rural. Urban is a word we use to describe a city. Urban communities have many tall buildings. There are a lot of people living close together. They often have freeways and public transportation systems.

A suburban community is a group of neighborhoods near a big city. Suburban areas are less crowded. There is more space for homes and businesses. There are usually large roads and many cars. Many suburbs have public transportation systems.

Rural communities have fewer people. They often have fewer buildings too. There are small towns, farms, and open spaces. Rural communities have smaller roads, but many people have cars. Few rural areas have public transportation systems.

title: Gutenberg and the Printing Press
text:
Before the invention of the printing press, the world was a very different place. Very few people could read, and only the wealthy could afford to buy books. Books had to be written by hand, which took a lot of time and effort. Making a single copy of a book could take months or even years to complete. In the 15th century, everything changed when German inventor Johannes Gutenberg came into the picture.

Gutenberg set up shop in Strasbourg, France, where he began designing a printing press in the mid-1400s. He improved upon existing block printing methods, which came from China, and modified the design of the screw press to make a printing press. The printing press he created used a large screw and a lever to press a piece of parchment between two plates. The top plate was flat, while the bottom plate had the inked type set. Gutenberg also created an oil-based ink that transferred better to paper than water-based ink.

Perhaps the most revolutionary part of Gutenberg's printing press was the use of movable type. In block printing, letters and entire pages of text had to be carved onto a single block of wood, which wore out quickly and led to blurry text after a while. Gutenberg used metal letters, called type, which could be used over and over again without wearing out. Individual letters of the alphabet were carved onto pieces of type, which could then be arranged into words and sentences.

Before the printing press, scribes could copy an average of three pages by hand per day. Thanks to Gutenberg's printing press, it was now possible to print up to 250 sheets per hour. By the year 1500, printing presses across Europe had printed between 15 and 20 million books. Gutenberg's press revolutionized the way information and ideas were printed and distributed.

title: Renaissance Art
text:
One of the defining features of Renaissance art was the revival of ancient Greek and Roman art styles. Special attention was given to the human form in paintings and sculptures. Freedom to study human anatomy grew during this time. This allowed artists to learn more about the structure and workings of the human body, which helped them to create more realistic and lifelike artwork of the human form. Many of the themes for art during the Renaissance were centered around the everyday life of the common person. Other themes included scenes from Greek and Roman mythology, as well as Christian religious subjects.

Oil paints became the most common type of paint used on canvas paintings by the end of the 15th century. Styles and techniques, such as contrasting colors or the use of light and shading, varied from region to region. Emphasis was placed on portraying a more lifelike human figure and creating more realistic and detailed scenes. Painters experimented with showing the human figure in motion, rather than in still poses. Realistic portraits also became popular, and everyday imagery and objects were used to tell a story about the subject. Another feature of Renaissance art was aligning subjects within paintings into geometric shapes. For example, three people in a painting could have been aligned to form a triangle.

Sculptors and engravers began to experiment with techniques and styles with different materials, such as wood, bronze, and different types of stone. Sculptures were often of realistic human figures, while engravings usually depicted scenes from mythology, biblical stories, and everyday life.

title: Patronage
text:
Historically, artists have heavily relied on patrons to make a living. The Renaissance era was no exception to this. A patron is someone who pays a person or group to create or do something for them. During the Renaissance, the artwork was mostly commissioned by the wealthy and those in power, such as members of the nobility and church and government leaders.

Art was a way for the wealthy to show off their wealth and standing in society and for the government or the church to demonstrate their power and influence. Cities usually commissioned artists to create artwork depicting military leaders, city rulers, or mythological figures associated with their city. Church leaders commissioned works of art portraying bible stories, such as King David, the Virgin Mary, and Jesus Christ. Wealthy individuals usually commissioned pieces that would demonstrate their piety, wealth, or other qualities they felt were important. The Medici family in Florence was one of the wealthiest and most famous patrons of the arts during the Renaissance.

Patrons dictated what they wanted the artist to make, which sometimes meant that artists had very little freedom to be creative. Skill, labor, completion time, and the cost of materials had to be considered when commissioning a work of art. A contract was drawn up between a patron and an artist before any work was done. What was wanted, when it should be completed by, and how much the artist would be paid were usually specified in the contract. Adjustments could be negotiated after the contract was signed, but the contract helped ensure everyone got what they wanted.

When a patron found an artist they liked, they would often employ them indefinitely, or for the foreseeable future. The artist would be employed to create works of art, decorate a person's home or certain rooms, create designs for coats of arms or emblems, and more. They could be paid in cash, but sometimes, they could be awarded land, property, tax breaks, or noble titles.

title: Michelangelo
text:
Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni spent the early years of his education and career studying art in the city of Florence. Michelangelo was able to study sculptures from Roman antiquity in the sculpture garden of Lorenzo de Medici of the wealthy and powerful Medici family. These classical sculptures are believed to have influenced the works he created throughout his life.

Michelangelo spent a few years in Rome, where he created the famous sculpture Pietá, which portrays the Virgin Mary mourning over the body of Christ. Upon returning to Florence, he was commissioned to create another sculpture. This sculpture, called David, was arguably the most famous sculpture he ever created. He spent three years feverishly carving his masterpiece out of a single massive block of marble. Today, David is a well-known symbol of the city of Florence and the Renaissance period.

Michelangelo's skills weren't limited to carving sculptures, however. Described as a true “Renaissance man," he was also a very accomplished painter. He painted frescoes in the Council Hall of Florence at the same time as Leonardo da Vinci. It is possible that the two may have exchanged ideas and learned from one another during this time.

Michelangelo returned to Rome in the early 1500s, where he was commissioned to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City. This project was a massive undertaking. However, despite the scale of the project and the fact that he worked mostly alone, he completed the frescos in just four years in 1512 C.E. One of the central images in the painting, which shows God reaching out to touch the finger of Adam, became one of the most iconic images produced during the Renaissance.

In addition to sculpting and painting, Michelangelo was a poet, writing hundreds of poems in his lifetime. He was also an architect, having a hand in the construction of several important buildings, including the massive dome of St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. To the end of his days, Michelangelo worked hard creating, building, and learning. At the age of 87, one year before his death, he was reported to have stated, “I am still learning.”

title: Shakespeare
text:
William Shakespeare is regarded as one of the greatest playwrights and poets in history. Although he rose to fame during the English Renaissance, little is known about his early life. What is known is that he was born in the town of Stratford-upon-Avon in England in 1564. He likely grew up attending a grammar school there, and at 18, he married a woman named Anne Hathaway.

A few years later, he moved to London, where he became established in his career as an actor and playwright. He helped found a company of actors called the Lord Chamberlain’s Men, which later changed its name to The King's Men. While working with this company, he wrote, produced, and acted in plays for 20 years. Over the course of his career, Shakespeare wrote 38 plays, 154 sonnets, and various other poems. Some of his most famous plays include Much Ado About Nothing, The Taming of the Shrew, Hamlet, Romeo and Juliet, and Macbeth. He and a few others owned the world-famous theaters of the Globe and Blackfriars Theatre. Replicas of these theaters still perform Shakespearean plays to this day.

Shakespeare was not only successful in writing plays and poetry, but he also was known for inventing new words and coining new phrases, many of which are still used today. "Wild goose chase," "the world is my oyster," "in a pickle," and "love is blind" are all phrases coined by Shakespeare. Over 1,700 words were first written down in Shakespeare's works, and it is believed that he invented hundreds of them, including, "lonely," "swagger," "downstairs," "bedroom," and "skim milk."

Shakespeare's writings remain popular because they deal with common themes about people and humanity, such as love, power, jealousy, greed, and bravery. Today, his works are still studied, read, and performed all over the world.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
text:
Leonardo da Vinci's life had humble beginnings in the town of Vinci near Florence. Born to a single mother, da Vinci showed talent in art and music, even as a child. When he was a young teen, he was sent to apprentice under the artist Andrea del Verrocchio in his workshop in Florence. Within eight years, da Vinci became a master in the painter's guild.

Although he had been trained for a career in painting, da Vinci had a wide range of interests, and he was passionate about learning all that he could about the world around him. He studied architecture, engineering, geometry, botany, anatomy, zoology, geology, and languages in addition to art. Everywhere he went, he carried notebooks in which to take notes, write down ideas, and sketch pictures and designs. Da Vinci studied how things were made and how they worked in order to make improvements and create new inventions. He created designs for tanks, cranes, a parachute, flying machines, and even a simple robot.

Because of his diverse skills and interests, Da Vinci took on a variety of jobs in his lifetime. The jobs included military and naval engineer, master painter and sculptor, architect, and others. He worked on many art projects that still survive today. Some of Da Vinci's artistic masterpieces included the paintings Mona Lisa and The Last Supper and his sketch titled The Vitruvian Man. In addition to his artwork, he left behind his many notebooks filled with his sketches and notes.

Da Vinci is also credited with greatly influencing the knowledge of human anatomy. He studied the human body and drew detailed sketches of human systems and functions that had an impact on medicine and art. Today, Leonardo da Vinci is still considered one of the greatest minds in history.

title: Renaissance Writers
text:
The Renaissance saw the rise and success of not only artists, but writers as well. This was, in large part, due to the invention and spread of Gutenberg’s printing press. Ideas, stories, plays, poetry, and more could be printed and distributed rapidly at a low cost. People began using the written word more than ever before, and it changed the world.

England was home to many famous playwrights, poets, and authors during what is sometimes called the “English Renaissance.” Playwrights such as William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe achieved international renown for their writings. Edmund Spenser was nicknamed “the poet’s poet.” He created a new style of poetry and was best known for his poem The Faerie Queene, which he wrote in honor of Queen Elizabeth I. The writings of Thomas More, best known for his book Utopia, criticized the government systems in Europe at the time. He also wrote various works devoutly supporting the Catholic Church.

Across the English Channel, continental Europeans were also creating revolutionary written works.

Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar, wrote and nailed his 95 Theses to the door of a Church. The 95 Theses condemned the corrupt practices of the Catholic Church at that time. His actions eventually led to the Protestant Reformation. Although not a prolific writer, Luther’s words changed the world.

Italian Niccolo Machiavelli wrote works that commented on ethics in politics. His writings sparked much discussion and influenced how governments work and how political leaders act. His writings are still discussed and examined today.

French poet Pierre de Ronsard, who lost his hearing as a young man, devoted his life to learning and studying. Ronsard worked to revive classical styles of poetry from Latin and Greek in French poetry. His work changed the form and style of French poetry.

Teresa de Ávila was a Spanish religious reformer and nun active during the Counter Reformation. De Ávila wrote several books about mysticism and her spiritual experiences. Her writings are considered some of the most important literature of the Spanish Renaissance. Christians from the Renaissance to the modern day have looked to her writings for spiritual guidance.

title: Architecture
text:
Like so many other subjects, architects during the Renaissance wanted to resurrect the architecture of the ancient Greeks and Romans, particularly in using columns, arches, and domes. Sebastiano Serlio wrote a work called Seven Books on Architecture that influenced Renaissance architecture. In it, he listed the five classical orders, or styles, of architecture: Tuscan, Doric, Ionic, Corinthian, and Composite. Renaissance architects worked to revive these styles and experimented with mixing them together to create new and beautiful buildings and structures. Beauty and symmetry were extremely important in Renaissance architecture.

One of the biggest achievements of Renaissance architecture was the completion of the dome on the Santa Maria del Fiore cathedral in Florence. Upon its completion, the cathedral was the largest and tallest building in Europe at that time. The construction of the dome used new designs that were stable and self-supporting, which surpassed even Roman engineering.

However, it wasn't long before Florence's cathedral was surpassed in size by St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Many architects were involved in the design and construction of St. Peter's Basilica, which took over 100 years to complete. Today, this architectural marvel remains the largest cathedral in the world.

title: Mount Rushmore
text:
Mount Rushmore stands in the beautiful Black Hills of southwest South Dakota. The Black Hills have been a sacred place for many groups of people throughout history, including the Lakota Sioux. The environment of the Black Hills is rich in natural resources. The Lakota Sioux respected the land and used its abundant resources for survival long before the creation of Mount Rushmore.

Mount Rushmore celebrates the American ideals of leadership, courage, and strength. Mount Rushmore honors four of our nation’s leaders. Large carvings of presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln are on permanent display at Mount Rushmore.

Gutzon Borglum, the sculptor of Mount Rushmore, selected presidents who represented different phases of American history. Washington was chosen to represent the founding of America. Jefferson represents the growth of the United States. Lincoln represents the success of the Union during the Civil War and the abolishment of slavery in the United States. Roosevelt represents the development of the United States during the 20th century.

Construction began in 1927. The granite carvings were created by drilling into the face of the hills and using explosives to blast through the mountain rock. The work was difficult and dangerous. Workers climbed hundreds of steps each day just to reach the site. Men held onto ropes to do most of the dangerous work. Borglum’s original design included full-body carvings of each president and engravings that commemorated important events in American history. These ideas were abandoned due to a lack of funding and the difficulty of the work.

In March 1941, Gutzon Borglum died before the project was completed. His son Lincoln completed the project in October 1941. The Sioux did not want the monument built on their ancestral lands, but their protests were ignored. To help preserve their culture, the Sioux began construction on the Crazy Horse Memorial in 1948. The monument commemorates the courageous actions of the Oglala Lakota warrior Crazy Horse.

The Iroquois Confederacy

Before the arrival of Europeans, the American continent was home to the great Iroquois Confederacy. A confederacy is a term for many groups coming together. The five nations of the Iroquois Confederacy were the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, and Seneca. The Tuscarora joined later. They became the sixth nation in 1722. The six nations of the confederacy formed a government. Each nation had one vote. The confederacy was used to keep peace and protect themselves from invasion. Each nation maintained its own unique culture and language.

The name the Iroquois Confederacy used for their alliance was "Haudenosaunee". It means "people who build a house". Their homeland extended from the Great Lakes to the Mississippi River, over the Appalachian Mountains, and south to Georgia. The confederacy had elaborate trade systems. Waterways were often used to connect and trade. Their alliances with each other and other Native American nations created security and protection for their people.

The French

Into this vast empire of the Iroquois Confederacy came two empires from Europe: the French and British. French explorers began coming to North America in the early 1500s. As they explored, they met many Native American tribes and began to trade with them. At first, it was just for small items. When fur became more popular in Europe, the fur trade took off. French traders made alliances with many Native American nations in the Great Lakes region. The French were in the northeast region of the continent in present-day Canada.

The British

Beginning in 1607 with the settlement of Jamestown, Virginia, the British began to establish colonies in North America. It became clear to many early British colonists that they were not prepared to live in North America. They began to trade with Native Americans for food, tools, and animal hides. However, by the 1750s, the Iroquois found the British moving westward into their territory. The British came into the Iroquois land and built permanent trading posts that expanded into settlements for colonists. New British settlements used many natural resources the Iroquois needed for their people. This created a conflict in trading and other relationships with the Iroquois Confederacy.

These three very different nations wanted the same territory in North America. The Iroquois Confederacy was trying to keep control of the land they had lived on for hundreds of years. The British and the French wanted the land for themselves and their interests. The empires were caught in a three-way struggle for power. This power struggle would eventually lead to war.

title: What Do You Want to Be?
text: What do you want to be when you grow up? You can be anything!

title: It Takes Work
text: You can work for what you want. You can practice. You can learn new things.

title: Don't Give Up!
text: Learning new things takes time. Do not give up. You can do it. You are smart. You can do anything!

title: Everyone Is Different
text: Everyone wants to be different things. You might want to be a teacher. Your friend might want to be a chef. Be what you love.

title: Needs
text: Needs are things your body has to have to stay alive. Food is a need. Water is a need.

title: Wants
text: Wants are things you can live without. A puppy is a want. A new toy is a want.

title: You Are Important
text: You are important. Your needs and wants are important. Everyone has needs. Everyone has wants.

title: Talk About Needs
text: You can tell someone what you need. Talk about what you want.

title: Self-Care
text: You are growing. You are learning to take care of yourself. You can eat. You can sleep. You can wash your hands.

title: Hard Days
text:
Some days are easy and smooth. Everything goes your way. Some days are hard and bumpy. Things may not go your way.

Carlos is having a hard day with lots of bumps. He wants to go see a movie tonight, but his grandma is busy and can’t take him.

title: Look for the Good!
text:
When things are difficult, you can look for the good.

Carlos is very upset and feels like he is about to scream. He wants to yell and kick. His mom sees that Carlos is feeling angry, so she reminds him of all the other fun things he has planned for the day. He is planning on playing with his friend, Jack. Carlos also knows that his dad is making chicken for dinner, which is his favorite.

title: Breathe
text:
There are things you can do to help you feel better. One thing you can do is take a deep breath.

When Carlos got to Jack’s house, Carlos wanted to build a tower with the blocks, but Jack wanted to play outside. Jack went outside to play. Carlos could feel himself getting mad. He knew he needed to calm down to solve the problem. He remembered learning about taking deep breaths at school. So, Carlos closed his eyes and took three deep breaths: 1. Breathe in. Breathe out. 2. Breathe in. Breathe out. 3. Breathe in. Breathe out. After that, he felt calm.

title: Get Help
text:
Sometimes we need help when we face challenges.

Carlos decided to ask Jack’s mom for help. Together, they decided it would be a good idea to go talk to Jack outside and come up with an activity they both liked.

title: Problem-Solve
text:
You can solve problems.

As Jack and Carlos talked, they came up with the idea to bring the blocks outside. That way, they could play with blocks like Carlos wanted and play outside like Jack wanted.

title: Great Job!
text:
Solving problems feels good.

Jack’s mom told Carlos and Jack that they did a great job solving the problem together. She looked at Carlos and said, “Thank you for staying calm and asking me for help.” That made Carlos feel happy inside.

title: Coping Strategies
text:
Coping strategies are things that help you manage your emotions.

Carlos had some bumps in the road during his day. He used coping strategies to help make his day better.

What things did Carlos do to help himself feel better?

He closed his eyes and took deep breaths.

He asked for help.

He problem-solved.

title: Frank’s Friends
text: Frank and his friends are playing with toys. They are having fun.

title: Choose Toys
text: Nina plays with blocks. Frank wants the fire truck. Lev wants the fire truck.

title: Conflict
text: Frank and Lev both want the fire truck. Frank and Lev have a conflict. Conflict is when people do not agree.

title: Talk It Out
text: Frank says he wants the truck. Frank says he is sad. Lev says he wants the truck. Lev is sad.

title: Take Turns

title: Resolving Conflict Feels Good
text: Lev is happy. Frank is happy. Nina is happy.

title: Draw the Resolution
text: To resolve conflict means to fix it. How did Frank, Lev, and Nina resolve their conflict? Draw a picture.

title: Human-Environment Interaction
text:
Humans have basic needs. We need food, clothing, and a place to live. The environment affects how people meet their needs. The food people eat, the clothes they wear, and the houses they live in often come from their physical environment. The climate affects the clothes people choose to wear and the homes they build.

If you live in the Great Lakes Plains of Ohio, your environment includes Lake Erie, the wildlife, the fertile land, and trees. People who live near Lake Erie might eat fish, such as steelhead, bass, and perch. They use the fertile land to plant crops. They also use wood from trees to build homes.

title: Essential Question
text: How do people interact with the environment in your community?

title: Depending on the Environment
text: People depend on the environment to meet their needs. The physical characteristics of a place provide materials, food, and clothing for people living there. People usually choose to live close to resources that help them meet their basic needs. One example is the need for water. Throughout history, towns and cities have been established near bodies of water. Easy access to water made these places desirable. They provided clean water for drinking, and the waterways were used for transportation and trade. Many people wanted to live there. The resources found in the environment made their lives easier.

title: Adapting to the Environment
text:
Humans adapt to their environment. To adapt means to change how we live because of our environment. People wear different clothes, eat different foods, and live in different houses around the world. These are all designed based on their environment. The jobs people do relate to their environment too. Forestry, mining, and drilling are examples of jobs that are based on the natural resources of a place.

People can use technology to help them adapt to their environment. For example, many people use air conditioning in hot climates. Some people use sunscreen when they are outside. When people who live near the ocean can’t find drinking water, they use desalination to take salt out of seawater. Through technology, we now have drought-resistant crops. These are planted in areas where there is little rainfall. Plains often have lots of wind to generate power. Wind turbines help to generate power using wind. Solar power is often used in hot deserts with a lot of sunlight.

title: Modifying the Environment
text:
To modify means to change. People modify their environment to meet their needs. For example, people build dams to get water for growing food. They plow and irrigate the fields. In addition, humans build houses, schools, and shopping centers. We need to be able to travel and move things easily. As a result, we build canals, highways, and airports.

The physical environment in which people live determines how they modify it. For example, some areas have minerals. People extract these minerals from the earth through mining. Logging in the forest helps us get wood to build homes and furniture. Draining wetlands can help us create farmland. Digging wells and irrigation ditches help us farm in dry areas.

title: Phirun’s Goal
text:
Phirun has a goal. A goal is something you want to do. His goal is to learn how to brush his teeth on his own. Phirun can already get dressed by himself. He can also get his own breakfast.

You can set goals by doing these three things:

Think of what you want to do.

Make a plan.

Do your plan.

title: Phirun’s Plan
text: Phirun decides to make a plan. A plan will help him reach his goal. He thinks about what he needs to brush his teeth. Phirun's mom helps him make a plan for learning to brush his teeth.

title: Phirun Practices
text:
Phirun’s mom shows him how to brush his teeth. He practices brushing his teeth every day.

Think of what you would like to learn. Here are some ideas:

Learn to jump rope.

Learn to tie a shoe.

Learn to ride a skateboard.

Learn to add numbers.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text: Modifying the environment has consequences. Everything people do impacts their environment. These changes can be both positive and negative. Advancements in science, technology, and industry have affected the environment. Discoveries in renewable energy sources create less pollution. When we cut down too many trees at once, we may destroy a forest or mountain. We need to use Earth’s natural resources wisely. For a community to thrive, people need to maintain a balance between the environment and the community.

title: Phirun’s Progress
text: Phirun and his mom make a chart. The chart helps him remember when to brush. Phirun marks off his chart each time he brushes his teeth.

title: Human-Environment Interaction in My Community
text: Identify three examples from your community. The examples should show how people depend on the environment, how they modify it, and how they adapt to it. On a separate sheet of paper, draw a picture to support each of your examples. Then, indicate whether your examples are positive or negative interactions with the environment.

title: Phirun Meets His Goal
text: Every day, Phirun practices brushing his teeth. He puts toothpaste on the toothbrush. He brushes in circles. He cleans up when he is finished. By the end of the week, Phirun has the hang of it. He met his goal!

title: Proud Phirun
text: Phirun looks in the mirror and stands tall. He made it his goal to brush his teeth by himself. He worked hard every day and did his best. He smiles and thinks, "This feels good! What goal will I set next?"

title: What Is Your Goal?
text: Think of something you would like to do. Write or draw a goal you would like to make.

title: Human Characteristics of Ohio
text:
The culture of Ohio is part of its human characteristics. So are the human-made structures in the state. The ancestors of modern-day American Indians built mounds. The Miamisburg Mound is an example. It shows us how ancient American Indians used the land in the past. It was part of their culture. European settlers moved to Ohio. They brought their culture with them. They also built structures. These structures include the Ohio and Erie Canal, the Eldean Covered Bridge, and the Cuyahoga Railroad. These human characteristics met their need for transporting products from Ohio to other places.

Oberlin University meets the need to educate people. Hospitals, like the Ohio State Medical Center, meet people’s need for good health. Places like the Cincinnati Zoo and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame meet people’s need for recreation. These are all human characteristics.

The languages people speak are also part of Ohio’s human characteristics. Celebrations and even the way people dress are human characteristics too.

title: Cause
text: A cause is why something happens. Sitting on a balloon can cause it to pop.

title: Effect
text: An effect is what happens when there is a cause. A balloon pops if you sit on it. A flower grows if you water it.

title: Because of Emotions …
text: Things that you see or hear can cause you to feel emotions. Our emotions have causes and effects. Feeling sad can cause you to cry. Feeling happy can cause you to laugh.

title: Your Effect
text: Your actions cause effects. They can cause others to feel emotions. Your actions can also protect you. What are the effects of your words and actions?

title: Trust
text: When you trust someone, it means you can believe them. Pay attention to who tells you the truth. Think about who you can trust.

title: Tell the Truth
text: A lie is something that is not true. If you lie, people cannot trust you. A person you can trust will not ask you to lie. You can tell the truth.

title: Respect Personal Property
text: Stealing is also lying. Stealing is taking another person's things without asking. A person you can trust will not ask you to steal. A trustworthy person will not steal from you.

title: Mistakes
text: Everyone makes mistakes. A mistake is when you do something wrong.

title: Make It Right
text: When you make a mistake, you can say, “I’m sorry.” You can make things better.

title: Essential Question
text: How do the characteristics of Ohio impact the people of the state?

title: Physical Characteristics of Ohio
text:
The physical characteristics of a place are the natural features found in that place. The physical characteristics of Ohio include the Great Lakes Plains, the Till Plains, and the Allegheny Plateau. Others are Campbell Hill, rock arches, and glacial grooves. There are also rivers, lakes, and islands. Ohio’s climate is part of its physical characteristics too.

Great Lakes Plains

The Great Lakes Plains lie along the shore of Lake Erie. Ohio used to be covered by a glacier. The glacier created Lake Erie when it melted. It also created the Great Lakes Plains. This land is flat and fertile.

Till Plains

Ohio’s Till Plains were also left behind by a glacier. The melting glacier began to drain. The water pulled some rocks, soils, and sand along. The rocks, sand, and soils are called “till.” These were left on the land by the water. The Till Plains are mostly flat and good for growing soybeans.

Allegheny Plateau

The Allegheny Plateau in Ohio is part of the Appalachian Plateaus. The core of the Earth is very hot. It is so hot that it melts rocks. Sometimes the molten rock pushes upward. This causes the land above it to rise. That is how plateaus are formed. The Allegheny Plateau has two sections. They are called “glaciated” and “unglaciated.” The glaciated part was once covered by a glacier. That part is a large area of flat, fertile land. The unglaciated part is mostly forest. However, it has a lot of coal, oil, and sandstone.

Campbell Hill

Campbell Hill is known as the highest point in Ohio. It was also left behind by a glacier. It has a flat top. Campbell Hill is made of minerals and rocks, such as limestone and sandstone.

Natural Arches

Ohio has many natural arches and bridges. A natural arch is a large rock that has a hole through it. An arch can be a bridge if it sits over a valley or stream. An arch that is wide enough may be called a natural tunnel. These arches are often formed by water. The water washes the softer part of the rock away and leaves a hole. This can take many centuries.

Bodies of Water in Ohio

Rivers, lakes, and streams are Ohio’s lifeblood. Some of them were left behind by a large glacier. The most famous bodies of water in Ohio are the Ohio River and Lake Erie.

Glacial Grooves

Ohio’s physical characteristics include glacial grooves as well. These grooves were created by a moving glacier. Water from the melting glacier dragged rocks and sand along. These sand and rocks scraped off the soft rocks on the surface of the rock beneath. This created the glacial grooves.

Ohio’s Islands

The glacier that once covered Ohio created islands too. Most of these can be found in Lake Erie and the Ohio River. An island is a piece of land surrounded by water. The islands in Lake Erie were formed by the same glacier that created the lake. The biggest island in Ohio is Kelley’s island.

title: Physical and Human Characteristics of My Community
text: Now that you have learned about some of the physical and human characteristics of Ohio, it is time for you to investigate your local community. Identify five physical characteristics and five human characteristics in your community. Draw an example of each. Then, explain how each of these characteristics impacts your community.

title: Phenomenon
text: A baker in the Great Blanton Bake-Off of Austin, Texas, can’t create an artistic dessert because his electric oven is not working.

Phillis Wheatley was a prominent author in early American history. She was born in West Africa in 1753. Enslavers captured her when she was just seven years old. They took her to Boston on a boat named The Phillis, where a wealthy tailor named John Wheatley purchased her. John named her after the ship that she sailed on and his own last name. This is how she became known as Phillis Wheatley.

At first, Phillis worked as a personal servant to John’s wife, Susanna. The Wheatleys let her study astronomy, history, literature, poetry, and the Bible. Phillis began writing her own poetry by the time she was 13. Her writing amazed people.

In 1773, Phillis’ collection of poems was published. The book was titled Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral. It was the first book written by a black woman to be published in America. The book meant that Phillis was a famous, celebrated poet. The Wheatleys took her to London, where she met many wealthy fans and politicians. She even met Benjamin Franklin, who praised her work.

Phillis gained her independence around 1774, but she continued to live with the Wheatleys. She married a free black man named John Peters. Sadly, the American Revolution made it hard for them to earn money. Phillis wrote letters and poems that supported George Washington and the Patriots in their fight for independence. In one of her poems she wrote "A crown, a mansion, and a throne that shine, With gold unfading, WASHINGTON! Be thine."

title: Engineering Scenario
text: Alana forgot her backpack at home and has a lot of supplies to bring home for a science project.

title: Introduction to Ancient Rome
text:
The vast civilization of Rome began as a small tribal village on the banks of the Tiber River. Thanks to good resources and a great location for trade, it grew quickly. Historians refer to this region as Latium and to the people as Latins. Around 800 B.C.E., a group of people called the Etruscans conquered the region. The Etruscans had been influenced by the Greeks, and, in turn, they shared Greek culture with the Latins. They shared their writing system, building techniques, and even their clothing style. The Etruscans also taught the people military strategy and weapon making. This may have helped the early Romans, as they conquered the Etruscans and kicked them out of their land about 100 years later.

Romans date the official founding of their city to 753 B.C.E. At first, Rome was ruled by a series of kings elected by citizens. The last king of Rome was said to be very cruel and unjust. He was overthrown, and the rule of kings was replaced with a republic form of government. Soon the Roman Republic controlled all of the Italian peninsula, and from there they conquered most of Europe, eventually becoming the Roman Empire. At its largest point, the Roman Empire controlled two million square miles, including parts of Africa and Asia, and encircling the Mediterranean and Black Seas.

Early Romans interacted frequently with the Greek colonies to the south. This gave Rome a model for building its own infrastructure and culture. Romans also borrowed Greek ideas about literature, religion, architecture, and more. Between 332 B.C.E. and 642 C.E., Greece and Rome were the two most powerful civilizations around the Mediterranean Sea. The term “Greco-Roman” is used in history to talk about the influence of the culture and beliefs of ancient Greece and Rome.

Rome existed for more than 1,200 years, and the Roman Empire lasted for more than 700 years. At the peak of its glory, it was the largest empire in the known world. The Romans left many examples of their culture throughout the impressive civilization they built.

title: Framing Question Week 17
text: What geographic and environmental factors helped the Roman civilization grow?

title: Geography of Ancient Rome
text:
Rome was located in what is now known as Italy. Shaped like a giant boot, the Italian peninsula stretches south from Europe into the Mediterranean Sea. The “heel” points toward Greece, and the “toe” points across the sea to Africa. It is surrounded on three sides by bodies of water. They are the Tyrrhenian Sea, the Adriatic Sea, the Mediterranean Sea, and the Ionian Sea. There are also three major rivers in Italy. The Po River, to the north, is the country’s longest and most important river. The Tiber River flows near the capital city of Rome. The Arno River is the third important river.

Italy has many mountains, but they are not so high and so numerous that they divide and isolate communities like the mountains did in ancient Greece and China. The Alps form a natural barrier along the northern border. The Apennine Mountains run from north to south down the middle of the peninsula, with the Tiber River cutting through them in central Italy. In ancient times, mountain passes helped connect people and allowed them to trade ideas and goods with each other. Italy has three active volcanoes: Mt. Etna, Mt. Vesuvius, and Stromboli. The islands of Sicily and Sardinia are also part of Italy. Italy has three main plains with many inland rivers flowing through lands that are perfect for farming. The coastal ranges and valleys of the peninsula also provided fertile land. The geography of the Italian peninsula created an ideal climate for early settlers to establish farming communities. However, Italy’s extensive coastline made Italy a desirable location for other cultures as well. Carthaginians from North Africa built settlements in the south and on nearby islands. Before Rome was founded, the Greeks had also explored southern Italy and set up settlements of their own. As a result, early Roman settlers were exposed to new ideas and ways of doing things.

Rome was built on seven hills. It was a perfect location for a city. The hills around Rome were covered with forests of oak and chestnut. The Tiber River provided a source of fresh water. It also gave the Romans access to the sea. Traders and soldiers could travel quickly by river and take advantage of many established routes to other areas of the Mediterranean. The seven hills helped protect the city from enemy attacks.

title: The Marvels of the Mediterranean
text:
The Roman Empire might never have become so large and successful if it weren't for the Mediterranean Sea. The sea is about 2,300 miles long and is bordered by Europe, Asia, and Africa. It connects to the Atlantic Ocean and is the largest inland sea in the world.

But why was it so special and unique in ancient history? The Mediterranean offered access to many trade routes. The Romans could send ships out with goods and bring back foreign goods. Rome was able to trade with places like the Middle East and Northern Africa. The Romans also used this sea to invade other territories, using their location to their advantage. At one point, they controlled all the shores around the Mediterranean.

The citizens living in Rome had access to amazing lands and opportunities to gain wealth and power, all because of what the Mediterranean Sea offered them. They believed it belonged to them and wanted it to be used exclusively for their own gain. They even called it "Mare Nostrum," which means "our sea" in Latin. Rome and Carthage fought three long wars over who would control Sicily and the Mediterranean Sea. The wars were called the Punic Wars. Although the Roman Empire collapsed long ago, the Mediterranean Sea still serves the countries surrounding it, especially for travel and fishing. People come from all over the world to visit the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Human Adaptation
text:
We have learned much about how a civilization and its culture can be shaped or sometimes dictated by geography. When groups of people settle in a new place, their first step is to make sure there are enough resources in the area. Often, people change their behavior based on those resources. Successful civilizations are filled with accounts of people who were willing to adapt to what was around them.

The earliest Roman settlers may have been nomads or shepherds who wandered into Italy across the Alps. They settled on either side of the Tiber River. The river gave them water, and the flatlands were perfect for farming. They learned to farm and found new ways to make clothes and shelter. As Rome expanded into more and more territory, it became difficult to make enough food to meet the demand of the growing population. Huge plantations were created to feed the people in Roman cities. Romans learned to import wheat from North Africa and olive oil from Spain.

Rome was at the center of a large network of trade routes. As Romans conquered new territories, they needed good roads and bridges to connect the territories back to Rome. The Roman soldiers led the construction projects. The system of roads and bridges was so strong that parts of it still exist today in Europe and the Middle East.

At one point, the city of Rome had more than one million citizens. The city also had many industrial businesses like blacksmiths, tanneries, and concrete manufacturers. With thousands of fires for cooking and heating burning daily, the Romans burned a lot of wood. So they turned to solar heat. They designed buildings that were oriented to use the sun’s rays for heating and to capture and store heat inside the door and walls. They added transparent stone or clear glass to increase the temperature. The Romans adopted, adapted, invented, and worked their way through problems to become one of the world's largest and most powerful empires.

title: Climate
text:
Although the Romans conquered many lands across Europe, Africa, and Asia, they probably felt most at home in the climate of the Mediterranean region, where they enjoyed mild winters and toasty summers. This mild climate also helped Rome grow and prosper economically. The warm summers and rainy winters made it possible for the people to develop a strong agricultural system and plant crops year-round. The climate was excellent for growing vegetables, grapes, olives, wheat, and other grains.

Because of the warm climate, people wore light-colored clothing. Both men and women wore tunics, which are loose fighting shirts or gowns. They could be sleeved or sleeveless and end at the knees or reach to the floor. A toga was usually worn only by the wealthy or for special occasions. A toga was a sheet-like cloth that wrapped around the body, leaving one arm free. Depending on a person’s rank in Rome, they might wear one or more stripes on their toga. Foreigners and enslaved people were forbidden to wear togas. Poorer people went barefoot, while wealthier people wore a cross between shoes and sandals. These were called calcei and were made of leather. Romans also wore open sandals, but wealthy Romans rarely wore sandals outside.

title: Legends of Rome
text:
Romans date the history of their city to 753 B.C.E., but how was it founded? The exact origins of Rome are clouded by mystery and legends. The early Roman time period is the most poorly documented time in Roman history. Later, ancient historians added exaggerations, folklore, and myth to incomplete historical records. To try to understand how Rome was founded, we have to look at both the facts and fiction surrounding the founding of this ancient city.

There is evidence of people living on the peninsula as many as 14,000 years ago. Archaeologists have found evidence that an early settlement existed on the hills near the Tiber River in about 750 B.C.E. One theory, based on those facts, is that Rome began as a small trading settlement and that the name simply came from Rumon, the ancient name for the river.

According to legend, Ancient Rome was founded by two brothers who were half-gods. The god of war, Mars, had twin sons named Romulus and Remus. The king ordered that the infants be abandoned in the river, but they survived and were cared for by a wolf until a shepherd found them. When they were older, the brothers decided to establish a city. In a fight over which of them would lead, Remus was killed, and Romulus named the city after himself. This story was first written down around 400 B.C.E. It is the best-known legend of the founding of Rome, but it is not the only one.

According to the Roman poet, Virgil, the city was started by a prince and hero of the Trojan War. In this legend, the hero Aeneas escaped Troy after the war, traveled to Italy, and founded the city. In some versions of the story, Romulus and Remus are his descendants.

Another legend claims the city was named after Roma, a noblewoman who traveled with Aeneas and the other survivors of the war. On the banks of the river, the men wanted to move on, but Roma and the other women protested and threatened to burn all of the Trojan ships. So while the date of the founding of Rome can be investigated through archaeology, the first inhabitants are still defined by the traditional stories handed down by the ancient Romans.

title: Geography’s Role in the Fall of Rome
text:
Physical features were an important part of ancient world civilizations. Cultures built agricultural communities, trade systems, and military defenses based on the features near their settlements. The Rhine River is a powerful waterway in the heart of Western Europe. The river gets its name from the Celtic word “renos,” which means raging flow. The beginning of the Rhine is high in the Swiss Alps. The Rhine River was an important natural boundary between the outside tribes and the Roman Empire. Anyone who wanted to challenge Roman rule knew they would need to cross the Rhine.

The Romans didn’t only use this mighty physical feature as a border. They also embraced it as a trade and transportation route and used it as a cultural highway. The river created a large, vibrant valley and provided resources for much of the vast empire. In the final years of the empire, the Roman armies were constantly defending Rome from nomadic tribes called the Vandals and Visigoths. The Rhine River was a natural boundary, but something unusual happened in the winter of 406 C.E. The river froze, creating a solid path of ice for the tribal troops. Marching through the weakened defenses and across the Pyrenees Mountains, the Visigoth king, Alaric, successfully conquered the city of Rome in 410. The Romans didn't think about the possibility of the river freezing and weren't prepared. Overlooking the river changed the course of history.

title: Life in Ancient Rome
text:
What was it like to live in ancient Rome? The main plaza in the center of the city was called the forum. This was also where the Roman government was located. Beautiful buildings with huge columns and archways lined the area. Many statues also decorated the forum. People came to the city center to socialize, listen to their government leaders, attend religious ceremonies, and go to the market. Historians think that at one point, around one million people lived in the ancient city of Rome. It must have been crowded and noisy. Shoppers, tradespeople with carts full of goods, construction projects, and public events would have made the center of Rome an exciting place to be.

Baths

Near the Roman forum, there were many public baths. Going to the baths was a very popular activity, but it was only for adults. Similar to spas today, the Roman baths were a place to get clean and relax. The baths had cold pools, warm pools, hot pools, steam rooms, and exercise areas. Romans cleaned themselves by applying oils to their skin and then scraping the oil and dirt off with a metal tool called a strigil. There were barbers at the baths to cut hair for a fee. Vendors sold food at the baths. Even acrobats and jugglers performed there. Historians think that at one time, there were around 900 public baths in ancient Rome. One famous Roman bath, built around 60 C.E., can still be found in Bath, England.

Food

In general, people ate breads, cheeses, fruits, fish, and vegetables. Wealthy Romans might enjoy boiled ostrich, peacock tongues, or roasted parrots. Those who couldn’t afford bread ate a type of porridge called puls. It was made from boiled grains and often included herbs or vegetables. Romans used honey or fruits as sweeteners. They ate most food with their fingers. The food was cut into bite-sized pieces to make it easier. In wealthy society, it became proper to eat with only three fingers and keep the ring and pinky fingers clean. People rested on cushions or sloping couches around a table rather than sitting on chairs.

School

Usually, only wealthy children attended school because it was costly. Paper was also very expensive. Roman students wrote on wax boards with a writing tool called a stylus. This way, they could erase and reuse their writing tablet. If students learned lessons too slowly, they were punished. Families who did not have enough money for school would teach their children at home. If the parents could read, write, and do math, they might teach these basic lessons at home. If not, the sons could learn the trade or skill their father had. Girls rarely went to school. They learned sewing, cooking, music, and other important skills from their mothers.

title: Framing Question Week 18
text: What factors contribute to a culture's peace and prosperity?

title: Politics and Classes
text:
According to written traditions, the first six kings of Rome were fair and kind rulers, but the seventh king was a cruel tyrant. The people rose up and defeated him. After this, the Romans decided they wanted a new form of government. They set up a system called a republic. There were two consuls at the top level. Senators gave advice to the consuls, and then there were other levels of leaders below the senate. In a true republic, all citizens should be given the power to elect their leaders. But the aristocratic families felt they were better at governing, so they took control. The majority of the citizens were not given any say in how they were ruled or who the rulers were. The rulers were all patricians.

Patricians were men from noble, upper-class families who were wealthy and privileged. Only certain families were part of the patrician class. The patricians held all the power, even though they were only a small section of the entire Roman population. The other Roman citizens were plebians. Plebeians were the working class. They were the farmers, shopkeepers, laborers, and soldiers of Rome. They were not given the same rights as the patricians.

Plebeians fought to have a say in government. Things finally began to change after the plebeians went on strike. They refused to fight in the army and threatened to leave and form their own city. The patricians were worried. Who would do the work if the plebeians left? Who would fight in the military? Who would pay the taxes? Finally, a few plebeians were allowed to participate in the government. If they wanted to reject a decision made by the patrician leaders, plebeians could stand up and yell, “Veto” (I say no). The plebeians fought for their rights for more than 200 years. Eventually, they were given more equality in the government.

There were also enslaved people. Slavery was very common in Rome. It was considered necessary for the survival and advancement of society. There were many ways to become enslaved, such as being captured in war, seized by pirates, refusing to serve in the military, or being born into slavery. Researchers believe that at some point, as much as one-third of the population of Rome was enslaved. Enslaved people served in shops, homes, farming, construction, and many other roles. They had no legal rights and could not participate in government or vote.

title: Roman Law
text:
The struggle between the powerful patricians and the working-class plebeians was called the Conflict of the Orders. One result of that conflict was a group of laws called the Twelve Tables. These laws were engraved on metal tablets and displayed in the Roman forum for all to see. They protected some basic rights regardless of a citizen’s social class. Punishment for committing a crime, however, was not the same for everyone. The punishment you received still depended on your class. If you were a wealthy patrician, the punishment would be much less harsh than it was for an enslaved person who committed the same crime.

The original tablets have been destroyed, but parts of the text of the Twelve Tables were preserved through excerpts and quotations written down by ancient Roman authors. We base some of our laws today on these ancient Roman laws. One important law was: No ex post facto. This law stated that a person couldn’t be punished for doing something wrong before there was a law against it. For example, say someone drives their car down the highway at 65 miles per hour. The next day, a law goes into effect that puts the speed limit at 55. That driver can’t be given a ticket for driving too fast the day before, because it wasn’t against the law when they did. The U.S. Constitution states that “No … ex post facto law shall be passed.”

title: Roman Power Grows
text:
Carthage was a powerful city on the coast of North Africa. It was a colony originally established by the Phoenicians. Carthaginians claimed they owned the Mediterranean Sea and threatened to sink Roman ships. The Carthaginians also wanted to control the island of Sicily. Rome and Carthage fought three long wars over who would control Sicily and the Mediterranean Sea. The wars were called the Punic Wars. The Romans won the first war in 241 B.C.E. In the Second Punic War, from 218 to 201 B.C.E., Rome also dominated, but Carthage was able to establish a strong influence in Spain.

Later, the Carthaginian general Hannibal set out to invade Rome. He sailed with his troops from Northern Africa to Spain. Then his army of about 46,000 soldiers climbed over the Alps and into Italy. Hannibal brought along something never before seen in Europe: elephants. Some accounts say there were 37 elephants, to be exact. Many of Hannibal’s troops and most of the elephants did not survive the crossing over the high, snowy Alps. He had hoped these animal “tanks” would help him in his efforts to conquer Rome, but he failed. So, the Carthaginians lost the Second Punic War, too. In 146 B.C.E., during the last Punic War, Rome destroyed Carthage. To make sure they would never rise again, it is said the Romans burned Carthage to the ground and covered the farmland with salt. The Roman republic was now the master of the Mediterranean Sea, and an empire was beginning.

title: Julius Caesar
text:
After the Punic Wars, Rome became more and more powerful. The Romans continued to expand their empire through the use of currency, trade routes, and conquest. Leaders began fighting for power and control. This began a civil war, or fighting between groups of people in the same country.

When the early Romans first created the Republic, they established a system of two elected consuls at the top of the government. This was done to keep one leader from becoming too powerful and making himself king. The two consuls were also like generals. They had the task to lead Rome’s armies. In times of war, when it was important to have unity and a strong central command, Rome could appoint one dictator instead of the two consuls. This dictator would have complete military control, but not for longer than six months.

During this time of civil war in Rome, Julius Caesar was a consul. Hoping he would bring peace to Rome, the government leaders made Caesar dictator, but they gave him the position for life instead of for a six-month period. In 46 B.C.E., Julius Caesar won the civil war. During his rule as a dictator, Caesar did many good things. He helped the poor by forgiving their debts. He gave land to farmers, replaced dishonest leaders, and built roads and buildings. Caesar also gave citizenship to the people conquered by the Romans.

Caesar's rule did not last long. Many patricians were jealous of Caesar’s power. They believed he was becoming too powerful, and they worried that he wanted to be king. A group of patricians decided to stop him. Caesar was assassinated by members of the Roman Senate. Following Caesar’s death, Rome again faced civil war. Eventually, Caesar’s adopted son, Octavian, came to power, and the Roman republic came to an end.

title: Religion and Culture
text:
With citizens from three different continents, there was a lot of variety in ancient Rome. Romans conquered cultures that spoke many different languages and had many different lifestyles. Rome was a site of encounter; this means it was a place where different cultural groups exchange ideas, goods, and technology. Through cultural diffusion, languages, religions, and cultures blended.

Different people often have contrasting beliefs, even if they live together. The early Romans were polytheistic. Citizens were free to worship more than one god and practice different religions. There were many Greek colonies on the lower part of the Italian Peninsula. The Roman people adopted many of the Greek myths and Greek gods as their own. Like the ancient Greeks, the ancient Romans believed gods and goddesses controlled all things in nature. They also believed they could ask the gods and goddesses for advice about the future. They gave gifts to the gods in hopes that they’d protect the people and their city. The chief god was Jupiter, the sky god. Other gods included Mercury, the god of trade; Neptune, the god of the ocean; Pluto, the god of the underworld; Apollo, the god of the sun; Terra, the goddess of the earth; and Venus, the goddess of love. As you can see, many of the planets were named for the gods of ancient Rome.

title: Language
text:
Researchers believe that from its earliest history, the original people of Rome spoke the Latin language. It got its name from Latium, the name of the region in the early days of Rome. Starting in about 700 B.C.E., people began to write Latin in addition to speaking it.

Many modern languages evolved from Latin. They are called Romance languages. Some people think that this is because they are flowery, romantic languages. Actually, the word “Romance” comes from their connection with Rome. The Romance languages include Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian, and Romanian. Although English is not considered a Romance language, Latin has given thousands of words to the English language. The word “veto,” in Latin, means “I forbid,” or “I say no.” When the plebeians wanted to stop a decision from being taken by the patrician leaders, they could stand up and yell, “Veto!” Today, in English, veto means the right to refuse to allow something to be done. Veto power is used in the United States government to stop a law from being passed or a decision from being acted upon.

There are very few people in the modern world who can speak fluently in Latin, but many can read it. Latin is considered a “dead language,” which means that it cannot be changed and new words cannot be added. A living language, for example, is English, which is often changing and adding new words. Today, Latin is used by scientists to name, organize, and classify species of animals and plants. Some Latin animal names are funny by just doing their job. For example, the Latin name of the nilgai, a large Asian deer, is Boselaphus tragocamelus. It means ‘ox-deer goat-camel,’ which, when you see a nilgai, fits.

Latin words are also used in government and law. You can find unique Latin sayings carved on monuments and buildings and used in official seals. E pluribus unum means “One from many.” It is the traditional motto of the United States and appears on the Great Seal. It refers to the effort to form a single nation from many states.

title: Beneath the Wings of Rome and Greece
text:
Have you ever wondered where the idea for our government came from? Our Founding Fathers were tired of living under a king. They did not want our government to be a monarchy. They looked to history for examples. They found inspiration in ancient Greece and Rome.

Ancient Greece had a democracy. Ancient Rome had a republic. A democracy is a government ruled by the people. A republic is a government in which its citizens choose representatives to speak and work for them. The founders of America combined these ideas to form our government.

Our Constitution is also based on an idea from ancient Rome. In 451 and 450 B.C.E., the Twelve Tables were created. They were 12 bronze tablets that held all the laws of ancient Rome. As they are in our Constitution, amendments allowed laws to change to better serve the people. The Twelve Tables were displayed in the capital of Rome for all to see. The original U.S. Constitution is on display in our capital today.

The government of ancient Greece had three branches. They were the Assembly, the Council of 500, and the People’s Court. Our government has three branches too. The executive branch is controlled by the president. The legislative branch is the Senate and the House of Representatives. The judicial branch is the Supreme Court.

The idea for our Senate came from ancient Rome. The ancient Roman Senate met to create and vote on laws, just as the U.S. Senate does. In ancient Greece, a law could not pass unless a majority of senators voted for it. That means to become a law, most of the leaders had to vote for it. Our government also uses the majority rule system. Having separate parts of a government means no one part has too much power. Only certain leaders in Greece and Rome had limits on how long they could be in power. In America, many positions have term limits. A president can only serve for two terms but for a total of 10 years. This allows for a vice president to serve out the remaining term of a sitting president in case of death, illness, or resignation.

Citizens of both ancient civilizations elected their leaders. However, only male citizens could vote in ancient Greece and Rome. At first, only white men could vote in America. But now, both men and women can vote. Any adult can vote, regardless of their race. Citizens of ancient Greece were also allowed to be part of their government. They could serve in the People’s Court. This was a jury of citizens that decided whether other citizens were innocent or guilty of crimes.

Creating a government that is fair and balanced is no easy task. The Iroquois Constitution and the Great Laws of Peace also helped to shape U.S. democracy. Luckily, the early leaders of America had examples from history to help them. It is cool to think that our government today is based on two different ancient civilizations from almost 2,500 years ago!

title: The Fur Trade
text:
As North America was being colonized, natural resources were becoming scarce in Europe. Resources were needed for construction supplies and other goods. The large reserves of natural resources in North America were needed in Europe.

A strong trade network was created between England, France, and the colonies. European merchants scheduled regular trips to and from the colonies. Manufactured goods were sent to America. Raw materials would then be loaded onto the ships for the return trip. Those materials were used in Europe to produce more goods.

Wood was a major resource. Lumber was used to support new construction. However, animal pelts were the most valuable resource. The leather from deer was prized. Leather doesn't wear down like cloth. It also offers protection against heat and fire. Gloves, aprons, and leggings were made from leather. Beaver furs were also highly favored. They are weather-repellent, or not affected by rain or snow. Beaver became fashionable for men’s hats. This caused the demand to increase rapidly.

The furs were supplied by Native Americans. Many Indigenous tribes would trade for manufactured goods from Europe, such as iron pots, weapons, and jewelry. Many Native Americans were expert hunters. Getting furs and pelts for trade was not difficult. In return, manufactured goods helped make their lives easier.

French traders traveled to Native American villages. The British traders set up trading posts. The original marketplaces of the Native Americans became international places of trade. They were vibrant places full of people, goods, and services. Many languages could be heard there. News and stories were exchanged. The British and French used these centers to make alliances, or unions, with the Native American tribes.

The British and French also wanted control of the waterways and footpaths used in the Native American trade network. Whoever controlled them could easily and safely use the network. That would give them power over trade to the interior of North America.

Near modern-day Pittsburgh, the Allegheny and Monongahela Rivers meet and form the Ohio River. The area is called the “Forks of the Ohio.” In the 1750s, the Forks of the Ohio was the most valuable piece of property in North America. The Ohio river flows to the Mississippi and the interior of North America. The French wanted a fort and trade center there. So did the British. The Native Americans didn't want either group to have control.

Western Pennsylvania became the center of struggle. The winner would gain control of the wealthy fur trade. Tensions between the three empires rose. Finally, in 1754, a French diplomat was killed by British militia. They were under the command of Major George Washington. The tensions erupted. The French and Indian War began.

title: Washington Travels to Fort LeBouef
text:
Primary documents are created by people who saw or experienced something themselves. They are usually created around the time of the event. This article is based on the journals of Major George Washington and Christopher Gist in 1753.

Read the journal entries of Major George Washington and Christopher Gist from 1753–1754. Mark the locations on the map that are mentioned in the journal.

Christopher Gist’s Journal

Wednesday, November 14, 1753

Then Major George Washington came to my house at Wills Creek, and delivered me a letter from the council in Virginia requesting me to attend him up to the commandant of the French fort on the Ohio river.

Thursday, November 15, 1753

We set out.

Friday, November 23, 1753

Set out to ... Allegheny to the mouth of Monongahela, where we ... encamped that night.

Saturday, November 24, 1753

Set out … to Logstown and we spoke to the chief’s this evening.

Friday, November 30, 1753

We set out ... and encamped at the Murthering Town ... on the branch of Great Beaver Creek.

Tuesday, December 4, 1753

Set out ... where we were kindly received by Monsieur Joncaqire, the French interpreter for the Six Nations.

Thursday, December 6, 1753

We set out late in the day, accompanied by the French General and four soldiers.

Saturday, December 8, 1753

We set out and traveled twenty-five miles to Cussewago, an old Indian town.

Monday, December 10, 1753

Set out, traveled about 15 miles to the French fort, the sun being set ... and they received us with a great deal of [politeness].

Wednesday, December 12, 1753

The Major ... showed his commission and offered the Governor’s letter to the commandant.

Sunday, December 16, 1753

We set out by water …

Saturday, December 22, 1753

Came to Venango ...

Sunday, December 23, 1753

We set out from Venango …

Monday, December 24, 1753

Here Major Washington set out on foot ...

Wednesday, December 26, 1753

It was very cold; all the small runs were frozen, that we could hardly get water to drink.

Saturday, December 29, 1753

We set out early, got to Allegheny, made a raft, and with much difficulty got over to an island about [the Forks]. The Major, having fallen in from off the raft, and my fingers frostbitten, and the sun down, and very cold, we contented ourselves to encamp upon that island. It was deep water between us and the shore; but the cold did us some service, for in the morning it was frozen hard enough for us to pass over the ice.

Monday, December 31, 1753

Next day we waited on Queen Alliquippa, who lives now at the mouth of Youghiogheny. She said she would never go down to the river Alleghany to live except the English built a fort, and then she would go and live there.

Major George Washington's Journal

Wednesday, October 31, 1753

I was commissioned and appointed by the Honourable Robert Dinwiddie, Esq; Governor of Virginia to visit and deliver a Letter to the Commandant of the French Forces on the Ohio, and set out on the intended Journey the same day.... We pursued the new Road to Wills Creek, where we arrived the 14th of November.

Wednesday, November 14, 1753

I engaged Mr. Gist to pilot us out.

Thursday, November 22, 1753

I spent some time in viewing the Rivers, and the Land in the Fork, which I think extremely well situated for a Fort; as it has the absolute Command of both Rivers.

Sunday, November 25, 1753

Came to town ... met the half king [Tanaghrisson, a Seneca who was leading the Seneca in the Ohio country].... He told me ... to go by Venango ... in less than five or six nights sleep ...

Friday, November 30, 1753

We set out about nine o’clock ... and traveled the road to Venango ...

Tuesday, December 4, 1753

[The French at Venango] told me that it was their absolute design to take possession of the Ohio ...

Friday, December 7, 1753

We passed over much good land since we left Venango ...

Wednesday, December 12, 1753

I prepared early to ... meet the commander.... I acquainted him with my business and offered my commission and letter … they received and adjourned to a private apartment for the captain to translate. After he had done it, the commander desired I would walk in and bring my interpreter to talk.

Friday, December 14, 1753

This evening, I received an answer to his honor, the governor’s letter, from the commandant.

Sunday, December 16, 1753

We had a tedious [not exciting] and very fatiguing [tiring] passage down the creek.... This creek is extremely crooked ...

Wednesday, December 26, 1753

I took my necessary papers, [changed clothes] I set out with Mr. Gist. the day following, just after we had passed a place called Murdering town where we intended to quit the path and steer across the the country.

Tuesday, January 1, 1754

This day we arrived at Wills Creek, after as fatiguing journey as it is possible to conceive, rendered so by excessive bad weather.

title: Logstown
text:
Logstown was a Native American town. It was located in modern-day Beaver County, near Ambridge. The Leni-Lenape (Delaware) and Shawnee tribes lived at Logstown in the 1740s. Members of other native groups also lived there. These included the Seneca-Cayuga, the Miami, the Mohawk, and the Wyandot. Logstown was an important trading center for Native Americans. Over time, Logstown became important to the European traders too.

Logstown was a vibrant marketplace. Many people from different nations went to Logstown. News, information, ideas, and goods were all traded there. The French and English had traders and allies in Logstown. The French there learned what the British were doing. The British did the same with the French. They each wanted information about the many Native American tribes and their alliances.

The Native Americans in Logstown had a history of trading with the French. However, they did not want the French to build forts or settlements on their land. The French began building forts anyway. They built Fort de la Presque Isle and Fort Leboeuf in Erie. Fort Machault in Venango and Fort Duquesne near the Forks of the Ohio River were built to supply the French military. Native American leaders in the area became more interested in trading with the British.

Native Americans negotiated better trade deals from France and England. France and England tried to gain each Native American nation as allies. During the French and Indian War, the Native American tribes fought to keep their homeland. The French and the English wanted full control of the land and its resources.
