Chinese explorers traveled on land and ocean for thousands of miles to visit new places. They kept track of where they were by using compasses.

title: Zheng He: Ancient Explorer
text:
Zheng He was born in 1371 C.E. He became the most famous explorer from ancient China. Zheng He was an educated man. He spoke several languages and studied the geography of the world. The emperor asked Zheng He to lead a fleet of ships. His job was to cross the oceans and reach other lands. Zheng He’s first voyage included more than 27,000 men. There were sailors, soldiers, artisans, and language interpreters. The fleet included 62 ships. Zheng He took along porcelain, silk, jade, and other trade items. The explorers brought back ivory, timber, and pearls. They also brought animals that Chinese people had never seen before, like lions, ostriches, zebras, leopards, and even a giraffe.

Zheng He went on seven ocean voyages. He was called the “Admiral of the Western Seas.” His travels extended China’s influence throughout Europe and into Africa. His ships were the largest that had ever been built. The flagship measured about 400 feet long. For comparison, Christopher Columbus’s Santa Maria was 85 feet long.

In 1433, Zheng He died while traveling the Indian Ocean. He was buried at sea. After that, a new emperor decided it was more important to protect China than to spend resources exploring. He ended sea travel and had all the ships destroyed. China’s contact with other lands was limited for hundreds of years until a new emperor sent ships to other lands again.

title: Maya Achievements
text:
The Maya civilization was one of the oldest and most advanced civilizations of Mesoamerica. The Maya adapted to, depended on, and modified the environment of the region to meet their needs and wants for thousands of years. They developed innovative and complex ways to survive in the diverse physical environment and climate of Mesoamerica.

The Maya were skilled astronomers, mathematicians, and builders. They developed very precise calendars based on the movement of the sun, moon, and stars. The Maya were also excellent mathematicians. They used the discoveries they made from studying astronomy and mathematics to help them understand the world around them. The Maya also used this knowledge to build monumental temples, palaces, and ceremonial spaces.

Maya artisans produced elaborate paintings, sculptures, statues, and murals. They used the natural resources of their environment to create their art. Maya art often reflected their religious beliefs. It was also used to record Maya history. Many historians and archaeologists have been amazed by the sophisticated system of agriculture of the Maya. They used a variety of farming techniques, including irrigation systems and terraced farming.

Today, over seven million descendants of the ancient Maya still live in areas that were once a part of the Maya civilization in Mesoamerica. Most descendants of the Maya civilization still keep many of the cultural practices, beliefs, and languages of their ancestors. They work hard to preserve the artifacts and traditions of their ancestors. Because of their work, archaeologists and historians continue to learn about the advanced and innovative civilization of the Maya.

title: Week 29 Framing Question
text: What achievements did the Maya make in art, writing, architecture, science, and mathematics?

title: Astronomy and the Maya Calendar
text:
The Maya were experts in the study of astronomy. Astronomy is the branch of science that deals with stars, planets, and other objects in outer space. Maya religious and cultural beliefs were closely linked to the study of astronomy. The priests were responsible for studying space and celestial objects. They recorded their observations and interpreted signs that they believed were from the gods. Much of what they observed was recorded in religious texts, called codices. There are very few Maya codices that have survived to the present, but those that have provide valuable information about the religious beliefs of the Maya and their study of astronomy.

Maya builders and engineers also observed the principles of astronomy. Temples, palaces, and ceremonial buildings were built so that important parts of the buildings were aligned to the cardinal directions. This was done as a sign of respect for the gods. On many Maya buildings, the placement of the doors was particularly important during the equinoxes, when the seasons changed from winter to spring and summer to fall. At precise times during the equinoxes, sunlight would shine on the interior of temples, palaces, and ceremonial buildings and light up important statues or art.

The Maya also developed a very precise calendar based on astronomy. The Maya took a calendar developed by the Olmec people and improved it. The calendars they created could accurately track both short- and long-term cycles of time, including the solar year and the lunar cycle. Maya calendars were used for both daily and religious events.

The regular calendar, or Haab, consisted of 365 days. In the Haab, there were 18 months of 20 days, which, multiplied, equals 360 days. The Maya added five days to the calendar to match the 365-day orbit of the Earth around the sun. The ceremonial calendar or Tzolkin had 260 days and is the oldest calendar known in Mesoamerica. A third calendar, known as the Calendar Round, was made up of 52-year periods; its use is not known. Another calendar was used to keep historical events in order and was widely used on monuments.

title: Mathematics
text:
Many experts claim that the Maya developed the most complex and revolutionary system of mathematics of any ancient civilization in the Americas. Current systems of mathematics use a base-10 system. Base-10 is also known as the place value system. In modern mathematics, each integer in a number can have a value between zero and nine. When more integers are added to a number, the number has more place values.

The Maya system of mathematics was very different from the modern system we use today. The Maya used base-5 or base-20. Instead of numerals, they used three symbols:

zero: a shell shape

one: a dot

five: a short line or bar

These symbols made it easier for all members of society to add and subtract numbers quickly. Maya numbers were written from the bottom of a scroll to the top. The example in the picture shows the number 13.

Armed with this knowledge and no modern instruments, the Maya made extremely accurate observations of the stars. For example, we know a year has 365 and one-quarter days. The Maya measured it to 365.242 days. We know it takes 29.53059 days for the moon to orbit the Earth. The Maya measured it at 29.5308.

title: Hieroglyphic Writing
text:
Like the ancient Egyptians, the Maya used a sophisticated system of pictographs called hieroglyphics for written communication. However, the Maya system of writing was more complex than the writing systems of the ancient Egyptians and other civilizations that used a written system based on hieroglyphs. Archaeologists and historians believe that the Maya system of writing was based on the Olmec system of writing. The Maya modified and enhanced the Olmec system of writing to include over 1,000 different images, glyphs, and symbols.

Words were created using a combination of pictographs, symbols, and phonetic glyphs. Pictographs represented actions or real objects. Symbols represented objects, adjectives, prepositions, plurals, and numbers. Phonetic glyphs represented sounds, such as consonants and vowels. Phonetic glyphs also represented the proper way to pronounce sounds, tenses of a word or phrase, prepositions, prefixes, and suffixes. Words could be represented in multiple ways. For example, the word “mountain” could be expressed as the word “witz” or represented by the pictograph meaning "mountain." The word “jaguar” could be represented by a combination of pictographs or the word “Balam.”

There are thousands of preserved examples of Maya writing. Some of the best examples are on stone monuments. Because they are generally larger than other artifacts, stone monuments often include many different types of pictographs, symbols, and phonetic glyphs. There are some examples of pottery that contain Maya writing that has been preserved. There are very few examples of Maya writing on paper sources.

title: Maya Medicine
text:
Among their other achievements, the Maya were skilled in health practices, such as medicine and healing. The Maya believed that people who were healthy were in a state of balance and that people who were not healthy were in a state of imbalance. They also believed that each person had a life force that could be directed to help with healing. Maya healers who practiced medicine were called shamans. It was a shaman’s job to bring balance to the body of a sick person.

The Maya used the things around them to aid in healing. Their shamans understood the properties of medicinal plants and used them regularly. The shamans also practiced some forms of surgery, such as dental surgery. They could create fillings for teeth out of minerals such as iron pyrite (fool's gold) or jade. They could even create entire fake teeth made from jade or turquoise. Sometimes these tooth alterations were used for fashion instead of health practices.

Shamans were also skilled in setting broken bones and closing up wounds using stitches made from hair. Another popular medicinal practice among the Maya was called a sweat bath. The Maya called a sweat bath a Temazcal. Temazcales were used to treat illnesses, such as fevers, and joint pain. The hot steam in a Temazcal was thought to help purify and restore the body and to bring a person a long and healthy life.

There are still Maya people today. Maya healers have learned Maya health practices passed down through many generations. Traditional Maya healing practices still continue today.

title: Pyramids and Temples
text:
Maya pyramids and temples were among the most striking and unique features of Maya cities. They were the centerpieces of many Maya cities. Most Maya pyramids were temples devoted to a specific god or multiple gods and also served as the home of the ruler and their family. The architecture of Maya pyramids and temples differed between the various city-states, but they shared many similarities.

Maya pyramids were constructed from large blocks of stone, including limestone, volcanic tuff, and sandstone. After the pyramids were built, the outside of the pyramids was covered with stucco. Stucco is a type of plaster used to coat walls and make them smoother. Some pyramids were covered in large slabs of rock to create a smooth exterior surface. Pyramids were often painted in bright colors, such as blue, red, green, or yellow, and covered in carvings and sculptures. The interior walls of pyramids were covered in large painted murals. Pyramids were multi-leveled and had stepped sides. This means they were built with a series of steps from the ground up to the top. This made them look like large stairways leading toward the sky.

One of the most famous Maya pyramids is located at Chichén Itzá. The Pyramid of Kukulcán was constructed around 960 C.E. It is one of the tallest Maya pyramids in Mesoamerica. The pyramid was built to honor the Maya god Kukulcán, who is depicted as a large serpent. Large statues of Kukulcán guard the pyramid. Like other Maya pyramids, the Pyramid of Kukulcán is a stepped pyramid with four sides.

Thousands of tourists visit the Pyramid of Kukulcán each year. Many people visit the pyramid to witness the phenomenon of “light and shadow” that takes place on the spring and fall equinoxes. On the spring and fall equinoxes, at around 3:00 in the afternoon, the sun lights up seven triangles on the northeastern side of the pyramid. The triangles form the shape of a serpent to honor Kukulcán.

title: A Pyramid Apart
text:
Pyramids of the ancient world differ from one another, especially the pyramids of Mesoamerica and Egypt. The Egyptian pyramids are immense and grand in design. These pyramids are also much older and do not have much decoration on the outside. In Mesoamerica, the exterior parts of the pyramids are decorated. The walls of many pyramids are covered with sculptures of the gods or carvings that tell stories and depict the culture.

Egyptian pyramids had mostly smooth sides and were built as tombs for deceased rulers. The pyramids of Mesoamerica had sides that were more stepped and were used mostly for religious ceremonies. Many were actually temples built on top of pyramid-shaped structures. Some pyramids were built with extremely steep sides to keep people from climbing them. These pyramids were considered sacred, and no one was allowed to ever set foot on them. Other Mesoamerican pyramids were public buildings and were used as tombs for important rulers.

The Maya pyramids show the innovation and skill of the Maya people, who were able to create these impressive structures using only primitive tools and labor. Tourists in Mexico and the Yucatán today often visit the pyramids. They can climb some of the ancient structures. While the view from the top has changed over the years, the pyramids still show us signs of what life may have been like for the people who lived there hundreds of years ago.

title: What is Research?
text:
To solve a mystery, good detectives ask questions and search for evidence. Research is a way to investigate a problem or to ask for more information. Successful research requires three steps:

Asking questions

To begin the process, you must start by asking questions. In order for your research to be successful, you have to ask specific questions throughout the process. By asking questions, you can develop your claim. A claim is a statement you make about what you believe can be supported with evidence.

Processing evidence

The next step is to collect and process evidence. Evidence is information gathered from sources to answer your questions. The more evidence you gather, the stronger your claims will be.

Completing tasks to help solve the mystery

The final step to completing your research is to create a final product that connects the questions you have to the evidence you collected. This could be something you create or present after completing your research.

title: Week 31 Framing Question
text: How does research help with learning?

title: Types of Questions
text:
Asking questions is the first step in a research project. There are many types of questions you can ask throughout the whole process.

Compelling Questions

The word compelling refers to something that sparks your interest and is exciting. Answering a compelling question requires deep thinking. There could be multiple answers to the same question. The answer you come up with depends on the evidence you find in your research. An example of a compelling question is: Does the Bill of Rights protect everyone?

Supporting Questions

A supporting question gives you the information that you need to answer the compelling question. While a compelling question might have different answers depending on your research, a supporting question usually has only one answer. These answers give you the evidence you need to solve the mystery!

Here is an example of a compelling question: Does the Bill of Rights protect everyone? To support your compelling question, you could ask:

What is the Bill of Rights?

What are rights?

What rights does this document protect?

Why was this document created?

Each type of question is important and is needed for your research to be meaningful.

title: The Lenses of Social Studies
text:
Problems and questions that are compelling are usually big. This means it is necessary to investigate them through the lenses of different professionals in the field.

Thinking like a …

Historian

A historian researches and studies the past. They make claims to help us understand how people used to think and live.

Geographer

A geographer thinks about people and how they live and work in their environment. They make claims that help people build communities and use resources.

Political Scientist

Political scientists think about how government works. They help community leaders make laws for their people.

Social Scientist

Social scientists study the whole person: academic, social, emotional, physical, and mental. They analyze the effects that behaviors and emotions have on people or groups of people.

Economist

An economist thinks about money and finance. They look at money and production in a community. They make claims about the economy to help people make financial choices.

title: What Makes You Think That?
text:
During the research process, we make claims about compelling questions. Your job is to research information and provide evidence to support your claim. Evidence can change our thinking and beliefs about a topic or idea. This is known as the reflection process.

To reflect on an idea means to think deeply about it and decide if it is still the best solution. The most successful thinkers are people who know how to reflect and change their thinking as needed. You can use the following sentence starters to build a claim for the compelling question: Does the Bill of Rights protect everyone?

Make a claim!

I think ________ because ________.

Then think about the evidence!

I know this because …

According to the author …

In the picture, we can see …

From what I read in the text, we can see …

The most important evidence I found was …

If you were to make an initial claim on the example compelling question, what would it be and why?

title: Counterclaims
text:
During the research process, we create claims, but a good research project also looks at the opposite perspective of your claim. This is called a counterclaim. This is also part of the reflection process. Take a look at the evidence you’ve gathered, think about the lens you are using, and create a claim that is opposite to your claim. Knowing what someone else might think about your topic by using a counterclaim can make your research stronger and your evidence clearer.

Make a counterclaim!

It’s easy to think … but when you look at the facts …

While some researchers say …, I claim …

Others may say that … but I argue …

A common argument against this position is … but …

Some people disagree, saying … I challenge this. I don’t think …

title: Finding a Problem to Solve
text:
People often face many problems that need to be solved. Think about the compelling question that we have developed: Does the Bill of Rights protect everyone?

Before the American Revolution, the British Parliament passed the Quartering Act. This act required colonists to house British soldiers in their homes or provide barracks for them at their own expense. To ensure this would not be a problem in the future, Congress included the Third Amendment in the Bill of Rights. The Third Amendment states that "No Soldier shall, in time of peace be quartered in any house, without the consent of the Owner, nor in time of war, but in a manner to be prescribed by law."

What steps can you take to answer the question and solve the problem?

Problem-Solving Steps:

What was your claim and why did you make it?

This is where we can look at the evidence and think about who needs help.

Ask yourself: “What has to happen for the problem to be solved?”

Think back to our lenses of social studies. Ask the questions that a historian, economist, geographer, or political scientist may ask. You may find a few possible solutions there! Write down three of those possible solutions.

Think about the hardest parts of each solution. Write those down.

Ask yourself: “Who needs to be involved? Who has the power to change the problem?”

Think about what you are good at and what may be difficult for you. Which solution makes the most sense for you?

Once you have looked at different solutions, pick one and do the research.

Ask yourself the compelling question again and determine how you can solve the problem!

title: Diving Deeper: Thinking About Point of View
text:
Your personal history is different from everyone else's. This means you think about problems in ways that are unique to you. This can influence your point of view on different topics.

When you make a claim about a problem or question, you make it based on your point of view. This is also called perspective. Your perspective is extremely important. It helps you think about your topic, define problems, and develop solutions to these problems.

Your perspective can be different from others. It is also important to think about other people's perspectives. Their insight might be different from yours, but it may help solve problems more efficiently.

title: Phenomenon Comic
text: Many trees are cut down in high numbers around the world so that we have paper to use.

title: Engineering Design Problem
text:
Directions: Highlight information you think is important.

Deforestation is a big problem in tropical regions of the world. One way people remove trees is through logging. This is when humans use machines to help them cut down the forest. Another removal method is slash and burn. This is when they cut the trees down and burn them. Both methods leave the environment in a very different state than it was before. People cut forests down for a few reasons. The wood from the trees is used as furniture and homes. Wood can also be used for firewood or paper. Sometimes the land is what people want. They will clear the land so they can farm and grow coffee, and plant rubber trees, or palm trees.. Sometimes they put animals on the land.

When an environment changes from a rainforest to farmland, there are a lot of unexpected effects. The plants and animals in a rainforest depend heavily upon the trees as a place to call home. When the trees are cut down, those plants and animals have to find new homes. If they cannot find new homes, they won't survive. Sometimes a plant or animal will become extinct because this is the only place they can live. Trees don’t just help the plants and animals in the forest. Trees also help keep our air clean. If trees are cut down in large numbers, there are less trees to fight the pollution made by people.

title: Ideate Ways to Recycle Paper
text:
Sometimes we can’t reduce or reuse our paper. However, we can recycle it. Every ton, or 2,000 pounds, of paper recycled saves 17 trees. We’ve all heard about recycling and put the paper into the recycle box. What happens after that? How is paper recycled?

Paper is placed into the recycle box.
Paper is taken to the recycle center.
At the plant, they sort the paper into different grades, or qualities.
Large machines, called pulpers, shred the paper into small strips.
They then mix the paper with water and chemicals.
They break the paper down into fibers by heating this mixture.
Next, the paper is cleaned. Ink and anything sticky is removed.
The paper fibers are sent through a machine that makes the fibers stick together into a flat sheet.
The bonded fibers go through heated metal rollers to dry.
New paper is put onto large rolls so it is ready for its next use.

title: John C. Freeman and Mario Molina
text:
John C. Freeman

A meteorologist is a scientist who studies and predicts weather based on patterns. They create weather reports. They report their findings to others. John C. Freeman was a meteorologist. He was born and raised in Houston, Texas. During his career, he worked for the U.S. Army Air Corps, U.S. Weather Bureau, and Texas A&M University. He also collected research at the Weather Research Center in Houston. You may have been to the old John C. Freeman Weather Museum that was in Houston. The museum was named after him.

Mario Molina

The Nobel Prize is a very special award that people can receive for the important work they do. Mario Molina won a Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1995. He went to school in Mexico City. He loved science. He often made his bathroom into a laboratory. He spent hours doing chemistry. He studied chemistry in college. He then worked with several universities doing research. Most of his research was studying changes in the atmosphere. This is the area high up in the sky. It is where clouds form and precipitation falls. His research has had a great effect on the environment.

This week, you started to research the weather and the atmosphere just like Mario Molina and John C. Freeman. Would you like to study the weather for your career? Why or why not?
