title: Where Did We Get It?
text:
Can you imagine Irish food without potatoes? Italian food without tomatoes? Thai food without chili peppers? How would life be different for you if there was no chocolate? Potatoes, tomatoes, chili peppers, and chocolate are all foods that came to European countries from the Americas.

Chocolate

Chocolate is made from cocoa beans that were first grown in Central and South America. Cocoa beans were probably first consumed by the Olmec. The Aztec created a chocolate drink from cocoa beans. The English then turned cocoa beans into solid chocolate bars.

Now, can you picture not having chickens, apples, and citrus fruits in the United States? These are just a few of the foods that were brought to the Americas from other countries and continents.

Apples

You’ve probably heard the phrase “as American as apple pie.” In truth, experts think apple trees were brought to North America from Asia. Apple pie was first cooked in Europe and brought to the United States by European immigrants.

In addition to new foods, people traded and shared new ways of cooking foods. This exchange of foods and cooking techniques happened as civilizations became more advanced, travel became easier, and trade became more common. Leaders started sending explorers across oceans and deserts in search of new lands and new opportunities. Some of these explorers were successful. They returned home with a variety of new and exciting things, such as food, artwork, tools, and ideas.

Here in Louisiana, there are different foods that come from a mixture of many places. For example, Cajun cuisine is famous for spicy seafood dishes. The cooking style blends French, West African, and Spanish cooking techniques. It uses local ingredients, like okra, bell peppers, and crawfish. Gumbo and boudin are some famous Cajun dishes.

The next time you enjoy a tasty treat, take a moment to think about where it came from.

title: The Conveniences of Our Modern Life
text:
In ancient times, people had to rely on ingenuity, physical strength, and the natural resources around them in order to survive. They did not have most of the modern technologies that we take for granted, such as electricity, running water, and hospitals.

Advances in technology have made day-to-day life easier for people. Before washing machines were invented, people had to spend hours washing their clothes by hand. Before the days of the refrigerator, people had to keep their food cool using only ice. Before vacuum cleaners were invented, carpets had to be swept or taken outside and beaten with a stick. Climate control is another thing that makes our lives easier. In cold climates, most buildings have electric heaters. In the past, people had to rely on fires to keep them warm. In hot climates, most buildings have air conditioning to help keep people cool. In the past, people had to fan themselves by hand to stay cool.

Advances in technology also led to better infrastructures for cities. Infrastructure is the word we use to describe things that support modern human life. Infrastructure includes things like water supply, waste treatment, and roads. Our modern infrastructure makes getting water as easy as paying a water bill and then being able to turn on a faucet. Throughout history, many people have had to collect their water by hand, using buckets. The water wasn’t always safe to drink.

Our modern cities have waste management systems. This means that our trash, dirty water, and the waste from our bodies all have a place to go. The waste gets taken care of at waste management facilities. In the past, before waste management technology existed, people didn’t have many good options for what to do with waste. Trash could build up and make cities polluted and stinky. Water supplies would sometimes get contaminated by waste. Life in ancient civilizations was difficult and often perilous. Despite these challenges, the people of these civilizations were able to develop complex and sophisticated cultures and societies.

title: Water, the Source of Life
text:
Water has always been a fundamental resource for human civilization. In ancient river valleys, such as Mesopotamia or the Indus Valley, water was essential for agriculture and the growth of early communities. In ancient seafaring societies, such as Greece and Rome, water was a vital means of transportation and trade. And in the rainforests of Mesoamerica, water was a sacred and powerful force, essential for survival.

In all of these cultures, water was the source of life and the key to prosperity. Water also brought healing, both physical and spiritual. It was often used in religious ceremonies and rituals. Water was believed to have the power to bring life and abundance. In early Indigenous cultures in North America, water was revered as a sacred gift from the Earth to be protected and preserved.

Water is just as important to us today as it was to civilizations of the past. In fact, we rely on water for many of the same things that our ancestors did. We use water for drinking, cooking, and cleaning, and it is essential for maintaining our health and well-being. But because it is so easily available to us, sometimes we don’t think about how vital it is. When we learn more about the importance of water and its role in our daily lives, we can better understand and appreciate human events and experiences throughout history. When we respect water and use it wisely, we help to conserve this precious resource to make sure that it is available for future generations.

title: Writing Things Down
text:
Today, there are many ways to communicate in writing with people all over the world. We have email, texting, and message apps. Books, the internet, and online media also allow people to share their ideas with others. But how did people do that thousands of years ago, before all of those things were invented?

These are some of the early developments in writing. These developments changed people's lives. Once they learned to write, people could share ideas and information, keep track of trade, write down laws, and record the important things that happened. Writing also allowed people to preserve stories that had been told for generations. Because of writing, we can learn about the past.

Cave Paintings
The first people communicated with each other by painting pictures in caves. They would use charcoal, dirt, or even dyes from vegetables. They used sticks or their fingers to make the drawings. As time went by, the pictures became symbols. Then the symbols became letters and words.

Cuneiform
The Sumerians of Mesopotamia developed a way of writing we call cuneiform. Cuneiform means “wedge-shaped.” The Sumerians used a stick with a wedge-shaped triangular tip to press symbols into wet clay tablets. When the clay dried, the writing was permanent. It is the first known form of writing.

Hieroglyphs
The Egyptians knew about cuneiform but decided to make up their own kind of writing. This kind of writing is called hieroglyphs. These pictures and symbols were often carved on temple walls and sacred objects. Hieroglyphs were not read from left to right, like English, but from right to left, from top to bottom, or even in alternating directions.

Shang Dynasty
The people of the Shang Dynasty began with picture writing, too. We know about their writing from the oracle bones that have been found in the Yellow River Valley. They were bones with writing carved on them. They were used to predict fortunes and futures.

Indus Script
The people who lived in the Indus Valley used a way of writing that was similar to the Sumerians. The problem is that no one has been able to understand it yet. Not many examples of the script are around today. Archaeologists have found clay pots with markings on them and a few other examples of this early writing.

title: The Power of Timelines
text:
Timelines are a great way to visualize the progression of events over a period of time. They help us understand information about ancient civilizations by placing them in chronological order and showing the relationships between events. Timelines can also help us see how different cultures are interconnected and how they have influenced each other.

Look at the timelines below. How do they show connections between ideas, events, and developments in world history? How do they help us compare developments over time and show how things change?

Communication in Ancient times

Make Your Own Timeline About Ancient Civilizations

In 1933, the United States was in the middle of a great economic depression. In that same year, Democrat Franklin Delano Roosevelt was sworn in as the new president of the United States. As president, Roosevelt faced many challenges. One of the greatest challenges was finding a way to bring the country out of the Great Depression.

The New Deal was the name Roosevelt gave to the expansive new plan he and his advisors introduced. This plan was meant to bolster the country's economy. The New Deal created government agencies to assist people in need. This included those in poverty, the elderly, farmers, and millions of unemployed Americans. Programs included:

AAA (Agricultural Adjustment Administration)

CCC (Civilian Conservation Corps)

CWA (Civil Works Administration)

FERA (Federal Emergency Relief Administration)

FSA (Farm Security Administration)

FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation)

NRA (National Recovery Administration)

NYA (National Youth Administration)

PWA (Public Works Administration)

REA (Rural Electrification Administration)

RFC (Reconstruction Finance Corporation)

SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission)

SSA (Social Security Administration)

TVA (Tennessee Valley Authority)

WPA (Works Progress Administration)

Many of these programs had a profound impact on the people, places, economy, and government of Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvanians benefitted from the Social Security Act (SSA). The SSA was another part of Roosevelt’s New Deal legislation. Under the SSA, the government taxed workers’ salaries. This money was given to older citizens when they reached a certain age. The age was usually 65. The Social Security Act is still in use today.

One program that had a large impact on Pennsylvania was the Works Progress Administration (WPA). The WPA provided jobs for the unemployed people in every economic sector. The jobs included those in social services, construction, public health, conservation, education, fine arts, and scholarly research. The WPA completed hundreds of projects in Pennsylvania during the Great Depression. The WPA helped to repair and maintain over 145 miles of roads in Philadelphia. One of the largest WPA projects in Pennsylvania was the construction of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. It connected the eastern and western parts of the state. The Pennsylvania Turnpike changed travel throughout the state. It received the name “America’s First Superhighway.”

The WPA also funded archeological digs to preserve the history of Pennsylvania. WPA archeologists conducted excavations in Somerset County, Pennsylvania during the Great Depression. They uncovered the remains of several indigenous villages in the county. Artists in Pennsylvania painted murals in government buildings, schools, and post offices across the state. Some of the murals depicted important moments in Pennsylvania’s history. Others depicted economic activities in the state. Writers wrote guidebooks about the state. They conducted interviews with members of different communities to record the history of Pennsylvania.

The Public Works Administration (PWA) also had a large impact on Pennsylvania and its people. PWA funds were used to construct new government facilities in Harrisburg. The construction included the Finance Building and the Northwest Office Building of the state capitol. The program also provided funds to improve the Pittsburgh & West Virginia Railway. PWA funds were also used to build 12 military armories around the state. Multiple schools and university buildings were also constructed. They used loans and grants for the PWA. Over $1,000,000 in funds were given to Pennsylvania State University by the PWA. The funds were used to construct new academic buildings.

The Federal Emergency Relief Administration (FERA) and National Youth Association (NYA) also helped thousands of people in Pennsylvania. The NYA and FERA awarded scholarships to Pennsylvania students to attend college. These programs provided funds to colleges and universities for student jobs and work programs. Multiple projects were completed in Canonsburg because of the FERA funds.

title: Needs
text:
A need is something that you have to have. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us warm or cool.

Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler to help you be successful each day.

title: Wants
text: A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. A want is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

title: Needs or Wants?
text: Which items are needs? Which items are wants? Make a T-chart and list the needs and wants.

title: Meeting Our Needs and Wants
text:
How do we get the things we need and want? In the past, many people worked the land to meet most of their needs. They grew their own food. They also built their own homes and made their own clothes. That took a lot of time. There wasn’t as much time for the things people wanted.

Today, we don’t usually make or grow everything ourselves. We get a job to make money and buy the things we need. People can choose from many jobs to meet their needs. Some people grow food. Other people make clothes. Builders make our homes. There are many different ways we can work to meet our needs. Working together in communities helps us get more of the things we need and want.

People use money they earn to buy the things they need and want. The amount of money people earn affects the choices they make. The more money you make, the more opportunity you have to meet your wants and needs. A person with very little money has to decide what things are most important. For example, a person may have to decide if they should buy food for the week or repair a car.

Sometimes, people face challenges when trying to meet their needs and wants. If someone loses their job, they may not have enough money to spend on wants. Basic human needs, such as food, water, shelter, and clothing, become more important. Resources can become scarce in times of war or natural disaster. This means they will not be easily available. It can be difficult for people to meet their basic needs. In difficult times, communities often come together to share resources and help each other.

title: Choosing Between Wants and Needs
text:
Everyone must make decisions about needs and wants every day. Our basic needs should always come first. They are the most important things we spend money on. We can start taking care of our wants after our needs are met. When you make a decision, you have to think carefully about the consequences of your choices. For example, you can’t eat only candy and still be healthy. If you buy too many summer clothes, you might not have enough for the winter clothes you need. By weighing our needs against our wants, we make better choices.

Many people create a budget to keep track of their money. A budget is a plan for how to spend money. When making responsible decisions, families first pay for everything they need. Then, they can use what’s left over to buy things they want. We must plan and choose wisely so all of our needs are taken care of. After that, we can take care of our wants.

title: What Is Agriculture?
text:
Agriculture is the farming and harvesting of resources. The term is broad and refers to many things. It is farming crops by preparing the soil, sowing, fertilizing, irrigating, and harvesting all types of plants. However, it is also raising animals, fishing, and forestry. It even includes services that support agricultural production, like equipment repair and transportation.

Agriculture is important to our lives for many reasons. Agriculture provides the food we need to survive. It also provides jobs for people. Agriculture produces and harvests raw natural resources that are used to produce other products. Our economy grows stronger through resources and products that can be traded with other states and countries.

title: History of Agriculture in Ohio
text:
The first farmers in the Ohio area were ancient American Indians. They planted corn, squash, beans, and pumpkins. They also harvested wild cherries, berries, plums, and pawpaw. Native Tribes also grew sweet potatoes, onions, yams, and cabbage during the 1600s. People still use some of their farming methods today.

European settlers planted many grains and raised livestock. However, it was after the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad opened that they began real trade. That was in 1830. Two years later, the Ohio and Erie Canal was also completed. When John Deere’s steel plow was invented in 1837, it made farming a little easier. Ohio farmers sold a record amount of corn and wheat in 1849.

Farming in Ohio has continued to change since 1849. Food processing has become big business in Ohio. Many jobs in Ohio today are related to agriculture. Many people are growing crops and raising animals. Others are doing research to improve crop and animal health. Some are working on finding better ways to transport fresh produce.

title: Physical Characteristics That Influence Agriculture
text:
Ohio’s physical characteristics make it a good place for agriculture.

Land and soil

Ohio has plains and plateau areas. Soils in the plains areas were mainly created by glaciers. The glaciers flattened the land. They also created rich soils that are very fertile. Soils in the Ohio plains have a lot of nutrients and are great for farming. Some of the plateau areas are much more rocky and are not as good for farming. The northern parts of the plateau are glaciated. This means the glacier that flattened the land in the plains smoothed the land in the plateau region. The area isn’t as flat as the plains, but it has rich soils and is used for agriculture.

Climate

Ohio experiences four seasons. The average temperature in January is 32 degrees Fahrenheit. In July the average is 75 degrees Fahrenheit. The temperatures vary a lot depending on the elevation, or how high the land is. Land that is further north is colder and often receives more snow in the winter. The average precipitation (rain and snow combined) for the year is between 30 and 40 inches.

title: Types of Agriculture in Ohio
text:
Ohio is one of the leading states in agriculture. Ohio farmers grow many crops. These are sold around the country and the world. State records show that Ohio had almost 77,000 farms in 2022.

Some of the most important crops include soybeans, corn, pumpkins, and cabbage. Others are strawberries, apples, grapes, oats, and wheat. Another important crop is hay. It is grown to feed animals.

Ohio farmers also raise a lot of livestock. Livestock are animals that provide eggs, milk, and meat. Cows, goats, sheep, hogs, chickens, and turkeys are all raised on Ohio farms.

Ohio is the fifth largest producer of flowers and plants in the United States. People often buy these for their gardens and homes.

title: Be Kind on the Internet
text: Digital character is the way you conduct yourself when you are online. It is your behavior and the words you use. Everything you say, do, or send online is always accessible online, even if it has been deleted. This is your digital footprint. Because you are not face-to-face when communicating digitally, it is important to be respectful and kind. You should not say or do things online that you would not say or do in person. You may see people who do not choose to be kind or respectful. You can be resilient. You can choose how you respond. You can demonstrate positive digital citizenship, and you can choose to create a positive digital footprint for yourself.

title: Stay Safe on the Internet
text: The internet is a place where anyone can post anything. It is important to have a plan for what to do if you find something that makes you uncomfortable. If someone asks you to do or say something you are uncomfortable with, you should get help right away. If something makes you uncomfortable, there are things you can do immediately. You can turn off the computer. You can block the sender and report the content. When you encounter problems online, it is important to tell an adult and to ask for help immediately. Don't wait.

title: Essential Question
text: How do needs and wants help me make choices?

title: Let’s Talk About Fear
text: Fear is an emotion people feel when they become aware of danger or when they anticipate something bad happening. Fear is like your body's alarm system for danger. When you experience fear, it is your brain sending signals to the rest of your body to start preparing to respond to something threatening. Usually, fear serves as a helpful emotion because it protects you from danger. Someone afraid of getting burned will be careful around an open fire. Someone afraid of getting stung by bees will be careful around a beehive.

title: You Don’t Have to Be Afraid of Fear
text:
Another helpful way to overcome fear is to use coping strategies. Coping strategies are helpful or useful ways to deal with fear. Coping strategies are skills that involve action in dealing with an uncomfortable feeling, like fear.

Add your ideas to this list of coping strategies you can use to help you when you feel fear:

Name, reject, and reframe your fears.

Exercise.

Make a list of things you are grateful for.

Use your energy to create something positive.

title: The Unknown
text:
Fear of the unknown is a fear of things you don't know yet. When you don't know about something, it is difficult to know how to respond. Sometimes, not having information creates a sense of anxiety for people. Anxiety is when a person has extremely unpleasant feelings associated with stress. Often when people experience fear of the unknown, it is because they are missing important information. Knowing there is missing information can make a person feel stressed.

One way to overcome fear of the unknown is by asking yourself, "Why am I feeling scared?" You can reflect on your answer. Think about what is needed for you to feel less scared. You can use your inquiry skills to ask questions and gather more information.

title: Getting Started
text: Fear can keep you from achieving your goals, especially if you are afraid to get started. Sometimes people are scared of getting started because they are not sure where to begin, or they are afraid they will make mistakes. When setting goals or getting started on something, you can make a plan. Make a list of the things you need. This will help you know where to start. Having a plan helps you break down your task into smaller parts. Smaller tasks can make the task easier to approach and easier to get started. Making mistakes is a normal part of learning and development. Mistakes help you make progress and learn.

title: What is a Fear of Success?
text:
Some people feel fear about what will happen after they succeed. Sometimes people feel like they don't deserve success. However, it is good to set goals and work hard to accomplish them. Some people might feel guilty that they are succeeding while others are struggling. Other people might not try something because they are afraid of failure. Can you relate to any of these feelings? If so, you may be experiencing a fear of success.

These ideas can help you overcome a fear of succeeding:

Believe in yourself.

Be resilient (try over and over and over again).

Be willing to make mistakes.

Have a growth mindset.

Celebrate small successes along the way.

Take time to plan your next goal, adventure, or challenge.

title: Thinking with a Growth Mindset
text:
A growth mindset is a way of thinking and talking to yourself that helps you accept growth and change. This helps you learn new things, grow, and develop appropriately. Having a growth mindset is being able to look at challenges as stepping stones to your development.

Can you think of a time when something was difficult, like playing a sport or learning a new skill? Maybe something made you want to give up, but then you did it. That is a perfect example of a growth mindset. It's not giving up. It's finding ways to become stronger. It's looking for solutions to solve your problems.

The more you use a growth mindset, the stronger your brain will be at learning new skills and remembering how to perform them.

title: Thinking with a Fixed Mindset
text:
It is important to understand the difference between a growth mindset and a fixed mindset. This helps us develop our growth mindset. When people think with a fixed mindset, they might believe that intelligence and talent cannot be changed. They may believe they never will be good at something if they aren't good at it now.

Imagine a rock. If you plant the rock in the ground and water it, it will not be able to grow. The rock will always be a rock and does not change.

You might be experiencing a fixed mindset if you find yourself thinking things like:

I am not good at this.

I am not smart.

I’ll never do this.

Often, fearing failure and avoiding new challenges are evidence, or signs, of having a fixed mindset. Pay attention to your thinking and see if you think with a growth or a fixed mindset.

title: Failing Is Growing!
text: People don’t usually like to make mistakes. Did you know that failure can actually help you? Remember, making mistakes and failing are normal parts of development. Failure helps us learn and grow. Making mistakes can be frustrating, but you can learn from your mistakes and make corrections. Using a growth mindset can help you when you encounter mistakes and failures. Instead of thinking about failures as defining you, you can use them to make corrections in your thinking or behavior and improve.

title: Change Your Words
text:
Sometimes, people say negative things about themselves when they feel frustrated. Has this ever happened to you? Your brain will start believing what you think and say, so it is important to pay close attention to your thoughts. If you tell yourself that you are not good at something or that you can't learn something, your brain will believe you. This can slow down your ability to learn new skills. Your thinking is very powerful. One thing you can do to help overcome this type of fixed thinking is to add the word "yet" to your thoughts.

If you notice thoughts like:

"I can't do this."

"I am not good at this."

"This isn't easy."

Try adding one simple word to your thoughts: "yet."

"I can't do this, yet!"

"I am not good at this, yet!'

"This isn’t easy, yet!"

Changing one small part of the way you think and talk about learning new skills, like adding the word "yet," helps you gain confidence and shift your thinking to a growth mindset.

title: A Growth Mindset Helps Your Well-Being
text:
Your well-being is impacted by your efforts to develop a growth mindset. The more you are open to changing the way you think, the more you will improve your well-being.

Impact to Physical Well-Being

A growth mindset helps you focus on your efforts and practices. It helps you learn new skills. Some examples are running, playing an athletic game, painting a picture, or playing the piano.

Impact to Mental Well-Being

A growth mindset helps you think about learning in a different way. When you change your thinking, you increase your capacity. This means increasing the amount of things you can learn.

Impact to Social Well-Being

A growth mindset helps your social well-being. You are able to recognize that mistakes and disagreements are a normal part of friendships and relationships. A growth mindset helps you work through mistakes and disagreements.

Impact to Academic Well-Being

A growth mindset improves your academic well-being. It allows you to focus on new concepts and opportunities at school, not on your failures or bad grades.

Impact to Emotional Well-Being

A growth mindset can help you identify, label, and communicate your emotions. Remember to be patient and have empathy with others' emotions. This helps you to be more forgiving with yourself and your emotions.

title: Learning Through Stress
text:
Feeling some stress is a normal part of life. It is how your body and mind can let you know that you need to take action. If you know how to manage it, stress can even be good for your well-being. Managing your stress can develop your resilience. It can strengthen your ability to overcome difficult things.

Dr. Daniela Kaufer studies how stress affects the brain. “Some amounts of stress are good to push you just to the level of optimal alertness, behavioral and cognitive performance,” she says. In other words, a little bit of stress can help you pay attention, act wisely, and think clearly.

When you think of stress as something helpful, it can change from an overwhelming feeling into an opportunity to learn and grow.

title: Analyze Your Stress
text:
Every feeling can teach us something. Positive feelings can help us feel safe and motivate us to have good habits. Negative feelings can warn us about danger or let us know when our choices are not helpful. Together, positive and negative feelings help us navigate our lives.

Stress can be a positive feeling when we use it as fuel to do our best. It can be a negative feeling if we don’t know where it’s coming from or what to do with it. Like other feelings, stress can be a signal to act, but it might also mean that you need to take some time to think and reflect. You can press pause, take a breath, and examine your feelings. Then you can decide how you want to respond to the stress you are feeling. Taking time to study your feelings will help you turn stress into something positive.

When you feel stress, ask yourself the following questions:

Is this good stress? Is this pressure?

What opportunities can this stress create?

How will I respond to this stress?

What do I want the outcome of this stress to be?

title: Identify Sources of Stress
text:
If you’re trying to play basketball and the ball keeps getting flat, you have to fix it before you can play. And you won’t know how to fix it until you find the source of the leak — the place where the trouble started. The same idea applies to stress: you need to find the source. Identifying the cause of your stress can help you decide what to do so you can keep playing.

The following questions may help you find the source of your stress. Ask yourself:

Is there a certain time of day that I feel stressed?

title: Stress Management
text: When stress feels overwhelming, there are things you can do to manage and self-regulate. Stress management is all about knowing what to do with the stress you feel. Because everyone is unique, there’s no perfect recipe for how to manage stress. Strategies that work for one person might not work for you. Don’t give up. Keep testing strategies, and you will find the ones that work best for you. If you need help, ask someone you trust for suggestions. Learning how to manage stress positively is worth every moment of effort.

title: Where Do Anxious Feelings Come From?
text:
You can’t see the future, but sometimes your feelings think they can. Anxiety is when you feel afraid or worried about something that might happen. Sometimes it’s clear where anxiety comes from. Other times, you might feel scared without knowing why. Processing (working through) your anxiety can help you tame your feelings of fear, both in the present and the future.

When you process your anxiety about something, your brain learns to produce less of the hormones that cause anxiety in that situation. Your brain learns to trust your ability to handle it. Ask yourself: What am I afraid will happen? For example, if you have an upcoming performance, you might be afraid of making a mistake and feeling embarrassed. Now ask: What can help? Practicing before the performance will make it less likely that you’ll make a mistake. So, practicing can help you feel less anxious. After the show’s over and your worst fears didn’t come true, you can feel less anxious the next time you perform. You handled it!

title: Symptoms of Anxiety
text:
Our bodies have developed an automatic response to help us survive dangerous situations. It’s called the fight-or-flight response. When you feel fear, your body releases stress hormones, which are natural chemicals that give you a burst of energy. Your body uses these chemicals to prepare to either fight or run away.

When you feel anxiety, your body might still automatically switch into fight-or-flight mode, even though what you’re afraid of hasn’t happened yet. Here are some things you might feel when you’re anxious—and why your body thinks you need it.

Sweaty hands: Stress hormones are pumping through you.

Pounding heart: Your muscles and brain need more blood to act quickly.

Stomachache: Your digestion slows to save energy.

Tense muscles: Your body is getting ready to fight or run.

Fast breathing: Your muscles need more oxygen.

Headache: Your brain needs more blood so you can think fast.

title: A Natural Part of Life
text: Feeling anxious sometimes is normal. It’s a natural response from your brain—specifically, the amygdala, a part of your brain that handles emotions. When the amygdala senses danger, it tells your body to release stress hormones. There are three major stress hormones. Adrenaline gives you a burst of energy. Norepinephrine is similar to adrenaline and acts as a backup. Cortisol is a slower-acting hormone that stays in your system longer. These can be helpful if you open your front door and there’s a bear on your porch. The problem is that sometimes your brain can’t tell the difference between a bear on your porch and your first day at a new school. Sometimes we have to help our brains understand that we aren’t in any real danger.

title: Mindfulness Reduces Anxiety
text:
One of the best ways to manage your anxiety is to focus on what is happening in the present instead of imagining what might happen in the future.

Try the following exercise to bring yourself into the present moment:

Close your eyes.

Breathe deeply. Focus on the air moving in and out of your body.

Focus on one or two sounds that you hear.

Notice what it smells like where you are now.

Notice what the chair you are sitting on feels like.

Notice what your feet feel like in your shoes.

Focus on what you feel with your fingertips.

Notice other things you can feel, smell, taste, and hear.

Focus on your breathing. Feel your lungs fill up with oxygen and release it.

Pay attention to your heart rate as it slows to normal speed.

Keep breathing.

Repeat this exercise whenever you need to remind yourself to stay in the present instead of worrying about the future.

title: Make a Plan
text:
Strategies are careful, well-developed plans to help you do something.

Here are a few ideas you can use to create your own strategy for managing anxiety:

Talk to a trusted adult.

Write down at least five things you are grateful for.

Get enough sleep.

Talk to your teacher about school-related fears.

Get plenty of exercise.

Practice skills to build your confidence.

Write in a journal.

Write a letter about your anxieties. Then, reply to it with kindness and advice, as if it were written by your best friend.

Create a list of coping ideas that work for you. Put it somewhere you can access when you are feeling anxious. Remember, practice makes habits. Practicing positive coping strategies for anxiety will help you get better at decreasing your anxiety quickly.

Anxiety can be difficult to overcome alone. It’s okay to ask for help. Use assertive communication with a trusted adult if you feel worried all the time and none of your strategies seem to help.

title: Solutions for Anxiety
text:
If your strategies aren't working and you feel like anxiety is starting to overwhelm you, try one of these techniques:

Separate the facts from your fears.

Put your worries away.

Write a list of worries and rip it up.

title: Getting Things Done with Motivation and Discipline
text: Motivation is the feeling of wanting to do something. Motivation is based on your emotions. Sometimes, it can be very hard to feel motivated to finish a task, simply because our emotions try to pull us in a different direction, like toward something that seems easier or more fun. That is when your personal discipline takes over! Discipline is the ability to focus and get things done, even when you don’t feel motivated.

title: You Can Persevere!
text:
Discipline can get you started on a task, but when that task gets difficult or frustrating, perseverance can help you keep going until you reach the finish line. Perseverance is a lot like resilience and grit. It helps you keep bouncing back instead of giving up.

Finding a source of motivation can help you persevere. You can find intrinsic motivation by finding something you love in the task. You can find extrinsic motivation by working toward a deadline or a goal. What helps you work hard and keep going?

title: You Have Abilities
text: When you have an ability, it means you have the skill to do something. For example, you may have the ability to speak, smile, write, sing, or give a high-five. Abilities can be things you can do without needing to think about it, or they may be something that you have to work hard to do. There may be abilities that you aren’t able to learn, because we are all unique. Not everyone has the same abilities. That diversity helps us all learn from each other! Use your motivation, discipline, and perseverance to focus on your unique abilities. What are some abilities you have gained this year?

title: You Have Talents and Strengths
text:
A talent is an ability that a person is naturally good at. When someone works hard and practices a talent, they can turn it into a strength, which means they can do it well over and over again. For example, a talent is being able to learn a new language quickly. A strength is being able to have long conversations in that language with new people.

Talents and strengths can be physical, mental, emotional, or even social. Find out what your talents are and then use motivation, discipline, and perseverance to turn them into strengths!

Born in Central Bridge, New York, in 1846, George Westinghouse became fascinated with technology at an early age. After serving in the Civil War, he moved to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in 1867. There, Westinghouse launched his career as an inventor. He received a patent for inventing a brake system for trains to use. Before Westinghouse's air brake, each car in a train had to have its own brakeman to apply the brakes at the same time. This caused many accidents. Westinghouse created a system using pressurized air to apply brakes at the same time in each car. His air brake enabled trains to stop with accuracy. This air brake was quickly bought by every railroad. In 1884, George Westinghouse started the Westinghouse Electric Company. Its focus was to improve the system that delivered electricity. He partnered with Nikola Tesla in creating alternating current. This is the delivery used today for electricity.

Westinghouse continued looking for innovations, including in communication. Telephone and radio were being used as communication methods. At the time, telephones were connected by a system of wires. Radio was wireless. Westinghouse took a chance on radio. Radio waves could be sent out from a station to be received by anyone with a radio receiver. So, Westinghouse started building receivers. He then created the first commercial radio station in the world. KDKA began broadcasting in October, 1920.

KDKA played music, broadcasted sports, weather forecasts and advertisements. The success of KDKA encouraged other companies to invest in radio. By 1921, eight radio stations were operating across the United States. Today there are over 15,445 radio stations in the United States. Westinghouse's efforts to innovate opened new avenues of communication and success for others.

title: Spending, Saving, and Investing
text:
When you earn money, you have the choice to save or spend your income. People should spend part of their income on goods and services to meet their basic needs. These include housing, electricity, food, water, clothing, transportation, and medical necessities. After paying for your weekly, monthly, or yearly needs, you must decide what to do with your remaining income. You can spend it on things you want or save it for the future. Many people spend too much income on their wants. This may not leave enough money to pay for things they need.

Saving money is very important. People save money to buy things in the future. Many families save money to buy a car or a house. Some families save money for a vacation. The more something costs, the more money you have to save. People can save money in many ways. You can place your money into a savings account at a bank. You can also compare prices on items you buy and use coupons to save on your purchases. It's important to make good choices with your money to plan for your future.

Most people try to save part of their income. If people invest some of the money they've saved, they can earn even more money for emergencies or later use. To make an investment means to purchase something with the hope that it will make more money in the future. People can invest in businesses, raw materials, goods, and services to earn additional funds.

When someone invests money, they usually buy an asset, like stock in a company. If that company does well, the stock is worth more. The more money someone puts into stocks, the more money can grow. Stocks can be a little risky. If the business fails, the stocks are lost. It is important to research and choose stocks that will grow. Over time, many businesses do well. People who invest can earn a lot of money.

title: Investing
text:
If there was a way to buy something now and sell it later for more money in the future, would you do it? That is the whole idea behind investing. Some people take money that they have saved and invest it in something like property or a business. The idea of investing your money is the expectation that the value of what you’ve invested in will grow in the future.

A house or property is a good example of an investment that many people make. When someone buys a house, they often take out a loan from a bank for the price of the house. When that person sells their house in the future, they take the money that they earned on the sale and pay off their loan. If they sold the house for more than the cost of the loan, the money left after paying off the loan is income for them. Another way that people invest their money is by buying stock, or a small part of a company. If the company makes a profit because the goods or services they provide are popular, then the stockholders share in the profits.

Investing money does come with risks. There is no guarantee that what you invest in will increase in value. While there are great rewards for investing, it is possible that your investment will lose value. When making decisions about investments, people consider the risks and rewards of what they’re investing in. If the risks of making the investment are greater than the rewards, then it might not be a wise investment. Just like with any decision you make, you need to rely on good sources of information to make a wise decision.

title: Equator and Latitude
text:
We divide up the world for mapping purposes. Imagine a horizontal line that runs around the middle of the world. Cartographers draw this imaginary line on many of the maps they make. They call this line the Equator. The Equator divides the Earth into hemispheres. A hemisphere is a division on Earth between north and south or east and west.

The Northern Hemisphere includes all of the land and oceans that are north of the Equator. The Southern Hemisphere includes everything to the south. The Equator crosses parts of South America, Asia, and Africa. Horizontal lines of latitude run east and west around the Earth. These lines show how far from the Equator places are. We call these latitude lines parallels.

title: Other Important Lines
text:
Absolute location uses latitude and longitude lines to pinpoint where something is located exactly on the Earth’s surface. Longitude lines, or meridians, measure the Earth's rotation in degrees. Each degree, or longitude line, is divided into 60 minutes, and each of those minutes is divided into 60 seconds. This creates the different time zones that we use. The Earth is divided into 24 different time zones. The reason for this division is because the Earth rotates on its axis once a day. The starting point for these time zones is the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, London, also called Greenwich Mean Time. All locations on the Earth are measured according to their position east or west of this line.

Larger countries have many time zones. The United States has six time zones. It would be difficult for smaller countries to have different time zones. In order to make things easier, time zone boundaries often follow political boundaries instead of the straight longitude lines.

The International Date Line is another imaginary line drawn on a map of Earth's surface to show the boundary between one day and the next. The International Date Line is located halfway around the world from the Prime Meridian. It isn’t straight because it follows political boundary lines.

title: Prime Meridian and Longitude
text: Cartographers draw lines on a map from the North Pole to the South Pole. This helps us be more specific in our mapping. One of these lines, the Prime Meridian, divides the world in half vertically. These halves are called the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere. The vertical lines of longitude that go from the North Pole to the South Pole show how far east or west places are from the Prime Meridian. We call these lines meridians. There are 24 meridians that divide up the Earth and represent the 24 hours that it takes for the Earth to rotate. The Prime Meridian helps to create an international standard of time. So when your friend says, “Let’s go to the movie at six o’clock,” you both know exactly what time that is.

title: The Skill of Asking For Help
text: Asking for help is a critical skill to learn. Everyone needs help to accomplish their tasks. Asking for help when you need it takes courage. It may be hard at first, but with practice, it gets easier. Appropriately asking for help connects you to your peer groups and social circles. It is part of learning. It does not mean that you aren’t smart or capable. Asking for help means you are being resourceful and working out your questions and problems in order to progress and improve your overall well-being.

title: Afraid to Get Help?
text:
Some problems are really big. They take a lot of people to help solve. Some problems are smaller and can be solved by one or two people. Fear can stop you from learning and growing. This happens especially if you know you need help but are afraid to ask someone to help you. You can overcome the fear of asking for help by using coping strategies.

Don't let fear stop you!

title: You Can Help Too!
text:
When other people ask you for help, how should you respond? As you think about your response, you should consider:

Is your response something that you would want to hear when you need help?

Is your response helpful?

What resources do you have to help?

Do you know how to help?

Do you have skills and abilities that will help?

What time limitations do you have?

What other responsibilities do you need to fulfill?

Your responses can vary. Don't be afraid to tell someone that you don't know how to help or that you don't have the answer. Trying to help without the proper tools can be dangerous, but helping others shows them that you care about them. Sometimes the best way to help someone is to direct them to a person who has the tools to help. Anytime you help others directly or refer them to someone with the right tools, it builds your empathy muscles and your well-being by opening your mind to what others are going through.

title: Coal In Pennsylvania
text:
In Pennsylvania, the Appalachian Mountains are called the Allegheny Mountains. Coal formed in the Appalachians over 300 million years ago. Plants in a wet marsh were subjected to heat and pressure as the mountains formed. This process created a combination of carbon and other materials in a hard, rock-like matter called coal. Coal comes in two hardness qualities: bituminous and anthracite. Both types of coal create heat when they are burned. Burning coal creates a tar, which is a thick, sticky substance.

Anthracite is only found in the northeastern region of Pennsylvania. This natural resource is buried deep inside the mountains. Anthracite, or hard coal, burns at very high temperatures and is excellent for manufacturing iron and steel. Mining companies gain the right to access coal from the land owner. To reach the coal, workers have to create a shaft or tunnel through the earth. The mining company has employees mine, or dig the coal from underground. Anthracite coal requires specific tools and equipment to mine and bring to the surface. The coal is then sorted by size and quality. The sorted coal is then transported to consumers, who use the coal to create heat and energy.

Another way of mining coal is by stripping the layers of earth off the coal layer. This is called strip mining, or surface mining. Large, earth-moving equipment reveals and mines the coal. Surface mining is done in the Allegheny Plateau region of Pennsylvania. The type of coal found here is bituminous, or soft coal. Bituminous coal doesn’t create as high a heat as the anthracite coal does when it is burned. The bituminous coal requires specific tools and equipment to mine.

Mining coal from Pennsylvania is a business. A business must have natural, human, and capital resources to bring goods to consumers. In the production of coal, coal is the natural resource. The coal is the good brought to consumers. Human resources are the people who do the work. Human resources bring the natural resource to consumers. To access the natural resource, the human resources must have tools, equipment, and clothing. Tools, equipment, and clothing are the capital resources. Natural, human, and capital resources are required for every business that brings goods to consumers.

Mining coal can have environmental consequences that must be addressed. For a long time, these consequences were ignored. Today, there are many regulations and laws to minimize the environmental consequences. The consequences to the health of the human resources are also considered and regulated in the 21st century.

title: Benefits of Sleep
text:
Your brain works hard all day, learning, making decisions, and processing information. When you sleep, your brain gets a break. Sleep also gives your brain a chance to organize and store information so you have room to learn new things.

Sleep is important for your body, too. When you’re resting, your body uses its energy to heal and grow. Sleep also gives your body a chance to fight off germs that can make you sick.

title: Food Is Fuel
text:
When you’re hungry, it’s hard to get anything done. Your body needs the nutrients and energy from food and water to move. Your brain needs food to focus and learn.

There are lots of different food options, but some give us more energy than others. It’s important to choose foods that provide the most energy and leave you feeling great and ready to conquer the day!

title: The Coal Town
text:
Early in the history of mining in Pennsylvania, towns were created at each mine. The mining company created the town by the mine. A network of railroads connected each mine to other mining towns.

Rows of identical cheap and unfinished houses were built. There could be 300–500 houses or more in a town. The town would be centered around the railroad tracks. One side of the tracks would be for English-speaking workers, managers, and company officials. On the other side of the tracks were neighborhoods of immigrants who spoke similar languages.

Conditions in the Town

There were no elected officials in the town. The owner of the coal company was the authority of the town. The coal company provided security with their own company police department. This also meant that the coal company could create its own set of rules and laws. Enforcement for consequences of breaking the rules and laws was also up to the company authorities.

A water well would be dug for families to use. Eventually, cold water was piped into the company houses that families rented. The company also created a general store of merchandise, or goods the families would need. The company would set the prices for goods. The mining company provided a doctor, church, and school. Everything in the town was provided by the coal company. However, the services were not free to the workers. The coal company charged the workers for everything that was provided to them.

The process of coal mining creates a black dust in the air. This black dust is fine particles of coal. The dust got on the coal miners' clothing, face, and hands. The miners inhaled the dust with each breath they took. A miner would end the work shift and emerge from the mine as dark and black as the coal itself. Homes were heated with coal and wood. The smell of coal burning is bitter and sickening in large quantities. The soot from burning the coal settled on everything inside and outside the homes. Keeping things clean took great effort from the families.

Pay for the Workers
Workers would work for one dollar a day, six days a week. Sundays were a day off. On payday, the workers would go to the coal office or to the company store. They received wages in scrip, or substitute for money. The rent for their homes was deducted, or subtracted from the miners' wages. This usually amounted to two days' wages. The remaining scrip was used at the company store to get groceries and other necessities for the families. Often, the debt at the store was more than the wages. This would keep miners continually in debt to the company. This would keep the workers continually having to keep working to pay the debt. A worker could not leave the mines without paying the debt in full.

Carl Sandburg, an American writer and poet, said, “You live in a company house. You go to a company school. You work for this company according to the company rules. You drink company water and all use company lights. The company preacher teaches us what the company thinks is right.”

When conditions for working and living offer little or no success for the workers, conflict increases. As company officials compromised and created better living conditions, conflict decreased.

title: Getting Strong Through Movement
text:
A stronger heart and stronger lungs, muscles, and bones are just a few benefits of exercising. Moving your body can also help you feel energized and happy!

There are lots of different ways to get your body moving. You can play team sports like basketball or soccer. If that’s not your style, turn on some music and dance, or ride your bike around your neighborhood. Invent games with your friends that get your heart pumping. Try lots of different activities. Remember, you don’t have to be the best at something to benefit from it!

title: Treat Your Body with Kindness
text:
When our bodies don’t perform perfectly or meet our exact expectations, our minds may say very unkind things about them. Instead of dwelling on unkind thoughts, focus on your strengths and goals.

It’s important to speak and think kindly about others, too. Every body is unique, and there isn’t one feature or characteristic that is better than another. Each body is worthy of love, care, and respect.

title: Conflict in the Mines
text:
Carbon, Lackawanna, Luzerne, Northumberland, and Schuylkill Counties are the center of anthracite coal mining. In the 1800s, living conditions in the mining towns were difficult for coal mine workers. Sometimes people in authority abused employees. Different coal companies had different rules about equipment. Some companies required the workers to provide their own shovels, picks, and lamps. All this equipment could be bought at the company store. The company set the price for the equipment.

Over the years, many workers tried to organize for better labor conditions. Their differences in languages, cultures, and conditions kept the organization from being widespread. Managers also created competition between the groups to cause conflict.

Managers did not respond to requests from the workers. The conflict increased. Mine bosses and other management personnel were physically attacked and their lives endangered.

In the summer of 1876, violence resulted in the deaths of coal bosses. Some mine workers were arrested and tried for murder.

A trial was held in the Schuylkill County courthouse. Prosecutors brought evidence against the group of workers who had been arrested. The workers were all from Ireland. Prosecutors accused the group of forming a secret society called the Molly Maguires. They accused the group of using violence to protect miners. No one provided evidence of such an organization. Still, 20 individuals were convicted of violence against coal company authorities. Their common link was that they were all Irish immigrants in the same social circles.

After the convictions of the Irish miners, violence in the mines lessened. However, suspicion of immigrants and miners continued for a long period of time.

title: Coke Ovens
text:
Coal became an important source of fuel in manufacturing. People discovered a use for coal in turning iron ore into steel. Baking coal in an oven at temperatures as high as 2,000° Fahrenheit caused the coal water, gas, and tar to separate. This left behind a hard, gray substance. This substance is coke, an industrial fuel that burns hotter and longer than coal, all without smoke. This process is done in a coke oven, a chamber in which coal burns hot enough to produce coke. Traditionally, people made coke ovens out of brick. These ovens were round and shaped like beehives. They were 12 feet wide and 5–7 feet tall.

For decades, over half the nation’s supply of coke came from Pennsylvania. It was a narrow strip of land running through Westmoreland and Fayette counties. The coal there supplied 38,000 coke ovens in the Connellsville district. Every day, 2,000 rail cars hauled the coke away. In the early 1900s, people saw that the beehive coke ovens were not good for the environment. The ovens released a toxic gas while the coke cooked. This gas destroyed the land. By 1920, manufacturers started using byproduct ovens. These were rectangular. The fronts and backs of the ovens were removable, and the toxic byproducts could be pumped out. Manufacturers built these byproduct ovens in more convenient riverside sites, like Pittsburgh. They abandoned the old beehive coke ovens. You can still find the remains of these ovens throughout southwestern Pennsylvania.

title: Hazards in the Mines
text:
Mining is a dangerous operation. Tunnels are deep in the earth. The ceilings of tunnels can collapse from the weight above them. Workers used timbers to frame the tunnels and give them support. However, sometimes timbers broke and tunnels collapsed. This is why different exits to the mining tunnels had to be built. Today, the frames for mining tunnels are steel.

A great hazard for coal mines is fire. Coal easily burns. A layer of coal can become fuel for fire. This is what happened in Centralia, Pennsylvania. In 1962, trash was being burned in a surface mine abandoned in the 1930s. The trash fire spread to a nearby active mine opening. The entire mine started to burn. Many attempts were made to extinguish, or put out the fire. Over the next 50 years, the U.S. government bought nearby homes and businesses to relocate the people to safe areas. The Centralia fire is still burning today, but under constant surveillance of the Department of Environmental Protection.

Miners are exposed to coal dust as they dig the coal from the earth. It wasn't until modern times that miners started wearing masks to protect themselves. Thousands of miners worked the mines and breathed the coal dust into their lungs. Over long exposure, their lungs become damaged, and breathing becomes difficult. In 1969, the federal government passed the Coal Mine Health and Safety Act. This act gave funds to help miners and their families with healthcare expenses. It also required inspections of all mines for safety. Health standards were adopted and enforced. The act led to safety regulations being adopted for all industries in the United States.

title: The Meaning of Mindfulness
text: Mindfulness means you are focusing your attention on your current thoughts, emotions, and bodily sensations. Being mindful can help you focus on the present instead of getting lost in worries about the past or future. Just like any activity, mindfulness gets easier with practice. As you practice, you form new neural pathways — paths that signals travel along in your brain. The more you practice, the stronger and deeper those pathways become. That means that the more you practice staying in the moment, the better at it your brain will become!

title: Focusing on the NOW
text: When you feel anxious and overwhelmed, those feelings usually come from one of two places: the past or the future. You might be worried about something that has happened, which means your mind is stuck in the past. Or, you might be worrying about something you’re afraid will happen, which means your mind has zoomed ahead to the future. But you can’t change the past, and you can’t control other people’s choices in the future. Worrying about things that have happened or might happen can be paralyzing, which means feeling like you're frozen and can't do anything to help yourself. Practicing mindfulness is all about focusing your attention and energy on what is happening in the present. It pulls you out of the past or the future.

title: Mindfulness Really Matters!
text: Does mindfulness really work? Is it worth taking the time to practice? The short answer is: YES! Many benefits come from practicing mindfulness. Mindfulness improves your overall well-being, but it also helps your physical well-being. Scientists have learned that practicing mindfulness helps you relieve stress and improves your sleep. It also improves your heart's ability to work correctly. As if that’s not enough, being mindful can also help you do better in school and will help you manage stress and anxiety even better in the future.

title: Practicing Mindfulness
text:
Mindful Breathing: Place your hand over your belly. As you breathe, pay attention to your hand and your breath. Feel your hand rise and fall with each breath.

Visualization: When you visualize activities, your brain doesn't know that it’s all in your head. Start by choosing a skill you want to improve. Close your eyes and imagine yourself performing the skill. Try to picture every part of it. In your mind, watch yourself perform the skill perfectly over and over.

Full body scan: Starting at your toes, notice how each body part feels as you scan upward toward your head. Is it tense? Relaxed? Hot? Cold? There’s no right or wrong answer. Just pay attention to what you are feeling in the moment.

Relaxation: Find a comfortable place to sit where you can be free of distractions. Breathe slowly and steadily. Relax your muscles in your face and neck. Then, relax your shoulders. Work all the way down to your toes.

title: Think Yourself to Success
text:
Self-fulfilling prophecy is a belief that comes true because you act as though it is already true. For example, you wake up one morning feeling grumpy. You tell yourself, "This is going to be a terrible day!" Well, guess what? You might actually have a terrible day! Here’s how the cycle works:

Beliefs: You have a certain belief about something.

Expectations: You expect something to happen based on your belief.

Behavior: Because of those expectations, you make certain choices.

Results: Those choices give you a positive or negative outcome. It all depends on you.

Thoughts are powerful. So, when you practice mindfulness, focus positively on the way you want your life to look! Expect more good days, and they’ll start coming your way.

title: Defining Confidence
text: Confidence is the belief that you can succeed. It is having a positive energy around you. When you are confident, you feel certain about yourself and your abilities. This includes your motivation to keep learning, growing, and improving. Confidence doesn’t come from comparing yourself to other people’s strengths or weaknesses. It comes from believing “I can” instead of “I can’t.”

title: The Power of Confidence
text:
When you face the world with an “I can” attitude, you will have more opportunities to learn new things, develop your talents, and make an impact on the world. Confidence helps you feel happier. If things don’t go the way you planned, being confident helps you to keep a positive attitude about your mistakes and keep trying.

Confidence can help you make friends, too. When you are confident about who you are, how you feel, what you believe, and what you can achieve, you can be your true self.

title: Effort Brings Confidence
text:
Imagine there's a talent show. Steven chooses to procrastinate and doesn't prepare. He doesn't want to be embarrassed, but he has to use his sock as a puppet for the show at the last minute. Natalia worked hard to prepare and even wore a costume. Who do you think feels the proudest of their performance? Who had the most fun doing it? Who is building their confidence?

You'll never know what you can achieve until you try your best. Working hard and putting your best effort into something feels great. Even if you don't win first prize or break a record, you can be proud of your effort.

title: Positive Thinking Brings Confidence
text:
Saying “I can” instead of “I can’t” is an example of self-talk. Self-talk is the internal dialogue you have with yourself about your own abilities. It also includes the questions you have and things you think about. Self-talk can be negative or positive.

Confidence is choosing to focus on positive self-talk and say encouraging, uplifting things to yourself. For example:

I am proud that I tried something new.

With enough hard work, I am going to figure this out.

I can keep practicing.

My effort makes a difference.

title: Confidence in Who You Are
text:
The world would be a very boring place if we all had the same talents and abilities. What if everyone was good at math but no one had a talent for writing books? Luckily, we live in a world where everyone is good at different things.

When you compare yourself to other people and start to feel bad about yourself, it can cause you to think you aren’t good enough. Comparison makes us focus on things we don’t have instead of recognizing what we do have.

When you start to compare yourself to someone else, redirect your self-talk. Remind yourself of your unique talents and your ability to learn and grow. Celebrate your uniqueness!

title: Help Others Build Confidence
text: Success isn’t like a pitcher of water, where filling one person’s glass means there’s less for everyone else. Someone else’s success doesn’t take away from your own ability to succeed. In fact, the opposite is true. The more we support each other, help each other, and celebrate each other’s success, the more positive we will feel. And the more positive we feel, the more positive our self-talk will be! Let yourself be inspired by other people’s success instead of being jealous of it. There’s plenty to go around!

title: Building Blocks of Confidence
text:
Can you think of anything that tears down your confidence? You can replace those things with some of these ideas that can help you build confidence:

Get to know yourself. What do you like and dislike? What is important to you? What are your good qualities?

Be your true self. You don’t have to be perfect!

Stop unhealthy and harmful behaviors.

Accept responsibility for yourself and your actions.

Practice new skills and notice how you are improving.

Care for your body and practice good personal hygiene.

Set a short-term goal and celebrate when you reach it.

Accept compliments and feel proud of your efforts.

Be kind to yourself when you make mistakes.

Know how to protect yourself from sickness and danger.

title: You Get to Choose!
text:
Feeling negative emotions is normal. Feeling positive emotions is normal. You have the power to choose how you respond to the emotions you feel and the experiences you have. It's okay to feel anger at times, but you choose whether to respond in an angry, negative way or in a helpful, positive way.

It can be helpful to “push pause” and think about how you want to respond. You may need to breathe deeply, remove yourself for a minute, or create space before you choose how to respond. When you are ready, you can choose a helpful way to respond.

title: Focus on What You Can Control
