title: Human-Environment Interaction
text:
The physical environment in different regions help make up that area’s landscape, landforms, elevation, climate, animal life, and water features. As vastly different and original to each area those features are, so are human characteristics within each region. A place's human characteristics are a result of people’s ideas, choices, and actions as they interact with the physical environment. This includes the population size, ethnic and religious identifiers, language patterns, and other aspects of culture.

In other words, where people live and the kinds of houses they build are human characteristics. The kinds of work people do and the activities they can enjoy are also human characteristics of a place.

When we discuss a place's human characteristics, we also examine its political, cultural, and economic characteristics. A place's political characteristics are organized by where people live. This includes cities, states, and countries. Cultural characteristics include a place's religious beliefs, languages, arts, and celebrations. A place's economic characteristics are based on natural resources. These natural resources are used for goods and services and contribute to a place's resulting economy.

title: Waterways Throughout North America
text:
Water influences where people live and work. Populations are almost always larger near water sources. Water is used for things like agriculture, energy, transportation, and washing and drinking. All the ways waterways are used in North America create jobs for thousands of people.

Agriculture

Farming and ranching rely heavily on dependable water sources. Water is needed for raising livestock and growing crops. Ditches and canals are used to divert water from rivers and tributaries to irrigate crops on farms.

River Transportation

Rivers help move goods and people. The longest river in North America is the Missouri River, at 2,341 miles. The Missouri River runs southeast from Montana in the north to Illinois, where it joins with the Mississippi River. The Mississippi River runs south from Minnesota all the way down to Louisiana.

Many states use these waterways to transport goods to ports and markets around the country and the world. Although it is not as fast as shipping overland, a significantly larger number of goods can be shipped for much cheaper on waterways.

One example of how this works would be transporting grain from Nebraska to one of the major sea ports in Louisiana. The grain would be transported to a river port in Nebraska on the Missouri River. From there, it would be loaded onto 15 large commercial barges. These barges would then be towed up or down the river to their next destinations. It would take six trains with over 216 rail cars or 1,050 semi trucks to carry the same amount of cargo as the 15-barge tow. The expense to fuel the trains or trucks would make the cost of shipping significantly higher than by barge tow.

Sea Ports and Trade

North American rivers flow into the Hudson Bay, the Gulf of Mexico, and the Pacific, Arctic, and Atlantic Oceans. The St. Lawrence Seaway allows ships to travel between the Atlantic Ocean and the Great Lakes. Busy port cities like Chicago and Toronto are near this seaway. Major North American seaports are found in California, Washington, and British Columbia in the west; Texas, Louisiana, and Florida in the south; and Georgia, North and South Carolina, Virginia, New York, New Jersey, and Quebec in the east. Millions of goods pass through these ports to and from places all over the world every year.

Energy

Along with agriculture, shipping, and trade, waterways in North America are also used to create energy. The U.S. shares one of the most famous waterfalls in the world, Niagara Falls, with Canada. The Niagara River forms part of the U.S.-Canada border. Some of the Niagara River is diverted to hydroelectric plants before it reaches the Falls. Both countries use this hydroelectric power. Another large power plant can be found at the Hoover Dam in the western U.S. state of Nevada. The Hoover Dam generates enough electric power to serve 1.3 million people.

title: Adapting to and Modifying the Environment
text:
People adapt to their environment to meet their basic needs and survive. This means people change how they live based on their environment. Everything from plants and animals to the weather can change the way people live. People must adapt to the climate. They must change the ways they live based on the climate where they live. People around the world wear different clothes, eat different foods, and live in different houses. People do all of this based on their environment. The jobs they do relate to their environment, too. Forestry, mining, and drilling are examples of jobs that were created based on a place's natural resources.

People modify their environment to meet their needs. This means they change the place where they live. For example, people build dams to provide water for growing food. People also build homes and schools. They set up irrigation and farming systems. They build roads and bridges to travel from one area to another. They cut down forests for lumber and to make farmland for growing crops. All of these interactions modify the environment in some way.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text:
When humans settle in an area, they begin to interact with the environment in many different ways. They use the land around them to help fulfill their needs. When people make changes to the environment, they modify it. These changes can have positive and negative impacts.

Positive Impacts on the Environment

People can have a positive impact on their environment. Some ways to do this are by cleaning up litter, protecting endangered species, planting trees, and growing your own plants and vegetables. Other things that can have a positive impact on the environment are conserving water and electricity, using reusable water bottles, and buying locally grown food. When we use natural resources wisely, we positively impact the environment.

It is a good idea to use natural resources more responsibly. One example is implementing recycling programs in communities. About 70 percent of all the garbage we throw away can be recycled. The best way to keep our landfills and garbage dumps from taking over the environment is to recycle as many items as possible. People can work together to protect natural resources and have a positive impact on the environment.

Various efforts have been made to conserve resources and protect the environment in California. In 1999, the California legislature passed the Marine Life Protection Act. This act established marine-protected areas throughout the state to protect marine animals, their natural habitats, and the ecosystems in which they live. Organizations like Environment California are working to create programs that promote clean air initiatives, drinking water conservation, and the development of cleaner energy sources.

Negative Impacts on the Environment

In many ways, people’s interactions with the environment can be negative. We change the environment when we cut down trees, remove stone, and use natural resources. Agriculture and mining can also pose a threat to the environment. These activities can change the landscape in ways that make it no longer usable. Gold mining has had a significant impact on the environment of California. While many people came to California to seek their fortunes during the Gold Rush, some of the methods they used to look for gold had a negative impact on the environment that can still be seen today.

People also produce a lot of trash. Trash often ends up in landfills and garbage dumps. Trash can also produce harmful chemicals that can pollute the soil, water, and air. People have to be careful to balance their needs with available resources found in their environment. This helps people avoid having a negative impact on the environment.

title: Clearing the Air
text:
When there is a fire, there’s usually smoke, and smoke in the air can cause problems. Smoke that is a result of burning fossil fuels can be especially harmful. More than 25 percent of the electricity used in North America comes from burning coal. In addition, we burn enormous amounts of other fossil fuels. Here are some ways that smoke and gases from burning fossil fuels can be harmful.

• When fossil fuels burn, they give off greenhouse gases, which trap heat on the Earth and keep it too warm.

• Acid rain is a result of gases that are trapped in the air. When moisture collects, particles of chemicals are collected as well. Acid rain can kill plants and destroy metal and paint.

• Smoke, or exhaust, can make it difficult for people to breathe and sometimes causes skin sores.

For these and many other reasons, research is being done to discover better ways to produce energy. Different car companies have released their own versions of a hybrid car that has both a gasoline engine and an electric motor. It uses less than half the gasoline a normal car would but gets almost the same power. Consumers will start seeing many new kinds of “cleaner” cars. In learning to use their natural resources more wisely, people will have a better place to live.

title: Pollution
text:
How many different types of pollution can you think of? There may be more than you think. There’s air pollution (outside and inside), land and water pollution (trash and chemicals, like fertilizers), and noise pollution (loud, unwanted noises, which can harm your ears), just to name a few. Why should you care? Well, all of these pollutants can affect your health and well-being. For example, air pollution can cause short-term effects, such as headaches or allergies. It can also cause long-term effects, such as lung cancer and heart disease. Pollution also harms other living things on our planet. Water pollution kills animals and harms our natural resources.

So, what can we do about it? There are a lot of things that you can do to slow down the effects of pollution on our planet. First of all, remember the three Rs: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. Reduce your waste by not throwing as many things in the trash. Reuse things you don’t need anymore. Can you give away that old toy instead of tossing it in the trash can? Recycle materials like plastic, paper, and aluminum.

You can also choose to purchase environmentally safe products. Look at the glass cleaner you have at home. Does it have ammonia in it? That could be harmful to your health. Look for products that list all the ingredients. It’s not too hard to find “green” products that are safer for us and for the environment. But don’t throw those old products in the trash or down the drain! That waste is hazardous and can cause land and water pollution. Your local Department of Public Works can tell you where and how to dispose of those things properly. Take charge of your health and the health of our planet. Everyone needs to work together to make our planet pollution-free.

title: Highways
text:
In 1919, Dwight D. Eisenhower was part of the military's first automobile caravan. It took the caravan 62 days to get from Washington, D.C., to San Francisco, California, because the roads weren't in good condition. Eisenhower saw the benefit of the U.S. having good roads. In 1956, Congress passed the Federal-Aid Highway Act. Under this law, any highway paid for by the government became an interstate highway. The 46,000 miles of the Interstate Highway System took nearly three decades to complete. Each state was responsible for the location and construction of the roads.

Although the highways have improved life and travel for people, they also negatively affect wildlife in several ways. Building these roadways often required workers to blast tunnels through mountain sides, level out hills, and add layers of sand, gravel, and rock. All of these activities disrupt natural habitats and wildlife. Animals that try to cross highways can get hit by oncoming cars. Larger animals, such as deer, elk, and moose, cross busy highways as they look for food, water, and shelter. Other animals like snakes and turtles are sometimes drawn to the surface of roads because of the warmth the asphalt absorbs from the sun. Reptiles like to lay down on these warm surfaces to regulate their body temperatures. When cars approach, they are often too slow to get out of the way in time. Some animals will avoid crossing roads altogether, but in doing so, they are cut off from the natural habitat and resources they may need to survive on the other side.

The vehicles driving on highways pollute natural habitats. Litter, CO2 emissions, fluid leaks, salts used for melting ice, and other things all contribute to polluting the natural environment. Animals may try to eat trash and litter they find discarded by the roads, which can make them get sick or die. Harmful chemicals can get into the soil or rainwater, which kills plant and animal life.

Today, conservationists are looking for ways to reduce the damage that highways and major roads have on the environment. Wildlife bridges and tunnels have been built in some places to give animals a way to cross major roads safely. Advances in electric-powered vehicles have the potential to reduce and even eliminate harmful CO2 emissions and chemical pollution on roads.

title: What Is Industry?
text:
Industry is a big concept. It involves all the work and processes of using raw materials to create products. It also is distributing the finished products. Ohio has many important industries. The automotive industry makes and distributes cars. The aviation industry makes, distributes, and flies aircraft.

Ohio creates many products that are used in these industries. Ohio is also one of the country’s largest producers of plastics, rubber, fabricated metals, and electrical equipment. Other industries that help Ohio’s economy include bioscience, healthcare, iron, and steel.

title: What Has Influenced Industry in Ohio?
text:
There are many things that made Ohio a good place for industry. Review the bullet points to learn more about some of the important reasons Ohio grew as an industrial state.

Ohio had fertile land for agriculture. This enabled many people to settle in Ohio.

Rivers around the state helped make transportation of goods easier.

The Ohio and Erie Canal opened in 1827. It enabled farmers to sell their products outside Ohio. This increased profits and attracted people to Ohio by making travel easier.

Agriculture provided raw materials for factories to use and the number of factories increased. This created jobs and pulled more people to the state. For example, in 1815, a woolen mill in Steubenville employed more than one hundred workers.

Ohio’s natural resources of coal, oil, and iron ore created new industries. For example, mining provided work for people. Coal powered transport like trains and heated people’s homes. Iron ore and coal are two main products in producing steel. By 1892, Ohio was the second largest producer of steel in the country.

As new products and machines were developed for agriculture, factories were also created that produced those products.

One of the first first gas-powered American cars was built in Ohio City in 1891. As automobiles became more popular, Ohio had the resources to become an important manufacturer.

title: Types of Industry in Ohio
text:
Many industries work together to help Ohio grow. Some of these industries make things we need to survive. Some take care of our well-being. However, they all employ people. The people they employ pay taxes. Industries are important in every state.

Bioscience and Healthcare

Bioscience and healthcare deal with life and well-being. Doctors, nurses, researchers, and all those who help them are in the bioscience industry. The industry provides a lot of jobs. The bioscience industry in Ohio has been around for a while. Cleveland Clinic was established in 1821. In 1834, the Wexner Medical Center began at Ohio State University. More hospitals, research centers, and laboratories have been built since then.

Bioscience helps to manage diseases that can close our schools. It also tests and treats students for eye and ear problems that may hinder their academic success. In addition, research from the industry enriches the science we learn at school.

Iron and Steel
Ohio got its first blast furnace in 1802. A blast furnace is a furnace that is used for smelting metals. The iron and steel industry in Ohio has come a long way since 1802. There is a lot of iron ore in Ohio. The steel industry turns this into farm equipment, automobiles, and airplanes. Some of the things we use at home are also made by the steel industry. During both WWI and WWII, metals like copper and steel were used for many things. This made Ohio very important. Cleveland and other cities benefited a great deal. Railroads helped Ohio’s economy. Railroads depend heavily on metals.

Today, the iron and steel industry still provides jobs for many people in Ohio. They produce raw materials for other industries. They also buy products from other industries.

The iron and steel industry helps in building our schools. They also provide the pots and pans in our lunch rooms. The stoves and our water fountains are also made of steel. Take a look at the giant trash bin at the back of your school. What is it made of?

Machines and Automobiles

In 1833 and 1837, two farm tools were invented. They were the reaper and the steel plow. These tools changed the way people farmed in Ohio. Since then, many more machines have been developed. Many more advanced machines are manufactured in Ohio today. Most of these machines are for agriculture. The machine industry uses rubber and metals from Ohio.

Many automobiles are also manufactured in Ohio. The automobile industry also uses rubber and metals from Ohio. The machine and automobile industries employ many people in Ohio. These industries did a lot for the United States during the Civil War, WWI, and WWII. They help us get around, and they make our labor easier.

The automobile industry helps us get to school and back. Whether your parents drive you to school or you take the school bus, you use an automobile. Many of our school supplies are made by machines. They are transported to us by automobiles.

Aerospace

On Dec. 17, 1903, Orville and Wilbur Wright made history. These two men from Ohio made a machine that could fly. It is fitting that the aerospace industry in Ohio is strong. The aerospace industry deals with air travel. The industry also manufactures equipment for space travel.

The aerospace industry also employs many people in Ohio. We have beautiful airports because of this industry. Many inventions have also come from the industry. Many aerospace materials make our lives easier. Satellites, for example, help us to predict the weather.

The maps and globes we use today are accurate because of the aerospace industry. The industry also helps us learn more about other cultures. It does this by making it easier to travel to other places. Organizations like NASA also improve our studies in science.

title: Human-Environment Interaction
text:
People are influenced by the world around them. The environments in different parts of the world have unique characteristics. These include various factors, like climate, terrain, natural resources, and more. These characteristics influence the lifestyles and cultures of people around the world. For example, the natural environment can help determine what kinds of foods people eat, how they make a living, and even what kinds of recreational activities they enjoy.

The actions of humans also affect the environment. Any time people do something that changes something about the natural environment, it is considered human-environment interaction. Often, when humans impact the environment, it involves some form of adaptation to or modification of the physical world. One example is the lumber industry clear-cutting trees for wood. Another example is the construction industry building roads and houses in an area that was previously undisturbed.

As human society progresses, efforts are being made to limit the negative impacts humans have on the environment, as well as the negative consequences that natural forces have on humans. Natural disasters like droughts and floods require innovative solutions to protect people and their interests. However, allowing humans to do whatever they want to the natural environment could cause a lot of harm. In each of these cases, humans and the environment would quickly suffer from the impact each one had on the other.

Studying human-environment interaction requires considering how humans impact the environment and how the natural environment has influenced the actions and lives of humans. The people of South America have affected and been affected by the continent’s environment. The diverse geography of South America has led to a variety of lifestyles and cultures. Soaring mountains, arid deserts, lush rainforests, as well as rivers, lakes, and ocean coastlines, all influence how people live and adapt to their environments.

title: Adapting and Modifying in South America
text:
One major category of human-environment interaction is the way people adapt to their environment. Natural forces require people to adapt their behaviors to survive in their environment. South America has environments that range from temperate and accommodating to extreme and hostile. The more extreme the environment, the more adaptation is required to survive there. South America has some of the most extreme environments in the world.

To adapt means to change one’s behavior. Research suggests that people living in the very high elevations of the Andes mountain range, over 12,000 feet above sea level, adapted their diet to include more starches, like potatoes. Those living in lower elevations could survive by hunting and gathering. Those who lived at higher elevations burned more calories to survive. By developing agriculture, those living at higher elevations were able to produce the food they needed to survive.

Changing their diet was one way people adapted to their environment. Other adaptations were changes in the human body itself. Those same people living in the extremely high elevations of the Andes Mountains in countries like Bolivia and Peru adapted to the low levels of oxygen in the air. Research has revealed that people living at these extreme elevations have bodies that are better able to utilize the oxygen in the air.

There are also many examples of people modifying the natural environment of South America. The climate of South America is perfect for growing crops like coffee and cacao, which is turned into chocolate. These cash crops must be cultivated in large quantities in order to make money from them. Because of this, farmers must clear large areas of land. This modification changes the natural environment, removing the diverse natural plants and replacing them with one type of plant.

Modification of the environment also occurs when people gather in cities and construct the structures needed to travel and live in large numbers. Major cities, like Rio de Janeiro and Brasilia in Brazil or Buenos Aires in Argentina, represent major modifications of the natural environment. Instead of forests or grasslands, there are tall buildings and major highways that have modified the land from what it once was. These cities are often established in areas that have good natural resources, climates, and access to waterways because these things all help with human survival. These modifications humans have made are examples of human-environment interaction.

title: Natural Resources in South America
text:
People in South America have benefited from the continent’s abundant natural resources. There are many examples of human-environment interaction between the people living there and the many resources that occur there. These natural resources allow people to access food and other valuable minerals and materials needed to feed, clothe, and support the establishment of towns and cities.

The climate of South America makes it an excellent place to grow crops. Its location along the Equator provides year-round precipitation and warmth. The people of South America take advantage of these excellent growing conditions by planting and harvesting crops like rice, wheat, coffee, and cacao. South America is becoming a major producer of soybeans as well.

People are developing new and innovative ways to limit the negative impacts large-scale farming can have on the natural environment. Modifying the environment to farm these crops can deplete the soil and ruin its ability to support crops in the future. In addition to crops, the natural environment of South America also supports ranching, which supplies meat and dairy products. These human-environment interactions can be damaging to the natural world. Taking steps to limit the damage and improve the ability to produce crops, meat, and dairy products will allow people to enjoy more benefits of human-environment interaction.

South America is also rich in minerals, which people mine from the ground. This is often a very invasive form of human-environment interaction. It removes material from the ground and modifies the landscape. Areas of heavy mining look very different from the natural environment. The largest mines in South America produce copper and iron in countries like Chile, Peru, and Brazil.

New technology is one factor that drives the demand for new natural resources. It leads to new impacts in human-environment interaction. Electric vehicle batteries require lithium, which is found in great quantities in Chile. Other technologies, like cell phones and computers, also use lithium. However, the process of mining lithium requires a massive modification of the natural environment. These environments are completely altered in order to enable the removal of lithium, and it can pollute the air and local water supplies.

title: Amazon River
text:
The Amazon River dominates the northern central part of South America. Although it mostly runs through Brazil, its tributaries and watershed extend into the countries of Suriname, Guyana, Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia. Its watershed, the area of land where precipitation eventually makes its way to the river, is the largest of any river system in the world. The Amazon River moves more water than any other river. The presence of such a massive river system naturally influences human-environment interaction in the region.

Such a large river system has had major impacts on the lives of people in that area of South America. A major river like the Amazon is a transportation route through the inland areas of Brazil and the rest of the watershed. In the past, native populations relied on the river for their food, which influenced what kinds of foods they ate. More recently, people have used the fertile land along the river to plant and grow crops as a food source and a way to make money.

Human actions have had a variety of impacts on the Amazon River. One major human impact on the river is pollution. As settlements have grown and multiplied along the river, more pollution has made its way into the water. Specific practices like gold mining have led to the introduction of mercury, a toxic metal, into the river. Pesticides used in farming have also leached, or run off, into the river, affecting the plants and animals in and along the river.

More recently, Brazil has been building dams on Amazon River tributaries. These dams are meant to generate electrical power. These dams flood the areas around them and divert the tributaries, changing the way the water flows and gathers. This impacts the people living in these areas. Lands become flooded, which forces people to move. Rivers become diverted, altering or threatening animal populations that live in the rivers. The modifications these dams make to the Amazon River and its tributaries are an example of human-environment interaction.

title: Positive and Negative Interactions
text:
Human-environment interaction can describe positive or negative interactions between people and the natural environment. Humans can influence the environment positively and negatively, just as the environment can affect humans in the same way. South America has many examples of positive and negative interactions between humans and the environment.

Humans must be careful that their actions do not negatively impact the environment. Any activity that impacts and modifies the environment has the potential to create negative consequences. It can be difficult to anticipate unintended consequences. Even the most well-thought-out actions can have effects that were not predicted. Actions that have positive benefits for humans can still have negative consequences for the environment.

For example, the dams constructed in Brazil on the Amazon River tributaries are meant to improve life in the area by producing more electricity from a renewable resource. The negative consequences of these dams are the flooding of large areas of land and the threat that presents to the animals and people that rely on these rivers. Forward-thinking planners could anticipate these negative consequences and take steps to lessen their impact. Other negative impacts occur due to mining and farming, which create byproducts like minerals and pesticides that pollute the land, air, and water of South America.

The environment can also have negative impacts on humans. Humans have to work to come up with plans and guides to help their communities when negative events occur. Earthquakes and volcanic activity occur in the mountainous western region of the continent. People living in the countries of Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Chile have to deal with these realities. The climate of South America can also be a major threat to people. Too much or too little rain can trigger floods or cause droughts that threaten the livelihood and lives of people affected by them. Floods are dangerous and damaging, while droughts can affect the availability of food.

There are also positive interactions between humans and the environment in South America. The abundant rain and heat near the Equator allow people to grow cash crops and provide food for large populations. With careful consideration, humans can even take steps to improve and heal the environment. Current projects include efforts to limit the impact of human activity on the waters of the Amazon River and its tributaries, cleaning the river, and keeping additional pollutants from entering the river. Additional efforts are working to limit destruction and restore forests that were lost due to farming and ranching.

title: Deforestation
text:
Perhaps the single largest example of human-environment interaction in South America is how humans interact with the Amazon Rainforest. The rainforest has more plant and animal species than any other place in the world. For this reason, it is an excellent source of lumber, as well as a great place to grow crops. In order to gather the lumber and plant crops in the dense rainforest, however, modifications to the natural environment are necessary.

This process of deforestation, or removing or destroying forested areas, is not new. On a small scale, people have been clearing land in the Amazon Rainforest in order to plant crops for themselves and their families since humans have occupied that region. Recently, though, deforestation has grown to include large-scale operations. This is meant to maximize the money to be made from logging, farming, and ranching, among other activities.

Human interaction with the Amazon Rainforest is increasing. From 1985 to 2018, modifying the rainforest increased by 60 percent. These modifications include altering plant life and changing how the land is used. At the same time, the rainforest lost around 16 percent of its natural tree cover. Deforestation at this rate and volume can have a devastating effect on the ecosystem.

Much of this tree-cover loss was due to the conversion of that land to pasture and farmland. Because the Amazon Rainforest is home to millions of species of plants and animals, the physical destruction of this ecosystem threatens the existence of these species. Destroying or uprooting plant and animal species has an impact on the ability of those plants and animals to survive as plants are destroyed and animals lose their food sources.

The Amazon Rainforest also plays a critical role in producing oxygen. The dense plant life in the rainforest absorbs carbon dioxide in the air. Destroying the plant life of the rainforest increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and can lead to warmer global temperatures. In addition, forest fires add to the carbon dioxide emissions from the rainforest. Some fires occur naturally, and others are set as a way to clear the forest for other uses, like farming or ranching.

title: What Is a Market?
text:
A market is a place where people sell goods and services. Everyone who buys or sells goods or services is part of a market.

There are different types of markets. Physical markets are actual places, like stores where you buy groceries. Shopping malls, department stores, and open-air markets are all examples of physical markets.

A market is not always a physical place. For example, some people buy and sell things in a virtual market. This is a market that is online. People use the internet to buy and sell.

Markets can be different sizes, too. A local market serves people who live near you. Other markets can include all of your state or country. The international market includes millions of people from different nations around the world.

title: Physical Markets
text:
A physical market is a real location. Buyers and sellers meet there to exchange goods and services. A physical market is for shopping in person. Grocery stores, clothing stores, hairdressers, and movie theaters are all physical markets. They have specific locations. Buyers go there to shop.

Sometimes, we need a physical market. For example, a car can’t get fixed online. Also, people often want to try some items before they buy them. It’s difficult to tell how comfortable a pair of shoes is unless you try them on.

Many communities have outdoor markets. Fruits, vegetables, and homemade products are sold there. These markets often use tents, carts or other temporary structures.

Some businesses run both a physical store and a virtual market.

title: Virtual Markets
text:
Virtual markets are not physical stores. They are companies that use technology to do business. Most virtual companies have a website which functions as an online store. People can see and buy the goods or services they provide online. You can buy almost anything online these days. There are virtual markets that sell clothing, books, games, and food. You can even buy a car or house online. Some virtual stores sell items by auction. Many companies today have both a physical store and an online store.

Virtual stores need a way to deliver their physical goods. Some large companies have their own delivery service. Smaller companies usually use a delivery company or U.S. Postal Services.

Virtual services can often be done completely online. For example, you can pay to watch a movie online. Some people go to school online. You can even visit with a doctor online.

title: West Side Market
text:
The first market on Cleveland’s West Side was opened in 1840. It was built on land donated to the city by Josiah Barber and Richard Lord. It was called the Pearl Street Market. Although the location has changed, Cleveland has always had a market on the West Side.

The new site for the West Side Market opened in 1912. It had an outdoor farmers market area where bread, meats, fruits, and vegetables were sold. It also had indoor stalls. The market was especially beneficial to immigrants in Cleveland. People could shop and buy things the way they used to in their home countries.

West Side Market has been updated over the years. Today, the West Side Market is a modern market. It has elevators, heating, and other modern features. It was recognized as a historic site in 1973. West Side Market celebrated its centennial in 2012.

title: Human Characteristics
text:
A place's human characteristics are a result of people’s ideas, choices, and actions as they interact with the physical environment. In other words, where people live and the kinds of houses they build are human characteristics. The kind of work people do and the activities they can enjoy are also human characteristics of a place.

When we discuss a place's human characteristics, we also examine its political, cultural, and economic characteristics. A place's political characteristics are organized by where people live. This includes cities, states, and countries. Cultural characteristics include a place's religious beliefs, languages, arts, and celebrations. A place's economic characteristics are based on natural resources. These natural resources are used for goods and services and contribute to a place's resulting economy.

title: Essential Question
text: How has education in Pennsylvania changed over time?

title: Education in Pennsylvania
text:
Education has always had an important place in Pennsylvania history. Dating back to its days as a colony in the 17th century, education was a priority in Pennsylvania. Under the leadership of William Penn, early settlers established public schools. Penn believed that education was important for everyone to be good citizens. Education was not only for rich people.

The Pennsylvania Constitution of 1790 allowed for schools to be created "in such a manner that the poor may be taught gratis [free]." The Free Public School Act of 1834 helped create free schools across Pennsylvania. In order to fund free education for students, taxes needed to be raised. The government needed money to pay for new schools and teachers’ salaries, or wages. People in the northern and western counties loved the idea of free public schools. Many in the southern and central counties did not want to see taxes raised. Those opposed to the increased taxes worked hard to overturn the law. The Pennsylvania legislature was ready to repeal, or vote to overturn, the law in 1835. Then, Representative Thaddeus Stevens gave a speech urging the legislature to change its mind. It worked! This speech is often thought to have saved public education in Pennsylvania. Stevens ended his speech by stating:

I trust that when we come to act on this question, we shall all take the lofty [high] ground … and so cast our votes that the blessing of education shall be conferred [given] on every son of Pennsylvania, shall be carried home to the poorest child ...

Another law that changed Pennsylvania education came in 1895. The Compulsory Attendance Act required children 8–13 years old to attend school. Many families had kept children at home to help run family businesses or family farms. This law also put more responsibility on schools to care for students. Things like school lunches, school nurses, and proper teacher training all came from laws like this.

While there were many improvements over time to the Pennsylvania education system, there were flaws as well.

The practice of segregation affected education in Pennsylvania and across the United States. Segregation is the forced separation of people based on class, the color of their skin, or any other distinction. The Supreme Court of the United States made this practice unconstitutional in 1954. Schools adapted and changed. Students came together to learn in the same buildings and classrooms.

Education changed and grew so much that in 1963, the Pennsylvania State Board of Education was created. This board oversees the entire state education system. The importance of education in Pennsylvania has only continued to grow ever since.

title: Timeline of Schooling in Pennsylvania
text:
The following is a timeline of some of the major events in the history of education in Pennsylvania. Since Pennsylvania was founded as a colony, education has been a priority to its leaders. These events show different ways the government of Pennsylvania has influenced education.

1682: William Penn provides for schools in the colony of Pennsylvania.

1755: The University of Pennsylvania is established as the first university in the state.

1789–90: The Second Pennsylvania Constitution provides for public schools.

1834: The Free Public Schools Act creates a general state system of common schools.

1835: State Representative Thaddeus Stevens delivers an address to the Pennsylvania state congress on free schools.

1852: The Pennsylvania State Teachers Association (PSTA) is founded.

1862: The Morrill Land Grant College Act passes. This creates new agriculture and engineering colleges.

1895: A compulsory, or required, school attendance law passes. The law requires children between the ages of eight and 13 to attend school.

1914: The first community vocational school in a rural area, or place that is not a city, opens in Indiana County.

1954: The U.S. Supreme Court declares segregation unconstitutional in Brown v. Board of Education.

1963: Legislation creates the Pennsylvania State Board of Education.

1975: Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) makes free public education available with appropriate services to children with disabilities.

2001: No Child Left Behind Act requires states to adopt accountability standards and perform yearly testing to measure student achievement.

title: Carlisle Indian Industrial School
text:
The Carlisle Indian Industrial School opened in 1879. It was the first government-run boarding school for Native Americans. The site was originally a barracks, or simple housing, for the United States Army. It was given to the Bureau of Indian Affairs. The bureau repurposed the site as a boarding school. The bureau represented the United States government to independent tribes across the country. The bureau told Indigenous tribes that the purpose of their boarding schools was to teach students English and protect tribes. Parents wanted their children to stay safe. They worried that their children would not be safe if they did not agree to the U.S. government's requirements. Knowing that tribal children were already at these schools, many tribes reluctantly agreed to changes they did not want. This meant moving to reservations. It also meant giving up cultural traditions they had held for generations.

At the boarding schools, students were forced to make many changes. They had to cut their hair and change their names to English-sounding names. They had to stop speaking their native tribal language and only speak English. Students had to convert to the Christian faith held by many of the government leaders and members of society around them. These Native American students experienced a loss of cultural identity, or sense of belonging to a specific group. They also experienced harsh discipline and abuse. Many children never made it home. Some died from disease, abuse, or neglect. Some students' native communities feared they would side with the U.S. government. These children were not welcomed back into their tribe.

Today, the Carlisle Indian School Project works to tell this complicated history. The project focuses on supporting families affected by these events. While the physical buildings of the school no longer exist, the impact of what happened there remains. Some experiences can be so distressing that they cause generational trauma, or trauma that affects people so deeply it impacts the emotions and responses of future generations.

After the school closed in 1918, the original site became a military medical center. It is now the U.S. Army War College. The cemetery was relocated in 1927 to its present site today. Beginning in 2017, the United States government began to make reparations, or repair past damages through actions and payment. The government will transfer the remains of those buried in the cemetery to their native homes on request from tribes. Many of the children who passed away at the Carlisle Industrial Indian School are now buried with their ancestors on their native land.

title: Laws and Decisions Impacting Education in Pennsylvania
text:
Many laws and government decisions have changed education in Pennsylvania. Some of these laws were created by the state legislature. Other laws were passed federally. Outside events impact teaching and learning too. Things like global pandemics, school safety, transportation, and population changes can influence laws that guide education.

The following are some of those laws and decisions.

---

1790: Pennsylvania Constitution, Article 3, Sections 14 and 15

Section 14. The General Assembly shall provide for the maintenance and support of a thorough and efficient system of public education to serve the needs of the Commonwealth.

Section 15. No money raised for the support of the public schools of the Commonwealth shall be appropriated to or used for the support of any sectarian (private or religious) school.

---

1834: Free School Act

This law created a general state system of common schools. It led to an increase in the number of public schools around the state.

An increase in schools meant an increase in the number of teachers needed. It also explained how those teachers were qualified.

---

1949: PA Act 14, Article V, Section 501

Section 501. Elementary Schools. The board of school directors in every school district shall establish, equip, furnish, and maintain a sufficient number of elementary public schools … to educate every person, residing in such district, between the ages of six and twenty-one years.

---

1954: Brown v Board of Education Supreme Court Decision

“We conclude that, in the field of public education, the doctrine [policy] of "separate but equal" has no place. Separate educational facilities are inherently [absolutely] unequal."

- Chief Justice Earl Warren

---

1963: PA Act 321, Transferring powers and duties from the State Council of Education to the State Board of Education

Section 1. All powers and duties imposed upon [given by] the State Council of Education by the "Public School Code of 1949," …are hereby transferred to and imposed upon the State Board of Education, unless otherwise specifically provided by law.

---

1963: PA Act 290, Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency Act

Section 2. Purpose. The purpose of such agency shall be to improve the higher educational opportunities [after graduation] of persons who are residents of this State and who are attending approved institutions of higher education, in this State or elsewhere, by assisting them in meeting their expenses of higher education.

title: Desegregation of Schools in Pennsylvania
text:
On May 8, 1854, the Pennsylvania legislature passed a common school law. This law created separate schools for children of different racial heritage. Often, the schools for children from minority groups were run-down. They did not have access to quality learning materials, like textbooks. Many years later, an African American parent named Elias Allen challenged this law. Allen lived in Meadville, Pennsylvania. He refused to enroll his children in the local school for Black students. It was farther away and not as well-equipped as a closer white school.

Allen sued the Crawford County School Board. He argued that his children were not given equal protection of the law. In 1881, courts ruled that it was unequal for African American students to meet all in one room. Instead, they should be taught by grades, as in white schools. For the Allen family, it was also ruled unequal because the Black school was farther away from their home than the white school.

Shortly after the case, Pennsylvania passed a new law. This law made it “unlawful for any school director, superintendent or teacher to make any distinction whatever … by reason of the race or color of any pupil … seeking admission to, any public or common school.” Today, a historical marker in Meadville reminds people of the case that started it all.

The 1881 law legally ended segregation in Pennsylvania’s schools. Still, many schools ignored the law. They remained segregated until 1954. This is when the United States Supreme Court made its decision in Brown v. Board of Education, which ended segregation in schools. After the Supreme Court decision, schools across the country began to bring all students to the same school for learning.

title: Land Grant Colleges and Universities
text:
America grew rapidly in the 19th century. Future farmers and engineers needed education to support the country. Senator Justin S. Morrill of Vermont proposed the Morrill Land Grant College Act. The purpose of the act was to create new colleges on federal lands. President Abraham Lincoln signed the act in 1862. Any state that accepted federal money for education had to follow specific rules on how to use the money.

The 1862 act led to entirely new types of colleges. These schools were made to "benefit the agricultural and mechanical arts." They were to educate the “industrial classes.” All this was to ensure the future of agriculture and engineering.

Through the Land Grant Act, the Pennsylvania Legislature created the Agricultural College of Pennsylvania. Today, this college is Penn State. Penn State is the only institution created in Pennsylvania through the Land Grant Act. It is a public university with many campuses around the commonwealth. Students from all around the country and the world attend Penn State. In its mission statement, the university states that it “supports individuals and communities through integrated programs of teaching, research, and service.”

Penn State is part of a land-grant conference for all recipients of the Morrill Land Grant College Act. The Association of Public and Land Grant Universities (APLU) was created to help these universities learn from each other. In the APLU, scholars from across the country study the history of land grants. They also look to the future during times of economic uncertainty.

title: Colleges and Universities in Pennsylvania by Enrollment
text:
Pennsylvania has a huge state-run university system with many campuses. There are also many other major universities across the commonwealth. Some institutions focus on medical fields. Others may have large teaching colleges or agriculture schools. There is a rich history of higher education in Pennsylvania. This tradition was enhanced in 1963 with the Higher Education Assistance Act. This act made higher education after graduation from public school more affordable. Attending college became possible for a larger and more diverse population of students.
