When friends or family go through hard things, you can be empathetic so that they don’t feel alone. You can use empathy to communicate respect for someone. Can you think of someone in your life who is good at showing empathy? What does it feel like to you when they show empathy?

title: Build Empathy, Build Connections
text:
You can have empathy for someone you have never talked to before. Have you ever heard someone talk about an experience and realized that you have been through the same thing? How do you feel when you learn that someone has been through the same thing as you? For example, if you have ever had a pet die, how would you feel if you heard that someone else’s pet died? You might feel sad for them or with them. You can imagine exactly how they feel because you have experienced it too. This is empathy! Feeling empathy can help you feel connected to a person or group. Shared experiences tend to unite people through empathy, even if they have different backgrounds.

You can build empathy by being open to new experiences so that you can relate to more people. You can also build empathy by being aware of others and what they are going through. You can ask sincere and respectful questions to learn more about someone. Asking genuine questions is important if you have not been through a particular experience. Sharing your own experiences can build trust and create the opportunity to understand someone better.

title: Ears, Eyes, and Empathy
text:
You can build empathy by being a good listener.

Everyone is different. Listening can help you understand why someone is different from you. The more you listen to someone and the better you get to know them, the more connections you will form and the more empathy you will experience toward one another.

You can be a good listener by focusing on the person who is talking. Set aside all distractions. Use your ears to hear what they are saying and feeling. Use your eyes to see what their body language and emotions tell you. Do not make assumptions about what they say. Instead, ask clarifying questions to understand better. You can ask questions like, “What happened next?”, “Why did that happen?”, or “How did that make you feel?” You can help other people feel heard and understood when you listen to them.

Some people may not be ready to talk. When that happens, you can pay attention to their body language and actions to understand them better and show support without pushing them to talk about their experience before they are ready. You can tell them you care. You can also help someone to talk to an adult if they tell you about thoughts of hurting themselves or others. Hearing things like this should alert you that this friend may need additional support from an adult. You can tell them you care about them too much to stay quiet about something so important.

title: Empathy and Moral Identity
text:
Moral identity is knowing right from wrong.

When you have a strong moral identity you know what’s right and wrong and you usually choose to do what’s right. You know you did something wrong when you feel sad. Usually this is because you are thinking how an action affected others negatively. You can know you did something good and right when you feel proud of yourself and happy about your choice.

Demonstrating empathy for others helps you think about the way your actions impact other people. When you work to understand what others are going through, it will be easier to know what might be right or wrong ways to treat them.

Strengthening your empathy skills will improve your moral identity.

Think about the behaviors you have shown others today. Do you think your actions have helped others or hurt them?

title: Empathy and Bullies
text:
Showing empathy is a prosocial behavior. It helps those around you and usually helps you too. Sometimes people around you may choose not to show empathy. When this happens, what can you do? You cannot change or control other people’s choices. You can be an example to them through what you choose to do.

What if you witness bullying? What if someone is bullying you? You can choose to show empathy despite what other people are doing. Remember the steps to building empathy. You can get to know the other person, or you can say something positive and redirect the conversation. You can be the example.

It can be scary to do the right thing when you are the only one, but you will feel best when you show people the empathy and kindness you know how to show. You can stand up to a bully or someone who lacks empathy. You can invite them to be kind. You can ask a teacher for help. When others do not show empathy, you can always choose your own response.

title: Empathy for You
text: Have you ever made a mistake? There is not a person alive today who has not made mistakes. Did you know you can show empathy for yourself? Having empathy for yourself means being patient with yourself. It means allowing yourself to feel your emotions and validating your own emotions. It means making mistakes and working to get it right the next time. You can share your experiences and say how you feel to help you connect with those around you. It can be easier to go through challenges when you know someone else understands you.

title: Emotional Overstimulation
text:
When you show true empathy for others, you may feel their emotions with them. It can be exhausting to take on other people’s feelings in addition to your own. Be aware and mindful of your own emotional well-being. It may be challenging if someone tells you something you don’t know how to help them with. If someone tells you they’re thinking of hurting themselves, you should ask a trusted adult helper to step in right away. If you feel overwhelmed when you show empathy for others, don’t hesitate to take a break or ask for help from an adult. Taking a break might look like asking to talk about the issue later. You can also just take a moment to step away and breathe on your own. You can say things like:

“I am glad you feel comfortable talking about this with me. I am feeling a little overwhelmed. Could we talk about this later?”

“I can see why you feel that way. Your feelings are important. Would it be helpful for you to talk to our teacher about it?”

“I care about you, and I think we can get better help if we ask an adult to help. Let’s ask the school counselor for ideas.”

Ultimately, you should take care of yourself before helping other people. You will not be helpful to others if you are not taking care of your own well-being. You will be able to show the best empathy when you are emotionally healthy.

title: Collaborate
text:
To collaborate means to work as a team. Usually people work together to create or achieve something. They might collaborate about health decisions so they can make the best choices. Adults collaborate at their jobs. Teammates cooperate at practice and in games.

You may not have a job yet, but you collaborate with people every day! You do this at school, at home, in clubs and sports, and even when you are playing with your friends. This is important because it allows you to accomplish things you could not have done on your own.

Can you imagine having to clean your entire house by yourself? Can you imagine trying to win a soccer game if you were the only player on the team? What if you had to do all of the work of group projects alone? These activities would take much longer and wouldn’t be as successful if there was no collaboration.

Collaborating means making decisions as a team. It means valuing everyone’s ideas. Collaborating with others can be fun and exciting as you work together, learn from each other, and accomplish great things.

title: Do Your Part
text:
Anytime you work in a group, each member of the group has a role to fill. Each person has responsibilities. In sports, for example, there are many positions. In baseball, there is a pitcher, a catcher, players assigned to each base, and players assigned to different parts of the outfield. Each player needs to do their part. If they get distracted or try to do someone else’s job, their part of the field is not covered and their responsibility will not be met.

When collaborating, you are given a job and your group, team, or family is counting on you to get it done. You can be reliable. Reliable means you are trusted to do what is asked and you do your best to fulfill your responsibilities. You can choose to do your best at whatever part you are given. If you cannot complete a task you have been assigned, use good communication with your team to let them know, then help find someone to fill in for you. When you are part of a group, you are partly responsible for its success. Everyone in the group is responsible for the group’s success.

title: Love to Listen
text: Being a good listener is an important part of collaboration. Everyone’s ideas and opinions matter. Listen to everyone’s ideas and suggestions. Listening means consistently hearing and considering what people say. Ignoring other people may cause them to shut down and not want to share what they think or know. When there are lots of suggestions, you might not be able to use them all, but you can listen and respect each idea. People who love to listen can help others feel valued. They gain new insights they may not have considered before. Listening to others will encourage people to continue sharing their ideas and contributing to the group’s end goal. Your club, team, family, or group will work more efficiently and be more successful as every member strives to love to listen.

title: “Roar” Respect
text:
Many animals roar to warn of predators and to communicate. Most animals have vocal chords shaped like a triangle, but lions have vocal chords shaped in a square and that can produce a roar as loud as a jet airplane taking off (144 decibels). The shape of their vocal chords allows lions to roar much louder than other animals.

As you practice collaborating, you will learn that being respectful will prove to be a powerful character trait. While you collaborate, you can demonstrate respect by sharing your ideas and listening to other people’s ideas. Some of your team members may set personal boundaries or expectations. You can be respectful by being mindful of those boundaries. For example, if one of your team members doesn’t feel comfortable meeting at someone’s house, you can find a new location to gather. If a team member uses a wheelchair or has dietary restrictions, you can be respectful by taking those things into consideration as you make plans as a group.

title: Everyone Has Strengths
text: Every person is different. Every person is unique. Every person has strengths. When you work with a group of people in any way, look for others’ strengths. Pay attention to what they are good at. People who are different from you will be able to contribute things to a group that you cannot. Ask questions and learn more about the people you are working with so you can combine your strengths with theirs and work toward a common goal. If you find out that one friend is a great artist, you might ask them to help do drawings on a poster. If you know another friend is a great public speaker, you might ask them to do the oral presentation or give you tips for presenting better. One person having strength in an area does not diminish (make smaller) the talents you or others have. Look for the strengths of the people around you at home, at school, and in your extracurricular activities. You can learn so much when you embrace the different talents you see in your peers, family, friends, and classmates.

title: Focus on Your Circle of Control
text:
As you work with others, remember that you cannot control what they do or say. You can be assertive by respectfully sharing your opinion, but you can also respect the opinions and beliefs of those in your group. Instead of focusing on other people’s choices, actions, or words, focus on what is within your control.

Circle of Concern

This is the circle of concern. You have no control over the things in the circle of concern. Things here include other people’s words and actions. You cannot control what other people do or say. You cannot control the weather or the past either. Write two more things that belong in the circle of concern because you have no control over them.

_______________________________________

_______________________________________

Circle of Influence

This is the circle of influence. You do not have control over things here, but you can influence them with what you do or say. In this circle is what other people think of you and your future. You can influence things out of your control by doing things like following the rules, serving others, and standing up for what you believe in.

Circle of Control

This smallest inner circle is the circle of control. There is only one thing here: you! You have control over everything about yourself, including your words, your moods, your thoughts, and your actions. You get to choose who you are and how you feel. Focus on what you can control. Be the best you you can be.

title: Farm Article #1
text:
GROWING CORN

Ohio is a great place for farming. It has some of the most fertile soil in the nation. Over half of the land in Ohio is farmland. Ohio is the nation’s seventh-largest producer of corn. Ohio farmers plant corn in the spring. They wait for the soil to be warm. The corn kernels (or seeds) need warm soil to grow. Today, farmers use technology to help them. Computers and even satellite images can show them just where to plant the kernels. Each kernel needs to have space. It needs to get nutrients, water, and sun.

Over the summer, the corn plant grows. Its leaves take in heat and sunlight. Its roots soak up water and nutrients. Each plant will grow two ears of corn. Hundreds of silks attach to each ear. The silks get pollinated. Once pollinated, each silk forms a new kernel. These kernels grow on a cob until ripe.

Corn farmers need land, water, workers to tend and pick the corn, a way to package the corn, and a way to transport them to market.

Corn plants need healthy soil, sunshine and warm weather, and plenty of water.

HARVESTING CORN

Field corn gets harvested when the kernels and the whole plant dry out. Sweet corn is different. The ears and plants are still green at harvest time. The kernels are still soft. Farmers know to harvest sweet corn when the silk on the end of the ears turns brown.

Sweet corn can be harvested by hand or by machine. As the ears are picked, workers sort them by hand. They pack the ears into crates that each weigh about 42 pounds. Each crate holds about five dozen ears of corn.

As soon as an ear of corn is picked, the sugar in the kernels begins to change. It starts to become starch. Starchy corn is less sweet. Cooling slows the process of sugar becoming starch. It is usually hot when farmers harvest sweet corn in late summer. It is important to cool the ears within hours of the harvest. Farmers run cold water through crates of packed ears to cool them down.

GETTING CORN TO MARKET

The clock starts ticking on fresh sweet corn as soon as the harvest begins. Farmers store the crates of cooled ears in sheds. There are many types of sweet corn. Farmers can store the different types for 5-8 days. The sooner they ship the corn, the better. Fresh sweet corn ships in refrigerated trucks or rail cars. Temperatures for shipping are kept around freezing. The corn must stay cold. This is so the sugars inside the kernels stay fresh and sweet. Once the corn reaches stores, employees set the corn out. Stores buy sweet corn by the crate. They sell the corn by the ear, though. Customers buy only as many ears of corn as they need. They can cook it right away, store the ears in the fridge, or freeze them.”

“The farmer starts with a good fertilized field. Fertilizing soil is important. The farmer waters and tends the corn plants. The workers harvest the corn and package the ears. The farmer sends trucks of corn to distribution centers for delivery. Some farmers sell corn kernels to feed animals or make other foods. The distributors transport the corn to stores. The workers in stores put corn out for the customers to buy.”

title: Honesty
text: Being honest means telling the truth. We should always be honest.

title: Farm Article #2
text:
“Sweet potatoes are native to North Carolina. North Carolina is the number one producer of sweet potatoes in the United States. About half of the nation's sweet potatoes are grown here. A lot goes into getting a sweet potato from the farm to your table.

Planting: Sweet potatoes aren’t planted by seed. Instead, farmers plant “slips.” These are pieces of a mature sweet potato that have been cut up. When buried in soil, the slips sprout a new plant.

Harvesting: Sweet potatoes need three to four months without frost to grow. When it is time to harvest, sweet potatoes are unearthed by tractors.

DID YOU KNOW? Sweet potato skins are so delicate that they need to be picked up and sorted by hand after they’re unearthed?

Curing and Storing: Most sweet potatoes get “cured” before selling. They are kept in a hot, humid room for about a week. Their starches turn into sugars, making them sweeter. Their skins get tougher too. This allows sweet potatoes to be stored for up to a year before being sold.

Packing and Selling: Next, sweet potatoes get sorted and packaged. Some get sold to factories for processing. Some get sent to stores or farmers markets. Some go straight to school cafeterias through the North Carolina Farm to School Program.

Eating: People like to prepare sweet potatoes in all sorts of ways. They serve them baked, mashed, plain, in pies or casseroles, or as fries or chips. Even babies love them when they are pureed into baby food!”

title: Farm Article #3
text:
Today, people get most of their food from grocery stores. With ships, airplanes, and refrigerated trucks, food can travel around the world. This has made food supply more interdependent. Farmers can specialize in one product. They can go to a grocery store and get the other things they need. Our grocery stores now have food from all over the world. We can buy apples from Washington or bananas from Ecuador. Strawberries from California are transported to other parts of the United States and the world.

California’s climate is good for growing strawberries. The growing season is the part of the year in which the temperature allows plants to grow. California has a longer growing season than other areas. Strawberries can be harvested almost year-round. They are grown in southern California in winter. In northern California, they are grown in spring and summer. Technology has improved the production of strawberries. Many farmers will apply covers to their plants to prevent damage. This is because strawberries will spoil if there is frost. Scientists have also created strawberry plants with special qualities. Some produce longer during the year. Others are resistant to diseases. There are also some that produce much larger berries. Water is very important to strawberry farmers. Technology has helped farmers use less water. Drip irrigation systems deliver water directly to each strawberry plant. This uses much less water. Some farmers also use recycled water. It is water that has been cleaned after being used.

Strawberry farmers need land, water, workers to tend and pick the fruit, a way to package strawberries, and a way to transport them to market. Strawberry plants need healthy soil, sunshine and warm weather, and plenty of water.

It takes a lot of workers to pick strawberries. Strawberries are mostly picked by hand. The fruit has to be handled carefully. It bruises easily. Many strawberries are grown using special fabric that covers the ground. This prevents the berries from getting dirty. Clean berries can be picked and packaged at the same time. Workers pack the fruit in the containers they are sold in. That reduces damage to the berries during distribution. Many strawberry farms are run by families working together. The farms hire many seasonal workers. These workers come when the fruit is ready to be picked.

Strawberries begin to go soft as soon as they are picked. They can last two weeks after picking. However, they need to stay cold and dry. Strawberries go in containers when they are picked. They are then packed in boxes called flats. The flats are taken to coolers. Coolers are a type of refrigerator. They reduce the temperature of the strawberries quickly. This helps them last longer. It is important for the berries to continue to remain cool until they reach their destination. This is why they are transferred from the coolers into refrigerated storage containers. These containers have sensors on them. The sensors can send a message if the temperature goes too high. That is how they are sent to stores. Trucks take California’s strawberries all across the country. Planes fly crops like strawberries around the world. There are distribution companies that specialize in selling berries all over the world.

Farm to Market Process

The farmer covers the earth with special fabric and plants the strawberry plants through the fabric. The farmer waters and tends the strawberry plants.

The workers pick the strawberries and package them.

The farmer sends flats of strawberries to coolers to chill them quickly.

The strawberries are transferred to refrigerated containers.

The distributors transport the strawberries to stores.

The workers in stores put strawberries out for the customers to buy.

title: Your Perspective
text:
Your perspective is the way you see things. It is what you think about things. Everyone has a different perspective. You can choose what perspective you want to have.

Your perspective can change when you get more information. You have your own perspective, or ideas, about education, sports, friends, nature, and everything else.

You develop your perspective because of the people around you. Your family can influence the way you see things. Your friends can influence what you think is important or popular.

Talking about different perspectives with others can be a great learning opportunity and a chance to show respect to your peers and their perspectives. Asking questions and collecting information can help you understand your perspective.

title: Exploration and Dividing a Hemisphere
text:
During the Renaissance, trade became very important to the economy of Europe. The coastal city-states of Genoa and Venice had the funds to produce well-made ships. Many of the people living in these places became sailors and started traveling the Mediterranean Sea. As trade increased, a desire to trade with East Asia also increased. However, for many centuries, the only way to get goods from East Asia was through the traders of Southwest Asia.

Traders from the Ottoman Empire in Southwest Asia knew the trade routes of the Silk Road. They also studied the currents and winds of the Arabian Sea that could take their ships to India and China. When these traders sold East Asian goods to European traders, they charged high prices to compensate for the money they spent on trading expeditions. Then, in the mid-1400s, the Ottoman Empire shut down trade with China, cutting off European access to goods from East Asia. European governments then began to put more money into developing tools, gathering supplies, and sending explorers to find new trade routes to East Asia.

Historians call this time period the Age of Exploration. Europeans eventually found ways to reach East Asia. While on a quest to find a western route to East Asia, Christopher Columbus encountered the Americas. These explorations in Asia and the Americas would have both positive and negative consequences for the people during that time period and beyond.

Because of exploration, Europeans enjoyed new foods, such as sugar, lemons, tobacco, chocolate, potatoes, and turkey. Some of these foods came from Asia; others came from the Americas. Many Europeans gained wealth, knowledge, and resources from the new lands that their explorers journeyed to.

However, the Age of Exploration also led to conflict and other negative outcomes. Europeans began claiming territory in the Americas and Asia as colonies. The act of colonization, or taking over an area of land for their own, became common practice. Conflicts developed over land and resources.

European, Asian, and African diseases were introduced to the Americas by European explorers. The Indigenous peoples did not have immunity against these illnesses. Entire groups of people disappeared, along with their cultures, knowledge, and histories. Archaeologists and historians are working to learn more about these groups and record their histories and stories.

title: Essential Question
text: How does colonization change a region's people, culture, and geography?

title: Trust
text: Being honest helps people trust you. They believe you will make good choices. They can believe the things you say.

title: Technology of Exploration
text:
There were many tools that made European exploration possible. Funds, like those that Prince Henry the Navigator provided, were vital to exploration. The caravel, a smaller, faster sailing ship, also made traveling on the open ocean possible. However, other tools were crucial to the Age of Exploration.

Cartographic Improvements

Accurate maps were not very common in the Middle Ages. Prior to the invention of the printing press, all maps were hand-drawn, which made them very difficult to create. During the Renaissance, cartography took on new importance. The Greek scholar Ptolemy studied cartography and developed a grid with lines called latitude and longitude. These could be used to help travelers determine their exact location on the globe. Latitude and longitude lines were tools used by Renaissance-era cartographers to create better maps.

As European explorers traveled to new areas of the world, they made maps to chronicle where they had been, stake claims for their governments, and help others travel back to these destinations. In 1569, Gerardus Mercator innovated cartography even further by creating a map that flattened out the globe. The longitude and latitude lines on these maps were straight. This flat map was a tool that allowed sailors to plot their destinations on fixed lines. It made traveling across oceans easier.

Astrolabe

For hundreds of years, people have looked at objects in the night sky to help keep track of where they were. Looking at the night sky and knowing where the stars are helps a person on the ground know which direction to travel. For example, the North Star will tell you which direction is north, no matter where you are. Once explorers know which way is north, they can use other scientific tools to pinpoint their location, chart their courses, and sail all the way around the world.

One of the most important tools navigators used during the Age of Exploration was the astrolabe. Sailors used astrolabes to travel across wide-open seas by measuring the latitude of a ship at sea. Using the sun during the day and the North Star at night, sailors would point the indicator on the astrolabe at their chosen celestial object (the sun or the North Star). Then, they would read the dial to determine their latitude. They compared their measurements to a table of latitudes that told them where they were.

Sextant

Sextants, like astrolabes, measure angles to determine the latitude of a ship. However, they also measure longitude. They measure the distance between the horizon and a celestial body, such as the sun or moon. That measurement is matched with the measurements on a table, which identifies a location’s latitude and longitude. Knowing both longitude and latitude gave explorers an exact location. Sextants are still used by sailors today.

Compass

One of the earliest navigational tools was the magnetic compass. It was first invented in China over 1,000 years ago. Europeans learned about the compass from the Arabs, who had originally learned of this invention from the Chinese in about 1000 or 1100 C.E. To use the first compasses, sailors rubbed an iron needle on a rock called a lodestone. The needle then became magnetized. The needle was then stuck into a piece of straw or something else that would float and placed in a cup of water. The needle would always point north. The compass did not pinpoint location, but it helped sailors know which direction they were traveling.

title: Mistakes
text: Sometimes, we do things the wrong way. This is called a mistake. Mistakes happen to everyone. Mistakes can be fixed.

title: Spanish Colonization
text:
The first Spanish colonists were mostly men. They came to the colonies to be conquistadors, hoping to gain land and wealth through conquest. The first Spanish settlements were on an island that Columbus named Hispañola. This island is located in the Caribbean and is the home of the modern-day countries of Haiti and the Dominican Republic. The native people from the island were called the Taíno, and they called their island home Quisqueya.

Because the Taíno were the first Native Peoples to have Europeans live in constant, close proximity, they suffered terribly from the diseases that the Spanish brought. The first Spanish colonists also forced the Taíno people to work for them in the encomienda system. Spanish writer Bartolomé de las Casas lived on Hispañola during the first wave of colonization. He estimated that 80–90 percent of the Taíno people died within the first 50 years of Spanish colonization.

Early Spanish colonization focused on the areas of major conquest: the Caribbean, the Aztec Empire, and the Inca Empire. The Caribbean islands that were conquered by the Spanish were often called the West Indies because Columbus mistakenly thought he had reached islands on the outskirts of India. The former Aztec Empire was called “New Spain” by the Spanish conquistadors. “Peru” was the name the Spanish gave the Inca Empire. This name most likely came into being when the Spanish misunderstood a Quechua word.

During much of the Spanish colonial period, only men migrated to the Americas. They often had relationships with and married native women. Because of these relationships, the population of the Spanish colonies grew to be mostly people of mixed Spanish and Indigenous heritage.

The Spanish colonies eventually extended into Florida and the southwestern portion of the modern-day United States. Spanish colonies also spread throughout all of Central America and everywhere in South America, except for Brazil. The Portuguese claimed Brazil as their own colony.

title: English Colonization
text:
English colonization allowed English citizens to start new lives across the sea. Some colonists were

motivated to make money and gain a higher status in society. Other colonists came to practice their religion freely and avoid persecution. Many others sought the chance to get land of their own, which was very difficult in Europe. Regardless of the motivations behind their decisions, all colonists came as a result of a charter.

A charter was a legal document given by the king of England. It gave land to a company or individual to create a colony. The charter included the geographic location for the colony. It also laid out the terms between the king and the government in the colony. The charter gave each colonist the rights and privileges of an English subject. The purpose of the colony was also described in the charter. Finally, the charter detailed the conditions for paying taxes to the king. The charter was the deed, or document of ownership, for the colony, its constitution, and the financial contract between the king of England and the colony.

Charters provided two important things. First, they guaranteed the colonists the same rights as citizens in England. This included the right of representation in government. Second, the charter allowed for an elected legislature, as long as the laws the legislature made did not go against the laws of England.

People who wanted to start a colony had different options. One option was to form a company. A company was made up of investors who provided ships, tools, food, water, and protection for the people who would move to America. Wages for the colonists were also paid with the investors’ money. The colonists were required to meet the goals of the charter. They worked for the company and lived by the rules of the charter. The colonists remained the king’s subjects but lived and worked across the ocean. They worked to provide the company with products such as furs, lumber, and agricultural products. The company would then sell the products back in England for profit. These profits were used to pay the company’s investors and the king. The colonies that were established by a company charter included Virginia, Plymouth, Massachusetts Bay, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Delaware.

At this time in England, there was great conflict over what church a person attended on Sundays. An official state church had been created that every person in England was supposed to attend. In colonies, the king’s people weren’t there to enforce that law. Colonists could attend the church they wanted to instead of the church the king said they must attend. The colonists had more freedom to choose what religion to practice. This freedom was included in the charter.

Another form of charter created a proprietorship. In this case, the king gave a charter to a person as a reward for services to the king. The person given the charter was called a proprietor, meaning “owner.” The charter gave the proprietor all the rights to govern the colony and choose the purpose for the colony and the conditions for paying taxes to the crown. The colonies that were established by proprietors included New York, New Hampshire, Maryland, North Carolina, New Jersey, South Carolina, and Pennsylvania.

Some of the colonies established by companies and proprietors later became royal colonies. The king rewrote their charters so that all of the profits and authority became his. These royal colonies included New Hampshire, New York, New Jersey, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

title: Portuguese Colonization
text:
The Portuguese had a great empire that they started building in the 1420s. They created trade centers from West Africa, around the Cape of Good Hope, to Asia and into South America. This allowed them to become one of the first intercontinental empires when they were able to create Portuguese Brazil.

Vasco da Gama was the third son of a minor nobleman in Portugal. In 1492, he earned a name for himself by seizing French vessels that had violated Portuguese shipping rights. After this success, the king chose da Gama to lead an expedition to East Asia to set up trade between Portugal and Asia.

In July 1497, da Gama set out with four ships. By January 1498, they had reached Mozambique, an island off of the eastern coast of Africa. The da Gama expedition spent an extended period of time there resting and recovering from scurvy. Scurvy is a disease that sailors often developed from not getting enough vitamin C. Sailors got this disease from not having enough fresh fruits or vegetables on their ships.

The trade routes, currents, and winds on the eastern side of Africa had been known and traveled for hundreds of years by Muslim traders. The Portuguese used this knowledge to reach India in May 1498. The expedition had achieved its goal. Da Gama returned to Portugal but later returned to India on two more voyages. This led to the creation of Portuguese trading posts from East Africa all the way to Japan.

Da Gama’s route around Africa and into Asia played a crucial role in Pedro Álvares Cabral sailing too far west and accidentally finding Brazil. The winds off the coast of Africa blew Cabral off course, and he and his crew landed in Brazil. After this discovery, an explorer named Gonçalo Coelho led an expedition into Brazil’s coastline to discover more about the country. The Treaty of Tordesillas gave Portugal their own sphere of influence in Brazil, and they were able to claim it as their own. Florentine Amerigo Vespucci also visited Brazil and was amazed by the sights he saw. He wrote the following description of what he saw:

This land is very delightful, and covered with an infinite number of green trees and very big ones which never lose their foliage, and through the year yield the sweetest aromatic perfumes and produce an infinite variety of fruit, gratifying to the taste and healthful to the body … and the fields produce herbs and flowers and many sweet and good roots, which are so marvelous … that I fancied myself to be near the terrestrial paradise.

Brazil had many natural resources that Portugal utilized to create goods and products to send back to Europe for a profit. Brazil became the largest sugar producer within a few decades of Portugal colonizing, or taking over, the area. It started with 60 sugar mills in 1570, and within 75 years, there were 350 sugar mills. Brazil also had a large timber industry that took advantage of the hardwoods for lumber and the dye that could be produced from the brazilwoods. The hardwoods were used to create everything from tables to violins.

The colonization of Brazil was similar to that of the English settlement in North America. A group of several hundred colonists came to the coast of Brazil to build different settlements. Portugal set up “captaincies.” This gave grants to Portuguese nobles and their workers to develop land to farm on. Many other colonists from Portugal moved to Brazil in order to practice the religion they chose.

title: French Colonization
text:
French colonization of the Western Hemisphere started in 1523 when the first expedition was led

by Giovanni da Verrazano. The goal of the French expeditions was to find a route that gave them access to the vast resources of Asia. France also wanted to colonize areas of the Western Hemisphere, as many of their European counterparts had already done. France wanted to open new centers of trade and use the natural resources in conquered areas for the benefit of France.

On the first expedition, da Verrazano was able to survey, or outline and describe, the coast of North America. He explored the North and South Carolina shoreline and went up to Cape Breton Island. It wasn’t until Jacques Cartier was sent out by French King François I that da Verrazano suggested France colonize the new territory and call it “New France.” This idea allowed France to send multiple explorers to set up new colonies throughout the Americas.

Many of the expeditions took place in the northern part of the Western Hemisphere, in present-day Canada and New England. French explorers worked to set up different trading colonies along rivers and at the mouth of bays. However, each of these sites were eventually abandoned, and the colonists moved back to France.

When Samuel de Champlain set sail in 1608, he was sent with the goal of setting up a colony

within the territory that had been previously explored, along with finding a route to Asia. As he did this, he had the opportunity to observe and describe many of the areas of present-day Nova Scotia and the Saint Lawrence Gulf and River. He wrote in his journal:

Their settled habitation, the till- age and the beautiful trees, gave me the impression that the air there is milder and better than that where we passed the winter, and than that of other places on the coast. The forests in the interior are very light, but, nevertheless, consist of oaks, beeches, ashes and young elms. In wet places there are a great many willows.

As Champlain moved inland, he knew that he needed to set up a location that would be easy for trade and exploration and a good starting point to build up for New France. He found the spot and noted it in his journal, saying:

… on that river, at which place I had all the goods unloaded, with the men, laborers and artisans, to go up the river to find a place convenient and suitable for a settlement. When I had found the narrowest place in the river, which the natives call Quebec.

Once Quebec was founded, Champlain turned his attention to the interior of the continent, hoping to discover more territory to colonize. This led him to the Great Lakes region and led many other explorers on unofficial expeditions to those areas.

South of the Great Lakes, French explorer Louis Jolliet was put in charge of surveying and describing the “great river” that many Indigenous tribes called the Michisspi, or Mississippi River. He went as far as the Arkansas River and realized that the river kept going south. He took this opportunity to turn around and go back. Jolliet went on to explore other riverways and areas of Canada.

It wasn’t until 1673 that another French explorer, Cavelier de La Salle, reached the mouth of the Mississippi River. He established a colony there, calling it “Louisiana” after King Louis XIV of France. The French went on to set up colonial centers in Mobile and New Orleans. These settlements were used not only for trade but as a way to control the Mississippi River.

The trading centers of Mobile and New Orleans were not the only areas that France focused on. Québec and Montréal also served as areas for trade and exploration. The fur trade became the primary resource for New France, as the colonists were able to send fur pelts back to France to supply hat and clothing companies.

France then went on to establish settlements in the Caribbean. Hispaniola was called Saint-Domingue, and it had one of the richest sugar plantations. This allowed France to colonize and take over many other islands throughout the Caribbean, including the Lesser Antilles, Grenada, and St. Croix.

title: The Effects of Conquest
text:
The Native Peoples of the Western Hemisphere met their wants and needs using resources from the land around them. They had vibrant societies and extensive trade routes. They had art, history, and protection for their communities. They had government and religion. They fed their families by hunting animals and gathering berries, nuts, and fruits. They cultivated crops of corn, squash, beans, tomatoes, potatoes, and some grains. They created tools from the resources around them. They traveled by walking or by using boats on the waterways.

The Europeans used natural resources to create manufactured goods. Like the Native Peoples of the Americas, they also had vibrant societies and extensive trade networks. They had art, history, and protection for their communities. They had government and religion. They fed their families by farming and going to markets. Europeans domesticated animals to keep on their farms. This meant they didn’t have to hunt for food. They had horses to help with the work on the farms and at the markets. They cultivated grain crops of wheat, oats, and barley. Europeans developed different modes of transportation. They used wagons and carts on land and ships on the sea. They manufactured goods out of metal and wood. They used many of their resources to help them explore new places across the ocean.

When these two societies met, there were intentional and unintentional consequences. The two groups traded ideas for the design of tools and transportation. The Europeans brought domesticated animals, such as pigs, chickens, and horses, with them on their ships. The people of the Western Hemisphere gave the Europeans plants, food, and precious metals. Sign language and gestures were used to help the two cultures communicate with each other.

Tolerance of differences between the two cultures could have expanded the positive exchanges. However, the Europeans were not tolerant of the differences they encountered. They believed the peoples of the Americas were inferior because their ways were different. Intolerance caused conflict and the captivity and deaths of many Native Peoples.

The introduction of domesticated animals in the Americas caused an imbalance in the ecosystem. Pigs were turned loose to forage in the forests. The pigs multiplied until there were so many they depleted the vegetation. Other animals that depended on the same vegetation had nothing to eat.

The horse was a new animal to the Western Hemisphere. The horse quickly became popular to help the people of the Western Hemisphere in their everyday lives. They used horses for transportation and work. Horses became a valuable trade resource. The horses quickly multiplied. Descendants of these horses are still found on the East Coast and in the western lands of the United States.

The most deadly exchange was unintentional. The Europeans brought disease with them. They had developed immunity to many bacteria and viruses over the centuries. The people of the Americas, however, had never been exposed to such deadly germs. Smallpox, tuberculosis, influenza, and other strains of disease were easily transported by unsuspecting people. Historians estimate that disease killed 90 percent of the native population within 150 years.

However, the Maya, Inca, Aztec, and Native Peoples of North America survived. Descendants of the American Indians, Maya, Inca, and Aztec still live in and near the places where their ancient civilizations and tribes began. Today, nearly 10 million Maya live in Central America, and there are many small villages in Peru where only Quechua (the Inca language) is still spoken. Tens of thousands of Mexican people can trace their family lines back to the ancient Aztec people. The conquests of the Western Hemisphere did not completely destroy the culture or the spirit of these ancient civilizations.

title: Essential Question
text: What lasting effects of exploration and colonization do we see today?

title: Advances in Agriculture
text:
There is evidence of people living in the Americas as early as 12,000 to 15,000 years ago. These early Americans found many food sources in their natural environment. They also developed new food sources over time. Later, Europeans arrived in the Americas. They learned to grow new foods from American Indians. They also shared their knowledge with native tribes.

There were many different agricultural systems in the Americas, and each was suited to its environment. Southern Canada is very different from the tropical forests of South America. There are the towering Andes Mountains in South America that are very different from the river valleys of what is today the eastern United States.

Native Peoples had a variety of food options. They grew corn — lots of corn. They often grew beans and squash along with corn. They called these plants "The Three Sisters.” They also grew many other plants, depending on where they lived. Crops included pumpkins, peppers, tomatoes, and potatoes. They also grew cacao, coffee, sunflowers, avocados, peanuts, quinoa, and cotton. Some raised llamas, alpacas, guinea pigs, and ducks.

In addition to growing food, many Native Peoples hunted wild animals and caught fish and shellfish. They also gathered wild plants for both food and medicine. They had different methods of farming. Native Peoples in North America often planted fields of corn. They grew beans, squash, sunflowers, and pumpkins in smaller gardens beside rivers and streams. The Maya and the Aztec had large empires with lots of people to feed, so they used irrigation systems to help them grow a lot of food. In the Andes, the Inca planted crops in a series of terraces that climbed up steep slopes.

When colonists arrived in the Americas, they brought their own farming knowledge with them. Not all of it was helpful. For example, the Puritans came from the south of England, where the soil is deep, soft, and full of nutrients. The soil in New England, where the Pilgrims settled, is very different. It is shallow, sandy, and stony. Crops like wheat and barley that grew well in England did not thrive along the coast of Massachusetts.

Native Peoples were sometimes willing to share their knowledge. This was fortunate for European settlers. Tisquantum, also called Squanto, was very helpful. He taught the Pilgrims how to plant native crops like corn, how to catch fish in Massachusetts Bay, and how to find shellfish along the shore. You have probably heard the story of the first Thanksgiving. In November 1621, the Pilgrims celebrated their first harvest. They were joined by the Wampanoag. The feast lasted for three days, and there was plenty of food to go around. The Pilgrims were thankful they had learned to survive in New England. They would not have done so without the help of the Wampanoag and their knowledge of agriculture.

The diets of the Native Peoples of the Americas did benefit in some ways from the arrival of European colonists. Native farmers traded with the Europeans for peach and watermelon seeds. They were introduced to apples. They also learned how to use horses to plow fields for planting. Native Peoples also traded with Europeans for steel tools.

Food from the Americas quickly spread around the world. Coffee became very popular in Europe. Pineapples, chili peppers, potatoes, and avocados made it into kitchens in far-off places, and people everywhere fell in love with chocolate.

Over time, Native Peoples lost most of their lands to European settlers. Farms got bigger, and more areas began producing food. Farmers replaced animal labor with machines, and they grew more food. More food allowed Europeans to support larger settlements, so their population grew. However, while farming changed, many of the foods stayed the same. Foods from the Americas are still enjoyed by people all over the world. Think about your favorite foods. Do you know where they come from?

title: Piracy and Privateers
text:
Kings and queens in Europe weren’t just excited about explorers heading out to the Americas. They were excited about explorers coming back. Their return meant new foods, goods, and gold. The more land their country claimed, the more resources could be brought to market. European countries wanted goods from the Americas.

Spain sent explorers first. Once the Spanish started to conquer land and peoples, they set up regular trade routes for their ships. The ships followed known routes. It didn’t take long for others to identify the ships and steal their cargo. Other Europeans began arming ships with cannons and their crews with weapons. Pirates threatened Spanish ships full of goods on their way back to Spain and stole their cargo.

Someone who attacks and robs a ship at sea is called a pirate. Pirates became a threat to merchant ships traveling between Europe and the Americas. The small islands in the Caribbean became the ideal place to hide stolen goods. Pirates became skilled at stealing cargo. The pirates of the Caribbean were ruthless in the pursuit of treasure and goods. Pirates were pursued by government authorities. When caught, they were punished with death.

There was rivalry and competition between the governments in Europe over the resources in the Americas. Due to this competition, monarchs saw an opportunity to use pirates. Pirates already had ships out on the sea and were fighting with their rival countries. The monarchs of England, France, the Netherlands, and Spain began granting special licenses to certain sea captains and their crews. Their job was to attack ships that belonged to enemy countries. That special license was called a letter of marque. A letter of marque made a pirate a privateer. Unlike pirates, privateers were protected from punishment. They could legally sell captured goods. Privateers would raid ships in the name of their country, then split the profits with the monarch. Privateering also helped spread each government’s influence.

title: Religious Conflict
text:
In the 16th century, there was conflict in Europe over religion. The conflict was about who was the authority for Christianity and the leader of the Roman Catholic Church. The Catholic Church was the only Christian denomination in Europe at this time. The Catholic Church was organized with a central leader: the pope. The pope was the religious leader for all Christians. All Christian governments obeyed the directions of the pope. This gave the pope more authority than the monarchs.

The king of England, Henry VIII, did not think anyone should have greater authority in England than the king. If the pope could tell the king what to do, then who was really the authority in England? This line of thinking led others to question who was the leader of the Christian church: the pope, the king, or the people?

The Catholic Church had rituals and rules of worship for people to follow. Many people began to think some of these were unnecessary and even wrong. They wanted the Catholic Church to be reformed. Some people began to turn to new beliefs and practices. They protested the Catholic Church. These people became known as Protestants.

The pope wanted everyone to be Catholic. Many Catholic monarchs felt the same way. The Catholic monarchs made laws to force their people to be Catholic. Those who disobeyed were persecuted.

Like the Catholic monarchs, Protestant monarchs also made laws to force people to be Protestant. Those who disobeyed were persecuted. The persecution between Catholics and Protestants increased the religious competition and rivalry between the countries of Europe.

title: Demand in Europe
text:
Spain sent explorers across the Atlantic to open trade with India and earn money. Finding the Americas instead had an even bigger effect on Europe’s economy. As new goods came back from the Americas, people rushed to buy them.

At first, most things brought back from the Americas were luxury goods for the rich. Europeans brought back gold and silver. Wealthy buyers in Europe also liked furs from American animals. American crops like tobacco also became popular. Many people wanted to try the new goods, and as a result, prices grew high. Sugarcane, originally from Asia, was introduced in the hot climate of the Caribbean, where it grew very well. People in Europe were willing to pay high prices for sugar. High demand made sugarcane producers in the Americas want to increase their supply.

Some American crops were only popular with certain people or in certain places. Wealthy Europeans did not like potatoes at first. However, potatoes were a good food because they had a lot of calories and grew underground. This kept them from being destroyed by bad weather. Slowly, potatoes spread to many countries. Potatoes never had high prices, like sugar did. As people learned how to prepare and cook them for meals, they increased in production.

Europeans did not make corn a popular purchase. Many Europeans used corn as an ingredient in other dishes and used it to feed animals. Corn was accepted in Asia and Africa as an import from Europe.

The demand for different American goods in Europe had an impact on life in the Americas. The way land was divided, the way people worked, and even ideas about who had rights were all influenced by economic demand in European countries.

title: Sugar Production and the Slave Trade
text:
In the 1400s, Europe traded with Asia for sugar. People loved the taste of sugar and paid high prices for it. Sugar is produced from sugarcane. Sugarcane needs a warm environment to grow. It also needs lots of rain or good irrigation. Europe did not have the right climate to grow sugar, so they had to trade for it.

When European explorers came to the Americas, they found a warm, wet climate where sugarcane could grow. Sugarcane grew especially well on islands in the Caribbean Sea. European colonists realized sugarcane could become a cash crop. A cash crop is a crop people grow to sell and make money. This led to large areas of land being used to grow only one kind of cash crop. These large farms became known as plantations.

It took hard work to grow and harvest sugarcane. Sugarcane doesn’t produce seeds. Someone had to cut hard stalks into pieces by hand and then plant them. It was also difficult to get soft sugar out of the tough stalks. As plantation owners earned more money from sugar, they looked for ways to get cheap labor to plant, harvest, and process the sugar. They began enslaving Native peoples of the Caribbean, taking away their freedom and forcing them to do the work. When many died from European diseases or risked punishment to escape, plantation owners turned to the slave trade from Africa. Men, women, and children were kidnapped in Africa and taken to the Caribbean and South America. Enslaved Africans were sold to plantation owners and forced to work in harsh conditions without pay or freedom. In Europe, sugar became easier to buy as the supply increased. European plantation owners became very wealthy at the expense of enslaved people.

title: How Do I Feel?
text:
We all need to pay attention to how we feel. We call these feelings emotions. Everyone experiences different emotions at different times. Think of something that makes you feel happy. Think of something that makes you feel comfortable. What makes you feel happy and comfortable might not for someone else. Observing your own emotions helps you to understand yourself better. When we know how we are feeling, it helps us understand our own emotions. There are things you can do to help you manage your emotions positively.

Sometimes we feel more than one emotion at a time. When this happens, you can ask, "How do I feel?" and you can wonder why you feel that way. Listening to your body and the way you feel can help you identify your emotions.

title: African Enslavement
text:
Prince Henry the Navigator was a Portuguese duke. Although he was called the Navigator, he never actually went to sea. Prince Henry did control a large amount of money for an organization called the “Order of Christ.” This organization brought navigators and geographers together. They planned expeditions to unexplored regions along the Atlantic coast south of Portugal. They hired a sea captain named Bartolomeu Perestrello and his ship for their expeditions.

The early voyages sent Perestrello to the mid-Atlantic islands, such as Madeira and the Azores. These explorations were followed by routes along the west coast of Africa.

As a result of their exploration, the Portuguese began to colonize new areas. Beginning in 1445, the Azores rapidly filled with colonists. They developed a rich, sugar-producing colony. The sugar was exported to European markets. The Portuguese also established trading posts along the west coast of Africa.

These trading posts were used to trade Portuguese goods to traders in Africa. The Africans traded something that was in high demand by the Portuguese. This “product” was people. Men, women, and children were captured by the African traders and sold to the Portuguese as enslaved people. The enslaved captives were taken to sugar plantations on the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores. Many enslaved people were also taken to Spain and Portugal. By the mid-1550s, 10 percent of Portugal’s population was enslaved men, women, and children from Africa.

Exploration of the Americas created a new market where traders could sell enslaved Africans. The first recorded ship carrying 200 enslaved African people sailed to the Caribbean in 1525. Sold into a lifetime of enslavement, these people worked on sugar plantations. This early trade by Portuguese ships began the long, tragic system of bringing enslaved people across the Atlantic.

title: My Emotional Vocabulary
text: There are many words we can use to tell others how we are feeling. These words describe our emotions. Emotions can be lumped into five categories. They are "joy," "sadness," "anger," "fear," and "disgust." We use these vocabulary words to describe our feelings. We can use our emotional vocabulary to help others understand us. Emotional vocabulary also helps us understand others. Using the right words to label our feelings helps others know exactly how we feel.

title: Farm Article #4
text:
People have grown corn in North America for thousands of years. It is a very useful crop. Only one percent of the corn grown in the U.S. is for people to eat. The other 99 percent gets used for other things. Corn is used to meet many different types of needs. There are two basic types of corn. Corn grown for people to eat is called sweet corn. The corn grown to be used for making other products is called field corn. Sometimes we use corn whole, just as it is. We eat sweet corn right off the cob. Corn can be frozen or canned for later use. We use whole kernels of field corn to feed animals.

Most field corn gets processed, or changed to make it more usable. Then the processed corn becomes an ingredient used in making other products. It can be turned into ethanol fuel. It can be turned into a starch or a syrup. Cornstarch and corn syrup are added to many products. There are about 4,000 products in your grocery store with corn listed as an ingredient!

Planting: Farmers plant the type of corn that is good for popcorn.

Harvesting: The corn is picked by large tractors, and the kernels are removed from the husks. The husks can be fed to farm animals.

Storage: The corn kernels are stored in large silos. Farmers can store the kernels for up to five years. The temperature is monitored so that the kernels keep their moisture for popping.

Tested: Popcorn is test-popped in the factory to be sure that the kernels are ready.

Sorting: The corn is cleaned and sorted by the size of the kernels.

Packaging: After the kernels are sorted, they are put into large bags for shipping to the businesses that ordered them.

Shipping: The corn is shipped to its destination in large trucks. Some of these destinations are places that repackage the popcorn into smaller bags to sell in stores.

Selling: Workers pop the popcorn kernels in theaters for us to enjoy with movies. Popcorn is also sold in stores to enjoy at home.

title: Communicating My Emotions
text:
Talking to other people can help you identify how you feel. Your thoughts can be affected by the people in your life. Your peers and family can impact your thoughts and emotions. Even media can influence you. It can help people understand how you feel when you talk about your emotions. Communicate how you feel honestly. When you understand your own emotions, you can be kind. You can also be more understanding of others.

You can communicate how you are feeling with your body language. You can communicate with your facial expressions. Learn and use emotional vocabulary words to help you. Using words to tell others how you feel is helpful.

title: Observe Emotions in Others
text:
Recognizing how other people feel is important. You need to be aware of what others around you are feeling. When you know how others are feeling, you can show them empathy. Empathy is the ability to understand and share somebody else's feelings. Showing empathy helps you create strong friendships.

To understand how people are feeling, we follow some steps:

First, when we talk to others, we watch their faces and their body language. We listen to the tone of their voice.

Next, we infer, or make a guess, about their feelings based on what we see and hear.

Then, we ask questions. If you see someone smiling, you can infer that they are feeling happy. You could ask them, “Are you having a good day?”

title: Self-Regulating My Emotions
text:
Understanding our feelings comes with responsibility. We have a choice in how we show our emotions. The words we use should tell people how we feel but not hurt them. Remember that emotions are there to help us.

Review the following example scenarios. Think of an appropriate way to show your feelings in each scenario.

You are angry because you didn't make the team.

You are happy that your basketball team won a game.

You are sad that your family is moving to a new house.

title: Overcome Emotional Obstacles
text:
It is important to let yourself feel your emotions. However, the way we act can sometimes be hurtful to the people around us. It is helpful to breathe and think before you act on your emotions. This helps you respond appropriately to your emotions.

The media you view can impact your thinking and behavior. The people in your life can too. If you view media that shows people being unkind to one another, you may think that is appropriate. Look for examples in your life of people who treat others with kindness. When you see others being respectful, you have a good example to follow.

You can train yourself to overcome emotional obstacles (difficulties). You can train yourself to "push pause" and think before you act. If you see someone being unkind, you can “push pause” and take a breath. Next, think about how to respond. Instead of yelling the first words you think of, "push pause" to help you choose your response.

title: Choose Your Response
text: Control means to manage what happens. Some things you cannot control. Some things you can control. You can control what you do and say. You can choose how you respond to being worried.

title: Respect Your Body
text:
Imagine you own the world’s greatest treasure. You’d take care of it and protect it, right? Well, your body is the most precious thing you’ll ever own, so treat it like the treasure it is!

One important part of caring for your body is keeping it clean. This includes bathing, washing and combing your hair, wearing clean clothes, washing your hands, and brushing your teeth. Personal hygiene is especially important as your body matures.

title: Keeping Your Body Safe
text:
Every body is unique, and every body is good. Every body deserves to be taken care of. You can take care of your body by keeping it safe. You can protect your body from common injuries like falls, sunburns, and bike accidents. Be smart about your choices. Wear sunscreen when you are outdoors, and wear a helmet when you are riding a bike or scooter. Use extra caution when you are around things that could easily cause you harm, like fire, guns, deep or fast water, and moving cars. Do your best to make choices that are healthy and safe for your body.

How can you keep your body safe?

How can you keep your body safe from the sun?

How can you prevent illnesses like colds and flus?

How can you prevent injuries on the road or sidewalk?

Who can you turn to for help if your body does get hurt? Name at least three people who could help you.

title: Move It!
text: Moving your body gets your heart pumping, makes you stronger, and gives you more energy. It can also put you in a great mood! There are lots of different ways to exercise. Sign up for a team sport, like basketball or soccer. Turn on some music and dance. Try lots of different activities, even if you don’t think you will be very good at them. Moving is fun!

title: Choose Your Attitude
text:
Attitude is how you choose to feel about life. Your attitude is not the same as your emotions and feelings. Let’s talk about the difference.

Things happen around you that may affect your emotions. Someone pushed Lita in the mud. She felt embarrassed and sad. Ben got a good grade on his math test. He felt excited and proud of himself. Attitude is how you choose to act and talk about things. You can have a good, hard-working attitude, no matter what happens to you.

Let’s look at what happens to Hattie as she goes about her day with a happy, hard-working attitude.

Hattie went to the kitchen before school. Her dad had made her favorite breakfast. She thought, “Today is going to be a great day!”

Hattie missed the bus. She felt anxious about being late. She thought, “That’s okay! It's not too far. If I walk quickly, I think I can still make it on time.”

Hattie’s science teacher handed their tests back. Hattie didn’t do as well as she had hoped. She felt disappointed in herself. She thought, “If I study more, I’m sure I can do better on the next test. I’ll talk to my teacher after class to see if there is anything I can do to improve this score.”

Hattie’s day was not perfect. There were some good things and some not-so-good things. Some of the not-so-good things caused her to feel unpleasant emotions, like anxiety and disappointment.

What kind of attitude did Hattie have today? Underline the evidence in the article that supports your claim.

title: Make a Plan
text: When you feel sad or worried, you can make a plan. You can talk to someone about your feelings. You can plan an activity you enjoy. You can ask for help.

title: What Is Conflict?
text: Conflict is when you disagree with someone. Sometimes, conflict makes people feel upset.

title: Focus on What Matters
text:
When you focus on something, it means you give that thing all of your attention. What you focus on can affect your perspective and your attitude.

Have you ever taken a picture with a camera? When you look through the camera lens, you can zoom in on specific things. This is like your focus.

Sometimes we zoom in or focus on things that don’t help us. Focusing on things like popularity, money, or someone who has a negative attitude will make it difficult to have a positive attitude and perspective. Social media, movies, and TV often send messages that impact how you feel about yourself or others.

You are responsible for your own health and well-being. When media, peers, or other sources steer you toward focusing on negative or unhealthy things, it can hinder healthy decision-making skills.

Changing your focus can help. You can shift the way you use your time. You can focus on your art, talents, positive friends or family, education, or goals. Focusing on these things can help you grow.

You can then be an influence for good to your peers. You can help them focus on the things that matter most.

What things can you focus on to improve your health and well-being?

title: Who Has Conflicts?
text: Friends will not always agree. Families will not always agree. Conflict is normal.

title: What Are Solutions?
text: Solutions help solve conflicts. There are always solutions to conflicts.

title: Help Everyone Be Happy
text:
Try a solution! A solution can help everyone feel happy. Solutions can be:

Sharing

Saying, “I’m sorry”

Choosing a new game

Asking a teacher for help

title: Positive Picks
text:
As young children, we all looked to the people around us to show us “right” from “wrong.” If our parents used certain language in the house, we got the message that it was okay for us to say these things as well. If people we looked up to smoke or drank alcohol, we may have believed that we could earn their respect or friendship if we did the same, even if it hurt us.

We were and still are looking to our environment to show us the appropriate ways to act in order to be accepted by others. Sometimes our peers’ behaviors inspire us to be kind, generous, and compassionate to the people around us. When we see our friends volunteering, helping other students with homework, or playing sports, we may be encouraged to do these things, too. However, we may see others being cruel, rude, or spiteful. If we are constantly around people like this, we may get the idea that this behavior is okay.

Think about the people in your environment. How have they inspired or encouraged you to behave?

Now explore the ways you may have inspired them with your actions. How can your actions affect someone else’s well-being?

title: Attitude of Gratitude
text:
How often do you say “thank you”? Hopefully, you say it many times each day. Saying “thank you” is a great way to show gratitude. Gratitude means you are thankful for something. It means you appreciate something someone does for you.

Say “thank you” to a parent or guardian who makes you a meal. Say “thank you” to your teacher for teaching you. Say “thank you” to your friend for inviting you to their birthday party or for helping you with an assignment.

Showing gratitude changes your brain in positive ways. It builds protective forces in the neurobiology of your brain by producing happy hormones. These hormones help your brain regulate your survival functions, like sleep and even your appetite.

What things are you grateful for?

title: Letting Go of the Bad
text:
Bad things can happen to anyone. When something bad happens to you, you can take time to feel and deal with your emotions. Process your sadness, frustration, guilt, or whatever other challenging emotions you feel. After you have experienced and understood your emotions, you need to take an important step in order to be happy. You need to let go.

Letting go of a bad experience or challenge can help you feel better. Letting go doesn’t mean you forget all about the experience. It’s good to remember your growth and lessons learned during hard times. When you let go of hard things in your past, it means you won’t let it affect you and your perspective, or your attitude, anymore.

These ideas can help you “let go” of negativity:

Write your feelings in a journal. Once you have written them down, allow yourself to let them go.

Forgive someone, if necessary.

Apologize, if necessary.

Shift your focus. Stop thinking about your challenge and focus on a solution.

Keep a positive perspective.

Recite positive affirmations, like “I can do this” and “I am strong and smart.”

title: Ask Questions
text: When you get information, you can ask questions. Think about what you know. What questions will you ask?

title: Search For Clues
text: Sometimes, our thoughts are wrong. Sometimes, our thoughts are right. Think about what you see and experience. You can find clues to help you know what is best.

title: What Is the Answer?
text: Sometimes, there is more than one right answer. Sometimes, there is more than one wrong answer. It is important to think.

title: Good Citizenship
text:
A citizen is a person who is part of a group or society. Citizens usually have certain rights or abilities and specific rules to follow as a result of being part of that group. The most common use of the word “citizen” refers to the country that you legally live in. This is a very important type of citizenship. As citizens of the United States, individuals have specific rights they are entitled to and must follow specific laws.

On a larger scale, everyone on the Earth is a citizen of the world. As such, we all have rights as humans. These are usually referred to as human rights. Some of these rights include life, liberty, work, education, and freedom from slavery. Every person living on the Earth is entitled to these rights.

On a smaller scale, citizenship could refer to your place in your community, your classroom, and even your family. As a citizen of these groups, you have certain responsibilities and expectations.

title: You Can Learn From Mistakes
text: Everyone makes mistakes. Mistakes help you learn. They help you grow.

title: Listening and Speaking
text: Communication has two basic parts. Listening is when you hear and observe what others say. Speaking is sharing your ideas with others. Communication helps you take care of your health and wellness.

title: Communicate Calmly
text:
There are different ways to let people know what you need and want. At school, you raise your hand to communicate that you have a question. You ask for food when you are hungry.

Which of these communicates a healthy and helpful way to communicate what you need?

Yelling: I can't find my socks!

Calmly: Can you help me find my socks?

Throwing a toy: How come she got an ice cream cone?

Raising a hand: I need some help figuring this out.

Grumpy: I don't get it!

Frustrated: I feel frustrated. Can you help me?

title: Getting Help
text: Asking for help is an important thing to do. Asking for help when you need it takes courage. Getting help when you need it can keep you safe.

title: Who Can I Ask for Help?
text:
For small problems, ask a:

friend

teacher

family member

For big problems or an emergency:

Call 911

Ask a police officer

Ask an adult you trust

title: Communicate Your Needs
text:
Every person’s body needs things at different times. You can take care of many of your needs. Match the need on the left with how these people communicate their needs on the right.

Cameron's stomach growls because he is hungry.

He asks his older sister if she will make him some pasta.

Gina feels thirsty.

She gets her water bottle from under her desk.

Aleki feels sick to his stomach.

He raises his hand to see if he can call his stepdad.

Alana feels dizzy. She thinks there might be something wrong with her insulin pump.

She goes to her teacher right away to ask for help.

Miguel feels tired before bedtime.

He brushes his teeth and gets in bed early.

title: Practice Makes Perfect
text: You can practice being brave by asking for help with small things. You can then be brave when asking for help with big things. Practice helps you overcome your fears.

title: Respecting Rights
text: Everyone has rights. As a human being, you have human rights. As a citizen of the United States, you have the rights to freedom of speech, freedom of religion, and many more. In your classroom, you have the right to access materials and to ask questions. You have the right to express your own opinions. Knowing and protecting your rights is only part of being a good citizen. It is also important that you respect and protect the rights of others. You can do this by allowing people to share their ideas and opinions. What else can you do to respect the rights of those around you?

title: Doing Your Part
text:
One aspect of being a good citizen is doing your part. As a citizen of the United States, you can do your part by voting when you are old enough and being educated about what’s happening in the country. You can also volunteer for service opportunities in your community, get involved in youth activities, and obey the law.

Some people choose to do their part by giving back. Giving back might be donating your old toys or clothes or donating money or time to good causes. Some people choose to donate blood or plasma at blood drives. Some people are organ donors. They agree to let doctors use their tissue and organs after they die. Organ and tissue donations save many lives each year. Just one organ donor can save eight lives with their organs and enhance the lives of more than 75 people with their tissue. Being an organ donor is completely voluntary, but it’s a great way to be a good citizen.

title: Respect for Others
text: Respecting others is an important part of being a good citizen. Being respectful means being kind and thoughtful. We allow others to feel and believe what they’d like. We stand up to bullies. It means appreciating people’s differences and recognizing and involving people of all ability levels. When citizens respect each other, communities are happier and work together better. Respecting those around you makes it easier to work as a team to get things done.

title: What Is an Emergency?
text:
An emergency is when you need help now or someone could get hurt. Some problems are emergencies. Some are not. If there is an emergency and no adults are around, you should call 911. You can get help during emergencies.

Here are examples of emergencies:

Fire

A stranger in your house

A bad injury

You are lost

title: Following the Rules
text:
What kind of rules do you have to follow at home? You might have a curfew or TV and screen time limitations. You probably have chores that you are expected to do. You might even have certain words you are not supposed to say or movies you are not supposed to watch. What are some rules you follow at your house?
