There are rules in your classroom that you are expected to follow. Doing your class jobs, respecting others, and respecting the classroom may be some of the rules you follow. What are some classroom rules you are asked to follow?

There is a difference between rules and laws. There are consequences to breaking both rules and laws. However, breaking a law has bigger and more permanent consequences. Laws are rules given by the state or the country that everyone is expected to follow. There are no exceptions. Some laws in the United States include no stealing, no hurting people or animals, no driving without a driver’s license, and paying your taxes. In some states, it’s against the law to use your phone while you are driving. Many drugs are illegal, and drinking alcohol is against the law if you are under the age of 21. To be a good citizen, you should be educated about the rules and laws where you live. Do your very best to follow them. Consequences for breaking a law could include paying money or going to jail.

title: Advocating for Equality
text:
A good citizen advocates for equality for everyone. To advocate means to publicly support. In the past, not everyone’s rights have been respected. In the past and even now in some places, people have been denied rights because of their skin color, religious beliefs, or other differences. Important people throughout history have stood up and fought for the rights of people who are different. Some of these people include:

President Abraham Lincoln helped abolish slavery in the United States.

Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony fought for women’s rights, including the right to vote.

Martin Luther King Jr. and Rosa Parks stood up against discrimination and racism and spoke out for civil rights.

Some Founding Fathers, including James Madison and Thomas Jefferson, stood up for religious freedom and made it a right for all citizens of the United States.

Think about the ways you can advocate for healthy and positive outcomes in your home, community, and school.

title: Listen and Share
text: People work and play in groups. You can help the group meet a goal. Share what you think. Listen to the ideas of others.

title: Emergencies
text: An emergency is when someone could get hurt. A fire is an emergency. Communicate to get help immediately if you see a fire or other emergency.

title: Talking to Others
text: Communication skills help us talk to others. They help us be good listeners.

title: Participating
text: Participating means joining others. Your ideas are important. You can share your ideas and talents with others.

title: Being a Helper
text: You can be a good helper. You can put things away. You can do your part.

title: Choosing Mindfulness
text: Mindfulness is when you focus all of your attention on what you are thinking and feeling. Being mindful can help you focus on the present. You can stop worrying about the past or the future. Just like anything, mindfulness gets easier with practice. The more you practice, the better you’ll get.

title: Be in the Present
text: Feelings of worry usually come from one of two places: the past or the future. You might be worried about something that has already happened, which means your mind is stuck in the past. You might be worrying about something you’re afraid will happen. That means your mind has zoomed into the future. However, you can’t change the past, and you can’t control everything in the future. Practicing mindfulness pulls you out of your worries and brings you back to the present.

title: How Mindfulness Can Help You
text: Does mindfulness really work? YES! It improves almost every type of well-being. Scientists have learned that it helps you feel less stressed, sleep better, and feel healthier. As if that’s not enough, being mindful can also help you do better in school and will help you learn to manage stress and anxiety even better in the future. Mindfulness is absolutely worth the time it takes to practice.

title: Breathing, Scanning, and Relaxing
text:
Mindful Breathing: Breathe in slowly, counting to five in your mind. Hold your breath and count to five. Then, slowly let your breath out, counting to five again. Hold your breath and count to five. Repeat this ten times.

Full body scan: Starting at your toes, notice how each body part feels as you scan upward toward your head. There’s no right or wrong answer.

Relaxation: Find a comfortable place to sit. As you breathe, relax the muscles in your face and neck. Then, relax your shoulders. Work all the way down to your toes. Sit quietly and enjoy the feeling of relaxation.

title: Visualize Your Success
text:
Visualization is a mindfulness skill that can help you meet your goals. It means mentally practicing the skills you want to improve. For example, if you want to be good at gymnastics, you can visualize yourself doing a perfect flip again and again. When you visualize activities, your brain doesn't know that it’s all in your head. It thinks you’re really practicing!

Here’s how to practice visualization.

Choose a skill you want to improve.

Close your eyes.

Imagine yourself performing the skill. Try to picture every part of it. Be patient; it may take some time.

In your mind, watch yourself perform the skill perfectly over and over.

title: Thinking Leads to Results
text:
You can make your thoughts come true, even if you don’t mean to. For example, you wake up one morning feeling fine. You tell yourself, "This is going to be the best day!" Well, guess what? You might have a great day! Here’s how it works:

Beliefs: You have certain beliefs about something.

Expectations: You expect something to happen based on your beliefs.

Behavior: Because of your expectations, you make certain choices.

Results: Something happens. The result can confirm or change your initial beliefs. It all depends on your thoughts.

Your thoughts are powerful! When you practice mindfulness, focus on positive things.

title: Introduction to Confidence
text: Confidence is the belief that you can succeed. When you are confident, you feel sure about yourself and your abilities. This includes your ability to keep learning, growing, and improving. Confidence can also mean standing up for what you believe in. Confidence in your standards can help you stand up to bullying and say “no” in risky situations that may involve drugs, alcohol, or gangs. Confidence doesn’t come from comparing yourself to other people’s strengths or weaknesses. It comes from believing “I can” instead of “I can’t.”

title: Why Confidence Matters
text: Believing “I can” will give you more chances to grow. Confidence helps you learn new things and strengthen your talents. It also helps you make friends and make the world a more interesting place! If things don’t go like you planned, confidence helps you learn from your mistakes and keep trying.

title: Confident Words
text:
Saying “I can” instead of “I can’t” is an example of self-talk. Self-talk is what you think or say to yourself about your own abilities. It can be negative or positive.

Confidence is choosing to focus on positive self-talk and say encouraging, uplifting things to yourself. For example:

I am proud that I tried something new.

I can keep practicing.

My effort makes a difference.

title: Confident Effort
text: Imagine there’s a drawing contest. Natalia gives it her best effort, using all of her favorite colors. Alana doesn’t want to feel embarrassed if she doesn’t win, so she doesn’t put very much work into her drawing. Who do you think feels the proudest of their drawing? Who had the most fun doing it? Who is building their confidence?

title: One of a Kind
text:
Everyone on Earth is unique. We all have different talents, skills, and abilities. Since you’re one of a kind, focus on your strengths.

Comparing yourself to someone else can make you feel like you aren’t good enough. It can make you focus on things you don’t have instead of recognizing what you do have. Technology, especially social media, has advantages and disadvantages. It is helpful to see and communicate with so many different people to recognize and appreciate diversity. However, it can be easy to fall into a trap of comparison when scrolling through posts and seeing everyone’s seemingly perfect lives.

When you start to compare yourself to someone else, stop and change your self-talk. Remind yourself of your unique talents and your ability to learn and grow.

title: Success for Everyone
text: Success isn’t like a pizza, where there are only a few slices for everyone to share. It’s unlimited! That means someone else’s success doesn’t take away from your own ability to succeed. Celebrate everyone’s success! Encourage people around you to make positive, healthy choices. The more you build other people up, the more positive you’ll feel. Let yourself be inspired by other people’s success instead of being jealous of it. There’s plenty to go around.

title: Steps to Confidence
text:
Here are a few tips to help you build confidence:

Practice using decision-making skills.

Stand up for your standards and beliefs.

Practice new skills and notice how you are improving.

Be kind to yourself when you make mistakes.

Get to know yourself. What do you like and dislike? What is important to you? What are your good qualities?

Care for your body and use good personal hygiene.

Set a short-term goal and celebrate when you reach it.

Keep trying!

title: Attitude Is a Choice
text:
Imagine a table covered with eyeglasses. All of the glasses have different-colored lenses. Which color would you choose to put on? Green, pink, blue? The glasses you choose will color the entire world, as long as you keep the glasses on.

Our attitudes and perspectives color how we see the world. Do you want to look through the lens of confidence and optimism? Or would you rather look through the lens of fear and frustration?

There is power in making choices. Use your power to choose your perspective. Encourage people around you to choose a positive perspective too.

title: The Gratitude Lens
text:
The fastest way to change your perspective is to look through a lens of gratitude. When we notice the good in our lives, we are more likely to see things (even challenges) with gratitude. Gratitude is a tool that can help you deal with difficult situations and feelings like sadness, anger, or stress. Looking for the good can help you feel better.

Think of three things you are grateful for every day.

Write those things down in a journal.

Ask yourself:

What am I grateful for right now?

What can I learn from this?

How am I getting stronger because of this?

title: Sweetening Up Your Life
text:
Have you ever heard the phrase “turn lemons into lemonade”? When you make lemonade, you turn something sour into something sweet by adding ingredients. Everyone faces sour situations in life. Sourness could come from difficulty in school, arguments at home, or troubles with friends. Challenges in life may cause stress or anxiety, but you can choose your attitude and perspective and sweeten the situation. Here are some ingredients you can add to sweeten a sour perspective:

Choose to focus on positive thoughts.

Find something positive to be grateful for.

Reach out to someone you trust.

Remember that difficult things can help you grow.

title: Take Time to Choose
text:
You don’t always choose what emotions you feel. Some feelings may lead to healthy behaviors, and other feelings may lead to unhealthy behaviors. Ultimately, you can choose how to act in response to your emotions. You choose whether to respond in a negative way or in a helpful, positive way.

Sometimes you need to use your “Push Pause” skill. You may need to breathe deeply or remove yourself for a minute before you choose how to respond.

title: A New Nation on the Brink of War
text:
During the early 1800s, the United States was a new country, forging its own path in the world. The people of the United States had just fought and won their independence from Great Britain. The former colonies were working hard to create a government and economy that could survive and thrive. However, the new government faced many challenges at home and abroad.

After the American Revolution, Great Britain still maintained a powerful empire, despite losing the war with the United States. Tensions were at an all-time high between Great Britain and France at this time. In 1803, the United States purchased the Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million. This expanded the United States by 828,000 square miles. As a result, the United States gained control of the Mississippi River and important trading posts along its banks. Following the Louisiana Purchase, France declared war on Great Britain.

The United States wished to remain neutral during the war between Great Britain and France. Both countries wanted the support of the U.S. government. In order to maintain neutrality, Congress passed the Embargo Act in 1807. An embargo is an order to stop ships from delivering goods. The law stated that goods couldn't be shipped to any foreign port. The United States hoped that both France and Great Britain would be devastated without American supplies. Unfortunately, the Embargo Act backfired. Great Britain and France survived without U.S. goods and were able to buy needed supplies and goods from other countries. The U.S. economy, on the other hand, suffered greatly due to the act. By keeping our supply of goods from meeting the demand in European markets, our industries were hurt and the economy declined because fewer people were buying U.S. goods.

President Thomas Jefferson repealed the Embargo Act before leaving office in March 1809. With conflict and uncertainty all around, the United States had a lot of work to do before it would become the country we live in today.

title: Essential Question
text: What were the causes and outcomes of the War of 1812?

title: Declaring War
text:
When James Madison was elected president of the United States in 1808, he inherited a country that was in disarray. The country was plagued with foreign and domestic issues. The relationship between Great Britain and the United States was hostile. The nation’s relationship with France, its ally in the American Revolution, was strained. The economy had suffered tremendously under the Embargo Act. With the repeal of the Embargo Act in 1809, Madison was forced to come up with a new plan to protect American ships, sailors, and goods from the British and French navies.

At this time in history, Great Britain had the largest and most powerful navy in the world. It allowed them to expand their military influence across the globe. For an island nation, it was the key to their power. The British used their navy to stop American merchant ships from trading with France, as well as keep American ships out of French ports. This made it very difficult for the United States to grow its economy.

To make sure they had enough sailors for their navy, the British captured American ships. They would then force the men on those ships to serve in the British Navy. This was called impressment. The impressed sailors were robbed of their freedom. The small United States Navy could not stop the mighty British Navy from doing this. A young, growing nation surrounded by oceans needed the ability to move and trade freely by sea. The actions of the British Navy frustrated and angered the new United States government.

In addition to impressment, the British formed alliances with Native People tribes in the Northwest Territory. They also supplied the tribes with weapons. The British hoped to remain in control of their territories in Canada and the profitable fur trade in the Northwest Territory. These alliances with the British caused tensions between American settlers and Native People tribes of the Northwest Territory.

Some members of Congress argued for direct military action against Great Britain. These people were known as the “War Hawks.” War Hawk leaders like Senator Henry Clay and others knew that the United States could not attack or invade Great Britain. Instead, they turned their attention to the nearest British colony at that time: Canada. They hoped an invasion of Canada would force Britain to finally stop their interference with American independence at sea and in the Northwest Territory.

On June 18, 1812, President James Madison signed a Declaration of War against Great Britain. Congress approved the declaration 17 days later, and the United States officially went to war against Great Britain and its allies. However, the United States wasn't prepared to fight another war. Congress was forced to quickly expand the army and navy to protect the country from a British invasion.

Madison ordered American troops to attack British colonies in Canada. This resulted in multiple British victories. The start of the war was a disaster for the United States. However, it did not dissuade, or convince, the country from selecting Madison for a second term of office in the fall of 1812.

title: Tecumseh's War
text:
In the years following the American Revolution, the U.S. government and its people continued expanding west. This created conflict between these citizens and the Native Peoples population already living there. In the early 1790s, a group of Native People tribes in what was known as the Northwest Territory joined forces to resist U.S. expansion. These tribes were located in what are now the states of Ohio, Indiana, Michigan, Illinois, Wisconsin, and Minnesota.

The final clash of this conflict occurred at the Battle of Fallen Timbers in 1795. Future president William Henry Harrison took part on the side of the United States. Shawnee chief Tecumseh was on the side of the Native People tribes. When the United States Army ended the battle victoriously, the two sides signed the Treaty of Greenville, but Tecumseh refused to sign it. The treaty created designated land for the Native People tribes. This treaty temporarily stopped the fighting, but it set up a future conflict in which Tecumseh and William Henry Harrison would play significant roles.

As hostilities began between the United States and England in the east, Tecumseh gathered a large alliance between Native People tribes. American settlers were continuing to cross into the land set aside for the tribes in the Treaty of Greenville. Tecumseh pursued negotiations with the territorial governor, William Henry Harrison. Instead of succeeding, the negotiations revealed to Harrison the strength and numbers of Tecumseh’s alliances. Harrison led an attack on Tecumseh’s forces at the Battle of Tippecanoe in 1811, resulting in an American victory.

The ensuing conflict between United States and Native Peoples forces in the west was short-lived. The British joined forces with the Native People tribes in the west, and Tecumseh led his people at his final battle at Moraviantown in 1813. It was at this battle that Tecumseh was killed. The confederacy of allied tribes Tecumseh had worked so hard to build up fractured and collapsed after his death.

As the United States leader, William Henry Harrison was seen as a hero. He defeated Tecumseh and his British allies and delivered the West to the United States. This removed a major obstacle to American expansion and helped win the War of 1812.

title: The Battle of Lake Erie
text:
The Great Lakes form a large part of the border between the United States and Canada. Their location made them a major geographical landmark in the War of 1812. The country that controlled the Great Lakes had a major advantage in the war between the United States and the British. To secure the area, President James Madison sent Oliver Hazard Perry to Lake Erie to build a fleet of ships he could use to defeat the British and gain control on the water.

Perry and his carpenter led the construction of nine vessels. The largest were the brigs Niagara and Lawrence. The presence of Perry and his fleet threatened British control of the area and kept them from freely moving people and supplies on and around the lake. The British sent their own fleet to retake control of the lake and open their supply lines. They had only six ships, but they carried more guns in total than the larger American fleet. Their guns could also shoot farther with more accuracy.

The British attacked the American fleet on Sept. 10, 1813. Perry rode his flagship, Lawrence, into battle. With the wind behind them, pushing forward, Perry and his fleet closed the distance between them and the British. The Lawrence sustained massive damage, forcing Perry to transfer to the Niagara. It was there that Perry led the American fleet to victory, gaining control of Lake Erie and dealing a major blow to the British goals in the area as they were forced to abandon the city of Detroit. Perry reported the victory to General William Henry Harrison with the now-famous statement, “We have met the enemy, and they are ours.”

title: Wages, Salaries, and Commissions
text:
People receive income in many different ways. The most common way that people earn income is through wages, or an amount of money paid for every hour of work completed. For example, a person working at a coffee shop might earn $12 for every hour that they work. If this person worked an eight-hour shift in a day, their wages for that day would be $96. When earning income through wages, the more hours you work, the more income you earn.

Another way that people may earn income is by working for a salary. A salary is a set amount of money paid to an individual for their work. An example of someone who is paid a salary is a teacher. Many teachers are paid a set amount of money each month or year to do their job. Usually, a person who earns a salary does not complete their work on a set schedule. A teacher may have to work longer hours, before or after school, to complete their job. Additionally, during the summer, teachers still have to work, even while school is not in session. They work through the summer to prepare for the next school year.

Some people earn income through commission. A commission is a payment that an employee makes when they sell something. Some employees earn commission in addition to wages or a salary, while other employees work only on commission. When an employee earns a commission, they take a portion of the sale as their income.

A real estate agent is a good example of someone who earns income through commission. If an agent sells a house, they earn a commission based on the sale price of that house. For example, if a real estate agent earns a five percent commission on every house they sell and they sell a house for $100,000, they would earn $5,000 in commission. This might sound like the best way to earn income, but earning income from commission can be very difficult. Each form of income has its positives and negatives.

Hourly employees earn more income the more hours that are worked. They might even have an opportunity to earn extra pay, or overtime, for hours worked beyond their work schedule. Hourly wages, however, might not be as secure as other forms of income. A business might limit the number of hours a person works based on the number of customers who come into their store or other factors.

Individuals earning a salary receive a set amount of income every month. This can be very appealing to some. However, an individual earning a salary might have to work many hours beyond their regular work day to complete the job. For those working on commission, their income depends on the amount of commission that can be earned, and they might earn more income than most. This income is not guaranteed like a salary, though. In many cases, if an individual working on commission does not sell their product or service, they do not receive income.

Regardless of the way that people earn an income, each person is performing an important role in their community.

title: Earning and Income
text:
People work in order to earn money to pay for their wants and needs. There are many different kinds of jobs and work you can do to earn money. You could work in a restaurant or grocery store. You could farm the land and grow crops. You could maybe open your own business. You could also become a teacher, veterinarian, doctor, lawyer, or computer programmer. The possibilities are endless.

Money that you receive for working is called income. You can do many things with your income. Most people use their income to meet their needs. This includes paying for housing, electricity, food to eat, and transportation. Medical services, like visiting the doctor or going to the dentist, also cost money.

You can also use your money to buy things you want. Some people choose to save a portion of their income for the future. You can earn money to buy goods and services you need and want. People have many choices about how to save and spend their income. Part of the income people earn is collected by the government in the form of taxes. Taxes pay for community, state, and national services.

title: Essential Question
text: How do income and earning help create financial goals?

title: Banks
text:
A bank is a business that deals with money. Banks provide many services to their customers. A bank's primary function is to hold their customers' money in accounts. It is safer to keep your money in a bank than to keep it at home. Banks also lend money to people in the form of loans. Loans are a type of debt in which the person borrowing the money agrees to pay it back within a certain amount of time. They also agree to pay interest. Interest is an additional fee people agree to pay to borrow money. People use loans for many reasons. Some examples are paying for college, buying a home, or purchasing a car.

There are three main types of banks. The first is a commercial bank. These banks serve both businesses and individuals. They offer checking accounts, loans, and saving accounts to their customers.

The second kind of bank is a savings bank. These banks are similar to commercial banks. Savings banks mostly offer savings accounts and loans.

The third type of bank is called a credit union. Credit unions were started to help people borrow money. People in the same type of employment put their savings together and loan it to others within that organization. In other words, they operate their own banks. Today, credit unions provide many of the same services as commercial and savings banks. However, they are nonprofit organizations. This means that all the members of the credit union share any profit they make.

title: Interest
text:
Did you know that you can earn income by lending someone some of your money? Interest is another form of income that people might earn. Sometimes, people need to borrow money in order to buy things they need or want. They may borrow money from a bank, a company, or another person, who is often called a lender. The loan, or money borrowed, must be paid back to the lender within a certain amount of time.

The person borrowing money has to pay interest on the loan. Interest is the amount of money a lender or financial institution receives for lending out money. For example, if a person borrows $100 from a bank, the bank will charge interest on that loan. When that person pays back the loan, they will have to pay $100 plus the interest charged. You might be wondering where banks get the money that they loan to people and business. That money can come from you. If you have a bank account that earns interest, the bank pays you to allow them to use your money.

title: Renting Property
text:
Another way that people can earn income is through rent. Rent is a fee paid by someone to use another person’s property. The most common thing that people pay rent for is housing. If someone is not able or does not want to buy housing, they might pay someone rent to live in their house or apartment. Renting is not just for housing, though. People rent many other types of property. Automobiles and tools are other examples of property that someone might rent.

Some people purchase property for the purpose of renting it to others. For example, a person might already have a home but purchase another one to rent to others. The rent they receive for the rental house is a form of income. That income might help pay for the property or enable the person to purchase more property. Individuals who do this are called entrepreneurs.

title: Paying Taxes
text:
A tax is a percentage of money that a person pays. There are many different types of taxes. You pay taxes on items you buy or items you already own. Sales tax is a tax you pay on things you buy. There are also taxes you pay every year on things you already own, like property taxes. Property tax is a tax you pay for owning a house or a car.

Federal income tax is a tax you pay to the federal government. State income tax is a tax you pay to the state you live in. Both state and federal income taxes are based on how much income you earn every year.

Taxes pay for public services. If it weren't for taxes, you wouldn’t be able to go to public school. You wouldn't have a town library where you can check out books for free. You also wouldn't have roads to drive on or garbage pick-up to take away your trash. In your community, taxes pay police officers and firefighters to keep you safe. Taxes also maintain local parks and provide clean water to drink. Being able to earn an income helps you buy the things you want and need. Paying taxes contributes to the well-being of your community, state, and country.

title: Setting Financial Goals
text:
This week, you have learned about the importance of making good financial decisions about your income. One of the most important things a person can do to achieve what they want is to set a goal. Just as a person who wants to get healthier has to set goals about their diet and exercise, you have to set goals about spending and saving to make sure your budget is healthy. Once you set a goal, you have to create a plan to reach that goal. Using the diet and exercise example, you can’t expect to get healthier and be able to run 10 miles overnight. You have to start small, like running half a mile a day to build up your strength and endurance.

Making a plan to reach your financial goal is the same thing. If you want to save your money for a new bicycle that costs $250, you have to create a plan that is S.M.A.R.T. The acronym “S.M.A.R.T.” stands for Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, and Timely.

Setting a S.M.A.R.T. financial goal to save money for a new bicycle might look something like this:

Specific: You need to save $250 for a new bicycle.

Measurable: You need to know how much money you have and how much money you still need to save.

Attainable: You have a good plan to earn the amount of money you need to save each week.

Realistic: The amount you save will be an amount that you can afford to save after all of your spending.

Timely: You will save money each week over a specific period of time until you have enough to meet your goal.

Putting that all together, your S.M.A.R.T. goal to save $250 for a new bicycle might be:

“I will save $10 per week for the next six months in order to save $250 for my new bicycle.”

While the thought of saving $250 for something you want might seem very difficult, making a S.M.A.R.T. financial goal can help you make it happen.

Now it’s your turn. Create a S.M.A.R.T. financial goal for yourself.

title: Where Does Grief Come From?
text:
Grief is a feeling of deep sadness that comes from losing something. Often, people feel grief because of the death of someone they love. Sometimes, it comes from different kinds of loss, like a severe injury or an illness. Although it can feel overwhelming, grief is a normal emotion.

Grief affects everyone differently. In fact, it may feel different every time you experience it. Even though everyone’s grief is unique, no one has to face it alone.

title: The Grieving Process
text:
Denial: "This isn't real." It’s hard to accept a loss, and you might want to pretend it’s not true.

Anger: "Why is this happening to me?" You may want to blame someone. Life might seem unfair.

Bargaining: "I have to change this." You might want to change the situation, even if it’s impossible (like curing a disease).

Depression: "What's the point?" When you realize you can’t change things, you can feel overwhelmed. You may cry or want to be alone.

Acceptance: "It's going to be okay." Eventually, you will be able to imagine living your life with the loss instead of trying to ignore or change it.

title: Talking About Your Grief Can Help
text: Talking about loss can be hard. You might not want to think about it, or you might not know what to say. But when you talk about grief, you don’t have to focus on negative things. There are no right or wrong words to say. Sometimes you might not even use words at all. Crying or simply sitting with someone you trust can help. Spending time with a friend or family member and talking about your loss can help you remember happy moments. You can even talk to a professional like a doctor, a school counselor, or a therapist if you feel like you need extra help.

title: Showing Sympathy to Grieving Friends
text:
Sympathy is when you feel bad that something has happened to someone. You don't know exactly how they feel, but you wish they didn’t have to feel that way. When your friend is grieving, knowing that you feel sympathy for them helps them feel less alone. It also lets them know that you care.

Here are some ideas for showing sympathy:

Make a card or write a letter that they can read when they feel lonely.

Tell them you are sorry they are going through this.

title: Empathy Is ...
text: Empathy is connecting what we think and feel with how someone else thinks and feels through common experiences. Think about a problem that is not your own and ask, “How does that problem make someone else feel?” “How did I feel when something like this happened to me?” Then, connect the two. This is why asking questions is so important. We don’t know how someone else feels until we ask.

title: Empathy Looks Like ...
text: We try to show empathy when we look at the world around us. We try to see things from another person's point of view. First, we try to listen without judging the other person. Next, we try to see what another person is seeing. Then, we try to feel what that person is feeling. Finally, we develop empathy for someone when we try to understand what they are going through or feeling. The goal is to observe and infer.

title: Empathy Sounds Like ...
text: When you are listening to someone, you pay attention to their words. You watch their body language. You think about what that person is saying.

title: Empathy Impacts My Morals by ...
text: Being moral means being concerned about right and wrong. Your moral identity is what you believe is right and wrong. Your behavior shows others what you believe is right or wrong. A person with high morals usually believes in being honest, kind, and fair. They believe in trying to be a good person. Building and practicing empathy helps you develop your moral identity.

title: I Can Practice Empathy by ...
text:
It is important to practice showing empathy to others. When you spend time with other people, you get to know them. You get to know what they like and dislike. This helps you understand how they see the world around them. It helps you become an empathic person. Being an empathic person helps you to be a better friend.

Here are some ways to practice empathy:

Ask lots of questions.

Get feedback from others.

Try to think in terms of “us” and not “them.”

Consider what you have in common with your classmates.

Work in a team or in groups.

Ask yourself, “How would that make me feel, so I can feel that with them?”

title: I Can Show Empathy to Myself by ...
text: It is important to remember to be patient with yourself as you learn. It is okay to make mistakes and learn from them. This is one way you can show empathy for yourself. There will be times when you forget or choose not to show empathy. If you hurt someone’s feelings, you should apologize. Apologizing takes courage. Talk to the other person. Tell them you feel sorry for what you did or said that may have hurt them. When you have empathy for yourself, you can overcome mistakes and be better because of them. Having empathy for yourself is a great way to improve your personal health.

title: When Others Don't Show Empathy I Can ...
text: Sometimes, others will not show empathy. People will make choices that surprise you. Be patient when this happens. You will need to make a plan to be patient. A plan helps you know what to say when someone is not being their best self. Saying something when you see a lack of empathy takes courage.

title: I Can Protect My Emotions by ...
text:
At times, showing empathy can take a toll on your emotions. It can be hard to feel what others are feeling all the time, in addition to what you are feeling. When this happens, it is called overstimulation. This means you are feeling a lot of emotions at once or too much of an emotion at one time.

Your brain is full of neurons. A neuron is the basic working part of the brain. There are special neurons called “mirror neurons.” These neurons have the job of creating empathy in your brain. Practicing empathy does not mean taking on other people's problems. It means being kind and understanding.

When you experience empathy overstimulation, you can use your self-regulation tools:

Pushing pause can help you take a moment to breathe and think before responding.

Take a break from a situation.

Take a break from a person.

Communicate your feelings.

Talk to a friend or trusted adult.

title: The Fugitive Slave Act of 1850
text:
Before slavery ended in America, several laws were passed by the federal government that restricted the rights of enslaved people. One of these laws was the Fugitive Slave Act. This law made it illegal for enslaved people to seek freedom by running away from their enslavers and for others to help those seeking freedom. The first Fugitive Slave Act was passed in 1793, but it was not strongly enforced. As more northern states abolished legalized slavery, enslavers believed that the free states would lure freedom-seeking enslaved people away from the South.

Representatives from the southern states encouraged Congress to pass the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850. The updated law gave enslavers the right to reclaim enslaved people who ran away, even in free states. It also required the government to help enslavers capture and reenslave people seeking freedom. No such requirement had existed before 1850.

Free African Americans also feared for their safety. There were many instances in which enslavers and agents called “commissioners” captured free African Americans and forced them into slavery. Some people who had been free for their entire lives now had no choice but to leave the United States to avoid the risk of enslavement.

The abolitionist movement grew to oppose the Fugitive Slave Act. New laws to help enslaved people were enacted in many Northern states. Attempts by the northern states to weaken the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850 caused tension between the northern and southern states.

title: Ohio Abolitionists
text:
Many individuals in America opposed legalized slavery. By the early 1800s, most of the northern states had abolished, or legally ended, slavery. However, slavery remained legal in all of the southern states. There were many people who hoped that slavery would be abolished in all states. People who worked to abolish slavery nationwide were called abolitionists.

Many Ohioans opposed slavery and were strong supporters of the abolitionist movement. In September 1817, Ohioan Charles Osborn started a newspaper called The Philanthropist, the first anti-slavery newspaper in the United States. Articles published in The Philanthropist discussed the importance of the abolitionist movement and the reasons why slavery must be abolished. It also discussed other important issues in the United States, including public education and equal rights for American Indians.

A religious group known as the Society of Friends, or Quakers, was very active in protesting the laws that kept slavery legal. Quakers believe in peace and equality for all people. The Quakers worked to end slavery and free all people. Ohio Quakers were very active in the abolitionist movement. Charles Osborn, founder and publisher of the newspaper The Philanthropist, was a member of the Society of Friends. Another member of the Quaker community, Benjamin Lundy, published his own abolitionist newspaper in Mount Pleasant, Ohio. Because of his work, Lundy was often called the “father of Abolitionism.”

Another famous Ohio abolitionist was John Rankin, one of the founding members of the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society. Rankin was born in Tennessee but moved to Kentucky following his religious training. Rankin preached against slavery and encouraged the members of his community to join the abolitionist movement. Rankin’s views were unpopular in Kentucky, so he moved to Ohio to help the state’s growing abolitionist movement. Rankin established a college in Ripley, Ohio, in 1829, which allowed African American students to attend.

Other abolitionists were African Americans who had escaped slavery or who had experienced slavery through their family members. John Malvin was born in Virginia in 1795. He was the son of a free Black woman and an enslaved man. Because his mother was a free woman, Malvin was not considered an enslaved person. Malvin moved to Cleveland in 1831 in search of better economic opportunities. Malvin became a member of Ohio’s abolitionist movement. He gave lectures for the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society. Malvin also spoke out against segregation, or the separation of people based on race or other factors, in Ohio churches and schools.

When people disobey a law, there are consequences. Knowingly going against a law in protest is called civil disobedience. Members of the abolitionist movement practiced civil disobedience. Breaking the law can have dangerous consequences. Law-abiding people willingly broke the law to express their beliefs and help enslaved men, women, and children to escape to freedom.

title: Anti-Slavery Societies in Ohio
text:
Several anti-slavery societies were established in Ohio to support the abolitionist movement. In 1835, members of the abolitionist movement in Ohio, including Asa Mahan, John Rankin, James Birney, Theodore Dwight Weld, and Charles Finney, formed the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society. The purpose of the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society was to support the country’s abolitionist movement. Members of the organization encouraged Congress to pass laws to abolish legalized slavery and protect the basic human rights of African Americans.

Members of the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society traveled around the state to speak about the importance of abolishing slavery and encourage others to join the abolitionist movement. The organization also hired well-known abolitionists to present at lectures.

Many Ohioans did not agree with the beliefs of the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society. Cincinnatians petitioned the city government to shut down the abolitionist newspaper The Philanthropist. When city officials refused to shut down the newspaper, a mob destroyed the newspaper office and all of the printing equipment.

Other organizations formed in Ohio to oppose slavery. Some organizations served specific cities and counties, like the Cleveland Anti-Slavery Society.

Other organizations were started by free African Americans, some of whom were formerly enslaved. John Mercer Langston formed the Ohio Colored American League in 1850. African Americans in Cleveland founded the Cuyahoga County Anti-Slavery Society. The Cuyahoga County Anti-Slavery Society petitioned the state government to create laws to protect African Americans' right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

title: The Underground Railroad
text:
When a person was enslaved for life, the only way for them to gain freedom was to escape. In the northern states, slavery was illegal. To an enslaved person, the trip to the North could be 10 miles or 110 miles. They had never seen a map. They only knew that “north” meant freedom. Staying put offered no freedom. However, seeking freedom was a big risk. Getting caught running away meant severe punishment or death. The punishment was meant to scare other enslaved people by showing them what would happen if they ran away. It was also meant to stop them from thinking of freedom.

To make the trip north, a person seeking freedom needed help. They needed people to guide, hide, and give them the supplies needed to make the journey. Abolitionists knew how to help, even though they knew that helping an enslaved person escape was against the law. The consequences for helping an enslaved person escape were severe. Many enslavers would come after their “property.” They would torment people they thought were helping freedom seekers. Farms were burned, people were injured, and some were even arrested. These consequences did not stop the abolitionists.

A system of secret codes, paths, and hideaways was created. This system became known as the Underground Railroad. The Underground Railroad was not a real railroad, but the name was used as a code. This code was meant to fool anybody searching for enslaved people seeking freedom. The paths, or “tracks,'' were hidden from the public eye.

People acted as guides on the tracks, like conductors on a railroad. Like railroad stations, there were places to rest along the way, such as homes, cellars, and barns. The people seeking freedom were called “passengers.”

Passengers were met in secret by a conductor. Each conductor guided them to the next station. The passengers were given food, clothing, and supplies for the next part of the trip. Passengers traveled by night as quietly and as quickly as they could.

Ohio became an important stop and destination on the Underground Railroad. Slavery was illegal in Ohio. It was also very close to Canada, where slavery was also illegal. Many African American and white Ohioans aided freedom seekers on the Underground Railroad. They served as conductors, gave people a place to rest and hide, and provided supplies and resources. Historians estimate that about 3,000 miles of Underground Railroad trails ran throughout Ohio.

John Rankin, one of the founding members of the Ohio Anti-Slavery Society, guided freedom seekers to Canada on the Underground Railroad. The Rankin home was an important station on the Underground Railroad. Rankin was one of the inspirations for the popular book Uncle Tom’s Cabin by famous author and abolitionist Harriet Beecher Stowe.

Levi Coffin, a prominent abolitionist in Cincinnati, helped over 3,000 people to freedom in Canada as a conductor on the Underground Railroad. For his brave actions, Coffin was given the name "president of the Underground Railroad."

John P. Parker was another Ohioan who helped people to freedom. Before becoming an abolitionist and conductor on the Underground Railroad, Parker was born into slavery. At the age of 18, Parker purchased his freedom and moved to Ohio. He became a conductor on the Underground Railroad. Parker made frequent trips across the Ohio River into Kentucky to help freedom seekers reach Ohio.

title: Harriet Tubman
text:
Araminta Harriet Ross was born into slavery in Bucktown, Maryland, in 1820. When she was a child, she was “hired out” to work for people. People paid her enslaver for her work. She worked for several very cruel people, who injured her. These injuries would bother her for the rest of her life.

In 1844, she was allowed to marry a free man named John Tubman. In 1849, when her enslaver died, she knew it was her chance for freedom. She ran north. She had no plan, and the journey was terrifying and difficult. She used different stations on the Underground Railroad. She had no conductor between stations. She traveled alone and made the 90-mile journey to Philadelphia. Harriet Tubman said about realizing she was in Philadelphia: “When I found I had crossed that line, I looked at my hands to see if I was the same person. There was such a glory over everything; the sun came like gold through the trees, and over the fields, and I felt like I was in Heaven.”

In Philadelphia, she met a man named William Still. He was a clerk and janitor for the Pennsylvania Society for the Abolition of Slavery. He introduced her to many people connected to the Underground Railroad. Tubman didn’t stay in the safety of Philadelphia for long. She became a conductor on the Underground Railroad.

Tubman made numerous trips along the Underground Railroad and helped hundreds of people escape from slavery. She was called “Moses” by many for leading people to freedom. She was feared and hated by enslavers and revered, or respected, by abolitionists and people seeking freedom. They couldn’t believe “Moses” was a woman. Tubman was one of the most successful conductors on the Underground Railroad.

title: William Still, Record Keeper
text:
We know more about the secret Underground Railroad thanks to William Still. Still was a janitor and clerk for the Pennsylvania Society for the Abolition of Slavery. He lived in Philadelphia. He met people who successfully escaped slavery on the Underground Railroad and encouraged them to change their names. Then he wrote their names in a book. Changing their names had two purposes. First, it would signal their new life as a free person. Second, it would help hide them from anyone wanting to take them back to slavery.

When asked how the Underground Railroad was successful, Still replied:

'How?' I answer, 'through extraordinary determination and endeavor,' such as are demonstrated in hundreds of cases in the pages of this book, in the struggles of men and women to obtain their freedom, education, and property. These facts must never be lost sight of.... The pulse of the four millions of slaves and their desire for freedom, were better felt through 'The Underground Railroad,' than through any other channel.

title: Essential Question
text: How did Ohioans contribute to the Abolitionist Movement and the Underground Railroad?

title: Everyone Has Rights
text: A right is something that everyone should be allowed to have or do. You don’t have to buy or earn a right. It belongs to you simply because you’re human. The Declaration of Independence gives U.S. citizens the right to live, be free, and do what makes them happy. You also have the right to think, speak, and make decisions for yourself. It’s important to stand up for others whose rights have been taken away.

title: Culture in Every Home
text:
We all have the same rights, but that doesn’t mean we’re all exactly alike. We all represent different races, genders, and abilities. We also represent different cultures.

Your culture is made up of the beliefs, customs, and languages that you learn from the people around you. It may be influenced by your location, religion, and race. Learning about other cultures helps you understand yourself and others better. You can learn a lot about a person’s culture through their family and their home practices.

title: Citizenship Vocabulary
text:
Fairness is about making sure that everyone has what they need to be successful. It is important that everyone is treated with fairness.

Equality means that all people are treated the same. For example, everyone in your class has the same teacher and the same amount of time in the classroom every day.

Equity means that people get different support depending on their needs. Imagine that someone has moved from a country where they spoke a different language. They may need extra time to read something. What if they aren’t allowed extra time? It may be equal, but is it fair?

title: Standing Up for What's Right
text:
Someday, you may notice something that is unfair. You may see that someone is not being treated equally. If you see something, speak up. Let people know what you think. Encourage others to be kind and avoid bullying. You can use your voice to advocate for change.

Advocating means supporting something that you think is right. When you advocate for change, you are trying to make something better. Being an advocate can be hard because you might have a lot of strong emotions about the change you want to make. You may want to react negatively. But it is important to advocate for change in a way that is assertive, not harmful.

title: The Forests of Pennsylvania
text:
Pennsylvania has been covered in forests for thousands of years. The Piedmont, Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians, and the Allegheny Plateau have the perfect conditions for growing trees. The soil, temperature, and rainfall support white pine, hemlock, maple, cherry, ash, chestnut, and oak trees.

The Allegheny National Forest is in the northwest area of Pennsylvania. It is a protected area managed by the federal government. There are 20 state forest regions and over 12 million acres of state game lands in Pennsylvania. Each of the designated areas contributes to the recreation, tourism, forestry, and energy production industries.

There was a time when Pennsylvania was in danger of losing its forests forever. During the 1800s, industry was growing in the state. Wood was needed to fuel the fires that helped make iron, steel, oil, and railroads.

Lumber companies would buy forested property and build temporary camps on it. Hundreds of workers and their families would live in tents and poorly made shelters. Temporary railroads and wagon roads would be built to haul the cut trees. When the trees were gone, the company would abandon, or leave, the area. They would leave behind broken buildings and equipment. This happened over and over again throughout Pennsylvania.

By 1895, thousands of miles of forests were gone. All that remained were branches and stumps. When rain fell, there was nothing to keep the water in the soil. Floods filled the valleys and endangered communities. Forest animals had nothing to eat. The white-tailed deer population was at its lowest count. The elk population was gone. There were more forest fires. The lumber companies did not pay taxes on the property. Many counties ran out of money. So, citizens created groups to raise awareness of the forest's destruction and its consequences to people.

The Pennsylvania Division of Forestry was created in 1895. Dr. Joseph T. Rothrock was its commissioner. Rothrock’s leadership began a tradition of forest conservation in Pennsylvania. Mira Lloyd Dock was the first woman appointed as a member of the Forestry Commission. She and Rothrock worked with Gifford Pinchot of the U.S. Forest Service. Conservation of natural resources was championed by U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt.

Through their leadership and the education of the public, Pennsylvania’s forests were replanted. The National Forest System was created. The state forests and state game lands flourished. The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission maintains the Lumber Heritage Region, including a museum that documents the lumber industry over time. Now, in the 21st century, Pennsylvania’s woods have recovered. We must be good stewards to keep the forests healthy.

title: Essential Question?
text: How does the Pennsylvania lumber industry demonstrate continuity and change over time?

title: From Tree to Lumber
text:
Trees are a valuable natural resource. Trees help clean the air. Their roots help the soil store water. They provide living space for many birds and forest creatures. The wood from trees can be used by humans to make things. Wood has been used by humans for thousands of years. Trees are a renewable resource. This means that new trees can be planted to replace the trees we use.

When a tree is cut down, it is called timber. The lumber industry provides wood to consumers. It creates thousands of jobs for workers in rural, suburban, and urban areas.

This is how the lumber industry works. A forester monitors woodland areas and identifies which trees should be harvested. A cutting crew comes in to cut the trees down. Once the trees are cut, the branches are removed and sorted for chipping, paper pulp, firewood, or material for animal habitats. Trees without branches are called logs.

Logs are transported to sawmills. Sawmills were traditionally located by a stream or river. The logs would be floated to a sawmill on the water. A log boom on the side of the river trapped the logs so they could be processed. The river’s current spun a large wheel on the sawmill. The wheel was attached to a series of rods and gears that caused the saw blades to move. The saw cut logs into boards, or lumber. Eventually, steam-powered engines replaced the water wheel. Today, electricity powers the saws.

Lumber is cut into various sizes, depending on the needs of the consumer. Large boards are used to build structures. Smaller boards are used to build furniture or home accessories. Every part of a log is used. The sawdust and chippings are pressed together and glued to make particle board.

Lumber is dried to remove the moisture from the wood fibers. Drying makes the boards strong. The boards are put in large stacks and wrapped for transport. Trucks and trains transport them to a lumber yard, construction site, or manufacturing facility. Pennsylvania’s lumber is shipped all over the world.

Different trees are used to make different products. Maple is used for flooring in bowling alleys and basketball courts. Oak is used for furniture and flooring. Cherry is prized as a furniture wood. Hemlock is good for constructing buildings. Ash is used for baseball bats.

The tops of many kinds of trees can be chipped to make pulp for paper. Cellulose from wood is used in foods. Shredded cheese is coated with cellulose to keep the cheese from clumping together. Mulch from the bark of trees is used in gardens, parks, and playgrounds.

Pennsylvania’s forests are a natural, renewable resource that is valuable to many industries. Using forests responsibly means that our environment will be healthy and that we will have lumber for many years to come.

title: Williamsport
text:
Located on the West Branch of the Susquehanna River, Williamsport was the center of the lumber industry in the 1800s. Each spring, the melting snow would turn the rivers into swollen highways of fast-moving water. Lumberjacks, or men who worked for the logging company, tied logs together to create rafts. They would ride the rafts and guide the logs down the river. They floated millions of logs in the river each spring. The lumberjacks would sort the logs to their assigned sawmill with long pikes, or poles that had iron hooks on the end. They would stand on the logs in the river while sorting the logs.

America was growing, and lumber was needed for mining, railroads, canals, transportation, and housing. Between 1868 and 1900, Williamsport’s 37 sawmills produced more than eight billion feet of lumber. This success made Williamsport home to more millionaires than any other city in the United States. These millionaires built large homes and structures in the community. Community and state leaders emerged from the millionaire group. Williamsport’s access to lumber attracted businesses that made furniture, carriages, wagons, and fine carvings. As a result, Williamsport became a vibrant city, with arts, colleges, hospitals, entertainment, and shops.

The great demand for lumber decreased the supply of forests in Pennsylvania. So, at the beginning of the 20th century, the lumber millionaires moved their operations to forests in the Midwest and Rocky Mountains.

Williamsport’s population increased and decreased based on employment opportunities. In 1850, its population was 1,615 people. In 1900, the population was 28,757. In 1950, 45,047 people lived in Williamsport. The 2020 census reported 27,754 residents.

title: Tools and Technology for Lumber
text:
The methods of harvesting trees have changed over time. Native Americans used knives to cut away the bark from around tree trunks. The trees would eventually die and fall to the ground. Later, people developed metal axes with sharp edges to chop at the tree’s trunk until it fell. With improvements to iron and steel, people developed saws. Saws are sheets of steel with carved teeth in the edge. Large trees needed a large saw to cut through the wood, so two-person saws were created. Then saws were attached to gas engines. The engine spun the saw so that it could cut the wood quickly. Power saws are the main tool used to cut down trees today.

To move a tree from where it has fallen, it must be skidded, or dragged, to a loading dock or stream. Draft horses were used to move logs. Draft horses are bred to be strong and pull heavy loads. Today, the Amish community still uses draft horses to skid logs out of the forest. Modern logging uses machines called skidders. Log loaders grapple, or lift, the cut logs onto a truck for transportation to the sawmill.

Today’s sawmills are fully automated with computerized tools and conveyor belts. The high demand for wood products can only be met because of the improvements in tree harvesting tools.

title: Lumber in the 21st Century
text:
The Pennsylvania Hardwoods Development Council created a report for the Department of Agriculture in 2020. The following is from that report. It talks about jobs in Pennsylvania’s lumber industry.

“Since [2008] employment statewide has been between 60,000 and 66,500.... More than 31,000 of the forest products industry jobs, or nearly half, are in south central and southeast Pennsylvania. With 5,756 jobs, Lancaster County is first in the state, with many Amish sawmills and furniture shops as well as several large kitchen cabinet manufacturers. York County is second, with 3,225 jobs, which includes a large paper mill, several secondary wood product manufacturers, along with other sawmills and forestry/logging businesses. It is important to understand that sustainable [continued] forestry, timber access, and logging issues impact the whole state. If municipalities [city, towns or townships] attempt to … restrict timber harvesting or legislation is passed that limits forestry operations, it negatively impacts jobs in the secondary wood products industry across the state especially in south central and southeast Pennsylvania.”
