When he was a teenager, Muhammad worked in a camel caravan. People called him “al-Amin” which means trustworthy or faithful. People could trust Muhammad to be honest.

When he was an adult, Muhammad had an experience. He told people about it. He said that the Angel Gabriel gave him a message to share with people.

Chapter 96 of the Qur’an, the Islamic book of scripture, says:

Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth,

Createth man from a clot.

Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous,

He who teacheth by the pen–

Teacheth man that which he knew not.

Muhammad told people that there was only one god. He told people God had created them. They should worship him.

Some people believed Muhammad. Others did not. Today, millions of people follow the teachings of Muhammad as a prophet of God.

At the end of 2020, there were 250,000 workers employed in the oil and gas industry. This does not include employment in government inspection and regulation departments. Opportunities for employment vary by physical demands, education, and location.

The oil and gas industries include three areas of focus.

Extracting or drilling and locating oil and gas as a natural resource.

Transporting the raw materials to processing centers. This includes pipelines, trucking and shipping.

Refining to create products for consumers from the natural resource.

Employment can be outdoors, traveling the highways, or in offices. Driving a gasoline tanker truck to gas stations is considered one of the most dangerous jobs. While completing regulation reports in an office offers different safety environments. The oil and gas industry in Pennsylvania will continue in career and employment offerings until alternative fuels are found.

title: The Gilded Age and the Progressive Era
text:
After the Civil War ended in 1865, a new time of growth began in America. In the North, many factories had been built to make supplies for soldiers in the war. After the war, these factories could be used to make things that regular people used every day, like fabrics and steel. They packaged food for millions of people. Railroads were built across the country. Tall buildings were built in the largest cities. Coal mining and oil drilling increased.

Before the Civil War, most people in America had lived on farms or in small towns. After the war, cities grew quickly. Many people moved from farms to the cities. People from other countries moved to American cities to find jobs. From 1870 to 1900, the population of the United States doubled in size.

All of this activity meant that some people became very rich and a few companies became very big. The decades after the Civil War are known as the Gilded Age. When something is gilded, it is covered with gold. By the early 1900s, the United States was the richest country in the world.

However, not everyone in America had a lot of money. There were a few very rich people and a lot of poor people. Many people in America earned small wages for their jobs. They did not have enough money to pay for a safe place to live. Many jobs in factories and mines were dangerous. When people got hurt or sick, they could not pay for good medical care.

Many Americans noticed these problems. The early 1900s became a time of reform in the United States. Reform means trying to change things so they get better. This time of reform is called the Progressive Era because it was a time when people wanted to make progress through reforms.

During the Progressive Era, laws were made to protect workers and make food safer. The government started to conserve natural resources by creating national parks. Women gained the right to vote.

In this issue of Studies Weekly, we will learn more about some of the amazing changes that happened in Pennsylvania and in the United States during the Gilded Age and the Progressive Era.

title: The Tale of Two Men: Andrew Carnegie vs. Henry J. Heinz
text:
Compare and contrast the business styles of Andrew Carnegie and Henry J. Heinz.

Proprietor: Andrew Carnegie

Type of business: steel manufacturing

Products made: steel cable, railroad rails, beams, plates, and building tools

Location: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

Employees: 3,500 men

Working conditions: heat from coal furnaces, molten steel, heavy equipment, loud noises, coal dust in air and on surfaces, 12-hour shifts, six days a week

Wages: daily, based on level of skill:

low skill (shoveling, raking): $1.40

medium skill: $2.25

higher skill levels (rollers): $5.10

Benefits: none

Union organization: Organization of labor was not permitted; labor organizers would lose their jobs; striking workers were met with armed security forces and military units.

Salary of the proprietor: $25 million as sole proprietor

Additional information: Carnegie was a philanthropist, donating libraries, concert halls, and universities to communities in the United States.

Proprietor: Henry J. Heinz

Type of business: food processing and storage

Products made: horseradish, pickles, tomatoes, ketchup, and vegetables in glass bottles

Employees: 2,000–18,000 men and women

Location: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

Working conditions: 10-hour days, six days a week, employee locker and shower rooms, dressing rooms and dining rooms, work uniforms provided, clean, safety precautions

Wages: $2 per day

Benefits: doctor and dentist visits, life insurance, death benefits for family, a safety office on site for first aid and hospitalization

Union organization: No Heinz employee ever went on strike or joined a union.

Salary of the proprietor: In 1900, H.J. Heinz made six family members owners of the company. He was not the sole proprietor. Profits were divided among the family members.

Additional information: The Heinz family continues to successfully operate “Heinz 57 Varieties.”

title: Child Labor
text:
Many new ways of making things were invented in the 1800s. Factories used new machines. Farmers and miners also used new machines. This period is called the Industrial Revolution. Many new jobs were created during this time.

Children did many of the new jobs in factories, in mines, and on farms. Children also worked as messengers, shoe shiners, and newsboys who sold newspapers. Families needed the money the children earned. However, the jobs were often dangerous and very hard.

Ten-year-old children often worked 12 hours a day for five or six days a week. In factories, there were accidents with unsafe machines. Small children had to carry heavy boxes and tools. Children working underground in coal mines had broken bones caused by heavy equipment. Even some children as young as four or five years old worked without pay as “helpers” for adults in dangerous places.

By the end of the 1800s, many people were concerned about the danger to children who worked. Many people wanted to make children safer. They also wanted to make sure that children got an education. When children worked such long hours, they did not have time to go to school. Organizations like the National Child Labor Committee were formed to tell people about the problem. They asked the government to make changes that would protect children.

Many states passed laws that limited child labor and required children to go to school. However, it was hard to enforce these laws. Employers often ignored them. Many families kept sending their children to work so the family could make a living. Years passed before the laws really protected children from doing dangerous jobs.

Today, most people follow the laws that protect children. Children do not have to work in dangerous places. Most children get the chance to go to school.

title: The March of the Mill Children
text:
In the early 1900s, more children were working at jobs in Pennsylvania than in any other state. Hundreds of thousands of children worked in Pennsylvania. Many of these children worked in cotton mills. A mill is a factory where pieces of cotton are woven to make yarn or cloth. Cotton mills used large machines that were dangerous for children who worked there. Children in these factories usually worked 11 or 12 hours a day, six days a week.

Mary Harris Jones was a woman who worked to organize better conditions for working people. She was known as “Mother Jones.” In 1903, Mother Jones visited the Kensington neighborhood in Philadelphia. Thousands of mill workers, including children, were on strike in Kensington. During a strike, workers refuse to do their jobs until they get better working conditions. Many of the children had lost fingers or hands in accidents at the mills. The children and their families were poor. The workers in Philadelphia wanted better pay. They also wanted to work only 55 hours a week.

Mother Jones wanted everyone in the country to know about the child workers. She organized a group of two hundred mill workers to march from Philadelphia to New York. Many people in the group were children. As the workers traveled, they gave speeches about the problem at the mills. They said the children needed to go to school instead of working in dangerous factories.

After three weeks, the mill workers finally arrived at the New York home of President Theodore Roosevelt. Roosevelt was the president of the United States at that time. The workers were not able to speak with him. However, newspapers all over the country reported on the march. The march helped many Americans learn about the problem of child labor.

title: Women Gain the Right to Vote
text:
When the United States Constitution was written in 1787, it only allowed white men who owned property to vote. Women could not vote. Black men and Asian men could not vote. During the 1800s, some people decided that this was wrong. They believed that all men and women should be able to vote.

Women who wanted to change the law created organizations for women’s suffrage. Suffrage means the right to vote. After the Civil War ended in 1865, new laws said that all men could vote, regardless of race. However, women still could not vote.

In Pennsylvania, there were women’s suffrage groups in every city. The first women’s rights convention in Pennsylvania was held in 1852 in West Chester. Women came from all around the country to talk about voting rights, education for women, and fair pay for women in their jobs. Suffrage groups in Pennsylvania kept working for many years.

The women in these groups held meetings, gave speeches, and made public demonstrations to convince people that the law should change. These women were brave. There were many people who made fun of them. Sometimes the women were even arrested. However, they kept speaking up for their rights.

Gradually, things started to change. In 1869, Wyoming became the first state that gave women the right to vote. Some other states also gave women the vote. Finally, in 1920, the United States Constitution was changed to let women vote everywhere in the country. Women in Pennsylvania voted for the first time on November 2, 1920. Today, women have the same voting rights as men.

title: Reforms That Made Life Better
text:
During the Progressive Era, reformers wanted to improve life for people who struggled to make a living. Reformers believed that there were ways to make life better for everyone, no matter how rich or poor they were. Many of these reforms improved American life permanently.

With a larger population, the United States needed more food. At the end of the 1800s, companies started building large food processing factories. Large amounts of meats, vegetables, and fruits were prepared in these factories. Unfortunately, the companies who ran the factories were not careful to keep food clean. People sometimes got sick from eating the food. Reformers passed new laws that required factories to treat food more carefully. Government inspectors started making sure that factories made clean food products.

By 1900, there were many new kinds of factories in the United States. The factories used large and dangerous machines. It was common for workers to be hurt at their jobs. Reforms changed the way factories worked to make them safer. New laws also created a system for paying workers extra money when they were hurt while doing their jobs.

As cities grew bigger, it got harder to keep them clean, safe, and beautiful. People learned that governments had to plan city growth. Governments started building public parks so everyone had pretty places where they could spend free time. City governments created sanitation departments to collect garbage and deliver clean water for people to use. Governments also started sending inspectors to make sure that apartments where people lived were clean and well-built.

title: Milton Hershey
text:
In 1871, when Milton Hershey was 14 years old, he started learning how to make candy. He decided he would earn a living as a candymaker. During the next 12 years, Hershey tried three times to start a candy shop. Each time, his shops failed to make money and went out of business. However, Hershey kept learning more about how to make delicious candies.

He finally succeeded by making caramel. His Lancaster Caramel Company sold caramel all over the United States. In 1893, Hershey learned how to make milk chocolate. Chocolate made with milk was a new kind of chocolate in those days. Milton Hershey believed that he could build an even more successful company by making milk chocolate.

Hershey built a giant chocolate factory in Derry Church, Pennsylvania. His new company made Hershey chocolate bars and Hershey Kisses. Today, more than 100 years later, millions of people around the world eat Hershey’s chocolate.

Milton Hershey did more than just make chocolate. He wanted the people who worked for his company to have a nice place to live. He built a beautiful town next to the factory. It had comfortable houses, nice streets, and good public schools. The town is called Hershey, Pennsylvania.

Hershey and his wife, Catherine, also wanted to help poor families and children. They created a school especially for orphan boys. Orphans are children whose parents have died. Hershey gave the school millions of dollars to make sure that the students got a good education. Today, students can still attend the Milton Hershey School.

title: Philanthropy
text:
During the Gilded Age, there were many problems to solve in

America’s growing cities and towns. It was also a time when some people in America were richer than ever. Some wealthy people decided to give their money to good causes. Donating money to help solve problems for everyone is called philanthropy.

We have learned about the ways that Andrew Carnegie and Henry Heinz created successful companies. They are two Pennsylvanians who became famous philanthropists.

In 1901, Andrew Carnegie sold his steel company for hundreds

of millions of dollars. He became the richest man in the world. Carnegie spent the rest of his life, until 1919, giving away money. His donations created more than 2,000 public libraries. He gave millions of dollars for colleges, universities, scientific research, and artistic organizations.

Henry Heinz was also one of the richest people in America. Heinz gave away millions of dollars to support good causes. Heinz’s children and grandchildren have continued to make donations in many ways that strengthen our community.

title: Being Dependable
text: Depending on someone means being able to rely on them to do something. Babies depend on their parents or guardians to feed, clean, and nurture them. You might depend on a neighbor or a parent to drive you to school. You might depend on your peers to do their part of a group project. Your teacher might depend on you to do your class job. Dependable people are those who do what they say they will do. They stick to their commitments. You can be a dependable person. You can follow through with your commitments. You have personal and social responsibilities, like treating others with respect, being kind, and being honest. When you carry out your personal responsibilities, you are being dependable. What are some other responsibilities you have? (Think about chores, jobs, and commitments to teams or activities.)

title: Respect and Dependability
text: Being respectful is another part of being dependable. Respect is being kind and accepting people with all their differences. In a classroom, you should be able to depend on others to respect each other. You can be respectful by appreciating people’s differences instead of making fun of them. You can be respectful by standing up to people who bully or tease others. You can be respectful and kind to people with disabilities or people who look or sound different than you. You can show respect through your words by asking kind questions to learn more about others and giving compliments. You can show respect through your actions by doing acts of service or not participating in gossiping or teasing. When you show respect to others, they will naturally want to be respectful in return.

title: Trust
text:
Trust means you believe someone. You believe what they say. You believe they will do what they say they will do. Choose to depend on people you trust. If you need to ask a friend to watch your pet while you are out of town, ask someone you trust and know you can depend on. You can trust someone you know will not forget to feed or take care of your pet. People you trust are usually dependable. Friends you trust will encourage you to make healthy choices. Friends you trust will respect you when you make choices that promote your health and well-being, like choosing not to drink alcohol or use drugs. Regardless of what your friends think, you can trust yourself and assume responsibility for your personal health behaviors.

Who do you trust in your life?

_________________________________________

_________________________________________

_________________________________________

title: How to Build Trust
text:
Trust is built like a tower of blocks. One piece is added at a time. Small, positive acts of respect and kindness add blocks to a tower of trust. When someone betrays your trust by telling a lie or treating you unfairly, it is like a few blocks being removed. If one person or group of people is bullying someone, you can say something. You can build trust by being kind to everyone and standing up for someone if they are being bullied. Bullying is unwanted and aggressive behavior that involves power imbalance, whether it is real or perceived. If someone is repeatedly mean to another person because of the color of their skin, their sexual orientation, or even the color of their hair or their style of clothes, that is bullying. You can build trust by not tolerating behavior like this. You can respond by changing the subject, calling the behavior bullying, or asking the victim if they are okay and helping them remove themselves from the situation.

Everyone makes mistakes. Trust can be rebuilt with more positive experiences, like being kind, helping, being honest, and following through on commitments. You can help contribute to an environment at your school, in your community, or even in your home that is respectful of individual differences between people. You can be someone who other people can trust. You can be trustworthy by always telling the truth, not gossiping, and doing what you say you will do. Pay attention to who you can trust. It is good to have friends you can trust.

title: Everyone Makes Mistakes
text:
Everyone messes up sometimes. You might be disrespectful to someone. You might tell a lie or spread gossip. You might forget about a commitment and let someone down. All of these things could result in other people trusting you less or depending on you less. Don’t get discouraged. If you make a mistake, you can fix it! It will take time and patience, but things will get better.

First, you can apologize quickly. Saying “I made a mistake, and I am sorry I let you down” can go a long way. Other people will appreciate it when you take responsibility for your actions.

Next, you can try to rebuild trust by learning from your mistakes.

Finally, you can do your best to not repeat your mistake and do things that show the other person you care about them.

title: You Can Forgive and Be Forgiven
text:
After making a mistake and trying to make it better, you probably hope to be forgiven. Forgiveness is when someone accepts your apology and moves on. Forgiving others can be hard, but it will help you and the other person feel better.

Be patient if someone does not forgive you right away. It can take time, especially if you made a big mistake.

You can choose to forgive others when they make mistakes. You can choose to forgive even if the person who wronged you does not apologize. What? Forgive someone who doesn’t apologize? Yes. Forgiving others helps you feel so much better. You do not have to wait for someone to say “sorry” to forgive them and start feeling happier. When you forgive someone, it means you are not holding onto anger toward them anymore. Now you can move on. That doesn’t mean that you have to trust them fully again. They still might need to do a few things to rebuild your tower of trust. You can choose to forgive others, and you can ask for forgiveness when you make mistakes. Asking for and receiving forgiveness from others helps you understand and relate to them better. You can show you are sorry with an apology and with your actions afterward. Your verbal and nonverbal communication about your mistakes will help you improve your relationships and your social and emotional health.

title: Communities
text:
A community is a group of people who work and play together. You have a home community. You have a school community. You have a friend community.

In your communities, you have responsibilities. One of your responsibilities is to make healthy choices. These choices are part of your responsibilities.

title: Online Communities
text: All community members can help each other make healthy choices. You show good character in your communities. Character is your thoughts, feelings, and actions. Online communities are where groups of people gather over the internet.

title: Media
text: Media lets you talk to lots of people. There are lots of kinds of media. Some are TV, radio, the internet, and social media. Media can help you find information. Internet media can help people share ideas. Media can help build communities. Be smart about what you share on media.

title: Bullying
text: Bullying is harmful. It is unwanted, repeated behavior. A person bullying others wants to cause harm. Cyberbullying is online bullying. Tell an adult if you see bullying. Bullying hurts communities.

title: Stand Up to Bullying
text:
You can make healthy choices. Standing up to bullying is a choice. It can improve your health and wellness. If you are being bullied or if you see bullying you can:

Say, “Please stop. That is bullying.”

Walk away and ignore it.

Talk to an adult who can help.

title: Be Alert
text:
Sometimes, people need help to stay healthy. Members of a community can help. Doctors help people who are sick. Dentists help people keep their teeth healthy. Teachers, counselors, and parents or guardians can help you too. They help you make healthy choices online and in real life. Citizens in any community can make healthy choices.

Talk about what you need.

If you see something that is harmful, tell an adult.

Ask for help when you see something dangerous.

title: Benefits of Taking Care of My Body
text:
You only get one body, so you need to take care of it! Caring for your body helps you:

Have more energy

Feel happy

Be confident

When you take care of your body, you’ll see how amazing it really is!

title: Nutritious Foods
text: How do you feel when you are hungry? You might feel cranky or tired. Your body needs food in order to work! Eating and digesting food is an important system in your body. Digesting is the process of your food breaking down and going through your body. Some foods are better for your body than others. Fruits and vegetables are great for you. So are beans, nuts, and whole grains. What’s your favorite healthy food?

title: Exciting Exercise
text: Moving your body is important. There are lots of fun ways to move. You can play tag or dance to music. You can do jumping jacks. You can hop around like a frog. You can even invent a new way of moving! Exercising makes you stronger and helps you feel happy. Take care of your body. Do a fun exercise every day.

title: Cleaning Is Caring
text:
You can care for your body by keeping it clean.

Use soap and water when you wash your hands.

Brush your teeth twice a day.

Take baths or showers.

Wash and comb your hair.

Wear clean clothes.

Brush your teeth.

Wash your hands after using the restroom or playing outside.

title: Sleep Helps Your Body and Brain
text: Doze, snooze, nap, and catch some “Zs.” Sleep is important! It gives your brain a chance to rest. It also helps your body heal and grow. Make sure you get 10-12 hours of sleep every night so you can feel your best.

title: Treat Bodies with Kindness
text:
Every body is unique, and every body is good. Every body deserves to be taken care of. You can take care of your body by protecting it. Parents can care for their children by helping protect them from dangers.

Risks

Protection

Sunburns and Overheating

Wear sunscreen, wear sunglasses, and spend time in the shade.

Falling

Follow warning signs like this. Walk carefully.

Car accidents

Wear a seatbelt.

Bike accidents

Wear a helmet.

Poisons

Pay attention to warning labels.

Lightning Storms

Find shelter, avoid water and tall metal fixtures, and get off elevated hills or mountains.

title: Why Are Goals Important?
text:
Goals help you progress (move forward) in every area of your well-being. Setting goals can help you make healthy decisions. If you know you want to become a doctor when you grow up, then you know you need to work hard in school to learn everything you can. If you know you want to be a photographer, you know you need to learn about cameras and develop healthy social skills so clients will want to hire you.

What do you want to be when you grow up?

Every choice you make has consequences. Healthy choices usually have positive consequences. Unhealthy choices usually have negative consequences. Some unhealthy choices and behaviors can distract you from your goals. No matter what your goals and dreams are for your future, you know that drugs and alcohol are substances that will not help you accomplish your goals. Your decision-making skills are also a powerful influence on your goal setting. Poor decisions can prevent, or stop, you from reaching your goals.

Steven sets a goal to run a mile under six minutes by the end of summer.

Is this a S.M.A.R.T. goal? Yes or No

Steven knows he needs to make choices that will help him remain safe and injury-free. He knows he needs to avoid harmful substances like drugs and alcohol to perform his best, so he sets a goal to remain drug-free. Steven chooses to eat nutritious food to give his body enough fuel. Stretching his muscles before and after his runs is important because Steven wants to prevent injuries. Hydration is another critical factor for Steven, so he makes sure to drink enough water before, during, and after his workouts to stay hydrated.

title: Sprint Goals and Marathon Goals
text:
Steven thinks about his running goals. He reflects on the success he had accomplishing his mile goal and decides to set a bigger goal.

Some races are short and fast. These are called sprints. Smaller goals are like sprints: they can be accomplished in a shorter amount of time. Steven knows that sprints require high amounts of very focused energy and effort. Sprint goals may only take days or even hours to achieve. Steven's one-mile run is an example of a sprint goal.

A marathon is a 26.2-mile race that usually takes runners a few hours to complete and many months to prepare for. Steven knows that a runner will not run a marathon and a sprint at the same speed. Marathons require different training and take more time to prepare for than sprints. Bigger goals tend to be more like marathons and may take months or years to achieve. Steven wants to run a marathon when he is older. That is a long-term “marathon” goal.

Short-term “sprint” goals can help you set and achieve long-term “marathon” goals. For Steven to complete his marathon goal, he created two sprint goals: to run one mile in less than six minutes and to run a 5K (3.1 miles) in less than 35 minutes.

If your marathon goal is to read a book with lots of pages, you can set a sprint goal to read one chapter each day.

If your marathon goal is to learn a new language, you can set a sprint goal to learn two new words in that language each day.

What is a marathon goal you have? _________________________________________________________

What is a sprint goal that will help you accomplish your marathon goal? _________________________

Any kind of goal can be stronger if it is a S.M.A.R.T. goal. Setting small goals can help your big goals seem more manageable and attainable. It also helps you make your goals more specific and realistic. You can use small goals to help you with the timing of meeting your large goal. Ultimately, setting small goals is part of setting a S.M.A.R.T. big goal.

title: Motivation and Discipline
text:
Steven just met his running goal.

After his race, he takes time to reflect on his training and set some new goals. Steven was motivated to run a mile in under six minutes because his older brother said it was impossible. Steven was motivated to meet his goal, so he made healthy choices and worked hard.

Motivation is when you feel like you want and need to do something. You are excited about getting it done. You might feel motivated to learn when you start a new activity or game.

There were some days when Steven felt tired or didn’t want to train. He used discipline to help him get his training done on those days. Discipline is when you do not want to do something, but you choose to do it anyway because you know you want to accomplish your goal.

Steven needed both motivation and discipline at different times. He needed support from family and friends at times. Steven made sure to tell his family he was eating healthy so he could train properly. His friends were excited for him and cheered him on at his race.

To reach your goals, you’ll need both motivation and discipline. You’ll probably feel motivated and excited right when you set your goal. Goals usually stretch a person and help them grow. This means that setting goals helps a person do new and sometimes challenging things.

Developing healthy habits helped Steven stay disciplined. He avoided making unhealthy choices and focused on achieving his goal. He stayed motivated by taking care of his body with stretching and proper nutrition. If Steven had not eaten healthy foods or taken care of his body, he could have felt sick and lost motivation or discipline. Steven knew if he used drugs or drank alcohol, it would impair his thinking and cause harm to his body.

To increase discipline, try to automate as much as you can. Every time you get in the car, it can be automatic to put your seatbelt on. Every time you get up in the morning, it can be automatic to make your bed. Every day when you come home from school, it can be automatic to wash your hands.

Avoid things that will impair your thinking and decision-making abilities like drugs and alcohol. Avoid situations that will cause unwanted or unnecessary stress on your mental health and social relationships, like gangs or cyberbullying.

Steven’s family and friends were a good support system for him. He followed some people on his social media account who trained properly and made healthy choices about running and nutrition. His friends even came to cheer for him at his race.

Social media, the people around you, and your family and friends may influence your decisions about goals relating to your health and well-being. You can also choose to be a motivating force to those around you. Encourage others to make healthy choices and set healthy goals. Making healthy choices improves your ability to stay motivated and be disciplined in meeting your goals.

title: Endurance
text:
Having endurance means that you keep going even though something is challenging. Long-distance runners, like marathon runners, need to build up their endurance. They do this by consistently increasing the mileage they run in a week.

Steven wants to run a marathon by the time he is 20 years old. For now, Steven decides his next sprint goal will be to run a race longer than one mile. He wants to do a 5K race, which is just over three miles. To prepare for his future marathon goal, Steven first works toward running a 5K. He knows he will need more endurance. He slows his mile time down and adds more distance to his runs. The first week, Steven gets used to running 1.5 miles consistently. The second week, Steven starts running two miles. Over time, Steven keeps increasing his mileage until he is able to run 3.5 miles without stopping.

When you set goals, you can build your endurance by pushing yourself just a tiny bit farther than you thought you could go at first. Over time, you’ll see you are capable of far more than you first thought you could do.

The most important time to use your endurance is when you make a mistake. Everyone makes mistakes. It’s normal, so don’t give up your goal just because you hit a bump in the road. You can fix what you need to and get right back on track.

Goals are even more satisfying to reach when you know you have to overcome obstacles along the way. Never give up! You can meet your goals.

title: Showing Kindness with Empathy
text: Empathy means understanding the feelings of another person. When you have empathy, you want to help others. Spending time with others can help you have empathy for them. Empathy helps you learn to treat people with kindness.

title: What Does Empathy Look Like?
text: When you show empathy, you look for ways to show kindness. You try to see things the way someone else does. Empathy can look like sitting with a friend and listening. It is sharing your feelings. Empathy is letting your friend know that you care.

title: I Can Listen to Others
text:
When you listen to someone, you pay attention to their words. You pay attention to how their face and body look. Think about what the person is saying.

Watch. Pay attention to how others feel.

Think. Have you experienced something similar?

Listen. Listen carefully to what others say.

Respond. Do or say something to help.

Practice. Go back to Step 1 and repeat.

Great work! KEEP PRACTICING! You are learning to feel and show empathy for others!

title: Feeling Stress
text: People have many emotions and feelings. Stress is a normal feeling. Stress can feel scary. Stress can feel frustrating. Many things can cause stress, like changes or challenges. Understanding stress can help.

title: Stress in the Body
text:
How do you know when you’re tired? You yawn. Your eyes feel heavy.

How do you know when you’re hungry? You have low energy. Your tummy growls.

When you feel stressed, your body will tell you. Your heartbeat speeds up. You breathe faster.

title: Stress in the Brain
text:
Stress can affect your brain. If you feel stressed, it can be harder to remember things. Taking care of stress can help your brain. Moving can help you get rid of stress.

Choose one of these movements to try right now:

Do five jumping jacks.

Stretch your muscles.

Wiggle your fingers and toes.

title: Stress in Emotions
text:
Sometimes stress affects your emotions. Stress can make you feel:

afraid

grumpy

moody

title: What Should I Do with Stress?
text:
Follow these steps to feel better when you are stressed:

Say how you feel.

Think about why you feel that way.

Close your eyes and take deep breaths.

Choose what to do.

title: Who Can I Talk To?
text: Which pictures show people you think you could talk to when you feel stressed?

title: When to Ask For Help
text:
When should you ask for help?

when you feel uncomfortable or unsafe

if you see someone has a weapon

if there is something you want or need

if you or someone else is injured

title: Who to Ask For Help
text:
When you need help, you need to know who to ask. Different people can help you with different problems.

Who can help you at school?

teachers

counselors

friends

Who can help you at home?

parents

siblings

neighbors

Who can help you in the community?

police

employees

doctors, dentists, and nurses

When you are not sure who to ask for help, look for someone wearing a uniform or nametag. People in uniforms are usually there to help you.

title: How to Ask For Help
text:
You can ask for help in different ways.

You can report a problem. That means you tell an adult something is wrong.

You can write a note.

You can use your words and say, “I have a problem. Can you help me?”

title: Emergencies
text:
Some problems are emergencies. An emergency is a problem that needs help right away. An emergency is when someone is in danger.

Fires, earthquakes, and hurricanes are emergencies. A person getting injured, lost, or kidnapped is also an emergency.

You should ask for help when there is an emergency. Asking for help during an emergency looks a little different than asking for help in other situations. In an emergency, you want people to hear and see you so they can help.

In an emergency, you can …

call 911 and ask for police or firefighters

scream or yell for help

title: My Morals and Empathy
text:
Is it right to lie? Is it right to cheat? The things you believe are right and wrong are called morals.

You can show what your morals are by what you do. Caring about the way your actions affect others is usually right. Showing empathy helps you understand others. Practicing empathy helps you do the right thing.

title: Empathy Activity
text:
Think about the way your actions affect people around you. Choose whether each picture shows someone doing something right or wrong. Think about how each choice will affect others. Then, circle which image demonstrates using empathy skills.

Stealing

Being Honest

Sharing

title: Respect Rocks!
text: Respect means you care about someone’s well-being. You are careful about what you say and do. Respect also means being kind and polite about differences.

title: We All Have Things in Common
text: We all have needs and wants. We are part of a community that works and lives together. We all have things we hope for. We are more alike than we are different.

title: A Helpful Tool
text: The internet is a useful tool. It can help you with school. It helps you communicate. You can also play games and have fun on the internet.

title: Social Skills
text: Having friends helps you feel happy. Being a good friend helps you be healthy. Social skills are skills you use to build friendships.

title: Facing Fear
text: Fear is an emotion. Fear is your body's alarm system for danger. When you feel fear, your body responds to the signals from your brain. Fear can be a helpful emotion. It protects you from danger.

title: Kindness and Respect
text:
Good friends are kind to each other. Good friends respect one another. How can you show kindness and respect?

Include others in activities and games.

Do not bully or tease.

Stand up to bullies.

Give others personal space.

title: Talking with Friends
text:
The way you talk and listen to others is a social skill. It can help you be a good friend!

Here are healthy ways to talk and listen:

Tell the truth.

Use kind words.

Listen when other people are talking.

Say what you think and feel.

title: Feeling Safe
text:
Feeling safe means knowing you are not in danger and that you have what you need. You have the right to feel safe. No one has the right to harm you or make you feel uncomfortable. No one has the right to make you feel disrespected.

If someone asks you to do something you feel is uncomfortable or unsafe, you can refuse by saying, “No, thanks.” If someone or something keeps you from feeling safe, comfortable, or respected, you can ask for help. There are people in your community who can help you if you ever feel unsafe or unhealthy. You can ask for help any time you feel you are unsafe or if you want to improve your health.

title: Riding a Bike
text:
When he was younger, Mom always told him what to do.

Not anymore. Cameron knew he should be safe.

He wore his helmet when he rode his bike.

He stopped at the corner and walked his bike across the street.

He never left home without talking to his mom.

Growing up was fun, but it was a lot of responsibility too.

title: Gather Information
text:
All kinds of information affect your choices. When you need to make a decision, learn about all your options. Gathering information can help you make the best choice that supports your health and wellness. Using a decision-making process reduces your risk of getting sick or injured. For example, you know it is safer to wear a helmet when you ride a bike. You also know that some of your friends think wearing a helmet doesn’t look cool. You can choose whether or not you wear a helmet. Thinking about the options helps you decide to wear a helmet and protect your brain. You can even set a positive trend for wearing helmets with your friends. Think about how each option might affect you and the people around you.

What information do you know about the options you listed?

title: What Things Can Help or Hinder Your Decision-Making?
text:
These things can help you make healthy choices:

Positive peer pressure

Goals

Wanting to feel healthy

Wanting to be happy

These things can cause you to make unhealthy choices:

Negative peer pressure

Hunger

Being tired

Sadness or frustration

Think about which of these things affects your decisions.

title: Playing Outside
text:
Today, Cameron was meeting Miguel to play soccer.

It was hot outside.

Cameron knew what to do.

He put on sunscreen. He put his helmet in his backpack.

He put his shin guards and cleats in, too.

Then he grabbed his water bottle.

It was time to go.

“Mom,” Cameron said. “I’m going to the park.”

title: Managing Peer Pressure
text:
At the park, Cameron saw Miguel. Lots of the kids from his soccer team were there.

“Come on, Cameron!” said Alana. “We’ve been waiting for you.”

Natalia and Aleki passed the soccer ball back and forth. Cameron joined in.

The kids played and had fun. Whenever someone made a goal, Cameron cheered. Cameron stopped the ball from going into the net. Everyone cheered for him. It was fun to be with his friends. When it was time to go, Cameron’s friends begged him to stay. Cameron told his friends he promised his mom to always go straight home after practice.

Alana said, “Oh, yeah, I promised my mom that too!”

Alana and Cameron got ready to go home.

title: Crossing the Street
text:
Cameron put on his helmet. He got on his bike and pedaled toward home.

At the crosswalk, Cameron got off his bike. He waited until the driver in the car saw him. Then he walked his bike across the street. There was a lot of traffic. Cameron was very careful. He followed all the safety rules.

title: Choosing Healthy Foods
text:
When Cameron came home, he was very hungry.

His mom waited for him while he washed his hands.

“Cameron, thanks for coming home on time. Here’s a snack,” she said. She gave him a sandwich and an apple. “Now, tell me how you did today.”

“It was great,” Cameron said. “I’m getting better at defending the goal.”

“Good for you,” Mom said. “You’re working hard.”

“Thanks, Mom,” responded Cameron, “and thanks for the healthy snack.”

title: Balancing Technology and Rest
text:
It was late.

Cameron was tired. It had been a long day. He knew he needed rest.

He showered and brushed his teeth. He even flossed.

“You look ready for bed,” Mom said.

Cameron knew that if he used the tablet, it would make it harder for him to go to bed.

“I am,” Cameron said. “But can we read our book first?”

“Sure,” said Mom.

Mom and Cameron read about dragons for a few minutes.

He was so tired that even dragons couldn’t keep him awake.

Mom turned off the light.

"Good night, Cameron. Love you," Mom said.

"Good night, Mom. Love you too."

Cameron fell asleep.

title: What Is Medicine?
text: Medicine is something that people can use to help their bodies and brains. Medicine can look many different ways. Some medicines are liquid. Some medicines come in a pill form. Some are small. Some help with headaches. Some medicines are helpful for people with conditions like diabetes or earaches. When kids need to take medicine, it is important that a trusted adult helps.

title: Emotional Changes
text:
Some changes will affect your emotions and feelings. As your body grows, so do your emotions. As you start transitioning from a child to an adult, you will have more complex emotions. For example, you are at the age that you may start to feel romantic feelings toward other people. You may find someone attractive. This is because of chemical changes happening in your brain and body. You may also start to feel bigger emotions than you did before. As you experience new or strong feelings, you may need to find new or better ways to express them and manage them. Here are a few ways to express your feelings during emotional changes:

Use your words. Talk to someone you trust about what you are feeling.

Cry. Crying is actually a great way to let out a lot of emotion. Just be sure to choose an appropriate place and time if possible.

Exercise. Exercise reduces stressful feelings and creates positive hormones in the brain.

Make a goal to stay in tune with your feelings. When you feel a big emotion, you can pause to figure out why you are feeling that way and what you should do with that feeling.

title: Why Is Medicine Used?
text: When a person gets an earache, they can take an antibiotic. An antibiotic is a type of medicine that can help an infection get better quickly. Insulin helps people with diabetes keep their blood sugar regulated. Medicine can treat and prevent diseases. A person should only take medicine if they need it.

title: Health Risks
text: Everything you do can impact your health. A risk to a person’s health is something that could cause their health to be affected negatively. Tobacco is a risk to a person’s health because it can cause cancer. Throwing a large rock is a risk because it can hit someone. Actions that hurt others are a health risk because they cause harm. If you know someone who wants to hurt others, talk to a trusted adult about the health risk right away.

title: Unexpected Changes
text: Unexpected changes are changes that you did not see coming. These could be things like the death of a loved one or someone near you becoming seriously ill. Losing your home or a parent losing a job might also be an unexpected change. Not all sudden changes are negative. Positive unexpected changes could be things like meeting a new friend, receiving a gift, or having a snow day. When unexpected changes come, you may need to practice being flexible. Being flexible is when you can easily adjust to something new.

title: Helpful or Harmful?
text:
Think about what is helpful and what is harmful to your body.

Helpful or harmful?

Harmful:

Taking too much medicine.

Taking someone else’s medicine.

Drinking or inhaling cleaning products.

Using drugs.

Drinking alcohol.

Helpful:

Eating fruits and veggies.

Taking the right dose of medicine for an earache.

Getting enough water each day.

Sleeping the right amount.

Exercising.

title: Refusal Skills
text: If someone offers you drugs, you can say “no.” Refusal skills are skills that help you say "no" when you need to. If someone asks you to do something that could hurt your body or mind, you can refuse and say “no.”

title: What Is Addiction?
text: Alcohol and drugs can be addicting. Screens can be addicting. Games can be addicting. Addiction means that a person feels like they cannot stop doing something. If a person is addicted to something, they can get help.

title: Coping With Change
text:
When you are going through any kind of change, there are some things you can do to make it easier. These four things can help you to enjoy life even when there is change. There will always be change.

Ask all your questions.

And ask the right people. You can ask a doctor or trusted adult questions about the physical changes in your body. You can talk to a teacher about the academic changes in the schedule or curriculum. You can ask your parents questions about an upcoming move or a new sibling on the way. Change is easier to handle when you know more about what is happening.

Do things you love.

When challenging changes are happening, try to make time for things you enjoy. Sing your favorite song, exercise, or read a book you love. Continue doing things that make you happy.

Try to keep some things consistent.

In times of change, think of things you can keep consistent from day to day. This will help you feel like your life is familiar, predictable, and in your control. You can create a morning or bedtime routine. You can choose to spend time with the same friends.

Distinguish between situations that require support from an adult and those you are equipped to manage independently.

Think about the skills you have. Think about the possible outcomes of the situation. Decisions that have long-lasting outcomes usually require a lot of thought and usually involve adult support.

title: How Do Addictions Start?
text:
Most things can become unhealthy if you do them too much. Eating cupcakes and other sweets can be fun and enjoyable. But if you have too many, it can make you sick. Technology can be helpful and entertaining, but if used too often, it can hurt your eyes, your brain, and even your emotions and relationships. Even exercise can become harmful or dangerous if it is taken to an extreme.

Everything you experience has an effect on you. You make decisions about your behavior and actions every day. A habit is something that you do regularly. You might be in the habit of brushing your teeth, cracking your knuckles, or saying specific words. Some habits are healthy, and some are not. A habit can become an addiction when you lose control and begin to be dependent on the habit. If you cannot enjoy regular activities because you are thinking about the habit, it has likely become a dependence, or something you depend on for regular function. An addiction is when the dependence becomes compulsive and harmful.

There is science behind addiction. Dopamine is a chemical produced in your brain that makes you feel good. A lot of positive, productive activities and foods can produce dopamine. Things like exercise, healthy foods, sunlight, meditation, and even the smell of cookies all help increase the amount of dopamine in your brain. Dopamine is your body’s internal reward system. When we do something that creates dopamine in our brains, we naturally want to do it again because it feels good. However, drugs and other harmful and addictive substances also produce a rush of dopamine. But these things are not good for our bodies or our brains. The dopamine in our brains makes us think that we want and need to do it again. The stages of drug dependence progress from experience to habit to dependence to addiction. When a person overloads their brain with dopamine from unhealthy sources, it can expose their brain to potential addiction.

Because many healthy things also create dopamine, it is important to pay attention to what you view, eat, and ingest. You can make choices about your body that are healthy. You can make choices that protect your body and brain, like getting sunlight, exercise, good sleep, and listening to music that makes you happy. Then you can make wise choices about the time you spend doing those things.

title: What Does Addiction Look Like?
text:
Addictions can affect people in every area of well-being: physically, mentally, socially, emotionally, and academically. Addiction affects people in different ways. Addiction is being obsessed with something and not being able to stop, even when you want to. Here are some side effects you might see in each area of well-being if you or someone you know is struggling with addiction:

Physically

Weight loss or weight gain

Poor hygiene (People may stop keeping their bodies clean if they are too focused on their addiction.)

Decreased coordination

Mentally

Distracted

Mentally distant (not being present in the moment)

Lack of motivation

Negative effects on sleep, memory, vision, and decision-making skills

Academically

Less interest in school

Late work or not completing assignments

Missing school

Not caring about grades

Socially

Being secretive or dishonest

Changing friends suddenly

Loss of job or money

Emotionally

Moody

Irritable and easily frustrated

Nervous or anxious

Keep in mind that these can be symptoms of addiction, but if you are experiencing some of these, do not assume you have an addiction. You should talk to a trusted adult or a doctor about your concerns.

title: How Can I Avoid Addiction?
text:
Make smart choices about your body and brain. You can make choices today and commit to avoid addiction in your future. Here are some ideas to help:

Set Personal Limits

Technology can be helpful, but it can also be very addicting. You can avoid screen addictions by limiting your screen time. Remembering the potential negative effects of screen addictions can help motivate you to limit your screen time. Some of these effects include weight loss or gain, having a hard time sleeping, headaches, eye problems, and anxiety.

Ignore Pressure

Ignore advertisements about addictive substances. TV, social media, and even video games often make it look like people who smoke, use drugs, or drink alcohol are beautiful, fun, and carefree. They intentionally use attractive models and beautiful locations like beaches. In reality, many people become addicted to those substances and face many challenges because of it. Companies like to convince more people to try their products. Some companies want you to become addicted to their products so that you will never stop buying them and they will make more money. Some companies even invest a lot of money to make their products more addictive.

Who or what could be a better resource to learn about a product that you think may be addictive?

Acknowledge Challenges

Many people believe that addiction is simply a matter of willpower. However, a number of genetic and environmental factors can make it difficult for an individual to avoid addiction. For example, a person who grew up in a home where smoking occurred daily already has exposure to cigarettes, so it may be more difficult to avoid for this person. A baby born to a mother who was using drugs while she was pregnant may experience harmful effects of the drugs without having made a conscious choice to use drugs. Each person has different life experiences that will affect their health and well-being. Acknowledge your own life and experiences. Acknowledge what challenges you may face in terms of avoiding addictions. Remember that addictions can make you feel like you don’t have a choice, but with support and the right resources, you can overcome and avoid addictions. Think about what is in your control to change or improve your health and well-being.

Make a Personal Commitment

Make a commitment to follow the rules. Schools and other locations in communities often have “no drinking,” “no smoking,” and “no drugs” rules. You can do your best to avoid addiction by following the rules of your school and community. You can avoid addictions by holding true to your personal commitments.

Use Prescriptions and Medicine as Directed

When dealing with prescription medicine (which is medicine given to you by your doctor that you must pick up from a pharmacy), only take medicine that is prescribed to you, and never take more than the amount instructed by your doctor. Taking someone else’s medicine or taking more than you are supposed to can be very dangerous and can lead to harmful effects, such as addiction. Taking someone else’s prescribed medication is illegal and can be very harmful.

When dealing with over-the-counter medicine (which is medicine that anyone can buy at a store), make sure you only take it if you are sick, and be sure you take the appropriate amount, as indicated on the bottle. When used correctly, over-the-counter medicine can be very helpful in healing your body.

title: Just Say "No"
text:
Gloria was hiking on a trail in the mountains. To her left, she saw a large cliff. Obviously, she doesn't want to fall. Should she peek over the edge?

Luca just got a new cast on his arm and is not allowed to get it wet. Should he dip his toes in the pool? What might happen if he does?

What do you think about these situations? What can you learn from these stories?

You can choose to stay far away from harmful situations. Walk away from any situation that may tempt you to try addictive substances. You cannot become addicted to something you have never tried before. Be aware of highly addictive substances like alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs, then make the decision that you will not use them. Any situation where someone offers you drugs is a great opportunity for you to practice your assertiveness and refuse (say “no”). Even if a friend or family member offers it to you, you can say “no.” If someone you know offers you addictive substances, it can be more tempting because you may want to feel like you fit in. But you can stay firm in what you know will keep you healthy. You can ask a trusted adult for help. You can also walk away. If you ever find yourself in a situation that makes you uncomfortable, you can make the choice to leave. Removing yourself from hazardous situations can help you avoid addiction.

If you are in a situation where people are offering you drugs or alcohol, or if you see people under the age of 21 drinking, leave and tell a trusted adult immediately.

title: How Can I Overcome Addictions?
text:
Addiction does not only affect the person struggling with the addiction. It can also affect their family members and friends. Having an addiction can alter someone’s judgment, meaning that they might not realize what is healthy and unhealthy. Someone with an addiction may not always act like themselves or treat others kindly. They might make poor choices because of their addiction. Things that were important to them before their addiction might not matter to them anymore. If you have an addiction, you can get help! Addictions don’t have to be permanent. You can take the right steps to overcome an addiction.

Here are some steps you can take to start overcoming an addiction:

Talk to someone you trust, like a friend or family member. You can also talk to a professional, like a therapist or doctor, if your addiction is dangerous or has lasted a long time.

Make a plan and set goals.

Tell people about your plan so they can support you.

Don’t give up. You can do it!

title: How Can I Help Others Overcome Addictions?
text:
If someone you know is struggling with an addiction, there are a few things you need to know:

It is NOT your fault. You cannot control what others do. Everyone is responsible for their own choices.

You CANNOT fix the person’s addiction. They have to do it for themselves.

You CAN ask for help. You can talk about your feelings with someone you trust.

Keep taking care of YOU.

People struggling with serious addictions can choose to use resources in their community to heal and recover. There are rehabilitation facilities where trained professionals can help people overcome their addictions.

title: Never Give Up!
text: Addictions can be scary, but never give up. You can say “no” anytime someone offers you alcohol or drugs. You can turn to reliable resources to learn about products to know if they are addictive or harmful to your body. You can ask trusted adults, counselors, and teachers questions. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration website also has reliable and accurate information you can trust. You can make smart choices that help your mind and body grow. You are smart. You are learning about the difference between what is healthy and what is not healthy. You know what will help your body grow and what will prevent it from growing and developing properly. You can encourage your friends and family to make good choices. Do your best to surround yourself with people who take care of their bodies and follow the rules. Be a force for good with your friends and family. Take care of your body and brain.

title: Benefits of the Internet
text:
The internet can be an amazing tool. Think of all the reasons you use the internet, including social media. Looking up recipes, watching entertaining or inspiring videos, and messaging friends who live far away are all positive ways to use the internet. Here are a few more:

fast communication

staying connected with people you don’t live near anymore

keeping others updated on your life

research or learning new information

spreading positive information and messages

When you use the internet in smart and safe ways, it can help you increase your knowledge. You can keep in touch with friends or family members who live far away from you.

title: Dangers of the Internet
text:
In addition to being helpful tools, the internet and social media also have some dangers. Being aware of the dangers can help you make better choices. Here are some things to be aware of as you spend time on the internet:

Cyberbullying: Cyberbullying is a serious problem on the internet. Cyberbullying is teasing or bullying someone using pictures or messages online, including on social media. People tend to say things online that they would never say to someone in person because they can’t see the person they are talking to or about. Many people believe they can post or do whatever they want online without consequences. Be respectful with what you send and receive. Talk to an adult if you are being cyberbullied or know someone who is being cyberbullied.

You Can’t Totally Trust: Some people on the internet pretend to be someone they are not. Predators are people who pretend to be someone they are not to get something they want. These people are manipulative and convincing. They may be friendly to gain your trust, but later, they may say things like “If you don’t do this for me, I’ll do this …” It is best to avoid talking to people you don’t know on the internet. A predator may try to convince you to do things you do not want to do or know you shouldn’t do. Then, after you do those things, they may try to use a poor choice you make to convince you to do more. Even if someone online sends you pictures of themselves and they look your age, you never really know who is on the other side of the computer.

Posting Is Permanent: People can post and screenshot anything that is shared online. If you post or send someone a picture of yourself, anyone can save it or take a screenshot of that picture and do whatever they want with it. Once you put something on the internet, you can never get it back. Even if you try to delete what you posted, it can still be accessed.

Remember Reality: Technology and social media can skew your view of reality. Technology affects your brain and can be hard on relationships with people in your life. It is easy to compare what you have to what everyone else says or shows that they have online. Comparing yourself to unrealistic depictions of reality can leave you feeling unsatisfied.

Search Smart: There is a lot of inappropriate content on the internet. Be careful and smart when you search for things online so you can avoid harmful images, videos, content, and influencers.

title: How to Practice Internet Safety
text:
Because the internet can be beneficial in so many ways, it is ideal not to cut it out of our lives completely. However, it is good to be aware of both its benefits and dangers. Without taking precautions, you may face risks to your personal health and safety.

Draw a picture to represent each of these guidelines you can follow to use the internet safely.

Set healthy limits. Be aware of how you spend your time. Don’t forget to develop your talents, study, and take time to be with friends in real life.

Follow school and family rules! Your school and community have rules that will keep you safe when you follow them. Your family can help you set healthy rules for internet use.

Keep personal information private. If someone asks you for your last name, address, birthday, phone number, or any other private information, do not share it. Say “no,” and tell an adult immediately.

Think before you post. Never post or send anything you don’t want everyone to have access to. People can screenshot and save your pictures. They can repost them or do anything else they want with them. Be sure that any picture you send, you are comfortable with your friends and family seeing it. You should feel comfortable with many people seeing any picture you post at any given time.

If someone sends you an inappropriate picture of themselves, tell a trusted adult immediately, such as a parent, teacher, or principal. Do not share the picture with friends. That is illegal. Report it, delete it, and ask that person never to send anything like that again. You may also wish to block or remove access for this person if the behavior continues.

If your friends or siblings think it’s cool to look at inappropriate images or videos online and invite you to watch with them, you can be resilient and assertive and say “no.” Tell an adult. Inappropriate images are harmful to your emotions and your brain.

If you have social media accounts, make the settings “private” so that only your friends can see your profile. Only let people follow you if you know them.

Practicing internet safety by adhering to, or following, these

suggestions will help decrease your risk of physical or emotional harm. If you decide to never send an inappropriate picture of yourself on your phone, no one else will ever have access to it. Make choices that will protect your health and wellness by deciding not to take or post compromising pictures of yourself or others. Making smart choices when using the internet will help keep you healthy physically, mentally, socially, and emotionally.

title: How to Practice Digital Citizenship
text:
If you are posting something or sending a message to someone, pay attention to the words you use. Real people with real feelings are on the other end of your messages. Never say anything online that you would not say to someone’s face. Being a good citizen means being kind and respectful to others. You can be a good citizen on the internet. This is called digital citizenship. Here are a few more ways you can display digital citizenship:

Use kind words. Do not insult, bully, or try to hurt people over text or social media.

Do not participate in cyberbullying.

If you see someone posting, sharing, spreading, or sending rude messages or images about other people, you can choose not to “like” or “share” that message or image. You can tell a trusted adult what is happening.

title: When to Ask for Help
text:
If anything you view while using the internet makes you uncomfortable, you can talk to a trusted adult and ask for help. Trusted adults in your life care for you and want to keep you safe, healthy, and happy. If you ever find yourself in a situation like this, talk to an adult you trust right away:

If someone you don't know in real life asks for your phone number, address, or pictures of yourself, say “no” and tell a trusted adult immediately. You should stop messaging that person.

If anyone sends inappropriate pictures of themselves or asks you to send them inappropriate content, tell a trusted adult immediately.

If you come across anything on the computer that makes you uncomfortable, you can get help right away. Turn off the computer. Block the user and report inappropriate content. Let an adult know what happened.

title: Changes and Feelings
text:
Positive changes usually help you feel happy. They are changes you look forward to. Positive changes could be things like getting a puppy or the seasons changing.

Challenging changes might cause you to feel negative emotions. You could feel stressed, anxious, or sad. Challenging changes might be things like your friend moving away or a birthday party getting canceled.

Talking about the way you feel because of changes can help you manage the changes in a positive way. Journaling or drawing can also help you manage changes in a healthy way.

title: Dealing with Unwelcome Changes
text:
When a hard change happens, it is helpful to have coping strategies (tools) to help you. Here are a few coping strategies you can practice when you experience an unwanted, scary, or sad change:

Name your emotions. Hard changes can cause strong emotions. It can be helpful to write down or talk about what emotions you are feeling.

Stay positive. Think about any good things that could happen because of the change instead of focusing on the bad. Remember: Things will get better.

Close your eyes and take deep breaths to calm down. If you get scared or nervous about a change, you might feel sick or shaky. You might feel like you want to hide or not talk. You can take time to calm those emotions by taking deep breaths.

Talk to people who are going through the same change. It can be helpful to talk to someone who is experiencing the same things you are.

Do something you love. Remember: Only some things are changing at once. You can focus on the good things that remain the same.

title: Why Is Critical Thinking Important?
text:
You make choices every day. You choose what to wear, what to eat, and who to spend time with. Every choice has a consequence. A consequence is a result. If you choose to eat sugary foods, the consequence is you might get cavities. Or if you choose to follow pool rules you will be safer when you swim. Critical thinking is important because it helps you make safe and healthy choices.

Jasmine wants to walk to school. Jasmine is a critical thinker. Let’s see what she does on her way to school…

Jasmine chose to cross the street at the crosswalk

Jasmine chose to look both ways before crossing the street

She made those choices because she knew that it would protect her from moving cars. Critical thinking helps you stay healthy in every way. You can think critically to make smart choices too!

title: Conflict
text:
Conflict can come in many different forms among many different people. Conflict is a disagreement between two or more people. Some conflicts are small, like arguing over who gets to use a resource in the classroom. Others are big, like countries or states arguing over natural resources. A conflict may occur because two people want different things and cannot come to an agreement. Conflict may occur between two people because they have hard feelings toward each other and are not able to forgive one another. Sometimes conflicts are really just a misunderstanding that can be solved with better communication. Other conflicts may occur because of differing opinions or perspectives. Conflict can even occur in cases of bullying or abuse, where a person is intentionally causing harm to another person.

Conflict can cause different emotions, like stress, anger, frustration, or sadness. Most conflicts are not permanent and are resolvable, which means they can be fixed. Having some conflicts in your life is normal. Learning how to resolve these conflicts will help you take care of your social, emotional, physical, mental, and academic health and wellness.

title: Opinions vs. Facts
text:
When you think critically, you consider facts and opinions. You think about what others say and think. You think about what is true. Culture is a mixture of facts and opinions and can also influence your thinking.

opinion: something someone thinks or believes

fact: something that is true at any time and for any person

These are examples of facts:

The sky is blue.

2 + 2 = 4

Apples grow on trees.

These are facts because they are always true.

What if everyone in your class believes it is healthy to wash their hands after using the restroom? You will probably choose to wash your hands too. The culture of your classroom is influencing your choices. You probably also know that washing your hands reduces germs. Choosing to wash your hands is using your critical thinking skills to take care of your health and wellness.

title: Prevent Conflict
text:
Bees are intelligent insects. They have a complicated communication system that allows them to find food and protect the queen and their hive efficiently. Bees plan ahead and store pollen so there are reserves during winter when pollen is in short supply. Bees work together to protect their hive and resources. Bees prevent shortages of food and injury to their hive or queen by working hard.

Like bees working hard to prevent potential problems, you can work to prevent conflict by planning ahead and cultivating positive personality traits. Your personal values and beliefs can help you. Your communication can help you. Your behaviors can help you. Here are some characteristics that can help you prevent conflict with friends, family, and others:

Be honest.

Be kind.

Be flexible.

Be forgiving.

Be humble.

Be inquisitive.

Be understanding.

Be willing to communicate.

Be mindful of the way media influences your health behaviors.

Be mindful of your actions.

How do you think each of these characteristics helps prevent conflict? Which of these would you like to develop so you can work to prevent conflict in your life? As you pay attention to your own behavior, also pay attention to the ways different things like media, family, peers, and school influence your health practices and your ability to navigate conflict.

title: Who Has Conflict?
text:
If you are facing a conflict at home with a family member or at school with a friend, don’t worry. You are not alone. Kids have conflicts. Adults have conflicts. Everyone experiences conflict at one time or another. Stay calm and stay positive, and you can help resolve the conflict.

You may have conflicts with your siblings, friends, or even strangers. Conflicts in family settings can be the most difficult and most emotional because people tend to spend most of their time with their family members. During the conflict, relationships can feel strained or weakened. However, two individuals who have a conflict can actually strengthen their relationship if they work together to resolve the conflict. Working through conflict helps you learn that you can resolve problems with others and what behaviors and characteristics tend to cause conflict. Keep a long-term perspective. Remember that getting through conflict with someone can strengthen your relationship.

title: Causes of Conflict
text:
The first step to resolving a conflict with someone is to identify exactly what the conflict is and what is causing it. As you are trying to pinpoint the problem, make sure you think about the conflict from the perspective of the other person too.

Did they see or feel something different than you?

Is there something you are missing?

Is social media influencing your reaction or behavior?

What is your perception of the norm (typical situation), and is it different from reality?

Is there any information you feel the other person doesn’t know?

You can even talk to others who are involved to make sure you completely understand their perspective and so they can understand yours. Sometimes it is best to work as a team to identify the conflict and the cause. If you do choose to identify the conflict as a team, you can both choose to stay calm and use your words to explain your side of the conflict.

title: Think of Solutions
text:
Alone or with the other person involved, you can think of solutions that may resolve the conflict. Some conflicts may have easier solutions than others. Some solutions will involve many people, and some you can find on your own. As you think of solutions for conflicts, try to think of everyone involved and how a possible solution will impact others. The goal of a solution is that everyone wins. Try to find a solution that would make everyone happy. Here are some ideas that can be used as solutions to conflict:

Apologize.

Invent something new that combines everyone’s suggestions.

Share resources.

Get help from an adult or expert.

Can you think of any other ideas that could help resolve a conflict?

title: Fix the Conflict
text: After you have identified a conflict and brainstormed solutions, it is time to put a solution into effect and see if it works. As you do your part to fix the conflict, keep in mind that you only have control over your own actions. You cannot force the other people who are involved to participate in the resolution or respond in a certain way. In fact, trying to control someone else would probably only result in more conflict. As you work toward solving the problem, remember that one problematic way to deal with conflict is with violence. Media often displays a lot of violence and yelling during conflicts. However, violence usually causes more conflict. Do your best to find another solution. Focus on staying calm and using your words to communicate your feelings, wants, and needs.

title: Ask for Help
text: If you and another person involved in a conflict cannot resolve it on your own, you can ask for help. If you are at school, talk to a teacher, counselor, or administrator. If you are at home, talk to a parent, older sibling, or trusted adult. Be mindful of others as you discuss the conflict and work toward finding and implementing a solution. No matter what the conflict is, you can work hard to find a solution that works.

title: Choices to Be Made
text:
The first step to making a choice is identifying the choice you need to make and knowing the best process to help you make the decision. Do you want carrots or broccoli? Do you want to do jumping jacks or jump rope? Do you need to do homework or practice your lines for the school play? These are examples of simple choices people make.

Some choices are more complicated, like who you want to spend time with and what you want to be when you grow up.

Some decisions are fun and exciting. Others can feel stressful or scary. You can use the decision-making process to think clearly about your choice, make the best choice for yourself, then reflect on your choice and its outcome. This process can help you become more independent and more confident in your decision-making skills.

Using a decision-making strategy helps you make choices that will improve your physical, mental, academic, social, and emotional health.

title: Gather, Create, and Predict
text:
There can be a lot to consider when you are making a choice. Do your best to gather relevant information. Create possible solutions, and predict possible outcomes of those solutions. Think about how your decisions could affect your own health and well-being and the well-being of others. Consider what factors are influencing your decision. Are you facing peer pressure from friends because “everyone is doing it”? Are messages from media sources attempting to persuade you to choose something? To make a choice you will not regret later, make sure you are the one who wants to make the choice and that you are able to manage the consequences.

Simple Choices
