Some choices need to be made quickly. You can weigh your options in your head.

Which do you want?

Which would make you happier?

Is it safe?

Do you need more time to consider which option will be best?

Complex Choices
Other choices may be bigger and have more of a long-term impact on you and your well-being. You may need more time to weigh your options.

You can utilize the decision-making process.

Make a pros and cons list to evaluate what options are best for you.

Here are a few questions you can ask yourself as you evaluate your options to make a decision:

Which choice would have more positive outcomes?

What negative consequences could come from these options?

What factors are influencing my decision?

Will it help me grow?

Could this choice hurt anyone, including me?

Why do I want to make this choice? Is the desire coming from me or from outside influences, like friends or media?

When you do the proper research and utilize a decision-making process, you will be more likely to make the best choice for you and less likely to regret the consequences of your choice later.

title: Utilize Resources to Help You Predict Outcomes
text: When you face a big decision, you don’t have to do it alone. You can talk to a trusted adult or friend. They can help you consider the consequences and go through the decision-making process. When you utilize resources to help you make the best choice, think about the possible outcomes your decision will have. Make sure you ask the right people for help. If it is a medical decision, talk to your doctor. If it is a social decision, like whether you should go to a party, you can talk to a friend or a family member. Turning to a trusted adult, like a parent or teacher, is also a helpful option if a decision becomes too stressful for you to make on your own. Sometimes, a decision needs to be made as a group. When this happens, think about collaboration, compromise, and cooperation.

title: Gathering Information
text:
Research means gathering information and facts about something. Each time you make a decision, you can research. When you are deciding what to eat for dinner, you might consider if you have any dietary restrictions (like allergies). You might think about special considerations (like if you have diabetes or have just been to the dentist.) This research helps you make informed choices. A person who is diabetic researches the nutrition facts of the foods they eat so their blood sugar doesn’t rise too quickly. A person allergic to dairy or wheat researches the nutrition facts of the food they eat so they don’t accidentally eat something harmful.

Some good sources to consider as you gather information are:

parents/guardians

nutrition labels

laws

classroom or school rules

consequences of your choices and actions

title: Peer Pressure
text:
Part of critical thinking is knowing about peer pressure and how to respond to it. Peer pressure is when peers (friends) encourage you to do something. Peer pressure can be negative or positive. Negative peer pressure is when your friends, family, or others encourage you to make choices that don’t consider your long-term health and wellness. If a friend tells you it is okay to break the law or take drugs, this is negative peer pressure. If a friend encourages you to wear your helmet while riding your bike or to say kind things to others, this is positive peer pressure. Think critically about the way you encourage your friends. Are you giving positive peer pressure or negative peer pressure?

Your friends’ opinions affect your own. You can think critically as you consider opinions and facts. You can think critically as you gather information. You can make decisions that will help you be healthy.

title: The Oil Industry in Pennsylvania
text:
Seneca Oil
Three hundred million years ago, plants and water were trapped under the Allegheny Plateau while the Appalachian Mountains were being formed. Pressure and heat over time created coal, oil, and gas pockets. The oil would seep or leak through the ground along stream banks. The crude oil is golden-brown in color. It is a sticky, gooey liquid that floats on top of water. The oil could be skimmed or removed from the surface. The Seneca skimmed the oil into containers. The oil was used as a salve. That means it was used as a healing ointment. It was also used as a tonic, or a drink used as medicine.

European settlers called the crude oil “Seneca Oil.” Settlers also used the oil as a salve or tonic. The settlers discovered the oil could burn. However, the smoke and obnoxious smell prevented further use as a fuel. The European settlers found the oil to be troublesome.

From the 1830s to the 1850s, many people experimented with Seneca Oil. Samuel Kier discovered the oil could be used to make different products. It needed to be heated or refined. The most valuable product was kerosene. Kerosene was used in lamps. To make products like kerosene, producers had to find more oil to meet the demand.

Drilling for Oil
In 1859, Colonel Edwin Drake and a banker, James Townsend, financed a drilling rig. Drake found William Smith, a blacksmith that worked for Samuel Kier. Known as “Uncle Billy,” Smith agreed to work the drilling engine and machinery. Drake was determined to drill for oil. Drake thought that oil had to be below the water in the ground. His plan was to drill past the water level into the oil pocket. Drake drilled a well near Oil Creek in Titusville, Pennsylvania. On Saturday, August 27, 1859, they hit oil. The great oil boom began. Within a year, more than 60 wells were drilled at Oil Creek.

The Oil Industry Begins
The area near Titusville and the Allegheny River Valley boomed with oil rigs and drilling crews. New people arrived making claims for oil. Pastures were filled with drilling equipment. Hillsides were covered in drilling huts. Towns were created overnight.

Other businesses were created because of the oil drillers. New jobs began that had never existed before. A refinery was needed to make kerosene. Barrels were needed to store the oil. Wagons and horses were needed for transport. Eventually, a railroad was built. It traveled to the most successful towns. Pipelines were used to transport oil from areas that were unreachable by roads. Iron tank cars were created to transport large quantities of oil.

Millions of dollars were made and lost in the rapidly growing economy. Eventually, one man came out on top. John D. Rockefeller organized Standard Oil Company in the 1870s. Standard Oil grew to dominate the oil business for the rest of Rockefeller's long life. Pennsylvania oil transformed the nation. And for decades to come, it would keep the nation dependent upon oil for its energy needs.

title: Ida Tarbell Investigates John D. Rockefeller
text:
John D. Rockefeller and Standard Oil
In the 1860s, John D. Rockefeller owned a small business in Cleveland, Ohio. In the neighboring state of Pennsylvania, the oil industry was booming. Oil is a natural resource that can be removed from the earth through drilling. Once removed, oil must be refined. Oil is refined by heating and cooling it to different temperatures. The refining processes create products like kerosene and gasoline.

Rockefeller invested in a Pennsylvania oil refinery. He then invested in more. Rockefeller continued investing in refineries until he was able to create the Standard Oil Company. Then Rockefeller invested in railroad companies that would transport the oil to and from the refineries.

Unlike Rockefeller, small drilling companies did not own refineries. These small companies needed to sell their oil to a refinery in order to make a profit. If the small company sold to an oil company that Rockefeller did not own, he would restrict transportation on his railroad. He would not accept their oil in his refineries. Oil was worthless if there was no buyer. Many small oil companies went bankrupt. Rockefeller would offer to buy their company. Through this process, Rockefeller created an oil monopoly in America.

Standard Oil made Rockefeller an extremely wealthy man. Later, Rockefeller followed the example of other moguls and became a philanthropist. Rockefeller foundations still exist today.

Ida Tarbell Takes Down Standard Oil
Muckrakers were the investigative journalists of the Progressive Era. They were writers, reporters, and photojournalists who went deeper than the surface-level facts of an issue to find out what was really going on. They investigated and exposed corruption in government and business. Ida Tarbell was one of the best muckrakers. She pioneered investigative journalism.

When Tarbell was 14 years old, her father had a small, successful oil refining business. He and his partner processed crude oil into a purer form that could be used in engines. They shipped it to customers using railroad lines.

Standard Oil Company was a large oil company owned by John D. Rockefeller. His company formed secret partnerships with railroads to raise the shipping prices. The railroads also gave rebates, or money back, to Standard Oil when they used their railroads to ship their oil. Many of the small companies couldn’t afford to pay the higher costs. When they struggled, Rockefeller offered to buy their businesses. Most of them sold, but Tarbell’s father wouldn’t sell. His company ended up in deep debt. He eventually had to mortgage the family’s house to pay the debts.

Ida Tarbell decided to become a writer when she was in college. After college, she was hired to write for a magazine called McClures. She wrote a series of articles about the French general Napoleon. She wrote another series about Abraham Lincoln. Her articles were so popular that subscriptions to the magazine doubled. In 1900, she saw her chance to fight for justice. Tarbell took on John D. Rockefeller and his Standard Oil Company.

Tarbell began to dig into the practices of Standard Oil and how they ran their business. She wrote a 19-part series and a book. Both were called "The History of the Standard Oil Company." The series of articles confirmed what many people had suspected for a long time. Her work uncovered patterns of deceit and corruption. She exposed efforts by Rockefeller to take complete control of the oil industry and its supply and distribution chains.

The information Tarbell published led to the break-up of Standard Oil’s monopoly of the oil industry. The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the company had violated the Sherman Antitrust Act. Standard Oil Company was broken into a number of smaller companies, which included Exxon and Chevron. These companies still supply oil and gasoline today. Rockefeller told his advisers not to comment publicly on any of Tarbell’s accusations, referring to her as, “that poisonous woman.” Tarbell’s courage and persistence resulted in justice. Her actions helped many small businesses survive.

title: Essential Question
text: How is continuity and change over time evident in the oil and gas industry in Pennsylvania?

title: Boom Towns
text:
The discovery of drilling oil directly out of the ground created a rush. Every available space in the Oil Creek and Allegheny River Valley was filled with drilling rigs. Each rig needed crews of laborers. There were six men on each crew. Crews included a blacksmith for working the drill. They also needed a mechanic to tend the engine. The rest of the crew helped prepare the oil for transportation. On some rigs, teams of laborers worked in shifts. By working in shifts, the crews kept the rigs running 24-hours a day.

Drilling rigs were built quickly. Fifty of them could be constructed overnight. That meant at least 300 crew members would need to live nearby. Their families might come too. Hundreds of people would need food and shelter. New towns could pop up in a matter of months.

Pithole was a boom town. That means it grew quickly. It was located in Venango County. The town was founded in May of 1865. By December, seven months later, there were 20,000 people there. Fifty-four hotels were built in Pithole. There were also three churches, a newspaper, a theater, and the world's first pipeline. The pipeline was used to transport oil to trains. In Pithole, the oil business was exploding.

The success wouldn't last. In the 1870’s, there was a great fire. It destroyed blocks of buildings, including 27 wells and drill huts. Difficulties continued for Pithole. Over drilling and depletion of oil ruined the town. Oil was being discovered in other areas of the valley. People moved to new towns, closer to the new discoveries. By 1877, the Pithole hotels were empty. Families and businesses had moved away. There was nothing left there to call it a town.

In 1961, the site was donated to the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission. A visitor center was built there. It remains to help educate people about the booming days of oil.

title: Population of Titusville 1850 - 1920
text:
Historians use data to understand what life was like in the past. They use the data to support information gained from other sources. Sources can include narratives, images, and artifacts.

Information from the U.S. Census can give historians insight into a time period. They can create an idea of what was happening in a specific location during a specific time.

title: Oil and Gas Today
text:
Natural Gas
Pockets of natural gas were discovered when crews drilled for oil. The gas was made from vegetation that decayed millions of years ago. Natural gas is often found near oil. Natural gas can be trapped in gaps between layers of rock. Gas can also be trapped in the tiny spaces between shale or sandstone layers. Natural gas can be accessed by drilling. The gas is brought to the surface. From there, it is transported by pipeline to processing centers. Natural gas is odorless. A harmless chemical is added to give it a scent. Natural gas can be used as a fuel. It can also be used as material in other products. After processing, natural gas is distributed to consumers in pipelines or container tanks.

Pipelines
The Federal Department of Transportation regulates the transport of oil and gas. Oil and gas are moved across the country to consumers. There are regulations and laws to keep consumers safe. There are also laws to protect the environment. Pennsylvania has more than 93,500 miles of pipeline. The pipelines can be built both above ground and below. Some pipelines are made of metal, such as steel. Others use high-grade plastic. The pipelines lead to processing centers. That includes refineries, distribution centers, and transmission centers. These processing centers help get the product to consumers.

Active drilling in Pennsylvania Today
Oil and gas drilling are not a thing of the past. Since 2014, Pennsylvania has seen an increase in drilling for natural gas. Drilling companies have to obtain a permit to drill. The permits are given out by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP). Drilling can't begin until a company has a permit. To get a permit, the drilling company has to provide a safe workplace. There are also safety rules for the environment. Inspectors from the DEP review drilling sites. Drilling companies can be fined if there are violations. They can even be shut down. Over $2 million dollars were collected in fines and penalties from drilling sites in 2020-21. The money is used to run the DEP. It is also used to help clean up environmental hazards.

title: Careers in Oil and Gas Industry
text:
At the end of 2020, there were 250,000 employees in the oil and gas industry nationwide. That's not even including government inspection and regulation departments. There are many different jobs in the oil and gas industry. Each job varies, with different physical demands and education requirements.

The oil and gas industry has three areas of focus:

Extracting, or removing, oil and natural gas by finding and drilling for them.

Transporting the raw materials to processing centers. This includes pipelines, trucking, and shipping.

Refining the natural resources to create products for consumers.

Some jobs are spent outdoors. Others are spent in offices. Some of the oil and gas jobs even require traveling the highways. Driving a gasoline tanker truck to gas stations is considered one of the most dangerous jobs. Whatever the position, the oil and gas industry is a major employer in Pennsylvania.

title: Brain Power
text:
Your brain is amazing! It can do so many things. Your brain takes in information. Your brain can create new ideas. Your brain tells your body what to do. What you put in your body affects your brain. You can take care of your brain when you pay attention to what you put in your body.

Draw some of the things that go on in your brain:

title: Make a Choice
text: After doing research, asking questions, and weighing your options, you are ready to take action. Make choices that will help you reach your goals. Make choices that will help you grow. Make choices that will take care of your long-term health and well-being. You can choose to follow the rules. You can make healthy decisions about your body and your social interactions. Make choices that align with your values and beliefs and that will help you to be your best self.

title: Addiction
text:
Addictions are dangerous habits. An addiction is a chronic need for a substance or activity. It happens when your brain tells you that you need something and you struggle not to do it. Addictive substances change the chemicals in the brain. They make someone think they need the substance.

Some things are addictive, and some things are not.

Not Addictive:

water

chicken

crackers

Addictive:

sugar and caffeine

tobacco (smoking)

alcohol, drugs, and vaping

You do not need to be afraid of addiction. You can choose NOT to consume addictive substances. You can not become addicted to something you have never tried.

title: Reflect
text:
Every choice has a consequence. A consequence is an outcome, good or bad. After making a choice, you can reflect on your actions. Think about when you look in a mirror. You see your reflection. When you make a decision, you can “look in the mirror” by thinking about the consequences of your choice. You can reflect by asking yourself questions.

Who did my decision affect?

Were there mostly positive or mostly negative outcomes?

Was my choice good for my health?

Did my choice have any unexpected consequences?

Would I make that choice again?

Reflection can help you know if you made the best choice. When you think about your past decisions, you can learn from them. Lessons you learn can help you make better choices in the future. If your decision negatively affected someone, you can choose to apologize and make better decisions the next time you face a similar situation.

title: Make Adjustments
text:
If you are happy with your choice and, after reflecting, you still feel like it was the best choice you could make, then celebrate and congratulate yourself. If, after reflection, you realize there was a better choice to be made, that’s okay too! Everyone makes mistakes, and you can celebrate the fact that you are learning from your experiences.

You can make adjustments. In some situations, you can simply change your mind and choose something different. In other cases, your choice may have been more permanent. Permanent choices are harder to take back. They could include saying something unkind, bullying, or missing a homework assignment.

If you have made a permanent choice and realize it was not the best choice, apologize to anyone you may have hurt. You can make new choices to fix your mistakes.

title: Dangers of Drugs
text:
Drugs, alcohol, and tobacco are very addictive. When a person tries them, their body and mind thinks they need the drugs all the time. It can be hard to stop.

Drugs hurt your brain and your body. Some of the negative effects drugs have on people can cause them to:

Treat others unkindly

Neglect keeping their body clean

Use money unwisely

Drugs can also:

Cause harm to teeth and gums

Cause cancer or other diseases

title: Medicine and the Brain
text:
Medicines are chemicals that can help your body heal. Medicines can be very helpful when you use them the right way. That means taking the right kind of medicine and taking the right amount. Some medicines have to be given to you by a doctor. These are called prescription medicines. They are stronger than other medicines that might be in your home. Prescription medicines are only for the person the doctor gave them to. Medicines that can be purchased at the store without a prescription are called over-the-counter drugs.

Medicines can help your body if you need them. But they can also hurt your body and brain if you do not take them correctly or take them when you do not need them. Trusted adults can help you know which medicine to take, when to take it, and how much.

Name three people who can help you know when and how to take medicine.

Draw a picture of how you feel when you are sick:

Draw a picture of how you can feel when you use medicine correctly:

title: Phenomenon Comic
text: Phenomenon: Sandcastles at the beach can get knocked over without people touching them.

title: Why Does Motivation Matter?
text:
Motivation can help you get things done. It can help you reach your goals and get excited about learning and growing. Finding things that excite you can help mundane tasks become more enjoyable. Reflecting on and paying attention to your motivation can also help you make decisions about your skills and talents as you look forward to the future. Understanding your motivation can help you make decisions about your education, family, and career.

Mandy always wants to help others. She invites and encourages her friends to make healthy choices. She’s also a very good student in math and science. These subjects come easily to her, and she enjoys doing her homework. Mandy talks with her father about wanting to be a doctor when she grows up so she can use her skills and motivation to help others.

Being motivated toward something can help your decision-making. Knowing what you want and why you want it will make your choices along the way much easier.

Mandy is motivated to get strong grades in all of her classes. She wants to qualify to get into medical school so she can become a doctor. She enjoys her homework and classes and is intrinsically motivated to do well. When her friends want to skip studying for a test, it isn’t even a question because Mandy is intrinsically motivated. She studies so she can perform well on tests.

title: Resilience
text:
Resilience is being able to adapt to change and recover from difficult situations.

As you grow up, you will face new challenges that stretch your abilities and talents. Learning to be resilient can help you bounce back from failure and be willing to take on new challenges and experiences. Your personal attributes, core values, and your ability to be resilient will help you take care of your health and wellness.

When her teacher introduces a new concept at school, Gina is resilient. She keeps trying to figure it out, even though it’s really challenging.

When his soccer coach teaches their team a new play that Miguel doesn’t understand yet, Miguel is resilient. He’s resilient because he keeps practicing, has a good attitude, and works until he figures the play out.

Steven is resilient when his little sister keeps taking his belongings. Steven feels frustrated, but he adapts to the emotions. He thinks of a way to help his sister play with other things instead of taking all of Steven’s model airplanes.

Alana is resilient after she does poorly on a test. She realizes she didn’t study like she should have. She talks to her teacher and plans to study better next time.

Being resilient means you don’t give up when things get hard. You bounce back quickly after a challenge. You can learn to be resilient at school when you are learning new things. You can learn to be resilient by forgiving others. You can build resilience in many ways, especially by trying new things and setting goals.

title: Resilience in Your Feelings
text:
Everyone goes through struggles. Your attitude and what you do with your feelings can make those struggles harder or easier. Emotional resilience is when you are able to manage negative emotions in a healthy way. You can manage your response to stressful situations or crises. There are many things you can do to build emotional resilience.

Kevin keeps a gratitude journal and chooses to think of things he’s grateful for. Expressing gratitude conditions your brain to filter negative thoughts and focus more on the positive. Writing down his grateful feelings helps Kevin spend more time thinking about what is going well instead of what is not.

Tavian tries to laugh every single day. Laughter decreases levels of cortisol (a stress hormone) and increases feel-good hormones like dopamine, oxytocin, and endorphins. Laughter can increase motivation, attention, and learning. After Tavian laughs, he feels like his emotional battery is recharged and he’s ready to go.

Melani loves to spend time with her friends. She has learned that being with other people helps her experience more positive emotions. When she’s around her friends, Melani can manage stressful situations in a more healthy way.

title: Resilience in Your Relationships
text:
Social resilience means the ability to bounce back when faced with stressors involving other people. You can increase your social resilience by choosing to spend lots of time with friends, family, or other people. Do your best to spend your time with those who are kind to you and build you up. When you encounter someone who is not kind, you can take care of yourself by telling them what you need.

Alana just moved to a new school. She is nervous about making friends and doesn’t know anybody. Alana introduces herself to someone and is rejected. She feels devastated at first. Then she remembers that everyone is different and has different experiences and interests. Alana loves to dance. She finds out where the dance team practices and who is on the team. She is socially resilient because she doesn't let one failure to make new friends affect her negatively. Alana tries again and finds a group of friends that fits her personality. Eventually, Alana makes many new friends and enjoys being at school.

Building social resilience helps a person know they deserve to be treated kindly. Sometimes peers ask one another to do something that’s not healthy. A socially resilient person is confident enough to refuse drugs, alcohol, or dangerous activities or objects.

Everywhere you go and everyone you associate with can influence the way you think and act. Your response can result in positive or negative consequences. You always have a choice in how you respond.

If someone asks you to do drugs or something else harmful to your health, you can be socially resilient by saying, “No. I have made a choice to not do things that can harm my body.”

You can walk away from dangerous situations.

You can stand up to bullies or stand up for victims of bullying behaviors.

You can withstand negative peer pressure.

Social resilience is the power to stand up for yourself and others. To help you build more social resilience, choose to spend time with people in places that will improve your health and not damage it in any way.

title: Saying “No”
text:
You can protect yourself and others when you say “no” to unsafe or unhealthy situations.

WHEN TO SAY “NO”:

If someone is offering you drugs, cigarettes, or alcohol, you should say, “No.” If someone is offering you medicine that is prescribed to them or medicine when you are not sick, you should say, “No.”

HOW TO SAY “NO”:

You can say “no” with your voice. That means saying or signing the word “no.” You do not need an excuse or a reason to say no. If you know it is wrong or unhealthy, just say, “no.”

You can say “no” with your body. That means walking away or putting your hand out.

You can say “no” with your actions. That means you can choose to stay away from parties or gatherings where you know there could be drugs or alcohol.

title: What Is Assertive Communication?
text: Assertiveness is a healthy and responsible way of communicating to others. It's the ability to look at others while you are talking and to speak up for yourself. Being assertive is being honest, caring, and respectful. Assertive people listen to what others have to say, even if they don't agree.

title: Styles of Communication
text: The style of your communication can affect your message. Being assertive is the best way to communicate because it is honest and respectful at the same time. There are other styles of communication besides assertive. Passive and aggressive communication styles are usually not as helpful as being assertive. Passive communication means you do not communicate what you think honestly. Aggressive communication is when you share your thoughts in a rude or harsh way. This type of communication can hurt people.

title: How Addiction Starts
text: When you experience something that you like, your brain remembers that good feeling and wants to experience it again. The more you repeat the experience, the more your brain wants it. This cycle in your brain can create an addiction. An addiction is a powerful feeling that tells you that you need to have a certain experience again and again. Addiction is hard to control. It can affect your daily life and ruin your friendships.

title: Confusing Wants and Needs
text:
When someone is addicted, their mind and body start to confuse wants and needs. Their mind tells them they need to do something, like play video games for just a little longer. But really, it’s just something that they want.

A person's body can also tell them it needs something that it really doesn’t. Remember that addictions are hard to control or stop. Sometimes, a person might feel like they need something that is very harmful. Addictions have many consequences.

title: Warning Signs
text:
Just like road signs warn us about hazards, people with an addiction can show signs of needing help. These signs don’t always mean someone has an addiction. They might mean someone needs help. If you’re worried, talk to a trusted adult. These are some of the warning signs.

Doing something even if it hurts them

Getting angry if they don't get what they want

Feeling sick if they don't get what they think they need

Not doing things that used to be fun

Wanting to be alone

Lying or hiding things

title: You Are Not Alone
text:
Asking for help is one of the smartest, bravest choices you can make. If you think you might have an addiction, talk to an adult you trust. You can also talk to a relative, school counselor, teacher, or school nurse. You are not alone!

An adult can also help you if you’re worried about someone you love or if someone else’s addiction is hurting you.

title: Making Plans to Improve
text:
Want to change your behavior? Here are some tips to create a plan.

Start with something easy. For example, replace one minute of screen time with something else you enjoy. Slowly add more minutes every day.

Notice what’s holding you back. For example, maybe you want to drink less soda, but you don’t like the taste of water. Brainstorm solutions.

Make a plan for hard days. For example, plan to talk to a caregiver or trusted friend when you’re having a hard time sticking to your goals.

title: Understanding Impulse
text:
Part of understanding addiction means understanding impulses. If your favorite game was open in front of you, what would you want to do? Play it. That is an impulse. An impulse is suddenly feeling like you need to do something. You may choose to act on that impulse by playing the game without thinking about what else you should be doing.

Part of making healthy choices is noticing your impulses and learning how to manage them. To practice controlling your impulses, try this: stop, think, and act. When you start to do something automatically, stop. Think about why you’re doing it. Think about what you could do differently. Then, act thoughtfully.

title: Specialization
text:
What are you good at? Do you like to draw? Play a sport? Beat video games? People have different strengths. That’s why specialization works in an economy. Specialization means that a person, company, or country concentrates on what it does best.

For example, many people are skilled at working on cars. In one community, a company might specialize in fixing car engines. Another company in the same community might specialize in repairing the outside of cars when they are dented or scratched. Both companies are in the same field: helping people maintain their cars. However, since each specializes in one skill, each company can focus on using that skill very well.

People who specialize in a specific good or service are called specialists. You might have visited a doctor who was a specialist. That means that the doctor spends a lot of time on a specific part of people’s health, such as the health of people’s stomachs or the health of children. The doctor did learn other things in medical school, but specializing in one thing means that they know even more about it. Other fields of work have specialists, too, and different parts of the world specialize in things, just like people do.

title: Why Divide Labor?
text:
A busy floor in a clothing factory is abuzz with activity. At large tables, workers use cutters and patterns as they snip smaller pieces from long swaths of fabric. Those smaller pieces are moved to sewing machines, where other workers join them together. Farther down the line, even more workers add finishing touches, such as buttons, to the clothing. At the end of the day, the team has produced many similar pieces of clothing. The way they work is a relatively new way of doing things.

Cottage Industries

For much of history, people producing goods worked alone on many steps of the process. In the above example, three different teams worked to sew a piece of clothing. Even more workers were involved in producing the fabric and designing the clothing. In the past, one person would have done most of those steps. One person would have woven the fabric to make a shirt. They would have decided on the design of the shirt and cut pattern pieces. Then, they would have sewn the pieces together to make the shirt. Finishing touches, such as buttons, would have been their job, too.

This way of doing work is sometimes called the “cottage industry” method. When you hear the word “cottage," you might think of a small house in the woods. Cottage industries were run out of people’s homes. One person in town might be a tailor making clothing. Another would work all day making shoes. Down the street, one person could build a wagon for you from start to finish.

Division of Labor

In modern times, having large numbers of people living in one place means that labor can be divided. In one factory, many people could work different jobs to make one type of product. Cars were produced in this way soon after they were invented. People would stand at an assembly line in a car factory. As the cars moved down the line, each person would add a part. One person’s job might be to add tires. That would be all that person did all day. As soon as a car got to their place in the line, they would attach the tires. Then the car would move on to the next person, who would attach a different part.

Assembly Line Advantages

Think about how many more shirts the people in the clothing factory could produce than one person working as a tailor from home. In one day, a group of people could produce many, many shirts, while the tailor would probably have produced only one. In modern times, assembly lines and dividing labor have greatly increased productivity. There are countless goods available for sale. With more goods available for sale, the owner of a company could make a lot of money. There are also more jobs available for people. The economy grows as more money changes hands.

Disadvantages

Not everything is about time or money, however. Goods speedily made by many on an assembly line may not have the same quality as goods carefully made by one person from start to finish. A tailor making a shirt for one customer can devote the time to making something really special, but they will also have to charge a high price for it. Factory workers might take pride in the product their factory makes, but a lack of opportunity for training or education might mean they will work for a long time in one spot on the assembly line.

Both the cottage industry and the assembly line methods have advantages and disadvantages. Depending on consumers’ needs and purchasing power, they both have a place in the modern world.

title: Productive Regions
text:
The Western Hemisphere is a vast area with many different countries and geographical regions. Because of this, the North and South American continents are rich in natural resources. Some resources exist underground, such as oil, gas, coal, iron, metals, and gemstones. Some regions have thick forests for lumber. Others have acres of farmland perfect for growing crops, from Canadian wheat to Brazilian coffee beans. Some have robust fishing industries. Many parts of the Western Hemisphere produce resources used by people worldwide.

Just having resources in the environment isn’t enough, of course. After all, large-scale crop farms don’t plant themselves. Trees don’t turn into lumber without help. Most minerals stay underground unless someone digs them up. People work hard to gather resources in their environment. People also have to work to transport the resources to places that need them.

Big Resources, Small Populations

Gathering any kind of resource requires some skill. Bringing oil to the surface from beneath the ground takes a lot of specialized tools. It also takes teams of workers who know how to use the machines. An oil rig is a structure that has machines that drill for oil. Many people with specialized jobs work on an oil rig to operate the equipment.

The places where people drill for oil tend to have smaller populations. A lot of land is needed to drill for the oil. The U.S. has the largest oil reserves in the world. Many of the places where oil is located, such as Wyoming and North Dakota, have smaller populations anyway. There aren’t millions of people close to an oil rig who know how to do the work. Oil companies looking for labor have to attract people to the job. By offering higher pay and training, oil companies can get workers from other places to move there.

Some oil rigs are in the ocean, such as in the Gulf of Mexico or in the Atlantic Ocean near Guyana and Suriname. These are known as offshore oil rigs. The work of bringing oil up from the ocean’s floor is difficult. Some parts of the job can be dangerous. There are large, heavy machines like cranes constantly moving. The oil itself is highly flammable. Living far from the land can also be challenging. Workers must stay on the large oil rig. They are often away from their families for long periods. Even if the pay is good, it is hard to find a lot of people who will do this job.

Big Populations, Small Resources

Other regions have the opposite problem. They have large populations. That means that there are many people looking for work. If the regions they live in are not rich in resources, these people have to leave to find work in other places.

Sometimes, these people become migrant farmers. Migrant farmers are seasonal workers who live in one place but go to work on a farm during the growing season. Brazil has about 300,000 coffee plantations, as well as large cattle farms. Many migrant farmers come from other South American countries looking for work. Migrant farmers also travel from Central and South America to big U.S. fruit farms in states like Florida and California.

The California Gold Rush

Some resources are renewable. That means they can be replaced or replenished. These include water, farm animals, and crops. Some resources are not renewable. These include oil, gas, coal, stone, and metal. Sometimes, a resource runs out. A famous example comes from the California Gold Rush. In 1848, a worker at a sawmill near Sacramento, California, found gold in a stream. Soon, millions of people rushed to the area to try their luck. The population of towns in California boomed as people worked to find gold. Some people were lucky. They found gold and were able to sell it for a lot of money. But there just wasn’t enough gold for everyone. There were too many people drawing upon a single resource. Most people had to give up and look for other kinds of work. Many places turned into ghost towns as the people who had moved there realized there weren’t enough resources or jobs for them.

Different Environments, Different Resources

Earth does not distribute resources equally. The kind of land, the climate, and millions of years of changes led to some regions being richer in resources than others. Population isn’t distributed equally, either. When a large number of people live near an abundant resource, that region will be able to gather and trade that resource. If a population is too small, that region won’t be able to produce much unless workers come from other places. If a population has no abundant resources close by, then many may have to seek work away from home.

Finding, producing, and transporting resources is not an easy job. The people who work with natural resources are doing important work. They are helping to support populations around the world. They are also helping themselves and their families. As long as there are resources available, there will be people working to harvest them and bring them to market.

title: What Can It Provide?
text:
Different regions have different kinds of resources that people find useful. It’s all a matter of geography. The Pacific Northwest has the right kind of land and climate to encourage the growth of large trees. This region has a large production capacity for lumber. This means that people living there are able to work to produce a large amount of lumber.

In a desert region, such as southern Arizona, there is not enough rain to grow large trees. There is no way that thick forests will cover the land. So, this area does not have a large production capacity for lumber. People who need lumber know that they will not be able to get lumber from there. People who live there will often use other materials to build, such as concrete, stone, and adobe brick.

Some places are wealthier in resources than others. Whatever that might be, every region of the world has some kind of useful resource. Think about the Arctic. There are fields of ice spread out in every direction. Farming is difficult. In some areas, it is not even possible. It might not seem like useful resources could be found there. However, oil and gas sit below the surface. There are valuable minerals like zinc and iron deep underground. Not many people live in the Arctic, so the world can’t easily use up these resources. Regardless, the land could provide them, if needed.

title: What Does “Landlocked” Mean to an Economy?
text:
Have you ever been stuck in a drive-through line at a restaurant? At some point, you are literally stuck; your car can’t go forward, you can’t go backward, and you can’t turn to the side. Just like cars in a line, some states are "stuck." Geographers refer to these states as "landlocked."

Look at the map of the U.S. and find your state. Does it touch a body of water, like a lake or the ocean? Now look at the other states of the U.S. and find a state that is landlocked. A state is considered landlocked when it is surrounded by land on all sides. A state without easy access to the ocean has to plan for shipping its products out and productive resources in. Coastal states can simply put their goods on huge ships and send them off to foreign markets. Landlocked states have to transport their goods across other states to get them to their destinations. They use trains or trucks to deliver them to ports where they are then sent to markets in other countries.

What if a country is landlocked? That can create challenges. Its goods must be transported across other countries before they get to the ocean. Its resources have to come in through these other countries, too. That means they have to make special agreements with those countries to let goods pass through their borders. Their economies rely on strong diplomatic relationships with their neighboring states and countries.

title: What Resources Are Near You?
text:
Every region in the Western Hemisphere has a wealth of natural resources. Within the United States, there are a variety of regions that are rich in different natural resources.

The Northwest and Northeast have forests of timber. The South has farms that produce cotton, sugar, and rice. California has fruit and vegetable farms. Florida has orange groves. There are fishing industries on nearly every coastline. There are coal mines in Wyoming and Pennsylvania. There are oil rigs in offshore Texas and Louisiana. The Midwest has wheat, corn, and livestock farms as far as the eye can see.

Take time to think about the countries within the Western Hemisphere. What resources can be found in different countries? There might be resources that aren’t quite as apparent. Take time to research a country within the Western Hemisphere. Look online to see what natural resources are present and used. Complete the chart with your findings. You can create another chart on a separate piece of paper if you need more room.

Now, create a fact sheet for someone visiting your country. Describe what resources they can find and what they are used for. Draw pictures to accompany the resources. In addition to the resources your country has, think about the resources your country might need. Offer suggestions for what your country can trade its resources for in order to benefit your country.

title: Assembly Race
text:
What is a faster way to work: on an assembly line, or in the cottage industry model? You’ll put that question to the test with a production race. On your marks, get set, create!

You will be working in a team of five to make paper masks. Your teacher will tell you whether your team will work as an assembly line or a group of five people working individually. Race the other teams to see who can make the most paper masks in 10 minutes.

You will need:

Steps for Making a Paper Mask:

Cut out eye and mouth holes.

Create designs for the mask on different-colored paper.

Cut out the designs and decorate the mask.

Take one craft stick and tape it to the bottom of the mask.
