title: Essential Question
text: How do productive resources promote specialization?

title: We Depend on Each Other
text:
There are three kinds of resources: natural, human, and capital. People use those resources to get things to consumers. Everyone who spends money is a consumer. The people who make the items that people buy are producers.

Every day, we eat things that come not only from other states but also from other countries and continents. Let's take a look at the banana someone ate for breakfast. Bananas are one of the most popular fruits in the world. This yummy fruit comes from a number of countries, like Ecuador, China, Brazil, and India. If bananas are the number-one fruit around the world, that means lots of other countries are buying them, too.

People all over the world need corn and wheat to make bread, cereal, and lots of other things we eat. So how does what we grow here in the United States end up on a kid's table in London, England? And don't forget about all the other great food we grow in the United States, like oranges, peaches, and cranberries. These foods can end up anywhere in the world. How do all these foods get to all the people who eat them?

It takes lots of people working together to get goods around the world to the people who want and need them. Lots of people benefit from depending on each other. Benefits are the good things that happen because of something you do.

In the countries that bananas came from, there are people who grow the bananas, pick the fruit, and work on the ships that bring bananas to the United States. These people all benefit from the work they have in growing, harvesting, and transporting the bananas. The truck drivers who deliver the bananas to a grocery store, the store owners, and even the store clerks all benefit because they earn their income doing their jobs. All of these people around the world benefit because you bought one little banana.

title: Week 12 Framing Question
text: How are the concepts of geography, economics, governments, and cultures connected?

title: Essential Question
text: How does interdependence increase specialization and trade in the Western Hemisphere?

title: Trade Balance
text:
The business of trade is the buying and selling of goods, such as grain, electronics, or automobiles. It is often the primary way in which nations are interdependent, especially when it comes to nonrenewable resources, such as oil.

According to official energy statistics from the U.S. government, the United States is one of the largest importers of oil in the world. That means we buy oil and bring it to the United States from other countries. The largest exporter of oil each year is Saudi Arabia. Exporters sell products to other countries.

The United States imports and uses more oil than most countries, and we use much more than we can make ourselves. This makes us extremely dependent on other countries for oil. When a country imports more of a product than it exports, we say there is a trade deficit. This is also called a trade gap. When a country exports more of a product, resource, or service than it imports, we say there is a trade surplus. When it comes to oil, the United States has a trade deficit. Can you think of an area where we might have a trade surplus?

title: Trade: Linking American Business to the World
text:
Moving Goods Around the World

Bananas don't grow very well in the United States. The climate just isn't quite right. However, look around the grocery store. There is always a good supply of fresh yellow bananas. How can that be? This is possible because those bananas are shipped across the ocean to the United States from countries in Central or South America. As a matter of fact, there are many goods in the grocery store that were grown or manufactured in faraway places.

These goods make it to the United States because we choose to trade with other countries. This means we buy and sell goods and services to people in other countries. The reason people trade is very simple. Someone else has something they want or need. Or, they have something someone else wants or needs.

International Trade

Trade that takes place between two different countries is known as international trade. No country can produce every type of product. That's why countries choose to work with one another. Countries can choose to import and export goods. Importing is buying goods made in another country. Exporting is selling goods to other countries. The United States buys and sells goods with many other countries.

Our country trades many goods with our closest neighbors, Canada and Mexico. In fact, the governments of these three countries have signed an agreement with one another. The agreement makes it easier for businesses to import and export goods. The agreement helps people make money and get the goods they want or need.

Domestic Trade

Not all trade in the United States takes place with other countries. Some trade is between states within our own country. This type of trade is known as domestic trade. Many states grow or manufacture goods that are not available in other places. These goods are shipped out daily in trucks, on railroads, on planes, or on ships. For example, pineapples grown in Hawaii are shipped to all of the other states. Potatoes grown in Idaho can be found in grocery stores in every other state. People in Hawaii and Idaho probably purchase automobiles manufactured in Michigan.

A Global Economy

Today, the world is more connected than ever. We are all linked by trade as well as technology. People are able to come together to get the goods and services they need.

The economies of most of the world's countries are linked as well. They depend on each other. For example, the United States buys many computers and computer equipment from Japan. What if a Japanese computer factory burned down? There could be a shortage of computers in America. The cost of computers would increase because of the scarcity, or shortage. Some American companies might have to reduce the number of people who work for them because they are spending more money on computers and can't afford salaries.

This could even affect other countries. The people who lost their jobs would not have as much money to purchase items at the store. They might not have enough money to buy clothes manufactured in Mexico. The businesses in Mexico would not make as much money because their products were not being sold.

The next time you go to the grocery store, take a look at the bananas. As a matter of fact, take a look at the labels and stickers on many products. You'll probably be amazed by how many different countries are sending goods to your neighborhood.

title: Interdependence
text:
“We are all in this together!”

This saying refers to something called “interdependence.” Interdependence is when two or more things depend, or rely, on each other.

When two or more countries are dependent on one another, it is called global interdependence. One country might have a good or service that another country needs, and vice versa. For example, Canada gets most of its rice from the United States. The United States gets wheat from Canada. The two countries also trade vehicles, machinery, and other goods and services. The two countries are interdependent.

Global interdependence can be very positive. A country that needs something it does not make or have enough of can get it from somewhere else. High demand for a good or service can create jobs. By exchanging goods and services with other countries, people are exposed to other cultures and ideas. Global interdependence can help bring the world together.

However, it can also have negative effects. If one country decides it will no longer trade with another, it can affect the jobs, economies, and the relationship between the two countries. If one country stops trading with another country, it may have an effect on even more countries. Sometimes, one country gets goods or services from a country that did not manufacture them but had to trade for them. Everyone is dependent on each other, for better or for worse.

Interdependence does not just exist globally. It exists in your environment and community, too. In nature, a bee depends on a plant’s nectar for food. Plants depend on bees to pollinate them. People depend on farmers to raise crops for them to eat. Farmers depend on people to buy those crops so that they can earn a living.

There are examples of interdependence in your school, too. Students depend on their teachers to help them learn. Teachers depend on having students to teach. What other examples of interdependence can you think of?

title: Coffee
text:
Did you know that coffee is one of the most consumed drinks in America? After water, many Americans prefer coffee over drinks like tea and soda. A recent study has found that Americans consume around 146 billion cups of coffee every year.

Brazil is the largest producer of coffee in the world. It became the top producer of coffee in the 1840s, and now, Brazil has over 300,000 coffee farms. Columbia is another well-known producer of coffee. In recent years, 14.3 million pounds of coffee were produced in Columbia. Two states in the United States can grow coffee. Those are California and Hawaii. The U.S. territory of Puerto Rico has been producing coffee for the past 300 years.

There are many reasons why coffee is so popular throughout the world. People can enjoy coffee hot or iced. Many people like the way it tastes. It can be flavored or sweetened. Coffee also contains caffeine. It can give people a boost in energy. It can also make people feel alert. This is why people like to make coffee part of their morning routine.

There is also an active social culture around coffee. Friends spend time together at coffee shops. Students meet at coffee shops for study groups. Coworkers even meet to work on projects over cups of coffee.

Coffee hasn’t always been America’s favorite drink, though. In fact, tea was originally the most popular drink in America. That changed when the Revolutionary War happened. The British government imposed high taxes on the tea imported to the colonies. Colonists realized importing coffee was much less expensive. They also realized that they loved coffee. "I have drank Coffee every Afternoon since,” John Adams wrote to his wife Abigail on July 6, 1774. Since the American Revolution, coffee has remained America’s most popular drink.

The United States depends on other countries for its coffee. We get most of our coffee from Colombia and Brazil. Vietnam and Guatemala also export coffee to the United States. Other exporters are Indonesia, Honduras, Nicaragua, Peru, and Mexico. These countries depend on the United States and other countries for jobs. Millions of people work growing, harvesting, and trading coffee beans. In 2017, the United States spent $6.3 billion on importing coffee alone. Americans love their coffee, and the number of American coffee drinkers keeps on rising.

title: Geographic Regions and Specialization
text:
Countries are interdependent on each other for goods and services, but what each country produces depends on its geography.

A country's climate could be polar, temperate, tropical, or somewhere in between. Certain climates and land features are best for producing certain kinds of food. For example, the coffee bean grows in tropical climates. Brazil in South America and the Ivory Coast in Africa are two of the largest coffee producers in the world. These countries have warm climates year-round, but their mountainous regions have cool nights. The coffee bean grows best in warm climates with cool nights.

China is the largest producer of rice in the world. Southern China has a subtropical climate with mild winters and humid, muggy summers. This means they have a long growing season. Rice grows best in the wet farmlands of China. Rice is also grown in the southeastern United States, which has a similar climate to southern China.

The Great Plains region of the United States is best for producing wheat and corn because of its dry climate with hot summers and cold winters. This area is mostly grassland, which makes it a great place to raise livestock. In fact, the United States is the largest producer of beef in the world.

A country’s geography dictates its climate. The climate dictates what that country can produce. Countries closer to the Equator tend to have longer growing seasons. That means they can produce more kinds of fruits and vegetables in greater amounts. Countries with cooler weather and shorter growing seasons are better suited to raising livestock. They are also better suited to growing hardy vegetables and grains.

Countries are able to trade with each other to get the fruits, vegetables, grains, meat, and dairy products that they might need. Every country is dependent on the weather for what it can grow. Many countries are interdependent on one another to get the foods they need.

title: Granville T. Woods
text:
Innovation is the process of taking something that exists and improving it to make something new. Invention is the creation of something totally new or creating something to perfect something that exists. Invention and innovation almost always overlap. Many Ohioans are considered innovators because of the technology they invented or perfected. The inventions of Ohio innovators have benefited people across the United States and the world.

Granville T. Woods was born in Columbus, Ohio, in 1856. At the age of 10, he left school and began learning everything he could about machinery and blacksmithing through apprenticeships and night school. As an African-American at that time, the education Woods was able to get was not common. He used his knowledge of machines and his ability to read to work on the railroads. Woods continued his education to understand engineering and new applications of electricity.

With his understanding of engineering and electricity, Woods began innovating and inventing new railroad applications. In 1880, after time spent in New York, he returned to Ohio and began a new business. He earned his first patent in 1884, and in 1887, he invented the induction telegraph, also known as the multiplex telegraph. This invention allowed moving trains to receive telegraph messages, something that was previously not possible.

Woods was eventually awarded over 50 patents for inventions and innovations in the fields of engineering and electricity. Due to his race, he was often forced to defend his patents from people who tried to steal credit for them and claim them as their own. He even won two patent disputes against the famous inventor Thomas Edison. Woods sold patents to major companies of the time like General Electric and Westinghouse.

title: Ella P. Stewart
text:
A pharmacist is a person qualified to provide medications prescribed by a doctor of medicine. It takes years of study at a college or university to be a pharmacist. A pharmacist requires advanced math skills and knowledge of chemistry and biology. In the early 1900s, Ella P. Stewart was determined to become a pharmacist. This wasn’t an easy path. For one thing, she was a woman, and universities discriminated against women. Second, she was an African American. African Americans were discriminated against socially. There were segregation laws in place to keep African Americans from publicly being with European Americans. This did not deter or prevent Stewart from pursuing her dream.

Stewart applied and persisted until she got accepted at the University of Pittsburgh. Stewart graduated from the School of Pharmacy with high scholastic marks. Stewart became the first woman to be a pharmacist when she passed the Pennsylvania state examination. She was part of a very small group of women pharmacists in the country and the only African American.

In 1922, Stewart and her husband, William Stewart, moved to Toledo, Ohio. They opened a successful pharmacy. Stewart became active in the community to stop discrimination. She was active in promoting civil rights for all people. She opened her home to many African American civil rights leaders. Stewart was active in national and international organizations that promoted civil rights and an end to discrimination. Later in life, Stewart was the Goodwill Ambassador for the U.S. Department of State. She visited more than 20 nations in Asia.

Stewart lived to be over 90 years old. Each year was filled with actions that are evidence of Ella P. Stewart as an innovator for social change.

title: Essential Question
text: How have inventors from Ohio contributed to the United States?

title: John William Lambert
text:
John William Lambert was born in Ansonia, Ohio, in 1860. He grew up with a father who made wooden parts for wagons and carriages. He quickly took to the family business and displayed an affinity for machinery and innovation. As a young man, he invented several farm implements, including a device for planting corn, as well as one for raking and loading hay. This early work with machinery led to the most notable invention of his life. An early encounter with a gasoline-powered engine inspired him.

He started working on creating an automobile powered by a gasoline engine. During this time, others were working on designing buggies and automobiles that were powered by something other than horses. Lambert’s design was the first to use gasoline as a fuel for its engine. Over the course of his life, Lambert invented several different automobile designs, making him a pioneer in the country’s early automobile industry. He eventually focused the efforts of his company on making automobile parts.

Lambert was a prolific, or very productive, inventor. While his gasoline-powered automobiles are most notable, he was awarded over 600 patents during his lifetime. These included innovations like car door locks and new transmission designs.

title: Orville and Wilbur Wright
text:
Brothers Orville and Wilbur Wright grew up in Dayton, Ohio, in the late 19th century. At this time, people were putting great effort into new transportation technologies. Automobiles were being developed and improved. People were also beginning to consider the possibility of powered flight. The Wright Brothers pursued academic and practical knowledge in their education.

They put their knowledge and initiative to work by opening a bicycle company in 1893. The successful company funded the real pursuit of the Wright Brothers: powered flight. They designed several different prototypes for different airplane components and tested glider designs in order to perfect all the various parts of their eventual powered airplane. The brothers completed their tests at the Outer Banks of North Carolina.

On Dec. 17, 1903, Orville Wright took off in their airplane and flew 120 feet. Recognized as the first powered flight, it was just the beginning of new innovations for the Wright Brothers. Over the next few years, their airplane designs were able to fly over 20 miles. The Wright Brothers continued to innovate and improve powered flight while marketing and selling their airplanes.

title: William Semple and Amos Tyler
text:
William Semple and Amos Tyler are both considered the inventors of chewing gum, as they both filed for patents for gum in the United States. Despite this, they did not work together on the invention, and neither of them appear to have made a business of selling chewing gum. Amos Tyler was from Toledo, Ohio, and William Semple was from Mount Vernon, Ohio.

Chewing gum was not a new invention at the time Semple and Tyler applied for their patents. People have been making chewy concoctions for thousands of years. The two men were simply the first ones to apply for a patent for chewing gum. The two men appear to have created their chewing gum independently of each other.

Their recipes included different ingredients, and Amos Tyler submitted his patent application about five months before William Semple. Their gum was very different from the gum we have today. William Semple was a doctor, and his goal was to help clean teeth and strengthen jaws with his gum. While Tyler applied first, they are generally considered to be co-inventors of chewing gum.

title: Charles Kettering
text:
Charles Kettering grew up on a farm near Loudonville, Ohio. Helping his father on the farm, he developed an interest in working with the farm machinery they used. After high school, Kettering went to college sporadically before finally graduating from Ohio State University at age 28 with a degree in electrical engineering. His first job involved designing improvements for cash registers for the National Cash Register Company. His innovations during this time made cash registers faster and more efficient.

This time of invention led to his experimentation with automobiles. At this time, people started cars using a hand crank. Kettering designed a way to start a car without the hand crank. He used this invention to start a new company, known as Dayton Engineering Laboratories Company, or DELCO, in 1909. He eventually developed the electric starter, and the first car to feature it was the 1912 Cadillac.

Kettering expanded his work at DELCO, eventually selling the company to General Motors and even working with aeronautical innovator Orville Wright. He spent time leading General Motors’ research division coming up with new innovations. His work in this capacity led to major improvements in all aspects of automobile production and operation. In his later years, he turned his research attention toward medical innovation and founded the Kettering Foundation for Medical Research, as well as the Sloan-Kettering Institute for Cancer Treatment.

title: Mária Telkes
text:
Solar energy is commonplace in the twenty-first century. This is because of people like Mária Telkes. In 1924, Telkes immigrated to the United States from Hungary. Telkes got a job with the Cleveland Clinic Foundation. She was the first woman to be employed at the Foundation as a scientist. Telkes believed solar energy was a possible long-term solution for fuel. She advocated that solar energy was a clean and healthier alternative to the fuels that were being used. Telkes did the research for the foundation but continued to investigate solar energy.

The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) was doing research to advance solar energy. In 1940, Telkes joined the staff at MIT. By 1948, she had designed and built the first house that was heated with solar energy. The Dover House had windows facing south. Storage units transferred the energy to heat and cool the house. The energy at the Dover House functioned for only two years. Telkes knew this was the first step to harnessing the sun for energy.

Telkes also developed a device to take salt water from the ocean and make drinkable water. This special evaporation process was used in World War II. The same technology is continued to be used today. After hurricanes devastate a community, technology can be used to provide drinking water to survivors. Telkes had many patents for heating and cooling technology as well as heat storage. During her 94 years of life, Telkes contributed to research that is continuing to influence today’s technology.

title: James Ritty
text:
James Ritty was born in Dayton, Ohio, and served in the Union Army during the Civil War. In 1871, following the war, he opened a saloon in Dayton, Ohio. At his saloon, he had no way of ensuring he knew exactly how much money was coming into his business, especially when other people were working. It was easy to lose money to miscounting or to someone being dishonest. A chance encounter with a new technology gave him a new idea to solve this problem. While traveling by steamboat, he discovered that the boat had a device that would count each time the ship’s propeller went around.

The process inspired him to work on a machine that would be able to count and keep track of each transaction in his business. James and his brother built a few different designs before finally settling on the one that would become the first cash register. The machine did such a good job that the Ritty brothers made improvements to the design and began making copies of it to sell to other businesses. James Ritty eventually sold the cash register business that eventually became known as the National Cash Register Company (NCR).

title: James Murray Spangler
text:
James Murray Spangler was born in Pennsylvania in 1848 before his family moved to Ohio. He was a salesman who also liked to work with machinery and invent things. While living with his wife and children in Akron, he developed several new inventions. These included things like an improved grain harvester and a machine for hay raking.

In his later years, he worked as a janitor in a department store called Zollinger Department Store in Canton, Ohio. The sweeping he did as part of his job aggravated his asthma, a lung disease. To solve this problem, he began working on a device to remove the dust by using a broom, which kicked up the dust and made his asthma worse. He came up with the first electric vacuum cleaner. The earliest vacuums were large contraptions that required horses to pull them around and were too big to take into a building.

Spangler began manufacturing his vacuums at his company, the Electric Suction Sweeper Company. Soon, he had enlisted his cousin’s husband, William Hoover, as a customer and investor. Hoover eventually bought the company from Spangler and developed new and improved electric vacuums under the well-known Hoover Company name. Spangler continued his work with vacuums for the Hoover Company.

title: Thomas Edison
text:
One of the most influential innovators from Ohio was Thomas Alva Edison. Edison was a native Ohioan, born in Milan, Ohio, in 1847. Edison started working at the age of 12. He sold candy bars and newspapers on the Grand Trunk Railroad. Edison was not content selling candy and newspapers, however, and wanted to pursue a career as a scientist. He set up a chemistry lab in one of the train cars to further his study of chemistry.

In 1863, Edison began working as a telegraph operator. The telegraph simplified the way people sent messages to one another. Messages were sent using Morse code. Morse code is an alphabet with letters that are represented by long and short signals of sound or light. It is transmitted by pressing the key on the telegraph machine, which creates a radio wave. This technological pattern allowed scientists to use long and short waves to create the Morse code alphabet and transfer information. As a telegraph operator, Edison began to experiment with telegraph technology and became interested in different methods of communication.

Edison devoted the remainder of his life to the study of science and inventing. He patented his first invention, an electric vote counter, when he was 22 years old. In 1877, Edison created the phonograph. The phonograph was the first machine to record and play back sound. The first voice recording Edison made was the phrase “Mary had a little lamb.”

In 1878, Edison turned his attention to electric lights. The first incandescent light bulb had already been invented by a British scientist in 1840, but it was too expensive for regular use. Incandescent light bulbs work by heating a wire until it produces light. Edison created many, many light bulbs that didn’t work. Many of the materials that could produce light burned too quickly. But Edison didn’t give up. After a lot of hard work, Edison and his assistants invented the first long-lasting electric light bulb.

Another important invention that Edison developed was the motion picture camera, called the Kinetograph. The Kinetograph was first shown to the public in 1891. Thomas Edison developed some of the most important inventions in modern history. With the help of his laboratory assistants, he patented more than 1,000 inventions in his lifetime. Without the inventions created at Edison’s laboratories, the world would not be the same.

title: Essential Question
text: How have Ohioans impacted the history, culture, government, and economy of the United States?

title: Judith Resnick
text:
Judith Resnick was an inspiration to many Americans during the 1980s. Resnick was born and raised in Akron, Ohio. Resnick was interested and very talented in math and science beginning at a very early age. She earned multiple college degrees in electrical engineering. Resnick worked as an engineer in different laboratories before being chosen as one of the first women to serve in National Aeronautics and Space Administration's space program.

In 1978, Resnick began her training to become an astronaut. She became the second American woman to travel into space. In 1984, Resnick was part of the crew that served on the space shuttle Discovery. She was an important part of this mission. Resnick conducted experiments with a solar sail to collect solar energy. This solar sail was used on many future missions to collect and provide energy to space shuttles. Resnick was instrumental in different experiments that helped future astronauts learn about and work in space.

title: Harry M. Stevens
text:
Harry M. Stevens is responsible for inventing one of the most iconic foods in American history: the hot dog. Stevens also revolutionized the snack industry through his love of sports. In his 20s, Stevens immigrated from England to Niles, Ohio. While living in Ohio, Stevens fell in love with baseball and wanted to make his mark on the game. He designed a card for fans to keep score while watching the game. Stevens’s scorecard is still used by baseball fans today.

Stevens also began to sell concessions and snacks at baseball games and other sporting events in the late 1800s. He specialized in selling peanuts, soda, and ice cream. Stevens realized that many people did not want to buy ice cream in the spring or fall because it was too cold. He came up with a brilliant idea to sell sausages in bread buns. The sausages resembled dachshund dogs, so the people began to call Stevens’s new snack “hot dogs.” Today, millions of hot dogs are consumed each year at sporting events and in homes across the United States.

title: Charity Adams Earley
text:
Charity Adams Earley played an important role in the fields of education and psychology, but one of her most important roles was as a trailblazer in the United States military. Because of her efforts, African Americans and women were given more opportunities in the military. After excelling at school during her youth, Earley attended Wilberforce University in Wilberforce, Ohio. She was very determined and took courses in mathematics, education, physics, and Latin.

Earley used her degree to teach mathematics from 1938 to 1942. She also pursued a higher college degree at the Ohio State University. When the United States entered World War II, Earley applied to serve in the newly created Women’s Army Corps (WAC). Earley trained other members of the WAC for service in the military and served overseas in Europe delivering important letters and documents.

Following the war, Earley returned to Ohio and became an active member in many organizations in Dayton. She worked with the American Red Cross, the Dayton Power and Light Company, and Sinclair Community College. Earley also founded the Black Leadership Development Program of Dayton to educate and train young African Americans to become leaders in their community.

title: John Glenn
text:
John Glenn was born in 1921 in Cambridge, Ohio. Glenn pursued an education and career in engineering but decided to join the United States Marine Corps and train as a pilot during World War II. He continued to serve in the Marine Corps following World War II, flying hundreds of combat missions and training other naval officers to become pilots.

In 1959, Glenn was selected by NASA to train as an astronaut. Glenn trained to become a spacecraft pilot and helped design some of the features of early spacecraft. In 1962, NASA chose Glenn to pilot the Friendship 7 spacecraft. Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit around the Earth. His mission was successful and proved that American spacecrafts could survive in space. Glenn served as an astronaut until 1964.

Following his career as an astronaut, Glenn returned to Ohio and became interested in politics. In 1974, Glenn was elected as a representative to the U.S. Senate for Ohio. He represented Ohio in the Senate for the next 25 years. He remained a lover of science and became a strong supporter of environmental, scientific, and healthcare bills during his time as a senator. In 1988, Glenn returned to space at the age of 77 to help NASA research the effects of space travel on older astronauts.

Glenn served as a senator until 1999. That same year, NASA named one of its research facilities at Lewis Field in Cleveland after Glenn. Today, scientists at the John H. Glenn Research Center at Lewis Field design and build technology to advance space exploration. Glenn remained a devoted scientist and worked with many organizations in Ohio until his death in 2016.

title: Garrett Morgan
text:
Garrett Morgan was an innovator from Ohio. Morgan was born in Kentucky but moved to Cleveland to pursue better economic opportunities. After moving to Cleveland in 1895, he worked in a sewing machine repair shop. Morgan began to experiment with different ideas to make sewing machines work more efficiently. Morgan's first invention was a better needle for sewing machines. He also invented a hair straightener and a breathing device to protect people, like firefighters, who had to work around a lot of smoke or gases.

While driving his car one day, Morgan saw an accident between a car and a horse-drawn carriage. He realized the stop-and-go signal was causing many accidents on city streets. Because the signal changed immediately from "stop" to "go," vehicles often did not have time to stop before other vehicles entered the intersection. In 1923, Morgan designed the first traffic signal with three signals: stop, go, and "all stop on all sides." This helped control traffic better, and it gave walkers time to cross the street. Over time, others improved upon his invention, and it became the red, yellow, and green traffic lights we have today. Morgan’s revolutionary system to control traffic improved lives and helped prevent millions of accidents around the world.

title: Elizabeth Blackwell
text:
Elizabeth Blackwell was a trailblazer in the fields of education, abolition, and medicine during the 1800s. Blackwell was born in England, but her family immigrated to Ohio when she was in her early teens. The Blackwell family were prominent members of the abolitionist movement in Ohio. Blackwell’s father believed that every person had the right to an education and economic opportunity, including his daughters.

When Blackwell was 17, her father died. She became a teacher to support her family. By her mid-20s, Blackwell wanted to pursue a career that would help more people. She applied to medical school. At that time, women were not allowed to attend most colleges, and no woman had ever been admitted to medical school in the United States. Blackwell became the first woman to gain admission to Geneva Medical College, and after years of hard work, she became the first woman to graduate from medical school in the United States.

Blackwell used her medical training to care for women and children. She founded the New York Infirmary for Indigent Women and Children in 1857 to provide poor women and children with medical care. During the American Civil War, Blackwell treated wounded soldiers and trained nurses to aid in the war effort.

Following the American Civil War, Blackwell became a champion for women’s education in the medical field. In 1867, she founded the Women’s Medical College in New York. It was one of the only colleges in the United States to offer medical training for women. For the rest of her life, Blackwell remained a supporter of women in the medical field and was an inspiration for many women around the world who wanted to become doctors.

title: Neil Armstrong
text:
Another famed astronaut who was a native Ohioan was Neil Armstrong. Armstrong was born in Wapakoneta, Ohio, in 1930. As a child, Armstrong dreamt of becoming a pilot. Later in life, Armstrong stated, “As a boy, because I was born and raised in Ohio, about 60 miles north of Dayton, the legends of the Wrights have been in my memories as long as I can remember.”

He went to college at Purdue University and earned a degree in aeronautical engineering. Then, he served as a navy pilot from 1949 to 1952. In 1952, Armstrong began working for the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) at Lewis Field in Cleveland. He worked as an engineer and pilot for NACA. Later, he became the test pilot for the X-15 rocket plane.

Armstrong became an astronaut in 1962. Seven years later, Armstrong did something that no one had ever thought possible: he walked on the moon. It was the first time a human had ever stepped foot on the moon. As he stepped onto the moon's surface, Armstrong said, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." Armstrong retired from the astronaut program in 1970 but continued working for NASA. Later, he taught at the University of Cincinnati.

NASA honored Armstrong’s achievements by naming a research facility in his honor. The Armstrong Flight Research Center is one of NASA’s primary facilities for atmospheric research. He received many awards, including the Medal of Freedom, for his contribution to the exploration and study of space. Despite working on many national and international projects and committees, Armstrong remained an Ohioan at heart. He lived in Ohio until his death in 2012.

title: William McKinley
text:
Ohio is often called the "Mother of Presidents" because seven presidents in the nation’s history were native Ohioans, and one claimed Ohio as his home. One of these men was William McKinley, the 25th president of the United States. McKinley was born in 1843 in Niles, Ohio. He served in the Union Army during the American Civil War. Following the war, McKinley returned to Ohio, earned a law degree, and opened his own legal practice in Canton.

McKinley was not content with just practicing law. At the age of 34, he was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives. He represented the people of Ohio in Congress for 14 years. In 1891, he returned to Ohio and served two terms as the state governor. McKinley’s experience and political knowledge made him an ideal candidate for the presidency in 1896.

McKinley’s campaign for the presidency was successful, and he was elected president in 1896. During his first term in office, McKinley was a strong supporter of improving railroads and increasing safety measures. He led the country during the Spanish-American War and encouraged trade with China and countries in Europe. McKinley also began negotiations for the area that would become known as the Panama Canal. McKinley was elected to a second term in office in 1900, but he died less than a year into that term. Today, a statue of McKinley looks over the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus and serves as a reminder of the dedication of Ohioans who have served in the national government.

title: Geography Impacts People
text:
The physical features of Pennsylvania have determined transportation systems, settlement patterns, and use of resources. It is people who have made changes to the physical environment. People adapt to and make accommodations to make their lives in a community easier. The people who come together and live in a community bring many things with them. People bring material things with them, such as furniture, books, and clothes.

People also bring family recipes, cultural songs, traditions, and celebrations. A physical location does not determine the traditions of celebration. When many diverse groups of people live in a community, their ideas and traditions are shared. Many languages can blend together to create common forms of communication for all. These types of common human characteristics make a region.

Regions are areas that are defined by certain characteristics, such as physical features, population, geography, economics, government, climate, or other features. Regions are also determined by things communities have in common. Building materials, jobs, architecture, and art can define a region. Common interests can also determine a region.

These interests can be a professional sports team the majority of people in the area support or types and flavors of foods that are popular in the community. The way a community votes and their political beliefs are another way to determine a region. Regions can be large or small. A group of fourth grade classrooms can determine a region in a school building. A group of schools all in one location can determine a region.

Two of the most diverse regions in the state are located around the cities of Philadelphia and Pittsburgh. About 1.6 million people live in the Philadelphia region. Pittsburgh has 302,971 residents. These regions share similar human characteristics. Both have deep roots in the history of the country. Both have professional sports teams. Each has a large river for trade and economics. Both have nicknames: the City of Brotherly Love and the Steel City. The regions of Philadelphia and Pittsburgh are also very different. The geography of Pennsylvania has influenced the differences in the architecture, food, language, and politics of these two cities.

No matter how a region is defined, Pennsylvania has many regions that are similar and different to each other. Each region is unique because of the state’s diverse population and culture.

title: Food Regions in Pennsylvania
text:
Regions can be determined by food, flavors, recipes, and ingredients. Many recipes are created by what ingredients are locally available. Food dishes can also be created by different circumstances, such as supply, demand, and scarcity.

All-in-One Sandwich

The strip district in Pittsburgh is an area with heavy truck traffic. Truckers load and unload goods on shipping docks for several hours each day. Workers have little time in their schedules to eat. Sandwiches, however, could be eaten while still working. Truckers and workers began putting French fries, cole slaw, cheese, and tomato slices on the grilled meat between two slices of bread. This sandwich became popular in Pittsburgh restaurants and can still be found on restaurant menus all over the city.

Cheesesteak

Philadelphia is famous for the cheesesteak sandwich. Thin slices of beef are grilled with onions or peppers. The grilled beef, onions, and peppers are then served on a long, crusty, Italian bread roll with melted cheese or cheese sauce. There are many steak and cheese sandwiches around the country, but they are copies of the original Philly cheesesteak. When ordering a sandwich at a Philly cheesesteak shop, customers use the terms “wit” or “witout” to specify if they want cheese or not on their sandwich.

Pennsylvania Dutch

There are many famous dishes and recipes that came from Pennsylvania Dutch communities in southeast Pennsylvania. Shoofly pie, panhaas (scrapple), and gobs are all Pennsylvania Dutch recipes. Shoofly pie is a molasses-, nutmeg-, and cinnamon-flavored pie. Made in farm kitchens, shoofly pie was once served as part of breakfast or a snack for farm workers.

The Pennsylvania Dutch also serve panhaas, or scrapple. Panhaas is a mush made with cornmeal and pork scraps. Panhaas and scrapple are sometimes served with hamloaf. A hamloaf is made from ground ham, which is baked like a meatloaf. Brown sugar is sprinkled on top to finish the dish.

For dessert, grab a gob! A gob is also known in other regions as a “whoopie pie.” Gobs are a sweet treat made with chocolate cookies and frosting. Gobs are assembled like a sandwich, with a layer of frosting between the two chocolate cookies.

Snack Food

Pretzels are a popular snack that have a deep connection to Pennsylvania. Early settlers brought the recipe with them from Europe. The hard pretzel was invented in Pennsylvania in the 1600s. Pennsylvania is home to the first commercial pretzel factory in the United States. York County is the home to many pretzel and potato chip producers. Data from York County Department of Commerce says that 80 percent of all pretzels in the United States are produced in Pennsylvania.

Pierogies

Eastern European immigrants who settled in western Pennsylvania introduced pierogies to the state. A pierogi is a Polish dumpling made of egg and flour dough. They are usually filled with potatoes, sauerkraut, cheese, or meat. Pierogies can be boiled or fried with onions and peppers.

Sweets

Pennsylvanians love sweet foods. The state is home to the famous Hershey Factory. Marshmallow chicks and rabbits, usually found in stores in the Spring, were first created in Bethlehem. Pennsylvanians also love water ice. Water ice is made from water, sugar, and flavoring. It is different from a snow cone or a slushy but still makes the perfect treat for a hot summer day.

There are many other foods that are unique to regions of Pennsylvania. It is the people living in the area that make food special and popular. What foods do students in your school think are special to your area?
