title: This for That: How Trade Works
text:
Have you ever swapped part of your lunch with a friend? Maybe you agreed to do a chore for a family member if they did a different chore that you don’t like to do. Those are examples of trades. A trade is an exchange of one thing for another.

The United States trades with other countries for goods and resources. It sends exports, or goods that leave a country, and in return, it receives imports, or goods that enter a country. How do countries decide what to export and import? That depends on what a country has and what it needs.

Trading for Resources

Different areas of the world have different resources. Some find it easy to grow particular crops, while others have mines full of precious minerals. An island nation might be able to catch more fish than its people need. A country with a large population could produce many electronics to sell to other countries around the world.

People around the world use oil as fuel, but oil is only found in a few places. It is mostly underground in very dry places, like some countries in the Middle East, such as Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, and others. Those countries export oil to countries that need it. Because it is hard to grow food in very dry places, the oil-producing countries might then import food. This benefits several countries, because nations that need oil get it from the nations who have it, and those that need food get it from other nations that have it.

Bartering

A very simple trade, called bartering, is a direct swap of one thing for another. The examples in the first paragraph are barters. One friend could say to another, “Can I swap my apple for your orange?” If the friend agrees, they have bartered, so they each get the fruit they’d rather eat.

Currency

Large amounts of trade aren’t always so exact. Currency, or money, makes these trades work. In the oil example, a country might pay for oil from another country. The country that sold the oil then has money it can use to trade for other resources.

The United States trades a lot with Canada and Mexico, which isn’t surprising, as they are its neighboring countries. It is easier to transport goods from one country to another by land. China is another one of the United States’ major trading partners, but China is located across the ocean. Enormous shipping vessels known as cargo or freighter ships cross the Pacific Ocean to carry imports and exports between the countries. Look at the labels on some of your clothing and electronics. Many of them have been imported from other countries. Trade is what carried them from far away to your home.

title: Essential Question
text: How does trade change throughout regions?

title: Community, State, and International Trade
text:
Trade takes place all over the world. It occurs on a small level between two people at a store. It also occurs on a huge level, with countries sending millions of dollars of goods across the ocean. Without it, people wouldn’t have access to the countless amazing resources on the planet.

Community Trade

On the local level, people trade within their communities. Most people specialize in a job and supply others with a good or service. In trade, they purchase goods and services from others in their communities. A carpenter offers their services to build something for a customer. With the money they earn, the carpenter can go to the grocery store and buy food. The owner of the grocery store then has money to purchase clothing. You can see how this everyday trade helps people get the things they want and need.

Trade Between States

The United States is vast, and its different regions are rich in resources. Trade between states gives everyone access to these resources. Take the example of corn. Besides tasting great as corn on the cob, this crop feeds farm animals and is an ingredient in many foods. Many states in the Great Plains, such as Iowa and Nebraska, have the right kind of land and climate to grow corn. Farmers in the region grow much more than the people in those states need. So, they sell it to other states that don’t have an abundant supply of corn. Stores in a state like Washington might buy the corn. In return, they send resources that they are rich in, like timber.

International Trade

International trade solves many of the same problems as trade between states does. It’s on a much larger scale, though. There are many resources found around the world that the United States doesn’t have easy access to. For instance, very little of the United States is located in a tropical climate zone. So, crops that grow well in the tropics, such as coffee, are especially useful for the United States to import.

Different regions specialize in certain kinds of goods and resources. Some countries in Asia, like China and South Korea, export electronics. They have skilled workers who know how to design these goods. The countries also have very large populations. There are many people available to help put the electronics together. Some countries in southern Africa are rich in minerals like gold and diamonds. These minerals are found in mines deep in the Earth in those regions. Many people work to bring these minerals to the surface.

Trade between countries also helps produce finished goods. Take the example of a car. The steel that makes its body could come from one country. The rubber from its tires might come from another. People trained in how to design a car’s computer parts could work in offices in a big city. The people putting the car together at the end might work in a factory close to an airport or harbor. That way, the cars can easily be shipped to different places. Trading resources and skills helps bring together one product that can be sold around the world.

Imports and Exports

The United States has many trade partners around the world. Trade between countries isn’t always even. Sometimes, a country imports a lot more from another country than it exports. This is especially true for countries without a lot of natural resources or with small populations. They often have to import many of the things they need. Ideally, a country would export more than it imports. That would help the country build wealth.

International trade isn’t as easy as it is between states or people in a community. Countries have rules for how much they will export to and import from others. The cost of transporting goods is, of course, very large, and a problem between two countries can hurt the trade between them. The people living in the countries would have to make other arrangements for meeting their needs in those cases.

title: Regulating Trade
text:
Trade is the economic practice of the exchange of goods and services between countries. Being able to export and import can mean countries have access to many products. Some countries start to specialize in certain goods or services. As long as everyone is able to trade and the supply keeps up with the demand, everything works great. However, if a certain country is unable to trade, the others may suffer.

The U.S. government tries to regulate the amount of goods being imported and exported. This helps keep exchanges fair and balanced. The government uses tariffs, which are taxes on imports. If government leaders want to encourage trade, they lower the tariffs on imports. If they want to discourage trade, they raise the tariffs. They also set up quotas, which are limits on the amount of goods being imported. Why do you think there are limits?

title: Trade Agreements
text:
Countries can make trading goods easier by forming trade agreements. The United States has made many trade agreements. During colonial times, ships from the colonies carried lumber, tobacco, rice, and dried fish to England. England sent textiles and manufactured goods back to America. At one time, colonists were not allowed to trade with any country other than England. Later, other countries became trade partners.

Countries throughout the world create trade agreements with each other. Trade agreements are very complex. They affect how economies interact. They often remove trade barriers. With fewer trade barriers, both countries’ economies flourish. One barrier that is often removed in agreements is tariffs. A tariff is a tax on imported goods. Without tariffs, goods are cheaper. For example, trade agreements allow food from other countries to come to the United States without tariffs. Grocery prices are lower as a result. The same is true with gasoline prices. Without tariffs, gasoline is more affordable. Trade agreements mean lower prices, which means that more people will buy things like gas and groceries. That increases the demand for products from other countries.

In order for trade agreements to work, they must be fair to all countries. Each country agrees to support one another. There are a variety of trade agreements throughout the Western Hemisphere.

NAFTA, or the North American Free Trade Agreement, is a trade agreement between Canada, the United States, and Mexico. The goal of NAFTA was to promote a way to benefit Canada, the United States, and Mexico with free trade and lower tariffs. This increased trade and helped many small and midsize businesses grow. It lowered the cost of taxes and allowed businesses to go to other countries to sell their products.

MERCOSUR, or the Southern Common Market, is the main trade organization specializing in South America. Its current members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Venezuela, and Bolivia. The main goal of this organization is to create opportunities for the member countries by increasing business production and investment opportunities.

CARICOM, or the Caribbean Community and Common Market, is the trade organization within the Caribbean Islands. It is made up of 20 developing Caribbean nations. The economic goal of this organization is to help form a community. This community is intended to help create free trade and competition between the countries. Competition helps increase productivity and communication about new innovations.

title: Film Industry in California
text:
The white letters of the Hollywood sign overlook Los Angeles, California. This sign greets people as they arrive to join the business of movies. Los Angeles has long been the center of the film industry. Why did so many movie studios start to move here a hundred years ago? There was one good reason: the weather.

Los Angeles has warm and sunny weather all year round. L.A.’s beautiful weather meant that film crews could shoot outside almost every day. They wouldn't have to wait for rain or snow to stop. For this reason, Hollywood, a specific section of L.A., became the home for major American film studios.

Many famous actors live around Hollywood so they can be close to work. Hollywood employs thousands of other people, too. The list includes camera operators, film editors, writers, costume designers, musicians, stunt people, and many more. Every film uses a wealth of human resources. Many people who specialize in these skills move to Los Angeles. They know it is a big location for the jobs they have training for.

As technology changes, more specialized roles spring up. For example, CGI, or computer-generated imagery, is technology used for many special effects. People with the skills to work in CGI are in big demand by the studios. Schools all over the world teach students the science of CGI. Many of the students will then likely spend time working in Los Angeles. Hollywood will always attract big dreamers with big skills.

title: Say Aloha to Pineapples!
text:
What do you think of when you picture Hawaii? Maybe you think of people surfing in the ocean. You might imagine leis, the flower necklaces that originate from Polynesian tradition. You may also think about the pineapple, a tasty fruit grown in Hawaii.

Spiky on the outside and juicy on the inside, pineapples are delicious treats. Even in the winter in a cold place, you can find one in a grocery store. You can buy frozen chunks of pineapple to put in a smoothie. You can buy a can of pineapple juice to remind you of warmer weather.

Historians believe pineapples were originally grown in areas of South America. Early Europeans brought pineapple home with them, where it was enjoyed almost exclusively by the nobility. Much later, pineapples began to be grown in Hawaii because of the good growing climate of the islands. Now, people all over the world can enjoy pineapple. Before modern transportation, however, that wasn’t the case. Two hundred years ago, it was unlikely that someone living in a cold climate would ever get a chance to try pineapple.

With its warm and rainy weather, Hawaii is the perfect place for pineapples to grow. It takes a lot of time for one pineapple to grow. Pineapples grow on plants low to the ground on large farms, and they can take up to two years for one fruit to grow.

Once workers pick grown pineapples, they package them for trade all over the world. Ships and planes carry them to the rest of the United States and other countries. As the ships and planes leave Hawaii, others arrive. These might be carrying goods that aren’t as easy to find in Hawaii, so people there can buy them. It’s a fair trade for this tasty, tropical fruit.

title: Trade: Imports and Exports
text:
The United States imports more goods from some countries than we export to them. With other countries, the opposite is true.

Look at the chart. It shows how many billions of dollars of goods the United States exports to a few of its most frequent trade partners. It also shows how many billions of dollars of goods the United States imports from them.

Now, look at the map. If the United States imports more from a country than it exports to them, draw an arrow from that country pointing to the United States.

If the United States exports more to a country than it imports from them, draw an arrow from the United States pointing to that country.

title: Parts of Positive Communication
text:
Positive communication and interactions are important. Communication skills are skills you can learn and practice. Positive communication helps you thrive by creating connections and forming relationships with others.

These are some communication skills you can develop:

title: Respecting Yourself and Others
text:
Respect is an important part of making and keeping friends. It is important to learn to show respect for others and their ideas. You can respect others while also having respect for yourself and your own ideas. Showing respect for others is courageous and mature. We can learn to respect others through words and actions.

You can show respect by:

Recognizing cultural differences

Accepting differences

Sharing and taking turns

Respecting people’s boundaries

Collaborating, being kind, and being patient

title: Making Friends Through Participation
text: Participation is an important part of learning. We practice using our communication skills when we participate. Being willing to join in gives you the opportunity to try new things. It's important to remember that participation is also about letting others join in. Including others is part of having good social skills. Participation builds up your confidence. You have value to add. You can add value by sharing your talents, ideas, and opinions.

title: Keeping Friends Through Conflict Resolution
text:
The world is made up of many people. Everyone has different beliefs and ideas. Since everyone has different beliefs, there are times when people experience conflict. Conflict is a disagreement between individuals or groups. When you interact with other people, there will always be differing opinions and ideas. Disagreements can be a good thing to help people solve problems and come up with new ideas. It is important to have a plan to resolve conflict.

You can follow these conflict resolution steps:

State the problem.

Identify the cause of the problem.

Suggest solutions for the problem.

Reach out to experts.

title: Working with Others
text: When you are playing and working with others, you will need to be adaptable. Being adaptable means you can easily adjust to change and work with whatever happens next. Being adaptable also means being willing to cooperate and compromise. Cooperating is working together to achieve a goal. For example, working together to play a game means cooperating. Compromising is when members of a group have different ideas, but they work together to find a solution that everyone can agree on. It helps everyone feel good about completing the project.

title: Always Willing to Learn
text: Being teachable is being willing to learn. Being teachable means that you might not know the answers, but you are willing to learn. Being teachable improves your relationships and well-being. Being teachable creates a safe place for everyone to learn together. When you are teachable, you are practicing your growth mindset. You are giving yourself a chance to make improvements. You are asking questions and looking for feedback to help you.

title: Taking Initiative Takes Courage
text:
Taking initiative is when you act before others ask you to. It is the ability to observe a need and initiate an action independently. You can take initiative by cleaning up your own messes, helping, or putting something away even when you aren’t asked. You show that you are responsible when you take initiative.

Practicing empathy is another way you can take initiative. Being aware of what is going on around you can help you find opportunities to support others.

title: All Kinds of Changes
text: Change happens when something around you becomes different in some way. Changes can be big, like getting a new pet. Changes can be small, like getting new shoes. Change happens to everyone. You get to choose how you respond to change. Dealing with changes in a positive way helps you keep your well-being in balance.

title: Feelings with Change
text:
Your emotions help you respond to change. When your brain reacts to change, it affects your emotions. Having lots of emotions at once can feel overwhelming. These are things you can do when you are overwhelmed:

Give yourself permission to feel emotions.

Communicate how you feel.

Ask questions.

title: Responding to Change
text: Changes can cause a lot of different emotions. You can respond in a negative way. You can respond in a positive way. Responding positively means making healthy choices.

title: Sensory Input
text:
When you taste, hear, smell, do, or see something that you like, your brain wants to experience that feeling again because hormones, like dopamine, are created in the brain that make you feel good. The more you repeat an activity that produces dopamine in the brain, the more your body craves it. Exercise, making healthy choices, feeling proud of your actions, and even hugging a caregiver can all create dopamine.

Dopamine is a good thing for the brain and body. In excessively large doses, however, any good thing can start to cause problems. An addiction is a powerful craving to repeat an experience over and over again, usually because of the dopamine and feel-good result. Addiction is hard to control and can affect your sleep, eating habits, and normal routines. It can even ruin your friendships.

Media, like commercials, ads, and even influencers on social media, all want to influence the way you view certain products or behaviors. Media can influence your thoughts and feelings positively or negatively.

Think critically about the impact that what you are viewing is having on you. Pay attention to the ways you behave because of what you view, hear, and experience.

If an activity or substance is impacting your health and wellness in a negative way or encouraging you to make unhealthy choices, you should talk to a trusted friend or adult.

title: Types of Addiction
text: Addiction can be physical, psychological, or a combination of the two. Physical addiction: A person's body becomes dependent on a substance. A substance can be as simple as sugar or caffeine, or it can be more harmful, like drugs or alcohol. Without that substance, an addicted person feels sick. Psychological addiction: A person's mind becomes dependent on a behavior or action. This can include checking social media, playing video games, or other behaviors that they feel like they “need.” Without that behavior, they feel strong negative emotions, such as anger or sadness.

title: Materials Calculator
text: State governments provide services for citizens in their states. They are responsible for building state roads and bridges. They build and maintain state parks. In Indiana there are 24 state parks. There are many more reservoirs, recreation sites, and even inns run and maintained by the state Department of Natural Resources. The state government also pays for state tourism services. They take care of public safety by providing state police officers. Keeping Hoosiers healthy is important. Citizens have access to the Indiana Department of Health.

title: Keep a Lookout for Symptoms
text:
Looking out for symptoms of addiction can help you maintain and improve your well-being and the well-being of others. Recognizing warning signs can help you avoid the health risks of addiction. Here are some signs that can mean that someone is struggling with addiction to a substance or behavior:

Repeating an activity or using a substance even if it’s harmful

Staying up late or waking up at night to do something

Losing interest in other activities

Wanting to be alone

Being secretive, lying, or hiding things

Big mood swings or personality changes

These signs don’t always mean addiction. However, they might mean someone needs help. If you’re worried about someone or if you are showing these symptoms yourself, talk to a trusted adult about how to feel better.

title: Help Is Available
text:
If you have an addiction or are affected by someone else’s addiction, you are not alone. You might feel like you need to take care of the problem yourself. However, asking for help is one of the smartest, bravest choices you can make. Start by finding an adult you trust. Trusted adults may be caregivers, parents, relatives, school counselors, teachers, coaches, religious leaders, school nurses, or doctors. Trusted adults will always have your health and wellness in mind and can help you make choices that will keep you safe and healthy.

You can ask for help in any way that you feel most comfortable. You can talk to the adult and say something like, “I am worried about a friend (or myself). I see some symptoms, and I am worried they (or I) may have an addiction.” If talking makes you nervous, write a note or ask electronically. Either way, make sure you explain clearly what is happening. A trusted adult may be able to help you or whoever is struggling with addiction to find support programs and addiction recovery programs online or in the community.

title: Improving Every Day
text:
Want to change your behavior? It’s tempting to change everything all at once. But that can be overwhelming, and then you might go back to those familiar habits you wanted to get rid of. Make one little change at a time and develop good habits to replace the bad ones.

These tips can help you improve:

Start with something easy. If you're spending too much time on screens, replace one minute of screen time a day with something else you enjoy. Slowly work up to more minutes per day.

Notice what’s holding you back. If you want to drink less soda but don’t like the taste of water, try flavoring your water with a little fruit juice.

Make a plan for hard days. Plan to talk to a parent or trusted friend when you’re having a hard time sticking to your goals. Keep an exciting book, new art supplies, or sports equipment ready for days when it’s difficult to make decisions.

title: Act Thoughtfully
text:
An impulse is a sudden desire to do something. An impulse is like a little alarm in your head that says, “Do this right now,” because that’s how your brain has learned to respond to something. Impulses can be part of addiction. Impulses can also be just impulses. For example, if you feel stress, your brain may tell you to look at social media. Or you may do an addictive behavior at the same time every day. Part of overcoming addiction and making healthy choices is recognizing your impulses and learning how to control them.

A good rule to follow is to stop, think, and act. When you start to do something automatically, notice it. Stop. Think about why you’re doing it. Think about what you might want to do differently. Then, act thoughtfully. This might look like saying “no” if someone asks you to participate in an unhealthy or unsafe activity.

title: What Is the Conflict?
text: Before a conflict can be resolved, the conflict must be identified. Every person is unique and sees things differently. We all have likes and dislikes. Sometimes things that bother us won't bother someone else. Conflict happens when people see things differently and disagree. The first step to finding a resolution is identifying what you disagree about.

title: What Caused the Conflict?
text:
Looking for the cause of a conflict can help you understand the conflict and find a solution. The cause of a conflict may be obvious, or it may be difficult to identify. You can be like a detective, looking for clues. The cause of the conflict is what is contributing to the disagreement.

You can ask:

What might I be missing?

What else should I consider?

What might the other person think?

Do I know something that the other person doesn’t know?

title: What Are Possible Solutions?
text: Once you have identified the conflict and possible causes, you can start to suggest solutions to help resolve the conflict. It is helpful to consider all options, even if they are silly or obviously wrong. Making suggestions will help you think about what can be a solution.

title: Give the Solution a Try
text: Decide which solution is best, then put it into action. Trying what you have decided will solve the problem is an important step. Be confident in your decision. Keep working, and don't give up. You can use your growth mindset. It’s okay to make mistakes. Sometimes we learn more by failing a few times before we get something right. You can also test your ideas on someone you trust. A test run or practice can help you feel good about your decision or give you a chance to modify your decision.

title: Need Some Extra Help?
text: You can consider asking others for advice when you are solving a problem. Other people may have already solved the same problem. They might be able to give you good suggestions. It can be helpful to reach out to experts when we get stuck resolving a conflict. Other people can help us see things a little bit differently.

title: Don't Forget to Follow Up!
text: After a conflict is over, it is important to follow up with others. You can ask how they are doing. You can be a good friend and use the social skills you have learned. You can also practice social resilience and show empathy for others as you move on after a conflict has been resolved.

title: Thinking Critically
text: Critical thinking is making observations. Ask questions. Write down your observations. You can compare and contrast. Comparing is looking at how things are the same. Contrasting is looking at how they are different. Compare and contrast your ideas.

title: Do You Give In to Peer Pressure?
text: What do you do if you think differently from someone else? Peer pressure is when someone is pushing you to think the way they do. When you think critically, you consider all the information you have. You make the best decision for you.

title: Goods and Services
text:
Goods are items you can use or consume to meet your needs and wants. They are produced using human, natural, and capital resources. Goods can also be things people grow. In the United States, goods fall into two categories. These are private and public goods. Private goods are items you can buy from a business with your own money. Private goods include food, clothing, furniture, and toys. Public goods are paid for by taxes, not individual consumers. Public goods include law enforcement, sewer systems, and public parks.

A service is work that one person does for someone else. Services are actions, such as haircuts, car repairs, medical check-ups, mail delivery, and teaching. Services provided by the government are known as public services. These include hospitals, schools, police and fire stations, trash pickup, and public transportation. An example of a public service is going to your community library. It doesn't cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. Businesses owned by people are considered private enterprises.

How do companies compete to provide goods and services to consumers? Specialization lets companies make more and better products. They make more money if they make more of a product to sell. When a company makes more money, they can hire more workers. Then, more people have money to spend on things they need and want. Many companies may specialize in the same goods and services. This allows consumers to make choices. They can choose goods and services they wish to purchase based on price, availability, and quality.

The United States produces many goods for consumers around the globe. It produces billions of dollars worth of public and private goods, industrial supplies, automobiles, and agricultural products. These goods are used by consumers in our country. They are also exported to countries all over the world.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
A producer is someone who makes a good or provides a service. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are used for other communities. Farmers, factory workers, car mechanics, and doctors are producers. The person who cuts your hair is also a producer.

People who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. People often depend on trade with others to meet their wants and needs. People can be both a producer and a consumer. When we buy groceries, gas, clothing, or toys, we are buying goods. When we go to the doctor, have our car fixed, or get a haircut, we are using services. When you get a haircut, you're a consumer because you're buying a service.

Both consumers and producers affect the prices of goods and services. For example, a company that produces bicycles may raise the price of their product if there's a metal shortage. A shortage is when something you need can’t be found in the amount needed. Consumers may stop buying bikes if the price is too high. Then the company might have to lower prices to get more sales. When a consumer doesn't buy enough of a good or service it may cause producers to lower the cost of it. If consumers are buying too much of a product, a producer might increase the product's price.

title: Opportunity Cost
text: People make choices on how to spend their money. Sometimes we want more than one thing at a time. This means we have to make a choice. We have to decide what to keep and what to give up. Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you make a choice. Imagine you have $20. Your friends want to go see the new movie, but there is also a book you would like to buy. Before you can make a choice, you need to find out how expensive each option is. You might ask a friend or family member for advice. If you are patient, the price may drop in a few weeks. It might be a good idea to wait for that to happen. Whichever you choose, you also have to think about the opportunity cost. It can be a hard choice!

title: Needs and Wants
text:
What are some of your basic needs? Food, shelter, clothing, sleep, love, education, safety, medical care, and others may come to mind. A need is something that you have to have every day to survive. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water to survive. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us safe by keeping us warm or cool. Needs are things you must have in order to survive.

In addition to your basic needs, you might also have other needs. Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If both of your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler to help you be successful each day.

A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. It is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

Sometimes, it's difficult to decide whether you want or need something. Each of us makes these choices throughout the day. We go through the process of determining the positive and negative consequences of purchasing our wants. We evaluate if it is still a need or a want. Then, we choose what would be best for us.

Each day, everyone must make decisions about needs and wants. The most important thing is that we take care of all of our basic needs first. Afterward, we can start taking care of our wants. When you make a decision, you usually can’t have it both ways. For example, you can’t eat only junk food and still be healthy. Likewise, you can’t spend money on new furniture for the house and still have enough left over to buy groceries. By choosing one thing, you decide not to choose the other, at least for the time being.

When people earn an income, they look at how much they must spend on their needs. They often create a budget, or a plan for keeping track of their money. A budget lists all of their expenses, or things that must be paid for for the month. A budget also lists resources, or money a person has available for spending that month.

Additionally, there are items that aren’t part of the regular monthly budget. When making responsible decisions, people should first pay for everything they need. Then, they can use what's left over to buy things they want. To make good choices, we must learn to see the difference between needs and wants. We must plan wisely so all of our needs are taken care of before we start fulfilling our wants.

title: Essential Question
text: How do goods and services help meet the needs and wants of a society?

title: Tourism
text:
Tourism is the business of encouraging people to travel for fun. Tourism is an economic activity. People travel to places that are different from where they live. Cities, states, and even countries have created businesses and resorts where people can shop and stay. These locations are sometimes based on a place's unique physical characteristics. This includes places like oceans, mountains, and national parks. Some tourist attractions are human-made.

Tourism changes a place's physical environment. The more people visit a place, the more accommodations are made. Bringing in visitors requires additional roads, hotels, restaurants, stores, and sites for people to visit. Tourism is an industry that brings a lot of money to cities, states, and countries and strengthens the economy.

There are many popular tourist destinations in the Western Hemisphere. One of the most popular tourist destinations in Canada is Niagara Falls. Located on the border of Ontario, Canada, and New York, Niagara Falls is the tallest waterfall in North America. Over 3,000 tons of water flow over the falls every second. More than 13 million tourists visit Niagara Falls each year.

The most popular tourist destination in the United States is Times Square. Times Square is located in New York City. Times Square is a popular destination for shopping, dining, and attending cultural events. It is also home to one of the most famous and visited New Year's Eve celebrations in the Western Hemisphere.

One of the most visited tourist destinations in Ohio is Cedar Point, an amusement park. Cedar Point is considered the roller coaster capital of the world. Millions of people visit Cedar Point each year to enjoy the rides, games, and entertainment the park has to offer.

Many popular tourist destinations in Central and South America are historic sites. Chichén Itzá, located on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula, was once home to the mighty Maya Empire. Tourists travel to Chichén Itzá to visit the city’s ancient ruins, pyramids, and temples that were built over 1,000 years ago. Machu Picchu is a popular historic site in Peru. Machu Picchu is located in the Andes Mountains. The city was built by the Inca civilization in the 1400s. Visitors travel to Machu Picchu to see the historic homes, temples, and shrines of the Inca.

title: Agriculture
text:
Agriculture is the business of growing crops and raising livestock. Agriculture impacts the goods and services in our state, country, and the world. Growing and harvesting plants and crops are a part of agriculture. Examples of crops that are grown are fruits, vegetables, flowers, grain, and cotton. Agriculture is affected by the environment and by location. The crops and animals raised in agriculture depend on temperature, rainfall, and soil. For example, mild climates that have sunshine and regular rain are ideal for growing wheat and corn. Natural resources are important to agriculture.

Agriculture is one of the main economic activities in the Western Hemisphere. The varied climates, weather, and soil of the Western Hemisphere allow farmers to grow hundreds of different crops. Corn, wheat, soybeans, cotton, and hay make up the largest portion of crops grown in the United States. Canada is a top producer of canola, wheat, potatoes, and soybeans. The top agricultural products grown and harvested in Central America include sugarcane, coffee beans, bananas, citrus fruits, and corn.

Animal husbandry, or raising animals or livestock, is another part of agriculture. Examples of this include ranching, dairy farming, and beekeeping. In the United States, cattle production is the largest of these agricultural activities. Cattle ranchers add over $6 billion to the U.S. economy each year. Dairy cows in the United States produced about 27 billion gallons of milk in 2021. Brazil is the largest producer of beef in South America and the largest exporter of beef in the world. Brazil is home to the second-largest cattle herd in the world, with over 230 million cows.

Forestry and lumber production are important sectors of the agriculture industry. Canada is a large producer of softwood lumber. It is the second-largest exporter of this type of wood in the world. Softwood lumber is used in construction and furniture production.

The United States is the leading producer of many different forest products. It is the second-largest exporter of hardwood in the world. Lumber from U.S. forests is used to make houses, furniture, pencils, paper, musical instruments, and other important items.

Because over 46 percent of Brazil’s total area is covered by the Amazon Rainforest, forestry and lumber production is a large part of its economy. Factories in Brazil produce many different products, including plywood, paper, and furniture.

title: Information Technology
text:
Another important sector of many economies in the Western Hemisphere is information technology. Information technology is the study and development of computer systems to store, retrieve, and send information. Millions of people work for thousands of U.S.-based information technology companies. The largest information technology companies in the United States include Apple Inc.®, Microsoft®, Oracle®, Cisco Systems Inc.®, and Adobe Inc.®

The information technology industry in Canada is made up of over 43,000 companies. Companies like Constellation Software Inc.®, Shopify®, and CGI Inc.® create software and computer products and provide technology services to businesses and companies around the world. Information technology companies in Canada export over $7 billion in software and computer products each year.

Brazil, Mexico, and Peru have the largest information technology sectors in Central and South America. Information technology companies in Brazil are the leading producers of software and security applications in South America. Information technology companies contribute about $23 billion to the economy of Mexico each year.

title: Life Sciences
text:
Life science is a growing sector of many economies in the Western Hemisphere. This field, which is also referred to as the biotech industry, includes finding new ways to make life safer in the fields of medicine and other sciences. Life science companies continue to experiment, learn, and grow while helping people in many ways.

The United States is a world leader in medical research and development. Research and development is the process companies use to gain new knowledge to make or improve goods and services. The purpose of research and development is to expand human understanding in a way that benefits people and the economy. There are 7,500 biotech companies in the United States that research and develop products to make life easier. The United States is one of the leading countries in the research and development of pharmaceuticals, or medicine, in the world.

Canada’s life science sector has been a leader in the biotech industry for many years. The country’s life science industry is made up of two large sectors: pharmaceuticals and medical devices. These sectors employ thousands of Canadians each year and produce some of the leading medical innovations in the world.

The life science industry is a growing field in Central and South America. Companies in Mexico, including Eva Tech® and Unima®, have conducted extensive research to study cancer and other diseases. Biotech companies in Chile are developing new technology to make surgery safer and easier. Argentina has the third-largest biotech industry, focusing on improvements to agriculture in the world.

title: Manufacturing
text:
Manufacturing is the business of using raw materials to make products or goods to sell. There are many types of manufacturing companies. Some examples of manufactured products are cars, computers, toys, and soft drinks. Some manufacturing products are made with natural resources. Others are made with human-made resources.

One type of manufacturing is the automobile industry. To build an automobile, workers must assemble over 15,000 manufactured parts. Many countries in the Western Hemisphere are some of the leading automobile manufacturers in the world. The United States, Mexico, Brazil, and Canada are among the largest producers of automobiles in the world. Automobiles manufactured in the United States, Mexico, Brazil, and Canada are exported to countries all over the world.

title: What Is Medicine?
text: Medicine can help people get better when they are sick. Every medicine has instructions for when to take it and how much to take. There are many types of medicines. Each medicine has a different purpose. Some medicines are meant for only certain people. To be safe, you should only take medicines that are made for you and your illness.

title: Helpful or Harmful?
text:
Medicine can help you. It is important to take medicine the right way. Taking medicine when you need it can help you. Taking medicine when you don't need it can be harmful to your body.

HELPFUL

Medicines prescribed to you

Medicines made for your symptoms

Nutritious foods

HARMFUL

Drugs

Alcohol

Tobacco (smoking)

Medicines prescribed to other people

Medicine when you are not sick

Cleaners

Unknown items

Don't smell or taste medicines to figure out what they are. They can be bad for your body. Harmful things can hurt your brain and body. They can make your brain foggy. They can make your body sick.

title: Chemicals Affect Your Brain
text: Drugs are chemicals. They change how your body and brain work. Sometimes, a person has the urge to do something that is hard to control or stop. Their body is telling them that they crave something they don’t need. They do it even if it hurts them. It causes them to make bad choices. This is called addiction. Using drugs, alcohol, or tobacco can cause addiction. They can make your brain and your body think you need them even though they are bad for you. You can say “no” to these substances to protect your brain and body.

The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) was another important New Deal program. It provided jobs for millions of men from 1933 to 1942. The main purpose of the CCC was to employ single men from urban areas. They performed conservation work in America’s forest, state, and national parks, and other public lands. Men who joined the CCC were given food, lodging, clothing, and a monthly salary. The CCC also organized education classes to learn academic and work skills.

During the Great Depression, the CCC established more than 150 camps in Pennsylvania. These camps housed thousands of men. They worked to improve the state’s public lands, parks, and forests. Many Pennsylvanians worked on CCC projects in the state. They also worked on other CCC projects around the country. Over 194,000 Pennsylvanians worked for the CCC from 1933 to 1942. The money they earned boosted the state’s economy. That money helped to pull Pennsylvania out of the Great Depression.

The CCC had a large impact on the natural environment of Pennsylvania. CCC workers in Pennsylvania planted over 60,000,000 trees from 1933 to 1942. Other projects completed by the CCC in Pennsylvania included:

Improvements to the Gettysburg National Military Park (constructing trails, fences, and roads, installing utility lines, and reconstructing Civil War earthworks).

Building bathrooms, picnic pavilions, campgrounds, and a dam to create a swimming area at Ole Bull State Park in Cross Fork.

Planting 781 acres of trees in burned and cut-over areas in the Allegheny National Forest

Construction of the Log Cabin Inn Environmental Education Center at Cook Forest State Park in Cooksburg

title: Asking for Help
text: You can ask for help if you feel unsafe. You can ask for help if you see an unsafe situation with drugs or medicine. Ask an adult you trust for help. When you feel sick, you can ask an adult to help you know what medicine to take and how much to take. People who have become addicted to alcohol or drugs can get help too.

title: On to Liberty
text:
Born in 1814 in Germany, Theodore Kaufmann studied painting in several large cities. He left for the United States in 1850. He was first exposed to slavery In the U.S. and became an abolitionist. When the Civil War broke out, Kaufmann fought for the Union Army. During that time, he witnessed enslaved people coming to Union encampments and gaining their freedom. His painting, On to Liberty, became a symbol of why he fought against slavery. Kaufmann died in 1896.

Describe what you see. What are 10 things you see in the painting?

What do you notice first?

What people and objects are shown?

How are they arranged?

What is the physical setting?

Why do you think this image was made?

Who do you think was the audience for this image?

What can you learn from examining this image?

title: What is a Natural Disaster?
text:
Natural disasters such as floods, severe storms, tornadoes, tropical storms, hurricanes, blizzards, cold temperatures, and earthquakes can happen right here in Pennsylvania. It is important to know what natural disasters are so we can be prepared. Natural disasters can cause damage to land, buildings, and other structures. They can also cause people injuries and sometimes death.

Floods are the most common natural disaster. They can happen when too much rain causes waterways to overflow. Floods can also happen when large waves come onto the shore, when snow melts too quickly, or when dams break. Dams are designed to keep water in place.

Storms are another common natural disaster. Storms appear in different ways. A few different types of storms can be experienced across the state. Those are severe storms, tornadoes, and tropical storms.

Tropical storms and hurricanes usually happen near the coast. Hurricanes can be downgraded to a tropical storm and move inward across the state. Tropical storms can still cause wind damage, floods, power outages, and other destruction.

In the winter, storms can include dangerous ice, snow, wind, and cold temperatures. Ice and snow can make travel challenging. When you combine ice and snow with wind it can cause power outages and damage to buildings. It is important to pay attention to the temperatures, because extreme cold can cause hypothermia and frostbite.

Earthquakes are natural disasters that are not based on weather. They happen when the earth shifts and rocks break underground. Earthquakes are very rare in Pennsylvania. They may cause damage to buildings and other structures. You may feel shaking above ground when this happens. After the shaking stops, there may be aftershocks hours, weeks, or months later that still cause damage.

People are often able to predict when natural disasters may occur because of science and technology. The ability to predict allows communities to prepare and give them time to protect their community. Severe storms can be predicted by weather forecasting technology. People who live in disaster-prone areas are able to adjust their lives in order to stay safe.

title: Essential Question
text: How does human interaction with the environment create difficulties in nature?

title: The Johnstown Flood
text:
On May 31, 1889, a devastating flood hit the town of Johnstown, Pennsylvania. The combination of geography, weather, economics, and social factors created a disastrous event that killed 2,209 people.

Social Factors

The South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club was an exclusive vacation spot for many of Pittsburgh’s wealthiest industrialists and bankers. There were 61 members of the club, including Andrew Carnegie, Andrew Mellon, Henry Clay Frick, Daniel Morrell, and Philander Knox. An earthfill, or dirt dam, on the Conemaugh River made a lake two miles long and one mile wide. Club members stocked the lake with expensive and rare fish.

The dam was built in the 1840s for the Pennsylvania canal transportation system. Starting in the 1850s, the dam was poorly maintained. The Club also modified the dam to make room for a road and put a fish screen in the spillway. These developments are believed to have weakened the dam’s structural integrity further.

Economic Factors

The South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club existed for industrialists to escape the pollution of the large steel mills in Pittsburgh, mostly during the summer. Much of its workforce came from Johnstown. Their wages were low, and their hours were inconsistent. Engineers and many local workers over the years warned the club members that the dam needed maintenance and repairs, yet no one took action.

Cambria Iron Works employed 7,000 local and immigrant workers for the city of Johnstown. They had no organized union. The company rented houses to its employees, which were built close together between the mills. Workers bought necessities at the company department store. Wages were typical for the time. People earned just enough to live on, but rarely saved any money.

Geographic Factors

Johnstown was located in the narrow valley at the confluence of the Conemaugh River and Stony Creek. A confluence is the point where two rivers meet. This particular confluence was located in the Allegheny Highlands of the Appalachian Mountains, 14 miles south of the South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club.

Rainfall was high in the Allegheny Mountains. By May 31, 1889, after two days of constant rain, Johnstown had accumulated 6 to 10 inches of rain. The Conemaugh and Stony Creek were overflowing. Most of the streets in Johnstown were under one to two feet of water.

The Facts

The constant rain had saturated the earth of the South Fork Dam as the water in the lake kept rising. The dam was weakened from years without maintenance. Workers from Johnstown tried to reinforce the dam, but it was not enough. At 3:00 in the afternoon, the dam began to collapse and the lake was released into the valley below.

A telegram came into Johnstown from the South Fork Club warning that the town was in danger. Train whistles sounded, warning people of the coming flood. People ran to reach higher ground. Many survived, but others were caught in the wall of water that came down from the dam. The buildings in Johnstown were wiped out in the flood.

Aftermath

The American Red Cross came to help with disaster relief in Johnstown. The South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club was eventually disbanded. The club never claimed any responsibility for the catastrophe, though some members sent support for rebuilding and relief for the people of Johnstown. The people of Johnstown rebuilt their city. Today, there is a national memorial to the victims of the May 31, 1889 disaster.

title: Hurricanes in Pennsylvania
text:
The state of Pennsylvania has been impacted by hurricanes and tropical storms. Two of the strongest hurricanes in the state’s history are Hurricane Agnes (1972) and Hurricane Sandy (2012). Hurricanes form over the warm ocean water of the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. A tropical storm has winds from 39-73 mph. Hurricanes have winds of 74 mph or greater. The strength of hurricanes is measured from Category 1 (weakest) through 5 (strongest). The categories are based on wind speed and the width of the storm.

Hurricane Agnes formed in June 1972. It reached the Gulf of Mexico as a category 1 hurricane, before hitting the Florida panhandle. The storm traveled up the Eastern Seaboard and reached New York. Some areas received little rain and others received too much. Then, it moved west towards Pennsylvania. The National Guard was called to help sandbag the levee of the Susquehanna River. On June 23, after 36 hours and 12 inches of rain, the levee broke and caused the Wilkes-Barre and Harrisburg areas to flood. The flood destroyed thousands of homes. There were $2 billion dollars in damages in the Susquehanna River basin.

Hurricane Sandy was a superstorm. It formed in the Atlantic Ocean and traveled up the Eastern Seaboard. The hurricane mixed with a cold air mass from the north, a Nor’easter, and caused snow along with the huge storm surge from the high tide. Sandy made landfall in the Northeast on October 29, 2012. The storm knocked out power for days. Over 1,000,000 people in southeastern Pennsylvania lost power. Superstorm Sandy caused $62 billion of damage from the superstorm in the United States.

The government learned many lessons during these two hurricanes and have worked on ways to better predict storms and protect land.

title: The Great Blizzards of 1888 and 1996
text:
The Great Blizzard of 1888 hit the Northeast on March 11 and 12, 1888. This storm was not predicted and caused massive damage in several states. On March 10, 1888, temperatures across Pennsylvania were mild. Within 24 hours, temperatures quickly dropped below freezing and into the single digits. A blizzard raged for more than a day and high winds blew.

Around two to four feet of snow fell in about 36 hours. The largest amount of snowfall in Pennsylvania was in Blooming Grove, which received 31 inches of snow. Telegraph and telephone wires were damaged and trains were stranded. Many people were stuck in their homes. The blizzard conditions only lasted a few days. The people worked together to get the snow cleaned up and get life back to normal.

After this blizzard, officials made improvements to plans for extreme weather events. They started to bury telegraph and telephone lines underground to keep them safe from snow and wind damage. State governments also began funding new ways to forecast storms.

The Great Blizzard of 1888 was so powerful that it was used to compare other winter storms that followed, including the blizzard of 1996. The 1996 blizzard was one of the worst predicted storms on record. Even with a warning, the amount and weight of the snow made it hard to manage. The 1996 Nor’easter, which hit from January 7-11, dumped more than two feet of snow on Pennsylvania and other states in the Northeast. A week later, the temperature rose to the upper 50s and brought rain. This made the snow melt quickly and caused major flooding. This caused over $1,000,000,000 in damages across the state.

The 1996 storm showed that even with more modern forecasts, safety plans still need to be in place to help people. Predicting storms can help people be prepared. Forecasts can help people find shelter, gather food, and have tools in place to clear the snow and get utilities working again.

title: Tornadoes of May 31, 1985
text:
Weather events that meteorologists think are near impossible sometimes happen. Just the right weather conditions must come together for a tornado to form. Tornadoes form over land when warm, moist air meets cool, dry air. This creates high speed winds blowing in circular patterns. Tornadoes have different strengths and are gauged using the Enhanced Fujita scale. They are rated from 0 (weakest) to 5 (strongest). Tornado winds can destroy anything in their path.

An outbreak of tornadoes did just that in May of 1985. Forty-three tornadoes formed in Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, and Ontario, Canada. Tornadoes rarely happen in this area of the country. To many Pennsylvanians, May 31, 1985 is known as “Tornado Day.” Twenty-three tornadoes were recorded in 13 counties across the state on May 31, 1985. These tornadoes caused severe damage to more than 2,000 structures, causing injuries and deaths.

The only EF5 tornado in Pennsylvania history happened during the tornado outbreak of 1985. It was called the Niles-Wheatland tornado. This tornado started in Ohio and traveled east across the state line. Wheatland, Pennsylvania received the most damage from this tornado. An EF4 tornado also touched down that day in Moshannon State Forest, destroying 88,000 trees. That same day, a tornado over a mile wide was recorded in Tionesta, Pennsylvania in Forest County.

Tornadoes are devastating storms, but there are systems in place to keep people safe from these terrible natural disasters. Tornado watches are issued before tornadoes touch down. This gives people time to get to a safe location before the tornado hits. After a tornado touches down, a tornado watch changes to a tornado warning. Tornado warnings are sent out through television broadcasts and radio stations. Sirens in towns notify people that they need to take shelter.

Homes, schools, and businesses have plans in place in the event of a tornado. When a tornado occurs, people should find shelter in a safe place, such as a basement, on the lowest level of their building or home, under tables, and away from windows. Having a plan and acting on it can help keep people safe from tornadoes.

title: Help!
text:
Every person grows and learns how to do new things. Over time, some things will become easier for you. As you take on larger projects or activities, other things can become challenging. Many activities and tasks can be managed on your own. However, there are some types of challenges that require another person to help you consider your options, make a plan, or find a solution.

When you can’t achieve something on your own, ask for help. Everyone needs help at some point. There are all kinds of reasons people might ask for assistance. There are also different people you can ask to help in different scenarios. When you communicate that you need help, it’s best to communicate clearly by using verbal and nonverbal communication. Think about when, how, and who to ask for help.

title: When to Ask For Help
text:
Most of the time, it’s your choice if you want to ask for help. Sometimes, though, it’s critical to ask for help. You should ask for help if you ever feel that you or someone you know is in physical or emotional danger, or if you’re facing danger on the internet.

Alana chooses to learn a new song on an instrument by herself. She can choose whether or not she needs to ask a friend or an adult for help.

Jackson decides to paint his bedroom all by himself. He could choose to ask for help. He knows what the rules about paint are at his house.

Steven's friend tells him that he’s been thinking about hurting himself. Steven cares about his friend and is really worried. Right away, he tells the school counselor and his mom what his friend told him.

Cameron’s friend has a cochlear implant. Something stops working with it, and she‘s in a lot of pain. Cameron doesn’t know what to do, but he knows this is serious. Cameron asks the playground aide for help immediately.

Gina gets a message on her phone asking her to send pictures of herself to someone she doesn’t know.

The request makes her uncomfortable. She doesn’t send anything and she asks her mom for help right when she gets home.

Ask for help from a trusted adult immediately if you are facing physical danger. Physical dangers could include:

Physical bullying or threats

Physical injuries such as burns, cuts, or broken bones

Someone pressuring you to do something with your body that you are not comfortable with

Ask for help from a trusted adult immediately if you are facing emotional danger. Emotional dangers could include:

Verbal bullying (name calling, swearing, etc.)

Difficulty dealing with feelings of loss, sadness, depression, or anxiety

Someone asking you to do something you are not comfortable with

Ask for help from a trusted adult immediately if you are facing internet danger. Dangers on the internet could include:

Someone asking for your personal information

Someone sending you inappropriate pictures

Cyberbullying (someone sending rude messages, someone posting pictures of you without your permission, etc.)

title: Earthquakes in Pennsylvania
text:
Did you know that the state of Pennsylvania has fault lines that cause earthquakes? Earthquakes happen when large sheets of rock, called tectonic plates, shift underground causing the earth to move and shake. The magnitude of the earthquakes in Pennsylvania is typically very low, so the shaking is rarely ever felt by people.

Seismologists are scientists who study earthquakes. They measure the magnitude of an earthquake using a seismograph. A seismograph measures how strong the movements are in an earthquake. The Richter Scale describes this measurement from 1.0 (very weak and not noticeable) to 10.0 (strongest and most destructive).

There are two seismic zones that have fault lines in Pennsylvania: the Ramapo and the Lancaster fault lines, also called seismic zones. A fault line is where tectonic plates meet. The Ramapo Seismic Zone is located in Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey that helped form the Appalachian Mountains thousands of years ago.

The Lancaster Seismic Zone is the strongest zone in Pennsylvania. Over the last 200 years, 26 small earthquakes have been recorded in Lancaster County. This is the most seismic activity of any Pennsylvania county.

The largest earthquake recorded in Pennsylvania occurred in 1998 near Pymatuning Lake. The 5.2 magnitude earthquake caused some structural damage to buildings and the groundwater system.

Scientists have tried predicting earthquakes but have had little success. Some believe that with enough study, predicting them might be possible. Others think that it is impossible to accurately predict earthquakes. However, scientists can observe the pressure at any fault line. Using these observations, they can tell that an earthquake will happen but not when it will happen.

title: How to Ask For Help
text:
How you ask for help will depend on the urgency of your situation.

When asking for help for small things, be polite and patient. In the classroom, you can raise your hand to let the teacher know you need assistance, and wait your turn. Say “please” when you need someone’s help and “thank you” after they have helped you. If you need help tying a bow on a present, it would not be appropriate to yell, “Help! Help! I need help!”

Before asking for help with small things, make sure you have already tried your best to accomplish the task on your own. Will your teacher want to help you solve a math problem if you haven’t even attempted it yet? No. People will be more willing to help when they can see you’ve truly done your best and still need help.

In emergency situations, politeness and patience may not be your first priority when asking for help. If you are in a restaurant and your little sister starts choking, you won’t say, “Um, excuse me. Could someone help her please?” In emergencies, you need others to know it’s a crisis. Your tone may be louder, and your words may be more straightforward. You might yell something like, “My sister is choking! Someone please help!” Emergency situations require immediate action. To get help right away, dial 911 or yell for help.

title: Who to Ask For Help
text:
Make sure you are asking the right person for help! You want to make sure you ask someone who is trustworthy and can give you reliable information. Ask yourself: Who could help me the most?

Sometimes you can ask friends or peers for help with things like a homework assignment or deciding what to wear to an event.

More intense matters usually require the help of an adult. If you are aware of people your age drinking or doing drugs, you should tell an adult immediately.

If you have a medical emergency, you will need help from a doctor.

If you have an emotional or mental emergency, you can talk to a school counselor, parent, guardian, or therapist.

If there is a fire, call 911 so firefighters can help you.

title: Overcoming Fear to Ask For Help
text:
Knowing what resources are available to help you can decrease feelings of fear. There are adults who care about you and want you to be successful. There are other helpful resources specializing in specific areas of need. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the World Health Organization publish medical information that is widely accepted throughout the world. Organizations like these usually have websites where you can research important medical questions or concerns. Doctors, nurses, coaches, and fitness and nutrition instructors can help you with physical needs. Friends, peers, teachers, and counselors can help with social needs. Teachers, tutors, and peers can help you with academic needs.

If you are afraid to ask for help, ask in whatever way makes you most comfortable. You can talk to a parent or guardian in private. You can meet with your teacher after school or during lunch. You can even write a letter instead of speaking in person if that would help you communicate easier. Practice asking for help. This will make it easier to ask for help when you need it. Practice in the mirror or with a friend. When you feel nervous or afraid to ask for help, remember that there are lots of people who want to help you.

title: Taking Care and Planning for Disasters
text:
After reading about different types of natural disasters, you may be wondering what you can do to prepare before, during, and after natural disasters. It is important to stay up to date on weather forecasts and to make a plan with those in your home.

Meteorologists are a great source of information if you want to learn more about weather and natural disasters. Meteorologists are scientists who study and forecast weather to help people to be aware and make safe decisions. Staying alert by watching the local news on television, listening to the radio, researching information on meteorological websites can provide good information.

To stay alert and up-to-date during natural disasters, it is a good idea to know your current location, such as your city and county, and terms having to do with the storm or natural disaster. Floods, winter storms, tropical storms, tornadoes, and thunderstorms all have alerts, including watches and warnings. A "watch" means to be aware and prepared. A "warning" means that it has been seen in person or on radar.

To prepare for possible natural disasters, many households make an emergency plan. The plan might include having extra food, clothes, flashlights, a battery-operated radio, batteries, first aid kits, and other household supplies on hand. It is also important to create an evacuation plan in the event of natural disasters. The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania recommends having at least three days of supplies on hand in order for emergency crews to have a chance to help where they are needed.

During and after the weather event, follow your plan and take advice from local authorities. While a natural disaster is happening in your area, you might need to take shelter or evacuate. Stay informed and seek guidance from local authorities. Listen to their instructions so emergency crews and vehicles can help those in need. Above all, stay calm and help those near you, if it’s safe to do so.

title: Essential Question
text: How can people make positive contributions to their community?

title: What Does It Mean to Think Critically?
text:
Critical thinking means asking questions and doing research. It means thinking for yourself. When you think critically, you ask questions and search for answers. You may have questions like:

What evidence supports this idea?

Are my choices helping me grow?

Are the people I spend time with helping me be my best self?

How do my actions impact others?

What are the consequences?

Critical thinking can help you in many different areas of your life. For example, thinking critically can help you reduce or even prevent injuries and health problems. At your age, there are some common childhood injuries to be aware of. You can use your critical thinking skills to help you make choices that will keep you healthy and safe. Some common injuries at this stage of life include:

Broken bones

Head, neck, or spinal injuries

Bicycle or scooter injuries

Motor vehicle injuries

Pedestrian injuries

Burns

Think about these types of injuries. Think about your behaviors. What can you do to reduce the risk of any of these accidents happening to you or your friends?

title: The Importance of Critical Thinking
text: Critical thinking can help you form your own thoughts and opinions. It can also keep you safe and help you make healthy choices. When you think critically, you think before you act. You consider consequences and potential outcomes of a choice or action. Critical thinking will improve your decision-making skills. You can analyze the validity of information you read, see, hear, and understand. Validity refers to how accurate something is. Critical thinking can help you become more independent because it helps you consider all of these ideas. Problem-solving, making healthy decisions, and forming your own opinions are all skills you need to be more independent. More independence can result in more confidence, growth, and learning.

title: Steps for Critical Thinking
text:
Critical thinking evolves as you gain more knowledge and apply what you learn. Your thinking can evolve through these steps as you take information and turn it into opinions and findings. In each step of critical thinking, there are questions you can ask yourself to help you understand what you’re learning and processing.

Recall What You Know

What do you already know?

What does this mean for you?

Can you recall new information?

How, when, and why did it happen?

Who was involved?

Demonstrate Understanding

What is your perspective of what happened?

How would you summarize it?

What is the main idea?

What could happen now?

What evidence is there?

Apply Learning

How can that work?

What would happen if ...?

What consequences are there?

What other questions do you have?

What could have prevented this?

Make Connections

How does this idea compare to another idea?

What conclusions can be drawn?

What does the evidence support?

Why do you think ...?

What else makes sense?

Synthesize Conclusions

What changes need to be made?

How does your behavior contribute?

What does this mean for you?

Can you construct a model?

How would you improve ...?

Evaluate Outcomes

Why is this idea important?

What is your opinion?

Why did you choose ...?

How will you present this to others?

Now what questions do you have?

title: Ask Questions
text:
An opinion is one person’s preference or thought. A fact is something that is true for everyone. If someone says, “Strawberry is the best ice cream flavor,” you can recognize that as an opinion. You can ask questions, such as: Why do you feel that way? What evidence supports this opinion?

Evidence is information that shows something is true. A person may have evidence to support their opinions, or maybe they just really like strawberry ice cream. You can ask questions to better understand people’s opinions, then consider the evidence and decide if you agree or disagree.

Ask questions that help you think critically. As you ask questions and consider evidence and facts, you gain knowledge and develop your own educated opinions.

title: Research
text:
Research helps you discover a variety of opinions and facts about a topic. Doing research will help you share your opinion with others in healthy ways. When someone asks you a question, you can feel more confident about your opinion and what you have to say because you’ll have facts and evidence to back up your opinion.

Be sure to pay attention to the source that information is coming from. The source may affect how reliable it is. For example, if you want to build a house, should you listen to a chef or an architect? If you want to purchase new shoes, what sources can help you make the best choice? Consider multiple sources as you make your decisions. Advertisements, opinions of friends, and product reviews can help you to think critically as long as you consider the source and its relevance to your research.

Your own experiences and knowledge can help you determine what will be best for you. If you’re trying to solve a math problem, use the facts and skills you already know to solve it. When you’re trying to prevent an injury, recall past experiences and rules about safety to help you think critically. You can come up with a good decision and make choices that help you stay healthy.

You can conduct research on many topics. Research ways to reduce and prevent injuries or illness. Go through the steps of critical thinking. Recall what you know, demonstrate understanding, apply your learning, make connections, synthesize conclusions, and evaluate outcomes. Analyze what your role is and what the roles of others are in causing or preventing injuries. Consider what personal behaviors lead to injuries and which involve critical thinking and will prevent injuries. Compile your findings and present them to your class.

Research Topic

What is the best way to prevent or reduce the risk of childhood injuries?

title: Your Thoughts Matter
text:
Every individual has the right to think for themselves and form their own opinions. Everyone has distinct perspectives and experiences. For this reason, it’s important that we all think for ourselves. New ideas, creations, inventions, and perspectives are created as people think critically.

Your thoughts and opinions are important. You have unique experiences and knowledge that you can share. Now is the perfect time for you to figure out your own opinions and ideas. Then, as you grow older, you can use your knowledge, opinions, and critical thinking skills in a job, with your family, in your relationships, to resist negative peer pressure, and in all other areas of your life.

title: edna - test
text:
Solar energy is commonplace in the twenty-first century. It is because of people like Maria Telkes. In 1924, Telkes immigrated to the United States from Hungary. Telkes got a job with the Cleveland Clinic Foundation. She was the first woman to be employed at the Foundation as a scientist.

Telkes believed solar energy was a possible long-term solution for fuel. She advocated that solar energy was a clean and healthier alternative to the fuels that were being used. Telkes did the research for the Foundation but continued to investigate solar energy.

The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) was doing research to advance solar energy. In 1940, Telkes joined the staff at MIT. By 1948, she had designed and built the first house that was heated with solar energy. The Dover House had windows facing south. Storage units transferred the energy to heat and cool the house. The energy at the Dover House functioned for only two years. Telkes knew this was the first step to harnessing the sun for energy.

Telkes also developed a device to take salt water from the ocean and make drinkable water. This special evaporation process was used in World War II. The same technology is continued to be used today. After hurricanes devastate a community, technology can be used to provide drinking water to survivors.

Telkes had many patents for heating and cooling technology as well as heat storage. During her 94 years of life, Telkes contributed to research that is continuing to influence today’s technology.
