title: Teri-test
text:
Matter is all around us. Matter is anything that takes up space and has mass. Matter can be solid, liquid, or gas. We call this the physical state. Matter can have different colors, sizes, shapes, and smells. We call these physical properties. When we combine two types of matter, we can make a mixture or a solution.

A mixture is when two types of matter are put together, but they still keep their original properties. When a mixture is created, matter is conserved. The two types of matter can still be easily separated. For example, you could have 5 pink round beads in your left hand and 3 green star shaped beads in your right hand. If you put the beads together you have 8 total beads but you can still see 5 pink round beads and 3 green star shaped beads. Matter is conserved. That means the amount of matter did not change. You did not add or lose any beads when you put them all together.

When a solution is created, one type of matter dissolves into another type of matter. The two types of matter combine so well that you can't tell them apart anymore. A new substance is created. When a solution is created, matter is also conserved. An example is what happens when we add salt to water. The salt slowly dissolves into the water and we have saltwater. We can't see the salt anymore, but it's still there. Matter is conserved even when it dissolves. If you measure the mass of both the salt and the water before they are added together and measure the mass of the saltwater, the masses will be the same. When you put them together, no matter was added, and no matter was lost.

title: Groundhog Day in Punxsutawney
text:
Since 1887, people have headed to Gobblers Knob in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, on February 2 to watch an exciting event. Thousands of people make the trip to the tiny town in Jefferson County each year. Millions tune in on television and social media to watch the celebration. All of these people want to witness a groundhog become a meteorologist. According to legend, Phil the Groundhog can predict the weather. If the groundhog sees his shadow, there will be six more weeks of winter. If he does not see his shadow, winter will be over soon.

Originally, February 2 was called Candlemas in the Christian church. Christians in Europe took their candles to church to be blessed. They hoped this would bring blessings to their homes for the rest of the winter. February 2 is also halfway through the winter season. The weather on Candlemas was used to determine if winter would continue or if spring would start early. Candlemas goers would say:

“If Candlemas be fair and bright,

Come, Winter, have another flight;

If Candlemas brings clouds and rain,

Go Winter, and come not again.”

Eventually, the tradition of Candlemas made its way to Germany. Ancient German legends told of a hedgehog who could predict the weather. According to legend, if the hedgehog saw his shadow midway through winter, there would be six more weeks of bad weather. The ancient legend and the new Christian holiday were combined by people in Germany. Farmers used this new tradition to predict when to prepare their plows and seeds for spring planting.

The earliest mention of Groundhog Day in Pennsylvania comes from a diary entry on Feb. 2, 1840. James L. Morris of Morgantown, Pennsylvania, wrote in his journal, “Today the Germans say the groundhog comes out of his winter quarters and if he sees his shadow he returns in and remains there 40 days.”

People bring their traditions and celebrations with them when they move to a new place. The traditions of German Groundhog Day continued and changed over time. Today, Groundhog Day is a way to have fun in the middle of winter. What could be more fun than asking a groundhog to predict the weather?

title: Essential Question
text: How do the physical characteristics of place influence recreation in Pennsylvania?

title: People in Pennsylvania Have Fun
text:
Pennsylvania has a rich history of encouraging its citizens to enjoy the great outdoors. Whether it be through work, athletics, or family activities, Pennsylvania has so much to offer. While many people have jobs that require them to be outdoors, there are also a lot of ways to have fun!

Sometimes work and fun can be combined, such as through farms and state or county fairs. The tradition of fairs in the United States began with the York Fair in 1765. Thomas Penn, the son of William Penn, granted a charter to the people of York so they could have a fair. This was to recognize “the flourishing state to which the town hath arrived through their industry.” It was originally a two-day agriculture show and has since grown to a week-long event.

Throughout the years, many events have been added to fairs. This includes events like horse racing, car shows, strong man competitions, and concerts. Each county in Pennsylvania holds their own fair during the summer. At a county fair, there are all types of livestock, or farm animals, including cows, horses, and pigs. Children raise these animals and show them in competitions. Sometimes fairs also have amusement rides, carnival games, and fun foods.

In the summer, Pennsylvanians can enjoy many different outdoor activities. There are 124 state parks in Pennsylvania. The state parks are managed by the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. Entry into the parks is free. Parks provide picnic areas, camping spaces, and other overnight lodging in cabins and yurts. A yurt is a type of round tent with a wooden floor and frame.

Pennsylvania’s many waterways provide a variety of water activities. The Delaware Water Gap is the state border in the east. The mountain streams falling quickly down the valleys provide white water rafting. The large rivers provide hours of fun for canoeing or people who want to leisurely float down the river. Fishing can be done on the many lakes and mountain streams. Lake Erie is on the northwest border between Ohio and New York. This Great Lake gives Pennsylvanians an opportunity to sit on a beach and watch a sunset.

The state forests and game lands have thousands of miles perfect for hiking, biking, all-terrain vehicles (ATV), and snowmobiling. Wildlife can be seen in their natural habitats. While in the forests, you could see white-tailed deer, ruffed grouse, and beautiful blooming mountain laurel.

The winter can be just as fun in Pennsylvania. The Appalachian Mountains are in the middle of the state. The Appalachians are home to a variety of resorts for skiing, snowboarding, and snow tubing. The trails can be used for snowshoeing and cross-country skiing.

The state government maintains these outdoor spaces for the public to enjoy. When visiting the natural areas in Pennsylvania, be respectful of private property. The forests, waterways, and fields are not all open to the public. Look for signs. Research the area before your visit to know what is available and expected. A permit may be needed to use ATV trails. Reservations and payment are expected when using overnight lodging. Try to leave nothing but a footprint and take a photo when enjoying the natural resources of Pennsylvania.

title: Sports in Pennsylvania
text:
Professional sports are very popular throughout the world. That is no different in Pennsylvania. The two biggest cities in the state, Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, host multiple professional sports teams:

Hockey: the Philadelphia Flyers and the Pittsburgh Penguins

Football: the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburgh Steelers

Baseball: the Philadelphia Phillies and the Pittsburgh Pirates

Basketball: the Philadelphia 76ers

There are also minor league baseball teams in Harrisburg, Scranton, Altoona, Reading, Williamsport, Allentown, and Erie and minor league hockey teams in Hershey, Johnstown, Wilkes-Barre, and Philadelphia. The Poconos also has a NASCAR racetrack.

Many sports are also offered at the college level. From wrestling to tennis to swimming to competitive cheerleading, there are a variety of options. Penn State University, Villanova, University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Pittsburgh are a few schools that have a long history of athletics and national championships.

What would fun in Pennsylvania be without its sports? From the Terrible Towel of the Pittsburgh Steelers to the “We Are” chant at a Penn State football game, Pennsylvanians love their sports teams. Pennsylvania has a long history of championship football, baseball, basketball, and hockey teams at the college and professional levels. Championship teams include the Philadelphia Eagles, the Flyers, the Phillies, the 76ers, and the Pittsburgh Penguins, Pirates, and Steelers. At the college level, Pennsylvania also has the University of Pittsburgh Panthers and the Penn State Nittany Lions.

Sporting events are a lot of fun for friends and family to attend together. Often, people have to travel in order to attend an event. This helps Pennsylvania’s economy through tourism. People who attend these events often go to restaurants, stay in hotels, and use public transportation. All of those needs help to create jobs and a lot of fun for Pennsylvanians!

title: Amusement Parks in Pennsylvania
text:
Amusement parks have rides, games, and events for entertainment. Amusement parks are very popular throughout Pennsylvania. From roller coasters to water slides to merry-go-rounds, there is something for everyone to enjoy. The most popular time of year to go to an amusement park is usually the summer. That way, patrons, or people who pay for entry, can enjoy a nice picnic, a wave pool, or even some pretzels and ice cream! Amusement parks sometimes offer events and games during the colder months with limited operations of the rides.

Pennsylvania’s first amusement park was Idlewild, located in Ligonier. Not only is it the oldest running amusement park in Pennsylvania, it is the third-oldest in the country. Idlewild was founded in 1878 by Thomas Mellon. Mellon wanted a tourist attraction close to the railroad he had recently purchased.

Technology and engineering for the railroad created an amusement park ride called a roller coaster. Small train cars roll on steel tracks. Wooden or steel trestles provide elevation, or height, for the track. The trestles provide highs, lows, and curves to keep the train coasting at a fast speed.

Roller coasters were first introduced in the late 1800s. The Leap-the-Dips roller coaster in Altoona, one of the earliest roller coasters in Pennsylvania, operated for 83 years, from 1902 to 1985.

One attraction at most amusement parks is the Ferris Wheel. The Ferris Wheel, which was first called the “Observation Wheel,” was invented by George Washington Gale Ferris Jr. in 1892. Ferris was a bridge builder from Pittsburgh. Ferris used construction technology from the steel industry to build the first Ferris Wheel. He bolted steel rods together into a giant frame like an upright wheel. Then, he added seating and an engine. This made the giant wheel spin slowly. The wheel lifted people high in the air and down again. The Ferris Wheel was introduced at the 1893 World's Columbian Exhibition in Chicago, Illinois, and was a huge success!

In 2010, the Pennsylvania House of Representatives recognized Ferris’s life and accomplishments. The House resolution quotes a reviewer who says, “You cannot advertise the wheel, anyway, any more than you can advertise the fair or the Atlantic Ocean. They are all too big.”

title: Hiking the Appalachian Trail
text:
The Appalachian Trail is one of the longest hiking trails in the world. The 2,175-mile-long trail follows the Appalachian Mountains from Maine to Georgia. This trail goes through 14 states, including 229 miles in Pennsylvania.

Creation of the Appalachian Trail began in 1921 and was completed in 1937. Since then, the trail has been a popular hiking destination. Both new and experienced hikers from all over the world have hiked on this trail.

The first person to do a thru-hike, or the entire trail, was Earl Shaffer. Earl Shaffer was from York County, Pennsylvania. He completed the hike in 1948 in just four months. Shaffer chronicled his entire journey in a small notebook. He used his research to write a book about his time and experiences on the Appalachian Trail.

The Appalachian Trail Conservancy estimates three million people use the Appalachian Trail every year. Three thousand hikers attempt a “thru-hike” from Georgia to Maine each year.

People don’t need to hike the entire trail to experience its natural wonders, including waterfalls, lakes, and wildlife. Small sections are perfect for an afternoon or day hike. A variety of birds can be observed, from chickadees to bald eagles. Hiking offers a quiet way to experience Pennsylvania’s natural resources. If the Appalachian Trail isn’t close, try a trail in a state park.

title: Winter Fun
text:
Pennsylvanians know how to make winter fun. Pennsylvania offers skiing, snowboarding, ice fishing, ice skating, and many other activities during the winter. The mountain ranges and waterways allow people to enjoy these activities across the entire state.

Do you like speed? If so, skiing or snowboarding might be your type of activity. The Pocono Mountains offer dozens of trails throughout their 2,400 acres. If speed is not your choice, however, there are also trails for snowshoeing and cross-country skiing.

State parks and forests also offer thousands of miles of designated snowmobile areas for exploration. Elk State Forest is known for its snowmobile trails. State parks and forests also offer trails for sledding. Frozen ponds across the state are used for ice skating.

Because of these activities, many businesses, such as ski resorts, have emerged. These businesses have created many jobs for the people of Pennsylvania. In 2021, the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development reported that tourism added $43 billion to the state’s economy. The businesses supporting tourism and recreation created 500,000 jobs.

title: Water Play
text:
Earlier this year, you read about the many waterways in Pennsylvania. You learned that there are thousands of miles of rivers and streams that run throughout the state. There are also hundreds of lakes and ponds in the Keystone State as well. These waterways allow Pennsylvanians to enjoy the great outdoors even more.

There are so many water activity options to choose from in Pennsylvania. If you like to take it slow, maybe you’d like to kayak or canoe on the Susquehanna River. You can also go swimming at one of the many state parks, such as Little Buffalo. If you like a faster pace, you might enjoy white water rafting at Ohiopyle State Park.

You could also go fishing, boating, or even water skiing. Prompton Lake in Wayne County offers great boating opportunities. Lake Wallenpaupack is one of the largest human-made lakes in Pennsylvania. Built as a reservoir for northeastern Pennsylvania communities, it doubles as a recreation area.

Many people also enjoy rowing. People row for fun or to participate in the sport competitively. Each year, thousands of people flock to the Schuylkill River to participate in or watch rowing events. Philadelphia is considered the birthplace of American rowing. Many rowing competitions are held in Philadelphia each year, including the Philadelphia Youth Regatta.

The mountains, valleys, and streams of Pennsylvania create waterfalls. Bushkill Falls in Pike County has eight cascades that people can visit and enjoy. Waterfalls are located along many streams throughout the state. A good time to see full streams of water tumbling over the rocks is during the spring after the winter snows melt. Waterfalls attract photographers, artists, and tourists who enjoy the sights and the sounds of moving water.

According to the U.S. Department of Commerce, outdoor recreation in Pennsylvania adds $14 billion to the economy each year.

title: The Great Depression
text:
In the 1920s, Americans were living extravagant and carefree lifestyles. People were buying many items using credit. Credit is a promise to pay later. Many people were not concerned with saving money. Manufacturers produced more items, expecting to sell them. Americans were also buying stock, or shares on the stock market. They were not paying the total price of the stocks. They hoped they could pay the difference if they achieved a profit from the market. The stock market is where people can buy into a company. Over time, their investment could increase or decrease. If too many stocks decrease, investments are lost. This results in people losing money and, eventually, a stock market crash.

On Tuesday, October 29, 1929, Americans and the United States economy were greatly affected by a stock market crash. It was the beginning of what became known as Black Tuesday. The price of stocks fell sharply and the shares became worthless. Many people lost huge amounts of money. When the stock market crashed, the U.S. economy crashed along with it. The stock market crash was only the beginning of tough times for the country. Many banks lost money, too. People worried that they could not withdraw their money out of the bank. They rushed to the banks. When banks were out of cash, they closed their doors. Some of the banks began to go out of business completely. People who had deposited and could not withdraw their cash in the banks were out of luck. There was no cash left. Businesses were also affected by the economic downturn. Some businesses lost most of their money in the stock market crash. They couldn’t pay employees.

The workforce was reduced significantly. There were too many products in the marketplace and no one to buy them. Many workers were laid off, or removed from their jobs. This happened in the coal mines. The coal miners were going on strike due to the overproduction of coal. Many Americans were turning their sights to new, cheaper technology like natural gas and oil. They were not buying coal.

The United States elected a new president in 1933. He was Franklin Delano Roosevelt. Roosevelt's first task as president was to stop the panic of the banks closing and the stock market crashing. The plan that he and his advisors worked on was called the New Deal. This government program created new government agencies that helped the economy recover and provided jobs for workers.

title: Essential Question
text: How do government actions affect communities?

title: New Deal Programs in Pennsylvania
text:
In 1933, the United States was in the middle of a great economic depression. That same year, Franklin Delano Roosevelt, a Democrat, was sworn in as the new president of the United States. As president, Roosevelt faced many challenges. One of the greatest challenges was finding a way to bring the country out of the Great Depression.

Roosevelt and his advisors introduced a plan. It was known as the New Deal. The plan was expansive. It was meant to bolster the country's economy. The New Deal created new government agencies. They were meant to assist people in need. This included those in poverty, the elderly, farmers, and millions of unemployed Americans. Programs included:

AAA (Agricultural Adjustment Administration)

CCC (Civilian Conservation Corps)

CWA (Civil Works Administration)

FERA (Federal Emergency Relief Administration)

FSA (Farm Security Administration)

FDIC (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation)

NRA (National Recovery Administration)

NYA (National Youth Administration)

PWA (Public Works Administration)

REA (Rural Electrification Administration)

RFC (Reconstruction Finance Corporation)

SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission)

SSA (Social Security Administration)

TVA (Tennessee Valley Authority)

WPA (Works Progress Administration)

Many of these programs had a profound impact. They affected the people, places, economy, and government of Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvanians benefitted from the Social Security Act (SSA). Under the SSA, the government taxed workers’ salaries. This money was given to older citizens. They were usually 65 or older. The Social Security Act is still used today.

The Works Progress Administration (WPA) had a large impact on Pennsylvania. The WPA provided jobs for unemployed people. It affected those in every economic sector. The WPA created jobs in social services, construction, public health, conservation, education, fine arts, and scholarly research. Hundreds of projects were completed in Pennsylvania because of the WPA during the Great Depression. The WPA helped to repair and maintain over 145 miles of roads in Philadelphia. One of the largest WPA projects in Pennsylvania was the construction of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. It connected the eastern and western parts of the state. The Pennsylvania Turnpike changed travel throughout the state. It received the name “America’s First Superhighway.”

The WPA also funded archaeological digs. They were meant to preserve the history of Pennsylvania. WPA archaeologists conducted excavations in Somerset County, Pennsylvania. They uncovered the remains of several ancient Indigenous villages. Also through the WPA, artists in Pennsylvania were hired to paint murals. The murals were put in government buildings, schools, and post offices across the state. Some of the murals depicted important moments in Pennsylvania’s history. Others depicted economic activities in the state. Writers wrote guidebooks about Pennsylvania. They conducted interviews with members of different communities. The writers helped record the history of Pennsylvania.

The Public Works Administration (PWA) also impacted Pennsylvania and its people. PWA funds were used to construct new government facilities in Harrisburg. The construction included the Finance Building and the Northwest Office Building of the state capitol. The program also provided funds to improve the Pittsburgh & West Virginia Railway. PWA funds were used to build 12 military armories around the state. Multiple schools and university buildings were constructed. They used loans and grants for the PWA. Over $1,000,000 in funds were given to Pennsylvania State University by the PWA. The funds were used to construct new academic buildings.

The Federal Emergency Relief Administration (FERA) and National Youth Association (NYA) also helped thousands of people in Pennsylvania. The NYA and FERA awarded scholarships to Pennsylvania students to attend college. These programs provided funds to colleges and universities for student jobs and work programs. Multiple projects were completed in Canonsburg because of the FERA funds.

title: The CCC in Pennsylvania and State Parks
text:
The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) was an important New Deal program. It provided jobs for millions of men from 1933 to 1942. The main purpose of the CCC was to employ single men from urban areas. They performed conservation work in America’s forest, state, and national parks and other public lands. Men who joined the CCC were given food, lodging, clothing, and a monthly salary. The CCC also organized education classes to teach men academic and work skills.

During the Great Depression, the CCC established more than 150 camps in Pennsylvania. These camps housed thousands of men. They worked to improve the state’s public lands, parks, and forests. Many Pennsylvanians worked on CCC projects in the state. They also worked on other CCC projects around the country. Over 194,000 Pennsylvanians worked for the CCC from 1933 to 1942. The money they earned boosted the state’s economy. That money helped to pull Pennsylvania out of the Great Depression.

The CCC had a large impact on the natural environment of Pennsylvania. CCC workers in Pennsylvania planted over 60,000,000 trees from 1933 to 1942. Other projects completed by the CCC in Pennsylvania included:

Improvements to the Gettysburg National Military Park (constructing trails, fences, and roads, installing utility lines, and reconstructing Civil War earthworks)

Building bathrooms, picnic pavilions, campgrounds, and a dam to create a swimming area at Ole Bull State Park in Cross Fork

Planting 781 acres of trees in burned and cut-over areas in the Allegheny National Forest

Construction of the Log Cabin Inn Environmental Education Center at Cook Forest State Park in Cooksburg

title: Rural Electrification: Bringing Electricity to Everyone
text:
In 1936, the Rural Electrification Administration was established. Its mission was to bring electricity to rural areas of the United States, particularly farms. In 1936, the U.S. government estimated that 90 percent of farms in the country did not have electricity. In the same year, a survey of farms in Pennsylvania showed similar results. It determined that 75 percent of the state’s farms did not have electricity. The REA hoped to change that. They wanted to bring affordable electricity to all farms and rural areas of the country.

The REA created government loans for building power lines. These power lines were installed in areas outside the cities. Loans were given to groups formed by people in rural areas. The groups were called cooperatives. The cooperatives helped complete the work. Cooperatives hired workers, bought materials, and cleared the land to bring electricity to rural areas. Fourteen cooperatives were established in Pennsylvania. They helped meet the needs of Pennsylvanians in rural areas.

Hundreds of Pennsylvanians worked for the state’s cooperatives. They brought much-needed funds into Pennsylvania homes. From 1936 to the end of 1941, Pennsylvania’s rural electric cooperatives installed 9,000 miles of electrical lines. About 25,000 families living in rural areas of the state finally received electricity. In 1994, the Rural Electrification Administration became the Rural Utilities Service. The RUS continues to help people in rural areas of Pennsylvania today.

title: Andrew W. Mellon and Banking
text:
Andrew W. Mellon had a large impact on the financial industry of Pennsylvania during the Great Depression. Mellon was already a wealthy banker, businessman, philanthropist, and industrialist in Pennsylvania when the Great Depression began in 1929. With the help of his brother and father, Mellon founded the Mellon National Bank. Within 50 years, the Mellon National Bank became one of the largest financial and money management institutions in the world. Mellon National Bank lent money to large corporations. Those included U.S. Steel, Heinz, General Motors, and Standard Oil.

Mellon was also a key player in Pennsylvania and U.S. politics. In 1921, Mellon was chosen to serve as secretary of the treasury for the United States. He served under President Warren G. Harding. During his first term in office, he developed the Mellon Plan. The Mellon Plan cut government spending. It also reduced taxes on wealthy industrialists and businesses. This plan significantly reduced the country’s debt.

Mellon was also a noted philanthropist. Throughout his life, Mellon gave about $10,000,000 to educational institutions and charities in Pittsburgh. He donated a portion of his fortune to the University of Pittsburgh. The money helped create the Mellon Institute of Industrial Research. He also donated funds and artwork to the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C.

Mellon served as U.S. secretary of the treasury until 1932. He returned to private business until his death in 1937. Mellon’s influence can still be seen in Pennsylvania today. Mellon donated the land for Pittsburgh’s Cathedral of Learning and the Heinz Chapel. He was also the founder of Donora, Pennsylvania. In 1967, the Mellon Research Institute merged with Carnegie Technical School. They formed Carnegie Mellon University. Students from around the world attend Carnegie Mellon University. It's regarded for its amazing academic programs.

title: Pennsylvania Governor Gifford Pinchot
text:
Gifford Pinchot had a profound impact on Pennsylvania during the Great Depression. Pinchot was a noted forester, conservationist, and environmentalist. He was first elected governor of Pennsylvania in 1922. He served until 1926. Pinchot was elected governor again in 1930, during the first year of the Great Depression.

Pennsylvanians faced many challenges during the Great Depression. When Pinchot began his second term as governor, over 11 percent of Pennsylvanians were unemployed. Hundreds of Pennsylvania banks and businesses had failed. Without employment, many Pennsylvanians were forced to wait in bread and soup lines to feed themselves and their families. As governor, Pinchot knew he had to work hard to help Pennsylvanians overcome these challenges.

One of Pinchot’s goals was to improve the state’s transportation system. During the Great Depression, thousands of roads in Pennsylvania were in need of repair and upgrades. Pinchot and the state government created a plan. They would build and update 20,000 miles of paved roads in Pennsylvania. This plan was the first state-funded work relief program created during the Great Depression.

Engineers and workers in the state created new roads based on the designs of British engineer John Loudon McAdam. McAdam’s design required roads to be elevated instead of dug out of the soil. To do this, engineers and workers laid stones over the dirt roads. Next, they dug ditches next to the roads. These were to collect water runoff. Gravel was spread over the stones. The gravel made the road more even. Finally, the gravel road was coated with asphalt. This created a smooth road for cars and trucks to drive on.

These roads became known as “Pinchot Roads.” Pinchot Roads had a profound impact on Pennsylvania. They made it more affordable for farmers to transport their crops to markets. It became easier for everyone to get the food they needed. It also helped many other Pennsylvanians who needed jobs. Thousands of Pennsylvanians were employed to build the Pinchot Roads. It also helped the oil industry. Asphalt is made using oil. Lots of oil was needed to pave the roads. The roads were simple, but they were just what Pennsylvania needed to connect the state’s farms, rural areas, and cities.

Pinchot created several reform programs during the Great Depression. He created a commission to investigate and stop mistreatment and unsafe working conditions in the garment industry. He also improved state child labor laws. Pinchot helped pass legislation to provide state-funded pensions for the elderly and blind. In 1932, Pinchot said, "Let it be said of this great Commonwealth that it never turned a deaf ear to the cry of the hungry. The honor of the Commonwealth demands a different reply." This was a belief he held until his second term ended in 1935.

title: Governments in North and South America
text:
Societies have created many different types of governmental systems. These different types of government reflect the values and beliefs of the societies that created them. Some forms of government are unique to certain times and places. Others have been reused, recycled, or reformed by other communities. When the ancient Romans created the Roman Republic, it was a completely new form of government. However, many other societies have created their own republican forms of governments since then. In fact, the United States is a constitutional republic.

No matter the type, the primary purpose of government is to create systems that manage the rights and liberties of individuals. Governments create processes that help them meet their own wants and needs as well as the wants and needs of the people. These processes include judicial systems, elections, and political parties.

Governments have the authority to control or direct the actions of citizens. A government’s authority comes from laws, morality, customs, or the consent of the people. Laws are the formal rules of a society that all citizens must follow. The government enforces the consequences for breaking laws. The laws that a government creates reflect the values and customs of the society they come from.

A constitution is a document that establishes the authority and power of a government. Most constitutions describe how power is passed from one person to another. They can define how people can be elected. They also state who is qualified to be elected. Many nations with written constitutions are democracies or republics. In a republic, the people elect, or choose, their leaders. The United States is a constitutional republic. Most Latin American countries are also considered republics, but there are other forms of government in the Western Hemisphere.

A confederation is a group of provinces or territories that are connected through a shared government. Canada's government is a parliamentary democracy and a constitutional monarchy. The Parliament is made up of three areas: the Crown, the Senate, and the House of Commons. The members of the Senate are appointed by the Governor General. The members of the House of Commons are elected by Canadian citizens. As a constitutional monarchy, the executive power goes to the current monarch. A monarch is someone born into power through their family line. The monarch chooses the governor of Canada with the advice of Canada's prime minister.

The prime minister is the head of the country's government and leader of the major political party. Canada belongs to a commonwealth. A commonwealth is a group of countries that forms for the good of the "commonwealth" of all its member countries. The largest commonwealth is the Commonwealth of Nations, which is made up of more than 50 nations that were once part of the British Empire.

The governments of Latin America were once largely controlled by dictators, or people who have all the power with no permission from the people. Revolutions across Latin America caused constant change and turbulence. New governments were formed that were primarily democratic forms of government. As new governments form, the economy is often unstable. Change is often slow to happen. Many of the governments and constitutions in Latin America are very new. They are sure to continue changing as the people rebuild their economies and adjust to change.

title: Types of Governments
text: A government is a group of people who lead a community. Government leaders work to serve the needs of the people in a community. There are many types of government systems. Three of these systems are democracy, monarchy, and dictatorship. Each government system works differently. Most of these government systems make and enforce laws. As we look at these types of governments, pay special attention to the services provided by the government. Also, pay attention to the role of citizens in each of these types of governments.

title: Types of Economic Systems
text: An economic system is the way communities and governments organize resources, goods, and services. Resources, goods, and services are then given to the people. Governments often determine the type of economic system of a country. There are many types of economic systems people use around the world. However, most people use one of three types of economic systems. These three types are traditional, command, and market economies. Each system shares the same basic features, but each one has specific characteristics that separate it from the others.

title: Free Market Economy
text:
The free market system is an important aspect of a market economy. Free market systems only work if a country's laws and its citizens' values support them. If this type of market doesn't exist, the system will fail. Six characteristics of a free market system make it successful. These are private property, specialization, voluntary exchange, price system, market competition, and entrepreneurship.

Private property is the first fundamental component in a free market system. It influences everyone to care for the things we own. Private property also provides us with incentive. Incentive is what motivates us to make the decisions we make. If a business doesn't take care of its office building or breaks equipment, it must pay to replace them. This gives the business incentive to care for things it uses.

Specialization means businesses focus on creating certain types of products or providing specific services. This allows companies to become experts in their field. They can also produce more goods over time. Companies that specialize in one or many products are able to save money on goods and resources. They can provide higher wages to their employees.

Voluntary exchange is another important element of free market systems. Voluntary exchange means people must exchange goods or currency to acquire resources they need. Consumers have the choice to purchase goods and services. It's not forced upon them by businesses or government regulations.

Creating a price system is crucial for a free market economy's success. Prices provide guidance for producers and consumers. Prices show the market how much customers value the producer's goods. They also provide clues for economists about whether a market is healthy or not. Prices also provide incentives for businesses and consumers. Most consumers try to shop for bargains if prices rise. This keeps businesses from overcharging their customers.

A free market system must have competition within the market to work properly. Competition between producers lowers product prices and creates more options for consumers. It can also make resources and products more valuable.

A free market economy's final characteristic is entrepreneurship. Entrepreneurship is the act of developing, organizing, and managing a new business. Entrepreneurs are people who create and run businesses. They must be able to adapt to changing markets and meet customer demands.

title: Adam Smith: "The Father of Economics"
text:
Economies have specific processes and concepts that help them run smoothly. They also use certain terms to describe these processes and concepts. Where did these terms come from? Some of them came from Adam Smith. He is known as the “Father of Economics.”

Adam Smith was a Scottish philosopher and economist. He wrote a book titled The Wealth of Nations. In his book, he explained many economic concepts. One of the concepts was the division of labor. Smith realized that dividing labor makes the process of producing goods faster. It works because people can focus on certain tasks. They can develop the skills needed for that task so that they become really good at it. Other people focus on different tasks. Producing goods goes a lot faster when people are good at what they do.

Producing goods and services is how countries make money. During most of world history, the wealth of a nation was measured in the amount of gold and silver it possessed. Smith thought of wealth in a different way. He developed the concept of gross domestic product. Gross domestic product, or GDP, describes the value of all the goods and services a country produces. When a country produces a lot of goods and services, it has a high GDP. We still use GDP to measure how well a country’s economy is doing.

How does a country know how much of each good or service to produce? It follows the rules of supply and demand. When people buy a lot of something, companies know to make more. When a product or service is not popular, companies know to produce less of it. This is what Smith called the “invisible hand.” The invisible hand guides the economy.

Smith believed that economies could regulate themselves with concepts like the invisible hand. This means he thought there was no need for a government to tell companies how much they could or should produce. An economy free of government regulation is called a free market. Adam Smith’s concepts are still a big part of our economy today.

title: Neighboring Economies
text:
Countries within the Western Hemisphere engage in trade with each other.

Canada

Canada and the United States share a similar economy. People own businesses and resources. They can sell products and services from their businesses to make money. It is a capitalist economy. But, like the United States, Canada cannot count on its own businesses to give it everything it needs. This is when the government steps in.

For example, Canada has two railway systems. One is a private business. The owner of the business makes a profit by providing a service. This railroad system cannot serve the entire country, so the second railway was created by the government to fill that need. It is owned and operated by the government for public use. The purpose of this railroad isn’t to make money. It is to provide Canada with an important service. The Canadian government also owns power plants, radio stations, communications systems, and other transportation systems.

Because Canada is part of the British Commonwealth, it shares aspects of government with Britain. It shares strong economic ties with Britain, too. The two countries have their own trade agreement. Most of the goods traded between the two countries do not have tariffs.

Although Canada and Britain are close, Canada and the United States play a larger role in each other’s economies. Around 75 percent of Canada’s trade is done with the United States. Trade helps us maintain a good relationship with our neighbor to the north.

Mexico

Mexico is also one of the largest trading partners of the United States. Ninety percent of Mexico’s exports are sent to the United States. These exports include things like food, oil, and cars. Manufacturing is one of the largest industries in Mexico. Many foreign auto companies have moved their production to Mexico. Mexico also has rich oil and silver reserves to trade with other countries.

The United States is an important trading partner for Mexico, but it’s not the country’s old trading partner. Mexico has free trade agreements with 46 different countries. It is also a member of the Pacific Alliance. The other members are Chile, Colombia, and Peru. These countries work together to develop their economies.

Brazil

Brazil’s government works with the people to make decisions about the economy. However, there are other elements of Brazil’s economy that make it different from other countries. In 2006, Brazil became independent in energy sources. This means that the country does not have to spend money trading with other countries for resources like oil. It has enough oil to supply the entire country. It even exports oil to other countries like the United States. The United States also imports goods like agricultural products and steel from Brazil.

Panama

Panama is important to the world’s economy. It allows many of the world’s goods to pass through the Panama Canal. The Panama Canal is a human-made seaway between the continents of North America and South America. Before it was built, ships had to carry goods all the way around the tip of South America. The Panama Canal greatly decreased the time it takes to transport goods across the world. The canal also contributes a lot of money to Panama’s economy.

Puerto Rico

Puerto Rico is a commonwealth of the United States. It’s not a state, but it does receive help from the United States government, and its citizens are considered U.S. citizens. It can receive funding in times of economic hardship and natural disasters. To encourage opportunity, Puerto Rico offers U.S. manufacturers tax breaks for establishing businesses on the island.

There are many different ways that governments and economies interact with each other across the Western Hemisphere. They have different ways of conducting trade. They all have different resources to share, but they are interdependent. They work together to give one another the resources their people need.

title: Role of Government in Economics
text:
The government's main economic role is to use money and funds to provide services to citizens. We use government goods and services every day. People who work pay a part of their income to the federal government in the form of taxes. When you buy something, you pay a little more than the price tag says. This is because you're also paying a small tax called a sales tax. Sales tax helps the government provide goods and services to everyone.

Many of the goods and services the government provides are known as public services. An example of this is your community library. It doesn't cost you any money to borrow books or other materials from your local library. The government provides this public service to the community through money collected from taxes. Other public services provided by the government include police, fire, and water departments, parks, and public health departments.

Businesses people own are considered private enterprises. What are some private businesses in your area? Think about the restaurants, stores, and gas stations you visit.

title: Environmental Economics
text:
One way the government affects the economy is through environmental economics. Environmental economists usually work for the government. They study the effect the economy has on the environment. They try to identify problems and examine the ways they use natural resources. They also look at the waste materials that products produce. They decide if the costs of using products are greater than the benefits.

Many products that people use create pollution. Pollution has a negative impact on the environment. Burning fossil fuels to power cars and power plants releases carbon into the atmosphere. These carbon emissions are a large contributing factor of global warming. Environmental economists study these costs and how they affect us. They work hard to make sure that the environment is safe for the benefit of everyone.

In many cases, products create too much pollution. When this happens, environmental economists place standards on these products. Companies have to make sure their products meet these standards. For example, there are standards on how much pollution cars can emit. Companies have to make sure their cars don’t exceed the limit. Companies must work to make cars more efficient. More efficient cars can go farther on less fuel. The hope is that more people will buy cars that don’t damage the environment.

Environmental economists help create sustainability. Sustainability is about balance. It means there is a good balance between the things we produce and the resources we use to produce them. Environmental economists perform research on sustainability. They make sure that people don’t use too many of the Earth’s natural resources too quickly. Another goal of environmental economists is to encourage people to leave enough resources for future generations.

title: Why Set Goals?
text: A goal is something you really want to do. You can make a plan to help you reach your goal. You won’t believe how much you learn and grow! Goals can help you see how amazing you really are.

title: One Step at a Time
text:
Think of a goal like a ladder. Your goal is at the very top. To reach it, you need to go up each step of the ladder. The steps are like mini goals. For example, if your big goal is to learn an instrument, you need to choose which instrument. That’s one step.

What’s on your ladder?

title: Keep Going!
text: Reaching a goal takes hard work. You don’t have to be perfect. Do your best to stick to the plan that you have made. Try to do something every day that gets you closer to your goal.

title: Conservation in Pennsylvania
text:
Pennsylvania, the Keystone State, is home to some of the most important events, people, and technological innovations in American history. It is also geographically diverse—filled with natural resources, waterways, and wildlife. These factors influenced Pennsylvania’s growth from colonial times to the present.

Although Pennsylvania’s rapid growth had many positive effects on the state, there were also many negative consequences. Lumber from Pennsylvania’s forests was used to build homes, towns, and factories. But by 1895, Pennsylvania’s forests were virtually empty. Deforestation threatened many areas and led to temperature changes across the state. Trees store carbon. Without trees, carbon is released into the air and transforms into carbon dioxide. High levels of carbon dioxide become trapped in the atmosphere and cause temperatures to rise.

Unrestricted hunting and trapping led to a decline in the animal population of the state. Areas of Pennsylvania that were once filled with indigenous animals, such as elk, beavers, deer, bear, and many species of birds, became empty. Many species were on the verge of extinction.

Pennsylvania’s steel industry began in the early 1800s. The state quickly grew to be the center for steel production in the United States. The steel, manufacturing, and mining industries contributed billions of dollars to the state’s economy. But the chemicals they produced caused widespread pollution. Harmful fumes filled the air. Many people called Pittsburgh “The Smoky City” because it had some of the worst air quality in America.

Sometimes sewage and waste pollute state waterways and lakes. In 1988, an oil tank at the Ashland Oil Company in Floreffe collapsed. Thousands of gallons of oil spilled into the Monongahela River. It contaminated drinking water in three states, killed wildlife, and damaged property.

Human modification of the environment caused many dangerous issues. In 1889, the South Fork Dam, located near Johnstown, Pennsylvania, burst, flooding the town. The Johnstown Flood of 1889 destroyed most of the northern half of the city and killed about 2,200 people.

In 1962, firefighters in Centralia, Pennsylvania, were cleaning up the town’s landfill, which was located in an abandoned strip mine. They tried to conduct controlled burns of the landfill, but the fire spread through the mines that ran under the town. The fires in the mines could not be put out and are still burning today. The fires have caused many environmental issues and a major decline in the town’s population.

In 1979, a nuclear reactor located on Three Mile Island, near Middletown, Pennsylvania, malfunctioned and stopped working. It released radiation into the environment. Three Mile Island is now a government superfund site. A superfund site is a location that is polluted by waste, radiation, or harmful chemicals that require extensive, long-term cleanup.

Conservation is the science of protecting or preserving something, such as natural resources or the environment. Pennsylvanians have worked tirelessly to protect the state’s water, land, air, resources, people, and animals.

title: Rachel Carson
text:
Pennsylvanians have had a profound impact on the conservation movement in the United States. One of the most successful and dedicated conservationists from Pennsylvania was Rachel Carson. Carson was born on a farm in Springdale, Pennsylvania. Her mother fostered her love of nature from an early age. She was also a gifted writer—a skill she would use during her career as a conservationist.

Carson pursued an education in the fields of biology and zoology. She began her career as a scientist and writer for the U.S. Bureau of Fisheries. Carson conducted research and wrote pamphlets about marine life in the United States. Her pamphlets were used to teach people about protecting wildlife in America’s lakes, rivers, bays, and other waterways.

In 1952, Carson left the U.S. Bureau of Fisheries to devote all her time to research and writing books. During the next three years, Carson published The Sea Around Us and The Edge of the Sea. These books were a comprehensive study of the ocean. They made Carson one of the leading authorities on the oceans of the world.

In the late 1950s, Carson shifted from ocean life to the harmful effects of chemicals on the environment. In her book Silent Spring, Carson showed the dangers of DDT, pesticides, and insecticides. They were used to kill insects on farms and insects that carried diseases. Carson wrote, “Man is a part of nature, and his war against nature is inevitably a war against himself.”

Carson called for an immediate stop to the use of pesticides and insecticides. She spoke with scientists, government officials, and chemical companies to advocate for change. Carson encouraged the U.S. Congress to take legal action to protect the natural world.

Rachel Carson died in 1964, but her work continued to have a profound impact. Carson’s research and her book Silent Spring encouraged lawmakers to ban the use of DDT nationwide in 1972. Her work also encouraged the creation of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in 1970. Her work continues to inspire environmentalists, scientists, and naturalists today.

title: Birds of Pennsylvania and Their Champions
text:
For thousands of years, Pennsylvania has been an important site for roosting birds. From the Piedmont region to the Allegheny Plateau, Pennsylvania is located along the migratory paths of many bird species.

Like the state’s other native animals, Pennsylvania’s bird population declined as the human population grew. Hunting, trapping, and habitat loss affected the turkey, bald eagle, grouse, peregrine falcon, and waterfowl populations.

Conservationists such as John James Audubon played a vital role in reviving the state’s bird population. Audubon was one of America’s first naturalists and ornithologists. An ornithologist is a scientist who studies birds. In 1803, Audubon moved to Mill Grove, a small farming community near Philadelphia. While living there, he began to study birds and conduct experiments. Through his experiments, Audubon determined that the Eastern Phoebe returned to the same place to nest each year.

Audubon drew and painted the birds he observed. In 1827, he published his highly detailed drawings and descriptions of birds he had observed throughout the United States. His book was called The Birds of America. The book included 435 life-sized watercolors of North American birds.

Many scientists and historians believe that Audubon’s book is one of the most important works on ornithology. His book helped people understand the natural world. Today, Audubon’s legacy lives on in the organization named after him. The National Audubon Society conducts research and educates people about birds and their natural habitats. It raises funds to preserve bird habitats around the world.

Charles Almanzo Babcock was another Pennsylvanian who championed the state’s bird population. Babcock served as the superintendent of schools for Oil City, in Venango County, Pennsylvania, during the late 1800s. Babcock wanted to share his love of birds with his students and his community. He wanted to teach people about the many types of birds that inhabit Pennsylvania’s forests, cities, and communities.

In 1894, Babcock started Bird Day, the first holiday in the United States dedicated to birds. Celebrations included researching and writing about birds, performing in plays, planting trees, and building bird houses. Babcock even published his own book in 1901 called Bird Day: How to Prepare for It. It included information about the many birds of Pennsylvania.

Pennsylvanians continue to serve as champions for hundreds of bird species that live in the state.

title: Air Quality
text:
In 1948, the city of Donora, Pennsylvania, experienced the worst case of air pollution in United States history. Located about 30 miles south of Pittsburgh, Donora was a center for steel and zinc manufacturing during the early 1900s. It was also a hub for the railroad. Thousands of tons of cargo moved through the community. The many factories and constant rail traffic polluted Donora’s air.

In late October 1948, cool fall air mixed with warm water vapor from the Monongahela River and smoke from the steel and zinc factories. It created a thick, yellow fog that covered Donora. It was so thick that, even during the middle of the day, people had to use lanterns to find their way through town. The fog lasted for five days. More than 7,000 people became sick and 20 people died.

Many Pennsylvanians and Americans called for change following the events in Donora. In 1950, President Harry Truman held the nation’s first national air pollution conference to discuss the events at Donora and how to prevent similar events in the future. Congress responded by passing the Air Pollution Control Act of 1955. It was the first federal law to limit air pollution. It provided funds to research air pollution.

There are many ways people can help make the air quality better in Pennsylvania. Ride sharing and driving less help keep chemicals out of the air. Using electric lawn equipment also cuts down on exhaust. Avoid burning waste or items that emit, or give off, harmful fumes.

title: Champions of Forestry
text:
Pennsylvanians have played a large role in forestry conservation, both in Pennsylvania and in the United States.

Dr. Joseph Rothrock is considered the founder of Pennsylvania forestry. Born on a farm in McVeytown, Pennsylvania, Rothrock had an appreciation for nature and the environment from a young age. Rothrock trained to be a doctor and practiced medicine before devoting his life to botany. Botany is the study of plants.

For the next 49 years, Rothrock was an important figure in botany. In 1886, he gave a speech about deforestation in Pennsylvania and his concern for the state’s natural wonders. His speech inspired prominent Pennsylvanians to form the Pennsylvania Forestry Association. Because of his passion and dedication to Pennsylvania’s forests, Rothrock was selected as the Association’s first president.

As president, Rothrock researched the state’s plants and educated Pennsylvanians about the importance of the state’s forests. Rothrock also served as the first Commissioner of Forestry for Pennsylvania from 1895 to 1901. He was a writer and editor for a forestry newsletter called Forest Leaves. Today, Rothrock is considered the “Father of Forestry in Pennsylvania.”

Gifford Pinchot is considered the “Father of American Conservation.” He founded the Yale School of Forestry at Yale University, served as the first chief of the United States Forest Service, helped establish more than 100 national forests, and created the Society of American Foresters. After working for the federal government for many years, Pinchot was appointed to the Pennsylvania Forest Commission in 1920 by Governor William Cameron Sproul. As commissioner of the Pennsylvania Forest Commission, Pinchot streamlined the commission’s procedures and hired trained foresters to oversee the state’s forest operations.

In 1922, Pinchot was elected as governor of Pennsylvania. While in office, he expanded Pennsylvania’s state parks and advocated for the protection of Pennsylvania’s forests. Throughout his life, Pinchot considered himself a forester first and a politician second. Numerous parks and forests are named after Pinchot, including Gifford Pinchot State Park in York County, Pennsylvania.

title: Water Quality
text:
Pollution has been an issue for Pennsylvania’s air quality. It has also been an issue for Pennsylvania’s water quality. In 1905, the first statewide policy to regulate water pollution was passed by Pennsylvania's state government. The Purity of Waters Act of 1905 limited the amount of sewage that could be dumped into Pennsylvania lakes, rivers, and other waterways. Unfortunately, pollution continued to contaminate Pennsylvania’s waterways. This caused a big decline in the fish population.

In 1909, the state legislature passed laws to protect Pennsylvania’s fish hatcheries. These laws made it illegal to dump any chemicals or waste considered harmful to fish into Pennsylvania waterways.

Today, there are many things Pennsylvanians can do to ensure better water quality in the state. People can contact lawmakers and attend public meetings to address concerns about poor water quality. People can also help clean up waterways by removing trash and work with organizations to test water quality.

title: Pennsylvania Game Commission
text:
Pennsylvania’s population grew quickly from colonial times through the 1800s. This quick growth had many positive impacts, but there were also many negative consequences. During the 1700s and 1800s, there were no government regulations that controlled hunting and trapping. Too much hunting and trapping depleted the population of indigenous animals. Widespread deforestation led to a loss of animal habitat. Lawmakers in Pennsylvania agreed that these things had to be stopped.

In 1895, Governor Daniel H. Hastings established the Pennsylvania Game Commission. The purpose of the Commission was to protect and conserve Pennsylvania’s wildlife, or game. The first initiative of the Commission was to increase the white-tailed deer, bear, elk, and beaver populations. In 1900, many native animals, including turkey, osprey, bald eagle, and peregrine falcon, were close to extinction.

From 1906 through the 1920s, the Pennsylvania Game Commission purchased deer from breeders in neighboring states. Laws were put in place to regulate deer hunting. As a result, the deer population of Pennsylvania grew steadily throughout the 1900s and continues to grow today.

In 1905, Pennsylvania was the first state to pass legislation that protected its bear population. By 2022, the bear population had increased to around 18,000. The game commission has also been successful at reintroducing beavers, river otters, elk, bald eagles, ospreys, and peregrine falcons into the state.

Today, the Pennsylvania Game Commission estimates that the population of deer, bear, and turkey are at their highest since colonial times. They also estimate that the elk population is higher than it has been in the past 150 years.

For more than 100 years, the Pennsylvania Game Commission has been instrumental in monitoring wildlife populations, establishing regulations and laws, and educating the public on wildlife conservation.

title: Conservation Today
text:
Pennsylvanians continue to champion conservation today. Many organizations play a vital role in these efforts. WeConservePA is one of them. Its goal is to help Pennsylvanians conserve land, protect waterways, use environmentally safe practices, and enjoy the natural wonders of the state. Another organization is the Natural Resources Conservation Service. It supports programs that protect watersheds, prevent flooding, restore the natural habitats of Lake Erie, and innovate farming practices.

Everyday Pennsylvanians can help conserve the state’s natural resources and environment. You can clean up litter, plant trees, and grow your own vegetables. You can also conserve water and electricity, use reusable water bottles, and buy locally grown food. About 70 percent of the garbage we throw away could be recycled. The best way to keep our landfills and garbage dumps from taking over the environment is to recycle as many items as possible.

With the help of conservationists, birds have learned to adapt to changing environments. Many of Pennsylvania’s major cities protect nesting birds. In fact, some birds only construct their nests in cities. The rare yellow-crowned night herons build their nests in one place: high above the city of Harrisburg. Conservationists, city officials, and the Pennsylvania Game Commission work together to protect these rare nesting birds.

Article I, Section 27 of Pennsylvania’s Constitution states:
The people have a right to clean air, pure water, and to the preservation of the natural, scenic, historic and esthetic values of the environment. Pennsylvania’s public natural resources are the common property of all the people, including generations yet to come. As trustee of these resources, the Commonwealth shall conserve and maintain them for the benefit of all the people.

Many Pennsylvanians work diligently to uphold this article of the constitution and protect the natural resources of Pennsylvania.

title: Pennsylvania’s First Hospitals
text:
Pennsylvania has been an important part of medical history for hundreds of years. It all started when Benjamin Franklin and Dr. Thomas Bond established Pennsylvania Hospital in 1751. Soon, other hospitals started in the surrounding neighborhoods.

Before there were hospitals, people who were sick were cared for at home. There were few doctors who had graduated from medical school. Most people who cared for the sick were family members. They learned from one another how to use herbs and natural ingredients to treat illnesses. Native Americans used herbal and natural remedies for thousands of years. European settlers learned from them and passed the knowledge onto others.

When many people live together in small spaces, the conditions create environments where germs grow. As populations in cities grew, there were not many large spaces for people to live. In Pennsylvania, many people lived in small spaces without the proper resources. Caring for the sick wasn’t easy. The hospital that Franklin and Bond started was a solution to these conditions. People in hospitals began to recover and go back home.

In 1762, William Shippen Jr. began giving medical lectures in Philadelphia. These lectures were the beginnings of the University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine. Founded in 1765, it was the first medical program in the nation. Soon, many other medical schools opened, including Jefferson Medical College in 1824. Educated doctors began treating patients, which increased recovery and wellness in Pennsylvania and across the country.

Pennsylvania made history again when the Female Medical College of Pennsylvania opened in 1850. It was the first school in the world to train women for medical degrees. One of the school’s first graduates was Ann Preston. In 1861, she opened the Woman’s Hospital of Philadelphia.

During this time, Philadelphia was the nation’s leading publisher of medical books. The most important medical journal at the time was the American Journal of Medical Sciences. It was edited and published in Philadelphia.

In 1895, University of Pennsylvania graduate Nathan Francis Mossell established the Frederick Douglass Memorial Hospital and Training School in Philadelphia. It was the second medical school in the United States for African Americans. Thousands of doctors were trained at the Frederick Douglass Memorial Hospital and Training School. Thousands of patients were helped because of this hospital and training programs.

Learning about diseases and receiving proper training allowed doctors to help their communities. Fear of sickness decreased. Doctors and hospitals improved the health, care, and welfare of everyone.

title: Keeping Children Safe
text:
As industry grew in Pennsylvania, new cleaning solutions were necessary to clean work clothes, automobiles, and businesses. These solutions were powerful chemicals that would clean dirt and grease quickly. However, the products were toxic and poisonous if swallowed. The cleaners were easy to open and provided no warning about the dangers. Unaware of the dangers, children could accidently harm themselves by swallowing the solutions.

Dr. Richard Moriarty, director of the Pittsburgh Poison Center in 1970, started a poison information hotline that parents could call at any time of day. He hired full-time nurses to answer the calls. Moriarty also started using a new technology, called the telecopier, to send information about different kinds of poisons to other hospitals when they needed it. The telecopier was an early version of a fax machine. It could send information through telephone lines that could be printed by the telecopier on the other end of the line.

Moriarty also helped to develop Mr. Yuk™. In 1971, bottles with poisonous contents were marked with a skull and crossbones symbol. The symbol of the Pittsburgh Pirates baseball team looked similar to the poison symbol. The skull and crossbones symbol was also used in other packaging that wasn’t poisonous. Doctors and state officials needed to find a new symbol to mark containers with harmful chemicals.

Moriarty hired a marketing company to find out what symbol would be better to use to warn people of harmful chemicals in products. The marketing researchers showed children lots of different symbols and colors. They did this to see which colors and symbols the children liked the least. The children were repelled by a face with its eyes squinched up and its tongue sticking out. No one liked the color neon green. A contest was held for school children to come up with the final design. Fourth grader Wendy Brown of West Virginia was the winner and gave the new symbol the name “Mr. Yuk.” Within months, Mr. Yuk™ started changing lives.

The Pittsburgh Poison Center printed millions of Mr. Yuk™ stickers. The organization mailed the stickers to parents so they could put them on bottles with dangerous contents. They even produced a television commercial about Mr. Yuk™ that aired during the Super Bowl™. By the end of the 1970s, the Pittsburgh Poison Center had sent out about 400 million stickers!

The Mr. Yuk™ program influenced more child safety protections from manufacturers. Today, child protection packaging is in place on any potentially dangerous product, thanks in large part to Mr. Yuk™ and Moriarty.

title: Emergency Responders
text:
Sometimes, accidents and injuries happen. When a serious accident or injury occurs, one of the first things that someone can do is call 911 for emergency medical services. An emergency medical responder (EMR) is called to the scene to help. The trained responders are part of the system designed to keep people safe. They are part of government services or voluntary community services. This is one way that the government uses money from taxes to provide services. First responders include firefighters, police officers, lifeguards, and ambulance workers.

Emergency Medical Responder (EMR): An EMR is someone trained to help an injured or ill person until an ambulance can arrive. They can control bleeding, perform CPR, and use an automated external defibrillator, which can help start a person’s heart again. It takes about 50 hours of training to become an EMR.

Emergency Medical Technician (EMT): An EMT works in an ambulance. EMTs can treat burns, splint broken bones, help with childbirth, administer medication, and transport a person to a hospital. It takes about 200 hours of training to become an EMT.

Advanced Emergency Medical Technician (AEMT): An advanced emergency medical technician can give life-saving treatments to patients needing an ambulance. An AEMT requires additional education and 134 practice hours to gain certification.

Paramedic: A paramedic is the most skilled of the different levels of emergency responders. They can use all the equipment in an ambulance and provide advanced life support care. It takes 1,200 hours of training to become a paramedic.

Today, there are about 37,000 volunteer emergency responders in Pennsylvania. More than 90 percent of fire departments are staffed with volunteers. Being a volunteer means they do not receive payment for their work. No matter where you are, if an emergency occurs, a trained professional will be there to help you. If you ever meet a volunteer emergency responder, make sure to thank them for their service.

title: James Durham
text:
For many years after the Revolutionary War, the best doctor for treating diphtheria was James Durham. He was the first African American to formally practice medicine in the United States.

In 1762, Durham was born enslaved in Philadelphia. However, he was encouraged, along with the other enslaved people in the household, to learn to read and write. This was very unusual for the time. In some states, it was illegal for enslaved people to learn to read and write.

When he was eight, Durham was enslaved by a doctor named John Kearsley Jr. Kearsley made Durham his apprentice in medicine. Kearsley taught Durham how to make medicine and take care of patients.

By this time, the British Army had captured Philadelphia and the surrounding region. The British captured many enslaved people in Philadelphia, including Durham. Durham was enslaved by a surgeon in the British Army. The surgeon was assigned to a station in Florida and took Durham with him. On the battlefield in Pensacola, Florida, Durham learned how to bind wounds and perform surgeries on wounded soldiers. When the British lost the war, Florida was given back to Spain. Spanish forces took Durham to New Orleans.

There, Durham was enslaved by a physician named Robert Dow. They worked together, treating diseases that were typical in a large city. The diseases were caused by poor sanitation and unclean water. Durham purchased his freedom from Dow and started his own medical practice, where he specialized in throat medicine. He treated people of many racial backgrounds.

Dr. Benjamin Rush, the most famous and successful doctor in the United States at the time, showed an interest in Durham’s work. Rush encouraged Durham to return to Philadelphia and work with him. Rush was very impressed with Durham’s medical knowledge. “I expected to have suggested some new medicines to him; but he suggested many more to me,” Rush wrote.

At this time, there were many laws preventing formerly enslaved people from participating in business. Because he did not have a medical degree, Durham was not allowed to practice medicine in Pennsylvania. Durham disappears from history after 1801. There are no records of his whereabouts or his life after this, but his work helped thousands of people.

title: Transplants and Medicine
text:
There can be times when a person's body needs replacement parts. Knee and hip replacements have helped many people with injuries lead a life of mobility, or movement. Not only can bones be replaced, but organs can also be replaced, or transplanted. Organs, such as a heart, kidney, and lungs, can be transplanted surgically to help patients who need them. Organ transplants were perfected at Pittsburgh’s Thomas E. Starzl Transplantation Institute. Established in 1985, the Starzl Transplantation Institute became one of the world's leading medical facilities for transplant surgery. The transplant team did amazing medical work that gave many people longer lives.

One of the first patients in Pittsburgh to receive an organ transplant was six-year-old Stormie Jones. On Feb. 14, 1984, Jones received a new heart and liver. Her own heart and liver did not work properly because of disease. Jones recovered as a result of this medical first. This encouraged the medical community to continue to develop new methods to help others.

Modern hospitals also focus on biochemistry to go with surgery. Having the right medicine to take after an operation is important. In 1943, Raymond Rettew mass-produced penicillin in his lab in West Chester, Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania continues to produce medicine that helps millions of people each year.
