title: Preventing Polio
text:
You’ve probably never heard of polio. Polio is a disease that causes damage to the nervous system and paralysis. Paralysis is the loss of movement in the body. Polio has affected people for thousands of years. Archaeologists and scientists have found evidence of polio in mummies from ancient Egypt. Even though it is an ancient and deadly disease, polio has almost completely disappeared from the United States.

During the 1920s, President Franklin D. Roosevelt contracted polio as an adult. He needed help walking and moving his legs. Roosevelt was one of the millions of people who suffered from polio during this time. Scientists knew that a change needed to be made to help the people suffering from polio.

During the 1950s, scientists began to research the causes of polio. They began working on a polio vaccine, or a way to prevent the disease, and help people with polio. In Pittsburgh, William Hammon and his team developed a way to decrease the effect of polio on a person. However, a person already needed to have polio to receive this vaccine.

While Hammon and his team worked on a cure for polio. Dr. Jonas Salk, the director of the Virus Research Laboratory at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, began to conduct his own research on polio. Salk and his team hoped to develop a way to prevent the disease altogether. Salk conducted several experiments to create a vaccine to prevent polio. After several attempts, Salk’s vaccine proved to be successful and killed the polio virus.

In 1954, there were 38,000 cases of polio in the United States. In 1955, millions of children in the United States received Salk’s polio vaccine. In 1960, the number of polio cases dropped to 2,500. By 1965, the cases had dropped to 61. Since then, many other scientists have worked to advance polio vaccines and research even further. Pennsylvania was once again a keystone in the medical community as the birthplace of the polio vaccine.

title: How Can I Respect Others?
text: When you respect someone, you are thoughtful about your words and actions. You show them that you care about their health, well-being, and feelings. You are also sensitive to their beliefs, rights, and traditions. Respect means being polite and kind, even if your beliefs and traditions are different. Respect builds with trust and understanding.

title: Diversity Makes Life Fun!
text: The world would be a very boring place without diversity. Diversity means that people are different from each other. All around you, there are people who look, speak, move, and think differently than you do. They have different abilities, talents, beliefs, and values. Get to know them! Ask kind, respectful questions. You may even make a new friend!

title: Find What You Have in Common
text:
It is good that everyone is different. But did you know that you also have similarities with everyone around you? Similarities are things you have in common with other people, or things that are the same between you and someone else.

Here are some similarities you could look for in the people around you.

Physical features (eye color, hair color, etc.)

Favorite activities

Interests

Even if someone seems very different from you, you can spend time getting to know them and find things you have in common.

title: Essential Question
text: How has the health and welfare of the people in Pennsylvania contributed to medical knowledge over time?

title: Facing Hurtful Words and Actions
text:
If someone says something hurtful to you or acts in a disrespectful way, you might feel unsafe. You might feel like your well-being is not important to others. Some words and actions treat people unfairly. Bullying is repeated, unwanted behavior targeting another person. Discrimination is showing an unfair judgment between categories of people. Each of these types of behavior can be harmful.

When you experience or witness bullying or discrimination, try to communicate assertively and respectfully. Explain that the person’s words or actions hurt your feelings. Try to work through any misunderstandings. If the situation doesn’t change, talk to a trusted adult. Adults can help you work through your feelings, worries, and fears.

title: Tribes of the Northeast
text:
Native Peoples of the Northeast, or Eastern Woodlands, lived in a land rich in fresh water, including the Great Lakes. The land was also good for farming and had many types of trees and other plants.

Many tribes lived in the Eastern Woodlands. These included the Iroquois, Algonquin, Penobscot, Chippewa, Odawa, and Powhatan. They grew corn, beans, and squash. The tribes used all the natural resources around them to meet their basic needs. They used birch bark to build canoes and to cover their homes. They burned wood to stay warm and cook. They used tools for work and as weapons. The animals they hunted fed the people. The hides, or skins, were used to make clothes, containers, and bags. Everything was used, and nothing was wasted.

Eastern Woodland tribes lived in larger villages in the summer and smaller family groups in the winter. The houses were different from tribe to tribe. Some tribes lived in wigwams, which are small, dome-shaped homes. The Chippewa lived in wigwams. Tribes lived in wigwams when they moved to hunt, fish, and gather natural resources. Other tribes lived in larger, more permanent longhouses. The Iroquois lived in longhouses. Many people could live in a longhouse. The homes fit the lifestyles of each community.

title: Tribes of the West
text:
Many tribes lived in the West. The West includes parts of Nevada, Idaho, Oregon, Utah, California, Colorado, Montana, and Wyoming. This area is very diverse, with mountains, rivers, coasts, and deserts.

Tribes relied on the region's abundant resources to establish a way of life. Many western tribes gathered, hunted, and fished for food. Coastal areas and the rivers of the Great Basin provided many fishing opportunities for native peoples. Tribes hunted large animals, such as bison, deer, and elk. They also gathered wild berries and nuts for food.

Many tribes followed large herds of animals and moved throughout the region. They lived in easy-to-move lodge homes, such as tepees or wickiups. A wickiup consisted of a wooden frame covered with woven leaves and brush. Some tribes lived along the Pacific coast.

Tribes of the Western region engaged in trade with one another. The tribes of the Great Basin traded shells, animal hides, furs, clothing, and baskets for other items. They used resources found in their environment for clothing. They traditionally wore furs in colder climates and seasons. In warmer areas and warmer parts of the year, they wore clothing made from bark, grasses, and animal skins.

Like other tribes, tribes of the West have a deep connection with their environment. Sacred sites that are important to the beliefs of the tribes, like mountains, sequoia trees, and rivers, are given special respect.

title: I Can Communicate
text:
Communication is the sharing of information. It takes at least one person sending information and one or more people receiving information. There are things you can think about when you communicate with others:

How are you going to communicate? Is it better to talk to the person face to face or write a text?

How do you feel when you communicate? Are you upset about something? Will you say something unkind or hurtful that you don't really mean?

Should you communicate differently at school than on the football field? Yelling at a friend might be okay if he is in danger, but what about if he is trying to help you? Talking to your teacher is different than texting a friend.

title: Talking with Words
text:
Did you know that sign language is a form of verbal communication? The speaker uses sign language to deliver words to the listener. Verbal communication is using your voice. You are able to share your ideas or information with someone else. Have you ever had to repeat yourself because someone couldn’t understand you?

Tips to communicate clearly:

Don't speak or sign too quickly.

Consider who you are speaking to.

Choose your words carefully.

title: Talking Through Actions
text: What does your smile tell people? What do your eyebrows or elbows communicate? You can communicate without using words. Nonverbal communication is what you communicate to others without the use of words. Your eyes, arms, hands, and body language can all communicate to others about how you are feeling and what you are thinking.

title: Who Are Scientists and Engineers?
text:
Science is the search for knowledge. Knowledge is used to solve problems by using science and engineering practices. When you take part in science, you understand this way of thinking and learning about the world. During science investigations, you gather evidence and look for patterns.

People who study science are called scientists. Scientists explore the world through their investigations. They are curious about the world around them. Scientists are inquisitive and want to learn more. Scientists observe and record their findings. As scientists explore, they answer their own questions. The answers to those questions might lead to new questions and answers.

There are many types of scientists. Different types of scientists have different disciplines. A plant scientist is called a botanist. They understand the properties of plants, how plants function, and the habitats of plants. A scientist who studies motion and forces is called a physicist. Physicists learn what matter is and why it behaves the way it does. They use special equipment to study how they can improve manufacturing processes or products.

Engineering is applying science to solve problems. You use what you have learned and what skills you have gained in science to help solve problems. Engineers create and build products for practical use. There are different types of engineers. Many branches of engineering overlap. Aerospace engineers create vehicles, aircraft, and rockets that go into space. They work closely with electrical engineers to develop guidance, navigation, and power systems. Aerospace engineers also work with civil engineers to plan airports and other public facilities. Biomedical engineers create devices to help solve medical problems. They work with chemical engineers to ensure they use the correct chemicals. Doctors and nurses use biomedical devices to help people.

You are a scientist and an engineer. Like scientists, you make observations during your investigations. You ask questions and seek answers. You see the world around you and wonder about it. Like engineers, you see problems that need solutions. You can design tools and methods to solve those problems. Scientists and engineers are not just people in lab coats. They are people like you who are curious about the world around them. They make tools and materials that make life better for everyone.

title: Talking Through Writing
text: Notes, texts, and emails are all forms of written communication. Writing is an important skill to master. You will write throughout your entire life. You will write letters, emails, and texts. Even signs, billboards, and emojis are written communication. Be clear and direct in written communication. It helps others understand you.

title: Talking Through Images
text: Visual communication means sharing information through images. Images help you get information quickly without using a lot of words. Our computers, TVs, and cell phones all use visual communication. When you communicate with images, be very careful with the images you choose. Be sure to choose images that reflect your character. Whatever you share online can be shared many times.

title: Communicating with Respect
text:
It is always important to be respectful. Choose words and body language that will communicate your ideas respectfully. It is helpful to know that every culture has different ways of communicating. What is respectful in one culture may not be respectful in another. Have a conversation with your friends. Ask them how you can show them respect. Work to understand each other and celebrate those conversations.

Choose one of these respectful words to create your own word art:

KIND

LISTEN

CARE

GRATITUDE

POLITE

SERVE

SHARE

GIVE

HELP

PATIENT

title: Entrepreneurs
text:
An entrepreneur is one person who takes on the financial risk of creating or running their own business. They are inventive or imaginative people. They have a vision about something new they can offer their community. Entrepreneurs begin with an idea for a business. It takes courage to start a new business and invest money for an idea you believe in.

Half of all new businesses fail within the first five years. Entrepreneurs must be knowledgeable about their goods and services to succeed. They have to come up with a great idea and use all their resources wisely. They have to work very hard to be successful. Can you think of any entrepreneurs in your community or from your state’s history?

title: Cocoa
text:
Do you like chocolate? Recent evidence suggests that Mesoamericans were consuming chocolate as far back as 1400 B.C.E. Cocoa beans were a very valuable gift, and people even used the beans as money. The Maya people called the beans xocoatl. The Aztec loved cocoa beans but were unable to grow the beans themselves. So, xocoatl became an important trading item for the Maya.

Eventually, the Aztec used the paste from the roasted cocoa beans and added vanilla, cinnamon and chili pepper to make a cold drink (called xocoatl or chocolatl) that only the wealthy could afford. They also added crushed flower petals and achiote seeds to make the drink red like blood. Aztec Emperor Moctezuma (1480- 1520 C.E.) really liked his xocoatl.

Many people think Moctezuma drank more than 50 cups a day. Hernán Cortés took the beans and the xocoatl recipe back to Spain in 1519. Wealthy people in Spain began to sip the new concoction, but only in secret. Cocoa beans were scarce, and they didn’t want to share the drink with others. It took about 100 years for cocoa beans to reach other countries in Europe.

Europeans began serving the beverage hot, sweetened and without the chili pepper. It continued to be something for the very wealthy. By 1657, the drink was served in London “chocolate houses.” People said the chocolate had medicinal purposes, especially for stomach distress. It was not until 1847 that someone discovered another great use for chocolate - chocolate bars.

title: Phenomenon Comic
text: It is warmer and brighter during the day than at night.

title: You Can Be Confident When You Ask For Help
text: Confidence means believing in yourself. You can be confident when you ask others for help. You might think that asking for help shows that you do not have confidence in yourself to do something, but that is not true. Asking for help shows that you are confident that you can accomplish anything with the right support. When you ask for help, you do not need to be embarrassed or quiet. You can confidently ask your parents, teachers, or friends for the help you need to be successful.

title: You Can Be Brave When You Ask For Help
text:
Asking for help shows that a person is brave. Asking for help is a smart thing to do. When you receive help, you get access to resources. These resources help you solve the problems you face.

Some problems we face are small and can be solved easily. Some problems are really big and take lots of resources to solve. Fear can stop you from learning and growing, especially if you know you need help but are afraid to ask. Learning to ask for help can help you become more confident.

title: Helping Others
text: When other people ask you for help, how should you respond? As you think about your response, you should consider: Is your response something that you would want to hear when you need help? Is your response helpful? What resources do you have to help? Do you know how to help? Do you have skills and abilities that will help? What time limitations do you have? What other responsibilities do you need to fulfill? Your responses can vary. Don't be afraid to tell someone that you don't know how to help or that you don't have the answer either. Helping others shows them that you care about them. Sometimes the best way to help someone is to direct them to another person who can help. Helping others builds your empathy muscles and your well-being by opening your mind to what others are going through.

title: Akramah Writes
text:
Scientists and engineers want people to believe the answers they find. They use the data they collect to back up their explanations. They also use the models they create.

The explanations that scientists and engineers share are very helpful. It makes other people learn more about their questions. Scientists and engineers write, draw, or build a model to share their explanations. They can share their explanations out loud as well. Scientists and engineers may share their explanations alone or in groups. It is important that people pay attention to what scientists and engineers have to share. They ask questions about the world around them. They carry out investigations. They then create models to explain what they learned. We all have a chance to learn a little more when they do that.

text: How did resources from Pennsylvania support World War 2?

title: Essential Question
text: How do human resources increase the need for entrepreneurship?

title: Family-Run Businesses
text:
One of the oldest versions of business organization and entrepreneurship comes from a family business model. A family business is a type of business where two or more family members are part of the ownership and operations of the business. In rural areas, a farm is considered a family business. Farms are one of the oldest forms of a family run business. Urban areas allow for shop owners to be part of the family business model.

There are many advantages to a family owned business in a community. Stability and commitment are two of the biggest advantages of a family owned business. Having a family that continues to pass on the family business to other family members shows long term planning and stability. This means the leadership of the business does not change. The main focus for the family is the business. This shows that they have a strong commitment in keeping the business running, even during tough economic times.

There are a few disadvantages to a family run business. There could be a lack of structure in how the family business will be run. Having a process for how money is managed, schedules are made, and how products will be distributed can be difficult to manage. A process needs to be put in place to manage all of these aspects of a business.

Family interest and finding someone to take over after generations plays another key role in the challenges of owning a family business. Owning a family business can cause stress for members of the family that may not want to be a part of it. Finding a member of the family that has the same goal and will want to continue running increases that challenge.

There are two current trends for family business ownership in many countries.

Current family owners will be changing owners soon and moving to another member of the family.

More women are becoming owners of family businesses.

Family businesses are still a part of the economic community in many areas throughout the Western Hemisphere and the world.

title: Elizabeth Arden
text:
Elizabeth Arden was born in 1884 in Ontario, Canada. During her early years, she worked many different jobs to help support her family. In 1908, Arden moved to New York City. She started her career in beauty as a helper for a beautician. Two years later, she opened her own beauty salon on Fifth Avenue, one of the busiest streets in New York City, with her partner Elizabeth Hubbard.

In 1924, Arden ended her partnership with Elizabeth Hubbard and created her own beauty salon. She named her new salon Red Door and worked to expand her business under this new name. Arden worked to become an advocate for women’s beauty. She worked hard to make beauty products marketable and available to everyone.

Arden formulated, manufactured, and sold her own makeup products. She learned new techniques and practices. She studied under the top makeup manufacturers in France. By 1922, Arden opened up her first beauty shop in France, making her products available in Europe. She then worked to expand her brand and businesses across Europe, South America, and Australia.

Much of Arden’s businesses and marketing focused on teaching women how to use and apply her makeup. She did this in her beauty shops and marketing campaigns. She evolved the use of different concepts on producing the formulas for makeup. She created color coordinating paletes for the eyes, lips, and facial makeup. Women across the world from all avenues of life used Arden’s makeup. Today, Elizabeth Arden is still a thriving company that brings in over $1,000,000,000 a year. Arden was instrumental in the development and growth of her company at a time when women were not accepted members of the business world.

title: Olive Ann Beech
text:
Olive Ann Beech was born in Waverly, Kansas in 1903. Her father was a building contractor and her mother worked on the family farm. Starting at an early age, her parents taught her how to run a business and about finances. Beech opened her own bank account when she was seven. By age 11, she helped her family open another business, selling hamburgers at a small stand.

In 1917, Beech began attending business classes at the American Secretarial and Business College in Wichita, Kansas. She took a job as a bookkeeper and office manager at the Staley Electrical Company, but she didn’t stop there. Beech took a job as the bookkeeper and secretary of the newly formed Travel Air, created by Lloyd Stearman, Walter Beech, and Clyde Cessna.

Beech used her financial knowledge to help the business grow. She became the office manager and a larger presence in the running of the company. Olive Ann married Walter Beech and they started their own aircraft business called Beech Aircraft Company. Beech Aircraft Company created planes for the military during World War II. Beech ran the company during this time. Even with the war coming to a close, she figured out how to keep the company moving forward. The Beeches decided to create more products, including civilian aircrafts and missile targets for the military.

After eighteen years of leading the company as the president and chief executive officer, Beech retired. She left a lasting legacy of success, awards, and honors. Beech was the first woman inducted into the National Aeronautic Association for her achievements. Many magazines, including The New York Times and Forbes, praised her for being a distinguished woman and executive in an American corporation.

title: Douglas Tompkins
text:
Douglas Tompkins was born in Ohio in 1943 but grew up in New York. Tompkins left school before graduating high school to pursue his love of nature and adventure. He traveled across the United States, South America, and Europe to chase his love of rock climbing and skiing. While in Chile, Tompkins decided to hone his skills of rock climbing and skiing. This was the start of his first business.

In 1963, Tompkins started the California Mountaineering Guide Service, but he didn’t stop there. The following year, Tompkins took out a loan from the bank to create a mail order business for camping, skiing, and rock climbing gear. He named his new company North Face. The company was successful and he then opened up the first storefront in San Francisco in 1966. Tompkins created new products for outdoor lovers, including the dome tent.

Tompkins wanted to continue traveling the world, so he sold his company in 1968. He traveled to Patagonia, where he achieved many accomplishments in hiking, skiing, and rock climbing. Tompkins and his team documented and filmed their expedition to Mount Fitz Roy. Their film won a prestigious award at a film festival in Italy.

After his time in South America, Tompkins and his wife created a clothing business called Esprit. Tompkins and his wife started Esprit in the back of a station wagon. Within a decade, Esprit grew to a multiple million dollar business.

Tompkins shifted his attention from business to environmental conservation. He bought land throughout South America and created parks and nature preserves. These areas were home to many endangered species. This allowed for the reintroduction of other endangered animals, including jaguars and giant anteaters. Tompkins worked tirelessly to preserve nature. He took a hands-on approach to ensure that areas could be conserved and returned to their natural habitat.

title: Olive Oil Industry
text:
In recent years, Brazil has become a leader in a new industry that is not common in South America: the olive oil industry. Brazil’s olive oil producers have achieved an 86% success rate on the international awards level for olive oil production, but this was not an easy task. This success took a lot of research, planning, and resources.

Physical Environment

Olive oil producers in Brazil first had to focus on the physical environment and choose areas where they wanted to grow olive trees. They chose a region in southern Brazil called Rio Grande do Sul. It is located in Campanha Gaúcha. This area is known for its hilly landscape and mild climate, with average temperatures between 44 to 82 degrees.

One of Brazil’s leading producers of olive oil, Azeite Batalha, chose this region to plant, grow, and harvest olives to produce olive oil. They are currently growing close to 1,235 acres of olive trees in this area.

Harvesting

Harvesting olives is a very delicate process. Olives need to be harvested when they are still green. This stage in the growing process is called “veraison.” This is when the olives are transitioning from green to purple. Producers pick olives during this stage to make extra virgin olive oil.

Picking the olives can be done in a variety of ways: either by hand or by machines. Machines called shakers or over-the-row harvesters are used to pick olives. Harvesting can also be done by hand. Workers pick the olives using rakes and tools that shake the olive tree. The olives then drop into a net.

It is crucial that as soon as the olives are harvested, they are taken directly to the mill for processing. If a delay occurs, this can cause a lower quality olive oil because the olives are not as fresh.

Processing of Olives to Olive Oil

Once the olives are at the mill, they need to be cleaned and washed. Olives need to have their leaves, twigs, and stems removed. All pesticides and dirt are also washed off at this time. Because the olive oil industry is new to Brazil, olive oil companies had to import equipment from other countries, including Italy. These machines are used at all stages of olive oil production. They are used to remove leaves and wash and crush the olives.

Once the olives are washed and crushed, the next step is to extract the oil. There are several steps to this process:

Machines grind the olives into a thick paste.

The olive paste is kneaded, or squeezed and mixed, to activate the chemicals that make it taste and smell good. The past is kneaded until microdroplets of oil appear.

The last step of taking the oil out of the paste is called centrifugation. This is when olive oil is separated from any other solids or water that could still be in the paste.

After the olive oil is processed, it needs to be filtered. This can be done through filtration or a racking system. This means the oil will sit in stainless steel drums until all the debris from the oil falls to the bottom. Then, the debris is removed. After processing, the olive oil has to be put through a variety of tests to ensure the quality meets certain standards. A chemical analysis, authenticity or purity test, and a sensory analysis are conducted. The olive oil must pass these tests before it is bottled.

Bottling and Exporting of Olive Oil

Once the olive oil has been filtered and passes the necessary tests, the next step is bottling. The olive oil is bottled and sent to markets throughout South America and the world. Prosperato, one of Brazil’s largest olive oil producers, was the country’s first exporter of olive oil. They ship most of their extra virgin olive oil to the United States. More companies are buying olive oil from Brazil because the tariffs are lower than olive oil from Italy.

The olive oil industry continues to grow and increase production throughout Brazil. Many companies in Brazil’s olive oil industry are family run operations. Many of the businesses are being passed down through families. This allows for the growing of olive trees and olive oil production to continue throughout the region.

title: Avocado Industry
text:
Mexico’s physical environment makes it an ideal location for avocado production. One of the best locations in Mexico for avocado production is Michoacán. Avocados grow year round in Mexico. This is due to a variety of reasons. Volcanic minerals make the soil rich in nutrients. Natural irrigation networks or sources of water make it easy to keep crops hydrated. Avocados need to be grown in a mild climate. Mexico’s climate is the perfect climate for growing avocados.

Avocado trees grow in orchards. An orchard is a large area planted with fruit trees. It takes about 6 months for avocados to mature. Once they have matured, avocados are harvested by hand. Workers use ladders to climb into the tree. They remove the fruit using a pole. The pole has a blade and a catching bag. If the avocado touches the ground, it can be damaged. A professional picker can harvest almost 3,500 avocados a day. The catching bag is then dumped into a crate and transported on trucks to the sorting and packaging center.

Once the avocados reach the sorting center, workers cut up the fruit to ensure they are ready for the next steps. The avocados must also pass a taste test. If they pass the taste test, the avocados are washed and brushed until the natural wax in the skin of the fruit is showing. The fruit is put on a conveyor belt. It moves at an incredible speed of 25 avocados per second. Cameras on the machine analyze and process the avocados as they move along the conveyor belt. The sorted fruit is then put in containers to be transported to market.

Large trucks take the avocados to a distribution center. Here, the avocado containers are placed in shipping containers to go to airports, seaports, or trucking centers. The shipping containers are then transported to cities and towns around the world. The cost of shipping increases the further away the avocados are shipped. Sometimes refrigeration is needed to keep the fruit from spoiling. This increases the cost of shipping. At the final destination, the shipping containers are unpacked. The avocados are then transported to markets for consumers to purchase. All costs associated with picking, packing, transporting, and delivery are considered in determining the price.

Another key piece to avocado production is food safety. The Avocado Producers and Exporting Packers Association of Mexico (APEAM) was created to help create and set food safety and quality standards. They work to keep up high standards of sanitation in avocado orchards and processing plants. They also work with national and international organizations to make sure products are safe for people.

Create a flow chart showing the production of avocados from tree to table. Be sure to identify the human and capital resources that make avocado production possible.

title: Young Entrepreneurs
text:
You don’t have to be an adult to start a business. People as young as five years old have become entrepreneurs by starting their own businesses. Some businesses have grown and become successful.

Take child entrepreneur Hannah Grace. Grace was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes when she was just a baby. At the age of 10, she started making her own health and beauty products to sell. She created a business called Hannah Grace BeYOUtiful and donates 20 percent of every purchase to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Fund.

Maya Penn founded her business, Maya’s Ideas, when she was just eight years old. Today, Penn is 19 and CEO of her own company, which sells fashion accessories that are environmentally sustainable. Not only does she run her own business, but Penn also donates 10 percent of her profits to charities and to help the environment.

When he was nine years old, Moziah Bridges wanted an eye-catching fashion accessory. Because of this, he got the idea to create Mo’s Bows. Bridges’s company sells all kinds of things, including bow ties, pocket squares, and other apparel. Today, despite his company’s international success, Bridges intends to graduate high school and continue his education by going to college to study fashion design.

Nohbo Drops were created by Benjamin Stern. Stern came up with the idea while he was sitting in his ninth grade biology class. Nohbo Drops are packets for shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and shaving cream that dissolve in water. They don’t contain chemicals that harm the environment, and they help to eliminate plastic waste.

These young people didn’t find success overnight. Their businesses started with an idea. They worked and improved their ideas until they were able to create businesses out of them. Hannah Grace had to try over and over to find a successful recipe for her bath bombs and beauty products. Moziah Bridges started out with an eye-catching bowtie and worked to design and create other accessories. Entrepreneurs work hard, often for years, before their businesses take off. Some businesses don’t make it, but with a good idea, hard work, and dedication, anything is possible.

title: Public Issues
text:
Citizens play an important role in a democracy. Abraham Lincoln once stated that a democratic government is a government “of the people, by the people, and for the people.” This means that people are in charge of their own governance. People control the government by voting in elections. They vote on issues. They express their opinions in writing and discussions. People make decisions and influence the decisions made by those they elect into office. To make good decisions, they need to understand the issues.

Public issues are complex. Before you can address an issue, you have to understand its causes. Most issues have more than one root cause and don’t have easy solutions. Many issues are also interconnected. An action that solves one problem may cause another.

There are many ways to learn about public issues. Many people keep up with public issues by watching the news on television. Others read the newspaper or internet news journals. This can be a good way to get a broad view of the many issues that people in your community, state, or the country face.

However, fully understanding an issue requires additional research. This means gathering accurate information from several sources. Some sources are more valid than others. People who write about issues likely have opinions about them. What they write may be biased, or based on someone’s personal point of view. It may even be inaccurate. There is more than one side to every issue.

Good citizens consider different points of view. They carefully weigh the evidence. Then, they use that evidence to make up their own minds. Looking at several sources can help you make your own decisions and understand both sides of an issue.

People in government and elected officials work to understand public issues. There are also organizations that help research and solve public issues. Finding solutions requires research. Take public health as an example. Doctors may see many patients to gather information about an illness. They do tests to figure out its causes. They try treatments to learn about possible solutions. This helps doctors find a cure.

Public policy analysts do the same. They gather information and analyze different points of view. They also conduct their own research. They hold hearings or participate in focus groups, where people can express their opinions. They may also gather information through surveys. They might send surveys to a large group of people. They may also call people to conduct interviews on the phone. These surveys include specific questions designed to learn more about issues. They might inquire which issues are most important or focus on one issue to investigate which solutions people prefer.

For citizens both in and out of the government, research is key to understanding public issues. Only by understanding these issues well can people make good decisions to solve them.

title: Essential Question
text: How does research help you understand public economic issues in the Western Hemisphere?

title: Asking and Developing Questions
text:
Asking Questions

To begin the process, you must start by asking questions. In order for your research to be successful, you have to ask specific questions throughout the process. By asking questions, you can develop your claim. A claim is a statement you make about what you believe can be supported with evidence. There are many types of questions you can ask throughout the whole process.

Compelling Questions

The word compelling refers to something that sparks your interest and is exciting. Answering a compelling question requires deep thinking. There could be multiple answers to the same question. The answer you come up with depends on the evidence you find in your research. An example of a compelling question is: What is the real cost of chocolate?

Supporting Questions

A supporting question gives you the information that you need to answer the compelling question. While a compelling question might have different answers, depending on your research, a supporting question usually has only one answer. These answers give you the evidence you need to solve the mystery!

Compelling question: What is the real cost of chocolate?

To support your compelling question, you could ask:

What type of physical environment does a cocoa bean farmer need?

How are cocoa beans and other natural resources needed to make chocolate harvested?

What type of resources are needed to produce chocolate?

What is free trade chocolate?

Each type of question is important and is needed for your research to be meaningful.

title: What Makes You Think That?
text:
After creating your compelling and supporting questions, it is time to research information and provide evidence to support your claim. Evidence can change our thinking and beliefs about a topic or idea. This is known as the reflection process.

To reflect on an idea means to think deeply about it and decide if it is still the best solution. The most successful thinkers are people who know how to reflect and change their thinking, as needed. You can use the following sentence starters to build a claim for the compelling question “What is the real cost of chocolate?”

title: Identify the Right Evidence
text:
Once you have analyzed your sources, it is time to evaluate them. To evaluate means to determine which information is most useful to you. When you evaluate sources in an inquiry, it means you determine the information that is most useful in answering the compelling question.

To begin this process, you should review all of the information you gathered from your research. This information is your evidence. Evidence is information or data that supports an argument. Evidence from your sources should be ranked by which pieces are most helpful in proving your point.

Then, make sure you are using credible sources. Once you have determined their credibility, you can use corroboration. Corroboration means finding evidence from multiple sources to support your claim. If you are able to provide corroboration with your sources, you strengthen your argument!

Conduct a close read for each source, and take notes (annotate). Then, think about what connections you can make between your sources (corroborate). What do you notice about your sources? What connections can you make?

title: Regions of Wisconsin
text:
Most of the physical features of Wisconsin were formed about 12,000 years ago by glaciers. As the glaciers receded, they created more than 15,000 lakes. Wisconsin’s physical features have influenced the state’s human characteristics. Both physical and human characteristics make Wisconsin and its regions what they are today.

This week, you will learn about the five regions of Wisconsin. The Lake Superior Lowland is located in the northernmost portion of Wisconsin. The Northern Highland has the highest elevation in the state. The Central Plain is a U-shaped region of rich farmland. The Western Upland is the only part of the state that was not formed by prehistoric glaciers. The Eastern Ridges and Lowlands border Lake Michigan.

title: Lake Superior Lowland
text:
Lake Superior Lowland

The Lake Superior Lowland only extends 5–20 miles inland from Lake Superior. From its southernmost point, the Lowland slopes north toward Lake Superior. The Lowland has many trees, including aspen and birch trees. The Apostle Island National Lakeshore is a part of the Lake Superior Lowland.

The Apostle Islands

The Apostle Islands were named by the first French explorers who ventured to Lake Superior. The two main objectives for most French explorers were to build forts and to establish fur trading relationships with Native Americans. They did both on the Apostle Islands. With a fort on Lake Superior, fur traders from the interior of the continent could sell their furs, which were taken to eastern cities on the Saint Lawrence River. From there, the furs were shipped to Europe. After the fur trade declined, logging became an important industry on the Apostle Islands. But eventually, most of the Apostle Islands were abandoned. In 1970, 21 of the 22 Apostle Islands were made into a national park. Today, tourists visit the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore to see historic lighthouses, explore sandstone sea caves, and engage in many water activities, such as canoeing and scuba diving.

title: Northern Highland
text:
Northern Highland

The highest point in Wisconsin is located in the Northern Highland Region. It is called Timms Point. There are rolling hills and forests throughout this region. The Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest is located in this region. The Northern Highland region covers about one-third of Wisconsin.

Chequamegon and Nicolet National Forests

One of the most abundant natural features in Wisconsin is forests. Most of the forests in modern Wisconsin consist of replanted trees because earlier forests were cut down for the logging industry. This is true of the Chequamegon and Nicolet National Forests.

Sometimes after the trees had been cut down, immigrants would buy the land and try to farm it. However, the soil was not good for growing crops, and most of the farms were eventually abandoned. Some trees grew back naturally, but many had to be replanted.

By presidential proclamation in 1933, the Chequamegon and Nicolet National Forests were created. The name “Chequamegon” is believed to come from an Ojibwe word meaning “place of shallow water.” The name “Nicolet” refers to French explorer Jean Nicolet, who came to the area in the 1600s. Technically, the Chequamegon and Nicolet are separate forests, however, they are run jointly. Combined, the forests cover 1,530,647 acres.

title: Central Plain
text:
Central Plain

A plain is a large, flat area with few trees. The Central Plain of Wisconsin has a lot of rich farmland. Prehistoric glaciers cut a large gorge that the Wisconsin River flows through. This area is called the Dells of the Wisconsin River. The Dells have tall cliffs, some over 100 feet high, that overlook the Wisconsin River.

Eau Claire

The city of Eau Claire sits at the confluence of the Eau Claire and Chippewa Rivers. A confluence is a place where two rivers meet. The rivers are significant to the city of Eau Claire in many ways. Eau Claire means “clear water” in French. According to legend, the river got its name when French explorers were traveling down the muddy Chippewa River. When they reached the confluence of the Chippewa and Eau Claire Rivers, they shouted, “Here is the clear water!”

The first major industry in Eau Claire was logging, which relied heavily on the rivers to transport logs and power sawmills. Once a tree was cut down, it was floated to the sawmill, which ran using water-powered machines. Then the cut timber was shipped by river to other places. Today, Eau Claire is the eighth-largest city in Wisconsin. Of Wisconsin’s 10 most populous cities, it is the only one not located in the Eastern Ridges and Lowland Region.

title: Western Upland
text:
Western Upland

The Western Upland has more rugged terrain than the rest of Wisconsin. The region is part of a larger geographical formation called the “Driftless Area,” which also includes parts of Minnesota, Iowa, and Illinois. It gets the name “Driftless” because it was not covered by glaciers, which leave behind a deposit called “drift.” The Western Upland is bordered by the Mississippi River and has large bluffs that overlook the river. There are many farms, trees, and caves in this region. The Baraboo Range is in the Western Upland region.

Devil’s Lake

Devil’s Lake is one mile long and half a mile wide. The lake sits on Ho-Chunk ancestral land in the Baraboo Hills. The Ho-Chunk called the lake De Wakacak, which means “sacred” or “spirit lake.” The area around Devil’s Lake has effigy mounds. These are human-made hills that have been formed to look like animals or other shapes. They are sacred to the Native Americans whose ancestors created them. Devil’s Lake is now a state park. There are many things to do and see at Devil’s Lake. There are nesting bald eagles in the area. The rocks are colored pink and purple. There is even a pygmy forest, which is a forest with very old trees that have not grown tall or wide because the soil lacks nutrients.

title: Eastern Ridges and Lowland
text:
Eastern Ridges and Lowland

The Eastern Ridges and Lowland is an important part of Wisconsin’s geography. Parallel limestone ridges are located in the western part of the region. The eastern part of the region is covered by a plain that slopes down toward Lake Michigan. This region has some of the world’s best farmland. It is also the location of Wisconsin’s largest urban centers. Nine out of the 10 largest cities in Wisconsin are located in the Eastern Ridges and Lowland.

Lake Michigan

Lake Michigan is one of the world’s largest lakes. It was made by a glacier. The surface area of the lake is 22,300 square miles. It probably gets its name from the Ojibwe word “mich-gami,” which means “great water.” The Great Lakes have served as important travel routes and lines of communication between the midwestern part of the continent and the Atlantic Ocean. Lake Michigan helped connect the Saint Lawrence River system to the Mississippi River System, which in turn connected the Atlantic Ocean to the Gulf of Mexico. The people of Wisconsin have always relied on Lake Michigan to provide transportation, communication, and drinking water. Lake Michigan is also one of the state’s most popular tourist draws.

title: Water and Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin has many lakes and rivers. These waterways have been important to every group of people who have lived in Wisconsin. They were vital to the Native Americans who lived, worked, and worshiped on this land for thousands of years. They were important to the immigrants who came to Wisconsin. They are important now.

There are many examples of conflict and cooperation in American history. There have been conflicts over land, resources, ideas, and more. Conflict is the opposition of persons or groups that gives rise to dramatic action. Though many conflicts have led to hardship and suffering, some have also led to the creation of great things. There are also many examples of cooperation where people have worked together to accomplish great things. Cooperation Is the process of working together to achieve a common goal or resolution. Cooperation has created new movements and ideas.

In American history, conflict has occurred between groups of people. As communication between people and groups decreases, conflict increases. Sometimes, people disagree over who should be in charge or what kind of government to have. This is what caused the American Revolution. The American colonists disagreed with the British government’s rule, so they fought to establish their own country. This conflict led to the creation of a new country. Other conflicts have been more destructive. The American Civil War was a conflict between the North and the South. It was the deadliest war in American history.

Cooperation between people has been common throughout American history, too. People have worked together to overcome difficult times or accomplish goals. The American Revolution is an example of a time of cooperation. The American colonies came together to become independent from England. Even though they had different ideas about what the future country should look like, they identified a common cause to work for and compromised. The creation of the United States government is an example of cooperation.

There are many examples of conflict and cooperation in Pennsylvania history. These events have shaped Pennsylvania’s culture, history, economy, and government.

title: Rosa Parks Inspired Change
text: America had laws that some thought were unfair. In some states, these laws said where people could and could not go based on the color of their skin. Black people had to sit in the back in public buses. They had to give up seats for white people. One day, Rosa Parks sat where she was supposed to on the bus. She was then told to move when a white person wanted to sit in that seat. Rosa said, “No.” She thought the law was unfair and wanted it to change. Rosa showed courage when she refused to give up her seat on the bus. Many people thought she was brave. They decided to not ride the buses until the law was changed.

title: Coping Strategies for Emotions
text: Have you ever seen someone bite their nails when they’re nervous? What about someone tapping their foot while they wait in line? These are just a few examples of coping strategies. A coping strategy is a tool people use to help them manage their emotions. Some coping strategies are positive and some are negative. Negative coping strategies are harmful and do not help us address the problem we’re facing. On the other hand, positive coping strategies can help you learn to accept your emotions and face challenges.

title: Fixing Problems or Helping Feelings
text:
There are two types of coping strategies: problem-based and emotion-based.

Problem-based coping strategies help us try to fix or change the problem that is causing our negative emotions. Here are a few examples:

Asking for support

Making a checklist

Creating a schedule to manage time

Emotion-based coping strategies can help us change our negative feelings into positive ones. We may not be able to fix the problem, but we can change how we respond to it. Here are some examples:

Writing down feelings

Exercising

Practicing mindfulness

title: Stock Your Fridge!
text:
Coping strategies are like having ingredients in your fridge. The more ingredients you have, the more meals you can make. The more coping strategies you have, the more emotions you can handle in healthy ways. Fill your fridge with helpful ingredients! You can create recipes of coping strategies to help you in lots of situations.

When Peter feels sad, this is the recipe he uses:

3 deep breaths

5 minutes of exercise

10 minutes of reading his favorite book

You can come up with recipes that help you cope with your emotions.

title: 1 Cup of Movement
text: When you move your body, your brain releases chemicals that help your mind and body feel better. Physical activity can also help get rid of the energy that builds up when you’re stressed. Here are some ideas to try: Go for a walk. Play a sport you enjoy. Dance to fun music. Run outside. Do yoga. Clean your room.

title: 1 Cup of Gratitude
text: When you’re feeling overwhelmed or upset, you might forget the word “grateful” even exists. But thinking of the people and things that you’re grateful for can change your perspective. It can start to pull your mind out of the stressful situation and help you focus on positive things. When you feel more calm, you can come back to the problem and look at it with a positive attitude. Your problem may not seem as big, or you may see a good solution. Gratitude is a powerful ingredient!

title: Bouncing Back with Resilience
text: Resilience is the ability to bounce back from difficulty and struggle. It allows you to master and manage difficult situations. Sometimes, things happen around us that we can’t control. Being resilient is being able to stay positive when things change unexpectedly. Resilience is sometimes referred to as grit. There are four types of resilience: emotional, social, physical, and mental.

title: Bounce Back After Hard Emotions
text:
Emotional resilience is knowing how to focus on what is going well. It can help you bounce back when you feel sad, angry, or frustrated. Learning to identify and regulate our emotions helps us build emotional resilience.

Our world is always changing, and our emotions change, too. As life happens, is it important to be able to understand and share how we feel. This will ultimately allow us to manage how we respond to how we are feeling.

title: Bounce Back After People Are Unkind
text: Social resilience is being able to adapt and grow in our surroundings. It allows us to be confident and successful in our daily lives. Social resilience is being able to bounce back when others are not their best selves. It is learning how to meet new people and make new friends. Social resilience is being kind to others and showing respect when others have different opinions. Adjusting positively to what happens around us helps us become more resilient.

title: Bounce Back After Physical Challenges
text:
You strengthen your physical resilience when you encounter and push through physical challenges. Some of these challenges come from trying new things, like learning a new skill or a new sport. Some of these challenges come from injuries or accidents. For example, if you break your arm, you will need physical resilience to learn new ways of brushing your teeth, writing, or practicing an instrument.

Some challenges come from physical disabilities that we overcome with help from others or with tools such as glasses, wheelchairs, and other devices. Anytime we overcome a physical challenge, we are strengthening our physical resilience.

These are some ideas to help you build physical resilience:

1. Get enough sleep and eat nutritious food.

2. Take time to rest, play, and recover from hard work.

3. Take time to breathe and practice mindfulness.

title: Bounce Back After Negative Thoughts
text:
Mental resilience is learning how to manage our thoughts and perceptions. We want to try and focus on the positive as we think about ourselves, our choices, how others view us, and the things that happen to us. Mental resilience involves motivating ourselves to do hard things and learn new skills. It is also being able to overcome the potentially negative effects of stress and hardship.

Sometimes, external factors can impact you. When you face something that isn't fair, you work on your ability to be strong and confident.

title: Resilience Through Resources
text:
Being resourceful helps you be resilient. Being resourceful means that you "find a way" to do what you need to do. Being resourceful means that you work hard to find a way to achieve a goal or complete a task. Always be proactive in searching for ways to achieve goals or complete tasks.

You can:

Ask for help.

Think outside the box.

Utilize your resources.

Collaborate with others.

Access resources available.

Consider all options.

title: Resilience Through Responsibility
text:
Being responsible is part of being resilient. Knowing what we are responsible for helps us achieve our goals. When we act in a responsible way, we are able to continually build resilience in ourselves. It helps us to follow through with what we need to accomplish. Being responsible helps you learn that you can count on yourself.

Ask yourself:

What am I responsible for?

How do I make sure I do it?

Who can help me if I need it?

title: Resilience Through Bravery
text:
Being brave is having the strength to face scary, hard, or difficult things. Bravery doesn't mean putting yourself in harm's way. Being brave helps you increase your resilience because you do things that stretch your skills. As you stretch your skills by being brave and resilient, you can begin to push through boundaries.

What is a challenge you are facing now? List three ways to bravely face that challenge.

title: Why Do People Create Governments?
text:
The purpose of government is to provide safety and security for those in the community from threats outside of the community, maintain justice and order within the community, and help the members of the community meet their wants and needs.

There are many different types and levels of government throughout the world and our country. Although there are many types and levels of government, their purpose is to make laws and rules about matters that guarantee and protect the rights of citizens. Laws and rules should provide safety and security. The government should make sure all people are treated fairly under these laws.

The Founders created our federal, or national, government to establish justice, promote peace within the country, defend the people, and protect the rights of citizens. The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law of our country and the blueprint for our government. Its purpose is to describe the duties of the government and the rights of the people being governed. It defines the basic responsibilities and structure of the federal government. The Constitution also sets up separation of powers and a system of checks and balances. The federal government and the U.S. Constitution serves as a model for state governments and constitutions throughout our country.

title: The Bracero Program of 1942
text:
In 1942, President Franklin D. Roosevelt created an executive order to help the economy of the United States. An executive order from the President does not have to go through approval of Congress. The president can direct a government agency to do something. Roosevelt’s Executive Order 8802 established the Bracero Program. The war had created a shortage of workers in the agriculture industry. The Bracero Program permitted millions of men from Mexico to come to the United States for work.

By 1943, the Bracero Program expanded to include workers on railroads and other non-agricultural jobs. The Lackawanna Railroad in Scranton, Pennsylvania, participated in the program. The Lackawanna Railroad was a large rail system of about 2,500 miles. Passenger and freight trains used the Lackawanna Railroad. Service, care, and maintenance of the system required a large workforce. With many American men enlisted in the war, men from Mexico were hired to maintain the railroad.

The men who participated in the Bracero Program were given transportation from Mexico to Pennsylvania. They were guaranteed food and housing. In 1945, 69,000 men from the Bracero Program worked on American railroads. The Lackawanna Railroad employed between 450 to 550 workers from Mexico.

The men worked mostly on the maintenance of the tracks. This meant replacing worn tracks and removing snow, ice, and other obstructions. They also inspected and repaired bridges. This was done in all kinds of weather. The Bracero Program helped keep the Lackawanna Railroad running during the 1940s.

The Steamtown National Historic Site in Scranton, Pennsylvania, keeps and preserves records from the time period. Primary documents show that the men of the Bracero Program were vital in supporting the war effort and maintaining the country’s railroads.

title: Native American Tribes in Wisconsin
text:
The area now known as Wisconsin has been inhabited for thousands of years. The Native American peoples who have lived in the area of Wisconsin had diverse cultures, languages, beliefs, economies, and governments. Today, there are 12 tribal bands in modern-day Wisconsin: the Menominee, Ho-Chunk, Potawatomi, Oneida, Stockbridge-Munsee, Brothertown, Red Cliff Ojibwe, Bad River Ojibwe, Lac Courte Oreilles Ojibwe, Lac du Flambeau Ojibwe, St. Croix Ojibwe, and Sokaogon (Mole Lake) Ojibwe. The borders and state designations we have today did not exist for Native inhabitants. For example, you will learn about six Ojibwe bands in Wisconsin, but there are also groups of Ojibwe who live in Canada, Michigan, and Minnesota. They are all connected to one another.

All the tribes in Wisconsin organized themselves into clans. The clans were represented by things from the natural world, usually animals. Each clan had a different responsibility in their tribe. Some clans were in charge of war, while others were in charge of peace. Some were artisans, and others were keepers of the law. There were many more responsibilities among tribal clans.

Most of the tribes that lived in Wisconsin did not have writing systems for their languages. Since they didn’t have written history, they spoke it. Older people would tell stories to younger people, passing down the lessons and traditions of their tribes. Passing knowledge, beliefs, and history from generation to generation this way is called oral tradition. The Ojibwe also wrote on birchbark; however, these records did not survive. The Ojibwe still used oral tradition as a tool to remember their traditions and history. Today, tribes create a written record of their history, but oral tradition is still a major component of their culture.

One thing that all the tribes living in Wisconsin have is strong spiritual traditions. These traditions were important in the past and are important today. Among these traditions is the belief that tobacco is a sacred plant. It is offered to the Creators and spirits during ceremonies. It is offered before prayers. Proper use of tobacco is very important to Native American tribes and bands. The drum is also an important feature of many of these tribes' spiritual traditions. The making, preservation, and use of drums is a significant spiritual tradition for many tribes and bands.

title: Menominee
text:
The Menominee tribe was given its name by other tribes. It comes from an Ojibwe word meaning “the people of the wild rice.” However, the Menominee call themselves the Kiash Matchitiwuk, which means “Ancient Ones.” The Menominee had many different clans, including the Bear, Eagle, Wolf, Moose, and Crane clans.

According to Menominee tradition, their original land is just 60 miles from the current Menominee Reservation. Before colonization, the Menominee migrated with the seasons and used the resources that were available to them. Three of their most important resources were wild rice, maple trees, and fish. They harvested wild rice in the late summer. They tapped maple trees in the early spring to make maple syrup and sugar. In the winter, they fished and hunted. These are still vital resources for the Menominee.

According to David Grignon, a tribal elder, when the Kiash Matchitiwuk made everyday things, such as clothing or canoes, there was a ceremony involved. They believed that every resource came from the Creator, so they gave thanks and honored the Creator whenever they used the Earth’s resources. Over the tribe’s long history, the Menominee have had to deal with interference and dishonesty by settlers and governments. In the early 1900s, the Menominee began to log. They only cut down mature trees and would let the forest regrow in an area before they logged there again. The U.S. Forest Service interfered and began to cut down all the trees on Menominee land. Eventually, after lawsuits, negotiation, and patience, the Menominee were able to take back control of their forest and resources.

The Kiash Matchitiwuk once had land all across Northern Michigan and Wisconsin, particularly around Green Bay. Today, the Menominee Nation is located in Menominee County, Wisconsin. The Wolf River runs through Menominee land.

title: Ho-Chunk
text:
The Ho-Chunk call themselves Hochungra, which means “people of the big voice” or “people of the sacred language.” An elder among the Ho-Chunk nation named Andy Thundercloud said that the language of the Ho-Chunk is what makes them who they are. It is sacred to them. The Ho-Chunk have also been called the Winnebago by others.

Ho-Chunk land once ranged across modern-day Michigan, Illinois, and Wisconsin. When settlers came to the area, however, they began to take Ho-Chunk land. There were many conflicts as a result. Some Ho-Chunk supported Red Bird, a warrior who took revenge on people stealing Ho-Chunk land, but he was convinced by other Ho-Chunk to surrender. Some Ho-Chunk also supported a Sauk warrior named Black Hawk who fought the U.S. Army. In the end, Black Hawk lost.

In the 1830s, the U.S. government began to force Native American people from their homes. The Ho-Chunk were forced to move to Minnesota, then to Nebraska. Some Ho-Chunk even have a reservation in Nebraska called the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska. However, there were Ho-Chunk who stayed on their land and others who made their way back home after being forced to leave. Today, the Ho-Chunk do not have a reservation in Wisconsin, but the nation owns about 4,200 acres of tribal trust land.

The Ho-Chunk are organized into clans. Eight of the clans are earth clans, and four are sky clans. Each clan has a different responsibility. According to Thundercloud, the clans still fulfill their responsibilities, especially during traditional ceremonies.

title: Potawatomi
text:
The Potawatomi tribe was a part of the Anishinaabe alliance. It was also called the Three Fires Confederacy. The Ojibwe, the Odawa (also spelled Ottawa), and the Potawatomi were part of the Anishinaabe. According to tribal elder Mike Alloway Sr., the Anishinaabe were all one tribe in the area of the Straits of Mackinac, but they decided to split apart. The Odawa were keepers of trade, so they stayed near the Straits of Mackinac. The Ojibwe were keepers of the faith and moved to Madeline Island. The Potawatomi were the keepers of the fire and settled on the western and eastern shores of Lake Michigan.

The fur trade became a significant economic activity between European settlers and Native Americans in North America. The Haudenosaunee fought with the Anishinaabe for control of the trade around the eastern Great Lakes. The Anishinaabe lost control of the fur trade. Because the Haudenosaunee were allied with the British, this meant that the Potawatomi were now enemies of the British. This would lead to further conflict and loss of land. The Potawatomi, like the Ho-Chunk, were also subjected to forced removal.

The arduous march from their home was called the “Trail of Death.” Some Potawatomi escaped to Mexico, others to Canada, and many Potawatomi were forced to go to Kansas and Oklahoma. However, some Potawatomi hid in the forests of their homeland. They became known as the Strolling Bands of Potawatomi. The Strolling Bands of Potawatomi and some groups that had made their way back home joined together. In 1937, they became known as the Forest County Potawatomi. Today, there are many Potawatomi tribes throughout the United States and Canada.

Like other tribes, the Potawatomi believe in the responsibility to take care of their natural resources. They believe their land and their language were given to them by the Creator. Because of this relationship, they treat their resources, language, and heritage as sacred.

title: Oneida
text:
The Oneida’s name means “People of the Standing Stone.” The Oneida were part of the Haudenosaunee, which consisted of five (later six) nations. They lived on the east side of the Great Lakes in what is now upstate New York. Haudenosaunee means “People of the Longhouse.” The nations that were a part of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy were the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca, and later the Tuscarora.

The tribes of the Haudenosaunee are matrilineal. Matrilineal means that members of the society trace their heritage through their mother. The government is influenced and chosen by the Clan Mothers of the Haudenosaunee. Clan Mothers meet and choose the men of the Tribal Council and the chief.

The Oneida that currently reside in Wisconsin came to the state after the American Revolution. A group of Oneida converted to Christianity and became spies for George Washington’s army. However, the majority of the Haudenosaunee were allied with the British. The Oneida were no longer welcome among the Haudenosaunee, so they left and went to Wisconsin. In a treaty with the Menominee, the Oneida got land. Most Oneida in this band assimilated into United States culture. According to Rand Cornelius, an Oneida Elder, starting in the 1970s, many Oneida sought to revitalize their heritage and Oneida culture.

title: Stockbridge-Munsee Community of the Mohican
text:
There are two tribal heritages among the Stockbridge-Munsee Community of the Mohican: the Munsee and the Mohican. The Munsee were a part of the Lenni Lenape, but while living close to the Mohican, some of them became affiliated with the Mohican. The Mohican call themselves the Muh-he-con-neok, which means “The People of the Waters That Are Never Still.” Their traditional territory was the Hudson River Valley.

The Mohican became allied with Dutch settlers, trading furs for European-made goods. Because of the depletion of beaver, the Mohican began traveling into Mohawk territory to find furs. This caused conflict between the Mohawk and Mohican. The Mohawk defeated the Mohican, and their population declined because of the war and European diseases.

The Mohican and many Munsee converted to Christianity and moved to Stockbridge, Massachusetts. After fighting in the American Revolution, Mohican soldiers came back to find that their homes, farms, and businesses had been taken over by European colonists, who would not give them back. They moved to New York and took refuge with the Oneida for a time. However, they were eventually forced to move again, this time to Wisconsin.

When they first arrived in Wisconsin, the Munsee and Mohican settled on the shores of Lake Winnebago. Later, they were forced to move again. The Stockbridge-Munsee Mohican were granted Menominee land.

title: Brothertown
text:
The Brothertown are descended from the Native American groups who lived on the East Coast, including the Pequot, Montauk, Niantic, Narragansett, Tunxis, and Mohegan. These groups converted to Christianity and banded together in a town called Brothertown. However, they call themselves Eeyamquiltoowauconnuck. Similar to the Stockbridge-Munsee Mohican, they were forced out of their homes and moved to Oneida land. Later, they were forced to move again, this time to Wisconsin.

As the Brothertown sought peace and hoped to stop forced removal, they signed an agreement with the United States government. In this agreement, the Brothertown were given U.S. citizenship and control over their land. However, this meant that they were no longer recognized as Native Americans. The Brothertown have since asked the U.S. government to recognize their claim as a sovereign group, but the government has refused. Sovereignty is the right to self-govern and to be an independent nation.

title: How Railroads Impacted Communities
text:
Railroads allowed people to transport resources and goods to markets in greater quantities than any other mode of transportation. This caused marketplaces to grow. When a railroad was built in a community, businesses dependent on the railroad were also created to support the larger marketplace.

Because of railroads, more resources could be transported for processing and production. This meant that more employees were needed to gather resources. Workers were then needed to package and transport the resources to the train. At the train, workers were also needed to load and unload the packaged resources for specific destinations. Warehouses were used to store the supply of goods until the train was loaded. The train was loaded by workers.

Inventory in the warehouse was tracked by workers. Managers were needed to coordinate schedules and work operations.

Each of these railroad-dependent workers had to meet their wants and needs through the marketplace in the community. They needed food, shelter, tools for work, and work clothing. Other families would also come to the community, increasing the population and the need for more goods and services in the marketplace. Schools, churches, and community buildings would be built and staffed.

The value of property was tied to how close to the railroad it was. Lower cost properties were near the railroad. The further away from the tracks a property was, the higher the cost.

If the railroad left a town or bypassed a community, the businesses that were dependent on the workers of the railroad would close. This was because there were fewer railroad workers and therefore fewer consumers. Without consumers, goods weren’t being sold. No sales meant no profits. No profits meant the costs of operating a business could not be met, and the business had to close.
