President Harry Truman said, “If we let Korea down, the Soviets will keep right on going and swallow up one place after another.” American and South Korean troops prepared for war. The war wasn’t just against the North Koreans. It was a war against communism itself.

The first goal of the U.S. was to defend South Korea and push the North Koreans back across the border. Early efforts did not go well. The North Korean army was well-trained and well-armed. The South Korean soldiers were not prepared. The mountainous terrain and a severe drought also made the fighting more difficult. By the end of the summer, American Commanding General Douglas MacArthur had decided to change tactics. Instead of waging a war to defend South Korea, it became an effort to free North Korea from the grip of communism.

As the Americans and South Koreans moved farther north toward the Chinese border, the communist Chinese government became concerned. They were afraid of military actions against their own country. Chinese leader, Mao Zedong, sent troops into North Korea. They threatened increased involvement with more military. President Truman feared it would spark another world war. He wanted to negotiate. General MacArthur did not. He favored an increased military action over a compromise.

President Truman fired General MacArthur. Then, the president and his military advisors began peace talks with North Korea. They met at a place on the border called Panmunjom. The negotiations took two years to complete while the troops continued to fight along the border. Neither side was making significant progress. In 1953, Dwight Eisenhower replaced Truman as U.S. President. He went to Korea to more aggressively pursue an end to the war. A peace agreement was finally signed on July 27, 1953. It didn’t declare an end to the actual war, but it did bring peace. A new boundary between North Korea and South Korea was set at the 38th parallel. The two Koreas would remain separated.

title: The Korean War Veterans Memorial
text:
The National Mall in Washington D.C. is a designated area extending from the Capitol Building to the Lincoln Memorial. The Korean War Veterans Memorial is one of many special monuments that was built to honor American soldiers. The memorial was dedicated in 1995 to honor all Americans who served in the U.S. military during the Korean War. Nearly 40,000 American soldiers lost their lives in this war. A simple message is engraved on one wall: “Freedom is not free.”

The Korean War Veterans Memorial has three parts. There is a polished granite wall, a group of stainless steel statues, and a reflecting pool. The main part of the memorial is made up of a 164-foot wall made of polished black granite. On the wall, there are 2,500 photographs from the Korean War etched into the stone. These images show troops from every branch of the military fighting for freedom in Korea.

The 19 stainless steel statues represent U.S. soldiers from the army, air force, navy, and marines. These statues are reflected in the polished stone wall. In effect, this doubles the number of soldier statues to 38. This number represents the 38th parallel as well as the 38 months that the Korean War lasted.

A Pool of Remembrance is also part of the monument. It is a shallow pool lined with more polished, black granite. Engravings in the pool list the number of soldiers killed, wounded, missing in action, and held as prisoners of war. Nearby, a large plaque displays this quote, “Our nation honors her sons and daughters who answered the call to defend a country they never knew and a people they never met.”

title: Consequences of the Korean War
text:
The Korean War was a proxy war. A proxy war is a war that happens when opposing powers use other countries to fight instead of fighting each other directly. The Korean War was North Korean leader Kim Il Sung’s idea. He wanted to unify the north and south under his dictatorship. He was supported in his efforts by the Soviet Union and China. These countries opposed America, but they didn’t want to fight America directly. The Americans supported South Korea on behalf of the United Nations, but they were not responsible for starting the war.

Military actions in Korea started in 1950 and ended in 1953. As in any military action there were political, economic and human consequences.

In the cease-fire agreement, South Korea gained an additional 1,500 square acres of land at the border.

A two-mile wide demilitarized zone was created as a buffer between North Korea and South Korea.

North Korea became one of the most heavily bombed countries in history.

Nearly all industries in North Korea were destroyed. North Korea lost trade resulting in failing economic structures.

Tensions between the U.S. and China over who would pay for the war resulted in an end to their alliance.

The U.S. cut off diplomatic relations with China.

The U.S. prevented South Korea from falling to communism.

The U.S. formed new alliances with Australia, New Zealand, and the Philippines.

The United Nations became a world respected organization.

Five million people are estimated to have died.

title: Woodrow Wilson Keeble
text:
The Medal of Honor is the United States’ highest military award. It is given to members of the military who risk their lives during battle to perform acts of extreme bravery. In March of 2008, President George W. Bush awarded this medal to Master Sergeant Woodrow Wilson Keeble. Keeble was from North Dakota. He was a full-blooded member of the Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate of the Lake Traverse Reservation, a federally recognized tribe of Dakota people.

Keeble was born on a Sioux reservation in South Dakota in 1917. He then moved to Wahpeton, North Dakota, where he attended the Wahpeton Indian School along with his brothers and sisters. Keeble became a star baseball player. He hoped to be a major league pitcher, but his National Guard unit was called into action during World War II.

Keeble served in both World War II and the Korean War. He was injured in battle multiple times, earning four Purple Hearts. The Purple Heart is a medal given to soldiers who are wounded or killed in battle. Keeble also earned the Distinguished Service Cross, the Silver Star, and the Bronze Star. The Distinguished Service Cross is the U.S. Army’s second highest award. It is given to those who display extreme courage during battle on behalf of their comrades. The Silver Star and the Bronze Star medals were both awarded to Keeble for valiant service to his country. Keeble’s extraordinary heroism and bravery was impressive. A soldier from his unit said that the “safest place to be was right next to Woody.”

After the war, Keeble went back home and taught at the Wahpeton Indian School. He suffered many health problems after he finished his military service. He died in 1982 at the age of 65. Still, he was not forgotten. He was awarded both the Medal of Honor and the Theodore Roosevelt Rough Rider Award in 2008. Woody Keeble is one of many brave Americans who served the United States with honor.

title: Geography of Korea
text:
The Korean peninsula juts out of the eastern portion of Asia. The 680-mile-long peninsula, a piece of land that sticks out into the water, is surrounded by two large bodies of water. On the east side of the peninsula is the Sea of Japan. It separates Asian countries from the Pacific Ocean. To the west, the peninsula is bordered by the Yellow Sea. The Yellow Sea is flat and shallow. The sea floor slopes downward quickly off the Korean coast, creating deep fishing waters that greatly add to Korea’s economy.

The peninsula is divided into North and South Korea. North Korea has about 55 percent of the peninsula’s land. It is full of mountains and deep, narrow valleys in the north. Mount Paektu, over 9,000 feet high, is the highest point on the peninsula. Another major physical feature of North Korea is the Yalu River. The Yalu, also called the Amnok, begins on the southern slope of Mount Paektu. It eventually empties into the Korean Bay. The Yalu River provides hydroelectric power and serves as a means of transportation to many cities.

South Korea covers about 45 percent of the land. It is also mountainous with small valleys and coastal plains. The mountains in South Korea are not as large as the mountains to the north. Its highest peak is in the Sobaek Mountains. The peak reaches over 6,000 feet. Off the South Korean coasts, there are more islands. Some are small, but others, like the volcanic islands of Cheju and Ullung, are larger. Cheju has a very mild climate. The island is a vacation destination for many Koreans and other tourists. Ullung is also a tourist destination. It is known for delicious seafood, fresh from daily catches in the island waters.

One of the main reasons that the Korean War was so difficult to fight was the mountainous terrain. Another difficulty was the climate in much of the Korean peninsula. The longest of Korea’s four seasons, winter, can be very harsh. Many in Korea experience extremely cold winds and temperatures. Most of Korea has hot, humid summers. During the Asian monsoon season in the summer, rainfall is more common than it is in the rest of the year. Spring and fall are mild and pleasant, but they are shorter seasons.

Seoul is the capital of South Korea. Almost 10 million people live in the city and its suburbs. Since the end of the Korean War, it has gradually developed into a very modern city. Many products Americans use are made in South Korea such as Hyundai cars, Samsung electronics, and LG appliances.

title: Women, Careers, and Family
text:
Picture it: A well-dressed man in a suit and tie holding a briefcase is greeted at the door by a lovely woman wearing a nice dress and a ruffled apron. He gives her a quick kiss on the cheek and asks when dinner will be ready. She leads him into the dining room. There, the table is set and ready for her to serve the home-cooked meal she has worked on all afternoon. Neat, happy children join them at the table. The children exchange humorous stories from their day at school. This was the ideal family portrayed on television in
the 1950s.

Postwar society was centered around the family unit of Mom, Dad, and kids living in the new suburbs. As the country faced the threat of global communism, the American people looked to the strength of this unit as a buffer against this threat. Therefore, the 1950s became a decade of conformity. As soldiers returned home, many young women focused on finding husbands and starting a family. The average age for a woman to get married in the 1950s was 20 years old. Once married, young wives rarely continued to pursue an education or career. Instead, they were expected to take care of home and children. During this time, families tended to be large. Between 1940 and 1960, the number of babies increased so dramatically that it is called “the baby boom.” People born from 1946 to 1961 are known as “boomers.”

News outlets and government propaganda portrayed women in communist countries in drab clothing, working in cold, gray factories. It also depicted their children being raised in government controlled daycare centers. On the other hand, capitalism and democracy allowed American women the opportunity to stay at home. Propaganda, magazines, television, advertising and movies portrayed women as happy companions, wonderful mothers, and lovely housewives. Women wore dresses even to do housework. Casual attire of pants or shorts were not available to purchase. After the difficult Great Depression and the war years, security for many people centered on building safe and nurturing home environments.

By comparison, men generally viewed themselves as the sole breadwinners at this time. While women performed housework, men worked outside the home and earned money for their family. It was a common assumption among many people that women couldn’t manage both a career and a family. Different communities were not supportive of a working mother. Many careers were denied to women because they were not men. Engineers, doctors, lawyers, and school principals were all jobs for men. Women need not apply for such jobs. Women could be nurses, secretaries or teachers.

Many women felt dissatisfied with limited opportunities and social expectations. The daughters of 1950s mothers were especially determined to have less constricted roles in society. Their efforts to gain more independence eventually led to an explosion of activism. The resulting women’s rights movements of the 1960s and 1970s challenged the traditional roles of women and fought for gender equality.

title: The Chicano Rights Movement
text:
The leaders of the Civil Rights Movement intended to include all Americans of color who were struggling for equality. Influenced by these leaders, Hispanic Americans began organizing their own movements for fairness and equal rights. Marches were held in places like Philadelphia, Chicago, New York City, and Puerto Rico. In the American Southwest, the Mexican Americans’ struggle became known as the Chicano Civil Rights Movement.

Both the African American and Chicano Civil Rights Movements shared common goals. Some of the issues Hispanic Americans faced were different. Puerto Ricans were American citizens, but they weren't treated as such. Puerto Rico is an unincorporated American territory. Many Puerto Ricans who migrated to the mainland ended up in low-paying jobs and poor living conditions.

Many Mexican Americans lived in rural areas and made a living as farmers and migrant workers. Generations of Mexican Americans experienced bias and prejudice for their cultural heritage from people who were not tolerant of others. Hispanic Americans faced racism in nearly every aspect of their lives. The environment and occupations available for them were different from opportunities for non-Hispanic Americans. Growing movements like the Chicano Civil Rights Movement helped minority voices be heard in the struggle against prejudice and injustice. Unfortunately, many of the issues involving Hispanic American rights still remain unresolved today.

title: César Chávez and the UFW
text:
César Chávez was born in 1927 on his family's farm near Yuma, Arizona. Things were going well for his family until the Great Depression when his family lost their farm. They became migrant workers, and Chávez had to quit school in the eighth grade to work full time. He worked in farm fields, orchards, and vineyards to help support his family.

When he was 17 years old, Chávez joined the Navy. After serving for two years, he came back to work in the fields, got married, and settled in California. There, he worked on a farm and then for a lumber company. However, because of his experience and observations as a migrant farm worker, he felt compelled to help improve migrant workers’ lives. To do so, he joined the Community Services Organization (CSO), a Latino civil rights association.

After moving to another town in California, Chavez met Delores Huerta, a woman dedicated to fighting for human rights. They founded the National Farm Workers Association (NFWA). Later, NFWA joined with another labor organization of farm workers. Both organizations worked to better the lives of their members. Many mergers of smaller unions became a large union named the United Farm Workers (UFW). It was the first successful farm workers' union in U.S. history. Today, the union continues its work to improve farm workers’ lives.

Working under the UFW, Chávez organized boycotts and strikes against fruit and vegetable growers. The growers refused to give farm workers fair pay, reasonable working hours, and safe places to live. A strike happens when workers refuse to work until their demands are met. Chávez asked all strikers to take a pledge of nonviolence. Chavez led a march of workers 300 miles to the state capital in Sacramento. The nonviolent approach to conflict gained great support from other unions, social groups, and political activists.

The UFW was successful in their goals. Workers gained better working conditions and better pay. Chávez continued to bring awareness of working conditions to the public. He went on speaking tours and gained national support for farm workers.

In 1993, Chávez died of natural causes. His wife, Helen, accepted the Medal of Freedom from President Bill Clinton on behalf of her husband in 1994. The Medal of Freedom is the nation's highest civilian honor.

César Chávez showed diligence, cooperation, and respect for authority through his peaceful work. His life of service to others is a shining example for all Americans.

title: Native American Issues in the 1960s
text:
In the 1950s and 1960s, the people who lived on Native American reservations lived in poverty. Their families had been forcibly moved there by the federal government. Healthcare was difficult to get or did not exist. The death rate of American Indians living on reservations was over 30 percent higher than it was in the whole U.S. population. Half a million Native Americans lived in unsanitary, run-down dwellings. Few were able to get an education. Employment opportunities were very limited. In the 1950s, the U.S. government tried to take over a number of reservations without tribal consent. Congress even proposed giving Native American land to various states and moving the tribes into urban areas.

Facing bigotry and continued racism from the federal government, Native Americans organized a modern system of cooperation. In the 1940s, the first intertribal association formed. Its purpose was to resist federal government efforts to remove American Indians from their land. This organization was called the National Congress of American Indians. Other groups formed in the late 1950s that also worked to protect Native American rights. For example, the National Indian Youth Council sponsored demonstrations and marches to protect fishing rights that had been guaranteed in treaties.

The best known organization of Native Americans began in 1966. It was called the American Indian Movement. This organization led Native Americans in an automobile caravan from California to Washington, D.C. They called the caravan the “Trail of Broken Treaties.” Their actions brought the government’s attention to the problems and injustices facing many Native Americans.

title: Government Acts for Native Americans
text:
Protests by American Indians that began in the 1950s finally saw results in the 1970s. It began with the Indian Education Act of 1972. This act gave American Indian parents more control over their children’s schools and education. The Child Welfare Act also gave tribes control of custody decisions that involved American Indian children.

Several important Supreme Court cases were decided in favor of American Indians as well. One decision supported the right of tribes to govern themselves. Another decision ruled that states couldn’t take away fishing and hunting rights that had been given to tribes in treaties. In 1980, several tribes sued the government to recover land that had been illegally taken from them. The government agreed to give the Passamaquoddy and Penobscot tribes in Maine $81.5 million in payment. The Lakota in South Dakota were awarded $105 million.

The problems facing American Indians have not all been solved. Advocating and protecting the rights of all people is ongoing for each generation.

Scarcity is when producers don’t make enough of something.

When there aren't enough goods and services, we have to choose what we need most.

title: Booker T. Washington
text:
Booker T. Washington was born into slavery in Virginia in 1856. He learned how to read in his spare time. At age 16, he walked 500 miles to a school in Virginia. He convinced the headmaster to let him work as a janitor to help pay for his tuition. Washington worked and studied hard to become an educator and leader.

When he was an adult, Washington was hired to lead the Tuskegee Normal School. A “normal school” was a school that trained teachers. The Tuskegee Normal School was one of the few schools that taught African American educators. Washington encouraged each student to do their best work. He believed education was important for African Americans. Booker T. Washington said, “I have learned that success is to be measured not so much by the position one has reached in life as by the obstacles which he has overcome.”

title: Income
text:
The money people earn from working is called income. People use their income to buy the things that they need and want. It’s important that people properly manage their income in order to keep buying the things they need. Saving and investing are two ways to manage money.

When people save money, they usually give it to a financial institution like a bank or a credit union. Saving money helps people be able to afford especially expensive needs and wants. Some people save up to buy something special. Others save money for emergencies, like paying medical bills when they get sick, or replacing a damaged roof after a storm. Many people save money for retirement, which is the time when they stop working. People usually retire when they are older. There are many good reasons to save money.

Another way to manage money is investing it. When people invest, they purchase something with the hope that it will make more money in the future. They can invest money by giving it to a bank or by buying real estate or stocks. A stock is a piece of the ownership of a company. As the company earns more money, the people who own stocks in the company also earn money. An investment can be risky, but good investments can earn money.

title: Financial Institutions
text:
Banks and credit unions are a great way to keep money safe. They are financial institutions where customers can open accounts and keep their money safe. Banks and credit unions both provide loans and other services.

Banks are businesses that deal with money. A commercial bank serves both businesses and people. They offer checking and savings accounts, debit, and credit cards. They provide loans and investments. Another type of bank is a savings bank. These banks are like commercial banks. However, they focus on savings accounts and loans. They also offer loans to customers who want to buy houses or cars. Commercial banks and savings banks are in business to make a profit. Stockholders own, control, and share profits.

Credit unions are different from banks. Members of the credit union put their savings together and loan it to other members. In other words, they operate on their own. Today, credit unions provide many of the same services as commercial and savings banks. Credit unions are nonprofit organizations. This means that all members of the credit union share the profits.

title: Credit and Debt
text:
Sometimes you can’t afford something you need or want. When this happens, you can buy the product or service on credit. Credit is money that is loaned and must be paid back. Usually, credit lenders require the borrower to pay interest. Interest is extra money that a borrower must pay back to the lender in exchange for using their money. It is usually a percentage of the amount of money borrowed.

When you buy something on credit, you are also now in debt. Debt is money you owe when you buy something by borrowing money. Although credit can be helpful, it should be used carefully. Most people must go into debt to make large purchases, like a car or a house, or to pay for college. Some people also choose to go into debt for everyday items like clothes, entertainment, and even food.

Credit cards are another way to make large purchases. When a shopper uses a credit card, they don’t have to pay back the money all at once. Credit cards also have an interest rate, so it’s a good idea to pay back the money quickly. Both banks and credit cards help people make important purchases.

title: Budgeting
text:
There are many choices to make about how to save and spend your money. It is good to have a plan to help make these choices. A plan for using money is called a budget. A budget does two main things. It shows how much money you have and how you are going to use it. Some people write their budgets on paper. Many adults use a computer to make their budgets on a spreadsheet. A spreadsheet is a worksheet that has rows and columns to keep track of money or numbers.

Why Use a Budget?

Most people don't have enough money to buy everything they want. Using a budget makes you think about what you want to do with your money. It also helps keep you from spending more than you have. A budget helps you plan for the future. When you grow up, you may want to buy a new car or some other big item. With a budget, you can make sure to put aside a certain amount of money each month for that big purchase. Opportunity costs are things you give up to get something else. Sometimes this means giving up buying something now to save the money for another purchase later. Or it could mean giving up time spent with friends to work more hours to earn extra money. What would you give up to get something you really want?

Budgets in Action

When you plan a budget, you should try to have a balance between money you earn (income) and money you spend (expenses). You can make a budget for each week, month or even year. To make a budget, think about how much money you will make for the time period of the budget. Then think about things you will need to spend money on. Most people must include money they will spend on housing, clothing, food, and transportation. Of course, you will also want to think about money to spend on things you want. Wanted items are different from needed items because you don’t have to have them to survive. Wanted items include things like movie tickets, video games, and fast food. A good budget will also note the amount of money you will save. Saving money is important. People need to be prepared to pay for things they might need in the future. Many people save for college or retirement.

title: Montgomery Bus Boycott
text:
The frustrations of segregated seating on Montgomery city buses in Alabama were not new. The city laws required African American passengers to sit in the back of the bus and to give up their seats to white riders. These laws were degrading and unjust. They had provoked suffering and anger for a long time.

Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing the bus driver’s request to give up her bus seat to a white person. A prominent African American civil rights leader, E.D. Nixon, decided that Parks should be the central figure of legal action attempting to overturn Montgomery’s segregation laws. At the same time, other civil rights leaders decided to attack the laws using different methods.

An African American women's civil rights group, the Women’s Political Council, organized a boycott of the bus system. A boycott is a voluntary refusal to buy goods or use services from a person or organization to protest. In Montgomery, 75 percent of the city’s bus riders were African American. That was about 40,000 people. On December 5, 1955, all of those people refused to ride the buses. They started a boycott. At the end of the day, civil rights leaders met and decided to continue the boycott until the city met their demands.

Originally, the boycotters were only asking for African American riders to be treated with courtesy. They asked officials to hire more African American bus drivers and to allow the first person in a bus seat to keep their seat. However, segregated sections of the buses would remain. Later, their demands changed. A group of five Montgomery women sued the city, asking that the bus segregation policy be completely removed.

With the majority of Montgomery bus riders refusing to board, the bus company began to lose money, but the city still wouldn't change the laws. The boycott went on for over a year. Finally, in December of 1956, the U.S. Supreme Court supported a lower court’s decision that segregated seating on buses violated the 14th Amendment to the Constitution. Part of this amendment guarantees equal treatment under the law. The court said that meant all riders should be treated the same. All seats had to be open to all riders. This was the successful ending to the 381-day boycott.

title: Civil Rights Organizations
text:
In the fight for civil rights, various organizations were formed to provide direction and leadership to African Americans striving to end injustice. The most well-known of these organizations is the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP). It is one of the oldest civil rights organizations. The NAACP was formed in 1909 as a biracial effort to work for justice for African Americans. The goal of this group is to secure for all people the rights guaranteed in the United States Constitution.

The Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC) was another important civil rights organization. Established in 1957, its purpose was to coordinate the actions of protest groups throughout the South. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. led the organization. It drew much of its support from African American churches. The SCLC also trained local communities in the nonviolent agenda taught and practiced by Dr. King.

In 1960, a group of young African American college students, dedicated to direct nonviolent actions, joined forces. They formed the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC). This student organization worked independently from the SCLC and other organizations. They came up with their own projects and strategies to further the cause of justice for all. The SNCC was involved with the Freedom Riders and voter registration efforts in southern states.

title: Freedom Riders
text:
The first group of Freedom Riders was organized in 1947 to test the enforcement of a U.S. Supreme Court decision. The court had ruled that segregated seating on buses was unconstitutional. African American and white people boarded buses together to ride through the South, testing cities’ compliance with the law.

The Congress of Racial Equality (CORE) revived the Freedom Riders initiative in 1961. They wanted to test another Supreme Court decision from 1960. This ruling said that segregation at terminals for buses that traveled between states was also unconstitutional. This time, women were included among the 13 riders. African American and white riders began their trip in Washington, D.C. They planned to travel through the southern states to New Orleans and stop at bus terminals along the way. African American riders would attempt to use white-only restrooms, lunch counters, and waiting areas.

The ride was fairly uneventful through Virginia and North Carolina. When the riders reached Rock Hill, South Carolina, an African American rider named John Lewis, a white rider named Albert Bigelow, and another African American rider tried to enter a whites-only waiting room. These three were violently attacked by white people waiting in the terminal.

As the ride continued, the group split onto two buses, a Trailways bus and a Greyhound bus. When the Greyhound bus arrived in Anniston, Alabama, a mob of 200 white people was waiting at the bus terminal. The driver kept driving past the terminal. The mob followed in cars. The tires on the bus were blown out. When the bus stopped, someone threw a bomb onto the bus. The Freedom Riders all escaped the burning bus, but then they were attacked by the mob. The Trailways bus riders also met with mob violence when they reached Birmingham, Alabama. The violence increased in Montgomery, Alabama.

Photographs of the burning bus were printed in newspapers and broadcast on television. The nation’s attention was drawn to the Freedom Riders. Hundreds of new Freedom Riders joined the cause. Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy ordered 600 federal marshals to go to Montgomery to stop the increasing violence. Pressure from the government and the shocked public resulted in regulations established by the Interstate Commerce Commission to be enforced. There were no more segregated facilities in bus terminals.

title: Ruby Bridges
text:
Ruby Bridges was born in Mississippi in 1954. When she was only six years old, she changed the world. Ruby was a six-year-old African American girl who integrated an all-white school in New Orleans in 1960.

Ruby and other children had to take a test to determine if they could go to the all-white schools. Ruby was very bright and passed the test, so she headed off to first grade. The New Orleans school board delayed Ruby’s entry into the white school until November. Four federal marshals were sent to the school to escort Ruby. When Ruby tried to go to class, an angry mob tried to keep her out. The marshals had to walk in front of and behind her to protect her. People were yelling and throwing things. Ruby was brave. When Ruby finally got inside she had her own room and teacher. None of the parents would allow their children to be in the room with Ruby. Barbara Henry was the only person who wanted to be her teacher.

Facing such turmoil everyday was difficult. Ms. Henry and Ruby met each school day for the rest of the year.

What does Ruby say about all this today? She says that she had no idea why people hated each other when she was six. She did not understand the concepts of racism and civil rights at the time. She didn't understand what was going on at school.

Today, Ruby Bridges is at the heart of change and equality. She fights for civil rights so that no one will ever have to go through what she went through again.

title: Students Get Involved
text:
In 1950, three years before the Brown v. Board of Education ruling, African American students began taking matters into their own hands. Adkin High School in Kinston, North Carolina was a school for African Americans. The school had no gym or cafeteria. The students were well aware of the advantages the white schools had. When the students at Kinston learned the white high school was going to get a second gymnasium, they were spurred to action.

A group of Adkin students went to the school board to ask for upgrades for their school. The board refused to consider their request. That’s when students decided to take action. John Dudley related, “So, that week, leading to Monday, we strategized. And we had everybody on board, 720 students.”

On Monday, a code phrase was given in the morning announcements. Every student walked out with a protest sign and headed downtown to march. Students refused to return to school for a week. Their actions were noticed. 18 months later, their school was renovated and a new gym was added.

At the same time, Barbara Johns was a sophomore at R.R. Moton High School in Farmville, Virginia. The high school had been built in 1939. It was the only high school for African Americans in the county. It had been designed for 180 students, but it was now overcrowded with 447 students. The roof leaked, there was no gym or cafeteria, and the only heat came from potbellied stoves. Science labs and musical instruments were nonexistent.

Johns decided that this inequality needed to be challenged. She got a group of student leaders together, and they began planning a strike. The students planned everything down to the last detail.

On the day of the strike, the principal received an anonymous phone call causing him to leave the building. Someone called an assembly over the intercom, and all the students and teachers gathered. The teachers were asked to wait outside while Barbara Johns appealed to the student body to join the strike. They did. The entire student body walked out and marched with picket signs.

The march didn’t last long. The students were threatened with arrest for creating a disturbance on public property, but the strike lasted two weeks. The students were supported by the African American community. During this time, they met with the white district superintendent. He told them that Moton was as nice as any other county high school.

Students called the NAACP who sent two lawyers to Farmville. With their help, the students sued to integrate Prince Edward County schools. This suit was later combined with four other lawsuits into what became Brown v. Board of Education.

title: The Cold War
text:
The Soviet Union expanded into Eastern European countries after World War II. In America, many people thought that the Soviets planned to take control of the entire world. On the other hand, the Soviets thought America was interfering in world affairs and trying to strengthen its nuclear arms. The result of this ideological conflict was a Cold War. This was not a war of weapons and armies. It was a war of beliefs, ideas, mutual threats, and suspicion. It was a competition to create and stockpile the most dangerous weapons.

Soviet threats caused President Truman to quadruple the amount of money that America was spending on defense. The money went to strengthen the military and develop atomic weapons technology. The Soviet Union reacted by trying to increase their own atomic weapons production. These actions in both countries began an “arms race.” This was a competition to see who could have the most destructive weapons aimed at the other. This created a very dangerous threat to the world.

Each country wanted to know what the other was doing. Projects became top secret. A network of spies was created by the United States and the United Soviet Socialist Republic to find out what the other country was doing.

During World War II, the U.S. government organized the country’s first large-scale spy effort. It was called the OSS, the Office of Strategic Services. OSS agents did many things. They carried out sabotage behind enemy lines and decoded messages. They infiltrated enemy groups to gain information. Agents even worked undercover in enemy territory to gain information that would help the Allies win the war.

Following the war, as the tension increased between the Soviet Union and the U.S., the OSS became the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). During the Cold War, spies were employed by the CIA to gather information about enemy technology, strategies, and how the enemy was spying on us. Agents were also used to pass false information to enemies of the U.S. government to confuse and mislead them about American technology and plans of action.

The popular media even used the Cold War and spycraft in movies, novels, and television shows. One of the most popular spies during this era was James Bond. He was the main character in a series of spy novels written by an Englishman named Ian Fleming. Bond was a master spy for the British equivalent of the CIA. The British spy organization was called MI6. These novels were made into movies in which Bond used all kinds of amazing spy gadgets.

None of Bond’s gadgets were any more spectacular than some of the real gadgets from the Cold War. Some of these are on display in the Spy Museum in Washington, D.C. The museum displays gadgets such as a pistol that looks like a tube of lipstick, a camera hidden in a cigarette lighter, and a radio transmitter in the heel of a shoe. A hollow silver coin could be used to hide an important message. These items may not seem so amazing compared to today’s electronic gadgets. However, in the 1950s and 1960s, they were the height of new technology.

America entered several regional conflicts during the Cold War period. There was the Korean War that began in 1950 and ended in 1953. Then U.S. troops fought in the Vietnam War from 1965 through 1975. The U.S. became involved in these wars in an effort to prevent the spread of communism into these countries. The Cold War years ended in 1991 when the Soviet Union collapsed, but the threat of nuclear war has never gone away.

title: The United States' Response to the Cold War
text:
How did the Cold War impact the economy and politics in the United States? For much of the Cold War, the United States experienced economic prosperity. World War II brought the United States out of the Great Depression. The Great Depression was a period of economic hardship that impacted the United States in the 1930s. During World War II, production increased, and the job market boomed.

Soldiers returned from the war with funds to purchase luxury items including homes, automobiles, and appliances. Banks offered affordable home loans, and housing communities sprang up in suburbs, or areas located near urban cities, across the country. Many women who had worked outside the home during wartime quit their jobs to be full-time, stay-at-home wives and mothers. Others stayed in the workforce.

During the 1950s and 1960s, middle-class families had money to spend on luxuries they couldn’t afford before World War II. With many people in the market for goods that made life easier, businesses offered inventions and products like never before. Televisions and radios became more affordable and connected Americans to the wider world. New children’s toys such as Barbie dolls, hula hoops, and Mr. Potato Head flooded the market. All of these new inventions and forms of technology changed U.S. culture in many ways.

title: Redstone Arsenal and Missile Development
text:
Redstone Arsenal was built in Huntsville, Alabama, at the beginning of World War II. An arsenal is a place where weapons are made or stored, and this arsenal was built to make chemical weapons. After World War II, the plant stopped production for a while.

It didn’t take long for the U.S. to realize that its greatest threat came from the Soviet Union and its development of new weapons. Then the Korean War crisis brought an urgent need for the United States to further advance its weapons. The U.S. brought German engineers and scientists to Redstone Arsenal to continue their work. Here, these scientists built the Redstone Rocket. A later model, the Jupiter-C missile, took the first U.S. satellite into space in 1958.

During the Cold War of the 1960s and 1970s, Redstone Arsenal was home to the U.S. Army Missile Command (MICOM) and 19 major missile systems, including missiles used in later conflicts. Today, Redstone Arsenal is home to the Army’s missile testing and development program.

title: America Loses Three Great Men
text:
The Civil Rights Movement in the United States was a time when Americans fought against segregation laws. While much of the country supported the positive changes, some people violently protested.

John F. Kennedy became president of the United States in 1961. While he was president, he worked for equal rights for all Americans. On November 22, 1963, President Kennedy was riding in a convertible through the streets of Dallas, Texas, when he was killed by a gunman.

Martin Luther King Jr. was a major leader in the Civil Rights Movement. In 1955, he joined the protest over the arrest of Rosa Parks. He led a year-long boycott of the Montgomery city bus service. His influence continued to grow as he supported other nonviolent protests.

In 1963, King spoke to a crowd of 250,000 people at the March on Washington. Some people did not agree with King's beliefs. King was killed on April 4, 1968. His death caused riots around the country. President Lyndon B. Johnson spoke out against the violence and supported the Fair Housing Act legislation in honor of King’s work.

Violence was also used against other politicians who supported civil rights. John F. Kennedy’s younger brother, Robert Kennedy, announced that he would run for president in 1968. He planned to fight for civil rights as president. Shortly after his announcement, he was killed. His death occurred only two months after that of Martin Luther King Jr. The assassination of these three prominent leaders made it clear that the country was suffering from an inability to agree on political matters.

President John F. Kennedy, Martin Luther King Jr., and Robert Kennedy were American leaders who believed that all people deserved to be treated equally. While their deaths were tragic, their legacies live on and inspire equality for all people.

title: The Columbian Exchange
text:
In 1494, one man who had sailed across the Atlantic Ocean returned home with all sorts of wild stories. He described the new world he had seen, full of strange plants, animals, and foods. He talked about the people he had met there. This man was not Christopher Columbus or a member of his crew. He was a Taíno from the Bahamas whom Columbus had captured and taken back to Spain. We don’t know his real name, but Columbus gave him the name Diego Colón.

After returning home, Colón told his friends and family about Spain. He described “the great cities and fortresses and churches” and “the people and horses and animals.” He saw strange “lands and food ... and bullfighting.” All were new to him, just like native peoples and their homelands were new to Europeans. As people traveled between the continents, they were exchanging ideas about technology, religion, and ways of life.

As European explorers reached different parts of North America, people from different groups, like the Iroquois and Patuxet, were brought across the ocean and saw Europe. People in the Americas and in Europe were not just curious about each other. As soon as they met, many saw new opportunities to meet their economic wants and needs. The people on the two sides of the Atlantic quickly exchanged goods, people, plants, animals and diseases.

This exchange between the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia is called the Columbian Exchange. It is named after Christopher Columbus. The Columbian Exchange had a huge impact on life for people all around the world. Without it, Italy would never have invented pizza, and Ireland would never have grown potatoes. American Indians would never have ridden on horseback.

Animals like horses, cattle, sheep, and pigs changed economic life in the Americas. Farm animals became new food sources. Horses changed the way tribes like the Sioux and the Comanche hunted and traveled. Riding horses was a much faster form of transportation than following bison herds on foot.

European settlers also brought sugarcane, olives, citrus, bananas, and even honeybees with them. Columbus brought sugarcane to Hispaniola in 1493. Sugarcane grew well in the Americas and sold well in Europe.

Many plants from the Americas also had a big impact on Europe, Africa, and Asia. For example, American plants like potatoes, tomatoes, and corn changed how people ate. On both sides of the Atlantic, new plants on farms and in settlements often spread and changed even what grew in the wild. The world was truly never the same because of the Columbian Exchange.

title: Life in the Soviet Union
text:
By the end of the 1950s, the Soviet Union had become one of the largest and most powerful nations in the world. It covered nearly one sixth of the Earth’s land area. The Soviets had 15 nations under its control by 1960. The Eastern Bloc countries that were controlled by Russia became the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, or USSR. This is the acronym used throughout the Cold War.

After World War II until 1953, the Soviet Union was led by Joseph Stalin. He built up the Soviet Union to create a military and industrial stronghold. Under Stalin’s control, the government took over all factories, farms, mines, and other industries. The people were not allowed to have their own businesses or earn their own profits. The government planners decided how much of a certain item would be produced each year. They decided what the price would be, and how much each worker would be paid. The government guaranteed that everyone would have a job. However, that often meant a low-paying, unpleasant job.

The Communist Party was the only political party allowed. When elections were held, there was only one choice on the ballot. A small minority of people held official membership in the Communist Party. Those people enjoyed many privileges. They lived in the nicest homes. They could get many Western goods that other citizens couldn’t get.

For the majority of Soviet citizens, life was difficult. There were constant shortages of goods. There was also not much variety in what was available. Often there was only one type of laundry detergent, or ice cream flavor, or brand of coffee to buy. Going shopping meant hours of waiting in long lines hoping there would still be something left to buy when their turn came.

Wages were low in the Soviet Union, but rent, goods, and services were cheaper than in the West. Housing was in short supply, though. Often two or three generations of the same family lived together in a three-room apartment. The wait to get an apartment could be years.

Child daycare was provided free by the government. Usually both parents needed to work to make enough to care for a family. Free daycare gave them one less thing to worry about. The health care system was good. Health care was also provided by the government. It was free for everyone, and it proved to be good care, though it did not rise to the quality of Western health care systems.

Individual human rights of citizens always came second to the interests of the government as a whole. There was basically no freedom of speech, press, or assembly. The practice of religion was discouraged. People could not travel outside of the USSR without specific government permission. The government secret police regularly used listening devices in telephones and hidden in homes to spy on millions of citizens. People were encouraged to report their neighbors if they violated any government restrictions. People in the USSR lived with a climate of fear in a highly restricted society.

Joseph Stalin was Premier of the country. He was brutal in his actions to the people. He took away all private land and livestock. He forced farmers to work on government-controlled collective farms. Stalin believed that these state-run farms would increase agricultural production. The opposite proved to be true. Stalin also moved to create an industrial economy in the country. The industry benefited the leaders of government. Production of goods was limited. The average citizen in the USSR had little freedom and little liberty.

title: Communism in China
text:
Communist China is largely credited to a man named Mao Zedong. He fought in wars and voiced his strong communist opinion in the early 1900s. By October 1949, communists were victorious in taking over China with Mao as their leader, and everything changed. Industry, farms, business, and resources came under state ownership. When individual citizens protested, they were mercilessly suppressed. Initially, emerging communist China received aid from the Soviet Union. Over time, relations began to quiet down and Mao Zedong embarked on his journey to lead China to its own form of communism by launching the Great Leap Forward.

The Great Leap Forward (1958)

The Great Leap Forward was a movement led by Mao Zedong to create a more “Chinese” communism (as opposed to a Soviet Union communism) and fix the country's agricultural problems. Due to China's dense population, there was limited farmland. China was unable to gain capital through the sale of crops. Without this capital, they were unable to buy machinery to industrialize. In 1958, Mao attempted to assemble labor forces to improve production on farms and in industries. He wanted to use more manpower instead of machines to increase productivity. However, productivity declined. This, coupled with poor harvests, created famine and caused the deaths of over 40 million people. Mao was forced to abandon the policy and looked weak in front of his followers.

The Cultural Revolution (1966)

Mao Zedong could not accept defeat. After the Great Leap Forward failed, he started the Cultural Revolution in 1966. He destroyed much of China's cultural heritage, trying to rid the country of tainted elements. He feared educated people like doctors or professors, who were more likely to criticize his leadership. His plan was to tap into China's urban youth and have them do the work. Adolescents were organized into groups known as the Red Guards. The Red Guards attacked Chinese bourgeois (middle-class property owners) who did not share Mao's vision of communism. Close to two million people died as a result of this movement. Industrial production also dropped about 12 percent during the 10 years that the Cultural Revolution existed.

Tiananmen Square (1989)

Reform started to happen in the years after Mao's death in 1976. New leaders emerged and the fight to gain control from communist leadership began. The death of leader Hu Yaobang resulted in the Tiananmen Square massacre in Beijing in 1989. Young people came to Tiananmen Square to mourn the loss of a leader with democratic ideals. Students started a peaceful protest to end government corruption. Weeks of protesting brought millions of people to Tiananmen Square.

Government officials were displeased with the turnout and the pro-democracy message of the students. The Chinese national troops were sent to break up the demonstration with violence. This action by the government left other world governments in shock. China suffered economic and political consequences for their actions.

Positive Effects During Communist Rule

You may be wondering how Mao Zedong could stay in power for close to 30 years. The people did have some positive effects from his policies. He abolished traditional foot binding for women, which had left them unable to walk normally. He provided assistance to students who could not afford an education. He also promoted the freedom to choose in marriages (eliminating arranged marriages). He changed labor policies making equal rights for women. These positive effects helped to keep a following for Mao throughout his years.

Impact of Communism in China

Currently, China still has the largest communist political party with over 80 million followers. The government controls what students learn in school by controlling materials. The government also controls what is available on television or radio. For Chinese citizens, it is beneficial to join the Communist Party. Members have benefits such as advancement in their career, better access to information, and more of an influence in decision-making.
