title: What Is Culture?
text: Culture is the beliefs, traditions, and celebrations of a group of people. There are many characteristics of culture. Architecture, arts, literature, music, and language are some. Religion, clothing, and food are others. Culture reflects a group’s way of life. It includes things they produce and use. It also includes the skills and traditions passed down to younger generations. People use resources around them to meet their needs. Local plant and animal resources are used to make food, clothing, and shelter. A group’s culture develops using these resources.

title: Essential Question
text: What is culture?

title: Language
text: Language is an important part of culture. When people move, they bring their languages with them. For example, explorers from Spain traveled around the world. Now, people speak Spanish all over the world. Early pilgrims to the United States spoke English. American Indian populations in these places now speak English as well as their native languages. Another example is the French language. It is an official language in 29 countries. The movement of language impacts culture.

title: Religion
text: Religion is another part of culture. Religion is a system of beliefs that a group of people share. Different cultures have different religions. Five worldwide religions are Buddhism, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Christianity. There are many other important religions throughout the world. Religion impacts culture in the ways that people celebrate.

title: Celebrations
text: One way people express culture is through celebrations. Geography influences how people celebrate and what the celebration is about. Some cultures celebrate the seasons. Other cultures celebrate planting and harvesting crops. As people move from place to place, they bring their cultures and celebrations with them.

title: Clothing
text: Environments people live in affect the way they dress. People in hot climates wear lightweight clothing to keep cool. People in colder climates wear heavy clothing to keep warm. The material of clothing reflects local resources. Grasses, palm fronds, pigskin, and cloth made from natural fibers are some things people use. Dye for cloth can be made from local plants. Traditional or ceremonial clothing is often very well made and decorated. It reflects the traditional skills of the people.

title: Comparing Cultures
text: Complete the web about you and your culture. Share it with a member of your class. Compare how your cultures are similar and different.

title: Architecture and Culture
text:
Natural resources and climate affect the types of houses people create. Traditionally, people built houses using local resources. They also built houses to suit their climate.

People built houses with the natural resources they had. In forest areas, people built log cabins. This is because there were many trees around them. Some desert communities built brick houses. Bricks are made of clay, which is abundant in some deserts. In areas where it floods frequently, people often build houses on stilts. Native tribes in the Arctic built igloos using snow.

In hot climates, people built round mud houses. The mud insulates the house from the heat. The shape allows air to move around. Some people used thatched roofs. Thatched roofs help heat to escape quickly. Some people build houses on stumps to allow air to flow under the house. This cools the house. In both hot and cold climates, some people build houses underground. The Earth’s temperature stays cooler in summer and warmer in winter. This helps people stay cooler and warmer during the year.

title: Music
text:
Music is important in every culture. It plays many roles from when we are born until we grow old. Parents sing lullabies to their children. There are also songs that help children learn. The words in a song may teach life’s lessons as well.

In many communities, music is also part of storytelling. It is used to set the mood of a story. It may also be used as sound effects. For example, the sound of a shaker may represent falling rain. In addition, music and dance keep children from falling asleep during a story.

Music is performed at festivals and celebrations. People play music and dance to celebrate the meaning of the occasion.

Religion is another part of culture that uses music. People use music to worship and to honor their faith. Some people also use music to perform rituals.

Music helps the economy of communities. People earn a living by playing music. Some people also use music to sell goods and services.

People who play music may become important role models. They use their fame to inspire other people to serve the community.

title: Culture and Transportation
text:
There were many reasons for people to move in every ancient culture. Walking was the first means of getting from one place to another. However, the environment sometimes made it difficult for people to walk to some places. As a result, communities developed means of transport based on the natural obstacles in their environment.

Communities that needed to cross bodies of water built canoes, kayaks, and gondolas.

Some communities had to cross large, sandy deserts. They used camels. Dog sleds were used in very cold climates. They used dogs that can survive the climate. Horses and elephants were also used in places where they were appropriate.

Today, some communities no longer use the means of transport they began with. However, they celebrate these as part of their history. Festivals and other important ceremonies feature these means of transport. They are now part of the culture of the people. Some have become tourist attractions.

title: Recreation
text:
Recreation is what people do to relax and have fun. Sports, sightseeing, music, dance, and drama are all types of recreation. Every community has forms of recreation that have become part of its culture.

Many of the games people play today started because of traditional cultural practices. Lacrosse started as part of Native American culture. Before soccer became a sport, many cultures had games that involved kicking objects. Dog sledding was a means of transport. It has now become a form of recreation.

Many of the activities people do for fun are based on the environment. For example, you cannot have a dog sled race in the desert. Hiking mostly takes place on mountain trails. Also, fishing only takes place where there is a body of water.

title: Settlement
text:
People move for different reasons. Throughout history, people have explored new places to find resources. Most people move to places they already know about. For example, many people from Europe moved to North America after explorers traveled here. We call this kind of movement from one place to another migration.

A number of factors affect where people settle. The climate plays an important role. The amount and types of resources available are also important. Historically, communities grew around water and other important resources. Water is necessary for people to survive. It is needed for growing food and for transportation. Places with more resources can support larger populations.

title: Essential Question
text: How does the environment influence settlement patterns?

title: Migration Patterns
text:
Look at the population map. It shows patterns of human settlement across North America. Most people settle where the climate, resources, and physical features are favorable.

Look at the colors on the population density map. The white areas of the map show where very few people live. Why do you think that is? What do you know about the physical features, climate, and resources of those places?

The dark purple areas of the map show where the most people live. Why do you think that is? What do you know about the physical features, climate, and resources of those places?

title: Canada’s Physical and Human Features
text:
Canada has many physical features. Each feature is important. Often, they provide necessities like food, water, transportation, and trade. Some of these physical features include the St. Lawrence River and the Hudson Bay. They also include the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, the Great Lakes, and the Rocky Mountains.

The border between Canada and the United States is very long. In fact, it is the longest border between two countries in the world. Canada is divided into sections. They are called provinces. Canada has 10 provinces and three territories. Territories are sections of the country with fewer people. People have built many bridges over Canada’s waterways. One famous bridge is the Capilano Suspension Bridge. It hangs over the Capilano River. This bridge was first built in 1889. It is 450 feet long.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe Canada?

title: Canada’s Climates
text:
The climate in Canada gets colder as you go north. Northern Canada is extremely cold. Very few people live in the north. In fact, 90 percent of Canadians live within 100 miles of the border with the United States. Canada covers a large part of the North American continent. The climates differ, or vary, from one area to the next.

Polar

The northern part of Canada is polar. This means it has very cold temperatures and little rainfall.

Continental

The middle areas of Canada are mostly continental. This means they have short summers and long, cold winters with lots of rainfall.

Temperate

Along the coastlines, the climate is temperate. While the summers are pleasant, these regions can be very cold throughout the winter.

Dry

Small parts of Canada have a dry climate. The winters here are cold, and the summers are warm and dry. There is very little rainfall, though it's not considered a "desert."

title: Canada’s Biomes
text: There are a wide variety of plants and animals in Canada's biomes. There are different types of forests in the forest biome of Canada. Squirrels, moose, and wolves live in these forests. There are also many pine trees in the forests. In the mountain biome, there are grizzly bears and cougars. Trout, pike, and bass are some of the types of fish that live in Canada’s freshwater biome. The tundra biome is home to polar bears, snowy owls, and arctic hares. Very few plants live in the tundra because it is cold and dry. One plant that can survive in the tundra is moss.

title: Canada’s Natural Resources
text: Canada is a land rich in natural resources. The vast forests in the country provide many natural resources. The trees in the forests provide raw materials for lumber and pulp for paper. The lumber industry provides jobs for 10 percent of Canada’s population. Alberta and the eastern coast are known for their oil and natural gas. Minerals are exported from Canada to other places. These minerals are nickel, silver, and gold.

title: Canada's Landmarks
text:
The Rocky Mountains form a beautiful mountain range. They are in the western part of North America, through the United States and Canada. They are often called the Rockies for short. The Rockies also have many streams and rivers. These help provide water and food to animals like beavers, moose, and deer. The Rockies are home to four national parks. Many campers and tourists visit these national parks each year. The Rockies are one of Canada’s natural landmarks.

Stanley Park is in British Columbia, Canada. It was created in the year 1888. It is the third-largest urban park in North America. About eight million people visit the park each year. One man-made landmark of the park is its many totem poles. Totem poles are symbols of the Pacific Northwest Native Americans. Each tribe had its own designs and styles. Historians think the Haida, Tlingit, and Tsimshian tribes were the first to make totem poles. Families used them to help tell important stories. Totems also honored the special relationship families had with different animals. Stanley Park and its totem poles are part of Canada’s important man-made landmarks.

title: Canada: Mixed Cultures
text:
Native Americans have lived in Canada for thousands of years. The First Nations are the people of Native tribes who lived in Canada before Europeans. Over 600 different cultural groups make up the First Nations. Bannock is a type of bread that came from the First Nations people. Pemmican is another First Nations food. It is made by mixing dried meat with fat, berries, and, sometimes, nuts. Both of these foods are still eaten in Canada today. There are also over 30 different Native American languages spoken by the First Nations peoples. In Nunavut, Inuktitut and Inuinnaqtun are official languages alongside English and French.

It has only been in the past 500 years that immigrants from all over the world made Canada their home. In 1534, explorer Jacques Cartier claimed northern North America for France. French settlers followed. They called the land they settled on New France. Later, England took over New France and renamed it Canada. But French settlers and culture remained. Today, almost one-fourth of Canadians are of French ancestry. French is the official language in Quebec. There, people eat traditional French-Canadian foods. One type of food is a meat pie called tourtière. Another is called poutine. It is made with French fries and gravy.

Today, Canadians can trace their roots to almost every continent of the world. Canada has a variety of customs, religions, and languages.

title: Mexico’s Physical and Human Features
text:
Mexico is the northernmost country of Latin America. It is very rich in history. The ruins of ancient civilizations attract many tourists. There are many cities that attract visitors. Mexico City is the city where the most people live. In fact, more people live in Mexico City than in any other city in North America. The warm, sandy beaches bring many tourists as well.

Mexico has water on two sides. The northern border is shared with the United States. Guatemala and Belize lie to the southeast. Mexico has mountains and volcanoes. The Sierra Madre Occidental and the Sierra Madre Oriental are two mountain ranges in Mexico. Mexico also has high and rolling plateaus. It has tropical rain forests, dry deserts, and fertile valleys.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe Mexico?

title: Mexico’s Climates
text:
The climate in Mexico ranges from a dry climate to a tropical climate. There are big differences in these climates. Some are very wet, and some are very dry. Mexico is divided into three main climates. This is what each climate is like:

Tropical

The average temperature is above 77 degrees Fahrenheit. The average yearly rainfall is about 50 inches.

Temperate

The average temperature is 64 to 77 degrees Fahrenheit. The average yearly rainfall is about 25 inches.

Dry

The average temperatures of a dry climate vary. Some places are very cold, and some are very hot. The dry climate has little rain.

title: Mexico’s Biomes
text: There are different climates in Mexico. This means there is a wide variety of plants and animals living there. There are forests in the forest biome of Mexico. One of the most famous animals in Mexico is the monarch butterfly. Every year, millions of monarch butterflies migrate to Mexico. The butterflies hibernate in the forest for the winter. Some of these forests have pine trees and bears. Some of these forests are rainforests that have huge, broadleaf trees and monkeys. Rabbits, snakes, and scorpions live in the sandy desert biomes of Mexico. Whales, rays, and tropical fish are some of the many animals that live in Mexico’s oceans.

title: Mexico’s Natural Resources
text: Mexico is rich in natural resources. Some of its biggest natural resources are silver, copper, oil, and agricultural products. Agriculture is the business of growing crops and raising livestock. Mexico has a diversity of agricultural crops. The biggest produce market in North America is in Mexico. The United States gets much of its produce from Mexico. Some of Mexico’s main crops are corn, tomatoes, and chili peppers. Mexico has two special crops that are rarely grown outside of the country. They are called maguey and henequen. They are both kinds of agave plants. Mexico also has some highly productive oil fields. Oil is an important natural resource. A lot of oil is used to make fuel for cars.

title: Mexico's Landmarks
text:
One very famous place in Mexico is called Teotihuacán. The name means “The City of the Gods” in the Aztec language. However, the city was not built by the Aztec people. It was built by a much older culture whose name no one knows. The city was built about 2,000 years ago. About 200,000 people lived in this city, making it one of the largest cities in the world at the time. The city has several pyramids, but the largest is the Pyramid of the Sun. This pyramid is one of the largest in North America. It is 216 feet tall. This city is one of Mexico’s ancient man-made landmarks.

Did you know that Mexico is home to the world’s largest underground river system? The Sac Actun river system is 95 miles long. It flows through a maze of underground limestone caves. These caves can be accessed by holes in the earth called cenotes. There are over 100 cenotes leading to the river system. The Mayan people used cenotes for all of their water needs. Cenotes are one of Mexico’s natural landmarks.

title: Mexico: Mixed Cultures
text:
Mexico was and is home to many Native American people. The Maya were one of the early peoples. They built large pyramids. Many of these pyramids still stand today. The Aztecs were one of the later Native American peoples. The Aztecs once lived in a large city that is now the capital city of the country, Mexico City. The Aztecs were conquered by Spanish explorers from Europe in the 1500s. Many Spanish people moved to Mexico after this time. The cultures of the Native Americans and the Spanish Europeans mixed. Many Mexican people are mestizos. Mestizo means having a mix of Native American and Spanish heritage.

Language

Spanish is the official language of Mexico. However, there are more than 50 Native American languages in Mexico. These languages are still spoken today.

Food

Mexico’s food is a mix of Spanish and Native American food. Corn, beans, and squash were eaten by the Native Americans. They are still eaten by Mexicans today. Rice, beef, and onions were brought to Mexico by the Spanish. They are also still eaten by Mexicans today.

title: Physical and Human Features of the Caribbean
text:
The Caribbean is south and east of the continental United States. This region has 26 island nations. There are lakes and rivers on many of these islands. There are also mountains, volcanoes, coral reefs, and rainforests in the Caribbean. The climate is tropical and mild. Tourists come to visit the region year-round to see the beautiful physical features there.

The population of the Caribbean varies greatly depending on the place. It ranges from over 10 million people in Cuba to under 5,000 people in Montserrat. Most of the countries in the Caribbean manufacture and process oil and agricultural goods for other countries. Many of the people living on the islands work in the tourism industry.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe the Caribbean?

title: Climate of the Caribbean
text:
The Caribbean has a mostly tropical climate. Tropical climates are warm, wet, and humid. The average temperature stays almost the same all year. In most places in the Caribbean, there is a dry season and a wet season. The dry months are usually from February to May, and June to November is the wet season. Hurricanes can happen during the wet season.

The temperatures vary in the Caribbean islands. However, the average high temperature is about 82°F (28°C). Generally the best time to visit the Caribbean is during its driest months.

There are many islands in the Caribbean. The amount of rain that falls depends on the physical environment of the specific island. The islands of Aruba, Bonaire, and Curaçao get the least amount of rain. In fact, their climate can be very dry. These islands are also much less likely to experience hurricanes.

title: Biomes of the Caribbean
text:
The Caribbean has freshwater, forest, and mountain biomes. Most of the plants growing there are tropical. There are rainforests with many plants and animals here. Parrots and monkeys live in the rainforests. Palm trees grow on the sandy beaches.

The ocean has many animals that live in salt water, such as sea turtles and rays. Many sea animals make their homes in and around coral reefs. A great variety of plants, animals, and insects form the wildlife of the Caribbean. The Caribbean is an example of a diverse biome.

title: Natural Resources of the Caribbean
text: The location and climate of the Caribbean make it rich in natural resources. The soil and temperature on many Caribbean islands make them great places to grow bananas, sugar cane, and coffee. Because the islands are located in the ocean, fish are a plentiful resource as well. The islands are also places where sailing ships get supplies of fresh water and food. There are natural oil deposits in the earth that are mined and then used.

title: Landmarks of the Caribbean
text:
One very famous place in the Caribbean is called the Caguana Ceremonial Site. It is located in Puerto Rico. This is where the Taíno Native American people built ancient structures out of stone. Many of these stones have beautiful carvings called petroglyphs. The site was used for different things. It was used for ceremonies, religion, and ball games. The ball games had ceremonial significance and influenced important decisions for the Taíno. The site is around 800 years old. The site has a museum with Taíno artifacts. It also has a garden featuring the plants the Taíno used for food. The site is one of the Caribbean’s ancient man-made landmarks.

Did you know that the Caribbean is home to the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. forest system? It is called the El Yunque National Forest. It gets its name from the Taíno god Yukiyú. This forest is located in Puerto Rico. It is rich in plants and animals. There are 23 plants and animals there that are not found anywhere else in the world. Eight large rivers flow through this rainforest. About 600,000 people visit this rainforest every year. Rainforests are one of the Caribbean's natural landmarks.

title: The Caribbean: Mixed Cultures
text:
Most people living in the Caribbean have mixed ancestry coming from different places. The Caribbean was and is home to many Native American people. The Arawak and Caribs are a few of these groups. Africans were enslaved and brought to the Caribbean to work shortly after Columbus arrived. Europeans immigrated to the Caribbean to take advantage of the natural resources there. Native peoples of the Caribbean, enslaved Africans, and European immigrants all influenced the culture of the Caribbean. Most people living there today are descended from one or a mix of these groups. This mix of cultures has influenced language and religion.

Language

European languages like Spanish, French, and English are usually the official languages of the Caribbean Islands. People also speak native languages and Creoles, which are mixes of multiple languages.

Religion

The Spanish, Portuguese, and other Europeans brought Christianity to the Caribbean. Santeria and Rasta are two religions that came to the Caribbean from Africa. Hinduism was brought to the Caribbean from Asia. There are many different religions being practiced in the Caribbean today.

title: What Is a Region?
text:
We organize the Earth into regions to help us to learn about our world. A region is an area that has similar characteristics. Some regions are organized based on their physical features, such as landforms, climate, or biomes. Some regions are organized by their human features, like population, culture, or language. We also organize regions based on hemispheres and continents.

The United States is often divided into five regions. These regions are organized based on state political boundaries. They are the Northeast, the Southeast, the Midwest, the Southwest, and the West.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe regions of the United States?

title: The Northeast
text:
Physical features

The landforms of the Northeast include highlands, mountains, and plains. The Green Mountains and the White Mountains in this region are part of the Appalachian Mountains. Niagara Falls and the Adirondack Mountains are also landforms in the region. The Atlantic Ocean, Lake Erie, the Hudson and Androscoggin Rivers are some of the bodies of water in the Northeast.

Human Features

The Northeast Region has some famous human features as well. One World Trade Center, which is 1,776 feet high, is in this region. The Erie Canal and the Statue of Liberty are also here.

Climate and Biomes

Winters are cold in the Northeast. Summers, however, are warm or hot. The region gets a lot of precipitation. Pines and chestnut oak trees abound in the region. Some of the animals found there are black bears, red foxes, white-tailed deer, and chipmunks.

Natural Resources

Natural resources like lumber, granite, and coal are abundant in the Northeast. Other resources there include seafood, maple trees, and quartz.

Culture

The Northeast Region is diverse in culture. Food, clothing, arts, and celebrations from all over the world can be seen in the Northeast. Native American culture still thrives in some parts of the region.

title: The Southeast
text:
Physical features

Mountains, wetlands, plains, highlands, and plateaus are some of the physical features of the Southeast Region. The Smoky Mountains and the Okefenokee Swamp are both in this region. The bodies of water in the region include the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. There are also rivers, lakes, and streams.

Human Features

The human features of the Southeast Region include large cities with big industrial areas. There are also agricultural areas and large shopping centers. Walt Disney World, The Mercedes-Benz SuperDome, and Cape Lookout Lighthouse are found in this region.

Climate and Biomes

Although winters are mild in the region, summers are hot. It rains a lot. However, there are times when the region experiences drought. Citrus, pines, and hardwood trees are some of the plants that grow in the region. Panthers and alligators thrive in the swamps. Other wildlife commonly found in the region are salamanders, bats, and black bears.

Natural Resources

The region has soil that is rich in minerals. Peanuts, cotton, and sugar cane grow well in the region. Other natural resources include oil and natural gas, coal, and seafood.

Culture

The culture of the Southeast Region is diverse. It grew out of African American, European, Cajun, and Hispanic cultures. Today, there are cultures from all over the world in the Southeast Region.

title: The Midwest
text:
Physical Features

There are 12 states in the Midwest. Peninsulas, the Great Plains, and highlands make the Midwest unique. Part of the Ozark Mountains is in this region. So are the Badlands. The bodies of water in the region include four of the Great Lakes. Many rivers also flow through the region, including the Mississippi River.

Human Features

Three of the human features of the Midwest are the Mackinac Bridge, the So Locks, and Mount Rushmore. There are also large residential, industrial, commercial, and agricultural areas.

Climate and Biomes

Climate in the region varies from east to west. The western part of the Midwest is drier. Winters in the region are mostly cold. Summers are hot or warm. There are not a lot of forests in the Midwest. There are, however, many types of grass and shrubs. Mesquite and sagebrush are common in this region. Wildlife found in the region includes bison, elk, wolves, black bears, prairie dogs, and white pelicans.

Natural Resources

The Midwest has a lot of natural resources. The soil is rich. There is also an abundance of water. Coal, oil, natural gas, and precious metals are other natural resources in the Midwest.

Culture

The Midwest has people from all over the world. Native American culture was the first to grow in the Midwest. Many Europeans came later and brought their culture. Each group from Europe brought its own style of building. Languages from different parts of the world can be heard in the region. Food, celebrations, and art come from all over the world.

title: Essential Question
text: How can I describe regions of the United States?

title: The Southwest
text:
Physical Features

The Southwest Region covers Arizona, Oklahoma, New Mexico, and Texas. The Gulf of Mexico is one of the main bodies of water in the region. The Santa Cruz River, the Gila River, and the Colorado River also flow through the region. There are lakes and streams as well.

The region has plains, plateaus, highlands, mountains, and deserts. The Grand Canyon, the Petrified Forest, and the White Sands are in this region.

Human Features

Some examples of human features in the region are the Alamo and Pueblo-style houses. The region also has dams and reservoirs, like Coolidge Dam and Elephant Butte Reservoir. They help provide power and water to people in this region.

Climate and Biomes

Much of the Southwest is very hot in the summer and warm in the winter. The mountainous areas get colder. Much of the Southwest gets very little rain or snow. Plants that grow here are mostly shrubs and brushes. However, there are yucca and cactus plants. There are also juniper and evergreen oak trees. Some of the animals that survive conditions in the region are the Gila monster, glossy snake, and Albert’s squirrel. There are black bears, elk, and bighorn sheep as well.

Natural Resources

The main resources of the Southwest Region are oil, natural gas, coal, and uranium. The soil is also good for raising some crops and cattle.

Culture

Native American and Spanish cultures are common in the region. People from all over the world have brought their culture to the region. However, place names, celebrations, food, and agriculture show a lot of Native American and Spanish influence.

title: The West
text:
Physical Features

The West has mountains, volcanoes, plains, highlands, and waterfalls. Mount Saint Helens, the Rocky Mountains, Bryce Canyon, Pikes Peak, and Redwood Forest are in this region. Earthquakes sometimes occur here. Bodies of water in the region include the Pacific Ocean, the Great Salt Lake, the Colorado River, and the Yukon River.

Human Features

Some of the human features here are the Hoover Dam, the Space Needle, and the Golden Gate Bridge.

Climate and Biomes

The West has many different climates. The northern part is usually very wet and the southern part is usually very dry. The temperature is warm year-round in one part of the region. In another part, it is cold year-round. Plants found in the region include coconut palms, cedar, redwood, and Joshua trees. Animals like whales, caribou, and moose thrive in the West Region. So do animals like mountain lions, bears, monk seals, and nene geese.

Natural Resources

The diverse soils in the region produce pineapples, potatoes, and apples. The Pacific Ocean provides seafood. Other natural resources in the West include lumber, oil, natural gas, and precious minerals.

Culture

Native American culture is the first to have grown in this region. It can still be felt in the names of places and animals. However, cultures from all over the world are also present. There are pieces of art, music, food, and celebrations from all over the world.
