title: What Is Research?
text:
Research means studying something thoroughly. There are many steps in research. These include asking questions, gathering answers, organizing information, and presenting ideas. When you are doing research, start with questions. You need to figure out what you want to know. This means you need to ask questions. Then, you begin seeking answers. You gather information to answer your questions. Next, you need to organize the information. This means presenting your information in a way that others can understand easily.

Let’s practice. Your challenge is to investigate how people perceive places. Perceive means how people see or think about something. An example is what someone thinks about America. People may form these opinions by talking to Americans, listening to the news, or reading stories, poems, or legends.

How might you research what people perceive?

title: Essential Question
text: How do people view places?

title: Ask Questions
text:
Questions help you focus your research. For example, your research question is: How do people view a place? Your first question would be: Which place? Let’s research how people perceive Florida.

Questions also help you decide what information you need to look for. What questions could you ask to help you answer your research question?

title: Gather Answers
text:
There are many primary and secondary sources you can use to find information. There are books, journals, and images. You can also use technology and maps. Artifacts and information at museums may also help. In addition, you can interview someone who knows about your topic.

The best way to understand an issue is to use several sources and perspectives to research it. Look for sources that are credible and reliable. A credible source is unbiased and backed by evidence. A reliable source is something you can trust to be accurate. It is also important that your source is relevant, or related to the topic you want to learn about.

title: Organize Information
text:
After you have gathered your information, you need to organize your ideas. This means you put the information in order. You need to decide which information is important. What is fact? What is an opinion? Be sure the information is useful. Your information should help you answer your questions.

Write out all your main ideas. Create an outline of the main ideas. Put them in an order that is clear. Then, write or present your information in that order. Add supporting details or examples to each main point.

title: Present Your Information
text:
Once your information is organized, you need to decide how to present it. Think about the sources you have gathered. Could you use charts, tables, maps, or graphs to organize and present your information clearly? Also consider using stories, pictures, and artifacts. What would make your presentation interesting and informative? Will you create a written or oral presentation?

Brainstorm how to share the information you have found. Use a separate piece of paper to write down your resources and make a plan.

title: Cultural Contributions
text:
There are many ways to contribute to our community, state, and nation. Writers inform and entertain us. Musicians and artists create beauty and enjoyment. Scientists work to improve our lives and discover new things. Educators teach us and help us improve. Adventurers explore new places. Business people create companies and products people need and want. Politicians make a difference by leading us. Journalists tell us what is happening around the world. Many people have contributed to our state and national heritage.

A culture is the way a group of people live, speak, and act. Cultures express a group's heritage. These expressions come through art, stories, music, clothing, food, religion, and language. People bring their culture with them when they move from one place to another. Elements of different cultures often combine to create new traditions.

American societies today are multicultural, which means they are influenced by many cultures. This week, you are going to research some of the ethnic groups that have contributed to the United States.

title: Essential Question
text: How have different groups contributed to the United States?

title: Plants
text:
Native Americans grew many plants that we use regularly in the United States today. One of the most important plants Native Americans grew is corn. The United States produces 15 billion bushels of corn a year. It is the most widely produced crop in the country.

Often, tribes also grew beans and squash along with corn. Native Americans grew many other plants depending on where they lived. Other crops included pumpkins, peppers, tomatoes, and potatoes. These plants are eaten every day in the United States.

Native Americans in Mexico and central America also grew cacao, coffee, sunflowers, avocados, peanuts, quinoa, and cotton. Many of these foods are grown and eaten in the southern areas of the United States. Cotton is now a major crop in the United States.

European settlers brought apple, peach, and watermelon seeds with them. They also brought sugarcane, olives, citrus, and even bananas with them. Now there are many varieties of these fruits, and they provide food and jobs for people all over the U.S.

title: Food
text:
The food that we eat comes from the plants that we grow. Each different culture prepares similar foods in different ways. For example, tomatoes are often used in sauces. Spaghetti Bolognese sauce comes from Italy, and salsa roja is a Mexican type of sauce. Both use tomatoes. Noodles and bread are similar. Basic ingredients, like flour, salt, water, and eggs, can be made into many different products.

The United States is a multicultural society today. Common foods we eat in the United States have been influenced by many different cultures. Look at the images of foods that we eat in the United States. What culture influenced them?

title: Music
text:
Because the United States is multicultural, its music has roots in cultures from around the world. Each style has evolved and often influenced other styles.

Native Americans frequently use vocals, drums, percussion, and flutes in their music. People can experience their music at powwow performances.

The music genres of gospel, blues, jazz, R&B, soul, funk, and Zydeco all have roots in African American culture.

Bluegrass and country music come from the Appalachian region. It has been influenced by English and Celtic (Scottish and Irish) ballads. The fiddle and the guitar are the main instruments used.

Polkas and waltzes were popular with eastern European immigrants. The style and beat were combined with instruments like fiddles, guitars, and accordions. Western swing bands were influenced by these elements.

New York salsa is a style of music that developed from influences of different Caribbean islands.

title: Celebrations
text:
There are a lot of celebrations that people in the United States enjoy. These celebrations come from different cultures.

Day of the Dead: Mexico

Chinese New Year: China

Cinco de Mayo: Mexico

St Patrick’s Day: Ireland

Kwanzaa: African America

Mardi gras: Europe

Shakespeare festivals: England

Powwows: Native American tribes

title: Language
text:
People in the United States speak many different languages. The influence of these languages can be seen in place names all around the country. There are also many words from these different languages that we now use in American English. We have included some of them here.

Native American Languages’ Influence on American English

Early settlers and trappers began interacting with Native American tribes, they began using many of their words to describe plants, animals, and places that they had never seen before. Many of the words and place names we use today come from tribal languages that have been used for hundreds of years. Some of these words are:

caribou

woodchuck

toboggan

pecan

skunk

moccasin

African Influence on American English

Enslaved people who were brought to the United States had their own native languages. As they learned the English language, they also dropped some of their own words into it. Words like “okra,” “bongo,” and “zombie” are all from African languages. Some of the words we still use in modern English include:

jenga

yarn

zebra

cola

Hispanic Influence on American English

Parts of the United States used to belong to Spain. Many people have immigrated to the U.S. from Spanish-speaking countries. Many Spanish words have become part of American English over the years. Here are just a few:

armadillo

mesa

adobe

plaza

cafeteria

rodeo

canyon

tobacco

jerky

tornado

llama

Asian Influence on American English

Many of the words we use each day are actually borrowed from Asian words. Take a look at the list to see the Asian roots of many familiar English words.

bangle (Hindi): bracelet

jungle (Hindi): forest

typhoon (Chinese): great wind

tycoon (Japanese): great prince

ketchup (Chinese): fish sauce

shampoo (Hindi): to knead or massage

tattoo (Polynesian): to make marks on the skin

ukulele (Hawaiian): jumping flea

honcho (Japanese): group leader

title: Week 17 Primary Sources
text: There are many groups who have contributed to the culture of the United States. One great example is the Harlem Renaissance. During the 1920s and 1930s, many African Americans moved from the South to cities in the North. As they created communities, they produced art, music, poetry, and more, which still influences the United States today. This is a portrait of Langston Hughes, a famous African American poet during the Harlem Renaissance.

title: Comparing North American Cultures
text:
We can compare cultures by looking at the elements of culture. The environment and natural resources shape culture. History also affects culture. The North American continent has many different cultures. The Native people of the land have their own culture. People have come from other parts of the world. In Canada, the Caribbean, Mexico, and the United States, Indigenous traditions have mixed with different cultures.

One way to compare cultures is by asking questions. For example, what kinds of houses do the people build? What languages do they speak? What festivals do they have? What is the most common food that the people eat? Answers to these questions tell us a lot about a culture and its people. This allows us to compare the similarities and differences.

title: Essential Question
text: How do I compare the culture of different places?

title: Housing in the Southeast
text:
The environment affects the ways people build their homes and the materials they use. In the Southeast Region of the United States, the weather is often hot. As a result, many homes have wide windows to let in the air. They also have elevated verandas, where people can sit and enjoy the breeze.

In marshy areas or areas close to the sea, flooding can occur. So some people build their homes on stilts or with a washout floor. In case of flooding, the water would flow under or through the lower level of their homes. The main rooms they live in would not be flooded.

Some areas in the Southeast Region have a lot of red clay. Red clay is great for making bricks. There are many brick houses in such areas.

Places near the beach also use seashells to decorate floors and their yards. Seashells may also be used to decorate pavements and walls.

title: Housing in Canada
text:
Canada has a varied climate and biomes. The north is very cold. This influences the resources and the homes that are built. For example, in the past, some Native tribes in Canada used to build their winter homes with snow. These homes were called igloos. Igloos were built in places where there was a lot of snow and hardly any trees.

There is a lot of variety in Canadian housing today. It is important for Canadian homes to be able to handle the cold and snow. The roofs are often steep. This allows snow to slide off the roofs more easily. Smaller, cottage-style homes are also common, especially further north. A smaller space is easier to keep warm in the cold. Often, traditional homes in Canada will have some type of cover over the front door to shield it from rain and snow. There are a lot of forests in Canada, so many homes are built and decorated with wood.

title: Housing in Mexico
text:
Most countries have many different styles of homes. Mexico is no different.

One style of home in Mexico is the hacienda. Haciendas are often built with stone and concrete. Haciendas have high ceilings, wide windows, and rounded archways. They also have open-air courtyards in the center. The courtyard in the center is often planted with trees and other flowers and greenery. These plants help cool the area and make the courtyard a lovely place. All these features help keep the house cool.

Another style of housing in Mexico is the adobe home. Adobe homes are built with brick, mud, and wood. These homes also have thick walls. These prevent the rooms from getting too hot or too cold. Flat roofs are also common in adobe homes. Adobe homes come from the ideas of the Native tribes of Mexico.

Tile is a very important building material. Red clay tile roofs are common. They are strong and last a very long time. Tile is also common on the floors and as decoration. It is easy to clean and lasts a long time.

Stucco is another material that is often used in Mexico. It is very easy to use and shape. Some areas have very colorful stucco walls.

title: Housing in the Caribbean
text:
There are many types of homes in the Caribbean. Many are colorful. They range from small huts to large mansions. Before European settlers arrived, the Native tribes of the region used timber to build their homes. They used palm fronds or grass for roofing. These made the rooms cool.

The architectural styles of homes in the region were then influenced by the different European settlers that came to each island.

There are some features that tend to be common in many areas of the region. Often the features are based on staying cool. For example, many larger houses in the Caribbean have high windows and ceilings. These features let the breeze in and keep the heat out. Some houses have a courtyard with a colonnade. Others have porches or verandas. These features allow people to sit or move about in the shade.

A lot of people live in the Caribbean. Many islands have steep mountainous land. Many places have houses and apartments built close together on the sides of mountains.

title: Week 18 Primary Sources
text: This map from 1898 shows the location of foreign-born people in the United States according to the eleventh census in 1890.

title: What Makes a Good Citizen?
text:
Good citizens help our governments to work well. A citizen is an official member of a country, state, or community. Citizens have the responsibility to behave in certain ways. Civic virtues are personal behaviors and actions that help improve communities. For example, good citizens are friendly and kind. They are willing to donate their time to help others. Good citizens respect others and themselves. They treat others civilly, or politely. They work together for the common good. They are responsible in their daily lives.

Citizens have the responsibility to participate in government. They educate themselves about government issues. They vote in elections. They respectfully hold public officials to their word. Good citizens are necessary for successful communities.

title: Essential Question
text: How do good citizens participate in government?

title: Respect
text:
Respect is showing all people they are important. When you respect someone, you treat that person with kindness. You show that you care about the person's feelings by respecting their beliefs and traditions. You can respect others even if you believe in different things. Respect is an important quality to practice every day.

You should also respect yourself. Having self-respect means you see the good things about yourself. When you respect yourself, it is easier to show respect to others. When you feel good about yourself, you are happy and treat others kindly. Respecting yourself also means admitting when you do something wrong. It means learning from your mistakes.

title: Working Together
text:
A community is made of people who live in the same place. It is important that all community members work together to make their community better. When we work together, a community is a great place to live.

When we do things that are good for everyone, we are working for the common good. Picking up trash keeps the playground clean. That makes it nicer for everyone. Working for the common good helps solve community problems.

Sometimes people disagree on the solution to a problem. Civility is a word that means acting in a civil, or polite, way. When we disagree, it is important we still have civility and respect.

We need to cooperate and compromise. Cooperating is two or more people working together to achieve a common goal. Compromising is when members of a group give up some things to reach an agreement. Working with others can help us see things from a different perspective and create better solutions. Working together makes communities better.

title: Voting
text: In the United States, voting is a right. When citizens turn 18 years old, they can vote. Voting is the way we choose our leaders. Voting gives people a chance to make their voices heard. Voters have the responsibility to learn about issues and the people they are voting for. If we don't have all the facts, we may find out later that we voted for something we didn't want. In some countries, people are not allowed to vote. Voting is an important civic responsibility in our system of government.

title: Paying Taxes
text: Taxes are money people pay to the government. Taxes help pay for community services, roads, parks, and many other things. The laws of our state and our country say taxes must be paid. Good citizens obey the law and pay their taxes. The money from taxes helps make our communities better.

title: Serving in the Military
text: Some people choose to be participating citizens by joining the United States military. A military is a group of people who are given power to defend a country. People choose to serve in the military in different ways. Some military members help when there is a natural disaster. Other military members fight in combat to protect the United States. We honor military members who choose to serve our country on special holidays like Veterans Day.

title: Week 26 Primary Sources
text:
During WWI and WWII, people were encouraged to plant Victory Gardens to provide food for themselves and reduce the demand for food in grocery stores. This was a way not only to help people have more food during the war. It was also a way to show patriotism.

Individuals must use ballots to vote, where they select individuals they would like to vote for, and policies that they would like to vote for and against. This shows a ballot box, like the ones used in early U.S. History. We use a similar system, though assisted by technology, in modern times.

title: Volunteering
text:
Citizens who want to give something back to the community can volunteer, or donate their time to help others. Many people volunteer because they want to help others in need. There are many ways you can volunteer in your community.

People can volunteer for drives. Different types of drives collect things for people in need. Some volunteers help with community clean ups. Other volunteers serve in community fire departments and neighborhood watch programs. The list of volunteer jobs is very long. If you want to give back to your community, find out about where you could volunteer. Someone will really appreciate your help!

title: Essential Question
text: How can I be a participating citizen?

title: Drives
text: Drives are events that collect things for people in need. There are book, food, and blood drives. You can participate in a book drive by donating some of your books. You can participate in a food drive by donating cans or boxes of food. When you become an adult, you can participate in a blood drive. This means giving some of your blood to help people who are hurt or sick. If you don’t have items to donate to a drive, you can still donate your time to help collect things for the drive.

title: Neighborhood Programs
text:
It is the job of the police to enforce laws in the city. But community members can help too. People can form neighborhood watch groups in their area. People in these groups watch their neighborhood for problems. They tell police about bad things that happen. They get training from the police. The training helps them learn how to help keep their community safe.

Other community programs plant community gardens. These are gardens that a whole community shares. People in the community volunteer their time to help take care of the garden. The food that comes from the garden helps feed the people in the community. Do you have a community garden near you?

title: Spotlights
text:
There are many organizations that serve Florida. Here are a few you can learn about:

Volunteer Firefighters

Fire departments can have full time firefighters. These people make a living fighting fires. Fire departments can also have volunteer firefighters. These people don’t work as firefighters full time. They have other jobs, but are trained to help put out fires and respond to disasters. Our country and communities are full of people who are trained and ready to jump in and help. They also help people before fires start by teaching their communities about fire prevention.

Keep Florida Beautiful

Keep Florida Beautiful is an organization that protects Florida’s environment. It is one of Florida’s largest volunteer based organizations. Volunteers for Keep Florida Beautiful help with many different projects. They help with cleaning up beaches and animal habitats. Volunteers also go to schools and teach kids about respecting the environment. Keep Florida Beautiful has a youth council. Kids on the council volunteer to help make their communities better.

Mound House

There is a place called Mound House in Fort Myers, Florida. This is a special place. Some of the first Native Americans made villages there. They were called the Calusa. They are known as the “Shell Indians” because they used shells for many things. They created mounds with these shells. There is now a museum built on top of one of the mounds. This museum teaches about how the Calusa lived. Some volunteers give tours and presentations. Other volunteers help take care of artifacts found at the site.

Habitat for Humanity

Habitat for Humanity is a program that builds homes and helps improve communities for low-income families. Habitat for Humanity does not give away homes for free. It helps people in need afford homes. It can do this with the help of donations and volunteers. Many people, clubs and businesses volunteer to help Habitat for Humanity. Families who buy the homes also help build them. Habitat for Humanity is trying to help fix the problems of poverty and homelessness.

title: Identify Participating Citizens
text: Identify a person or organization that demonstrates volunteerism or other civic virtues. Write a paragraph to explain your choice. Create an award for them in the box.

title: Holidays Help Us Remember
text:
How can someone learn about a country’s history? One way is to learn about its patriotic celebrations. We honor people and events in United States history through celebrations and holidays. We also build monuments and memorials to recognize their contributions.

National monuments and memorials are symbols of our nation. They were built to remind us of important events and people in our history. Monuments and memorials teach us why these people are important to America. Knowing the history of our country helps to unite us as citizens.

title: Essential Question
text: What do we celebrate on patriotic holidays?

title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
text: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. is an important part of American history. He believed in equal rights for all people. He taught that everyone should be treated equally. His words guided people to solve problems peacefully. On the third Monday in January, we honor and remember his work. It’s called Martin Luther King Jr. Day. The Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial is in Washington, D.C. It is a symbol of King’s ideals and sacrifice.

title: Memorial Day and Veterans Day
text: We honor those who have served in the armed forces on Veterans Day. We honor military members who died serving our country on Memorial Day. These veterans are examples of courage and sacrifice. We can go to Arlington Cemetery and the Vietnam Veterans Memorial to honor those who served our country. Other memorials include the World War II Memorial and the Iwo Jima Monument. The Korean War Memorial, and the Pearl Harbor Memorial are also memorials.

title: Independence Day
text: The Fourth of July is also called Independence Day. The Declaration of Independence was voted on and accepted on July 4, 1776. This is the day we celebrate the United States becoming a country. We honor the people who worked for freedom. Many people celebrate this holiday. People watch parades and spend time with family and friends. People also watch fireworks.

title: Constitution Day
text: On Sept. 17, 1787, the U.S. Constitution was finished. Today, many people celebrate Constitution Day on September 17. Some people celebrate by memorizing the Preamble of the Constitution and reciting it together. Others sing the national anthem or dress in red, white, and blue. At some schools, students play games, act out plays, or write reports that help them learn more about the Constitution.

title: Celebrate Freedom Week
text:
During Celebrate Freedom Week we celebrate freedom. We also learn about how our country was created. This holiday reminds us to think about the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. Celebrate Freedom Week helps us recognize the contributions and sacrifices made by our veterans and Founders. It also reminds us of our freedoms and rights as guaranteed in the Constitution.

Mark the things you would like to do to celebrate your American freedom and add some ideas of your own!

Visit or talk to a soldier

Study the Declaration of Independence

Recite part of the Constitution

Sing or listen to a patriotic song

Look at primary source pictures of our freedom documents

Learn about a Founding Father

Draw a picture or make a poster about celebrating freedom

Wear red, white, and blue clothing

title: Patriot Day
text: We honor Patriot Day. It is on September 11. We remember the attacks that occurred on Sept. 11, 2001. We honor the people who were affected. We remember the heroes. It is a day to reflect on our freedom.

title: American Founders Month
text: We celebrate American Founders’ Month. We learn about the difficulties of creating a new nation. We learn about the founders of the United States. We study the history of the United States and its leaders. We study the important documents of the United States.

title: Medal of Honor Day
text: In March, we celebrate Medal of Honor Day. This day honors people in the military who received the Medal of Honor. The Medal of Honor is the highest military award for valor in the United States. Valor means courage and bravery. The award was created in 1861.

title: Week 28 Primary Sources
text: Memorial Day is a time when people honor and celebrate those who have fought for the United States. This is an image of the title page for music written for a Memorial Day celebration in 1870.

title: Events That Represent the U.S.
text:
What are two events that represent the United States?

The Constitutional Convention (May 1787–September 1787)

The Constitution of the United States was written over a long period of time at an event called a convention. A convention is a series of meetings. The Constitutional Convention was held in Philadelphia, from May through September of 1787. Fifty-five representatives from 12 of the new 13 states were there. George Washington was also there. Later, he would become our first president. The members of the Constitutional Convention wrote most of the laws that we still follow in our country today.

The Signing of the U.S. Constitution (September 17, 1787)

At the end of the Constitutional Convention, the United States Constitution was finished. Thirty-nine out of the 55 representatives signed the Constitution. This ratified, or put into effect, the new Constitution.

These events represent the United States because they created the foundation for the laws and government of our country.

title: Essential Question
text: What are symbols that represent the United States?

title: Mount Rushmore
text: Mount Rushmore is a sculpture in South Dakota. It represents four important presidents. George Washington and Thomas Jefferson were Founding Fathers. Abraham Lincoln helped free people who were enslaved. Theodore Roosevelt developed the National Parks Service. We honor their service to our country through this sculpture.

title: Uncle Sam
text: Uncle Sam isn’t a real person, but a symbol of the United States. Uncle Sam is a cartoon figure whose name first showed up on containers of supplies during the War of 1812. Soldiers joked that the initials “U.S.” on the containers stood for “Uncle Sam.” In 1832, the first pictures of Uncle Sam began appearing in newspapers. Uncle Sam had a long, white beard and wore a tall, star-spangled hat. He also wore a suit covered in red, white, and blue stripes. The red, white, and blue colors of the poster remind people of the American flag. Later, Uncle Sam appeared on posters asking Americans to stick together during times of war and to fight for liberty and justice. The United States Congress made Uncle Sam an official national symbol in 1961.

title: The Washington Monument
text: Many people think that George Washington represents the United States because he was our first president and a great leader. He is often called the "Father of his country." The Washington Monument was built in honor of George Washington. The monument is located at the center of the nation’s capital, Washington, D.C.

title: The American Flag
text: One of the patriotic symbols of the country is the flag. The stripes represent the 13 original colonies that became the new United States. The stars represent each state of the union. The red, white, and blue colors have meaning, too. Red symbolizes valor, or courage, and being willing to sacrifice for the country. White symbolizes innocence and purity in holding to the ideals of the country. Blue represents vigilance, perseverance and justice for all.

title: The Statue of Liberty
text: The United States and France have a special relationship. France helped the colonies in the War for Independence from Great Britain. The people of France wanted to give America a gift to honor freedom and democracy. The gift was the Statue of Liberty. The statue was placed in the harbor of New York City. The statue is of a woman holding a torch for all to see the light of freedom. The statue is a symbol of freedom, a sign of hope for people seeking a better life in America.

title: The Great Seal of the United States
text: The Great Seal of the United States was designed and approved in 1782. It is a symbol of freedom. It represents the United States as an independent country. It shows our beliefs and values. The bald eagle holds a saying that means "out of many, one" to remind us that we are a unity of states. In one claw is an olive branch to represent peace. In the other claw, there are arrows to represent defending our country. There is a shield with 13 stripes for the original 13 colonies. Above the eagle is a cloud with 13 stars.

title: Week 29 Primary Sources
text: The Liberty Bell is a famous symbol of freedom in the United States.

title: Susan B. Anthony
text: Many important women worked to improve the quality of life for women at the beginning of the 20th century. One such woman was Susan B. Anthony. She supported the anti-slavery and women's rights movements. Anthony proved that women could be leaders in society. After the Civil War, Anthony wanted both formerly enslaved people and women to have the right to vote. She was disappointed when the 14th and 15th Amendments to the Constitution did not grant these rights to women. Anthony traveled all over the nation to convince people to support her cause. Women did not gain the right to vote during Susan B. Anthony's lifetime. The right came 14 years after her death. She did, however, influence many other Americans to continue with social reform. Thanks to Susan B. Anthony, women today can vote on election day.

title: Essential Question
text: Who are some people that represent the United States?

title: Alexander Hamilton
text: At the age of 16, Alexander Hamilton enrolled at King’s College in New York. In 1774, he wrote an article that supported American independence. He then left King’s College to join the Revolutionary War. His bravery and courageous actions caught the eye of George Washington. He served as Washington’s right-hand man for the remainder of the war. After the war, Hamilton was elected as a delegate to the Constitutional Convention. He did everything he could to see the Constitution become the supreme law of the land. He believed in the principles outlined in the Constitution. In 1789, he became George Washington’s secretary of the treasury. As secretary of the treasury, he established the First Bank of the United States.

title: César Chávez
text: César Chávez was the son of Mexican immigrants. He and his family were migrant workers. These are people who move from place to place to work. Chávez saw that migrant workers were not treated well. He believed that migrant workers should have the same rights as others. When Chávez grew up, he helped migrant workers get better pay and homes. He founded the United Farm Workers of America. This is a union of workers who make sure they get fair pay and good working conditions. The union still exists today. It still works to make sure that farm workers are treated fairly. César Chávez worked for equality for thousands of migrant workers throughout the United States.

title: Booker T. Washington
text: Booker T. Washington was an African American leader. He was born into slavery in Virginia in 1856. He learned how to read in his spare time. At age 16, he walked 500 miles to Hampton Normal Agricultural Institute in Virginia. He convinced the headmaster to let him work as a janitor to help pay for his tuition. Washington worked and studied diligently to become an educator and leader. The Tuskegee Normal School was founded on July 4, 1881. A “normal school” was a school that trained teachers. The Tuskegee Normal School was one of the few schools that focused on teaching African American educators. Washington was hired to lead the school. He began teaching students before any of the campus buildings were finished. He designed the courses and hired a staff of skilled educators. He encouraged each student to do their best work. Booker T. Washington believed education was a key to advancement for African Americans in the South. He said, “I have learned that success is to be measured not so much by the position one has reached in life as by the obstacles which he has overcome.”

title: Shirley Chisholm
text: Shirley Chisholm was born in New York in 1924. Her parents had come to New York from Barbados. She wanted to make things better for the people in her neighborhood. She knew that being involved in the government could make that happen. She got involved in local politics; then she looked at state elections. Chisholm won the election to be in the New York State Assembly. She did good things for her neighborhood. Wanting to do more for more people, Chisholm looked to the national government. In 1968, Chisholm ran for U.S. Congress. She won, becoming the first African American woman ever to be elected to Congress. In 1972, Chisholm decided to run for president of the United States. She wanted to bring attention to causes that were important to her. Chisholm left Congress in 1982 and spent the rest of her life giving speeches and teaching. Her leadership made life better for those around her.

title: Thurgood Marshall
text: Thurgood Marshall was born in 1908. During his free time as a boy, he enjoyed reading about lawyers and trials. Sometimes he even went to court and sat in the visitor section. He learned about law from his father. Marshall’s mother was a teacher. She taught him the value of a good education. In 1930, Marshall wanted to attend law school at the University of Maryland. He was denied admission because of his skin color. He did not give up. Instead, he went to Howard University and became a lawyer. He wanted to change how people of color were treated. In the 1950s, a case about education went to the Supreme Court. It was called Brown vs. Board of Education. Thurgood Marshall was the lawyer. He argued that having segregated schools was wrong. The Supreme Court agreed with him. As a result, all children in the United States can now attend the same schools. Marshall continued to work for equality. On August 30, 1967, he became a justice in the Supreme Court. He was the first African American Supreme Court justice.

title: James Madison
text: James Madison is known as the “Father of the Constitution.” Many of the ideas in the Constitution were Madison’s own ideas about the rights and freedoms individuals should have. Our rights and responsibilities are defined and protected in the Constitution. In 1789, Madison was elected to the Virginia Assembly. He worked to create religious freedom in his home state. During Thomas Jefferson’s presidency, Madison served as secretary of state. In 1808, Madison was elected as the fourth president of the United States. Madison continued to serve as president until 1817. Without the hard work and dedication of James Madison, the government of the United States would not look the way it does today.

title: How Did Florida Become a State?
text: The first people in Florida were Native Americans. These included the Apalachee, Calusa, Mayaimi, and Tocobaga. Spanish, French, and British explorers and settlers then came to the area. Later, In 1821, Florida became a territory of the United States. The population of Florida kept growing, and it became the 27th state of the United States. This happened on March 3, 1845. This was the beginning of Florida state as we know it now.

title: Essential Question
text: What are symbols that represent Florida?

title: The Florida Constitution
text:
Just like the U.S. Constitution, state constitutions guarantee and protect citizens' basic rights. State constitutions list the rules for state government. They also explain how a state can make laws. State constitutions describe how the state government divides and shares power with counties and cities. Florida has a state constitution. It has a similar structure to the United States Constitution. It has changed over time to reflect the unique needs of the people of Florida. The first state constitution was written in 1838, before Florida became a state.

Florida’s current constitution was written in 1968. This document represents Florida. This constitution is set up with an introduction, called a preamble. The preamble helps citizens know why the constitution was written. The rest of the constitution is divided into 12 sections, called articles. The first article contains a Declaration of Rights. This part of the constitution tells us about all of the rights of every Florida citizen. The other articles explain how the Florida government should work.

title: The Great Seal of Florida
text: Most states have a symbol, or seal, that has phrases and pictures that describe the state. Florida has one, too! Florida’s first seal was first created in 1868. It was changed in 1985. Our seal has a picture of a sunset over a boat. It also has a woman and a tall sabal palm tree on it. The revised seal corrected errors that were on the old one. The woman on the seal is now a Seminole Native American rather than a Western Plains Native American. The steamboat is more accurate. Look at each part of our seal. Why do you think each part was included?

title: The State Shell
text: In 1969, the Florida legislature named the horse conch as our state shell. The horse conch is a sea snail that can grow up to two feet long. It is native to the marine waters around Florida. People find horse conch shells all along our Florida coastlines. Horse conchs are quite heavy for their size. Adult horse conchs can be orange, cream, or brown.

title: The Florida Panther
text:
In 1982, Florida students chose our state animal. They picked the Florida panther. The Florida panther is an important animal. It helps keep the plants and animals balanced. The Florida panther used to live in a few states. Now it only lives in Florida. It is an endangered species. This means that it needs to be protected. It has been protected from being hunted since 1958.

The Florida panther is cream-colored on its back and gray on its belly. The tip of its tail, back of its ears, and sides of its nose are dark brown or black.

title: The Mockingbird
text: Did you know Florida has the same state bird as four other states? Our popular state bird is the mockingbird. It has amazing vocal abilities. It can make the sounds of other birds. It can even sound like a machine. It also fiercely defends its family nest. It also helps people by eating bugs and seeds that grow into weeds. It became our state bird in 1927.

title: The Moonstone
text: The moonstone is our state gem. But moonstone doesn’t come from the moon. It doesn’t come from Florida either. So why is moonstone our state gem? In 1969, American astronauts landed on the moon. They left Earth from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Florida lawmakers chose moonstone to mark this special event.

title: Week 31 Primary Sources
text: This is a U.S. postal stamp from 1982 commemorating two Florida symbols: the mockingbird and the orange blossom.

title: Mary McLeod Bethune
text:
Mary McLeod Bethune was born in 1875. Her family was not wealthy. Bethune worked hard to help support her family. When she was nine years old, Bethune was given the opportunity to go to school. She grew up in a time when most African Americans were not allowed to attend school. She was a dedicated student. Eventually, she was able to go to a college in North Carolina.

Bethune knew that the education she and other African Americans got was not the same as the education that white people got. She wanted to change that. She decided to start a small school in Daytona, Florida. It was called the Daytona Normal and Industrial Institute. It was especially for African American girls. People in the community helped her build the school. Her school is still there today, and it is now called Bethune-Cookman University.

Bethune eventually met and became friends with powerful leaders in Washington, D.C. One of her friends was Eleanor Roosevelt, whose husband Franklin was the president of the United States. Bethune and Eleanor both fought against discrimination. In 1936, President Roosevelt asked Bethune to work with him. She became the director of a group that advised the president on African American matters. The work of this group made it possible for African Americans to work where previously only white workers had been allowed to work. All her life, Bethune continued to work to get equal rights for all people.

title: Essential Question
text: Who are some people who represent Florida?

title: Janet Reno
text: Janet Reno was born and raised in Miami. As a young girl, she used to go to work with her father, who was a newspaper reporter for criminal trials. This experience made a great impact on Reno. She went to Harvard Law School and got a degree in law. She worked as an attorney in Florida for several years. Attorney is another word for lawyer. Later, she ran for a position in Dade County and was elected. She served as Dade County’s district attorney for 15 years. In 1993, Janet Reno made history when she became the first woman U.S. attorney general. This meant she had the highest government position available as an attorney. She stayed in this position for a long time. She was the longest serving attorney general in the century.

title: Josiah Walls
text:
Josiah Walls was born in 1842. He was born enslaved. As a young man, he was freed. He went to school and served in the army. Walls served in the Union Army during the Civil War. After he served in the army, he worked as a teacher in Gainesville, Florida. By 1868, he had enough money from working to buy a farm.

He was later drawn to participate in government. He wanted to make a positive difference for others. He began his political career by representing Alachua County in the 1868 Florida Constitutional Convention. The same year, he also ran for and won the political position of state assemblyman. He was elected to the Florida State Senate a year later. He was one of five men serving in the Florida Senate who had formerly been enslaved. Walls was a strong supporter of education and economic opportunities in Florida for all races.

In 1872, Walls became Florida’s first African American member of the House of Representatives. In the political circles of Washington, D.C., African American representatives were met with opposition. Few established members of Congress worked with them or treated them as colleagues or members equal in their work. Being a leader of the African American population took great courage. Walls overcame deep political divisions. He was the only African American representative from Florida until the early 1990s. Throughout his political career, Walls worked for the good of Florida. He worked for improvements to be built, such as telegraph lines, courthouses, and post offices. He worked to improve Florida’s harbors and rivers.

title: Jacqueline Cochran
text: Jacqueline Cochran was one Floridian who made a difference in her community and the world. Cochran was born in 1906 in Florida. After working for some time as a beautician, Cochran trained to become a pilot. She earned her pilot’s license in 1932. During World War II, many American men left their homes and went to war. This left many jobs open that needed to be filled. The United States military decided to train women to fill these jobs. They wanted women to fly military planes. These women were known as the Women Air Service Pilots, or WASPs. Cochran was chosen to lead the WASPs. They flew new military aircraft to places where they were needed. They also delivered supplies to many places. It was a dangerous job, but the WASPs were willing to help their community and country. Cochran contributed greatly to civic life in the United States. She continued to train pilots. She also worked with NASA to test female pilots who wanted to become astronauts. She set and broke many records in flying. She was also awarded the Distinguished Service Medal for her service.

title: William Pope Duval
text: William Duval was born in Virginia in 1784. He left home at the age of 14. He eventually settled in Kentucky to study law. In 1821, President Monroe made Duval a federal judge in the Eastern District of the Florida Territory. Later, President Monroe made Duval a governor of the Florida territory. Duval was the first civil governor of the Florida territory. Andrew Jackson had served as a military governor before Duval. Duval served as the civil governor for 12 years. While governor, Duval made many contributions to the Florida territory. He helped establish peaceful relations with Florida’s Native American people. He revised the code of laws that were used. He created a board of education to help grow schools. He established Tallahassee as the capital of the territory. He helped determine land boundaries. He served as a senator in the Florida legislature from 1839 to 1842. He did many great things for Florida. Duval County is named after him.

title: William Dunn Moseley
text: Florida has had many governors. It has also had several first governors. Andrew Jackson was the first military governor. William Duval was the first civil territory governor. William Moseley was the first governor after Florida became a state. This means he was the first state governor. Moseley was born in North Carolina in 1795. As a young man, he studied law and became a lawyer. He moved to Florida in 1835. Ten years later, Florida became the 27th state of the United States in 1845. The very first Florida State election happened that year. Moseley ran for the position of state governor and won. As governor, Moseley made many contributions to Florida. He encouraged the development of agriculture in Florida. This meant growing citrus, avocados, and cotton. He wanted state-funded public schools to be established. The state capital was completed during his first year as governor. After his service as governor, he moved to Palatka. There, he became a citrus farmer.

title: John Young
text: John Young was born in 1930. As a boy, Young loved to learn. He loved reading and building model airplanes. When he grew up, he became a famous astronaut. He worked for NASA for 42 years. He was one of the pioneers of space travel. He was known for his bravery and commitment. He was the first person to fly into space six times. He landed on the moon and drove a lunar rover. He spent three nights on the moon before coming back to Earth. After he stopped flying to space, Young continued to work for NASA. Young helped with many space missions.

title: What Is Money?
text:
Before people used money, they bartered for the goods or services they wanted. Bartering is trading goods and services. If you were a farmer and raised chickens, you might trade a chicken or two for sugar, bread, or a cooking pot. You might also give someone food for working on your farm.

Eventually communities began to exchange goods and services with other mediums. This meant they used valuable items like shells, salt, or pieces of precious metal in exchange for goods or services. Eventually, gold and silver became the most acceptable mediums of exchange. They were rare, and this made them valuable. Since mediums of exchange must be easy to carry, precious metals began to be made into coins. Gold, silver, bronze, copper, and iron were made into coins.

The word “money” began to be used to describe all mediums of exchange. It comes from the word “minted,” which is the way coins were made.

title: Essential Question
text: What are the characteristics of money?

title: Characteristics of Money
text:
There are some qualities that money must have to be a good medium of exchange.

It must be portable. That means it is easy to travel with it.

It must be durable. This means it is strong and will last a long time.

Money has to be divisible. This means it can be divided to pay for things that cost different amounts.

Money needs to be recognizable. This means everyone must recognize it is money.

Money must also be acceptable. This means that it must be accepted by everyone. You must be able to use it to pay the government and others.

Today, the money people use comes in two main forms. These are paper and coins. However, digital money is also widely acceptable. Paper and coins are also called cash.

Digital money is not physical money. It is money that can be transferred online. It allows people to pay for goods and services with a card. A debit or credit card represents a lot of paper and coins.

title: Money in the United States
text:
When the United States was founded, there were 13 states. Each state had its own currency. The federal government decided that one currency should be made for the whole country. In 1787, the first U.S. coin was minted. In 1792, Congress decided that our currency would officially be called “dollars” instead of “pounds.”

The government kept minting coins using gold and silver. The coins came in denominations like $10, $5, and $2.50. Today’s coins are made of a mixture of metals.

In 1861, the government began printing paper money. It was nicknamed “greenbacks” because the back of the money was green.

Before 1913, some banks and companies used to print their own paper money. These were called notes. People exchanged these at banks for gold or silver coins. In 1913, the federal government decided that only the government could print money. From 1913 on, everyone used the same coins and bills as a medium of exchange.

title: Money in Mexico
text:
Mexico’s money is the peso. One peso can be divided into 100 centavos. The symbol for the peso is the “$” sign. Centavos are shown using the “¢” symbol.

Paper pesos are in denominations of $20, $50, $100, $200, $500 and $1,000. There are also coins worth one, two, five, 10 and 20 pesos. There are also 20 and 50 centavos coins. The one-, two-, and five-peso coins each have a gold-colored center with a silver border. The size of each coin depends on how much the coin is worth. The bigger the coin, the more it is worth. Mexican money has important people, places, and events pictured on it. Every coin has Mexico’s coat of arms on it. It is the image of an eagle sitting on a cactus and holding a snake.

Around 2005, printers added raised bumps to the peso bills so that people who can’t see can still identify the value of each bill.

title: Money in Canada
text: The official currency of Canada is the Canadian dollar. There are 100 cents in a dollar. The Canadian bills are in $5, $10, $20, $50, and $100 denominations. Canadian bills are brightly colored, which makes it easy to tell them apart. That makes them difficult to counterfeit as well. Canadian coins come in one-, five, 10-, 25- and 50-cent denominations. There are also one- and two-dollar coins. The one-dollar coin is nicknamed the Loonie, and the two-dollar coin is the Toonie. They have replaced the one- and two-dollar bills.

title: Money in the Caribbean
text:
The Caribbean has many countries and territories. Each country has its own currency. A territory usually uses the currency of the nation that controls it. As a result, the region has many different currencies. For example, the Cayman Islands has its own dollar. However, eight countries use one currency known as the East Caribbean dollar. Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands both use the United States dollar because they are territories of the United States. Here are some Caribbean nations that have their own official currencies.

Cuba

The official currency is the Cuban peso. Cuban pesos feature Cuba’s national heroes, important buildings, and important places. At the top of the bill, it says in Spanish “Central Bank of Cuba.”

The Bahamas

The Bahamas’ unit of currency is the Bahamian dollar (B$). It is based on the U.S. dollar. The Bahamian currency features important island symbols, like a starfish. It also features national heroes and important places. The phrase “Central Bank of The Bahamas” and the Bahamian coat of arms are printed on all the notes.

Jamaica

The Jamaican currency unit is the Jamaican dollar (J$). The Jamaican coat of arms appears on all Jamaican money. You can find it on the front of notes and on the back of coins. All the monies also have the face of a national hero on them.

Haiti

Haiti’s currency is the gourde, and one gourde (G) is equal to 100 centimes. Important historic figures of the Haitian Republic appear on all coins and bills.

Dominican Republic

The Dominican Republic’s unit of currency is the peso. The peso is made up of 100 centavos, and its symbol is the “$” sign. Important people and buildings are featured on the paper money.

title: Week 19 Primary Sources
text:
Today, the U.S. government issues all currency, but there was a time when banks and states printed money as well. This is a dollar bill printed by the Merchant's Bank of Trenton in 1861.

Even though this dollar bill printed by the Merchant's Bank of Trenton in 1861 is no longer valid currency in the United States, it still looks familiar because of the image of Abraham Lincoln and other aspects of its design. Many countries, including Canada and Mexico, use images of noteworthy people on their money.

title: Needs and Wants
text:
A need is something that you have to have every day. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us warm or cool.

Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler to help you be successful each day.

A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. A want is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

title: Essential Question
text: How do we use money?

title: Goods and Services
text:
Goods are things that are made for people to buy and use. Goods include clothing, furniture, and toys. Goods are also things we eat or drink. Fruits, vegetables, and milk are examples of goods we consume.

A service is work that one person does for someone else. Services are actions such as a haircut, car repair, and teaching. If you send a package to someone else, you pay for a delivery service. If you have a cell phone, you pay for cell phone service. You might choose to have your pizza delivered. That’s a service too.

title: Producers and Consumers
text:
The people who make goods or provide services for other people are producers. Some goods and services stay in the community. Some goods and services are created for other communities.

The people who buy goods and services are called consumers. Consumers can buy goods and services in their community or from other communities. When you get a haircut, you are buying a service. This makes you a consumer. You are also a consumer if you buy a book.

People can be both producers and consumers. For example, a baker is a consumer when they purchase flour, sugar, and supplies to make their baked goods. A baker is a producer when they sell their baked goods.

title: Supply and Demand
text:
The price of a good or service depends on two things. First, it depends on how much of the good there is for people to buy. That’s called supply. Next, it depends on how many people want or need it. That’s called demand. When the supply is low and the demand is high, the price goes up. When the supply is high and the demand is low, the price goes down.

When the newest smartphones come out, many people want them. There is a large demand. At clearance sales, stores want to get rid of products that haven’t sold. In this case, there is a larger supply.

title: Scarcity and Surplus
text:
Scarcity is when there is more demand for something than supply. In other words, it is not having enough of something people want or need. Sometimes, scarcity can be a big problem. If basic resources like food or water are scarce, it is hard for people to live. When goods and services become scarce, families have to decide what they need most. Families have to make choices about how to spend their money to meet their needs.

Surplus is when the supply of a good or service is more than the demand. In other words, there is more than people need or want. A surplus of a good or service usually makes the price go down.

title: Trade
text:
Our country does not produce everything we need. We have to buy things from other countries. That is called trade. Trade is when you buy, sell, or exchange a good or service for something else you want or need. Businesses, states, and countries trade goods and services all around the world. Trade between countries is a very important part of a nation’s economy. Because of interdependence and trade, our community is affected by events around the world.

Bartering is trading goods without the use of money. In early cultures, people were able to get many things they needed and wanted through bartering. Today, we use money to buy what we need because it is much easier to use.

title: Imports and Exports
text: International trade depends on imports and exports. Imports are goods brought in from other countries. Exports are goods sent out to other countries to be sold. Rice, oil, and computers are made in Asia and imported to the United States. They are imports. Cars, airplanes, and machines are made in the United States and exported to other countries.

title: Week 20 Primary Sources
text:
The United States trades with other countries. The scarcity of bananas made them a prized import at different times. This photograph from 1900 shows early banana importers and distributers. Many people who imported bananas at this time were Italian immigrants.

This photo from 1942 shows people crowding around an ice cream truck to get a treat. This is an example of buyers and sellers coming together to exchange money for ice cream.

title: Essential Question
text: How can budgeting help me?

title: Budgeting Time
text: When we are in third grade, we may not have money. However, we can have a budget for our time. We need to spend our time wisely. We save time when we don’t spend it on things that are not useful. If we spend too much time playing, we may not have enough time for school work. If we do our chores on time, we save enough time to play. There are five hours between 1:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. If we have five things to do within that time, we can budget one hour for each of them. If we finish all the chores in three hours, we would save two hours. We can use those two hours to do something fun.

title: How to Make a Budget
text:
Some people make budgets for a whole year. Others prefer to budget month to month.

Most people look at the amount of money that they receive from their job. They then set aside, or allocate, money to the important items that they have to pay for each month. This includes things like housing, food, utilities, and transportation.

After you set aside money for your needs, it is wise to plan (or make goals) for the things that you want. These could be things like a vacation, a new car or computer, or even a special hobby like water skiing. You decide how much money you want to save each month toward these goals.

title: Create a Budget
text:
Using a budget helps you think about what you want to do with your money. It also helps keep you from spending more than you have. A budget helps you plan for the future. By sticking to a budget, you will make more responsible money choices.

You are going to make a practice budget for a month that shows income and spending. Use the steps below to help you complete your budget.

Your income is $3,000 a month.

Look at the Budget Choice Card and choose one option from each "Needs" category: Housing, Transportation, Utilities, and Food. Write your choice and cost in the correct box and subtract what you spend from your income as you go.

The money you have left after meeting your needs can be spent on Wants, Savings, or Donations.

Think about Savings and Donations first. What will you save for future needs or emergencies? How much money do you want to give? Subtract your Savings and Donations from your budget.

Look at the list of Wants and think about what you really want vs what can wait until next month. Write your choices in the correct box and subtract the amount from your budget.

Now that you have completed your budget, do you have anything left?

title: Pregunta esencial
text: ¿Por qué es importante estudiar geografía?

title: Tecnología SIG
text:
Los Sistemas de Información Global, también conocidos como SIG, son una forma de visualizar datos en mapas. En cuanto se inventaron ordenadores capaces de hacerlo, se empezaron a utilizar para cartografiar información. Si tienes datos o información que coinciden con ubicaciones en un mapa, puedes utilizar los SIG para hacer una representación visual de esos datos en un mapa. Observar los datos superpuestos en un mapa puede revelar nuevas relaciones y patrones que quizá no parecían obvios al principio.

Sin la capacidad de mapear los datos y visualizarlos, puede resultar difícil comprender lo que representan. Las tendencias y pautas de los datos suelen pasar desapercibidas si no se comprende la relación física entre los distintos puntos de información. Cualquier información que pueda cartografiarse puede visualizarse mediante SIG.

Muchas profesiones dependen de los datos y elementos visuales de los SIG para realizar su trabajo. Los urbanistas pueden utilizar los SIG para cartografiar a los usuarios de transportes públicos, como autobuses y metros, y asegurarse de que sus planes de transporte se adaptan a las personas allí donde se encuentran. Los biólogos observan la presencia de especies en peligro de extinción y planifican estrategias de protección gracias a la información que obtienen con los SIG.

En Florida, los arqueólogos utilizan los SIG para cartografiar la presencia de yacimientos y artefactos históricos. Los arqueólogos excavan en la tierra y bucean en aguas estatales en busca de artefactos. Utilizan el SIG para hacer modelos digitales detallados de los yacimientos donde encuentran estos artefactos. El mapeo de los datos mediante SIG les permite visualizar el yacimiento completo y encontrar patrones que de otro modo pasarían desapercibidos. Recrear el yacimiento digitalmente también les permite limitar la perturbación de los frágiles lugares históricos.

Los gobiernos de los condados del estado utilizan los datos del SIG para identificar las zonas amenazadas por los numerosos huracanes que se desarrollan en las aguas de la costa. Esto les ayuda a crear y compartir rutas de evacuación con los ciudadanos. También permite a los condados compartir otra información importante, como las zonas inundables y el acceso a servicios importantes como parques de bomberos y escuelas.
