title: The Treaty of Ghent
text:
In 1814, leaders from Great Britain and the United States met in Ghent, Belgium. Their goal was to find a peaceful end to the War of 1812. The war had seen brutal fighting across the country and the burning of the U.S. Capitol building by British forces. Both sides had tired of conflict and decided that an end to the war would be beneficial to everyone.

The Treaty of Ghent began with the declaration of a “firm and universal peace” between the two countries. This ended several decades of conflict between the two countries. The United States had gained its independence and successfully survived a second war with Great Britain. Despite these early struggles, the Treaty of Ghent created peace between these two countries that lasts to this day.

The United States was not the only North American country affected by the Treaty of Ghent. The treaty also set the border between the United States and Canada. Much of the actual fighting between Great Britain and the United States occurred in and along the border of Canada. The Treaty of Ghent established a long and lasting peace between the United States and Canada. These two countries maintain that border today.

Many Native People tribes fought in the war. However, they were not included in the peace talks that led to the Treaty of Ghent. Their British allies abandoned them following the war. With no support, they were left to resist American expansion alone. At the same time, the war convinced Congress to make the U.S. Army into a permanent, professional fighting force.

If the American Revolution created the United States, the Treaty of Ghent secured its position as a permanent country. In the years to come, the United States would claim even more Native People territory during the period after the War of 1812 and the Treaty of Ghent.

title: Civic Responsibility
text:
A civic responsibility is something that citizens are expected to do in the community. All citizens are expected to make choices for the common good. Members of a community are expected to obey laws. We are all expected to work to improve our communities.

Some civic responsibilities are enforced. This means that there are consequences if we do not follow them. Obeying the law and serving on a jury are enforced responsibilities. A jury is a group of citizens that is selected to decide a court case.

We vote to elect public officials. However, voting is not enforced. It is by choice. Volunteering is also by choice. It helps the community and people in need. Serving in the military or holding a public office are also things citizens can do to help their communities.

title: Andrew Jackson and the Battle of New Orleans
text:
The greatest victory for the United States during the War of 1812 actually happened after the signing of the Treaty of Ghent. The treaty was signed on Dec. 24, 1814. It wouldn't go into effect until after the U.S. Congress approved it and the president signed it. In the weeks it took to complete this process, the British and American forces fought one final major battle.

The Battle of New Orleans was fought over the mouth of the Mississippi River. Whichever country controlled the river would also control all traffic along the river. They would be able to ship goods and troops into and out of the inland areas of the United States. This advantage could turn the tide in a war.

Andrew Jackson took command of the United States' defense of New Orleans in late 1814. Like many American generals during the war, he lacked the number of troops he felt were necessary to defend the city. He quickly gathered a ragtag group of defenders. They included U.S. soldiers, marines, frontiersmen from Kentucky and Tennessee, local militia members, Choctaw people, pirates, and anyone else willing to take up arms.

This patchwork force was outnumbered by a force of around 8,000 professional British soldiers. What the American forces lacked in numbers, they made up for in preparation. They created a defense line called Line Jackson. The British would have to attack it in order to win. As the British attacked, Line Jackson held, and the American forces defeated the British attack. For 18 days, Jackson’s forces defended New Orleans against enemy attack and defeated the British on Jan. 26, 1815.

The victory ensured that the recently signed Treaty of Ghent would end the War of 1812. It also allowed the United States to end the war on a high note after a difficult war. This time in American history would become known as the "Era of Good Feeling." Andrew Jackson would ride the momentum of this victory all the way to the presidency in the years to follow.

title: Search for Freedom
text:
People from Europe wanted to explore the land in North America. Then, people from Europe wanted to live there. People move to new communities for different reasons. Sometimes the reason is for safety. Sometimes the reason is for new opportunities. Sometimes the reason is adventure. A group of people from England came to America in 1620 to start a new life.

In 1620, 102 people came to America on a ship called the Mayflower. They wanted to be free to worship in their own church. They wanted a chance to build a new home. They also wanted land to farm and make a living. They created a village called Plymouth. It was by the ocean in a state we call Massachusetts today. We call these people the Pilgrims.

title: Framing Question
text: How was the United States formed?

title: Thirteen Colonies
text:
The Pilgrims were not the only people who left England and came to America. More and more people came. Soon there were 13 colonies. The people cleared land by cutting down trees and large plants. This gave them room to plant more crops and build more houses.

Life in the colonies was very hard at first, but it got easier. The people learned how to live in their new land. They built better homes. Some people opened shops. The shops sold clothes, tools, food, and other things people needed. In 1635, the first public school opened in America.

title: The American Revolution
text:
The United States was once a colony. A colony is land controlled by a different country. Before the United States became a country, it was a colony of England. It was divided into 13 different colonies.

The colonists were required to give resources to England. They were required to give goods to England. They were also required to pay money to the government in England. This money was called taxes. Many people who lived in the colonies did not want to pay taxes to the English government. They wanted to create their own country.

In 1776, members of the colonies met in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. They agreed that the colonies should no longer be a colony of England. The English government did not like the decision the colonists made. The colonists and the government in England could not agree. The result was the American Revolution.

The American Revolution was a war. It was fought between the 13 Colonies and England. It was a long war. The war finally ended in 1781. After the war, the 13 Colonies became an independent country. The new country was named the United States of America. Many people fought in the war. Other people supported the soldiers and leaders of the army. They did this so our country would be free.

title: Patrick Henry
text: Patrick Henry was a famous writer. He was also famous for his speeches. He supported American independence. Henry also played an important role in the early government of the United States. He helped create many of the principles of American democracy that we still have today!

title: Abigail Adams
text: Abigail Adams was the wife of John Adams. John was an important member of the early government of the United States. Abigail wrote many letters to her husband during and after the war. She would often give him advice. She would help him with the problems he faced. John Adams became the second president of the United States. Abigail became the First Lady. She continued to help her husband lead the country.

title: Anne Hutchinson
text:
Anne Hutchinson and her family settled in the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1633. At the time, the colony was led by a group of people called the Puritans. The Puritans were very strict. Women were not allowed to be leaders in the church or community.

Hutchinson did not agree with this idea. She began to hold meetings in her home. She encouraged people to talk about their ideas and beliefs.

title: Dolley Madison
text:
Dolley Madison was the wife of James Madison. Her husband was the fourth president of the United States. Dolley Madison helped to raise funds for the Lewis and Clark expedition. This expedition explored land in the Pacific Northwest. It helped people learn about other parts of the country.

There was once a fire in the White House. Mrs. Madison saved important objects. She saved a very famous painting of George Washington

title: Betsy Ross
text: Betsy Ross lived in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Many people believe she made the first American flag. The story says that George Washington asked her to make a flag. It had 13 stripes and 13 stars. The stars and stripes stood for the 13 Colonies that became the first states.

title: Phillis Wheatley
text: Phillis Wheatley was a gifted author. She wrote many poems. Her poems supported the American cause for independence. She even wrote a poem about General George Washington. She was invited to meet him. Many people still read her poems and books today. They help people learn about life during the American Revolution.

title: Laws of Our Community
text:
We have community laws. They keep our community safe and clean. We use the crosswalk. We put our trash in bins.

People pass laws that help others. In Louisiana, we have a law that requires people to wear seatbelts. This helps keep people safe while driving.

Other laws that help keep people safe are speed limit laws. Louisiana sets speed limits on roads. That is so people do not drive too fast.

text: What is research? Research is a way to investigate a problem. It is a way to ask for more information. Research has three parts: asking questions, gathering evidence, and presenting ideas. For thousands of years before European exploration of the Western Hemisphere people called these continents home. These first peoples were very diverse. There are many different names that Canadian "Indigenous peoples" or Aboriginal people are called. The Canadian Constitution refers to three different group names: Indians (more commonly referred to as First Nations), Inuit and Métis. Each of these groups developed, practiced, and expressed their histories, languages, cultural practices, and their religious beliefs. According to the 2016 Census taken in Canada, more than 1.67 million people identify and refer to themselves as an Aboriginal person.

The early First Nations People were based on six geographical regions throughout the entire country of Canada. Woodland First Nations were based in the eastern part of Canada in the dense forests. The Iroquoian First Nations were in the fertile lands of the southern part of Canada. The Plains First Nations are located throughout the grasslands of the prairies throughout Canada. The Plateau First Nations are to the north in semi-desert to high mountains and forests. Pacific Coast First Nations are along the coast with red cedar lodging. The last geographical group is the First Nations of the Mackenzie and Yukon River Basins located with many different environments of dark forest, swamps, and barren land.

The Inuit people are known to some historians as the first people to have known and lived within Canada shorelines. Mainly located in the Northern part of Canada, this tribe is made up of 53 communities across four different regions with an estimated population of over 64,000 people. The Inuit’s have their own language, Inuktut, that is spoken throughout the regions with different dialects.

The Métis are based on two categories of racial categorization or political categorization. This has resulted in the way the Métis identify as a racial group as they have a deep history within Canada. Many Indigenous people married to Europeans or Euro-Canadian people. The Métis have their own spoken language called Michif and it is an identifier as well as the practicing of their culture and telling the history and stories of their ancestors.

Within Quebec there are three main geography based cultural groups of aboriginal people. They range from being a mixture of The Eastern Woodlands, the Subarctic Indigenous Peoples, and the Arctic Indigenous Peoples. The Eastern Woodlands Indigenous Peoples are located along the St. Lawrence River in Southern Québec. They can be categorized under a variety of language tribes throughout the region, however, the two prominent ones are the Algonquian and the Iroquois language groups. This group had the greatest contact with European explorers as they grew the fur trade along the Southern part of Canada and throughout the St. Lawrence River area.

The Subarctic Indigenous Peoples live throughout the middle section of Canada. Ranging from the Bering Sea to NewFoundland. Their primary languages broke off from the Algonquian and the Iroquois language groups. However, their own dialect and the influence from the Cree indigenous group helped each tribe to develop their own linguistic subgroup. The Arctic Indigenous People are also referred to as the Inuit tribe. They were mainly in the Northern part of Canada. They had very little contact with European explorers as they were isolated due to their geographical region.

title: American Geography and Resources
text:
Early colonists in America had to use every available resource to get what they needed to survive. Native Americans had been using natural resources for centuries. What resources were available to the colonists?

New England Colonies

In the New England Colonies, the Appalachian mountain range is close to the coast. The shoreline is rocky with small beaches. The mountains are snow-capped in winter and are covered in thick forests. The soil is rocky and thin. The weather is harsh in the winters and mild in the summers. Because of the cold winters, the animals have thick furs and many birds migrate south. The ocean and streams are home to a variety of wildlife.

Middle Colonies

The Appalachian Mountains are farther from the ocean in the Mid-Atlantic Colonies. The soil in the meadows is fertile and deep. Where rivers flow into the ocean, there are deep, natural harbors. The mountains are lower and don't have snow-capped peaks. There are thick, dense forests, and thickets provide protection for deer, small game, and birds. Chesapeake Bay is a home for birds and sea life.

Southern Colonies

In the Southern Colonies, the Appalachian Mountains are a greater distance from the coast. The hills extend from the foot of the mountains to the coastal plain. The waterways from the mountains come to the coast and provide deep harbors. In the hills, the soil is fertile and deep. Mild winters give way to long, hot summers. The birds from the north find homes in the south during the winters. The ocean currents are warm and bring many varieties of sea life.

title: Treatment of Diverse Groups in the Colonies
text:
As the colonies grew, they attracted people from all over Europe. Early colonists sailed from England, Ireland, and Scotland. Over time, more traveled from the Netherlands, France, Germany, and Sweden. Thousands of immigrants journeyed to the Americas seeking new opportunities. People came from diverse cultures with different backgrounds and belief systems. Jewish people settled mainly in port cities like New Amsterdam (now, New York City) or Newport, Rhode Island. They were especially attracted to colonies founded on religious freedom. Some colonies, like Georgia, had charters that promised religious liberty to all people. Not all migrants were welcomed into the colonies or treated fairly, though. The poor and the powerless were often mistreated in the colonies, just as they had been in England.

Women were expected to follow strict guidelines of behavior. These guidelines restricted women to certain roles. They were expected to perform household chores like cooking, cleaning, and laundry. Women could wash other people’s laundry to earn money or food. They could also be midwives, who deliver babies, because these jobs were considered suitable for women. Women couldn’t have any rights unless they were married or had a male guardian.

A lot of people died of disease or starvation in the early colonies. Parents lost children, and children lost parents. Orphaned children often became servants for other families so they could survive. They had few rights until they married.

Most colonists didn’t trust people who were not residents. The law was not kind to a person without a home. Strangers were treated with suspicion. A person who could not pay their way or was deep in debt would be imprisoned until the debt could be paid.

English colonial leaders never accepted Native Americans as citizens in their towns. Native Americans were not seen as equals to white European settlers. Some were even enslaved by the colonists.

Most African Americans in the colonies were enslaved people. A few were born free, bought their freedom, or were set free by their enslavers. African Americans were rarely accepted by white colonists.

title: Framing Question
text: How does the United States government work?

title: Democracy and Monarchy
text: A government is a group of people who lead a community. Government leaders work to serve the needs of the people in a community. There are many types of government systems in the world. Each system works differently. Most systems make and enforce laws. Pay special attention to the services provided by the government. Also, pay attention to the role of citizens in each of these types of governments.

title: Levels of Government
text: In the United States, we have a national government that leads the country. We have state governments that lead each state. We have local governments that lead our parishes. Local governments lead our cities. Local governments also lead our towns.

title: Framing Question

title: Sacrifices of the Founders
text:
Many of the Founders made sacrifices for the Revolution. The people who helped found our country pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor for the foundation of a new nation.

In letters to family and friends, Washington said he did not want to be president, but he was concerned that he didn’t have enough money to live out his retirement. In other words, he needed the job! Like other Founding Fathers after the war, he had land but no cash.

Washington owned a lot of land, but no one wanted to buy any of it. People who rented parts of his land didn’t have money to pay him. During the Revolution, he refused to accept pay for being the commander of the Army. He fed his staff and paid spies with his own money. After the war, the government paid him back in Continental dollars, which were worthless. Washington even had to borrow money to get to the Constitutional Convention in 1787.

Esther Reed lived in Philadelphia. She and her husband, Joseph Reed, supported the Revolutionary cause. Joseph was elected to the First Continental Congress and became a part of Washington’s army staff. Because of her husband's position, Esther had to leave Philadelphia. She spent much of the war evading British troops with her children. By 1780, Esther had moved back to Philadelphia and started the Ladies Association of Philadelphia. The Association raised about $7,500 for the Continental Army. Unfortunately, Esther got sick and died before she could see the money given to the Continental Army. Many Founders sacrificed their fortunes and lives for the cause of freedom.

title: Work
text:
Work helps communities grow. Work is an activity that makes a good or provides a service. It can be physical or mental. Baking and firefighting are physical work. Writing and doing math are mental work.

A job is work we do to earn money. Income is the money a person earns for doing their job. People use income to pay for their needs and wants.

title: Spending
text: Spending means using money to pay for goods or services. Spending your money carefully takes thought. There are many choices to make. People must choose where to spend their money. They also must choose how much they are willing to pay. The goods and services we need and want do not always cost the same. For example, not all shoes cost the same amount. Responsible people make wise decisions about spending their money.

title: Saving
text: Saving is keeping some of your money for the future. When you save money, you must decide where to keep it safe. Many people save money in a bank or credit union. This helps them to save up for something expensive. For example, people might save money for a vacation, house, or car. Sometimes we only need to save for a short amount of time. You can save money at home in a piggy bank, wallet, or safe. This works to save for less expensive things, like a new toy or shirt.

title: Education and Training
text:
There are many ways people can achieve their financial goals. One way is through education and training. Education is important no matter what job you do. It is important no matter what career you want. Colleges and universities teach people many topics or subjects. People that want to be teachers go to a college or university. There, they can earn a specific degree or education.

Some people go to a special school called a trade school. There, they can learn a specific skill. There are many types of trade programs. There are many schools that teach specific skills. People who want to become a car mechanic can attend a trade school. People wanting to become a welder can attend a trade school. So can people wanting to become a plumber. Someone wanting to become a medical assistant can attend a trade school. Many skills are taught at trade schools.

title: Goal Setting
text:
A goal is something that you want to do. You can create a plan to do it. Setting goals is a healthy behavior. It helps you grow. Setting goals shows that you believe in yourself. You can set goals to help you progress in every area of your life.

There are different types of goals:

Short-term goals can be reached quickly. You might be able to reach a short-term goal the same day you set it.

Example: Ramon set a goal to eat all his vegetables at dinner tonight.

Long-term goals take more time to reach. These goals may take weeks or months to reach. It could even take years to reach long-term goals.

Example: Julietta set a goal to not miss a day of school during her whole third grade year.

title: S.M.A.R.T. Activity
text:
The next time you want to set a goal, try this! Make your goal a S.M.A.R.T. goal. What does that mean? A S.M.A.R.T. goal is:

Specific

It should be clear what you want to do and how you will reach it.

Measurable

You must be able to measure your growth.

Attainable

It should be challenging but possible to reach.

Realistic

It should be a goal that makes sense and will help your life.

Timely

You must have a timeline to follow or a deadline.

Help Tanya with Her Goal!

Directions: Analyze Tanya’s goal. Determine if her goal is a S.M.A.R.T. goal. Answer each question with a “yes” or “no.”

Tanya’s Goal: Get a good grade in math.

Is Tanya’s goal specific? _______

Is Tanya’s goal measurable? __________

Is Tanya’s goal attainable? ________

Is Tanya’s goal realistic? ________

Is Tanya’s goal timely? _________

Now, with a partner, rewrite Tanya’s goal to make it a S.M.A.R.T. goal.

Specific

Measurable

Attainable

Realistic

Timely

title: Making Decisions
text:
It is important to make responsible decisions. We should think about decisions first. There are steps we can take to make responsible decisions.

Stop and think.

Think about the choices.

Think about the consequences.

Make your decision.

Think about your decision.

title: Europe Before Westward Exploration
text:
In the 1400s, the whole world was on the move. In the Americas, Africa, Asia, and Europe, empires were growing. Rich empires served as patrons, meaning they could pay people to study, explore, or create art for the glory of the empire. This patronage led to new advances in knowledge and exchanges of ideas through trade routes. A trade route is an area used by merchants for economic purposes.

In the Americas, new empires were rising. Near the Great Lakes, the Iroquois Confederacy was gaining more control over trade. Trade was expanding throughout the continent, including what is now Mexico and South America. In Central America, the Aztec Empire was expanding. Aztec rulers were patrons for many great poets. In South America, the Inca Empire was expanding. Inca rulers were patrons for inventors who developed new technologies for farming, medicine, and bridge building. The empire used this new knowledge to increase trade and exchange ideas.

Across the Atlantic Ocean, in Africa, the Songhai Empire was growing. Trade across the Sahara in salt and gold made the empire wealthy. Songhai leaders became patrons for education. Under the Songhai, thousands of scholars and students gathered to study at the famous libraries in the city of Timbuktu.

In the 1400s, most of the world’s people lived in Asia. China and India had the world’s largest economies because of their trading. Spices, silks, gold, and other goods were traded all the way to Europe. In the 1400s, the Ottoman Empire was rising between Asia and Europe. The Ottomans soon gained control of trade connections between Asia and Europe. The Ottomans were responsible for stopping trade to Europe.

For merchants in Europe, losing control of trade with Asia was hard. The countries of Portugal and Spain, however, saw an opportunity. These countries looked for new routes across the sea to Asia. Patrons from Portugal hoped to make money from trade in Africa and find a way to sail around Africa to Asia.

By 1490, Ferdinand and Isabella were the king and queen of Spain. Spain had just ended a religious war persecuting non-Christians. They had taken property from Jews and Muslims in Spain, which made them rich enough to be important patrons. Ferdinand and Isabella wanted new trade routes and income. They just needed the right idea to pay for and the right person to try it.

An entrepreneur named Christopher Columbus had an unusual idea. He hoped to sail west across the Atlantic Ocean and reach India that way. Columbus was looking for a patron. Columbus went to Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in Spain.

Isabella and Ferdinand agreed to be patrons for Columbus. They paid for three ships Columbus could use. They also paid for the tools and crew needed for the voyage. Columbus made an agreement with Ferdinand and Isabella. The agreement described what both Spain and Columbus would receive if his journey was successful. This agreement clarified that Spain and Columbus would share the profits from any cargo he brought back.

Columbus set sail from Spain in 1492. His journey would launch the biggest changes in government, knowledge, and trade the world had ever seen.

title: Government Leaders
text: Government leaders lead our city. They lead our state. They lead our country. Community members vote to choose government leaders.

title: Introduction to the Lesson
text:
Georgia’s geography, water, and other resources make it an ideal place to live. Historically, American Indians settled, lived, and thrived here for many generations. In the 1400s and 1500s, European empires began to send explorers all over the world. The explorers were charged with several responsibilities. These included searching for new trade routes, claiming land, and obtaining riches for their empire. In addition, some European empires wanted to convert anyone they encountered to their way of life and religion. Historians refer to this time in history as the Age of Exploration.

Spain and Britain, in particular, were interested in what are now Georgia, Florida, and South Carolina. Spain and Britain competed fiercely to claim these lands and their resources. When they arrived in North America, they found highly developed civilizations of Indigenous people already living there. These people had established cultures and religious beliefs. They had also cultivated the land and used its natural resources for their people.

title: Spanish Exploration of the Americas
text:
During the Age of Exploration, many Europeans explored lands and seas in North America. Historians generally agree that there were three big reasons for European exploration of the Americas: God, gold, and glory. Explorers looked for new lands and riches to conquer and claim for their country. They also hoped to convert new people to their religion and way of life. Europeans believed this would bring great glory to their country’s empire.

Shortly after Christopher Columbus traveled to the Americas in 1492, Spanish explorers called “conquistadors” followed. Conquistador is a Spanish term meaning “conqueror.” The Spanish were the first to explore the areas that are now the states of Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina.

One of the first known Spanish explorers of these areas was Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón. Ayllón set sail from Spain and landed in present-day South Carolina in 1526. He then traveled down the Georgia coastline. He and those with him established the first Spanish settlement on one of Georgia’s barrier islands. Due to winter conditions, the settlers could not plant crops for food. They soon had to abandon the settlement. Only 150 of the original 600 settlers survived the harsh winter.

Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto followed in Ayllón’s wake. De Soto had experience exploring and conquering lands in Central and South America. In 1532, de Soto was the chief lieutenant on conquistador Francisco Pizarro’s expedition to South America. There, the Spanish encountered the Inca civilization in present-day Peru. De Soto played a key role in conquering the Inca Empire. The Inca had never encountered European weapons before. The Spanish muskets and cannons led to the Inca’s demise.

After returning to Spain, de Soto learned of newly claimed land in North America. The Spanish called this land "La Florida." De Soto believed there would be civilizations and riches similar to the Inca there. De Soto assembled a team of 600 conquistadors to travel to La Florida. They set out in search of riches and glory and landed on the west coast of La Florida in 1539.

In 1540, de Soto traveled north from St. Augustine, Florida, into southeastern Georgia. Between 1540 and 1543, the Spanish explored the land. They followed American Indian trading trails, rivers, and creeks. De Soto and his men explored all over Georgia, South Carolina, and Alabama. They were often the first Europeans to encounter certain American Indian tribes. As they traveled, they also unknowingly spread European diseases. American Indian people had never been exposed to these diseases before. These diseases devastated American Indian communities. De Soto himself perished from fever near the Mississippi River on May 21, 1542.

Hernando de Soto never found the riches and gold he expected in North America. Some of the explorers, including de Soto himself, considered his expedition a failure. Despite this, maps and notes from his travels provided guidance for future Spanish explorers to navigate the region. Hernando de Soto and his expedition led the way for more people from Spain to sail to Georgia and the La Florida region.

title: French Settlement at Fort Caroline
text:
The Spanish weren’t the only Europeans looking to establish settlements in North America. French settlers and explorers came to what is now Florida in 1564. They were hoping to form religious Huguenot settlements. Huguenots were members of the Protestant Reformed Church of France. Because of their religion, they were persecuted by the Catholic Church and the French government between the 1500s and 1600s.

Many French Huguenots fled from France. They hoped to find new places to worship freely in North America. A man named René Goulaine de Laudonnière established Fort Caroline as an early Huguenot French settlement in La Florida. Fort Caroline was not a successful settlement for the French. Lack of supplies and unstable weather conditions, such as hurricanes, led to disaster for the settlement.

Spanish distrust of the French finally led to the demise of the settlement. In 1565, Spanish Admiral Pedro Menéndez de Avilés and his Spanish troops attacked the poorly guarded settlement. It is estimated that only 60 women and children survived the attack. The end of Fort Caroline led to the end of French claims to La Florida. This area is now the southeastern region of Florida and Georgia. This also led to a rise in Spanish interest in the area.

title: Spanish Missions on the Barrier Islands
text:
In the 1500s, the Spanish Empire was one of Europe's most powerful empires. Spanish explorers sailed around the world searching for gold, land, and resources. An important aspect of the Spanish Empire was its connection to the Catholic Church. The Catholic Church and the Spanish monarchy supported each other in many ways. Spanish military troops protected Spanish Catholic missionaries as they set up missions around the world. The Catholic missionaries’ purpose was to convert anyone they encountered to their religion and way of life.

The first missionaries in present-day Florida, Georgia, and South Carolina tried to build and establish Catholic missions. Between 1568 and 1570, Catholic Jesuits tried to convert the American Indian groups they encountered. Their efforts were mostly unsuccessful. Jesuits are an order of priests in the Catholic Church. Another group of Catholic missionaries, Franciscan friars, arrived from Spain in 1587. A friar is a member of a religious order or group of men in the Catholic Church. This marked the beginning of the Franciscan mission era in the area. Shortly after they arrived, Franciscan friars established the first missions along the barrier islands in Georgia. By 1595, missions were built in the northern coastal region of Georgia. This area was home to the Guale people.

Spanish missions were created specifically to convert Indigenous people to the Catholic faith. Converting to the Catholic faith required Indigenous people to reject their own people's traditions and adopt European culture. Missions were usually built within American Indian communities and served by a single friar. Missions usually had a chapel where mass was held. They usually also had a farm or workshop and living quarters for the friar. The Spanish used a labor system called "repartimiento" to produce crops or sellable goods. Repartimiento was the forced labor of American Indian men in exchange for a small wage. Under this system, the Spanish required American Indian community leaders to provide a certain number of men to work on the Spanish missions. These men worked in rotation. This means they traveled to the missions and worked for a period of weeks before returning home. Indigenous men had to work in the fields, workshops, and mines or build fortifications around the missions.

The Indigenous people faced harsh and often violent conditions in the missions. Sources show that missions became known for working and starving the American Indians to death. Other workers contracted European diseases to which they had no immunity. Those returning home from working at the missions carried disease back with them. Outbreaks and epidemics of these foreign diseases increased within Indigenous communities. Over time, this system contributed to the decreased American Indian population in Georgia and Florida. Some historians believe that during the years that the mission system was in place in Georgia, the Indigenous population declined by almost 90 percent. The Spanish government supported this system to control Indigenous people and the land. However, some Indigenous groups refused to accept the Spaniards' attempts at religious conversion and control.

In 1597, many Guale American Indians rose up to fight against the implementation of the Catholic Church’s rules and structures. A Guale leader named Juanillo did not want to give up his culture and way of life. He and his followers attacked five missions located on Guale land. All but one of the friars perished in the uprising, and all of the missions were burned to the ground. Sometimes called “Juanillo’s Uprising,” this revolt by the Guale people ended the push to continue the Spanish mission system in the Guale territory in Georgia. The remaining Spanish missions moved to the barrier islands. This lasted until raids by British pirates and privateers ultimately forced them to move south to St. Augustine, Florida. While the Spanish mission system remained in Florida for another hundred years, it never fully regained the power it once had. The remaining Spanish missionaries left Florida and moved to Cuba in 1763.

title: British Empire Exploration and Expansion
text: Like other European empires, the British were interested in finding new trade routes by sea. They also wanted to find new resources in the Americas. Foods like corn, tomatoes, and potatoes were highly sought after by Europeans. Other items from the Americas, such as tobacco and fur, were also in high demand in Europe. If they could secure reliable sources for these products, British explorers and merchants could sell them to other countries for a profit. Like other European countries, the British Empire sought to establish settlements and colonies in the Americas. This would allow them to grow crops and produce goods to sell back in Europe. Having colonies in the Americas also enabled an empire to extend its land holdings and control trade with Indigenous peoples.

title: Conflicts Between the Spanish and British over North America
text:
Conflicts between the Spanish and British empires can be dated back to the 1530s. King Henry VIII of England formally broke with the Catholic Church in 1534. He formed the Protestant Church of England. This became the official church of the British Empire. This new church allowed Henry VIII to divorce his wife and marry again. Divorce was not allowed by the Catholic Church.

The Catholic Church heavily influenced the leaders of the Spanish Empire. Some Spanish rulers felt that it was their moral obligation to convert the British back to the Catholic religion. This created a conflict between the two empires that lasted for generations.

In an effort to weaken the Spanish Empire, Henry VIII’s daughter, Queen Elizabeth I, instructed privateers (legally authorized pirates) to attack Spanish ships traveling to and from the Americas. Sir Francis Drake, an English sailor and explorer, was sent by Elizabeth I to burn the Spanish ports in the West Indies (modern-day Cuba, Puerto Rico, Haiti, Dominican Republic, and Jamaica) and the Americas. Drake also attacked Spanish settlements. This included burning St. Augustine, Florida, in 1586.

Elizabeth I also assigned the English explorer Sir Walter Raleigh to build a permanent settlement on the southeastern coast of North America. This was intended to disrupt Spanish influence in this region. It would also provide a strategic North American base for the British Empire.

Raleigh’s plans for a settlement were ultimately unsuccessful. He attempted to create a settlement on Roanoke Island. The island was located just off the coast of modern-day North Carolina. What happened to Roanoke Colony is still unclear. When the governor of the settlement, John White, sailed back to England in 1587 for supplies, the settlement appeared to be thriving. The naval war between the British and the Spanish Armada delayed White’s return for three years. When White finally arrived back at Roanoke Island in 1590, all 115 British settlers he had left there had disappeared without a trace. This included his daughter and granddaughter. There were only two clues about their disappearance. The first was the word "Croatoan" carved into a post within the fort. The second was the letters “CRO” carved into a tree. It was another 17 years before the British tried to establish another settlement. This second settlement, north of Roanoke, was given the name of Jamestown, Virginia.

The conflict between the Spanish and British empires lasted for nearly 20 years. The signing of the Treaty of London achieved a temporary end to the conflict in 1604. In the treaty, the Spanish and the British made many compromises to end the fighting. This included the end of the British attacks on Spanish ships in the Atlantic Ocean. In exchange, the Spanish acknowledged the Protestant Church of England as a legitimate religion. The treaty kept the peace between the two empires until 1625 when the 30-year Anglo-Spanish War broke out.

title: Impact of European Contact with American Indians
text:
European empires sailed all over the world during the Age of Exploration. They were driven by the lure of God, gold, and glory. Early successful expeditions to the Americas fueled the drive for empires to conquer Indigenous peoples and claim their lands. Along the way, these Indigenous people and their civilizations were changed forever.

The lasting impact of European exploration on American Indians and Indigenous peoples of other lands contributed to the destruction of their cultures and way of life. The introduction of European diseases decimated Indigenous populations. The impact of European contact was not limited to Spanish and British explorers. However, both empires had a long and lasting impact on the American Indians of the southeastern United States. This included tribes in modern Georgia and Florida.

The Spanish continued to send explorers and settlers into modern-day Mexico and South America. The British continued to expand their empire in North America. They did this by establishing colonies on the East Coast. Georgia was the last of the original 13 colonies to be established under British rule. The Europeans' presence and influence in the Americas changed the lives of American Indians and Indigenous peoples forever.

title: Documentos importantes
text:
El gobierno de los Estados Unidos se basa en valores específicos. Los valores de nuestra nación están definidos en documentos jurídicos, políticos e históricos. Los documentos escritos durante la historia de nuestra nación son los resultados visibles de reglas y leyes. Protegen los derechos de los ciudadanos. Encontramos estos documentos a nivel local, del estado y nacional.

A nivel nacional, entre los documentos importantes figuran la Declaración de Independencia, la Constitución de los Estados Unidos y la Carta de Derechos. Las leyes, los tratados y los acuerdos comerciales también se consideran documentos nacionales importantes. Estos documentos describen nuestros derechos y responsabilidades como ciudadanos. A nivel del estado, los documentos importantes incluyen la constitución del estado, las leyes y códigos del estado, el registro de votantes y los documentos que protegen a los animales y la tierra.

title: Estatutos y tratados
text:
Un estatuto era un documento legal emitido por un gobernante o un gobierno a una persona o grupo de personas. Un estatuto describe acuerdos y otorga ciertos derechos. Durante la exploración europea, muchos reyes emitieron estatutos en diferentes países, que a menudo se aplicaban a la misma tierra. Cuando esto sucedía, ambos países creían que eran dueños de esa tierra. Los estatutos para las nuevas tierras eran a menudo otorgadas por reyes o reinas a personas muy apreciadas. Si esa persona caía en desgracia, no era raro que el gobernante emitiera un estatuto para la misma tierra a otra persona.

Los estatutos establecían el gobierno de la colonia. Definían los derechos y privilegios de los colonos. Los estatutos también explicaban el propósito de la colonia y describían el sistema de impuestos que debían pagarse al rey patrocinador. Estos documentos eran contratos vinculantes entre el rey y los colonos y funcionaban de la misma manera que una constitución.

Un tratado es un documento legal creado para poner fin a un conflicto. Los representantes de ambas partes en un conflicto se reúnen y discuten lo que debería estar en el acuerdo o tratado. Ambas partes dicen lo que quieren y qué están dispuestas a conceder para poner fin al conflicto. Este debate se llama negociación. Una vez que ambas partes llegan a un consenso, el tratado puede convertirse en ley. Ambas partes hacen lo que acordaron. Si violan el tratado, hay consecuencias que a menudo tienen que ser aplicadas en un tribunal por jueces y abogados.

title: Declaración de Independencia
text:
La Declaración de Independencia es uno de los documentos más importantes de la historia de los Estados Unidos. Ayudó a crear los cimientos de los Estados Unidos como nación independiente.

Muchos colonos americanos pensaban que el rey Jorge III y su gobierno eran injustos y no respetaban sus derechos o libertades. En el verano de 1776, el Segundo Congreso Continental se reunió en Filadelfia para discutir estas preocupaciones. Después de muchos intentos de obtener concesiones del rey, el Congreso votó a favor de la independencia. Redactaron un documento que explicaba sus razones para declarar la independencia. También proporcionaban evidencia de los errores del rey y de lo que tenían la intención de hacer con respecto a sus preocupaciones. El Congreso Continental argumentó que el rey les había denegado sus derechos inalienables. Estos son los derechos a "la vida, la libertad y la búsqueda de la felicidad". Estos derechos no pueden quitarse.

Los colonos proporcionaron una lista de veintisiete agravios en respaldo de esa afirmación. Los colonos explicaron que si el rey no respetaba sus libertades, romperían todos los lazos políticos con él. Se convertirían en una nación soberana independiente. Las ideas y creencias de la Declaración de Independencia sentaron las bases para otros documentos importantes de la historia de nuestra nación.

title: La Constitución
text:
En el verano de 1787, los Fundadores se reunieron para crear un nuevo gobierno para nuestra joven nación. Después de meses de opiniones contradictorias y acalorados debates, finalmente llegaron a un acuerdo.

Los Fundadores de la Constitución eran delegados designados por las legislaturas de los estados para velar por el bienestar de cada estado. El propósito de los Fundadores era revisar los Artículos de la Confederación. Los Artículos de la Confederación fueron la primera constitución de nuestra nación. Fueron escritos en 1777, después de la Guerra Revolucionaria con Gran Bretaña. La Constitución fue el resultado del arduo trabajo y dedicación de nuestros Fundadores.

La Constitución de los Estados Unidos es la ley suprema de nuestro país y el plan para nuestro gobierno. Su propósito es describir los deberes del gobierno y los derechos del pueblo gobernado. La Constitución establece nuestro gobierno con principios específicos, o verdades básicas, en mente. Define las responsabilidades básicas del gobierno federal o nacional. La Constitución organiza los tres poderes del gobierno. También garantiza nuestros derechos individuales, que no pueden ser denegados ni arrebatados por el gobierno.

La Constitución establece el principio de la soberanía popular. La soberanía popular significa que el pueblo debe estar a cargo de crear el gobierno. Significa que el gobierno debe escuchar la voluntad del pueblo, o lo que la mayoría del pueblo quiere. La Constitución se basa en el concepto único de proteger los derechos individuales y dar poder al pueblo.

Nuestro país se rige por la Constitución desde hace más de 200 años. Es la constitución escrita y aún vigente más antigua del mundo.

title: El Pacto de Mayflower
text:
El Pacto del Mayflower tenía sólo 166 palabras, pero es uno de los documentos más famosos de los primeros años de la historia estadounidense. Un pacto es un acuerdo. Los líderes de los Peregrinos se preocupaban por que, sin un conjunto claro de leyes para la colonia, no habría orden. Sin orden, la colonia no tendría éxito. El Pacto le dio a cada hombre una porción del liderazgo de la colonia. Afirmaba que sólo se aprobarían leyes que fueran buenas para todos. El Pacto también señalaba que todos estarían de acuerdo en obedecer las leyes. Todos los hombres adultos leyeron y debatieron acerca del Pacto y luego accedieron a firmarlo.

El Pacto del Mayflower muestra la idea del autogobierno. Autogobierno es la capacidad de las personas de crear leyes por sí mismas en beneficio de todos los ciudadanos. Esta es una idea central en nuestro gobierno de hoy. Las mujeres desempeñaron un papel importante en el Mayflower y en Plymouth. Sin embargo, no se les permitió firmar el Pacto del Mayflower. En ese momento, sólo los hombres creaban las leyes y reglas en un gobierno.

Los colonos cumplieron con el Pacto, y la colonia sobrevivió. Un año después, un hombre llamado John Pierce amplió el Pacto del Mayflower. Lo hizo para que el gobierno inglés lo apoyara. El Pacto del Mayflower se siguió utilizando para gobernar la colonia de Plymouth durante más de 70 años.

title: Enmiendas a la Constitución
text:
Cuando el Congreso creó la Constitución, sabía que algunos cambios podrían ser necesarios en el futuro. Incluyeron un proceso para agregar o cambiar partes de la Constitución original. Los cambios en la Constitución se denominan enmiendas. Las enmiendas son adiciones destinadas a mejorar un documento. Hoy en día, hay 27 enmiendas a la Constitución de los Estados Unidos. Las 10 primeras enmiendas se conocen como la Carta de Derechos. Estas enmiendas a la Constitución fueron creadas por sus autores para proteger los derechos de los ciudadanos y crear la estructura de nuestro gobierno.

Ha habido muchos cambios en la Constitución en sus 200 años de historia. Sin embargo, no es fácil enmendar la Constitución. Para insertar una enmienda a la Constitución, se debe presentar una enmienda al Congreso. Ambas partes del Congreso, el Senado y la Cámara de Representantes votan sobre cualquier cambio. Si dos tercios o más de los miembros del Congreso están de acuerdo en el cambio, entonces pasa al Presidente. Si el Presidente no está de acuerdo, puede vetar, o votar en contra del cambio. Todas las enmiendas actuales han pasado por este proceso. Este proceso asegura que todos los ciudadanos tengan la capacidad de participar en las decisiones gubernamentales.

title: Controles y equilibrios
text:
Los escritores de la Constitución de Estados Unidos querían que el gobierno de la nueva nación fuera fuerte y duradero. Para lograr esto, tuvieron una idea. El gobierno utilizaría un sistema de controles y equilibrios entre los tres poderes del gobierno. Esto significa que cada poder del gobierno estadounidense tiene

la facultad de controlar a los otros dos.

Cada poder tiene la facultad de impedir ciertas acciones de otro poder. Esto sucede si un poder cree que esas acciones son inconstitucionales o que no se realizan en beneficio del país. El sistema de controles y equilibrios ayuda a asegurar que ningún poder del gobierno se vuelva demasiado poderoso.

El Congreso puede crear una ley, pero el presidente debe aprobarla. El Congreso también puede anular la decisión del presidente de vetar o rechazar una ley. La Corte Suprema tiene el poder de anular una ley que ha sido aprobada tanto por el Congreso como por el presidente si considera que la ley es inconstitucional. El presidente nombra jueces a la Corte Suprema, pero el Congreso debe aprobar a los candidatos. Debido al sistema de controles y equilibrios, los ciudadanos estadounidenses pueden estar seguros de que sus derechos estarán siempre protegidos.

title: Constituciones de los estados
text:
Al igual que la Constitución de Estados Unidos, las constituciones de los estados garantizan y protegen los derechos básicos de los ciudadanos. Las constituciones de los estados establecen las reglas para el gobierno del estado. También explican cómo un estado puede hacer leyes. Las constituciones de los estados describen cómo el gobierno del estado divide y comparte el poder con los condados y las ciudades.

Las constituciones de los estados pueden cambiar con el tiempo. Estos cambios se denominan enmiendas. Los legisladores y votantes pueden trabajar juntos para enmendar la constitución existente del estado, para satisfacer las necesidades de los ciudadanos. Enmendar significa cambiar o añadir. Los ciudadanos pueden votar para enmendar la constitución de su estado.

title: Análisis de la Constitución de tu estado
text:
Cada estado tiene su propia Constitución. Para esta tarea, analiza la Constitución de tu estado. Determina si tiene los mismos elementos que la Constitución de Estados Unidos que se enumeran en el cuadro que figura a continuación. Si comparte el mismo elemento, tilda la columna «Sí». Si no lo comparte, tilda la columna «No».
