title: Connecting Themes
text: In social studies, there are a number of common themes that you will encounter. These themes show up throughout history and in all parts of the world. Trained historians, geographers, anthropologists, and other experts use these themes to understand the history and development of cultures and societies. Exploring social studies through these themes will help you make connections across time and space. You will begin recognizing similarities and trends. Making these connections will enhance your understanding of the world and its past, present, and future.

title: Conflict and Change
text: Throughout history, there have almost always been conflicts. Societies have competed for land and resources. Groups with opposing ideas have fought to impose their beliefs on one another. Conflict has developed because of mistreatment, injustice, and a variety of other causes. In each instance of conflict, there has been a change of one kind or another. Conflict and change have been connecting themes throughout history. Usually, the goal of conflict is to bring about change. Changes can include the availability of resources, practicing certain beliefs, the treatment of certain groups of people, and more. People who engage in conflict usually do so because they do not like the way things are. When things cannot be changed peacefully, people often resort to conflict. This can include rebelling or going to war to achieve their goals and change the world.

title: Essential Question
text: How do the connecting themes of social studies help people understand the past, present, and future?

title: Gain from Trade
text: No society has access to all of the natural resources and manufactured goods in the world. In order to gain the resources and goods they lack, societies trade what they have for what they need. Some societies have natural trade advantages. Early societies benefited from easy-to-travel geographies, like long, safe coastlines or flat terrain. This allowed them to more easily move their goods and resources to other places, where they could trade them. As transportation technology improved, large bodies of water, tall mountain ranges, and arid deserts became less of a barrier to trade. This allowed more societies to meet their needs through trade. As trade routes and trade relationships developed, more and more people began to use trade for gain. When done well, both sides of a trade benefit from the interaction.

title: Human-Environment Interaction
text:
The interaction between humans and the natural environment is a connecting theme throughout human history. The environment has long impacted human society. Humans have met their needs for food and shelter from the plants and animals around them. Rivers and lakes provided fresh water for early civilizations. As societies developed, people became more capable of extracting natural resources from the environment.

Different climates exist around the world, which affect the distribution of resources. Deserts provide very different resources than forests or grasslands. Natural disasters, such as droughts and fires, have altered natural environments. Their impact has changed the course of history as a result. Humans have also had positive and negative effects on the environment. The development of modern cities has changed landscapes permanently. Pollution has also affected the environment. The connecting theme of human-environment interaction has been persistent throughout human history in every society. It has affected when, where, and how human societies have developed, succeeded, and failed.

title: Location
text:
In social studies, location refers to where something is on the Earth. A society’s location affects its economy, development, and culture, among other things. A location near valuable natural resources can benefit a society. It allows that society to use and trade those resources to advance the economy.

For example, a coastal location could create a maritime culture in which fishers gather seafood and trade requires shipping goods across the seas. A society like this likely trades and expands more quickly than other societies because of ocean access.

Due to its harsh climate, a desert location might require cultural adaptations that value the conservation of resources like water.

A forest location can supply timber to build structures, tools, and modes of transportation. This can improve economic opportunities.

Location can also hinder a society. A lack of resources or trade routes can keep a society from developing. Some locations can prevent people from trading with neighboring societies or accessing their resources. Throughout history, the connecting theme of location has influenced the formation and development of societies worldwide.

title: Movement and Migration
text: The connecting theme of movement and migration has been common throughout history. Migration, or the movement of a group of people, happens for many reasons. People have been forced to move due to events like natural disasters, war, famine, or a lack of economic opportunities. A push factor is a negative factor that drives a person or group to move away from a place. People also move to new locations due to economic opportunities, freedom, or better living conditions. A benefit that draws a person or group to move to a location is called a pull factor. Push and pull factors for migration have influenced the movement of people around the world for thousands of years.

title: Production, Distribution, and Consumption
text:
Each society produces, distributes, and consumes goods and resources in unique ways. This is usually determined by the society's location, beliefs, and government. A society’s location determines what resources it has available and what kinds of goods it can produce. These goods can then be distributed and consumed.

Societies have different ideas about how to distribute their goods. Government policies and actions often enforce how distribution is handled. Some governments distribute goods more evenly amongst their people. Other governments are less involved in the distribution of goods as people buy and sell things in a market system.

The connecting theme of production, distribution, and consumption explains the actions of many different sectors of society. People produce goods and resources, which are then distributed and consumed according to government policies and the people's customs.

title: Time, Change, and Continuity
text: The passage of time naturally leads to change. Ideas, customs, technologies, languages, and more all change over time. As much as things change over time, many things stay the same. Continuity over time gives cultures and societies an identity. This connecting theme is a major component of the study of history. A close study of history reveals how societies have changed and stayed the same over time. Each society changes or enjoys continuity at a different rate. Some societies change at a faster rate, while others maintain continuity more distinctly. Comparing the change and continuity of societies over time reveals a great deal about their history and culture.

title: Scarcity
text: Renewable resources are limited, and most have only recently been made available through technology. Most resources are finite, which means that they will run out eventually. A forest only has so many trees in it. Coal deposits only contain a certain amount of coal. The scarcity of resources forces people to choose what resources to use and what to use them for. These choices require costs that people must consider when they make their choices. The more scarce a resource, the more valuable it is. If a society possesses a scarce resource, it can use it to boost its economy. If a society needs a scarce resource, then it must decide what costs it must pay to acquire that resource.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: The connecting themes that have been studied provide scholars with a way of framing society and studying its past, present, and future. As unique as each society is and has been, they all share many similarities. Each one deals with change and continuity over time. They have all been affected by migration and the ways people in those societies have interacted with the environment. All societies have developed cultures influenced by scarcity, governance, and location. Conflict has created change in them all. Economies have grown and shrunk through production, distribution, consumption, and trade. Studying societies through connecting themes will reveal the similarities and differences between societies around the world.

title: Introduction to Geography
text:
Geography is the study of the Earth and its various characteristics. It helps us understand the Earth, its regions, its cultures, and its relationship to those living there. People who study geography and help others understand it are called geographers. Geographers study the Earth’s physical and human features. Physical features occur naturally, such as mountains, rivers, and oceans. Human features are those created by people. These include boundaries, towns, and roads. Geographers also study the relationship between the land's physical characteristics and human activities. They examine how different cultures interact with the land and how location impacts the people living there.

There are two types of geography: physical geography and human geography. Physical geography studies the exterior physical features and changes of the Earth. That includes seasons, climate, atmosphere, soil, bodies of water, and landforms. Human geography is the study of how humans in all places and cultures adapt to their natural geographic environments.

The study of geography also includes how things change over time. Geographers ask questions to understand and solve problems. Knowing where problems exist in the world helps geographers see how those problems impact the environment. Suppose the environment is polluted or people in the environment are struggling. In that case, geographers identify where the problem is so that solutions can be found.

The themes of geography are location, place, human-environment interaction, movement, and regions. They serve as a framework to aid in understanding the world. These themes help to ask and answer important questions about the world and its people. When geographers study these themes, they organize their thinking about the world into spatial terms. They gather geographic data through field observations, maps, globes, graphs, diagrams, aerial photographs, satellite imagery, and censuses.

Modern technology provides geographers with sophisticated tools to help them better understand the Earth’s physical and cultural features. A global positioning system (GPS) uses satellites to identify locations on the Earth’s surface. Remote sensing (RS) equipment on aircraft, satellites, ships, and similar vehicles collects data on large areas or areas that were once inaccessible. Once the data has been gathered, geographic information systems (GIS) help geographers analyze and display the data collected.

title: Essential Question
text: How does the use of maps help to retrieve social studies information?

title: Map Skills
text:
Globes

Globes have been used for over 2,100 years. The oldest surviving globe dates back to 1492, just before Christopher Columbus sailed to explore the world. A globe is a three-dimensional model of the Earth. Globes show the location of water, land, and countries. Because a globe is round, it can represent surface features, directions, and distances more accurately than a flat map.

Maps

Maps show locations of features of the Earth and distances between places. They are usually flat. Maps also show the sizes and shapes of countries. However, they are not as accurate as globes. Globes are the same shape as the Earth. Globes show the location of water, land, and countries. A globe represents the size and shape of oceans and continents more accurately. This makes it easier to represent shapes, distances, and sizes closer to how they really are on Earth. Shapes, distances, and sizes become distorted on a map.

A person who creates a map is called a cartographer. Like the author of a book, a cartographer has a point of view and a purpose. A cartographer decides what to include on a map. The title of the map tells us what the map is about. There are map tools that we use to help us when using maps and globes.

Map Tools

Map tools include the title, legend, compass rose, cardinal directions, and scale. A cartographer includes different map tools to help people read a map. The map’s legend explains what the symbols and colors on the map represent. The legend also includes a scale. The scale helps people understand distance when using the map. Distance is how far it is from one place to another.

Most maps have a compass rose. The compass rose is a symbol that shows the cardinal directions. Cardinal directions are the four main points on a compass: north, south, east, and west. They help us to locate places around the world. North and south refer to the poles of the Earth. Sometimes, a compass rose can include intermediate directions. Northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast are all intermediate directions.

Hemispheres

To make mapping and navigation easier, the world is divided up with imaginary lines. Cartographers use these lines on most of the maps they make. The lines drawn around the Earth divide the Earth into equal halves, called hemispheres. The prefix "hemi-" means half, so a hemisphere is half of a sphere. The Earth has four hemispheres: Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western.

The Equator is an imaginary line dividing the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. North America, the northern part of South America, Europe, the northern two-thirds of Africa, and most of Asia are located in the Northern Hemisphere. Most of South America, one-third of Africa, Australia, Antarctica, and some Asian islands are located in the Southern Hemisphere.

The Prime Meridian divides the world into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres. It runs from the North Pole to the South Pole. Historically, Earth's Prime Meridian passed through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich in London, England. Today, cartographers use the International Reference Meridian. It is 102 meters east of the old Greenwich meridian.

Longitude and Latitude

Every place in the world has coordinates. They are sort of like an address. Coordinates are identified by imaginary lines around the Earth, called lines of latitude and longitude. Lines of longitude are vertical lines that go from the North Pole to the South Pole. They show how far east or west places are from the Prime Meridian. These lines are also called meridians. The lines of latitude are the horizontal lines that measure how far north or south places are from the Equator. Latitude and longitude are measured in degrees.

Lines of latitude and longitude are the lines cartographers use to determine the position or location of any place on the surface of the Earth. The place where latitude and longitude meet determines that place’s coordinates.

International Date Line

The International Date Line (IDL) is a relatively new line. It, too, is an imaginary line on Earth's surface. The line is drawn from the North Pole to the South Pole. It is located halfway around the world from the Prime Meridian. The IDL is the line that defines the boundary between one day and the next. When traveling east from the International Date Line, travelers subtract a day. If they are traveling west, they add a day.

Imagine this: If it was 7 a.m. in Georgia and someone wanted to call a friend on the west coast of the United States, it would be 4 a.m. If that person wanted to call a friend who lived in Auckland, New Zealand, the time would be 17 hours ahead of Georgia, or midnight the next day. That's because New Zealand is so far east of Georgia.

title: Forms of Government
text:
How a government is organized determines who has power and how much power they have. Some forms of government put power in the hands of very few people, or even just one person. Other forms of government spread power and responsibilities amongst many groups and individuals. In some governments, citizens can participate by voting, running for office, and even contributing their thoughts and ideas during government meetings. Not all forms of government allow this level of citizen participation.

Autocracy vs. Democracy

One main difference in forms of government is who has power and how much power they have. In an autocratic form of government, or autocracy, one person has all the power. In government, the word "power" means the ability to make decisions and direct the actions of others, especially citizens and government officials. Depending on the specific government, that person might be referred to by a title like king, queen, emperor, or dictator. They may be advised by one or more people. Other government officials carry out their orders. The leader of an autocratic government shares power with no one.

There are several ways an autocratic leader gains power. In a monarchy, the leader gains power due to their family. Kings and queens gain power in many ways. Some monarchs inherit the throne through their family lines. The same is usually true of an emperor. Other autocratic leaders take power through rebellion or war. Others gain power over time by using their power to change laws and influence the government in a way that gives them more power.

By contrast, in a democratic form of government, or democracy, power is shared by all citizens. In some democratic governments, citizens make decisions together through debate and voting. In others, citizens come together to vote for their leaders. In this process, all citizens have the right to vote for their leader or leaders. Because they have been elected to their position, a democratic leader is seen as a representative of the people. They exercise their power according to specific rules and restrictions that keep them from gaining too much power.

Presidential vs. Parliamentary Democracy

There are different forms of democratic governments. In a presidential democracy, citizens elect their leaders to different levels and branches of government. These levels and branches are independent of one another. The highest government office is the president. The president is elected by the citizens with specific powers and responsibilities. These powers are checked by an independent group of elected officials called a legislature. The legislature also has its own powers and responsibilities, which are meant to balance the power of the president and ensure no one branch of government gains too much power.

In a parliamentary democracy, the citizens elect the members of the legislative body, which is called parliament. The legislature then appoints the leader of the country to a position similar to a president. This position is often called the prime minister, and that person has specific powers and responsibilities as well. Those powers are much more likely to be closely monitored and aligned with the positions of the legislative majority than in a presidential democracy.

title: Essential Question
text: How do government and economic systems impact the development of a country?

title: Citizen Participation in Government
text:
Citizens can participate in government in a variety of ways. Voting is the most common form of citizen participation. Depending on the form of government, citizens can vote for who they want to represent them in the government. They can also vote on specific issues and laws. Citizens can also participate in government by serving in the government. They might work for the government or be elected by their fellow citizens as a representative. There are other ways to participate in government. These include participating in public government meetings, interacting with elected officials, and even protesting the actions and decisions of the government.

Autocratic governments offer no opportunity for citizens to participate in government. All the ways that citizens can participate in the government and exercise political power are denied to them by the autocratic leader. That person holds all power and shares none with the citizens. Citizens have no opportunity to vote for their leaders or participate in the government. Even protesting and speaking out against the government can be illegal in an autocratic government.

By contrast, a democratic government requires citizen participation. Leaders within a democratic government are chosen by the citizens through voting. Every citizen’s vote counts the same. No one has more influence on an election than anyone else. In a presidential democracy, citizens elect officials to different branches of government. They vote for representatives to serve in the legislature. There, they have certain responsibilities, like making laws. They also elect the president, who serves independently of the legislature. In a parliamentary democracy, the citizens elect their legislative representatives, who appoint an overall leader.

Democracies are also much more likely to ensure that the right to participate in the government in ways other than voting is protected. In some democratic governments, certain levels of government are required to hold public meetings that citizens can attend and participate in through comments and debates. There can also be certain rules that elected officials must follow regarding being available for communication with the people they represent. There are usually laws that protect the right of citizens to protest the government as well.

title: Types of Economies
text:
A country’s economy is the collection of all the ways resources and goods are created, acquired, traded, and consumed by the people of that country. There are different ways to organize and operate an economy. Each economy is unique due to different locations, available resources, and other factors. Despite this, economies generally incorporate features of one or more economic systems. Each economic system has advantages and disadvantages.

Traditional Economy

A traditional economy usually revolves around gathering and using basic resources. Economies that rely on farming are considered traditional economies. People in a traditional economy usually only create enough for themselves and their families. They do not usually produce an economic surplus that can be used to trade with other countries or societies. Before more complex versions developed, this is how the first economies worked.

Command Economy

In a more complex economy, laborers are able to create a surplus of goods and resources. People are able to do different jobs. They can become specialists at one job instead of everyone doing the same job of growing food or gathering resources. Because there are more resources than needed and people are doing different jobs, there is a question as to how to ensure the economy is producing everything that is needed. Surplus goods and resources are used or traded effectively.

In a command economy, the government takes on the role of economic planner. Economic decisions and efforts are directed by a government organization. This organization is tasked with meeting the needs of its people and maximizing the wealth of the country. In a true command economy, the government determines all aspects of the economy. What resources are gathered, what products are created, and perhaps even what job each person does are all controlled by the government. Command economies are more likely to be found in autocratic governments, in which power is held in the hands of one person or very few people. They have the power to make these decisions and use the influence of the government to make them happen.

Market Economy

In a market economy, the government plays no role in economic planning and decisions. People in a market economy have complete freedom to pursue whatever economic activities they want. The theory is that the forces of supply and demand will create positive economic conditions. Demand describes how much of a desire there is for a resource, good, or service in society. Supply is how much of that resource, good, or service is available. In a market economy, it is argued that the forces of supply and demand will naturally guide people’s economic decisions. Workers will direct their efforts to create things that people want, and people will then buy those things. In a pure market economy, there is no central organization of the economy.

Mixed Economy

Command and market economies are two extremes. There is either complete control of the economy, or there is no centralized control, and all actions are permitted. It is rare that a real-world economy is at one extreme or the other. Most economies are somewhere in the middle between a command and a market economy. This is called a mixed economy, where aspects of each are combined. An economy might be mostly organized by the government while including components of the economic freedom in a market economy. A market economy might still include certain government restrictions in order to ensure fair and proper economic outcomes.

title: What Is Trade?
text:
Trade is the exchange of goods between individuals or groups of people. In an economic system, trade is the process by which a country will produce a surplus of something and sell that surplus to another country for money. People can then use that money to buy goods from other countries. In this context, goods can refer to any item that can be bought or sold. This includes natural resources, like iron and gas, as well as products like cars and chocolate bars.

The goods and resources sold to another country are called exports. Countries export those goods to make a profit. The country that receives the goods is importing them. Goods received through trade are called imports. A complex modern economy will include a system of imports and exports. Surplus goods will be sold to other countries. Goods that are needed will be purchased from countries that have a surplus of that good.

In this way, countries can take advantage of a surplus in natural resources or in their ability to manufacture a certain product. In a command economy, the decision of which natural resources to gather or which products to manufacture for export is directed by the government. In a market economy, the people decide what goods to gather and manufacture. The expectation is that people will decide which products or resources will generate the greatest amount of money. They then pursue the manufacture of those products and gathering of those resources.

The same is true of imports. In a command economy, imports are decided upon by the government. In a market economy, imports are pursued by individual companies and people with no interference from the government.

In mixed economies, imports and exports are determined by a combination of governmental decisions and supply and demand. Companies generally conduct international trade. The government sets rules and regulations to ensure that economic efforts generate positive outcomes for the country and its citizens.

title: Voluntary and Involuntary Trade
text:
Trade that follows the principles of a market economy is called voluntary trade. People in a market economy are free to pursue the import and export of goods without government intervention or direction. Actions in voluntary trade are driven by supply and demand. People make decisions to create a supply of goods for which there is demand. Voluntary trade is often the result of a democratic form of government. The freedom citizens enjoy in a democracy often results in a more market-driven economy. Voluntary trade is encouraged in a market economy.

A benefit to voluntary trade in a market economy is that people are encouraged to pursue the greatest profit they can create. Their decisions are driven by market forces. Decisions are not determined by the government. A market economy can create substantial economic growth through freedom and voluntary trade. The downside to this is that there is no central organization controlling economic decisions. This could lead to situations in which actions are taken that enrich individuals or companies but ultimately harm the overall economic system. This system creates risk for people because they are left to make their own economic choices, which could succeed or fail.

Trade that is controlled and directed by the government in a command economy is called involuntary trade. There is no freedom in a command economy to respond to supply and demand. The government may take those things into account when making decisions. However, people in a command economy are not free to choose what goods to import and export. Involuntary trade is more often the economic system of an autocratic government. The leader of the government maintains power over the economy. They direct the economic actions of the people. The lack of freedom in an autocratic government usually extends to the economic system as well.

A benefit to involuntary trade in a command economy is that all aspects of the economy can be planned out. If done correctly, this can lead to all economic needs being met through centralized planning. It can provide for all the needs of its citizens without excessive waste or effort. This system takes economic risk from individuals and puts it on the collective population of the country. Individuals are generally protected from the risks of economic failure. However, it is possible that the government can make bad economic choices that affect everyone.

Mixed economic systems include aspects of both voluntary and involuntary trade. Individuals and companies in a mixed system are usually allowed to pursue economic opportunities for international trade without specific directions from the government. Instead, the government places certain restrictions or regulations to control the level of risk to the people and the country as a whole. There are a variety of barriers the government can place on trade. Barriers control imports and exports without completely taking over all aspects of the economic system.

title: Barriers to Trade
text:
Barriers to trade are anything that interrupts or regulates voluntary trade. Sometimes, trade barriers can be natural. Think of geographical features that make travel and trade difficult or impossible. Tall mountain ranges, wide rivers, oceans, and deserts have all historically been barriers to trade. Even in our modern world, with airplanes and ships that can travel long distances, it still takes great effort to overcome these geographic barriers. The cost and effort of overcoming these barriers can also be considered a barrier.

Other trade barriers can be imposed by the government. The most likely trade barrier used by a government is a tariff. This is a tax the government can charge on imported goods to protect manufacturers in their country. If imported goods are less expensive than goods produced in their country, then everyone will buy the imported goods. The company in the country might go out of business. In order to encourage people to buy the local product, the government can use a tariff to make imported goods more expensive. This will lower the demand for imported goods and increase demand for the local goods.

Another way governments can impose barriers to trade is to create quotas on imports and exports. A quota is a limit on the amount of a certain good or resource that can be imported or exported by companies in a given country. In a completely free market economy, there is no limit to the amount of imports and exports. However, governments will use quotas to restrict imports or exports. If too much of a good is being traded, the government can use quotas to regulate the trade of that good. Changing the supply of a good can then impact the demand for it. This can change the behavior of the market economy as a result.

Governments can even use trade barriers to punish other countries. An embargo is a restriction on trade with a target country. Governments can place an embargo on specific goods. They can also place one on the import and export of all goods to and from a target country. Embargoes can be put in place by one country or a group of countries in an effort to punish a country. They can also force that country to take a specific action, like ending a war. Embargoes can have a major negative impact on a country’s economy. They limit the ability of a country to trade surplus goods to make money and import things they need.

title: Specialization and Trade
text:
Countries are not generally able to gather all of the resources or manufacture all of the products they need and want within their borders. Sometimes, there are only certain resources available to them. Some may lack the manufacturing abilities to make a certain product. Most countries, to one degree or another, specialize in certain resources and goods. Some may have a natural resource that is particularly abundant in their country. An industry may have developed in turning that resource into certain products. They can then trade those products with other countries.

Putting resources and effort into the gathering or production of one or more resources or goods is called specialization. Producing a surplus of that resource or good allows the country to offer something that other countries do not have. In this way, they can acquire resources and goods that would otherwise be unavailable to them. In order to make this kind of international trade happen, countries need to be able to exchange their form of currency, or money, for the currency of other countries. The rate at which one currency can be exchanged for another currency is called the exchange rate. Having a set exchange rate allows countries with different currencies to do business with one another.

title: Standard of Living
text:
The success of a country’s economy is reflected in its standard of living. This is a measurement of how well the average citizen of a country is doing financially. It generally explains how much money the average person makes in that country. It also correlates to the type and quality of goods they can buy, including things like housing. A country with a higher standard of living usually features a better average housing situation for its citizens. These countries usually have easier access to food and other things people need to live.

A country’s standard of living is most often measured by its gross domestic product (GDP), per capita. GDP is the measurement of all the economic production of a country. This is expressed in the amount of money that production is worth. In order to get the average production of a citizen in a country, the total GDP is divided by the population of that country. This calculation shows the average GDP per capita, or per person. It is not an exact measurement. However, it does reflect the relative economic production of the average citizen in a country. A higher GDP per capita generally correlates with a higher standard of living. This is usually because citizens of that country are more economically productive.

Literacy Rates

There are certain metrics, or measurements, that help explain the success of a country’s economy and the strength of its GDP per capita. One of those metrics is the country’s literacy rate. The literacy rate is a measurement of the percentage of the adult population that can read. A higher literacy rate will generally correspond to a higher GDP per capita. A higher literacy rate is an indicator of a strong education system. A country with a strong education system has the resources and money to support such a system. It also means that children have been able to go to school rather than join the workforce. An educated workforce is generally more productive and capable of more complex tasks and jobs. This also provides a boost to the production of individuals and the country as a whole.

Relationship Between Investment and GDP

There are things that a country can invest in that should lead to an increase in its GDP. This would also increase its standard of living. GDP measures the overall production of a country. A population that has access to more and higher levels of education produces more productive workers. It allows those people to contribute to the country’s higher standard of living. If a country with lower literacy rates wants to improve its GDP, one way to do that is to invest money in the country’s educational system. Making higher-quality education available to children for longer will allow them to get better jobs doing more complex things. These people will be more productive and be able to do jobs that strengthen the country’s economy. With a stronger economy, the GDP will increase, and the standard of living will, too.

A country can also invest in physical things to increase its GDP and standard of living. Countries with a low GDP often rely on gathering resources, like farming and mining, for their economy. The people working these jobs usually make very little money. However, if the country invests in building factories as well as buying or making new technologies and machinery, the workers can be more productive and hopefully make more money. Investing in people and in the things they need can increase production and lead to a stronger economy, a higher GDP, and an increase in the standard of living in a country.

title: The Role of Natural Resources in a Country’s Economy
text:
The strength and focus of a country’s economy are determined, at least partially, by the natural resources that exist there. A country with a variety and abundance of natural resources will have an economic advantage. They can use those natural resources to make things. Resources like trees and metals can be used to build houses and factories. Different kinds of metals can be used to make a variety of machinery and goods. Rivers can contribute to rich soil. This allows people to grow crops in large quantities. Excess resources can be used in trade with other countries that need those resources. A country lacking natural resources would have a harder time growing its economy. It would need to put more effort into acquiring resources.

Most countries have only certain amounts and types of natural resources available within their borders. Because of this, they are forced to specialize in the mining or gathering of those specific resources. If they are able, they can develop industries using those resources to create products or goods to use and sell to other countries. They may also export some of those resources and import resources they do not have. This could develop a complete economy that is less reliant on one or a few natural resources.

title: The Role of Entrepreneurship
text: Entrepreneurship requires the freedom of a free market system. An entrepreneur is a person who creates and pursues economic possibilities. They start businesses. They invest money and resources in other businesses. They use the freedom of a market economy to pursue economic growth. Entrepreneurs help grow an economy by creating and growing economic opportunities. Their actions can create jobs and goods. When done well, this creates profits and wages for the entrepreneurs and workers. An economic system that encourages the actions of entrepreneurs can increase its GDP and standard of life.

title: Introduction
text:
Australia has been known by several names since its discovery by Europeans. In 1606, the Dutch were the first Europeans to claim the land. They called it “New Holland" after their native country of Holland (present-day Netherlands). Before that, it was called Terra Australis, Latin for “Unknown South Land.” From 1801 to 1803, British explorer Matthew Flinders circumnavigated the continent. Afterward, he recorded details of the voyage to be published. In his book, A Voyage to Terra Australis, he argued in favor of the name "Australia." It was formally adopted in 1824 by the British.

The Aboriginal Australians and Torres Strait Islander peoples were Australia's first settlers. Torres Strait Islander peoples sailed from what is known today as Papua New Guinea. Current theories suggest the Aboriginal people arrived in Australia more than 50,000 years ago. They may have traveled from Asia across land bridges when sea levels were lower. Other theories suggest they used rudimentary boats.

After the Dutch, the British began settling in Australia in 1788. These early British settlers were sent to establish prisons or penal colonies. These colonies were created for British prisoners who had committed crimes in England, Ireland, Scotland, and Wales.

Australia is the smallest of all seven continents. Surrounded entirely by water, Australia is the only country that covers an entire continent. Today, the Commonwealth of Australia consists of six states: New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria, and Western Australia. Although Australia is rich in natural resources, almost a third of the country is desert.

title: Essential Question
text: How does location impact a country's cultural, social, and economic development?

title: Location and Population
text:
Australia is located in the Southern Hemisphere. It is both a continent and a country. It is part of the region of Oceania, which lies between the Indian and South Pacific Oceans. Oceania has a variety of landmass characteristics. It has thousands of islands, such as New Zealand, and different subregions, such as Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia.

Australia covers nearly three million square miles of land area. Its size makes it the sixth-largest country in the world. It is bordered by the Pacific Ocean to the east and the Indian Ocean to the west. The continent presents a variety of environments and climates. They are directly influenced by how near or far they are from the coastline. Areas along the coast receive abundant amounts of rainfall. These tropical environments resemble the rainforests of Africa and South America that are populated by diverse plants and animals.

Because of its size, Australia has a wide variety of climates. Nearly 35 percent of Australia can be classified as a desert. However, 70 percent of the country is arid or semi-arid. Because dry climates are so common in Australia, most Australians live along the southeastern coastline in urban, or city, settings. Australia's two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne, represent about 40 percent of Australia's population. The continent's interior is known as the Outback. Few people live there due to its harsh and extreme conditions.

title: The Great Barrier Reef, Coral Sea, and Oceans
text:
Australia is surrounded by three oceans: the Indian Ocean to the northwest, the Pacific Ocean to the east, and the Southern Ocean to the south. The Coral Sea is one of Australia's most popular destinations. It is located off Australia's northeast coast. It earned its name from its many coral reefs. The sea's reefs and islands provide refuge to diverse birds and marine life. Critical to ocean life, the Coral Sea has a warm and stable climate. It is home to many endangered species and a wide variety of sea life.

The Great Barrier Reef is one of the most well-known oceanic features in the world. Oceanic refers to something related to the ocean. The Great Barrier Reef borders the Coral Sea and is the largest reef in the world.

It is made up of more than 3,000 individual reef systems and coral bays. The reef is home to more than 1,500 types of fish and 100 kinds of sharks and stingrays. It is also populated with many marine turtles and mammals.

The Coral Sea links the Pacific Ocean and the Great Barrier Reef through ocean currents. This allows for new sea life and helps different animals, such as turtles and birds, migrate. The Great Barrier Reef spans over 130,000 square miles. That is roughly half the size of Texas.

title: Great Dividing Range
text:
Eastern Australia’s most prominent physical feature is the Great Dividing Range. Despite its name, it is not a single mountain range but a collection of several smaller ranges. The Great Dividing Range extends over 2,000 miles. It runs from the tip of Queensland in the north to Western Victoria in the south. At certain points, it is anywhere from 100 to 200 miles wide.

There are many protected areas within the Great Dividing Range. They are meant to protect and preserve the natural wonders of the area. Alpine National Park, Blue Mountains National Park, and Grampians National Park are a few of the well-known protected areas.

title: Great Victoria Desert
text: The Great Victoria Desert is the largest single desert region on the continent. It is located in southwestern Australia. The desert is divided almost in half by the border between the provinces of South Australia and West Australia. The Great Victoria Desert is over 430 miles wide. It covers more than 160,000 square miles. This is about five percent of Australia’s total land area. The desert’s arid climate has produced many unique physical features. These include red sand dunes, dry salt lakes, and stony plains. The harsh climate makes it difficult for many plant and animal species to survive in the Great Victoria Desert. Some plant and animal species have adapted to the arid climate. Desert grasses and shrubs, some bird species, lizards, and marsupials have found ways to survive. Most of the people who inhabit this area belong to different Aboriginal tribes. Many of their ancestors have lived in this region for thousands of years.

title: Uluru and Ayers Rock
text:
In central Australia, Uluru, or Ayers Rock, is one of Australia’s most recognizable natural landmarks. Uluru is a large sandstone rock that stands 1,142 feet above the desert. It is located in the Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park. At certain points of the day and throughout the year, Uluru appears to change colors. Most notably, it glows red in the morning at sunrise. The term “Uluru” comes from the Pitjantjatjara language, one of the most widely spoken Aboriginal languages in Western Australia.

Although already well known and sacred to the Indigenous peoples of Australia, Europeans first came upon the site of Uluru in 1873. Explorer William Gosse named the ancient rock formation Ayers Rock. He chose the name to honor the chief secretary of South Australia, Sir Henry Ayers. In 2002, Ayers Rock was renamed Uluru/Ayers Rock. This was an effort to honor the culture, history, and traditions of the Aboriginal people. Uluru/Ayers Rock is surrounded by an Indigenous Protected Area. This allows Aboriginal Australians, the traditional owners, to better preserve areas of cultural significance. They work to protect the culture, social features, and environment around Uluru/Ayers Rock.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Australia has many unique physical features. They range from the Great Barrier Reef to the arid climate of the Great Victoria Desert. Australia’s varied climate influences the natural resources that are available across the country. The distribution of natural resources and Australia’s environment have influenced settlement patterns throughout the continent. That has been the case for thousands of years. People have used the abundant resources of the country to meet their wants and needs for centuries. They continue to do so today. This has resulted in a great connection between humans and the environment of Australia.

title: Introduction
text:
The physical characteristics of Australia make it an incredibly unique and diverse place to visit and live. Australia is a land rich in natural resources. The primary natural resources of Australia include minerals, oil, natural gas, timber, and water. Mining is one of Australia’s largest industries. It relies heavily on the continent's natural resources. Australia is one of the world’s leading producers of mineral resources. These minerals include aluminum ore, iron ore, coal, uranium, cobalt, zinc, gold, lead, and nickel. Australia’s mines are also a rich source of mineral sand. This type of sand has large deposits of minerals and precious gems, such as diamonds, emeralds, sapphires, rubies, and opals. The mining industry plays a major role in the economy of each of Australia’s regions.

Australia’s climate consists of three very different climate types and zones. Coastal areas along the Tasman and Coral Seas and a small portion of southwestern Australia near the Southern Ocean have a temperate climate. This means that the climate is generally mild with moderate amounts of rain. Coastal areas in northern Australia have a tropical climate. Places with a tropical climate receive large amounts of rain. The average temperature in those areas is around 64 degrees throughout the year. Tropical climates have above-average levels of humidity. The majority of the continent has a dry, or arid, climate. This climate area has large deserts, sparse vegetation, and minimal rainfall.

Other factors have influenced patterns of settlement throughout Australia’s history. These include the physical environment, resources, and economic opportunities. People need food, clothing, and shelter to survive. The physical environment influences where people settle, their jobs, and their lifestyles. People depend on the environment to meet their needs and wants. The natural features and resources available in an area provide materials, food, and clothing for the people living there.

When people migrate or immigrate to a new place, they generally settle where resources are easily accessible. Early settlers in Australia formed towns and cities near bodies of water to meet their basic needs. These places provided a source of clean water for drinking and growing crops. They also provided waterways that could be used for transportation and trade. Many of the plants and animals needed for food and other resources also live near Australia’s waterways. Materials from these plants and animals were used to supply food, make clothes, and build homes.

As more and more people settled in Australia, they formed communities to meet their needs. They opened shops, started schools, and built public meeting places. Many small communities eventually grew into larger cities. New forms of technology, such as the railroad, cars, improved roadways, and air travel, made it easier for people to move and establish new communities throughout Australia. However, these communities and towns remained concentrated in coastal areas because of the rich resources available along the coast. Today, the largest cities in Australia are still located in coastal areas because they provide easy access to natural resources.

title: Essential Question
text: How does location impact a country's cultural, social, and economic development?

title: Location
text: Location, climate, and distribution of natural resources have been the major influences on Australia's population distribution and density. The majority of Australia’s population resides in coastal regions. Australia’s largest cities, by population, are located in coastal areas of the continent. These include Brisbane, Melbourne, and Sydney. Cities in the northern regions of Western Australia, the Northern Territory, and Queensland are less populated than the eastern part of the continent. The bulk of the continent is sparsely populated or not inhabited by people at all.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Location, climate, and distribution of natural resources profoundly impact where people settle and build communities in Australia. People require access to natural resources to meet their needs and wants. If an area does not have as many available natural resources, it is generally less populated than areas with large amounts of natural resources that are easily accessible. These factors also influence economic activities and industries across the continent.

Environmental issues also influence population distribution and patterns of settlement. In recent years, Australia has experienced various environmental issues that impact the continent’s population, natural resources, and climate. Some of the most detrimental issues include:

bush and forest fires

climate change

deforestation

growth of urban areas

introduction of invasive plant and animal species

overfishing

pollution

vegetation clearing and overgrazing

water scarcity

Despite these issues, millions of people continue to move to and visit Australia each year. Approximately two million tourists visited Australia in 2022. Those visitors contributed billions of dollars to Australia's economy. As of March 2023, the total population of Australia was over 26 million.

title: Australia's Economic System
text:
Australia has a mixed economic system that combines the freedom of a market economy with some of the regulations of a command economy. This system encourages economic growth while making sure that growth is controlled. This helps the entire country benefit from the country’s economic strength. Australia’s economy is one of the world’s most free economic systems. Government control is minimal, especially on international trade. This means that Australian companies can pursue the economic opportunities they think will best grow their business, contributing to their strong economy.

Australia is a country rich in natural resources. These resources provide opportunities for investment and trade. They can be used to manufacture goods in Australia. They can also be sold to other countries. Australia has trade agreements with other countries that make it easier to import and export goods. This allows the economy to benefit from its wealth of natural resources.

The freedom of Australia’s economy encourages entrepreneurship. Individuals and businesses are encouraged to pursue economic opportunities. A strong, stable government creates an environment where taking economic risks as an entrepreneur is worth it. In an economy where most jobs involve performance services, people can start their own businesses, which helps grow the economy.

The freedom and entrepreneurship of Australia’s economy are supported by investment in human capital. Human capital refers to the skills and knowledge that people have which allow them to increase productivity and boost a country's economy. A strong government-funded education system leads to high literacy rates and a productive workforce that allows for the economic growth seen there. Australia has a strong higher education system. Colleges, universities, and opportunities provide career training and education. This produces a population of highly-educated individuals that raises the potential for economic growth.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors impact the economy of Australia?

title: Impact of Education on Australia's Economy and Entrepreneurship
text:
Countries that can invest in education are more likely to benefit from their educated population. Over six percent of Australia’s GDP is invested in educating its citizens. This level of educational investment leads to higher literacy rates. This increases Australia’s GDP. It allows the country to reinvest that money into education and further strengthen its economy. The citizens will be more productive and better able to take advantage of the economic opportunities in their free economy.

The government of Australia creates an environment that supports the creation of businesses as entrepreneurs pursue economic growth and success. Starting new businesses and investing their money in the growth of businesses and industries allows Australia’s economy to grow. About 33 percent of Australia’s GDP is generated by small and/or family-operated businesses. These businesses employ more than two-thirds of Australian citizens. Australia’s economy is very friendly to entrepreneurs. Many operate more than one business. The country’s investment in education reflects its higher literacy rates. This creates an educated population capable of starting and running their own businesses.

title: Natural Resources of Australia
text:
One of Australia’s economic strengths is its amount and variety of natural resources. Specific resources include metals like copper, gold, iron, silver, and tungsten. Energy resources, like natural gas and petroleum, are abundant as well. Australia is one of the largest exporters of coal in the world. Australians also produce agricultural goods, like wheat, barley, sheep, and poultry. The country has large quantities of natural resources that are usually in high demand. The metals, minerals, and energy resources are widely sought by other countries and industries, allowing Australia to gain more revenue.

Australia’s natural resources and location allow it to serve as a major exporter in the region. Long coastlines provide several useful port cities to export goods. They send resources to Asian countries like China, Japan, and Thailand. Other trade partners, like the United States and Germany, are further away. Given the richness of its natural resources, Australia has traditionally been one of the most profitable exporters in the world. Despite this, they are dependent on the strength of the global economy. If other countries lower their demand for Australia’s natural resources, it would weaken Australia’s economy. They would have to export those resources for less money if countries did not want those resources at the same level of demand.

Hundreds of mines throughout the country extract metals, minerals, and other resources from the earth. Some resources are available throughout Australia. Precious metals like gold and silver are present in different regions. Zinc, bauxite, and lead are also extracted from various parts of Australia. Offshore drilling of natural gas and petroleum occurs along the coastline. Western Australia is rich in iron. Eastern Australia has large quantities of coal. The interior of Australia has fewer resources. The climate is so severe that limited farming occurs there.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Australia’s Indigenous population is known as the Aboriginal peoples and the Torres Strait Islander peoples. Before colonization, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples had a traditional economy. Resources were gathered and used as needed. Their nomadic lifestyles meant they hunted and gathered what they needed to eat. They crafted tools and weapons from their environment. Until European colonists arrived, no widespread mining or trading occurred in Australia.

When England began to colonize Australia, they recognized the wealth of natural resources available in the country. Like other parts of the world, Australia witnessed a gold rush in the 1800s. Aboriginal people were used for labor at mines and on farms. They were paid much less than colonists for doing the same work. During this time, Australia became a much larger part of international trade. Resources from Australia made their way around the world. Investments by England grew and strengthened Australia’s economy. This was the start of the modern economy we see today.

As a part of colonization, the local Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples saw no profit from the sale or trade of Australia’s natural resources. Colonization improved the standard of living and economy of Australia’s white population. It did little to improve the lives of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. The economic goal of the colonial government was to make money for England and its people. The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples of Australia continue to lag behind other groups in Australia in certain education and economic metrics.

title: Framing Question
text: How can maps help us describe places?

title: Trade in Australia
text:
One of the largest economic industries in Australia is trade. Trade is the action of buying, exchanging, or selling goods and services. Trade is a vital economic activity that allows people to meet their needs and wants. Trade is often determined by the natural resources and goods a country has or can produce independently. If a country does not have particular natural resources or cannot produce goods that are needed, then it must trade for these items with another country. Goods and services brought into a state or country are called imports. Goods and services produced in a country that are shipped to other states or countries are called exports.

Australia has a mixed market economy. A mixed market economy is a combination of market, command, and traditional economies. This type of economic system includes government-run and private companies that have the ability to own, produce, sell, and exchange goods and services in a state or country.

A mixed market economy relies on many different factors. Some of these factors include how much of a resource or product is available (the supply) and how much consumers want the resource or product (demand). It also includes how unique or rare a product or resource is (specialization) and how willing others are to trade for products or resources (voluntary trade). In a mixed market economy, the government does not directly control resources. This prevents the government from becoming too powerful and claiming total control over the economy. Regulations and economic rules are created by the people. Supply and demand dictate what producers make. Producers can decide how much to produce. They also determine the price of their products and where to sell them.

Different types of trade exist in Australia, including voluntary trade and specialization of trade. Voluntary trade, also called a voluntary exchange, occurs between buyers and sellers or producers and consumers. It is the free exchange of goods and services in markets. Voluntary trade allows for specialization to occur. Specialization is the process of creating a product or providing a service for a specific reason. Many countries specialize in specific products and services based on available natural resources.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors impact the economy of Australia?

title: Currency
text: Currency is the system and type of money used in a region or country. Currency is traditionally found in the form of paper bills and coins. Currently, there are approximately 180 different currencies used throughout the world. In Australia, the monetary unit used is the Australian dollar. Australia’s currency consists of five plastic bills and six coins in various denominations. When people from around the world visit Australia, they often exchange their country’s currency for Australian dollars. Usually, currencies between two countries do not exchange at the exact same rate, like one Australian dollar for one American dollar. The exchange rate varies between countries and currencies. Rates can also change very quickly.

title: International Trade
text:
International trade solves many problems for different countries. Some resources found around the world are not found in Australia or are not easily accessible. For instance, very little of Australia is located in a tropical climate zone. Crops that grow well in the tropics, such as coffee, citrus, and sugarcane are especially useful for Australia to import. Many natural resources are found in abundance in Australia. One of the most abundant natural resources in Australia is the mineral, iron ore. Since Australia has more iron ore than it needs, it can export it to other countries that do not have access to this resource. Iron ore makes many different goods, including steel and other metals.

Countries also engage in international trade by exporting services. The top services that Australia exports to other countries are education-related travel services. Education-related travel services help students attend education or training programs around the world. Another service that Australia exports is computer and information services. Computer and information services help people store, distribute, and communicate information through different technological platforms.

Australia engages in trade with many different countries across the world. Australia’s primary trading partners include the United States, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore. Trading partners also include China, Thailand, Malaysia, India, and the United Kingdom. On average, Australia exports over $343 billion worth of goods each year. In 2021, Australia was the largest exporter of zinc ore, wool, raw nickel, coal briquettes, and iron ore. Australia is also a leading oil, natural gas, gold, cattle, and grain exporter. These goods were exported to markets across the world.

Because Australia lacks specific natural resources, the government and businesses often import goods from other countries. This helps Australians meet their needs and wants.

title: Barriers to Trade
text:
International trade is complex. Countries often face various barriers to international trade. A barrier is an obstacle that prevents movement or access to an object or idea. Australian businesses face challenges and barriers to international trade. Trade barriers in Australia include tariff and non-tariff barriers. A tariff is a tax that has to be paid on imports and exports. Tariff barriers include taxed or monetary barriers to imports and exports. Non-tariff barriers are not linked to monetary barriers, including trade rules and agreements, government policies, and other factors.

Tariff barriers in Australia include import tariffs. Businesses that import goods to Australia are required to pay different tariffs. These include customs duty taxes and goods and services taxes (GST). Customs duty taxes are tariffs that are placed on international imports. The amount or percentage of customs duty tax varies, depending on the imported item. Fuel, tobacco, and alcohol are charged a higher customs duty tax than other items. A goods and services tax, or GST, is a 10 percent tax placed on most goods and services imported by Australian businesses. For example, if an Australian company imports $3 million of goods from Japan, the company will also have to pay a $300,000 GST.

Many non-tariff barriers impact trade in Australia. One example is free trade agreements. Free trade is trade that is not affected by tariffs or other restrictions. Australia has free trade agreements with several countries, including:
