These trade agreements remove certain barriers and tariffs between Australia and these countries. Sometimes, the government or businesses want to conduct trade with countries that do not have a free trade agreement with Australia. In these cases, larger tariffs and other barriers may be imposed on goods and services that are imported and exported.

Other non-tariff barriers that impact trade in Australia are trade rules and regulations. These can include health and safety regulations, and customs procedures. Technical barriers can include labeling and packaging requirements, ingredients, weight and size of goods, testing of goods, and certification processes. One of the biggest barriers to international trade in recent years was the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. Many countries, including Australia, had to close their borders to international trade to prevent the spread of the virus. People and goods could not travel or be transported in and out of Australia. Trade and businesses in Australia recovered from the barriers created by the 2020 pandemic, though it took a few years.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Trade is the action of buying, exchanging, or selling goods and services. Australia is a leading producer of many goods and services. Still, Australian producers can only provide some goods and services people need. Australia’s government and businesses trade with many countries so that Australians can meet their needs and wants. International trade is a challenging process. Many factors influence trade between Australia and other countries. Trade is just one factor that has led to Australia's economic growth. The economy of Australia continues to grow because of many factors.

title: The Aboriginal People of Australia
text:
People have lived in Australia for thousands of years before European explorers reached the continent. Historians and archeologists believe that the first people to inhabit Australia arrived on the continent between 30,000 and 60,000 years ago. Some historians believe that Australia’s first people lived on the continent for over 100,000 years. They traveled across the Timor Sea from Indonesia and the Torres Strait from New Guinea. They settled in Australia, eventually migrating and building communities across the continent.

The descendants of these original settlers are referred to as the Aboriginal people of Australia, First Australians, and First Nations People. The word “Aboriginal” comes from the Latin term “Aborigine,” which means “original inhabitants.” Historians estimate that between 300,000 and 1.5 million Aboriginal Australians inhabited the continent when Europeans first arrived in the late 1700s.

The ancient Aboriginal people formed societies, clans, and tribes. They had their own language and cultural customs. While the Aboriginal people belong to nearly 500 different groups, they share a set of common beliefs. Aboriginal people call the time before the world was created "Dreamtime." They believe that during this time their ancestors rose from a place below the Earth. They formed the Earth, sky, animals, and all of the elements of nature. Aboriginal people believe that their ancient ancestors then changed themselves into rock formations and rivers to keep their spirits alive forever. They believe that humans are no greater than any other creation in nature.

Aboriginal people relied on the natural resources of their environment to survive. The ancient Aboriginal people of Australia lived in hunter-gatherer societies. Men were responsible for hunting and fishing. Women gathered grasses, seeds, fruits, nuts, vegetables, and roots. They were also responsible for cultivating gardens and preparing meals. Children learned from their parents and began helping with daily chores at an early age. Aboriginal people were also semi-nomadic. They traveled seasonally from place to place, looking for food.

Aboriginal people heavily depended on and adapted to their environment. However, they also modified the environment to meet their needs. They used controlled burns to clear the land of brush and small plants. With the land cleared, they could build settlements and small farms. The Aboriginal Australians also created irrigation systems to transport water to their farms. They moved from place to place, enriching the soil with nutrients for farming and gardening.

Aboriginal people used many different tools to survive in their natural environment. Stone tools were used for hunting and for carving wooden utensils. Baskets were an important tool used by all Aboriginal people. Clans and tribes who lived in coastal regions wove baskets and string bags, They used string made from the bark of banyan trees. In contrast, Aboriginal people in central Australia carved baskets from wood. They are called "coolamons."

The Aboriginal peoples are the oldest known people to have used the boomerang. A boomerang is a curved piece of wood historically used for hunting. The iconic “returning” boomerang was not actually used for hunting. The distinct bend in the middle of a returning boomerang’s shape allows it to catch the wind and return back to the point from where it was thrown. Hunting boomerangs, or throwing sticks, had a more subtle curve and sometimes had a handle on the end, giving them the look of an ax or an arch. Images of the boomerang appear in some of the oldest rock art in the world. This rock art was painted by Aboriginal tribes thousands of years ago. It can still be seen today in the Kimberly region of northwest Australia.

Music and art are another important aspect of Aboriginal culture. Aboriginal music is full of the sounds of nature. The didgeridoo is one of the best-known Aboriginal instruments. The instrument is made from a long hollow pipe that is roughly four feet long, although some can be as long as 10 feet. The didgeridoo was originally played to accompany singing and dancing in special ceremonies, but the didgeridoo was and still is played for fun.

Sand painting is another custom of Aboriginal culture used in ceremonial rituals. Sand paintings were created by mixing grass, leaves, or feathers with special natural dyes. The ground was raked smooth to make a good surface to work on. The dye was mixed with natural materials and paste. Then, it was placed on the sand in a pattern with circles, waves, and other sacred symbols. Sand paintings recorded important events, told stories, and marked territorial boundaries. Sand paintings are still used today to preserve the cultural traditions of Aboriginal peoples.

Petroglyphs are another form of Aboriginal art. They can still be found in Australia today. A petroglyph is a picture carved into rock. Petroglyphs represent important cultural beliefs, tribal stories, and significant events. Aboriginal people consider petroglyphs sacred and often gather around in areas where petroglyphs are present for celebrations and ceremonies.

Today, the majority of Aboriginal people live like other modern Australians. However, many Aboriginal people and groups work diligently to preserve their cultural customs and traditions through music, art, cuisine, storytelling, and language.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors and events have impacted the culture and government of Australia?

title: English Colonization of Australia
text:
English explorers, under the command of the British government, explored and colonized continents around the world from the 1500s through the 20th century. In 1770, Captain James Cook became the first English explorer to reach Australia. Cook claimed the land for the British government and mapped the east coast of the continent. English colonization of the continent began in 1788. There were several motivations for the colonization of Australia. In 1783, the British government lost control of its primary colonies in North America. Because of this, the English no longer had access to these colonies' vast collection of natural resources, goods, and services.

Another motivation was the soaring crime rates in many cities. As more cities became industrialized, people left their farms and rural areas of the country for better economic opportunities in cities. As more people moved to the cities, crime rates soared. Prisons were overrun, and resources became increasingly scarce. The British government wanted to establish a colony from which they could pull resources and send prisoners. They believed it would help with the overcrowding of English prisons.

In 1788, the first English settlers arrived in Australia. Of the 1,500 original settlers, more than 700 of the settlers were prisoners from English prisons. Captain Arthur Phillip was appointed the first governor of the new colony. Philip established the first European settlement in Australia. The settlers named it Port Jackson. Port Jackson later became the thriving city of Sydney. In 1793, the first voluntary immigrants, or “free settlers,” arrived in Australia. They settled in what is now New South Wales. The population of voluntary immigrants grew steadily from 1793 to 1850. When gold was discovered near Bathurst, New South Wales, about 500,000 fortune hunters traveled to Australia. The majority of the fortune hunters came from England. When the gold rush ended, the majority chose to settle in Australia. Even today, thousands of people from England choose to settle permanently in Australia each year.

title: Impact of Colonization on Aboriginal People: Basic Rights
text:
English colonization profoundly impacted the Aboriginal people of Australia. At first, the Aboriginal Australians and English settlers lived together peacefully. The English quickly began to claim the land for themselves. They cleared the land, built fences, and established farms. This cut-off access to natural resources that the Aboriginal Australians relied on to survive. Disputes and misunderstandings began to arise between the Aboriginal tribes and the English concerning the land and resources. As the population of Australia grew, competition for land and resources increased.

The English colonists believed in the concept of land ownership. They felt they had a right to own the land where they built their homes and farms. The Aboriginal Australians believed that people belonged to the land and that the land was there for their use, not their possession. Over time, the English settlers began building homes and settlements on land traditionally used by the Aboriginal people for hunting and gathering food. This led to more conflict between the two groups. After many years of conflict and competition over land and resources, the British government imposed laws to restrict the rights of the continent's Aboriginal people. Many English settlers felt that the Aboriginal Australians did not have a right to the lands they inhabited because they didn’t believe in land ownership.

The colonial Australian government removed thousands of Aboriginal Australians from their ancestral lands. The colonial government forced them to move to reservations. The Aboriginal people were cut off from resources they relied on to survive. The Aboriginal way of life changed dramatically after they were forced to live on reservations. They could no longer hunt and gather their food. Aboriginal people were not allowed to travel around the country like they had done for thousands of years. They were also cut off from many cultural and sacred sites.

The Australian government hindered the basic rights of Aboriginal Australians in other ways too. In 1869, the government passed the Aboriginal Protection Act. This act allowed the government to remove Aboriginal children from their homes and place them in new homes. Many of these children were also sent to boarding schools to teach them about English history and customs. They were not allowed to practice their cultural traditions or speak their own language. The government extended this act in 1905 with the passage of the Aborigines Act. Under this act, guardianship of all Aboriginal children under the age of 16 was granted to the government. This act was first enforced in Western Australia but extended to other states within a few years.

Clear records weren’t kept at the time of the removals. However, historians estimate between 20,000 and 100,000 children were taken from their families. Many people refer to these children as the “Stolen Generations.” Once taken, children weren’t allowed to have any contact with their families. The institutions and missions the children were sent to tried to strip them of their cultural identities. The children’s names were often changed to European names. They were forbidden to speak their native languages. The institutions and missions were poorly run, with little food or care and strict discipline. Many children of this generation grew up with no sense of identity and suffered mental and emotional trauma from being taken from their families. Removal policies and laws remained in place until 1969.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
The effects of colonization on the Aboriginal Australians can still be seen today. Less than four percent of Australia’s population is of Aboriginal descent. In recent years, efforts have been made by Aboriginal people to preserve their cultural traditions and history.

Aboriginal civil rights movements began in the 1930s. They did not gain national attention until the 1950s. In 1971, Neville Bonner was elected to Parliament. He became the first person of Aboriginal descent to serve in Australia’s government. Since then, 15 Aboriginal Australians have served in government positions. Ten of them still hold office today.

In 2021, more than 150 Aboriginal languages and dialects were spoken by approximately 76,000 people of Aboriginal descent. Some of these languages and dialects are still considered endangered. However, Aboriginal organizations and scholars are working to save these languages. In 1990, Aboriginal scholars and activists encouraged the Australian government to pass legislation to help preservation efforts. They established the Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies (AIATSIS). The mission of the AIATSIS is to preserve Aboriginal languages and culture. They also provide assistance and access to Aboriginal heritage collections.

Aboriginal Australians have successfully reclaimed and renamed some of Australia's most important Aboriginal cultural and sacred sites. Uluru is an example of these efforts. Uluru is a massive sandstone formation in the Northern Territory. In 1873, explorer William Gosse was the first European to explore Uluru. He renamed it Ayers Rock after the chief secretary of South Australia. The Aboriginal name Uluru was used for thousands of years before Europeans arrived in Australia. White settlers refused to use the traditional name. Through the efforts of Aboriginal leaders, groups, and organizations, the rock was officially named Ayers/Uluru in 1993. Aboriginal Australians continued to petition the government to use traditional names before English names. As a result, the rock was renamed Uluru/Ayers Rock in 2002.

The Australian government has made some effort to right the wrongs of the past committed against the Aboriginal people. In 1976, the Aboriginal Land Rights Act was passed in the Northern Territory. This act provided land to 11,000 Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory. Aboriginal people were finally granted the right to vote in 1987.

In recent years, more and more Aboriginal people have been given the opportunity to participate in government. They've been able to finally influence policies towards Aboriginal Australians. In 2008, Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd issued a formal apology from the government to the Aboriginal community for the terrible actions committed against the Stolen Generations. With the help of Aboriginal representatives, the Australian government passed a national Indigenous language policy in 2009. This policy stated the government's dedication to addressing the loss of Indigenous languages. It also created programs to address those losses.

Aboriginal Australians continue to work with government and cultural organizations. Their efforts are spent preserving their ancestors' traditions and customs. Through this preservation, Aboriginal Australians can teach others about Australia's rich history.

title: The Role of Government
text:
The purpose of government is to enforce rules and provide services to the community it serves. Some of those services include safety and security, providing a justice system, and helping the community meet its wants and needs.

There are many different types and levels of government throughout the world. Each type and level of government makes laws and rules that guarantee and protect the rights of its citizens. Laws and rules provide safety and security. The government tries to make sure all people are treated fairly under these laws.

A primary focus of all governments should be to promote the common good. The common good means working to create laws and rules that benefit everyone. To promote the common good, governments provide services. Examples of services include schools, police and fire departments, public transportation, sanitation, libraries, and more.

The rule of law means citizens and government leaders must obey the same laws. Every citizen, including police officers and politicians, should follow the same rules and have the same consequences if they break the law. The rule of law means that all government officials and all private citizens must follow the laws of the nation, state, and community. Everyone must be treated equally under these laws. The rule of law is based on fairness, equality, and justice. It means that the government is accountable to the law. The government can only use its power as defined by laws. The rule of law has four basic principles that must be followed to ensure order:

Laws have to be adopted and approved through government processes.

Laws have to be clear, and everyone needs to know about them.

Laws are applied equally to all citizens.

When there are disputes about the law, individuals will have representatives who are neutral to deliver the best outcome.

Parliamentary Democracy

The government of Australia is a parliamentary democracy. A parliamentary democracy is a form of government in which citizens vote for representatives. The elected representatives, or elected officials, represent the interests of the people. They work with one another to make laws and decisions for the people of Australia. Effective leaders work to meet the needs of citizens and protect their rights. Representatives in a parliamentary democracy must balance individual rights with the common good to meet the needs of the people.

Before it was a parliamentary democracy, Australia’s government consisted of six self-governing colonies. Although they had some form of self-government, these colonial governments still had to follow the laws and customs of the British Parliament.

The Australian Constitution was written in 1900. This constitution established Australia’s current system of government. In 1901, the colonies of Australia united to become one country with a central government. Delegates, elected by the citizens of Australia, gathered at the first constitutional convention. Citizens of each colony voted to approve the constitution. Since 1901, the Australian Constitution has been the country's supreme law. The constitution outlines the purpose and structure of the federal government. It also outlines Australia’s relationship with other commonwealth governments and other countries.

National Government

The head of state is the monarch of the United Kingdom, but this is a symbolic or ceremonial position. The leader of Australia's government is the prime minister. The prime minister has administrative power over the government. They appoint ministers to assist them in the decisions of the government. The prime minister advises members of the government on important issues.

There are multiple branches of Australia’s national government. Australia’s constitution sets up the separation of powers between the branches of government. The constitution authorizes each branch to share powers with the other branches. This provides for a system of checks and balances.

Australia’s national government is divided into three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial. The executive branch of Australia’s government includes the monarch, governor-general, and prime minister. It also includes ministers, parliamentary secretaries, and executive councilors. The legislative branch is made up of Parliament. Australia’s parliament is divided into two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. The judges of the High Court of Australia and other federal courts control the judicial branch.

State and Territorial Governments

Each of Australia’s six states has its own government. Like the national government, the structure and function of state governments are outlined in the Australian Constitution. States also have their own constitution that establishes the structure and function of their governments. Each state government is divided into three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial.

The head of state government is the governor. The governor is part of the executive branch of state and territorial governments. Members of the ministry and other government departments assist the governor. The legislative branch includes the lower and upper houses of the state parliament. Judges and lower-level court officials lead the judicial branch.

Australia has two territorial governments. Territorial governments are similar to state governments in some ways but different in other ways. Territorial governments have three branches, like a state government. However, the legislative branch is made up of one house. Territories do not have a constitution. The national government of Australia has more authority over government decisions in territories than it does over state governments. These powers and responsibilities are outlined in the Australian constitution.

Local Governments

The lowest level of government in Australia are local governments. Australia has over 500 local governments, also called local councils. Local governments are led by council members. Council members appoint and elect administrative leaders who help organize and run the local governments. Local government leaders work directly with state and territorial governments to properly organize the governments of their council area.

title: Essential Question
text: How does citizen’s participation impact Australia’s government?

title: Citizen Participation in Australia
text:
A democratic form of government relies on the active participation of the people at all levels of government. At every level, the people's consent gives the government the power to act. In the national, state, territorial, and local governments, leaders are selected by the people and represent them in government.

Voting is one of the most important civic responsibilities that people have. It is the most direct way to impact a community. Voting is a formal process in which a group of people makes a choice to inform decisions in their community. An important part of voting is being informed about issues and the people who are running for public office. Voter guides provide background information on the candidates and ballot measures. These guides list the candidates running in each race. It offers details on each candidate's experience and goals.

People can also gain information and knowledge about candidates by listening to speeches. They can watch, listen, or read news stories about the candidates to learn how they feel about important issues. Informed voters gather information from reliable sources. They use this information to inform their opinion. In order to vote in Australia, people must register to vote. Citizens must meet certain requirements in order to vote in local, state, territorial, and national government elections. These requirements include:

hold Australian citizenship or be an eligible British subject (British subjects who hold permanent residency in Australia)

be 18 years or older

retain residency at an address for at least one month

Citizens in Australia can participate in the government in other ways. Responsible citizens also respect and protect the rights of others. Citizens can contribute to their community's economic development. They respectfully hold leaders to their word. Citizens can contact elected officials by writing letters, making phone calls, and sending emails to express their concerns and opinions. This allows citizens to have a voice in decisions that improve their community. Citizens can also attend public and open meetings of Parliament. Most meetings of Parliament are also televised, so that people can stay informed on the issues and decisions being made by Parliament.

Another way that citizens can participate in Australia’s government is by serving in public office. Citizens can run for public office. They can be elected to serve as members of their local, state, territorial, and national governments. Each level and position in government has certain qualifications that people must meet in order to be eligible to hold office. All elected officials must be 18 or older and be Australian citizens.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Australia’s unique physical environment and rich history make it a unique continent. Australia’s environment and distribution of natural resources have influenced settlement patterns throughout the continent. For centuries, people have used the country’s abundant resources to meet their wants and needs. They continue to do so today.

Because of Australia's natural resources and varied environment, people have lived in Australia for thousands of years. The first inhabitants of Australia settled on the continent between 30,000 to 100,000 years ago. They traveled across the Timor Sea and Torres Strait to settle in Australia, eventually migrating and building communities across the continent. The descendants of these early settlers formed societies, clans, and tribes and became the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples of Australia.

The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples lived in almost complete isolation from the outside world until the late 1700s. English explorers first landed in Australia in 1770. English exploration of the continent led to years of colonization and settlement. Conflict over land and resources led to the persecution of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Thousands of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples were denied their basic rights. They were forced to leave their ancestral homelands to make way for new settlers. The British and Australian governments supported those practices. Many of those practices lasted well into the 20th century.

In recent years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have successfully reversed these laws and become participating members of the government. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples continue to work with government and cultural organizations. They preserve their ancestors' traditions and customs and teach others about Australia's rich history. Because more and more citizens have been granted the right to participate in Australia’s government, the needs and rights of all Australians are now protected by the law.

Australia’s geography, environment, economy, and government continue to change daily. The people of Australia are determined to make those changes positive and preserve the rich history and culture of the continent for future generations.

title: Introduction
text:
Canada is the second-largest country in the world by geographic land area. It encompasses 3.8 million square miles of North America. Canada’s national motto, "A Mari Usque ad Mare," which means “From Sea to Sea,” demonstrates the country's size. Canada extends east from the Atlantic Ocean, west to the Pacific Ocean, and north to the Arctic Ocean. Some historians believe that the name “Canada” comes from the Huron-Iroquois word “kanata.” Kanata means “settlement” or “village.” The name was first used in 1535 by French explorer Jacques Cartier. Cartier learned the word from members of the Huron and Iroquois people. By 1547, European mapmakers began using the name “Canada” to refer to all of the land north of the St. Lawrence River.

Today, Canada is divided into 10 provinces. A province is an administrative division of a country. It includes Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Manitoba. It also includes British Columbia, Prince Edward Island, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and Newfoundland and Labrador. It has three territories. They are the Northwest Territories, Yukon, and Nunavut. There are distinct differences between provinces and territories. Canadian provinces have their own provincial governments and leaders. They work with the national government to address the needs of the people in each province. The government created Canadian territories under federal law. Because of this process, the national government is more involved in the decision-making process in the territories.

title: Essential Question
text: How does location impact a country's cultural, social, and economic development?

title: Location and Population
text:
Canada is located in the Northern Hemisphere. It is the largest country by total area in North America. The majority of Canada has a subarctic or a warm-summer humid continental climate. This means that the climate is usually very cold in the winter and warm in the summer. Areas with a subarctic climate also receive very little precipitation. A small area along Canada’s Pacific coast has an oceanic climate. This area has a milder climate, with warm summers and cool winters. A small region near the border with the United States has a cold semi-arid climate. Grasslands characterize this region. They receive little precipitation throughout the year. The northernmost regions of Canada have a tundra climate. These regions are very cold. They have long winters and short summers. Many areas in this region experience below-freezing temperatures all year long.

Canada’s climate plays an important role in the settlement and the location where people live. The most populous cities in the country are located in the continental, dry, and temperate climate zones. The following table shows the most densely populated cities in each of Canada’s climate areas. Population data demonstrates that cities in temperate climates have a larger population than cities with a tropical climate. The least densely populated cities in Canada have a polar climate. The harsh elements of a polar climate make it more difficult for people to settle in this region of Canada.

title: Physical Characteristics of Canada
text:
Bodies of Water

St. Lawrence River

One of the most important waterways in Canada is the St. Lawrence River. The St. Lawrence River is about 800 miles long. It flows from Lake Ontario in the Great Lakes and empties into the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The St. Lawrence River has been an important transportation route and source of natural resources for thousands of years. Early settlers depended on the river. Because of its navigable waters, vegetation, and wildlife, French settlers established Montreal and Québec City along the river banks.

Hudson Bay

Hudson Bay is located in northeastern Canada. It covers roughly 316,000 square miles. It is the second-largest bay in the world. There are hundreds of islands located throughout the Hudson Bay. People have also used Hudson Bay as a source of natural resources and transportation for thousands of years. The bay was named in honor of British explorer Henry Hudson. He was the first recorded European to explore the bay.

Atlantic Ocean

The east coast of Canada borders the Atlantic Ocean. The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean in the world. Approximately 26,000 miles of Canada’s coastline is located along the Atlantic Ocean. Many of Canada’s rivers and waterways lead into the Atlantic Ocean. The rivers and waterways that flow into the Atlantic Ocean make it an important route for travel and trade.

Pacific Ocean

The Pacific Ocean borders Canada’s western coastline. It extends approximately 17,000 miles. The Pacific Ocean is the world’s largest ocean. It covers more than 30 percent of the Earth’s surface. It has always been an important resource for the people of western Canada. The entire coast of British Columbia borders the Pacific Ocean. About 75 percent of the population of British Columbia lives within about 30 miles of the Pacific Ocean.

Great Lakes

The Great Lakes include Lake Erie, Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, and Lake Superior. They are located on the border of Canada and the United States. The Great Lakes cover over 94,000 square miles. They contain about six quadrillion gallons of water. The lakes hold about 21 percent of the Earth's fresh water.

Landforms

Canadian Shield

The massive geological formation that makes up most of Canada is called the Canadian Shield. The Canadian Shield is made up of rock from the Earth’s crust. It formed over billions of years and was originally mountainous. Forces of erosion and the friction caused by the movement of glaciers have flattened this region into what it is today. Because it is made up of the Earth’s crust, it is rich in natural resources. Gold, copper, and iron are just a few of the many mineral deposits in the Canadian Shield.

The climate of the Canadian Shield is influenced by the region’s proximity to the Arctic Circle. The ground remains frozen all year in the farthest northern reaches. This frozen soil is called permafrost. It makes plant growth almost impossible. The climate remains cold in the southern regions of the Canadian Shield. However, it is warm enough to thaw the soil during the summer months. With enough rain and snow, this region is warm enough to support forests with varieties of tree species that can survive cold winters or periods with little precipitation.

While geological forces have generally flattened it, the Canadian Shield is quite rocky. It has many hilly areas, lakes, and rivers. The rugged terrain limits the ability of people to use this area for agriculture.

Rocky Mountains

The Rocky Mountain Range is the biggest mountain range in North America. It begins in Canada and extends through central New Mexico. Many of the peaks of this mountain range are more than 12,000 feet high. The portion of the Rocky Mountains in Canada is often called the Canadian Rockies. Mount Robson is the tallest peak in the Canadian Rockies, with a total elevation of 12,972 feet.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Canada is a vast country with many different physical features, ranging from the Canadian Shield's rocky terrain to the wetlands surrounding the Great Lakes. Canada’s varied climate influences the natural resources that are available across the country. The distribution of natural resources and Canada’s environment have influenced settlement patterns throughout the region for thousands of years. People have used the country's resources to meet their wants and needs for centuries. They continue to do so today. This has resulted in a great connection between humans and the environment.

Unfortunately, interactions between humans and Canada’s environment have not always been positive. For many years, Canada’s environment has been impacted by settlements, industries, transportation, and overuse. Environmental issues have become a great concern for many Canadians in recent years. Combating these issues will take time, resources, and determination for generations to come.

title: Natural Resources of Canada
text:
Canada has a wealth of natural resources. In 2022, agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining, and oil and gas extraction accounted for nearly 10 percent of Canada's gross domestic product, or GDP. Most of these natural resources are found in the Canadian Shield.

Mining and Fossil Fuels

The Canadian Shield is a large, U-shaped area of Canada. It is roughly half the size of the whole country. It is centered on Lake Huron, one of the Great Lakes shared across the United States and Canadian borders. The Canadian Shield is made from ancient rocks. It is home to some of the world's oldest rocks. It dates back to prehistoric times. It is often called by another name: the Laurentian Shield.

The Canadian Shield is home to many of Canada's natural resources. Salt, potash, limestone, coal, iron, gold, silver, diamonds, copper, oil, natural gas, and lumber are some of the natural resources found there. Canada is the third-largest producer of diamonds in the world. Mining has been an important industry and part of the Canadian economy since the 1700s. It is a major part of the country’s history and its present economy.

Canada mines its metals and minerals and exports them to other countries, which brings in money for the economy.

Forestry

Roughly one-third of Canada is covered in forests. Most of the forests are found in Canada’s boreal region. Of these forests, 234.5 million hectares are used for commercial purposes. Canada’s forests play an important role in providing habitats for wildlife. They also encourage tourism to national parks. Canada's forests create jobs that employ 205,365 people in Canada.

Trees are cut down and hauled to companies where they are turned into lumber, paper, newsprint, tissues, and pulp. Canada is one of the world’s leading producers and exporters of lumber and paper. The U.S. buys more lumber from Canada than any other country. Canada’s forestry industry contributes around $25.2 billion each year to its economy.

Fishing and Farming

Canada's economy also relies on farming. Canada is one of the largest wheat producers in the world. It also exports barley, canola oil, tobacco, apples, peaches, dairy products, and beef cattle. Farms cover 6.3 percent of Canada's land area, mostly in the prairies in the south-central region. Over 241,500 people in Canada work in the agriculture sector. Crops and livestock bring in $31.9 billion of Canada’s GDP.

The fishing industry also brings money into the country. Canada exports salmon, cod, and lobster to over 100 different countries around the world. Fish and seafood are some of Canada’s largest food exports. They bring about $8.7 billion to the nation’s economy each year.

title: Distribution of Natural Resources
text:
Climate is often one of the biggest deciding factors when it comes to human settlement. People settle in places where they can survive and find resources in the environment around them to meet their needs. As of 2021, Canada is home to nearly 37 million people. Most of Canada’s population lives in the southern part of the country. There, the climate is warmer. Second to climate, people also tend to live where their work takes them. There are many natural resources all over Canada. However, the harsher climate of the north makes them harder to get to. In the south, most Canadians work in industries near where they live. These industries include mining, oil and natural gas extraction, fishing, forestry, and agriculture.

Mining Industry

Mines in Canada produce many valuable metals and minerals. These include diamonds, gold, and silver. They also include copper, zinc, and uranium. Gypsum, potash, salt, limestone, coal, and many more minerals are produced. Mineral and metal mines are found in the provinces of British Columbia and Saskatchewan. There are also mines in Ontario, Québec, and New Brunswick.

Mines in the southern half of Saskatchewan produce various minerals, such as potash and salt. Many mines in New Brunswick and Québec produce limestone, lime, and other minerals. Between Ontario and Québec, there are a number of mines for precious metals like gold and silver. Farther north, several iron ore mines can be found along the border between Québec and Newfoundland and Labrador.

Oil and Natural Gas Industries

To the west, in Saskatchewan, Alberta, and British Columbia, fossil fuels are extracted. These include coal, oil, and natural gas. Canada has the third-largest reserve of oil in the world. Alberta is Canada's largest producer of natural gas and petroleum.

Fishing Industry

Most of Canada’s fishing industry is found along its east and west coastlines. Clams, salmon, lobster, tuna, halibut, and capelin are fished. Nova Scotia is one of the largest producers of lobsters in Canada.

Each fishing area is carefully monitored and managed by an organization called Fisheries and Oceans Canada. This organization takes stock of fish populations and catches. It works with local fishers and Indigenous groups to create plans to ensure the health and sustainability of Canada’s fishing industry.

Forestry Industry

Québec is the largest and one of the original four provinces in Canada. Québec is Canada’s largest producer of paper and pulp due to its vast forests. The majority of Canada’s forests are boreal forests. Boreal forests are made up of trees such as birch, poplar, and conifer trees. Along the Pacific Coast and southern border, there is also a mix of Pacific Coast, montane, deciduous, and Acadian forests.

Agriculture Industry

Farmland is found in southern Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba. This area is known as the prairie region of Canada. The climate there is mild. The soil is fertile and good for growing crops. Over half of Canada’s wheat is grown in Saskatchewan. Much of the land in Alberta is used for raising cattle and other livestock.

The very southern tips of Québec and Ontario have a high concentration of farms and farmland as well. They raise livestock and dairy cows, produce milk and dairy products, and grow various crops.

title: Climate
text:
All of Canada is located in the northwestern hemisphere. It is above the 40th parallel, or 40 degrees north of the Equator. Climates above the 40th parallel tend to be colder the farther north one goes. Still, the sea currents on each coastline and the Great Lakes located inland regulate the various climates throughout Canada.

Most of northern Canada has cold winters lasting as long as 8–11 months. In the Northwest Territories, Yukon, and Nunavut, the average winter temperature is -24 degrees Fahrenheit. The average summer temperature is 61º F. The summers here are short and sunny, with little rainfall. Because the climate is so harsh in northern Canada, most of the population lives in the southern part of the country.

The climate is milder along the western coast of British Columbia because of Pacific air and ocean currents. Canada’s west coast is humid and rainy. Winter temperatures are in the upper 30s and summer temperatures are in the low 60s.

Canada's prairies are east of the Rocky Mountains. In Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba, fierce storms often hit. This area is known to experience intense blizzards in the winter and high temperatures in the summer. The temperatures here can reach 100º F in the summer and drop to -30º F in the winter.

The eastern provinces have milder weather than the northern and western provinces. These include Ontario, Québec, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador. The mild weather is because of the warmer Atlantic Ocean currents. This area experiences a lot of precipitation in winter and summer.

The variety of climates in Canada impacts the industries found in each region. The coastlines tend to have larger fishing industries, while the prairies are more heavily agricultural.

title: Environmental Issues
text:
Mining, forestry, and oil and gas extraction are important to Canada's economy. However, over the last few years, the extraction, or removal, of resources from the Canadian Shield has been causing problems for the environment.

Logging

Harvesting lumber from the forests on the Canadian Shield can potentially harm the environment, if done improperly. Historically, loggers and lumber companies worked slower because they had to saw trees down by hand. Today, modern machinery and equipment make it fast and easy to cut down trees. Clearcutting, or cutting down entire sections of forest, is one of the most hotly debated tree harvesting methods.

Cutting down trees removes natural habitats. It can cause animals to migrate. It can lead to soil erosion. Roads created to reach logging areas give people access to previously undisturbed areas. Camping, hunting, pollution, and litter can cause further harm to the environment.

To protect the environment and prevent deforestation, the Canadian government has regulations that companies must follow when cutting down trees. There are limits on how many trees they can cut down each year, where they can cut trees, and what methods and equipment they can use.

Mining and Oil and Gas Extraction

The Canadian Shield is important to Canada's economy, but extracting minerals and ore can harm the environment. There are concerns about environmental damage from the mining and extraction of fossil fuels, like coal and oil, and minerals, like gold and iron. There is pollution involved in the mining and extraction processes. Harmful chemicals like lead, mercury, and arsenic are released into the air and surrounding water sources from these sites. These chemicals harm the environment and can make people sick.

Another negative effect of pollution from mining and extraction is smog and acid rain, an ongoing problem in Canada. Acid rain occurs when harmful chemicals are released into the air and then brought back to the ground by precipitation. Acid rain can poison or harm plants, animals, and people. It can contaminate water sources and increase rock and soil erosion.

Since the 1990s, Canada has worked to find ways to lessen the damage from air pollution. It has launched a monitoring program. It also works with the United States to limit harmful chemicals in the air.

The Great Lakes are some of the biggest bodies of water to be impacted by pollution. Many people live and work around the Great Lakes. The lakes play a significant role in the life and economy of Canada. They hold more than 20 percent of the world’s fresh water. They help farming in Canada by providing water for crops. They are also an important waterway for the transportation of people and products.

One of the results of pollution in the Great Lakes is algae blooms. Algae blooms can make the water deadly to fish. They can also make it dangerous for animals and people. Rain washes farm fertilizers, industrial waste, and runoff from cities and mining into the rivers that flow into the Great Lakes. This, as well as acid rain, can cause harmful algae blooms.

The lakes are part of the fishing industry in Canada, and pollution harms the fish populations. The condition of its waterways directly impacts the fishing industry. Overfishing, illegal fishing practices, climate change, and invasive species can all harm marine life. They negatively impact the fishing industry and those who work in it.

On the coasts, global warming is also having an impact on marine life. As ocean waters warm, fish populations are predicted to move farther north to colder waters. This will force fishers to move their businesses to follow the fish.

Some organizations and governments in Canada are working to protect and ensure the long-term well-being of the oceans and bodies of water. It’s not a problem that can be solved overnight. However, with hard work and perseverance, everyone can help protect the environment.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Location, climate, and natural resources play crucial roles in Canada’s development and trade patterns. Its vast territory and strategic position have made it a key player in international trade. Its diverse climate and rich natural resources greatly impact its population distribution and economic industries.

Canada’s government has taken steps to protect its resources and environment. Efforts are being made to promote sustainable forestry practices, such as reforestation. Fishing quotas and regulations are in place to protect fish populations. In agriculture, sustainable farming practices are being encouraged to minimize environmental impacts. Canada is also actively investing in renewable energy sources to reduce carbon emissions.

Understanding the interactions between location, climate, natural resources, population distribution, and environmental challenges is important. In doing so, we can develop sustainable strategies for Canada's future growth and preserve its unique ecosystems.

title: Canada's Economic System
text:
Like Australia, Canada has a mixed economy. The characteristics of a market economy are combined with the regulations of a command economy. Canada’s economic system encourages economic growth. But the government regulates this growth to ensure it is controlled and does not become unmanageable. The economic environment created by Canada's mixed economy encourages entrepreneurship. A strong, stable government encourages entrepreneurs to take economic risks to grow their businesses.

The freedom and entrepreneurship of Canada’s economy are supported by investment in human capital. Human capital refers to the skills and knowledge that people have which allow them to increase productivity and boost a country's economy. Other factors influence Canada’s economic growth. A strong, government-funded education system leads to high literacy rates and a productive workforce. A strong higher education system leads to many opportunities for career training and specialized education. These factors all contribute to Canada having one of the largest economies in the world.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors impact the economy of Canada?

title: Natural Resources and the Economy
text:
Canada’s economic strength also comes from the amount and variety of its natural resources. Canada’s natural resources drive many of the country’s industries. Mining is a major industry in Canada. This is because of the amount and variety of minerals and metals throughout the country. Canada is one of the world's leading producers of cobalt, graphite, and nickel. Many other metals and minerals are mined in Canada. These include aluminum, coal, diamonds, gold, uranium, zinc, copper, iron ore, and graphite. Each year, metal and mineral mining contributes over $40 billion to Canada’s economy.

Forestry and lumber production are important sectors of Canada’s economy. Forestry is the science of developing, caring for, or cultivating forests and the management of growing timber. Millions of acres of forest land make Canada a leading producer of timber, lumber, and paper products. These products are exported to markets around the world. The forestry industry contributes billions of dollars to Canada’s economy each year. Over 300,000 Canadians are employed by the industry.

Canada’s forests also provide people with another important natural resource: maple syrup. Canada is the largest producer of maple syrup in the world. About 75 percent of maple syrup in the world comes from Canada. Ninety-five percent of Canada’s maple syrup exports come from maple tree farms in Québec. Maple syrup and sugar production has been a major part of Canada’s economy since European exploration of the area. It continues to be one of the most important parts of the economy today.

title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
text: Gross Domestic Product, or GDP, is the measurement of a country's economic production. GDP is expressed in the amount of money that the production of a country is worth. In 2022, Canada’s GDP was around $2.14 trillion, making it the 9th largest economy in the world.

title: Factors of Economic Growth
text:
Literacy Rates

Many factors foster economic growth in a country. The Canadian government invests about five percent of its gross domestic product (GDP) educating its citizens. This level of educational investment leads to higher literacy rates. Many countries use literacy rates as an indicator of economic success and potential. In recent years, Canada has consistently been among the most literate countries in the world.

Investments in Capital Goods

Canada’s economic growth is also a result of investment in capital goods. This is one of the major categories determining a country's national income and total GDP. Investment in capital goods helps businesses grow. The government also provides economic and tax incentives for businesses investing in capital goods. Capital goods investment has grown significantly in most of Canada’s economic sectors since 2019. The largest capital goods investment sectors include mining, utilities, transportation and warehousing, public administration, and manufacturing.

title: Entrepreneurship
text: Canada’s mixed economy encourages entrepreneurship without the pressure of strict government regulations. In 2021, an estimated 1.2 million businesses employed more than one person. Over 97 percent of these businesses were considered small or family-owned. These businesses employed over 8 million Canadians in 2021. On average, small businesses contribute over 36 percent of all revenue generated by the private sector to Canada’s yearly GDP. Small businesses also were major contributors to Canada’s total exports. Small businesses accounted for over 42 percent of all business exports in 2021. Entrepreneurs and small businesses play a major role in Canada’s economic growth.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Canada’s economy has changed drastically over time. European explorers and settlers tapped into the rich natural resources of Canada. The earliest settlements were established along the Atlantic coast. Fishing was the earliest of Canada’s industries. As settlers moved further inland, they established the fur trade. Europeans traded with the Indigenous people of Canada for furs. In return, they supplied the Indigenous people with metal goods, tools, and weapons. Furs were sent back to Europe, creating an international trade system.

As more people settled in Canada, the economy became more diversified. Agriculture and lumber became big business in the early 1800s. As new technology became available, other industries developed. As a result, manufacturing, mining, tourism, and other industries grew and strengthened the economy.

In 1867, the British government passed the Constitution Act. This created the Canadian Federation and the current system of government. The government was granted economic responsibilities over the country. Since 1867, Canada’s government, economy, and history have been, and continue to be, closely linked with a common foundation: the will and determination of the Canadian people.

title: Trade in Canada
text:
Trade is one of the most important economic activities in Canada. Canada’s economy relies on the import and export of goods to markets around the world. Trade has been a major economic activity in Canada for hundreds of years. International trade began with European exploration and colonization and has continued to grow. According to 2021 data, Canada is the ninth-largest exporter of goods and services globally. Additionally, it is the 12th-largest importer of goods and services globally.

Canadian imports and exports are directly impacted by the natural resources available in the country. Access to specific natural resources, some only found in Canada, allows Canadian producers to specialize in specific products and markets. This also allows for the specialization of trade. Canada’s mixed economy encourages trade while still protecting the rights of consumers and producers. Voluntary trade is also a key component of Canada’s economy. Canada’s focus on voluntary trade allows specialization to occur.

text: What factors impact the economy of Canada?

title: Currency
text: The Canadian dollar is the national currency of Canada. Canada’s currency consists of five plastic bills. They are often called notes or bank notes. Canada also uses six coins with various denominations. When people around the world visit Canada, they often exchange their country’s currency for Canadian dollars. Usually, currencies between two countries do not exchange at the same rate (like one Canadian dollar for one American dollar). The exchange rate varies between countries and currencies, but the United States dollar is generally worth more than the Canadian dollar. This means that the U.S. dollar is usually worth about $0.30 more than the Canadian dollar. This rate varies and can change very quickly.

title: International Trade
text:
International trade is an important part of Canada’s economic growth. Canadians rely on imports and exports to meet their needs and wants. Many goods cannot be produced in Canada. The natural resources are not available or are difficult to obtain. Like Australia, Canada does not have a tropical climate. Crops that grow well in tropical climates do not grow well in Canada. Canadian markets must import crops that grow in tropical areas to meet the needs and wants of Canadians. That includes citrus fruits, sugarcane, and coffee. In 2021, Canada was the largest importer of cabbages, iron radiators, and magnesium.

Goods are not the only things imported and exported by Canada. Canada also imports and exports different services. This helps meet the needs and wants of Canadians and people worldwide. Canada imports many services from its largest trading partners. The United States is the largest exporter of services to Canada. In 2019, the United States exported over $67 billion in services. That included travel, computer, software, audio-visual, and management services. Canadian services exported to the United States totaled $38.6 billion. This sector of Canada’s exports included travel, transportation, information, computer, and telecommunication services.

title: Barriers to Trade
text:
Like most countries throughout the world, Canada experiences some barriers to international trade. Trade barriers are often divided into two categories: tariff and non-tariff. Both categories place restrictions on trade in Canada. Tariffs are taxes that must be paid on certain types of imports or exports. High tariffs can be an obstacle for companies. Vehicles, footwear, clothing, and apparel are subject to higher tariffs than other goods.

Another tariff barrier is created by the Special Import Measures Act (SIMA). This act imposes additional duties or fees on items imported from foreign markets by Canadian producers, manufacturers, and businesses. The duties and fees only apply if the importation of goods and resources is found to cause financial harm to Canadian industries.

Non-tariff barriers are also obstacles to trade in Canada. Non-tariff barriers include licensing requirements and restrictions, product bans, safety regulations, and customs procedures. Technical requirements also create non-tariff barriers. These include labeling and packaging requirements, ingredients, weight and size of goods, testing, and certification processes.

A lack of free trade agreements is one of the largest barriers to trade for Canada. Trade agreements remove specific barriers and tariffs between Canada and other countries. The government and businesses can still conduct trade with countries that do not have a free trade agreement with Canada. However, larger tariffs and other barriers may be imposed on goods and services that are imported and exported. Currently, Canada has 15 free trade agreements. These agreements facilitate trade between Canada and 51 other countries. This allows Canadian producers and manufacturers to reach 1.5 billion consumers worldwide.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Canada’s economy has changed in many ways throughout its history. Despite these changes, trade has remained a constant and important part of the country’s economy. Many factors impact trade. One of the biggest factors that impacts trade is the government. Government actions and policies can encourage or hinder trade. This has occurred in Canada throughout history. Conflict and change can also have a major impact on trade between countries. This has also played a major role in trade economics in Canada. Nevertheless, trade continues to help Canadians meet their needs and wants.

title: Territorial and Provincial Governments
text:
Canada is one of the largest countries in the world by land area. Today, a country that size is difficult to govern. When the Constitution Act of 1867 was created, it was even harder. The government of Canada needed a way to govern all regions of the country effectively. At the time, there was no immediate long-distance communication or fast transportation. When the Constitution Act created the national, or federal, government, it established a local government for each of the various provinces that made up Canada. The smaller provinces could run programs and address issues at the local level. They were equipped to handle these situations in a way that the federal government could not. This was due to the distances and issues involved. Today, there are 10 provinces in Canada, and each has its own government.

There are three levels of government: federal, provincial or territorial, and municipal (city). The Constitution of Canada lays out the roles and responsibilities of each. The federal government is divided into three separate branches. Each branch shares power evenly. This creates a balanced system of government. The executive branch is led by the prime minister of Canada. Cabinet members assist the prime minister on different issues. Cabinet members also head committees with specific purposes, such as finance or transportation. The legislative branch is divided into the House of Commons and the Senate. The judicial branch of the federal government is made up of the supreme court and the provincial courts.

The provincial governments are organized much like the federal government’s parliamentary democracy. Each one has a governing body. It is made up of members elected by citizens of that province. The majority political party in that body chooses a leader. The leader is known as the Prime Minister of the Province, just like the federal government has a prime minister. The provincial prime ministers are usually called provincial premiers. The provincial governing bodies are responsible for operating all of the programs and organizations appointed to them by the Constitution of Canada.

In addition to the 10 provinces, there are three territories in Canada: Yukon, Nunavut, and the Northwest Territories. Canadian territorial governments have different roles and responsibilities than provincial governments. The territorial governments are under the control of the federal government. The federal government gives local control to the territorial governments. The ability of territorial governments to run their own affairs is not guaranteed in the Constitution of Canada like it is for the provincial governments.

Municipal governments lead and make decisions at the local level. Municipal governments include county, city, town, and village governments. Cities with a population of at least 100,000 people are considered metropolitan municipalities. Municipal governments are led by a chief officer, also known as a mayor, chief executive officer, or head of council. Members of an elected council work with the head of the municipal government to meet the needs and wants of the people of each municipality. Because Canada is so large and populous, it is vital that all levels of government work together to support the country. The separation of power also creates a balance to the government that allows all citizens to participate.
