title: Essential Question
text: What factors and events have impacted the people and culture of Latin America?

title: Origins of the Cuban Revolution
text:
The United States established an economic foundation and partnership with Cuba. As a result, the capital city of Cuba, Havana, became a dominant city on the island. Havana grew due to the sugar production taking place throughout the island. Havana became a very wealthy city. Cuba was a thriving country that was ranked third in life expectancy. It had a 76 percent literacy rate. It had the highest number of televisions per household. This prosperity allowed for most of the country to have a favorable income distribution and a strong middle class.

There were many inequalities that Cuba faced. Even though Havana showed Cuba's good side, the rest of the country did not have that same quality. Health care and education barely reached the countryside. Many people were facing poverty and poor living conditions.

Many social issues turned into problems that caused corruption and violence throughout Cuba. These problems started in 1902 when Cuba broke away from Spain and gained independence. Since then, Cuba has not had an easy way to form a government or an economy. In 1933, revolution came. A rebellion for freedom took place against the fifth president of Cuba, Gerardo Machado y Morales. The rebellion was led by Fulgencio Batista, who would later become president. Batista worked on a constitution for Cuba but also allowed the communist party to become part of the government. This led to many years of corruption and violence. Batista’s government model allowed for the rise of nationalism, or the radical support of the country, to rise up. Fidel Castro, a young lawyer, started to make his thoughts known about Batista. Castro started his own rebel army against Batista and began a movement for a free Cuba.

Many Cubans were calling for democracy and freedom. They no longer wanted Batista to be president. One such Cuban was Huber Matos. Matos started out as a school teacher. He was moved into the rank of comandante by Fidel Castro in his rebel army. Matos recalls the day that Castro gave him the rank:

Our primary objective was to reestablish democracy, and I saw that the people, the young people who joined the rebel army, embodied this urge of all Cubans to return to democratic rule. But, at the same time, the revolution began to nurture itself with new ideas. In addition to reestablishing democracy, let's adopt economic and social reforms to benefit the Cuban people …

Fidel Castro led the Cuban Revolution, which started in 1953. Forcibly changing a type of government to another government is called a revolution. Castro felt there was too much corruption within the government. He felt that Batista needed to be removed from power. Batista ruled as a dictator and controlled everything, including the press and Congress. Batista embezzled (stole) large sums of money from the Cuban economy. He also largely supported the wealthy citizens of Cuba. His interest always favored those who could make him more wealthy.

Legal means to remove Batista failed. Castro knew he needed an army of fighters to attack and take over the government of Cuba. It was easy for Castro to find outraged, poverty-stricken citizens of Cuba to support him. Castro reached out and helped establish better schools and medical aid. The good work Castro was doing to support undeveloped farms and the poor people of Cuba spread quickly. Castro soon gained the strong following he needed to overthrow Batista.

January 2, 1959, Castro’s rebel army made their way to Havana. Batista and his family and friends had fled the city. Castro slowly made his way into Havana. Along the way he met with citizens of cities, towns, and villages. On Jan. 9, 1959, Castro finally reached Havana. Castro set up his political allies and friends into positions of power around the country. Originally, Castro was seen as a nationalist. As time went on, his support for the communist party and his partnership with the Soviet Union led to other issues.

title: U.S. Relationship with and Involvement in Cuba Today
text:
Over time, the United States and Cuba’s relationship remained strained. Fidel Castro fell ill in 2006. His brother Raúl Castro took his position in 2008. However, Cuba’s relationship with the U.S. was never mended fully. It wasn’t until 2015 that the relationship between the U.S. and Cuba became diplomatic. Embassies in both countries were reopened. President Barack Obama visited Cuba in 2016. This allowed for some travel restrictions to be lifted. Many United States airlines started offering direct flights to Cuba. As the years went on, many political movements occurred. Cuba is still listed as an area of concern for the United States.

Currently, Cuba has an autocratic government that gives the majority of the power to one leader. Raúl Castro was known as the chief of state, president of Cuba, and commander in chief of the armed forces. He was the man with the most power in Cuba and had the authority to control everything. However, he made many changes to Cuba’s government. He opened foreign relations, including with the U.S. He lifted some citizen restrictions on travel and commerce. He allowed parts of the military to become privatized. All these reforms contradict a lot of what Fidel Castro accomplished with the revolution.

Raúl Castro instituted a two-term limit for the office of president. Each term will last five years. Raúl Castro was re-elected in 2013 for his final term. In 2018, Miguel Díaz-Canel was elected president of Cuba.

title: Post Revolutionary Cuba
text:
The Cuban Revolution lasted many years. It began to strain Cuba’s relationship with the United States of America. In the past, Batista had been friendly with the U.S. The United States continued to help Batista’s army as Castro was trying to overthrow it. The U.S. was wary of Castro’s intentions. Soon, the U.S. realized that the people of Cuba and many Cuban-Americans supported Castro and his beliefs. This forced President Dwight D. Eisenhower to sign an arms embargo. The embargo limited the resources and weapons given to aid Batista’s forces. Without the help of the U.S., Batista's power slowly diminished.

Castro’s revolution was successful and a lot of changes were made to the government. Castro sought to end the United State’s heavy involvement in Cuban affairs. He also took over much of the Cuban industry and American-owned farms and businesses. He limited freedom of speech and the press. He often imprisoned those who opposed his rule. Cuba’s government changed because of Castro’s strong Marxist beliefs and quickly turned into a communist country.

Marxist beliefs refer to the theories of Karl Marx. Marxism is a system in which public ownership overrules private ownership. Public ownership dictates the means of production, distribution, and exchange. Communism eliminates the ownership of private property. All goods and resources are owned in common or publicly. They are then given to those who need them. Houses, farms, and other privately owned properties were taken away from the citizens of Cuba and were now owned by the government. The economy was also largely controlled by the government. The Communist Party controlled production and the workforce.

Fidel Castro remained strong despite U.S. attempts to weaken his dictatorship. His force and control grew. He allied himself with the Soviet Union. Through this alliance, the Soviet Union placed missiles in Cuba capable of striking the United States. Luckily, the missiles were never launched and have been removed. Fidel Castro remained in control of Cuba for nearly 50 years.

title: Current Affairs in Latin America
text:
Throughout Latin America, there are many issues that impact the United States and Latin America. Illegal drugs have been a problem in the United States for decades. Illegal drugs are not prescribed by a doctor and are harmful to users. They are often connected with crime. In the United States, the war on drugs refers to a battle by law enforcement against those selling and using illegal drugs. This war is to stop the sale and educate the public about illegal drugs. The U.S. government has given more than $1 billion to help in the fight against illegal drugs.

In parts of Mexico and South America, many people live in poverty. They turn to their geography and the natural resources available to them to meet their wants and needs. Some people resort to or are forced into selling illegal drugs and working for drug cartels to make ends meet. Drug cartels are groups that help move and sell drugs from Latin American countries to the United States. The cartels compete to sell drugs, usually in the United States or border cities. Illegal drugs are also notorious for causing social instability and breakdown. Many families and towns see these effects.

In 2006, the president of Mexico, Felipe Calderón, launched the Mexican war on drugs. He sent troops to stop drug dealers and other cartel members. The troops destroyed large amounts of drugs, as well as the crops and labs that were being grown and used to manufacture them. In some South American countries, troops from the U.S. have even gone in and destroyed crops that can be used to make drugs. Unfortunately, sometimes food crops are destroyed as well. This leaves many people without any food to eat or sell. The war on drugs has been costly to everyone involved. The war on drugs is an ongoing battle, but collaboration between the U.S. and Mexican governments has led to many successes, including dozens of arrests during Calderón’s term in office.

Starting in the 1970s, President Richard Nixon declared a war on drugs in the United States. Nixon set forth with the funding going toward treatment options and helping find the causes. This also led to the founding of the Office of Drug Abuse Law Enforcement in 1972. After Richard Nixon, many other presidents continued the war on drugs. First Lady Nancy Reagan started the “Just Say No” campaign in 1984. In 1990, President George H. W. Bush increased military spending to support the war on drugs effort. This global crisis is still one that many countries are partnering together to help solve.

The impact of politics and the economic environment of many countries in Latin America have led to many people being in poverty. Push factors have increased, such as freedoms being taken away and little to no job opportunities. These push factors cause many people to want to immigrate from their home country to another country, such as the United States. To immigrate means to move to a different country.

Many people from Latin American countries immigrate to the United States. Mexico has the highest number of people who immigrate to the United States. In Mexico, some people live in poverty, are unemployed, or have poor jobs. For many people who are living in poverty, there aren’t many options in their home country to improve their situations. Some people decide to move to another country to find better job opportunities and living conditions. Some believe the United States has more opportunities. They come to explore those opportunities.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Change and continuity occurred throughout Latin America for most of the 20th and 21st centuries. There are many ways that the United States and Latin America are working together to give Latin American countries more opportunities and solve social problems. Latin American countries have reinstated their diplomatic ties to the United States. The United States has helped rebuild Latin American economies. Latin America has changed due to many factors, including government instability. Push factors, such as poverty and the war on drugs, can increase migration, which is felt globally. The countries of Latin America continue to work to solve problems as they arise to help improve the lives of those who live there.

title: Location and Population
text:
The Eastern Hemisphere, which includes Europe, is home to a variety of geological features. Tourists flock from all over the world to marvel at the beauty these features offer. The range in climate, elevation, wildlife, and plant life makes Europe a very unique continent. Physical characteristics across Europe include water systems, mountains, and land. People have formed a deep connection to these physical characteristics. Over time, this deep connection has influenced the culture and history of the continent. Today, Europe is divided into 44 different countries.

Italy, located in southern Europe, is a peninsula that extends into the Mediterranean Sea, toward the island of Sicily. Italy was the home of the ancient Roman Empire and the birthplace of the Renaissance period. Because of this, Italy has a rich history and vibrant cultural background.

Southwest of Italy and located in the southern region of Europe is Spain. Spain is culturally and geographically diverse. One of the most famous celebrations in the world takes place in Spain each July. This celebration is called the Running of the Bulls.

Northwest of Italy lies the country of France. France has a distinct cultural background with a vibrant historical past. Many well-known cultural landmarks are located in France, such as the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre, one of the most famous art museums in the world.

Off the northwestern coast of France is the United Kingdom and Ireland. The United Kingdom is made up of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. The United Kingdom has a long history, which has largely revolved around the British monarchy. It is home to many famous cultural landmarks, such as Tower Bridge, Big Ben, Stonehenge, and the Tower of London.

Germany, one of Europe’s most populous countries, is located in central Europe. Germany is often called “the land of poets and thinkers.” Music composers, including Johann Sebastian Bach and Ludwig van Beethoven, were from Germany. Many celebrated scientists and inventors were also from Germany, including Albert Einstein, Johannes Gutenberg, and Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit.

Located southeast of Germany, in eastern Europe, is the country of Ukraine. Ukraine earned its independence in 1991. Despite being one of the younger countries in Europe, Ukraine has a rich and deep culture and history.

Russia’s location is unique and different from other countries in Europe. Russia stretches across two continents. It makes up the eastern border of the continent of Europe and the entirety of northern Asia. The country of Russia covers over six million square miles of land and encompasses 700,000 square miles of water. Russia has a unique culture and history. Among its most famous citizens are Leo Tolstoy and Fyodor Dostoevsky, who wrote well-known classics in literature.

Population distribution varies around Europe. Location, geography, and climate are key factors that influence population distribution across the continent. Densely populated areas have high populations. Sparsely populated areas have low populations. Germany has a population of over 83 million. Most Germans live in urban areas, such as Berlin, Hamburg, and Munich. However, there’s also a large number of people living in rural areas of the country. Russia is the largest country in Europe geographically and by population. Most people live in urban areas because of the country’s harsh climate and difficult terrain. The majority of people live in and around Moscow and Saint Petersburg, the largest cities in Russia. The United Kingdom is home to over 67 million people, with around 84 percent living in urban areas. The bulk of the population lives in and around London.

Many of Europe’s largest cities are located near navigable waterways or large bodies of water. Waterways in Europe were used as the primary means of transportation and trade for centuries. Cities like London, Cologne, Budapest, Barcelona, Lisbon, Naples, Kyiv, and St. Petersburg grew quickly as a result of their proximity to major waterways and bodies of water in Europe.

title: Essential Question
text: How does location impact a region's cultural, social, and economic development?

title: Bodies of Water
text:
The Danube River

The Danube River is the second-longest river in Europe. It flows for about 1,770 miles, from the Black Forest Mountains of western Germany to the Black Sea. The Danube passes through 14 different countries, including Germany, Austria, and Slovakia. In ancient times, it created the border between the Greek and Roman Empires and the Germanic peoples of northern Europe. The Danube River has facilitated trade among many countries for centuries and continues to do so today. The Danube River has been a major cultural influence on various cities, including Budapest and Vienna. Austrian composer Johann Strauss was so inspired by the natural wonders of the river that he composed the piece “The Blue Danube” in 1866.

The Rhine River

The Rhine River is one of the longest rivers in Europe. It is a great catalyst for trade between different countries. It stretches over 800 miles and travels through the Netherlands, Germany, and Switzerland. It has acted as a political border between France and Germany for many years. The Rhine is an important trade route. It is used to move goods throughout Europe. Coal, steel, and chemical industries utilize the resources and power of the Rhine for manufacturing purposes. The Rotterdam Port in the Netherlands is another important area along the Rhine River. This is Europe’s largest port and the third-largest port in the world.

The English Channel

Another important body of water in Europe is the English Channel. The English Channel is a narrow part of the Atlantic Ocean. It separates the southern coast of England from the northern coast of France. At its widest, the English Channel stretches about 112 miles, but it is only 21 miles at its narrowest point. Although it is narrow at several points, the English Channel still serves great purposes. The English Channel serves as a barrier and transportation channel between Great Britain and markets in Europe.

The Mediterranean Sea

The Mediterranean Sea stretches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Black Sea and the Tyrrhenian Sea to the north. It is almost completely surrounded by land. It separates Europe from Africa and borders over 20 countries. Commercial fisheries are a large part of the Mediterranean because of the great demand for fish and seafood in surrounding countries.

title: Landforms
text:
The European Plain

The European Plain extends from the Pyrenees Mountains, between Spain and France, all the way to the Ural Mountains in Russia. Due to its vast size, the plain gives Europe the lowest average elevation in the world. The great span of the European Plain creates varying climates and a strong contrast in vegetation. It has many navigable rivers, such as the Rhine River, within its boundaries. Due to the lower elevation and different climates, a variety of seasonal crops grow throughout the region. Because of its location, the European Plain is home to some of the most fertile areas in Europe.

The Alps

The Alps form the largest mountain range in Europe. The name “Alps” comes from the location of the mountain range. This mountain range covers parts of the Alpine countries of France, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia, Herzegovina, Montenegro, Serbia, and Albania. The Alps are crucial because they are the source of major European rivers like the Rhine. They are also the source of some tributaries, or rivers that feed into a larger river, like the Danube River. Vineyards and farms thrive within the valleys and the slopes of the Alps because of the climate and fertile soil. However, the success of the economy within the Alps relies heavily on a combination of mining and tourism. The Alps are home to abundant wildlife, plant life, and varying environments. These factors make it one of the world's most geographically diverse mountain ranges.

The Pyrenees Mountains

The Pyrenees are a mountain range located in southwestern Europe. They stretch from the Mediterranean Sea on the east to the Atlantic Ocean on the west. They form a natural boundary between France and Spain. This range is much smaller than the Alps but still offers great beauty. Historically, the people of the Pyrenees depended on agriculture and raising livestock to support their economy. The Great Pyrenees, a breed of dog, was first bred in this area to guard livestock and was named after the mountain range.

The Ural Mountains

The Ural Mountains extend about 1,500 miles through Russia. The Ural Mountains create a physical border between Europe and Asia. Scientists consider the Ural Mountains one of the world's oldest, most heavily eroded mountain ranges. This mountain range has a variety of vegetation and forests. The last remaining boreal forest in Europe is located within the Ural Mountains. The Urals contain important minerals and metals. These minerals are still used today for commercial purposes.

The Iberian Peninsula

The Iberian Peninsula is another remarkable geographic feature of Europe. The countries of Spain, Portugal, Andorra, and the territory of Gibraltar are located on the Iberian Peninsula. The Pyrenees Mountains create a border between the Iberian Peninsula and the rest of Europe. To the south, the narrow Strait of Gibraltar separates the Iberian Peninsula from Africa. Surrounding the northern and western parts of the peninsula is the Atlantic Ocean. The eastern portion of the peninsula is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea. The center of the Iberian Peninsula is known as the Meseta, or central plateau. The majority of the peninsula, about two-thirds, is covered by mountain peaks and ranges.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Europe is a diverse continent with many different physical features. These features have influenced the continent's history, culture, and population. The different physical characteristics across the continent have been used as natural borders between countries for thousands of years. Waterways were used not only to move goods but also for transportation and communication. Tourism and recreational activities rely heavily on the physical characteristics of Europe. Europe’s physical environment has influenced economic and government decisions throughout the continent’s long history. These characteristics continue to play a vital role in Europe's economy, culture, and governments today.

title: Natural Resources of Europe
text:
Europe's varied geography and climate create the ideal conditions for many resources to occur naturally. The natural resources of Europe influence the economic activities of the continent. Europe’s major industries are dependent upon its natural resources.

Mining, Oil, and Natural Gas

Mining is one of the major economic activities in Europe. Europe is home to some of the world’s largest mineral mines. The type and quantity of minerals depends on a country's geography. Coal is primarily mined in Western Europe. Large deposits of coal are found in the United Kingdom, Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Poland. Copper is mined in Northern Europe (Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Poland). Copper is also mined in Southern Europe (Portugal, Romania, Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Albania).

Türkiye is the largest producer of chromium in Europe. Norway is the leading producer of titanium on the continent. Poland has more silver mines than any other country in Europe. Other minerals mined throughout Europe include lead, iron ore, uranium, and zinc. Oil and natural gas are also mined and extracted throughout Europe. Russia has the largest deposits of oil in Europe. The United Kingdom is the second-largest producer of oil. The majority of the oil is extracted by offshore wells in the North Sea. Russia is the leading producer and exporter of natural gas in Europe and the world. Norway, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom are also major producers and exporters of natural gas.

Fishing

Fishing is a major industry in coastal areas of Europe. The European fishing industry makes up roughly five percent of the worldwide fishing industry. Most of Europe’s fishing industry occurs near the Mediterranean Sea and the eastern Atlantic Ocean. Spain, France, Denmark, and the United Kingdom lead Europe’s fishing industry. Their proximity to fishing grounds and Europe’s primary bodies of water are vital to the success of the industry.

Forestry

Forestry has been one of the largest industries in Europe for hundreds of years. This is due to the continent's variety, diversity, and abundance of forests. On average, forestry generates $600 million a year, accounting for roughly one-tenth of Europe’s total GDP. Traditionally, European woodworkers were skilled craftsmen. They crafted timber and lumber from the dense forests of the continent into furniture, homes, ships, and luxury goods. Many Europeans still work in this sector of the forestry industry.

Europe’s forests are vital to the paper industry in many countries. Forests provide resources other than timber that contribute to the forestry industry in Europe. Mushrooms, truffles, fruits, and berries grow throughout Europe’s forests. These agricultural products are gathered, processed, and shipped to markets worldwide. Natural cork is also gathered from Europe’s forests. The continent is the world’s largest exporter of cork.

Agriculture

Another important industry in Europe is agriculture. Many countries in Europe specialize in crops that grow well in the soil and climate of the area. Olives and grapes are major crops grown in Italy, Greece, and Spain. The region's Mediterranean climate supports the growth of these crops and allows them to flourish. The climate of Northern Europe is generally colder and receives more precipitation than other areas of Europe. Root vegetables grow better in Northern Europe because they can withstand a harsher climate. Europe’s climate and fertile soil also support large-scale livestock industries. Farms across Europe raise cattle, sheep, pigs, and poultry.

title: Essential Question
text: How does location impact a region's cultural, social, and economic development?

title: Distribution of Natural Resources
text:
Europe is rich in natural resources. Their availability and distribution depend on an area's climate and geography. Mountainous areas generally have larger deposits of mineral resources than areas of lower elevation. Areas with sandy or rocky soil are not ideal for growing a variety of crops. Additionally, some crops do not grow well in Mediterranean climates and require a temperate climate. More natural resources are available in countries with more varied geography and climate.

Many of the largest cities in Europe are located on or near ancient settlements. This includes cities in Germany, the United Kingdom, and Russia. The early peoples and empires of Europe chose where to settle based on the availability of natural resources. Large quantities of natural resources are still found near the cities that were built near ancient settlements. As a result, many of Europe’s most populous cities are found near sites of ancient settlements.

title: Climate
text:
Germany

Germany’s climate varies depending on location. Parts of northern Germany border the Baltic Sea. Areas of western Germany border the North Sea. The North Sea is fed by the Atlantic Ocean. Because of their proximity to the Baltic and North Seas, these regions of Germany have an oceanic climate. This kind of climate has smaller changes between summer and winter temperatures. Rainfall occurs throughout the year. Cities such as Hamburg and Bremen have an oceanic climate.

Southern Germany is farther from the sea and has a more continental climate. Areas with a continental climate experience larger temperature differences between summer and winter. Rainfall occurs more often in warmer months than in colder months. Cities such as Munich, Nuremberg, and Frankfurt experience a continental climate.

Another factor that impacts the climate of Germany is wind patterns. Germany receives winds that usually blow from west to east. This brings oceanic air from the Atlantic Ocean into Germany. It makes the western part of the country more oceanic and the eastern part more continental.

The United Kingdom

The United Kingdom is part of the British Isles, which consist of Ireland, Great Britain, and thousands of smaller islands. The British Isles have a temperate oceanic climate. This means that the air is humid. There is regular rainfall throughout the year with no dry season. The temperatures are mild, with warm summers and cool winters.

Occasionally, some areas further inland experience snow when the temperatures drop below freezing. Even though the United Kingdom is located so far north (only 396 miles south of the Arctic Circle), it does not experience extreme cold. It does not have areas of frozen tundra, much like the northern parts of Canada and Russia. This is due to the North Atlantic Drift. The North Atlantic Drift is a warm ocean current that travels north from the Gulf of Mexico into the Atlantic Ocean and northwest toward the British Isles. The warm waters of the Atlantic Ocean make the United Kingdom warm and mild instead of frozen tundra.

Russia

With such a large land area, the climate of Russia varies greatly. Russia has two main seasons: a warm to hot summer and a cold winter. The area of Russia located on the European continent has a cold winter and comfortable summer. The southern region of Russia in the plains, or steppe, is much different. It is hot and dry during the summer. In these regions, winters are cold but do not last long.

Central Russia, often referred to as Siberia, has severe winters, as is often associated with the area. This region has warm and pleasant summers and receives moderate rainfall. The eastern region of Russia can get quite hot. The coastal areas are cooler and wetter due to their proximity to water. Winters in the country's eastern area are less severe than in Siberia. They are much like the winter months in the southern and western regions of the country.

title: Environmental Issues in Germany
text:
Following World War II, Germany began to rebuild its economy. Manufacturing became one of the largest industries because of the country's abundant natural resources. Factories and manufacturing plants produced millions of goods a year. However, Germany’s economic growth came at a price. Factories, manufacturing facilities, vehicles, and machinery released dangerous chemicals and pollutants into the atmosphere. As a result, acid rain became a major point of discussion and worry for Germans during the 1980s.

Acid rain occurs when pollutants and harmful chemicals in the atmosphere mix with precipitation, mostly rain. Acid rain pollutes soil and waterways. It damages plants and buildings. During the 1980s, acid rain impacted many areas of Germany. Experts were concerned that acid rain would destroy all of Germany’s forests. They were particularly concerned about the Black Forest in southwestern Germany. German citizens feared that the loss of Germany’s forest would destroy the environment and economy of the country. Many people took action to combat the environmental issues caused by acid rain.

Thousands of Germans protested. They demanded change to protect the environment. Government officials and elected representatives from around the world visited the diseased forests to view the effects of acid rain. They recounted their time in Germany and used the trip as a cautionary tale in their own countries. Germany’s government passed laws to limit pollution and stop acid rain. Companies across Germany are developing cleaner forms of energy. Solar, hydroelectric, and wind energy are a few of the alternate forms of energy being developed.

title: Environmental Issues in the United Kingdom
text:
Air pollution is mostly caused by the exhaust released by factories, vehicles, and machinery. It’s made worse by cold geographic factors. These include elevation, weather patterns, and climate. Air pollution is a health hazard. In large cities, it is especially dangerous for people to breathe the air daily.

One of the worst instances of air pollution in the United Kingdom occurred in London in December 1952. In the weeks leading up to the Great Smog of 1952, the weather in England had been unseasonably cold. This led to increased use of coal-burning furnaces to heat homes across the city. The smoke from coal furnaces bellowed from chimneys and smoke stacks. At the same time, an anticyclone, or system of rotating air, hung over the city, trapping the smoke in the atmosphere. This created dense smog. Smog is a system of fog or haze that combines with smoke and other atmospheric pollutants. This thick smog hung over London from Dec. 5 to Dec. 9. The smog interrupted everyday life for days and resulted in the deaths of over 4,000 people.

In recent years, efforts have been made to cut down on pollution in the United Kingdom. People are required to pay additional fees for driving vehicles that cause more pollution. Efforts have been made to convert London buses and taxis to clean-burning fuels. Cities like London have also established monitoring stations to help keep track of the air quality. Animals have also been recruited to help detect air pollution. Scientists and environmentalists use pigeons to help determine air quality in an area through special vest monitors.

title: Environmental Issues in Ukraine
text:
One of the worst environmental disasters in modern history occurred in 1986 in Chernobyl, Ukraine. Chernobyl is a city in northern Ukraine near the border of Belarus. The city of Chernobyl was home to a nuclear power facility called Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant.

The power plant and complex consisted of four nuclear reactors. These reactors were mostly used for producing electricity. As the crew at Reactor 4 prepared for their routine shutdown on the night of April 25, 1986, something went horribly wrong. The workers wanted to see how long the turbines could supply power if the main electrical power supply was compromised. This was a test that had been successfully completed the year before. The plant had even received upgraded voltage regulator designs since the last test.

During the testing process, the automatic shutdown mechanisms were turned off. This started the problem that was to happen. Operators ran the reactors at a very low power. That was against safety precautions. They also did not properly communicate with safety personnel. This caused a giant power surge. Hot fuel mixed with the cooling water produced steam at a rapid rate. The pressure rose rapidly.

High pressure, the release of fuel, and the rapid creation of steam produced the perfect conditions for an explosion. The intense surge of power ruptured fuel lines, causing two explosions. Chemicals used to fuel the reactors were released into the atmosphere. Fuel ejected from the machines ignited fires. The fires burned for over 10 days. The fires released radioactive materials into the environment.

Countless efforts were made to put out the blaze and stop the radioactive material from spreading any further. Emergency crews responded immediately. They used helicopters to drop sand to stop the fires and the additional release of radioactive material. Boron was also dropped to prevent other nuclear reactions within the remaining reactors.

The Chernobyl disaster is the largest uncontrolled release of radioactivity in history. It greatly affected the areas of Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia. Some areas of Scandinavia and Europe were also affected. Officials closed the area within 18 miles of the power plant. When the disaster occurred, about 115,000 people were evacuated from their homes since they were so close to the blast. Later, another 220,000 people were removed from their homes because their area was also thought to be contaminated.

It is reported that over five million people lived in an area that was exposed to some level of radiation as a direct result of the disaster. Most reactors have containment structures. However, at the time of this disaster, Chernobyl did not. Therefore, during the explosion, radioactive material was capable of leaking out into the atmosphere. Cleaning up the radioactivity was of great concern because the three remaining reactors needed to be turned on and the remains of Reactor 4 needed to be protected.

Today, Reactor 4 at Chernobyl is enclosed in a concrete structure to prevent further damage and radiation leaks if a malfunction occurs. A new concrete sarcophagus, or stone coffin, was completed in 2017. It is estimated to last over 100 years. Since the disaster, new safety measures are in place to prevent another disaster on the scale of Chernobyl. These measures include decontaminating inhabited areas and removing contaminated food and food sources that humans consume. Measures also include treating pastures for radiation contamination and providing clean food for farm animals. It is important to learn from history so that accidents like the Chernobyl disaster are not repeated.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
The environment of Europe is very diverse. No two countries are the same. The physical characteristics, geography, and climate allow many resources to occur naturally and in great quantities. The amount, diversity, and availability of natural resources in Europe make the continent one of the largest exporters of goods in the world. Natural resources have played an important role in the settlement of Europe and the decisions of governments.

The economies of many countries depend on natural resources. Humans have learned to adapt to and modify the environment to meet their needs and wants, but this often comes at a price. Human-environment interaction has impacted the physical environments of Europe. However, efforts are being made to reduce the impact of humans on the environment across the continent.

title: Economic System in the United Kingdom
text:
The United Kingdom has a mixed market economy. A portion of its economy is driven by supply and demand. That involves producers and consumers. The other part of the economy is controlled by the government. The United Kingdom's government once owned many companies. Over the past few decades, it has turned ownership over to private individuals and corporations. This action has created a free-market competition in the country.

For several centuries, the United Kingdom has had one of the most prosperous economies in the world. Much has changed as other countries in the world have grown and developed. The United Kingdom is ranked as the sixth-largest national economy in the world. The United Kingdom's exports accounted for 32.7 percent of the country's GDP in 2022.

Manufactured goods accounted for almost half of those exports. Some of the United Kingdom's main exports include machinery, computers, and vehicles. Gems, precious metals, and mineral fuels are exports that contribute to the economy. Aircraft, medical equipment, plastics, and organic chemicals are also exported. The United Kingdom's main export partners include the United States, Germany, France, and the Netherlands. Partners include Ireland, Switzerland, and China. Belgium, Italy, and Spain are also export partners.

A large part of the United Kingdom's economy comes from services. These services are in areas such as education, health, and finance. Business services, tourism, and transportation are also services that contribute to the economy. The economy also benefits from services in communication and retail. The service industry accounts for nearly 78 percent of the U.K.’s economy.

In recent years, the economy of the United Kingdom has changed dramatically. The European Union (EU) was a major network for trade and commerce in the United Kingdom. In 2016, citizens voted to leave the EU. This separation was known as Brexit. The EU used to buy 44 percent of the United Kingdom’s exports. The EU supplied 53 percent of the United Kingdom’s imports. The long-term effects of this decision are unclear as of yet. The economy will most likely see many changes in trade in the years to come.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors impact the economic systems of Europe?

title: Factors of Economic Growth in the United Kingdom
text:
There are many factors that influence economic growth in the United Kingdom. Literacy rates play an important role. Roughly 95 percent of employers in the country require proficient literacy skills. Higher literacy rates among the population translate to higher employment rates. This also provides more opportunities for advancement. About 84 percent of adults in the United Kingdom have proficient or advanced literacy skills. The average literacy rate among the total population is 99 percent.

The United Kingdom has a history of investing in human capital goods and capital goods. Education is an important sector in their economy. Institutions of higher education in the United Kingdom include universities and specialized training schools. In 2020–2021, there were nearly 300 institutions with over two million students. These educational institutions help to build and bolster the economy of the country. The economy also relies on investments in capital goods. In 2021, over 18 percent of the country’s total GDP was invested in capital goods. Those investments included manufacturing, industrial, and service resources.

Another important factor that impacts the United Kingdom’s economy is entrepreneurship. For centuries, the monarch and Parliament controlled large-scale industries. They also controlled the means of production. This began to change during the 18th century. Specialization and trade began to grow. Resources and businesses that were once owned by the government had their ownership transferred to individuals and corporations. This action created a free-market competition in the country.

title: Economic System in Germany
text:
In 1990, West and East Germany reunified. Since then, Germany’s economic system continues to evolve. Like Canada, Australia, Brazil, and Mexico, Germany has a mixed economy. The major difference in Germany’s economic system is that it combines a market system. There is some government control and some social welfare. Social welfare is when the government assists the poor. A welfare economy considers the distribution of a nation’s resources. It also considers its citizens' sense of well-being.

Today, Germany has one of the largest and strongest economies in Europe. In 2022, Germany had the fourth-largest economy in the world. They recorded a GDP of $4.503 trillion. Those goods and services were exported to countries worldwide. Germany is the world’s largest exporter of cars, motor vehicle parts, and accessories. They also lead the world in exporting electrical control boards and packaged medical equipment.

Germany is a popular destination for tourists from around the world. Because of that, Germany’s economy relies heavily on the tourism industry. German companies and businesses are also one of the largest exporters of services in Europe. These include business, technical, and financial services. Germany's economic growth and success are due in large part to the availability of natural resources in Germany and its capital and human resources.

title: Factors of Economic Growth in Germany
text:
In terms of GDP, Germany has the largest economy in Europe. It has the fourth-largest economy in the world. Many factors contribute to Germany’s economic prosperity. Factors include literacy, capital resources, human resources, and entrepreneurship.

Another factor that influences Germany's economy is capital resources. After World War II, the United States implemented the Marshall Plan to help the German economy recover. The money given to Germany was used to help rebuild destroyed homes and businesses. It also helped switch from manufacturing weapons and war goods to making domestic products. This investment in capital resources helped Germany’s GDP grow dramatically after the war.

Human resources are another factor that makes Germany one of the leading economies in the world. Education is important to the German economy. Germany has several types of schools. After elementary school, students go to a certain school depending on their academic level. Each school leads to different higher education opportunities and different careers. Many students learn a career through an apprenticeship. They go to a vocational school a few times per week and spend the rest of their time learning on the job. Because of its focus on education, the literacy rate of the German population is well over 90 percent.

Germany also has some large and well-known companies, like famous carmakers. However, most German companies are small, family-owned businesses. About 60 percent of working Germans are hired by small businesses. Many of these businesses find success by selling their goods outside the country. These companies are started by entrepreneurs who find a specific role they can play in the economy. By making highly specialized goods or services, they help the German economy run smoothly.

title: Economic System in Russia
text:
Before the collapse of the Soviet Union, Russia had a centrally planned economy. The government made most of the decisions that drove the country's economy. Today, Russia has a mixed market-oriented economy. This means that economic decisions are mostly guided by supply and demand and aggregate well-being. The concept of aggregate well-being refers to the comfort and interests of the community as a whole. While Russia's economy is a mixed economy, the government controls more of the activities in private businesses than in other types of economies. This inhibits economic growth for the country.

Russia's economy is greatly affected by changes in the price of oil. Gas and oil are abundant in Russia. They are one of the world's leading oil and natural gas producers. Russia is much larger in land size than the United Kingdom and Germany. However, it does not have the largest and strongest economy in Europe. At the end of 2022, Russia’s GDP was roughly $3.995 trillion. That made it the 11th-largest economy in the world.

Bountiful natural resources make Russia a prime location for economic growth. Just recently, money is now being put into the factories, machinery, and technology to yield a higher profit from these resources. Russia is also investing in other industries. Mining and the production of precious and non-precious metals are examples of those industries. High-quantity metals, such as steel and aluminum, are exported from Russia each year.

Mining, manufacturing, construction, electricity, water, and gas make up the industrial sector of Russia’s GDP. They account for about 37 percent of the total GDP. Part of the industrial sector is known as the fuel and energy complex (FEC). This area of the industrial sector is the highest contributor to Russia's growing economy. The service sector is another area of Russia's economy that is continuing to grow. This sector includes financial services, tourism, advertising, health care, and social services. Russia’s service sector makes up about 60 percent of the country's GDP.

title: Factors of Economic Growth in Russia
text:
Since the collapse of the Soviet Union, Russia has expanded its economy in many ways. Russia is investing in foreign affairs. Recently, they have been putting money into internal improvements through capital investments. They have invested heavily in factories, machinery, and technology. This is in hopes of yielding a higher profit from the country’s natural resources, including oil, natural gas, and minerals. By doing so, Russian businesses are able to increase production and exports. This will bring more money into the country in the long run.

Investment in human capital through education is crucial for improving Russia’s economy. Since the collapse of the Soviet Union, the Russian government has invested heavily in education for both children and adults. Russia has a 99 percent literacy rate. Almost half of its citizens have received post-secondary education and/or degrees. Russia has also invested more in small businesses in recent years. They have actively encouraged entrepreneurship. With Russia being so heavily dependent on the export of natural gas, the importance of entrepreneurs creating practical, innovative ideas has never been so pressing.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: The economies of the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia have changed in many ways throughout history. Despite these changes, the economic systems of each country continue to rely heavily on the area's natural resources. Many factors impact the economy of any country. One major impact is government action. Other factors such as the GDP, literacy rates, capital and human goods, and entrepreneurship also heavily impact the economies of these countries.

title: Trade Within Europe
text:
Trade is one of Europe’s most important economic activities. Many European countries’ economies, including Germany, Russia, and the United Kingdom, rely on importing and exporting goods and services to markets around the world. European imports and exports are directly impacted by the natural resources available in each country. Some natural resources can only be found in Europe. That access allows producers in Europe to specialize in specific products and markets. This also allows for the specialization of trade.

Trade in Europe is often impacted by a country's structure and type of economy. Like Australia, Canada, Brazil, and Mexico, Germany has a mixed economy. Germany’s government encourages trade, specialization, and entrepreneurship. It imposes very few restrictions on its citizens. The United Kingdom has a free market, or advanced open market economy. This means that producers and consumers drive the means of production with little interference from the government. Russia has a mixed market-oriented economy. This type of economic system is a combination of a mixed economy and a command economy. Russia’s government plays a large role in the production of goods and trade.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors impact the economic systems of Europe?

title: European Union
text:
The first half of the 20th century was a period of great conflict and change. It impacted every facet of life in Europe. After World War II, many coalitions and treaties were created to encourage peace across Europe. These coalitions also promoted economic cooperation. While well-intentioned, the treaties and coalitions did not address all the issues that Europe faced. There were still human rights issues that needed responses.

In 1957, Belgium, Germany, France, Italy, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands formed the European Economic Community (EEC). Economic policies were established by the member nations. Their initial focus was on trade between the member nations. Each government wanted to improve their country’s economy. More countries joined, creating a large single market.

In 1993, European leaders created and signed the European Union Treaty, also called the Maastricht Treaty. This treaty created the European Union. The EEC was integrated into the European Union. Like the EEC, the EU's purpose was to create a single market among member nations. Members had to support the four fundamental economic freedoms of the treaty: the free movement of people, goods, services, and money. The Union's policies were meant to facilitate and protect European security, trade, and home affairs.

The European Union began with 12 nations. The United Kingdom and Germany were two of the first. In 1995, Austria, Finland, and Sweden joined the European Union. Border-free travel was implemented between Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain. A single currency called the euro was introduced in 11 member countries. These included Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain. The euro is still the primary currency in each of these countries.

Between 1999 and 2013, 13 more countries joined the EU. The new members were Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. In 2016, voters in the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union. This movement was popularly known as “Brexit.” The United Kingdom officially left the European Union on Jan. 31, 2020.

The EU has an international government. It is structured similarly to that of the U.S. government. The leaders of each member state are part of the European Council. They meet regularly to discuss important issues that affect the EU. The EU has three main institutions: The European Commission drafts and enforces the laws. The European Parliament makes the laws. The European Court of Justice ensures that these laws are applied equally in each EU country.

The EU’s vision is to create a place where all EU citizens can develop their full human potential. In addition, the EU’s goal is to improve the economy and the quality of life for all of its citizens, wherever they live. The European Union is continually evolving, but it continues to work toward economic growth and making Europe environmentally sound for future generations.

title: International Trade
text:
International trade is an important part of the economic development of many European countries. They rely on imports and exports to meet their needs and wants. Many goods cannot be produced in European countries. Only certain natural resources are available because the climate across Europe is largely temperate. That makes other natural resources difficult to obtain if they're available at all. Many countries can only obtain the goods and services they need through trade.

Many areas of Europe specialize in producing specific goods. This is dependent upon the volume and type of natural resources available in each area. Europe does have a wealth of natural resources. These include fruits, vegetables, lumber, and fish. Many European countries also have an abundant variety of mineral resources. Europe is home to some of the world’s largest coal, copper, natural gas, and oil deposits.
