title: Currencies
text:
Trade in and out of Europe is dependent on many factors. One factor is the exchange of currency. This can be a difficult task. Over 20 different official and unofficial currencies are used throughout Europe. The euro is the primary currency used across most of Europe. Twenty countries use it as their official currency. These include Germany, France, Ireland, and Italy. The euro is divided into multiple denominations. The paper banknotes range in value from 5 to 200 euros. Smaller denominations are available as coins, including 1 euro and 2 euros. There are six other coins, ranging in value from 1 cent to 50 cents.

The primary currency of the United Kingdom is the pound sterling. The pound sterling is made up of various denominations of polymer, or plastic, banknotes. Pound banknotes are printed and distributed in denominations of 5, 10, 20, and 50 pounds. The currency of the United Kingdom also includes eight coins. These include coins that are equal to 1 and 2 pounds. The remaining six coins in circulation are called pence.

Like the euro and pound, Russia’s currency is made up of banknotes and coins. Russian banknotes are called rubles. The coins are divided into kopecks and rubles. Rubles are printed in nine denominations, ranging from 5 to 5,000 rubles. Minted coins include 1, 5, 10, and 50 kopecks and coins that equal 1, 2, 5, and 10 rubles.

title: Trade Barriers
text:
Trade relationships in Europe vary from one country to another. Countries place tariffs and quotas on goods. They can even create an embargo that bans trade completely. Tariffs are taxes that must be paid on imports, exports, or both. Quotas limit the number of items that can be imported or exported. Each country in Europe creates its own tariffs, quotas, and embargoes.

Germany imposes tariff and non-tariff barriers on trade. Tariffs are imposed on most imports coming into the country. The tariffs particularly target imports from outside the European Union. Germany places other restrictions on imports coming into the country. These include licensing requirements and restrictions, product bans, safety regulations, and customs procedures. Beginning in 2023, importers in Germany are required to provide reports on the emissions created during the production process.

In 2022, Germany placed embargoes on imports from Russia. This was done as a result of political issues between the two countries. Germany has an embargo on imports of gold, iron and steel products, and crude oil from Russia. As of June 2023, the embargo remains in effect.

Like other countries in Europe, the Russian government also imposes tariff and non-tariff barriers on trade. In 2012, Russia became a World Trade Organization (WTO) member. As a result, Russia lowered trade tariffs for member nations by 10 percent. They also created new import quotas. The membership helped establish lower tariffs on imports within the quota. However, higher tariffs were placed on imports outside of the quota. This applies to nearly all nations that trade with Russia.

Russia has also enforced embargoes on imported goods from various countries in recent years. In 2014, Russia created an embargo on foods imported from the European Union, Australia, Canada, the United States, and Norway. They were created in response to diplomatic hostility between Russia and the various nations. In 2022, many nations placed an embargo on Russian imports. This embargo was created as a result of the Russian war on Ukraine. It is enforced by many countries in and out of Europe. The embargo places sanctions and/or bans on the importation of gold, iron and steel products, and crude oil from Russia.

Trade in and out of the United Kingdom has changed in many ways since 2016. Brexit was the primary catalyst for many of the changes. To retain trading partnerships and networks between the United Kingdom and members of the European Union, the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement was created. It went into effect on Jan. 1, 2021. This agreement is more than just a free trade agreement. The EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement creates economic, environmental, and social cooperation between the EU and the United Kingdom. It addresses issues with international fisheries, creates a close partnership to protect the security of citizens, and sets up a framework for governing the agreement.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Economies across Europe have changed in many ways throughout its history. Despite these changes, trade has remained a constant and important aspect. Many factors impact trade. One of the biggest factors that impacts trade is government. Government actions and policies can encourage or hinder trade. This has happened across Europe throughout history. Europe’s economic history is deeply rooted in trade. Cultural similarities and differences have also played a vital role in trade throughout the continent’s long history. Culture continues to influence political and economic decisions in Europe.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors and events have impacted the people, culture, and governments of Europe?

title: Languages of Europe
text:
There are 287 languages spoken today in Europe. The languages in Europe with the highest number of speakers include English, French, German, Italian, Russian, and Turkish. Of all the languages spoken, English is commonly used in business matters between different countries. In European Union (EU) countries, children are required to learn a foreign, or different, language in school. German, French, and English are among the most commonly learned languages. Since English is studied so widely, it is often used as a common language between people from different countries.

There are many language groups in Europe. Europe is home to the five major Romance languages. These languages came from the ancient Roman time period. They were influenced by the use of Latin as it spread across Europe. The five Romance languages are Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, and Romanian. The Germanic language groups are German, Dutch, Danish, Swedish, and Norwegian. The Slavic language groups are Russian, Ukrainian, Czech, and Polish. There are also the Uralic languages. This group of languages is separated geographically and ethnically. The languages consist of the Finns, the Hungarians, and Estonians.

The EU has identified and documented 24 official languages that are spoken within their organization. These languages are Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Irish, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, and Swedish. The EU has also worked to create and enforce a multilingual language policy. As a result, most citizens in Europe are able to speak more than one language. It has also created a culture that allows for more connections among social, educational, professional, and economic communities.

Just as physical features affected the development of cultures throughout Europe, they also affected language development. Many areas of Europe are more isolated than others. The Alps are an isolated geographic area of Europe. Because it is an isolated region, many archaic or ancient languages are still spoken in the region. This has created linguistic diversity in the area.

title: Judaism
text:
Like many religions, Judaism has changed and developed over time. Judaism originated in an ancient area of the Middle East, or Southwest Asia, called Canaan. This is now modern-day Israel. The founding of Judaism dates back to 2000–1700 B.C.E., with Abraham and his family line. The religious practices of Hebrews and Israelites have also changed over time. These people have relied on scholars and leaders to interpret their laws. Scholars do this by studying important sources of ethical teaching and their central beliefs. The Torah is one such source. It is the holy book of Judaism. It contains the first five books of the Hebrew Bible. The Hebrew Bible contains many of the same books as the Old Testament in the Christian Bible. The teachings of the Torah are often taught in Jewish places of worship, called synagogues.

Jewish traditions can be found in the morals and ethics of many Western civilizations. The basic foundation of many laws that countries write today are similar to the laws and teaching found in the Torah.

Another source of teaching in Judaism is the Oral Law. It is also known as the Talmud. The word “Talmud” means “to study.” Hebrew scholars, rabbis, and teachers study ancient texts and scriptures in order to understand and explain their laws. The Talmud is a commentary by early rabbis who studied the Torah.

The Torah lists 613 mitzvot, or Hebrew holy laws, that God gave the Jews to follow. The Talmud also explains how the holy laws should be followed and gives examples of how to be just and righteous. The Talmud helps explain why it is important to study and why so many scholars have written about it over the centuries.

Today, the Jewish population in Europe is approximately 1.3 million. However, there are over 15 million Jews worldwide.

title: Christianity
text:
Christianity was established as a religion around the first century C.E., in what is now called Israel. Like Jews and Muslims, Christians also believe in one God. Christianity follows the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, also called Jesus Christ. Christians follow the teachings of the Bible. The Bible is the holy book of Christianity. It contains the Old Testament and the New Testament. The Old Testament contains many of the same books as the Hebrew Bible. The New Testament is a record of the life and teachings of Jesus Christ, the writings of his followers, and early Christian communities. Those who practice Christianity adhere to a set of ideas and practices that have been handed down since its origin. Much of Christianity is based on Jesus's teachings on love and forgiveness. One example is the “Golden Rule,” which states that people should treat others the way that they would want to be treated. These teachings have had a significant impact on Christian philosophy and practices.

Although Christianity was established in ancient Israel, it has spread and grown into a major world religion. During the Middle Ages, Christianity spread from its origins in the Mediterranean to northern Europe. Religious institutions, such as monasteries and convents, were formed to further spread the teachings of Christianity. Christianity also became integrated into the political systems of Europe. Christian monarchs began to send people to remote areas of Europe to convert others to the religion. These religious emissaries were called missionaries. Christianity reached areas of what is now the United Kingdom by 410 C.E. From there, Christian missionaries, like St. Patrick, Gregory the Great, and St. Boniface, traveled throughout Europe to share their views and beliefs. Within a few centuries, Christianity became the predominant religion in Germany, Russia, France, Sweden, and other areas of Europe.

Eventually, the Roman Catholic Church, the first Christian church, became very powerful. This was especially true in Western Europe. It had a hierarchy of religious leaders, with the pope at its head. The Church made laws for people to follow. It controlled the courts and even taxed, or tithed, the people, just like a government. The Church used money it collected to build large churches and other places of worship, such as cathedrals. These buildings were intended as monuments to God. Two very famous cathedrals are Notre Dame in Paris, France, and Westminster Abbey in London, England.

In many European countries, the Church had more power than the monarchs of Europe. If a monarch didn’t do what the Church asked of them, church leaders excommunicated them, or cast them out of the church permanently. Church members often persecuted non-Christians who did not join the church, including Jews and Muslims.

Today, most Western Europeans who practice religion identify as Christians. Christianity is practiced by over 2.8 billion people worldwide. It is the largest of the world's religions.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Europe has many diverse cultures, languages, and religions. The cultures of each geographic region are unique. Each region showcases its rich culture through its history, food, architecture, and traditions. The European Union promotes and maintains cultural diversity as the prime focus of Europe. Many festivals and events celebrate the diverse cultures and religions that take place throughout the year in different countries. Religion has been one of the key factors in the development and beliefs of cultures throughout Europe. There are three major monotheistic religions in Europe: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. They have had a major impact on Europe's history, governments, economies, and cultures.

title: Historical Forms of Government in Europe
text:
Governments in Europe have changed in many ways since the establishment of major European countries. For centuries, the majority of European countries, including the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia, had absolute monarchies. An absolute monarchy is a form of government in which all government decisions are made by the monarch. A monarch is a hereditary position. It is passed down through a particular family line. In absolute monarchies, the rights of citizens were not always protected or guaranteed. Spain, France, Austria, Prussia, Hungary, Denmark, and Norway are just some European countries that were ruled by an absolute monarch for centuries.

Another form of government that has been prevalent for centuries among European nations is an authoritarian government. In an authoritarian government, such as a dictatorship or oligarchy, one person or a small group of people take authority by force. An oligarchy is a form of government in which power is controlled by a small group of individuals. They generally belong to the aristocracy, nobility, or military. A dictatorship is similar to an oligarchy, but the government is controlled by one person, called a dictator. Citizens are expected to obey government leaders. They have no role or say in government policies. In an authoritarian government, the rights of the people are not guaranteed. Countries that fall under the umbrella of communism or fascism traditionally have authoritarian governments.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors and events have impacted the people, culture, and governments of Europe?

title: Government of Russia
text:
Like the United Kingdom and Germany, Russia’s government has changed dramatically through the centuries. Today, the country of Russia is a federal presidential republic. The president and prime minister have shared responsibilities as the head of state and the head of government. However, the president holds more power and influence. The Russian legislature, or parliament of the Russian Federation, consists of the State Duma (the lower house) and the Federation Council (the upper house). The judicial system is made up of courts that are managed by the Russian Ministry of Justice.

According to the Russian Constitution, the people elect the president for a six-year term. Previously, the president could only serve for two consecutive terms. For example, Vladimir Putin was elected president in 2000, serving two consecutive terms until 2008. He was then appointed as Prime Minister for four years while Dmitry Medvedev served as president. Since Putin had not been president for four years and the terms were no longer consecutive, he ran again in 2012 and won. He was reelected president for a fourth term in 2018. The constitution would not allow him to run again without taking another position. However, in 2020, the Russian government held a referendum. This allowed them to amend some articles of the constitution. One change removed part of the clause about consecutive terms of office. It also nullified, or erased, the previous terms served by former presidents, including Putin and Medvedev. The amendments were signed into law in April 2021 by Putin. This change allowed Putin to again be eligible for election.

In order to win, the president must have the majority of votes. If this is not the case, there is a second election round between the two candidates with the most votes. Russia’s voting age is 18. The Russian president appoints the prime minister and is confirmed by the State Duma.

The Federation Council has 170 seats. They are filled by two senators of each of Russia's 85 federal entities or regions. Accordingly, the State Duma has 450 seats. The State Duma’s members are popularly elected for a five-year term. Russian citizens of at least 21 years of age can become a member of the State Duma. Similarly, Russians 30 years of age or older can be appointed as members of the Federation Council.

During the Soviet era, Russians didn’t have elections as they do now. The people were not allowed to choose from competing political parties. However, after the end of communism, reforms were made, intending to give Russians more freedom to choose their leaders.

Timeline of the Government of Russia

862: The modern state of Russia is established.

1017: Yaroslav I establishes the first Russian code of law called the Russkaya Pravda.

1547: Ivan IV (Ivan the Terrible) is crowned the first tsar of unified Russia.

1598: Following the death of the childless Feodor I, a parliament called the Zemsky Sobor is assembled to select a new tsar. This is the start of the Romanov dynasty, which lasts for over 300 years.

1649: The Zemsky Sobor creates a new legal code called the Sobornoye Ulozheniye (Council Code). This legal code creates a new class system, which includes the serf class (which includes slaves and free peasants).

1708: Peter the Great and the Zemsky Sobor divide Russia into eight guberniyas (governorates). Each guberniya is run by a governor that reports to the tsar and Zemsky Sobor.

1711: Peter the Great establishes the Governing Senate, a political body that is given the authority to rule in his absence if necessary.

1767: Empress Catherine the Great creates the Nakaz Yekateriny Velikoy (Instruction of Catherine the Great). This legal code revises existing laws to create equality and protection for all men under the law.

1861: Alexander II issues the Emancipation Reform. This legislation abolishes serfdom and gives former serfs and peasants the right to buy land.

1864: The Russian government creates the Zemstva, a system of local governments that work under the direction of the guberniyas and the national government to solve local issues. New reforms are also implemented to reform the judicial system of Russia.

1882: Alexander III approves laws to make working conditions safer and places restrictions on the working hours for women and children.

1906: The country’s first free elections to the Duma are held.

1906: A new constitution is created, and the Fundamental Laws are passed. These laws reaffirm the political power of the emperor.

1917: The Russian Revolution comes to a close, ending over 300 years of Romanov rule in Russia. Revolutionary Vladimir Lenin and the Communist Party seize control of the government. The Soviet Union is established.

1929: Joseph Stalin seizes control of the government and rules as a dictator until 1953.

1985: Mikhail Gorbachev is selected as the leader of the Communist Party and introduces several economic forms.

June 1991: The Soviet Union holds its first free elections. Boris Yeltsin is elected president.

December 1991: The Soviet Union collapses and readopts the traditional name of Russia.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: The governments of Europe are as diverse as the continent's economic systems, cultures, and traditions. The economic and cultural needs of the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia have changed. So has the political landscape of each country. Despite their vast differences, Russia, Germany, and the United Kingdom's governments have expanded citizens' participation. Today, citizens have more opportunities in the government than at any other time in each country’s history. The governments' actions have and will continue to impact the citizens of the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia.

title: Conflict Around the World
text:
In the late 1800s and early 1900s, European countries were competing with each other for money and trade. Germany felt other countries were stopping it from doing business. Many Germans blamed England for these problems. To feel safer, nations began making alliances, or agreements where countries promised to help each other.

Germany made an alliance called the Triple Alliance with Austria-Hungary and Italy. On the other side, England, France, and Russia formed the Triple Entente. These alliances worked like teams. If someone attacked one country in the alliance, the other countries promised to fight back. Nations began putting soldiers and weapons along their borders. Everyone was getting ready for possible war, and tension was building.

On June 28, 1914, something terrible happened. Archduke Franz Ferdinand, who was going to become Austria's next leader, and his wife were assassinated. A young man from a terrorist group called the Black Hand killed them. Austria blamed Serbia's government for the attack. One month later, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. This started a chain reaction.

Russia jumped in to help Serbia. Germany declared war on Russia. When Germany's army marched through Belgium, England declared war on Germany. The Triple Entente became known as the Allies. The Triple Alliance became the Central Powers. By Christmas in 1914, England, France, and other Allied countries were fighting hard against Germany, Austria, Bulgaria, and the Ottoman Empire.

The United States stayed out of the war at first. However, things changed in 1917. Germany used submarines called U-boats to sink ships. When a German U-boat sank a British passenger ship called the Lusitania, killing many people including Americans, the United States joined the war.

The United States Declares War

President Woodrow Wilson protested the sinking of the Lusitania but was treated coldly by the German government. Then, a telegram was sent by Arthur Zimmermann, the German secretary of state for foreign affairs. The intercepted telegram set off a firestorm of concern in the United States. Zimmermann offered to help Mexico regain Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona. In exchange, Zimmerman wanted Mexico to allow Germany to set up submarine bases along the Mexican coast.

Mexico's president, Venustiano Carranza, was angry with the United States. He was willing to provide submarine bases for Germany. These actions made Americans very angry with Germany. This led to the United States entering the war. President Wilson approached Congress and said that the United States should fight Germany "to make the world safe for democracy." On Apr. 6, 1917, the United States declared war on Germany. Congress then passed the draft law. Two million men were sent overseas to serve in the navy and the American Expeditionary Force (AEF). With the entrance of the United States, World War I became a total war. This means the war impacted every area of society.

The United States Breaks Through German Lines

In 1918, the Germans launched five massive offensives (attacks) against Allied troops. They tore a huge hole in Allied lines and tried to reach the English Channel and Paris. American troops helped stall both drives. For about two months after this, the Allied nations began a counterattack all along the Western Front. The fighting was bitter. U.S. casualties (people who were wounded and killed) grew quickly to 100,000. Finally, the Americans broke through the German lines and began advancing.

All across the Western Front, Allied troops pushed the Germans and their supporting troops back. It was too much for the Central Powers. Bulgaria petitioned for peace on Sept. 29, 1918. On Oct. 30, 1918, the Ottoman Empire signed an armistice. Austria-Hungary surrendered to Italy on Nov. 3, 1918. The Allied troops finally pushed Germany into surrendering. They demanded that the German kaiser step down before a peace treaty could be signed.

The End of the War

At 11 a.m. on Nov. 11, 1918, the war ended. Troops couldn't believe that the war was over. The Treaty of Versailles was drafted by England and France. It laid out conditions that had to be agreed on before there would be peace. Germany had to agree to give up its colonies around the world. Germany had to surrender most of its fleet and all of its artillery and heavy military equipment. Germany also had to pay for the damages it caused during the war.

Treaty of Versailles, 1919

On June 28, 1919, the Treaty of Versailles formally concluded World War I, establishing peace terms between the Allied powers and Germany. Allied leaders held conflicting visions for postwar Europe. French Prime Minister Georges Clemenceau sought to permanently weaken Germany's military capabilities, while British and French governments demanded financial compensation for wartime expenditures.

In contrast, U.S. President Woodrow Wilson advocated for peace through his 14 Points, a comprehensive peace framework developed with approximately 150 foreign policy experts. Wilson's proposal addressed fundamental causes of international conflict, including secret diplomatic agreements, arms proliferation, territorial disputes, and restricted maritime commerce. His vision emphasized the League of Nations as a mechanism for resolving disputes through international diplomacy rather than military force.

Despite Wilson's peacemaking approach, the following terms for Germany were in the final treaty:

Territorial losses included 10 percent of European lands and all colonial possessions.

Demilitarization requirements severely restricted army and navy size while prohibiting air force development.

War crime tribunals targeted Kaiser Wilhelm II and other Axis leadership.

The war guilt clause assigned Germany complete responsibility for initiating the conflict.

Reparations payments imposed massive financial obligations to compensate Allied losses.

These harsh conditions created widespread resentment among Germans who felt their government had betrayed national interests. Combined with global economic depression, the treaty's terms generated severe financial hardship and political instability. This volatile environment facilitated the emergence of extremist political movements, particularly the National Socialist Workers' Party, also known as the Nazis. This ultimately enabled Adolf Hitler's ascent to power 13 years later.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors and events have impacted the people, culture, and governments of Europe?

title: Worldwide Economic Depression
text:
World War I impacted every facet of life in Europe. Homes were destroyed. Economic industries were decimated. Millions of lives were lost. European nations struggled to rebuild their economies, governments, and societies. The economy of Germany was hit particularly hard by World War I. Following the signing of the Treaty of Versailles, Germany adopted a new form of democratic government, which was called the Weimar Republic. This was the first time in the nation’s history that the government was a democratic system. Historically, Germany was ruled by kings, emperors, and kaisers. This new form of government experienced opposition from many German citizens. This opposition made it difficult to run the government effectively.

The Treaty of Versailles required the new German government to pay reparations to the Allied governments for damages in the war. The government went into debt to pay for the war. It was forced to pay even more as a result of the war. To make matters worse, the new democratic government made decisions that led to inflation. These problems negatively affected the economy. Money became nearly worthless, including anything people had saved. Economic instability caused social unrest throughout the country.

Economic issues in Germany and other countries in Europe eventually spread to the United States. With the end of World War I, the United States entered the 1920s. This was an energetic period in American history. It was an age of prosperity and wealth for the nation. From 1921 to 1929, the average income per person rose from $522 to $716 a year. Americans had more money to spend and more time for entertainment.

Consumers bought new products, including radios, beauty products, frozen foods, watches, clothing, and more. New technologies made previously expensive items available to the middle class. Even those who did not see a rise in their incomes could join the buying spree by purchasing goods with credit. Of course, the credit wasn’t free money. It was a type of loan with interest that had to be calculated into the repayment plan.

Consumers could also make use of another new financing option: installment buying. A family could buy its first radio and pay for it over time in small monthly payments rather than all at once. Installment loans included interest, too. However, the introduction of credit and installment buying came at a cost. Overbuying without having enough money sometimes leads people into debt. This would become a huge issue for many people in the years to come.

Black Tuesday, Oct. 29, 1929, was the end of a successful and hopeful time in the United States. During the 1920s, millions of people bought shares of stock or partial ownership of companies. Stock prices continued to rise. People borrowed more and more money from banks to buy more shares. On Black Tuesday, the prices of stocks fell sharply, and the shares were worth nothing. Many people lost everything they owned that day. The stock market crashed, and the U.S. economy crashed along with it.

The stock market crash was only the beginning of tough times for the country. Many banks lost money too. People worried that their money in the bank might not be safe. They rushed to the banks to withdraw their funds. When banks were out of money, they closed their doors. Some of the banks began to go out of business completely. People who had deposited money in the banks were out of luck. There was no money left. Many banks tried to get back some of the money they had let people borrow. They began to ask people to pay back their loans immediately. Sometimes, the banks took people’s homes and farms when their loans weren’t paid.

Businesses were also affected by the economic downturn. Some businesses lost most of their money in the stock market crash. Many of them had to cut back employees’ hours, reduce their pay, or terminate employment altogether. Other businesses lost everything and were forced to close. This caused high rates of unemployment throughout the country.

Farmers in America had already been suffering economically since the end of World War I. During the war years, Europe needed food and was willing to pay high prices for it. Farmers were making profits, and many wanted to expand their farms and buy new equipment. The farmers borrowed money from banks to help pay for the land and machinery. When the war ended, crops' supply far outweighed their demand. This caused the price of crops to drop. Farmers could not pay back the money they had borrowed from the banks. Many farmers lost their land, and the unpaid loans contributed to the failure of some of the banks by 1929.

Within a few years, millions of Americans were out of work. Some of these people traveled on railroads from town to town, looking for new jobs. Farmers who had lost their land traveled all over the country to find work on other people’s farms. Some businesses had more than 1,000 people apply for a single job opening.

Although the Great Depression started in the United States, it quickly became a worldwide problem. After World War I, the United States helped many European countries pay their debts. When the American economy failed, there was no money to send to foreign countries. As a result, the western European countries fell into a period of economic depression too. Great Britain and Germany were hit the hardest. The Great Depression lasted for more than a decade. Unfortunately, it took another great war to bring prosperity back to the world.

title: The Rise of Dictatorships in Europe
text:
After the chaos of World War I and the economic instability of the Great Depression, people wanted strong national unity and leadership. This gave rise to many new forms of government in Europe and Asia. Strong leaders emerged in Italy, Russia, and Germany.

After World War I, Italian leaders had to deal with unhappy citizens. Benito Mussolini stepped in. He created many relief programs to assist Italian citizens. He also set himself up as a dictator. A dictator is a leader who has all of the power to run a government. In 1935, Mussolini ordered the Italian military to invade Africa to expand Italy’s empire.

The government of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) was a communist dictatorship. Joseph Stalin became the leader of the USSR in 1929. In a communist government, there is no private property. Stalin took farmland from the poor. He placed it under government control. He also set and reached many goals for mining and manufacturing. These goals were part of his “Five-Year Plans.” Stalin’s Five-Year Plans made the Soviet Union a productive industrial nation. However, it was at the expense of many citizens of the Soviet Union. Stalin focused on agricultural collectivism, or ownership of land and agricultural production by the government. This change led to famine and food shortages in many rural areas of the Soviet Union.

Adolf Hitler was one of many people who were unhappy with the outcomes of WWI and the actions of Germany’s democratic government. Hitler served in the German Army during WWI. He became involved in the National Socialist German Workers' Party in 1919. Within two years, he was elected the leader of the NSDAP, which became known as the Nazi Party. In November 1923, Hitler and members of the Nazi Party attempted to overthrow the government through force. The attempt failed, and Hitler was imprisoned for eight months.

Following his failed attempt to overthrow the government, Hitler realized that he would have to gain control of Germany through the proper political and legal channels. He reorganized the Nazi Party. Over time, Hitler gained a larger following. He exploited the feelings that many Germans had against the government of the Weimar Republic. He was also influential in getting Nazi Party officials elected to government office.

In 1933, Hitler achieved one of his political goals and became chancellor of Germany. In 1934, Hitler took over the German government. He ruled as a dictator. Hitler promised the millions of poor and unemployed citizens of Germany that with his help, the country would become powerful again. In March 1938, Nazi troops marched into Austria and took control of the country. Many Austrians felt that all German-speaking people should belong to a united country. Some Austrians felt differently. Soon after, Hitler moved to take control of German-speaking areas in Czechoslovakia.

In October 1938, Hitler, Mussolini, and the prime ministers of France and Britain met in Munich, Germany. They agreed that an area made up of parts of Czechoslovakia, known as the Sudetenland, would come under German control.

British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain agreed to Hitler’s demands to prevent another world war. Unfortunately, this wouldn’t be the end of Hitler’s demands. On Sept. 1, 1939, Germany invaded Poland. England and its allies officially declared war against Germany. The world became embroiled in World War II.

title: The Government of the Third Reich
text:
After World War I, nations worldwide worked to recover from the conflict. Europe had been the site of much of the fighting, and this period brought significant change. In Germany, Hitler and the Nazi Party directed old hatreds and misbeliefs toward Jews. The country's problems were blamed on the Jewish population by many people. Jewish politicians were held responsible by the Nazi Party for the Weimar Republic's weaknesses and shortcomings. The Nazi Party also claimed that Jewish financiers and business owners controlled the nation's economy. Germany's economic depression following WWI was blamed on Jewish financiers by the Nazi Party. Hitler and his followers believed that Jewish philosophers and thinkers promoted dangerous communist ideas.

The Nazi government implemented policies and actions that discriminated against and segregated specific groups. Discrimination is the unfair treatment of people based on their race, age, gender, religion, abilities, or beliefs. Segregation is the forced separation of different groups of people based on race, age, gender, religion, abilities, or beliefs. Persecution, or hostile feelings or actions toward a person or group, can result from unchecked discrimination and segregation. Jews were the largest group targeted for such actions. The Jewish population was targeted for erasure by the Nazi government and its collaborators. Propaganda became a powerful tool for spreading Nazi ideology. The government used propaganda to fuel hatred and misconceptions further.

Laws and actions of the Nazi government against Jews were anti-Semitic. Antisemitism is prejudice against or hatred of Jews. Intense feelings of antisemitism, along with the blame placed on Jews for Germany’s struggles following World War I, led to the Holocaust. The Holocaust was the systematic, state-sponsored persecution and murder of European Jews by the Nazis. The Holocaust occurred between 1933 and 1945. It is history’s most extreme example of antisemitism. The following is a timeline of the legalization of segregation, discrimination, and persecution of the Jews and other groups by the Nazi government.

title: Snapshot of World War II
text:
Sept. 1, 1939: Germany invades Poland. In response, Poland’s allies declare war on Germany.

Sept. 17, 1939: The Soviet Union invades Poland to support their German allies.

Sept. 27, 1939: Warsaw, the capital of Poland, is captured by German troops after a nine-day siege.

Dec. 13, 1939: The first sea battle of World War II is fought, resulting in a British victory.

April 1940: Germany invades Norway and seizes control of the government.

June 1940: German forces capture and occupy Paris. In response to Germany’s invasion of France, Italy enters the war as an ally of Germany.

July–October 1940: The German Luftwaffe (air force) continuously bombs areas of Great Britain in an effort to weaken defenses and invade. The Royal British Air Force defeats their attempts and prevents a full-scale invasion of Great Britain. This period of the war is known as the Battle of Britain.

Sept. 22, 1940: Germany, Italy, and Japan sign the Tripartite Pact, which is meant to deter other countries from joining the war on the side of the Allied Forces.

June 22, 1941: Germany invades the Soviet Union, ending the alliance between the two nations.

Dec. 7, 1941: Japan bombs the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. As a result, the United States and Great Britain declare war on Japan and its allies.

August 1943: Allied Forces invade and take control of Sicily from the Axis Powers.

September 1943: Italy surrenders and withdraws from the war.

June 6, 1944: Allied Forces land at Normandy to begin the invasion of France.

March 1945: Allied Forces cross the Rhine River and successfully invade Germany.

April 1945: Russian forces reach Berlin.

May 1945: Germany surrenders and withdraws from the war.

July 8, 1945: Russia declares war on Japan.

Aug. 6, 1945: The United States drops the first atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan.

Aug. 9, 1945: The United States drops the second atomic bomb on Nagasaki, Japan.

Sept. 2, 1945: Japan formally surrenders, ending World War II.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: The 20th century was a period of great conflict around the world. It was also a period of change. Many European countries experienced struggles as a result of World War I. These struggles were cultural, economic, and political. The economic and political issues led to social, cultural, and political issues that impacted the lives of millions of people. These issues affected the lives of people in many European countries, particularly Germany. The worst of these issues was the Holocaust, in which the Nazi regime systematically persecuted and murdered European Jews. Following World War II, new issues arose from the end of the war. These new issues caused a rift between the major powers of the world for many years to come.

title: The World After War
text:
World War II's conclusion brought dramatic global transformation. The United States and the Soviet Union emerged as superpowers, but these former allies rapidly became rivals. Following Nazi Germany's unconditional surrender, the Allied Powers assumed responsibility for European recovery. "The Big Three," or Great Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States, directed post-war planning efforts. After their initial February 1945 meeting in Yalta, these leaders convened again in Potsdam, Germany, in July 1945 to determine Europe’s future path.

The Allied nations represented a mixture of governmental systems, including democracies and communist-based governments. Soviet Union leader Joseph Stalin strongly advocated for communist principles. Communism is a form of government in which a small group of people has total control of the government and economy and determines how much everyone is paid according to their needs. Under communism, citizens do not have a say in the government. Citizens do not own property. Instead, they share goods as a community, depending on how much the government determines they need. This ideological difference created significant tensions in post-war negotiations.

At the Potsdam meeting in 1945, the Big Three reached numerous agreements to conclude the war and establish peace. They established a Council of Foreign Ministers to oversee peace treaty negotiations. This council assisted new governments in developing peaceful international relations.

Europe's economies lay in ruins after the war's devastation. Nazi Germany's currency had become worthless, factories stood destroyed, transportation networks were disrupted, and agricultural production couldn't meet the population's food needs. Addressing the European nations' economies was essential for building a strong future. U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall developed the "European Recovery Plan," commonly known as "the Marshall Plan." This four-year reconstruction program aimed to rebuild cities, industries, highways, and railroads while establishing international trade connections for European countries. The Marshall Plan operated on capitalist principles, emphasizing private business ownership and free trade. The Soviet Union's communist government opposed capitalism and therefore did not support the Marshall Plan.

The Marshall Plan distributed over $13.3 billion to war-torn Western European nations. Sixteen countries received these funds, but the Soviet Union refused to participate. This decision significantly impacted countries within the Soviet Union's sphere of influence.

title: Essential Question
text: What factors and events have impacted the people, culture, and governments of Europe?

title: Division of Germany and the Beginnings of the Cold War
text:
Following the surrender of Germany in 1945, the leaders of the Allied forces met to determine how to rebuild Europe after six years of war. Allied forces agreed to divide Germany into four zones. These zones were controlled by the United States, the Soviet Union, Great Britain, and France. The United States, Great Britain, and France controlled the area known as West Germany. The Soviet Union controlled the area of East Germany. Berlin, the capital of Germany, was also divided between the Allied forces.

Government structures were different between Eastern and Western Europe. Problems occurred very quickly because of this. Countries in Western Europe hoped to create democratic forms of government. The Soviet Union wanted to spread communism throughout Eastern Europe.

Communism began to spread after World War II. The Allied forces worried that more nations would turn to or be forced into communism by the Soviet Union. This put the United States and the Soviet Union head to head in a dangerous struggle. By 1947, Türkiye and Greece were under attack by pro-communist forces. The president of the United States, Harry S. Truman, feared that if communists took over Türkiye and Greece, it would spread to Western Europe.

The world watched closely as disagreements grew between the United States and the Soviet Union. In 1947, American businessman and political advisor Bernard Baruch described the relationship between the two countries as a “cold war.” This was because neither side officially declared war on the other. This term was used to describe the world's political climate for the next 40 years.

Former British Prime Minister Winston Churchill delivered a speech at a small college in President Harry Truman’s home state of Missouri. President Truman attended the speech. Churchill used this opportunity to speak to the world about current happenings and their impact on the future. In his speech, he stated, “From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the Continent.” He then urged the American people to “adhere faithfully to the Charter of the United Nations” and pave the way for a brighter future.

title: The Berlin Wall
text:
After WWII, the Allied Powers occupied Germany. They split the country into four occupation zones. Great Britain, France, and the United States organized the areas they occupied into West Germany, a democratic nation. The Soviet Union, however, installed a communist government in East Germany. The capital city, Berlin, was divided in half. Although Berlin was within East German territory, West Berlin belonged to West Germany.

Many people were unhappy with the economic and political conditions in East Germany. From 1949 to 1961, millions of East German citizens immigrated to West Germany. The leader of the Soviet Union, Nikita Khrushchev, did not want people to leave East Germany. He also feared that democratic values would spread throughout the country. To prevent those things from happening, the East German government closed the border it shared with West Germany on Aug. 13, 1961, and began construction of the Berlin Wall. The wall was built to surround West Berlin and prevent East Germans from fleeing the country.

The Berlin Wall took important freedoms away from East Germans. Leaving the country was made illegal. People who opposed the communist government could not escape punishment. The citizens of East Germany did not have access to news or technological innovations, such as personal computers, video games, and the internet. The Berlin Wall became a symbol of the Iron Curtain, dividing the communist East and democratic West.

title: German Reunification
text:
Following World War II, many countries around the world spent years locked in the Cold War. For decades, the democratic nations fought to spread the ideals and beliefs of democracy. The Soviet Union wanted to expand communism. Throughout the Cold War, the Soviet Union seemed strong but was slowly weakening. The cost of confronting the United States around the world was taking its toll. The Soviet Union provided economic assistance to communist forces in conflicts like the Korean War and the Vietnam War. However, their economy could not keep up with the demands of the Cold War.

The Soviet Union spent so much money on its military that the rest of its economy suffered. The people lacked money for food and other basic needs. Starvation became a harsh reality in the Soviet Union. The people began speaking out against the communist system. It was not providing the strong economy that the people hoped for. Movements supporting democracy and independence began in the many Soviet republics that belonged to the Soviet Union.

When Mikhail Gorbachev came to power in 1985, the Soviet Union began to loosen its grip on its empire. In 1986, Gorbachev enacted the policy of "glasnost" in the Soviet Union. This policy created political reforms. The Communist Party, the only political party in Soviet countries, allowed new parties to form. Freedom of the press was increased, and other political parties could participate in elections. The next year, Gorbachev enacted the "perestroika" plan. Perestroika relaxed restrictions on trade and the economy. Farmers and manufacturers were allowed to make choices about what to produce, how much to produce, and what prices to charge.

East Germans, still divided from West Germany, wanted the same changes in their country. They began to protest for change. Soon, high-ranking officials also wanted to see reform in East Germany. The conflict broke the East German communist party. Some countries in the Soviet Union began to request their independence as early as 1989. From June to September 1989, communist governments fell in Hungary, Poland, Czechoslovakia, Bulgaria, and Romania.

Many countries in Eastern Europe began to open their borders. In East Germany, thousands of East Germans flocked to the surrounding countries. In East and West Berlin, the borders were opened ahead of schedule due to one man’s confused answers to the press. East German officials had planned a lengthy process in order for its citizens to visit West Berlin. However, Günter Schabowski, an East German politician, read a statement and, in the confusion of questions, indicated that the borders would open “immediately.”

When the German people heard this, thousands from both sides of Berlin showed up at border checkpoints. In the chaos, the guards eventually let them through. With an atmosphere of celebration, people began to cross, climb, and even demolish the Berlin Wall. The push for change won in the end. The Berlin Wall was finally opened on Nov. 9, 1989. Around the rest of East and West Germany, people on both sides flocked to the borders to reunite with family and friends.

For the first time in nearly 30 years, the citizens of Germany were free to travel between the East and West. Families were reunited, travel barriers were removed, and the city of Berlin was unified. The citizens of Berlin were overjoyed, but they had to find new ways to live together in harmony and create a new culture. The reunification of Germany one year later and the resulting reforms in its government and economy were some of the factors that led to the collapse of the Soviet Union in the early 1990s.

title: Fall of the Soviet Union
text:
During the 1980s, the Soviet Union faced serious internal problems. Power struggles broke out among leaders, and growing tension spread across the empire. To fix these problems, Mikhail Gorbachev was elected General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1985. This position made him the leader of the entire Soviet Union. Unlike previous Soviet leaders, who ruled with strict control, Gorbachev took a different approach. He believed the Soviet Union would work better without communist rule, and his revolutionary ideas transformed both the Soviet Union and the entire world.

After taking office in 1985, Gorbachev introduced two major plans to move the Soviet Union away from communism and create social change. His first plan was called "glasnost," a Russian word meaning "transparency" or "openness." Through glasnost, the government expanded citizens' rights in ways that would have been unthinkable under previous leaders. People gained the right to express their opinions freely and access more information about their government and the world. Freedom of the press also expanded, allowing newspapers and television to report more honestly about problems in Soviet society. These changes represented a dramatic break from the secretive, controlling government of previous decades.

Gorbachev's second major plan was called "perestroika," which means "restructuring" in Russian. This plan encouraged the development of free-market systems in the Soviet Union, allowing some private businesses to operate alongside government-controlled industries. Perestroika also promoted democratic elections for various government positions, giving citizens a voice in choosing their leaders for the first time. However, these reforms had an unintended consequence. As citizens gained more freedom and economic control shifted away from the central government, the power holding the Soviet Union together began to weaken.

The changes proved too much for the old system to handle. On December 25, 1991, the Soviet Union officially collapsed. Overnight, the world's political map changed completely. The Soviet Union no longer existed as a single nation. In its place stood Russia and several smaller independent countries that had once been part of the Soviet empire. As the largest country from the former Soviet Union, Russia retained much of the old union's military strength and economic resources, though it struggled with the communist systems it inherited. Boris Yeltsin was elected president of Russia, and the country began installing a new democratic government system.

The collapse of the Soviet Union meant the Cold War was officially over. However, many problems remained between Russia and other countries around the world, particularly the United States. The United States government, which had been the Soviet Union's primary opponent during the Cold War, took on the responsibility of helping Russia transition away from communism. One of America's biggest concerns was Russia's massive collection of nuclear weapons. During the Cold War, the Soviet Union had built up enormous stockpiles of nuclear arms that could destroy the world many times over.

To address the nuclear weapons problem, U.S. President George H.W. Bush met with President Yeltsin to discuss reducing Russia's nuclear arsenal. Together, they created the Cooperative Threat Reduction Program, which worked to decrease the number of nuclear weapons in Russia and build trust between the two former enemies. The United States also provided assistance to help Russia deal with widespread food shortages that resulted from the economic collapse following the end of communism.

Russia wasn't the only new country the world needed to recognize and work with after the Soviet collapse. Countries around the world officially recognized the independence of 12 new nations that had been part of the Soviet Union. The United States moved quickly to establish diplomatic relationships with these countries. In 1991, the U.S. created official relationships with some of the larger new nations, like Ukraine. The following year, in 1992, the United States established diplomatic ties with the remaining six nations, helping these countries join the international community as independent states.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: The history of Europe has been heavily influenced by the geography, political landscape, and economies of the continent. As empires rose and fell, changes occurred that impacted the continent's traditions, beliefs, and culture. These changes had both positive and negative effects on the people of Europe. Because the needs of the people change, the economies, governments, and cultures of Europe are ever-changing and evolving.

title: Earning an Income
text: People work in order to earn money to pay for their wants and needs. People can do many different kinds of jobs and work to earn money. The money that people receive for working is called income. People can do many things with their income. Most people use their income to meet their needs, including paying for housing, electricity, food to eat, and transportation. Medical services, like visiting the doctor or going to the dentist, also cost money. Some people choose to save a portion of their income for the future. People can also earn money to buy goods and services they want. People have many choices about how to save and spend their income.

title: Essential Question
text: What are the principles of personal money management and why are they important?

title: Types of Income
text:
People receive income in many different ways. The most common way that people earn an income is through wages, or an amount of money paid for every hour of work they complete. For example, a person working at a coffee shop might earn $12 for every hour that they work. If this person worked an eight-hour shift in a day, their wages for that day would be $96. When a person earns income through wages, the more hours they work, the more income they earn.

Another way that people may earn income is by working for a salary. A salary is a set amount of money paid to an individual for their work. An example of someone who is paid a salary is a teacher. Many teachers are paid a set amount of money each month or year to do their job. Usually, a person who earns a salary does not complete their work on a set schedule. A teacher may have to work longer hours, before or after school, to complete their job. Additionally, teachers still have to work during the summer, even while school is not in session. They work through the summer to prepare for the next school year.

Some people earn income through commissions. A commission is money that an employee makes when they sell something: typically a percentage of the sale. Some employees earn commission in addition to wages or a salary, while other employees work only on commission. When an employee earns a commission, they take a portion of the sale as their income.

A real estate agent is a good example of someone who earns income through commission. If an agent sells a house, they earn a commission based on the sale price of that house. For example, if a real estate agent earns a five percent commission on every house they sell and sell a house for $100,000, they would earn $5,000. This might sound like the best way to earn income, but earning income from commission can be very difficult. Each form of income has its positives and negatives.

Another way that people can earn income is through rent. Rent is a fee paid by someone to use another person’s property. The most common thing that people pay rent for is housing. If someone is not able or does not want to buy housing, they might pay someone rent to live in a house or apartment they own. Renting is not just for housing, though. People rent many other types of property. Automobiles and tools are other examples of property that someone might rent. Some people purchase property for the purpose of renting it to others. For example, a person might already have a home but purchase another one to rent to others. The rent they receive for the rental house is a form of income. That income might help pay for the property or enable the person to purchase more property.

Hourly employees earn more income the more hours that they work. They might even have an opportunity to earn extra pay, or overtime, for hours they work beyond their work schedule. Hourly wages, however, might not be as secure as other forms of income. A business might limit the number of hours a person works based on the number of customers who come into their store or other factors.

Individuals earning a salary receive a set amount of income every month. This can be very appealing to some. However, an individual earning a salary might have to work many hours beyond their regular work day to complete the job. For those working on commission, their income depends on the amount of commission that can be earned, and they might earn more income than most. This income is not guaranteed like a salary, though. In many cases, if an individual working on commission does not sell their product or service, they do not receive income.

Regardless of how people earn an income, each person performs an important role in their community.

title: Creating a Budget
text:
A budget is a plan for how to spend money wisely. A budget shows how much money you have and how you're going to use it. When planning a budget, try to balance your income, or the money you earn, and your expenses, or the money you spend. People can make a budget for each week, month, or even a year. To make a budget, people should think about how much money they will earn for the time period of the budget. Then, they must think about things they will need to spend money on. Most people include the money they will spend on housing, clothing, food, and transportation.

People must also think about the money they will spend on things they want, including entertainment, dining out, vacations, etc. A good budget will also note how much money someone plans to save. Saving money is important. People need to be prepared to pay for things they might need in the future. Using a budget helps people think about what they need and want to do with their money. It also helps prevent someone from spending more than they have. A budget helps people plan for the future. By sticking to a budget, they will make more responsible money choices.

title: Reasons for and Benefits of Saving Money
text:
All income a person earns is either spent or saved. It is important to make good financial choices. Creating a budget, or spending plan, and making sure to save some income is important for a person's future. There are some goods and services that people must spend money on, like food, clothing, housing, and taxes. However, choosing how much money to spend on some of these items, like the kind of food or clothing to buy, will impact how much income is left to save for the future.

One way to save money for the future is to create a savings goal. For example, imagine there is a new skateboard or piece of sports equipment that you want but don’t have the money now to pay for. A savings goal can help you identify how much money you need to save over time to be able to afford it. Some people save their money in a bank or credit union and earn interest. Interest is the amount of money a lender or financial institution charges for lending out their money. In that case, you are lending money to the bank, and the bank is paying you.

Another way that people save their money is by investing in the stock market. A stock market is a large group of companies that sell shares to investors. Shares are like a small part of a company. So, if you are a stockholder (also called a shareholder) in a toy company, you own a small part of that company. Companies sell stocks to raise money. They might need to build a new factory, hire more people, or design a new product. They could borrow the money, but they would have to pay interest, and they'd have to pay back the money by a certain date. Instead, they allow people to buy a small part of their company.

Stockholders make money when the company makes money, but they can also lose it if the company does not do well. Being a stockholder means you share both the profits and the risks. People buy stocks hoping that a company will be successful and that their stocks will be worth more over time. If someone buys stock in different companies and leaves their money in the stock market for a long time, they can often earn more than they would in a savings account in a bank. However, sometimes, the stock market goes down, and investors lose money if the company loses profits or goes out of business.

Using a money market account is another great step in long-term financial planning and saving money. A money market account is an account that a person deposits money into that has a high interest rate. This means that it will earn more money over time than a savings account. A money market account also allows a person to write checks or have a debit card.

title: Uses and Costs of Credit
text:
People can pay for their wants or needs in many ways. Besides using cash or a check, people can also use credit. Credit is obtaining goods or services now with the expectation to pay later. There are also many types of credit accounts a person can apply for. These types of credit accounts can have a variety of purposes.

Credit cards allow a person to go into debt to purchase their wants and needs. Debt is money that one person owes another. When someone borrows money from a bank, that money must be paid back. An interest fee is charged for borrowing the money. Individuals, businesses, and governments can have debt. Many people go into debt to pay for a house, a car, or college. However, people who aren’t careful with their money can also go into debt for everyday items. This includes clothes, entertainment, and food. One way to stay out of debt is to save money for large purchases. Additionally, try not to spend more than you earn. To get rid of debt, begin paying it off a little at a time until the debt is gone.

Managing Credit

Learning how to manage credit and debt is a great way to keep someone's finances in a positive place and can lead to many helpful benefits.

Credit Scores

Checking someone’s credit score is an example of looking at their financial well-being. A credit score is a record that builds up a person’s credit history, or how responsible a person is in paying back their debts. Often, people must show their credit score when they make a large purchase, such as buying a car or a house. Credit bureaus keep track of people’s credit scores. There are three major credit bureaus that people use in the U.S. today: Equifax®, Experian®, and TransUnion®.

Having a high credit score helps people get approved for mortgages, car payments, other credit cards, and low-interest loans. Having a good credit history can also be a deciding factor in applying for apartments or getting a new job. Building a good credit history can be done by paying items off, paying on time, and not having large balances.

Payment History

Part of a person’s credit score is based on their payment history. A person’s payment history makes up about 298 points of the 850 points of credit a person can achieve. If late payments occur or if a person skips a payment, their credit score is affected. Payment history can go as far back as 7–10 years.

The Amount You Owe

Another part of a person’s credit score involves looking at how much they have on their credit accounts. This means looking at the amount of credit that has been used and the amount that is still available. Maxing out credit cards can have a negative impact on a person’s credit. In contrast, if a person uses their credit cards but pays them off regularly, it can positively impact their credit score.

Length of Credit History

Being able to show a credit account's use and history will also help a person increase their credit score. Credit history shows the oldest account opened with a person’s credit. It also shows the newest account and how regularly the accounts have been used and paid off.

New Credit

Opening up many new credit accounts all at once or applying for multiple loans at one time can have a negative impact on a person’s credit score. However, a person can create a positive credit history when they open up one account at one time and pay it off regularly. This can give a person a positive new credit history.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
There are many ways for people to earn income. People can earn hourly wages, a salary, commission, make investments, or rent property. A person’s income supports their needs and wants. Creating a balanced budget to determine how much can be spent on needs and wants is important. Saving is also important in creating a budget and planning for the future. There are different ways that people can save their money or income to be prepared for emergencies or future expenses.

One of the best ways a person can achieve what they want is by setting a goal. Just like fitness goals, people have to set goals about spending and saving to make sure their budget, credit, spending, and saving habits are healthy. Setting financial goals means creating a plan to reach those goals.

title: Test
text:
A long time ago, there was a clever man named Gerardus Mercator. He loved to learn. He went to a special school where he studied geography. He learned about many new places.

Gerardus became very good at writing and at drawing. He drew maps of different places around the world. His maps showed mountains, rivers, and cities.

People loved Gerardus's maps because they helped them find their way. His maps were so important. Today, many, many years later, mapmakers still use his ideas. These ideas help us explore and understand the big world around us!

title: Impact of Colonization on Aboriginal People: Health
text:
English colonization also had a large impact on the health of the Aboriginal people of Australia. As more English and eventually European and Asian settlers immigrated to Australia, resources were taken from the Aboriginal people and given to the new settlers. The land was also given to immigrants for settlement. This created a scarcity of resources for the Aboriginal Australians. Many Aboriginal people suffered from malnutrition. Others died from starvation.

English, European, and Asian settlers brought many diseases with them to Australia. These diseases included smallpox, scarlet fever, measles, and influenza. These diseases were very contagious and often deadly. Aboriginal Australians had no immunity to these diseases. They spread very quickly and easily in Aboriginal communities. Thousands of Aboriginal Australians died from these diseases, particularly smallpox. The diseases ravaged the population from the arrival of the first English settlers through the early 1900s. Scientists developed a smallpox vaccine in the mid-1900s that helped stop the spread of the disease.

Today, many Aboriginal Australians still suffer from more health issues than other ethnic groups in Australia. Aboriginal people who live on reservations often do not have easy access to affordable healthcare. Data has been collected by health organizations and government agencies in Australia. It shows that Aboriginal people suffer from disabilities and chronic and terminal illnesses at a higher rate than people living in non-Aboriginal communities. This has led to a lower life expectancy among Aboriginal groups.
