title: Data, Data, Everywhere
text:
The census counts people and collects information about each person who is counted.

Let's look at the questions on the 2020 Census:

Who lives in the household?

How are they related to each other?

Age, sex, and race?

Own or rent the house?

Phone number?

The Census of 1880 had 26 questions. Questions from 1880 asked for the number of people living in the dwelling as well as their ages, sexes, and races. Other questions included whether the people in the dwelling could read and write. They answered what country they were born in. They also wrote their occupations. In 1880, the most populated city was New York City. San Francisco was ranked ninth in population.

The actual counting of people was done by individuals. This process sometimes took years to finish. In 1890, counting everyone was done using an electronic punch card system. A modern computer was first used in 1950. Today, the use of computers makes the census count go faster. Computers also help share the information collected in tables, charts, and maps.

A line graph shows the increase or decrease of something over time.

A bar graph is used to compare things between different groups.

A pie chart is another method of displaying information. A pie chart is round. It represents the total number of things counted. The slices show parts of the totals. The larger the slice, the greater the number. The smaller the slice, the smaller the number.

A map can also display data. A map can represent larger or smaller numbers by using different colors.

A table chart gives data in columns and rows. Each column and row is labeled with the type of information shown.

title: Introduction to Ethnic and Religious Groups of Southwest Asia
text:
Cultures and religions are unique to areas and regions around the world. The people in a specific geographic location often form ethnic groups that have a shared culture. Culture includes things like shared customs, art, beliefs, values, history, celebrations, cuisine, and social institutions passed down from generation to generation.

When studying history, it's important to understand the culture of different times and places. Sometimes, past cultural beliefs, ideas, and values may have been different from what is acceptable in modern society. By studying past cultures, we can gain insight into how some ideas change over time and how others stay the same.

Having a shared culture and religion is a common characteristic of ethnic groups. However, this is not always the case. Some members of a particular ethnic group may be a part of a different religious group. Religious groups share the same religious beliefs, practices, and ethics. Ethics refers to what is considered moral behavior, based on shared beliefs.

title: Essential Question
text: How have culture and religion influenced the development of Southwest Asia (the Middle East)?

title: Different Ethnic Groups of Southwest Asia: Kurds, Arabs, and Persians
text:
Many of the ethnic groups in the world are mapped by region or country. However, not all ethnic groups can be assigned to a specific country. This is because a country's borders may change through war or treaties over time. Despite this, ethnicity and culture may remain constant.

Kurdish Culture

Many Kurdish people live in a specific region of Southwest Asia. They can be found primarily throughout eastern and southeastern Türkiye, northwestern Iran, northern Iraq, and northern Syria. Most Kurds speak a dialect of the Kurdish language. They also share a common ancestral background and culture. In the past, many Kurds had a nomadic culture of goat and sheep herding. In relation to Kurdish culture, nomadic refers to animal herders who move from place to place in a pattern for their livestock.

However, much of that changed after World War I, with the boundaries of countries being changed and enforced. While most Kurdish people practice Islam, there are some differences between religious groups based on the region.

Kurdish cuisine is an important part of the culture. With cultural roots in the nomadic herding of animals, many Kurdish dishes include rice, lamb, and chicken. Kurdish culture continues to be shared through food and hospitality today.

Arab Culture

There were over 456 million Arab people in the Arab world as of 2021. Arabic people speak a common language, Arabic, and have a shared culture. In many Arab communities, culture and religion are intertwined. Cultural norms and values are set by the practice of the Islamic religion. Most, but not all, Arab cultures practice Islam. Their religion is part of the structure of daily life and cultural identity. Strong family relationships and support are also an important part of Arab culture.

Hospitality toward guests is extremely important. Mealtimes are an important part of each day, as is common in many cultures throughout Southwest Asia. They are an opportunity to share culture. Arabic cuisine is served in a communal style, with shared plates. People often eat with their right hands and no utensils.

Iranian (Persian) Culture

Iranians live in the modern-day country of Iran. The country was called Persia by Western governments until 1935. In that year, Reza Shah Pahlavi, who was the monarch and ruler of Iran, requested other countries to use the name "Iran." The shah requested this to respect the culture and heritage of the area and its people. Many Iranians speak Farsi and practice the religion of Shia Islam. Iranian culture has cultural roots that go back to the sixth century B.C.E. Over the centuries, Iranian artistic culture has flourished. Iranian rugs, as well as pottery and calligraphy, are well-known throughout the world. Another important part of Iranian culture is its traditional food. Iranian culture uses distinct spices and flavors, such as saffron, pomegranate, dried limes, and rosewater.

title: Diversity of Religion
text: While Islam is the religion that is practiced in most cultures in Southwest Asia, it is not the only one. Three prevalent religions in this region are Islam, Christianity, and Judaism. While there is diversity in how followers of each of these religions practice their beliefs, there are also similarities. All three religions are monotheistic. This means they believe that there is only one god. While each of the religions is unique, they all have cultural ties to the people who practice them.

title: Islam
text:
Basic beliefs and practices of Islam include the belief in one god (Allah), the importance of prayer (Salah), fasting during Ramadan (Sawm), and acts of charity (Zakat). Islam also includes studying the life and teachings of the prophet Muhammad and the early Muslim community. Those who practice the religion of Islam are called Muslims. Muslims follow the Qur’an, which is the holy book of Islam. Muslims believe the Qur’an is the word of Allah, as revealed to the prophet Muhammad. It contains guidance on how to live a good and righteous life. Islam has ethical teachings, such as honesty, kindness, compassion, and justice. These values are integral to the lives of Muslims throughout the world.

There are five pillars, or essential practices, in the religion of Islam:

The first pillar is Shahada, which is the declaration of faith. It is the statement that there is no god but Allah and that Prophet Muhammad is his messenger.

The second pillar is Salah. Salah is observed by praying five times a day. Muslims believe in praying to Allah regularly and use specific prayers and movements during their prayers. There are five prayers: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha. The first prayer is read in the morning, and the last one is read at night.

The third pillar is Zakat. Zakat means to give to charity. Charity is giving a portion of one's earnings to help those in need. This is a way of showing gratitude and helping others in the community.

The fourth pillar is Sawm. Sawm is observed by fasting during the holy month of Ramadan. During this month, Muslims fast from dawn until sunset. Fasting involves not eating food or having anything to drink during daylight hours. This is considered a way to purify the soul and practice self-discipline.

The fifth pillar is Hajj. Hajj is a pilgrimage Muslims take to the city of Mecca in Saudi Arabia. It is an important journey that Muslims try to make at least once in their lifetime if they are physically and financially able. During Hajj, Muslims perform specific rituals and join together with other Muslims from all around the world.

There is much diversity among different cultural groups that practice Islam. There are two main branches of the religion of Islam. The groups that follow these branches are called Sunni Muslims and Shia Muslims. Both share the same core beliefs. These include belief in Allah and following the teachings of Prophet Muhammad. They also have many similarities in their practices. These include praying, fasting, and performing the Hajj. However, there are some differences in the interpretations and practices of their religion.

title: Sunni Islam
text:
Sunni Islam is the largest branch of Islam. Sunni Muslims follow the teachings and practices of the prophet Muhammad. Sunni Muslims believe in one god, called Allah. They believe that Allah sent prophets to guide and teach people. This includes the prophet Muhammad. Sunni Muslims consider the prophet Muhammad to be the last and final prophet.

Sunni Muslims also have scholars and teachers who provide guidance on understanding the teachings of Islam. They teach about the life of the prophet Muhammad and the lessons he taught through stories and teachings passed down through generations. It's important to note that the Sunni practice of Islam has different schools of thought and interpretations. However, they all share the same core beliefs and practices, based on the Qur’an and the teachings of Muhammad.

title: Shia Islam
text:
Shia Islam is a smaller branch of Islam. Shia Muslims follow the teachings of the prophet Muhammad. Shia Muslims also believe in one god, called Allah. They also believe that Allah sent prophets to guide and teach people. This includes the prophet Muhammad. However, unlike Sunni Muslims, Shia Muslims also believe in the prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, Ali ibn Abi Talib, as his rightful successor.

The leadership of the Muslim community is known as the caliphate. Shia Muslims believe that the caliphate should have been passed down to the descendants of Ali. They consider Ali to be the first imam (leader) after the prophet Muhammad. They believe that the imams are chosen by Allah and have special knowledge and guidance. Shia Muslims have a different set of imams compared to Sunni Muslims. Shia Muslims also have their own books of traditions and interpretations of the Qur'an, called Hadiths. These Hadiths contain the sayings, actions, and approvals of the prophet Muhammad and the imams. Additionally, Shia Muslims have their own religious rituals and observances.

The religion of Islam and its branches have had a distinct influence on art, literature, and architecture throughout Southwest Asia and the world. Islamic art is known and appreciated for its intricate geometric patterns, calligraphy, and arabesque designs. These same geometric patterns can be found in Islamic architecture, pottery, textiles, and manuscripts. Islamic literature encompasses a rich tradition of poetry, storytelling, and philosophy. This literature includes the contributions of Islamic scholars and poets, such as Rumi. Islamic architecture has distinctive features. These include the use of domes, arches, and intricate decorative elements. Islamic architectural styles have had a significant impact on Western architecture. This influence was seen during the European Renaissance with the incorporation of Islamic motifs in the buildings and architecture in Spain.

title: Christianity
text:
Christianity is one of the world's major religions, with over two billion followers. The geographic origins of Christianity are found in Southwest Asia, particularly in the region of modern-day Israel. Christianity has several branches. Each has its own traditions and practices. Three of the major branches of Christianity include Roman Catholicism, Eastern Orthodoxy, and Protestantism. There are many different churches or denominations within these three branches. Religious denominations are organizations that have a particular set of beliefs and traditions. Some Christian denominations include Baptist, Greek Orthodox, Lutheran, Methodist, Presbyterian, and Russian Orthodox. However, there are many nondenominational Christian-based churches that don’t have established organizations.

Christianity originated in the Roman Empire in the first century C.E. It is based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, also called Jesus Christ. Jesus was raised as a Jew in Nazareth, a town about 90 miles north of Jerusalem in modern-day Israel. When he was about 30 years old, he began his ministry. He traveled throughout the region, teaching principles through the use of parables, or short, simple stories that teach a moral or spiritual lesson. Much of Christianity is based on Jesus's teachings on love, forgiveness, and the “Golden Rule”: treating others the way that you would want to be treated. These teachings have had a significant impact on Christian philosophy and ethics.

The Bible is the sacred text of Christianity. It is divided into two sections. The first is the Old Testament (Hebrew Bible). The Old Testament is a collection of religious texts that began as scriptures, or sacred writings, from the Jews. Called Hebrew Scriptures, they play a significant role in both Judaism and Christianity. The Old Testament outlines both the concept of God’s relationship with humans and religiously based belief systems.

The second section of the Bible is the New Testament, which is the life story of Jesus and his disciples, or followers. The New Testament contains multiple records of the life and teachings of Jesus Christ, the writings of his followers, and records of early Christian communities. The core, or fundamental, Christian beliefs includes the belief in one God, the Holy Trinity (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit), and the divinity of Jesus as a holy being. Christians believe in Jesus Christ as the savior of their faith. Christians regularly honor holidays of observance and prayer, including Christmas and Easter. Each is significant in its connection to the role of faith in the divinity of Jesus Christ.

Christianity has significantly impacted Western civilization. It is only one of the many factors that have shaped cultural heritage through art, literature, and architecture. Early Christian art primarily focused on symbolic representations and narrative scenes from the Bible. In the Renaissance period, works by artists like Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, and Raphael used biblical themes and Christian symbols. Christianity has had a distinct influence on the writings of different authors. Biblical stories, parables, and teachings have shaped literary works across centuries. Architecture through the ages has also been influenced by Christianity. Christian symbolism is used in churches. Church spires and designs and the images in stained glass windows are some examples. Each of these has been used to reflect Christian beliefs and provide a sense of spiritual awe.

title: Judaism
text:
Judaism is one of the oldest religions in the world. As with Christianity and Islam, followers of Judaism worship one god. According to the Hebrew texts of the Old Testament, an ancient prophet called Abraham entered into a covenant with God. The religions of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam all recognize Abraham as their first prophet. This is why they're called “Abrahamic religions.” Judaism is the oldest surviving monotheistic religion and dates back over 3,500 years. Rabbinical, or mainstream, Judaism began around the first century C.E. Today, Judaism is practiced throughout the world. It is particularly practiced in the region of modern-day Israel.

The Torah is the central religious book of Judaism. The Torah contains the first five books of the Hebrew Bible (also known as the Old Testament). Some Jews believe that the Torah was written by several authors over a long period of time. Others believe it was revealed by God to an ancient prophet called Moses. The Torah contains depictions of the origins of the world, humanity, and the Jewish people. It includes stories, such as the creation of the universe and other significant events. It also has a record of ancestors through the history of patriarchs and matriarchs. The Torah serves as a historical and cultural foundation for Jews. It provides a sense of identity, continuity, and connection to their ancestors and heritage.

The Torah contains numerous religious obligations and commitments, called mitzvot. The mitzvot guide Jewish ethics and practices. These religious commitments cover a wide range of areas. These include relationships, social justice, religious practices, and dietary restrictions. Observance of the mitzvot is seen as a way to practice Judaism and deepen one's relationship with God. The ethical teachings found within the Torah emphasize principles of justice, compassion, honesty, and kindness. This provides a moral framework for Jewish life. It also guides individuals in everyday conduct.

Another important guiding principle includes the importance of Shabbat (the Sabbath). This is the weekly day of rest and worship in Judaism. There are also important Jewish holidays and observances. These include the Passover (Pesach), Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year), Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement), and Hanukkah (Festival of Lights). There is also an important coming-of-age ritual for Jewish children. This is called the bar mitzvah or bat mitzvah. This ceremony happens when a child reaches the age of 12–13 years old. It marks when that child becomes a Jewish adult.

Judaism is a religious foundation for culture and identity within Jewish communities. Many Jewish communities share religious beliefs, historical foundations, celebrations, and values. However, there is much diversity within these communities. There are people who identify as Ashkenazi (having heritage from France and Germany), Sephardi (having heritage from Iberia, Spain, and the former Spanish Empire), Mizrahi (having Southwest Asian and North African heritage), and Ethiopian Jews. The diversity in Jewish cultures can also be attributed to their ethnic identities and religious beliefs. Many Jews throughout the world have a combination of cultural and religious practices.

Judaism has impacted literature, art, and architecture throughout the ages. Jewish literature has a rich tradition of storytelling, poetry, and philosophy. Many Jewish authors have used themes of Jewish identity, history, and spirituality in their writings. Some famous Jewish authors include Franz Kafka, Isaac Bashevis Singer, Saul Bellow, and Elie Wiesel. Jewish artists, such as the famous 20th-century painter Marc Chagall, depicted Jewish themes and symbols in their visual art and paintings. Musicians, like Leonard Bernstein and Gustav Mahler, have enriched classical music with their compositions and performances. Jewish actors and directors, such as Steven Spielberg and Dustin Hoffman, have left a lasting impact on the film industry. Jewish artistic style has also contributed to architecture. Jewish architect Erich Mendelsohn was known for his innovative modernist architectural designs.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Southwest Asia has been home to ancient civilizations and cultural traditions for thousands of years. These traditions and cultures have been passed down through generations, contributing to a rich cultural heritage. Religion has played a major role in this heritage. It has also brought change to the region.

The cultural heritage of Southwest Asia includes unique languages, literature, music, dances, cuisine, and traditional ethnic and regional practices. Southwest Asia is also the birthplace of major world religions. Some of these include Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. These religions have greatly impacted this region's history, society, and cultural development.

Political conflicts, religious differences, and social changes have posed challenges to the cultures of Southwest Asia. However, there have been many efforts by local communities, international organizations, and governments to protect and preserve cultural heritage sites and traditions. These sites and traditions are crucial for maintaining cultural continuity.

title: Influences on the New American Experiment
text:
The members of the Constitutional Convention were students of government. They studied types of government from history. Some of the governments and ideas they studied included the Iroquois Confederation, the Ancient Greeks, the Roman Empire, and the philosophies of the Enlightenment.

Native Americans

The various Native American nations had diversity in government. A strong central chief made decisions for the nations. This was like a monarchy in Europe. Authority rested with one person to make decisions for the people. The Iroquois Confederation had alliances with member nations. All the member nations worked together for the common good. The leadership of the Iroquois was in a council of equal votes from the chief of each member tribe. The council of leaders considered the good of the people when making decisions. This type of government was modeled in the Articles of Confederation.

Ancient Greeks

The Ancient Greeks, who lived 2,000 years before the Constitutional Convention, had a government of the people. Each free male citizen of the country voted when decisions were being made. This was called a direct democracy, meaning “ruled by the people.” There were three branches of the Ancient Greek government. One branch wrote the laws. Another branch was a council of representatives. The third branch was a court of justice with a jury to decide cases. The Ancient Greek system of direct democracy paved the way for representative democracies. This type of government was modeled in the colonial and state governments of America.

Ancient Romans

Fifteen hundred years before 1787, the Roman Empire had a government that changed and expanded to meet the needs of the people. It was called a republic. A republic has citizens elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf. Rome started the concept of elections to choose leaders. Roman government was made up of executive, legislative, and judicial branches. Each had various responsibilities. The Romans had great respect for the law. The law in a republic was written down and followed by the judiciary. Judges in the courts consulted the law and determined the consequences of breaking the law. This type of government was modeled in Parliament in Great Britain.

Philosophers of the Enlightenment

The new ideas of Enlightenment philosophers, such as Locke, Montesquieu, Rousseau, and Voltaire, suggested that there were different reasons for government. These philosophers believed that government is a creation of people to protect themselves. They also believed that the creation of law serves to protect the people. They were concerned that the laws and power of government can become overbearing and inhibit the rights of the people. This authority should be balanced with the people. This balance includes separate offices or departments with checks and balances to control each other. They advocated that elections decide the representatives and that active participation by the people was expected. The philosophers also believed that each person had inalienable rights. This was a new idea in 1787 because the governments in the world were controlling and limited the rights of their people.

The representatives at the Constitutional Convention of 1787 learned from all of these ideas. They created a government that protected the rights of the people by limiting the powers of those in authority. The founders used the experiences of the Iroquois, Ancient Greeks, Romans, English, and other governments. The men in Philadelphia debated, argued, and compromised to begin a new experiment in government.

A canyon is a deep valley with steep, rocky sides. Canyons are like river valleys. Most canyons are formed when rivers erode mountains or plateaus. Plateaus are landforms with flat tops that rise above the surrounding land. The Grand Canyon was formed as the Colorado River carved through the Colorado Plateau.

The Palo Duro Canyon is the second largest canyon in the United States. It is near Amarillo, Texas. It was formed over millions of years. Water from the Prairie Dog Town Fork Red River deepens the canyon as it erodes the canyon walls.

Weathering and erosion can do more than create canyons. Weathering created the Lighthouse hoodoo in Palo Duro Canyon. A hoodoo is a tall, thin tower of rock formed mostly by water.

Scientists used to think that the Colorado River was no longer eroding the sides of the Grand Canyon. However, current research suggests that the river is still cutting away at the canyon walls. Both the Grand Canyon and the Palo Duro Canyon will continue to change as water flows through them.

title: The Constitution of the United States of America
text:
The Constitution consists of the Preamble, seven articles, and 27 amendments. The preamble explains the purpose of the document. The seven articles lay out the three branches of government and the rules for each branch. The 27 amendments guarantee the rights of the people. The amendments have been added as the nation has grown. The amendments give clarity and specific rules to the government.

Article 1: The Legislative Branch

“All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives.”

Section 1: Congress is granted the power to make laws in two organized parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives.

Section 2: The House of Representatives is defined. The election of members is every two years. Each member must be at least 25 years old and a citizen of the United States for at least seven years.

The number of representatives will be determined by the population “... of free persons, including those bound to Service for a term of years [indentured] and excluding Indians not taxed, three fifths of other persons.” The country will be counted every 10 years in a census. If there is a vacancy from any state, the executive branch will call for an election. The House of Representatives will have the sole power of impeachment (to challenge and investigate a member of government).

Section 3: The Senate is defined. Each state will have two elected senators to Congress for a six-year term. Each senator must be at least 30 years old and a citizen of the United States for at least nine years. The vice president of the executive branch will be president of the Senate. The vice president may only vote to break a tie. The Senate will also elect a president to serve in the absence of the vice president. The Senate will have the sole power to try all impeachments. Impeachment will not extend to more than a removal from office in the government.

Section 4: Congress will meet at least once every year on the first Monday in December.

The remaining six sections define the rules and responsibilities of each group in the system of checks and balances. They help to keep power distributed across the branches of government. There are clear directions on what Congress is forbidden to do. Only Congress can raise and spend money. Congress is responsible for the Army, Navy, Marines, Air Force, and Coast Guard. The representatives of the people are in charge of the military. The final section closes with powers forbidden to the states.

Article 2: The Executive Branch

“The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America. He shall hold his Office during the Term of four Years, and, together with the Vice President, chosen for the same Term.”

Section 1: A person who is a natural-born citizen, at least 35 years old, and a resident of the United States for 14 years can work for the executive office. Once elected, the president shall take the following oath or affirmation: "I do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will faithfully execute the Office of President of the United States, and will to the best of my Ability, preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the United States."

Section 2: Sets up the president as the commander-in-chief of the armed forces. It further defines the powers within the office for hiring people for government posts with the advice and consent of the Senate.

Section 3: The president is required to give information on the state of the Union to Congress.

Section 4: "The President, Vice President, and all civil Officers of the United States shall be removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors."

Article 3: The Judicial Branch

“The judicial Power of the United States, shall be vested in one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish.”

As established under Article 2, the president will nominate a judge for the judicial branch. The nominee must then be confirmed through the Senate.

Section 2: The office of the judiciary will extend to all cases of law arising under the Constitution. It also covers the laws of the United States and all controversies between the state, citizens and states, and citizens and citizens.

Section 3: Treason against the United States is defined. Treason is giving aid and comfort to enemies or waging war against the United States.

title: Mountains
text:
A mountain is an area of land that is at least 1,968 feet taller than the land around it. Mountains have peaks at the top with sloping sides. They can have sharp or rounded shapes. Mountains are found on every continent and even under the ocean.

It takes millions of years for mountains to form. They are formed from movement of the Earth's crust. Mountains are shaped over time by weather. Rich minerals are found in the core of mountains. Mountain peaks are often covered in snow. The snow melts and sends water down the sides in streams, creeks, and brooks.

title: Natural Hazards
text: People choose to live where they can meet their needs. Sometimes those places also have hazards because of the environment. Hazards are dangers. Some areas of the world have a lot of earthquakes. Other areas often have hurricanes and flooding. There are other natural hazards too. Look at the images and make a list of the types of natural hazards.

title: Hurricanes
text: Hurricanes are strong storms that form over the ocean. These storms can cause heavy rain, high winds, and flooding. When hurricanes hit land, they can be devastating to cities and coasts. As a hurricane moves through an area, it can also produce thunderstorms and tornadoes. People who live in hurricane zones know how to prepare for these dangerous storms. They protect their homes by boarding up windows and using sandbags. Floodgates and dams can also be built. Sometimes, they must evacuate. This means they must leave their homes before the storm arrives.

title: Tornadoes
text: A tornado is a storm with high, rotating winds that forms over land. It often looks like a funnel. Tornadoes form very quickly. Sometimes, they give only a few minutes’ warning before they strike. People adapt to areas that have tornadoes by building shelters. Most towns have alarm systems to warn people about tornadoes. Digging underground shelters modifies the land.

title: Earthquakes
text: An earthquake occurs when part of the solid ground under Earth’s surface suddenly shifts. This causes waves of movement. Rocks and soil vibrate. This causes buildings and roads to shake. People who live in places where earthquakes often occur usually build their homes with wood. They also brace shelves on their walls and secure small objects in buildings. This prevents them from flying off if an earthquake occurs. They also use flexible material for gas pipelines so they do not break in an earthquake.

title: Floods
text: A flood is an overflow of water on ground that is normally dry. Some floods are caused by heavy rain, hurricanes, or rapidly thawing snow. Ice jams and broken dams can also cause flooding. People can drown in floods. Expensive property can also be destroyed. People adapt to areas that flood by building their homes on stilts. People near water bodies may build levees to prevent flooding. This modifies the landscape.

title: Blizzards
text: During cold winter months, warm air and cold air sometimes meet in the atmosphere. This can create high winds and snow. When the wind reaches a high speed, it becomes a blizzard. It is difficult to go outside in these conditions. Trees may fall. Powerlines may also go down. This is dangerous for people who get trapped without warmth or food. Falling trees and powerlines can damage property or hurt people. Snow tires are important tools during blizzards. Most people also own snow shovels and snow blowers. Roads can also be marked with hot melt marking paint. This helps drivers to stay in their lanes during a snowstorm.

Situated in the far north of Africa is the Atlas Mountains. The Atlas is the longest mountain range on the continent. The Atlas Mountains run across 1,600 miles of northern Africa, including Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia. Covering much of northern Africa, the Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world. It lies just south of the Atlas Mountains. A desert is a place that gets very little rainfall, less than 10 inches a year. Temperatures in the Sahara Desert regularly reach over 110 degrees Fahrenheit. The highest temperature ever recorded in the Sahara Desert was 136˚F. The Sahara Desert covers about 25 percent of the African continent. The land in the desert is covered mainly by sand or small rocks. People, animals, and plants in the Sahara have adapted to live in this region using very little water.

title: Multiple Perspectives
text:
When we see or read something, it's important to identify if it is fact or opinion. A fact is something that can be proven true through evidence. An opinion is a statement that expresses someone’s feelings or beliefs.

Everyone brings a unique perspective. Experiences and events may be interpreted differently by people with different cultural or individual perspectives. It's important to understand the perspectives of others. When we look at multiple perspectives, we can have a deeper understanding of what happened in the past. This helps us create the most accurate analysis of people and events in history.

When we study historical sources, it's important to be aware of multiple perspectives. Historians look for bias in sources. Bias means favoring one belief or opinion over others. Historians look for bias to separate the true meaning of the information from the author’s perspective.

title: Innovations
text:
Tools

Native American tribes created and used many tools before Europeans arrived in North America. Various tools were used for hunting, fishing, farming, and in everyday life. Native American tools were made from stone, wood, animal bones and antlers, and shells. They created drills and chisels to build homes, canoes, and weapons. Sewing needles were made of animal bone. They used them to sew clothing, shoes, and fishing nets. Many tribes also had specific tools for grinding corn, nuts, and other plants for eating and medicinal purposes.

Agriculture

Native farmers studied wild plants and learned which foods would grow well in certain areas. They also learned how to create new plants from old ones. Great Lakes peoples cultivated wild rice. The Iroquois grew crops in small mounds called milpas to prevent soil erosion. Tribes of the Northeast used fish to fertilize their crops. This allowed them to grow in sandy soil. Many native cultures created irrigation systems to water their crops. They built canals, pipelines, reservoirs, and dams to bring water from distant sources to their farms.

Medicine

Native peoples found many ways to use plants as medicine. Native Americans knew which plants and herbs would cure common ailments, such as fever, pain, burns, and wounds. Black willow bark was brewed into a tea and consumed to prevent pain. Sage was used to cure stomach issues and skin rashes. Some tribes used milkweed plants to treat sore throats and prevent coughing.

Transportation

Before the arrival of Europeans, water was the main mode of transportation for Native Americans. Waterways were vital to the movement of people and goods. American Indians have used canoes for thousands of years. Their invention made transportation, trading, and fishing much easier. Tribes used materials from the environment they lived in to make canoes. Bark canoes were very popular because they were lightweight. They could also be made from materials in forested areas. Sometimes, people used animal skins to wrap around the stick frames of their canoes. In the northeastern United States, birch bark was very popular.

Canoes were also made by digging out the inside of large logs. This was long, hard work. The final canoe, called a dugout, was very heavy. The Native Americans of the Pacific Coast made dugout canoes from cedar. Cedar is wood that naturally resists water and rot. People burned the inside of a log. Then they used sharp-edged rocks or shells to scrape out the burned part. Another interesting canoe was made with planks that were carefully split from a log and sewn together with strands of animal hide. The cracks between the planks were filled with a substance like tar made from plant materials and mud. A swift canoe could take travelers 150 miles or more after a long, hard day of paddling!

title: Life in the Middle Passage
text:
In the first 300 years after Columbus reached the Americas, ships that crossed the Atlantic almost always came from Europe. However, most didn’t sail straight from Europe to the Americas. The sea currents and wind directions made sailing south toward Africa easier and faster than sailing directly west across the Atlantic. This route presented opportunities for trade by staying near the continents. European traders found a market with the nations in West Africa.

This voyage from Europe to Africa was called the Outward Passage. Ships carried tools, weapons, cloth, and other goods to Africa. Merchants and soldiers would pressure African leaders to trade those goods for people who had been captured in wars or kidnapped.

People were imprisoned and held as products to be traded. The European traders did not care about the welfare of the people they considered “cargo.” These men, women, and children were put in dark, dank ships. The living conditions were inhumane. The traders who held the Africans against their will were transporting them to be sold to new owners in the West Indies and American colonies. The voyage from Africa to the colonies in the Western Hemisphere was called “the Middle Passage.”

No words can describe the terror and hopelessness felt by the African men, women, and children who experienced the Middle Passage. Nothing can justify the choices the European traders and colonists made in the past that impacted so many lives. No words can be expressed for those who survived, except to learn of their suffering and share in their sorrows.

title: Maurice Rabb Jr.
text: Maurice Rabb Jr. was born in Shelbyville, Kentucky, in 1932. He is known for his work as an ophthalmologist. An ophthalmologist is a doctor who specializes in eye care. These doctors usually diagnose and treat specific vision conditions. Rabb became one of the first African American students to attend the University of Louisville. He graduated in 1958. He completed a residency medical training at the University of Illinois Eye and Ear Infirmary. He was the first African American to become a chief resident there. Later, he started his own medical practice in Chicago. He focused his work on cornea and retinal vascular diseases. Maurice Rabb Jr. was a very respected ophthalmologist. An award is given each year to a student in the field, called the Rabb-Venable Ophthalmology Award for Outstanding Research.

title: Coordinate and Alphanumeric Grids
text:
Geographers use many tools to determine location on maps. Coordinates help geographers determine the absolute location of a place. Coordinates can help you find a place’s location on a map. A coordinate grid uses lines of latitude and longitude to locate places on a map. The grid lines indicate where a place is located. You can use the coordinate grid on the map below to determine locations of places in the United States. What lines of latitude and longitude intersect, or cross, in Kentucky?

Geographers also use alphanumeric grids to determine location. An alphanumeric grid helps you describe the absolute location on a map using grid lines with letters and numbers. Like a map that includes a coordinate grid, lines on an alphanumeric grid map form small squares. These squares can be identified using coordinates that contain one letter and one number. When using an alphanumeric grid, you should determine the letter, then the number of the coordinate. For example, the capital of Kentucky is located in the square F, 15.

title: Getting Water in Africa
text:
Africa is the second-driest continent in the world, after Australia. Almost 1.2 billion people live there, however, and they need water to drink. There are different ways to obtain water in rural parts of Africa.

A spring is a place where groundwater comes up to the surface. Building a casement onto a spring can protect the water from contamination. Then a pipe can bring the water to a pump, where people can fill their water containers.

In places where there is a lot of rain, catchment tanks gather water from rainstorms and store it so that people can have water during dry parts of the year.

Wells can be drilled down to the groundwater and attached to a pump, where people can fill their water containers.

In places where there isn’t much rainfall, sand dams can be built across river beds that only fill with water during rainstorms. Most of the water flows over the top of the dam, but the dam catches sand. The sand can store a lot of water. When the sand reaches the top of the dam, people can use a pump or dig a hole in the sand to get water.

title: Trapped in the Antarctic
text:
In 1896, Adrien de Gerlache was preparing for a scientific expedition to Antarctica. He had a lot to do, including finding a ship that could survive hitting icebergs. But his biggest problem was finding the ship’s crew. He was from Belgium, which has very little coastline, so not very many people in his country knew how to sail. He realized that he would need people from other countries to staff his ship.

He hired Roald Amundsen, an explorer from Norway. He found scientists from Poland and Romania. He hired Frederick Cook as the ship’s doctor. Cook was from the United States, and he had already explored the Arctic region.

At first, the expedition was difficult. The men on board spoke different languages and had a hard time understanding each other. Then their ship got caught in Antarctic sea ice for almost a full year. They had to rely on one another to survive.

They worked hard to free their ship from the ice and finally made it back to Europe. Together, they had mapped out unknown parts of Antarctica’s coastline. They had gathered many scientific specimens that provided important information about the ocean and climate.

This international team was inspirational in many ways. Decades later, the Antarctic Treaty was signed by the 12 countries that had active scientists in and around the area. The countries agreed that no one would lay claim to Antarctica or fight over it. The continent would be used only for scientific purposes, and everyone would have access to it. Antarctica is a place where scientists from all nations can work together.

title: Transporting Goods in Colonial Times
text:
During colonial times in Kentucky, there was a lot of land but few roads. People traveled on trails, which were not paved. Even the streets of the largest cities were usually unpaved. When people wanted to go somewhere new, they often had to make new trails themselves, especially if they wanted to bring wagons along.

The main vehicle used for moving goods was the Conestoga wagon. These wagons could carry several tons of goods, but they were so big that it took eight horses or a dozen oxen to pull one wagon. A loaded wagon could travel about 15 miles a day. Transporting goods over land was slow and difficult.

Traveling on rivers was easier and more popular. If you had a boat or a barge, the river would move your goods for you. Kentucky has many rivers. The Ohio River runs along most of Kentucky’s northern border. The Kentucky River runs through the eastern half of the state. Rivers provided an important method of transporting goods during colonial times.

title: Transporting Goods in Modern Times
text:
Today, people in Kentucky have many ways to travel and transport goods. Instead of limited trails, people can travel on roads and railroads. Kentucky has more than 62,000 miles of roads and 2,600 miles of railroads. The roads and railroads make it much easier to transport goods than in colonial times.

Rivers are still an important part of moving goods in Kentucky. In fact, the largest inland port in the United States is the Port of Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky. The most common cargo transported by both railroads and rivers in Kentucky is coal.

title: Introduction
text: The Earth is a wondrous place with a variety of continents, climates, and landscapes. One of the most diverse continents on Earth is Africa. A continent is a large, continuous area of land. Seven continents make up the surface of the Earth, and Africa is the second-largest in the world. The only continent larger than Africa is the continent of Asia. North America is the third-largest continent in the world. North America includes the United States, Canada, Mexico, Greenland, and the many islands in the Caribbean Sea. To put the size of the continent of Africa into perspective, all of the land in the state of Georgia could fit inside the land area of Africa almost 200 times.

title: Essential Question
text: What effect does Africa’s geography and environment have on the way people live and work?

title: Location
text:
Africa is located between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. It is over 4,000 miles east of the state of Georgia. Due to its location, Africa is divided almost in half by the Equator. Its size makes Africa’s location on the globe unique. The Prime Meridian, Tropic of Capricorn, Tropic of Cancer, and the Equator all run through the continent of Africa.

The northernmost countries in Africa and the southernmost countries experience the seasons at different times of the year. For example, summer in the north, like in Tunisia, occurs between June and September. Conversely, summer in the south, like in South Africa, occurs between December and March every year. These seasonal differences occur because the northern half of Africa is north of the Equator, and the southern half is south of the Equator.

title: Features
text:
With over 11 million square miles of land, it is easy to understand that Africa has many climates and landscapes. Africa has a very diverse geographic landscape with mountains, deserts, vast jungles, and grasslands. Climate is the average weather in an area over a long period of time. Climates in Africa range from very hot and dry (over 100 degrees Fahrenheit during the day) to very tropical and rainy. Some areas of Africa get over six feet of rain during the year.

As a large continent, Africa has 54 independent countries. The population of all of Africa totals more than 1.4 billion people. Currently, the people living on the continent of Africa make up close to one-fifth of the world’s population. People live in almost every region on the continent. Most live near places with access to water. Others live in some of the driest regions as well.

title: The Sahara
text:
Situated in the far north of Africa are the Atlas Mountains. The Atlas is the longest mountain range on the continent. The Atlas Mountains run across 1,600 miles of northern Africa, including the countries of Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia.

Covering much of northern Africa, the Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world. It lies just south of the Atlas Mountains. A desert is a place that gets very little rainfall: less than 10 inches a year. Temperatures in the Sahara regularly reach over 110 degrees Fahrenheit. The highest temperature ever recorded in the Sahara was 136 degrees Fahrenheit. The Sahara covers about 25 percent of the African continent. The land in the desert is covered mainly by sand or small rocks. People, animals, and plants in the Sahara have adapted to live in this region using very little water.

title: The Nile River
text: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world. It stretches 4,100 miles long and flows through East Africa from Lake Victoria to the Mediterranean Sea. That is almost the same as the distance from Georgia to the northern coast of Africa. Egypt is one of the countries in the Sahara Desert where millions of people live because the Nile provides fresh water for their needs. Cairo, Egypt, is one of the largest cities in the world and is located along the Nile.

title: The Sahel
text:
To the south of the Sahara is a region called the Sahel. The Sahel stretches from west to east across the African continent. The Sahel has a semiarid climate. This means it has more water than a desert but is still very dry. Some locations in the Sahel receive about 20 inches of rain every year. Plants and vegetation grow during the rainy season in the Sahel. The Niger [nai-jer] River flows through the Sahel in West Africa. Having access to water makes it easier for people to live in the Sahel than in the Sahara. People in the Sahel must still conserve water since the rainy season lasts only 4–6 months. The rest of the year, the Sahel receives very little, if any, rainfall.

Cities in the Sahel region have been important for travel and trade in Africa. People have traveled through the Sahel to move between eastern, central, and western Africa. The Sahel was used like a highway because the weather there was more tolerable than the Sahara to the north and the rainforests to the south. Through trade and social connections, the Sahel has served as a link between the cultures of northern African peoples and the larger populations of western and central Africa. People worldwide have traveled and traded their goods and ideas across the Sahel for thousands of years.

title: The Savanna
text:
Africa is often characterized by vast grassland areas called savannas. A savanna is a grassland with thick, tall grass, scattered trees, and a diverse group of animals. Animals such as lions, giraffes, and zebras can be found in savannas. The savannas of Africa begin south of the tropical rainforests. Savannas cover almost half of the continent of Africa, almost to the southern coast. The climate of the savanna regions varies from tropical to subtropical. In these regions, temperatures are typically warm, and rainfall is abundant. Most African people live in the savanna regions, where resources are more readily available than in other regions.

Africa’s largest lake and tallest mountain are both located in the savanna of East Africa. Lake Victoria is the second-largest freshwater lake in the world. Lake Victoria is one of the main sources of the Nile. Mount Kilimanjaro is the largest freestanding mountain in the world. A freestanding mountain is not part of a mountain range. Mount Kilimanjaro is an incredible sight, rising over 19,000 feet above the savanna grasses.

title: The Great Rift Valley
text: On the African continent, the Great Rift Valley begins in the deserts of the north and continues for 4,000 miles to the country of Mozambique in the south. Over 40 million years ago, two tectonic plates in eastern Africa separated. The movement of these plates caused a deep divide in the land. It formed the geographic feature called the Great Rift Valley. Astronauts have said that it is the most obvious physical detail on Earth visible from space. The Great Rift Valley has tall mountains and deep lakes. Humans have lived in the Great Rift Valley for at least 400,000 years. Anthropologists and other scientists have learned a lot about the history of people and animals by studying the fossils found in the Great Rift Valley. Fossils of some of the earliest humans have been found in this area of Africa.

title: The Kalahari
text: The Kalahari stretches across the southwestern region of Africa. Though it is often called the Kalahari Desert, this area is technically not a desert. It is more like the Sahel. This region of the continent is hot and sandy in many places. However, the Kalahari receives more rainfall than the Sahara. The Kalahari’s climate is considered semiarid. The rainy season of the Kalahari allows different plants to grow there. The growth of plants attracts diverse animals, such as African lions, cheetahs, wild dogs, and hyenas.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Africa is a beautiful and diverse continent. People and animals have adapted over hundreds of thousands of years to live in most regions of the continent. People in African countries represent unique and ancient cultures. Today, African countries face many challenges in keeping their environment strong and healthy. These challenges include maintaining good farmland and ensuring people have access to health care and clean drinking water. Through technology and the global community's support, progress is being made to ensure all Africans get the resources they need to survive.

title: Introduction
text: In the early 20th century, China faced political turmoil, social unrest, and foreign invasion. The continuity of thousands of years of Imperial Chinese rule through emperors was coming to an end. Conflicts and wars in the 1800s with Japan, Great Britain, and other countries weakened China's imperial power. The Xinhai Revolution in 1911 was a significant turning point in China’s history. It led to the overthrow of the Qing (Manchu) Dynasty. The revolution caused the end of over 2,000 years of imperial rule in China. Led by people such as Sun Yat-sen, the revolutionaries aimed to establish a republican government based on democratic principles. In 1912, the last emperor abdicated his throne. Abdication is when a leader gives up their position. This officially marked the change to new government systems in China. As Imperial rule ended, China faced many problems, like poverty and political instability, in forming a new government. Many in China wanted a new system of government in which people would have more control over their lives.

title: Essential Question
text: How have economic and government systems influenced the development of China and India?

title: Mao Zedong
text:
Mao Zedong, also known as Chairman Mao, was a Chinese communist leader who lived from 1893 to 1976. He played a major role in shaping China's history and is considered one of the most influential figures of the 20th century. Mao was born in 1893 in a rural Chinese village. His parents were farmers. Mao fought against the last Emperor of China in the Xinhai Revolution of 1911, which led him to study communism in college. Communism is a form of government and an economic system in which people share all of society's goods, services, and structures. In communist societies, everyone is supposed to share in the wealth that is created. In 1921, Mao officially joined the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). He was one of the earliest members. Mao emerged as an important figure during the Chinese Communist Revolution. The goal of the revolution was to overthrow the new government, which was controlled by the Nationalist Party. The communists, led by Mao, eventually won the civil war in 1949 and established a communist government. This new government was named the People’s Republic of China, and Mao was named its leader, or chairman.

As China’s new leader, Mao introduced communist policies and a new collectivist social structure throughout the country. He aimed to transform China into a modern and equal society through communism. Mao believed that the working class and peasants, who were the majority of the population, should be the driving force behind the revolution. He promoted collectivization, or sharing, of land and resources. This meant the government owned the land and shared it among the people. This policy was supposed to ensure fairness and equality for all Chinese citizens.

title: The Great Leap Forward
text:
One of Mao's most ambitious policies was the Great Leap Forward, which was the focus of the Chinese government from 1958 to 1962. This policy was enacted to transform and increase China's economy and society quickly. The Great Leap Forward, as a government policy, had two main objectives: increasing agricultural production and rapid industrialization. Farmers were introduced to communal living and "backyard furnaces” to increase steel production. In the communal system of living and farming, 20–40 families lived and worked together to organize labor, eliminate waste and inefficiency, and increase production. The government confiscated or took over people’s private property within the communal system. This also included land, farm buildings, tools, private homes, and livestock. In addition, people were encouraged to make small steel furnaces on the collective lands to produce iron and steel to increase industrialization. However, this led to many problems. People who made these furnaces were not trained in proper steel production techniques. As a result, the quality of the steel produced was generally poor. Also, resources that could have been used for farming were diverted.

There were serious consequences of the Great Leap Forward. Mismanagement of resources to encourage “backyard” steel production and the inefficiencies of the commune system led to a decline in agricultural output. Natural disasters like floods and droughts also resulted in widespread famine and food shortages. Millions of people lost their lives due to starvation and related diseases. The Great Leap Forward taught many valuable lessons to the Chinese government, including the significance of agriculture as a foundation for its economic structure.

By the early 1960s, the Great Leap Forward was changed, and eventually, the policies were stopped. In 1962, the Chinese government shifted its focus back to agriculture and implemented policies to improve food production. Private property was returned to people, and communal farms were broken up. After the failure of the Great Leap Forward and the widespread famine that followed, many people in China became disillusioned and critical of the government's policies. They blamed the leadership, including Mao Zedong, for the disastrous consequences of the Great Leap Forward. There were also many divisions within the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), with some questioning Mao's authority and the direction of the country. Mao was threatened by these challenges to his power and sought to regain control and restore his authority. He believed that a new movement was necessary to reestablish his leadership as well as eliminate his political opponents. This led to the launch of the Cultural Revolution in 1966.

title: The Cultural Revolution
text:
The Cultural Revolution officially began in 1966. It was a direct attempt to regain political control of China after the failure of the Great Leap Forward. This new movement was intended to remove people Mao considered enemies, or "counter-revolutionaries," from positions of power. He believed that there were both government officials and civilians who were not following his communist ideas correctly, and he wanted to remove them from Chinese society. This was intended to reestablish Mao's power as the leader of China.

During the Cultural Revolution, Mao encouraged young people, including students, to rebel against authority figures and challenge the old ways of thinking. He wanted to create a society where everyone was equal and where traditional ideas and values were questioned. One way this was done was through the formation of groups called "Red Guards." The Red Guards were made up mostly of students and young people. They wore red armbands and carried Mao's “Little Red Book.” This book contained Mao’s ideas and sayings. The Red Guards would go to schools, government offices, and other places to criticize and sometimes even attack authority figures, teachers, and anyone they thought was not following Mao's ideas. Red Guards were urged to destroy the “four olds:” old ideas, old habits, old customs, and old culture. Large rallies were held with speeches promoting Mao's revolutionary ideas. Chaos and instability in the country began to increase as the Cultural Revolution continued.

Eventually, the Chinese government realized that the Cultural Revolution had gone too far and caused much damage. In 1976, Mao Zedong passed away, and new leadership was established in China. They put an end to the Cultural Revolution and tried to restore stability to the country. The Cultural Revolution had a profound impact on China. It changed the lives of millions of people, and many cultural and historical artifacts were destroyed during that time. It also led to a loss of trust in the government and a period of reflection and rebuilding afterward.

Mao's policies had a profound impact on China. There were some positives, such as the unification of China, and creating a modernized infrastructure for the country. He also provided access to education and healthcare for many. There was also a strong emphasis on self-reliance, nationalism, and a sense of pride for the Chinese people. However, there were many negative consequences to Mao’s rule. These include the loss of life, destruction of historical artifacts, and political isolation during the Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution.

title: Tiananmen Square
text:
The Tiananmen Square protests were a tragic event that took place in 1989 in Beijing, China. It began as a peaceful, student-led protest that demanded political reforms and greater freedom in China. Under the Chinese Communist Party, the government had strict control over people's lives, including their freedom of speech and expression. Many young students and intellectuals in China felt that there was a need for more political openness and democratic reforms.

In April 1989, a large-scale protest began in Tiananmen Square, a famous public square in Beijing. Students and other citizens gathered to express their concerns and demands for political change. They wanted more freedom, government accountability, and an end to government corruption. The protest gained momentum. Many members of the public who identified with the students’ concerns joined. The demonstrators used banners, speeches, and songs to express their desire for a more democratic society.

The Chinese government initially tolerated the protests. However, concerns increased as the protesters' numbers and influence increased. The government leaders viewed the demonstrations as a threat to their authority. They believed the protests weakened the stability of the country. The government declared martial law, which meant that the military took control to maintain order and stop the protests.

On June 4, 1989, the Chinese government used the military to forcefully stop the protests. Military troops were sent to Tiananmen Square, and clashes between the military and protesters started almost immediately. The military used tear gas, batons, and firearms to try to force the crowds to leave and regain control of the area.

No one knows for sure how many people were killed or injured in the protests. In recent history, the Chinese government has controlled the information made available to the world about the protests. The Chinese government officially stated that 200 civilians and several dozen security personnel had died. Reporters and Western diplomats to China estimated that hundreds to thousands were killed, and over 10,000 protesters were arrested.

Memorials to remember the protesters throughout China have been covered or dismantled. The last Tiananmen Square memorial in Hong Kong was covered by the government in 2022. However, memorials, museum exhibits, and annual candlelight observances by people around the world continue to teach about and memorialize the victims.

title: Conclude and Connect
text:
Communist China has gone through many changes throughout the 20th century. While the continuity of communist principles has remained similar, changes in leadership have resulted in changes to government policies.

Following Mao Zedong's death in 1976, China shifted its focus to economic reforms. The new leadership changed some of the systems that Mao had put into place.

Deng Xiaoping became the new leader of the Chinese Communist Party following Mao’s death. His vision for China was different. His policies aimed to open up China to the outside world. They also focused on improving the Chinese economy, modernizing industries, and encouraging foreign investments. These reforms helped China's economy to grow rapidly and lifted millions of people out of poverty.

Other leaders, such as Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, continued to increase China's role by integrating into the global community and strengthening its position on the world stage. In 2012, Xi Jinping became the leader of China. He has introduced the "Chinese Dream," which focuses on national revitalization through “The Road to Rejuvenation.” Since then, China's economy has developed, and its global influence has grown. Xi has introduced policies to combat corruption and increase the political party's control. He has continued to lead China's presence in various fields, including technology, military, and international relations.

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 9A
text:
The sun, moon, and Earth are all in space. People live on the Earth, so when we look up into the sky, we see the sun and the moon. The sun, Earth, and moon all interact.

The sun is a star, and it is the closest one to Earth. The sun is very important to Earth. It provides Earth with light and heat. The sun produces bright light. Light from the sun is called sunlight. Sunlight shines on Earth’s surface. Sunlight helps people and animals see. It helps plants grow. The sun also provides Earth with heat. When sunlight shines on Earth, its surface heats up. The heat helps people, plants, and animals survive.

Close your eyes and picture the moon. What do you see? Usually, people picture a big, glowing object in the night sky. But did you know the moon is not actually glowing? The moon does not make its own light. The moon reflects the sun’s light. The sun’s light shines on the moon’s surface. The moon’s surface reflects, or bounces back, the light. When this happens, the moon looks like it's glowing. However, people are seeing the reflection of the sun’s light.

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 9B

Go outside at different times of the day, and observe the objects in the sky. During the daytime, you see the sun, clouds, and birds. Sometimes, you can see the moon during the daytime. Next, go outside during the nighttime to observe objects in the sky. You can see the moon and many stars.

Objects in the sky can be very far away. They are more visible when you use a tool to observe them rather than just using your eyes. A telescope is a tool that helps people study the sky. With a telescope, objects are more visible. Compare what the moon looks like using a telescope and not using a telescope. Without a telescope, the moon might look like a flat, glowing object. You may see some darker lines. Now, look at it using a telescope. How is it different? The moon is more visible. It appears bigger and clearer. Its appearance is more detailed, too. You can see craters on the moon!

title: John C. Freeman and Mario Molina
text:
John C. Freeman

A meteorologist is a scientist who studies and predicts weather based on patterns. They create weather reports. They report their findings to others. John C. Freeman was a meteorologist. He was born and raised in Houston, Texas. During his career, he worked for the U.S. Army Air Corps, U.S. Weather Bureau, and Texas A&M University. He also collected research at the Weather Research Center in Houston. You may have been to the old John C. Freeman Weather Museum that was in Houston. The museum was named after him.

Mario Molina

The Nobel Prize is a very special award that people can receive for the important work they do. Mario Molina won a Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1995. He went to school in Mexico City. He loved science. He often made his bathroom into a laboratory. He spent hours doing chemistry. He studied chemistry in college. He then worked with several universities doing research. Most of his research was studying changes in the atmosphere. This is the area high up in the sky. It is where clouds form and precipitation falls. His research has had a great effect on the environment.

This week, you started to research the weather and the atmosphere just like Mario Molina and John C. Freeman. Would you like to study the weather for your career? Why or why not?

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 10B
text:
Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is. People measure temperatures with a tool called a thermometer. The weather can be hot or cold. To measure the temperatures of weather, place a thermometer outside. We record temperatures using degrees on a Fahrenheit or Celsius scale. Record the temperatures each day by writing it down on a sheet of paper. After a week or month, use your data to create a graph. Make a bar graph that shows each day’s temperature. Use your bar graph to notice any patterns with the temperatures.

Precipitation is water that falls from clouds in the sky to the ground. There are different forms, or types, of precipitation. Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all types of precipitation. They are forms of water that fall from clouds. People measure rainfall using a tool called a rain gauge. A rain gauge collects rain like a cup. Numbers on the rain gauge’s side show the amount of rainfall. This amount is the measurement. Precipitation may be measured in inches or centimeters. Record the amount of precipitation by writing down the number on a piece of paper. After a week or month, create a bar graph to show the data. Use your bar graph to notice any patterns in precipitation.

As you can see, temperature and precipitation are important parts of weather! It’s fun to measure, record, and graph them, and then look for patterns!

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 10C
text:
Weather can be severe. This means the weather is extremely bad and serious. Hurricanes, tornadoes, and floods are types of severe weather events. Different regions have different types of severe weather. In some regions, certain events are more likely to happen than others.

Hurricanes are most likely to form in regions with warm ocean water. Areas near the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean are most likely to experience hurricanes. To investigate hurricanes, you need a few things. Get a large bowl, cornstarch, blue food coloring, gravel, sand, and a wooden spoon. Place the gravel and sand in your bowl. Fill the rest of the bowl with water. Then, stir the cornstarch into the water. Stir until the water looks milky. Wait for the water to stop moving. Now, add blue food coloring to it. Slowly stir the food coloring with the spoon. You’ll see the food coloring move in a circular motion. This is how a hurricane forms and moves.

Tornadoes form over land. Their energy comes from large, severe thunderstorms. Tornadoes form in regions that have strong thunderstorms. Tornado Alley is a region that experiences a lot of tornadoes. To investigate tornadoes, you need a jar, water, liquid soap, and vinegar. Fill the jar three-fourths of the way with water. Put three squirts of liquid soap inside the jar. Add one tablespoon of vinegar. Close the jar tightly. Move the jar in a swirling motion. Look inside and you’ll see a funnel shape. This resembles a tornado. This investigation shows what a tornado looks like and how it moves.

Floods can happen anywhere. They are most likely to occur in areas near water, like coastal areas or rivers. title: TEKS Explained - Standard 6A
text:
Matter has physical properties. Texture, flexibility, and temperature are properties. Texture is how something feels when you touch it. Flexibility is how well matter bends. Temperature is how hot or cold something is. You observe and measure these physical properties. Observations and measurements help you classify matter by texture, flexibility, and temperature.

Classify the following materials: yarn, a cotton ball, a craft stick, and a pencil. First, observe the object’s physical properties. Then, classify them based on similar properties. Start by touching each object to decide its texture. Classify the yarn and cotton ball as soft and fuzzy. Classify the craft stick and pencil as hard and smooth. Next, decide the object’s flexibility. Try bending them. Classify the yarn and cotton ball as flexible. The craft stick and pencil are not flexible.

Classify the following objects by temperature: ice cubes, fire, hot chocolate, and ice cream. To classify them, use what you already know about the object. Classify ice cubes and ice cream as cold. Classify fire and hot chocolate as hot.

Matter can be solid or liquid. A solid keeps its shape. Pencils and books are solid. A liquid takes the shape of its container. Water is liquid. When you put water into a cup, the water takes the cup’s shape. To identify if a material is solid or liquid, think about its shape and if it changes. Is a computer solid or liquid? It keeps its shape. It’s solid. Is milk solid or liquid? Milk does not keep its shape. Its shape changes when you pour it into a cup.

The bed has a new purpose. The bed’s purpose is for sleeping.

Sometimes you need different materials for building certain objects. Wood, paper, clay, and glass are materials. Different materials have different physical properties. To make a kite, you need a material that the wind can lift. That means the material’s weight needs to be light. Paper is not heavy. Paper is light. Use paper to make your kite. Choosing the right material for what you want to make is important.

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 11B
text:
When humans use materials, they impact Earth. Human impact can be limited by making choices. One choice is to conserve materials. When you conserve something, you use it carefully. Humans conserve by reducing, reusing, and recycling. Reducing means using less of something. You do not use a lot of it. Using less limits your impact on Earth. It causes less pollution. It also saves natural resources. Reusing means using something more than once. This is important because you stop materials from piling up in landfills. Also, fewer resources are needed to create new materials.

Humans have another choice to limit their impact on Earth. This is to properly dispose of used materials. This means you get rid of them the right way. It’s important to properly dispose of materials like paper, plastic, and metal. Recycling can be used to dispose of these materials. Recycling means turning used materials into something new. Old paper can be made into new paper. Old plastic can be made into mats and rugs. Old metal can be made into cans.

There are many ways human impact on Earth can be limited. We just need to make choices to conserve. We need to properly dispose of materials.

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 8A
text:
Many things cause vibrations. Vibrations are when an object moves quickly back and forth. Objects make vibrations in different ways. Hitting a baseball causes vibrations. Slamming a door causes vibrations. Sounds from objects also cause vibrations.

To demonstrate that vibrations can be caused by different things, including sound, use a bowl, cling wrap, rice, and a drum. Place the cling wrap over the bowl. Make sure it is very tight. If needed, hold it in place with a rubber band. You have created a drum. Put a few pieces of rice on top of the cling wrap. Now, hit the drum many times with your hand. Watch the rice as you hit the drum. The sound from the drum makes the rice vibrate.

Sound is vibrating matter. Sound vibrations move through the air. Many things make sounds with their vibrations. For example, people talk. This is a sound. That means that people make sound vibrations. Talking creates sound vibrations that move through the air. We are able to hear them. Drums are an instrument that makes sound vibrations. Trains make sound vibrations, too.

To demonstrate that sound is made by vibrating matter, use a rubber band and a cup. Place the rubber around the top and bottom of your cup. The rubber band should be over the cup’s opening. Next, use your finger to pluck the rubber band over the top of the cup. This is similar to plucking a guitar string. Plucking the string causes vibrations. You are able to see the string move quickly back and forth. This demonstrates how vibrations are caused by various things. Also, you will hear a sound from your string and cup. This is sound vibrations reaching your ears.

title: TEKS Explained: Standard 8B
text: There are different levels of sound. Sounds can be loud or soft. Sounds can be low or high. We use different levels of sound every day. Can you think of a very loud sound? A fire alarm is a loud sound. It’s important that alarms are loud because we use them to alert people. For example, fire alarms are used to alert people of danger. Another loud sound is an alarm clock. They alert people to wake up in the morning. Can you think of a soft sound? Soft sounds are quiet. A whisper is a soft sound. We use it to talk quietly. Another soft sound is the hum of a refrigerator. We want this sound to be quiet because refrigerators are on all day. We do not want them to disturb us. As you can see, we use many levels of sound! We use them every day, and we use them for different reasons.
