Natural gas is, as the name says, a gas. You know that gases are lighter than liquids and solids. They quickly fill the air when released. This is like letting out air from a balloon. Imagine natural gas being trapped underground. A gas can fill small open spaces of rocks over great distances. What holds the gas underground? Another layer of rock that doesn’t have any pores, or holes, for the gas to escape. These rocks are thick and non-porous. This traps gases underground. Because of this property, solid rock can trap gases deep underground for millions of years. Scientists and engineers find pockets of natural gas deep in the earth. They use powerful drills to break through the rock. The gas escapes and is used to meet our needs. A similar process occurs with oil. This can also be trapped underneath layers of non-porous rock.

title: Asking Questions
text:
Asking Questions

Scientists and engineers are curious. They ask questions about the world around them. No matter what the situation, scientists and engineers always want to know more.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 6A
text:
To classify temperature, mass, magnetism, relative density and physical state, you can make observations and take measurements of materials. For temperature, you can often directly measure the temperature of an object using a thermometer. To classify something by temperature, you can record and compare the temperatures of materials and classify them as being hotter or colder compared to each other. To be more specific, you can also record the actual temperature and observe differences.

Mass is a measurement taken by using a balance. Usually, we measure mass in grams. By recording the mass of various objects, you can compare the masses of objects and classify them as being heavier (more mass) or lighter (less mass). For magnetism, you can determine if the material is attracted to a magnet or not and classify it as either being magnetic or not. Physical states consist of whether or not the material is a solid, liquid or gas. Relative density is a comparative measure where you can classify items as to whether they sink or float. The item that sinks has a higher relative density to water than the item that floats.

Using this information, you can take any item and classify it by temperature, mass, magnetism, relative density and physical state. Let’s look at an example to show you how to describe matter by these properties. For a pencil, you can measure its temperature using a thermometer. If it’s room temperature it will be around 20 degrees Celsius. Using a balance to measure the mass of a pencil, it should be around 16 grams. Put a magnet close to a pencil. Is it attracted to the magnet? No, so it’s described as being non-magnetic. When a pencil is placed in water, it may float. You can describe the pencil’s relative density as being less than water. The physical state of a pencil is a solid. You can classify and describe many different materials by these physical properties.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 6D
text:
There are three states of matter: solid, liquid, and gas. All three common states of matter are made up of particles. Particles are too small to be seen, but it’s important to know that everything is made of them! Particles are constantly moving, but they move differently depending on the state of matter.

In solids, the particles are so close together that they cannot move past one another easily. Solid particles are arranged in a fixed pattern, which is why solids keep their shape. To illustrate particles in solid matter, you can first draw a cube. A cube is solid. Next, you can draw little circles to represent particles. Inside your cube, draw a layer of little circles (particles). Make sure each circle is touching. On top of that layer, draw another layer of little circles, exactly like the one below it. This is a fixed pattern! Keep drawing layers of circles until your entire cube is filled with particles. You’ve illustrated particles in solid matter.

In liquids, the particles are close together, but have the ability to easily slide past each other. Although the particles can move freely, they are still linked to one another. To illustrate particles in liquid matter, first draw a container. Then, add a line to represent water. In the part of your container that represents water, draw your circular particles. Since particles in liquids move freely, they do not need to follow a set pattern, or layers, like the solid particles. You simply must have the particles touching to show that they are linked. Be sure your particles fill the liquid portion of your container.

Lastly, in gases, the particles are far apart and can move around freely. They are not constantly touching like solids and liquids. How do we know that air particles exist if we can’t see them? Filling a transparent balloon with air is a perfect example. Air is a gas, so its particles move about freely. As air fills the balloon, the balloon expands. Even though you cannot see anything inside the balloon, it maintains its new, inflated shape. To illustrate gas particles, first draw the balloon. Then, draw circles inside the balloon to represent particles. The circles do not need to touch. They do not need to follow a pattern. They move around freely.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 7B
text:
Forces can affect objects. They set objects into motion, and affect the object’s speed. It’s exciting to design investigations that test the effects of forces on objects in a system. To do this, you can design an investigation using a toy car and a ramp. You can use your hand as the force in this investigation by using your hand to push the toy car. The toy car, ramp, and your hand make a system. They work together to perform a task, which, in this case, is to test how the car moves.

One thing you can choose to do is to design your investigation to calculate measurements, like distance and time. For example, you can test how different strengths of forces affect the distance the toy car moves beyond the ramp. Or, you can test how different strengths of forces affect the amount of time the car rolls after you push it.

To carry out your investigation, you’ll want to first create a ramp. What materials do you want to use in your design? Think about materials that will help your car move. For instance, you want your ramp to be smooth rather than bumpy. Next, you want to make sure your ramp is angled so the car can move down it. You can use objects to prop one side of the ramp up. Next, you’ll want to decide how many times you will test your investigation. It’s important you test more than one time to make sure your findings are consistent! As you test your design, collect your data. Measure how far the car moves with lighter or stronger pushes, or measure the time the car continues rolling with lighter and stronger pushes. After you test, you’ll discover through your investigation that pushing the car harder with your hand increases the force on it. The car will move faster and farther. When a smaller amount of force is applied, the car will move slower and won’t travel as far.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 8A
text:
Energy transformation includes a change of one form of energy into potentially multiple forms. Different forms of energy include chemical energy, electrical energy, and light energy. Energy does not disappear, even when it transforms from one form to another. It is simply changing its form.

You can use a flashlight to investigate the transformation of energy in systems. Flashlights are a system with a two-stage energy transformation. It’s important to know that batteries contain stored chemical energy. To start your investigation, remove the batteries from the flashlight. What do you think will happen when you turn the flashlight on? The flashlight does not light up. When batteries are not in a system, the chemical energy inside of them does not transform into electrical energy. There are no energy transformations in your flashlight system.

Now continue your investigation and place the batteries in the flashlight. Turn the flashlight on. Do you see a difference in the flashlight system? Yes, you will see the flashlight’s light bulb lights up! How do you think this investigation shows multiple energy transformations? When the flashlight is in use, the chemical energy in the battery transforms into electrical energy. This shows the first energy transformation — chemical energy transforms into electrical energy. Then, the electrical energy moves through the flashlight’s closed path. As it interacts with the lightbulb, the electrical energy transforms into light energy. Light energy is the energy we can see in this flashlight system. The electrical energy to light energy was the second energy transformation. Now you’ve investigated energy transformation! You’ll notice energy transforms in many of the systems we use each day.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 10A
text:
Every day, the Sun and ocean interact in the water cycle. As the Sun heats the ocean’s surface, the water absorbs heat energy. This causes ocean water to evaporate. When it evaporates, it rises into the atmosphere as water vapor, which is a gas. Once in the atmosphere, the water vapor cools. Then, the gas condenses into clouds and becomes liquid again. This step is called condensation. Wind causes clouds to move all over Earth. Then, the water returns to Earth’s surface as precipitation. Types of precipitation include rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Sometimes, this water even returns to the ocean! The water cycle continues when, once again, the Sun heats Earth’s surface and causes evaporation.

When the Sun and ocean interact in the water cycle, they affect the weather. Both the Sun and ocean contribute to cloud formation, storms, and rainfall. Remember, the Sun evaporates ocean water, which condenses into clouds holding precipitation. When the wind moves the clouds all over Earth, it moves the precipitation in the clouds, too. When these clouds travel to surrounding areas, it affects the weather in that location. For example, clouds that form over the ocean often hold a lot of rain. When the rain clouds move to another area, that area eventually experiences heavy rain. The clouds created in the water cycle also affect an area’s temperature. The Sun’s light shines and warms Earth’s surface. Clouds can trap heat to warm the Earth and reflect sunlight to cool the Earth. The water cycle can affect other types of weather, such as storms, cloud coverage, and air pressure. As you can see, when the Sun and ocean interact in the water cycle, they directly affect the weather!

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 10C
text:
Earth’s surface is constantly changing. Water, wind, and ice are elements that change Earth’s surface. They assist in the formation of many landforms, including deltas, canyons, and sand dunes.

Deltas are wetlands formed at a river’s mouth, which is the river’s end. Deltas are often triangular in shape, or in the shape of a fan, and they are flat. As water flows in rivers, it carries sediment in its currents. Sediment includes gravel, sand, and clay. Deltas form when the river slows at its mouth and deposits the sediment. There, in the slower moving water, sediment settles and collects. This becomes a new landform – a delta.

You can model how a delta forms by using a baking pan, one pound of sand, a cup, and water. Place the sand in the upper half of the baking pan. Press it lightly so it’s flat, and then create a slope leading into the bottom half of the pan. Leave enough space for the delta to form in the tray’s bottom half. Next, slowly pour water from your cup onto the sand. The water will run down the sand and begin to fan out. You’ll see a delta begin to form in the pan’s bottom half! You’ve modeled changing Earth’s surface by using water to form a delta.

Canyons are deep, narrow cuts in rock. They have steep sides, and rivers often run through the middle of them. Canyons form as water pressure repeatedly cuts through the rock, weathering and eroding pieces until the landform develops. Water can seep into the rock’s surface. It freezes in the cracks and expands. The ice acts as a wedge, and forces pieces of rock to break apart. This causes huge chunks of rock to break off of the canyon’s sides. Wind also contributes to the formation of canyons. High winds move through the canyon, which shape and smooth its sides.

You can model how a canyon forms by using sand, gravel, clay, soil, a baking pan, a watering can, and water. Spread the sand, gravel, clay, and soil in individual layers in the baking pan. After each layer, press it firmly with your hands before adding a new layer on top. These represent the rock layers on Earth. Next, use your finger to draw a curved line in the top layer. Your line should go from one end of the baking pan to the other end. This represents the river running through the rock. Next, pour water from your watering can into your river. Start with a little bit of water, and then increase the amount. You’ll see layers of rock wash away, and a canyon starting to form! You’ve modeled changing the Earth’s surface by using water to form a canyon.

Sand dunes are hills of sand along a beach or desert. They form when the wind carries sediment into a sheltered area and deposits it. The sand accumulates into a mound. Once the mound is formed, the sand continues to collect. Water assists in forming sand dunes along a beach. The ocean carries sediment onto the coast and deposits it into the existing mound. Wind can also move sand from the beach onto the dune. Due to how easily sand moves, dunes are always changing their shapes and heights!

You can model how a sand dune forms by using a deep container, a pound of dry sand, and a blow dryer. Start by placing the sand into the bottom of the container. Next, turn the blow dryer on a low setting. Carefully use it to blow “wind” across the sand’s surface. Watch as the sand begins to accumulate into a mound at the opposite end of the container! You’ve modeled changing the Earth’s surface by using wind to form a sand dune!

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 12C
text:
A healthy ecosystem has many different types of organisms living in it! We call the living organisms in an ecosystem the biotic factors. A healthy ecosystem needs nonliving factors, called abiotic factors, too. Sunlight, air, water, and temperature are abiotic factors. You can describe an ecosystem as healthy when it’s able to support the range of biotic factors living in it. That means a healthy ecosystem can provide plants and animals with food, water, shelter, and air. In a healthy ecosystem, the biotic factors will live, grow, and reproduce. Sometimes, human activities affect a healthy ecosystem. Human activities can be harmful, or they can be beneficial.

Human activity has been harmful to healthy ecosystems in many ways. Pollution, deforestation, overhunting and overfishing, and introducing invasive species to habitats are all harmful human activities. Human activity can be described as harmful when it hurts the organisms living there by destroying the resources needed for shelter, water, and food. Harmful activity can cause a population to decrease, which negatively impacts food webs. Let’s look at an example of human activity, and describe how it hurts an ecosystem. Zebra mussels, which are small, striped, freshwater mussels, are an invasive species in Texas’s lakes. Humans accidentally brought zebra mussels to North America. Now, zebra mussels harm native mussel species by over-eating their common food source. This leaves less food for native mussels so their numbers decrease.

Human activity can be beneficial to ecosystems, too. Humans work hard to help struggling species, plant and grow more plants, reduce human waste, and preserve habitats. Human activity can be described as beneficial when the ecosystem continues to thrive. The plants and animals living there grow, live, and reproduce. Here is a real-world example of beneficial human activity. Currently, humans are trying to protect and preserve coastal ecosystems. They are strengthening sand dunes and planting seagrass. This will protect the plants and animals living along the coast from the wind and ocean waves. Humans are removing invasive plants from sand dunes, and planting native ones to provide food and shelter for living organisms. Providing food will help the organisms stay healthy, live, and grow. Shelter ensures the organisms have a safe place to live and raise their young.

When humans help take care of an ecosystem's biotic and abiotic factors, the ecosystem continues to thrive and stay healthy. The next time you head outside, think about your actions. Are you harming or helping the ecosystem?

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 13B
text:
Behavior in organisms can be either instinctual or learned. Both types of behavior are key to increasing the organism’s chances of survival.

Instinctual behavioral traits are inherited from past generations. These traits do not need to be taught to an organism. This means instinctual behavioral traits happen automatically – they are not learned. Hibernating, walking, taking care of offspring, and building nests are examples of instinctual behaviors. These instinctual behaviors provide the organism with food and energy, ensure the offspring can live and grow, and provide shelter from danger. All are essential to the organism's survival. A great example of an instinctual behavior trait is when turtle hatchlings return to the sea. The mother lays eggs in the sand, and leaves them to develop and hatch on their own. This means there is no parent to teach the turtle hatchlings once they're born. Once the babies hatch, it is instinctual for them to return to the sea as a large group. This increases the chance that they’ll survive waiting predators.

Learned behavioral traits are behaviors learned through experience. This means an organism’s experiences change how the organism acts. Sometimes offspring learn these survival skills by watching their parents. Avoiding danger, finding food, and communicating are behavioral traits organisms can learn from their parents, and increase their chances of survival. A great example of a learned behavioral trait is orca whales hunting in packs. Orcas teach their young how to hunt along with the pack to increase the chances of catching prey. In fact, orcas have been known to catch and release seals as a way for their young to practice catching seals. As you can see, orca hunting is not entirely instinctual. The young experience hunting in packs and learn through observing their parents. These learned behaviors help the orcas survive.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 10B
text:
The formation of sedimentary rocks is a very long process. It can take thousands, or even millions, of years! Sedimentary rocks form on Earth’s surface through weathering, erosion, and deposition. To start, weathering breaks down large rocks into small pieces, such as sand and pebbles. The weathered rock pieces become part of sediment. Sediment is a solid material made up of weathered rocks, minerals, and the remains of plants and animals. Then, erosion carries the sediment, along with other minerals, and deposits them in a new location. Over time, layers of sediment build up on top of one another. As they build up, their weight causes the layers of sediment to compress and harden into sedimentary rocks.

The formation of fossil fuels is another long process that occurs with the formation of sedimentary rocks. Fossil fuels are natural substances that form from the remains of buried organisms like plants and animals. The dead plants and animals settled into the ground and decompose. Then, they were covered by sediment and compressed along with the layer of sedimentary rock. Eventually, the remains of the plants and animals changed into fossil fuels through heat and pressure. Now, fossil fuels are buried beneath the many layers of sediment.

The processes of sedimentary rock and fossil fuels formation are slow and difficult to see in the natural world. Therefore, a model can help us demonstrate the concepts. Start with gathering four colored clays — red, blue, black, and green. Break the red, blue, and green colored clays into tiny pieces – this models weathering! Next, you need one cup. Place the red pieces of clay into the cup. Then, place the blue pieces of clay onto the red layer. Now, take your black clay. Roll a few balls of black clay, and place them on top of the red layer. These represent organisms that have died, which become fossil fuels. The black clay models how organisms become buried under layers of sediment, and results in fossil fuels forming along with sedimentary rocks. Lastly, place the green clay pieces on top. Firmly press the layers with your fingers. The layers need to be compact to represent the compressed, hardened layers of sediment buildup. Now, flip your cup upside down and carefully pop the layers out. The clay layers stick together. You’ll see you’ve made a sedimentary rock model! You can see three, distinct colored layers of clay. If you break the model in half, you’ll see the black clay (or fossil fuels) between the second and third layers. From the pressure of you flattening the layers, the fossil fuels will be embedded in between layers.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 6B
text: A mixture contains two or more combined substances. Some mixtures maintain the physical properties of their substances, despite being combined. That means, the substances will retain their color, texture, weight, mass, magnetism, and so on. You can demonstrate that mixtures retain their properties by mixing two substances: iron filings and sand. First, you want to note the substances’ physical properties. Iron filings are black, small, rectangular, soft, and magnetic. Sand is tan, small, round, gritty, and nonmagnetic. Next, mix both substances together in a bag to create a mixture. The mixture will look different because the two substances are now combined. To demonstrate that some mixtures maintain the physical properties of their substances, you need to separate the iron filings from the sand. Use a magnet to move the iron filings to one side of the bag. The iron filings' properties remained the same, even though they were mixed. They are still black, small, rectangular, soft, and magnetic. The properties of the sand also remained the same. The sand is still tan, small, round, gritty, and nonmagnetic. It’s interesting to see how some mixtures maintain the properties of their substances!

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 7A
text:
When we talk about forces, we generally categorize them as equal and unequal forces. Both equal and unequal forces act on objects. Remember, forces are pushes and pulls. When pushes and pulls act on an object, they cause patterns of motion, and the transfer of energy. Energy transfer occurs when the energy of one object affects another object. It’s important to know that energy is not gained or lost, but transferred between objects.

When equal forces act in opposite directions, there is no change in motion or position. Neither force is stronger than the other, which causes them to cancel their effects. You can investigate equal forces by playing a game of tug-of-war. Create two tug-of-war teams with the same amount of players and strength. Each of the two teams holds opposite ends of a rope. Then, both teams start to pull the rope with the same amount of force. In this investigation, you may see that the forces from both teams are equal and acting in opposite directions. The amount of energy transferred between the teams pulling the ropes is the same in both directions. You know the forces are equal because the tug-of-war teams don’t move — they stay in their position. Also, the rope doesn’t move in one direction or the other.

With unequal forces, one force is stronger than the other. Unequal forces cause a change in motion or position. You can investigate unequal forces by playing another game of tug-of-war. This time, make sure one team has more players and strength than the other team. Now, when both teams pull the rope, the side with more players will be pulling with greater force. The transfer of energy is not the same on both sides. One side is transferring more energy, or pulling with greater strength, than the other side. This creates an unequal force. How do you know the forces are unequal? In this investigation, the tug-of-war rope and team will move, and its position will change. It will move in the direction of the stronger tug-of-war team.

This pattern of motion or non-motion can be predicted when we investigate equal and unequal forces.

title: Phenomenon
text: A baker in the Great Blanton Bake-Off of Austin, Texas, can’t create an artistic dessert because his electric oven is not working.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 8B
text:
It’s important to identify the requirements for a functioning, or working, electrical circuit. For a circuit to be complete, it requires a closed path. The closed path must contain a power source, an energy pathway, and an energy receiver called a load. These parts must be connected for the electrical energy to continue to flow throughout the circuit. The power source in an electrical circuit can be a battery or an electrical outlet. The energy pathway usually consists of metal wires, which are a great tool for connecting pieces of the circuit. Common examples of energy receivers are lightbulbs, motors, fans, and buzzers. When these three components are connected correctly, the electrical circuit functions properly.

When in a complete circuit, electrical energy can be transformed into motion, light, sound, or thermal energy. You can demonstrate this by building a simple circuit with a battery, wires, and a lightbulb. The battery is the power source. It contains chemical energy. The load is the lightbulb. You can use wires to connect the battery to the lightbulb. You do this by touching one wire to the top of the battery and the side of the light bulb’s base. Then, touch a second wire to the bottom of the battery and the bottom of the light bulb’s base. You can use electrical tape to hold the wires to the battery. When the parts of the circuit are connected, the circuit is closed. Chemical energy transforms into electrical energy, then into light energy. How can you observe this in the lightbulb? The light bulb lights up! That’s evidence of light energy. Using the same circuit, you can show the transformation of electrical energy into thermal energy. If you were to carefully touch the light bulb, it would feel hot. The light bulb heated, which shows evidence of thermal energy. You can demonstrate the transformation of electrical energy into motion energy using the same circuit. Replace the lightbulb with a small fan. The fan moves once the circuit is complete, showing evidence of motion energy. As you can see, energy transformations are everywhere!

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 9
text:
Earth rotates, or spins, on its axis. Earth’s axis is an imaginary line that runs through Earth’s center from pole to pole. Earth rotates counterclockwise. Earth’s rotation causes two things to happen: the day and night cycle, and the appearance of the Sun moving across the sky, resulting in changes in shadows.

You can set up your own demonstration to show that Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours. All you need is a styrofoam ball, a stick, a marker, a flashlight, and a timer. First, carefully poke your stick through one end of the ball. Push it through the center of the ball until it exits the ball’s opposite side. The stick represents Earth’s axis, and the ball represents Earth. Next, use your marker to draw a dot on one side of the ball. Turn the flashlight on, and set it on a table. Start by facing the dot toward the flashlight, which represents the Sun. Now it is daytime. Start your timer for 24 seconds to represent 24 hours. Now, slowly rotate the ball (which is Earth) counterclockwise. Different sides of the ball face the flashlight (which is the Sun) as the dot slowly faces away. After 12 seconds, the dot faces entirely away from the flashlight. Now it is nighttime. Keep on rotating! After 24 seconds (which represents 24 hours), the dot faces the flashlight once again. You’ve demonstrated that it takes Earth 24 hours to rotate on its axis one full time.

Earth’s rotation is why we have a day and night cycle. As Earth rotates, different sides face the Sun. When a side faces toward the Sun, it experiences daytime. At the same moment, the opposite side of Earth is facing away from the Sun. That side experiences nighttime. As Earth continues to rotate, the sides facing toward and away from the Sun continue to change. The side experiencing daytime rotates away from the Sun. Then, they experience nighttime. After approximately 24 hours, the process starts again, giving us 24 hours in a day.

Earth’s rotation makes it look like the Sun is moving. In fact, the Sun isn’t moving. It’s Earth that moves! When Earth spins on its axis, it changes the position of the Sun in the sky. This creates the patterns we observe in shadow positions. A shadow occurs when an object blocks the Sun’s light. Shadows take the shape of the object. The Sun’s position in the sky creates patterns in shadows that we can predict. When the Sun is to the left of an object, the shadow is cast to the right of the object. Similarly, if the Sun is in front of an object, the shadow is cast behind it. Additionally, the Sun’s position affects how short and long shadows appear. When the Sun is high, the shadows are short because the Sun is directly overhead. Shadows are long when the Sun is low because the light is at an angle.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 12A
text:
In a healthy ecosystem, a variety of organisms survive by interacting with living and nonliving factors. Biotic factors are living factors in an ecosystem. They include plants, animals, and bacteria. These are the producers, consumers, and decomposers that cycle matter and energy throughout the ecosystem. The cycle of matter and energy helps the organisms live and grow, and the ecosystem stays healthy. Abiotic factors are the nonliving factors in an ecosystem. Abiotic factors include sunlight, water, air, temperature, and soil. These nonliving factors are necessary for biotic organisms to survive. For example, they provide the oxygen to breathe. They provide the water to drink and grow plants. They include the necessary temperature for species to thrive.

Let’s study a healthy Texas ecosystem. If you go outside, you can find a grassy field. If you’re able to stay and observe your surroundings, you’ll see many things! You’ll see both biotic and abiotic factors. These factors are around you each day, and now you can observe how they interact.

First, observe the biotic factors, which are the plants and animals around you. On the ground, you may observe plants that include flowers and grasses. You may observe rabbits and lizards, too! In the air, you’ll see bugs, bees, and birds, like hawks. Now that you’ve identified the biotic factors, you can observe how they interact to survive. Remember, living things rely on one another for food and energy. In the grassy field, you can observe a rabbit eating grass. The bees may be buzzing from flower to flower, eating pollen. There are many dependencies in the grassy field’s ecosystem. You might not see them today, but the hawks depend on rabbits for food, and the lizards depend on bugs. When organisms eat properly, they stay healthy, continue to grow, and produce offspring.

Next, study the abiotic factors in the grassy field. You can observe sunlight, rocks, and water. You can’t see oxygen, but you know it’s there because you’re breathing. You can feel it fill your lungs. Now, let’s observe and describe how the biotic factors interact with these abiotic factors to survive. When you see sunlight shining on the grass, you’re seeing how the Sun provides grasses (the producers) with the energy needed to make their own food. If you watch the animals carefully, you’ll see they are breathing. They are breathing in the air around them. If you are able to find any streams or puddles in the field, you may observe animals drinking water from them. Oxygen and water help the animals stay healthy. These organisms will appear energetic and strong.

As you can see, in all healthy ecosystems, you can observe and describe how various organisms survive by interacting with biotic and abiotic factors.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 13A
text:
A structure is something that’s made up of parts. Its function is what the structure does. Structures can be internal or external. Internal structures are structures on the organism’s inside, like the heart and lungs. External structures are structures on the outside of the organism, and include things like eyes, claws, and tails. Sometimes structures are common, like a heart or brain. Other times, structures are unique to the organism, like flamingos' long legs. Structures and functions are necessary for survival. For example, they help the organism find food and water, or they help the organism hide from danger.

aDifferent species are able to survive in the same environment due to their unique structures and functions. Elephants and lions are organisms that survive in the same environment. Their environment is open land with plants, different animal species, and watering holes. You can analyze the elephant’s structures and functions to see how it survives in its environment. A trunk is an important elephant structure. The trunk has several functions that provide the elephant with nutrients. It helps the elephant breathe air and drink water. The trunk helps the elephant grab food and bring the food to its mouth. Another structure is the elephant’s ears. They are able to funnel in sound waves and hear any nearby predators. They also help the elephant stay cool on hot days. Now, analyze the lion’s structures and functions. Lions have structures that help them obtain nutrients. Lions have powerful leg muscles, which allow them to sprint and capture prey. Lions’ claws function as a way for them to catch, grip, and tear their food. Lions have ears that rotate. This allows them to hear prey from all sides. Even though elephants and lions have different structures and functions, they can both survive in the same environment.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 12B
text:
In order to predict changes in a food web, you’ll need to first look at the cycling of matter and the flow of energy. Consider the following food web in a pond ecosystem: the Sun, algae, flies, frogs, herons, and bacteria. Algae are producers. Flies, frogs, and herons are consumers. Bacteria are decomposers. The Sun’s light transfers energy to the algae. Algae use sunlight, and matter from the air and water to produce their own food. When flies consume algae, energy and matter transfer from the algae to the flies. Next, the flies are food for frogs. Flies contain energy, that, when eaten, transfers to the bodies of frogs. The matter from the flies helps the frogs physically grow and repair their bodies. Similarly, frogs are food for herons. When herons eat frogs, they receive energy and matter. Finally, when living plants and animals die, their remains become energy and matter for bacteria and new plant growth.

Now, let’s predict what will happen in the food web if there are changes in the pond ecosystem. Sometimes in an ecosystem, the population of a producer, consumer, or decomposer can change. A population can increase or decrease. Let’s pretend the population of flies decreases. We will predict how this change affects the cycling of matter and the flow of energy. First, remember that frogs eat flies. A decrease in the fly population means there will be less food for the frogs. Now, what do you predict will happen to the cycling of matter in the food web? Most likely, with less food, there is less matter available to help the frogs grow and repair their bodies. The frogs may not appear as healthy. They could get sick and die. If the frogs begin to die, the herons will begin to lose their food source. What do you think will happen to the herons? With less food, there is less matter available to help the herons grow and stay healthy. When the flies are removed, they also affect the flow of energy. What do you predict will happen to the food web’s flow of energy? When flies are moved, there is less energy available for the frogs and herons. There are no flies to provide the frogs with energy. In turn, this decreases the amount of energy available to the herons because they eat the frogs. As you can see, if you first study the cycling of matter and the flow of energy in a food web, you’ll be able to predict how changes in the ecosystem will affect it!

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 6C
text:
A solution is a combination of two or more substances. In a solution, the substances have dissolved entirely, and can’t be easily separated again. You can compare the properties of the substances before and after they’re combined into a solution. The combination of salt with water is a good example of a solution. Before being mixed into a solution, you can identify the properties of the salt and the water. Salt is solid, white, hard, and brittle. Water is liquid, colorless, clear, and odorless. Both substances have mass and can be weighed. Once the two substances are combined, the salt will dissolve into the water. This makes a solution: salt water. Now, you can compare the properties of the substances after they are combined. You’ll notice the properties have changes in the solution. The salt is fully dissolved, which makes the salt participles impossible to see. You can no longer identify its properties like you could prior to mixing. Water is still liquid, but may now appear cloudy.

It’s important to know that matter is conserved in solutions. It is not gained, and it is not lost. You can demonstrate this by measuring and recording the mass of both the salt and the water prior to mixing them together. Once you combine them, you can find the mass of the saltwater solution. You’ll see their combined mass will be equal to the individual masses. This confirms that matter stayed the same in the solution, despite any physical changes to the substances. You’ve demonstrated that the amount of matter in your solution did not change, it was conserved.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 8C
text:
Light energy travels in a straight line, a lot of them! Once light is produced, it continues in straight lines until it comes in contact with something else. When light comes in contact with something, it can be reflected, refracted, or absorbed.

You can demonstrate how light travels in a straight line by using three CDs, clothespins, and a candle. Clip the clothespins to the bottom of the CDs, to create a base that helps the CDs stand straight up. Next, in a straight line, place each CD a few inches apart on a table, checking that their holes line up. Then, place your candle at the opposite end of the table. Line up its wick with the CDs’ holes. Light your candle, go to the table’s opposite end, and look through the first CD's hole. You’ll be able to see the candle’s flame through all three holes! This demonstrates how light travels in a straight line because it’s shining through the three CDs three holes.

Reflection occurs when the light bounces off of an object. Smooth, shiny surfaces such as mirrors, smooth water surfaces, and metal are great at reflecting light, but they aren’t the only reflective surfaces. To demonstrate light being reflected, you need a flashlight and a mirror. Turn the flashlight on, and shine it on the mirror. Now, look behind you. You’ll see the light from the flashlight because the light has bounced off the mirror.

Refraction happens when the light bends, or changes direction, after passing through a substance. It’s easy to observe refraction using a transparent substance, like water, glass, or plastic. You can demonstrate how light is refracted by placing a straw into a glass of water. The part of the straw extending outward from the water’s surface looks straight. However, when you observe the straw beneath the water’s surface, the straw will look bent.

Lastly, light can be absorbed. This means an object can soak up light. To demonstrate light absorption, you need a flashlight and a book. First, turn on the flashlight. Place it on a table facing a wall. You can see the light on the wall. Next, place the book in front of the flashlight’s light. When the light hits the book, you can see the light on the book. You can’t see the flashlight’s light on the wall anymore. The book is absorbing the light.

title: Phenomenon
text: Each American who uses a reusable water bottle can keep an average of 156 plastic bottles a year out of the land, ocean, and air.

title: TEKs Explained - Standard 11
text:
Using natural resources impacts the environment. It’s important to develop solutions that minimize the environmental impact of the use of natural resources. A solution means you are solving a problem. Conservation, recycling, and the proper disposal of materials are peoples’ solutions to minimizing environmental impact.

You can design your own solution to minimize environmental impact! Water is a natural resource that is limited. Therefore, it’s important that people conserve water. However, people need to continue to use water. For example, in the spring and summer, people often plant gardens in their yards or communities. People need to water their gardens to help their fruits and vegetables grow. What solution can you design to conserve water, but also still be able to water a garden? Your solution needs to allow you to collect water and store it to use at a later time.

First, think about how you use water each day. Is there any leftover water you can collect? We have leftover water from when we make food, like when we boil potatoes or pasta, or steam vegetables. Next, think about other ways you have access to water. When it rains, we have access to rainwater that we can collect. Finally, think about how you can store the water until you use it to water the garden’s plants. You can design a container to hold water you collect. You can reuse a clean plastic jug from a gallon of milk. If you cut the top of the jug off, you can place it outside to collect rainwater. Whenever you have leftover water from cooking, you can add the water to your rainwater collection. You can use the collected water to water the garden! Now, you’ll use less water from a hose. You’ve designed a solution to conserve water!

title: Economies in the Colonies
text:
While it is true that many colonists came to America in search of religious freedom, they also sought economic freedom. The geography and climate in America were different from what they were used to in Europe, but the colonists soon adapted. They found ways to make their environment work for them, using the land and natural resources to develop their economy.

In the New England Colonies, farms were small. They barely produced enough for the families who lived on them. Agriculture was not a big part of the economy in this region. Access to the sea did give rise to maritime trade. Fishing and whaling became profitable industries. Large forests provided lumber for shipbuilding. Sawmills were built and powered by water to cut trees into lumber. Oak and maple woods were used for ship frames, and tall white pines were perfect for the masts and planking of the ships. Cargo ships also required wooden barrels and crates for storage. Over time, the New England Colonies became an ideal place for factories to build and process goods. Boston was a major port and center of activity in this region.

With the richer soil in the Middle Colonies, more food could be produced on the land. Farms were bigger and more productive, providing grains to all of the colonies. Large mills called grist mills were needed to process the grain into goods like flour and bran. Before grist mills, grain was processed by hand with a grindstone. Grist mills used water-powered machinery to process a larger amount of grain faster and easier than older methods. The Middle Colonies were busy with trade, too. Colonists utilized the forested areas. They sold the trees for lumber. They also trapped small animals for their fur, which was in demand in Europe. Coal and iron mining boosted the economy. Ports in Philadelphia and New York City were important centers of trade and grew quickly. They attracted more than just merchants, though. All sorts of people flocked to these larger towns. During the colonial period, these same towns became influential centers of culture and thought.

In the Southern Colonies, the economy was almost entirely dependent on agriculture. Some colonists had small family farms. However, most grew cash crops during long growing seasons. These are crops grown only for their financial value, not for the farmer to use and live off of. Some of the cash crops grown in the Southern Colonies were tobacco, rice, sugarcane, and indigo (a deep purple-blue dye). While crops like tobacco and sugarcane needed to be dried or ground down, indigo required a chemical process to extract the color and make it into a marketable product. This made cash crops very labor intensive to grow and process. To make a profit, large areas of land had to be planted. This developed into a plantation system. Each plantation was a large farm. People worked on their own farms. Sometimes, they had indentured servants to help them. When the colonists realized that their plantations required more labor, enslaved people were captured from Africa and forced to work in the colonies. To trade and sell their crops, the Southern Colonies made use of their natural sea ports. Charleston, South Carolina, was a major port for the Southern Colonies.

title: Treatment of Diverse Groups in the Colonies
text:
As the colonies grew, they attracted people from all over Europe. Early colonists sailed from England, Ireland, and Scotland. Over time, more traveled from the Netherlands, France, Germany, and Sweden. Thousands of immigrants journeyed to the Americas seeking new opportunities. People came from diverse cultures with different backgrounds and belief systems. Jewish people settled mainly in port cities like New Amsterdam (now, New York City) or Newport, Rhode Island. They were especially attracted to colonies founded on religious freedom. Some colonies, like Georgia, had charters that promised religious liberty to all people. Not all migrants were welcomed into the colonies or treated fairly, though. The poor and the powerless were often mistreated in the colonies, just as they had been in England.

Women were expected to follow strict guidelines of behavior. These guidelines restricted women to certain roles. They were expected to perform household chores like cooking, cleaning, and laundry. Women could wash other people’s laundry to earn money or food. They could also be midwives, who deliver babies, because these jobs were considered suitable for women. Women couldn’t have any rights unless they were married or had a male guardian.

A lot of people died of disease or starvation in the early colonies. Parents lost children, and children lost parents. Orphaned children often became servants for other families so they could survive. They had few rights until they married.

Most colonists didn’t trust people who were not residents. The law was not kind to a person without a home. Strangers were treated with suspicion. A person who could not pay their way or was deep in debt would be imprisoned until the debt could be paid.

English colonial leaders never accepted American Indians as citizens in their towns. American Indians were not seen as equals to white European settlers. Some were even enslaved by the colonists.

Most African Americans in the colonies were enslaved people. A few were born free, bought their freedom, or were set free by their enslavers. African Americans were rarely accepted by white colonists.

title: Tribal Government
text:
Some Native American tribes in the United States are considered sovereign nations. A sovereign nation means there is a government that has authority over a geographic region. Tribal nations have their own governments. Many also have constitutions. Tribal governments within the United States also have to follow laws created by the federal government and the U.S. Constitution. The U.S. Congress has final authority on Native American nations. The federal government has a responsibility to protect the rights of Indigenous tribes. Tribal members are often invited to join local, state, and national groups. This is to make sure that laws passed there are fair to their tribes.

There are different types of tribal government. Generally, the leaders of tribal nations are known as chiefs, presidents, or governors. Often, a group of leaders form a council. Tribal councils make laws for their nations. Tribal councils also decide how to spend money on roads, water, and electricity. Tribes also have their own court system and police who help interpret and enforce tribal laws. Some tribal councils tax their people. They use the money to pay for police officers, education, and healthcare for the people.

title: What Are Needs?
text:
What are some of your basic needs? Food, shelter, clothing, sleep, love, education, safety, medical care, and others may come to mind. A need is something that you have to have every day to survive. We need certain things to stay safe and be healthy. The things that we need every day don't change with time. We need air to breathe. We need food and water to survive. We need a safe place to live. Clothing is a need that helps keep us safe by keeping us warm or cool. Needs are something you must have to have in order to survive.

In addition to your basic needs, you might also have other needs. Some of your needs may be different from those of your classmates. If both of your parents work, you may need a place to go after school until they return home. If you have a special medical condition, you may need to take medicine each day. You may also need special tools, such as a wheelchair, crutches, or an inhaler to help you be successful each day.

title: What Are Wants?
text:
A want is something that you would like to have but can live without. It is something that you can wait for. Not everyone wants the same things at the same time. You may want a new bike or a new video game. Someone else may want a new book. Wants are things that are optional. You don’t need them to survive.

Sometimes it's difficult to decide whether you want or need something. Each of us makes these choices throughout the day. We go through the process of determining the positive and negative consequences of purchasing our wants. We evaluate if it is still a need or a want. Then, we make a choice of what would be best for us.

title: Needs and Wants of a Community
text:
Just like individuals, communities have needs and wants. Goods and services meet community needs and wants. Goods are things that people buy to meet their needs and wants. People produce goods like food, clothing, furniture, and toys to meet the wants and needs of a community.

A service is work that a person does for someone else. Communities provide services to people. Important community services include providing water, electricity, schools, and hospitals to meet people’s needs.

A community must evaluate if something is a want or a need. Communities work together to provide goods and services. Together, they examine needs and the possible resources available to meet those needs. Community members share their opinions. They talk, give demonstrations, write articles for the newspaper, or put up signs to make their wants or needs known.

When all of the opinions are heard, people begin to compromise to reach a positive outcome. In a compromise, everyone gives something up to create a solution. When we compromise, we think about what is best for the group. We don't just think about what we want individually.

Needs and wants can change due to personal, environmental, and economic events. If your parents lose their job, they may not have enough money to spend on wants. Basic human needs, like food, water, shelter, and clothing, become the main priority. Resources can become scarce, or not available, after a natural disaster or in times of war. It can be difficult for people to meet their basic needs. Communities must work together to share resources and help each other.

title: Economic Systems
text:
There are many different economic systems for countries located on the continent of Africa. An economic system is how a society or government organizes and distributes resources, services, and goods to its people. Each country’s system is influenced by its unique historical, social, and political events. A country’s economic system is also closely tied to its form of government. While most African countries have unique economic systems, some fall into a few categories.

A command economy is mostly controlled by the government. This control includes how resources are made available and how goods and services are sold. In a command economy, the government also sets the prices of certain goods and services. They may also control how much profit, if any, people can receive for their work. A command economy is the most restrictive kind of economy for businesses. However, a command economy can be helpful in countries or regions where resources are scarce and people may need help accessing them. Generally, countries with strong command economies have more autocratic forms of government. An autocratic government controls most aspects of people’s lives.

In a market economy, the way people get resources is driven by supply and demand. Generally, the price of goods and services is determined in two parts. First, prices are driven by the available goods and services, or the supply. Second, it depends on whether or not people want or need the goods and services. That's called the "demand." For example, if there is a lot of a product but no one wants or needs it, then the price for that product may be low. The opposite may also be true. If a product is scarce, that means the supply is low. The price of that good or service may be high if it is in great demand. A pure market economy has few government restrictions on how resources are produced, bought, and sold. The government may promote private ownership of businesses, free trade, competition, and work. They may also try to attract foreign investment to increase economic growth.

Some African countries operate economic systems guided by tradition and history. This system is called a traditional economy. That means economic activities are not necessarily motivated by wealth and profit. In a traditional economy, the goal is to ensure communities have the resources to survive. Traditional economies are often not regulated or monitored by the government. People in this system might operate small-scale subsistence farms. These are farms where people grow enough for their families and communities. They also conduct trade with their neighbors. Other activities, such as street vending in community marketplaces, take place in traditional economies. While there are benefits to a traditional economy, there are also many challenges. Some drawbacks include a lack of governmental protections and safety measures for workers and consumers.

Most countries throughout the world operate as a blend of economic systems. A mixed economy combines elements of command, market, and traditional economies. Mixed economies may have governmental regulations of activities but also allow people to own and operate businesses.

African countries operate their economies on a continuum, or range, between pure command, pure market, and pure traditional systems. On one end of this range is a command economy, in which the government controls everything. On the other end is a market economy, driven by supply and demand. Most countries’ economies operate somewhere between these two extremes.

title: Essential Question
text: How does a country’s location and government affect its economic activities?

title: South Africa’s Economy
text:
South Africa is located in the southern region of the African continent. The country has a mixed economy. It combines parts of the command, market, and traditional economies. Its economic system is closer to the middle of the range. There are private companies and opportunities for personal wealth. In South Africa, people are allowed to start their own businesses. They can also profit from their work. Personal economic freedom exists, but the government plays a large role in regulating economic activities.

The government in South Africa plays a significant role in its economy. It sets rules and regulations to protect workers' rights and ensure fair business competition. The government also provides essential services, like education and healthcare. Additionally, the government owns and operates some important industries and services. These include transportation systems, access to electricity, and telecommunications systems, like internet and telephone services.

South Africa has many natural resources, such as gold, diamonds, and platinum. These natural resources have played a significant role in the economy. Mining for these resources brings income to the country. It also provides thousands of jobs. Fertile farmland is another important natural resource. Farmers in South Africa grow crops like maize, wheat, fruits, and vegetables. They also raise animals for meat and dairy products.

South Africa has a well-developed manufacturing industry. Goods such as cars, clothing, electronics, and furniture are created in South African factories. Manufacturing also provides jobs for many South Africans. The industry contributes to the country's economy. Some factories even export their products to other countries. This helps to bring more money into South Africa’s economy.

Tourism is another important part of the South African economy. People worldwide come to South Africa to see its beautiful landscapes, wildlife, and historical sites. Tourism brings in money from outside the country. The travel industry provides more employment opportunities as well.

One of the main goals of South Africa's economic system today is to address historical inequalities caused by apartheid. Apartheid is the name for the system of racial segregation that was in place in South Africa until the early 1990s. Apartheid was an official policy established by the South African government at the time. Under apartheid, Black South Africans experienced violence, segregation, or separation from white South Africans. Almost no economic opportunities were available for Black South Africans under this system. Today, the government of South Africa is working to reduce poverty and promote economic opportunities for all South Africans.

title: Factors of Economic Growth in South Africa
text:
Many factors determine how well an economy grows in a country. Literacy rate, entrepreneurship levels, and investments in industries, human capital, and capital goods can tell economists a lot about the health and future of a country’s economic system. Economists also measure how healthy a country’s economy is by measuring the Gross Domestic Product, or GDP. GDP measures the total value of goods and services bought in a year. When a country produces and sells more valuable goods and services, its GDP will be higher.

Literacy rates can contribute to the overall economy of a country. The literacy rate is the percentage of people in a country who can read and write. In South Africa, the adult literacy rate is approximately 94 percent. That percentage includes citizens aged 15 and above. This means that more people in the country have the skills necessary to work in industries that contribute to the economy.

Many of South Africa’s industries struggle to keep up with the growing population. There's a greater demand for goods and services. Many industries are looking for new ways to get the electricity and resources needed to increase production. The South African government is working to solve this by investing in renewable energy sources. This includes energy systems like solar, wind, and water power. With these resources, South Africa’s industries will have the power to grow and meet the population’s demand.

In economics, the term “capital” means anything that gives a person or business value. Capital goods are resources, like machines, used to produce other goods and services. Human capital refers to the skills, knowledge, and health of the people in a society. Human capital and capital goods are both needed to make an economy stronger. If a country has state-of-the-art equipment but no one with the skills to operate it, the economy cannot grow. The opposite is true: Skilled workers with outdated and inefficient equipment cannot help the economy succeed. The South African government has created Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to attract businesses to invest in capital goods and human capital. The government has made it easier to start a business in these zones. Because of this, South Africa’s GDP will increase as more companies invest in the country.

Entrepreneurship is the ability and willingness of individuals to start their own businesses. They take risks to create new economic opportunities. Many South Africans may not have the resources or business knowledge needed to open their businesses. That's where the Small Enterprise Development Agency, or SEDA, comes in. SEDA is a government agency created to help people create new businesses. It also offers training, support, and loans to South Africans who want to become entrepreneurs.

South Africa faces some significant challenges in growing its economy. The policies of apartheid denied many Black South Africans the opportunity to attend school or receive a quality education. The current government is working to address this issue. They are creating policies to reduce poverty. They are also seeking to improve South Africans' access to education and healthcare. While it may take time for South Africans to recover from the effects of apartheid, these efforts are working toward equal access for everyone to grow and thrive.

title: Nigeria’s Economic System
text:
Nigeria is a country in West Africa. Nigeria has a mixed economic system that combines elements of a market economy and a command economy. Several sectors contribute to Nigeria’s economic growth. One important economic area is agriculture. This involves farming and production of crops like cocoa, palm oil, and yams. Many Nigerians work in agriculture, which provides food and raw materials for other industries.

Another important area of Nigeria’s economy is oil and gas. Oil and gas are the most important natural resources that Nigeria produces. Nigeria is a major oil producer and exporter. Income from oil plays a significant role in the country's economy. The government earns money from selling oil to fund various projects and programs. However, there are drawbacks to Nigeria’s oil industry. When oil prices are high due to high demand, Nigeria’s economy is very strong. When oil prices are low, the economy is weak. These economic swings may cause some companies outside of Nigeria to be unwilling to invest their resources. This can present several challenges to Nigeria’s economy.

Nigeria also has a growing services sector. This area of the economy provides services to people worldwide. Some of these services include banking, telecommunications, tourism, and entertainment. The service industry contributes to the overall economy by providing jobs and generating income.

As part of a mixed economy, the Nigerian government regulates and guides the economy. It sets policies, creates laws, and provides support for economic activities. The government also collects taxes from individuals and businesses. The taxes fund public services. Public services include education, healthcare, and developing infrastructure, like roads and buildings.

Nigeria faces some economic challenges. Poverty and inequality are widespread. Many Nigerians struggle to access basic services and job opportunities. The country also deals with issues like government corruption, inadequate infrastructure, and a high unemployment rate. These impact economic growth and development.

title: Factors That Influence Nigeria’s Economic Growth
text:
The adult literacy rate in Nigeria is approximately 62 percent. A significant percentage of people cannot read and write. This makes it difficult for people to find high-paying skilled labor jobs. The Nigerian government has established several programs to help increase access to education. To improve its literacy rate, the Nigerian government has made school free for all children between the ages of six and 15 years old. The government also provides meals to students to help them stay in school. The government is also investing in programs to teach adults how to read and write.

Currently, Nigeria lacks resources to modernize its industries. Companies worldwide are not often willing to invest in Nigeria’s industries due to concerns. These issues include lack of security and political instability within the country. The Nigerian government is investing resources in updating and improving the country’s security. The government also has created new policies that will make it safer and easier to do business within the country.

Much of Nigeria’s infrastructure requires updating. In its current state, it is not always reliable. The electrical power supply does not always work. Transportation systems can frequently be disrupted. Historically, natural resources have not been distributed equally among Nigeria’s citizens. Many wealthy people receive the majority of access to resources. The poorer citizens have little to no access. Nigeria’s population is increasing at a high rate, which strains access to healthcare and education. Like South Africa, the Nigerian government has Special Economic Zones (SEZs) throughout the country. The government also invests in improving the country’s healthcare facilities and education system.

Many entrepreneurs in Nigeria have concerns about the country’s ability to provide political stability and reduce crime. Many highly educated Nigerians leave in search of better jobs elsewhere in the world. The government is partnering with organizations worldwide to address crime in its communities. Safer communities can help keep businesses in Nigeria. More businesses will strengthen the economy, and Nigerians will not have to leave the country to look for employment opportunities.

Nigeria’s economy faces many challenges but has great potential to grow. The most pressing issue facing Nigeria is high crime. When citizens are unsafe in their communities, economic growth is challenging. Efforts to improve security can enable other programs to expand. Nigeria is working to increase literacy rates, invest in human capital and capital goods, and ensure an equitable distribution of natural resources.

title: Kenya’s Economic System
text:
Kenya is located in East Africa. The economic system of Kenya can be described as a mixed economy. It combines elements of both a market economy and a command economy. Businesses and individuals decide what to produce and buy based on supply and demand. The government also plays a role in regulating and guiding economic activities.

Kenya is known for its rich natural resources and varied economy. One of the key areas of the economy is agriculture. This involves farming and the production of crops. Kenya has nutrient-rich soil and a climate suitable for farming. This allows for growing various crops, such as tea, coffee, and maize. Horticultural products, such as flowers and vegetables, are also grown in Kenya.

Tourism is an important part of Kenya’s economy. Kenya is home to remarkable landscapes and wildlife. National parks, such as the Maasai Mara and Amboseli, provide sanctuaries for plants and animals. They also preserve the environment. Tourists from around the world visit Kenya for wildlife safaris, where they can see wildlife in its natural surroundings. Tourists also come to take part in cultural experiences. One of the most popular is the Turkana Festival. The festival is a three-day celebration of the culture of Kenya’s northern nomadic communities. Income from tourism creates economic opportunities for Kenyans through hotels, restaurants, and transportation.

One of Kenya’s top natural resources is geothermal energy. Geothermal power plants use heat from deep inside the Earth to make steam, which generates electricity. This renewable energy source helps meet the country's electricity needs. It also reduces the country’s reliance on fossil fuels, such as gas and oil.

The Kenyan government plays a role in regulating and promoting economic activities. Recently, the government provided funding and support to 500,000 small-scale farms nationwide. This will support individual entrepreneurs. The funding will also provide resources for local communities. The government has started promoting its location in East Africa with access to the Indian Ocean as a center for international trade. This location and access allow companies to ship their goods from Eastern Africa to Europe and the rest of the world. Energy projects to support economic growth have become a priority. The government has sought to improve the power supply and internet connectivity as well.

Kenya faces some economic challenges. Poverty and income inequality are ongoing issues. The government is also creating programs to ensure that people from all areas of Kenya have the opportunity to become economically successful. Programs include agricultural productivity, access to education and healthcare, and promoting entrepreneurship and job creation.

title: Factors That Influence Kenya’s Economic Growth
text:
A large portion of the adult population in Kenya cannot read or write. The adult literacy rate is measured at around 58 percent. Access to education in Kenya’s remote villages and towns has been difficult for many years. Due to this, literacy rates in rural and remote Kenyan areas are much lower than in urban ones. To address this, the government is focusing on teaching adults who did not attend school how to read and write. The government is using technology to help increase education. Many citizens have access to mobile phones and the internet. Mobile and distance learning are becoming popular ways for Kenyans to learn.

Kenya’s population is growing. The country's infrastructure needs to be updated to keep up. Government policies for businesses are outdated. They can sometimes get in the way of economic progress. To address this, the government is creating new policies. They are trying to make doing business in the country easier. Access to basic services can be difficult in certain areas as well. Kenya’s roads and transportation systems need repair. The country is also investing in updating its infrastructure to give citizens better access to the necessary resources. Government projects have been started to build railroads and rapid transit lines. These will connect major cities to more rural areas. There are also efforts to upgrade existing roads to be more permanent. Many roads in Kenya are not paved. They are often washed out or destroyed in bad weather.

Because many of Kenya’s industries are outdated, most of the capital goods for Kenya’s industries must be imported, or brought in from other countries. This makes it difficult and expensive to acquire the machines and resources that industries need to grow. The government is encouraging businesses to build machines and other capital goods they need themselves rather than import them. The “Buy Kenya, Build Kenya” campaign is designed to boost the manufacturing of capital goods in Kenya.

Due to Kenya’s low literacy rate, there are more jobs that require skilled labor than there are people with the necessary skills to fill them. This is called a skills gap. To address this, Kenya invests in adult education and training programs. These programs are designed to train citizens in the skills they need to work in specialized industries.

Like other countries, entrepreneurs in Kenya may not have access to the financial support needed to start a business. Starting a business in Kenya can be a difficult process. The steps a person has to follow can be confusing. Government policies often change without notice. Programs like the Youth Enterprise Development Fund, the Women Enterprise Fund, and the Uwezo Fund provide financial support, training, and other help for entrepreneurs. Among other services, these programs can help people follow the steps needed to start and develop their businesses.

Despite its many challenges, Kenya's economy is experiencing positive economic growth. The literacy rate is slowly improving. Efforts to invest in education and training are improving human capital. In recent years, Kenya’s government has successfully attracted investments, improved the availability of capital goods, and supported entrepreneurship.

title: Conclude and Connect
text: Every country has its own economic system to help meet its citizens' needs and wants. Many factors influence the ways that governments make economic decisions for their country. Some African countries, like South Africa, are still trying to overcome past discriminatory practices, such as apartheid. Today, South Africa is working to increase access to resources for citizens. This is helping them become more economically successful. Natural resources in many countries help boost the economy. They provide opportunities for jobs and a steady workforce. Natural resources like oil can help boost the economy in countries like Nigeria. However, demand for natural resources can influence the price and the overall benefit to the economy. Countries invest in their economies by increasing access to education. Boosting literacy rates can help citizens access jobs requiring reading and writing skills. The government in Kenya is working to reduce the “skills gap.” They are increasing literacy rates through adult education programs. Governments throughout the world consider how to utilize natural resources, industry, and human capital to help improve the economy and their citizens' lives.

title: Physical Characteristics
text: Physical characteristics tell us about a place. They are natural features of the Earth. Land and water are physical characteristics.

title: Landforms
text: Landforms are big areas of land. Deserts and valleys are landforms. Coasts and mountains are landforms.

title: Bodies of Water
text: Bodies of water are areas on Earth where water collects and covers the land. Oceans and lakes are bodies of water. Rivers and ponds are bodies of water, too.

title: Louisville, Kentucky
text:
Louisville, Kentucky, is an example of a town that grew to be a city. The geography and location along the Ohio River have contributed to population growth and urban development over time. Indigenous peoples occupied the area through 1650. Eventually, the people fought over land and resources, including beavers. During the 1600s, the Indigenous population in the area decreased because of the Beaver Wars. After the Beaver Wars, European and American explorers began settling in the area. As a result, the population of Louisville increased again.

In 1778, the town was founded and then later named after King Louis XVI of France. People began to gather in Louisville to trade and distribute goods and services. Many Native American tribes were unhappy with the number of new settlers who came to the area. Conflicts began to occur between settlers and Native Americans. The new settlers built forts to protect the town of Louisville. The first fort was called Fort-on-Shore, which was located on present-day 12th Street. A larger fort, Fort Nelson, was located on present-day Main Street.

title: Louisville-Jefferson Metro Area
text:
The population of Louisville grew slowly during the late 1700s. During this time, families migrated to the area. Services, such as a fire department, were added to the community as the population increased. People began to build homes and businesses.

Growth in Louisville increased in the 1800s. The invention of the steamboat changed Louisville. Steamboats allowed more people and goods to reach the town. In 1828, the population of Louisville reached more than 7,000 people. In the 1820s and 1830s, public schools, a library, and a newspaper all became part of the community. As transportation in the United States changed and became better, more people came to Louisville. In 1900, the population reached 204,731.

The 20th century brought even more change to Louisville, including a zoo, restaurants, and more opportunities for higher education. Factories, museums, and cultural centers brought additional change to the city. Today, there is even an area of Louisville called Museum Row.

In 2003, Louisville and Jefferson County merged into a larger metropolitan, or urban, area known as Louisville-Jefferson Metro. In 2023, Louisville had the largest population in the state of Kentucky.

title: Theodore Roosevelt
text: Theodore Roosevelt was born in 1858. He lived in New York City. He was an explorer. He loved nature and traveling to different places.

title: Young Theodore Roosevelt
text: As a child, Theodore Roosevelt loved to study nature. He read books about it. He studied real birds and animals.

title: Theodore Roosevelt and the Environment
text: Theodore Roosevelt loved the United States. He respected the plants and animals that live here. He worked hard to take care of the places where plants and animals live.

title: National Parks
text: Theodore Roosevelt became president of the United States. He wanted to protect the land. National parks were a way he could do that. He created national parks for people to enjoy.

text:
