title: Leaders of the Armies: Federal and Confederate
text:
A civil war is a type of conflict where citizens of the same country are fighting against each other. The war in the United States in the 1860s was a civil war. Some citizens of the United States decided to rebel against the established government and the decisions that it was making.

The cause of the war was a debate over the legalization of slavery. The question was: Could states decide on their own if enslaving people was legal? Many of the southern states thought they had the right to choose if they would allow slavery. They also believed this was the right of any territory that became a state. Some Americans quickly decided to join the rebelling Confederate States of America. Other Americans chose to stay in the Union of the United States of America. Some citizens of the United States weighed the decision and had great difficulty making a choice between the Confederacy and the Union.

The leaders of the Union and Confederacy were not strangers to each other. Many of the military and political leaders had very close social connections. In fact, Ulysses S. Grant, the leader of the Union army, and Robert E. Lee, the leader of the Confederate army, both attended the military academy at West Point. They even served together during the Mexican-American War in the late 1840s. Every military officer in the United States in 1861 knew Robert E. Lee. He was so highly respected that President Abraham Lincoln offered Lee the command position of the Army of the Potomac. Lee carefully weighed his thoughts, loyalties, and convictions, as did every officer. Their choices changed their lives and made history. In the end, Lee chose to join the Confederacy.

title: The Atlanta Campaign
text:
William T. Sherman had fought in the war since some of the first battles. He had been fairly successful in these battles. He had seen war across many states. As the war stretched into its third year, Sherman thought about how to defeat the Confederacy with the least amount of death. He believed that this would require that the Southerners’ desire to fight be broken. He figured that one way to accomplish this was by destroying the South’s resources.

In May of 1864, Sherman and his troops were in Tennessee. The next goal was to capture Atlanta. This city was the heart of the South’s resources for manufacturing and railroads. If the Union forces could take this city, the South’s supply lines would be broken.

Sherman left Tennessee for Georgia but had to fight Confederate troops all the way to Atlanta. The Union troops would not attack Confederate troops head-on. Instead, the Union troops would outflank, or go to the side of, the Confederate troops. This forced Confederate troops to continually retreat. By July, Confederate troops had retreated to Atlanta. Sherman’s tactic was to surround the city, cut off the Confederates' supply lines, and force them to surrender. On September 1, 1864, Confederate troops evacuated Atlanta before the Union army entered the city. The city surrendered to the Union army that same day.

The casualties of this campaign were large, but the victory gave the Union renewed hope. The capture of Atlanta was also a major factor in getting Abraham Lincoln reelected as president.

title: Sherman’s March to the Sea
text:
General William T. Sherman’s men controlled Atlanta from September through mid-November. Before leaving the city, Sherman evacuated all the citizens of Atlanta. He then ordered his men to burn down Atlanta’s military resources. This included weapon factories, clothing mills, and railway yards. After a two-month siege and this final destruction of resources, the city was left in ruins.

Sherman’s next goal was to make it to the Atlantic Ocean and Savannah, Georgia. Once at Savannah, Sherman could reconnect the Union army with naval supply lines. During the march from Atlanta to Savannah, Sherman continued to pursue his goal to stop the bloodshed. He focused on destroying Southern property and support for the Confederate cause. Because Sherman had destroyed all supply lines in Georgia, his men had to find their supplies along the route. Union soldiers stole livestock and food. Sherman’s army also destroyed military targets: tunnels, bridges, and railroad tracks. Sherman’s army left a trail of ransacked farms and supply lines across the state.

On December 21, 1864, Sherman and his troops arrived in Savannah. The city was unguarded because the Confederate soldiers had already fled. Sherman offered the city to President Abraham Lincoln as a Christmas gift. In early 1865, Sherman and his troops left Savannah and headed north to the Carolinas.

title: Thomas “Stonewall” Jackson
text:
Thomas "Stonewall" Jackson was born in Clarksburg, Virginia, on January 21, 1824. Jackson graduated from West Point Military Academy at 22, just in time for the Mexican-American War. He fought in the war and retired from the military as a war hero. Later, he served as a professor at the Virginia Military Institute. In April of 1861, Jackson was ordered back to Virginia Military Institute to act as a drill instructor. There, he trained new recruits to fight in the Civil War. Soon after, Jackson was stationed in Harper’s Ferry, Virginia to train his new troops. Jackson became famous. He earned his nickname at the First Battle of Bull Run on July 21, 1861. He led a brigade into the battle at the perfect time. He helped the Confederates hold an important position. A Confederate general named Barnard Bee told his men to be brave. He told them to look at Jackson standing there “like a stone wall.” The nickname “Stonewall” stuck for the rest of his life.

After Bull Run, Stonewall Jackson was promoted. He became a major general where he continued to win battle after battle for the Confederates. His troops became known as the “Stonewall Brigade,” during a three-month march that included five battles and more than 650 miles. These battles took the attention of the Union away from the Confederates moving into Richmond, Virginia. By distracting the Union in other battles, Jackson saved Richmond from being taken. After a huge success at the Battle of Chancellorsville, Jackson was accidentally shot by his own men and died eight days later, at the age of 39. Military historians regard Stonewall Jackson as one of the most gifted commanders in United States history. His strategies are still studied at West Point Academy and Virginia Military Institute to this day.

title: Opportunity Cost
text:
Most of the time, we want many things. However, we usually can’t get everything we want. This means we have to make choices. Our choices are affected by the price and by what is available.

Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you make a choice. For example, imagine that you wanted to play at the park. Instead, you chose to go swimming. The opportunity cost of swimming is giving up the park and the enjoyment of playing there.

title: Essential Question
text: What affects economic choices?

title: Supply and Demand
text: The price of a good or service depends on two things. First, it depends on how much of it there is for people to buy. That’s called supply. Next, it depends on how many people want or need it. That’s called demand. When the supply is low and the demand is high, the price goes up. When the supply is high and the demand is low, the price goes down.

title: Surplus
text: Surplus is when there is more of something than people need or want. A surplus of a good or service usually makes the price go down.

title: Scarcity
text: Scarcity is not having enough of something. Scarcity usually makes prices go up. When goods and services become scarce, families have to choose carefully. They have to decide what they need most. Sometimes scarcity can be a big problem. If food or water are scarce, it is hard for people to live.

title: The United States Constitution
text:
The Constitution of the United States was written in 1787. The Constitution gives directions on what the government can and can't do in the United States. It matches the ideas in the Declaration of Independence.

Members of the government met in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, to create the national government. The government is based on the people having the right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. It is the people who give their consent, or agreement, to be governed. The way they are governed is described in the Constitution.

The people elect representatives to make decisions for the common good. Representing the people is an important democratic principle. President Abraham Lincoln said the United States is a “government of the people, by the people, for the people.”

Changes to the Constitution are called amendments. Today, there are 27 amendments to the Constitution. The first 10 amendments are known as the Bill of Rights. They are not the only amendments that have been made. Amendments have made slavery illegal, given women the right to vote, and made the voting age 18.

Congress sets up the process for states to ratify, or approve, an amendment. Three-fourths of the states must pass it. The system of checks and balances helps make sure all voices are heard. Citizens can voice their ideas about amendments to their elected officials. This gives the people a voice in the government.

title: Introduction to the Southeast
text:
The Southeast region of the U.S. includes land from the Ohio River to the Gulf of Mexico. It also includes land from Texas to the Atlantic Ocean. The southeast region of the United States was once home to thousands of American Indians. This was before European explorers came to the region. The tribes of this region met their needs using the natural resources available to them. The Southeast region has very fertile soil. This means that the soil has many nutrients. It is good for growing crops.

Many of the American Indians in this region were farmers. The Southeast is a perfect place to plant corn, beans, and squash. This is because of the climate and soil in this region. Corn, beans, and squash were known as the Three Sisters to many tribes. Corn was an important crop. It was traded with other tribes. They gathered wild plants, berries, and nuts. They ate these for food. Some plants were used to make medicine.

Southeastern tribes also hunted and fished for food. They hunted deer, raccoons, bears, turkeys, and squirrels. Some tribes even hunted alligators. The rivers and coastlines of the Southeast provided fish and other food as well.

Homes in the Southeast ranged from grass huts to wooden houses. Some tribes, like the Creek and Cherokee, used sticks and logs to build their homes. Most used wild grasses to make the walls or roofs of their homes. The Choctaw and Chickasaw built summer and winter homes. They used different materials. Winter houses were sturdier log houses with clay walls. Summer houses had thinner walls. Sometimes, summer houses had removable walls to let cool breezes enter the home.

Groups like the Creek, Cherokee, Choctaw, and Chickasaw built large mounds of earth. These were used for ceremonies and other purposes. You can still see the mounds throughout the Southeast. American Indian tribes of the Southeast were similar to each other. However, they also had their own cultures, beliefs, and languages. They had their own governments, economies, and traditions.

title: Essential Question
text: How were the tribes of the Southeast similar? How were they different?

title: Government Structures
text:
The American Indians of the Southeast had their own governments. The tribes of the Southeast were usually divided into clans or families. A clan is a small group of people. A clan is made up of one or more families. Many clans in the Southeast were matrilineal. This means that children were members of the same clan as their mothers. Clans join together to form tribes. A tribe is a group of people connected by a common language, belief, land, and culture.

Each tribe was organized in a different way. In some tribes, like the Choctaw, the clans were ways to organize families together in certain locations, like towns or villages. The Creek, Cherokee, and Chickasaw clans all lived together in their villages. Each clan had a different role in the village. Some were hunters or healers. Others fished and farmed.

Towns and villages were usually the lowest level of government in the Southeast. Council groups would help make decisions in the towns and villages. Leaders of the clans would often serve on these councils. Other members of the clan served on these councils too. Some tribes were led by a main chief. Many tribes split the duties of the chief between two people. Tribes like the Creek and Cherokee had a chief during war times and a chief for peace times.

title: Clothing
text:
The tribes of the Southeast made their clothing. They used the natural resources around them. They made clothing from animal fur and hides. Deer hide was a common source of clothing. Deer hides were used to make shirts, pants, dresses, aprons, and moccasins, or shoes.

Winter clothing was made from thicker furs. These furs came from bears and bison. Many tribes used these furs to make robes and leggings. They protected themselves from the cold. Some tribes in what is now Florida used alligator skin to make clothing.

Some tribes also made clothing from plant fibers and tree bark. The Timucua tribe of Florida used Spanish moss to make clothes. They made skirts and aprons from the moss. Tribes throughout the Southeast decorated their clothes. They used animal feathers and scales, shells, stones, and beads.

title: Language
text:
Several groups of American Indians in the Southeast have similar languages. These languages belong to the same family. They belong to the Muskogean language family. Choctaw and Chickasaw languages are very similar. Many people think they are two groups from the same language. The Creek language is also a member of the Muskogean language family.

Many words we use today come from the American Indian languages of the Southeast. The Chattahoochee River is an example. The river is named after a Creek word meaning “painted rocks.” The Creek word for "town" is another example. It is in the name of Florida’s capital city, Tallahassee.

The Cherokee language is a part of the Iroquoian language group. This group is different from the Muskogean languages. This language family has a relative in the northern region of the United States. This suggests that at one point the Cherokee people lived closer to the Great Lakes. The word “Cherokee” is from the Creek language.

title: Religion
text:
American Indian tribes of the Southeast had different beliefs about religion. Many beliefs centered on the natural world. They used these beliefs to explain the world around them. Many tribes believed that gods and goddesses were connected to the Earth and the environment. Some cultures of the Southeast included the idea of a supreme deity, or god. The Chickasaw believed that Aba’Binni’li’ created life on Earth. The Choctaw believed in a similar creator god, who went by many names.

American Indian religions have many stories that explain the world around them. One Choctaw legend is the story of the Unknown Woman who brought corn to her people. Corn is the most important crop to the Choctaw. Many tribes in the Southeast have gods and goddesses that represent thunder and lightning. Some gods take the forms of animals. These animals can be rabbits and birds. Legends of the southeastern peoples include mythological creatures. Cherokee legends include creatures made of rocks and invisible creatures.

The nations of the Southeast also participated in traditional ceremonies. Some of these ceremonies were unique to the tribe. Others were celebrated by more than one tribe. One common traditional ceremony was the Green Corn Ceremony. When the corn crop ripened in summer, the peoples of the Southeast would gather for the multi-day ceremony. The ceremony included feasts, performances, and the repair and improvement of the village.

title: American Indian Life Today: The Southeast
text:
The Southeast region is still home to many American Indian tribes today. Arkansas and North Carolina have the largest American Indian population in the Southeast. The largest tribe in the Southeast is the Cherokee tribe. The largest Cherokee population is in North Carolina.

There are three bands of Cherokee. All three Cherokee bands are recognized as sovereign nations. This means that the Cherokee have their own constitution and independent government. The Cherokee hold their own elections. The Cherokee tribes work with the U.S. government. The Eastern Band Cherokee also work with North Carolina state and local governments.

The Cherokee share many of their traditions with others. The Cherokee National Holiday honors the signing of the Cherokee Constitution of 1839. Thousands of people come together for a large celebration called a powwow. People demonstrate traditional arts and crafts. They have a competitive stickball game. There is also a parade and a cook-off with native dishes like fry bread.

Today, the largest tribe in Georgia is the Lower Muskogee Creek tribe. The Lower Muskogee Creek tribe has 2,800 members. The members of the tribe practice many of the same traditions as their ancestors. They hold many ceremonies each year. Many members of the tribe teach people about Muskogee Creek culture. They teach people in the local area about Muskogee Creek clothing, stories, basket making, and games.

title: Beekeepers and Bees
text:
Beekeepers have a very important job. They take care of bees. Bees help fruits and vegetables grow. Bees make sweet, delicious honey.

Bees are like a community. They live together in large groups. Bees have many different jobs to do. They all work together to keep each other safe.

Worker bees are the smallest … and the busiest! They keep the hive clean. They feed the babies. They care for the queen. They build storage spaces. They guard the hive. They also gather and make food.

Does that sound like some community workers and helpers you know? Let's say thanks to the bees and beekeepers because they help make life sweet!

title: Maps and Globes

title: Mercator’s Maps
text:
A long time ago, there was a clever man named Gerardus Mercator. He loved to learn. He went to a special school where he studied geography. He learned about many new places.

Gerardus became very good at writing and drawing. He drew maps of different places around the world. His maps showed mountains, rivers, and cities.

People loved Gerardus's maps because they helped them find their way. His maps were so important. Today, many, many years later, mapmakers still use his ideas. These ideas help us explore and understand the big world around us!
